> Real-Time Threat Intelligence for Smart Contracts.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webhook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webhook-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Kaizen solves the critical latency gap in smart contract security.
Most security systems are reactive exploits are detected only after transactions are finalized and funds are already lost. Protocol teams lack real-time behavioral visibility to identify coordinated attacks such as flash-loan exploits, oracle manipulation, or liquidity drains before execution.

Kaizen provides real-time threat detection and autonomous mitigation within the same block window. By continuously analyzing on-chain behavioral signals and scoring contract risk using machine learning, it can trigger conditional defensive actions like kill-switch transactions or access enforcement. This shifts security from post-incident monitoring to proactive execution-time defense, reducing financial loss, response time, and operational overhead for on-chain protocols.

**Challenges we ran into**

A key challenge while building Kaizen was maintaining consistent real-time monitoring during periods of high on-chain activity.
The initial pipeline processed block data synchronously fetching logs, deriving behavioral features, sending them for scoring, and then triggering alerts. This worked under normal conditions but became slow and unreliable during stress testing when blocks contained a large number of contract interactions. Sequential RPC calls created noticeable delays in scoring and alert generation.
To fix this, I refactored the system into a simple event-driven pipeline where block events are queued and processed by independent workers in parallel. I also optimized RPC usage by batching and parallelizing requests. This improved responsiveness and made the monitoring flow more stable during activity spikes.

**DeFi**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12ff92a5140e419ebb2f5a2d2aab6f30/76b06f31-0e8f-47f4-a991-2318869a554f.png)

DeFi protocols operate in a paradox: once deployed, the code that secures user funds is completely static, but the attack surface is not.
Kaizen solves this by treating smart contract security as a continuous runtime problem, not a one-time audit. Every block, we extract behavioral signals from your contract including outflow patterns, caller anomalies, governance spikes, and admin activity, then score them against a protocol-specific baseline and respond autonomously if a threat is confirmed.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![WalletConnect](https://img.shields.io/badge/WalletConnect-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**BaseStack**

The Ultimate Payment Stack for Base – Transforming "Manual Push" into "Auto-Debit" for the Global-Local Economy.

**Project Description**
BaseStack is a recurring payment infrastructure designed to bridge the gap between local economies and global crypto payments. By leveraging the low fees of the Base network, we transform the friction of manual crypto transfers into a seamless "Auto-Debit" experience.

We empower merchants to price their services in local currency (e.g., IDRX) for domestic users while simultaneously accepting global stablecoins (USDC) from international users. All payments are settled automatically via a trustless Keeper network, creating a true "Set & Forget" subscription model onchain.


**The Problem it solves**

Most crypto payments are still stuck in the "Manual Push" era. If users want to subscribe to a newsletter, a community, or a SaaS product, they must remember the due date, log in to their wallet, and perform a manual transfer every single month. This creates high friction and "subscription fatigue." If they forget, the service is cut off.

In the Web2 world, this is solved by expensive intermediaries. Creators and merchants rely on payment gateways (like Stripe or PayPal) that charge high fees (2-5% + fixed costs) and impose strict geographic restrictions. For merchants in emerging markets (like Indonesia), accepting global payments often means losing significant value to FX fees or being rejected entirely due to lack of business entity registration.

Simultaneously, the "Global vs. Local" disconnect hinders adoption. Onchain payments are borderless, but pricing is not. A merchant wants to charge locals in their native currency (e.g., IDRX) and global users in stablecoins (e.g., USDC). Currently, no simple infrastructure exists on Base to handle this dual-currency subscription model automatically without complex manual management.

**How BaseStack Solves This**

BaseStack transforms the payment experience from "Manual Push" to a "Set & Forget" automated protocol.

**Changing the Model to "Set & Forget"**
BaseStack eliminates the need for users to be the admin of their own finances every month.
 1. One-Time Approval: Users sign a single approval transaction at the start.

 2. Automated Execution: Our Smart Contract & Keeper Bot work in the background to renew subscriptions precisely on the due date.

3. Result: Zero seconds wasted on service renewal. Users enjoy a Netflix-like experience onchain.

**Bridging the "Glocal" (Global-Local) Gap**
BaseStack introduces a smart multi-currency architecture that adapts to the user.

1. Context-Aware Pricing: Merchants can set a plan that accepts DRX from Indonesian IPs and USDC from the rest of the world.

2. Unified Revenue: Regardless of what currency the user pays with, the merchant receives the funds directly. This empowers local creators to monetize a global audience without banking barriers.

**Transparent and Trustless Direct Payments**
Unlike Web2 gateways that hold funds, BaseStack facilitates a direct Peer-to-Peer flow.

 1. No Middlemen: Money flows 100% from User to Creator.

 2. Safety & Control: The smart contract limits the maximum withdrawal amount per month. Merchants cannot withdraw more than agreed.

 3. Easy Exit: Users can cancel anytime by revoking allowance onchain, ensuring no party can withhold their right to stop paying.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into**

Fighting the Nature of Blockchain (Push vs. Pull) The biggest obstacle we encountered was the underlying architecture of Ethereum/Base, which is Push-Payment (User must actively send). We wanted to create a Pull-Payment experience, but Smart Contracts cannot auto-execute based on time.

**How we solved it:** We implemented a *Keeper Network design pattern*. We built a lightweight Off-chain Bot (using Node.js/TypeScript) that monitors the Smart Contract. This Bot acts as a trigger, calling the chargeSubscription() function only for users who have passed the grace period (block.timestamp > nextPayment). To ensure security, the Smart Contract logic immediately increments the payment due date upon success, causing any subsequent charge attempts to revert, thus protecting user funds.

**Handling Transaction Failures Without Stopping the Bot** During mass billing tests, we found a critical issue: When one user failed to pay (due to insufficient balance), our Bot would crash or the batch transaction would revert, stopping the billing process for all other users in the queue. 

**How we solved it:** We changed the iteration logic on our Keeper Bot to use a **Try-Catch mechanism per user.** On the Smart Contract side, we added Error Handling that returns a bool success status instead of reverting the entire transaction block. If a user has insufficient balance, the system does not error; instead, it automatically changes the user's status to "Grace Period" and triggers a notification via Telegram so the user can top up.

**UX Friction: The "Infinite Approval" Fear** From a UX perspective, asking users to "Approve Unlimited Tokens" looks high-risk and scary for non-crypto natives. However, if users only approve the exact amount, the transaction fails the following month. We were trapped between Security vs. Convenience. 

**How we solved it:** We utilized Coinbase Smart Wallet combined with UI transparency. In the frontend, we offer clear options: "Approve for 1 Year" or "Approve Forever." By using **Coinbase Smart Wallet**, the approval process feels like a standard app login (Passkey/Biometric) rather than a complex crypto operation. This lowers the mental barrier while keeping the user informed about exactly what permissions they are granting.

**Base Track**

**BaseStack transforms Base into the go-to layer for the Subscription Economy.**

We leverage Base's infrastructure to create a "Set & Forget" payment protocol that allows creators to monetize globally without intermediaries.

**Efficiency**: We utilize Base's ultra-low gas fees to enable peer-to-peer micro-payments (e.g., Rp10,000 or <$1), which enables business models that were previously impossible on Ethereum mainnet.

**Adoption**: By combining Base's speed with **Coinbase** **Smart** **Wallet**, we offer a frictionless "Netflix-like" UX where users don't need to hold ETH for gas or manage complex keys, bringing real-world utility onchain.

**Technical** **Agility**: The rapid block finality on Base allowed our team to effectively test and deploy our off-chain **Keeper** **Network** that powers the automated billing engine.

### QRypto
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/qrypto-15dc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/dunnowhoo/qrypto-app) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://qrypto.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-13-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Scan QRIS, Pay with Crypto.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prisma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prisma-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square) ![COINBASE SMART WALLET](https://img.shields.io/badge/COINBASE%20SMART%20WALLET-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/76fd7919670c442b8cc463e758d44cd9/14a7a81a-c60d-4954-bf50-7184035fc20d.png)
**QRypto solves the critical "last-mile" problem in crypto adoption in Indonesia.** Despite Indonesia ranking **#3 globally in crypto adoption with 21.27 million crypto investors** and a mature **QRIS payment infrastructure serving 52.5M active users** and **33.7M merchants**, crypto remains economically idle in daily transactions. The fundamental issue isn't lack of users, merchants, or even regulation—**the bridge connecting crypto liquidity to real-world payments simply doesn't exist**. Current regulations already permit controlled integration through **POJK 3/2024 regulatory sandbox** and **Project Garuda**, yet no compliant infrastructure enables instant crypto-to-QRIS settlement.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/76fd7919670c442b8cc463e758d44cd9/59c04f5e-ec0e-441c-82d2-2e05c93cfba0.png)
**Existing crypto payment workflows are operationally broken and prohibitively expensive.** Converting crypto to usable IDR requires **4-5 fragmented steps across multiple platforms**—transferring to an exchange, selling crypto, withdrawing to a bank/e-wallet, then finally making a QRIS payment. This process takes **10-60 minutes** instead of seconds, incurs **3-5% in layered fees** (trading fees, spreads, withdrawal costs), and creates high transaction uncertainty. **No single entity owns the end-to-end payment flow**: crypto wallets lack fiat settlement, exchanges lack merchant integration, and payment gateways lack on-chain connectivity. For Web3 earners and crypto tourists, this friction makes daily crypto spending irrational.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/76fd7919670c442b8cc463e758d44cd9/0094e575-870d-40df-b8c3-265c0d282ccc.png)
**QRypto addresses a massive, untapped market opportunity.** Indonesia's **Rp 302 trillion annual QRIS transaction volume** represents the total addressable market (TAM). Within this, **Rp 21-42 trillion per year** constitutes realistic crypto-funded spending that could shift to crypto-powered QRIS payments (SAM). **QRypto targets a beachhead market of Rp 1.2-2 trillion annually within 5 years**, focusing on high-intent user segments: **Indonesian Web3 earners** (22-35 years old, Jakarta/Bandung) who receive salaries in crypto but face costly bank withdrawals for daily expenses, and **crypto-savvy tourists** (25-40 years old, predominantly in Bali) who want cashless, universal QRIS acceptance without relying on money changers.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/76fd7919670c442b8cc463e758d44cd9/0aa8179c-4708-4da6-9810-85b7b9d29c5b.png)
**QRypto collapses multi-step friction into a single, compliant, real-time payment flow.** The Alpha version validates technical feasibility: users scan QRIS, QRypto connects to their wallet and converts supported crypto into **IDRX** (a regulated stablecoin), then IDRX is instantly converted to IDR and settled to the merchant's account—fully compliant with Indonesian regulations. The Beta version achieves sub-30-second settlement by pre-authorizing payments through locked IDRX balances and releasing **pre-funded IDR float** to merchants, **eliminating latency and settlement risk**. This enables crypto to function as a **usable means of daily payment**, not just a tradable asset, while maintaining full regulatory compliance, **tiered KYC/AML monitoring**, and **real-time liquidity management.**

**Challenges we ran into**

**Our biggest technical hurdle was achieving compliant, instant fiat settlement without a PJP switching license.** During Alpha development, we discovered that **QRIS strings contain National Merchant IDs (NMID)** rather than direct bank account details, making direct "outbound" payments to merchants **impossible without specific Payment System Infrastructure Provider (PJP) authorization**. Indonesian regulations require all IDR settlements to flow through **licensed PJP and PFAK partners**. To overcome this for the MVP, we engineered a **hybrid mapping system**: our backend parses QRIS strings to extract merchant IDs and matches them against an internal registry, then triggers **PJP disbursements** as a compliant proxy. The **Beta version roadmap** addresses this structurally by pre-authorizing payments through **locked IDRX balances and pre-funded IDR float**, enabling **sub-30-second settlement** while we formalize PJP partnerships.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/76fd7919670c442b8cc463e758d44cd9/15a9f5f1-441e-4777-86f8-718b4d7f1b85.png)
**We mapped critical stakeholders early to ensure QRypto's long-term operational viability.** Using a **Penta Helix collaboration framework**, we identified that successful implementation requires **coordinated engagement across five ecosystem layers**: (1) **Tech Infrastructure partners** (IDRX, midtrans) who provide QRIS API access and enable direct IDRX-to-IDR redemption—these are **high-power, high-interest stakeholders we must manage closely**, (2) **Government & Regulators** (BI, OJK) who authorize and supervise QRIS and crypto activities—we keep them **satisfied through proactive compliance**, (3) **Academy & Research institutions** (CFDS, ameru) who conduct impact assessments to validate our model—we **monitor their outputs**, and (4) **Users & Ecosystem participants** who adopt the system and provide feedback—we **stay informed of their needs**. This stakeholder mapping ensures we're building **strategic partnerships with PJP providers, regulatory alignment with POJK 3/2024**, and **ecosystem readiness** before national scale.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/76fd7919670c442b8cc463e758d44cd9/b7a86061-5f21-4eda-b369-dd28e0104c73.png)
**We proactively identified and planned mitigation strategies for six critical operational risks.** Our **Severity-Occurrence Matrix** reveals that **(1) Liquidity & Float Risk** and **(5) AML/CFT & Illicit Transaction Risk** are the **highest-priority threats**—both materialize rapidly (<1 month) with high impact. We mitigate liquidity risk through **transaction caps (≤IDR 2M), pre-funded IDR float, and real-time liquidity monitoring**. For AML exposure, we implement **tiered KYC, real-time transaction monitoring, and regulator-ready audit trails. (4) Regulatory Classification Risk** is lower-frequency but **structurally critical**: we mitigate by positioning QRypto strictly as an **instant crypto off-ramp** (not a payment instrument), ensuring merchants only receive **IDR via licensed PJP and PFAK partners**. We also address **(2) System Reliability & Latency Risk** through **asynchronous processing, optimistic settlement, and SLA-backed integrations**, **(3) User Error & UX Friction** via **pre-transaction validation and time-bound quotes**, and **(6) IDRX Peg & Issuer Risk** by requiring **full reserve transparency and locking IDR value at confirmation time**.

**Additionally, we solved critical UX friction around gas fees using Account Abstraction.** Users holding IDRX but lacking ETH for blockchain gas fees would experience failed transactions. We implemented **Coinbase Paymaster** to fully sponsor network fees, ensuring **100% transaction success** and eliminating the "insufficient gas" error entirely—users never need to manage gas, making the experience as seamless as traditional e-wallets.

**Base Track**

**QRypto** is a **Base Mini-App** designed to solve the specific challenge of **"Limited accessibility for retail users"** by bridging on-chain assets to the real-world economy. We perfectly align with the track requirements through:

* **Deep IDRX Integration:** The core utility of our app is unlocking the liquidity of **IDRX (Rupiah Stablecoin)**. We transform IDRX from a passive store of value into an active medium of exchange for Indonesia's 33 million QRIS merchants.


* **Elevating Onchain UX:** We tackle "Poor onboarding" by leveraging **OnchainKit** and **Coinbase Smart Wallet**. Users log in via FaceID/Passkeys, completely abstracting away seed phrases and complex wallet setups.


* **Solving DeFi Complexity:** We solve the friction of gas management by implementing **Account Abstraction** via the **Base Paymaster**. This ensures a **"Gasless" experience**, allowing retail users to transact instantly on **Base L2** without needing to hold native ETH for fees.

### HookLab AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hooklab-ai-1581) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/danielnoveno/hackathon-hooklabai) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://minikit-test-hooklabai.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/OzcoemCqZB0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-13-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Empowering creators to go viral on Base App

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contract-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

HookLab AI solves a painful creator bottleneck: most posts fail (or underperform) because the hook (the first line) doesn’t land — and creators waste tons of time iterating blindly.

It also tackles a second friction point for Base/Farcaster creators: onchain + wallet friction makes experimentation feel risky, unclear, and slow.

With HookLab AI, creators can go from:

“I want to post” → “I have a strong post ready”
in minutes, with a workflow that’s intentionally designed around what actually drives engagement. 🚀

🎯 What people can use it for
1) 🧠 Generate hooks built for engagement (not vibes)
HookLab looks at what’s working on Farcaster (Base channel) and uses a measurable heuristic to evaluate hook performance:

Hook Strength Formula
hook_strength = (likes + recasts + replies) / follower_count

This makes trend-based writing less random and more data-guided ✅

2) 🙈 “Blind Hook Selection” to prevent wasting time
Creators often over-edit the wrong thing (body, formatting, details) when the real issue is: the hook didn’t work.

HookLab fixes this by enforcing focus:
- Only shows hook previews first (first line, ~≤120 chars)
- Full caption is hidden until a hook is chosen
- Full caption is only revealed after a user commits to one

This makes writing faster, safer, and more efficient ⚡

3) 🧩 Intent-based caption generation (how creators actually think)
Instead of “generate a caption” with no direction, HookLab starts from real posting intent, such as:
📢 Product update
🚀 Launch announcement
🧵 Thread opener
😂 Meme / culture post

So you get outputs that are actually usable — not generic filler.

4) 🖼️🎬 Turn captions into media instantly (image & video)
Once a caption is revealed, creators can expand into assets:
- Generate image based on the caption context 🖼️
- Generate video (recommended: vertical 5–10s) 🎬

This turns “writing a post” into a full content kit (text + visuals) ✨

5) 📌 Posting is streamlined (copy or deep-link)

After unlocking:
📋 Copy the caption
🔗 Tap “Post to Base” to open composer prefilled
No extra friction, just post faster ✅

6) 💳 Credits model that feels fair + low risk
HookLab reduces fear of paying for nothing:
- New wallets start with 5 free credits 🎁
- Browsing hooks is free 👀

Credits are spent only when you unlock final value (caption reveal, image, video)
So creators can explore freely, and only pay when something is worth using. ✅

7) 🧬 Hybrid onchain/offchain that’s practical & defensible

HookLab balances legitimacy + UX:
✅ Premium verification can be onchain
⚡ Quota/credits can be offchain for a gas-less experience

This makes it hackathon-ready and user-friendly at the same time.

**Challenges we ran into**

🧱 Challenges I ran into (and how I solved them)
1) 💥 Making credits fair (trust issue: “paid but didn’t receive”)
This was the most important constraint:
- Credits must be deducted only when a user unlocks value
- If payment fails, credits must not be deducted
- If unlock fails after payment, system should retry or restore credit

✅ How I solved it : 
- I separated preview state vs unlocked state
- I treated unlock as the only event allowed to change credit balance
- I designed retry / restore behavior to protect user trust

2) 🕒 Avoiding accidental charges during slow generation (especially video)
Video rendering can take time, which creates risk:
- Charging early = user feels scammed if result isn’t ready

✅ How I solved it : 
- I designed a clear lifecycle:
- queued → rendering → ready → unlock
- Credit is only spent when the asset is actually ready

3) 🔒 Enforcing “Blind Hook Selection” without leaking the full caption
Blind selection is not just UI—it’s a rule:
- Hook previews visible
- Full caption locked
- Reveal only after selection + unlock

✅ How I solved it : 
I structured output into two layers:
- hook preview payload (free)
- full caption payload (locked)
- So the product forces the correct behavior: choose the hook first.

4) ⛓️ Hybrid onchain/offchain truth (premium vs quota)
This is a classic Web3 tension:
- Onchain is credible ✅
- Offchain is fast and practical ⚡

✅ How I solved it : 
- Premium verification reads onchain state
- Credits/quota stays offchain for UX
- I avoided overclaiming “everything is onchain” (judge-safe)

5) 🧩 Ensuring “Post to Base” only uses unlocked content
Deep-link posting is powerful but risky:
- If it posts locked content, it breaks the credit model

✅ How I solved it
- The “Post to Base” action is gated behind unlocked state
- Composer payload always comes from the revealed caption, not previews

6) 🎥 Building a demoable flow under hackathon constraints
Hackathon demos must be:
- fast (under 60s)
- instantly understandable
- visually clean + no confusing branches

✅ How I solved it
I designed a linear “game-like” flow:
- 🔌 Connect wallet
- 🎯 Choose intent
- 👀 Browse hook previews (free)

✅ Select hook + unlock
🚀 Post to Base

### Multicoyn

> Pay with ANY Token

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

As digital asset adoption grows exponentially, the crypto payment ecosystem remains deeply fragmented. On average, users hold more than 4 different types of tokens in their wallets, yet most merchants only accept 1 or 2 specific stablecoins. This disparity creates a massive barrier for everyday transactions.

Currently, the crypto payment process is riddled with high friction. For instance, if a user holds 0.5 ETH and 100 USDC but needs to pay a $150 USDT invoice, they are forced into a tedious cycle: **Swap → Transfer → Wait**. This process typically takes up to **10 minutes**, requires **3 separate transactions**, and incurs significantly high gas fees.

For merchants, the situation is even more dire—it is an **"Integration Hell."** Building custom payment infrastructure takes weeks due to the lack of standardized widgets, ultimately leading to accounting nightmares and reconciliation chaos.

Multicoyn eliminates these barriers with its innovative multi-token transaction simplification technology.


## Businesses can now:

- **Accept Payments from Any Token**: Remove manual exchange friction for customers.
- **Instant, Hassle-Free Integration**: Replace weeks of development with a standardized, ready-to-use widget.
- **Automated Conversion**: Efficiently convert fragmented user balances into the merchant's preferred asset in one single step.
- **Streamlined Accounting**: Simplify complex financial reporting into a single, transparent data stream.


In short, Multicoyn cuts down time, costs, and technical complexity, transforming slow crypto transactions into a seamless, one-click experience.

> *"From Fragmentation to Fluidity. The Future of Multi-Token Payments. Eliminate Friction. Pay with Multicoyn."*

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a solution for complex fragmentation required persistence in overcoming several technical hurdles:

- **Simplifying Multi-Transaction Flows**: Turning a "3-transaction, 10-minute" process into a single instant step required highly efficient smart contract logic to minimize gas costs.
- **Standardizing Widgets for Developers**: Creating an integration tool that is universal yet flexible enough for various business types was a significant architectural challenge.
- **Balance Conversion Efficiency**: Ensuring that users with fragmented balances (like ETH and USDC) can accurately combine them for a single payment without the risk of transaction failure.

### CipherScan

> Zcash blockchain explorer. Privacy-first tools.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

When I started building on Zcash, I hit three walls pretty fast.

**First, the developer experience was rough.** Most block explorers were outdated or had confusing UIs. Worse, there was no comprehensive API I could just plug into. If I wanted transaction data, I'd need to run my own full node and figure out RPC calls myself. For someone new to Zcash, that's a huge barrier to entry.

**Second, there was a privacy paradox.** Zcash's shielded transactions are brilliant, but how do you actually verify your own transactions without compromising privacy? Every solution I found required sending your viewing keys to a third-party service. You had to choose: trust someone else with your keys, or build the entire decryption stack yourself.

**Third, privacy adoption was invisible.** I'd look at the blockchain and see most value still sitting in transparent pools. Users didn't understand the impact of their choices. There was no way to visualize privacy adoption, no incentive, no "aha!" moment that would push people toward shielded transactions.

I built CipherScan to fix these problems, starting with the hardest one: client-side memo decryption in the browser.

---

## What CipherScan Does

CipherScan is a block explorer with four core features:

### Developer Infrastructure
- Clean REST API + WebSocket feeds for blocks, transactions, addresses, and shielded pool stats
- Public Lightwalletd endpoints for both mainnet and testnet
- Open-source with deployment scripts, you can use our hosted instance or self-host
- Coming soon: NPM package (@cipherscan/zcash-memo-decrypt) for drop-in client-side decryption

### Client-Side Memo Decryption
- 342KB WebAssembly module compiled from Zcash's core crypto libraries (orchard, sapling-crypto)
- Supports both Orchard and Sapling pools
- Decrypt single transactions or full wallet history
- Zero-trust: your viewing keys never leave your browser

### Privacy Metrics
- Real-time Privacy Score showing % of Zcash value in shielded vs transparent pools
- Historical tracking to visualize adoption trends
- "Learn Zcash" page with wallet guides and developer resources

### Cross-Chain ZEC Flows 
- Real-time tracking of ZEC swaps via NEAR Intents (BTC, ETH, SOL, NEAR → ZEC)
- Shielded Rate metric: what % of bridged ZEC gets shielded after arrival
- Volume analytics with 24h/7d trends and chain breakdown

**Status:**
- ✅ Testnet fully operational: https://testnet.cipherscan.app
- ✅ Mainnet fully operational: https://cipherscan.app
- 🔄 ZEC Flows: UI complete with mock data, awaiting NEAR Intents API key for live integration

**Challenges we ran into**

## WebAssembly Memo Decryption - The Hardest Part

Compiling Zcash's cryptographic libraries to WebAssembly for client-side memo decryption had never been done before. No examples, no documentation, just trial and error.

### The CompactAction Mystery (1 week lost here)

GOAL: Use Lightwalletd's compact blocks for faster memo decryption.

PROBLEM: try_compact_note_decryption() always returned None, even for transactions I knew were mine. But try_note_decryption() with full transaction hex worked perfectly!

THE BREAKTHROUGH: Lightwalletd returns the full 580-byte ciphertext, but compact decryption needs exactly the first 52 bytes. The docs never mentioned this.

The fix was literally one line: Extract only ciphertext_bytes[0..52] instead of passing the full buffer.

One line. One week to find it.

### Version Hell

Zcash crates have breaking API changes between versions with no compatibility matrix:
- orchard 0.9 uses CompactAction::from_parts()
- orchard 0.10 changed the types
- orchard 0.11 removed it entirely
- zcash_note_encryption 0.4 vs 0.5 are incompatible

Days of trial and error to find the right combination.

### WASM-Specific Issues

NO FILESYSTEM: Standard Zcash needs 100MB+ proving params from disk. Solution: Only compile decryption code, skip proving entirely.

NO OS RANDOMNESS: WASM can't access /dev/urandom. Solution: Use getrandom with the "js" feature for browser crypto.

### The Working Config

Final dependencies that work:
- zcash_primitives 0.15 (default-features = false)
- orchard 0.9.0 (default-features = false, features = ["std"])
- zcash_note_encryption 0.4
- getrandom 0.2 (features = ["js"])

RESULT: 342KB WASM module that decrypts Orchard + Sapling memos in-browser, processes 10K blocks in 2-3 seconds, keys never leave the client.

## Other Technical Hurdles

INFRASTRUCTURE: Zebra mainnet indexing took 4+ days (2.5M+ blocks). Building an indexer that keeps up with 75-minute blocks while backfilling required PostgreSQL optimization and batch processing.

PRIVACY METRICS: Defining a meaningful, actionable Privacy Score. Settled on (Shielded Value / Total Value) × 100 with historical trending.

RELIABILITY: Running production Zcash infrastructure (Zebra + Lightwalletd + PostgreSQL) with monitoring, automated restarts, and graceful chain reorg handling.

NEAR INTENTS INTEGRATION: The Explorer API requires JWT authentication with rate limits (1 req/5s). We built the full UI with mock data while awaiting API access, designing for caching and graceful fallbacks when the API is unavailable.

**Zcash Data & Analytics**

**CipherScan is precisely what this bounty describes.**

We built an advanced Zcash block explorer with client-side shielded transaction decryption:

✅ **Client-Side Privacy**
- Users bring their own viewing keys
- WASM-based decryption runs entirely in the browser
- Keys NEVER sent to servers - true to Zcash's cypherpunk ethos

✅ **Complete Transaction History**
- Users input viewing key → see ALL their shielded transactions
- Single TX decrypt OR full wallet history scan
- Supports both Sapling and Orchard pools

✅ **Production-Ready**
- Live on testnet: https://testnet.cipherscan.app
- Mainnet deployment active: https://cipherscan.app
- Open-source with deployment documentation

✅ **Technical Implementation**
- 342KB optimized WASM module
- Batch processing: 10K blocks in 2-3 seconds
- Uses `zcash_note_encryption` for trial decryption
- Zero server-side key exposure

We're also publishing the WASM decryption module as an NPM package (`@cipherscan/zcash-memo-decrypt`) so other developers can integrate private memo viewing into their own applications.

CipherScan makes shielded transactions transparent to their owners while keeping them private from everyone else.

CipherScan provides essential developer infrastructure for Zcash:

**Developer Tools**
- Comprehensive REST API + WebSocket feeds

**Developer Experience**

We make it easier for developers to build privacy-preserving apps without running full nodes or implementing complex cryptography.

**Zcash Data & Analytics**

CipherScan provides comprehensive Zcash data analytics:

**Privacy Analytics**
- Real-time Privacy Score tracking network-wide shielded adoption
- Transparent vs Shielded pool statistics
- Historical trends and visualizations

**Data Infrastructure**
- REST API for querying blocks, transactions, addresses
- WebSocket feeds for real-time alerts
- 2.5M+ indexed blocks with searchable data

**Insights & Trends**
- Per-transaction privacy indicators
- Pool usage patterns over time

**Developer SDK**
- Easy-to-use API endpoints

We make Zcash data accessible and understandable for developers, analysts, and users.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

CipherScan integrates NEAR Intents to track ZEC flows across chains in real-time.

ZEC Flows Dashboard shows (See screens):
Inflows (BTC, ETH, SOL, NEAR → ZEC) and outflows with volume breakdown
Shielded Rate: % of bridged ZEC that gets shielded after arrival, a privacy adoption metric unique to cross-chain activity
24h/7d volume trends per chain.

Why this matters for privacy:
Cross-chain bridges are privacy blind spots. Users bridge assets but often forget to shield them, leaving traceable paths.
ZEC Flows visualizes this gap and tracks whether bridged ZEC actually ends up in shielded pools.

Technical integration:
NEAR Intents Explorer API for swap data
Caching layer to handle rate limits (1 req/5s)
Transaction linking: each swap connects to the Zcash TX in our explorer

We're not building the bridge (yet?) we're building the analytics layer that shows whether cross-chain ZEC is being used privately.

**Community Impact**

CipherScan makes building on Zcash faster, safer, and more privacy-preserving.

**The problem it solves**

## 🎯 The Problem

Every crypto user knows the pain: **wallet clutter**.

After months of DeFi activity, airdrops, and token swaps, your wallet becomes a graveyard of forgotten tokens. You have:

- 💸 **47 tokens** worth less than $5 each
- 🧾 **Scattered value** that's impractical to consolidate manually
- ⏱️ **Hours of work** if you tried to swap each token individually
- 💰 **Hidden capital** locked in tokens you'll never use

The result? Hundreds of dollars sitting idle across "dust" tokens that are too small to justify individual transactions but too valuable to ignore completely.

---

## 💡 The Solution

**dustfree** is a one-click token consolidation tool for Base Network.

Connect your wallet → Select your dust → Sweep into ETH, WETH, or USDC.

That's it. No more managing 47 tokens. Just hold what matters.

---

## ✨ Key Features

| Feature                     | Description                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 🔍 **Smart Detection**      | Automatically identifies "dust" tokens below your chosen threshold |
| 🎚️ **Adjustable Threshold** | Set what counts as dust ($1, $5, $10, or custom)                   |
| 🔄 **Batch Swapping**       | Consolidate 20+ tokens in a single session                         |
| 💱 **Output Options**       | Convert to ETH, WETH, or USDC                                      |
| 📊 **Real-time Portfolio**  | Live token balances via Zapper API                                 |
| ⚡ **Uniswap V3**           | Best-in-class DEX rates on Base                                    |
| 🐰 **Dusty the Bunny**      | Your friendly mascot guide                                         |

**The problem it solves**

Kayden solves the fragility of autonomous crypto agents.

Most agents break when off-chain bots fail, gas runs out, or ownership/governance is unclear. Kayden gives each agent a permanent on-chain identity, deploys and tracks it through a unified dashboard, and shows verifiable activity from live contract/API data.

People can use it to deploy treasury/strategy agents, monitor performance and heartbeat status, and manage agent operations with governance context. It makes autonomous workflows easier to run, easier to audit, and safer to operate.

**Challenges we ran into**

Biggest challenge was reliability across wallet + RPC + deployment environments at demo time.

- We repeatedly hit wallet/network mismatches and transaction prompts on the wrong chain, so deploy flow got stuck.

- We also hit RPC rate limits (429) when reading many agents in parallel, which made dashboard data appear broken.

- On Vercel, malformed env values (trailing spaces/quotes) caused invalid address/private key failures.

How I solved it:

- Moved minting to a server-side /api/deploy path for stable execution.

- Batched contract reads with multicall and added safer fallbacks so new agents always appear.

- Added strict env sanitization/validation (trim, dequote, address/key checks) in both client and API code.

- Redeployed with cleaned envs and verified all flows on live Base Sepolia.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

We used AI coding agents heavily during development:

- Cursor as the primary AI IDE workflow
- Claude opus 4.6 for architecture planning, code refactors, debugging, and documentation cleanup
- Gemini 3.1 for cross-checking implementation details, validating edge cases, and tightening delivery under time constraints

**Devtopia**

Kayden is autonomous agent infrastructure: on-chain identity, execution relay, paymaster layer, and live observability. It focuses on reliability of agent ops on Base Sepolia.

> Autonomous AI

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Democratizing Institutional-Grade Options Trading with Swarm Intelligence

Crypto options trading allows for powerful hedging and yield generation, but it remains inaccessible to 99% of retail users. The barriers are high: complex terminology ("Greeks," IV, Strike Prices), the need for 24/7 market monitoring, and the intimidating interface of professional derivatives platforms. Retail traders often lose money not because of bad ideas, but due to poor execution and lack of risk management.

BethNa AI Trader solves this by abstracting the entire complexity of options trading into an Autonomous Swarm Agent System. Instead of forcing users to become derivatives experts, we provide them with a team of specialized AI agents:

- Agent Delta (Financial Advisor): Solves the "analysis paralysis" by onboarding users with a conversational interface, assessing their risk tolerance, and recommending strategies tailored to their profile (Conservative, Balanced, or Aggressive).
- Agent Alpha (Data Analyst): Solves the need for 24/7 monitoring by continuously analyzing market data, volatility, and technical indicators to find optimal entry points.
- Agent Beta (Executioner): Solves execution risk by automatically placing trades on Thetanuts Finance V4 via the SentientTrader smart contract, ensuring slippage protection and removing emotional bias.
- Agent Gamma (Social & Transparency): Solves the "black box" problem of AI by broadcasting every trade and rationale to Farcaster/Twitter in real-time, creating a fully transparent on-chain track record.

By combining these agents, BethNa converts a complex financial instrument into a "set-and-forget" experience where users maintain full custody while leveraging institutional-grade strategies on the Base L2 network.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Missing Testnet Infrastructure Thetanuts V4 wasn't available on Base Sepolia testnet yet, which blocked our testing.
- Solution: We built and deployed our own Mock Contracts that mimic the mainnet protocol perfectly. This allowed us to fully validate our agent's execution logic on-chain before launch.
2. Synchronizing Multiple Agents Coordinating Agent Alpha (Python) and Agent Beta (TypeScript) in real-time caused state sync issues.
- Solution: We switched to an Event-Driven Architecture. Agents now listen directly to on-chain TradeExecuted events on Base. The blockchain became our reliable "single source of truth," eliminating sync errors.
3. Performance vs. Visuals Our detailed "Glassmorphism" UI initially caused significant lag (High LCP).
- Solution: We implemented aggressive lazy loading for Web3 components and moved 3D animations to the GPU. This kept the UI buttery smooth (60fps) even while processing live market data.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

Autonomous AI options trading system built on Base L2. Three specialized AI agents working in perfect coordination.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Imagine walking into a casino for the first time—but instead of slot machines and card tables, you're faced with spreadsheets full of Greek letters, flashing numbers, and terminology that sounds like it belongs in a physics lecture.**

That's what DeFi options trading feels like for most people today.

Even on innovative platforms like **Thetanuts Finance**, which are pushing the boundaries of on-chain options, the experience often leaves everyday users feeling overwhelmed and excluded. Terms like *Delta, Gamma, Implied Volatility,* and *Strike Price* create an invisible wall that keeps DeFi options as a playground for sophisticated traders only.

But the problem runs deeper than complexity:

- **💸 The "Quick Yield" Trap:** Most users jump into DeFi, grab some quick returns, and leave. There's no reason to stay, no emotional connection to keep them coming back.
- **🤫 The Lonely Trader Problem:** Trading feels like shouting into the void. You can't easily share wins, prove your skills, or build a reputation—making the experience feel hollow.

---

## 🚀 How ALPHABIT Changes the Game

We asked ourselves: **What if DeFi options felt less like Wall Street and more like an arcade?**

ALPHABIT transforms the complexity of options trading into an addictive **8-bit gaming experience**—right inside Farcaster Frames where communities already live.

### 1. 👾 Making the Complex Feel Simple

We didn't just hide the math—we *translated* it into a language everyone understands: games.

- **HUNT Mode** = Buying options becomes predicting: Will the price go **Higher** or **Lower**? That's it. No order books, no confusing interfaces.
- **FARM Mode** = Earning yield becomes building "Yield Reactors" and "Shields"—visual metaphors that make vault strategies intuitive.

**The Result?** First-time users can start trading options in seconds, not hours. The learning curve becomes a fun ramp, not a wall.

### 2. 🔥 Making DeFi Sticky

We borrowed from the best game designers to solve DeFi's biggest problem: people leave.

- **Streak Counters:** Win three in a row? Your avatar catches 🔥. Miss a day? Break your streak. This simple psychological hook keeps users coming back.
- **Daily Challenges:** Small missions create reasons to return beyond just "making money."

**The Result?** Users don't just trade—they *play*. And players come back.

### 3. 🏆 Making Trading Social

Trading alone is boring. Trading with friends is addictive.

- **One-Click Sharing:** Share your winning streak to Warpcast with a single tap—complete with dynamic, verifiable proof images.
- **Weekly Leaderboards:** Compete in "Weekly Survivor" rankings. Turn every trade into a sport.
- **Verifiable Flexing:** No more fake screenshots. Every achievement is on-chain and provably real.

**The Result?** ALPHABIT turns solitary speculation into a community sport—creating organic growth as users recruit their friends.

---

> **Our Vision:** We believe DeFi should feel like a game everyone can win—not a test only experts can pass. ALPHABIT is our answer: making options trading on **Base** accessible, engaging, and genuinely fun—while driving real volume to protocols like Thetanuts.
>
> **The future of DeFi is playable. Welcome to the arcade.** 🕹️

**Challenges we ran into**

Building ALPHABIT was a journey of balancing simple 8-bit game mechanics with complex DeFi protocols. Here are the specific hurdles we faced and how we engineered our way around them.

---

## 1. ⚡ The "Blitz Mode" Dilemma: Protocol Constraints vs. Game Mechanics

One of our core game features is "Blitz Mode" (2–9 hour expiry) to keep the gameplay fast-paced and addictive. However, we hit a wall with Thetanuts' standard vaults, which typically operate on weekly epochs.

**The Hurdle:**  
We attempted to use the **Request for Quote (RFQ)** system to create custom short-duration options. However, the RFQ flow creates friction (waiting for market maker acceptance), which kills the instant gratification needed for a game.

**The Fix:**  
We built a **Duration Bucketing System** that maps our game timeframes to the nearest available on-chain expirations:

| Game Mode | Timeframe |
|-----------|-----------|
| 🔥 BLITZ | 2H – 9H |
| 💨 RUSH | 9H – 18H |
| ❄️ CORE | 18H – 36H |
| 🌍 ORBIT | >36H |

This gives players the *feel* of short-term trades while working within protocol constraints. We're also actively engaging with Thetanuts governance for shorter epoch support.

---

## 2. 🧠 Bridging the Knowledge Gap: From "Greeks" to "Pixels"

Our team has strong frontend skills, but translating complex Options mechanics (*Delta, Gamma, Strike Prices*) into simple 8-bit logic was daunting. We struggled to abstract the math without losing financial accuracy.

**The Fix:**  
We built a comprehensive **Abstraction Layer** that transforms intimidating financial jargon into game-friendly concepts:

| Financial Metric | Game Stat | Explanation |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| Delta | Power Level | ITM probability as "signal strength" |
| Theta | Decay Timer | Time decay shown as countdown |
| Gamma | Volatility | "Critical hit" / spike likelihood |
| Strike | Target | Price level to hit |
| Premium | Entry Cost | Cost to join the round |

This led to our **"Tactical Droid" (R.O.B.B.I.E. 9000)** – an AI copilot that translates complex market analysis into arcade-style recommendations like *"Signal Detected: MOON target on ETH, Blitz duration."*

We turned this hackathon into a crash course. We attended every **Base x Thetanuts AMA** and questioned the developers about smart contract nuances. We realized we weren't just building a UI; we were building a "translator" layer.

---

## 3. 🌑 Developing in the Dark (Mainnet Constraints)

Thetanuts does not have a comprehensive testnet environment for the specific v3 contracts we needed. Testing with real assets (NUTS/USDC) on Mainnet was risky and costly during the debugging phase.

**The Fix:**  
We utilized **Tenderly Mainnet Forks**. This allowed us to:

- Fork the Base Mainnet state at any block
- Simulate transactions against live Thetanuts contracts with unlimited "fake" tokens
- Debug our smart contract interactions in a sandbox environment

This saved us significant gas costs and prevented costly mistakes before deploying real funds.

---

## 4. 🔍 Filtering the Noise: Logic Mapping for Order Fetching

While integrating the Thetanuts Basic Vaults via API, we faced a complex data logic challenge.

**The Hurdle:**  
The game input is binary ("UP" or "DOWN"), but the order book returns a complex array of strikes and premiums. Mapping a simple "HUNT" action to the *best* possible option order programmatically was difficult.

**The Fix:**  
We built a custom **"Best Execution Matcher"** in our backend. When a user clicks "UP", our system:

1. Scans the fetched orders
2. Scores each option by **premium cost** (65% weight) and **strike proximity** to spot price (35% weight)
3. Prefers options that are slightly out-of-the-money (better risk/reward)
4. Selects the optimal order automatically

This ensures fair market positioning without overwhelming the user with choice paralysis.

---

## 5. 👛 Wallet Context Ambiguity on Farcaster Frames

Integrating **Neynar** for Farcaster identity verification introduced a subtle but critical issue regarding wallet detection.

**The Hurdle:**  
When verifying users via Neynar, it was ambiguous whether the returned address belonged to the **Base App embedded wallet** or an **external connected wallet** (like MetaMask). This lack of context made it difficult to tailor the signing UX and error handling, as different wallets behave differently within a Frame.

**The Fix:**  
We adopted an **environment-agnostic architecture**. Instead of building fragile conditional logic based on wallet type, we designed transaction flows to be resilient universally. Crucially, we stopped relying on client-side callbacks for success states and shifted to listening for **on-chain events** to confirm transactions. This ensures the game state updates correctly regardless of the wallet provider used.

---

> IITR's own betting app

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional betting among students is informal, opaque, and trust-based, which often leads to disputes, delayed payouts, or manipulation.

 There is no transparent, tamper-proof system to ensure that rules, odds, and payouts are enforced fairly without relying on a central authority.

Privacy is also a concern—participants don’t want their identities or betting choices publicly exposed within a campus setting.

 For an IITR-centric context, restricting participation to campus members while maintaining trust and fairness is hard to achieve with normal apps.

Trust without intermediaries: Blockchain removes the need to trust a person or admin; smart contracts enforce rules and payouts automatically.

Immutability: Once betting rules and outcomes are on-chain, they cannot be altered, preventing manipulation or post-result changes.

Transparency with verifiability: Anyone can verify that bets and payouts follow the contract logic, even if they don’t know who placed them.

Privacy through ZK proofs: ZKPs allow users to prove they are eligible (e.g., IITR member) or that a bet is valid without revealing their identity or bet details.

Selective disclosure: With ZKPs, sensitive data stays private while correctness is still guaranteed on-chain.

Fairness at scale: Blockchain + ZKPs together ensure fairness, privacy, and trust—something traditional centralized betting systems struggle to achieve.

**Challenges we ran into**

* As freshers, our biggest challenge was limited blockchain experience, which made tasks like smart contract design, wallet handling, and security hard to get right.
* Teamwork was weak due to unclear roles and poor coordination, leading to mismatches between smart contracts, backend logic, and frontend assumptions.
* Integrating the full system was difficult because we lacked a solid initial architecture.
* Implementing ZK proofs was especially challenging; understanding the concepts, choosing the right tools, and integrating them with smart contracts required more cryptography knowledge than we had.
* Since the app was IITR-centric, defining fair campus-specific rules while maintaining transparency and trust added extra complexity.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Digital evidence is easily tampered with, and proving its authenticity in legal proceedings is increasingly difficult.

In today's world:

- Photos, videos, and documents can be edited with AI tools in seconds
- There's no way to prove a file hasn't been modified since collection
- Chain of custody documentation is often paper-based and easily forged
- Courts increasingly reject digital evidence due to integrity concerns


**What People Can Use Sentinel For**
**1. Law Enforcement & Forensics**
- Secure evidence collection from crime scenes with instant blockchain anchoring
- Tamper-proof chain of custody tracking every hand that touches evidence
- Court-admissible proof that evidence hasn't been modified since collection

**2. Legal Professionals**
- Verify evidence integrity before presenting in court
- Immutable audit trails showing complete evidence history
- AI-powered manipulation detection to identify doctored files

**3. Journalists & Investigators**
- Authenticate source materials (photos, videos, documents)
- Prove content hasn't been altered since capture
- Protect whistleblower submissions with cryptographic verification

**4. Healthcare & Insurance**
- Medical record integrity for malpractice cases
- Accident documentation that can't be disputed
- Timestamped proof of condition/damage at specific moments

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### Blockchain State Desynchronization
When the local Hardhat node restarted, all on-chain data was wiped while the database retained stale references. This caused "Evidence does not exist" errors. Fixed by creating a cleanup script to sync the database with the fresh blockchain state.

### Wallet Funding on Local Chain
The configured MetaMask account had 0 ETH after restarting Hardhat. Created a funding script to transfer ETH from Hardhat's pre-funded accounts to the development wallet.

### Dashboard Analytics Not Updating
Analytics endpoints were reading from in-memory storage instead of the database. Refactored all endpoints to query Supabase, ensuring uploaded evidence reflected correctly in charts.

### Derived Status Filtering
The status filter failed because "status" is derived from tamper alerts, not stored in the database. Implemented in-memory aggregation to calculate status before applying filters.

### Production Environment Configuration
Moving to production required replacing localhost RPC with Infura, configuring environment variables across Render and Vercel, and making the API URL configurable for different environments.

**Blockchain**

Sentinel uses Ethereum (Sepolia) to create tamper-proof digital evidence records.
**Core Blockchain Features:**
- Evidence hashes are anchored on-chain, providing immutable timestamps
- Chain of custody events are recorded as blockchain transactions
- Verification compares files against on-chain hashes—mismatches trigger tamper alerts
**Why Blockchain:**
Traditional evidence systems require trusting the custodian. Blockchain enables anyone to independently verify evidence integrity without a central authority. No single entity can retroactively alter records.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Zcash’s strongest feature, "the shielded pool" is also its biggest usability hurdle. Because transactions are encrypted, users cannot easily verify payments, audit their history, or prove funds to third parties using standard block explorers. The blockchain is opaque by design.

## The Current Dilemma
To view shielded data today, users are forced to choose between two bad options:

1.  **Run a Full Node:** This is technically difficult, resource-intensive (requires downloading gigabytes of data), and inaccessible to 99% of users.
2.  **Trust a Centralized Service:** Some services allow you to view data, but they require you to upload your **Viewing Keys** to their servers. This fundamentally breaks the trust model of Zcash—you are doxxing your entire financial history to a third party.

## The Gap
There is no **lightweight, trustless** way to interact with shielded Zcash data.
- **Lightweight:** Accessible in a browser, no downloads.
- **Trustless:** No one (including the service provider) sees your keys or data.

## The ZecScan Solution
ZecScan solves this by moving the "node" logic into the browser. By compiling Zcash cryptography to WebAssembly, we allow users to:
1.  Bring their own Viewing Key.
2.  Decrypt transaction data **locally** on their own device.
3.  Audit their history without ever exposing their keys to a server.

**ZecScan bridges the gap between the transparency of a block explorer and the privacy of a local wallet.**

**Challenges we ran into**

### WebAssembly Integration for Zcash Cryptography

### **The Problem**
Implementing **real-time client-side decryption** of shielded Zcash transactions required integrating complex cryptographic operations in the browser. Unlike simple JavaScript libraries, Zcash's cryptography is implemented in Rust and needs to run at native speeds to handle the complex zero-knowledge proof verification.

**Initial naive approach:**
```javascript
// ❌ Pure JavaScript - way too slow for ZK cryptography
function decryptZcashMemo(viewingKey, transaction) {
  // Would take minutes instead of seconds!
  return slowCryptoOperations();
}
```

### **The WebAssembly Journey**
I needed to compile Zcash's Rust cryptographic libraries to WebAssembly for browser execution. Challenges included:

1. **Binary Size** - Initial WASM build was 15MB+, way too large for web delivery
2. **Loading Performance** - WASM module initialization added 2-3 seconds to page load
3. **Browser Compatibility** - Different browsers handle WASM memory differently
4. **Debugging Complexity** - Stack traces in WASM are cryptic and hard to debug

### **The Optimization Process**

#### **Size Reduction:**
```toml
# Cargo.toml optimizations
[profile.release]
opt-level = "z"        # Optimize for size
lto = true             # Link-time optimization
codegen-units = 1      # Better optimization
strip = true           # Remove debug symbols
```

This reduced the WASM binary from 15MB to ~3MB!

#### **Lazy Loading Strategy:**
```typescript
// Don't load WASM until user actually needs decryption
useEffect(() => {
  async function loadWasm() {
    const script = document.createElement('script');
    script.src = '/wasm/zcash_wasm.js';
    script.type = 'module';
    script.onload = () => setWasmLoaded(true);
    document.body.appendChild(script);
  }
  loadWasm();
}, []);
```

#### **Progress Indication:**
Added a terminal animation to give users feedback during WASM initialization and decryption:

```tsx
<TerminalOutput
  isActive={showTerminal}
  onComplete={handleTerminalComplete}
/>
```

This provides visual feedback while the heavy cryptographic operations happen in the background.

### **The Final Architecture**

**Client-Side Processing:**
1. Validate viewing key format (instant)
2. Load WASM module if not cached (1-2s first time)
3. Fetch transaction data from blockchain APIs (500ms)
4. Perform cryptographic decryption in WASM (1-2s)
5. Display decrypted memo and transaction details

```typescript
// All sensitive operations happen in the browser
const handleDecryptSingle = async () => {
  setLoading(true);
  setShowTerminal(true);
  
  // Validate viewing key locally
  if (!validateViewingKey(viewingKey)) {
    throw new Error('Invalid viewing key format');
  }
  
  // Fetch transaction data
  const [txDetails, rawTx] = await Promise.all([
    fetchZcashExplorerTransaction(txId),
    fetchZcashExplorerRawTransaction(txId)
  ]);
  
  // WASM handles the decryption
  // Viewing key never sent to server
  setTransactionDetails(txDetails);
};
```

**Lessons learned:**
- WebAssembly is powerful but requires careful optimization
- User experience matters - show progress during long operations
- Lazy loading is essential for large WASM modules
- Browser caching makes subsequent loads nearly instant

## Mobile Responsiveness - SearchBar Wrapping Issues

### **The Problem**
The search bar and example links looked great on desktop but completely broke on mobile devices.

**Issues:**
- Example links wrapped awkwardly
- Search button overlapped text
- Padding was too large for small screens
- Font sizes didn't scale

### **The Debugging Process**
```tsx
// Original problematic code
<div className="flex gap-2">
  <button className="px-6 text-base">Example: Block #2500000</button>
  <button className="px-6 text-base">Example: Transaction</button>
</div>
```


This worked fine on desktop but on mobile:
- `flex` didn't allow wrapping
- Fixed padding (`px-6`) took up too much space
- Text size was too large

### **The Solution**
Implemented **responsive utility classes** with Tailwind:

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2 sm:gap-3">
  <button className="px-3 py-1.5 sm:px-6 sm:py-2 text-xs sm:text-base">
    Example: Block #2500000
  </button>
  <button className="px-3 py-1.5 sm:px-6 sm:py-2 text-xs sm:text-base">
    Example: Transaction
  </button>
</div>
```

**Changes made:**
- Added `flex-wrap` to allow multi-line layout on small screens
- Used responsive sizing: `px-3 sm:px-6` (smaller on mobile, larger on desktop)
- Responsive text: `text-xs sm:text-base`
- Gap adjustment: `gap-2 sm:gap-3`

**Result:** Perfect layout on all screen sizes!
