> Private trades, unaffected markets, effortlessly.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**On-chain auctions have no privacy.**

On a public blockchain, every bid is visible to everyone in real time. This creates three critical issues:

**1. Bid manipulation: **later bidders can see existing bids and only outbid by the minimum, suppressing the true price
**2. Identity exposure: ** bidder addresses are public, linking financial activity to real-world identities
**3. Front-running: ** bots and other participants can exploit visible bid data before it's finalized

Traditional sealed-bid auctions (common in government bonds, real estate, spectrum allocation) solve manipulation, but no one had made them work privately on-chain.

Penumbra brings sealed-bid auctions to Ethereum using ZK proofs, bid amounts and bidder identities never appear on-chain, not even after the auction ends. The winner claims tokens by proving knowledge of a secret, not by revealing who they are.

Penumbra solves the transparency problem of on-chain auctions, bids, amounts, and winner identities stay private end-to-end using zero-knowledge proofs.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. ZK proofs on a hackathon timeline**
Generating and verifying ZK proofs server-side, then submitting them from a burner wallet so the winner's real address never touches the claim transaction. Getting the circuit, proof generation, and on-chain verifier to agree took significant iteration.

**2. The off-chain/on-chain split**
The whole point is that bids never appear on-chain, but Ethereum needs something to verify. Designing the nullifier scheme (bidders commit a hash on-chain, the backend knows the preimage, the winner proves knowledge without revealing it) required careful architecture so neither side could cheat.

**3. Stealth address key derivation**
Deriving spending and viewing keypairs deterministically from wallet signatures — without ever sending private keys to a server. The secp256k1 point multiplication needed to generate real uncompressed public keys is not natively available in the browser.

**4. BitGo custody for private ETH deposits**
Each bidder gets a unique deposit address so their ETH can't be correlated on-chain. Integrating BitGo's wallet API to generate these addresses, track confirmations, and route payouts to stealth addresses added a whole backend layer that most Ethereum projects don't need.

**5. Auction phase state machine**
Five phases (commit → settle → ended → claimed / cancelled) each with different UI, different allowed actions, and live on-chain polling. Keeping the frontend consistent across all states without race conditions was genuinely fiddly.

**Privacy**

## Core Thesis
Penumbra is privacy infrastructure for on-chain commerce. Every architectural
decision, from bid commitment to winner claim, is made to eliminate
information leakage at every step of the auction lifecycle.

## End-to-End Privacy Guarantees

### 1. Private Bids (ZK Commitments)

Bidders never post their bid amount on-chain. Instead, they submit a
zero-knowledge commitment, a cryptographic hash that proves they have a valid
bid without revealing what it is. The actual amount only exists off-chain,
encrypted in the backend.

### 2. Anonymous Deposits (Stealth Addresses)
Each bidder receives a unique, one-time ETH deposit address via BitGo custody.
This breaks the on-chain link between a bidder's wallet and their deposit,
chain analysis cannot correlate who bid on what.

### 3. Private Winner Declaration (Nullifiers)
The winner is declared on-chain using only their **nullifier**, a
cryptographic identifier with no link to their wallet address or bid amount.
No one watching the chain can determine who won.

### 4. Private Claims (ZK Proofs)
The winner claims their tokens by generating a ZK proof that they know the
secret behind the winning nullifier. The proof is submitted from a **burner
wallet**, so even the claim transaction reveals nothing about the winner's
real identity.

### 5. Private Seller Payouts (Stealth Addresses)
The seller receives their ETH payout at a **stealth address** derived from
their registered viewing and spending keys, not their public wallet, so the
payment cannot be linked to them on-chain.

## What Makes This Different from Existing Privacy Tools
Most privacy tools (Tornado Cash, Railgun, etc.) are **mixers**, they
anonymize existing transactions after the fact. Penumbra builds privacy
**into the auction primitive itself**. There is no "before" state where
information was ever public.

## Why This Matters Beyond the Hackathon
Sealed-bid auctions are the standard format for:
- Government bond issuances
- Real estate portfolio sales
- Spectrum licensing
- High-value NFT drops

None of these can move on-chain today because public bids destroy price
discovery and expose participants. Penumbra removes that blocker.

**DeFi**

# Why Privacy is a Natural Fit for DeFi
## The Core Problem with Transparent DeFi
DeFi runs on public blockchains, every transaction, every position, every
wallet balance is visible to everyone, forever. This is great for auditability
but catastrophic for financial privacy.
In traditional finance, your brokerage account is not broadcast to the world
in real time. In DeFi, it is.
## How Transparency Actively Harms DeFi Users
### Front-Running & MEV
When a trader submits a large swap, bots see it in the mempool and
insert their own transactions ahead of it, extracting value directly
from the user. This is only possible because everything is public.
### Whale Watching
Large wallets are tracked obsessively. When a known address moves funds,
the market reacts before they finish, making it impossible to execute
large positions without moving the market against yourself.
### Liquidation Hunting
Lending protocols expose every collateral position publicly. Attackers
deliberately manipulate prices to trigger liquidations on specific wallets
they've identified as vulnerable.
### Bid Manipulation in Auctions
In any on-chain auction without privacy, bidders can see all existing bids
and game their strategy accordingly, suppressing true price discovery and
disadvantaging honest participants.
## Privacy is Not Optional for Serious DeFi
For DeFi to serve institutional players, DAOs managing treasuries, or any
user transacting at meaningful scale, **financial privacy is a baseline
requirement**, not a nice-to-have.
Privacy in DeFi means:
- Strategies cannot be front-run
- Positions cannot be targeted
- Identity cannot be linked to on-chain activity
- Market participants compete on information, not surveillance
## Where Penumbra Fits
Penumbra addresses the auction layer of DeFi, one of the most
information-sensitive operations in any financial system. Sealed-bid
auctions are the gold standard for fair price discovery precisely because
no participant can see what others are bidding.
By bringing ZK-based sealed-bid auctions on-chain, Penumbra makes a
class of DeFi activity, token sales, liquidation auctions, DAO asset
disposals, viable for participants who cannot afford to have their
strategies exposed publicly.
**Privacy isn't anti-DeFi. It's what DeFi needs to grow up.**

**Best creative use of ENS**

# How Penumbra Uses ENS
## The Problem with Auction Identities
In a sealed-bid auction, the seller needs to be discoverable and
trustworthy. A raw `0x` address tells bidders nothing. It provides
no reputation, no identity, and no assurance that the seller is
who they claim to be.
Penumbra integrates ENS to solve this.
## ENS as the Seller Identity Layer
When a seller creates an auction, they can attach their **ENS name**
to the listing. This gives bidders:
- A human-readable identity tied to the auction (`vitalik.eth` vs `0x1234...`)
- On-chain reputation linked to a real identity
- Confidence that the seller is accountable
This is especially important in a **private auction** where bid amounts
are hidden and trust in the seller is the only signal bidders have before
committing funds.
## ENS + Privacy = Accountable Anonymity
Penumbra's design creates an intentional balance:
| Party | Privacy Level | Identity |
|---|---|---|
| Bidder | Fully anonymous | No on-chain trace |
| Seller | Publicly accountable | ENS name attached |
The seller is **known via ENS**, providing trust and accountability.
The bidder is **fully private via ZK**, protecting their strategy.
Auctions require sellers to be trustworthy and discoverable.
ENS makes that possible on-chain without centralised identity infrastructure.
## The Bottom Line
ENS transforms Penumbra's auction listings from anonymous contract
addresses into **trusted, human-readable storefronts**, making
private auctions safe enough for real participants to commit real funds.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

# How Penumbra Uses BitGo
## BitGo as the Core Privacy Layer
Penumbra uses BitGo as the **core custody layer** for its ZK sealed-bid
auction protocol, not as an optional add-on, but as a load-bearing
component without which the privacy guarantees collapse entirely.
## Private Deposits via Unique BitGo Addresses
When a bidder places a bid, they receive a **unique BitGo-generated deposit
address** completely isolated from their on-chain wallet identity.
This breaks the correlation between:
- A bidder's Ethereum address
- Their ETH deposit amount
- Their participation in the auction
A naive on-chain deposit would immediately link a bidder's wallet to their
bid amount on the public ledger, destroying privacy. BitGo's programmable
wallet infrastructure is what makes this separation possible.
## Full Money Movement Through BitGo
BitGo handles every step of the financial layer:
| Step | BitGo's Role |
|---|---|
| Bid placement | Generates unique deposit address per bidder |
| Deposit tracking | Detects and confirms incoming ETH |
| Auction settlement | Routes payout to the winning seller |
| Seller privacy | Sends proceeds to a stealth address |
## Why BitGo Makes Penumbra Possible
Without BitGo, Penumbra cannot exist. The entire auction lifecycle, 
from private deposit to anonymous payout, depends on BitGo's
programmable custody infrastructure running in parallel with the
on-chain ZK proof system.
**BitGo handles the money. ZK handles the truth. Neither works without
the other.**

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

# How Penumbra Uses BitGo for DeFi
## A New DeFi Primitive, Private Sealed-Bid Auctions
Penumbra is a **ZK-powered sealed-bid auction protocol** built on Ethereum.
It enables token sales, DAO treasury disposals, and asset auctions where
**bid amounts and bidder identities are never revealed on-chain**, a class
of DeFi activity that was previously impossible without privacy infrastructure.
BitGo is the financial backbone that makes this work.
## How BitGo Powers the DeFi Flow
### Private Bid Deposits
Every bidder receives a **unique BitGo wallet address** to deposit their ETH.
This decouples their on-chain identity from their bid, chain analysis cannot
link who bid, how much, or on what auction.
### Trustless Settlement
After the auction closes, BitGo confirms all deposits, and the backend
settles the auction off-chain, determining the highest bid without ever
posting amounts on-chain. The winner is declared using only a ZK nullifier.
### Stealth Payouts to Sellers
The seller receives their ETH payout routed through BitGo **directly to a
stealth address**, so even the final payout cannot be linked to their
public wallet.
## Why This is DeFi Infrastructure
| DeFi Need | Penumbra + BitGo Solution |
|---|---|
| Fair price discovery | Sealed bids prevent sniping and manipulation |
| Participant privacy | BitGo deposit addresses break on-chain correlation |
| Trustless execution | ZK proofs enforce winner validity on-chain |
| Private settlement | Stealth address payouts via BitGo custody |
## The Bottom Line
Penumbra uses BitGo to bring **institutional-grade sealed-bid auctions**
to DeFi, the same auction format used in sovereign debt and spectrum
licensing, now available on Ethereum with full privacy guarantees.

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

## Why Sealed-Bid Auctions are a Missing Primitive
DeFi today has:
- Public AMM swaps
- Public order books
- Public liquidation auctions
- Public token launches
Every single one of these leaks information. Bids, strategies, and
positions are visible to everyone in real time, enabling front-running,
MEV extraction, and market manipulation.
The sealed-bid auction, the gold standard for fair price discovery in
traditional finance, has never existed on-chain. Until now.
## What Penumbra Adds to the DeFi Stack
Penumbra is a composable auction primitive that any protocol can use for:
- **Token launches** where early bid visibility would allow manipulation
- **DAO treasury sales** where whale strategies must stay private
- **Liquidation auctions** where front-running destroys fairness
- **NFT drops** where bid sniping undermines true price discovery
- **On-chain M&A** where deal terms cannot be public before closing
## The Technical Stack that Makes it New
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Bid privacy | ZK commitments, amounts never on-chain |
| Deposit privacy | BitGo custody, wallets unlinked |
| Winner privacy | Nullifier-based declaration |
| Claim privacy | ZK proof via burner wallet |
| Payout privacy | Stealth addresses |
## The Bottom Line
Penumbra is not a DeFi app built on existing primitives.
It is a new primitive that makes an entirely new category of
on-chain financial activity possible, one that traditional
finance has relied on for decades and DeFi has never had.

**Privacy**

# Why Penumbra Fits the Base Privacy Track
## Privacy as a First-Class Citizen on Base
Penumbra is a **ZK-powered sealed-bid auction protocol** that delivers
end-to-end privacy for on-chain commerce. Every layer of the system is
designed to eliminate information leakage, making it a natural fit for
Base's privacy track.
## What Penumbra Protects
### Bidder Privacy
Bid amounts are never posted on-chain. Bidders commit a ZK hash, send
ETH to a unique deposit address, and are identified only by a nullifier.
No one watching the chain can determine who bid or how much.
### Winner Privacy
The winner is declared using only their **ZK nullifier**, not their wallet
address. They claim tokens by generating a ZK proof server-side, submitted
from a burner wallet. Their real address is never revealed.
### Seller Privacy
Auction proceeds are routed to a **stealth address** derived from the
seller's registered keys, so even the final payout cannot be linked to
their public wallet.
## Privacy at Every Step
| Auction Step | Privacy Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Bid submission | ZK commitment, amount never on-chain |
| ETH deposit | Unique custody address, wallet unlinked |
| Winner declaration | Nullifier only, no address revealed |
| Token claim | Burner wallet + ZK proof |
| Seller payout | Stealth address |
## The Bottom Line
Penumbra does not add privacy as a feature on top of an existing protocol.
Privacy is the protocol. Every architectural decision exists to ensure that
participants in an auction reveal nothing they do not choose to reveal.

**BEST Overall Project**

# Why Penumbra is the Best Overall Project
## It Solves a Real Problem, Not a Demo Problem
Most hackathon projects wrap an existing protocol in a nicer UI or add a
feature nobody asked for. Penumbra solves a fundamental, unsolved problem
in Ethereum, the complete absence of privacy in on-chain auctions.
This is not a toy. Sealed-bid auctions are used for sovereign debt,
spectrum allocation, real estate, and M&A. None of it exists on-chain
today because transparency makes it unusable. Penumbra removes that blocker.
## The Technical Depth is Genuinely Rare
Building any one of these in a hackathon would be impressive:

- Nullifier-based anonymous winner declaration
- Stealth address key derivation from wallet signatures
- BitGo custody integration for private ETH deposits
- A five-phase on-chain auction state machine
Penumbra ships all of them working together as a single coherent system.
That is not a weekend project. That is a protocol.
## Full-Stack, End-to-End
Most DeFi hackathon entries are either:
- A smart contract with no frontend
- A pretty frontend with no real contract logic
Penumbra has a production-grade smart contract, a ZK backend, a BitGo
custody layer, a stealth address system, and a polished frontend with
a complete user experience from auction creation to token claim.
Every component is real. Nothing is mocked.
## Privacy at Every Layer
It would be easy to claim privacy and only deliver it at one step.
Penumbra delivers it at every step:
| Step | Privacy Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Bid submission | ZK commitment — amount never on-chain |
| ETH deposit | Unique BitGo address — wallet unlinked |
| Winner declaration | Nullifier only — no address revealed |
| Token claim | Burner wallet + ZK proof |
| Seller payout | Stealth address |
No other project in this hackathon has this surface area of privacy coverage.
## It Has a Clear Path Beyond the Hackathon
This is not a proof of concept that gets deleted on Monday. The use cases
are immediate and the market is large:
- DAO treasury asset sales
- Private token launches
- Institutional-grade NFT auctions
- On-chain M&A and IP licensing
The infrastructure built here is reusable for any sealed-bid auction on
any EVM chain.
## The Bottom Line
Other projects built features. Penumbra built infrastructure.
It is technically the most ambitious, architecturally the most complete,
and addresses a gap in the Ethereum ecosystem that has existed since day one.

**The problem it solves**

DeFi today is fragmented and reactive. Traders juggle multiple tabs: block explorers, DEX interfaces, Discord alerts — just to stay on top of what's happening on-chain. By the time you spot an opportunity, it's already gone.

Chaintology collapses the entire DeFi workflow into one surface:
Real-time, streaming analytics on any Uniswap pool or Monad token. No stale subgraphs, no manual refreshes. Data flows directly from QuickNode Streams to live charts in milliseconds.

A visual rules engine lets you define strategies like "if ETH/USDC drops below $2,000 with >$50k notional" using drag-and-drop conditions. Rules evaluate on every single swap event in real time.

When a rule fires, an actionable swap recommendation lands in your inbox. One click routes it through the Uniswap Trading API. Quote, approve and execute without ever leaving the app.

Who it's for:
Active DeFi traders who want automated alerts and instant execution instead of watching charts all day
Liquidity providers tracking TVL, fee accrual, and pool health across chains in real time
Anyone exploring Monad's ecosystem who needs live analytics on nad.fun token activity

What it replaces: A patchwork of Dune dashboards, Telegram bots, custom scripts, and manual DEX visits. We've unified this into a single, real-time intelligence layer powered by QuickNode Streams and the Uniswap API.

**Challenges we ran into**

Matching user-created rules to incoming swap events was surprisingly tricky. 

Users type "ETH/USDC" but on-chain the pool is "WETH/USDC," and the pair order can be flipped — "USDC/WETH" is the same pool. 

I built a normalization layer that aliases common names (ETH→WETH, BTC→WBTC) and matches pairs bidirectionally. 

This was a silent bug until I added debug logging that printed the exact strings being compared side by side.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Chaintology's Rules Engine acts as an autonomous trading agent. It continuously evaluates real-time on-chain events against user-defined conditions and generates actionable swap recommendations — no human monitoring required.

How it works:
QuickNode Streams deliver decoded swap events to the backend in real time
The Rules Engine evaluates every event against user-configured conditions (price thresholds, volume windows, directional filters) using AND/OR logic
When a rule fires, it generates a swap action with full context — token pair, direction, amount — routed through the Uniswap API
The user reviews and executes in one click, or dismisses

AI in development:
The project was built using the Uniswap AI Skill for swap integration patterns, API usage, and approval flow implementation — accelerating development of the Uniswap Trading API integration.

**New France Village**

Chaintology brings institutional-grade DeFi tooling to Main Street. It's a real-time intelligence and execution platform that makes active DeFi trading accessible, automated, and safe — bridging the gap between Wall Street-style trading infrastructure and everyday on-chain users.

Why it fits "The Future of Finance":
DeFi made actionable — Instead of raw block explorers and fragmented dashboards, users get a unified analytics surface with live-streaming charts, pool metrics, and liquidity data across Ethereum and Monad.
Automated trading strategies without code — A visual, drag-and-drop rules engine lets anyone build conditional trading logic (e.g. "swap if price drops below X with Y volume") — the kind of tooling previously limited to quant desks and trading firms.
One-click execution — When conditions trigger, users review and execute swaps directly through the Uniswap API. No context-switching, no copy-pasting addresses, no manual DEX visits.
Main Street Adoption — The entire UX is designed to lower the barrier: connect wallet, pick a pool, set rules, get notified, execute. No CLI, no scripts, no Solidity knowledge required.
Multi-chain from day one — Supports both Ethereum mainnet and Monad, positioning users to participate in emerging ecosystems alongside established ones.

**Best Use of Quicknode Monad Streams**

Chaintology uses QuickNode Streams as its sole blockchain data ingestion layer — no custom indexers, no subgraphs, no polling. Streams handles extraction, transformation, and delivery end-to-end, powering every chart, metric, and automated rule in the platform.

How Streams is integrated:
Dual-chain ingestion — Two Streams configured: one for Ethereum mainnet (Uniswap V3 pool events), one for Monad (nad.fun CurveBuy/CurveSell events). Both deliver decoded data via webhooks to our backend.
On-the-fly transformation — Raw block receipts are decoded inline: ABI log parsing, sqrtPriceX96 → human-readable price conversion, and USD enrichment — all before hitting the database.
Real-time delivery — Stream webhook → Express backend → Supabase insert → WebSocket broadcast to frontend. Users see live-updating charts with zero polling.
Backfill support — Historical data is loaded through Streams so charts display full history from the moment a pool is tracked.
Filtering — Streams are filtered to specific contract addresses and event signatures, keeping the pipeline lean.
Rule evaluation trigger — Every streamed swap event is immediately evaluated against user-defined rules, enabling sub-second automated reactions to on-chain activity on Monad.

What Streams powers in the app:
Live price, volume, fee, and swap count charts (1H / 24H / 7D)
TVL and liquidity tracking from Mint/Burn/Collect events
A dedicated Streams Dashboard showing the raw decoded event feed
The entire Rules Engine — conditions are evaluated on every incoming stream event
Monad token analytics from nad.fun activity

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

Chaintology is a real-time DeFi intelligence platform that integrates the Uniswap API as its core swap execution layer — not just for simple trades, but as the action engine behind an automated rules system.

How we integrate the Uniswap API:
Quoting — Every swap surfaces a real-time quote via POST /quote to the Uniswap Trading API
Execution — Swaps are built via POST /swap, constructing Universal Router calldata that the user signs directly from their wallet
Approval flow — Automatic check-approval detection handles ERC-20 approvals vs Permit2 signatures before execution
Multi-chain — Works on Ethereum mainnet and Monad (chain ID 143)

The Uniswap API isn't just wired to a swap button — it's the execution backend for an automated rules engine. Users define conditions visually (e.g. "if ETH/USDC price drops below $2,000 with >$50k notional"), and when on-chain data triggers a rule, a ready-to-execute swap action appears in their inbox. One click → quote → approve → execute, all through the Uniswap API. This turns the API into the backbone of a trading agent that reacts to real-time blockchain events.

Voting limited to annual elections (not individual projects)

Contractors selected based on personal connections, not merit
No competitive bidding process
Residents lack expertise to evaluate technical proposals (lift repair, waterproofing, etc.)

5. Project Failures

Contractors disappear after receiving full payment
Work quality poor with no accountability
No mechanism to verify milestone completion

# 1. The Problem: The Precarious Reality of Indonesia’s Daily Workforce

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/72e5293723fc4b03b09a0b5505a1341d/233a1cf9-c85b-4581-95a7-984b5eb46936.jpeg)
The digital economy is thriving, yet it leaves behind the very people who build our cities, clean our homes, and power our events. In Indonesia, over **77.9 million people** operate in the informal sector, often referred to as **"Buruh Harian Lepas."** For this massive demographic, working hard is not the challenge—being treated fairly is.

The current informal labor market is broken, suffering from three systemic crises:

---

## 1. The Trust Deficit & Payment Peril

The most painful reality for any daily worker is payment uncertainty. In the informal sector, "contracts" are usually nothing more than verbal promises or informal chat messages. This creates a dangerous power imbalance:

- **The Ghosting Phenomenon:**  
  Workers frequently complete grueling physical tasks only to be "ghosted" or ignored by employers on payday.

- **Zero Legal Leverage:**  
  Because there is no formal record of the agreement or the work performed, these workers have zero recourse to claim their rightful wages. To them, a day's work without pay isn't just a loss of time; it is a loss of a family's meal.

---

## 2. The "Reputation Void" and Economic Stagnation
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/72e5293723fc4b03b09a0b5505a1341d/845e2a15-e027-4b47-9dcc-023e28d97894.jpeg)
A daily worker may have **10 years of experience** and a perfect track record, but on paper, they are invisible.

- **The Resume Problem:**  
  Informal work history is non-portable. When a worker moves to a new city or employer, they start from zero. They cannot prove their skills, their punctuality, or their reliability.

- **Stuck in the Cycle:**  
  Without a verifiable "Proof of Work," these laborers stay trapped in low-paying roles, unable to use their history to negotiate better wages or "level up" to more professional opportunities.

---

## 3. High Friction and Exploitative Intermediation
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/72e5293723fc4b03b09a0b5505a1341d/42c2c1c1-44aa-466d-8d76-192cbc4879e0.jpeg)
Traditional middleman agencies often prey on the vulnerability of these workers.

- **The Wage Tax:**  
  Centralized agencies often take a massive "cut" (**10% to 30%**) for simply connecting a worker to a job. For someone earning a daily survival wage, this deduction is predatory.

- **Financial Exclusion:**  
  Many workers are "unbanked" or "underbanked." Traditional digital platforms often require complicated banking setups or charge high withdrawal fees that make them inaccessible to the average daily laborer.

---

# 2. The Solution: Turning Promises into Immutable Code

**JobCoUi** is a decentralized marketplace built on **Base L2** that replaces fragile "human promises" with the mathematical certainty of blockchain technology. We empower the informal workforce by providing a secure, transparent, and low-cost digital ecosystem.

### How JobCoUi makes employment safer and easier:

- **Trustless Escrow Protocol:**  
  Before work begins, the employer’s funds are locked into a Smart Contract. The funds are only released to the worker once the job is verified.  
  *If you do the work, you get paid—guaranteed.*

- **Stability with IDRX:**  
  We use **IDRX (Rupiah Stablecoin)** for all settlements. This ensures workers receive their wages in a currency they understand and can spend immediately, without the volatility of typical cryptocurrencies.

- **Immutable Professional Identity:**  
  Every completed task is recorded on-chain. This creates a permanent, tamper-proof **Professional Reputation Score**, allowing workers to "carry" their resume wherever they go.

- **Optimized Performance on Base L2:**  
  By leveraging Layer 2 technology, we reduce transaction (gas) fees to near-zero, ensuring that not a single Rupiah of the worker's hard-earned wage is wasted on network costs.

---

# 3. Impact: Beyond a Marketplace

**JobCoUi** transforms the gig economy from a landscape of risk into a platform of **Dignity and Security**.

By using our **Progressive Web App (PWA)**, even workers with low-end mobile devices can access the power of DeFi. We don't just find people jobs; we provide a safety net that ensures fairness, fosters trust, and builds a verifiable digital future for the marginalized workforce.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Development Challenges: A Journey of Grit and Innovation

Developing JobCoUi was more than just a technical project; it was an intensive journey of rapid learning and problem-solving for our team. We combined our passion for social impact with the grit to master complex technologies in a very short timeframe.

---

## 1. Navigating the Steep Blockchain Learning Curve

As a team where every member was a first-timer in the blockchain space, we faced a massive knowledge gap from day one.

- **The Struggle:**  
  The world of Web3, Smart Contracts, and Decentralized Finance (DeFi) is vastly different from traditional development.

- **The Hustle:**  
  We dedicated **30 consecutive days (Dec 10 to Jan 8)** exclusively to deep-dive research. We consumed endless technical literature, documentation, and case studies just to understand the underlying architecture of a trustless system. This period was crucial to ensure our escrow protocol wasn't just functional, but mathematically sound and secure for our users.

---

## 2. Rapid Skill Adaptation in Frontend Development

Our frontend was spearheaded by a single developer who was completely new to React.

- **The Struggle:**  
  Mastering a modern component-based framework while building a production-ready Progressive Web App (PWA) is a high-pressure task.

- **The Hustle:**  
  Our team member embarked on a "learning-by-doing" journey, adapting to the nuances of state management, responsive mobile-first design, and PWA service workers in real-time. This resilience allowed us to build an interface that is both lightweight and powerful, optimized perfectly for the low-end devices often used by daily workers.

---

## 3. Infrastructure and Deployment Hurdles

Connecting a blockchain backend to a stable live environment proved to be one of our biggest "invisible" challenges.

- **The Struggle:**  
  We initially attempted to deploy our infrastructure using platforms like Railway and Fly.io. However, we were met with persistent access bugs, networking issues, and environment configuration errors that stalled our progress.

- **The Hustle:**  
  Rejecting defeat, we pivoted to a more robust and manual solution: Deploying on a **Virtual Private Server (VPS)**. This move gave us full control over our environment, allowing us to stabilize the connection between our backend API, the MySQL database, and the Base L2 blockchain nodes.

---

## 4. Designing a "Fail-Safe" Hybrid Architecture

Building for the informal workforce meant we couldn't just build a "cool app" we had to build a reliable tool.

- **The Struggle:**  
  Blockchain can be slow, but our users expect speed. Furthermore, since workers aren't "crypto-experts," we couldn't expect them to handle gas fees or private keys.

- **The Hustle:**  
  We solved this by creating a **Hybrid State Management** system. We anchored critical financial tasks (the IDRX Escrow) on Base L2 for safety, while using a traditional database for fast UI metadata. This **"Web2 feel with Web3 security"** approach ensures that workers get the protection of blockchain without the technical headache.

**Base Track**

JobCoUi is a Base Mini-App that focuses on improving the onchain user experience for real-world, non-technical users, specifically informal workers and small employers.
It does not focus on options trading or derivatives, which is the core requirement of the Thetanuts Track.

Instead, JobCoUi directly addresses the UX and onboarding gaps that prevent everyday users from benefiting from onchain systems exactly what the Base Track is designed for.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Wallet Connection Issues**: Initial MetaMask integration had compatibility problems with multiple wallet extensions. **Solution**: Migrated to RainbowKit for robust multi-wallet support.

2. **Gas Estimation Errors**: Transaction failures due to incorrect gas limits. **Solution**: Implemented dynamic gas estimation and fallback mechanisms using wagmi.

3. **Contract ABI Parsing**: Complex tuple return types caused ABI parsing errors. **Solution**: Used full JSON ABI format instead of function signatures for accurate type definitions.

4. **Environment Variable Loading**: Next.js wasn't loading environment variables correctly in production. **Solution**: Hardcoded fallback values and improved env configuration.

5. **CORS Configuration**: Backend API blocked frontend requests after deployment. **Solution**: Implemented dynamic CORS with regex patterns for Vercel and Railway domains.

                         Verification must be derived from oracle state
        This required handling:
                         Oracle staleness
                         Missing feeds
                         Zero or invalid values
                         Automatic un-verification
                         Getting this right was critical for trust.

**Ethereum Track**

1. Avoiding “Fake” Tokenization

One of the biggest challenges was not cutting corners.

Most tokenization demos:

Hardcode prices

Toggle “verified” manually

Show assets before liquidity exists

I had to deliberately design the system so that:

Assets appear only after real on-chain deployment

Marketplace stays empty until all conditions are met

This made development slower, but ensured correctness and trust.

2. Coordinating Governance With On-Chain Execution

Admin approval alone cannot make an asset real.

The challenge was to correctly separate:

Governance (admin review and approval)

Execution (contract deployment, liquidity, oracle setup)

Bridging this gap required:

Secure backend execution

Proper use of an admin deployer wallet

Event-driven indexing instead of UI-driven state

3. Liquidity Provisioning on Testnet

AMM-based pricing requires real liquidity, even on testnet.

Challenges included:

Limited Sepolia ETH availability

Transactions failing due to insufficient funds

Marketplace remaining empty until liquidity was seeded

Instead of bypassing this, the system enforces:

Liquidity as a hard requirement

“Liquidity pending” states when funds are unavailable

This mirrors real-world constraints.

4. Oracle Integration Without Admin Overrides

A major design challenge was ensuring that:

Admins cannot manually mark assets as verified

Verification must be derived from oracle state

This required handling:

Oracle staleness

Missing feeds

Zero or invalid values

Automatic un-verification

Getting this right was critical for trust.

5. End-of-Life Asset Handling

Fractional ownership becomes complex when the entire asset is sold.

The challenge:

Preventing manual coordination between token holders

Designing a fair exit mechanism

Solution:

Forced redemption model

Pro-rata distribution

Token freezing and burning after final sale

This required thinking beyond typical DeFi patterns.

6. Build & Deployment Limitations

A known compatibility issue between:

Next.js 15

wagmi v2

caused production builds to fail.

Instead of downgrading or hacking around it:

The app was deployed using SSR via Firebase Functions

The limitation was documented transparently

This preserved correctness while allowing live demos.

**The problem it solves**

Technical interviews often suffer from "tool fatigue"—where candidates and interviewers have to jump between a video calling app (like Zoom), a shared document for notes, and a separate coding environment. This context-switching leads to lost time, technical friction, and a poor candidate experience.

AlgoInterview solves this by consolidating the entire interview lifecycle into a single, specialized workspace.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/3bbbf1a777704493ae70048e634d83ff/0ccb4498-6cc5-4007-9a62-846a3e7bc4fd.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/3bbbf1a777704493ae70048e634d83ff/35fb4076-2278-4a21-80c5-1e1ce93706b7.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

some of the challenges i ran into was 
1)it was difficult to use shadcn and stream.io together as (convex) is different from other backend server like mongodb
2)Synchronizing Identity Across Platforms
Managing a user's identity across three different services (Clerk, Convex, and Stream) is a major hurdle.

The Challenge: Clerk handles the login, but Convex needs to know the user's role, and Stream needs to know the user's permissions.

The Solution: We had to implement a Sync Mutation that "teleports" user data from Clerk into Convex as soon as they log in, ensuring the interviewer role is assigned correctly and immediately available to the Stream Video provider.
3)Managing the "Prototype" and Hydration Errors
Next.js uses a mix of Server and Client components. A common challenge is accidentally importing a Node.js-only library (like the Stream Server SDK) into a file that the browser tries to read.

The Symptom: This leads to the cryptic TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype').

The Fix: Precisely defining boundaries using the "use server" and "use client" directives is essential to keep server-side secrets (like API keys) hidden from the browser.

**Open Innovation**

AlgoInterview alligns with open innovation as
1)Democratizing High-End Tools: It provides a "Pro-level" interview environment—typically reserved for FAANG companies with massive internal budgets—to startups and individual developers for free.
2)Scalable Collaboration: It solves the "latency barrier" in remote work by leveraging edge-ready technologies (Next.js and Stream), making global collaboration as fast as local interaction.
3)Modular Architecture: Built with a "plug-and-play" mindset, allowing different modules (Convex for data, Stream for video, Clerk for auth) to be swapped or upgraded without rebuilding the entire system.

**The problem it solves**

**The Privacy Paradox Problem**
Most zero-knowledge platforms claim to provide privacy, yet require server-side proof generation - your sensitive data gets transmitted to their servers, violating the core principle of privacy.
The Three-Part Problem We Solve:
1- Privacy Tools That Don't Respect Privacy
Existing ZK platforms require you to send private inputs to their servers
Your secrets (passwords, balances, credentials) leave your device
You must trust the platform operator not to log or misuse your data
This defeats the entire purpose of zero-knowledge proofs
2- Massive Learning Curve
Building ZK applications on Zcash requires deep cryptography expertise
Months to learn Circom, snarkjs, Groth16 mathematics
Only cryptography PhDs can build privacy-preserving apps
This limits ecosystem growth to a handful of experts
3- Slow Development Cycles
Teams spend 3-6 months just learning the tech stack
Another 2-3 months building their first working circuit
Circuit compilation, trusted setup, verification key generation - all manual
Total time: 6-12 months from idea to production

Our Solution: zkRune
1- True Client-Side Privacy
All cryptographic operations happen in the user's browser. Private inputs never leave the device. No server calls, no data transmission, no trust required.
Use case: A DeFi app can prove you have >$10,000 balance without revealing your 2- Zero Learning Curve
Visual drag-drop circuit builder. Non-cryptographers can understand and build zero-knowledge proofs in 5 minutes.
Use case: A frontend developer with zero crypto knowledge can add age verification to their app without learning advanced mathematics.
3- Hours, Not Months
13 production-ready templates. Copy-paste working circuits. npm install zkrune-sdk and ship.
Use case: A startup can add privacy features to their MVP in an afternoon instead of hiring a ZK expert for 6 months.


Real-World Applications
🗳️ Governance & Voting
Problem: On-chain voting exposes your vote publicly
Solution: Prove you're eligible to vote without revealing your choice
Impact: True secret ballots on blockchain
💰 DeFi & Finance
Problem: Proving creditworthiness means sharing your bank statements
Solution: Prove you have minimum balance without revealing exact amount
Impact: Privacy-preserving loans and credit
🎫 Identity & Access
Problem: Age verification requires showing full ID (name, address, photo)
Solution: Prove you're over 18 without revealing birthdate or identity
Impact: Anonymous age-restricted services

🖼️ NFT & Gaming
Problem: Proving NFT ownership reveals your entire wallet
Solution: Prove you own a specific collection NFT without revealing which one
Impact: Private membership proofs for DAOs and communities
🔐 Authentication
Problem: Password recovery leaks your email/phone
Solution: Prove you know the password hash without revealing the password
Impact: Zero-knowledge authentication systems

Making Privacy Accessible
Before zkRune:
❌ Send data to servers (privacy risk)
❌ Hire a cryptography PhD ($200k+/year)
❌ 6-12 months development time
❌ Limited to experts only
After zkRune:
✅ 100% client-side (true privacy)
✅ Visual builder (no expertise needed)
✅ Hours to production (templates ready)
✅ Accessible to all developers

The Bigger Impact
Zcash's Groth16 has secured billions of dollars in shielded transactions since 2016. It's battle-tested, production-proven cryptography.
By making this technology accessible, we enable:
More developers → More privacy apps → Stronger ecosystem
Faster innovation → Privacy becomes standard, not luxury
Wider adoption → Privacy for everyone, not just crypto natives
zkRune democratizes privacy technology. Just like how Figma made design accessible to everyone, zkRune makes zero-knowledge proofs accessible to every developer.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Three Major Challenges (And How I Solved Them)
🔴 Challenge #1: The Viewing Key Security Disaster
The Problem:
Early in development, I implemented shielded balance checking with viewing keys sent via GET request URL parameters:
// WRONG - Security vulnerability!fetch(`/api/balance?address=zs1...&viewingKey=zxviews...`)
Why This Was Catastrophic:
Viewing keys appeared in browser history (unencrypted)
Server logs captured viewing keys (permanent record)
Network monitoring could intercept keys (MITM attack)
This defeated the entire purpose of privacy 
The Solution:
Rewrote the entire endpoint to use POST requests with body encryption:

// CORRECT - Secure implementationfetch('/api/zcash-balance-shielded', {  method: 'POST',  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },  body: JSON.stringify({ address, viewingKey }) // Never in URL!})
Key Learning: Security-first architecture isn't optional in privacy tech. One careless API call can destroy months of cryptographic work.

Challenge #2: Client-Side ZK Proof Generation (The "Impossible" Feature)
The Problem:
Industry standard is server-side proof generation. Generating Groth16 proofs in-browser seemed impossible:
snarkjs is 2.5MB+ (slow initial load)
WASM circuits are 200KB-500KB each
Proving keys are 3-5MB per circuit
Browser memory limits (~2GB)
Total: 50MB+ assets for all 13 circuits
The "Expert" Advice:
Everyone said: "Just use a server, client-side is impractical."
My Response:
"If I use a server, I'm just another privacy theater platform."
The Solution:
Built a progressive loading system with aggressive caching:
Lazy Loading: Only load circuit files when user selects a template
const { proof } = await snarkjs.groth16.fullProve(  inputs,  new Uint8Array(wasmBuffer), // Loaded on-demand  new Uint8Array(zkeyBuffer)  // Cached in service worker)
Service Worker Caching (PWA):
// Cache circuit files for 365 days{  urlPattern: /^https?.*\.(wasm|zkey)$/i,  handler: 'CacheFirst',  expiration: { maxAgeSeconds: 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 }}
Result:
First load: 3-5 seconds
Cached: <1 second
Zero server calls, true privacy maintained ✅
Key Learning: "Impossible" usually means "no one bothered to optimize it properly."

Challenge #3: The Trusted Setup Transparency Dilemma
The Problem:
Groth16 requires a trusted setup (generating .zkey proving keys). Options:
Single-party setup (fast): I generate keys alone
⚠️ I could theoretically forge proofs (if I keep "toxic waste")
⚠️ Users must trust me
Multi-party ceremony (secure): 20+ people contribute randomness
✅ Trustless (only one needs to delete their secret)
❌ Takes 4-6 weeks to coordinate
❌ Impossible during 8-day hackathon
The Dilemma:
Do I ship a working demo with trust assumptions, or miss the hackathon for perfect security?
The Solution:
Radical transparency - document everything in README:
## ⚠️ Security Note (Hackathon Demo)

**Current Setup:**  
Single-party trusted setup (timestamp-based entropy)

**What This Means:**
- ✅ Proofs are mathematically valid
- ⚠️ Key generator could theoretically forge proofs
- 🔒 Production requires multi-party ceremony

**Production Path:**
MPC ceremony with 10+ contributors (timeline: 4-6 weeks)

he Response:
Community appreciated honesty over false claims. Several members already volunteered for the ceremony.
Key Learning: In crypto/privacy, transparency about limitations builds more trust than hiding them.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

zkRune directly supports ECC's mission of mainstream Zcash adoption by solving the developer accessibility problem.
Why this matters for ECC:
Zcash has world-class privacy technology, but adoption is limited because building with Groth16 requires cryptography expertise. zkRune bridges this gap:
Developer Onboarding: Visual builder teaches Zcash's ZK principles in 5 minutes vs 6 months
Production Tools: NPM SDK makes integrating Zcash-grade privacy as simple as npm install
Real Integration: Lightwalletd infrastructure (transparent addresses working, shielded in development)
Ecosystem Multiplier: Every developer using zkRune becomes a potential Zcash application builder
Bottom line: We're turning Zcash's technical excellence into developer-friendly tools that accelerate mainstream adoption.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

zkRune is developer infrastructure for zero-knowledge proofs: NPM SDK (zkrune-sdk), CLI tool (zkrune-cli), visual circuit builder, and 13 production-ready templates.
Unique differentiator: 100% client-side proof generation. Unlike other "ZK developer tools" that use servers (defeating privacy), zkRune maintains zero-knowledge properties end-to-end.
We're not building a privacy app - we're building the infrastructure that lets others build privacy apps.

Louis Stein

### VaultID
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vaultid-0333) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Crew-object-Object/VaultID) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/kNMljHOG6n8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHIndiaVilla-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethindia-villa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-11-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Portable, wallet-encrypted authentication sessions

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Application sessions today are **device-bound, fragile, and centralized**.  
Users lose access when switching browsers or devices, and developers rely on insecure cookie-based storage.

---

## 💡 What VaultID Does

VaultID **stores encrypted session data on IPFS** and **anchors a proof of that session on-chain**, creating a decentralized, portable session system.

- **IPFS** → stores the encrypted session securely  
- **Blockchain** → records a tamper-proof reference (no secrets on-chain)

---

## 🔑 Key Capabilities

- **Portable Sessions**  
  Use the same login across:
  - Multiple browsers
  - Multiple devices
  - Different environments (desktop → laptop)

- **Shared Sessions**  
  Multiple users using the **same wallet** can access the same authenticated session  
  (useful for teams, shared dashboards, DAOs, ops accounts)

- **Single Login, Everywhere**  
  One authentication → usable across all supported clients

- **Decentralized by Design**  
  No central session store  
  No server-controlled cookies  
  No plaintext credentials

---

## 🚀 What’s Coming Next

- **Refresh Token Management**  
  Secure rotation to extend session validity without re-login

- **Mobile Support**  
  Designed to work seamlessly on mobile browsers and apps

---

## 🧠 In Short

VaultID turns sessions into **portable, shared, and decentralized assets** —  
usable across browsers, devices, and users, without sacrificing security or control.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building VaultID involved solving problems that **don’t have standard patterns yet**, especially around browser behavior, sessions, and decentralization.

---

### 🔍 Detecting Login / Logout State Changes

**Challenge:**  
Websites don’t expose a clear signal for “user logged in” or “user logged out”.  
Each app handles authentication differently — cookies, redirects, silent refreshes, etc.

**Why it was hard:**
- No universal event for auth state changes
- Sessions update silently in the background
- Logout flows vary wildly across apps

**How we solved it:**
- Monitored **cookie mutations and storage changes**
- Compared session snapshots over time
- Triggered the extension popup only when a **meaningful auth state change** was detected  
  - Login → prompt to **save session**
  - Logout → prompt to **delete session**

---

### 🔐 Syncing & Decrypting Sessions from IPFS

**Challenge:**  
Session data stored on IPFS is encrypted and fetched asynchronously, making synchronization tricky.

**Why it was hard:**
- IPFS retrieval is non-instant
- AES-GCM requires exact nonce + key handling
- Partial or out-of-order data breaks decryption

**How we solved it:**
- Strict versioning of session payloads
- Deterministic encryption/decryption flow
- Validated decrypted data before applying it

---

### 🍪 Rehydrating Cookies into Websites

**Challenge:**  
Correctly restoring cookies into a website after decryption is non-trivial.

**Why it was hard:**
- Cookie attributes (domain, path, secure, sameSite) must match exactly
- Incorrect flags silently break login
- Browsers enforce strict security rules

**How we solved it:**
- Preserved full cookie metadata during encryption
- Restored cookies in the correct order
- Applied browser-compliant constraints to avoid rejection

---

## 🧠 Key Takeaway

The hardest part wasn’t encryption or blockchain —  
it was **bridging real-world browser behavior with decentralized storage** in a way that feels seamless to users.

> StarkNET - IIoT Data NFT Validate

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Internet of Things (IoT)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Internet%20of%20Things%20(IoT)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Industrial IoT (IIoT) devices across manufacturing, energy, supply-chain, healthcare, and environmental industries generate massive amounts of operational data. However, this data is often transmitted without proper verification, allowing attackers, insiders, or misconfigured devices to send fake, altered, or manipulated sensor data into the system.

Such falsified data leads to:

❌ Wrong R&D decisions

❌ Incorrect operational analytics

❌ Faulty predictive maintenance models

❌ Risky safety and compliance evaluations

❌ Financial loss and wrong investments

❌ Zero traceability for who sent what data

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧 Challenges I Ran Into
1. Receiving Unstable Sensor Data From the IIoT Device

The ESP8266 was sending noisy or incomplete air-quality readings through the serial port.
This caused corrupted JSON, missing values, and inconsistent uploads.

How I fixed it:

Added a newline-terminated protocol for every sensor message

Introduced buffer cleaning and retry logic on the Python backend

Added basic filtering and averaging to stabilise the sensor output

2. IPFS Upload Failing Due to Invalid or Partial Data

Sometimes the Pinata API rejected the upload because the payload arrived before the sensor reading was fully parsed.

How I fixed it:

Implemented strict input validation

Uploaded only after successful checksum verification

Added exception handling + retry mechanism

3. StarkNet Testnet RPC Not Responding / Rate Limiting

The biggest hurdle was interacting with StarkNet testnet.
RPC nodes were sometimes down, slow, or returned signature errors.

How I fixed it:

Switched to a stable Sepolia StarkNet RPC provider

Added automatic exponential backoff

Implemented transaction polling with timeout

4. Smart Contract Rejected TokenURI Updates

While minting NFT metadata, the contract rejected some CIDs because of URI encoding issues.

How I fixed it:

Cleaned CID formatting

Ensured tokenURI string length matched Cairo contract expectations

Used a consistent IPFS prefix (ipfs://)

5. Fake / Manipulated Data Detection Logic

One of my main goals was preventing fake industrial data.
Initially, any serial input—even spoofed—would get uploaded and minted.

How I fixed it:

Added a device-identity signature (simple hash-based validation)

Implemented timestamp signing before IPFS upload

Ensured every CID minted on-chain matches a validated, genuine device reading

This helped prevent false or manipulated sensor values.

6. Syncing Frontend Dashboard With Real-Time Data

The client dashboard did not show new NFT updates instantly.

How I fixed it:

Added a WebSocket listener for NFT mint events

Queried StarkNet indexers for new token IDs

Auto-refreshed Pinata metadata without manual reload

7. Debugging the Full Pipeline End-to-End

IIoT → Serial → Python → IPFS → StarkNet NFT → Dashboard
is a long chain — a single break stops the whole flow.

How I fixed it:

Added logging at each stage

Used small mock payloads for testing

Debugged layer-by-layer instead of all at once

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon (Matic)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20(Matic)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygonscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygonscan-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

*Today, a significant portion of purchased cloud storage remains unused. Individuals and businesses often subscribe to storage plans from providers such as **Dropbox**, but only use a fraction of their allocated capacity. The remaining storage sits idle, effectively wasting a digital resource that has already been paid for.*

At the same time, many users, startups, and small teams require **affordable and flexible storage solutions**, yet they are forced into fixed subscription models offered by centralized providers. These services often come with rigid pricing structures, limited customization, and no way for users to monetize unused storage capacity.

This creates two major inefficiencies:

- **Underutilized Resources** – Large amounts of paid cloud storage remain unused.
- **Centralized Control** – Storage markets are dominated by centralized platforms with limited transparency and user ownership.

## How Rentabyte Solves This

**Rentabyte** introduces a decentralized storage rental marketplace that transforms unused cloud storage into a valuable, tradable resource.

With Rentabyte:

- Users can **contribute their unused cloud storage** and earn income from it.
- Buyers can **rent storage on demand** without committing to expensive subscription plans.
- All transactions are secured through **smart contracts** on the polygon network.

## Impact

By enabling peer-to-peer storage sharing, Rentabyte:

- Improves **global storage utilization**
- Reduces **storage costs for users**
- Introduces **transparency and trust through blockchain**
- Creates a **decentralized marketplace for cloud storage**

In short, **Rentabyte turns idle cloud storage into an economic opportunity while making storage more accessible and decentralized.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Key Challenges Faced During Development

### 1. Invisible Transaction Feedback
When users paid POL for storage, **no visual feedback appeared**.  
The issue was caused by toast notifications using a .alert class that had display: none.  
**Fix:** Implemented a dedicated #toast-container with a .toast class and slide-in animation for visible notifications.

---

### 2. Raw Blockchain Errors Shown to Users
Errors from MetaMask and ethers.js v6 (e.g., RPC error codes) were displayed directly to users.  
**Fix:** Created a getErrorMessage() function to convert complex blockchain errors into **clear, user-friendly messages**.

> Make your idle USDC work harder without the risk

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**There are 4 billion people in the world who save money and watch it lose value every year.** Gold went up 30% in 2025. Miami real estate climbed 12%. Bitcoin doubled. Meanwhile their savings account paid 3 to 4%. They didn't participate in any of that upside because participating means risking their principal, and they cannot afford to lose what they have.

On the other side, DeFi gives you yield vaults paying 3 to 6%, but that yield just sits as USDC doing nothing. And if you want exposure to real assets like gold or real estate, you have to trade perpetuals with leverage where a 5% move can wipe your entire position.

**PPN.fi solves both problems at once.** It takes the yield your USDC is already generating in Morpho, Aave, or Moonwell and uses it as margin for leveraged positions on 25 real world assets including gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and 19 US real estate city indexes. Your principal stays in the yield vault and grows back to exactly your deposit amount using the zero coupon present value formula, the same math Goldman Sachs uses for their $7 trillion structured notes business. The yield becomes your risk budget. If the trade wins, you earn leveraged returns on top of your deposit. If it loses, the yield absorbs the loss and you get every dollar back.

**What people use it for:**

A saver who wants gold exposure without any possibility of losing their deposit picks a Gold shield at 5x leverage. Backtested across 3,707 simulations, this averaged 5.8% annualized with only 10% liquidation risk and 100% principal protection.

A crypto believer who thinks SOL will keep running picks a Solana shield at 1x. Zero leverage risk, zero liquidation, 44.6% annualized returns in our backtest. The bull trend does the work.

A degen who wants to go 50x long on Charlotte real estate or short gold at 20x can use the RWA perps exchange directly with full leverage, TP/SL, and liquidation mechanics across all 25 markets.

An LP who wants better than Morpho yield deposits into the vault and earns base yield plus trading fees plus funding rates plus profit from liquidated positions across 25 diversified asset markets.

A person with no crypto wallet and no DeFi experience texts our WhatsApp number, says "protect my savings from gold going up," and the AI agent creates a BitGo custodial wallet, executes the full shield, encrypts the record on Fileverse, registers an ENS subname, and sends them a confirmation message. Zero app downloads. Zero seed phrases. Zero financial literacy required.

**PPN.fi makes it safe to get market exposure, makes idle yield productive, makes RWA markets liquid, and makes DeFi accessible to people who have never used it.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

**The $0.90 problem that almost broke everything.** Our first implementation used simple yield calculation: $1,000 at 6% for 6 months equals $30 of yield, so send $970 to Morpho and $30 to the position. But $970 earning 6% for 6 months returns $999.10, not $1,000. That $0.90 gap seems tiny until you scale it. On a $10 million deposit that is $9,000 missing. You cannot call something "principal protected" when thousands of dollars are unaccounted for. We spent hours debugging this before realizing TradFi solves it with the zero coupon present value formula: PV = FV / (1 + r)^t. This gives the EXACT amount that grows to EXACTLY the deposit. No approximation. No gap. Once we switched to this formula, the math became airtight at any deposit size, which our 12.5 million simulation backtest confirmed with 100.0000% principal protection.

**Real estate liquidation scanning was way harder than crypto.** For crypto assets, checking if a position got liquidated during a holding period is straightforward because you have hourly or minute level price data. Real estate indexes from Parcl Labs update once per day. A position could appear safe at the daily close but might have breached the liquidation level intraday if we had finer data. We solved this conservatively by checking every daily data point during the entire holding period, not just the entry and exit price. This means our backtest slightly overestimates liquidation rates for real estate (because a daily close below liquidation triggers a liq even if the intraday low was only briefly there), but it ensures our principal protection claim is honest and defensible.

**Yield rates kept changing on us.** We initially hardcoded yield rates at 5 to 6% based on what Morpho historically paid. Midway through building, we pulled live rates from DeFiLlama and discovered current rates were 2.46 to 3.63%. This completely changed the product economics. Exposure budgets shrank, returns got more modest, and strategies that worked at 6% didn't work at 2.5%. We had to rebuild our backtest engine to pull live APYs from DeFiLlama's API on every run and recalculate everything. The silver lining is this forced us to find strategies that work at TODAY's rates, not theoretical ones, making our backtest results genuinely honest.

**Making 5 sponsor SDKs work together in one flow was a nightmare.** The WhatsApp shield activation touches Twilio for messaging, OpenAI for intent parsing, HeyElsa x402 for wallet analysis (paying real micropayments on Base mainnet), BitGo SDK for custodial wallet creation on Base testnet, our smart contracts on Base Sepolia for the actual deposit, ENS NameWrapper on Ethereum Sepolia for subname registration, and Fileverse agents on Sepolia with Pinata storage for encrypted document creation. That is 7 different services across 3 different chains in a single user flow triggered by a WhatsApp message. Getting the async orchestration right, handling failures gracefully at each step, and making sure the user gets a clean confirmation message even when one service is slow took more debugging than building the actual PPN math.

**CoinGecko rate limits during backtest runs.** Running 12.5 million simulations requires fetching historical price data for multiple assets. CoinGecko Pro has a 500 calls per minute limit. Our first backtest run hit the limit, got throttled, and returned incomplete data that silently corrupted thousands of simulations. We solved this by building a local cache layer that fetches historical data once, saves it to disk, and reuses it across all subsequent runs. This also made iteration dramatically faster since we could rerun the full backtest in minutes instead of waiting for API calls.

Our `server/services/bitgoCustodyService.js` uses `BitGoAPI` with `registerEthCoins` from `@bitgo/sdk-coin-eth` to programmatically create MPC wallets on Base testnet (tbaseeth via `BITGO_CUSTODY_COIN`). All of this happened through BitGo's programmatic transaction building and signing, with enterprise policy controls governing every step.

We implemented the **exact zero coupon present value formula** that banks use to construct Principal Protected Notes: `PV = FV / (1 + r)^t`. When a user deposits $10,000 with a 365 day duration at 3.63% Morpho APY, the protocol calculates the precise present value ($9,649.72), routes that to the yield vault, and uses the exact remainder ($350.28) as margin for a leveraged position on the user's chosen real world asset. The yield portion grows to exactly $10,000 at maturity. The exposure portion trades with leverage. **The user's principal is mathematically guaranteed to return in full regardless of what happens to the leveraged position.** This is not an approximation. This is not a promise. This is the same bond math that Goldman Sachs uses, implemented as a composable DeFi primitive on Base.

12,523,401 individual simulations across 25 assets, 3 real yield protocols (Aave V3 2.46%, Morpho 3.63%, Moonwell 3.43% from live DeFiLlama data), 11 leverage levels, 7 duration windows, and every possible entry date in the historical dataset. **Principal protection held in 100.0000% of simulations. Zero failures.** Charlotte real estate at 10x leverage had zero liquidations across 1,462 simulations. Solana at 1x delivered 44.6% annualized returns with zero liquidation risk. Gold at 5x returned 5.8% annualized with under 10% liquidation. These are not projections. These are results from real price data.

They charge 2 to 5 percent in hidden fees, require $100,000 minimums, full KYC, accredited investor status, and lock your money for 3 to 5 years. Billions of dollars flow through these instruments every year because the value proposition is unbeatable: **you participate in market upside while your principal is mathematically guaranteed to come back.**

**Nobody has ever built this on chain. Until today.**

PPN.fi takes the *exact same zero coupon bond math* that powers Wall Street structured notes and implements it as a permissionless DeFi protocol on Base. We didn't approximate it. We didn't simplify it. We used the **precise present value formula** that banks use, verified it against **12.5 million backtested simulations** across **25 real world assets** including crypto, gold, silver, oil, natural gas, and **19 US real estate markets**, and achieved **100.0000% principal protection across every single simulation**. Not 99.9%. Not approximately. One hundred percent. Zero failures.

**What makes this historically significant:**

The structured products market is $7+ trillion globally. It is one of the largest and most profitable segments in all of finance. And it has been completely inaccessible to 99% of the world's population because of minimums, fees, KYC, and geographic restrictions. A developer in Mumbai, a student in Lagos, a freelancer in Manila could never access a principal protected note. Today they can. With $100 and a wallet.

**What we built is not a wrapper or a frontend.** It is a complete financial protocol: smart contracts for custody on Base Sepolia, a multi source price engine pulling real prices from CoinGecko, OilPriceAPI, and Parcl Labs, a full perpetual derivatives engine with 25 markets and 1 to 100x leverage, an LP vault with epoch based withdrawals, AI powered recommendations via HeyElsa with x402 micropayments, encrypted position records on Fileverse, financial identity on ENS, and custody infrastructure via BitGo. Every sponsor integration is a core feature, not a bolt on.

**And the DeFi yield advantage is the killer innovation.** Banks build PPNs on top of 4% bond yields. We build on top of Morpho, Aave, and Moonwell yields. Higher yields mean bigger exposure budgets which mean better returns for users on the exact same structure. DeFi doesn't just replicate TradFi here. **DeFi makes it fundamentally better.**

> **We took a product that took Wall Street 40 years to perfect, made it permissionless, made it cheaper, made it better, proved it with 12.5 million simulations, and shipped it in a weekend. That is why PPN.fi is the best overall project.**

**The problem it solves**

##### Hackathons reveal a consistent pattern: developers without blockchain expertise want to ship full-stack dApps but hit a wall. They ask ChatGPT or Bolt "build me a DAO" and get fragmented code—no contract deployment, no security audit trail, no wallet integration. Existing AI tools lack:

- End-to-end automation (contract → compile → deploy → audit → UI, all in one)
- Smart contract expertise and security practices
- Deployment automation with real gas cost handling
- Immutable audit logs for compliance
- Automatic frontend-to-blockchain wiring

Igriz closes this gap. One prompt generates and deploys production-ready contracts with audit logging and complete Dapp with pre-built frontends, no blockchain knowledge required.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. DataHaven Audit Log Integration
- File status polling stuck in "inProgress" for 27+ attempts under load
- MSP backend latency causes delayed audit verification
- Docs were not the best
- Solution: Configurable timeouts with async retry and local intent caching - still takes too much time

## 2. Multi-Provider API Rate Limiting
- Groq, OpenAI, and Google AI Studio have different quota models and limits
- Required robust fallback logic and provider switching mid-stream
- Solution: Implemented cascading provider fallback whenever api hits limit

## 3. WebContainer Node.js v20 Incompatibility
- Hardhat v2.23+ requires Node.js 22+ but WebContainer runs v20
- Built custom Solidity compilation pipeline using pure JavaScript `solc`

## 4. WebContainer File System Race Conditions
- Parallel file writes create incomplete directory structures
- npm install starts before all dependencies are declared
- Compilation fails on partially written contracts
- Solution: Grouped file writes by type (contracts → scripts → configs → frontend) with explicit await barriers

**Grand Prize**

##### igriz is a **Web3 Infrastructure & Developer Tooling** project that directly addresses the critical gap in blockchain onboarding. We fit this track by:

**Democratizing dApp Development**: Breaking down barriers for non-blockchain developers to build production-ready Web3 applications. Most hackathon participants lack Solidity expertise but want to ship on-chain products - igriz enables them with zero blockchain knowledge.
