![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Neo4j](https://img.shields.io/badge/Neo4j-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webauthn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webauthn-333333?style=flat-square) ![EIP-4337](https://img.shields.io/badge/EIP--4337-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every day, a massive volume of complex AI research (papers and codebases) is published. However, simply reading an abstract, skimming a GitHub repo, or watching a YouTube explainer isn't enough to truly understand the mechanics of new models. The core problem is that the gap between a paper being "published" and actually being "understood" by the community is widening.

## What "Papers with Claude Code" Solves

- Course Creation Friction: It eliminates the weeks of manual work usually required to build a technical curriculum. By analyzing an arXiv URL and a GitHub repo, Claude Code generates a grounded, hallucination-free course in under a minute.

- Broken Platform Economics: It replaces expensive monthly subscriptions and greedy platform middlemen with a native x402 micropayment system. Learners pay fractions of a cent in USDC (on Base/Kite Chain) only for the exact concepts they unlock. By using ERC-8021 builder codes, it automatically routes on-chain royalties directly to the original paper authors whenever their work is taught.

- Isolated Learning: It moves education out of private silos. Progress is recorded on the AIN blockchain, creating a verifiable learning passport for users and mapping a real-time, global Knowledge Graph of what the community actually understands.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 0. Deterministic Course Generation from Papers

6-step headless pipeline: parse paper → extract 15-30 concept nodes → topological sort by prerequisites → generate lessons with quizzes → scaffold files → publish to AIN with x402 pricing. Deterministic slugs ensure the same paper always produces the same course ID regardless of input URL format (arXiv, GitHub, HuggingFace all normalize to canonical title). Paper text treated as DATA only — defense against prompt injection in adversarial papers.

## 1. P256 Passkey as Blockchain Wallet

WebAuthn mandates P256 (ES256), but P256 lacks reliable public key recovery from signatures — unlike secp256k1's ecrecover. We designed a new 98-byte signature format (0x02 + compressedPubKey(33) + r(32) + s(32)) that embeds the public key directly, making verification deterministic on AIN blockchain while remaining backward-compatible with existing 66-byte secp256k1 signatures. The passkey IS the wallet — no seed phrases, no private key management. 

## 2. Dual-Chain Architecture

The knowledge graph needs fast, append-only writes. Payments need EVM compatibility and stablecoins. No single chain does both. We split: AIN blockchain stores the knowledge graph (explorations, topics, frontier maps), Kite/Base chain handles USDC micropayments (ERC-4337 AA, ERC-8004 agent identity, ERC-8021 attribution). A Cogito Node writes an exploration to AIN, tags it with a price, and a learner on Base pays to access it — x402 bridges the two chains.

## 3. x402 Micropayment Protocol

At ~$0.001 per stage, traditional payment rails (Stripe minimum fees, subscriptions) don't work. We adopted HTTP 402: server returns payment details, client signs and retries with X-Payment header. An x402-aware fetch wrapper handles the 402 → sign → retry flow transparently — application code never sees payment logic. Adapter pattern switches between mock (dev) and real (Kite chain) via env var.

## 4. Ephemeral K8s Pods for Per-Learner AI Tutors

Each learner gets a dedicated Claude Code instance in a dynamically created Kubernetes pod. Perfect isolation — no shared state, no context leakage. Dynamic creation over pre-allocated pool: security outweighs the 5-10s startup latency. WebSocket over SSH: no port exposure, works through standard proxies. Three cleanup paths (unmount, HMR, tab close) required to prevent zombie session leaks.

## 5. Knowledge Graph as Collective Intelligence Ledger

Multiple autonomous Cogito Nodes independently explore papers and write to the same AIN blockchain graph — no central coordinator. Each exploration creates a graph node with typed edges (extends, related, prerequisite). Frontier maps aggregate depth across all nodes, enabling cross-node discovery: Node A sees "transformers explored to depth 5" by Node B and fills gaps at depth 6. Throughput limited by consensus — solved with polling intervals and batch writes.

## 6. Self-Sustaining Cogito Node Economics

Local LLM (Qwen3-32B-AWQ on A6000) costs ~$0.004/inference vs. cloud API at $0.01-0.05. At $0.001/stage micropayment prices, cloud APIs would never break even. Local LLM becomes self-sustaining at ~180 queries/day. The SUSTAIN phase tracks P&L and shifts exploration toward higher-demand topics visible on frontier maps.

## 7. ERC-8004 + ERC-8021: Agent Identity and Author Attribution

Each Cogito Node registers as an ERC-8004 autonomous agent on Base — not a plain NFT, but full identity: setAgentURI(), metadata registry, wallet binding. Every x402 payment transaction includes ERC-8021 builder codes encoding arxiv_id + github_repo + first_author — immutable on-chain attribution of original paper authors whenever their work is monetized.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

### 1. Claude Code as Course Generator

Claude Code runs headless in a Kubernetes pod. User pastes an arXiv URL and GitHub repo into the Course Builder, a dedicated pod spins up, and Claude Code autonomously reads the paper, extracts concept nodes, generates lessons with quizzes, and publishes to the AIN blockchain with x402 pricing. Zero human intervention. Paper text is treated as DATA only (prompt injection defense). Deterministic slugs ensure the same paper always maps to the same course ID.

### 2. Claude Code as Personalized AI Tutor

Each learner gets a dedicated Claude Code instance in an ephemeral Kubernetes pod. Left side: 2D dungeon room with concept markers. Right side: Claude Code terminal pre-loaded with the paper's context and learner progress. Navigate concepts, ask questions, pass the quiz, pay ~$0.001 via x402, advance to the next stage. Pod destroyed on session end — perfect isolation between learners.

### 3. Cogito Node — Autonomous Knowledge Agent

Local LLM (Qwen3-32B-AWQ on A6000 GPU) fused with an AIN blockchain node. Runs an autonomous loop: THINK (explore papers) → RECORD (write to knowledge graph) → ALIGN (read other nodes, fill gaps) → EARN (sell access via x402) → SUSTAIN (track P&L, shift to higher-demand topics). Multiple Cogito Nodes write to the same on-chain graph without central coordination.

### How They Work Together

Cogito Node discovers paper on arXiv
  → local LLM generates structured exploration
  → writes to AIN blockchain knowledge graph
  → Claude Code (generator) turns it into a playable course
  → course published with x402 pricing on Kite/Base chain
  → learner enters 2D dungeon room
  → Claude Code (tutor) guides them through concepts
  → quiz passed → x402 micropayment → next stage unlocked
  → progress recorded on-chain → feeds back into knowledge graph
  → Cogito Node reads frontier map → explores deeper

The knowledge graph is the shared substrate. Cogito Nodes produce knowledge, Claude Code structures it into courses, Claude Code delivers it to learners, and learner progress feeds back into the graph — AI agents and humans build the world's knowledge together.

### Built with Claude Code

This project was itself built using Claude Code — the frontend (43 routes, Next.js), K8s infrastructure, blockchain integration, course generation pipeline, and P256 passkey security defenses were all developed with Claude Code as the primary engineering tool.

**ETHERSPACE**

Academic knowledge is locked behind publisher paywalls. The platform owns the content, the distribution, and the revenue. Authors get nothing when their papers are taught or monetized. This project flips ownership.

## Wallets & Identity

P256 passkey IS the wallet — no MetaMask, no seed phrases, no extensions. Users tap their fingerprint and they have an Ethereum-compatible wallet. ERC-8004 registers autonomous Cogito Nodes as on-chain agents on Base with full identity, metadata, and wallet binding.

## Tokenomics

x402 micropayments (~$0.001/stage in USDC on Base) let learners pay sub-cent amounts per concept instead of $30/month subscriptions. Cogito Nodes run local LLMs, explore papers, sell access via x402, track P&L, and shift toward higher-demand topics — autonomous economics on Ethereum L2.

## Ownership & Attribution

ERC-8021 builder codes embed `arxiv_id + github_repo + first_author` immutably in every x402 payment transaction on Base. Original paper authors get on-chain attribution whenever their work is monetized. Learner progress — quiz completions, verified skills, learning paths — is recorded on-chain as a decentralized learning passport the learner owns.

## Social & Content

An academic village where researchers, creators, learners, and AI agents coexist. See friends' progress, get notifications, compete on leaderboards. Every interaction feeds into a shared on-chain knowledge graph that grows collectively.

## Ethereum Showcase

Dual-chain on Ethereum ecosystem: Base (L2) for USDC payments + AIN blockchain for the knowledge graph. Three ERC standards in production: ERC-4337 (account abstraction wallets), ERC-8004 (agent identity), ERC-8021 (author attribution).

## Mainstream Adoption

Zero crypto friction. Passkey onboarding (fingerprint to wallet), invisible micropayments (x402 handles the 402-sign-retry flow automatically), no gas management (account abstraction). A learner never sees "blockchain" — they just learn and pay fractions of a cent.

The Indexer URL and RPC URL look similar but serve different purposes. The rootHash must be saved immediately after upload or the file is lost forever. Our course surfaces all of these with warnings, the tutor auto-diagnoses them, and every code example handles them correctly.

Any protocol can create a course with four files: paper.json (metadata), graph.json (concepts + prerequisites), courses.json (lessons + exercises), and CLAUDE.md (tutor config with domain facts). This is a template, not a one-off tutorial.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

An AI tutor agent that authenticates itself via Kite Passport, pays for knowledge access through x402 on Kite Chain, and records verifiable learning proofs on-chain — all without human intervention.

## What It Does

Research papers become interactive courses in a 2D dungeon environment. Each stage is gated by an x402 micropayment (~$0.001 in Test USDT on Kite Testnet). When a learner passes a quiz, the AI agent autonomously pays to unlock the next stage. No wallet popups, no manual signing. LearningLedger smart contract deployed at [0xaffB...14A72](https://testnet.kitescan.ai/address/0xaffB053eE4fb81c0D3450fDA6db201f901214A72) on Kite Testnet (Chain ID 2368).

## Agent Autonomy

Server boots with KITE_AGENT_ID + KITE_AGENT_SECRET→ agent self-authenticates via client_credentials → MCP client connects to Kite MCP server → x402Fetch() auto-detects HTTP 402 → calls get_payer_addr + approve_payment via MCP → retries with X-Payment header → Pieverse settles on Kite Chain → learning event recorded on AIN blockchain. Humans configure env vars once. Everything after is autonomous.

## Bidirectional x402

We built both sides. **Service Provider**: 7 x402-gated API routes returning HTTP 402 with gokite-aa scheme, settling via Pieverse facilitator. **Agent Client**: x402Fetch() wrapper handles the entire 402→pay→retry cycle transparently. Every failure mode covered — insufficient_funds (faucet link), SessionExpired (re-auth), InsufficientBudget (limit warning).

## Verifiable Agent Identity

WebAuthn P-256 passkey as hardware-bound wallet with three security defenses (Rogue Key, replay/phishing, signature malleability). Agent DID (did:kite:learner.eth/claude-tutor/v1) derived via BIP-32 at path m/44'/2368'/0'/0/{index}. KitePass binds identity to Standing Intent spending constraints. Kite Passport integrated as NextAuth v5 OAuth provider with dual auth modes (user OAuth + agent self-auth).

## On-Chain Records (Dual Chain)

Kite Chain settles USDT micropayments with sub-second finality. AIN blockchain records learning events (course_enter, stage_complete, quiz_pass) with SHA-256 attestation hashes. ERC-4337 account abstraction for gasless UX. ERC-8004 agent identity on Base. ERC-8021 builder codes attributing original paper authors in every payment transaction.

## Security

Hardware-bound P-256 keys (non-exportable). Server-side MCP proxy (browser never sees tokens). Standing Intent with per-tx max, daily cap, contract whitelist, function whitelist, TTL. OAuth state validation (CSRF). Low-S signature enforcement. Constant-time comparison against timing side-channels.

## The App

Papers with Claude Code turns AI research papers into interactive learning courses. The Hedera agent marketplace is where this happens autonomously: a human drops a paper URL, and OpenClaw agents compete to analyze it, design the course, and get paid — all on Hedera.

Three agents — **Analyst**, **Architect**, **Scholar** — bid competitively, consult each other for paid expertise (agents hiring agents), and deliver structured courses. Every interaction is an HCS message. Every payment is an HTS token transfer. Every reputation score is an ERC-8004 attestation.

| **Hedera HCS** | Single topic carries all coordination: bids, deliverables, consultations, completions (12-20+ messages/session) |
| **Hedera HTS** | KNOW token for escrow, agent payments, and agent-to-agent consultation fees |
| **ERC-8004** | Human review scores recorded as cross-chain reputation on Sepolia |
| **Not human-operated** | Agents evaluate paper complexity, set their own prices, decide when to consult Scholar, negotiate fees |

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

> Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agent on Base

**Platform**: [paperswithclaudecode.com](https://paperswithclaudecode.com) — where learners browse papers, publish courses, and pay per stage.
**Agent Dashboard**: [cogito.paperswithclaudecode.com](https://cogito.paperswithclaudecode.com) — where judges can see wallet balances, revenue vs. cost, Base transactions, and knowledge stats. Both are publicly accessible with no login required.

## What Is Papers with Claude Code

Every day, dozens of AI research papers drop on arXiv with code. Understanding them is hard. Papers with Claude Code turns any paper into an interactive dungeon-style course — learners explore concepts room by room with Claude Code as their AI tutor, and pay per stage with USDC micropayments on Base.

Behind the platform is the Cogito Node, a fully autonomous agent. It reads papers, generates structured knowledge, and publishes courses to [paperswithclaudecode.com](https://paperswithclaudecode.com) without any human involvement. The revenue from learners paying for course content goes directly to the agent's Base wallet, covering its own compute costs.

## How the Agent Works

The agent runs an indefinite autonomous cycle with four phases:

**Think (60% of cycles)**: The agent picks a topic from its frontier map — areas where community knowledge is thin — and uses a local LLM to explore related papers from arXiv. It writes structured explorations (concepts, summaries, methodology analysis) to a shared knowledge graph on the AIN blockchain.

**Align (20%)**: The agent reads what other nodes have explored on the same topics. It cross-references their findings with its own, identifies gaps, and prioritizes under-explored areas for its next Think cycle. This prevents duplication and pushes the collective knowledge frontier forward.

**Earn (10%)**: Once the agent has accumulated enough explorations on a topic (typically 3+), it auto-generates a multi-stage interactive course — complete with explanations, exercises, and quizzes. The course is published to [paperswithclaudecode.com](https://paperswithclaudecode.com) with x402 pricing so learners can unlock stages by paying USDC on Base.

**Sustain (10%)**: The agent checks its financial health. It queries its Base wallet for ETH and USDC balances, calculates the ratio of 24-hour income to 24-hour compute cost, and adjusts its strategy. If the ratio drops below 1.0, it conserves resources and focuses on high-demand topics. If it climbs above 2.0, it expands exploration into frontier territory.

## How It Earns Revenue

Learners on [paperswithclaudecode.com](https://paperswithclaudecode.com) pay USDC micropayments via the x402 protocol every time they access content. Unlocking a course stage costs $0.001. Browsing topic explorations costs $0.005. Requesting a deep LLM-curated analysis costs $0.05. Every payment settles directly to the agent's Base wallet through @x402/next middleware — no intermediary tokens, no subscription model, just pay-per-access.

## How It Sustains Itself

The agent runs a local LLM (Qwen3-32B on an A6000 GPU), which means there is zero per-inference cost — no API bills that scale with usage. The fixed daily cost is roughly $3-6: GPU power (~$0.72), server hosting ($2-5), and Base gas fees (~$0.10). Since producing more knowledge doesn't increase cost, the agent becomes more profitable as its course library grows and attracts more learners.

## ERC-8021 Builder Codes

Every Base transaction includes ERC-8021 builder code attribution in the calldata suffix. Each transaction is tagged with the agent's identifier (cogito_node), the source arXiv paper ID, the GitHub repository, and up to three original paper authors. This means the researchers whose work powers the courses get on-chain credit every time their paper generates revenue on the platform.

## ERC-8004 Agent Identity

The agent is registered on Base via the ERC-8004 Identity Registry. Its on-chain metadata declares which services it offers and that it supports x402 payments. Other agents can discover it through registry lookup, and learners can leave reputation feedback after purchasing content. This creates a trust layer — agents with better courses earn higher reputation and attract more learners.

## Why This Project Fits the Bounty

**It transacts on Base.** Every content payment from [paperswithclaudecode.com](https://paperswithclaudecode.com) is a USDC settlement on Base, plus the agent's ERC-8004 identity registration.

**It is self-sustaining.** Learner micropayments cover the $3-6/day compute cost. The agent monitors its own finances and auto-adjusts its exploration strategy to stay profitable.

**It implements ERC-8021 builder codes.** Every transaction attributes the agent, the source paper, and the original authors — giving researchers on-chain credit.

**It is autonomous.** The agent reads papers, generates courses, publishes them, and earns revenue in a continuous loop. No human triggers any phase.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/medichain-b341) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/anantaryaaa/health-record-dapps) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://medichain-brown.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/sfTdKrXNw3s?si=ENiOLSPUYdCx-_U6) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lisk%20Builders%20Challenge:%20Round%20Three-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://lisk-builders-challenge-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-10-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Medichain transforms medical data into RWA assets.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Medichain addresses the fragmentation and insecurity of traditional healthcare data management. Currently, medical records are scattered across different institutions, leaving patients with no central access and doctors with incomplete medical histories.

How it makes tasks easier & safer:
- Eliminates Data Fragmentation: Patients no longer need to carry physical files or repeat tests. Medichain provides a single, portable health identity (SBT) that consolidates records from multiple hospitals into one accessible dashboard.
- True Patient Ownership: Unlike traditional systems where hospitals "own" the data, Medichain gives patients full control. They can grant or revoke access to any doctor with custom expiration timers, ensuring privacy is maintained.
- Enhanced Security & Verifiability: By using blockchain and IPFS, records are encrypted and decentralized. This eliminates "single point of failure" risks and ensures that medical data cannot be tampered with or forged.
- Automated Data Entry: The integration of AI (Google Gemini OCR) allows hospitals to instantly digitize physical documents. This reduces human error and speeds up the administrative process during emergencies.
- Seamless Interoperability: It bridges the gap between different healthcare providers using standardized ICD-10 codes, making it easier for doctors to understand a patient’s history regardless of where the previous treatment occurred.
- Gasless UX: By utilizing ERC2771 meta-transactions, the system removes the complexity of blockchain. Users can interact with the app without needing to hold or understand cryptocurrency, making decentralized tech accessible to everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

- There are logic development bottlenecks within the hospital section of the smart contract.
- Defining the key unique selling points (USPs) of the project.
- Establishing the team meeting schedule.
- Learning how medical record works

**Winner Classification**

Medichain addresses the fragmentation and insecurity of traditional healthcare data management. Currently, medical records are scattered across different institutions, leaving patients with no central access and doctors with incomplete medical histories.

> Privacy that disguises itself

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SafeMask helps you stay private by hiding your real crypto wallet inside an app that looks completely normal. It keeps your money out of sight so no one can judge, question, or pressure you if they happen to check your phone. With things like a decoy wallet and hidden balances, you can use crypto anywhere without feeling watched or unsafe. It’s simply a calmer, safer way to manage your money.

**Challenges we ran into**

I ran into a few hurdles while building SafeMask. The first was getting the hidden/decoy mode to work without crashing, so I separated the fake UI from the real wallet logic and loaded it only after the secret gesture. Fetching real on-chain balances across multiple networks was also tricky because RPCs would sometimes fail, so I added retries and fallback providers to make it stable. Managing seed phrases safely inside a disguised app was another challenge, which I solved by encrypting everything and never storing anything in plain text. And keeping the CI/CD pipeline running smoothly took time tests would break often because of small changes so I added automated checks and cleanup scripts to keep builds consistent. Together, these fixes made the whole system more reliable and secure.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

SafeMask supports Aztec and Zcash and can implement bi-directional private bridging using efficient note constructs and optional viewing keys for auditability.

Key features:
* Aztec + ZEC support and private bridging primitives
* Partial notes and MPC/EigenLayer AVS options for security
* Optional viewing keys for compliance auditing

**Private DeFi & Trading**

SafeMask can provide private collateral management, range proofs, and private yield mechanisms to enable a ZEC-backed stablecoin on Aztec.

Key features:
* Private collateral tracking and range proofs
* Oracle price integration for ZEC/USD
* Private lending and liquidation flows

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

SafeMask implements Sapling-style cryptography and can extend to support PCZT, enabling T-address users to send to Z-addresses via a TypeScript library.

Key features:
* PCZT API implementation plan and TypeScript library
* Transparent → shielded transaction tooling
* Mobile-compatible Sapling wallet library

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

SafeMask integrates Osmosis and Zcash to enable private swaps, liquidity provision, and IBC-based transfers with hidden amounts.

Key features:

* OSMO + ZEC integration with private swaps
* IBC support for Cosmos transfers
* DEX integration within a privacy layer

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

SafeMask is a self-custody wallet with Osmosis support, privacy-by-default design, and strong mobile UX.

Key features:

* Self-custody with BIP39 seed phrase
* Local-only data storage, no servers
* Privacy-first transaction defaults
* Native Osmosis support with IBC

**Private Payments & Transactions**

SafeMask enables private payments on Osmosis and other chains with QR payments, NFC tap-to-pay, and zero-knowledge protection.

Key features:

* Range-proof backed private payments
* QR code and NFC payment flows
* Cross-chain settlement support

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

SafeMask delivers a multi-chain wallet toolkit built for Pump.fun devs, with smooth Solana support, Fusion swaps, and cross-chain execution.

Key features:

Deep Solana integration for fast TXs, balance reads & history

1inch Fusion swaps for efficient, gas-optimized token trades

Cross-chain flow (ETH-to-SOL and more) for seamless movement across chains

**Private DeFi & Trading**

SafeMask provides private DeFi primitives using ZEC as the privacy anchor for swaps, lending, and liquidity across multiple chains.

Key features:

* ZEC-powered private DeFi flows
* Hidden amounts and cross-chain DeFi access
* Decentralized design with production test coverage

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

SafeMask offers Sapling libraries, a mobile ZEC SDK, PCZT tooling, and circuit libraries for developer use.

Key features:

* Sapling library and mobile SDK
* Shielded transaction tooling (T → Z)
* Circuit library and documentation

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

SafeMask is a mobile-first self-custody wallet with stealth addresses, private asset management, and a streamlined UX.

Key features:

* Mobile-first app (85MB APK)
* One-tap private transactions and wallet hiding
* Multi-chain private portfolio
* BIP39 seed phrase backup

**Private DeFi & Trading**

SafeMask supports private swaps using DEX aggregators with a zero-knowledge layer that hides swap amounts while providing competitive pricing.

Key features:

* Private swaps via 1inch/0x integrations
* Cross-chain DEX aggregation with privacy layer
* Portfolio analytics without transaction exposure

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

SafeMask uses NEAR intents to enable Zcash holders to access DeFi across 12 chains privately. The cross-chain intent engine lets ZEC holders lend on Ethereum, provide liquidity on Osmosis, and swap across chains through a unified private interface.

Key features:
* NEAR Intents SDK integration for cross-chain action orchestration
* 12-chain support: ZEC → ETH, MATIC, SOL, BTC, NEAR, MINA, STRK, ARB, OP, BASE, AZTEC
* Private cross-chain swaps with zero-knowledge protection
* DeFi access: lending, staking, and liquidity provision across chains

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

SafeMask integrates NEAR AI with TEE-based inference to create an AI-powered privacy assistant. Users can instruct natural-language actions (e.g., “Donate 0.5 ZEC to education charities privately”) and the agent finds causes, routes through the shielded pool, and executes privately using NEAR TEE.

Key features:
* NEAR AI integration with TensorFlow Lite models and TEE inference
* Natural language ZEC spending and routing
* Privacy optimization based on transaction patterns
* Agentic philanthropy and preference-driven spending
* Cross-chain AI routing for optimal privacy and fees

**Private Payments & Transactions**

SafeMask enables private real-world payments using shielded ZEC and NEAR intents. Users can pay merchants, send remittances, or donate privately; NEAR intents handle cross-chain routing where needed.

Key features:
* Private QR code payments with shielded ZEC
* NEAR intent routing to merchant-preferred currencies
* NFC tap-to-pay support (Android)
* Unstoppable Domains integration for human-readable addresses
* Cross-chain settlement (ZEC → USDC/ETH)

### Fuel-On-Call

> Because every journey deserves a safe finish.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Fuel-On-Call is an emergency petrol delivery service that brings 1–3 liters of fuel directly to stranded riders using GPS-based live location tracking. Designed for safety, speed, and convenience, it helps commuters stuck on highways, rural roads, or late-night routes by providing instant fuel support with verified delivery partners and secure OTP-based handovers.

**Challenges we ran into**

Live Location Accuracy:
Getting precise GPS coordinates for stranded riders was tricky, especially in low-network or rural areas.

Real-Time Tracking Integration:
Setting up continuous location updates and syncing them smoothly with the backend caused delays.

Fuel Safety Regulations:
Understanding BIS-approved containers, transport safety rules, and legal restrictions required deep research.

User Verification & Security:
Implementing OTP verification and making sure both rider and delivery partner identities were safe and authentic took extra effort.

Choosing the Right Tech Stack:
Balancing between Firebase, Node.js, Google Maps API, and real-time databases needed multiple iterations.

UI/UX Complexity:
Designing a simple, emergency-friendly interface that even a panicked user can use was more challenging than expected.

Service Model Logistics:
Planning how delivery partners reach remote locations quickly and defining coverage areas required a lot of thought.

Night-time Safety Concerns:
Ensuring safe delivery operations during late hours, especially for women riders, needed additional features and protocols.

### Zeus-Cont
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeuscont-da5d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vorsv/Zeus-Cont) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](http://zeus.xenopent.tech/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/IMjWdcQLZTU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-9-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Less Weighing Collaborative Malware Analysis Env.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Analyzing a virus or "malware" is usually a slow, dangerous, and complicated process. Zeus-Cont makes
  it fast, safe, and easy for everyone.

  1. It creates a "Digital Cage" for Viruses
   * The Problem: You can’t just open a suspicious file on your laptop to see what it does—it could steal
     your data or break your computer.
   * Our Solution: We provide a safe, isolated container (a "sandbox"). You can run the virus inside this
     cage, and it can’t escape to hurt your actual computer or the internet.

  2. It Translates "Matrix Code" into Plain English
   * The Problem: Malware generates thousands of lines of confusing technical logs. It takes a human
     hours to read through them all.
   * Our Solution: We use Gemini AI to read all that "boring" data for you. In seconds, it writes a
     simple report explaining exactly what the virus was trying to do.

  3. It’s a "GPS" for Security Training
   * The Problem: Most hacking tools are very intimidating and hard to learn.
   * Our Solution: We integrated a Voice Assistant (using Sarvam AI). It actually talks to you and guides
     you through the app, making advanced security research as easy as following a GPS.

  4. No More Working Alone
   * The Problem: Usually, security experts work in silos. If they find something, they have to take
     screenshots and send emails.
   * Our Solution: Our platform is collaborative. Multiple people can jump into the same session to hunt
     a threat together in real-time, just like a shared Google Doc.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Container Orchestration: Making the backend "talk" to Docker to create and destroy isolated sandboxes on demand.
2. Network Isolation: Building a "fake internet" so malware stays trapped but still tries to execute its code.
3. Real-Time Streaming: Pushing file, network, and process events to the browser instantly without any lag.
4. Noise Reduction: Automatically hiding normal system processes so the analyst only sees the malicious activity.
5. AI Data Management: Condensing thousands of raw log lines so Gemini can generate a smart, human-readable report.
6. Forensic Tooling: Packaging heavy-duty security tools (like Radare2 and Volatility) into a lightweight, fast-loading image.

**Gemini**

The Gemini API is the project's "Intelligence Layer." While the sandbox and C agent collect raw data, Gemini acts as the Senior Malware Researcher who interprets that data.

  Its involvement is broken down into three key roles:

  1. Automated Forensic Synthesis
  The most significant involvement is in the Report Generation Engine. When an analyst finishes a session, the backend sends a massive volume of telemetry logs (Process trees, File changes, Network packets) to
  Gemini. 
   * The Task: Gemini parses thousands of lines of raw logs into a structured, professional ANY.RUN-style Malware Analysis Report.
   * The Value: It saves analysts hours of manual work by identifying the "needle in the haystack"—such as distinguishing a normal system file edit from a malicious persistence attempt.

  2. Contextual Intelligence & IOC Extraction
  Gemini is used to identify and categorize Indicators of Compromise (IOCs). It scans the telemetry to extract:
   * Malicious Hashes: Identifying suspicious files dropped during execution.
   * C2 Infrastructure: Spotting Command & Control domains or IP addresses hidden in network traffic.
   * Threat Scoring: Based on the activity patterns, Gemini calculates a "Threat Score" (0-100), helping the analyst prioritize the risk level of the sample.

  3. MITRE ATT&CK Reasoning
  While the system can detect what happened, Gemini explains why it matters. It analyzes the sequences of events to confirm MITRE techniques. For example, if it sees a process modifying ~/.bashrc, Gemini maps
  this to T1546.004 (Persistence via Unix Shell Configuration), providing the technical rationale for why that specific action is a security risk.

  Technical Implementation Details:
   * Models Used: Optimized for gemini-2.0-flash for high-speed analysis and long context windows (to handle large log files).
   * Prompt Engineering: Uses a high-precision system prompt with explicit rules to ensure reports are professional, monochromatic, and free of AI "hallucinations."
   * Determinism: Set to a very low temperature (0.1) to ensure that the same malware activity always results in the same technical conclusion.

**Sarvam.ai**

The Sarvam API serves as the "Voice of Zeus," providing the narrative layer for the platform's onboarding and tactical guidance. While the Gemini API handles the "brain" (logic and reporting), Sarvam provides
  the "voice" (audio and communication).

  Its specific involvement includes:

  1. Indic-Specific Tactical Assistance
  The project uses Sarvam’s Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities (specifically the bulbul:v3 model) to provide a localized, natural-sounding audio guide. 
   * The Persona: It powers the "Zeus Tactical Assistant," which speaks to the analyst in high-fidelity Indian dialects/accents.
   * The Goal: This makes the platform more accessible and provides a modern "Mission Control" feel, where the system talks to you while you perform high-stakes analysis.

  2. Interactive Guided Onboarding (Walkthrough)
  The Walkthrough Application is entirely driven by Sarvam. As the user moves through the platform's different zones (Terminal, Telemetry, Intel Column), Sarvam generates real-time audio instructions:
   * It explains complex cybersecurity concepts (like MITRE mapping) through spoken word.
   * It reduces the cognitive load on the analyst, allowing them to keep their eyes on the telemetry feeds while receiving audio cues about the environment.

  3. Real-Time Instruction Proxy
  Technically, the project implements a FastAPI Proxy for Sarvam to ensure security and performance:
   * Security: The API keys are kept on the server side, preventing exposure in the frontend.
   * Speed: It uses Sarvam's low-latency endpoints to ensure that when an analyst clicks "Next" in the walkthrough, the audio response is nearly instantaneous.
   * Hybrid Fallback: The system is designed to check for Sarvam’s availability and fallback to standard Web Speech APIs if the network is disconnected, ensuring the "Assistant" never goes silent.

**CyberSecurity**

Zeus-Cont is a modular Dynamic Malware Analysis Sandbox designed for high-performance threat research. It maps directly to several critical cybersecurity operations:

   1. Isolated Threat Detonation (Sandboxing): The core of the project is the secure execution of suspicious binaries. By using Docker-based isolation and a custom "Fake Internet" gateway, analysts can observe
      malware behavior in a 100% contained environment, preventing any risk to the host system or external networks.
   2. Advanced Behavioral Telemetry: Unlike static analysis, Zeus-Cont captures real-time system behavior. This includes:
       * Process Tree Visualization: Identifying process hollowing, spawning chains, and stealthy execution patterns.
       * Network Forensics: Monitoring DNS queries and C2 (Command & Control) callbacks to identify malicious infrastructure.
       * File System Auditing: Detecting unauthorized modifications to sensitive system configurations.
   3. Framework Alignment (MITRE ATT&CK): The project integrates a real-time mapping system that translates technical telemetry into standardized tactics (e.g., Discovery, Persistence, Exfiltration). This aligns
      analysis with global industry standards used by SOC (Security Operations Center) teams.
   4. Collaborative Incident Response: By supporting multi-user shared sessions and synchronized terminals, the project facilitates collaborative threat hunting. This mirrors modern "War Room" scenarios where
      multiple researchers must coordinate to dissect a high-priority threat.
   5. AI-Augmented Forensics: Through Gemini AI integration, the platform automates the generation of structured forensic reports. This solves the "Documentation Gap" in cybersecurity, allowing analysts to move
      from detection to mitigation significantly faster.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**
Imagine you want to send $5 to a friend using crypto.
First, you're told to write down 12 random words and store them somewhere safe forever. Then you're told you need to buy a separate token just to pay for the transaction. Then the app crashes.
Your friend never got the $5. You never came back.
**This is the reality for every new user entering Web3 today. **The technology is powerful, but the experience is broken. Wallets feel like they were built for engineers, not people.

**Lazorkit flips this.**
You open the app. You use Face ID. You're in — with a real Solana wallet, no seed phrase, no gas fees, no confusion.
Sending crypto feels like sending a Venmo payment. Your balance is right there. You pick a token, enter an amount, hit send. Done. The fee? We cover it.

This is what Lazorkit is built for **making blockchain invisible, so the experience is all that's left.**
Developers get a production-ready starting point. Users get something they'll actually use twice.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Gasless Transactions Were Lying to Us**
SOL transfers worked. USDC didn't. Same code, different token — no useful error. After hours of logging raw transaction bytes, we found the paymaster expected a specific account ordering in the instruction that our ATA derivation wasn't producing. One reordering. Fixed.

**The Wallet Would Forget Who You Were**
Refresh the page and the app would sometimes boot you back to login — not because you were logged out, but because AuthGuard was checking connection state before the SDK finished rehydrating the session. Classic race condition. Fixed by adding an isReconnecting flag that makes the guard wait before making any routing decision.

**Devnet RPC Has Trust Issues**
getBalance succeeds. getSignaturesForAddress times out. On the same connection. We stopped trusting RPC to be consistent and added retry logic with exponential backoff — plus decoupled balance and history fetching so one failure doesn't nuke the whole dashboard.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. ENS Privacy Leak (Critical)
**The Problem:**  
Early in development, our mentors pointed out a major flaw: resolving `bob.phoneno.eth` returned his main wallet address directly. This meant anyone could view his entire transaction history on Etherscan. **We were doxxing users by design.**

**The Solution:**  
We built a **Privacy Forwarding Contract**.
- Users deploy a lightweight forwarder contract.
- ENS records point to the *contract address*, not the main wallet.
- Funds received auto-sweep to the main wallet internally.
- **Result:** Public sees only the contract. Main wallet stays hidden.

---

## 2. x402 Payment Interception
**The Problem:**  
Integrating HeyElsa's x402 API wasn't just a normal HTTP request. Every call returned `HTTP 402 Payment Required`. Our initial code crashed because it didn't know how to sign and attach the USDC payment proof automatically.

**The Solution:**  
We wrote a custom **axios interceptor** using `viem`:
- Detects 402 responses.
- Parses payment requirements (amount, recipient).
- Signs payment locally with user's wallet.
- Retries request with `X-Payment-Token` header.
- **Result:** Seamless micropayments ($0.001 per data call) without user friction.

---

## 3. Network Mismatch Errors
**The Problem:**  
During testing, transactions failed with:  
`Error: network changed: 1 => 11155111`  
The wallet was on Mainnet, but our agent tried to execute on Sepolia/Base. Ethers.js refused to sign across mismatched networks.

**The Solution:**  
Added a **network validation hook** before execution:
- Checks current wallet chain ID.
- Prompts user to switch networks if mismatched.
- Forces provider alignment before signing.
- **Result:** Reliable execution across multiple chains.

---

## 4. AI Agent Decision Making
**The Problem:**  
Our first version used hard-coded rules for route selection. It wasn't actually using OpenClaw/AI. We risked missing the HeyElsa bounty criteria.

**The Solution:**  
Refactored the orchestrator to call `agent.execute()`:
- Sends route options to OpenClaw.
- AI analyzes gas, speed, and security.
- Returns structured recommendation with reasoning.
- **Result:** Genuine AI-powered routing, not just scripted logic.

# How TapOut Fits With ENS

## The Core Insight

**ENS is not just a naming service. It's a decentralized preference layer.**

Most projects use ENS as a "pretty wallet address." TapOut uses ENS as **user-controlled payment configuration that travels with your identity everywhere.**

## ENS Features We Use

| ENS Feature | Standard Use | TapOut's Use |
|-------------|--------------|--------------|
| **Primary Name** | vitalk.eth → 0x... | +91-9876543210.phoneno.eth → identity |
| **Text Records** | Twitter, GitHub, Avatar | Payment preferences (chain, token, gas) |
| **Multichain Addresses** | Store addresses per chain | Privacy forwarder contracts per chain |
| **Reverse Resolution** | Address → ENS name | Verify sender identity automatically |

| **One identity for everything** | Same ENS for friends, business, public → No context separation |
| **Phone numbers aren't native** | Crypto uses 0x addresses. Normal people use phone numbers. |

**We solved all three.**

### 2. Sub Domain (Context-Separated Identities)
### 3. ENS for Wallet Address (Privacy-Forwarding)

## The Problem We're Solving for HeyElsa

**Most "AI + Crypto" projects are fake:**
- Chatbots that don't execute transactions

## How We Use x402 (Micropayments)

### Every AI Data Call Pays via x402

| Data Call | Endpoint | Cost | Payment Method |
|-----------|----------|------|----------------|
| Chainlink Price | `/api/get_token_price` | $0.002 | x402 USDC on Base |
| Pyth Price | `/api/get_token_price` | $0.002 | x402 USDC on Base |
| Gas Prices | `/api/get_gas_prices` | $0.001 | x402 USDC on Base |
| Swap Quote | `/api/get_swap_quote` | $0.01 | x402 USDC on Base |
| Transaction Status | `/api/get_transaction_status` | $0.001 | x402 USDC on Base |

**Total per transaction: ~$0.015 USDC**

## How We Use OpenClaw Skills 

## OpenClaw Agent Flow:

1. **User initiates payment**  
   → `"Send $20 to +91-98765-43210.phoneno.eth"`

2. **OpenClaw agent activates**  
   → Connects to gateway: `ws://127.0.0.1:18789/gateway`

3. **Agent calls tools (with x402 payments)**  
   → `resolve_ens`: Get recipient preferences  
   → `get_token_price`: Fetch 3 price feeds (x402)  
   → `get_swap_quote`: Compare routes (x402)  
   → `analyze_wallet`: Security check (x402)

4. **Agent makes decision**  
   → **Route**: Arbitrum → Base via USDC  
   → **Confidence**: 87%  
   → **Reasoning**: Lowest gas + fastest settlement

5. **User confirms → Agent executes**  
   → `execute_transfer` (optional tool, requires allowlist)

**The problem it solves**

# DeFi Automation

**Drag-and-Swap** is like Scratch for DeFi. Instead of writing code or scripts, users connect blocks to: **Monitor markets** via QuickNode streams, **Automate swaps**, **Reduce risk**, and most of all **Save time**.

It makes DeFi automation **easier**, **safer**, and **faster** by allowing agents to be built without deploying contracts or writing integrations

**Challenges we ran into**

## Conditional branching in the execution graph

We had to decide when a block’s output should trigger downstream blocks. For filters (e.g. General Filter), we only continue when passed === 'true'. For other blocks, we require a non-empty output. We also support execution handles (exec-out) where the block has no explicit output key but should still advance the flow.

We fixed it by centralizing the logic: check `passed` for conditional blocks, then require a truthy value or a valid execution handle before queuing downstream nodes.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

## Research & Documentation

We used AI mainly for research and implementation guidance. It was great for helping us look up the Uniswap and QuickNode API docs, debugging, and finding patterns for conditional branching in execution graphs.

## Uniswap Swap Integration Skill

We used the **Uniswap swap-integration skill** to implement the Swap and Get Quote blocks. The skill was super useful and made uniswap integration really easy. The skill was used when wiring the Uniswap service, building the swap block UI, and handling edge cases like Permit2 and quote expiry.

**New France Village**

DragnSwap fits New France Village because it’s a DeFi tool that makes trading automation accessible to beginner traders through a visual, no-code interface. 

It wraps complex functions into easy to digest blocks that can be put together like Scratch.mit.edu!

**Best Use of Quicknode Hyperliquid HyperCore Streams**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/95fc7d4a894945028c82457ae9881545/64a36af4-d5fc-4324-b069-1c5a4273cb3e.png)DragnSwap uses QuickNode’s Hyperliquid HyperCore Streams as the main trigger layer. 

The Hyperliquid Stream block connects to the QuickNode WebSocket and subscribes to trades, orders, book updates, TWAP, events, and writer actions. 

Filters (coin, user, side, liquidations, etc.) are applied before events reach the flow. These streams drive the rest of the agent (filters, swaps, notifications), so the app is built around QuickNode’s Hyperliquid streaming.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

![Uploading image...]()DragnSwap integrates the Uniswap Trading API into a visual agent builder. Users build flows that call the API for quotes and swaps, with blocks for Get Quote and Swap wired to the standard flow (quote → approval → swap). 

Swaps run through the connected wallet on all Uniswap supported chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, etc.).

## What can people use this system for?

This system acts as an **early warning layer for DeFi activity**, helping users and protocols identify risky behavior *before* damage occurs.

---

###  DeFi Protocol Security
- Monitor incoming transactions for abnormal patterns  
- Detect potential flash-loan abuse, whale manipulation, or liquidity attacks early  
- Reduce financial loss by responding before confirmation

###  Developers & Security Teams
- Get real-time alerts instead of manual log analysis  
- Focus on high-risk events rather than all transactions  
- Test security logic using simulated mempool behavior  

---

###  Institutional Users (Funds, DAOs)

- Make informed decisions during high-volatility events  
- Add an extra security layer without changing core contracts  

---

###  Research & Education
- Study DeFi attack patterns in a controlled environment  
- Experiment with ML-based anomaly detection  
- Understand how mempool-level behavior leads to attacks

###  How it makes existing tasks easier and safer

- **Before:**  
  Security teams react *after* an exploit is confirmed  

- **Now:**  
  Risks are flagged *before* confirmation, enabling early action  

- **Before:**  
  Rule-based alerts miss unknown attack patterns  

- **Now:**  
  Behavior-based ML detects anomalies without predefined rules  

---

###  Why this matters

- Faster response time  
- Lower financial impact  
- Better visibility into hidden risks  
- Safer DeFi ecosystem  

---

**In short:**  
> This system helps people *see risk earlier*, *act faster*, and *reduce damage* in DeFi.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

While building this project, I faced multiple real-world technical challenges across frontend, backend, and deployment. Solving them helped shape the final architecture.

---

###  Real-time Simulator Not Reflecting in UI

**Problem:**  
The simulator was running on the backend and returning `200 OK`, but no transactions appeared on the frontend.

**Root Cause:**  
The simulator was generating data asynchronously, but the frontend was not polling or reacting to state changes.

**Solution:**  
- Clearly separated **simulator control** and **data consumption**
- Added periodic polling for alerts and statistics
- Ensured simulator runs as a background async task

**Learning:**  
Real-time systems require explicit data flow; successful API calls don’t guarantee UI updates.

---

###  Deployment Issues with ML Models on Render

**Problem:**  
Backend crashed due to missing `.pkl` files and incompatible ML library versions.

**Root Cause:**  
- Model files were not committed to the repository  
- Scikit-learn version mismatch during model loading  

**Solution:**  
- Explicitly added trained model artifacts to the repo  
- Pinned exact library versions in `requirements.txt`  

**Learning:**  
ML systems are tightly coupled to their environment — reproducibility is critical.

---

###  Case-Sensitive File Path Errors (Frontend Build)

**Problem:**  
Vercel builds failed due to missing component imports that worked locally.

**Root Cause:**  
Linux-based build systems are case-sensitive, unlike Windows.

**Solution:**  
- Standardized file naming conventions  
- Renamed components to match import paths exactly  

**Learning:**  
Cross-platform builds expose hidden assumptions in local development.

---

###  Async Task Lifecycle Management

**Problem:**  
Multiple simulator loops were starting unintentionally, causing inconsistent behavior.

**Root Cause:**  
Improper global state handling in async background tasks.

**Solution:**  
- Introduced a single controlled async task  
- Used explicit start/stop state management  

**Learning:**  
Async systems need strict lifecycle control to avoid race conditions.

---

###  CORS & API Integration Issues

**Problem:**  
Frontend could not consistently communicate with the backend after deployment.

**Root Cause:**  
Environment variables and API base URLs differed between local and production.

**Solution:**  
- Centralized API configuration  
- Used environment-based URL switching  

**Learning:**  
Frontend-backend contracts must be environment-aware and consistent.

---

###  Overall Takeaway

> Most challenges were not algorithmic but **system-level** — async behavior, environment consistency, and integration boundaries.

Solving these made the project more realistic and production-oriented.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem:**
Freelancers and clients lack a reliable, trust-minimized payment system. Clients risk losing upfront payments to incomplete or delayed work, while freelancers often face payment defaults, sudden deadline changes, and client ghosting. Existing platforms solve this with centralized control, high fees, and subjective dispute resolution.

**Solution:**
TrustChain is a blockchain-based escrow platform that replaces platform trust with smart contract–enforced rules. Payments are locked on-chain and released automatically through predefined time conditions or mutual agreement, ensuring neither party can cheat unilaterally. The system is non-custodial, transparent, and integrated with MetaMask for secure DeFi payments.

**Impact:**
TrustChain reduces payment disputes, eliminates intermediaries, and lowers costs for both clients and freelancers. By enforcing fairness through code rather than human judgment, it enables faster, safer, and more confident collaboration—especially for remote and cross-border freelance work

**Challenges we ran into**

**FrontEnd** 
The layout of the webpage was difficult since we were handling both freelancers and clients. We were handling multiple cases related to the agreement. Designing the system architecture and paradigm. The connection with MetaMask was also difficult.

**Backend**
The connection of the backend and frontend was challenging. Integration of backend and frontend is very difficult. The operation is not seamless and smooth; we are still working to enhance it for a better experience. The idea was a bit broad so to implement it we had to narrow it down to single contract.

**Open Track**

The project is about Defi and Payment rails.

> Darkmode trading & payment agent

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![nestjs](https://img.shields.io/badge/nestjs-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Noir](https://img.shields.io/badge/Noir-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people who care about privacy in crypto face a bad choice: either use tools like Zcash that are hard to plug into daily trading and payments, or stay on familiar chains and give up privacy. Using shielded pools, bridges, and onchain trading together usually means juggling multiple wallets, UIs, and mental models. As a result, most users fall back to transparent wallets on public chains and hope no one is really watching.

zkPal tries to fix that. It uses Ztarknet as the execution layer and Zcash as the privacy backbone to give you one place, your own Telegram chat, where you can hold STRK, shield and unshield it, pay people, and trade, without exposing your balance and history. The problem it solves is simple: people want private day to day crypto use, but they are not going to fight five different tools to get it.

**What people can use zkPal for**

zkPal is a private trading & payment agent that plugs directly into Ztarknet and turns it into something people can use in a few taps:

• spin up a non-custodial Ztarknet wallet without dealing with dashboards, extensions, or config.
• shield and unshield STRK using Ztarknet’s connection to Zcash, without needing to understand the plumbing.
• send private payments where the sender, receiver, and amount are not exposed on a public ledger.
• do private swaps so traders and users can rebalance or trade without broadcasting their balance or strategy (In-progress).

From the user’s perspective, it feels like “a smarter, private Telegram wallet.”
Under the hood, every action is powered by Ztarknet’s execution layer and Zcash-style shielding.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into While Building zkPal**

1. Outdated Noir support on Ztarknet
The version of Noir that Ztarknet currently supports is quite old, and most of the modern documentation, examples, and libraries no longer match it. A lot of the code we wrote required trial-and-error, digging through old repos, and debugging issues that weren’t documented anywhere.

2. Field element limitations on Starknet
Starknet only supports field elements under 252 bits. But when you use hash functions like Poseidon for generating or verifying zk-proofs, the output is typically 254 bits. That mismatch forced me to rethink parts of the design and find workarounds so proof-related data could actually fit into Starknet’s constraints.

3. Handling self-custody UX (wallets, keys, privacy)
Because zkPal is fully non-custodial, I had to design a secure system for managing wallets and private keys on Telegram. Getting this right, safe, simple and private, took more time than expected, especially with no existing wallet tooling for Ztarknet to lean on.

4. The Ztarknet explorer wasn’t reliable
The block explorer was still unstable while we were building. Transactions didn't always show up correctly, indexing failed, and sometimes data was missing entirely. This made contract testing and debugging slower and more complicated.

Liam Stark

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c13192f850d54213a0c941a169c153d1/99f61969-9fd2-403f-8cd1-d4f4148a6468.png)

The Zucchini Wallet Extension addresses the common frustrations faced by Zcash users who need a seamless, browser-based way to manage their ZEC assets without compromising on privacy or usability.

Many Zcash enthusiasts struggle with the lack of dedicated browser extensions for Zcash wallets—relying instead on mobile apps, desktop clients, or built-in browser features like Brave Wallet that offer limited Zcash-specific functionality. This often leads to clunky workflows, especially for tasks like testing on the Zcash testnet, where support is inconsistent across wallets (e.g., YWallet may not fully support testnet, and others require complex setups). Additionally, syncing issues plague many existing Zcash wallets, with users reporting hours or even days of delays due to shielded transaction backlogs, network load, or inefficient data handling.

Zucchini solves these by providing:
- **Instant access in your browser sidebar**: Persist your wallet across tabs without obstructing your workflow, making it easier to send, receive, and swap ZEC on the go.
- **Built-in testnet support**: Seamlessly switch to testnet for development and experimentation, avoiding the pitfalls of wallets that lack this feature or require manual configurations.
- **Fast, reliable syncing**: Leverage optimized light-client technology to sync in minutes, not hours, even for shielded balances—bypassing common "data pileup" problems in other wallets.
- **Effortless shielded address generation**: Create privacy-focused z-addresses tied directly to your wallet using integrated tools inspired by Rust crates like `zcash_client_backend` and JS SDKs, without needing external repos or coding knowledge.
- **Secure cross-currency swaps**: Swap ZEC to any other currency (or vice versa) directly within the extension, enhancing safety by keeping everything self-custodial and reducing exposure to centralized exchanges.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c13192f850d54213a0c941a169c153d1/ba8b5d6f-22e3-4b85-8f62-e5e52a9f2f9e.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c13192f850d54213a0c941a169c153d1/296ceffc-10e3-4026-84aa-1dbfa0541f38.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c13192f850d54213a0c941a169c153d1/12d011dc-9c5f-4686-b988-65278e95674e.png)



Whether you're a developer testing shielded transactions, a privacy advocate managing daily ZEC use, or someone tired of slow syncing and fragmented tools, Zucchini makes Zcash more accessible, faster, and safer right from your browser.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c13192f850d54213a0c941a169c153d1/0a91fa63-03d9-44a0-890e-c812cde1e696.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a fully functional, non-custodial Zcash wallet extension in the browser came with several significant technical hurdles:

1. WASM & Manifest V3 Compatibility
One of the biggest challenges was integrating the Zcash Rust libraries (librustzcash) into a Manifest V3 extension. MV3 enforces a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) that disallows remote code and restricts how WASM is loaded.

Hurdle: Getting the WASM binary to load correctly within the service worker and UI contexts without violating CSP.
Solution: We utilized WXT and Vite with specific plugins (vite-plugin-wasm, vite-plugin-top-level-await) to bundle the WASM correctly and configured the build to be compatible with the extension's sandbox environment.
2. Complex State Synchronization
The wallet architecture involves multiple isolated contexts: the DApp (web page), Content Script, Background Service Worker, Side Panel UI, and a Web Worker for heavy cryptography.

Hurdle: Keeping the wallet state (balance, sync status, pending requests) synchronized across all these layers in real-time.
Solution: We implemented a robust Message Passing architecture and used chrome.storage.local as a reactive source of truth. We also built a custom hook system in React to listen for storage changes and update the UI instantly.
3. The "Account Not Found" Race Condition
We encountered a critical bug where the wallet would sometimes fail to find the account immediately after creation, causing connection failures.

Hurdle: The Web Worker was initializing or resetting its in-memory state before the IndexedDB persistence layer had fully committed the new account data.
Solution: We refactored the initialization flow to enforce an atomic save operation immediately after account creation and added a post-creation verification step in the worker to ensure the account ID was valid and persisted before allowing any further interactions.
4. Designing for the Side Panel
Moving away from the traditional "Popup" wallet experience to a persistent Side Panel required a shift in UX thinking.

Hurdle: Handling connection requests gracefully without blocking the user's browsing experience.
Solution: We implemented a Badge Notification system on the extension icon and a dedicated "Connection Request" view that automatically activates when the user opens the panel, ensuring a seamless flow between the DApp and the Wallet.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional digital certificates have long been plagued by serious flaws—they are easy to forge, hard to verify quickly, and lack mechanisms to prevent tampering. This creates ongoing frustrations for educational institutions, employers, and learners alike, who face fake credentials, slow verification, and limited cross-border validation. Our blockchain-powered Web3 learning platform revolutionizes certificate management by making credentials immutable, instantly verifiable, and virtually fraud-proof. For learners, it means tamper-proof certificates recorded permanently on Ethereum that can be verified by employers worldwide in seconds. Educators gain the ability to issue cryptographically secured certificates with strict authorization controls, drastically reducing forgery risks and administrative overhead. Employers benefit from one-click verification, eliminating the need to contact institutions or rely on insecure PDFs. More broadly, this creates a decentralized credential ecosystem powered by Ethereum’s immutable ledger and advanced cryptographic techniques, fostering trustless, global interoperability of learning achievements and credentials

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, several challenges arose that were tackled with effective solutions. The first challenge involved certificate generation failing due to limitations in encoding complex SVG templates with the btoa() function. This was resolved by switching to an HTML5 Canvas API-based renderer that is more robust, coupled with comprehensive error handling and fallback mechanisms to maintain reliability. Another challenge was large bundle sizes impacting performance in production, which was fixed by optimizing the Vite build configuration through manual code splitting, better vendor chunk management, and environment-based build optimizations tailored for Netlify deployment. Managing state across multiple certificate tabs (Generator, Verifier, Quests, Gallery) required a modular component design using React hooks for isolated state per tab, alongside reusable UI components from shadcn/ui to ensure a consistent user interface. To simulate Web3 functionality during development without actual blockchain integration, a realistic mock system was built for wallet connection, transaction loading states, and certificate creation with embedded steganographic messages. Finally, deployment was streamlined by configuring SPA routing with proper redirect rules and fallback settings in Netlify’s config, ensuring smooth user navigation post-deployment. These experiences reinforced the importance of robust error handling, progressive enhancement, and resilient systems that handle edge cases gracefully while delivering excellent user experiences

**Ethereum Track**

This project demonstrates a comprehensive and secure Ethereum-based certificate system built with production-ready smart contracts following best practices such as ownership-based access control, robust input validation, and certificate uniqueness safeguards. It ensures anti-tampering through immutable on-chain storage, decentralized IPFS document hosting, steganographic security, and cryptographic hashing to prevent forgery. The system’s decentralized trust model eliminates any central authority, offering transparent on-chain verification and an immutable audit trail for certificate events. Integrated seamlessly with Web3 tools like MetaMask and employing a multi-layered security design, this project showcases real-world, enterprise-grade security for educational certificates and exemplifies the Ethereum track's focus on smart contract development, decentralized storage, and innovative blockchain verification, all live on the project link

> there is no bridge, i love you

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keccak256](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keccak256-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![EIP-4788](https://img.shields.io/badge/EIP--4788-333333?style=flat-square) ![SSZ](https://img.shields.io/badge/SSZ-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most cross-chain applications still rely on relayers, bridges, or oracle networks to tell one chain what happened on another. **Anyware** removes that trust assumption.

Using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788) beacon roots, it allows EVM networks to verify recent Ethereum state directly onchain through cryptographic proofs instead of externally signed messages.

**The demo use case is exploring trustless lending:**
1. a user locks ETH on Ethereum Sepolia
2. a proof of that vault state is generated
3. Base Sepolia verifies the proof onchain
4. demo USDC is issued without trusting a bridge or relayer

**The same primitive can power:**
cross-chain lending | governance verification | proof-of-reserves | attestations | generalized Ethereum state reads

**Challenges we ran into**

A major hurdle was proving that an execution payload header truly belonged to a beacon block trusted through [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788), while also resolving the correct destination-chain beacon-root timestamp window.

**We solved this by building a prover pipeline that:**
1. scans beacon blocks
2. matches execution payloads
3. constructs SSZ inclusion proofs
4. resolves the correct EIP-4788 anchor timestamp for onchain verification

**Ethereum Core**

Anyware builds directly on top of Ethereum consensus infrastructure using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788).

We demonstrate via PoC how Ethereum beacon roots can become a native trust anchor for cross-chain verification without relying on bridges, relayers, or oracle committees.

**It combines:** EIP-4788 beacon roots | SSZ verification | execution state proofs | Ethereum Merkle-Patricia Trie verification; into a working trust-minimized interoperability primitive.

**Anyware improves:** security by reducing external trust assumptions, transparency through fully onchain verification, and interoperability across EVM networks.

**Network Economy**

Anyware enables trustless cross-chain economic interactions without relying on bridges, relayers, or oracle networks.
Using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788), the project allows EVM networks to verify Ethereum state directly through cryptographic proofs anchored to Ethereum consensus.

**The demo shows this through cross-chain lending:**
1. a user locks ETH on Ethereum
2. another chain verifies that state onchain
3. credit is issued without trusting an intermediary


**Our library enabled developers to explore use-cases like:**
- cross-chain lending
- proof-of-reserves
- governance verification
- attestations and reputation
- shared liquidity systems

The project puts user control and protocol-level verification first by replacing externally trusted middleware with direct onchain proof verification.

### PoisonGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/poisonguard-c32b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/cybersecurity-three-engineers) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/-wVVMq83cjA?feature=share) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> cybersecurity+AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Several Companies are integrating their websites with chatbots, that are built on a RAG pipeline. RAG pipelines often use external documents to produce resources for the chatbot to supply the user answers. When a user asks a chatbot for an image, the chatbot tests the metadata against the user's request to give an output. Attackers can take advantage of this and edit the metadata using misaligned information, hence providing the user with a variation of the request. Our PoisonGuard aims to solve this very problem by comparing the metadata of the image to the description of the image produced by an LLM. If there's an anomaly the answer is withheld from the user thereby preventing the user from getting misinformation.

**Challenges we ran into**

We got inspiration for our idea, from a research paper published in the month of February, 2026. Considering the novelty of the paper we ran into trouble finding trustworthy dataset as well as getting a clear idea of the workflow.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Our project focuses on protecting the LLM output, by removing the poisoned documents while retrieving the documents through RAG pipeline. We trained our own ML model that was able to detect whether the document was poisoned (attacker changed the metadata) or not, based on the title and description of the image.
