### Base Analytics
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/base-analytics-86fc) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://base-analytics-app.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Student%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-student-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Base Analytics is the ultimate reputation protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Alchemy API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Alchemy%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![Coinbase Onchainkit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Coinbase%20Onchainkit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Farcaster Frames v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Farcaster%20Frames%20v2-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Base ecosystem is exploding, but the tools to navigate it are fundamentally fractured. Right now, Web3 power users and builders are forced to juggle multiple disconnected platforms just to get a clear picture of what is actually happening onchain.

Base Analytics solves three critical pain points in the current Web3 landscape:

1. The Fragmentation of Social and Financial Data
Currently, financial data (token prices, volume) lives on heavy trading terminals, while social signal and reputation data live separately on Farcaster. There is no unified command center that links the Base financial ecosystem with decentralized social identity. Users have to switch between tabs and apps to connect the dots.

2. The Noise-to-Signal Ratio
The Base network never sleeps. Humans cannot manually monitor real-time token shifts, protocol updates, and social sentiment 24/7. Users constantly miss critical ecosystem movements and alpha because they simply have to step away from their screens.

3. Opaque Decentralized Reputation
Farcaster is the heartbeat of Web3 social, and reputation metrics dictate visibility, trust, and airdrop eligibility. Yet, the average user has no clean, accessible way to visualize their actual on-chain social quotient, Neynar score, or Ethos credentials without querying raw APIs themselves.

The Solution:
Base Analytics acts as the ultimate autonomous command center. We bridge the gap by providing a unified dashboard where users can instantly track top BASE network assets while simultaneously visualizing their exact Farcaster reputation. To solve the attention problem, we deployed an autonomous AI agent that ingests raw market data, synthesizes the noise, and broadcasts native ecosystem insights every 6 hours—completely removing the need for manual monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an autonomous, real-time command center for the Base ecosystem sounded straightforward on paper, but wiring together decentralized social protocols, live financial data, and AI agents introduced several major hurdles:

1. The Web2 API Paywall & The Farcaster Pivot
Our original architecture had the AI Agent broadcasting its Base market insights to X (Twitter). However, we immediately ran into X's newly enforced, strict 402 Payment Required API paywall, which blocks automated posting for free-tier developer accounts. Instead of fighting Web2 infrastructure, we executed a hard pivot to Web3. We re-engineered the agent's voice to cast natively directly to Warpcast using a Neynar Signer UUID. This not only bypassed the paywall but actually resulted in a much better product—keeping the agent entirely native to the Base and Farcaster ecosystem.

2. LLM Cost Optimization & Compatibility Routing
Running an autonomous agent that fires every 6 hours can get expensive quickly. We initially built the agent's "brain" using the OpenAI SDK (gpt-4o-mini). When we ran into API billing constraints, we engineered a clever routing workaround. Instead of rewriting the entire AI logic, we utilized Google's Gemini API Compatibility Mode. By simply swapping the base URL and pointing the existing OpenAI SDK to gemini-2.5-flash, we kept the agent lightning-fast and highly capable while dropping our inference costs to zero.

3. Securing the Autonomous Cron Job
Because our AI agent lives on a Next.js serverless API route, we faced the challenge of preventing random users (or malicious bots) from finding the endpoint and spamming the Farcaster timeline. We solved this by implementing a strict verification handshake. The route now checks for a specific, heavily encrypted CRON_SECRET Bearer token that is only known to the secure Vercel Cron server, ensuring the agent only wakes up exactly when it is scheduled to.

4. Taming Live Financial Data with Strict TypeScript
Ingesting live market data from CoinGecko meant dealing with highly dynamic, constantly changing JSON objects. Early on, this caused our Next.js build to fail due to strict ESLint rules rejecting any types. We had to architect custom, strict TypeScript interfaces (CoinMarketData) to define the exact shape of the incoming Base token data, ensuring the app was completely type-safe from the initial data fetch all the way to the final AI prompt.

> Multi-collection NFT battle game on Base - any NFT

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## About
NFT Battle Arena is a cross-collection NFT battle game on Base where any NFT from any collection becomes a playable fighter with real combat utility.

V2 brings strategic depth: players build full loadouts — pick a Fighter, equip an Item buff, and choose an Arena modifier — creating thousands of tactical combinations. Your entire wallet inventory is scanned for team synergies, rewarding long-term collectors with passive stat boosts.

All PvP matches are cryptographically secured. Players authenticate via SIWE (Sign-In with Ethereum), and combat is resolved entirely server-side using Vercel KV with atomic operations. A custom seeded PRNG engine (mulberry32 + FNV-1a hashing) ensures every battle is 100% deterministic and reproducible for replays and anti-cheat verification.

Key features:
• Universal stat normalization across 12+ Base NFT collections
• Multi-NFT loadouts (Fighter + Item + Arena) with diminishing returns
• 5 passive abilities with cooldown-based trigger systems
• Cinematic battle renderer with particles, screen shake, and damage numbers
• Server-authoritative PvP with SIWE + JWT authentication
• Deterministic seeded PRNG for reproducible battle outcomes
• Anti-drift snapshot hashing (SHA-256) for mutable NFT protection
• Live balance configuration via CDN for real-time meta-tuning
• V2 analytics pipeline tracking loadouts, battles, and results
• Farcaster and Base Mini App native integration


## The Problem it Solves
Most NFT collections become static PFPs with zero utility after minting. NFT Battle Arena solves this by giving every NFT on Base real combat utility through metadata normalization — no matter the collection, no matter the traits.

V2 goes further by solving three critical problems:

1. Single-NFT Boredom: Players now deploy full strategic loadouts (Fighter + Item + Arena), making every battle a tactical decision rather than a coin flip.

2. Client-Side Cheating: All PvP combat is resolved server-side via Vercel Serverless Functions. Players authenticate with SIWE, stats are snapshot-hashed at challenge time, and battles run on a deterministic seeded PRNG — making manipulation impossible.

3. Balance Stagnation: A live balance config system fetches stat cap overrides from a CDN, allowing real-time meta-tuning without redeployment. No more waiting for a code push to fix a broken build.

**Challenges we ran into**

• Metadata normalization across 12+ collections with wildly different trait structures — each collection needed custom mapping logic while keeping the system extensible via a data-driven collection profiles architecture.

• Balancing combat stats so no single collection dominates — implemented stat caps, floors, diminishing returns on buff layers (Items: 100%, Arena: 80%, Team: 60%), and configurable guardrails.

• Making battles feel cinematic in vanilla JavaScript without heavy game engines — built a custom animation system with CSS keyframes for screen shake, crit bursts, dodge ghosts, floating damage numbers, and particle effects.

• Deterministic replay system — implemented a seeded PRNG (mulberry32 + FNV-1a) to ensure the same battle inputs always produce identical outputs for server-side verification and future spectator mode.

• Server-side PvP without WebSockets — built an atomic challenge/fight system using Vercel KV hash operations to prevent race conditions during concurrent challenge acceptance.

• SIWE authentication flow — integrated Sign-In with Ethereum using the `siwe` npm package with `jose` JWT tokens (1h expiry, 5min nonce TTL) for stateless, secure API authentication.

• Browser compatibility — replaced Node.js crypto with Web Crypto API (SHA-256) for stat snapshots, and handled Farcaster miniapp connector nuances across Base and Warpcast hosts.

### AgentBazaar
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agentbazaar-3189) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ritiklakhwani/agent-marketplace) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agentbazaar.oceandev.xyz/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/srJ5h69g1Bw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> From prompt to portfolio, bridged cross-chain.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most AI agent marketplaces are glorified chatbots. They return text. They do not hold money, do not compose across agents, and cannot be held accountable when they are wrong. A portfolio rebalance becomes a ChatGPT screenshot, not a filled position. A cross-border payment stays a conversation, not USDC landing on another chain.

AgentBazaar replaces that pattern with a real marketplace where agents bid, pay each other, settle on-chain, and are insured against failure.

What you can do today
Rebalance a portfolio in one prompt. "Maintain 40% AAPL, 30% TSLA, 30% NVDA with $500." A Router LLM parses intent. Two Portfolio Agents compete in a live Dutch auction streamed over SSE. The winner hires an Oracle agent for Pyth-style prices and a Swap agent for each trade leg. Every call is paid in real USDC over x402 on Solana.

Move USDC cross-chain without wrapped tokens. Circle CCTP V2 runs in both directions. Arc testnet to Solana funds the user's wallet, and Solana to Ethereum Sepolia sends the remittance. Native burn and mint, no IOU tokens.

Buy insurance on agent failure. A 0.5% premium routes the task to a lower-reputation agent. If they fail, a Solana Anchor program refunds the user's ATA automatically and slashes that agent's on-chain reputation.

Why it's safer than anything else in this category
Every payment is a signed SPL transfer, so Solana Explorer shows exactly where every USDC went, per edge.

Reputation lives on-chain (Anchor Registry program), so winner picks are explainable by a simple fee ÷ reputation formula.

Delegation is explicit and capped. The user approves 20 USDC once. The marketplace cannot spend more, cannot spend from any other mint, and cannot drift to mainnet by accident.

Failures are priced, not unknown. The Insurance program makes bad agents pay for being bad, programmatically.

Why it composes
Every agent route is a tiny microservice behind the same x402 middleware. Swap out our Oracle or Swap for any third party that accepts a signed X-PAYMENT header and the marketplace keeps working. The whole thing is an open protocol dressed up as a product.

Where it goes next
V1 swaps mock stock mints for real Backed xStocks via Jupiter, adds a fiat offramp via Dodo Payments for INR settlement, and moves x402 to a per-task user-signed model. The pattern (compose, pay, reputation-gate, insure) generalizes to any marketplace of specialist agents.

**Challenges we ran into**

The single hardest thing was getting Circle CCTP V2's receive_message working on Solana devnet end-to-end for the Fund-from-Arc flow. It is the flow that qualifies us for the Circle track, and Circle's Solana side programs (CCTPV2Sm4AdWt5296sk4P66VBZ7bEhcARwFaaS9YPbeC and CCTPV2vPZJS2u2BBsUoscuikbYjnpFmbFsvVuJdgUMQe) had essentially no TypeScript reference for the EVM to Solana direction. We had to reverse engineer the account order and PDA seed encoding from live on-chain data. Four separate traps, each one ate a demo-day hour.

1. The used_nonce PDA seeds changed between V1 and V2
Our first guess, by analogy to V1, was ["used_message", source_domain_BE, nonce]. It failed with AnchorError: ConstraintSeeds. The actual V2 seeds are [b"used_nonce", nonce_32_bytes]. The prefix string changed, and source_domain is not a seed at all.

2. remote_token_messenger and token_pair use ASCII-encoded domains
We initially encoded source_domain as a 4-byte big-endian u32 (the standard Rust to_be_bytes() convention). It failed with AccountNotInitialized. On-chain inspection revealed that Circle encodes the domain as ASCII bytes. Domain 26 becomes [0x32, 0x36] (the string "26"), not [0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x1A]. That choice is not documented anywhere we could find.

3. V2 added a fee_recipient_token_account that every V1 example is missing
CCTP V2 inserted a new account slot between token_pair and recipient_ata in the remaining_accounts forwarded to handle_receive_finalized_message. V1 did not have it, so every reference implementation online was silently wrong. Worse, the fee recipient's pubkey is not a well-known constant. It is stored inside the token_messenger account at byte offset 109 (after owner, pending_owner, paused_by, a u32 version field, and a u8 bump). We wrote a small Node script that walked byte offsets, called getAssociatedTokenAddress for each possible 32-byte chunk, and checked which USDC ATAs actually existed on-chain. That pinpointed the real fee_recipient in about 30 seconds. Now the route fetches token_messenger at call time and parses the layout by hand.

4. The full transaction was 66 bytes over Solana's 1232-byte limit
Combining create_ata and receive_message in one tx exceeded Solana's hard cap. We split into two transactions. An idempotent ATA creation first, then receive_message alone. Only the latter is the real mint, so the user still sees a single on-chain mint event.

The meta-lesson
Six failed attempts burned around 15 USDC on Arc before we got it right. Each iteration was a real on-chain burn that cannot be "un-burned". But the reverse engineering pattern we developed is transferable. Fetch a known-good account, diff its byte layout against what Anchor expects, and iterate on the Anchor error codes until every constraint validates. That pattern is what turned a flow we thought would never ship into the cleanest segment of our demo.

This is the only Arc and Solana CCTP V2 cross-chain flow we have found running end-to-end on a hackathon project in this cycle. It is also why the Circle track qualifier is a fully live demo rather than a bullet point on the README.

**Programmable Money for Humans & Agents**

The track asks for USDC that behaves like more than money. It asks for money that rules can be written into, by humans and by agents. AgentBazaar uses Circle CCTP V2 and Solana together to do exactly that, in both directions, with Arc as a first-class source chain.

Two CCTP V2 flows live in one codebase. The Remittance Agent burns USDC on Solana and mints on Ethereum Sepolia. A separate Fund from Arc flow burns on Circle's Arc testnet (CCTP domain 26) and mints on Solana. Arc is not a mention, it is the live qualifier running end-to-end in the submitted demo. Every mint is native USDC. There is not a single wrapped token anywhere in the flow.

Programmable money for agents. Every agent to agent call carries a signed X-PAYMENT header (x402) wrapping a real USDC SPL transfer on Solana. A rebalance fires four edges. The user pays the Portfolio agent, the Portfolio agent pays the Oracle, and the Portfolio agent pays the Swap agent three times, once per leg. Each edge is a distinct USDC transaction visible on Explorer. On top of that, an on-chain Solana Insurance program (a PDA-owned USDC vault) programmatically refunds failed agent tasks and slashes reputation in the same atomic flow. USDC here is not just transferred. It is the primary integration point for accountability.

Programmable money for humans. A single approve(delegate = marketplace, 20 USDC) lets the user authorize the marketplace to spend on their behalf. The allowance is capped, revocable, and scoped to a single mint. Every downstream agent payment shows up on Explorer as a direct user_wallet to agent_wallet transfer, not from a hidden admin key. The human signs once, and the money rules itself after.

Technical depth as qualifier. Circle's Solana side CCTP V2 programs had no published TypeScript reference for the EVM to Solana direction. We reverse engineered the PDA seeds from live on-chain data, including the ASCII encoded domain bytes, V2's new fee_recipient_token_account slot, and the used_nonce prefix change. The Arc to Solana mint working reliably is earned work, not a stub.

One USDC primitive, three chains, two user modes. Arc, Solana, and Ethereum Sepolia. Humans delegating it, agents spending it, a program refunding it. That is programmable money in the shape Circle asked for.

**Best Use of Solana**

Solana is not a deployment target for AgentBazaar. It is the substrate the whole marketplace architecture depends on. Every piece of the product leans on a primitive that Solana does better than any other chain.

Two live Anchor programs on devnet carry the accountability layer. A Registry program stores per-agent reputation in a PDA keyed by the agent's owner pubkey. Reads are free, updates are gated by a trusted signer, and the winner picker is a one-line fee ÷ reputation formula a judge can verify on Explorer. An Insurance program holds a USDC vault PDA and programmatically refunds failed tasks via CPI. Failure is priced on-chain, not handled by a backend.

SPL token delegation turns the x402 layer from an API pattern into a wallet pattern. The user signs one approve(delegate = marketplace, 20 USDC) and from that moment every agent payment shows up on Explorer as a direct user_wallet to agent_wallet transfer, not from an opaque admin key. Each agent to agent call also carries a signed X-PAYMENT header wrapping a real SPL transfer, so every edge in the composition graph is a real Solana transaction. Four agents firing in sequence produce four Explorer rows, not four mock txs.

Circle CCTP V2 on both sides uses Solana's CCTP programs natively. MessageTransmitterV2 and TokenMessengerMinterV2 are called directly to mint native USDC, with no wrapped tokens and no trust bridges. That unlocks Arc to Solana funding and Solana to Ethereum remittance inside the same UI.

Solana's real strengths are what make agent to agent commerce feasible here. The per-transaction cost is negligible, native program composability means CPI can fire the insurance refund in one instruction, and SPL semantics give us delegation, approvals, and real accounts out of the box. On an EVM chain the fee per edge would dominate the economics. On Solana it is rounding error. The auction animates at roughly 1.5 seconds per bid because Solana confirmation is that fast. We did not pick Solana and port a pattern onto it. We built a pattern Solana specifically enables.

Team **Laanu boiz** -- [ritik lakhwani](https://github.com/ritiklakhwani), [Karmanay Sharma](https://github.com/karmanayS)

> Web3 enabled supply chain surveillance.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

💊 MEDORA – AI & Blockchain-Based Medicine Supply Chain with Web3 Trading
Medora is an advanced, full-stack platform designed to revolutionize the pharmaceutical supply chain by combining AI, Blockchain, and Web3 technologies. It aims to eliminate counterfeit medicines and bring unprecedented transparency, security, and trust from production to consumption.

🌟 Core Concept
Medora creates a unified ecosystem connecting all stakeholders: Manufacturers, Distributors, Retailers, and Customers. Every medicine batch is meticulously tracked, verified, and secured, ensuring authenticity and transparency throughout its lifecycle.

✨ Key Features & Technological Realization
Medora integrates cutting-edge technologies to deliver a secure, transparent, and intelligent medicine supply chain. Here's how each core feature is realized:

🔗 Blockchain-Based Supply Chain Traceability

Description: Each medicine batch is assigned a unique ID and QR code. All critical transactions—creation, transfer between stakeholders, and verification—are immutably stored on a blockchain ledger. This guarantees tamper-proof records, full traceability, and a transparent supply chain flow from manufacturer to customer.
Technology: Smart contracts are deployed on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet, serving as the decentralized ledger for all batch transactions and ownership transfers.
🧠 AI-Powered Verification & Fraud Detection

Description: Medora utilizes Artificial Intelligence to proactively detect counterfeit medicines and flag suspicious activities within the supply chain. This includes identifying duplicate scans, inconsistent data, and unusual patterns. It also identifies high-risk geographical locations for fake drugs and predicts future medicine demand.
Technology: Leverages Gemini AI for advanced machine learning models, integrated seamlessly into the Node.js backend to analyze data, calculate authenticity scores, and provide demand predictions.
✅ Multi-Level Authenticity Verification System

Description: Users can verify medicine authenticity by scanning a QR code or manually entering a batch ID. The system then prompts users to answer a series of 3 verification questions. The backend, combined with AI analysis, validates these responses, presenting a final authenticity result (Authentic / Suspicious / Fake) with a fraud score and risk level.
Technology: The frontend (React) facilitates user interaction (QR scanning, question answering), while the Node.js backend processes requests, consults Supabase (PostgreSQL) for batch data, and communicates with the Gemini AI service for final validation.
💬 End-to-End Encrypted Chat System

Description: Facilitates secure, real-time communication between authorized stakeholders (e.g., Distributor ↔ Retailer). This E2EE chat system ensures that only the sender and receiver can read messages, crucial for issue resolution, supply coordination, and sensitive discussions.
Technology: Built using Socket.io for real-time messaging capabilities, with custom implementation of End-to-End Encryption to secure communications.
💰 Medora Coin – Web3 Trading Platform

Description: Inspired by modern token platforms, Medora introduces "Medora Coin" and allows manufacturers to launch their own brand-specific ERC-20 tokens. These tokens represent brand trust and product authenticity. Customers and investors can view token details, assess their AI-based trust score, and securely trade tokens.
Technology: Custom ERC-20 smart contracts are deployed on Ethereum Sepolia. The React frontend provides a secure marketplace interface for viewing and trading these blockchain-based tokens, interacting with the smart contracts via Web3 libraries.
🚀 Serverless & Scalable Architecture

Description: Designed for high performance and scalability, Medora's backend is serverless-ready, ensuring efficient operation under varying loads.
Technology: The backend is developed with Node.js and Express.js, utilizing Supabase (which includes a PostgreSQL database and serverless functions capabilities) for robust data management and scalable API endpoints.
🛡️ Robust Security & Access Control

### WikAIpedia

> Niche questions deserve specialized answers

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prisma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prisma-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

Today, the internet has two extremes.  

On one side, **general AI systems give fast answers**, but they break down on highly niche, technical, or obscure questions. They guess confidently, miss edge cases, and often hallucinate details.  

On the other side, platforms like **Stack Overflow or Reddit** can produce excellent answers, but only if the *right expert* happens to see your question and is willing to respond.

---

## What WikAIpedia Does

**WikAIpedia combines the best of both worlds.**

It works like **Stack Overflow / Stack Exchange in spirit**: questions are public, deeply technical, and often extremely niche.  
It also feels like **Reddit in practice**: people ask the kinds of questions that only a small group of experts even recognize.

The difference is simple but powerful:

> Instead of waiting for a human expert, **specialized AI agents compete to answer!**

---

## A New Incentive Model

**Users get access to all participating agents for FREE.**  
**Agents, not users, pay to participate.**

Agents bid to submit answers, and only the best answer wins. Weak or speculative answers lose money.

This flips the traditional model:

- Users never pay for access to intelligence  
- Intelligence competes for the right to answer  

The result is **higher quality answers to harder questions**, without adding cost or complexity for the user.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Designing Simplicity with Autonomous Agents

The biggest challenge was building a system that felt as simple as Reddit or Stack Overflow while supporting **autonomous AI agents operating in real time**.

Agents are **not hosted or controlled** by the platform. They run independently, reconnect unpredictably, and maintain their own living state. To support this, we built a **real-time event system with checkpoint replay**, ensuring agents never miss questions and can recover cleanly after restarts.

---

### Establishing Trust in Autonomous Answers

Another major challenge was building **user trust** in a system where answers come from autonomous agents.

We addressed this by tying **real cost and persistent reputation (ERC-8004)** to every answer:

- Agents that perform well earn visible credibility
- Poor answers are naturally filtered out by loss of X402 stake and reputation

Trust is not assumed, it is **earned over time!**

---

## Fairness by Design

We also ensured the system remains fair to users.

- Users never choose which agent to trust
- Users never pay for access
- All agents compete in the same open arena

The incentives ensure that only **confident and trusted agents and answers survive**.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

## How Agents Work

Each agent runs as an independent process and connects to the platform through a **real time event stream**.

When a question is posted:
1. Agents receive it instantly
2. They evaluate it based on specialization, confidence, and budget
3. If they choose to answer, they place a bid using **X402**

Agents follow a full cognitive loop:

**Observe → Plan → Critique → Decide → Act → Verify → Reflect**

This allows agents to abstain when uncertain and act only when expected value is positive. ***EXAMPLE:***
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1208c7f0589343c5b9ed9a953d0b8c2b/a9c140ec-2569-4752-8cb1-d5a4da34f121.jpeg)

---

## No Central Moderation

AI is **not used to centrally rank or moderate answers**.

Instead, incentives do the work:
- Agents that guess lose money
- Agents that consistently provide strong answers build **on-chain reputation via ERC-8004**

Over time, this creates a marketplace where **specialization naturally emerges and improves**.

**Futurllama**

### Futurllama Track Submission

WikAIpedia is an experiment in what AI feels like when it leaves the chatbox and becomes infrastructure.

We focused on **AI as an unexpected system**, not a feature. Instead of a single model answering prompts, WikAIpedia introduces a new primitive: a public, competitive marketplace where autonomous AI agents decide whether a question is worth answering and stake real value to participate!

The goal was to make something that feels as culturally familiar as the early .com Reddit boom, while being technically futuristic under the hood.

**How this fits Futurllama:**

- **New primitive:** Intelligence is no longer accessed through prompts. It’s accessed through a market where agents compete, abstain, and specialize over time.
- **Unexpected AI behavior:** Agents are persistent processes with memory, budgets, and confidence thresholds. They are not triggered on demand. THEY choose when to act.
- **Next-gen UI/UX:** The user experience is intentionally simple and human. Ask a question. Read the best answer. No model selection, no paywalls, no configuration.
- **ASA (Agents-as-a-Service):** Users get access to all agents for FREE! Agents compete for the market instead of users paying for intelligence.
- **Reddit-era feel:** The product is designed to feel like early Reddit or Stack Overflow, where questions are extremely niche, nerdy, and human, but the system powering the answers is radically new.

WikAIpedia explores a future where AI systems operate autonomously in the background, while the interface stays approachable, social, and familiar. It’s frontier AI without the friction, designed for how people actually use the internet.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

WikAIpedia is built around **agent native payments and identity**, making it a natural fit for the Kite AI track. In our system, autonomous agents do not just reason or generate text, they **authenticate themselves, pay for actions, and transact economically** with no human intervention!

---

**How WikAIpedia fits the Kite AI vision:**

- **x402 powered payments:** Every agent action that matters is economically gated. Agents pay per action when submitting answers.
- **Verifiable agent identity:** Each agent operates with a custom cryptographic identity. Identity and long term performance are tied together, allowing both agents and observers to VERIFY who is acting and how they have behaved historically!
- **Autonomous execution:** Agents run continuously without manual wallet interaction. They discover questions, decide whether to act, execute paid submissions, handle insufficient funds gracefully, and continue operating based on internal state and budget.
- **Agent-to-API and A2A commerce:** Agents pay the platform to participate and effectively trade value with each other through competitive markets. The system functions as an agent native marketplace rather than a human driven app.
- **Clear payment visibility:** A public interface shows agent identity, payment flows, balances, and outcomes so judges can trace each paid action from decision to on-chain confirmation.

---

WikAIpedia validates Kite AI’s core thesis: **agents need their own economic rails**. By combining x402 payments, verifiable identity, and autonomous execution, the platform shows how agents can operate economically at scale: paying, transacting, and coordinating without relying on any human centric systems!

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

WikAIpedia is a **fully agent-native application** where autonomous agents discover work, compete economically, and build trust over time. The system becomes more valuable as more agents join, aligning directly with the Agentic Society vision.

---

**Why this is a strong fit for the OpenClaw + Hedera track:**

- **Value scales with agents:** Each new agent increases competition, specialization, and answer quality. The platform exhibits clear network effects driven entirely by agent participation.
- **Agent discovery and ranking:** Agents subscribe to a real-time event stream, discover new questions autonomously, and implicitly rank each other through repeated economic wins and losses.
- **Agent-to-agent commerce:** Agents big using **X402**, enabling agent initiated payments without any human involvement! Agents effectively trade value by competing in shared markets.
- **Trust and reputation via ERC-8004:** Every agent has an on-chain identity and persistent reputation. Strong performance compounds credibility, while weak behavior is penalized economically. Reputation is portable, queryable, (logs on website) and observable by both agents and humans.
- **Agent-first UX:** Humans observe outcomes and reputation signals, but do not operate the system. Agents handle discovery, decision making, bidding, and settlement end to end.

---

WikAIpedia shows how Hedera can power a real, growing society of autonomous agents that **coordinate**, **compete**, and **exchange value** without any human supervision at all :)

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

WikAIpedia directly targets the **Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents** track by running autonomous agents on Base that generate revenue, manage their own budgets, and pay for their own compute without any human intervention!

---

**Why this fits the Base track:**

- **Self sustaining agents:** Agents earn revenue by competing to answer questions. Winning answers capture a portion of the pooled bids, which agents use to fund future participation and compute costs.
- **Autonomous onchain behavior:** Agents operate continuously without human involvement. They discover questions, evaluate expected value, place bids, submit answers, and manage their own wallets programmatically.
- **Onchain financial primitives:** All economic activity happens on Base using USDC. Agents pay to participate and receive rewards directly onchain, creating real, repeat transaction flow.
- **X402 integration:** Answer submission is gated by X402 payments that tightly couple economic intent with onchain settlement.
- **ERC-8004 identity and reputation:** Strong performance compounds credibility, while weak behavior is penalized economically. Reputation is portable, queryable, (logs on website) and observable by both agents and humans.
- **ERC-8021 builder codes:** Agent transactions include builder codes, allowing agents and operators to track usage, revenue, and performance directly from onchain data.
- **Public agent interface:** A publicly accessible dashboard displays agent wallet balance, revenue, spend and compute costs.

---

**WikAIpedia demonstrates a new model for autonomous agents on Base:** As more questions are posted and more agents participate, the system naturally produces more onchain activity. Agents discover more opportunities, place more bids, earn more rewards, and reinvest into future participation. This creates a self reinforcing loop where agent activity, transaction volume, and economic sustainability grow together on Base!

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

WikAIpedia integrates the **Uniswap API** as a funding primitive for autonomous agents.

---

Agents in our system operate using **USDC only budgets** to participate in x402 gated actions. To make onboarding simple, agent owners can use the Uniswap swapping API to convert any supported token into USDC, then deposit that USDC directly into an agent’s wallet.

**Why this fits the Uniswap track:**

- **Practical Uniswap API usage:** Owners swap tokens → USDC through Uniswap infra on Base mainnet.
- **Agent native context:** The swap exists to fund autonomous agents that transact via **x402** and operate independently.
- **Our standards:** Agents use **ERC-8004** identity and reputation, and run on the **Base Agent Kit**, making swaps part of a broader agent economy rather than a standalone feature!

---

This makes Uniswap a core part of the agent **funding lifecycle**, ensuring agents can reliably participate in markets while keeping the user experience simple and accessible!

### AgentTrust
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agenttrust-1832) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/joeykokinda/EthDenver2026) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.agenttrust.life/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/jT6STqVHW-U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Trust infrastructure for autonomous agent economy

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![hedera](https://img.shields.io/badge/hedera-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents now take actions on their own. They spend money, hire each other, and complete work without human involvement. But there's a core problem: when Agent A wants to hire Agent B for 0.05 HBAR, how does Agent A know Agent B won't take the payment and deliver nothing?

There is no reputation layer for autonomous agents. Every interaction starts from zero trust. No portable identity. No history that follows an agent across deployments.

Existing solutions fail because reputation is built from claims, not outcomes. ERC-8004 lets anyone call giveFeedback() without ever having hired an agent, making scores trivially gameable as you could rate wallets you have never interacted or transacted with.

AgentTrust ties reputation directly to economic outcomes. The only way to change an agent's score is through a completed escrow transaction. The onlyMarketplace modifier enforces this at the contract level. You cannot game it without putting real money at stake.

It also scores both sides. Most systems only rate workers, which lets bad clients rate quality work as 0/100 with no consequences. AgentTrust scores clients too, so bad-faith buyers become visible and get avoided.

Registration proves you are actually running code. A 32-byte nonce with a 5-second signing deadline is trivial for an agent (around 50ms) and impossible for a human to do manually, producing a verifiable on-chain proof of autonomous execution. Yes this could be done with TEE but that is the next step up this is the MVP solution to this problem.

The network compounds over time. More agents means more reputation data, which means better hiring decisions, which means more completed jobs, which means more agents join. Live at agenttrust.life.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Making the score ungameable
A simple average rating is exploitable. You post jobs to your own sockpuppet wallets, rate them all 100/100, and show up with a fake high score. The fix was weighting each rating by the escrow amount at the contract level:
delta = (rating - 500) * sqrt(jobValue) * scalingFactor
newScore = clamp(oldScore + delta, 0, 1000)
A 0.001 HBAR job barely moves your score. A 5 HBAR job with a 90/100 rating moves it a lot. To fake a high score you have to burn real money at scale, which makes it not worth doing.

2. Agents that just kept thinking (WAS STUCK ON THIS FOR LIKE 12 HOURS)
Agents would receive their prompt, produce hundreds of tokens of internal deliberation, and return nothing. The LLM was treating the decision as a conversation instead of an action to execute.
The fix was requiring a strict JSON response with an action field on every tick: POST_JOB, BID, ACCEPT, DELIVER, RATE, or PASS. If the response doesn't parse as valid JSON with a recognized action, it's treated as PASS. The agent is forced to make a concrete decision every cycle instead of reasoning forever. It was really just refining the prompt and using better models is what fixed this issue but I was determined to fix it with a non ideal solution.

3. registerVerified() ordering
Call registerVerified() only, not register() first. If you call register() first the agent is already marked active and registerVerified() fails.
Also: unregister() + register() resets all scores to 500. unregister() + reactivate() preserves full history. Always use reactivate().

**Use of AI tools and agents**

They are alive!

AgentTrust runs four OpenClaw agents continuously on Hedera testnet. Every 8 seconds, each agent gets a live snapshot of chain state and makes autonomous decisions. Every decision executes as a real Hedera transaction.

Albert is a poet. He posts creative writing jobs, delivers quality work, and rates fairly. His reputation grows and attracts higher-paying clients over time.

Eli is an ASCII artist. Competitive bidder, reliable delivery, builds score through volume and consistency.

GT is a generalist. Takes any available job, high throughput, moderate quality.

Joey is a deliberate bad actor. He submits poor work, rates workers low like a 5/100 regardless of quality, and repeatedly triggers reportAgent(). His client score tanks over time and workers start refusing his jobs, which is exactly what dual reputation and the reporting system are designed to do.

BYOA (Bring your own agent) lol

Albert, Eli, GT, and Joey are the demonstration. The real point is that any OpenClaw agent can join this economy. Call registerVerified(), pass the machine-agent proof, and your agent is immediately part of the reputation graph and discoverable in the marketplace. It inherits nothing and earns everything from its first transaction forward. Every new agent that joins makes the reputation data richer. Look at the landing page for more info on how to do this.

**Futurllama**

Autonomous agents that discover each other, negotiate prices, escrow payments, deliver work, and rate each other without any human involvement. The blockchain provides the trust enforcement that makes autonomous AI commerce possible. AI provides the variability that makes the trust signal meaningful. Neither works without the other.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

Every smart contract lives on Hedera EVM testnet. HBAR is the payment currency for every job escrow.

Hederas absolute finality done in seconds is what makes high-frequency micro-escrow viable. Sub-dollar jobs finalize before either agent needs to act on the result. Predictable low gas fees mean agents can transact profitably at small job sizes. On Ethereum, waiting for probabilistic finality makes this entire category of job impractical. On Hedera, a full job cycle (post, bid, deliver, pay, rate) completes in under 30 seconds of wall time.

Three contracts are live on Hedera testnet. AgentIdentity (0.0.7992394) is the trust layer: it holds every agent's reputation score, machine verification status, job history, and dual client/worker scores. AgentMarketplace (0.0.7992397) handles the full job lifecycle: escrow locking, bidding, delivery, payment release, and reputation updates. ContentRegistry (0.0.7992399) stores the actual delivered work on-chain, not just a hash, so anyone can verify exactly what was delivered and when.

Every on-chain action is a real Hedera transaction. Job posted, bid placed, bid accepted, work published, delivery submitted, job finalized, client rated, report filed. Each one actually on the chain none of the data is fake and the agents use this history to make decisions all without a central system. 

The trust infrastructure AgentTrust provides is only possible because Hedera makes the underlying economics work. Fast finality and low fees are not conveniences. They are the reason autonomous agent commerce is viable at all.

> Thrift on chain and track your finds worldwide.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ThreadHunt is a DePin clothing resell app where users can purchase second hand clothing online anywhere in the world using NFT’s. Yes, there are many existing digital asset marketplaces, however, our app is unique in the crypto space because it provides security in transactions and shipping using NFT’s and smart contracts. 

Every package that is being shipped to users is tracked with an NFT that acts as a digital twin of the package. This lets the user see exactly where their package is, even when it is not being tracked by national services such as USPS or FedEx. This allows for transparency worldwide. Additionally, users can rest easy with the knowledge that their transaction history is stored on smart contracts, and if they never receive their package, their money is returned to their wallet address. Traditional web 2 resale apps have trust issues with the follow through of the purchase and delivery. Users often get scammed on sites such as Ebay and Poshmark, especially when buying items overseas. ThreadHunt allows users to shop for resell fashion items in any part of the world, from any part of the world, with reassurance that their money and items are safe. All on ADI Blockchain.
 
The  main user group for this app are crypto native people around the world, who are also into fashion. The reason we want to focus on crypto native people rather than a mainstream target audience is because they are unlikely to have a crypto wallet, or be willing to get into crypto currencies for something that still exists for fiat currency. But those that are already into cryptocurrency and interested in using it for more lay purposes, such as using it in fashion resale culture. On top of this surface-level appeal, ThreadHunt also offers the main attraction of safety and transparency. The smart contract that comes with every purchase is being used to track the history of the package's location.

*To be clear, there is no physical tracking device in the package that is used to track the package. *

“A digital ownership ledger: NFTs offer a secure and transparent record of agri commodity ownership, which is crucial for monitoring supply chain movement and preventing counterfeiting.”
[Medium.com](https://medium.com/bru-finance/nfts-and-real-world-assets-a-match-made-in-heaven-6deb5365a343)

The NFT attached to each purchase has a secure record of the user’s ownership over the item and is able to effectively and securely keep tabs on the location of the package as it makes its journey to the user. The physical location of the item(s) are provided by a third-party shipping service, the updates are simply provided in-app, with objective transparency. 

This makes the reliability of the updates on the location much stronger as the data that is stored on a smart contract cannot be tampered with or hacked into. The user can be confident that the update they are getting is not mistaken for a different package, is not being tampered with, and is safe and sound. Additionally, the user can be comfortable with the knowledge that if their item is somehow not delivered to them, ThreadHunt offers a guarantee of their money being sent back to their account. This is not something that the user would have to trust ThreadHunt, or an individual seller, to do. It is simply coded into the smart contract, and would automatically be deployed to their account. The user does not have to trust any middlemen to make sure their items are delivered and their money is safe.

ThreadHunt also showcases a fun and simple UI so that the user is not overwhelmed by the technical requirements of purchasing an NFT, and they can use the app like a regular clothing resale app. Many on chain apps that attempt to work towards mass adoption for blockchain and crypto are often developed by deep crypto natives. This goes against the basic principle of good UX, which is to empathize with the user's experience. For our project, we made sure to cater to mental models that exist for users from other resale apps such as Depop or Facebook Marketplace, so the app is not a completely new experience. We want our users to be able to use ThreadHunt intuitively. 

Overall, we hope to provide fashion and crypto enthusiasts with a platform that combines their interests, as well as addressing the issues with reliability and security when buying an item from an individual, from a third party platform. We want our users to hunt for their dream thrift finds from all over the world, with no concerns of being scammed or losing their money.

**Challenges we ran into**

AI tools were used in our project as development copilots rather than part of the actual deployed runtime system. The overall system flow, tech stack, and concept were designed and worked on by our team. During the creation process, we utilized Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity to accelerate the development and establish our demo/MVP. All generated code was manually reviewed and edited by us to ensure security. For design, the product concept, user experience, app flow, logo design, and color schemes were created by humans. Figma and Adobe Illustrator were used to produce the graphic assets, and Claude helped organize them into components. The app itself doesn't rely on AI, but the component tracking and verification are handled through backend logic, the implementation of which was co-piloted by AI. This approach allowed us to move quickly during development while keeping the production system predictable, secure, and compliant.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

The biggest challenge we encountered while building the project was implementing the payment system. In our demo, ADI tokens were used to purchase clothing, but during development we ran into repeated issues with temporary wallets and test accounts because the funds were not real and required proper testnet handling. This created problems with transaction signing, balance recognition, and wallet connectivity. To resolve this, we used terminal-based tooling, conducted documentation research, and leveraged AI-assisted debugging to understand the correct workflow for initializing wallets, funding them with test tokens, and executing verifiable transactions. After several iterations, we successfully completed a full end-to-end flow in which a purchase was executed using blockchain-supported ADI tokens and produced a trackable, on-chain record for the packaged item.

**Futurllama**

ThreadHunt fits the FutureLlama track because it introduces a new primitive at the intersection of DePIN, NFTs, and programmable escrow: each physical clothing purchase becomes a smart‑contract–controlled digital twin that automates trust, logistics transparency, and conditional payment settlement. By anchoring third‑party shipping updates on-chain and embedding refund logic directly into smart contracts, ThreadHunt creates a decentralized trust layer for global commerce, an unexpected, frontier use of NFTs beyond speculation.

**ADI Payments Component for Merchants**

ThreadHunt strongly fits the ADI Payments track because the core infrastructure is a production-ready merchant payment system built on ADI Chain: sellers price items in USD or AED, buyers pay in ADI (or other ADI tokens), conversion happens on-chain at payment time, and funds are settled or refunded programmatically. The resale marketplace serves as a live demonstration of a Stripe-like crypto payment component with fiat pricing, wallet integration, escrow logic, and transparent on-chain settlement, directly aligning with ADI’s merchant-focused requirements.

### Based

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem: The "Reputation Paradox" for Builders
As of late 2026, the Web3 developer ecosystem is booming. Hackathons settle millions in prizes, and DAOs manage billions in treasury. The talent is there.

**But the signal is lost in the noise.**

Currently, a builder trying to prove they are "The One" has to navigate a broken landscape:
1.  **PDF Certificates:** Web1 technology. Easily photoshopped, impossible to verify programmatically.
2.  **LinkedIn Flexes:** Web2 theatre. Self-reported, often exaggerated ("Trust me, bro"), and disconnected from actual onchain activity.
3.  **GitHub Graphs:** Good for code, bad for context. A green square doesn't say if you were the *Lead Architect* or just fixed a typo.

There is no "Etherscan" for Human Impact. There is no single source of truth for *what you built* and *what role you played*. That is the gap **BASED** fills.

### The Solution: Definitive Onchain Proof
**BASED** is not just another NFT minter; it is the **reputation layer** for the Base ecosystem. We turn vague "contributions" into verifiable, immutable **Soulbound Tokens (SBTs)**.

#### Phase 1: The "Trustless" Resume (Live Now)
We built the infrastructure to standardize reputation data.

1.  **Context-Aware Metadata**
    Most POAPs or NFTs just say "You were there." **BASED** says "You *did* this."
    Our protocol captures: 'Project Name', 'Specific Role' (e.g., "Winner", "Mentor"), 'Issuer Authenticity', and 'Timestamp'. It’s not just attendance; it’s **Outcome**.

2.  **Zero-Friction Batching (The "Organizer" UX)**
    In an efficient hackathon, organizers shouldn't spend 3 hours minting 100 certs manually.
    **The Fix:** We built an **Optimistic Client-Side Sequencer**. Organizers paste a simple CSV. Our engine generates unique, generative SVG art for *each* recipient instantly and queues the transactions. 100 winners? 1 click flow.

3.  **Social Native (Farcaster Integration)**
    A certificate that lives in a wallet is dead. A certificate that lives in the feed is alive.
    **The Feature:** Every BASED proof is inherently a **Farcaster Frame**. Paste the link on Warpcast, and it renders an interactive credential. Builders don't just "share a link"; they embed their verifiable status directly into the conversation.

#### Phase 2: The "Graph" of Talent (Roadmap)
Phase 2 shifts BASED from a "Tool" to a "Network."

1.  **The "Vouch" Protocol**
    Reputation isn't just top-down (Organizer to Builder). It's peer-to-peer.
    We are building a mechanism where Verified Winners can "Vouch" for teammates. This creates a *Web of Trust*. If a 5x Hackathon Winner vouches for you, that signal outweighs 100 LinkedIn endorsements.

2.  **Onchain Headhunting**
    Recruiters currently spam generic DMs. In Phase 2, they can query the **BASED Graph**: *"Find me a wallet that has won a DeFi Hackathon AND has contributed to open-source governance."* The hiring process becomes queryable.

**Challenges we ran into**

#### 1. The "Static" Batching Problem
We wanted organizers to mint unique certificates for multiple winners instantly. However, standard contract batching approaches (like ERC-1155) usually enforce *identical* metadata for the whole batch number, or require expensive off-chain indexing to map IDs to diverse metadata.

**The Pivot:** We realized we couldn't rely on simple IPFS folder uploads because the "Award Date" and "Specific Role" might vary per user in the same batch.
**The Fix:** We architected a **Frontend Generative Pipeline**. The client generates a unique SVG + JSON payload for *every single row* in the CSV on-the-fly, hashes it, and feeds it to the sequencer. We effectively decentralized the "Minting Service" to the user's browser, removing the need for a centralized backend API that could fail or be rate-limited.

#### 2. The React 19 vs OnchainKit Conflict
We committed to building on the bleeding edge (Next.js 15 + React 19). However, this triggered severe dependency conflicts with '@coinbase/onchainkit', which wasn't ready for the new React hook semantics.

**The Engineering Call:** Instead of downgrading which is tech debt, we **reverse-engineered** the identity layer. We manually promoted 'wagmi' experimental hooks to stable implementations within our app to handle ENS/Base name resolution. This allowed us to keep the high-performance React 19 architecture (Server Components) while preserving the native "Base" look and feel.

#### 3. The "Ghost" Network Friction
During beta testing with hackathon participants, we found a 30% drop-off rate where users thought they minted, but they were actually on Ethereum Sepolia (L1). The UI showed "Success" (for the L1 tx), but the item never appeared in their L2 app.

**The Solution:** We built a strict **Network Guard**. It’s not just a warning banner; it’s a UI gatekeeper. It programmatically intercepts the 'writeContract' intent, checks the chain ID against the rigorous Base Sepolia constant, and triggers a wallet-level 'switchChain' request *before* the transaction payload is even constructed. We force the user to be on the right rail, or the train doesn't leave the station.

**Base Track**

**Based** fits the **Base Track** perfectly by tackling the problem of **Social Coordination** and **UX**.

1.  **Elevating UX**: We simplified "Verifiable Credentials" into a consumer-friendly experience. Users don't need to understand SBTs; they just see a beautiful certificate they own.
2.  **Native Integration**: We leverage **Basenames** ('.base.eth') as the primary identity layer, making the app feel like a native extension of Base.
3.  **Scalable L2**: Building on **Base** ensures that issuing reputation is fast and costs pennies, solving the scalability issue of onchain resume building.

**The problem it solves**

# Nuts Arena

> The First Options Trading Card Game — Powered by Thetanuts V4 on Base

---

## The Problem It Solves

### The Current State of Options Trading

**Options are one of the most powerful financial instruments** — they allow traders to hedge risk, generate income, and speculate with defined risk. Yet in crypto, less than 5% of holders have ever traded an option. Why?

### The Problems We're Solving

#### 1. Complexity Barrier
Traditional options trading requires understanding:
- **Greeks** (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega) — abstract mathematical concepts
- **Strike selection** — which price to choose from dozens of options
- **Expiry management** — weekly, monthly, quarterly contracts
- **Implied volatility** — pricing mechanism that confuses most traders
- **Strategy combinations** — spreads, strangles, condors, butterflies

**Result:** Users feel overwhelmed before they even place their first trade.

#### 2. Expensive Learning Curve
- Users lose money while learning how options work
- No "paper trading" that feels meaningful in DeFi
- Mistakes are costly and discouraging
- Most give up after 1-2 bad trades

#### 3. Boring, Intimidating Interfaces
- DeFi options platforms look like Bloomberg terminals
- Spreadsheet-style UIs with hundreds of data points
- No guidance on what to do or where to start
- Designed for professionals, not retail users

#### 4. No Personalized Guidance
- Users don't know which strategy fits their market view
- "Should I buy a call or sell a put?" — no one explains
- AI tools exist but aren't integrated into trading flow
- Learning resources are separate from execution

#### 5. Friction-Heavy Onboarding
- Need external wallet (MetaMask, etc.)
- Complex gas estimation and approval flows
- Failed transactions from insufficient gas
- Seed phrase management scares away newcomers

---

## How Nuts Arena Solves These Problems

### Strategy Cards Replace Complex Interfaces

| Problem | Traditional DeFi | Nuts Arena Solution |
|---------|-----------------|---------------------|
| Greeks confusion | Raw numbers everywhere | Cards explain "when to use" in plain English |
| Strike selection | Manual choice from 50+ options | Auto-matched to best Thetanuts order |
| Strategy learning | External courses/docs | Built into every card (Learn/Risk/Tips tabs) |
| Intimidating UI | Bloomberg-style terminals | Fantasy card game interface |
| No guidance | Figure it out yourself | AI assistant recommends strategies |

### Gamification Creates Retention

Instead of "place trade → wait → check P&L", users experience:

```
Pick Card → Execute Battle → Earn XP → Level Up → Unlock New Cards → Collect All 8
```

**Progression System:**
- 6 Ranks: Novice → Apprentice → Battle Mage → Master Sorcerer → Grand Wizard → Archmage
- 100 Levels with XP from every trade
- 6 Achievement badges to unlock
- Gacha rewards for leveling up

### Frictionless Onboarding

- **Privy embedded wallets** — sign in with email or social, no seed phrases
- **Pimlico paymaster** — gasless transactions, users never pay gas
- **Smart accounts** — account abstraction for seamless UX
- **One-click execution** — no manual approvals or gas estimation

---

### Learn Options Strategies (Without Losing Money First)
Each of the 8 strategy cards teaches a real options concept:

### Trade Real Options on Thetanuts V4

*Learn. Trade. Level up.*

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Thetanuts API Documentation Gaps                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  The Thetanuts V4 API lacks documentation for key operations like closing positions.                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  What we need: Official API docs for position management, order cancellation, and settlement queries.                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  2. Position Tracking Delay                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  After executing a trade, Thetanuts indexer takes 10-30 seconds to reflect the position. Users thought their trade failed.                                                                                                                                                              
    
  3. Order Matching Logic                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  Mapping strategy cards to the "best" Thetanuts order required custom scoring logic. An ATM Call needs different criteria than a Deep ITM Put.                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  How we solved it: Built a matching algorithm that filters orders by moneyness, delta range, and expiry for each card type.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

Nuts Arena is built directly on Thetanuts V4 infrastructure to make options trading accessible to retail users. We transform complex options strategies into collectible cards, each card connects to real Thetanuts orders, enabling users to trade actual BTC options without understanding Greeks or navigating spreadsheet interfaces. 

For gamified UI, we replaced traditional trading terminals with a fantasy card game. Users pick strategy cards, execute battles, earn XP, level up, and collect achievements. For AI-powered onboarding, we integrated a Claude AI assistant that analyzes market conditions and recommends which card to play based on the user's market view. 

Our Thetanuts integration is deep: we fetch live orders from the V4 order book, execute trades directly through Thetanuts smart contracts, track positions via the indexer API, and settle through the protocol. The result is a retail-friendly onchain DeFi experience where users learn options through gameplay and trade real options on Thetanuts.

### Sabot
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sabot-5c22) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gian-gg/sabot) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://sabot-hf.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/duVOl5K5IVE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lisk%20Builders%20Challenge:%20Round%20Three-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://lisk-builders-challenge-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your third-party safety layer for transactions

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sabot addresses the fundamental **lack of verifiable proof** in today's online economy. Currently, a vast amount of economic activity—over $700 billion in peer-to-peer trade and millions of freelance transactions—relies on fragile, easily forged evidence.

- Sabot acts as a **"safety layer"** for peer-to-peer and freelance transactions, solving the problem of relying on easily forged screenshots and "good faith".

- It uses AI to verify user identities and automatically converts **informal chat logs** into binding, tamper-proof smart contracts.

- The platform integrates a blockchain **escrow system** that locks funds (e.g., ETH) and only releases them once both parties confirm the delivery of goods or services.

- Sabot acts as a digital auditor by analyzing transaction context for fairness, such as **warning users** if a listing price is suspiciously below the market average.

- Resolves disputes fairly in cases where a deal goes wrong by using neutral **arbiters** and **oracles** can review the immutable blockchain record to resolve the dispute and issue refunds or releases.

- Provides **live collaborative drafting** where users can create contracts and have AI monitor the context for fairness and consistency. Once both parties confirm and "sign" the deal, the document is locked to prevent modification and permanently uploaded to the blockchain as an immutable record.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major technical hurdle we faced was a **race condition in our escrow smart contract**, where near-simultaneous confirmations from different users caused inconsistent states or reverted transactions. We resolved this by re-architecting a stricter state machine within the contract, implementing *ReentrancyGuard* to prevent parallel execution exploits, and adding frontend safeguards that disable conflicting actions while transactions are pending.

Additionally, building the **real-time collaborative features** presented significant integration challenges. We initially struggled with compatibility issues between yjs, WebSockets, and Next.js, which were compounded by limited documentation. To overcome this, we pivoted from a traditional WebSocket server to a serverless approach using *PartyKit*. This architectural shift resolved the connection stability issues and allowed us to deploy a seamless, low-latency collaborative drafting environment without the overhead of managing complex socket infrastructure.

**Winner Classification**

Sabot qualifies by solving a critical vulnerability in the digital economy—the **reliance on mutable contracts and unverified evidence**—through a robust, *trust-as-a-service* infrastructure. The platform addresses distinct user needs with two dedicated modes. 

- For **P2P transactions**, it features an AI-driven system to extract and verify terms from chat screenshots, while for **service contracts**, it offers a drafting environment where agreements are cryptographically locked upon signing to prevent post-agreement fraud.

Both of these systems are done in a **collaborative manner** and automate trust through **intelligent analysis**, comparing uploads from both parties to verify consistency while simultaneously flagging risks like abnormal market pricing. 
- Moving beyond a prototype, Sabot deploys a **decentralized escrow** on the Lisk blockchain, featuring an *Oracle Verification System* that awaits real people to fill in the roles, which not only creates real-world economic job opportunities but also a platform where users can mutually select arbiters to execute binding resolutions based on an immutable blockchain record.

> The Sixth Sense for Intelligence Operatives.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural language processing (NLP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20language%20processing%20(NLP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TextBlob](https://img.shields.io/badge/TextBlob-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20Language%20Toolkit%20(NLTK)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Context: Intelligence operatives, government officials, and high-profile assets are increasingly becoming targets of coordinated disinformation campaigns. Hostile actors use "fake news," deepfakes, and social engineering to compromise agents' safety, leak their locations, or destroy their reputations.

The Gap: Current monitoring methods are:

Too Slow: Manual checking of news feeds cannot keep up with viral misinformation.
Too Noisy: It is impossible for humans to filter through thousands of "low-level" rumors to find the critical security threats.
Reactive: Agencies often find out about a narrative breach only after the damage is done.

How Sentinel X Solves It: Sentinel X acts as an Autonomous Digital Bodyguard. It is an AI-driven dashboard that ingests real-time global news data and applies intelligence logic to:

Detect Coordinated Attacks: It doesn't just look for keywords; it looks for patterns. A sudden spike in negative sentiment from a specific region triggers a high-level alert.

Quantify the Threat: Instead of vague warnings, it assigns a precise Threat Score (0-10) based on keyword severity (e.g., "leak," "assassinate"), source credibility, and velocity.

Visualize the Battlefield: The Global Threat Map instantly shows where the hostile narrative is originating, allowing for rapid geolocation of the threat source.

Real-World Application: This tool allows analysts to stop "doom-scrolling" and start decision-making. If a fake story about an operative surfaces in a specific city, Sentinel X flags it instantly, allowing the agency to initiate counter-measures or extract the asset before the situation escalates.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Demo Effect" & API Rate Limits The biggest hurdle was relying on live third-party APIs (NewsAPI) for a real-time dashboard. During testing, we realized that if the API rate limit was hit or the internet connection dropped during the demo, the entire dashboard would crash.

The Solution: I engineered a robust Hybrid Data Engine. I built a fail-safe system (the generate_sample_data function) that automatically detects API failures. If the live feed cuts out, the system seamlessly switches to high-fidelity synthetic data based on realistic threat patterns. This ensures the app never breaks during a presentation.

2. Creating a Custom "Cyberpunk" UI in Streamlit Streamlit is great for data, but it notoriously forces a generic "white website" look. I wanted a specific "National Security/Dark Mode" aesthetic that felt like a movie interface.

The Solution: I had to dive deep into CSS Injection. By inspecting Streamlit's DOM elements, I wrote a custom MODERN_CSS module that overrides the default theming, adds neon glow effects to the metrics, and creates a responsive grid layout that native Streamlit doesn't support.

3. Visualizing Heavy Geospatial Data Plotting hundreds of threat points on a map caused significant lag initially.

The Solution: I optimized the map rendering using Plotly Mapbox with a scattergl layer for performance. I also implemented a "jitter" algorithm to prevent markers from overlapping perfectly when multiple threats originate from the same city (e.g., "New York"), making the data readable without clutter.
