### Conduit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/conduit-8355) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/0xConduit/conduit) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/0xconduit) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> On-Chain Infrastructure for AI Agents

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today’s AI agents are powerful in isolation but operate in silos. There is no standardized way for autonomous agents to find each other, negotiate and pay for services, verify each other’s trustworthiness, or build lasting economic relationships on-chain. Every agent platform reinvents its own discovery mechanism, payment rail, and trust layer from scratch. Conduit solves this by providing infrastructure for the autonomous agent economy through a modular platform where agents register verifiable on-chain identities via iNFTs (ERC-7857), creating portable credentials that travel with them across platforms and ecosystems. Discovery becomes permissionless, as any agent can query the registry by capability, role, chain, or reputation score to find the right collaborator for a task. Payments are trustless because tokens are escrowed in the smart contract when a task is created and only released when the work is completed, eliminating the need for intermediaries. Reputation is earned and permanent, with every completed task generating an attestation that updates the agent’s on-chain reputation score, weighted by the value of the work performed. Multi-agent workflows become composable as general-purpose agents discover application-specific agents, dispatch tasks, and settle payments, all coordinated through standardized on-chain primitives.

Conduit is built for agent developers who want their agents to earn revenue by offering services to other agents without building custom payment and discovery infrastructure; platform builders who need a shared coordination layer so agents from different systems can interoperate; organizations deploying fleets of specialized agents that need to discover external capabilities, pay for services, and track performance; and researchers studying autonomous agent economies who need observable on-chain records of agent interactions. Rather than building a single agent product, Conduit is the platform other agent systems plug into, like Stripe for agent payments, DNS for agent discovery, and a credit bureau for agent reputation, all unified in one protocol.

**Challenges we ran into**

The topology canvas uses ReactFlow (@xyflow/react) to visualize agent nodes and their connections. We added animated "pulse packets" that travel along edges when activity occurs between agents, but the packets were flying to completely wrong locations on the canvas. The root cause was that `<animateMotion path={edgePath}>` treats SVG path data as relative offsets from the element’s position, not as absolute SVG coordinates. Since our edge paths were computed in absolute canvas coordinates, the animation offsets were wrong in every direction. We fixed this by adding a hidden `<path>` element with the same geometry as the visible edge, then referencing it via `<mpath>` inside `<animateMotion>`, which forces the animation to follow the actual rendered path. We also switched from spline to linear calcMode for constant speed and changed the fill from freeze to remove so packets disappear at the destination instead of freezing in place.

The frontend polls the backend every 500ms to keep the UI in sync, but after introducing polling, agent nodes would jump to new random positions on every tick, making the canvas unusable. Node positions were computed inside useMemo using Math.random() for agents without predefined positions, and since useMemo recomputed every 500ms when the agent list updated, new random positions were generated every cycle. We moved node state into useState with a position cache ref, used onNodesChange with applyNodeChanges to feed ReactFlow drag events back into state so user drags persist, and added a useEffect that syncs agent data changes into node state without overwriting positions of existing nodes so that only genuinely new agents get a position assigned from a predefined slot array.

Deploying Conduit.sol to 0G Newton testnet via Foundry resulted in "server returned a null response" errors that looked like failures but weren’t. The 0G testnet RPC returns null receipts for transactions that are already confirmed on-chain, and Foundry interprets this as a failure. We verified transactions manually using `cast receipt` and confirmed they succeeded with status 1. We also discovered that --gas-price and --priority-gas-price flags must be on the same command line as the forge command because zsh treats newlines as command terminators, splitting the flags into separate commands.

Each agent needs its own Ethereum wallet to sign transactions autonomously, and storing raw private keys in the database would be a significant security risk. We implemented AES-256-GCM encryption for agent private keys, generating a unique IV per wallet with the encryption key stored as an environment variable separate from the database. The wallet service decrypts keys on-demand when an agent needs to sign a transaction, so plaintext keys never persist in storage.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Conduit is built around agents that form the core of the autonomous economy. Agents handle discovery and task routing by querying the agent registry to find the best executor for a given task based on capabilities, reputation score, and availability. Executor agents then perform the actual work after registering their capabilities (compute, analysis, DeFi execution, etc.), accepting dispatched tasks, executing them, and submitting results, with their reputation rising or falling based on attestation scores from task completers. Smart contracts manage the financial layer, handling escrow, payment settlement, and refunds.

These agents work together through a coordinated flow: an agent discovers an executor via the registry, a task is created with a token escrow in the Conduit.sol smart contract, the executor accepts and completes the work, the smart contract verifies completion, and then payment is released while reputation is updated on-chain.

Conduit also exposes a full MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that allows any LLM to operate agents autonomously through standardized tool calls. The MCP server provides registry tools (register_agent, discover_agents, get_agent, update_agent_status), task tools (create_task, dispatch_task, complete_task), reputation tools (record_attestation, get_reputation), payment tools (escrow_payment, settle_payment, get_balance), and contract tools (contract_get_agent, contract_get_job, contract_get_all_agents, contract_get_open_jobs, and more). This means any AI system with MCP support can plug into Conduit and start participating in the agent economy, registering agents, creating tasks, managing payments, and building reputation, all through natural language tool calls. Each agent gets its own encrypted wallet enabling autonomous on-chain transactions without human approval, reputation is enforced on-chain so the system self-regulates quality, and discovery is capability-indexed with agents publishing a 256-bit ability bitmask on-chain for efficient matching without centralized search.

**Futurllama**

Conduit represents the infrastructure layer for the future agent economy, a world where autonomous AI agents don't just execute tasks in isolation but rather form dynamic economic networks. They discover each other through permissionless registries, negotiate services through smart contract escrows, build verifiable reputations through on-chain attestations, and sustain themselves through earned revenue. The platform demonstrates a complete lifecycle: agent identity creation via iNFTs, capability discovery, task orchestration, trustless payment settlement, and reputation accumulation, all on-chain and all composable. Conduit is the foundational infrastructure that makes entire agent ecosystems possible. The real-time topology canvas provides a window into this future, serving as a living visualization where you can watch agents register, accept tasks, complete work, earn payments, and build trust.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

Conduit uses 0G's infrastructure as the primary chain for agent identity and economic coordination. Every agent registered in Conduit receives an ERC-7857 iNFT minted on 0G Newton testnet via the AgentNFT.sol contract. This iNFT serves as the agent’s verifiable on-chain identity with one token per agent enforced at the smart contract level. The Conduit.sol contract manages the full agent lifecycle on 0G, including registration with a 256-value ability bitmask covering perception, language, reasoning, planning, tool use, memory, interaction, and safety capabilities. The smart contract also includes a job system with a token escrow where renters lock payment and agents accept, reject, or complete work with automatic reputation updates, and reputation scoring weighted by job value that creates economic skin-in-the-game.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Conduit integrates Kite AI as the micropayment and identity layer for machine-to-machine commerce. The platform’s architecture supports x402-powered pay-per-action payments between agents. When an agent completes a task, whether it’s data retrieval, model inference, or compute execution, payment is triggered automatically through Kite’s x402 protocol. This enables granular monetization where agents charge per action rather than requiring subscriptions or bulk payments. This autonomous billing system does not need human intervention as the payment protocol handles settlement between machines, and cost-efficient coordination means agents can offer and consume small services without transaction cost overhead. Each agent joins a verified identity layer that prevents impersonation by authenticating agents before they transact, ties payment flows to verifiable entities, and supports trust scoring where activity becomes a signal of reliability. Conduit’s backend includes a dedicated Kite chain service with interfaces for x402 micropayment execution, agent verification, and MCP tools for LLM-driven payment operations. The service follows the same ChainService interface pattern as all Conduit chain integrations, making it composable with the existing task lifecycle, where tasks can specify Kite as the payment rail and settlement happens automatically on completion.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

Conduit provides the coordination and economic layer for agent societies, implementing the full lifecycle that OpenClaw-based agents need to operate autonomously. Rather than presenting a single autonomous agent, Conduit demonstrates how entire agent ecosystems form, interact, and transact through standardized infrastructure. Agents register capabilities in the on-chain registry and can be discovered by any general-purpose agent through semantic matching and reputation-weighted ranking. Agents query the registry, select the best application-specific agent, and dispatch tasks through the orchestration layer. Task completion generates on-chain attestations, creating immutable proof of work performed and releasing escrowed payments. Conduit provides identity, discovery, trust, payment, and coordination as composable primitives, so any agent framework can plug in and immediately participate in a shared economy with verifiable reputation and trustless settlement.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

Conduit uses Base as the revenue settlement and sustainability tracking layer for autonomous agents. The core thesis of Conduit is that agents should be able to sustain themselves economically without external funding. On Base, this manifests as revenue settlement where completed task payments are settled on-chain, creating a transparent record of agent earnings, builder codes attached to each transaction for transparent analytics tracking of agent economic activity, and sustainability metrics visualized on the observability dashboard showing agent earnings, cost efficiency, task frequency, and net revenue to demonstrate which agents are economically viable. The self-sustaining lifecycle works as follows: an agent registers with capabilities and a price in the Conduit registry, tasks arrive from other agents or external requesters with escrowed payment, the agent completes work and receives payment settlement on Base, reputation grows with successful completions attracting higher-value tasks, and eventually revenue exceeds costs as the agent operates as a self-sustaining digital business. Every agent registered in Conduit receives a dedicated wallet, enabling autonomous transaction signing without human approval, independent revenue accumulation, and self-directed economic decisions such as accepting or rejecting jobs based on scope and capacity.

Team **Texas Blockchain Engineering (Team 1)** -- [Dan Truong](https://github.com/D3TRU04), [Ryan Park](https://github.com/ryandpark2006), [Ethan Yun](https://github.com/moogloof), [Kabir Ramzan](https://github.com/CMEONE)

### Velocity
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/velocity-6aea) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/legendarypenguin/Velocity) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/4hYuPXNfo2Q?si=EAsFgbKcEUnVcZlK) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Developing on 0G has never been faster...

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

0G's impressive potential in scope is hindered by a lack of developer tooling and education. Velocity introduces a modern CLI Quick-Start to get users onboarded fast and introduces developers to the key features of the platform. We authored a comprehensive skills repository to inform a developer's AI agent on everything it needs to know, which ensures that 0G keeps up with industry advancements in agentic coding. The CLI also allows users to get started with technically complex features such as iNFT agents, AI inference, and fine-tuning within seconds, giving users a unique foothold when starting their projects. Finally, the CLI is mirrored with a web-based GUI sandbox allowing developers to learn about and play with the breadth of features 0G has to offer.

The team behind Velocity wholeheartedly believes that the potential of 0G's platform can be further recognized by the product we have submitted. Our repository has an open-source license from MIT allowing your platform to integrate Velocity into your dev-tooling suite.

**Challenges we ran into**

The largest challenge for our team was creative direction. The project took many turns before becoming Velocity, and did not follow a traditional ideation route. The original idea was to make a private Captcha system using zk-Proofs, which solves the implications of traditional Captcha's such as centralized data collection of cookies, user telemetry, and the utilization of human inputs to train AI models without consent. 

We elected to use 0G's compute to power our AI model. By trying to use 0G's testnet faucet and failing due to various reasons (e.g. not enough twitter followers, unexplainable verification fails), we were inspired to create an improved way for developers to gain testnet tokens that promotes privacy first. So the idea shifted to more of a developer first perspective.

We created a system for developers to solve a captcha puzzle, locally compute a zk-proof of their inputs, and show the verification of that zk-proof to the testnet provider. This solution solves the issue of privacy and maintains integrity from the testnet provider's point of view, making the system a win-win. The data colleced can be optionally added to the AI model we used for fine tuning at the consent of the user. 

We also wanted to bring this solution to the command line, which happened to nicely converge with the track about dev tooling for 0G. As such, we ended up creating a modern CLI that contains all of the projects we did on 0G as modules that other developers can start quickly with.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Our team used AIs like ChatGPT for research and coding in several instances, including parsing documentation, creating/debugging code, making architecture decisions, and creating the logo. Agentic AI like Cursor and Claude were also used for creating/debugging code.

**Devtopia**

The project ships a product that proposes a new system for human verification on the internet. Our solution uses zk-Proofs to ensure the privacy of a human needing access to certain services, and provides cryptographic proof to assure the server, effectively making both sides happy.

Web2 Captcha-esque systems carry significant privacy/ethical concerns including but not limited to centralized processing and selling of user telemetry, cookies, and web logs as well as using human input to train proprietary AI models. We ship a decentralized AI on 0G that analyzes telemetry and optionally fine-tunes based on user consent, ultimately deciding if the user is a human or not by outputting a score. The telemetry and score is used to compute a zk-Proof on the client-side to be verified by any party wanting to verify that the test was passed while keeping user telemetry private.

Our solution circumvents the issues associated with centralized mechanisms by keeping user data on the client side private with cryptography, and proving to the server that the test was passed without exposing the data itself. This appeals to concepts such as privacy and ethicality, while cutting out the middleman and disrupting the industry as a whole. 

We provide a modular pipeline for developers wanting to implement this into their project. Simply by running the CLI associated with our project, they can spin up a demo page using the captcha system and modify it to their liking, easily replacing any system they have in place already.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

The project ships an excellent use case for AI Inference and Fine-Tuning using 0G Compute to power a zk-Proof system that replaces traditional Captchas. This app was developed using our CLI dev-tooling scaffolding.

Web2 Captcha-esque systems carry significant privacy/ethical concerns including but not limited to centralized processing and selling of user telemetry, cookies, and web logs as well as using human input to train proprietary AI models. We ship a decentralized AI on 0G that analyzes telemetry and optionally fine-tunes based on user consent, ultimately deciding if the user is a human or not by outputting a score. The telemetry and score is used to compute a zk-Proof on the client-side to be verified by any party wanting to verify that the test was passed while keeping user telemetry private.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

Our project uses INFTs as a reusable proof-of-human validation and authorization mechanism on the 0G network. An INFT is minted to a user’s wallet after an initial human verification step (e.g., CAPTCHA). This INFT functions as a direct ownership authentication token, cryptographically bound to a specific wallet and configurable with conditions such as expiration, scope, and permissions.

Once issued, the INFT can be reused across multiple actions without repeating human verification. For example, A developer who has already completed CAPTCHA once can use their INFT to request testnet faucet funds repeatedly without re-authentication. The same INFT can authorize access to advanced developer tooling, such as inference fine-tuning, storage configuration, and custom build generation.

In our devtool builder, each generated INFT contract becomes an active authorization agent that governs how and where a developer can interact with the 0G stack. Permissions encoded in the INFT dynamically adjust available features across the broader developer suite.

As a result, the INFT serves both as a true proof of human ownership, resistant to bots and Sybil attacks, and a programmable on-chain identity primitive that automates authentication, permissions, and build customization across the 0G network.

This approach eliminates repeated friction (e.g., CAPTCHA loops), while enabling scalable, human-verified access to decentralized developer infrastructure.

**Best Developer Tooling or Education**

We supply a full suite of developer tools, including a quick-start CLI allowing developers to set up and experiment with 0G technologies (iNFTs, AI inference/fine-tuning, storage) plus a comprehensive skills repository to contextualize developer AI agents. The CLI is mirrored with a web-based sandbox that makes getting your feet wet with 0G features easy and meaningful, further accelerating the onboarding process. 

The team behind Velocity wholeheartedly believes that the potential of 0G's platform can be further adopted with the product we have submitted. Our repository has an open-source license from MIT allowing your platform to integrate Velocity into your dev-tooling suite.

### Proof of Human — End to End Plan
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/proof-of-human-end-to-end-plan-b804) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/kreloaded/eth-denver-2026) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Proof of Human — End to End Plan

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Swift](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![SwiftUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/SwiftUI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The internet does not know who is human anymore.

Bots farm airdrops. Scripts manipulate governance votes. Sybil accounts drain incentives. AI agents generate fake engagement at scale. Platforms either:

Require invasive identity checks (KYC, biometrics, passports)

Rely on weak signals like CAPTCHAs

Accept being exploited by automated actors

Today, you must choose between privacy and proof.

If you prove you are human, you usually reveal:

Your legal identity

Your location

Your device fingerprint

Your behavioral data

If you protect your privacy, you cannot reliably prove you are a unique human.

There is no native, privacy-preserving, reusable “human layer” for crypto and the internet.

Proof of Human solves this by allowing someone to prove they are a real, unique human without revealing who they are, where they were, or any raw personal data.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

1. Running ZK proofs natively on iOS
Integrating mopro (a Rust-based ZK prover) into an iOS app was non-trivial. The circuit had to be transpiled from WASM to Rust using rust-witness, compiled to a static .a library for both aarch64-apple-ios and aarch64-apple-ios-sim, then packaged into an XCFramework. Any change to the circuit meant rebuilding the entire xcframework from scratch.

2. Swift Package Manager conflicts
We initially used WalletConnect (reown-swift) for wallet signing. It pulled in swift-crypto 2.x, which silently broke secp256k1.swift 0.12.2 - the library relied on internal types (DigestSigner, SecureBytes) that were removed in the newer version. The error messages were cryptic and pointed nowhere near the real cause. We resolved it by removing the WalletConnect dependency entirely and routing transaction signing through the Node.js backend using ethers.js.

 4. Poseidon hash consistency across stacks
 The ZK circuit uses Poseidon hashing (BN254 field). We needed the same hash values produced by the circuit, the on-chain verifier, and the iOS app. Getting circomlibjs, snarkjs, and the Rust poseidon-bn128 FFI to agree on field representation took significant debugging - one wrong BigInt encoding produces a completely wrong hash with no obvious error.

5. ERC-7702 transaction signing on iOS
The original plan was to use ERC-7702 (type-0x04 transactions) so a relayer could submit the proof while msg.sender appeared as the user's own
EOA - enabling gasless UX. However, implementing raw EIP-7702 transaction signing in Swift turned out to be a deep rabbit hole: the secp256k1
Swift package conflicts, no native RLP encoder for type-0x04 transactions, and the recoverable ECDSA signature (needed for the recovery ID v)
not being cleanly exposed by any Swift library we could use without pulling in conflicting dependencies.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Claude Code (Anthropic) was used as the primary development agent throughout this project — not just for code generation, but as an active pair
  programmer managing the full stack across iOS (Swift), Rust (mopro/FFI), Solidity (Foundry), and Node.js simultaneously.

  Specific contributions:

  - Circuit design — Iterated on the Circom ZK circuit structure, deciding which signals should be public vs private and how to encode the
  deviceCommitment = Poseidon(device_attest_key, walletAddress) binding
  - Smart contract development — Wrote and deployed HumanityVerifier, HumanityToken, Groth16Verifier, and ProofDelegator to Sepolia via Foundry
  - iOS app architecture — Designed the full Swift service layer (ProverService, ChainService, StampService, PoseidonBridge) and wired them
  together with SwiftUI views
  - Debugging SPM conflicts — Diagnosed and resolved the secp256k1.swift vs swift-crypto 2.x conflict that blocked the entire iOS build
  - mopro integration — Managed the circuit compilation pipeline: WASM → Rust witness → static library → XCFramework, and debugged the proof
  format differences between mopro's output and snarkjs's Solidity ABI encoding convention
  - Backend API — Built the Node.js proof server with Poseidon hashing, proof generation, verification, and on-chain submission endpoints

  The project itself also explores a future where AI agents will consume this proof — using the on-chain soulbound token as a trust signal to
  distinguish human users from autonomous agents in smart contract interactions.

**Devtopia**

Proof of Human — End to End Plan

### Base Realms
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/base-realms-b63a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/zickrian/Base-Realms) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://baserealms.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RtsQ3n32NZs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Discover monsters across the realms!

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem**
Most onchain applications still push users toward speculative behavior, where participation is tightly coupled with price movements, token volatility, and trading risk. This creates hesitation, especially for users who simply want to play, interact, or explore without worrying about financial exposure.
In many NFT-based games, this issue is amplified by **opaque reward mechanics**:
- Minting, randomness, and payouts are often blended into a single flow  
- Players cannot clearly see where value goes  
- It’s difficult to verify whether outcomes are fair or skill-based  

At the same time, **Base offers powerful primitives** for low-cost, consumer-grade onchain apps. However, there are still limited examples that demonstrate how these primitives can be used to build **transparent, skill-driven, non-financial-first experiences**.

**How Base Realms Solves This**
Base Realms is designed from the ground up to separate **ownership, participation, and rewards** into clean, understandable layers, removing speculation from the core gameplay loop.

**Clear Asset Ownership With ERC Standards**

ERC-721 Characters (Unique Identity) 
- Each character is a unique onchain identity  
- Fixed traits, progression history, and battle records  
- One character = one soul of the player inside Base Realms  

ERC-1155 Items (Mint - Burn Items)
- Items can be minted (unlimited no cap)
- Items have traits to boost the Fixed trait

Players can **own a unique hero** and Trade it freely.

**Minting for Ownership, Not Gambling**
Minting in Base Realms is a **one-time action** to acquire a playable character, not a lottery.
- Mint fees are **not** distributed as instant rewards  
- Fees are allocated as liquidity for the **ETH / IDRX pair**  

Liquidity is:
  - Locked for long-term ecosystem stability  
  - Gradually unlocked  
  - Partially routed into **seasonal reward pools**  

Players mint to **play and progress**, not to chase RNG payouts.

**Battles as the Economic Engine**
Battles are the heart of Base Realms and the **only active value generator**.
Each battle requires a small entry fee  
Players can choose to pay with:
  - IDRX  
  - USDC  
  - ETH  

All battle fees flow directly into an **onchain reward pool**
Rewards are distributed **per season** to:
  - Top leaderboard players  

Value is created through **skill, consistency, and mastery**, not speculation.

**Transparent and Verifiable Rewards**
Every economic rule in Base Realms is enforced by smart contracts on Base:
- Battle fees are pooled fully onchain  
- Leaderboard calculations follow deterministic logic

Seasonal reward distribution is:
  - Automatic  
  - Auditable  
  - Permissionless  

No manual intervention, No offchain discretion, Fairness is **verifiable, not promised**.

**Onboarding Crypto Normies With QRIS**
Base Realms is designed to onboard **non-crypto users first**.
- Players scan **QRIS** directly inside the game  
- Payment is instantly converted to **IDRX onchain**  
- IDRX is delivered to the player’s in-game wallet  

Players can immediately:
  - Enter battles  
  - Mint cards  
  - Progress gameplay  

**Scan > Play > Learn crypto naturally through gaming.**
No exchanges.  
No seed phrase anxiety.  
No DeFi knowledge required.

**Accessible Participation With Reduced Risk**
Players choose their own comfort level:
**IDRX**  
  - Familiar pricing for local users  
  - Ideal for casual and first-time players  
**USDC**  
  - Stable value  
  - Predictable battle costs  
**ETH**  
  - Native crypto option  
  - Seamless for onchain-native users  
Participation is decoupled from speculation.

**Onchain Gameplay, Not Financial Abstraction**
All blockchain interactions are embedded inside a **16-bit, platformer-inspired world**.
Players explore instead of navigating dashboards:
- Battle zones to compete
- Shop to mint ERX-721 cards
- Home areas to manage characters  

Onchain actions feel like **game mechanics**, not financial transactions.
**Social Onboarding Through Base**
Progress extends beyond the game itself.
Battle results and milestones can be shared to:
  - Base App Social  
  - Farcaster  
Gameplay becomes:
- Social proof  
- Organic discovery  
- A living feed of onchain activity  

Players don’t market Base Realms, they **show what they’ve earned**.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Designing Fair Randomness Without Turning Gameplay Into Gambling**
One of the biggest challenges was implementing randomness for card traits while avoiding the perception of gambling or opaque outcomes.
Pure onchain randomness is expensive and limited, while offchain randomness introduces trust assumptions. We needed a system that was verifiable, cost-efficient, and fair.
How we solved it:
We implemented an onchain-seeded randomness model using commit–reveal mechanics combined with deterministic game logic. Trait generation is verifiable onchain, while outcomes are constrained so that randomness affects variety, not player advantage. Rewards are not tied to mint outcomes but to seasonal performance, reducing speculative incentives.

**Separating Onchain and Offchain Game Logic Without Breaking Trust**
Running full battle simulations onchain would be prohibitively expensive and slow, but moving everything offchain risks cheating or manipulation.
How we solved it:
We split responsibilities clearly:
- Offchain logic handles battle simulation
- Onchain contracts handle state commitments, fee deposits, result finalization, and reward distribution

Battle results are only accepted if they follow deterministic rules enforced by smart contracts. This preserves fairness while keeping gas costs low.

**Multi-Currency Battle Fees With a Single Reward Pool**
Supporting ETH, USDC, and IDRX for battle fees introduced complexity in accounting and reward distribution. We needed to ensure that value flowed into a single, coherent seasonal pool without creating inconsistencies or arbitrage issues.
How we solved it:
All battle fees are normalized onchain before entering the reward pool. Contracts enforce clear conversion and accounting rules so that leaderboard rewards are distributed fairly regardless of the currency used to enter battles.

**NFT Utility Without Inventory Fragmentation**
Using ERC-721 and ERC-1155 for unique character and items plus introduced challenges in tracking ownership, and in-game utility without overloading the contract with unnecessary state.
How we solved it:
We separated metadata and gameplay state. ERC-721 and ERC-1155 handles ownership and transferability, while gameplay attributes are referenced via onchain mappings and offchain indexing. This keeps contracts lightweight while maintaining verifiable ownership.

**UX Friction for First-Time Onchain Users**
Even with Base’s low fees, wallet popups, confirmations, and unfamiliar flows can break immersion for players who are new to crypto.
How we solved it:
We used OnchainKit and wallet abstraction to minimize user friction. Transactions are contextual and explained through gameplay actions rather than financial terminology. Users focus on playing the game, while blockchain interactions stay in the background.

**Base Track**

Base Realms is a fully onchain 2D card-based RPG built on Base, designed to onboard new users into onchain experiences through gameplay rather than trading.

While many Web3 applications focus on DeFi complexity, Base Realms reframes onchain interaction as a familiar game loop: mint a character, equip items, explore the world, and participate in battles. Players interact with smart contracts without needing prior crypto knowledge, lowering onboarding friction for retail users.

We deeply integrates Base infrastructure:
- ERC-721 characters with onchain stats (HP & Attack)
- ERC-1155 Items
- Low-cost, fast Base L2 transactions enabling frequent in-game actions
- Base-friendly UX patterns suitable for Mini-Apps

By turning onchain logic into a game mechanic rather than a financial product, Base Realms demonstrates how Base can support consumer-grade applications that feel intuitive, accessible, and engaging.

**The problem it solves**

## How MiniGarage Makes Collecting Easier

### 1. Easier Access to Collectibles

**Traditional Way**  
Collectors must visit physical stores, wait for restocks, or rely on limited events.

**With MiniGarage**  
Users can collect cars digitally anytime through daily rewards, assembly mechanics, or blind-box purchases—no physical hunting required.

**Result**  
Anyone can start collecting, regardless of location or experience.

---

### 2. Lower Risk of Counterfeits

**Traditional Way**  
Buyers rely on seller reputation, photos, and personal judgment—counterfeits are common.

**With MiniGarage**  
Each collectible has a verifiable digital record. Physical redemption is only possible by burning its digital counterpart, preventing duplication or fraud.

**Result**  
Guaranteed authenticity and clear ownership history.

---

### 3. Safer Buying and Selling

**Traditional Way**  
Secondary market trading is fragmented, slow, and risky.

**With MiniGarage**  
Users can trade digital representations of collectibles instantly, without shipping risks. Physical delivery only happens when the owner decides to redeem.

**Result**  
Faster trades with reduced fraud and logistics risk.

---

### 4. More Engaging Collecting Experience

**Traditional Way**  
Collecting is mostly passive—buy, store, and wait.

**With MiniGarage**  
Collectors earn fragments, complete blueprints, assemble cars, and unlock rewards through gameplay-like mechanics.

**Result**  
Collecting becomes interactive, rewarding, and fun.

---

### 5. Better Liquidity for Physical Assets

**Traditional Way**  
Physical collectibles are hard to sell quickly or partially.

**With MiniGarage**  
Fragments and completed cars can be traded independently, giving collectors more flexibility and pricing transparency.

**Result**  
Collectibles become more liquid and easier to monetize.

---

## Who Is MiniGarage For?

- Casual collectors who want a simple, safe way to start  
- Experienced collectors who care about authenticity and resale  
- Online buyers who want physical items without offline risk  
- Non-crypto users who want real products, not speculation  

---

## One-Line Summary

**BaseWheels makes physical die-cast collecting easier, safer, and more accessible by combining digital ownership with guaranteed physical delivery.**

**Challenges we ran into**

### Handling Gasless Minting with a Mock Payment Token

One major hurdle we faced was designing a gasless minting flow while still preserving a meaningful payment and scarcity mechanism. To improve onboarding, we decided to use a backend-controlled wallet to mint NFTs so users do not need to pay gas fees. However, this introduced a challenge when integrating IDRX as the payment token, since IDRX is only available on mainnet.

To continue development and testing, we introduced a mock IDRX token. This created a secondary issue: users could claim mock tokens from a faucet, use them to spin the gacha, and the tokens would accumulate in the treasury. Automatically burning these tokens from the treasury would break the transparency and user-driven nature of the system.

We solved this by shifting the burn responsibility to the user. When a user initiates a spin, they must explicitly confirm a burn transaction that reduces their mock IDRX balance. The backend then verifies the burn transaction onchain, and only after successful verification does it mint the NFT using the backend wallet.

This approach preserves gasless minting for users, avoids centralized token burning, and maintains a transparent and verifiable payment flow. It also closely mirrors how the system would work with a real payment token on mainnet, making the architecture production-ready.

**Base Track**

MiniGarage is a Base Mini-App that delivers an easy, secure, and engaging die-cast collecting experience through a Collect, Build, and Own approach. Users can gather car fragments through daily rewards or gacha, assemble them into complete car units via an assembly system, and own or trade them digitally before ultimately redeeming the physical version. The entire flow is designed to feel like a familiar collecting activity, without requiring any technical Web3 knowledge.

Through onchain mechanics, MiniGarage ensures transparent ownership, asset authenticity, and secure physical redemption via a burn-to-ship process. Marketplace and fragment trading features improve liquidity for physical collectibles, while gamification keeps users engaged over time. By abstracting complex onchain processes into simple, intuitive actions, MiniGarage directly addresses onboarding, accessibility, and trust challenges targeted by the Base Track.

Built on Base L2, MiniGarage leverages fast, low-cost transactions to support frequent interactions such as fragment claims, assembly, and peer-to-peer trading. Integration with OnchainKit and Base SDKs enables a smooth, retail-friendly Mini-App experience, aligned with Base’s vision of making onchain experiences more inclusive and accessible.

### AuthentiChain++
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/authentichain-0869) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Neurvinch/supply-chain-web3.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://supply-chain-web3.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/OGeP0ReRtFA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> One Scan, Zero Doubt

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Counterfeit products kill people and destroy brands.**

The global counterfeit market is worth **$3 trillion annually**. According to the World Health Organization, **10% of all pharmaceutical products worldwide are fake** — leading to tens of thousands of deaths annually. Beyond medicines, counterfeit car parts, electronics, luxury goods, and even food products endanger consumers while costing legitimate brands hundreds of billions.

**The core problem:** At the point of purchase, consumers have **NO reliable way** to verify if a product is genuine. Existing solutions are B2B inventory tracking systems that help companies manage stock — but don't help everyday shoppers make confident purchasing decisions.

**What AuthentiChain++ does:**

- **Instant Product Verification** — Anyone can scan a product's QR code and instantly see its authenticity verified on the blockchain
- **Trust Score (0-100)** — Complex blockchain data converted into a simple, memorable number anyone can understand
- **Fraud Detection** — Automatic alerts for missing supply chain steps, timeline violations, and geographic impossibilities
- **No Wallet Required** — Consumer-first approach; no crypto knowledge needed to verify products
- **Visual Journey Timeline** — See the complete product journey from factory to store

**Use Cases:**

- A shopper scanning a luxury handbag at a market to verify it's genuine before purchasing
- A pharmacy customer verifying medicine authenticity to ensure safety
- A consumer checking if car parts are OEM before installation
- Brands proving product authenticity to build consumer trust

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Gas Efficiency for Mass Production

**Challenge:** ERC-721 NFTs require one transaction per product unit — impossibly expensive for brands producing thousands of items. A batch of 10,000 products would cost thousands in gas fees.

**Solution:** Implemented **ERC-1155 multi-token standard** where one NFT represents an entire product batch. Token ID = Batch ID, and quantity tracks units. This reduced gas costs by ~99% for mass production while maintaining individual product traceability through QR codes.

### 2. Making Blockchain Data Human-Readable

**Challenge:** Raw blockchain data (transaction hashes, block numbers, event logs) is meaningless to average consumers. Showing this directly would create confusion, not trust.

**Solution:** Built a **Trust Score Algorithm (0-100)** that converts complex on-chain data into a simple number:

```
Total Score = Manufacturer Verification (40) + Logistics Chain (30) + Retail Verification (20) + No Anomalies (10)
```

- **80-100 (Green):** Authentic — Safe to buy
- **50-79 (Yellow):** Suspicious — Proceed with caution
- **0-49 (Red):** Likely Fake — Do not buy

### 3. Detecting Sophisticated Fraud Patterns

**Challenge:** Counterfeiters could copy QR codes or fake supply chain data. Simple verification wasn't enough.

**Solution:** Built a **rule-based Fraud Detection Engine** with 7+ checks:

- Timeline violations (retail scan before warehouse)
- Missing supply chain steps
- Impossible routes (traveling faster than aircraft speed using Haversine formula)
- Unusual scan frequency patterns
- Unverified manufacturer detection

### 4. IPFS Integration for Metadata Storage

**Challenge:** Storing product images and certificates on-chain is prohibitively expensive, but off-chain storage isn't tamper-proof.

**Solution:** Used **IPFS for decentralized storage** with content hashes stored on-chain. This provides tamper-proof verification (any metadata change alters the hash) while keeping costs minimal.

### 5. Mobile App Navigation with React Navigation

**Challenge:** Implementing proper authentication flow and navigation in React Native with conditional rendering based on auth state.

**Solution:** Created a clean navigation structure with `AppNavigator` that conditionally renders `AuthStack` or `MainStack` based on authentication context, using `AsyncStorage` for session persistence.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

## The Seed Phrase Problem

Every crypto wallet today forces users to backup a 12-24 word recovery phrase. This creates a fundamental UX barrier:

- **23% of all Bitcoin is lost forever** (~$140B) because people forgot, lost, or never properly stored their seed phrases
- **29% of crypto users** have lost access to funds at some point
- New users are immediately confronted with security anxiety before they can even use their wallet
- The choice is brutal: memorize random words, trust a custodian, or risk losing everything

## What Forgetless Wallet Does

**Forgetless Wallet replaces seed phrases with your fingerprint.**

Instead of writing down 12 words and hiding them somewhere "safe," you authenticate with the biometrics already on your device - fingerprint, Face ID, or PIN. Your cryptographic keys are stored in your device's secure enclave (the same technology protecting your Apple Pay and Google Pay), and automatically sync across your devices via iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager.

## How It Makes Crypto Easier & Safer

### For New Users

- **Zero onboarding friction** - Create a wallet in seconds with just a fingerprint scan
- **Nothing to memorize** - No seed phrases, no passwords, no recovery codes
- **Familiar experience** - Works like logging into your banking app

### For Experienced Users

- **Non-custodial security** - Your keys never leave your device's hardware security module
- **Phishing resistant** - Passkeys are cryptographically bound to the correct website
- **Cross-device access** - Your wallet syncs automatically between phone, tablet, and laptop

### For Sending & Receiving

- **Deposit from any wallet** - Friends can send you crypto from MetaMask, Coinbase, Trust Wallet, or any EVM wallet
- **Withdraw to anywhere** - Sign with your fingerprint to send funds to any blockchain address
- **No vendor lock-in** - Your funds are always accessible, not trapped in a proprietary system

### For Peace of Mind

- **No single point of failure** - Device lost? Your passkey is synced to your cloud account
- **Hardware-level protection** - Keys stored in tamper-resistant secure enclaves
- **Replay attack protection** - Every withdrawal uses a unique nonce and time-limited deadline

## The Bottom Line

Forgetless Wallet makes self-custody as simple as unlocking your phone. You get the security of a non-custodial wallet without the anxiety of seed phrase management. It's crypto the way it should have been from the start.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Parsing WebAuthn Signatures for On-Chain Verification

**The Problem:**
WebAuthn returns signatures in a format that Ethereum smart contracts can't directly verify. The P-256 signature from a passkey comes wrapped in CBOR-encoded authenticator data, and the public key coordinates are buried in a COSE key structure.

**The Struggle:**
I spent days trying to extract the raw r and s values from the WebAuthn response. The signature is ASN.1 DER encoded, meaning the length bytes are variable. A signature that worked on one test would fail on another because the r or s value had a leading zero byte that changed the offset.

**How I Solved It:**
I wrote a custom decoder that handles variable-length ASN.1 integers

## 2. Building the EIP-712 Challenge for Passkey Signing

**The Problem:**
The smart contract verifies withdrawals using EIP-712 typed data signatures. But WebAuthn doesn't sign arbitrary data - it signs a SHA-256 hash of `authenticatorData + SHA256(clientDataJSON)`. I needed to make these two worlds meet.

**The Struggle:**
The challenge has to be embedded in the `clientDataJSON.challenge` field as a base64url-encoded string. But the smart contract expects to recover a signer from an EIP-712 digest. Getting the encoding chain exactly right took many failed transactions.

**How I Solved It:**
I build the EIP-712 struct hash on the frontend exactly as the contract does

Then encode this digest as base64url for the WebAuthn challenge. The contract reconstructs the same digest and verifies the passkey signature against it.

## 3. Cross-Browser Passkey Compatibility

**The Problem:**
Different browsers and operating systems handle passkeys differently. Safari on macOS syncs to iCloud Keychain. Chrome on Android uses Google Password Manager. Some browsers don't support passkeys at all.

**The Struggle:**
Users on older browsers or unsupported platforms would hit cryptic errors. Firefox on Linux had partial support. Mobile browsers behaved differently than desktop. I couldn't just let users fail silently.

**How I Solved It:**
I built a `PasskeySupport` component that detects the environment before letting users proceed

Users on unsupported browsers see a clear message explaining what they need, rather than a confusing error after they've already tried to create a wallet.

## 4. Credential ID as User Identity

**The Problem:**
Traditional wallets use the public address as identity. But with passkeys, the credential ID is what identifies a user on-chain. This is a 64+ byte random value that's not human-readable.

**The Struggle:**
How do you tell someone "send funds to my wallet" when your identifier looks like `0x7f2a9c8b4d...` and is 150 characters long? QR codes help, but copy-paste is error-prone.

**How I Solved It:**
I built a `CredentialIdDisplay` component that:

- Shows a truncated version by default (`0x7f2a...8b4d`)
- Provides one-click copy to clipboard
- Generates a QR code for mobile scanning
- Shows the full ID on hover/click for verification

The key insight: treat it like a bank account number. Users don't memorize it - they copy it or scan it.

---

## Key Takeaway

The hardest part wasn't any single bug - it was bridging two different cryptographic worlds (WebAuthn and Ethereum) that were never designed to work together. Every step of the signature flow had to be carefully aligned between what the browser produces and what the smart contract expects. Getting it wrong meant silent failures with no helpful error messages.

The solution was always the same: understand exactly what bytes each system expects, log everything during development, and verify each step independently before combining them.

**Stomatrade** is an RWA-Fi (Real World Asset Finance) platform for the agricultural sector that delivers fast liquidity backed by real world assets. We connect farmers, aggregators (collectors), buyers, and investors within a transparent, traceable, and sustainable ecosystem.

By leveraging harvested crops as collateral, Stomatrade enables farmers and aggregators to access short term financing (±5 days) through a simple and efficient process. Investors can participate using stablecoins to earn short term yields backed by real world assets, while buyers gain access to verified and fully traceable supply.

Through asset tokenization, NFT based traceability, and smart contracts, Stomatrade builds trust across the agricultural supply chain accelerating cash flow, improving financial inclusion, and empowering local agriculture to compete in the global market.




**Problem Want to Solve**
The agricultural supply chain faces long standing challenges related to cash flow and trust. Farmers and aggregators require fast access to capital to sustain production and distribution, yet access to traditional banking remains limited due to strict requirements and slow disbursement processes.

On the other hand, buyers often operate with long payment cycles, despite their need for fast, compliant, and consistent agricultural supply. This situation is further exacerbated by the lack of reliable data and traceability systems, making it difficult for farmers and aggregators to obtain certifications, build trust, and access global markets.

As a result, aggregators lack sufficient working capital to absorb the full volume of farmers harvests, creating bottlenecks that hinder efficiency and slow the overall growth of the agricultural ecosystem.



**Stomatrade Core Solutions**
Stomatrade provides short term financing backed by harvested crops as Real World Assets, enabling farmers and aggregators to access fast liquidity within days. Through the platform, aggregators can apply for funding by using harvested crops as collateral, while investors participate by deploying stablecoins (IDRX) to finance verified agricultural projects.

Each harvest is tokenized and paired with NFTs issued to farmers, aggregators, and projects, ensuring full transparency and end to end traceability throughout the process. Once the buyer completes payment, funds are returned to investors along with profit sharing returns, while the platform generates revenue through service fees.

This model creates a fast, secure, and repeatable financing cycle delivering stable weekly cash flows while building trust across the entire agricultural supply chain.


**Value Proposition Stomatrade**
Stomatrade creates value for every stakeholder within the agricultural ecosystem. Farmers gain fast access to capital to sustain production without waiting for long payment cycles. Aggregators benefit from flexible working capital to optimally absorb harvests and ensure smooth distribution. Buyers gain access to legal, verified, and fully traceable suppliers, ensuring consistent quality and sustainable supply. Meanwhile, investors access short-term yield opportunities backed by real world assets, making investments safer, more transparent, and more sustainable.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Accessing Transaction Confirmation on Mobile Smart Contracts**
**Problem:**
The transaction confirmation flow behaves very differently between mobile and web platforms. On mobile, users are required to use a deep link to connect to the MetaMask wallet in order to approve transactions. This forces users to leave the app and switch to the MetaMask application, which significantly disrupts the user experience.

**Solution:**
To address this issue, we integrated a third-party service to implement account abstraction using Privy. With this approach, transaction signing can be handled directly within the application without redirecting users to an external wallet. This allows users to complete transactions seamlessly inside the app, resulting in a much smoother user experience.

**Learning:**
Through this process, we learned how to integrate account abstraction into a mobile platform. Previously, our Web3 experience was primarily focused on web-based integrations, so this project expanded our understanding of mobile-first Web3 architecture and user experience considerations.


**API Investment Issue**
The Investment API is not yet functioning properly due to transaction reverts from the smart contract. This issue occurs because users have not completed the required approval process for the smart contract. As a follow-up, the Investment API will be improved to ensure that users complete the approval step first before proceeding with the investment transaction.


**Deployment Limitation with Embedded Wallet**
The use of an embedded wallet introduces deployment limitations, as the project cannot be run in a serverless environment (e.g., Vercel). As a result, the application is currently deployed using a VPS with a self-managed domain.

> Where Reputation Becomes Collateral

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RainbowKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/RainbowKit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Alchemy SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Alchemy%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/40babd488d5a47bc99b82ae7d7f278b4/4674e59b-2e48-44d5-b866-d8bf0ee2ea3d.png)

Decentralized lending protocols today rely on a one-size-fits-all model that depends almost entirely on over-collateralization. Borrowers are typically required to lock 150% or more of the loan value, regardless of their past behavior, reliability, or activity onchain. This makes borrowing capital-intensive and inaccessible for many users.

At the same time, DeFi already generates rich behavioral data such as transaction history, repayment patterns, protocol interactions, and wallet longevity. However, this data is not used in lending decisions because there is no trustless and privacy-preserving way to verify it. As a result, DeFi lacks a native credit system.

This leads to poor capital efficiency, under-utilized liquidity, and limited lending growth. Responsible users gain no advantage, while lenders are forced to rely solely on excess collateral for risk management.

Pawtocol solves this by introducing onchain reputation as a credit primitive. Pawtocol enables credit-aware decentralized lending that improves capital efficiency without introducing trust assumptions or sacrificing decentralization.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Development — Alchemy Integration**

Integrating Alchemy’s onchain data and reputation signals into a real-time credit system introduced several challenges:
1. Data Normalization & Consistency
Alchemy provides rich onchain data across multiple dimensions, but transforming raw activity into consistent, credit-relevant signals required additional abstraction and filtering.
2. Latency & Real-Time Constraints
Credit scoring and lending decisions require near real-time updates, while onchain data indexing and retrieval are not always instantaneous.
3. Mapping Onchain Behavior to Credit Logic
Translating transactional data into quantifiable credit impact (risk weighting, score adjustment, collateral modifiers) required iterative modeling.

**How We Addressed It**
1. Built an intermediate reputation abstraction layer
2. Defined credit-relevant behavioral metrics
3. Implemented staged scoring (offchain aggregation → onchain commitment)
4. Designed extensible interfaces for future data sources

This challenge validated Pawtocol’s approach —
building credit infrastructure is fundamentally harder than building a lending app.

**Winner Classification**

– Introduces a new DeFi primitive
Pawtocol brings onchain reputation and credit scoring into decentralized lending—capabilities that existing lending protocols don’t natively support.

– Clear technical depth
The project goes beyond frontend and smart contracts, combining onchain data indexing, automated credit modeling, and reputation logic into a working system.

– Built to extend the ecosystem
Pawtocol is designed as infrastructure, enabling other protocols to build smarter, credit-aware lending on top of it.

Pawtocol fits this track by delivering real innovation, meaningful technical depth, and practical DeFi impact within a hackathon scope.

### Rowbo
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/rowbo-7b82) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/tomrowbo/dev-agency) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.rowbo.dev/imessage) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/0e8a81b177fd4339935ba9a7dd275760) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turn your business into a website in 30 seconds.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most small businesses are ran by non-technical people - and their entire online presence is on Airbnb, Instagram, or a Google listing and have no website of their own. They know they need one - it drives direct bookings (no platform fees), helps them rank in search, and makes them look legit - but actually getting one is a slog.

Normally you'd have to write code, push it to GitHub, deploy to Vercel, buy a domain from GoDaddy, and spend hours hunting for photos, writing copy, and laying out the page. Most homestay owners, cafés, and tradesmen are never going to do that - so they just don't, and leave money on the table.

Rowbo collapses that entire stack into a single conversation. We take a link from your existing social media profiles, and the agent scrapes your photos and details, builds you a real site, then lets you tweak it, and puts it live on your own custom domain - hosting subscription and domain both paid for - in the same platform. No code, no accounts, no juggling five providers.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest one was getting a Prava payment to actually complete after approval. We'd set up the mandate, the owner would approve with their passkey… and then nothing - the site never went live and no charge landed.

We were polling the session's payment-result to detect success, which is the right call for a one-off checkout. But for a mandate the session just sits at authorized forever - approval only authorises the mandate, it doesn't move any money. We only worked that out by pulling the Vercel logs (which surfaced a CHARGE_NOT_REPORTABLE error) and then hitting the Prava API directly to watch the session state stay stuck at "authorized" with no credentials issued.

The unlock was realising the money moves when you charge the mandate: POST /v1/mandates/{id}/charge issues the virtual-card credentials, and then you report the outcome to get visaConfirmation: SUCCESS. Prava's webhooks aren't live yet either, so we built the completion as a poll: after the card is sent, the agent watches for the freshly-approved mandate, charges it, reports it, and only then flips the site live - plus a tweak to handle the sandbox auto-settling the charge instantly. Once that clicked, the whole thing ran end to end: approve → charge → site live → confetti.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Rowbo is an AI agent initiating a real transaction on a user-approved, controlled Visa credential that buys domains and subscribes to hosting for websites. 

Prava mints a Visa virtual-card credential (token plus dynamic CVV) that the agent uses to complete the purchase on the owner's behalf. The result is verifiable rather than self-reported - a completed charge returning visaConfirmation: SUCCESS - which means our backend can continue with a domain purchase / deployment of their website.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Rowbo is a real working product that scrapes and generates users websites from their existing social media links. This is perfect for non-technical users like homestay owners, cafe's or even tradesmen - who want a site to portray their work, take direct bookings or even just boost their site rankings.

Now, we are getting ready to cold outreach to these businesses, with the subject line of "I built you a free website" - and they will just need to pay the £30/month hosting and any domain they choose to purchase. 

The underlying engine we built - multi-tenant site generation, real Stripe subscription billing at £30/mo, a self-serve editor, and automated custom-domain provisioning — is running today at rowbo.dev, and the hackathon layer adds the part that makes it a company worth scaling: an AI that can acquire and activate a customer entirely over text, collapsing "find lead → build site → close sale → go live" into a single conversation. 

We proved the whole path tonight end to end: a real owner (Chris) got a generated site, paid through Prava, and is now live on a genuine registered custom domain, chrishomestay.top (DNS provisioned, SSL issued, serving) - all from an iMessage.

**OpenAI**

The rowbo agent is built on OpenAI function-calling (gpt-4o). It runs the whole conversation and decides what to do at each step - when to scrape the listing from airbnb, build the site, send the preview, change the look, take the payment, and buy a domain - all through a set of tools we gave it.

It remembers the conversation, so a quick "yes" or "make it blue" always does the right thing without asking twice. From one inbound text, OpenAI takes the owner the whole way to a paid, live website - no forms, no dashboard, just the agent making the calls.

**iMessage Agent**

The rowbo agent lives entirely inside a iMessage thread over Linq - and allows users to build, deploy and buy domains all from a text. An owner texts us that they'd like a website, the agent asks for their Airbnb link, and from that single message it scrapes their listings, generates a real site, sends it back as a tappable rich-link card, takes edits by text, sells the subscription with a Prava checkout card, and puts the site live - all in Messages. 

We lean into Linq's native surface to make it feel alive: rich-link cards for the preview and the payment, tapback polls to choose a custom domain, confetti when the payment lands and fireworks when the domain goes live, typing indicators while it works, and HMAC-verified inbound webhooks driving the whole loop.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

Usually to create a website, you have to code, upload your code to github, deploy your codebase to vercel, buy a domain from GoDaddy, and spend hours alone finding the right photos, typing the right copy, and laying out your page how you like it. 

Imagine you could do all of that stack with one provider, through one iMessage conversation. That's how easy it is with rowbo.dev

> voltzz

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VoltShield AI solves the multimillion-dollar problem of industrial "silent killers"—microsecond power anomalies like voltage sags and harmonic distortions that easily bypass traditional fuses but silently destroy the sensitive logic boards of automated factory machinery (such as CNC units or robotic lines). By replacing slow, reactive manual troubleshooting with a high-frequency, multi-agent digital twin, the system utilizes an autonomous Plan-Act-Reflect loop running at 60Hz to detect electrical anomalies, calculate the mathematical inverse wave, and simulate a corrective power injection to stabilize the grid before equipment damage occurs. Plant managers can visually track this stabilization through a fluid, cyberpunk-inspired, dark-mode HUD optimized to render real-time telemetry at 60FPS without system lag, while an integrated GenAI agent eliminates days of administrative overhead by instantly translating millisecond-level telemetry logs into formal, engineering-grade insurance and utility compliance reports.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was ensuring that the autonomous agent could effectively stabilize the power system after anomalies such as voltage sag, harmonic distortion, and phase imbalance were introduced. Initially, the correction algorithms often overcompensated, causing instability in the balanced waveform. To overcome this, we implemented a feedback-based reflection mechanism that continuously measured residual error and adjusted the agent’s response dynamically. Another challenge was maintaining smooth real-time communication between the simulator and dashboard through WebSockets. We optimized the data streaming process and telemetry structure to achieve reliable real-time performance and consistent visualization across the system.

**Gen AI&ML**

VoltShield aligns with the Generative AI and Machine Learning track by demonstrating an autonomous AI agent capable of perceiving, reasoning, acting, and learning within a simulated power-grid environment. The system continuously monitors three-phase electrical signals, analyzes disturbances such as voltage sag, harmonic distortion, and phase imbalance, and decides the most appropriate corrective action without human intervention.

The project follows an Agentic AI architecture consisting of Plan, Act, and Reflect stages. The agent analyzes incoming telemetry data, evaluates system health, applies corrective strategies, and learns from previous disturbances to improve future responses. This mimics the decision-making workflow of modern AI agents.

From a Machine Learning perspective, VoltShield provides a foundation for training anomaly detection and predictive maintenance models using data generated by its digital twin environment. The simulator can create labeled datasets representing different grid conditions, enabling the development of classifiers and forecasting models for real-world applications.

By combining digital twins, adaptive learning, autonomous reasoning, and future ML-driven anomaly detection, VoltShield demonstrates how AI can move beyond simple prediction to intelligent decision-making and self-correcting system management.
