### RedLine
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/redline-f658) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vynride/redline) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://redline.vynride.dev) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SjL5Z8V1uUw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Crisis communication, practiced

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

When production breaks at 2 AM, an outage, a payment system double charging, a security breach, or a botched release, the hard part usually isn't the technical fix. **It's the conversation.** Talking a stressed VP off a ledge, calming an angry customer, running an incident bridge, and giving a clear status update *while the clock is running* is a skill, and almost nobody gets to practice it before it counts.

Teams drill the *mechanics* of incidents (runbooks, postmortems, on call rotations), but they rehearse the *communication* for the first time live, in front of the people who matter most. A runbook doesn't prepare you for a CTO asking "how long until it's fixed?" when you don't know yet. That gap is where incidents spiral: panic, vague answers, lost trust, and bad escalation calls.

**Redline is a flight simulator for crisis communication.** It drops you into a realistic, high pressure incident and an AI plays the other side of the call, an angry customer, a confused stakeholder, or an outage commander pushing for timelines. You respond **out loud, by voice, in real time**. The AI escalates when you fumble and calms down when you handle it well, so you feel the actual pressure of the moment instead of reading about it.

## What you can use it for

- **Onboarding and training**: Get new engineers and support staff reps handling incidents *before* a real SEV 1, in a space where mistakes are free.
- **Realistic, repeatable practice**: 25+ authored scenarios across production outages, payment failures, security breaches, broken releases, latency spikes, and support escalations, each at three difficulty tiers (warmup → production like → redline). The same incident plays completely differently as the pressure ramps up.
- **Practice *any* incident**: Describe a scenario in plain English ("Kafka cluster dropping messages during Black Friday") and Redline authors a brand new drill on the spot: the persona, the stakes, the facts they're hiding, the objectives, and the severity model.
- **Objective coaching**: After each drill you get a debrief that scores not just *what* you said but *how* you handled it across five dimensions: clarity, de escalation, information gathering, escalation judgment, and status communication, with concrete rewrite suggestions for your weakest turns.

## Why it makes things safer

Incident response is one of the few high stakes skills people are expected to perform well without ever rehearsing under realistic conditions. Redline turns crisis communication into something you can **practice deliberately, measure, and improve**, so when a real incident hits, the conversation is muscle memory instead of a first attempt. Better communication under pressure means faster resolution, calmer stakeholders, and fewer incidents that get worse because of how they were handled.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest problem was **latency**. Our pipeline runs mic → Saaras v3 STT → LLM reasoning → scenario state update → Bulbul v3 TTS → playback, and even small delays killed the sense of urgency. The whole point of Redline is that the conversation feels *live*, and a two second pause breaks the pressure instantly. We fixed it by **streaming both STT and TTS over WebSockets** instead of waiting on full request to response cycles. Audio starts transcribing as you speak and the persona starts talking back before the full reply is generated. That's what made the call feel real time instead of laggy.

The second hurdle was making the AI **feel like a real stakeholder under pressure, not a polite chatbot**. Early versions were too helpful, but real incidents involve people who interrupt, demand ETAs, and panic. We solved it with a **structured scenario engine**. Every incident carries hidden facts the persona knows but won't volunteer, escalation triggers, and severity progression rules. So instead of following a script, each persona reacts to *how* you handle them, withholding information when you're vague, escalating when you stall, and calming down when you take control.

We also wanted Redline to **remember how someone performs across sessions**. We wanted to track where they hesitate, escalate late, or go quiet under pressure. We used **PostgreSQL** to store transcript embeddings and behavioral patterns, turning each drill into data that sharpens future coaching, and hosted it on **Vultr**.

But the real challenge underneath all of these was **balancing technical realism with emotional realism**. We weren't just building a simulator. We were building *pressure*. Getting the AI to feel genuinely stressful while still being useful to learn from was the breakthrough that made Redline work.

**Vultr**

Redline's production stack runs on a Vultr VPS, fronted by nginx, with the full app deployed via Docker Compose and shipped through GitHub Actions CI/CD:

Host — Vultr: production VPS running the full Dockerized stack (FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Postgres)
Reverse proxy — nginx: routes traffic to the right container and terminates TLS
CI/CD — GitHub Actions: builds and tests on every push, then redeploys the containers to the Vultr box automatically

Redline ships from a single git push GitHub Actions builds and tests the stack, then deploys it via Docker Compose behind nginx on a Vultr VPS, taking the project from commit to live in minutes.

**Sarvam.ai**

Redline runs its entire real-time voice loop on Sarvam, with a single API key powering all three modalities:

  - STT - Saaras v3: transcribes the responder's speech (streaming WebSocket, WAV-per-turn).
  - LLM - sarvam-30b: the scenario brain. Drives live branching roleplay and the post-drill debrief via Sarvam's OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint with strict JSON-schema structured output.
  - TTS - Bulbul v3: speaks as the crisis persona, with emotion mapped to speaking pace and Indian-voice speakers.

  One line: Redline is an AI voice crisis-drill simulator built entirely on Sarvam's stack - Saaras (STT) + sarvam-30b (LLM) + 
  Bulbul (TTS) - closing the full mic → understand → respond → speak loop in real time on a single Sarvam API key.

**Open Innovation**

Redline is a voice-first crisis communication simulator. You speak in real time with an AI playing the angry customer, the panicking PM, or the CTO demanding "how long?" across 30+ scenarios covering outages, payment failures, security breaches, and broken releases.

incident.io, Rootly, FireHydrant they all detect and manage incidents. None of them train the humans inside one.

Built on Sarvam's speech and language models for the voice loop, every drill gets scored on clarity, de-escalation, info-gathering, escalation judgment, and status comms then debriefed with rewrite suggestions and hosted on Vultr with CI/CD.

It's not another incident tool. It's the flight simulator for incident response.

Team **The Cyphers** -- [Vivian Demello](https://github.com/vynride), [Aarpit Jethwa](https://github.com/Aarpitjethwa)

> Threat Detection and Defense System for Satellites

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keras](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keras-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![NLP](https://img.shields.io/badge/NLP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Space missions conducted by organizations like ISRO and NASA involve extremely high financial and strategic stakes, with satellites costing millions of dollars to design, launch, and maintain. These systems remain vulnerable to two critical risks: undetected system failures and sophisticated cyberattacks. Both can lead to mission degradation or complete failure, resulting in irreversible losses.

Existing infrastructures lack a unified, proactive framework for real-time anomaly detection and response. Additionally, telemetry data and system logs which are crucial for monitoring and post-incident analysis are often mutable, making them susceptible to tampering. This compromises forensic integrity, leaving investigators without a reliable trail to trace the root cause of failures or breaches.

ARGUS addresses these gaps through a 3+1 layered architecture that combines AI-driven detection with blockchain-based auditing. It enables:

1. Real-time anomaly detection across satellite subsystems using multi-layered AI models
2. Automated threat response mechanisms to mitigate failures before escalation
3. Tamper-proof logging using blockchain, ensuring immutable and verifiable telemetry records
4. Reliable forensic traceability, allowing precise post-incident analysis

By integrating intelligent monitoring with secure, decentralized auditing, ARGUS transforms satellite operations into a more resilient, transparent, and failure-resistant ecosystem saving space agencies millions of dollars.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was handling the overall system complexity. ARGUS combines multiple technologies, and getting everything to work smoothly together wasn’t straightforward. Blockchain was completely new to us, so figuring out how to use it for secure, tamper-proof logging took a lot of trial and error.

But the worst issue was RESOLVING MERGE CONFLICTS ON GITHUB.

**Ethereum Track**

Ethereum is actively used in the backend for the hybrid blockchain based audit logging system

**Open Innovation**

As we are implementing tech stacks from multiple domains, Open Innovation is the best fit

🔗 Wallet & Multi-Chain Handling

Managing wallet connections across different chains and ensuring accurate portfolio data was tricky.
Solution: Used Wagmi + multicall to batch requests and handle chain detection more reliably.

🤖 AI Strategy Accuracy

Getting meaningful and structured responses from Gemini was challenging initially.
Solution: Refined prompts and enforced a strict JSON output format for consistent, usable strategies.

⚡ Smart Contract Execution Flow

Handling token approvals + Aave supply in a seamless “one-click” flow caused UX and transaction issues.
Solution: Built a guided execution pipeline that checks allowance, estimates gas, and sequences transactions properly.

📊 Real-Time Data Sync

Fetching prices and balances without slowing down the UI was difficult.
Solution: Implemented caching and periodic refresh using optimized API calls.

💳 OrbitX Integration (Spend Layer)

Integrating a real-world spending layer with DeFi earnings required bridging two different systems.
Solution: Designed a modular integration (API/deep link) to simulate seamless “earn → spend” flow.

🎯 Key Takeaway

Balancing real-time blockchain data, AI insights, and smooth UX was the biggest challenge—but solving it made the product feel truly seamless.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### Problem
Training AI models requires large amounts of **human-labeled data**, but current data labeling platforms are centralized, take high commissions, and lack transparency in how tasks are evaluated and paid. Workers often receive low compensation, while companies struggle with trust, fairness, and efficient global participation.

### Solution
**SolveMint** is a decentralized platform where companies can post AI data labeling tasks and lock rewards in a smart contract. Workers complete these micro-tasks, and once a majority consensus is reached, the smart contract automatically distributes rewards to the correct contributors. This creates a **transparent, fair, and global marketplace for AI data labeling powered by Web3.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

- **Testnet Setup & Network Migration:**  
  Initially the project was configured for Celo Alfajores, but we migrated to **Celo Sepolia**, which required updating Hardhat configs, wallet chains, and deployment scripts.

- **Wallet & Network Integration:**  
  Ensuring **MetaMask and RainbowKit** correctly detected and connected to the Celo Sepolia network required custom chain configuration.

- **Consensus Logic Design:**  
  Designing a simple yet reliable **majority consensus system** to validate task results before distributing rewards was a key challenge.

- **Smart Contract & Frontend Coordination:**  
  Synchronizing the **Solidity smart contracts with the React frontend** for task creation, submissions, and reward distribution required careful handling of contract calls and state updates.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![ENS](https://img.shields.io/badge/ENS-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VCR Protocol (Verifiable Capability Routing) is the missing policy layer for autonomous AI agent payments sitting at the intersection of ERC-8004 agent identity, ENSIP-25 naming, and x402 HTTP-native payment rails. While existing standards give agents an on-chain identity and the ability to transact, nothing stops them from spending without boundaries; VCR fixes this by letting agent owners define verifiable JSON spending policies (capping transaction amounts, daily limits, allowed tokens, recipient whitelists, chain restrictions, and time windows) that are pinned to IPFS and resolved through ENS. Every payment attempt runs through a 9-step canAgentSpend() verification from ENS lookup and IPFS policy fetch all the way through expiry, amount, recipient, token, chain, and daily-limit checks  before a single wei moves. Built on Express 5, React 19, Solidity, BitGo multisig wallets, and Pinata IPFS, with 69 passing unit tests and a live deployment on Sepolia, VCR gives the agentic economy what it's been missing: cryptographically grounded, human-defined guardrails over how AI agents spend money.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we faced into:

BitGo wallet flow parity (Terminal vs UI): aligning backend API calls with SDK behavior, especially passphrase handling and runtime env differences.
Sepolia ENS integration: fixing ENS app navigation + ensuring all ENS links/records consistently target Sepolia.
Owner-signed policy updates: implementing secure signature verification so only owner/creator can publish policy changes.
Policy update propagation: making each policy edit generate a new IPFS CID, persist it, and sync ENS pointers correctly.
Policy vs Rules separation: resolving confusion between enforceable policy data and human-readable dDoc snapshots.
dDoc auto-refresh on policy change: ensuring “View dDoc” reflects latest policy version instead of stale CID content.
Document version history system: building full CID history (save, browse, view, restore) end-to-end with Mongo + IPFS.
Legacy compatibility/data migration: handling CID-to-document lookup and schema/index issues for older records.
TypeScript drift fixes: resolving server compile breaks from mismatched fields in incident/demo typing.

**AI**

Our project fits the AI track because it turns AI-driven automation into a verifiable onchain system instead of a black-box bot. In VCR Protocol, agents can act autonomously (e.g., payments/workflows), but their behavior is constrained by machine-readable policies (limits, tokens, recipients, time windows), resolved through ENS identity, and anchored to immutable IPFS/Fileverse document versions. Policy changes are owner-signed and auditable, so intelligence can evolve safely over time. This directly matches the track theme: combining AI + blockchain to build applications that are not just automated, but smarter, accountable, and production-safe.

**Best creative use of ENS**

ENS is the agent identity layer: each agent is anchored to a human-readable ENS name instead of opaque addresses.
ENS stores live policy pointers: your app writes records like vcr.policy / vcr.rules that point to IPFS CIDs.
Immutable + updatable design: policy/docs are immutable on IPFS (new CID per update), while ENS resolves the latest approved version.
Owner-governed updates: policy changes are owner-signed and permission-checked, matching ENS ownership/security assumptions.
Verifiable trust UX: anyone can resolve ENS → inspect policy/document state and history without trusting a centralized backend.
Testnet-ready ENS integration: flow is wired for Sepolia ENS

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

Keys stay protected: wallet generation/signing follows BitGo flow, so the app does not need raw private-key custody for normal operation.
Least-privilege access: agents get strict spend constraints (token, chain, recipient, per-tx and daily limits), reducing overexposure of funds and permissions.
Minimal on-chain disclosure: ENS stores pointers (CIDs/records), while detailed policy/doc content is versioned off-chain via IPFS dDocs.
Tamper-evident auditability: immutable CID history + owner-signed updates provide accountability without relying on mutable centralized logs.
Safe policy lifecycle: policy updates are controlled, signed, and restorable, which matches institutional privacy/compliance needs BitGo cares about.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Fileverse dDocs are first-class artifacts: policy/rules snapshots are rendered and managed as dDoc JSON, not plain text blobs.
Immutable document lifecycle: every update publishes a new IPFS CID (no mutation), matching Fileverse’s decentralized document model.
Built-in version history: your app stores CID timelines, lets users browse old versions, preview them, and restore prior states.
Transparent provenance: each version is timestamped/attributed, giving a clear audit trail for governance and compliance workflows.
Interoperable access: docs can be loaded directly from IPFS gateways and re-rendered in the Fileverse editor/viewer flow.
Practical Web3 UX: users get familiar “save version / view history / restore” controls while remaining fully content-addressed and decentralized.

> Reconnecting The Threads Of Life

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Hospitals in **India** often face *long patient waiting times* due to *inefficient queue* systems, high patient footfall, and sudden surges during festivals, seasonal pollution peaks, or disease outbreaks. Traditional hospital queues usually operate on a **first-come-first-serve basis**, which does not account for patient urgency or real-time hospital conditions. As a result, patients may experience delays in treatment while hospital staff struggle to manage overcrowded waiting areas.

**Rapide Retort** is a smart hospital queue management system designed to *reduce waiting times* and improve patient flow using a digital token-based queue system. When patients arrive, they are *registered and assigned digital tokens*, allowing hospitals to manage queues more efficiently and provide patients with estimated waiting times.

Beyond basic token management, **Rapide Retort** incorporates *machine learning and predictive analytics to support hospital staff during high-demand situations*. The system analyzes historical hospital records, environmental conditions, seasonal health trends, and festival calendars to predict patient surges and potential case types.

By combining digital queue management with predictive healthcare insights, **Rapide Retort** helps hospitals dynamically adjust patient queues, prioritize urgent cases, and allocate medical staff and resources more effectively.

The system offers:

• Digital token-based queue management for organised patient flow
• Smart prioritizations of patients based on symptoms and urgency
• Waiting time estimation to reduce uncertainty for patients
• Predictive analysis of patient surges using historical and environmental data
• Real-time triage recommendations for interns and nurses
• Dynamic staff and supply allocation suggestions during peak demand

Through these capabilities, **Rapide Retort** improves hospital efficiency, reduces waiting times, and ensures that critical patients receive timely medical attention.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/02a777d5eb6b4a86a5d851b454d14e65/328f3fd6-56df-4008-aa66-a883f5d32cd0.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles while building Rapide Retort was **integrating predictive analytics with real-time queue management**. Initially, our system could predict patient surges using historical and environmental data, but translating those predictions into actionable queue adjustments proved difficult. The challenge was ensuring that predictions did not disrupt the fairness and stability of the token-based queue system.

To solve this, we redesigned the queue logic to include a **priority scoring layer**. Instead of replacing the token order entirely, the system dynamically adjusts priority based on urgency indicators such as symptoms, predicted case severity, and current hospital load. This allowed the system to maintain a structured token queue while still prioritizing critical cases.

Another challenge was **handling incomplete or inconsistent healthcare data** during model training. Real-world medical datasets often contain missing fields or irregular formats. We addressed this by implementing data preprocessing techniques such as normalization, missing-value handling, and filtering unreliable records before feeding them into the prediction model.

Finally, designing a **user interface simple enough for hospital staff** was also a hurdle. Since nurses and interns may need to interact with the system during high-pressure situations, we focused on building a minimal dashboard that clearly displays token queues, priority alerts, and estimated waiting times.

By iterating on these issues and testing different approaches, we were able to create a system that balances **predictive intelligence with practical usability in hospital environments.**

**HealthCare**

**HCM-1004 – Hospital Queue Management System**

Rapide Retort directly addresses HCM-1004, which focuses on reducing hospital waiting times through a digital queue management system.

Our platform introduces a smart digital token-based queue system that registers patients through a digital intake process and organizes them based on urgency and hospital workload. Instead of relying on traditional first-come-first-serve queues, Rapide Retort uses real-time triage and prioritization to ensure that critical patients receive attention faster.

The system features a Real-Time Patient Triage Dashboard that continuously monitors incoming patients and classifies them into Urgent, Medium Priority, and Low Priority categories. This allows hospital staff to quickly identify critical cases and manage queues more effectively.

Key modules of Rapide Retort include:

- Patient Overview Dashboard for real-time patient monitoring

- New Patient Intake System for digital registration and token generation

- Health Issue Analyzer to evaluate symptoms and categorize urgency

- Stabilization Protocols Module that provides step-by-step emergency guidance for interns and nurses

- Predictive Analytics that forecasts patient surges using historical and environmental data

- Resource Management System that helps allocate staff and medical resources efficiently

By combining digital token-based queue management with AI-powered triage, predictive analytics, and emergency protocol guidance, Rapide Retort reduces waiting times, improves patient prioritization, and helps hospitals operate more efficiently during both normal and high-demand situations.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/02a777d5eb6b4a86a5d851b454d14e65/f8cb4e47-0b2b-4aed-92f8-8b4999a0eecc.png)
*Figure: Real-Time Patient Triage Dashboard showing patient prioritization, emergency alerts, and stabilization protocol guidance.*


**Scalability & Deployment**

Rapide Retort is designed as a cloud-deployable platform that can integrate with existing hospital information systems and scale across multiple departments or healthcare facilities. Its modular architecture allows hospitals to deploy individual components such as queue management, triage analysis, or predictive analytics independently based on their operational needs.

### Meridian
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meridian-6958) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Meridien-protocol/meridian) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://meridian-vote.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/50Ye2tUzcBg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Quantum Decision market

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Prediction markets have proven that skin-in-the-game produces better decisions than voting the stock market identified the cause of the Challenger disaster in hours while the official investigation took months. Futarchy proposed using this power for governance: vote on values, bet on beliefs. But traditional prediction markets fragment liquidity across separate YES/NO pools for each outcome. Every new proposal thins the pool further, making markets easier to manipulate and less informative. This is why futarchy never shipped.

Meridian solves the liquidity fragmentation problem by putting all competing proposals into a single unified pool, priced through LMSR (Logarithmic Market Scoring Rule) implemented as a Uniswap V4 hook. Users deposit once and that capital backs every proposal simultaneously. When the settlement window closes, the market collapses to the highest-amplitude proposal, and the winning strategy executes on-chain.

**What people can use it for:**

- **DAO governance** - Instead of token-weighted voting, communities can run quantum decision markets where proposals compete in a single pool. Capital-backed conviction replaces popularity contests. The winning proposal executes automatically.
- **Treasury allocation** - A DAO asks "how should we allocate this quarter's treasury?" Multiple strategies compete in one market. Participants trade on which allocation will maximize the chosen metric. The market converges and executes.
- **Agent-driven strategy selection** - Autonomous agents can propose, evaluate, and trade on competing strategies without human intervention. The agent generates proposals via AI inference, trades based on amplitude analysis, and executes the winning outcome.
- **Parameter tuning** - Protocols can use decision markets to set parameters (fee tiers, collateral ratios, emission rates) through market-based consensus rather than multisig decisions.

The key improvement over existing prediction markets: liquidity scales with the pool, not per-proposal. Adding a fifth proposal to a market does not split the depth five ways. It shares the same pool as the first four.

**Challenges we ran into**

**LMSR fixed-point math in Solidity.** The core pricing function `b * ln(sum(exp(q_i / b)))` requires exponentials and logarithms in WAD (1e18) fixed-point arithmetic. Solidity has no native floating point, so we built a fixed-point math library with 6th-degree rational approximations for `exp()` and 7-term series approximations for `ln()`. The main issue was accumulated rounding errors from cascading divisions. We had to clamp exponential inputs (overflow at `e^88 ~ 1.65e38`) and handle underflow at the lower bound to prevent zero-division in the logarithm. There are no formal error bounds on the approximation  getting this right required extensive testing against known LMSR outputs.

**Uniswap V4 hook state synchronization.** The `beforeSwap` hook intercepts trades and routes them through LMSR instead of the standard AMM curve. The tricky part: the hook must return a `BeforeSwapDelta` telling the PoolManager how much was consumed, but the actual cost comes from the LMSR calculation. If these diverge, the pool drains. We also had to disable standard `addLiquidity`/`removeLiquidity` entirely - all capital enters through a custom `deposit()` function because V4's native liquidity management doesn't understand LMSR positions.

**Cross-chain coordination across four networks.** The agent operates across Base Sepolia (markets), Base mainnet (swaps), 0G Galileo (compute + identity), and Kite AI testnet (payments). Each chain has its own RPC client, wallet, and failure modes. Early on, the x402 payment middleware was registered on the wrong chain ID `eip155:8453` (Base mainnet) instead of `84532` (Base Sepolia) which silently failed every payment attempt. The environment variable was also misnamed (`X402_FACILITATOR` in `.env` vs `FACILITATOR_URL` in code). These bugs were invisible because the agent gracefully falls back to direct on-chain calls when x402 fails.

**0G Compute inference reliability.** The 0G Compute SDK loads dynamically and can fail silently if the broker initialization races with the agent's monitoring loop. If the import fails once, the agent runs the entire session using deterministic fallbacks without ever retrying. We made the fallbacks context-aware - they parse the market question and metric type to generate relevant proposals instead of generic responses - but the lack of a retry mechanism means the agent may never use AI inference in a session where initialization fails.

**ERC-7857 iNFT transfer deadlock.** The oracle-verified transfer protocol requires three steps: owner initiates, oracle approves, anyone executes. We discovered there is no timeout or cancellation mechanism. If the TEE oracle goes down after a transfer is initiated, the token is permanently stuck in a pending state. The owner cannot retract the transfer. This is a known limitation we plan to address with a timeout-based auto-cancel.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Meridian's autonomous agent uses AI inference as its core reasoning layer for two critical functions: **proposal generation** and **trade signal computation**. Both run through [0G Compute Network](https://0g.ai/), a decentralized inference network.

### Proposal Generation

When the agent discovers a market with no proposals, it generates one using AI:

1. The agent reads the market's question and metric type from the on-chain factory contract
2. It constructs a prompt with the market context (question, metric type, settlement window, existing proposals)
3. The prompt is sent to 0G Compute, targeting one of three models:
   - **Qwen 2.5 7B** - fast, general purpose
   - **GPT-OSS 20B** - deeper reasoning
   - **Gemma 3 27B** - strongest capability
4. The model returns a structured JSON with a proposal description, target metric value, and reasoning
5. The agent submits the proposal on-chain via the QuantumMarketFactory

The AI is prompted to generate proposals that are specific, measurable, and tied to the market's metric type (predicted yield, token price, agent score, or custom).

### Trade Signal Computation

Every 30 seconds, the agent evaluates open markets and decides whether to trade:

1. It reads current amplitudes (probabilities) for all proposals in a market
2. It reads its own position and remaining deposits
3. It sends this state to 0G Compute with a prompt asking for a trade signal
4. The model returns a JSON with: which proposal to trade, direction (buy/sell), amount, and reasoning
5. The agent executes the trade through the Uniswap V4 hook

### Fallback Intelligence

If 0G Compute is unavailable, the agent does not stop. It falls back to deterministic strategies:

- **Proposal fallback**: Parses the market question with regex, matches against known metric types, and returns context-appropriate proposals (e.g., yield strategies for PREDICTED_YIELD markets, price targets for TOKEN_PRICE markets)
- **Trade fallback**: Momentum strategy - buys the highest-amplitude proposal with a fixed size (0.1 WAD)

### Payment for Compute

The agent settles inference costs through 0G's broker-based payment system. After each inference call, `processResponse()` is called to settle with the compute provider. The agent also earns revenue through x402 micropayments on its own API, creating a self-sustaining loop: external users pay the agent for services, and the agent uses that revenue to pay for AI inference.

### How the Components Work Together

```
External User/Agent
        |
   x402 payment ($0.01)
        |
   Meridian Agent API
        |
   +---------+---------+
   |                   |
0G Compute          Base Sepolia
(AI inference)     (on-chain execution)
   |                   |
Proposal/Signal   Factory/Hook/Registry
   |                   |
   +----> Agent executes trade on Uniswap V4
                       |
              Market collapses
                       |
              Base Mainnet swap
              (ERC-8021 builder codes)
                       |
              Kite AI payment log
```

The AI is not a chatbot or assistant. It is the agent's decision-making engine, it proposes strategies, evaluates markets, and drives autonomous trading. The agent reasons through markets the same way a human trader would, but at 30-second intervals with no downtime.

**Prosperia**

Meridian is a governance primitive built on a cypherpunk conviction: decisions should be made by markets, not committees.

**Governance without gatekeepers.** Today, DAO governance is broken. Token-weighted voting concentrates power in whale wallets. Multisigs create committees that mirror the centralized institutions crypto set out to replace. Snapshot votes are non-binding popularity contests. Meridian replaces all of this with a permissionless decision market where anyone human or autonomous agent  can propose a strategy, back it with capital, and let the market converge on the best outcome. No admin keys. No quorum games. No governance theater.

**Futarchy as a public good.** Robin Hanson proposed futarchy in 2000. Vitalik wrote about it in 2014. It never shipped because traditional prediction markets fragment liquidity across outcomes, making them thin, manipulable, and useless at scale. Meridian solves this with quantum decision markets, all proposals share one pool, priced through LMSR on Uniswap V4. This is the missing infrastructure that makes futarchy practical. The protocol is open source and permissionless. Any community can deploy a decision market for any question.

**Community coordination at scale.** Quantum decision markets are not just for DeFi. Any community that needs to make a collective decision, budget allocation, strategy selection, parameter tuning, grant distribution can use Meridian instead of voting. Participants put skin in the game. The market aggregates dispersed knowledge into a single actionable outcome. The Challenger disaster proved markets outperform committees at information aggregation. Meridian brings that power to communities.

**Autonomous agents serving communities, not corporations.** The Meridian agent is fully autonomous, open source, and self-sustaining through x402 micropayments. It generates proposals, trades on markets, and executes outcomes without human intervention. It is not a corporate product extracting rent, it is infrastructure that any community can run, fork, or build on. Agent identity is verifiable on-chain through ERC-7857 iNFTs, and every payment is logged transparently on Kite AI. No hidden extractors. No closed APIs. No trust required.

**The cypherpunk thesis:** cryptography and markets can replace institutions. Meridian is a working implementation of that thesis applied to collective decision-making.

**Best DeFAI Application**

The full loop ties 0G's compute and identity layers to on-chain DeFi execution. The agent discovers markets on Base Sepolia, reasons about them via 0G Compute, proposes and trades through a Uniswap V4 LMSR hook, and executes winning outcomes as real swaps on Base mainnet. Identity is anchored on 0G Chain, inference runs on 0G Compute, and all market activity settles on-chain. The AI is not a UI assistant -- it is an autonomous market participant with verifiable identity and decentralized intelligence.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

The autonomous agent's reasoning runs entirely on 0G Compute Network. Two inference pipelines proposal generation and trade signal computation - call into 0G-hosted models (Qwen 2.5 7B, GPT-OSS 20B, Gemma 3 27B) through the `@0glabs/0g-serving-broker` SDK. The broker handles provider discovery and payment settlement after each call. The agent pays for its own inference from x402 micropayment revenue, creating a self-sustaining economic loop: users pay the agent for market data, the agent pays 0G for intelligence.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

Each Meridian agent mints an ERC-7857 intelligent NFT on 0G Chain (Galileo testnet). The iNFT stores the agent's encrypted strategy state URI (referencing 0G Storage) and an on-chain strategy hash. To operate on Base Sepolia, the agent signs a cross-chain attestation `sign(keccak256(tokenId, baseWallet))`and registers it on the AgentRegistry contract. This links the verifiable 0G identity to the DeFi execution wallet. Transfers require oracle approval, preventing unauthorized agent identity theft.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Meridian uses Kite AI as the payment audit and identity layer for its autonomous agent. Every x402 micropayment is logged on-chain on Kite, and agent identity is registered on a dedicated Kite registry contract.

### x402 Payment Flow

The agent's Express API is gated by x402 middleware (`@x402/express`). Three endpoints are priced:

| Endpoint | Price | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| `POST /api/propose` | $0.01 | Submit a market proposal |
| `POST /api/trade` | $0.001 | Execute a trade |
| `GET /api/amplitudes/:id` | $0.0001 | Query proposal amplitudes |

When an unpaid request arrives, the middleware returns HTTP 402 with payment requirements. The caller pays on Base Sepolia via a Coinbase facilitator. Once the payment settles, the request proceeds no manual wallet interaction required. If a caller has insufficient funds or the payment fails, the middleware blocks the request and returns the 402 status with clear payment instructions. The agent never receives unpaid requests.

### On-Chain Payment Logging on Kite

After every successful x402 settlement on Base, the agent logs the payment on Kite AI testnet (chain 2368) via the `KitePaymentLogger` contract. Each record stores:

- **payer** / **payee** addresses
- **amount** paid
- **resource** the API endpoint that was called
- **network** the origin chain (e.g., `eip155:84532`)
- **paymentTxHash** the original Base Sepolia transaction hash
- **timestamp**

Logging is fire-and-forget: if Kite is unavailable, the payment still succeeds on Base and the failure is logged as a warning. The payment record is stored locally and the Kite log hash is backfilled when available. This gives full auditability without blocking the payment flow.

### Agent Identity on Kite

The `KiteAgentRegistry` contract on Kite AI testnet stores agent identity. Registration follows a cryptographic attestation flow:

1. Agent creates attestation: `sign(keccak256(iNFTTokenId, walletAddress))`
2. Agent calls `registerAgent(tokenId, attestation)` on Kite
3. Contract recovers the signer via ECDSA and verifies it matches `msg.sender`
4. Agent profile is stored on-chain with its iNFT token ID, wallet, and registration timestamp

This links the agent's 0G Chain iNFT identity to its Kite payment activity. Any external party can verify the agent is registered by calling `isRegistered(address)`.

### Public Stats Dashboard

The web frontend at `/stats` provides a real-time view of the agent's payment activity with no login required:

- **Agent identity** wallet address, ERC-8021 builder code, uptime
- **Wallet balances** Base Sepolia, Base Mainnet, 0G Galileo, Kite Testnet
- **Self-sustainability indicator** revenue vs. compute cost (green when profitable)
- **x402 payment flow** recent payments with payer, resource, network badge (Kite/Base), and transaction hashes
- **Kite vs. Base split** visual bar showing payment distribution across chains
- **0G Compute metrics** inference count, errors, active model

Stats auto-refresh every 15 seconds, payments every 10 seconds.

### Autonomous Execution

The agent operates with zero human intervention:

- 30-second monitoring loop scans markets, generates proposals, and executes trades
- x402 revenue is earned passively from API consumers
- Kite payment logging happens automatically after each settlement
- If x402 is unavailable, the agent falls back to direct on-chain transactions
- If a direct transaction fails (e.g., wallet unfunded), the agent logs the error and continues its loop without crashing

### Open Source

The full codebase is MIT-licensed: contracts (Solidity/Foundry), agent runtime (TypeScript/Express), and web dashboard (Next.js 15).

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

The Meridian agent is a self-sustaining autonomous agent built on Base. It earns its own revenue, pays for its own intelligence, and executes on-chain actions without human intervention.

**Revenue.** The agent exposes a REST API gated by x402 micropayments (Coinbase's HTTP 402 protocol). External users and agents pay $0.01 per request for market data, portfolio analysis, and trade signals. Payments settle on Base Sepolia through a Coinbase facilitator. Every payment is logged on-chain via a dedicated PaymentLogger contract for full transparency.

**Expenses.** The agent spends its revenue on AI inference through 0G Compute Network proposal generation and trade signal computation. The broker SDK settles each inference call automatically. The agent also pays gas for on-chain transactions: submitting proposals, executing trades through the Uniswap V4 hook, and registering its identity on the AgentRegistry.

**Autonomous loop.** Every 30 seconds, the agent scans open markets on Base Sepolia, evaluates proposal amplitudes, requests a trade signal from 0G Compute, and executes the recommended trade through the LMSR hook. When a market's settlement window closes, the agent triggers the collapse and executes the winning strategy as a real swap on Base mainnet. No human in the loop.

**On-chain execution.** All market activity runs on Base: market creation, proposal submission, LMSR-priced trading via a custom Uniswap V4 hook, position tracking, settlement, and post-collapse swaps. Every protocol transaction includes ERC-8021 builder attribution codes for Base ecosystem tracking.

**The economic loop:** users pay the agent (x402 on Base) -> agent pays for intelligence (0G Compute) -> agent trades on markets (Uniswap V4 on Base) -> agent executes winning outcomes (swaps on Base mainnet) -> agent earns more from better market data -> cycle repeats. The agent funds itself.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

Meridian integrates Uniswap at two layers V4 hooks for prediction market pricing and the Uniswap Trade API for real token swaps on Base mainnet.

### Uniswap V4 Hook (Market Pricing)

The `QuantumMarketHook` is a custom Uniswap V4 hook that replaces the standard constant-product AMM with LMSR (Logarithmic Market Scoring Rule) pricing. It imports `IPoolManager`, `Hooks`, `PoolKey`, `BalanceDelta`, and `BeforeSwapDelta` from `@uniswap/v4-core` and extends `BaseHook`. The hook intercepts swaps in `_beforeSwap()`, runs LMSR cost calculations, and returns a `BeforeSwapDelta` to the PoolManager with the computed amount. Standard `addLiquidity`/`removeLiquidity` are disabled all capital enters through a custom `deposit()` function because V4's native liquidity management does not understand LMSR positions. A `QuantumSwapRouter` handles flash accounting: it calls `poolManager.unlock()`, syncs collateral, and triggers the hook via `poolManager.swap()`.

This is not a standard token swap. It is a novel use of Uniswap V4 infrastructure to price competing proposals in a decision market.

### Uniswap Trade API (Real Swaps)

When a market collapses and a winning proposal is selected, the agent executes the outcome as a real token swap on Base mainnet through the Uniswap Trade API (`trade-api.gateway.uniswap.org/v1`). The integration uses three endpoints:

1. **`POST /quote`** get a swap quote with routing, gas estimates, and price impact
2. **`POST /check_approval`** check whether token approval is needed for the swap
3. **`POST /swap`** get an unsigned transaction with `methodParameters` (to, calldata, value)

The agent parses the winning proposal description (e.g., "allocate to USDC", "swap into WETH") to determine swap intent, resolves token addresses on Base mainnet (ETH, WETH, USDC, DAI, cbETH), requests a quote, and sends the transaction. Every swap transaction includes ERC-8021 builder attribution codes.

### Swap UI

The web app at `/swap` provides a user-facing swap interface on Base mainnet. Users select tokens, enter an amount, and get a quote from the Uniswap API (proxied through the agent). The UI displays routing details and gas estimates, handles ERC-20 approval when needed, and links to BaseScan after confirmation. Transactions are signed client-side via wagmi/RainbowKit.

### How It Fits Together

The Uniswap API is the execution layer that connects prediction market outcomes to real DeFi activity. Markets run on Base Sepolia using a V4 hook for LMSR pricing. When the market settles, the winning strategy executes as a real swap on Base mainnet via the Uniswap Trade API. The agent does this autonomously. Users can also swap directly through the web interface. Both paths use the same Uniswap API with server-side API key authentication.

### Secretariat
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/secretairat-766b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SrijanChallapalli/Secretariat.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DG0g9N39yvg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Onchain-terminal for racehorses

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Thoroughbred racing is a massive $115 billion industry, but it has a high barrier to entry, strong cultural and economic exclusivity, and the data that drives decisions (pedigrees, performance history, injuries, and breeding outcomes) is aggressively guarded. This data opaqueness is by design: owners and trainers intentionally hide medical records in restricted "Sales Repositories" to protect their betting edge and prevent algorithmic devaluation at auction. Valuations are often negotiated privately, and bloodlines live in disconnected databases or even paper records. This severe informational asymmetry makes it difficult for owners, breeders, and fans to price horses fairly, make breeding and investment decisions, and compete against legacy breeders and LLCs.

Secretariat is a high-fidelity DeFAI database and marketplace on the ADI Foundation network that turns registered racehorses into on-chain intelligent NFTs (iNFTs) with a verifiable pedigree and an AI-driven valuation agent. By replacing "handshake-based" valuations with cryptographic truth, people can use it to:

Track provable lineage and history: A 5-generation family tree, trait evolution, and network-effect events are all recorded immutably on-chain.

Get real-time valuations that solve the privacy paradox: Instead of demanding raw veterinary X-rays that ruin a trainer's betting edge, our 0G Labs verifiable AI ingests the physical data but outputs ONLY macro-health percentages (e.g., "Respiratory Health: 80%", "Breeding Potential: 90%") to the public market. Only the verified iNFT owner can decrypt the granular "why"—the specific words, explanations, and audit trails behind those scores. This maintains the industry's traditional "Repository Shield" for private data while giving investors the mathematical proof they require.

Make smarter breeding and investment decisions through incentivized honesty. The platform provides AI recommendations and projected ROI for breeding pairs. To navigate firewalled medical data, we pivot middlemen from "trust" to "cryptographic liability". Bloodstock Agents act as "Certified Curators" who receive an immutable 5% sourcing fee, but must stake $ADI tokens to certify a horse's medical standing. If subsequent public race performance or state regulatory filings contradict their report, their stake is programmatically slashed. Democratize access through fractional ownership: The platform offers SEC-compliant fractional equity via bankruptcy-remote Delaware Series LLCs on a KYC-gated ledger. We standardize financial primitives around breeding revenue (stud fees) and performance-based value changes, protected by a mathematically locked OpEx buffer to ensure the biological asset is always safely funded.

In short, it’s a “Bloomberg Terminal for Biology” with accessible data, automated valuation, and decision support, all tied to a verifiable on-chain asset rather than paywalled spreadsheets and closed networks. We provide investors with the mathematical models they demand, give regulators the transparency they require, and offer owners a valuation premium for verified biological integrity.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest hurdles was a visibility bug. After breeding, the on-chain transaction succeeded and our breed event executed, but the new horse still didn’t show up in the user’s Portfolio/LiveFeed, making it look like the mint failed. Tracing the full path from contract to RPC to frontend revealed a multi-step pipeline problem: cached contract reads (Wagmi/React Query) were serving stale state, our refresh logic had a race condition between refetching the horse list and checking ownership, some RPC responses lagged 1–2 seconds immediately after confirmation, and a hardcoded tokenID scan cap silently skipped higher IDs. We resolved this by invalidating queries on breed success, serializing the refetch order, adding a short polling retry loop with debug tracing, and removing the scan ceiling with a direct on-chain fallback. We refactored the minting code and set up logs/tracing so we could see exactly where the execution flow was stalling.

Separately, we ran into contract-level breeding reverts with opaque errors that initially made it seem like the contracts themselves were broken, when in reality we were missing prerequisites. After debugging the revert conditions, we found two root causes: our deploy/seed scripts weren’t pre-verifying deployer/test wallets (they never called KYCRegistry.verify()), so the breed() function consistently failed eligibility checks, and our UI’s “Approve ADI” step wasn’t reliably executing our adi approval function before purchasing breeding rights, leading to insufficient allowance reverts. We fixed this by updating the seed scripts to verify test accounts, implementing a proper approval flow with allowance checking, and adding clear error toasts for each failure mode (KYC not verified, insufficient allowance, breeding rights not purchased), which made the entire breeding experience predictable and demo-ready.

Another issue in general is the lack of mass data when it comes to pedigrees and biometric statistics. There are no public API's or free databases. This makes it difficult to populate our registry with many horses. We are currently using demo horses alongside some horses that we do have data for. Overall, this is a problem we can fix through licensing and future adoption of our product.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Secretariat uses AI/agent components to recommend breeding decisions, update valuations, and safely automate on-chain actions.
Breeding Advisor (recommendation agent): Given a mare, it returns the top 3 stallion matches with scores + explainability. Scoring blends heuristics (trait vector similarity, pedigree synergy, trait complement, budget/fee penalty, injury/form risk) and an XGBoost model that predicts expected offspring value. Output includes risk flags (e.g., high fee, injury, weak match). The UI calls /breeding/recommend, shows the “why,” and lets the user proceed manually or delegate execution.


Horse Valuation Agent: Computes a horse’s USD/ADI valuation with a clear breakdown (racing performance, breeding value, and modifiers like age/health/status). It’s used both for on-demand valuations in the app and as the intelligence inside the oracle workflow.


Oracle pipeline (event → valuation → chain): When real-world events occur (race result, injury, news), the system fetches current on-chain state, runs the Valuation Agent to propose an updated value, and commits the update on-chain (optionally persisting an auditable payload).


AgentExecutor (guardrailed automation): If the user enables automation, they sign an EIP-712 BreedingPlan (mare, chosen stallion, max budget, max stud fee, deadline, optional allowlist). The on-chain executor verifies constraints and then purchases breeding rights (if needed) + breeds to mint offspring. No funds move without a user signature, and execution is strictly limited by the plan.


How they work together: recommend (Advisor) → user reviews “why” → optional signed plan → on-chain execution (Executor) → valuations update over time via the oracle pipeline (Valuation Agent).

**New France Village**

Real-World Assets (RWA) + on-chain markets
Thoroughbreds are real, high-value assets (often worth millions) that currently trade in private, illiquid, relationship-driven markets. Our platform tokenizes horses as iNFTs with on-chain pedigrees and event histories, giving the average buyer valuations, and a marketplace layer for transactions like breeding rights and stud fees.
Bridging traditional finance concepts with DeFi primitives
We model horses like financial assets whose value changes with new information (wins, injuries, offspring performance), similar to how public markets price risk and fundamentals. Our AI agents power dynamic valuations and produce actionable financial outputs (e.g., stud fee guidance, breeding ROI forecasts), enabling DeFi-style mechanisms such as:
pricing + settlement of breeding rights in a tokenized marketplace


fractional ownership as a path to broader participatio


Compliance & policy-aware design (not “DeFi in a vacuum”)
This track explicitly values compliance innovation. Our system includes KYC gating and prerequisite enforcement for sensitive actions like breeding and marketplace participation. That’s a practical step toward institutional and regulated adoption, and it mirrors how real financial systems manage access control, eligibility, and counterparty risk.
Financial inclusion for a historically gated asset class
Ownership and breeding participation have traditionally been limited to insiders with large capital and privileged access. By creating transparent on-chain records and enabling fractionalization/standardized transactions, we open a path for smaller participants to gain exposure to an otherwise inaccessible market aligning with “Main Street” inclusion.
In short, Secretariat is the “future of finance” applied to a real economy: RWA tokenization + compliant access + transparent pricing + AI-driven financial decisioning, bringing an opaque, high-value industry onto Ethereum in a way that can scale toward both retail and institutional use.

**Best DeFAI Application**

Secretariat is a DeFi-style app built around a real economic workflow in a tokenized horse ecosystem: stallions can list breeding rights for a stud fee, users pay in ADI to acquire those rights, and the protocol executes breeding (mare + stallion) to mint an offspring NFT. On top of that, each horse can have a syndicate vault (buy shares, deposit breeding revenue, claim payouts), giving a complete financial loop: list → pay → execute → distribute.

The “AI” isn’t a chat layer, it’s a Breeding Advisor that makes the DeFi flow measurably better. The agent outputs structured decisions: a ranked set of stallion candidates with scores and a clear breakdown (trait fit, pedigree synergy, inbreeding risk, projected offspring potential). Those recommendations translate into a concrete execution-ready plan when the user wants automation.

User safety is built into the workflow. The system generates a BreedingPlan with explicit guardrails, max ADI spend, max stud fee, deadline, optional stallion allowlist, and trait thresholds, and nothing happens until the user reviews and signs it (EIP-712). The executor contract enforces those limits on-chain, so the agent can’t buy rights or breed outside what the user approved. The UI shows the “why” behind each recommendation and a preview of the exact action (selected mare + stallion + estimated cost) before the signature.

End-to-end demo scenario: connect wallet → select mare → “Get recommendations” → choose a stallion → set constraints (budget/deadline/limits) → sign the plan → executor performs purchase + breed → offspring NFT appears in portfolio (and revenue can flow into the horse’s syndicate vault).

We use 0G to make the AI component verifiable: the agent’s model bundle is stored on 0G Storage and referenced by hash/CID, and the system can attach 0G hashes to updates for auditable history. The result is a real DeFAI product where AI provides planning + guardrails + safe automation for a financial workflow, while the user retains full control at every step.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

On-chain ownership + identity: The agent is an iNFT on 0G Chain with an on-chain profile (name, version, specialization) and a pointer to its “brain” (model bundle). Only the iNFT owner can update that pointer when publishing a new model bundle.

0G usage (chain + storage): We deploy the agent iNFT on 0G Chain and store the model bundle on 0G Storage. The content hash/CID is recorded on-chain, so anyone can verify exactly which agent version is being used and fetch it from 0G.

Meaningful agent action (guardrailed execution): In “recommend-only,” the agent returns the top 3 stallion picks (off-chain scoring). In “execute-with-approval,” the user signs a Breeding Plan (mare, stallion, max spend/stud fee, deadline, etc.). Our AgentExecutor contract verifies the signature + constraints, then executes the workflow on-chain (buy breeding rights if needed → call breeding contract → mint offspring).

Composability: Other contracts can read the agent’s on-chain profile + model hash and can trigger the same execution path with a valid user-signed plan, making the agent reusable beyond our UI.

Verifiable state/history (bonus): We can attach a 0G storage hash to valuation/agent outputs so updates are auditable (“this update corresponds to this 0G snapshot”).

UI: Users can mint/initialize the agent, view its identity/status + model version, refresh from 0G, run recommendations, and sign a plan to trigger the on-chain breeding action.

**Open Project Submission**

Secretariat is a deployed RWA/tokenisation MVP on ADI Chain that brings a real-economy asset class, thoroughbred horses, on-chain with clear economic rights, cashflow rails, and institutional-grade controls. It is not a memecoin or gaming project; it is purpose-built for compliant, auditable adoption by stables, syndicates, and other professional operators.

1) RWA + Tokenisation 

We tokenise real-world thoroughbreds as on-chain assets and standardise the rights that matter economically:

Horse tokenisation: each horse is represented by an NFT with on-chain identity/pedigree/traits and valuation fields (an auditable asset profile).

Tokenised economic rights + cashflows: we tokenise breeding rights (stud access) and settle stud fees in ADI, turning an offline, relationship-driven process into an on-chain market.

Fractional ownership: each horse can have a syndicate vault that mints ERC-20 shares, supports revenue deposits (e.g., breeding income), and enables transparent claim/receipt distribution, making institutional syndication native on-chain.

2) ADI Chain as the primary execution layer (core requirement)

All key actions are executed and settled on ADI Chain:

Marketplace settlement in ADI: listing and purchasing breeding rights is paid in ADI (MockADI on testnet).

On-chain breeding execution: the protocol calls the breeding contract to mint offspring directly on ADI.

Vault accounting on ADI: syndicate shares, deposits, claims, buffers, and invoices are processed on ADI.

3) Institutional suitability (adoption + controls)

We designed for institutional deployment requirements: permissioning, auditability, governance, and operational risk controls:

Compliance-aware access: optional KYC gating for marketplace participation.

Permissioning & roles: role-gated oracle updates and executor permissions (e.g., ORACLE_ROLE, EXECUTOR_ROLE) to prevent untrusted inputs and support operational oversight.

Risk controls: configurable constraints for vault and execution (thresholds/limits) to support conservative operating policies.

Governance readiness: syndicate-friendly governance patterns so operators and LPs can manage policies transparently.

4) Live demo + test environment + public repo

Deployed and usable on ADI testnet with a functional UI oriented toward monitoring, execution, and auditability (portfolio, marketplace, breeding, vault/risk views).

Public code repository + docs with reproducible deployment/testing steps.

### Maiat
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/maiat-117a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/JhiNResH/maiat) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://maiat.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/COLhmJOhJ3I) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The trust layer for the internet.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every AI agent is about to start moving money, and we’re ignoring how easy it will be to manipulate them when they have no fucking clue who to trust.

In the near future, asking your AI to handle decisions will be normal:

“Find the best place to swap into ETH.”
“Book the highest-rated coffee shop nearby.”
“Buy this product at the best price.”

Your agent pulls from search results, review sites, and scraped data, all of which can be gamed with SEO tricks, fake reviews, botted engagement, and spam. Bad actors can very easily just manipulate what the agent sees, and the agent follows it blindly.

**hence Maiat a trust layer agents can query before they act.**

1. You make a purchase on-chain, say you buy a coffee.
2. Right after, Maiat messages you on Telegram: “How was it?”
3. You leave a review, which is verified and is then added to Maiat database.
4. The trust score then updates and the next person (or agent) asking where to buy gets an answer based on real experiences, not fake shit.

**Challenges we ran into**

The "5 chains, 1 weekend" problem

Integrating 5 different chain ecosystems (0G, KiteAI, Base, Hedera, Uniswap/Ethereum) in a hackathon is insane. Each has different SDKs, RPC quirks, and testnet faucet issues.

0G Compute — The 0G Serving Broker SDK had limited documentation for TeeML verification flows. We had to reverse-engineer the broker's expected request format by reading their Go source code. Ended up building a clean abstraction layer that handles provider selection and fallback gracefully.

Hedera HCS — Topic message submission kept failing silently. Turned out our transaction was hitting the max message size (1KB). Had to compress review attestation data and hash the full payload, storing only the hash + metadata on-chain with the full data in our DB.

Uniswap V4 Hook — Building a beforeSwap hook that queries an external oracle (our TrustScoreOracle) while staying within gas limits was tricky. We optimized by batching trust score updates off-chain and only storing the latest scores on-chain, so the hook does a simple mapping lookup instead of a cross-contract call during swap execution.

Chain mismatch bug — We accidentally deployed our on-chain review proofs to BSC Testnet instead of Base Sepolia. Caught it during end-to-end testing when the Base Verify integration couldn't find our contract. Quick fix but would've been embarrassing in a demo.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

In the product:

• 0G Compute Network — All review verification runs on 0G's decentralized AI inference. Models (Qwen 2.5, GPT-OSS, Gemma 3) analyze reviews for: content quality, spam detection, sentiment authenticity, and factual consistency. This runs inside 0G's Trusted Execution Environment (TeeML) so verification is verifiable and tamper-proof.
• Google Gemini — Powers the Telegram bot's conversational review flow. Users chat naturally with @MaiatBot, and Gemini extracts structured review data (rating, pros, cons, category) from free-form messages.
• Trust Score Engine — AI-computed composite scores combining: review sentiment analysis, on-chain activity correlation, reviewer reputation history, and cross-reference with market data (CoinGecko integration).

In the build process:• Claude Code (Anthropic) — Primary development agent. Built the entire Next.js frontend, all 5 chain integrations, and the smart contracts. Ran as autonomous background agents with specific tasks (one agent per integration).
• Codex (OpenAI) — Used for parallel code review and security auditing of smart contracts.
• AI-driven testing — Automated end-to-end verification of all bounty integrations using AI agents that simulated the full user flow.

The agents collaborated through a shared task board — one built features while another audited them. Human oversight on all merge decisions.

Shoutout-  Jensen Huang

**Futurllama**

AI agents are about to manage billions in autonomous transactions — trading tokens, paying merchants, allocating capital across chains. But right now, they have zero way to verify who they're transacting with. There's no trust infrastructure for the agentic economy.

Maiat is the reputation oracle AI agents query before every transaction. We combine five frontier technologies into one trust primitive:

• Decentralized AI verification (0G Compute) — Reviews are scored for authenticity by AI models running inside Trusted Execution Environments on 0G's decentralized network. No central authority decides what's trustworthy.
• Immutable trust attestations (Hedera HCS) — Every verified review is permanently attested on Hedera Consensus Service. Tamper-proof, publicly auditable, queryable by any agent.
• Agent micropayments (KiteAI x402) — AI agents pay per trust query using the x402 HTTP-native payment protocol. Machine-to-machine commerce with no human in the loop.
• Anti-sybil identity (Base Verify) — Real humans verified on Base. Bot farms can't game the trust scores.
• Trust-gated DeFi (Uniswap V4 Hook) — Our beforeSwap hook blocks trades on low-trust tokens and charges dynamic fees based on reputation scores. Trust enforcement at the protocol level.

The wild idea: What if every financial transaction — human or agent — had to pass a trust check first? Maiat makes that possible. We're not building another DeFi app. We're building the credit score system for a world where your AI agent does the shopping, and it needs to know who to trust before it spends your money.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

**0G — Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning:**

Maiat uses 0G Compute Network as the backbone of its trust verification engine. Every review submitted to the platform is sent to 0G-hosted AI models (Qwen 2.5, GPT-OSS, Gemma 3) running inside TeeML Trusted Execution Environments for authenticity scoring.

The AI analyzes reviews across four dimensions: content quality, spam detection, sentiment authenticity, and factual consistency with on-chain data. This isn't a simple API wrapper — 0G inference is the core verification primitive that determines whether a review becomes a trusted signal or gets flagged.

Why decentralized AI matters here: No single entity should decide what's "trustworthy" in crypto. By running verification on 0G's decentralized compute, trust scores are verifiable and tamper-proof. The verification results include 0G proof metadata that gets attested on-chain.

**Technical integration:** `@0glabs/0g-serving-broker` SDK → `POST /api/verify-0g` → TeeML-verified scoring → trust score update → on-chain attestation. 0G Testnet (`https://evmrpc-testnet.0g.ai`).

KiteAI — Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered):

Maiat's Telegram bot (@MaiatBot) is an autonomous agent that pays for deep review verification on Kite chain using the x402 micropayment protocol. This is agent-to-agent commerce in action.

The flow: User submits a review via Telegram → MaiatBot determines it needs deep verification → MaiatBot autonomously pays for AI verification on Kite chain via x402 → verification result with on-chain transaction proof is returned → trust score updated.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

**Hedera — Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw):**

Maiat is the trust layer AI agents need before they can transact safely. Every AI-verified review is permanently attested on Hedera Hashgraph Consensus Service (HCS Topic `0.0.7987770`), creating an immutable, publicly auditable trust record.

The agentic society flow: An AI agent wants to swap a token or pay a merchant → it queries Maiat's trust API → Maiat returns a trust score backed by HCS-attested reviews → the agent makes an informed decision. Without this, agents are flying blind — no way to distinguish legitimate protocols from scams.

Hedera HCS is critical because trust records must be tamper-proof. If trust scores lived only in a database, they could be manipulated. HCS attestations make every review permanent and verifiable by any agent or human.

**Technical integration:** `@hashgraph/sdk` → review verified → `TopicMessageSubmitTransaction` to HCS Topic `0.0.7987770` → attestation hash stored in DB → queryable via trust API. Viewable on [HashScan](https://hashscan.io/testnet/topic/0.0.7987770).

Base — Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents:

2. On-chain proofs: All review verification results are recorded on Base Sepolia as on-chain proofs, creating a permanent trust registry that any agent or protocol can query.

Agent wallets powered by Privy (non-custodial, server-side signing, policy-enforced spending limits) on Base.

Uniswap — Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform:

Maiat integrates Uniswap at two levels:

1. Uniswap V4 Hook — TrustGateHook: A beforeSwap hook that queries our TrustScoreOracle contract before every swap. Tokens with trust scores below 30 get their swaps reverted. 2. TrustScoreOracle: On-chain contract that stores aggregated trust scores from Maiat's AI verification pipeline. Scores are batch-updated from off-chain computation to stay within gas limits. The oracle is queryable by any protocol, not just our hook.

How it works in practice: A user tries to swap ETH for a sketchy new token → TrustGateHook fires → queries TrustScoreOracle → score is 15 → swap reverts with "Trust score too low." User protected. Alternatively, score is 45 → swap goes through but with a 50bps fee premium reflecting the risk.
