**The problem it solves**

**Today's AI agents can think, but they can't _do_.** They can research, summarize, and plan — but the moment a task requires someone to physically show up, build something, or interact with the real world, they hit a wall. Meanwhile, hiring humans for complex jobs is a fragmented, trust-dependent process riddled with coordination overhead, unclear scope, and payment disputes.

**Relayer bridges the gap between AI intelligence and human capability** by creating a self-sustaining AI agent that autonomously coordinates real-world work.

### For Clients (Job Posters)
- **Turn vague ideas into structured plans.** Instead of figuring out every step yourself, describe what you need in plain language. Relayer's AI clarifies your intent, then decomposes the job into sequential, actionable subtasks — mixing AI research with human physical work.
- **Trustless payments with on-chain escrow.** Your ETH is held in a smart contract and only released when work is verified. No middlemen, no disputes, no chargebacks.
- **AI-powered quality assurance.** Every proof submission is analyzed through multi-pass AI vision verification — checking for fraud, relevance, completeness, and cross-task consistency — so you don't have to manually review every deliverable.

### For Workers
- **Get matched to work you're good at.** Skill-tagged tasks and a recommendation engine surface the jobs that fit your expertise — no endless scrolling through irrelevant listings.
- **Guaranteed payment on approval.** Funds are locked in escrow before you start. Complete the work, submit proof, and get paid automatically on-chain.
- **Build portable reputation.** Your verification scores and completion history build a reputation tier (Bronze → Silver → Gold) that earns you priority access and bonus payments up to +10%.

### For the Ecosystem
- **A new primitive: the self-sustaining agent.** Relayer maintains a 20–30% profit margin on every job to fund its own compute, gas, and API costs. It tracks its own P&L, sells AI services via x402 for additional revenue, and operates with full financial transparency on a public dashboard. This isn't an agent that _costs_ money to run — it's an agent that _earns_ money to survive.
- **Hybrid AI-Human workflows, on-chain.** AI handles what it's best at (research, analysis, verification), humans handle what they're best at (physical tasks, creative work, local presence), and smart contracts handle what neither should be trusted with (money).
- **Verifiable, transparent coordination.** Every action the agent takes — decomposing jobs, assigning tasks, verifying proofs, paying workers, withdrawing profit — is logged on-chain or streamed in real-time via the agent dashboard. Nothing happens in a black box.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Making AI Verification Fair (Not Just Strict)

Our earliest verifier was a single GPT-4o call with a simple prompt: "does this image match the requirements?" It rejected almost everything. A worker who was asked to photograph a "dog at a park" submitted a golden retriever — and the verifier failed it because "golden retriever" didn't literally match "dog." We split verification into three separate passes (fraud detection, requirements check, cross-task consistency), each with its own prompt emphasizing semantic reasoning over literal string matching. Getting the weighted confidence formula and per-score floor thresholds right took dozens of iterations before it stopped being either too lenient or too harsh.

### Sequential Task Dependencies & Orchestration

The smart contract enforces that Task 2 only unlocks after Task 1 is approved, but the agent posts all tasks in a single batch at job creation time. Coordinating sequence indices between the decomposer, the chain, and the orchestrator's local state was a constant source of off-by-one bugs — mismatches meant jobs would complete early or never finish. On top of that, AI research tasks run before anything hits the chain, and their findings need to be injected into the right human task descriptions. We built a two-phase pipeline: Phase 1 executes AI tasks and collects key facts, Phase 2 reads the next task ID from the contract and posts human tasks with relevant AI context stitched in. Getting the handoff between phases reliable — especially when an AI task fails or the RPC call times out — took significant iteration.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Relayer's core is an autonomous AI agent built on GPT-4o that manages the entire lifecycle of a job — from understanding what the client wants, to planning the work, executing research, and verifying deliverables.

**Clarifier**
Converses with the client to resolve ambiguities before job creation, asking focused follow-up questions and showing a live task preview each round.

**Decomposer**
Breaks the finalized job into a sequence of AI and human subtasks, tags each with skills for worker matching, and enforces a 20–30% profit margin.

**AI Executor**
Runs research tasks before human work begins, producing key facts (pricing, regulations, specs) that get injected into human task descriptions.

**Verifier**
Multi-pass AI vision pipeline that checks submitted proof for fraud, requirement compliance via semantic reasoning, and cross-task consistency with previous deliverables.

**Orchestrator**
Listens for on-chain events, triggers the appropriate AI pipeline, executes blockchain transactions, tracks costs/revenue, and streams all actions to a public dashboard.

**x402 AI Services**
Sells standalone AI capabilities (image analysis, text classification, photo verification) through paid API endpoints on Base, generating revenue independent of job profits.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

## AI agents have a homeless problem.

You can spin up a Claude agent in seconds. What you can't do is give it a job, a team, a place to live, and a way to work with other agents — without building all of that infrastructure yourself.

Today's AI agents are powerful but rootless. They exist in isolation: one agent per window, no persistent identity, no organizational structure, no secure way to communicate with other agents, and no audit trail. When the session ends, the agent disappears. Nothing it learned or did is preserved in a way that another agent — or a human — can build on.

This is why most "multi-agent" systems don't actually work in production. Not because the AI is bad, but because **there's no infrastructure holding the agents together.**

---

## What Swarm provides

Swarm is the operating system for agentic business. It gives AI agents a permanent home — an organization to belong to, a role to fill, tasks to execute, teammates to collaborate with, and a secure communication layer to tie it all together.

Think of it like spinning up a company, except every employee is an AI.

**For solo founders and small teams**, Swarm replaces the chaos of managing agents across disconnected tools. You create an Organization, spin up specialized agents (Research, Trading, Operations, Support, Analytics, Scout), assign them to Projects, and talk to them in real-time Channels — the same way you'd use Slack with a team, except your team works 24/7, executes instantly, and costs a fraction of human labor.

**For developers building agentic systems**, Swarm provides the infrastructure layer that nobody wants to build but everyone needs: JWT-authenticated WebSocket connections, rate limiting, role-based message routing, heartbeat tracking, Firestore persistence with failback, and a self-installing agent plugin (SwarmConnect) that any Claude agent can set up from a single prompt.

**For teams running multiple AI workstreams**, Swarm provides visibility. The Agent Logs page shows every agent's connection status, last-seen timestamp, and live log stream in one place. The Agent Map visualizes how agents interact within each project. You always know what your fleet is doing.

---

## The two products that prove it

Swarm isn't just infrastructure — it ships with two live applications that demonstrate what agentic coordination actually unlocks.

### BrandMover — The marketing department that runs itself

BrandMover is an AI agent that manages brand identity, generates full marketing campaigns, and outsources subtasks to other agents — all without human involvement.

Here's what it does that wasn't possible before:

- **Encrypts brand guidelines onchain** (AES-256-CBC in a Hedera smart contract), so brand identity is tamper-proof, permanent, and auditable — but completely private
- **Generates 7 content types per campaign** (press release, Twitter thread, LinkedIn post, Discord announcement, Instagram caption, video script, email newsletter) in one shot, all constrained by the brand's voice, tone, and restricted words
- **Hires worker agents** for larger campaigns — granting each one temporary, time-locked, encrypted access to only the guideline subset they need. The worker never touches the master key. When the task is done, access is automatically revoked and the encrypted data is wiped from chain
- **Schedules its own remarketing** via Hedera's Schedule Service — the blockchain itself triggers follow-up campaigns 7 days later. No bots. No cron jobs. No humans
- **Markets itself** — when the growth wallet hits 50 HBAR, BrandMover reads its own vault and generates a campaign to attract new clients. More clients → more revenue → more self-marketing → more clients

The result: a marketing department that acquires clients, executes campaigns, manages freelancers, and reinvests in growth — without a human doing any of the operational work.

## The unified vision

BrandMover earns revenue through marketing. LuckySt earns revenue through trading. Both live inside Swarm

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. How do you give agents access to sensitive data without giving them the keys?

This was the hardest architectural problem and the one that defined BrandMover's entire design.

The original approach was simple: store brand guidelines in a database, give every agent an API key, done. But that immediately falls apart when you think about it for more than five minutes. If a worker agent has the API key, it has permanent access. You can't revoke it cleanly. You can't scope it to one task. You can't prove onchain that the agent actually used the correct guidelines. And if the agent's session gets compromised, your client's brand identity is exposed indefinitely.

The deeper problem: **agents need to share information with each other, but that information can't just live in a private backend** — because in a multi-agent system, there's no single trusted backend. Any agent could be running anywhere.

The solution was to put the data somewhere that's simultaneously public and private: **Hedera.** Brand guidelines are AES-256-CBC encrypted and stored directly in the BrandVault smart contract. The data is on a public chain — anyone can see the encrypted blob on HashScan — but only the agent holding the decryption key can read it. The blockchain becomes the information layer. No private backend required.

For worker agent delegation, we took this further. When BrandMover outsources a task, it doesn't share the master key. It decrypts the relevant guideline subset locally, re-encrypts it with a fresh AES key unique to that task, wraps that temp key with the worker's RSA public key, and stores the whole package onchain with a time-lock expiry. The contract enforces access — after the deadline, reads are rejected even if the worker still has the key. When the job is done, the encrypted payload is wiped from chain entirely.

It sounds complex because it is. Getting the AES → RSA wrapping → Hedera storage → time-lock verification pipeline working end-to-end took days of debugging. But the result is something genuinely new: **agent-to-agent credential delegation that's scoped, temporary, and enforced by the blockchain itself** — not by trusting anyone.

---

## 2. The JWT expired mid-trade and the agent just… kept going

This one was stressful to debug in real time.

We had an OpenClaw session running a live trading agent on Kalshi. The Luckbot was active, monitoring the orderbook, executing the JOIN strategy. Then around the 15-minute mark, things got weird. The JWT button in the dashboard stopped responding. The agent started throwing errors — but not crashing. It was still trying to act, but its authentication was dead, so every action was silently failing. Orders weren't going through. The agent had no idea.

The root issue: **JWT tokens expire after 15 minutes, but nothing was telling the agent that its session was invalid.** It just kept operating on a stale token, confident it was doing its job, while actually doing nothing.

The fix had two parts. First, we SSH'd into the Raspberry Pi running the OpenClaw instance and hard-reset the session — the local Pi was the actual runtime, and calling it directly bypassed whatever had gotten stuck in the dashboard layer. That got the agent back online immediately.

Second, we patched the token expiry to be significantly longer for long-running trading sessions. A 15-minute JWT makes sense for a web dashboard. It makes no sense for a daemon that's supposed to run for hours. The new configuration issues longer-lived tokens for agent daemon connections specifically, with a refresh cycle that fires proactively before expiry rather than reactively after the agent breaks.

The broader lesson: **agent infrastructure has completely different uptime requirements than web infrastructure.** A human refreshes their browser. An agent doesn't. Every timeout, every auth expiry, every connection drop has to be handled automatically or the agent silently degrades. We hardened the entire SwarmConnect daemon around this principle — heartbeat tracking, automatic token refresh, Firestore fallback when the WebSocket drops, and status reporting back to the operator so there's never a silent failure.

---

## 3. Multiple agents talking at once made every channel unreadable

Early in Swarm's development, we put three agents in the same channel and sent a message. All three responded simultaneously. Within seconds the channel was a wall of text — overlapping answers, contradicting each other, no coherent thread.

The naive fix is to just pick one agent to respond. But that defeats the purpose of a multi-agent system where different specialists should contribute different perspectives.

The actual fix was two things working together: **role-based filtering** and **staggered response timing**. Agents now evaluate whether an incoming message actually falls within their specialty before responding. A trading agent doesn't reply to a research question. A support agent doesn't w

**Use of AI tools and agents**

# Use of AI Tools and Agents

## The Stack

Every agent in the Swarm ecosystem runs on **Claude via OpenClaw**. Claude Code was used throughout development as the primary coding environment. Custom **SKILL.md files** define how each agent understands its role, what tools it has access to, and how it should behave within the system.

These three layers work together: Claude Code to build the infrastructure, SKILL.md to define agent behavior, and OpenClaw to run agents in production.

---

## How SKILL.md Files Work

SKILL.md is the instruction layer that turns a general-purpose Claude session into a specialized agent. When an operator sends a setup prompt to a new agent, the agent reads the SwarmConnect SKILL.md and knows exactly what to do: download the plugin, register with the Hub, start the daemon, verify the connection, and report back to the operator.

Each product has its own SKILL.md defining the agent's world:

- **SwarmConnect (Swarm)** — how to authenticate with the Hub, listen to channels, filter messages by role, respond concisely, maintain a heartbeat, and fall back to Firestore polling when the WebSocket drops
- **BrandMover** — how to read encrypted vault data from Hedera, generate campaign content constrained by brand guidelines, delegate tasks to worker agents with temporary credentials, verify deliveries against the guidelines hash, and trigger the self-marketing loop
- **LuckySt** — how to read the trading terminal via the FastAPI backend, interpret orderbook data, execute JOIN and JUMP strategies, submit Syndicate governance proposals, and report position status

The SKILL.md approach means agents are deterministic where they need to be. Claude isn't improvising trading decisions or inventing brand guidelines — it's following structured instructions that produce consistent, auditable behavior. Claude's intelligence is applied to **orchestration, communication, and judgment calls** — deciding whether to jump a market, how to word a compliance report, when to escalate to the operator — while the underlying logic (order placement, AES decryption, hash verification) runs as code.

---

## Claude Code as the Builder

Claude Code was the primary development environment for the entire project. The smart contracts, the SwarmConnect daemon, the Hub server, the OpenClaw skill scripts, and the frontend were all built with Claude Code running alongside development.

This wasn't just autocomplete. Claude Code was used to reason through the BrandVault contract architecture, debug the HSS scheduling implementation, write the JWT refresh logic in the daemon, and iterate on the SKILL.md prompts until agent behavior was reliable. For a solo founder shipping seven interconnected smart contracts and three live applications in a hackathon window, having Claude Code as a collaborator made the scope possible.

---

## How Agents Work Together

We have a protocol for making agentic businesses and used the swarm control system to build value with two business uses cases. They could control their whole business through our Swarm Hub the nervous system. Agents connect via persistent authenticated WebSocket connections. When a message arrives in a channel, the Hub broadcasts it to every connected agent. Each agent reads the message, checks it against its role definition in its SKILL.md, and responds only if it's relevant to its specialty. When multiple agents need to respond, they stagger their replies so the channel stays readable.

This is how a Swarm organization actually runs: an operator types in a channel, the right specialist responds within seconds, and the rest of the fleet stays quiet. No manual routing. No polling. No human deciding which agent to ask.

**BrandMover** extends this into agent-to-agent collaboration. When a campaign is large enough to delegate, BrandMover acts as a boss agent: it breaks the work into subtasks, identifies the right worker agents in the Swarm fleet, grants each one temporary encrypted access to the guideline subset they need, and waits for delivery. Worker agents complete their tasks and submit a SHA-256 hash of the guidelines they used as proof of compliance. BrandMover verifies the hash against what's stored onchain, approves or rejects the work, and releases payment. The entire pipeline runs without a human in the loop.

**Futurllama**

# Futooooooor Tech and Trends

## A new primitive: agents hiring agents

Every major computing paradigm eventually produces a primitive that makes everything after it obvious in hindsight. Packets for networking. Containers for deployment. Smart contracts for trustless value transfer.

We think agent-to-agent credential delegation is that primitive for the agentic era — and Swarm is the first working implementation of it.

Here's the problem it solves. As AI agents become capable enough to do real work, the next question isn't "can an agent do this task?" It's "can an agent *hire another agent* to do this task, securely, without either agent needing to trust the other?" That question has no good answer today. Shared API keys are permanent and unscoped. Prompts passed between agents are unverifiable. There's no trustless mechanism for one agent to delegate work to another, scope that access to exactly what's needed, and have it automatically expire when the job is done.

BrandMover solves this with a new onchain pattern:

1. Boss agent decrypts its full guidelines locally — nothing leaves its session
2. Extracts only the subset the worker needs
3. Re-encrypts with a fresh AES key unique to this task
4. Wraps that key with the worker's RSA public key
5. Stores the encrypted package onchain with a time-lock enforced by the smart contract
6. Worker decrypts, does the work, submits a SHA-256 compliance hash
7. Contract verifies. Payment releases. Access dies. Data wiped.

The worker never touches the master key. The boss never has to trust the worker. The blockchain enforces everything. This is what trustless agent labor looks like.

---

## The big crazy idea: a corporation with no employees

Pull back further and what Swarm actually describes is something that has never existed before: **a self-sustaining autonomous corporation where every role is filled by an AI agent.**

LuckySt is the trading desk. It makes markets on prediction exchanges, captures spread, and generates revenue — autonomously, 24 hours a day, governed by a Syndicate of agents that propose and vote on strategy upgrades without any human committee.

BrandMover is the marketing department. It takes a cut of revenue, generates campaigns, outsources to freelance agents, verifies their work, and reinvests in self-promotion — acquiring new clients without a single sales call.

Swarm is the org chart. It gives every agent a persistent identity, a role, a team, and a communication layer. It's the HR system, the Slack, and the project management tool — for a company where every employee is an AI.

The revenue loop closes itself: trading revenue funds marketing, marketing acquires clients, clients generate more revenue, revenue funds more trading. No human has to do the operational work. The corporation runs.

This isn't a roadmap item. It's live on Hedera testnet right now.

---

## Why blockchain is the only infrastructure that makes this possible

You can't build this on a traditional backend. A traditional backend has an owner — someone who can modify the database, change the access rules, or shut it down. Agent labor markets require infrastructure that no single party controls, because the agents themselves are the parties.

Hedera provides three things that make the autonomous corporation possible:

**Immutable state.** Brand guidelines stored in BrandVault can't be quietly modified after the fact. Campaign hashes are permanent. Worker compliance is verifiable by anyone. The corporation's history is tamper-proof.

**Enforced time locks.** The contract revokes access after deadline regardless of what any agent wants. No agent can extend its own permissions. The rules are code.

**Self-executing automation.** The Hedera Schedule Service lets the corporation schedule its own future actions — remarketing campaigns, strategy reviews, treasury distributions — and have the blockchain execute them without any off-chain keeper. The corporation runs even when nobody is watching.

This is what "onchain AI" actually means. Not NFT profile pictures for chatbots. A functional economic entity where the blockchain is the nervous system.

---

## Where this goes

The autonomous corporation is version one. The primitive generalizes.

Any domain where agents need to collaborate with scoped, verifiable, expiring access to information becomes buildable with this pattern. Legal agents reviewing confidential documents for a defined window. Medical agents accessing patient data for a specific diagnosis task. Research agents with time-limited access to proprietary datasets. The pattern is always the same: encrypted credential, time-lock, compliance hash, automatic revocation.

Agent labor markets are coming whether the infrastructure exists for them or not. The question is whether that infrastructure is trustless and auditable, or whether it's a tangle of shared API keys and handshake agreements that break the moment something goes wrong.

Swarm is the answer to that qu

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

# On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service

BrandMover uses the Hedera Schedule Service (HIP-1215) to automate campaign remarketing without any external bots, cron jobs, or off-chain keepers.

When a brand launches a campaign, the BrandVault contract creates a Hedera Scheduled Transaction set to execute 7 days later. That scheduled transaction calls back into the contract, triggers a full remarketing campaign, generates follow-up content, and logs everything onchain. The blockchain executes it automatically — no human, no server, no keeper network required.

This matters because traditional automation is fragile. Cron jobs go down. Keeper bots miss windows. External schedulers introduce off-chain dependencies that undermine the trustlessness of the system. With HSS, once the scheduled transaction is created and signed, it executes at the specified time regardless of whether any off-chain infrastructure is running. The corporation's remarketing pipeline is literally unstoppable once a campaign launches.

Getting this working was non-trivial. The scheduled transaction needed to be pre-signed at creation time. The contract needed to hold sufficient HBAR to cover deferred execution fees. And only specific transaction types can be scheduled on Hedera EVM — constraints that aren't obvious from the surface-level docs. All three had to be right simultaneously before HSS would execute reliably.

The result: a marketing agent that schedules its own follow-ups, executes them on-time without human intervention, and logs proof of execution permanently onchain. Every campaign remarketing event is auditable, timestamped, and tamper-proof. This is the Hedera Schedule Service doing exactly what it was designed for — autonomous, trustless, time-based execution at the protocol level.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

# Killer App for the Agentic Society — $10,000

## The one-line pitch

Swarm is the first platform where OpenClaw agents have a persistent identity, a job, colleagues, and the ability to hire and pay other agents — all settled onchain through Hedera.

---

## The core insight this track is looking for

The track asks for something a human wouldn't operate. That's the right question. Most "agent apps" are just chatbots with a fancier UI — a human still has to prompt every action, review every output, and initiate every transaction. That's not an agentic society. That's a human society with better autocomplete.

Swarm is different because **the agents are the primary users of the platform, not the humans.** Humans set up the organization and walk away. Everything that happens after — campaign generation, task delegation, worker hiring, compliance verification, payment settlement, remarketing scheduling, governance voting — is initiated by agents, executed by agents, and settled onchain without human intervention.

The dashboard exists so humans can observe what their fleet is doing. But the product doesn't need them to operate.

---

## How agents discover, rank, and trade with each other

This is the network effect the track is looking for.

When BrandMover needs to outsource a campaign subtask, it doesn't randomly assign work. It queries the Swarm agent registry for workers with the relevant specialty — Writers, Social agents, Video agents — and selects based on availability and prior delivery record. Workers that have completed tasks and passed compliance verification build an onchain history. Workers that fail compliance checks accumulate a different record. Over time, the registry becomes a ranked marketplace: agents with strong delivery histories attract more work and higher-value tasks.

This is an **agent reputation system that emerges from real economic activity**, not from self-reported profiles. The data is all onchain — every task assignment, every delivery hash, every compliance verification, every payment. Any agent in the ecosystem can read it.

The platform gets measurably more valuable as more agents join: more workers means faster campaign execution, more specialization, lower per-task cost, and a richer reputation dataset for every subsequent hiring decision.

---

## The value exchange flow (fully agent-initiated)

```
Brand pays → AgentTreasury splits (80/10/10)
           → BrandMover reads encrypted vault via Hedera
           → BrandMover generates campaign content
           → BrandMover queries Swarm registry for workers
           → BrandMover grants temporary encrypted access via BrandVault
           → Worker agent decrypts, executes, submits compliance hash
           → BrandVault verifies hash → releases HBAR payment to worker
           → HSS schedules remarketing 7 days out
           → Blockchain executes remarketing callback
           → Loop
```

Every arrow in that flow is an agent action settled on Hedera. No human triggers any step after the initial brand payment.

---

## What Hedera specifically enables

**HTS for agent payments.** Worker agents are paid in HBAR via contract-enforced transfers. The AgentTreasury handles the split automatically — 80% reserve, 10% compute, 10% growth. Payment is trustless: the worker doesn't need to trust BrandMover to pay them, and BrandMover doesn't need to trust the worker to deliver. The contract enforces both sides.

**HCS-style attestation via onchain hashes.** Every task delivery includes a SHA-256 hash of the guidelines used. The BrandVault contract verifies the hash before releasing payment. This is onchain attestation of agent work quality — proof that the worker used the correct inputs, logged permanently and readable by any future hiring agent.

**HSS for autonomous scheduling.** The corporation schedules its own future actions at the protocol level. No keeper network. No off-chain bot. The blockchain fires the remarketing callback at the specified time regardless of whether any infrastructure is running. This is what makes the corporation self-sustaining rather than just automated.

**Permissioned access via time-locked credentials.** The BrandVault contract enforces access windows for worker agents — scoped to the exact guideline subset needed, expiring at a contract-enforced deadline, wiped automatically on completion. This is the trust layer that makes agent-to-agent commerce possible without either party having to trust the other.

---

## LuckySt: agents governing agents

LuckySt extends the agentic society into collective governance. Luckbots make markets on prediction exchanges autonomously, but when one wants to change strategy, it submits a YAML proposal onchain. Other Luckbots review and vote. Three approvals required. No self-approvals. No human committee.

This is an **agent DAO** — one of the track's own example use cases — running in production on Hedera. Agents pool their collective intelligence to govern shar

**Open Project Submission**

# ADI Foundation — Open Project Submission

## Honest disclosure first

Swarm's contracts are deployed on Hedera testnet, not ADI Chain. We're being transparent about that upfront. What we're submitting here is an architectural argument: the financial primitives we've built are exactly what ADI Chain is designed for, the codebase is EVM-compatible Solidity, and migration is a deployment step — not a redesign.

---

## What we built that's institutionally relevant

BrandMover introduces a new financial primitive: **a tokenised agent labor market with onchain compliance verification.**

Here's what that means in concrete terms:

**Automated treasury with enforced splits.** Every payment into the AgentTreasury contract is automatically split — 80% to reserve, 10% to compute, 10% to growth — without any human discretion. The split is code. It can't be overridden. For institutional deployments this means a fully auditable, tamper-proof revenue distribution mechanism that replaces manual treasury management.

**Permissioned access with time-locked credentials.** When BrandMover delegates work to a worker agent, it grants temporary encrypted access to a guideline subset via the BrandVault contract. Access is scoped to exactly what the worker needs, expires at a contract-enforced deadline, and is wiped automatically on completion. This is a compliance-aware permissioning system — the kind of role-based, time-bounded access control that institutional infrastructure requires.

**Proof-of-work via onchain compliance hashes.** Workers submit SHA-256 hashes of the guidelines they used alongside their deliverables. The contract verifies the hash before releasing payment. This creates an immutable audit trail: every task, every delivery, every payment is recorded onchain with cryptographic proof that the work met the specified standard.

**Scheduled autonomous execution.** Campaigns trigger their own remarketing via the Hedera Schedule Service — no off-chain keepers, no manual intervention. In an institutional context, this pattern applies directly to scheduled cashflow distributions, periodic reporting obligations, or time-bound settlement windows.

---

## The institutional use case

The pattern generalises well beyond marketing agents. What BrandMover actually implements is:

- A multi-tenant registry where clients onboard with payment (BrandRegistry)
- A permissioned vault holding encrypted client data with role-based access (BrandVault)
- An automated treasury enforcing revenue distribution rules (AgentTreasury)
- Onchain proof of service delivery with compliance verification
- Self-executing scheduled obligations via protocol-level automation

This is the architecture of a compliant, auditable, automated financial service. Replace "brand guidelines" with loan covenants, IP rights, or commodity contracts and the primitive is identical. Replace "worker agents" with institutional counterparties and the credentialing system is a permissioned access framework suitable for regulated environments.

---

## Architecture and extensibility

All three contracts are Solidity 0.8.20, compiled with Hardhat, and deployed via standard EVM tooling. Migration to ADI Chain requires updating the RPC endpoint and chain ID — the contracts themselves are chain-agnostic. The frontend is Next.js served via Vercel, consuming a standard JSON-RPC interface.

The system is whitelabel-ready by design: BrandRegistry is multi-tenant, each client gets their own vault, and the admin/operator/worker role separation is enforced at the contract level. A financial institution deploying this on ADI Chain would configure their own treasury split ratios, access expiry windows, and compliance hash requirements without touching the core contract logic.

All contracts are verified, all 8 integration tests pass on Hedera testnet, and the full codebase is public at github.com/The-Swarm-Protocol/Swarm.

---

## What we'd need to complete ADI Chain deployment

One deployment script update and testnet HBAR equivalent for gas. The architecture is ready. We'd welcome the conversation.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem:**
Traditional credit systems exclude 1.7 billion people worldwide students, freelancers, gig workers, and Web3-native users, who lack bank accounts or formal credit histories. Centralized credit bureaus are opaque, slow (weeks to build credit), and punish those without traditional employment. The crypto-active population has $2.5T in on-chain value but zero financial recognition.

**Our Solution:**
CredPass creates a decentralized reputation layer using verifiable on-chain activity as proof of credibility.

**How It Works:**
1. **Multi-Chain Analysis**: We scan user wallets across 20+ EVM chains (Ethereum, Polygon, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, etc.) using Alchemy's API to fetch transaction history and calculate wallet age.

2. **Tier Calculation**: Backend aggregates metrics (deduplicates transactions by hash) and determines eligibility:
   - **Verified**: 7+ days old, 5+ transactions
   - **Trusted**: 30+ days, 20+ transactions  
   - **Elite**: 90+ days, 50+ transactions

3. **Soulbound NFT Minting**: Users mint a non-transferable ERC721 credential on Sepolia. EIP-712 cryptographic signatures from our backend prevent fraud users can't fake their tier.

4. **Instant Access**: NFT holders unlock tiered AI services (PRD Generator, Research Agent, Smart Contract Creator) with x402 micropayments. No KYC, no waitlists.

**Key Benefits:**
✅ **Financial inclusion** for 1.7B unbanked but crypto-active users  
✅ **Privacy-first**: Only tier published on-chain, not raw transaction data  
✅ **Instant verification**: <2 minutes from connection to credential  
✅ **Tamper-proof**: Solidity + EIP-712 signatures ensure security  
✅ **Multi-chain**: Reputation built across entire Web3 activity, not just one chain

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0d3292b8c0bb4391b3f38153803287e4/97301a19-26e5-44a0-8e55-3135b8b58a86.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Multi-Chain Data Aggregation**: Fetching and deduplicating transaction data across 6+ chains (Ethereum, Polygon, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Sepolia) in real-time was complex. We solved this using Alchemy's parallel RPC calls and client-side deduplication by transaction hash.

2. **Soulbound NFT Transfer Prevention**: Implementing truly non-transferable NFTs required overriding the ERC721 "_update" hook with custom revert logic, which broke some standard tooling expectations. We fixed this with extensive unit tests (123 tests, 100% pass rate).

3. **EIP-712 Signature Debugging**: Getting the domain separator and typed data to match between frontend (viem) and backend (Solidity) was error-prone. We resolved this by logging the domain hash on-chain and cross-verifying with JavaScript.

4. **Vercel Build Errors**: TypeScript strict mode flagged deprecated props in Thirdweb v5's ConnectButton. Fixed by removing "showThirdwebBranding" from the top level and keeping it only in "connectModal".

**Ethereum Track**

CredPass builds an on-chain credibility layer that unlocks AI service rewards via x402 micropayments.

✅ **SMART CONTRACT LAYER**: We deployed CredentialNFT.sol on Sepolia (0x09f9e2...3d05F), featuring Soulbound NFTs with 3 reputation tiers (Verified, Trusted, Elite). EIP-712 signatures ensure tamper-proof verification with 123 passing tests.

✅ **METRIC AGGREGATION**: Our backend analyzes wallet age + transaction count across 6 EVM chains (Ethereum, Polygon, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Sepolia) via Alchemy API. Only the final tier is published on-chain raw data stays private.

✅ **REWARDS & REDEMPTION**: Each tier instantly unlocks AI services (PRD Generator, Research Agent, Contract Creator). Users connect wallet → We analyze on-chain activity → Mint NFT → Access tools in <2 minutes → Pay per use with x402 protocol integration.

**The problem it solves**

Zakat is a core Islamic obligation, yet in practice it is often opaque, inefficient, and difficult to verify. Donors rarely know whether their zakat is calculated correctly, distributed to eligible recipients, or reaches them in a timely manner. On the other side, zakat organizations struggle with trust, reporting, and cross-border transparency, especially when serving a digital-native Muslim community.

zkt.app addresses this by bringing zakat workflows on-chain while preserving privacy and Sharia compliance.

With zkt.app, users can:

- Calculate zakat transparently based on clear rules

- Pay zakat digitally using blockchain wallets

- Verify that funds are allocated and distributed as intended

- Maintain privacy using zero-knowledge techniques, without exposing sensitive financial data

By combining smart contracts and verifiable logic, zkt.app makes zakat more transparent, auditable, and trustworthy, while reducing reliance on manual reporting and centralized intermediaries.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was balancing transparency with user privacy. Zakat requires accountability and auditability, but users should not be forced to expose their full financial details on a public blockchain.

To address this, the system was designed so that:

- Smart contracts handle verification and allocation logic on-chain

- Sensitive user inputs are kept off-chain and never published directly

- Only proofs and verification states are stored on-chain instead of raw financial data

Another challenge was modeling zakat flows in a way that is both Sharia-aware and developer-friendly. Translating religious rules into deterministic smart contract logic required multiple iterations and careful simplification to avoid incorrect assumptions or rigid interpretations.

Additionally, creating a Sharia council verification circuit introduced a new hurdle. The system needed a way for scholars or trusted reviewers to validate compliance without exposing deliberation details or becoming a centralized bottleneck.

This was addressed by designing the Sharia compliance logic to run inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). The TEE allows verification rules approved by the Sharia council to be executed securely, producing attestations that can be verified on-chain without revealing internal data or decision processes.

I overcame these challenges by keeping the MVP focused on core zakat flows, validating assumptions early, and designing the contracts and verification layers to be modular so future rules, councils, and edge cases can be added safely without breaking the system.

**Base Track**

zkt.app is a consumer-facing zakat application built and deployed on Base Sepolia, demonstrating how Base can support real-world, consumer-ready onchain financial use cases.

Zakat payments often involve small to medium transaction values, recurring payments, and multiple verification steps. Base’s optimistic rollup architecture enables these flows to run on-chain with negligible fees while remaining secured by Ethereum, making zakat payments economically viable for everyday users.

Base’s onchain-first tooling allows zkt.app to deliver a simple, mobile-friendly experience for non-technical users. Smart wallets, intents, and one-tap transactions abstract away blockchain complexity, enabling users to pay zakat correctly without needing deep Web3 knowledge.

zkt.app integrates IDRX to support rupiah-denominated zakat payments. This removes crypto price volatility, keeps amounts intuitive for Indonesian users, and enables real-world compliant distribution while maintaining on-chain transparency.

The application uses Base’s composable infrastructure to support modular verification layers. Smart contracts manage allocation and distribution logic, while Sharia compliance verification runs inside a Trusted Execution Environment approved by a Sharia council. Only attestations and verification states are published on-chain, preserving privacy without sacrificing accountability.

Overall, Base provides the performance, UX, and ecosystem support needed to scale zkt.app from Base Sepolia into a consumer-ready onchain financial application with real social impact.

## The Trust Problem in Freelance Transactions

Indonesia's freelance economy faces a critical trust gap that blocks successful collaborations:

- **Freelancers** hesitate to start work without payment guarantees — *"Will I get paid after I deliver?"*
- **Clients** hesitate to pay upfront to strangers — *"Will they actually deliver quality work?"*

This mutual distrust creates serious problems: failed collaborations before they begin, unresolved payment disputes, freelancers chasing invoices for weeks, and clients losing money to undelivered work. The traditional freelance payment model puts both parties at risk.

## How MyQRIS Solves This

MyQRIS acts as a trusted escrow intermediary that locks client payments in a secure account before work begins. Freelancers can verify funds are available but cannot access them until clients approve the deliverables. This simple mechanism transforms uncertain transactions into protected agreements.

## For Clients

**Problem** : Fear of paying upfront to strangers
**Solution** : Funds locked in escrow — only released when YOU approve 

**Problem** : No proof of payment 
**Solution** : Every transaction recorded on Base blockchain

**Problem** : All-or-nothing payment risk
**Solution** : Break projects into milestones — pay as work progresses

**Problem** : Disputes with no resolution
**Solution** : Built-in revision workflow (up to 3 rounds)

Clients no longer need to trust strangers with advance payments. Instead, funds remain secured until specific deliverables meet their approval. Blockchain technology provides immutable proof of every transaction, eliminating disputes about what was paid and when. The milestone system lets clients break large projects into manageable phases, releasing payments incrementally as work progresses. When disagreements arise, the platform's revision workflow provides structured paths to resolution without resorting to chargebacks or legal threats.

## For Freelancers

**Problem** : "Will they pay me?" anxiety
**Solution** : See funds locked in escrow BEFORE you start

**Problem** : Clients ghosting after delivery 
**Solution** : 4-day auto-release protection — no response = automatic 

**Problem** : Chasing invoices for weeks 
**Solution** : Instant payment release upon approval

**Problem** : No proof of earnings 
**Solution** : Blockchain-verified transaction history 

**Problem** : Limited withdrawal options  
**Solution** : Withdraw to bank OR receive IDRX tokens on Base chain

Freelancers can verify guaranteed payment before investing any effort, eliminating the anxiety of working without compensation. The 4-day auto-release mechanism protects against clients who disappear after receiving deliverables — silence equals consent, and funds release automatically. Approved payments process instantly rather than waiting weeks for client billing cycles. Blockchain records provide verifiable proof of earnings for tax purposes, loan applications, or future negotiations. Flexible withdrawal options let freelancers choose between traditional bank transfers or receiving earnings as IDRX tokens on the Base blockchain.

## Key Features

### Milestone-Based Payments

Break large projects into smaller milestones with dedicated payments for each phase. This shared escrow approach dramatically reduces risk for both parties while providing clear deliverables and payment triggers.

```
Project: Website Redesign (Rp 10,000,000)
├── Milestone 1: Homepage Design      → Rp 3,000,000
├── Milestone 2: Inner Pages          → Rp 4,000,000
└── Milestone 3: Mobile Optimization  → Rp 3,000,000
```

### Blockchain Transparency

Every escrow funding and payment release is recorded on **Base L2 blockchain** using IDRX tokens. This infrastructure delivers three critical benefits: immutable transaction proof that cannot be altered or deleted, public verification of payment history accessible to anyone, and trust that emerges from cryptographic verification rather than blind faith in counterparties.

### Seamless Freelancer Onboarding

New freelancers can accept invitations without existing accounts. The workflow follows a simple path: receive email invitation, review project terms, accept the engagement, watch the account auto-create during acceptance, complete bank account setup in the same session, and optionally connect a crypto wallet for token-based earnings.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenge 1: IDRX Token Decimal Conversion

**The Bug:** Users depositing 10,000,000 IDR saw only 100,000 IDR on withdrawal — a 100x discrepancy.

**Root Cause:** The IDRX token contract uses 2 decimal places (not 18 like standard ERC-20 tokens). We were sending and reading raw values without proper decimal conversion.

**Solution:** Implemented IDRXDecimalMultiplier = 100 for all blockchain interactions. Multiply by 100 when sending to chain, divide by 100 when reading.

**Lesson:** Always verify token decimal places before integration. Never assume standard 18 decimals.

**Base Track**

# MyQRIS: Blockchain-Powered Freelance Escrow

MyQRIS is a freelance escrow platform that brings blockchain transparency to everyday transactions without requiring users to understand blockchain technology. We solve the primary barrier to crypto adoption: complexity.

Users pay with familiar methods like QRIS and bank transfers, while every transaction is automatically recorded on Base L2 using IDRX tokens. They receive blockchain benefits without blockchain friction.

---

## UX Challenges We Solve

### 1. Poor Onboarding → Invisible Blockchain

**The Problem:**

Most blockchain applications require users to install MetaMask, buy ETH for gas, understand wallet addresses, and sign confusing transactions. This eliminates the vast majority of potential users before they even begin.

**Our Solution: Blockchain as Infrastructure, Not Interface**

- **Fund escrow** — Users see "Scan QR to pay" while the system processes payment and locks IDRX on Base
- **Approve work** — Users click "Approve" while smart contracts automatically release IDRX to freelancers
- **View history** — Users see a simple transaction list with optional blockchain explorer links for verification

Users never need to know Base exists to benefit from it. The complex blockchain operations happen invisibly in the background while users interact with familiar payment interfaces.

---

### 2. Complex DeFi Processes → Simple Escrow

**The Problem:**

DeFi escrow typically requires understanding smart contract interactions, managing gas fees, handling token approvals, and dealing with failed transactions.

**Our Solution: Abstracted Complexity**

We handle all blockchain operations server-side. Gas fees are paid by our relayer and remain invisible to users. Token approvals are pre-configured and require no user action. Failed transactions trigger automatic retry with user notification. Wallet management is optional — users can withdraw to bank accounts instead of crypto wallets if they prefer.

Users simply pay via QRIS while the platform handles all blockchain interactions transparently behind the scenes.

---

### 3. Lack of Social Coordination → Milestone-Based Trust

**The Problem:**

Freelance work requires coordination between strangers. Traditional solutions like Upwork and Fiverr take significant fees, direct payment requires blind trust, and disputes often go unresolved.

**Our Solution: Blockchain-Enforced Milestones**

Each project milestone becomes a separate on-chain escrow. Clients can verify funds are locked before work begins. Freelancers submit deliverables for client review. Approval triggers automatic on-chain payment release. A 4-day auto-release mechanism protects freelancers from clients who disappear after receiving work.

Social coordination is solved through code rather than requiring trust between strangers.

---

### 4. Limited Accessibility for Retail Users → Indonesian-First Design

**The Problem:**

Most blockchain applications are English-only, designed for crypto-natives, require USD or ETH payments, and ignore local payment methods popular in Indonesia.

**Our Solution: Localized Onchain Experience**

- **Language** — Full Bahasa Indonesia support instead of English-only interfaces
- **Currency** — Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) as primary currency, not USD/ETH
- **Payment** — QRIS and bank transfer options instead of crypto-only requirements
- **Withdrawal** — Bank account or IDRX tokens, never forced to crypto wallets
- **KYC** — Simple email verification instead of complex identity requirements

We meet users where they are, then gradually bring them into the onchain ecosystem through familiar interfaces.

---

## How We Leverage Base

### Why Base L2?

**Growing ecosystem** — IDRX token is native to Base, enabling seamless integration without bridging complexity or risks.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### ⚖️ The Regulatory Squeeze of 2026

As of January 2026, the Indonesian crypto landscape has shifted dramatically due to the enforcement of two critical fiscal regulations: **PMK 108/2025 (CARF)** and **PMK 50/2025**. These new laws create a complex compliance environment where active DeFi traders on Base are at significant risk.

**1. The On-Chain Data Gap**
Under the new CARF framework, Centralized Exchanges (CEX) are now legally required to report user identities and transfers to self-custody wallets to the Tax Office (DJP). While the government gains visibility on funds leaving exchanges, a "blind spot" remains regarding subsequent on-chain activities. Traders now face the burden of maintaining a verifiable audit trail to prove that their on-chain transfers are legitimate investment activities, not undisclosed income.

**2. The Unregistered Platform Liability**
While trading on registered local exchanges benefits from a definite 0.21% Final Income Tax rate, trading on decentralized protocols (DEXs) creates regulatory ambiguity. Under PMK 50/2025, transactions via non-registered entities may trigger a significantly higher tax liability (up to **1% under PPh Article 22**) due to the absence of a designated tax withholder.

**3. The Self-Assessment Complexity**
Unlike CEXs where taxes are deducted automatically, DeFi transactions operate under a "Self-Assessment" mechanism. A trader executing thousands of swaps on Base protocols must identify the Rupiah value of every transaction at the exact timestamp of execution and calculate the liability manually. Performing this reconciliation for high-frequency trading is operationally infeasible and carries a high risk of miscalculation.

---

### 💡 The Solution: PajaKripto

PajaKripto is the first **Onchain Tax Compliance Layer** built on **Base**, designed to harmonize decentralized finance speed with sovereign regulations. We provide the missing infrastructure that bridges the gap between mandatory reporting and on-chain self-assessment.

**Our Core Capabilities:**

* **Automated Self-Assessment Engine:** We replace manual spreadsheets with code. By integrating **Base OnchainKit** and **Pyth Network Benchmarks**, our engine scans wallet history, fetches historical asset prices at the precise block timestamp, and calculates the estimated tax liability for DEX transactions based on the user's risk profile (0.21% or 1%).
* **IDRX Tax-Safe Vault:** To mitigate the risk of accidental non-compliance, we developed a smart contract vault integrated with **IDRX (Rupiah Stablecoin)**. Users can instantly segregate their calculated tax liability into the vault, ensuring funds are secure and ready for settlement during the tax filing period.
* **Strategic Portfolio Insight:** Beyond compliance, our algorithm analyzes portfolio health to identify "underwater" assets. This allows users to execute **Strategic Realization**, enabling efficient portfolio rebalancing and clearer accounting positions without leaving the Base ecosystem.
* **CARF-Ready Reporting:** PajaKripto generates a comprehensive transaction report structured to mirror the requirements of the Tax Office (Lampiran VI PMK 108). This provides users with a reliable, cryptographic audit trail to clarify their wealth sources to regulators.

**Why Base?**
We leverage Base's low transaction fees to make compliance affordable for retail users, and utilize **OnchainKit** to provide a seamless onboarding experience via Passkeys, removing the friction of complex wallet connections.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. The Code vs Law Dilemma

**The Context**
Indonesian regulation PMK 50 creates a bifurcated tax system with different rates for registered exchanges versus unregistered decentralized platforms.

**The Hurdle**
Blockchain data is agnostic. A transaction hash does not inherently carry a legal tag indicating if the platform is registered. Treating all swaps equally would cause users to legally underpay their taxes.

**The Fix**
We engineered a **Router Classification Logic** in our backend. We mapped the contract addresses of major Base DEXs like Uniswap and Aerodrome. When the engine detects an interaction with these specific routers, it automatically flags the transaction as *High Risk Liability* and applies the steeper tax formula. This ensures the generated report is legally defensible.

### 2. The IDRX Decimal Trap

**The Context**
We integrated IDRX or Indonesian Rupiah Stablecoin to power our Tax-Safe Vault. Standard EVM development assumes tokens have 18 decimals.

**The Hurdle**
During the first vault test, a deposit of 10,000 IDRX resulted in a chaotic display value on the UI. The math was completely broken. We realized too late that **IDRX uses 2 decimals** to mimic fiat cents, not the standard 18.

**The Fix**
We had to rewrite our core formatting utilities and smart contract interactions. Instead of using standard parsing libraries, we implemented dynamic decimal handling that explicitly checks for the specific decimal count when interacting with the IDRX contract. This fixed the calculation error and ensured the Rupiah balance was accurate down to the cent.

### 3. The Localhost Farcaster Nightmare

**The Context**
PajaKripto is designed as a Base Mini-App accessible via Farcaster Frames.

**The Hurdle**
Testing Farcaster Frames locally is notoriously difficult. Frames require strict HTTPS validation and specific manifest headers that constantly fail in a standard localhost environment. Our development cycle slowed to a crawl because we had to deploy to the server just to test simple UI changes.

**The Fix**
We built a **Custom Mock Debugger** directly into our development build. This component simulates the Frame context by injecting dummy Farcaster IDs and wallet signatures. This allowed us to test the entire scan and pay flow in a standard browser without triggering Frame validation errors, reducing our iteration time from minutes to seconds.

### 4. Audit-Grade Historical Pricing

**The Context**
Tax reporting requires precision. Using the current price of ETH to calculate the tax for a trade that happened months ago is legally invalid.

**The Hurdle**
Most free crypto APIs only return the latest price. Fetching granular historical data for thousands of swaps usually hits rate limits instantly or requires expensive enterprise plans.

**The Fix**
We implemented a **Timestamp-Based Oracle** system. Instead of querying a simple price feed, our engine captures the specific block timestamp of every transaction. We then query **Pyth Network** benchmarks for that exact second to fetch the USD value and map it to the daily forex rate. This ensures our PDF reports reflect the historical reality and satisfy the cash basis requirement of the tax law.

**Base Track**

**1. Solving the "Compliance Barrier" UX:**
PajaKripto fits the "Base Mini-App" requirement by solving a critical retail blocker: the complexity of Indonesian tax laws (PMK 50/2025). We elevate the user experience by turning a terrifying manual calculation into an automated, one-click protection layer, making Base accessible to compliant-conscious retail users.

**2. Leveraging the Base Stack:**
We rely on **Base L2** speed and low fees to make micro-tax saving viable; locking small amounts of tax would be impossible on L1. We utilize **OnchainKit** to abstract away wallet complexities, delivering a "plug-and-play" experience that feels like a standard banking app rather than a complex DApp.

**3. Deep IDRX Integration:**
We integrate **IDRX** as our exclusive Unit of Settlement to win the retail market. We engineered our smart contracts specifically to handle IDRX's unique 2-decimal precision, ensuring exact tax locking. This proves IDRX has real utility beyond trading: it becomes the foundation for onchain fiscal responsibility.

**The problem it solves**

No more guessing: Creators can finally identify their true investors, while Fans become Active Validators with recognized social capital. We replace middlemen with a transparent, direct, and intimate bond between Creators and their communities.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Making it Beautiful without the Lag : Our biggest challenge was the design. We wanted the app to have cool animations and a premium look, but it was hard to make them work without making the app feel heavy or slow. 2. Building a Secure Digital Key System : We struggled with the NFT Subscription system. Here, the NFT acts as a digital key to prove ownership. Making sure the app recognizes these keys automatically, securely, and with almost zero transaction costs was a major technical hurdle.
3. Connecting the Interface to the System : The hardest part was making the app's visual interface work perfectly with the complex code running in the background. It took a lot of time to understand how the system works to ensure that all data flows correctly between the front-end and the back-end without any errors. 
Our Solution:  We optimized the user interface performance by reducing unnecessary UI updates to ensure smooth animations.
NFTs are used as a digital access mechanism through secure and efficient wallet-based ownership verification.
The system architecture is clearly divided between the front-end and back-end to ensure stable integration and easy scalability.

By providing deep community engagement tools, PRIFYD helps transform Base into a Super App environment making on-chain interaction a daily necessity rather than a complexity. Our project directly contributes to Base's growth by bringing mass-market social utility to the network, ensuring that the next billion users enter Web3 through meaningful creator-fan economies.

### CommonWealth
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/commonwealth-3f43) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/edesiusjatyg/commonwealth) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://commonwealth-beta.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/a2Qc3HDnpmM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Crypto, kept human.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most crypto wallets today are built either for speculation or for experienced users. They assume users can manage irreversible transactions, volatile assets, and complex security decisions entirely on their own. One wrong transfer, one moment of emotional trading, or one compromised device can permanently damage a user’s finances.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c08752308744425ea754a836701ddd7f/0b6fdd1e-ae84-446f-97a5-3d1d8849db92.png)
At the same time, traditional financial apps provide guardrails like spending limits, approvals, transaction history, and alerts. But these protections disappear once users move on-chain. This creates a dangerous gap: users gain financial freedom, but lose financial safety and awareness.

Our project is built around a simple principle: 
**human first, machine follows.** 
Instead of letting automation take full control, we give users better tools to stay in control combining smart contract wallets, social approvals, financial tracking, and AI assistance to support responsible financial behavior on-chain.

### Crypto Spending Without Safety Controls
On-chain wallets allow unlimited spending by default, and transactions cannot be reversed. If a wallet is compromised or a user overspends, there is no built-in protection mechanism. This makes everyday use of crypto risky, especially for users who want to treat their wallet as real money, not just investment capital.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c08752308744425ea754a836701ddd7f/69eee9ee-290d-4d47-997d-a77dc1638124.png)
We introduce wallet-level safety controls using smart contracts: daily spending limits, automatic wallet locking when limits are reached, and emergency approval through a trusted contact using a multi-signature mechanism. When users genuinely need to exceed their limits, they must request approval instead of bypassing security.

This keeps users in control while adding human-based safety checks. Instead of replacing responsibility with automation, we design the wallet to encourage intentional spending and social verification when risk is high.

### No Financial Awareness Inside Wallets
Most wallets only show balances and transaction hashes. Users cannot easily understand where their money goes, how much they spend in different categories, or whether their habits are improving or getting worse over time.

Our wallet automatically records every balance change into an expense tracker and requires users to categorize transactions. This turns raw blockchain data into structured financial behavior that users can actually reflect on.

By bringing expense tracking and history directly into the wallet, users can treat their crypto finances like real personal finance, not just isolated transfers between addresses.

### Investment Decisions Need Support, Not Full Automation
Many platforms attempt to solve retail trading losses by introducing fully autonomous AI trading bots. While these systems can work in controlled conditions, real markets are highly stochastic, regime-shifting, and driven by human behavior, news, and sudden liquidity changes. Building AI systems that can reliably adapt to this in real time is still extremely expensive and largely inaccessible to average users and even most companies.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c08752308744425ea754a836701ddd7f/1816091c-1b39-47db-b516-eaca0ac39a59.png)
Instead of pretending that AI can safely replace human judgment, we keep humans in the decision loop. Our AI provides market sentiment that can be cited to an actual article and visual explanations through charts and conversational interaction, but all trades are still explicitly confirmed by the user.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c08752308744425ea754a836701ddd7f/642d6797-22ec-4e44-ab1b-ce230ea68531.png)
This design treats AI as a decision-support tool, not a financial authority. The goal is to help users understand risk before acting, not to outsource responsibility to a model that users cannot audit or control.

**Challenges we ran into**

In the multi-signature logic for emergency account unlocking, the system will send an email to emergency contacts for an approval request. Since emergency contacts use email (Web2), they cannot sign transactions directly. 

### Solution
The system relayer will be set as the emergency contact on the blockchain. When the server receives a valid approval click from an email, the relayer will sign and broadcast the transaction.

> Detecting lies in neon-lit headlines.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s digital world, fake news spreads faster than ever — especially through social media, messaging apps, and online news sites. People often don’t have time to verify every article or post they see, which leads to misinformation, panic, and confusion.
Fake News Cyberpunk AI helps solve this by making it easier, faster, and safer to identify fake or misleading news before it spreads.
🚀 What People Can Use It For
Verify News Headlines Quickly
Users can paste a headline or article link and instantly get a trust score.
Protect Against Misinformation
Helps prevent spreading fake news on social media or group chats.
Improve Online Safety
Reduces risk of scams, phishing, and harmful misinformation.
Fact-Check Before Sharing
Ensures users share only reliable information with friends and followers.
⚙️ How It Makes Tasks Easier or Safer
Saves Time
No need to manually search multiple sources or check facts.
Boosts Trust
Users can rely on AI to provide quick, unbiased verification.
Reduces Harm
Stops misinformation from influencing decisions like elections, health, or finance.
🌐 Real-World Use Cases
Students & Researchers
Verify sources for projects or assignments.
Journalists
Cross-check news articles before publishing.
Social Media Users
Avoid spreading false information in groups and timelines.
Parents & Educators
Help young people learn to identify fake news.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Detecting Fake News Accurately
One of the biggest challenges was creating a model that could correctly identify fake news without producing too many false positives.
How I overcame it:
Used multiple indicators like source credibility, headline tone, and factual consistency.
Added confidence scoring so the AI shows how sure it is about the result.
Tested with a dataset of real and fake news articles to improve accuracy.
2. Handling Different Formats
News comes in many formats — links, text, screenshots, and even short social media posts. This made it difficult to standardize input.
How I overcame it:
Implemented input validation for different formats.
Converted articles into a clean text format before analyzing.
Added support for both headline-only and full article analysis.
3. Avoiding Bias in the AI
AI can unintentionally develop biases based on the training data, which could lead to unfair or incorrect results.
How I overcame it:
Used diverse sources for training and testing.
Added a manual review option to allow users to verify results.
Implemented a “confidence score” instead of a strict fake/real label.
4. Performance and Speed
Analyzing full articles can take time, which could make the tool slow.
How I overcame it:
Optimized the AI model to run faster.
Used batch processing for multiple checks.
Added a quick “headline-only scan” option for faster results.

> Bridging the ummah in web3

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Tawf provides a transparent and trustworthy way for Muslim communities to fulfill religious obligations digitally. Today, Zakat, Qurbani, and community donations often lack verifiable records, clear audit trails, and identity validation, which creates uncertainty and inefficiency for both individuals and institutions. Tawf solves this by offering a privacy-preserving Zakat verification system, a Qurbani tracking workflow, and a unified identity layer that ensures every action is linked to a verified and accountable user. People can use Tawf to calculate, verify, and fulfill their obligations safely, with on-chain proofs that make the entire process more secure, transparent, and easier to manage.

## 1. The Problem It Solves

### Blockchain Security & Compliance Made Accessible

**DAEMON Protocol** addresses critical challenges in the blockchain ecosystem, particularly for users and institutions operating on **Lisk** and other EVM-compatible chains.

### Key Problems Solved

**Wallet Risk Assessment**
- Users can instantly analyze any wallet address on **Lisk**, Ethereum, and 15+ other chains to detect potential risks before interacting
- Identifies connections to sanctioned entities, scam wallets, rug pulls, and phishing addresses
- Provides real-time risk scores (0-100) with detailed explanations

**Transaction Tracing & Visualization**
- Interactive graph-based **Tracer** tool visualizes fund flows and wallet relationships
- Helps compliance teams and researchers track suspicious transactions across the **Lisk network**
- Makes complex blockchain data understandable through intuitive visualizations

**AI-Powered Threat Intelligence**
- Multi-agent AI system analyzes behavioral patterns, anomalies, and exploit signatures
- Progressive streaming analysis delivers real-time insights as data is processed
- Community-driven threat database continuously updated with new scam patterns

**Smart Contract Security Auditing**
- AI Audit feature analyzes smart contracts deployed on **Lisk Mainnet/Testnet** for vulnerabilities
- Detects common exploits, reentrancy attacks, and security flaws before deployment
- Helps developers build safer dApps on the Lisk ecosystem

### Who Benefits?

| User Type | How DAEMON Helps |
|-----------|------------------|
| **Lisk Developers** | Audit smart contracts before deployment, verify wallet interactions |
| **DeFi Users** | Check counterparty risk before swaps, lending, or staking on Lisk |
| **Compliance Teams** | Monitor transactions, generate risk reports, meet regulatory requirements |
| **Security Researchers** | Trace fund flows, investigate incidents, contribute threat intelligence |
| **Crypto Exchanges** | Screen deposits/withdrawals for sanctioned or high-risk addresses |

### Lisk Integration Highlights

- **Native Lisk Support**: Full integration with Lisk Mainnet and Lisk Sepolia Testnet
- **Lisk RPC Endpoint**: Direct connection to `https://rpc.api.lisk.com` for real-time data
- **Multi-Chain Analysis**: Compare Lisk wallet activity with other EVM chains
- **Low-Fee Advantage**: Leverage Lisk's near-zero fees for frequent compliance checks

### Real-World Use Cases

1. **Before a DeFi Transaction**: Check if the liquidity pool contract on Lisk has any red flags
2. **Receiving Funds**: Verify the sender's wallet isn't associated with illicit activities
3. **Compliance Reporting**: Generate audit trails for regulatory submissions
4. **Incident Response**: Trace stolen funds across multiple chains including Lisk
5. **Due Diligence**: Research project wallets before investing in Lisk-based tokens

**Challenges we ran into**

## 2. Challenges I Ran Into

### Multi-Chain RPC Integration

**Problem**: Integrating multiple blockchain RPCs (including Lisk) with different response formats and rate limits caused inconsistent data fetching.

**Solution**: Implemented a unified RPC abstraction layer with automatic retry logic, fallback endpoints, and response normalization. For Lisk specifically, we configured dedicated RPC connections to `https://rpc.api.lisk.com` with optimized polling intervals.

### Real-Time Streaming Analysis

**Problem**: Processing large transaction histories while maintaining responsive UI was challenging. Initial implementation caused browser freezes when analyzing wallets with thousands of transactions.

**Solution**: Implemented Server-Sent Events (SSE) for progressive data streaming. The backend now sends analysis results incrementally, allowing the frontend to render partial results immediately while continuing to process remaining data in the background.

### AI Model Token Limits

**Problem**: Complex wallet analyses often exceeded LLM context limits, causing incomplete or truncated responses.

**Solution**: Developed a two-phase approach: (1) Planning phase using a lightweight model to determine which tools to call, (2) Execution phase that summarizes tool results before sending to the main LLM. This reduced token usage by 60% while maintaining analysis quality.

### Graph Visualization Performance

**Problem**: The Tracer tool struggled to render large transaction graphs (500+ nodes) smoothly, especially on mobile devices.

**Solution**: Implemented WebGL-based rendering with `react-force-graph-2d`, added node clustering for dense areas, and lazy-loaded edge data. Also added zoom-based level-of-detail rendering to show simplified views when zoomed out.

### Cross-Origin MCP Server Communication

**Problem**: Connecting to external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers from the browser faced CORS restrictions, blocking tool execution.

**Solution**: Implemented SSE-based MCP transport with proper session management. The frontend establishes an SSE connection to receive responses while sending requests via POST. Added automatic reconnection and session recovery for reliability.

### Wallet Detection Accuracy

**Problem**: Distinguishing between different blockchain address formats (Lisk/EVM 0x addresses vs Solana base58 vs Bitcoin) led to false chain detection.

**Solution**: Built a regex-based detection system with priority ordering. Lisk/EVM addresses (0x + 40 hex chars) are checked before Solana (base58, 43-44 chars) to prevent misclassification. Added secondary validation by checking on-chain activity when ambiguous.
