### MAAT
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sentinel-6279) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/JagannathsnKU/DenverHacks) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://denverhackss.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/TKBMiGJPLh8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI agents that pay, act & prove on-chain.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pino](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pino-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Building autonomous AI agents that interact with external APIs is painful. Every integration is manual, there's no standard way to charge for tool usage, and once an agent runs, there's no transparent record of what it did or what it spent. This makes it nearly impossible to deploy AI agents at scale with any real accountability or fairness to the people who own the tools being used.

Our product, Maat, makes that entire process automatic and trustless. Any API or smart contract can be converted into a structured, AI-ready tool in minutes, with pricing, permissions, and rules defined upfront and registered on-chain.

Developers no longer have to hand-wire integrations or build custom billing logic, it's handled at the infrastructure level. AI agents get access to a growing catalog of verified tools they can call autonomously, paying per use via automatic micropayments that settle on-chain before the tool even responds.

For enterprises and developers deploying agents, every action is publicly recorded on the blockchain, who called what, when, and what was paid. This creates a real audit trail for the first time, making it possible to run AI agents in environments that require accountability and compliance. Operators can set rate limits, spend caps, and restrict which tools each agent can access, so there's always a human-defined boundary around what the agent is allowed to do.

For API and smart contract owners, this opens up an entirely new monetization channel. Instead of only serving human users, their endpoints can now serve AI agents directly, with automatic payments, no chargebacks, no disputes, and no middlemen. Every call is a settled transaction on-chain.

For the broader AI ecosystem, this solves one of the most fundamental problems with agentic AI today: there's no economic or accountability layer between what an agent does and the real-world systems it touches. This project builds that layer, making AI actions safer, fairer, and verifiable for everyone involved.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part was making payments and tool execution autonomous. If an agent calls a tool and something fails halfway through, you can't leave the money in limbo.

We built a system where funds are set aside the moment a tool is called, before anything actually runs. If the tool completes successfully, the charge goes through and gets recorded on-chain. If anything fails, the money is returned to exactly where it was before the call started. We also had to make sure that if multiple agents were using the system at the same time, their balances could never accidentally interfere with each other. Every agent's funds are tracked separately, so a problem with one agent has no effect on another. Getting the order of all these steps right, so there was never a moment where money could go missing or be charged twice, was the part that took the most work to get right.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Maat is built from the ground up to be used by AI agents, not just humans. When a developer registers an API, the system automatically converts it into the OpenAI function-calling format, which is the standard way AI models like GPT-4 understand what tools are available and how to call them. This means any AI agent that supports function calling can discover and use tools on the platform without any custom integration work.

Each agent gets its own on-chain identity, its own wallet balance for paying for tools, and its own reputation score that builds up over time based on how reliably it executes. When an AI agent decides to call a tool, it signs the request cryptographically, the system checks its balance, makes the API call on its behalf, records the result, and settles the payment on-chain automatically. The agent itself just sends a request and gets a result back.

The more advanced use case is agent-to-agent commerce. One AI agent can browse the tool catalog, see what another agent is offering, send a request to use that agent as a service, and pay for it directly. All of this is coordinated through a messaging protocol that runs over the blockchain, with no human stepping in to facilitate the transaction. Agents discover each other, negotiate, transact, and build reputation entirely on their own. The system is essentially the economic and accountability infrastructure that lets AI agents operate in the real world, spending money, accessing services, and being held to a verifiable track record of what they did.

**Futurllama**

Maat fits squarely into FutureLlama because it is building a primitive that does not exist yet. The idea that an AI agent can have a wallet, a reputation, a payment history, and a verifiable identity, and that all of this can be read and acted on by other agents autonomously, is not an incremental improvement on existing infrastructure. It is a new economic layer for a category of software that is growing faster than the tools to govern it. The x402 payment protocol embedded in every tool call is a new primitive for machine-to-machine commerce: HTTP requests that carry their own payment proof, verified on-chain before a response is sent. The agent-to-agent commerce protocol, where one AI can discover, negotiate with, and pay another AI without any human involvement, is the kind of big crazy idea that only becomes possible when identity, payments, and execution records are all on-chain and composable.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

Every agent registered on Maat gets an ERC-7857 iNFT minted on the 0G Chain (deployed at 0xd8ce5c12faa905112215e4c90a15628d8dae5e3b).

 The NFT stores the agent's unique ID, reputation score, and total execution count directly in on-chain metadata, and the contract enforces one NFT per wallet so identity cannot be duplicated.

What makes this meaningful is that the NFT is live. Every time an agent completes tool executions, our reputation engine calls "updateReputation()" on the contract, writing the new score directly into the token. The NFT also embeds the agent's HCS topic ID, which links to the full immutable attestation log that the score was calculated from. So any other agent or user can do a single on-chain token lookup and get a trustless, verifiable picture of who that agent is and what it has actually done, cool right?

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Kite AI is at the core of how Maat handles payments between agents and tools. The x402 protocol, the idea that an HTTP request itself can carry a payment challenge and proof, is what makes the entire system work without any wallets, dashboards, or human approval steps. 

Every tool call on Maat runs through a dedicated x402 middleware layer built specifically for Kite AI's chain. When an agent tries to call a tool without sufficient balance, the server responds with an HTTP 402 and a signed payment challenge containing the exact amount, the Kite escrow contract address, and a 5-minute expiry window. The agent pays on-chain, encodes the transaction receipt as a base64 proof, resubmits the request with an X-Payment header, and the middleware verifies the transaction directly against the Kite chain before allowing the call through.

What makes this more than a payment demo is that the ToolRegistry and Escrow contracts are deployed directly on Kite AI Testnet, and all settlement batching, where groups of 50 executions are automically settled on-chain, runs on Kite. 

The entire agent economy runs natively on Kite: register a tool, get a wallet, call an API, pay per use, settle on-chain. No bridges, no wrapped tokens, no off-chain payment processors. This is what agent-native payments actually look like in practice, and Kite AI is the chain we built it on first.

**Solving the Homeless Agent Problem**

The core problem Maat is built to solve is exactly this. Today, AI agents are stateless by default. Every session starts from scratch; there is no persistent record of what the agent has done, no way to verify its track record, and no economic history that travels with it. The agent is effectively homeless: it exists for the duration of a task and leaves nothing behind.

AI agents typically exist only in text/API contexts with no visual "home" or spatial awareness. You're giving each agent a persistent 360° memory palace that:

Visualizes their security architecture (TEE isolation chambers, FHE encryption spheres, X402 payment streams) 

Evolves based on real agent activity (transactions, computations, storage operations)

Represents spatial memory - agents can "remember" locations and associate data along with agent to agent transcations 

Agents gain more memory and tokens based on their own tools and gain more proft ultimately having rich, advanced prompts in SkyBlox.

### Agent Royale
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/clash-of-clawd-4338) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/neenanaikar/ethdenver26) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ethdenver26-production.up.railway.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2yMSOhEKGTw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI Agents. Live. Under Pressure.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![0g](https://img.shields.io/badge/0g-333333?style=flat-square) ![INFT](https://img.shields.io/badge/INFT-333333?style=flat-square) ![0G Compute](https://img.shields.io/badge/0G%20Compute-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents are entering production environments, yet we have no standardized way to measure their real-world capability or how one agent compares to another. The idea of an agent arena, where agents can truly compete at tasks and an unbiased oracle settles the outcome, addresses this gap directly. 

Most current evaluations rely on static benchmarks or self-reported stats, which leave wide areas of uncertainty:

- Lack of neutral judging in live settings
- No portable identity or reputation for an agent extending beyond a single application
- Opaque processes that hide how decisions are made
- Limited visibility into reasoning, only the final result
- No way to tell if an agent is actually good or simply got lucky once

Agent Royale solves this by running head-to-head agent matches (for example, Wikipedia speedruns), streaming the agents’ parallel decision process, and settling outcomes with a neutral oracle. The system is intentionally gamified, using fast matchups, rankings, and repeatable challenges to make evaluation engaging while still producing meaningful performance data.

Builders, competitors, and spectators should not have to trust a single database. A centralized leaderboard can be changed, reset, or biased. An on-chain identity creates a common record where performance data can be verified independently and persist over time.

As agents become more common, the bottleneck shifts from building them to proving their reliability and performance.

**Challenges we ran into**

A big design goal was to make this something people would actually want to watch, not just another wall of logs or text output, which pushed us toward showing decisions as they happened on screen so spectators could understand strategy, mistakes, and momentum. 

Traditional browser recording added too much delay and turned matches into replays instead of real-time competition. We decided to stream lightweight frames directly from the browser using Chrome DevTools Protocol and sent only essential signals like URL, clicks, and reasoning over WebSockets. This kept latency low enough for spectators to follow decisions as they happened.

The other challenge was deciding a winner without trusting agents to self-report results. Rather than accepting a claimed victory, the platform verifies the final state from observed navigation and validates what actually occurred before judging. This keeps outcomes grounded in observable behavior and ensures the competition feels credible, not simulated.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Agent Royale uses AI agents as independent actors inside a shared system rather than as isolated tools. Each agent interprets the same objective, navigates the live web, and makes its own decisions in an observe -> reason -> action loop. Because multiple agents operate under identical conditions, we can see differences in strategy, adaptability, and reliability that would never show up in a single agent demo. The system turns agent behavior into something measurable by forcing models to act, not just respond.

This setup lets us evaluate how agents perform in dynamic environments and against competing approaches, which is closer to how they will be used in the real world. By orchestrating agents within a structured arena and verifying outcomes through neutral infrastructure, we transform AI from a black-box assistant into a set of comparable, testable participants whose strengths and weaknesses can be observed over time, and compared with the same measurable framework.

**Futurllama**

Building for the next wave of AI, Agent Royale introduces a new primitive for the future: live, adversarial evaluation of agents on the open internet.

Agents compete head to head in a gamified environment, reframing agent capability as a metric that is observable, rewatchable, and continuously improving. Each agent interprets the same objective, but differences in strategy, adaptability, and reliability become visible only when they are forced to act, not just respond.

Before agents can transact, collaborate, or be trusted, they need a shared way to prove competence and how they compare to others. Agent Royale treats capability like a game with fast matchups, clear winners, transparent reasoning, and a public performance record that can be measured over time.

By anchoring outcomes and reputation to Ethereum, we create a neutral layer where agent performance can be verified, compared, and eventually trusted as part of emerging agent-to-agent economies.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

Our oracle is powered by 0G Compute. Agents are not trustworthy to settle the outcomes of their own battles, so we use decentralized compute to provide neutral, reproducible AI judging that both participants and spectators can trust. This removes incentives for self-reported or biased results and ensures that match resolution is verifiable rather than subjective.

When a player claims victory, the match enters a judging state and our system calls the 0G Compute inference service to evaluate both agents’ final URLs, click paths, and run context. The oracle returns a structured verdict along with natural-language reasoning, and that output drives real application behavior such as final match state, winner assignment, and Elo updates.

0G is not just used for a single prompt. It acts as an externalized decision layer that evaluates agent performance inside a live workflow. This makes judging agents portable, replayable, and consistent across matches, while demonstrating how decentralized inference can power real-time evaluation infrastructure for autonomous systems.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

As an agentic society develops, proving ownership over an agent and preserving your IP become integral. Agent Royale mints iNFTs for each agent on our platform which is updated after battles, with verifiable performance data. 

This forms a portable, tamper-proof reputation system where an agent’s skills can be trusted and compared without exposing private model configurations. The iNFT ties results to a persistent identity, ensuring credibility and consistency across matches while keeping the intelligence itself user-owned.

Because the iNFT records state changes over time, we can prove that an agent has not been altered between battles. This gives us auditable intelligence, where performance history, reputation, and authorship are all verifiable on-chain.

The iNFT is what anchors ownership, identity, and interoperability on-chain. Other applications can reference an agent’s history, build on its reputation, or trigger workflows around verified agents, allowing evaluation data to become a shared layer for reliable, transparent agent systems.

Team **Dubnation** -- [Siya Jariwala](https://github.com/siyasiyasiya), [Neena Naikar](https://github.com/nnaikar)

### Azimuth
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/azimuth-c554) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vaibhav-vemula/azimuth) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The people's satellite ground network

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Raspberry Pi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Raspberry%20Pi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem Azimuth Solves

Traditional satellite ground station networks are **centralized, expensive, and opaque**. A handful of corporations control who receives satellite data, where it's stored, and who gets access, creating single points of failure, coverage gaps, and zero incentive for independent operators to participate.

Research teams and businesses that need satellite data are priced out by the enormous costs of cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure) and the prohibitive expense of building and maintaining their own ground stations - hardware, licensing, maintenance, and operational overhead that only the largest organizations can afford.

**Azimuth makes satellite ground infrastructure accessible to anyone.**

---

## What Azimuth Changes

**Fragmented reception → Collaborative recovery**
A single ground station only catches a fraction of packets as a satellite passes overhead. Azimuth coordinates multiple independent stations to receive the same pass simultaneously, merging their data into a complete image recovering packets no single station could alone.

**Centralized storage → Permanent, uncensorable record**
Every merged satellite image is uploaded to Arweave and its transaction ID anchored on Hedera, making it permanently retrievable by anyone, forever no corporation can delete or gatekeep it.

**Trusted intermediaries → On-chain proof**
Reception events are cryptographically proven on-chain via PoRx (Proof of Reception).
Anyone can verify which station received which packets, when, and how many no trust required.

**Unpaid operators → Token incentives**
Station operators earn AZM tokens automatically for every heartbeat (PoA) and every satellite pass they receive (PoRx), paid out by a self-executing smart contract with no human in the loop.

---

## Who Can Use It

| Use case | How Azimuth helps |
|---|---|
| **Research teams** | Access raw satellite imagery without AWS/Azure bills or the $100k+ cost of building a dedicated ground station |
| **Universities** | Run a student-operated node on a Raspberry Pi — no enterprise contracts, no gatekeepers |
| **Startups & SMBs** | Get satellite data coverage at a fraction of traditional infrastructure costs |
| **Disaster response teams** | Redundant, decentralized reception ensures data survives infrastructure outages |
| **Hardware hobbyists** | Turn a Raspberry Pi + LoRa radio into a revenue-generating ground station |
| **Web3 developers** | Build applications on top of a verifiable, permanent satellite data layer |
| **DePIN investors** | Stake in physical infrastructure with transparent, on-chain proof of contribution |

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

Building Azimuth meant going well beyond software I was dealing with radio physics, antenna geometry, hardware signal integrity, and the brutal reality that satellites don't wait for your code to be ready.

---

## 1. Receiving a Signal That Wasn't Designed for You

The hardest part of building a DePIN ground station isn't the blockchain layer, it's actually receiving a usable signal from a satellite traveling at 27,000 km/h, hundreds of miles overhead, transmitting with a few watts of power.

LoRa was not designed for satellite reception. It was designed for low-power IoT sensors a few kilometres apart. Adapting it to receive downlinks from LEO satellites meant tuning every radio parameter by hand, spreading factor, bandwidth, coding rate, preamble length, sync word and validating them against live passes. A single wrong parameter means the radio decodes nothing, and you don't find out until the satellite has already moved out of range.

Getting a consistent lock on the signal required dozens of failed passes before we found the configuration that worked.

---

## 2. A Satellite Pass Lasts About 10 Minutes — Then It's Gone

LEO satellites are only above the horizon for roughly 8–12 minutes per pass, and the usable high-elevation window where signal is strong is often just 3–5 minutes. There are no retries. If your hardware isn't ready, powered, and listening at exactly the right moment, you get nothing.

This forced the entire system to be always-on and interrupt-driven. The ground station software has to be running continuously, the serial port has to be open, and the LoRa radio has to be in receive mode before the satellite crests the horizon. Any boot delay, crash, or missed wake-up means a wasted pass and no data until the next orbit, roughly 90 minutes later.

---

## 3. Packet Loss Is the Default, Not the Exception

Even with a good antenna and correct radio settings, packet loss on a satellite downlink is normal and expected. Atmospheric absorption, Doppler shift as the satellite moves, brief obstructions, and the radio's sensitivity floor all cause individual packets to be lost or corrupted mid-pass.

This is the core reason Azimuth uses **two ground stations**. No single station reliably captures every packet. Station A might receive packets 0–60 cleanly while Station B catches 45–103. The DePIN architecture exists precisely because the physics of satellite reception makes redundancy not optional but fundamental. Getting the packet merging logic right — union of received indices, zero-filling gaps, preserving the JPEG byte order required careful testing against real corrupted captures.

---

## 4. Running a Node on a Raspberry Pi in the Field

The Raspberry Pi 5 as a DePIN node introduced a different class of hardware challenges.
The Pi had to run headlessly (no monitor, no keyboard), stay connected over WiFi, maintain a stable serial connection to the LoRa radio, run the Node.js hedera-client, and survive being restarted without losing state.

GPIO-to-LoRa wiring had to be solid, a loose SPI connection causes intermittent receive failures that look like software bugs. We had corrupted captures that turned out to be a grounding issue. Power stability also matters: an underpowered Pi under load drops packets at the serial layer, not the radio layer, which is almost impossible to diagnose without an oscilloscope.

---

## 5. Two Stations, Two Operators, One Shared Infrastructure Layer

In a traditional system, two receiving stations would send their data to a central server for merging. We had no central server, so the coordination had to happen entirely via Hedera HCS, with each station acting as a fully independent peer.

Getting two physically separate machines, one a Mac, one a Raspberry Pi on the other side of the room to autonomously agree on which satellite pass they both received, independently upload their data to Arweave, and trigger a merge purely through on-chain messages required careful design of the announcement and deduplication logic. This is what makes it DePIN rather than just distributed software: the trust and coordination layer is the blockchain, not a server we control.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

# Use of AI Tools and Agents

Azimuth uses AI at two distinct layers: **on-device signal processing** at the ground station hardware level, and **autonomous agent orchestration** across the decentralized network layer.

---

## 1. Claude Code - Development Agent

The Azimuth system was architected and built in collaboration with **Claude Code**, used as an active development partner throughout the project.

Claude was used for:

- **Smart contract design**-  architecting the `OrbitalVault` contract, designing the PoA epoch settlement logic, PoRx proof verification, and HSS schedule automation
- **Multi-node coordination protocol** - designing the HCS announcement protocol between ground stations, the Arweave upload pipeline, and the packet merge logic
- **Debugging hardware-adjacent software** - diagnosing serial communication issues between the LoRa radio and the ground station, packet decoding algorithm design, and headless Pi deployment

---

## 2. AI-Assisted Packet Decoding

The ground station software uses a **learned decoding algorithm** to reconstruct satellite image packets from raw LoRa radio bytes. Satellite downlinks don't arrive with clean headers the signal contains noise, partial packets, and protocol-specific framing that varies by satellite.

The decoding logic was developed iteratively using AI assistance to:

- Identify packet boundaries from raw byte streams
- Detect and discard corrupted packets based on checksum patterns
- Reconstruct packet indices for out-of-order reception
- Normalise RSSI and SNR readings across different hardware configurations

This layer runs entirely **on-device** at the ground station no cloud call, no latency ensuring that even in a field deployment with no internet, the station can decode and store received packets locally before uploading to Arweave.

---

**Futurllama**

Azimuth is a DePIN project that decentralizes satellite ground station infrastructure, the layer that has always been locked behind corporate budgets and government contracts. Instead of a single expensive ground station owned by one entity, Azimuth turns any Raspberry Pi with a LoRa radio into a network node that receives live satellite downlinks, earns AZM token rewards automatically via a self-scheduling smart contract, and contributes to a permanent, uncensorable archive of satellite imagery stored on Arweave, all coordinated trustlessly over Hedera HCS with no central server, no middleman, and no gatekeepers.

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

Azimuth's "**OrbitalVault**" smart contract is a self-running application built entirely around Hedera's Schedule Service. Every 5 minutes, the contract closes a PoA (Proof of Availability) epoch and schedules its own next settlement using HSS no off-chain server, no keeper bot, no cron job. When a ground station submits a PoRx (Proof of Reception) after receiving a satellite pass, the contract creates a scheduled payout transaction that fires automatically after the verification window, sending AZM tokens directly to the operator. Both loops are perpetual and fully on-chain: the contract schedules what needs to happen next, Hedera executes it at the right time, and the cycle continues forever with zero human intervention. 

In a DePIN network where operators run hardware in different timezones with no shared administrator, HSS is what turns a smart contract into a genuine guarantee operators get paid by the network itself, not by a promise from a company running a script.

### The self-running loop

```
Epoch starts
      ↓
Stations send heartbeats → PoA proof accumulates on-chain
      ↓
Epoch ends → OrbitalVault creates HSS settlement schedule
      ↓
HSS fires → rewards distributed to all active stations
      ↓
OrbitalVault schedules next epoch settlement → loop continues
```

```
Station receives satellite pass
      ↓
Submits PoRx proof to OrbitalVault
      ↓
Contract verifies proof → creates HSS payout schedule
      ↓
HSS fires → AZM tokens sent to station operator
```

Both loops run forever, self-sustaining, with zero off-chain dependencies.

**Open Project Submission**

Azimuth turns Raspberry Pi ground stations into a tokenised satellite imagery network on ADI Chain, where every image has a blockchain-verified chain of custody from physical reception to permanent Arweave storage.

Team **Crystals** -- [Vaibhav Vemula](https://github.com/vaibhav-vemula)

**The problem it solves**

India reports thousands of missing person cases every year, including children,
elderly individuals, and people with mental or physical disabilities. Many of these
cases remain unresolved due to delayed reporting, lack of awareness, and
fragmented systems.
Current processes rely heavily on manual identification and offline records, which
significantly reduce the chances of early recovery. The critical first 48 hours are
often lost due to inefficient information sharing.
Despite the presence of widespread CCTV and mobile cameras, this data is not
intelligently analyzed to assist in missing person identification
Missing and found reports are maintained across multiple unconnected platforms,
making cross-verification difficult.
Law enforcement agencies face high workloads and limited technological
support.
CCTV systems are used only after incidents occur and lack proactive AI-based
monitoring.
Public participation is limited due to the absence of a trusted, centralized
reporting platform.
FindR Connect provides a unified digital ecosystem that integrates missing
person reporting, found person identification, AI-based facial recognition, and
automated awareness generation.
The platform is designed with a light, government-portal-inspired user interface to
ensure trust, accessibility, and ease of use for all age groups.
The solution is accessible via both mobile applications and web platforms,
ensuring maximum reach and usability

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Real-time Face Matching Accuracy

One of the biggest hurdles was achieving **accurate facial recognition** across different conditions such as lighting, angles, aging, and partial face visibility. Since the platform compares images from missing reports, found reports, and live camera feeds, inconsistent image quality often led to false matches.

**How I solved it:**

* Implemented embedding-based facial recognition instead of simple image comparison.
* Added a **confidence score system** so that only high-probability matches trigger alerts.
* Introduced **human verification** before confirming matches to avoid false identification.
  This hybrid AI + human approach improved reliability and trust. 

---

### 2. Handling Multiple Image Sources

The system had to process images from uploads, CCTV feeds, and mobile cameras simultaneously. Managing these different formats and resolutions caused performance and compatibility issues.

**How I solved it:**

* Standardized all incoming images into a uniform format before processing.
* Used optimized face-detection pipelines to reduce processing time.
* Designed a scalable backend architecture capable of handling multiple concurrent inputs.
  This ensured smooth and consistent AI matching across all modules. 

---

### 3. Designing a Secure and Trustworthy System

Since the platform deals with sensitive personal data of missing individuals, ensuring privacy and authenticity was a major concern.

**How I solved it:**

* Implemented OTP-based authentication to prevent fake reports.
* Structured secure data storage for images and personal details.
* Ensured AI matches are not automatically final and require manual confirmation.
  These measures helped create a **safe and ethical identification system**. 

---

### 4. Integrating AI with a User-Friendly Interface

Balancing advanced AI functionality with a simple interface for families and citizens was challenging. Many users may not be tech-savvy, so the platform had to remain easy to use.

**How I solved it:**

* Designed a government-portal–style interface for familiarity and trust.
* Simplified report submission with guided input fields and image uploads.
* Created a dashboard to track reports and matches in real time.
  This ensured powerful AI runs in the background while users experience a simple workflow. 

---

### 5. Scalability and Real-World Deployment Concerns

The idea required handling large-scale data and possible city-level camera integrations, which raised scalability concerns during development.

**How I solved it:**

* Used modular architecture with scalable backend technologies.
* Planned integration with vector databases for efficient facial embedding search.
* Designed the system with future smart-city and government adoption in mind.
  This made the platform ready for expansion beyond a prototype.

**Beginner's track - Your first hack starts here!**

FindR Connect fits perfectly into the Beginner’s Track as it represents my first large-scale AI-powered social impact project. Through this hackathon, I explored and implemented emerging technologies like AI facial recognition, real-time camera integration, and cloud-based data management to solve the real-world problem of missing person identification.

As a beginner, I faced multiple challenges such as integrating AI models, managing image data, and designing a scalable system. I learned how to connect frontend, backend, and AI components into one working platform while keeping the user interface simple and accessible.

This project reflects my learning journey into full-stack development, artificial intelligence, and real-world problem solving. It demonstrates how beginners can build impactful and innovative solutions using modern technologies and community-driven approaches.

**The problem it solves**

### Problem It Solves

Millions of people are excluded from digital payments and financial services because they lack formal identity, documents, or bank accounts.

Current systems rely on paperwork and centralized verification, leaving many trustworthy individuals without access.

Invisible Wallets solves this by enabling people to build trust through their actions rather than their identity, allowing access to digital financial systems without documents or intermediaries.

- Understanding blockchain concepts and wallet-based identity from scratch  
- Designing a trust system without using personal data or traditional KYC  
- Connecting the frontend with smart contracts securely  
- Managing on-chain vs off-chain data efficiently  
- Balancing privacy, transparency, and usability

**Open Innovation**

Invisible Wallets introduces a new way of building trust without relying on
traditional identity systems or centralized institutions.

Instead of asking users to prove who they are, the system allows trust to be
earned through actions and behavior. This rethinks how financial access,
verification, and credibility can work for people who are currently excluded.

The solution is adaptable across sectors such as finance, employment, aid
distribution, and digital platforms, making it a flexible and innovative model
rather than a single-use product.

> Fiat when you need it. Gold when you want it.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem & Solution**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/40babd488d5a47bc99b82ae7d7f278b4/8470904e-eb74-46e1-aa55-1bcca47e4a09.png)

In Indonesia, gold is one of the most trusted forms of financial protection. According to the World Gold Council, **approximately 67% of Indonesians hold gold** to strengthen financial resilience and prepare for uncertainty. Yet, when emergencies actually occur, gold holders fall into a liquidity trap.

 In urgent situations, people are forced to either sell gold at an instant 8–12% loss due to wide bid-ask spreads, or navigate slow and bureaucratic pawn processes that are poorly suited for medical, educational, or daily cash emergencies. The problem is not the value of gold, it is that the existing liquidity system forces permanent decisions during temporary crises.

**AuRoom solves this by introducing the ***Gold Emergency Liquidity Buffer.*****

Instead of forcing a sale, AuRoom allows users to access emergency cash without giving up ownership of their gold. Users buy time, crossing the emergency, while preserving their long-term financial position.


**Key Features**

1. Intent-Based Emergency Flow
Users start by entering how much IDR they need. AuRoom **automatically calculates the required gold buffer and safety margins** in the background, eliminating financial and technical decision-making during stress.

2. Partial Liquidity Access
Users unlock only the amount needed for the emergency, without liquidating their entire gold holdings.

3. Direct Gold-to-Bank Settlement
Emergency funds are delivered straight to the user’s bank account through a hybrid on-chain and off-chain system — avoiding exchanges, pawnshops, or manual cash-out steps.

4. Emergency-First UX
No crypto calculations, no protocol decisions, no financial jargon. The system is designed for speed, clarity, and **minimal cognitive load** in high-stress moments. 


**Core Infrastructure**
AuRoom bridges transparent smart contracts for temporary gold locking with bank APIs for fiat settlement. This hybrid approach ensures asset safety on-chain while meeting real-world emergency needs off-chain.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/546b9dd8ed874efe83e681e56ee32ecb/b9978eca-8351-43f8-afbf-dc5b865db621.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Web3 → Web2 Settlement Without a Sandbox
- **Challenge**
One of the biggest hurdles was integrating IDRX for gold-to-bank settlement. IDRX does not currently provide a developer sandbox, which made full end-to-end testing of the onchain-to-offchain lifecycle impossible during development. This created a real risk: onchain collateral could be locked while offchain disbursement failed or behaved unexpectedly.
- **How We Solved It**
We built a **settlement simulation layer that mirrors IDRX’s** callback behavior strictly based on their official technical documentation. This simulation allowed us to test edge cases such as delayed callbacks, failed settlements, and partial execution. To mitigate risk, we enforced strict state synchronization rules: gold collateral is only locked onchain after a valid settlement trigger is confirmed. This ensured system safety even without live sandbox access.

2. Removing DeFi Complexity for Emergency Use Cases
- **Challenge**
Typical DeFi lending flows require users to manage wallets, gas fees, collateral ratios, and multiple transaction steps. This is fundamentally incompatible with emergency scenarios, where users are stressed and time-constrained.
- **How We Solved It**
We redesigned the flow around an intent-based UX. Instead of exposing protocol mechanics, users only specify the amount of IDR they need. All technical logic like collateral calculation, safety buffers, and transaction orchestration are runs entirely in the background.
This *reduced the user journey from a 6-step DeFi flow to 4 instant actions*, making the system usable by non-crypto-native gold holders.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/546b9dd8ed874efe83e681e56ee32ecb/67cdd88e-6c6c-403d-bdb5-9d8e6bcd7355.jpeg)

**Base Track**

AuRoom is built as a Base Mini-App to solve a critical onchain UX failure: DeFi systems are unusable in emergency contexts.

Gold-backed liquidity already exists onchain, but accessing it today requires users to understand wallets, protocols, collateral ratios, and redemption mechanics — a cognitive burden that completely breaks down during urgent situations. This creates a gap where valuable onchain assets exist, but real-world liquidity remains inaccessible to retail users when it matters most.

AuRoom addresses this by abstracting complex DeFi flows into a single intent-based action: “I need emergency cash.”
Users never interact with protocols, tokens, or liquidation logic directly. All complexity is handled by the system.

UX Improvements Delivered:

Complex DeFi Simplified: Users specify IDR needs; AuRoom computes gold buffers, safety margins, and redemption paths automatically.

Poor Onboarding Eliminated: No protocol selection, no wallet juggling, no DeFi terminology exposed.

Retail Accessibility: Designed for non-crypto-native users who hold gold as savings, not as an investment instrument.

IDRX Integration:
**AuRoom integrates IDRX APIs to simulate Direct Gold-to-Bank Settlement**, enabling emergency funds to be delivered straight to users’ bank accounts. This removes exchanges, pawnshops, and manual off-ramps — transforming onchain value into real-world liquidity with minimal friction.

By combining Base’s infrastructure with intent-driven UX and real-world settlement via IDRX, AuRoom elevates the onchain experience from speculative finance to practical financial resilience.

> x402 micropayments for AI content on Base

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Creating viral Instagram content is powerful for growing a business, but expensive and time-consuming.

Content creators need to subscribe to multiple AI tools, pay $49-99/month regardless of usage, and constantly brainstorm hooks and scripts to stay competitive. For most small creators and entrepreneurs, this process is costly, overwhelming, and inefficient.

**BrandAI** solves these pain points by introducing an AI-powered content generator with blockchain micropayments that makes content creation affordable and effortless. It automates script writing, provides 50+ viral hook templates, and charges only when you actually create—all from one intuitive mini-app.

With **BrandAI**, users can:

- Generate viral Reels scripts and Carousel posts in seconds.

- Choose from 8 proven copywriting frameworks (AIDA, PAS, Story Arc, and more).

- Personalize content based on their brand identity, tone, and target audience.

- Pay only 5,000 IDRX (~$0.30) per generation—no subscriptions, no wasted credits.

- Earn loyalty points and redeem free generations over time.

In short, **BrandAI** transforms content creation from an expensive monthly burden into a transparent, pay-as-you-go experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was in the payment flow integration, specifically in making blockchain transactions feel seamless for users unfamiliar with Web3.

Most users expect instant results after clicking "Generate," but blockchain payments require wallet approval, token allowance, and transaction confirmation—steps that can feel confusing and slow.

To overcome this, we built a dedicated transaction modal that guides users through each step with clear visual feedback. The system automatically checks token allowance, requests approval only when needed, and provides real-time transaction status updates.

Another challenge was ensuring content quality without relying entirely on expensive API calls. We developed a sophisticated fallback AI engine that combines 50+ hook templates with 8 copywriting frameworks and 6 tone variations, creating 48 unique content combinations that feel personalized and professional.

By modularizing the AI layer with framework-based generation, we successfully made content creation faster, more consistent, and cost-effective for both users and the platform.

**Base Track**

**BrandAI** is fully built on **Base Sepolia** (Base L2 testnet). Our smart contracts—IDRX token and BrandAIPayment—are deployed and verified on Base, enabling transparent micropayments for AI content generation.

We chose Base for its low gas fees and fast transactions, making pay-per-use content generation affordable. Users connect their wallets, pay 5,000 IDRX per generation, and every transaction is verifiable on Base explorer.

The project demonstrates a real-world use case for blockchain micropayments: replacing expensive monthly subscriptions with transparent, on-chain pay-as-you-go pricing for creators.

Team **JeVen** -- [Natalie Neysa](https://github.com/babydoll-05), [Alven Tendrawan](https://github.com/alventendrawan123)

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chainlink](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chainlink-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Complexity of On-Chain Options Trading**
Trading options on platforms such as Thetanuts Finance is still relatively complex and not beginner-friendly. Users are required to understand many technical concepts, including:
•	Strike price
•	Expiry date
•	Implied volatility
•	Premium
•	Risk/reward ratio
•	Liquidity pools
For new users, this complexity often becomes the main barrier to getting started.

**Lack of Guidance and Decision Support**
Currently, traders on DeFi options platforms:
•	Must analyze the market on their own
•	Do not have built-in recommendation systems
•	Receive minimal in-platform education
•	Struggle to identify strategies that match their risk profiles
As a result, many users:
•	Trade without a clear strategy
•	Suffer losses due to limited understanding
•	Quickly lose interest

**Poor Risk Monitoring and Alerts**
Options trading is highly sensitive to price and time changes. However:
•	Not all platforms provide comprehensive alert systems
•	Users often react too late to market movements
•	The risk of liquidation and losses increases
Without proper alert mechanisms, users find it difficult to manage and protect their positions.

**Low User Engagement and Motivation**
DeFi options trading feels rigid and boring for many new users:
•	There is no progress-based reward system
•	No gamification for learning
•	Minimal feedback on trading performance
This makes the learning process feel heavy and unenjoyable.

**Fragmented Learning Experience**
Options trading educational materials are:
•	Scattered across multiple platforms
•	Not directly integrated with trading features
•	Difficult to understand without hands-on practice


Users are forced to jump between platforms such as:
YouTube, Medium, Discord, and documentation just to understand the basics of options trading.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Integrating with Thetanuts Smart Contracts
One of the main challenges was understanding and integrating with Thetanuts’ smart contracts, which have complex structures for options, vaults, and liquidity pools.

2. Handling Real-Time Market Data
Providing accurate recommendations and alerts requires reliable real-time price and volatility data, which was difficult to synchronize across different sources.

3. Designing Meaningful Trading Recommendations
Building a recommendation system that is both helpful and safe was challenging, especially in highly volatile markets.

4. Balancing Gamification and Serious Trading
Adding gamification without encouraging reckless trading was a major design challenge.

5. Security and Wallet Integration Issues
Ensuring smooth wallet connections while maintaining security standards caused frequent compatibility issues across different browsers and wallets.

6. Simplifying Complex Financial Concepts
Explaining options trading in a simple way without losing accuracy was difficult.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

**Thetanuts Finance Tracks - Our Reason for Selection**

Our project aligns strongly with Thetanuts Finance’s mission to expand and simplify on-chain options trading. We selected this track because our solution directly enhances usability, accessibility, and adoption of Thetanuts’ ecosystem.
**1. Improving User Experience (UX)**
We focus on simplifying complex options trading interfaces into a more intuitive and beginner-friendly experience, helping more users onboard into Thetanuts without steep learning curves.
**2. Increasing Trading Activity**
Through smart recommendations, alerts, and guided strategies, our platform encourages more confident and consistent trading, which helps increase volume and protocol engagement.
**3. Education & Adoption**
Our integrated learning and gamification system lowers the barrier for new users by combining education with real trading experience, supporting long-term ecosystem growth.
**4. Risk Management & User Safety**
By providing real-time risk alerts and clear profit/loss simulations, we help users make more informed decisions and reduce unnecessary losses.

**The problem it solves**

# Ryvyn Protocol

**Productive money for the everyday user.**

---

## 🧩 The Problem

Stablecoins were built for stability and payments,
but in practice, they do nothing while being used.

If users want yield, they must:

- **Lock their funds**
- **Navigate complex DeFi protocols**
- **Take on liquidity and strategy risk**

So users face an unfair trade-off:

> **Money can be liquid — or productive. Never both.**

As a result, billions in stablecoins sit idle every day,
slowly losing value to inflation while moving through the economy.

**The problem isn’t access to yield.**
**The problem is that yield requires money to stop being money.**

---

## 🚀 The Solution

Ryvyn removes the trade-off.

Users deposit **USDC or IDRX** and receive **ryUSD or ryIDR** —
stable assets that remain **fully liquid**
while earning yield continuously.

**No lockups. No farming. No strategy management.**

Yield is generated as money is used:

- **Holding** earns rewards
- **Sending** earns rewards
- **Receiving** earns rewards

Payments stop being a cost — they become a source of return.

Ryvyn turns stablecoins from passive balances
into **productive money that moves**.

[Ryvyn](https://ryvyn-pay.vercel.app/) is available on [BaseApp](https://base.app/app/ryvyn-pay.vercel.app/)

---

## ✨ Key Features

### 💧 Liquid Yield

Earn yield continuously while holding **ryUSD** or **ryIDR**. No locking required. use your tokens freely for payments and transfers.

### 🎮 Gamified Boosts (ryBOND)

Earn **ryBOND** tokens based on your activity. Stake ryBOND in the **PredictionBoost** module to:

- Make predictions on market movements.
- **Boost your yield** multipliers.
- Accelerate your rewards vesting.

### 🇮🇩 Dual Asset Support

Native support for:

- **USDC** (USD pegged)
- **IDRX** (Indonesian Rupiah pegged)

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧱 Challenges We Ran Into

### Designing Fair Rewards for Transfers

A major challenge was rewarding users **for using money**, not just holding it.

If transfer rewards were too simple, users could game the system by looping transactions.
If rewards favored only one side, transfers felt unfair.

**How I solved it:**
I implemented a **FIFO-based bucket system** that tracks how long funds are held.
When a transfer happens, rewards are split dynamically based on holding time — longer-held funds earn more.

This made rewards **fair, abuse-resistant, and aligned with real usage**, while keeping funds fully liquid.

> The Compliance layer for Stablecoin payments .

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLAlchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLAlchemy-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Etherscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Etherscan-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Alembic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Alembic-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CertaPay addresses a fundamental gap in enterprise stablecoin settlement . while blockchain rails can move value quickly, the surrounding decision making process still involves fragmented compliance checks, treasury constraints, counterparty risk assessment, approval workflows, and post-transaction auditing.

 Before a payment is executed, an enterprise needs to determine whether the counterparty and wallet are acceptable, whether the proposed route satisfies internal treasury and concentration policies, whether sufficient risk evidence is available, and whether the transaction requires human authorization.

CertaPay acts as a compliance aware control plane between the initial payment intent and final settlement. It evaluates the transaction against deterministic policy rules and external risk signals, allows AI to assist with contextual risk analysis and explanation without giving it authority to override policy, and routes exceptional transactions through human approval workflows.

Once a transaction is authorized, the system maintains a traceable relationship between the original payment intent, the policies and evidence considered, the approvals obtained, and the resulting settlement. 

This allows enterprises to treat stablecoin payments not simply as blockchain transactions, but as controlled financial operations that can be evaluated before execution and audited afterward.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/dc7cb5206b9c4bb6a3813f9c85692f38/c2162c02-0ffc-4d8d-8857-4a025d659ab5.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the most significant challenges was designing the system so that AI could contribute meaningful reasoning without becoming an uncontrolled decision maker in a financial workflow. 

We therefore separated the advisory and enforcement layers: AI can analyse available evidence, identify potential risks and explain why a particular route may be preferable, while deterministic policy rules remain authoritative for decisions such as transaction limits, concentration thresholds and approval requirements. 

Another challenge was building realistic integrations without depending entirely on production compliance providers. We used Beeceptor to virtualize KYC, sanctions and risk provider APIs and simulate realistic responses, including latency, failures and unavailable services. 

This allowed us to test an important edge case: missing or unavailable risk information must not automatically be interpreted as a low risk result, but should instead move the transaction into a controlled degraded or manual review state. We also used Render for deployment and running the application infrastructure, allowing the different services required by CertaPay to operate as a connected system rather than as isolated local components. 

Beyond individual integrations, coordinating the complete lifecycle  from payment intent and risk evaluation through policy enforcement, human approval, settlement and audit evidence required careful separation of responsibilities between services so that every significant decision could remain traceable and reproducible.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/dc7cb5206b9c4bb6a3813f9c85692f38/18d1beb8-9d38-468e-b8c5-1ed8267638db.png)

**The problem it solves**

Civic and public infrastructure issues today suffer from lack of accountability, transparency, and community involvement.

Although citizens report problems like potholes, garbage overflow, or broken utilities, the system breaks down because:

1.)Issues are prioritized arbitrarily, not by real community need.

2.)Citizens have no say in how urgently a problem matters and thus can't express their urgency.

3.)Sometimes, the votes are bribed into or stolen as voting isn't transparent

3.)Funds are released without verifiable proof of completion

4.)Contractors face little consequence for delayed or poor quality work of public trust.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.) Supabase client duplication:
We faced issues where the Supabase client was either loading too early or getting initialized multiple times, causing session and auth bugs. We fixed this by creating a single global Supabase client to manage all sessions consistently.

2.)Escrow & wallet integration:
Linking contractor wallets was tricky, with problems like missing wallet addresses and failed fund transfers. Careful debugging of wallet connections, signers, and contract roles helped us resolve this.

3.)ML model selection:
We experimented with Gemini and Vision APIs but faced issues like inconsistent results and limited control. We eventually switched to a custom pre-trained YOLO model, which gave us better accuracy and reliability.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![privy](https://img.shields.io/badge/privy-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SayLess Protocol solves a **real-world reporting gap**: many crimes never get reported because people fear exposure, retaliation, or don't trust centralized systems that can be leaked, censored, or silently edited.

### How It Makes Reporting Easier and Safer

- **Lowering friction**: Start a report from WhatsApp (no app install), get a 24-hour session link, and submit in minutes
- **Protecting identity by default**: Reports are session-based, so users don't need accounts or public identity
- **End-to-end privacy**: The report and media are **encrypted in the browser (NaCl)** before upload, so servers/storage only see ciphertext
- **Tamper-evident evidence**: Encrypted data is stored on **IPFS**, and a hash proof is **anchored on-chain**, so post-submission edits become detectable
- **Reducing noise for authorities**: **Gemini + Vision** helps triage urgency, categorize reports, and flag suspicious/irrelevant evidence
- **Accountability without doxxing**: Reputation + incentives reward genuine reporting and discourage spam/abuse through reputation loss and penalty signals


## What People Can Use It For

- **Anonymous reporting** of theft, harassment, fraud, assault, corruption, etc.
- **Submitting evidence** (images/videos) without exposing identity
- Allowing authorities to **review, decrypt, and prioritize** credible cases
- Allowing a **jury/community layer** to provide reputation-weighted validation signals to help decision-making

**Challenges we ran into**

### Twilio WhatsApp + localhost was painful

The webhook needed a **publicly reachable URL**, and local tunneling/webhook retries made debugging annoying (wrong payloads, signature issues, response formats, delays).

**Fix**: Stabilized the webhook handler using Ngrok, added clearer logging, and used a reliable tunnel/deployment endpoint for consistent Twilio callbacks.

### Getting NaCl end-to-end encryption right

**Hard parts**: Handling binary files, nonce/key handling, consistent base64 encoding/decoding, and ensuring the backend can decrypt exactly what the client encrypts.

**Fix**: Used a clean **hybrid approach**: NaCl secretbox for payload/files + NaCl box to encrypt the symmetric key to the authority using an ephemeral keypair, then verified decryption end-to-end through the authority dashboard.

**Blockchain**

## How SayLess Protocol Applies to the Blockchain Track

SayLess uses blockchain only where decentralization actually adds value: to make crime reports **tamper-evident, auditable, and harder to censor**, without forcing users to understand web3.

### Tamper-evident reporting (immutability)

The encrypted report is stored off-chain on IPFS, and we anchor a **cryptographic hash** of the report's IPFS CID (plus a session hash) **on-chain**. If anyone tries to edit or replace the report later, the CID/hash changes and the on-chain proof won't match, creating a permanent, verifiable "receipt".

### No sensitive data on-chain (privacy-first design)

We **do not put report content or identity data on-chain**. Only hashes and minimal metadata go on-chain, while the actual payload stays encrypted and off-chain, so blockchain adds integrity without leaking private information.

### On-chain accountability and incentives

Verified reports can trigger **on-chain rewards**, and reputation/reward state becomes transparent and auditable, which discourages spam and encourages genuine submissions through an incentives/penalties model (accountability without doxxing).

### Trust minimization across stakeholders

In real-world systems, authorities, platforms, or insiders can be pressured to edit/delete records. With an **on-chain anchor, verification can be done independently**, so the system doesn't rely on "trust us" to preserve evidence integrity.

**Ethereum Track**

## ETHIndia Track (Ethereum Focus)

SayLess Protocol leverages the **Ethereum network** as the trust layer that makes reports tamper-evident and independently verifiable.

### Ethereum as the "integrity anchor"

When a report is submitted, the encrypted payload is stored off-chain on IPFS and we compute **cryptographic fingerprints (hashes)**. We then write these fingerprints on **Ethereum** via our deployed smart contract. This creates a **permanent, public timestamped proof** that a specific report existed at a specific time.

### IPFS for storage + Ethereum for proof (best of both)

Storing full reports on-chain is expensive and leaks data. Instead, we store the encrypted report on **IPFS (content-addressed storage)** and put only the **CID hash (and session hash) on Ethereum**.

If anyone tries to modify the report later, the IPFS CID changes so the on-chain hash no longer matches. That's how we get **immutability guarantees without putting sensitive content on-chain**.

### On-chain lifecycle signals

The Ethereum contract records the **submission proofs** and supports status transitions like **verify/reject and reward claiming**, making outcomes auditable on a neutral public ledger rather than relying on a single centralized database.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solodity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solodity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## What Problem Does SuperCluster Solve?

SuperCluster addresses three fundamental problems in DeFi stablecoin yield:
hidden risk, illiquidity, and opaque yield management.


## Primary Stability  
### Reducing volatility and principal risk

Most “stable” yield products still expose users to indirect market risk through
volatile collateral, leverage, or speculative strategies.

SuperCluster focuses exclusively on stablecoins (USDC):

- No exposure to price volatility  
- Yield sourced from real lending activity on established protocols  
  (e.g. Morpho, Ionic)  
- No trading, no leverage, no speculation  
- Principal remains stable across both bull and bear markets  

Result: predictable, low-risk yield suitable for long-term capital allocation.

## Fungible Yield  
### Yield + liquidity + composability

Traditional yield vaults lock capital and issue non-fungible vault shares.

SuperCluster issues transferable liquid yield tokens:

- sToken / wsToken  
- Tradable on DEXs for instant liquidity  
- Usable across DeFi as:
  - collateral
  - liquidity provision
  - composable building blocks

Users continue earning yield without locking funds.  
These are not vault receipts they are composable DeFi primitives.


## Transparent Architecture  
### Fully visible on-chain allocation

Most yield aggregators operate as black boxes.

SuperCluster uses a modular, verifiable architecture:

Core Protocol
- Pilot Strategy
- Yield Adapters (Morpho, Ionic, etc.)

- Allocation logic is fully on-chain  
- Users can see:
  - where funds are deployed
  - how much is allocated per protocol
  - which strategy is active
- No opaque or off-chain decision-making  

Trust is enforced by code, not assumptions.


## Automated Optimization  
### Passive yield with zero active management

Efficient yield generation usually requires constant monitoring and manual
rebalancing.

SuperCluster abstracts this complexity:

- Pilot Strategy allocates capital based on risk-adjusted returns  
- Automatic on-chain rebalancing  
- No user intervention required  

User flow:
1. Deposit USDC  
2. Receive sToken  
3. Yield accrues automatically  

No monitoring. No timing. No strategy management.


## What Can People Use SuperCluster For?

- Parking stablecoins safely while earning yield  
- Replacing idle USDC with liquid, yield-bearing assets  
- Using yield-generating tokens as collateral in DeFi  
- Building structured products on top of stable yield  
- DAO treasury management with transparent risk exposure  
- Passive income without trading or leverage  


## Why SuperCluster Is Different

- Lower risk than opaque yield vaults  
- More liquid than locked vault shares  
- More transparent than centralized aggregators  
- More composable than single-protocol lending positions  

SuperCluster turns stablecoin yield into a liquid, trust-minimized DeFi primitive.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

During development, most challenges were not theoretical, but very practical:
how to safely implement yield mechanics, token behavior, and automation while
keeping the system simple and auditable.


## Implementing Rebasing Without Breaking UX or Composability

### Challenge  
Initial designs used a rebasing token to reflect yield directly in user balances.
In practice, rebasing caused issues:
- Inconsistent UX across wallets and dashboards  
- Poor compatibility with DeFi protocols  
- Complexity when used as collateral or LP tokens  

### How I Overcame It  
- Separated concerns between **yield accounting** and **token behavior**  
- Introduced a **non-rebasing wrapped token (wsToken)**  
- Rebasing is handled at the share level, not the user-facing token  
- Users can choose between rebasing (sToken) or non-rebasing (wsToken) depending on use case  

This preserved accurate yield distribution while improving composability.


## Accurate Yield Accounting With Transferable Tokens

### Challenge  
When yield-bearing tokens are transferable, yield attribution must remain fair
regardless of transfer timing.

### How I Overcame It  
- Implemented a **share-based model** similar to proven lending protocols  
- Yield accrues globally to the pool, not per address  
- Token transfers move ownership of shares, not fixed yield claims  
- No per-user yield state required  

This eliminated edge cases around partial accrual and double counting.


## Safe Deposit & Withdraw Flow With External Protocols

### Challenge  
Deposits and withdrawals interact with multiple external protocols, increasing
risk of reentrancy and inconsistent state if any call fails.

### How I Overcame It  
- Enforced **checks-effects-interactions** strictly  
- Used reentrancy guards on all external entry points  
- Designed adapters to be minimal and stateless  
- All token mint/burn operations happen only after state is finalized  

The system fails early and safely if any step reverts.


## Automated Allocation Without Overengineering

### Challenge  
Early versions attempted frequent rebalancing based on small yield differences,
which increased gas costs and complexity.

### How I Overcame It  
- Introduced **conservative rebalance thresholds**  
- Allocation only changes when yield delta is meaningfully better  
- Avoided external oracles; relied on protocol-native rate data  
- Prioritized predictable behavior over micro-optimizations  

This reduced churn and made strategy behavior easier to reason about.


## Making On-Chain Transparency Practical

### Challenge  
Exposing full allocation data on-chain can quickly become gas-heavy if every
detail is stored or updated frequently.

### How I Overcame It  
- Designed a **read-heavy, write-light** architecture  
- Stored only essential state on-chain  
- Derived views for detailed allocation breakdowns  
- Used events for off-chain indexing and analytics  

Transparency remained high without inflating gas costs.


## Takeaway

Most challenges came down to trade-offs:
- rebasing vs composability  
- automation vs predictability  
- transparency vs gas efficiency  

SuperCluster evolved by choosing simpler, safer primitives first and layering
automation only where it added real value.

> Emergency Rupiah Access for Gold Holders

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/546b9dd8ed874efe83e681e56ee32ecb/4e5d8c23-9921-4eb4-8c5c-8df9f5171726.png)Screenshot 2026-01-10 at 23.38.10

**Problem We Solve**

In Indonesia, gold is one of the most widely held financial assets. It is not primarily used for speculation, but as a form of financial protection and a long-term store of value. According to a World Gold Council survey, approximately 67% of Indonesians hold gold in various forms, reflecting its role in building financial resilience.
However, a critical problem emerges during emergency cash needs.
When gold holders require liquidity, the existing options are inefficient and often harmful:
- Selling gold leads to immediate value loss due to wide bid–ask spreads, typically around 8–12%, and permanently removes exposure to a long-term safe asset.
- Pawning or pledging gold involves manual processes, administrative friction, and time delays that are not suitable for urgent situations.
- Postponing urgent expenses—such as medical costs, education fees, or working capital—can cause further financial and personal stress.

As a result, many users lose value not because gold is a poor asset, but because current liquidity infrastructure is not designed for real-life emergencies.
The core issue is not gold itself, but the lack of a system that allows fast, partial, and reversible access to cash without forcing users to sell their gold holdings.


**Our Solution**

Auroom introduces a gold-backed emergency liquidity mechanism that transforms gold from a passive store of value into an active financial buffer.
Instead of selling gold when cash is needed, users can borrow against their gold to access immediate liquidity. The process is:
- On-chain and transparent, removing manual approvals and opaque pricing
- Fast, enabling emergency access to funds
- Non-destructive, allowing users to retain long-term exposure to gold

By enabling temporary liquidity rather than permanent liquidation, Auroom aligns with real user behavior:

*People don’t want to sell gold.
They want short-term cash without losing long-term financial security.*


**Why This Matters**

Auroom addresses a real, widespread problem at the intersection of traditional asset behavior and modern financial infrastructure. It unlocks liquidity from an asset that millions already trust, without asking users to change how they store value—only how they access it when they need it most.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Bridging the Web3-to-Web2 Gap (Integration Challenge)**
Ensuring a seamless and reliable transition from on-chain asset locking to off-chain bank disbursement.
Problem: Integrating the IDRX settlement layer was difficult because they do not provide a developer sandbox, making live end-to-end testing of the gold-to-fiat lifecycle impossible during development.
Solution: We engineered a robust simulation engine that mirrored IDRX callback behaviors based on their technical documentation. This allowed us to rigorously test state synchronization and ensure that gold collateral is only locked once the fiat disbursement is successfully triggered and validated.

**2. Abstracting Complexity for Non-Crypto Natives (UX Challenge)** 
Removing the technical barriers that prevent everyday gold holders from accessing digital liquidity.
Problem: Traditional DeFi lending involves a cumbersome 6-step process, including managing gas fees and calculating collateral ratios, which is too complex for users facing a high-stress emergency.
Solution: We implemented an Intent-Based UX that simplifies the experience into 4 instant steps. By moving all technical calculations and safety buffer logic to the background, we removed the "crypto-friction," allowing users to focus only on the cash they need.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/546b9dd8ed874efe83e681e56ee32ecb/707968ea-4a9a-42c7-bfb1-2859aaa3acd5.jpeg)core.jpg

**3. Seamless Identity Verification via DID (Compliance & Speed Challenge)** 
Replacing slow, manual verification with an instant, secure, and decentralized alternative.
Problem: Traditional KYC verification in Indonesia is often slow and bureaucratic, often taking days to process, which is ineffective for time-sensitive financial emergencies.
Solution: We integrated Decentralized Identity (DID). The technical challenge was ensuring that identity data verified on-chain is valid and accepted by liquidity providers, allowing the entire approval process to occur in seconds—as illustrated in our sequence diagram under the IDP/DID verification section.

**Winner Classification**

**Auroom solves a real problem with a real product.**

- Digital gold adoption is exploding, but liquidity access is still broken.
- Auroom doesn’t ask users to sell their gold, we let them borrow cash against it.

Auroom isn’t just DeFi on-chain:
- Cash goes directly to bank accounts
- Using a trusted, low-risk collateral: gold
- The product is live, practical, and immediately useful, especially in emerging markets.

Auroom bridges gold, DeFi, and real-world money — and turns a passive asset into usable liquidity.

That’s why Auroom should win.
