### BlindBid
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/blindbid-ff70) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vishu-2004/blindbid-protocol) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://blindbid-protocol.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/cxVlZ2UkTZE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackFiesta-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackfiesta.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Blind NFT auctions, Fully on-chain.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional NFT and digital auctions suffer from several fundamental issues. Since bids are fully visible, they are prone to bid manipulation, intimidation by whales, front-running, and last-second bid sniping. Most platforms rely on centralized backend logic, forcing users to trust intermediaries for custody, auction execution, and settlement.

Additionally, transparent auctions remove excitement and fairness bidders simply react to others instead of bidding based on true valuation. NFT marketplaces also amplify wash trading and artificial rarity signals, making price discovery unreliable.

BlindBid addresses these problems by introducing blind, vault-based NFT auctions that are fully on-chain. Sellers bundle NFTs into sealed vaults, and buyers bid without knowing the exact contents or other bids. This prevents manipulation, eliminates front-running, and enables fair price discovery enforced entirely by smart contracts without centralized control.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing a blind bidding mechanism that preserves bid privacy while still allowing on-chain verification and settlement. Implementing a commit–reveal scheme required careful handling of bid hashes, secrets, and reveal validation to prevent duplicate reveals, fake bids, or manipulation.

Another challenge was building fast-paced auctions on-chain. Blockchain latency and gas costs make real-time experiences difficult, so the auction logic had to be optimized to support short bid windows while remaining secure and deterministic.

Ensuring trustless NFT custody was also critical. NFTs needed to be safely locked inside vaults with no admin privileges, no upgrade keys, and no backend intervention. This required careful smart contract design to handle custody, winner selection, refunds, and settlement automatically.

On the frontend, presenting complex auction states (commit phase, reveal phase, settlement) in a simple and intuitive UX was challenging. We solved this by clearly separating auction phases and deriving real-time state directly from on-chain data instead of relying on centralized servers.

**Ethereum Track**

BlindBid directly aligns with the ETHIndia track by building a fully on-chain, Ethereum-based auction protocol that explores new primitives for decentralized marketplaces. The protocol leverages EVM smart contracts to enforce blind bidding, NFT custody, settlement, and refunds without relying on centralized backends or trusted intermediaries.

By introducing blind, vault-based NFT auctions, BlindBid addresses key Ethereum ecosystem challenges such as front-running, bid manipulation, and unfair price discovery. The commit–reveal bidding mechanism ensures bid privacy while preserving on-chain verifiability, showcasing Ethereum’s strengths in trustless coordination and programmable economic logic.

BlindBid demonstrates how Ethereum can be used not just for asset transfers, but for building fair, transparent, and innovative market mechanisms, making it a strong fit for the ETHIndia track.

**Open Innovation**

BlindBid fits the Open Innovation track by introducing a new, open, and composable auction primitive for Web3 ecosystems. Instead of relying on centralized NFT marketplaces and opaque auction mechanisms, BlindBid provides a fully on-chain, trustless, and permissionless protocol that anyone can integrate, extend, or build on top of.

The protocol enables blind, vault-based auctions that prevent bid manipulation, front-running, and centralized control problems that remain unsolved in most existing NFT platforms. By keeping all auction logic transparent at the protocol level while preserving bid privacy, BlindBid rethinks how fair price discovery can be achieved in decentralized systems.

BlindBid is designed as an open building block for developers, DAOs, and creators, with applications ranging from NFT vault auctions and DAO treasury liquidations to experimental auction models and digital asset bundles. This openness, composability, and protocol-first approach directly align with the spirit of Open Innovation.

**The problem it solves**

# VoucherDAO

## Overview

VoucherDAO is a Web3 protocol that turns unused vouchers and gift cards into liquid, on-chain assets users can actually use instead of letting them expire. It tokenizes each voucher type as an ERC-1155 asset and routes trading through an AMM-style liquidity pool, so anyone can swap a voucher for ETH, buy discounted vouchers, or provide liquidity and earn fees.

On top of that, it offers a simple interface to view all vouchers, see real-time on-chain value, choose between selling, pooling, or redeeming, and finally redeem on-chain vouchers into off-chain claim codes or QR codes that can be used at real stores, bridging traditional voucher value into DeFi and back.

## Problem Statement

A large amount of value locked in vouchers and gift cards expires unused because people forget about them, move cities, or don't like the specific brand. Existing ways to sell vouchers are fragmented and risky: informal P2P trades on chats/OLX, or opaque centralized resale platforms with high spreads.

Users have no unified place to see all their vouchers, current value, and best action (sell, hold, or redeem). There is no simple way to plug vouchers into DeFi primitives like swaps, liquidity pools, and yield.

## Use Cases

### Instantly Sell Unwanted Vouchers

Convert unused vouchers directly into ETH through an automated market maker (AMM) instead of hunting for a buyer. Get a transparent, on-chain price based on pool reserves rather than arbitrary discounts. Turn "I'll probably never use this card" into liquid crypto that can be reused anywhere.

### Buy Discounted Vouchers

Users who actually want to shop at a brand can buy vouchers at a discount using ETH. AMM pricing means more sell pressure leads to cheaper vouchers, rewarding buyers who are willing to use them. This creates a continuous, permissionless discount marketplace for popular brands.

### Provide Liquidity and Earn Fees

Users can deposit vouchers + ETH into liquidity pools and receive LP tokens in return. Every swap pays a small fee to LPs, giving them yield on top of otherwise idle gift cards. This lets both crypto-native users and regular voucher holders participate in DeFi-style fee farming using real-world value.

### Safely Trade Without Trusting Strangers

All swaps and deposits go through transparent smart contracts, removing "who sends first?" risk from informal P2P deals. Either the transaction succeeds atomically (both sides receive assets) or it reverts; there is no partial failure or ghosting. Users can verify pool balances, prices, and their own positions directly on-chain.

### Unify and Manage Voucher Portfolio

Users see all supported vouchers in one dashboard: brand, face value, expiry, and on-chain market value. The app makes it easy to decide per voucher: "sell now", "hold and LP", or "redeem at store". This reduces cognitive load and prevents vouchers from being forgotten in inboxes and SMS threads.

### Bridge On-Chain Value Back to Real World

When a user wants to actually use a voucher, they trigger an on-chain `redeemVoucher` flow that burns or locks the voucher token. The system then issues an off-chain claim code or QR that can be presented at a store or in an app checkout. This completes the loop: real-world voucher → on-chain trading/yield → real-world redemption again, showing a clear integration path for brands.

### Enable Future Integrations and Automation

Brands and platforms can later integrate via APIs to automatically issue on-chain vouchers instead of legacy gift codes. Corporate or bulk vouchers can be instantly made liquid, solving "corporate gifting that nobody uses" problems. Over time, users could set rules like "auto-sell any voucher 7 days before expiry" or "auto-LP my high-value vouchers," automating value preservation.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## Getting the swap math and pricing right

The main challenge was implementing the AMM swap logic correctly so that voucher ↔ ETH prices updated smoothly without breaking invariants. The first version of the formula was too naive and either underpriced vouchers or caused huge slippage on small trades. To fix this, the constant-product AMM math was re-derived carefully on paper, then verified with a small local simulation and unit tests in Hardhat. Reading DeFi contract examples and discussions, and checking multiple explanations of Uniswap-style x·y = k, helped settle on a correct pattern, and a friend cross-checked the edge cases for zero liquidity and tiny trades.

## Designing a clean escrow flow for redemptions

Designing the escrow/redeem flow was also tricky: the question was when to burn/lock the voucher on-chain versus when to issue an off-chain claim code without opening up race conditions or double spends. The first design tried to mix too much logic into the smart contract, which made it complex and hard to reason about. The solution was to simplify the contract to just emit a clear "Redeemed" event and handle claim code generation in the backend, using event listening and a simple status field in the database. To get there, documentation and forum posts on event-driven Web3 backends were reviewed, a couple of Stack Overflow answers on escrow patterns were studied, and the final design was sanity-checked with peers.

## Coordinating frontend, contracts, and backend data

Another subtle challenge was keeping the frontend in sync with both on-chain state (balances, reserves, prices) and off-chain data (voucher metadata and claim codes). Initially, the UI was mixing concerns and trying to pull everything from one place, which led to inconsistent views and stale data. The fix was to clearly split responsibilities: contracts are the source of truth for balances and prices, while the backend only serves metadata and redemption info. The integration was then refactored so the React app calls contracts directly for financial data and uses simple REST endpoints only for metadata and claim codes, guided by examples from documentation and by asking more experienced friends how they structure hybrid Web2/Web3 frontends.

**Ethereum Track**

# Ethereum Track Eligibility

## Overview

This project is built natively for the Ethereum ecosystem and fits the ETHIndia track.

## Smart Contract Architecture

All core smart contracts ("VoucherToken", "LiquidityPool", and "Escrow") are written in Solidity and deployed on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet for testing and demo purposes.

## Contract Verification

The deployed contract addresses (for Sepolia) are documented in the project's Git repository (e.g., in a "README" or "deployments"/"contracts.json" file), so anyone can independently verify and interact with them using a browser wallet or block explorer.

## Frontend Integration

The frontend dApp connects to Ethereum via a standard RPC endpoint (configured for Sepolia), and all key user actions—swapping vouchers for ETH, providing/removing liquidity, and redeeming vouchers—are executed as real Ethereum transactions signed by the user's wallet.

## Security Model

The protocol relies on Ethereum's security model for escrow, atomic swaps, and invariant-preserving AMM logic, so safety and correctness are enforced at the smart contract layer rather than by a centralized server.

## Development Pipeline

For local development and rapid iteration, a local Ethereum-compatible node (like Ganache/Hardhat network) is used, and the same contracts and scripts are then deployed to Sepolia without code changes, demonstrating a fully Ethereum-native development and deployment pipeline.

**Best Innovation**

# Best Innovation Track Eligibility

## Why This Project Fits Best Innovation

This project fits the Best Innovation track because it tackles a very common, very under-served problem: most people simply never use a large chunk of the vouchers and gift cards they receive.

## Real-Life Examples

### Google Pay scratch cards and offers

Users frequently get cashback vouchers, partner coupons, or limited-time offers in apps like Google Pay, but many of them expire unused because they are small amounts, restricted to specific merchants, or valid only in narrow time windows. A system that lets you instantly convert those into liquid value—or pool them with others for yield—captures value that would otherwise just disappear.

### Clothing store and mall gift cards

People receive gift cards from brands like clothing stores or malls (e.g., a ₹2000 card for a store that isn't in their city, or doesn't match their style). Often:

* The card sits in email/SMS until after the expiry date.
* The remaining balance after one purchase (₹150–₹300) is too small to motivate a second trip.

Turning those vouchers into on-chain assets that can be sold, swapped for ETH, or pooled means recipients are no longer forced to either use a store they don't like or lose the value entirely.

### E-commerce platform vouchers

E-commerce apps often give out promo codes or gift cards tied to specific categories, minimum order values, or banks. If the user can't meet the conditions (wrong category, no need to order that month, wrong payment method), the voucher just expires. With this protocol, those vouchers become tradable: someone who can meet those conditions can buy them at a discount, and the original holder recovers value instead of wasting it.

## The Innovation

By treating vouchers as tokenized, liquid assets and plugging them into AMM-style pools and safe redemption flows, the project creates a new, composable layer between traditional vouchers and DeFi, which is a genuinely innovative angle rather than just "another token" or "another DEX".

**The problem it solves**

## 🧩 The Problem Paycheck Solves

Independent work breaks down not because people are dishonest, but because **disagreement is inevitable**.

Today, freelancers, students, and independent consultants face recurring problems:

- **Ambiguous scopes and milestones**  
  Work is often described in natural language, which different people interpret differently.

- **Weak or subjective proof of work**  
  One side believes the work is complete, the other disagrees — with no objective way to resolve it.

- **Power imbalance**  
  Clients usually control payments. Freelancers have little leverage once work is delivered.

- **Centralized arbitration failures**  
  Platforms act as judges, making opaque decisions that users cannot verify or appeal.

- **“Trustless” escrow limitations**  
  Most escrow systems only lock funds. They fail the moment humans disagree.

In short:  
**Money can be locked trustlessly, but disputes cannot be resolved fairly.**

---

## 🚀 What People Can Use Paycheck For

Paycheck is a **dispute-resistant payment protocol** that makes independent work safer, fairer, and more predictable.

People can use Paycheck to:

### 🧑‍💻 Pay Freelancers with Confidence
- Lock payments in Ethereum smart contracts
- Prevent ghosting or non-payment
- Ensure funds are released automatically if no dispute is raised

### 🎓 Pay Students or Contributors for Projects
- Define milestones clearly
- Reduce misunderstandings in academic or collaborative work
- Ensure fair outcomes without relying on authority figures

### 🤝 Work With Strangers Safely
- No need to trust the counterparty
- No need to trust a platform
- Only the protocol enforces outcomes

### ⚖️ Resolve Disputes Without Judges
- No juries, votes, or reputation systems
- Disputes are resolved by **capital-backed conviction**
- Truth becomes the most profitable outcome

### 🌍 Participate in Dispute Resolution Markets
- Anyone can support an outcome by staking ETH
- Earn rewards by backing truthful outcomes
- No identity, permission, or governance tokens required

---

## 🔐 How Paycheck Makes Existing Workflows Safer

### Before Paycheck
- Trust the client  
- Trust the freelancer  
- Trust the platform  
- Hope disputes don’t happen  

### With Paycheck
- **Ethereum locks the money**
- **AI warns about risky agreements early**
- **Disputes require real economic commitment**
- **Outcomes are enforced automatically**

Paycheck does not assume people behave perfectly.  
It designs systems that remain fair **when they don’t**.

---

## 🧠 In One Line

> **Paycheck turns escrow from a passive money locker into an active, dispute-resistant system where economics protects fairness.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧗 Challenges We Ran Into (and How We Solved Them)

Building Paycheck wasn’t just about writing smart contracts — it was about designing a system that stays fair when humans disagree. Along the way, we ran into several **technical and design challenges** that forced us to rethink assumptions and iterate quickly.

---

### 1️⃣ Designing a Dispute System Without Human Judges

**Challenge:**  
Most dispute systems rely on juries, voting, or reputation. We wanted *none* of that — no identities, no opinions, no governance tokens.

The hard part was:
- How do you resolve a dispute with **no humans deciding outcomes**?
- How do you prevent bribery without relying on trust?

**How we solved it:**  
We reframed disputes as an **economic coordination problem**, not a moderation problem.

By turning disputes into a **binary, capital-backed market**, we let:
- ETH act as the signal of conviction
- Profit motivate truth-seeking
- Loss penalize false claims

Once we realized that *capital, not votes*, could act as consensus, the entire design became simpler and more robust.

---

### 2️⃣ Preventing Frivolous Disputes Without Blocking Honest Ones

**Challenge:**  
If raising a dispute is cheap, users will abuse it.  
If it’s too expensive, honest users may be discouraged.

Finding the right balance was tricky.

**How we solved it:**  
We introduced a **30% bond requirement** for opening a dispute.

- It’s high enough to deter bad-faith disputes
- It’s proportional to the milestone value
- It keeps incentives aligned for both sides

This single rule eliminated most attack vectors while keeping the system accessible.

---

### 3️⃣ Separating AI Intelligence from On-Chain Authority

**Challenge:**  
Using AI in financial systems is risky.  
Letting AI influence outcomes directly would break trust guarantees.

The challenge was:
- How to use AI meaningfully **without** letting it decide anything

**How we solved it:**  
We enforced a strict separation of concerns:

- AI agents **observe and advise**
- Smart contracts **enforce and settle**
- AI outputs are never inputs to contract logic

By making AI purely advisory, we gained the benefits of intelligence without compromising security or determinism.

---

### 4️⃣ Handling Edge Cases in Smart Contract State Transitions

**Challenge:**  
Escrow contracts have many states: funded, submitted, disputed, resolved.  
One invalid transition could lock funds forever.

**How we solved it:**  
We implemented a **strict finite state machine (FSM)** in the contracts:

- Every function checks the current state
- Invalid transitions revert immediately
- Settlement is allowed only from a single terminal state

This made the contract predictable, auditable, and safe.

---

### 5️⃣ Making the System Work Without a Backend

**Challenge:**  
Removing a traditional backend meant:
- No centralized database
- No orchestration server
- No off-chain authority

But most Web3 apps rely heavily on backends.

**How we solved it:**  
We redesigned the system to be:
- **Event-driven**
- **Contract-centric**
- **Frontend as a signer, not a controller**

AI agents listen to on-chain events directly, and the UI simply reflects contract state.  
This made the system more decentralized and reduced the attack surface.

---

## 🧠 Key Takeaway

The biggest challenge wasn’t a single bug — it was **unlearning traditional system design**.

Once we stopped assuming:
- Trusted servers
- Human judges
- AI decision-makers

…the system became simpler, safer, and more aligned with Ethereum’s core principles.

---

> **Paycheck taught us that strong incentives often replace complex rules — if designed correctly.**

**Ethereum Track**

#### Paycheck is fundamentally an Ethereum-native protocol that demonstrates how smart contracts can be used not just for custody, but for fair economic coordination under dispute.

*1. Ethereum as the Source of Truth*

Paycheck places all authority on Ethereum smart contracts:

Escrowed ETH is locked and released only by deterministic on-chain rules

Disputes are resolved entirely on-chain, without admins, juries, or off-chain verdicts

Settlement is final, transparent, and verifiable on Ethereum

This directly aligns with Ethereum’s core value: credible neutrality through programmable trust.


*2. Smart Contracts Beyond “Simple Escrow”*

Most Ethereum escrow projects stop at:

“Funds are locked safely.”

Paycheck goes further by using Ethereum to:

Enforce bonded dispute entry (30% bond requirement)

Freeze funds during disputes

Run a binary, capital-weighted resolution mechanism

Automatically distribute funds based on economic consensus

This showcases Ethereum as a platform for mechanism design, not just payments.


*3. Native Use of ETH as Economic Signal*

Paycheck uses ETH itself as the signal of truth:

No governance tokens

No reputation systems

No off-chain voting

No synthetic assets

Participants must stake real ETH to back an outcome.
This leverages Ethereum’s strongest primitive: value-secured consensus.


*4. Permissionless, Composable, and Trust-Minimized*

Anyone can interact with the contracts

Anyone can participate in dispute resolution

Anyone can build a frontend on top of the protocol

The system continues to function even if the UI or AI agents go offline

This makes Paycheck a protocol, not a platform — fully aligned with Ethereum’s composability ethos.


*5. AI as an Ethereum Complement (Not a Replacement)*

Paycheck intentionally keeps AI off-chain and non-authoritative:

AI agents only analyze data and publish warnings

Ethereum contracts always have final control over funds and outcomes

This preserves Ethereum’s guarantees while improving UX and dispute prevention

This demonstrates a clean separation of concerns, strengthening Ethereum rather than weakening it.


*6. Real-World Ethereum Use Case*

Paycheck targets a real, unsolved problem:

Freelance payment disputes

Power imbalance between clients and workers

Centralized arbitration failures

By solving this with Ethereum primitives, Paycheck shows how Ethereum can support real economic relationships, not just DeFi speculation.

**Build for Axicov**

#### Paycheck integrates Axicov as its AI agent layer, where we deployed a dedicated agent called PayFriend to reduce disputes before they happen.

Rather than using AI to make decisions or control funds, Paycheck uses Axicov in a non-authoritative, advisory role, which aligns strongly with Axicov’s agent-first philosophy.

*1. PayFriend: A Purpose-Built AI Agent on Axicov*

We deployed Pay-friend AI on Axicov as a Dispute Risk Prediction Agent.

Pay-friend AI operates by:

Reading escrow scope and milestone descriptions

Analyzing ambiguity, imbalance, and unrealistic timelines

Flagging potential dispute vectors before funds are locked

This makes PayFriend an AI co-pilot for both client and freelancer.


*2. AI That Prevents Problems Instead of Judging Them*

Unlike arbitration bots or AI judges, PayFriend:

Does not approve or reject work

Does not decide disputes

Does not move funds

Instead, it provides:

A risk score

Human-readable explanations

Early warnings that require explicit user acknowledgment

This improves decision quality while preserving human and on-chain autonomy.


*3. Clean Separation Between AI and Authority*

Axicov agents in Paycheck:

Observe on-chain events

Perform off-chain intelligence

Publish advisory outputs

All enforcement remains on Ethereum smart contracts.

This separation ensures:

No AI hallucination risk affecting funds

No hidden decision logic

Full auditability

Axicov strengthens the system without becoming a trust dependency.


*4. Agent-Native Integration with On-Chain Workflows*

PayFriend is triggered by:

Escrow creation events

Scope and milestone metadata

It fits naturally into Axicov’s event-driven agent model, reacting to protocol activity rather than controlling it.

This demonstrates how Axicov agents can be used as real-time intelligence layers for Web3 protocols.


*5. Real-World Utility for AI Agents*

PayFriend addresses a real, recurring problem:

Most disputes are caused by unclear expectations, not malice

By catching these risks early, PayFriend:

Reduces dispute frequency

Improves user trust

Increases protocol efficiency

This is a practical, non-speculative use of AI agents.

##  The Problem It Solves

Disaster response systems today are **slow, opaque, and unreliable**.

Damage assessment depends heavily on **manual reports**, relief funding is delayed by **bureaucracy**, and there is **little transparency** in how emergency funds are distributed. In critical situations, this lack of speed and accountability can cost **lives, resources, and trust**.

---

##  How AEGIS Makes It Better

**AEGIS automates disaster response end-to-end** using AI agents and blockchain technology.

* **AI-powered detection** rapidly analyzes satellite or drone imagery to identify disasters within seconds
* **Autonomous verification** reduces false reports and misinformation before any action is taken
* **On-chain fund disbursement** ensures relief funds are released transparently and only after verification
* **Real-time dashboards** present complex AI and blockchain activity in a clear, human-readable format

---

##  Why It’s Safer and More Reliable

* Prevents fund leakage through verifiable blockchain transactions
* Creates an immutable public audit trail for every relief action
* Combines AI speed with verification for responsible automation

---

##  Who Can Use AEGIS

* **Governments** for faster and accountable emergency response
* **NGOs** for transparent and efficient aid distribution
* **Donors** for verifiable proof of impact
* **Disaster response teams** for real-time situational awareness

---

##  In One Line

> **AEGIS transforms disaster response into a fast, verifiable, and trust-minimized system powered by AI agents and secured by blockchain.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/15de75362d8e445ca851936ed9803a15/c9ce6b5b-cdb6-43c1-a710-8305d1bfe8df.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

##  Challenges I Ran Into

Building AEGIS involved integrating **AI, multi-agent systems, blockchain, and frontend visualization**—each of which introduced unique challenges. Some of the most impactful hurdles are outlined below.

---

###  Blockchain Transaction Failures

**The Issue:**
Even after successful disaster detection and verification, Ethereum transactions were failing with errors such as underpriced replacement transactions or silent funding failures.

**Root Cause:**
The funding logic depended on values that were not always set correctly by upstream agents, causing invalid or zero-value transactions.

**How I Solved It:**
I traced the entire pipeline end-to-end, identified the missing fallback logic, and implemented defensive checks to guarantee safe transaction execution. I also resolved Web3.py version mismatches that affected raw transaction handling.

---

###  AI Confidence vs Real-World Accuracy

**The Issue:**
Initial computer vision detections produced inconsistent confidence scores, making it difficult to determine when an event should trigger funding.

**Root Cause:**
Different disaster types required different detection strategies and thresholds, which were not initially calibrated.

**How I Solved It:**
I separated detection pipelines by disaster category (fire, flood, structural damage, casualties) and tuned confidence thresholds individually to balance sensitivity and false positives.

---

###  Agent Coordination & State Flow

**The Issue:**
Synchronizing multiple agents caused race conditions where one agent acted before another completed its task.

**Root Cause:**
A lack of clear execution boundaries between detection, verification, and execution stages.

**How I Solved It:**
I introduced a message-queue-based workflow and enforced strict state transitions, ensuring that each agent only acted once the previous stage was fully completed.

---

###  Image Processing Pipeline Errors

**The Issue:**
Image format mismatches (bytes, PIL, OpenCV arrays) caused crashes and inconsistent results during analysis.

**Root Cause:**
Different libraries required different formats, and error handling was missing during conversions.

**How I Solved It:**
I standardized the image processing pipeline, added validation checks at each stage, and implemented graceful fallbacks to prevent system-wide failures.

---

###  Rapid Frontend Prototyping vs System Complexity

**The Issue:**
Displaying real-time AI decisions and blockchain transactions without overwhelming users.

**Root Cause:**
Complex backend processes needed to be simplified for human understanding.

**How I Solved It:**
I focused on clarity-first UI design—showing only essential states, using real-time status indicators, and progressively revealing technical details when needed.

---

**Ethereum Track**

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

HireScope connects skilled candidates with the unclear "Black Box" of modern Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS). Job seekers often find it hard to understand why their resumes don’t pass initial screenings, even when they have the right skills.

How it makes tasks easier:

Semantic Matching: Unlike simple keyword scanners, HireScope uses AI to recognize that a candidate with "AWS Lambda" experience is a great fit for a "Serverless" role, even if the exact term isn’t used.

Actionable Feedback: Instead of getting a vague "No," users receive a Match Percentage and a Radar Chart that shows exactly where their skills (cloud, DevOps, coding, etc.) don’t meet the Job Description (JD).

Secure & Private: By using JWT (JSON Web Tokens), the platform keeps sensitive personal data in resumes secure and protected throughout the analysis.

AI Copilot: The built-in chatbot helps users by creating "Sample Resumes" that combine their current professional history with important JD keywords.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The Parsing Issue Faced by PDF Libraries  
Parsing resumes with multi-column layouts has always been a challenge for standard PDF libraries. A lot of text gets jumbled within the application, causing confusion for artificial intelligence (AI).  
To fix this problem, we developed a more reliable pre-processing layer using pdf-parse and a Rule-Based Semantic Engine. This layer helped normalize text and map synonyms before sending the text to the LLM (Large Language Model).

2. The Problem of Maintaining State Between Five Pages  
We encountered difficulties sharing data—such as Analysis Results, Match Score, Radar Data, and AI tips—from the Dashboard page to the Resume Preview Page when the page was refreshed. As a result, the data would be lost.  
To tackle this issue, we used a combination of Context API for State Management and Local Storage. This approach kept the current JWT-authenticated session active and maintained access to complex JSON objects across all five routes of the application.

3. The Delay in the AI's Response to a User's Input  
The user interface might feel unresponsive while users wait for the OpenAI API to process the data between two large text blocks.  
To address this issue, we plan to implement the Aceternity UI Version of the “typewriter effect” and skeleton loaders to mimic the AI’s “thinking” process. This change will improve the user experience, turning a five-second wait into a more positive moment.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The majority of the $700+ billion that advertisers spend on web2 is controlled by GDN and Facebook Ad Network. In addition, nobody in web3 is focusing on DAPPS using web3 data rather than web2 data. Therefore, there is a need for a Decentralized Ad Network to ensure that these major businesses don't also establish their duopoly in web3. We serve as the link between advertisements and DAPPS. We offer data to the advertiser with creative intelligence so they may run more effective campaigns for less money. We provide as the entry point for DAPPs to be monetized with advertisements and analysis technologies to ensure that nobody gets inundated with unrelated adverts.

**Challenges we ran into**

We ran into several real challenges while building the system. Getting the smart contract design right took time, especially around structuring the submitTransaction event so it could be cleanly indexed by The Graph. Subgraph setup was another hurdle — configuring the manifest, mapping handlers, and deploying to Subgraph Studio demanded multiple iterations because even a small mismatch in event names or types caused failures. On the frontend, wallet connectivity was tricky due to network mismatches, local server issues, and MetaMask not injecting window.ethereum under certain conditions. Managing CORS and integrating the backend analytics service with on-chain data also required debugging. Finally, stitching everything together — contract, subgraph, backend, and UI — highlighted how sensitive Web3 pipelines are to small inconsistencies. These challenges shaped a stronger, more modular system by the end.

**Ethereum Track**

Our project fits the Ethereum track because it rebuilds digital advertising as a trustless, transparent system powered entirely by smart contracts. Every ad campaign is registered on Ethereum Sepolia through our Transaction contract, making spend limits, targeting personas, and publisher identities publicly verifiable instead of hidden in centralized platforms. Events are indexed through a dedicated subgraph, enabling tamper-proof analytics and transparent campaign tracking. Wallet-based authentication, on-chain submissions, and cryptographic accountability ensure advertisers and publishers interact without needing to trust each other. The system cannot function without Ethereum—its transparency, verifiability, and event-driven architecture form the core of how ads are created, settled, and audited.

### What can people use it for?
**1. The "Ghost Wallet" (Private Gas Injection)**
The Problem: To use Starknet, you need ETH for gas. If you send ETH from your main Ethereum wallet or a centralized exchange (Coinbase/Binance) to a new Starknet wallet, your identity is permanently linked on-chain. Everyone knows that "Fresh Wallet A" belongs to "Public Person B." The ZKStarvion Solution:

A user sends Shielded ZEC to the bridge.

The bridge mints BZEC (or swaps for ETH in the future) on a brand new, empty Starknet wallet.

Result: The user now has a funded Starknet wallet with zero on-chain link to their past history.

**2. Anonymous DeFi Participation**
The Problem: Zcash offers great privacy but has no DeFi ecosystem (no Uniswap, no Lending). Starknet has amazing DeFi, but no privacy. The ZKStarvion Solution:

Users can bridge their dormant Zcash holdings into the Starknet ecosystem as BZEC (Bridged ZEC).

They can immediately deploy this capital into Starknet DeFi protocols (like JediSwap, Ekubo, or Nostra) to earn yield, swap for stablecoins, or lend.

Result: Zcash becomes a productive asset, and Starknet gains private liquidity.

**3. Cross-Chain Account Abstraction**
The Problem: Users hate managing multiple wallets and private keys for different chains. The ZKStarvion Solution:

The bridge acts as a primitive for Cross-Chain Account Abstraction.

A user can theoretically "control" a Starknet Smart Account simply by signing messages with their Zcash wallet.

Result: One wallet to rule them all.

## How it makes tasks Safer & Easier

**Eliminating Centralized Exchanges (CEX)**
Before: To move value from Zcash to Starknet privately, a user currently has to:

- Deposit ZEC to a CEX (Risk of freezing/KYC).
- Sell ZEC for ETH.
- Withdraw ETH to Starknet (Links identity).

With ZKStarvion: It is a direct, code-based transfer. No signup, no permission, no middleman holding your funds longer than the block time.

**Cryptographic Security vs. Trust**
 - **Existing Bridges**: Often rely on complex, opaque multi-sig networks that are frequently hacked.

- **ZKStarvion**: Uses a transparent Lock-and-Mint mechanism verified on-chain. The Starknet contract explicitly verifies the cryptographic signature of the Relayer before allowing any minting, ensuring that only valid Zcash transactions result in Starknet assets.

**Developer Experience (Zero Friction)**
We solved the "Language Barrier" between the UTXO Model (Zcash) and the Account Model (Starknet). Developers building privacy apps on Starknet no longer need to build their own ZK-circuits for deposits; they can simply integrate BZEC as a standard ERC-20 token.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Cryptographic "Language Barrier" 
**The Hurdle:** Zcash uses the Jubjub elliptic curve for privacy, while Starknet uses the STARK curve. Implementing a Jubjub verifier directly in Cairo was computationally prohibitive for a hackathon timeline. The Solution: We built a Trusted Relayer architecture. The Node.js Relayer acts as a cryptographic translator: it verifies the Zcash transaction locally (off-chain) and attests to its validity on Starknet using a native ECDSA signature on the STARK curve.

### 2. Zcash Regtest "Time Travel" ⏳
**The Hurdle:** When containerizing the Zcash node, we encountered ```Error -8: Cannot create shielded transactions```. 
We realized the default Regtest mode starts at Block 0 with legacy consensus rules, meaning modern privacy features (Sapling/Orchard) were disabled. 
**The Solution:** We engineered a custom Docker entrypoint that injects specific -nuparams flags (e.g., -nuparams=5ba81b19:1). This forcibly activates all major Zcash network upgrades at Block 1, simulating a modern mainnet environment instantly.

### 3. Infrastructure Instability (RPCs & Faucets) 🛠️
**The Hurdle:** Relying on public Testnet infrastructure was a bottleneck. Public Zcash faucets were frequently empty or offline due to the Nu6 network upgrade, and public RPC endpoints suffered from high latency and timeouts. The Solution: We pivoted to a "Sovereign Stack" approach. By wrapping the official zcashd node in Docker, we created a local Regtest environment where we act as the miner. This granted us:

- Zero Latency: RPC calls to localhost are instant.
- Infinite Liquidity: We script the mining of 101 blocks on boot to self-fund the bridge.
- 100% Uptime: The demo works perfectly even without an internet connection.

#### 4. Cloud Container Amnesia ☁️
**The Hurdle:** Deploying the node to cloud providers (like Render/Railway) caused data loss. Every time the free-tier instance idled or restarted, the blockchain data was wiped, resetting our wallet balance to zero. The Solution: We wrote an automated Orchestrator Script (start.sh) that runs on every boot. It dynamically initializes the node, mines maturity blocks, generates fresh wallets, and injects the new addresses into the application runtime. This made our stateful bridge compatible with stateless cloud architecture.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

We developed a Dockerized Zcash Regtest orchestrator and a Node.js Relayer that acts as a translation layer for the Zcash protocol, making it easier for Layer 2 applications to interact with the Zcash Shielded Pool.

**General Bounty**

ZKStarvion unlocks a previously impossible use case for Zcash: Private DeFi participation on Layer 2.

Historically, Zcash Shielded funds were isolated on L1, limited to simple payments. Our project breaks this silo. By building a trust-minimized bridge to Starknet, we allow Zcash users to deploy their private assets into a programmable environment (DeFi, DAOs, Gaming) without compromising their anonymity.

This innovation expands the Zcash ecosystem from 'Private Money' to 'Private Programmable Money,' directly aligning with Project Tachyon's goal of scaling encrypted money.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

ZKStarvion is a cross-chain private payment processor.

We built a system that allows users to send value privately using Zcash's shielded pool and have it received on Starknet Layer 2. By utilizing encrypted Zcash memos to trigger on-chain minting, we created a confidential transaction layer that breaks the link between sender and receiver.

This enables innovative use cases like "Private Gas Injection"—allowing users to fund fresh Starknet wallets anonymously—and "Shielded Payments to L2," where a user can pay a Starknet merchant using ZEC without exposing their financial history.

# SLPM V2 - The Problem It Solves

## Executive Summary

**SLPM (Starknet Lightning Privacy Mixer)** solves the critical problem of **financial surveillance on public blockchains**. Every transaction on Ethereum, Starknet, and other networks is permanently visible—creating comprehensive financial profiles of users, exposing spending patterns, and enabling tracking of fund flows.

**SLPM V2** breaks this chain of surveillance through a revolutionary multi-layer privacy architecture, now enhanced with **cross-chain atomic swaps** for **ZEC (Zcash)** and **STRK (Starknet)**.

---

## The Problem: Blockchain Transparency = Financial Surveillance

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    THE SURVEILLANCE PROBLEM                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│    Every blockchain transaction reveals:                                     │
│                                                                              │
│    - WHO sent funds          →  Your address is your identity               │
│    - WHO received funds      →  Links you to every recipient                │
│    - HOW MUCH was sent       →  Your exact wealth & spending patterns       │
│    - WHEN it happened        →  Timing analysis reveals habits              │
│    - TRANSACTION GRAPH       →  Chain analysis links all your addresses     │
│                                                                              │
│    Result: Complete financial dossier on every user                         │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| **Donations**         | Political/social causes become public    |
| **Business Payments** | Competitors see your suppliers & pricing |
| **Personal Savings**  | Anyone can calculate your net worth      |
| **Medical Expenses**  | Health conditions become traceable       |

## The Solution: SLPM V2 Multi-Layer Privacy

│  │  • Noir circuits for ZK proof generation                             │   │
│  │  • Garaga for on-chain proof verification                            │   │
│  │  • Merkle tree anonymity set (256 commitments)                       │   │

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. ZK Toolchain Version Compatibility

### The Problem

The biggest challenge was getting the entire ZK proof pipeline working end-to-end. We needed to integrate three separate tools that had to be exactly compatible:

- **Noir** (circuit language) - For defining the privacy circuit
- **Barretenberg** (proving backend) - For generating UltraHonk proofs
- **Garaga** (Cairo verifier) - For on-chain proof verification

Each tool has its own versioning, and they must all be compatible with each other AND with Starknet's Cairo VM.

```
Incompatible versions led to:
- Proof generation failures
- Verifier contract compilation errors
- On-chain verification returning false positives/negatives
```

### How We Solved It

After extensive testing, we found the exact version combination that works:

```bash
# The working stack:
noirup --version 1.0.0-beta.5      # Noir circuit compiler
bbup --version 0.87.4-starknet.1   # Barretenberg with Starknet support
pip install garaga==0.18.1         # Garaga Cairo verifier generator
```

We also had to use specific flags for proof generation to ensure Starknet compatibility:

```bash
bb prove --scheme ultra_honk --zk --oracle_hash starknet
```

The `--oracle_hash starknet` flag was critical - it ensures the proof uses Starknet-compatible hash functions.

---


## 2. Merkle Tree Root Synchronization

### The Problem

The privacy mixer uses a Merkle tree to store commitments. When generating a withdrawal proof, the Merkle root in the proof must match the current on-chain root. But:

- New deposits change the root
- If someone deposits between proof generation and withdrawal, the proof becomes invalid

### How We Solved It

We implemented root history tracking in the contract:

```cairo
// Store historical roots (last 100)
fn is_known_root(self: @ContractState, root: felt252) -> bool {
    // Check current root
    if self.merkle_root.read() == root {
        return true;
    }
    // Check historical roots
    // ...
}
```

This allows proofs generated against slightly older roots to still verify.

---

## 3. Large Proof Calldata Size

### The Problem

A single ZK proof with Garaga hints requires ~2900 felt252 elements. This is:
- Expensive in terms of calldata costs
- Near the transaction size limits
- Slow to serialize/deserialize

```
Proof calldata breakdown:
- Proof points: ~64 elements
- Pairing hints: ~2800 elements
- Public inputs: ~23 elements
Total: ~2900 elements
```

### How We Solved It

We accepted this as a tradeoff for the security guarantees. Garaga's approach of pre-computing pairing hints client-side reduces on-chain computation significantly, making verification gas-efficient despite the large calldata.

Future optimization: Recursive proof aggregation could batch multiple withdrawals into a single proof, amortizing the calldata cost.

---

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

# Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools - Track Fit

SLPM provides comprehensive developer infrastructure through its modular SDK (`@slpm/sdk`), enabling any application to integrate privacy-preserving transactions without understanding the underlying cryptography. The SDK exposes three independent modules - `@slpm/sdk/privacy` for ZK mixer operations, `@slpm/sdk/swaps` for cross-chain atomic swaps, and `@slpm/sdk/cashu` for ecash bearer tokens - allowing developers to import only what they need to minimize bundle size. Developers can execute a full privacy pipeline in under 10 lines of code: initialize SLPM with a Starknet account, call `deposit()` to generate a ZK commitment, and later call `withdraw()` with the commitment to receive funds at a fresh address with zero on-chain linkability. The SDK handles all complexity internally - Noir circuit witness generation, UltraHonk proof creation via Barretenberg, Garaga hint computation, and Merkle proof construction. For cross-chain privacy, developers simply call `slpm.swap({ direction: 'strk-to-zec', amount: '10', destinationAddress: 'zs1...' })` and the SDK orchestrates the entire flow through Lightning Network HTLCs and FixedFloat exchange. Full TypeScript support with exported types (`Commitment`, `DepositResult`, `SwapQuote`, etc.) and custom error classes (`PrivacyError`, `SwapError`, `CashuError`) ensure robust error handling. This transforms complex multi-layer privacy from a research problem into a simple API call, dramatically lowering the barrier for building privacy-preserving applications on Starknet.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

# Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions - Track Fit

SLPM V2 directly addresses the cross-chain privacy problem by enabling trustless, private atomic swaps between Zcash (ZEC) and Starknet (STRK) using the Atomiq Protocol. When users move assets between blockchains, traditional bridges create permanent, traceable links that chain analysis tools exploit to track funds across ecosystems. SLPM V2 breaks this surveillance chain by combining Zcash's shielded transactions (z-addresses) with Starknet's ZK mixer, routed through Lightning Network HTLCs. A user can enter from Zcash with complete privacy, swap atomically to STRK without any custodian, pass through our Noir-powered privacy mixer with Garaga verification, and exit to a fresh wallet with zero on-chain linkability. The reverse flow works identically - STRK holders can exit to Zcash shielded addresses, effectively disappearing from Starknet's transparent ledger. This creates a true cross-chain privacy corridor where assets can move between ecosystems without leaving traceable footprints on either chain, solving the fundamental problem that cross-chain activity has historically been the weakest link in blockchain privacy.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Zcash Integration Challenge

Initially planned to integrate Zcash as a second bridging option, but faced several hurdles:

- **Verification Complexity**: Verifying shielded Zcash transactions required running a full node or third-party APIs
- **Time Constraints**: Limited hackathon time meant choosing quality over quantity

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mintmarksfun-0b60) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/trionlabs/mintmarks.fun) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://mintmarks.fun) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/fGWVI6_7h6U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Unlock Web3 benefits with your emails. Privately.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square) ![RainbowKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/RainbowKit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Noir](https://img.shields.io/badge/Noir-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Unstoppable, composable and verifiable Marks (POAPs) for emails. 

Proving you attended an event currently relies on POAPs that anyone can farm with multiple wallets, or screenshots that anyone can fake. Mintmarks solves this by verifying the DKIM signatures on "Thanks for joining" emails, the ones Luma sends after the event only if your ticket is scanned at entry. We use zk-proofs to verify the signature without exposing the email content, so your attendance becomes provable on-chain while your inbox stays private. To prevent sybil attacks, we integrated ZKPassport which ties each mint to a unique human identity. This way, verified attendees mint soulbound NFTs as permanent, on-chain proof they were actually there.

Beyond event attendance, any DKIM-signed email becomes a provable credential. Protocols can offer unstoppable perks based on verifiable history like Uniswap giving trading fee discounts to users who can prove they're in Binance's top 100 leaderboard, or DeFi platforms offering better loan rates to anyone with a verified .edu email. Besides that, private social also becomes possible with use cases like an EthCC Speakers forum where membership is verified via acceptance email, or a Tesla Owners Club gated by delivery receipt without any doxxing, just a proof.

With recursive proofs, these credentials can be used in a composable such as prove you're a verified student who attended three hackathons and trades on Binance, enabling unique and niche use cases.

Private. Verifiable. Composable.

**Challenges we ran into**

Browser-based proof generation was one of the challenges. The compiled circuit is around 40 MB, and running it through wasm hits memory limits fast. We had to precompile circuits, load them async, and coordinate worker threads to avoid freezing the UI, which took some time. Also, the ZKPassport binding logic was tricky. We needed one passport to bind to one wallet , but still allow that passport to mint multiple different events. This meant tracking three separate mappings: wallet-to-passport, passport-to-wallet, and passport-used-per-event. Additionally, integrating Coinbase CDP for email-only onboarding while maintaining support with external browser EOA wallets was challenging from a UX perspective and required us to think about a unified, clean interface. On top of that, handling dual authentication (email + wallet) created another layer of complexity, so we designed a new modal flow specifically for that hierarchy.

**General Bounty**

Mintmarks allows people (ie:Network School attendees) to mint soulbound NFTs proving their event participation using zk-proofs. The way it works is Luma only sends "Thanks for joining" emails to people who got their ticket scanned at entry, so by verifying the email's DKIM signature in a ZK circuit, we can cryptographically prove someone actually attended without exposing any personal data on-chain. 

However, email verification alone doesn't prevent someone from using multiple wallets to farm NFTs, which is why we integrated ZKPassport, it provides passport-backed identity verification that ensures each minted NFT represents a unique person. This gives us two verification tiers: email-only for proved attendance, and passport-verified for proved unique human. With this project, Network School can offer on-chain benefits to verified attendees while keeping user data private.

### AI Fraud & Compliance Platform with Audit Trails
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aidriven-compliance-and-fraud-detection-platform-with-blockchainproven-audit-trails-b9ff) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Nishasathish105/ai-compliance-platform) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://app-7pees0naf2f5.appmedo.com/dashboard) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20with%20Stack-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-with-stack.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Stopping Financial Fraud with AI & Blockchain

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern financial institutions struggle with rising document fraud, fake KYC submissions, altered salary slips, and high-risk transactions that slip through manual checks. Traditional verification is slow, error-prone, and relies heavily on human judgment, making it vulnerable to sophisticated forgeries and compliance failures. Audit trails can be tampered with, investigations take too long, and regulators demand faster, more transparent anti-fraud processes.

How People Can Use It / Why It Makes Work Easier and Safer

Our platform provides automated, AI-powered compliance and fraud detection that replaces hours of manual verification with a fast, accurate, and secure system. Users can:

Upload any document (ID, salary slip, bank statement, proof of address) and instantly get authenticity checks powered by OCR, metadata inspection, and visual forgery detection.

Verify customer identity safely using face-matching and liveness checks.

Detect suspicious activities early through real-time risk scoring and AML pattern analysis.

Track all actions with confidence, because every verification is stored on a tamper-proof blockchain audit trail that prevents manipulation.

Reduce compliance workload by automatically generating reports for auditors and regulators.

Accelerate onboarding, reduce fraud losses, and improve trust with a fully transparent system.

In simple terms, our platform makes financial verification faster, safer, and more reliable, helping institutions catch fraud before it happens and ensuring full compliance with zero manual effort.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project, one of the biggest challenges I faced was converting the auto-generated project structure from the AI builder into a fully functional codebase that could run locally and deploy properly. The AI-generated platform created a complex folder structure with many nested components, but it didn’t provide a direct download option. This meant I had to manually recreate every file, maintain the correct structure, and fix several missing imports, build errors, and configuration mismatches.

Another major hurdle was ensuring that the project could be deployed successfully. The initial build kept failing due to incomplete TypeScript configurations, missing Tailwind/PostCSS setups, and incorrect Vite settings. I resolved this by carefully reconstructing each config file, validating dependencies, and testing the project locally until it finally built without errors. Once the build stabilized, I deployed it using Netlify/Vercel and verified the live version.

Overall, the biggest challenge was transforming an AI-generated design into a real, production-ready React + Vite application, but through debugging, restructuring the code, fixing configs, and testing multiple deployment environments, I was able to complete it successfully.

**Ethereum Track**

Our platform uses a blockchain-inspired audit layer that creates immutable, hash-linked verification blocks for every document processed. Each verification generates a SHA-256 block, chained with the previous block, ensuring tamper-proof compliance records—similar to Ethereum’s core principles of decentralization, transparency, and immutability.

This allows document verification, fraud detection, and compliance actions to be cryptographically secured, auditable, and trustless—making the system align strongly with the Ethereum track's focus on secure, verifiable, blockchain-backed infrastructure.

> AI-Powered Trust for Micro-Loans.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/d01aa4e61fca468e804ef8edf7633a92/c1b5dcdb-7834-4add-ae3e-c08eec070d65.png)

MicroLend addresses critical challenges in the traditional lending ecosystem:

###  **For Borrowers:**
- **Financial Exclusion** - Traditional banks often reject individuals with limited credit history or unconventional financial profiles
- **High Barriers to Entry** - Lengthy application processes, excessive documentation requirements, and minimum credit score thresholds
- **Opaque Decisions** - Rejection letters with no explanation of why credit was denied or how to improve
- **Geographic Limitations** - Access to credit varies dramatically by location and local banking infrastructure
- **Predatory Lending** - Vulnerable individuals forced into high-interest payday loans or unregulated lending

###  **For Lenders:**
- **Limited Investment Options** - Traditional savings accounts offer minimal returns, while peer-to-peer lending is centralized
- **Lack of Transparency** - Unclear risk assessment in existing P2P platforms
- **No Control** - Lenders can't choose which borrowers to fund based on their own criteria
- **Hidden Fees** - Centralized platforms take significant cuts from both borrowers and lenders
- **Trust Issues** - Centralized platforms can be hacked, go bankrupt, or manipulate data

###  **How MicroLend Solves These Problems:**

####  **Democratized Access to Credit**
Anyone with a wallet can request loans regardless of geographic location, banking relationships, or traditional credit scores. Our AI model evaluates alternative data points like employment length and income stability.

####  **Explainable AI Risk Assessment**
Unlike black-box credit scoring systems, MicroLend uses SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) to show exactly which factors impact creditworthiness. Borrowers understand why they received their risk score and how to improve it.

####  **Direct Peer-to-Peer Lending**
Smart contracts eliminate intermediaries, reducing fees and enabling borrowers to get better rates while lenders earn higher returns. No central authority can freeze accounts or manipulate terms.

####  **Transparent & Immutable Records**
All loan terms, repayments, and reputation scores are stored on-chain. This creates an immutable credit history that borrowers truly own and can prove to anyone.

####  **Trustless Escrow System**
Funds are held securely in smart contracts with programmatic release conditions. No need to trust a centralized platform - the code guarantees fair execution.

####  **Empowered Decision Making**
Lenders see detailed AI explanations for each borrower's risk profile, allowing them to make informed decisions based on factors they care about, not just a single credit score.

####  **Building Financial Inclusion**
By accepting alternative data and providing clear feedback, MicroLend helps underbanked populations build legitimate credit histories and access fair financing.

MicroLend makes lending safer through blockchain transparency, easier with AI automation, and fairer by removing gatekeepers and providing explainable decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

**MetaMask Transaction Signing Issues:** Initially struggled with ethers.js v6 breaking changes. The switch from signer.sendTransaction() to contract method calls required restructuring our Web3 provider initialization.

**SHAP Integration with Flask:** The SHAP LinearExplainer required specific numpy array formatting. We solved this by preprocessing user input to match the exact feature order and data types expected by our LightGBM model.

**MongoDB Atlas Connection Timeouts:** Intermittent connection drops during JWT authentication. Fixed by implementing connection pooling and proper error handling with automatic reconnection logic.

**Smart Contract Gas Optimization:** Our initial MicroLending contract exceeded gas limits for loan creation. We optimized by removing redundant storage operations and using events instead of storing detailed loan histories on-chain.

**Cross-Origin CORS Conflicts:** React frontend couldn't communicate with Flask backend during local development. Resolved by configuring Flask-CORS with specific origins and credential handling.

**Gemini API Rate Limiting:** Hit API limits when generating explanations for multiple loans. Implemented caching for risk explanations and graceful fallback to SHAP-only mode when API is unavailable.

**Ethereum Track**

MicroLend is a comprehensive demonstration of full-stack blockchain development that aligns perfectly with the hackathon's goals:

### **Blockchain Integration**
We built production-ready smart contracts using Hardhat for a real-world DeFi use case. Our MicroLending.sol contract implements secure escrow, on-chain reputation, and automated interest calculations - showcasing advanced Solidity patterns like ReentrancyGuard and Ownable.

### **Modern Web3 Stack**
The project integrates ethers.js with React for seamless blockchain interaction, demonstrating how to build user-friendly Web3 applications. We handle MetaMask wallet connections, transaction signing, and real-time blockchain event listening.

### **AI/ML Innovation**
Beyond typical blockchain projects, we integrated machine learning risk assessment with SHAP explainability and Gemini AI for natural language explanations. This shows how AI can enhance DeFi applications with data-driven decision making.

### **Complete Full-Stack Architecture**
- **Frontend:** React + Vite + TailwindCSS for responsive UI
- **Backend:** Flask REST API with MongoDB for user management
- **Blockchain:** Ethereum smart contracts with Hardhat tooling
- **ML Layer:** Logistic Regression model with SHAP explanations
- **Authentication:** JWT-based secure user sessions

### **Real-World Problem Solving**
We're not just building for the sake of technology - MicroLend addresses genuine financial inclusion challenges by democratizing access to credit through blockchain transparency and AI-powered fair assessment.

This project demonstrates mastery of the entire modern Web3 development stack while solving meaningful problems in the DeFi space.

> Attack. Verify. Learn. Evolve.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![SPRINGBOOT](https://img.shields.io/badge/SPRINGBOOT-333333?style=flat-square) ![MAINFRAME](https://img.shields.io/badge/MAINFRAME-333333?style=flat-square)

**Software**

**CoEvolve Sandbox** fits strongly within the Open Innovation track by addressing an emerging challenge at the intersection of Generative AI, autonomous software development, and cybersecurity. As AI coding agents become increasingly capable of writing and modifying software, ensuring that their outputs remain secure is a continuously evolving problem. Our project proposes an innovative, self-improving security framework that allows coding agents to learn from verified failures without retraining their underlying models.

The system creates a continuous attacker–developer co-evolution loop: an Attacker LLM generates adversarial coding tasks, a Developer LLM attempts to solve them, and a Hybrid Judge validates vulnerabilities using both static analysis (SAST) and dynamic exploit replay (DAST). Confirmed failures are transformed into natural-language security rules and incorporated into the developer agent's system prompt. This creates a non-parametric alignment mechanism where defensive capabilities evolve while model weights remain frozen.

The project demonstrates innovation through adaptive Elo-based difficulty, hardened Docker isolation, regression guarding, Git-backed prompt evolution, and portable security rules. It already supports multiple LLM providers, three programming languages, 29 SAST rules, and 19 vulnerable applications for DAST validation.

Therefore, CoEvolve is not simply another cybersecurity scanner; it is an **adaptive innovation platform for continuously improving the security of autonomous AI coding systems**, with potential to evolve alongside new models, attack techniques, and software environments.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gammashield-f8d8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/jasonwong1025/GammaShield) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gamma-shield.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous AI Position Manager for DeFi Options

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![options](https://img.shields.io/badge/options-333333?style=flat-square) ![Thetanuts Finance SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Thetanuts%20Finance%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

DeFi options are useful for hedging, but managing them is still difficult. A user has to watch spot prices, expiry, liquidity, dealer positioning, and the changing options book, then decide whether to buy protection, hold, close, or roll a position. That is a lot to monitor manually, especially when market conditions move quickly.

> **The problem:** options protection is valuable, but interpreting the market and acting safely is too manual for most users.

GammaShield turns this into a **guarded workflow**, not an open-ended trading bot.

It reads the live Thetanuts OptionBook for BTC and ETH on Base, combines it with live spot-market data, and explains the market's dealer-gamma and liquidity conditions in a single dashboard. The user can review a real options quote and make a normal wallet-signed trade. For autonomous hedging, the user first creates a dedicated ERC-4337 policy account and signs a mandate with clear limits: asset, maximum loss, trade size, allowed actions, risk thresholds, persistence, cooldown, expiry, and pause/revoke controls.

The agent monitors the market, but it cannot spend outside those signed rules. Before any action, GammaShield rechecks the market, confirms that a fresh eligible quote exists, and applies the on-chain policy guard. This makes options protection easier to use while keeping the user in control of the money and the rules.

In practice, GammaShield helps users:

| What a user needs | How GammaShield helps |
| --- | --- |
| Understand a fast-moving options market | Translates the live Thetanuts book, spot prices, dealer gamma, liquidity, and expiry into an understandable risk view. |
| Review a potential options trade | Surfaces real Thetanuts OptionBook opportunities and fresh SDK-built quotes. |
| Automate cautiously | Lets the user set bounded hedging rules instead of handing a private key to a bot. |
| Stay in control | Supports pause and revoke controls before any later policy-account fill. |
| Learn safely | Provides a complete Base Sepolia policy-account flow before using Base mainnet. |

**Challenges we ran into**

| Challenge | What we did | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Making autonomous execution safe instead of simulated** | Replaced fixed application-level guards with owner-signed EIP-712 mandates and ERC-4337 policy accounts. | The policy account enforces signed limits, pause state, revocation, risk evidence, persistence, and cooldown—not a backend private key or hardcoded cap. |
| **Separating a live quote from an executable order** | Kept RFQ estimates advisory and enable trades only after a fresh SDK preview validates a listed order. | The agent cannot treat a price estimate, synthetic contract, or stale order as executable. |
| **Testing without misrepresenting a testnet as Thetanuts mainnet** | Built `ShadowOptionBook` on Base Sepolia for policy signing, funding, UserOperations, execution receipts, and positions. | Users can test the guarded flow without real funds, while the UI clearly distinguishes Shadow positions from Thetanuts positions. |
| **Operating under real RPC and upstream limits** | Narrowed and paged chain-log queries, added bounded retries and fallbacks, and cached short-lived snapshots. | The dashboard handles rate limits and upstream failures clearly instead of silently showing mock data. |
| **Making AI useful without letting it override the user** | Treated AI as a policy-drafting and second-opinion assistant; deterministic logic and the signed policy remain the final gate. | An unavailable or malformed AI response cannot bypass the user's limits or create a trade. |

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

Thetanuts is GammaShield's live options venue. We use the SDK server-side to read and normalize the Base OptionBook for BTC and ETH, power the risk dashboard, construct fresh quotes, and generate exact approval/fill calldata for eligible listed orders. A connected wallet signs a mainnet fill. GammaShield then uses the live book to calculate dealer-gamma and market-structure risk, show per-contract risk and trade impact, and gate policy decisions on a fresh eligible quote.

**AI × OPTIONS**

GammaShield uses AI where it helps most: converting a complex live book and risk model into a policy draft and readable second opinion. It does **not** give AI unrestricted execution. AI cannot raise signed limits, bypass risk checks, invent an executable order, or send funds. Every autonomous action still requires live market checks, a fresh SDK-safe quote, deterministic logic, and the user's on-chain policy.

GammaShield combines AI assistance with verifiable user controls. The result is a more understandable and safer way to use DeFi options—not a black-box trading bot.

**AI For Society**

GammaShield uses GonkaRouter to build a high-public-value Multi-Model Market Rumor & Narrative Fact-Checker. It cross-examines viral claims across independent models on the Gonka Network, scores their factual and structural threat (0–100% Truth Score), exposes transparent reasoning traces and verifiable Gonka Request IDs, and equips the public with actionable financial protection.
