### Thetaduel
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nuttyduoduel-c9fc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/POTATO0826/MUBA.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://taygood-project.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ezUYEzhZRFE?si=skrsCG6fN87KmW0Q) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Options trading as a 1v1 game

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chainlink](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chainlink-333333?style=flat-square) ![sepolia](https://img.shields.io/badge/sepolia-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/bun-333333?style=flat-square) ![Thethanuts sdk](https://img.shields.io/badge/Thethanuts%20sdk-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

Anyone can read a betting slip. Almost nobody can read an options chain.

Sports betting took $167B in wagers in the US last year and 51% of active accounts belong to 21–34 year olds — people already comfortable taking a position, who never sat a course to do it. Options ask for strike, delta, implied volatility and moneyness before your first trade, so that audience never arrives. The liquidity isn't the bottleneck. The interface is.

THETADUEL puts two familiar game formats on top of Thetanuts Finance's live options book on Base, so a first-time user takes a real options position without being taught the vocabulary first.

Parlay. The game deals you a few cards. Each is up or down on a coin, and how far you think it moves. Every card is a real option bought off Thetanuts' order book. Under the hood a "tier" is a delta band queried against live resting orders, not a difficulty setting we invented — so the "70% chance" a beginner reads and the "delta 0.70" a trader reads are the same number, and there is no second vocabulary to unlearn later. A card only exists if a real order backs it; when the book has nothing in that band, the card renders as a dead slot rather than a number we made up.

Draw a box. Drag a price band and an expiry on a chart. That box is a four-strike zone option: it pays maximum if the price lands inside your band at expiry, decays through the wings either side, and is worth nothing outside them. If the box matches a zone a market maker has already listed, it fills straight off the OptionBook as a RANGER. If it doesn't — which is most boxes, since the book carries only about three zones per asset-expiry — it goes to the OptionFactory's sealed-bid RFQ as a CALL_CONDOR, where the player names their own max bid and market makers answer.

Why the reward is honest. Draw a tighter box, or pick a bigger move, and the contract is cheaper to buy — so the same payout divided by a smaller premium is a bigger multiple. We never wrote a payback rate. Every multiplier on screen is derived from a real premium off the book, and because every position is a bought option, max loss is the premium and it's printed above the upside on every card.

Two players stake to enter, lock blind, and the better position takes the pool. The duel scores in minutes on mark-to-market return on premium — so it isn't a size contest — while the option itself settles at its own expiry, on chain.

How we built it
Thetanuts SDK @thetanuts-finance/thetanuts-client 0.3.0 on Base — live order book, MM pricing, greeks, previewFillOrder / fillOrder, and the OptionFactory RFQ path (buildCondorRFQ, requestForQuotation, settleQuotationEarly).
Chainlink price feeds on Base for the chart history behind the box grid, so the chart reads the same oracle the option settles against.
React + TypeScript + Bun, wagmi / viem / RainbowKit for wallets.
DuelEscrow.sol — stake, winner-takes-pool, with an unconditional refund path so a duel that never resolves returns both stakes without anyone signing.
An EIP-712 attestor that re-derives the winner from committed picks and its own market snapshot — it never signs a winner a client claims.
Market data sits behind one MarketSource interface, so every live feature degrades to a frozen fixture and the seeded game runs fully offline.

We also ran three measurements against Base mainnet before building the RFQ path

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into

The docs and the shipped SDK disagree in ten places. We built a probe harness and verified every claim against the live chain, committed at tnuts-test/FINDINGS.md. Example: the docs cap the MM fee adjustment at 3e-4; the shipped code uses 4e-4 and live data agrees. We treat our measurements as the source of truth, not the docs.

RANGER looked like the perfect instrument and isn't mintable. It has exactly the payoff our box needs and Thetanuts calls it unique to them — but client.ranger exposes only payout, close, split and transfer. There is no create method anywhere in the SDK. So the box fills a listed RANGER off the book, and mints a CALL_CONDOR through RFQ when nothing matches.

The book is not a ladder. Real strikes cluster ~$20 apart near spot and $100+ in the wings, and expiries are tomorrow, the day after, then weeklies. An evenly spaced grid would have promised instruments that don't exist, so the box snaps to strikes that actually carry orders and the grid is irregular by design.

Settlement is terminal, not path-dependent. We initially assumed a box meant "price stays in the band." It doesn't — the price has to land there at expiry. Every line of copy on that screen had to change.

There is no testnet for Thetanuts. It's Base mainnet only, so every rehearsal of a fill costs real money. We put a $2 cap in code above the network — checked per leg and against the slip sum — rather than in the UI.

Connecting deployed smart contracts to thethanuts frontend to make sure it works on mainnet and testnet

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

THETADUEL is built on the Thetanuts SDK end to end, and uses both execution venues rather than one.

OptionBook. fetchOrders and getMarketData drive every number on screen — strikes, greeks, MM pricing, depth. Our parlay cards are delta bands queried against live resting orders, so a card only exists when a real order backs it; previewFillOrder and fillOrder execute the picks, with ensureAllowance sized exactly per leg and never MaxUint256.

OptionFactory RFQ. A drawn box that matches nothing listed is minted as a CALL_CONDOR through the sealed-bid auction — buildCondorRFQ, validateRFQRequest, requestForQuotation, settleQuotationEarly — with calculateReservePrice suggesting a bid the player can override, and client.rfqKeys handling the ECDH keypair so offers decrypt.

We also use client.ranger to identify listed zones, client.utils.calculatePayout and validateCondor for payoff math, and chainConfig.optionImplementations to type every order by product.

**AI × OPTIONS**

AI webscrapes news to help in option trading during parlay game and helps translate live option details into simplified terms for users

### FortiFi

> Financial Firewall Between Information and Action

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Financial information can move markets quickly, but users often have to make decisions based on claims, headlines, or articles that may be misleading, incomplete, or difficult to verify. Even when a claim is identified as risky, users may not have a clear way to understand how that risk could affect their ETH holdings or what protection options are available.

FortiFi addresses this by combining multi-model AI verification with evidence gathering, portfolio risk assessment, and live options protection. It helps users evaluate financial claims before acting, understand potential downside exposure, and discover suitable ETH protection strategies through Thetanuts. The system also provides an auditable record of its analysis and completed protection actions through Sui, making the decision-making process more transparent and verifiable.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

One of our biggest challenges was our team's background. We are all cybersecurity students rather than software engineering students, and most of us had limited experience building a complete application involving AI, blockchain, frontend, backend, and smart-contract integrations.

This was also the first or second hackathon for everyone on the team, so we had to learn how to work with unfamiliar technologies while developing the product under a strict time constraint. Integrating multiple external technologies such as Gonka, Thetanuts, Base, and Sui required us to understand APIs, wallet interactions, blockchain transactions, and different development environments simultaneously.

Testing the blockchain components presented another practical challenge. We did not have sufficient funds in our wallets to freely test every on-chain operation, particularly automated contract interactions on Sui. As a result, we had to be careful with testing and work within the available testnet resources while ensuring that the core functionality could still be demonstrated.

Despite these limitations, the challenges forced us to simplify our architecture, divide responsibilities across the team, and focus on delivering a working end-to-end prototype rather than attempting to build every feature to production scale.

**AI × SUI**

FortiFi uses Sui to create tamper-evident records of AI-assisted financial analysis and subsequent protection actions. Financial claims are assessed by multiple AI models through Gonka Router, and users can authorize anchoring a report hash through a Move contract on Sui testnet. After an options purchase on Base, a separate protection record links the analysis report hash to the associated Base transaction. The contract prevents duplicate report hashes, while the backend sponsors the Sui transaction. This gives users a traceable connection between the assessment and the recorded action, allowing saved reports to be checked for changes without publishing their full contents on-chain.

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

FortiFi integrates the Thetanuts SDK into a guided ETH protection workflow, from live option discovery to wallet-confirmed purchase on Base mainnet. It retrieves OptionBook orders and market data, filters eligible ETH puts, and presents Basic, Balanced, and Strong protection choices based on the user's budget and preferences. Users can compare strike prices, expiry dates, estimated costs, and settlement types before selecting an option. Before execution, FortiFi refreshes the selected order and checks for material changes in price or quantity. The SDK then handles USDC allowance and order execution through the user's wallet, making options protection more accessible through a single interface.

**AI × OPTIONS**

FortiFi connects AI-assisted financial claim assessment with actionable ETH options protection. Through Gonka Router, multiple AI models evaluate submitted claims against retrieved evidence and provide assessments of credibility, potential market impact, and missing context. Connected users can review their ETH exposure and estimated losses under hypothetical price declines. Claim-impact assessments and ETH allocation inform an initial protection preference, which users can adjust alongside their budget. FortiFi then uses live Thetanuts data and rule-based selection to suggest eligible ETH puts. Users review the terms and confirm purchases through their own Base wallet, bringing evidence review, risk awareness, and options execution into one workflow.

**AI For Society**

FortiFi helps users assess potentially misleading financial information before making decisions that could affect their savings or crypto holdings. It uses Gonka Router to compare assessments from multiple AI models alongside retrieved news evidence and available article content. Results present model verdicts, confidence, reasoning summaries, and missing context, helping users understand uncertainty and identify what needs further verification. A faster mode uses two successful model responses, while an optional mode waits for all three. By combining accessible claim assessment with ETH downside scenarios and user-controlled protection choices, FortiFi aims to support financial literacy and more informed decisions when users encounter uncertain or conflicting information.

### PreFlight
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bold-name-service-or-bns-8c78) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://bafybeib34kld4dhyejv2zxzixen3taalianypy3t7azatlhlan2j5xqyi4.ipfs.inbrowser.link/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_gXAKlvX8NI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Dora%20Hack%202.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dora-hack.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A Browser extension that prefly's every URL

![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sandbox Isolation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox%20Isolation-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people only discover a site is malicious after it has already loaded, by which time trackers have fired, cookies are set, or a steganographic payload may already be executing.
Preflight flips that model. It acts as a pre-click safety layer:

Intercepts every URL (typed, clicked, or redirected) before the real browser ever resolves the host.
Executes the page in a disposable sandbox with zero network egress and no persistent storage, so even if the site is malicious, only the sandbox is affected.
Delivers a clear, plain-language report that surfaces trackers, fingerprinting scripts, security misconfigurations, known vulnerable libraries, and hidden steganographic data inside images.
Lets the user decide in one tap: Visit (one-time), Leave, Greenlist, or Redlist the domain forever.

In short, it turns the risky act of “clicking a link” into a controlled experiment. Users stay in control, phishing and drive-by threats are stopped before they reach the real browser, and the cognitive load of constantly second-guessing links is dramatically reduced.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest technical hurdles was building a true zero-egress sandbox that still produces a useful scan report under Manifest V3 constraints.
Manifest V3 severely restricts remote code execution and network access inside extensions. Getting a headless/isolated environment that could:

Load an arbitrary URL,
Intercept every network request and API call at the boundary,
Analyse images for LSB / trailing-byte / EXIF steganography,
…and then safely tear itself down with zero residual state

required careful use of sandboxed pages, service-worker coordination, and strict isolation boundaries. Early versions either leaked network requests or couldn’t extract enough signal from the page.
I solved it by treating the sandbox as a completely disposable “crash-test dummy”: the real browser never touches the target origin until the user explicitly chooses to Visit. All analysis happens inside the isolated context, results are postMessaged back, and the sandbox is destroyed. This kept the security model clean while still delivering the depth of scanning (including the steganography decoder) that makes Preflight useful.

### Argus
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/argus-2efe) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Samarth208P/Argus) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://tryargus.netlify.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20To%20Devcon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-iitr.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The lie detector for Ethereum RPCs — one endpoint

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Honest nodes kept "lying" (client diversity)
Geth, Erigon and Reth return different extra fields for `eth_getBlockByNumber`, so comparing full objects flagged honest nodes as deviant.
**Fix:** compare only the consensus-critical tuple `(hash, parentHash, stateRoot, transactionsRoot)` — false positives gone.

## 2. The "latest" tag made truth subjective
Honest nodes legitimately disagree about `latest` due to propagation delay, which would have caused false accusations.
**Fix:** pin every canonical query to an explicit **finalized block hex**. This made "lying" objectively definable — and made every piece of evidence reproducible forever via curl.

## 3. The router recommended the worst node
Our first "Best RPC" widget read `scores[0]`, but the query was sorted by timestamp — so it recommended whichever provider *finished polling last*, even a score-20 node.
**Fix:** dedupe to the latest row per provider, sort by score, and add safety thresholds (min score 50, score freshness, flagged fail-open instead of silent recommendation).

## 4. "Why should we trust YOUR server?"
Our first architectures kept failing this question. We iterated from client-side → federated observers, and finally landed on **"server is a reporter, not a judge"**: publish raw evidence, commit Merkle roots on-chain, and let a `/verify` page recompute the math in the skeptic's browser. That turned our biggest weakness into the product's core feature.

**The problem it solves**

Every wallet and dApp silently trusts a single RPC provider. If that provider serves stale balances, mutated state, or quietly censors your transaction (published research shows ~46% of mainnet blocks have been produced by censoring builders), you would never know — no receipt, no proof, no recourse.

**Argus is a lie detector and failover router for Ethereum RPCs.**

## What people use it for

- **Devs & wallets:** paste one endpoint (`/api/rpc`) into any dApp or wallet. Argus pools the major free public RPCs plus any paid ones you add, routes every request to the highest-integrity live provider, and auto-fails-over the instant one degrades.
- **Auditors & skeptics:** click any flag to see raw evidence — expected-vs-got diffs, a reproducible `curl` frozen at a finalized block, explorer links, and an on-chain attestation. The `/verify` page re-runs our open-source math in *your* browser and checks it against on-chain Merkle roots: `browser math == server verdict == on-chain hash`.
- **The ecosystem:** a public, tamper-evident reputation ledger for RPC providers — accuracy, uptime, latency, censorship flags, and improving/degrading trends over time.

## How it makes things safer

- Cross-examines 8+ providers every 20s at pinned finalized blocks, reaches an independence-weighted consensus, and classifies deviations as `DEVIANT / STALE / CENSORING / DOWN`.
- A dedicated probe EOA detects write-path censorship that read-only checks can never see.
- The server is a **reporter, not a judge**: raw evidence is public, hourly Merkle roots are committed to Sepolia, and anyone can recompute every verdict. A server that cannot lie undetectably.

**Censorship Resistance**

Argus implements both directions of this track — a consensus-driven decentralized RPC aggregator and a verifiable routing layer — as one shipped product.

**Consensus mechanism among providers (aggregator):** Every 20s Argus fans out identical canonical queries to 8+ RPC providers, pinned to a *finalized* block, normalizes and hashes the responses, and selects truth via an independence-weighted majority vote (one operator = one vote, so a single company running many endpoints cannot fake a majority). If no group holds >50%, the poll is marked INCONCLUSIVE instead of guessing.

**Accurate data selection:** Outliers are retried before accusation and classified as `DEVIANT / STALE / CENSORING / DOWN`. A dedicated probe EOA runs differential write-path tests to catch silent transaction filtering — the censorship mode read-only checks can never see.

**Load balancing:** A single `/api/rpc` endpoint routes every request to the highest-integrity live provider (integrity → uptime → latency), with automatic failover and hot-swap the instant a provider is flagged.

**Verifiable routing infrastructure:** Every accusation ships with independently checkable evidence: expected-vs-got diff, a reproducible `curl` frozen at the pinned block, explorer links, and an on-chain attestation. Hourly Merkle roots of all polls are committed to Sepolia so history can never be rewritten. The `/verify` page re-runs the open-source math in the user's own browser: `browser math == server verdict == on-chain hash`.

The tool itself practices what the track preaches: no trusted center — the server is a reporter, not a judge, observers are replaceable, and Ethereum holds the log.

**The problem it solves**

Since then the bridge grew into a full agent. Its brain is OpenAI — function/tool calling decides which paid endpoint to buy (100% routing accuracy across 120 eval cases). 

The same agent also lives in iMessage via Linq: you text it, it buys Predge data over x402 and replies in the bubble. And Predge itself is published as verified, machine-discoverable citeables via Senso (signed ed25519 outcomes, live on cited.md) with GEO monitoring across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini. 

One card-only agent — on the web, in iMessage, and across the agentic web.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Two payment rails that don't share a language.** x402 speaks EIP-3009 USDC authorizations; Prava speaks cards + passkeys. 
The bridge had to read an x402 '402' challenge, translate the amount into a Prava payment session, complete the card charge, *then* settle the crypto leg — and keep the human in control on the expensive path.

**Passkey in a cross-origin iframe.** The card leg first ran with Prava's embedded SDK, but WebAuthn passkey creation is blocked inside a cross-origin iframe and kept failing ("Security Check Failed" / "Authentication couldn't be completed"). Fix: switch to Prava's **hosted 'full_checkout'** mode so the passkey runs same-origin on Prava's own page. Sandbox auth is also flaky — retrying the passkey/OTP a couple of times clears it.

**Keeping the demo honest and free.** Rather than spend real mainnet USDC on every test, I pointed the x402 leg at **Base Sepolia** so the settlement is a real on-chain transaction that costs nothing — while the same code path settles real USDC on Base mainnet against the live Predge API.

Publishing honestly: the Senso onboarding can auto-generate case studies, but Predge has no real named customers — so we deliberately withheld fabricated case studies and published only factual, source-grounded content.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

The transaction flows through Visa's rails via Prava: a single-use, network-tokenized Visa credential, authorized by the cardholder with a **Visa Payment Passkey** (biometric WebAuthn) on Prava's hosted checkout. That is the whole point of the bridge — it lets a card-only AI agent pay a crypto-native, wallet-only x402 API using a tokenized Visa card instead of a private key.

We map directly to the track's judged axes — **permissions, trust, controls**:
- **Permissions / controls:** a spend-policy gate sits in front of every 402. Small machine calls run autonomously under a standing Prava mandate; anything above the cap **escalates to a passkey**, so the human explicitly approves expensive spend. The limits are set by the human, not the agent.
- **Trust:** the card is never exposed to the agent or the merchant — it's a single-use Visa network token. Every bridged payment is audit-logged, and the paid data carries a machine-readable 'outcome_verified' trust flag.
- **Intelligent commerce:** this widens the buyer market for every x402 seller from "agents holding USDC" to "any agent with a Visa card" — the agent decides it needs data, pays with a card, and gets the data, end to end.

Evidence in the demo: the Prava hosted checkout (VISA ···· 2465), the passkey approval, "Payment Successful", the bridge reporting the charge APPROVED, and the paired on-chain USDC settlement.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Not a hackathon toy — this is shippable today:

- **Live seller:** Predge is already an x402 API in production on Base mainnet, with real paid routes ($0.005–$0.03/call), on-chain settlement, and an audit trail.

- **The unlock:** today x402 sellers can only be paid by the tiny set of agents holding USDC on the right chain. The bridge lets ANY agent with a card pay them — a crypto-native niche becomes a mass market.

- **Already shipping** across web, iMessage, and discoverable feeds.

Ready to onboard paying agents now, not "someday".

**Participation Credits (Already Claimed)**

We genuinely used our OpenAI participation credits to power the agent's brain — gpt-4o-mini via function/tool calling (planning, trust audit, and reply generation), including a 120-case eval (100% routing accuracy) and the live iMessage demo. 144+ real API calls, visible in the usage dashboard.

**OpenAI**

The agent's brain is OpenAI (src/brain.mjs, gpt-4o-mini) at three points:

- **Plan (tool calling):** two buy-tools — buy_whales_latest and buy_wallet_history({wallet}) — with tool_choice=required. The model's tool call IS the purchase decision: which paid Predge x402 endpoint, which wallet.

- **Trust audit:** a call reads the outcome_verified flag and states what to act on vs discount.

- **Answer:** a final call writes the reply over the bought data.

`npm run eval:brain` measures the planner at 100% routing accuracy across 120 labeled cases. Without a key it falls back to regex — so OpenAI is doing the real commerce decision.

A real two-way iMessage agent on Linq's Partner API:

- The agent BUYS Predge whale data over x402 (pays per query)
- Replies via /chats/{id}/messages — right in the iMessage bubble

Live demo: text the Linq number, get back a verified whale-trade answer. It's genuine agentic commerce inside a text thread — not a chatbot; the agent pays on-chain for what it sends.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

The UX is the spend-control surface:

- **Human-approved when it matters:** anything above a threshold escalates to a passkey (biometry), so the person stays in control of expensive spend.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Agentic commerce at its core: a card-only AI agent buying from a wallet-only x402 API — a transaction that couldn't happen before.

The gap:

It ships across three surfaces — web, iMessage (Linq), and discoverable feeds (Senso) — turning "agents that can pay" from a crypto-native niche into any agent with a card.

**The problem it solves**

# 🚑 The Problem DeccanAid Solves

In a medical emergency, the difference between life and death is often measured in minutes. Yet across India, emergency response systems continue to face challenges such as delayed ambulance dispatch, traffic congestion, fragmented communication, lack of hospital visibility, and inefficient resource allocation.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1cdef346d5ca4a73bd42226b5d907941/cf847e3a-6185-42a1-8f5f-e9a93edacec4.png)

India recorded over **461,000 road accidents and 168,000+ fatalities in a single year**, making road trauma one of the country's most pressing public health challenges. Experts estimate that a significant percentage of these deaths could be prevented through faster emergency response and timely medical intervention during the critical *Golden Hour* — the first hour after a severe injury or medical emergency.

The challenge is even more evident in rapidly growing urban centers like **Hyderabad**, where emergency vehicles often struggle with heavy traffic, delayed dispatch decisions, and limited real-time coordination between ambulances and hospitals. Reports have highlighted emergency response times extending well beyond recommended limits, reducing the chances of successful treatment during critical situations.

## ⚠️ Current Challenges

### Delayed Emergency Assessment

Emergency calls are often manually assessed, resulting in slower prioritization of critical cases such as cardiac arrest, stroke, trauma, and severe accidents.

### Inefficient Ambulance Allocation

The nearest ambulance is not always the most effective choice. Factors such as vehicle availability, traffic conditions, equipment readiness, and hospital destination are rarely optimized together.

### Lack of Hospital Visibility

Patients are frequently transported without real-time awareness of hospital capacity, ICU availability, specialist access, or emergency preparedness.

### Communication Barriers

India's linguistic diversity creates challenges during emergencies, especially when patients and responders speak different languages.

### Fragmented Emergency Ecosystem

Patients, ambulances, hospitals, emergency operators, and family members often operate on disconnected systems, causing delays and information loss.

## 💡 Our Solution: DeccanAid

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1cdef346d5ca4a73bd42226b5d907941/0f288107-5d69-45e8-a1e0-aaec67281dd9.jpeg)

**DeccanAid** is an AI-powered emergency response platform designed to transform how emergencies are managed from the moment a distress call is received until the patient reaches definitive care.

Using intelligent automation and real-time coordination, DeccanAid creates a connected emergency ecosystem that enables faster, smarter, and more effective emergency response.

### Key Capabilities

#### 🧠 AI-Powered Emergency Triage

Analyzes emergency reports and determines severity, priority level, and required medical resources within seconds.

#### 🚑 Smart Ambulance Dispatch

Identifies and dispatches the most suitable ambulance based on location, availability, emergency type, and route conditions.

#### 🗺️ Real-Time Route Optimization

Uses live traffic intelligence to reduce travel time and improve ambulance arrival speed.

#### 🏥 Intelligent Hospital Matching

Recommends the most appropriate hospital based on medical capabilities, capacity, distance, and patient condition.

#### 🌐 Multilingual Emergency Support

Enables emergency communication across multiple Indian languages, reducing misunderstandings during critical situations.

#### 📡 Live Emergency Coordination

Provides real-time updates to patients, responders, hospitals, and caregivers through a unified platform.

#### 📊 Operational Intelligence Dashboard

Offers emergency operators and healthcare authorities actionable insights into response performance, resource utilization, and system efficiency.

## 🎯 Impact

DeccanAid is designed to reduce response delays, improve emergency decision-making, and strengthen coordination across the healthcare ecosystem.

By combining **Artificial Intelligence**, **real-time location intelligence**, **smart dispatch systems**, and **hospital coordination**, DeccanAid helps ensure that the right ambulance reaches the right patient and transports them to the right hospital at the right time.

### Our Vision

**To make emergency healthcare faster, smarter, and more accessible, ensuring that no life is lost because help arrived too late.**

**Every Second Counts. Every Life Matters.**

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

## 🔌 IoT-to-Cloud Connectivity

One of the biggest challenges we faced was establishing reliable communication between our IoT devices and the cloud-hosted backend.

During local development, the ESP32 devices could easily communicate with our backend using local network endpoints. However, after deploying the application to the cloud, we encountered multiple issues related to:

* Network accessibility and public endpoint configuration
* CORS and API communication restrictions
* Device authentication and request handling
* Intermittent connectivity between the IoT hardware and cloud services
* Data synchronization delays between the device and server

To overcome this, we reconfigured our backend architecture, optimized API communication, implemented proper endpoint management, and extensively tested device-to-server interactions under real-world network conditions until we achieved stable communication.

---

## 📱 Cross-Platform Responsiveness

Another significant challenge was ensuring a consistent user experience across multiple platforms and screen sizes.

Our application needed to work seamlessly on:

* Mobile devices
* Web browsers
* Linux desktops
* Different screen resolutions and aspect ratios

Several UI components initially appeared correctly on one platform but broke or became difficult to use on others. We encountered issues such as:

* Layout overflows
* Inconsistent component scaling
* Navigation inconsistencies
* Responsive dashboard rendering problems
* Device-specific UI behavior

We addressed these challenges by redesigning critical layouts, implementing responsive design principles, testing across multiple devices, and continuously refining the interface to ensure a smooth experience regardless of platform.

---

## ⚡ Real-Time System Integration

Integrating multiple moving components into a single emergency response workflow was also challenging. The system combines:

* IoT accident detection
* Real-time location tracking
* AI-powered emergency analysis
* Ambulance dispatch workflows
* Hospital coordination

Ensuring that data flowed reliably and efficiently between all these components required careful API design, error handling, and extensive end-to-end testing.

---

## 🎯 Key Takeaway

The biggest lesson from this project was that building individual features is often easier than making an entire ecosystem work reliably in real-world conditions. Solving cloud deployment issues, IoT connectivity challenges, and cross-platform responsiveness helped us transform DeccanAid from a prototype into a scalable emergency response platform.

**Gemini**

DeccanAid leverages Gemini to bring intelligence into emergency response workflows. When an incident is reported or automatically detected, Gemini analyzes the available information, assesses emergency severity, identifies potential risks, and helps prioritize response actions in real time.

Gemini powers our AI-driven triage system, enabling faster decision-making for ambulance dispatch, hospital recommendations, and emergency coordination. By transforming raw incident data into actionable insights, Gemini helps responders make informed decisions during the most critical moments, reducing delays and improving patient outcomes.

Through Gemini, DeccanAid transforms emergency response from a reactive process into an intelligent, context-aware system capable of accelerating life-saving interventions when every second matters.

**MongoDB**

DeccanAid relies on MongoDB as its primary data layer for managing real-time emergency operations. The platform stores and processes emergency incidents, ambulance availability, live location updates, hospital information, patient records, and response workflows in a flexible and scalable document-based structure.

MongoDB enables us to efficiently handle dynamic emergency data, support real-time updates from multiple sources, and maintain high availability for mission-critical healthcare operations. Its flexible schema allows DeccanAid to seamlessly integrate accident alerts, AI-generated emergency assessments, ambulance telemetry, and hospital coordination data into a unified platform.

By leveraging MongoDB, DeccanAid delivers fast, scalable, and reliable emergency response management capable of supporting thousands of concurrent incidents and real-time healthcare interactions.

**Sarvam.ai**

DeccanAid leverages Sarvam AI to make emergency services accessible across India's diverse linguistic landscape. During emergencies, users can communicate naturally in their preferred language through voice interactions, eliminating language barriers during critical situations.

Sarvam AI powers our **Speech-to-Text** and **Text-to-Speech** workflows, enabling emergency reports to be accurately transcribed, processed, and communicated in real time. This allows callers to describe emergencies using voice while responders receive structured information instantly.

By integrating multilingual voice capabilities into emergency response workflows, DeccanAid ensures faster communication, improved accessibility, and more inclusive emergency care for people across different regions and language backgrounds.

**IoT and Embedded System**

DeccanAid incorporates a vehicle-mounted embedded emergency detection system that continuously monitors vehicle conditions and can automatically identify potential accident events in real time. When a critical incident is detected, the device instantly triggers an emergency alert and transmits incident data to the cloud platform without requiring manual intervention.

This embedded intelligence bridges the gap between physical vehicles and digital emergency services, enabling faster accident reporting, real-time incident monitoring, and automated emergency response activation. By combining edge-based sensing with cloud-connected emergency coordination, DeccanAid demonstrates how IoT and embedded systems can directly contribute to reducing emergency response times and improving public safety.

**Key Embedded Features:**

* Real-time accident detection
* Automatic emergency alert generation
* Live location transmission
* Vehicle-mounted edge intelligence
* Cloud-connected emergency response integration

### FlowState
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/flowstate-2e0b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Crepco/flowstate) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ni39-Cver78) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> FlowState — catching the moment a mind wanders, fr

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Ever read a whole page and realized you absorbed nothing? Your eyes kept moving, but your brain had checked out. This "zoning out" happens constantly while studying, in online classes, and on long drives — and the problem is you almost never notice it in the moment. There's no outside signal of what's happening inside your head, so the lapse just silently costs you: wasted study hours, missed lecture content, or — behind the wheel — your life.

FlowState fixes the "you don't know you've drifted" problem. It reads your brain activity from a forehead EEG sensor, turns it into a live focus score, and alerts you the instant your attention drops — so you can catch the lapse and refocus while it's happening, not after.

What people can use it for:

Studying & self-learning — get nudged the moment you start reading without comprehending, and see exactly when you focused or faded during a session.
Online classes — give students and instructors real visibility into engagement, which webcams can't capture (you can stare blankly at a screen and look perfectly "present").
Late-night & long-haul driving 🚗 — drowsy, zoned-out driving is a leading cause of fatal crashes, and drivers rarely realize they're drifting until it's too late. The same detection that nudges a student could wake a drifting driver and save a life.
Any high-stakes focus job — pilots, machinery operators, security/monitoring roles, surgeons in long procedures — anywhere one lapse in attention is dangerous.
Focus & ADHD training — biofeedback that helps people learn to recognize and rebuild their own attention.
Why it's different: most attention trackers use a webcam and only see your gaze — easily fooled by a blank stare. FlowState measures a physiological signal of engagement directly, which is much harder to fake. We're honest that it's a relative, personalized proxy, not a medical device — but it makes an invisible mental state visible in real time, which is the thing no one else does.

Studying is just the use case we built and demo today. The core capability — detecting the exact moment a human brain stops paying attention — generalizes to almost any task where staying focused matters. From there, the only limit is imagination.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Pulling a real brain signal out of a wall of noise. A single dry electrode on the forehead picks up way more 50 Hz powerline hum than actual microvolt-level EEG — raw, the brain signal is basically buried. I built a cleanup chain: a 50 Hz notch filter plus its 100 Hz harmonic, then a 1–40 Hz bandpass, all using zero-phase filtfilt so the wave peaks don't shift in time. We wrote a separate analyze_csv.py tool that prints band power before vs. after filtering — it confirmed the 50 Hz peak drops by orders of magnitude and real theta/alpha/beta survive underneath.

2. A random crash under load: OpenBLAS error: Memory allocation still failed after 10 retries. This one was brutal because it was intermittent. The cause: NumPy/SciPy's BLAS backend allocates a memory pool per thread, and we were calling it from two threads at once (the Flask server + a background compute loop), exhausting the pool. The fix was non-obvious — pin BLAS/OpenMP to a single thread by setting OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 (and OMP/MKL) before NumPy is ever imported. Our FFT windows are tiny, so single-threaded costs us nothing, and the crash disappeared.

3. Real-time updates without freezing the dashboard. Reading the sensor, filtering, running FFTs, and scoring 20 times a second can easily block the web server. We split it into background threads (one reads the data source, one runs the analysis loop) and push results to the browser over Server-Sent Events, downsampling the waveform for display so the stream stays light. The UI now updates smoothly at 20 Hz while the heavy math runs out of the way.

**Gemini**

FlowState uses Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash) as an AI Focus Coach. After each session we feed Gemini the real EEG-derived stats (avg focus, zone-outs, focus trend, band mix) inside a grounded system prompt that forbids inventing numbers, then let the user chat with it for personalized, actionable advice on why they lost focus and how to improve. Gemini is what turns raw brainwave data into coaching a human can act on — with a graceful offline fallback so the demo never breaks.

**IoT and Embedded System**

FlowState is a wearable brain-computer interface: a BioAmp EXG Pill sensor + Arduino UNO R4 that samples forehead EEG on A0 at a precise 500 Hz (jitter-free micros() timing, 14-bit ADC) and streams it live over serial. It's a classic embedded IoT architecture — a constrained MCU doing rock-solid real-time biosignal acquisition at the edge, feeding a host that filters, analyzes, and reacts. A real physical-sensor-to-decision pipeline, not a simulation.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Razorpay API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Razorpay%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SkillSeekho addresses a critical gap in India's informal skill economy. Millions of skilled individuals possess valuable expertise but remain undiscoverable due to literacy barriers, lack of digital access, and absence of trust mechanisms. By combining voice-first onboarding, hyperlocal discovery, community verification, and seamless payments, SkillSeekho enables skilled professionals to earn from their expertise while helping learners find trusted local mentors and trainers.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was implementing accurate voice-based onboarding. Since SkillSeekho is designed for users who may not be comfortable with typing, we had to ensure that speech-to-text conversion worked reliably across different accents and speaking styles. Another challenge was structuring unorganized voice input into meaningful profile information such as skill category, experience, and service description. We addressed this by integrating AI-powered transcription and processing pipelines that convert natural speech into structured, user-friendly listings.

**Sarvam.ai**

Sarvam AI enables voice-first accessibility by converting speech into text in real time. This allows skilled professionals who may not be literate to onboard themselves using voice commands, while users searching for local skilled workers can also interact with the platform through speech instead of typing. The technology makes the platform inclusive, accessible, and easy to use for India's large non-English-speaking and digitally underserved population.

**Open Innovation**

SkillSeekho aligns with the Open Innovation track by addressing a fundamental gap in India's informal skill economy. Millions of skilled individuals possess valuable expertise but lack digital visibility, trust mechanisms, and accessible ways to connect with potential learners or customers. By creating a voice-native, community-verified platform that enables discovery, booking, and payments, SkillSeekho brings traditionally offline talent into the digital economy. The solution combines AI, hyperlocal networking, trust-based verification, and accessibility to empower underserved communities, making it a scalable innovation with social and economic impact across multiple sectors.

### EthTwin
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/twinpilot-5f89) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/danielshx/ethtwin) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ethtwin-woad.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1190886982?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Crypto for everyone — even my grandma.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solodity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solodity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Crypto has a 500M-user ceiling, and it's a UX problem not a tech problem.

  Ask your grandma to send 100 USDC. She has to: install a wallet, write down 12 words, copy a 42-character address, pick the right chain, hold ETH for gas, pray she didn't send it on Polygon when the
  receiver expected Base, and hope she didn't fat-finger a hex digit. One mistake = funds gone forever. This is why crypto still feels like a hobby for engineers, not money for humans.

  EthTwin replaces all of that with one sentence:

  ▎ "Hey Twin, send 100 USDC to my grandson Tom."

  ---
  What changes with EthTwin

  - Seed phrase → Passkey / Face ID. No 12 words. No paper backup. Privy + smart wallet.
  - 0x742d35Cc6634C0532... → tom.ethtwin.eth. Names, not hex.
  - Public forever-receipts → Stealth addresses by default. EIP-5564, unlinkable.
  - "What's a gas fee?" → Gasless. Smart wallet sponsors gas.
  - Chain → bridge → swap → sign → confirm → wait → "did it work?" → One voice command.
  - Agents with no identity or economy → ENSIP-25 + ERC-8004 + x402 micropayments. Agents that can prove who they are and pay each other per-call.

  ---
  Three problems, one interface

  1. Onboarding is hostile. Voice-first + ENS subname + passkey. Maria (67, Stuttgart) goes from zero to her first on-chain transfer in under 60 seconds. No seed phrase. No hex. No "are you sure you're on the
   right chain?"

  2. Privacy is opt-in and painful. Every public ENS name is a forever receipt. EthTwin makes stealth addresses the default — payments resolve through an EIP-5564 stealth meta-key stored as an ENS Text
  Record, seeded by cosmic randomness from a real satellite (Orbitport cTRNG). Unlinkable by default, verifiable on-chain.

  3. Agents have no economy. AI agents today can't prove who they are, can't hire each other, can't pay for work. EthTwin's Twin is a fully ENSIP-25-compliant agent registered in the ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry
   — it can discover other agents via ENS, verify them on-chain, and pay them per-call via x402 micropayments. The Twin literally hired an Apify scraping agent for $1 USDC live during the demo.

  ---
  The "wow" moment

  Maria's voice command silently triggered: an ENS subname resolution, an ENSIP-25 agent verification, a satellite-seeded stealth address generation, an EIP-5564 announcement, and an x402 micropayment to a
  third-party agent — across two chains.

  She just thought she sent her grandson money.

  That's the bet: the next billion users don't want to learn crypto. They want crypto to learn them.

**Challenges we ran into**

We bet on five bleeding-edge specs in 48 hours: ENSIP-25 (drafted weeks ago), ERC-8004, EIP-5564 stealth addresses, x402 micropayments (v2 just shipped), and Vercel AI SDK v6 (released days before the
  hackathon). Every single one bit us. Here are the four that almost killed the demo.

  ---
  1. The x402 ecosystem split — same name, different package

  We installed x402-fetch and spent 4 hours debugging "401 Payment Required" loops that never settled. Turns out there are two competing x402 libraries with nearly identical names:

  - x402-fetch@1.2.0 — Coinbase's original implementation
  - @x402/fetch@2.11.0 — the x402-foundation v2 standard

  They speak different protocols. Apify's facilitator only accepts v2. The npm search results showed v1 first, every blog post we found used v1, and the error messages were silent — payments just… never
  settled.

  Fix: ripped out x402-fetch, installed @x402/fetch + @x402/core + @coinbase/x402 (facilitator), wired up x402Client with ExactEvmScheme. Locked the verified versions into CLAUDE.md so future-us couldn't
  repeat the mistake.

  ---
  2. Privy deprecated their server SDK during the hackathon

  We started with @privy-io/server-auth (every tutorial uses it). Twelve hours in, the package showed a deprecation warning we'd been ignoring: "Use @privy-io/node instead."

  The new SDK has a completely different shape — no PrivyClient class, just free functions. It also requires a PRIVY_VERIFICATION_KEY you have to manually fetch from the Privy Dashboard (not documented in the
   migration guide we found).

  Fix: rewrote every server route that touched auth, regenerated the verification key, and added the env var. Lost ~3 hours but ended up on the supported path.

  Bonus gotcha: Privy v3 also nested embedded-wallet config. v2 was embeddedWallets.createOnLogin, v3 is embeddedWallets.ethereum.createOnLogin. Silent change. Wallets just… didn't auto-create. Took an hour
  to find.

  ---
  3. AI SDK v6 silently renamed every tool definition

  Vercel released AI SDK v6 four days before the hackathon. We followed every tutorial we knew. Tools wouldn't fire. No error — Claude just refused to call them.

  The diff: in v5, tools used parameters: z.object(...). In v6, it's inputSchema: z.object(...). Same zod, same shape, different key. The TypeScript types accepted both. The runtime silently treated v5-style
  tools as having no schema.

  Fix: found one obscure GitHub issue confirming the rename, migrated all 15 Twin tools (sendMessage, hireAgent, inspectMyWallet, etc.) in lib/twin-tools.ts. Also discovered convertToModelMessages is now
  async — must await it or the chat route crashes with a confusing "messages.map is not a function" error.

  ---
  4. Apify's x402 minimum killed our original demo math

  Original pitch: "Twin hires an Apify agent for $0.20 USDC." Cute number. Live demo we'd practiced for hours.

  Two days before submission, we actually read Apify's x402 docs carefully: the minimum is $1 USDC per request, not $0.20. Only Pay-Per-Event Actors are x402-enabled. And Base Sepolia support depends on the
  facilitator — Mainnet is the safe path.

  Fix: rewrote the demo script around a $1 USDC payment (still cheap enough to feel like a micropayment, expensive enough that the live tx is satisfying to watch). Switched the facilitator config to Base
  Mainnet for the demo, kept Base Sepolia as the dev-mode fallback. Updated docs/06-Demo-Skript.md accordingly.

  ---
  What we learned

  When you build on five specs that are all younger than your hackathon, the documentation is the codebase, the ecosystem is forking in real time, and yesterday's tutorial is today's footgun. Our defense
  became CLAUDE.md — a living document of every verified package version, every silent breaking change, every "wait, that's not how it works anymore" moment. Future-us reads it first; past-us would have saved
   12 hours.

  The bet paid off: every primitive that almost broke the build is the same primitive that makes the demo feel like magic.

**Ethereum Core**

EthTwin is built on a stack of recent Ethereum specs, most of them younger than this hackathon. We composed them in ways the specs themselves haven't documented yet.

  - ENSIP-25 (AI Agent Identity). Every Twin gets the canonical agent-registration[<registry>][<agentId>] text record at spawn time. verifyAgentRegistration() in lib/ensip25.ts reads it back and checks the
  registry.
  - ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry. Live integration on Sepolia and Base Sepolia (0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e). The hireAgent tool runs this check before any x402 payment fires.
  - EIP-5564 Stealth Addresses. Implemented via @scopelift/stealth-address-sdk. The recipient's meta-key lives in a custom stealth-meta-address ENS text record, which we're submitting as a future ENSIP
  candidate.
  - EIP-5564 spending keys doing double duty. The same secp256k1 spending keys that derive stealth addresses also derive a static-static ECDH secret used as the AES-256-GCM key for our on-chain ENS
  sub-subname messenger. One key material, two privacy primitives.
  - ERC-7930 interoperable addresses. Used in lib/ensip25.ts:encodeInteropAddress to build the cross-chain identity references ENSIP-25 requires inside its text-record key format.
  - x402 v2 micropayments. @x402/fetch v2, @coinbase/x402 facilitator, @x402/next withX402 wrapper. Both v1 and v2 schemes registered for Base Sepolia and Base Mainnet so the wrapper handles whichever the
  server negotiates.
  - ERC-4337 smart wallets. Privy's Kernel/ZeroDev embedded wallet (passkey-signed, gasless), with Orbitport KMS as the signing authority underneath (lib/kms.ts viem LocalAccount adapter, ECC_SECG_P256K1).
  - ENS subnames as identity. Every Twin is a real Sepolia subname under ethtwin.eth, minted via a single multicall that sets addr, seven text records, the ENSIP-25 entry and the agents.directory listing
  atomically.

  All of these run silently underneath one voice command. The point isn't that we used a lot of specs, it's that they fit together when you build for the user instead of the spec.

**Network Economy**

EthTwin is an agent network where every user spawns a Twin that lives at their ENS subname (maria.ethtwin.eth), and Twins hire each other using x402 micropayments.

  The pieces:

  - ENSIP-25 + ERC-8004. Every Twin has an on-chain identity entry. Discovery is an ENS read, verification is an ERC-8004 read against 0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e on Sepolia and Base Sepolia.
  No central registry, no API keys.
  - x402 micropayments. When Maria's Twin needs an answer it doesn't have, it pays analyst.ethtwin.eth $1 USDC via @x402/fetch v2 and the Coinbase facilitator. The on-chain tx hash and Basescan link show up
  in the chat receipt so the judge can click through.
  - ENS text records as the agent manifest. Capabilities, endpoint, persona, KMS key, stealth meta-key. The ENS name is the API surface.

  Demo flow: Maria speaks one sentence. Her Twin discovers the peer through the on-chain agents.directory, verifies it via ERC-8004, pays it $1 over x402, signs the tx through Orbitport KMS, folds the answer
  back into the conversation. Under 10 seconds, end to end on-chain.

  That's a working agent economy in miniature, with humans addressing agents by name, agents addressing each other by name, and money moving at the speed of an HTTP request.

**Future Society**

Crypto today assumes the user is an engineer. Seed phrases, hex addresses, gas tokens, chain selection, RPC errors, hex calldata you sign blind. The next billion users will not learn any of that.

  EthTwin is what crypto looks like when it's built for humans:

  - Voice-first onboarding. Maria, 67, from Stuttgart, gets her ENS subname, smart wallet, and first on-chain transfer in under 60 seconds, by speaking. No seed phrase, no hex.
  - Privacy by default. Public ENS names are forever-receipts. We make EIP-5564 stealth addresses the default payment path, with the recipient's stealth-meta-address published as an ENS text record. Sender
  and recipient stay unlinkable on-chain. The recipient's main address never appears.
  - No blind signing. Every approval is decoded against Sourcify-verified ABIs and a wallet-risk classifier. Unlimited approvals get flagged HIGH-risk in language Maria understands.
  - Names, not numbers. Every approval modal and recipient label shows an ENS name reverse-resolved from chain.
  - Voice as accessibility. It's not a gimmick. Anyone who can talk can transact, regardless of vision, motor skills, or technical literacy.

  The bet: the next billion users don't want to learn crypto. They want it to learn them. Our test case is whether Maria can use it without help. So far, she can.

**SpaceComputer Bounty**

We use Orbitport KMS as the signing authority for every Twin we mint.

  When a user onboards (app/api/onboarding/route.ts), we call createTwinKey() to mint a fresh ECC_SECG_P256K1 Ethereum-scheme key in KMS. The keyId goes into a twin.kms-key-id ENS text record, the derived
  address goes into addr. We never see the private key.

  For signing we built a viem-compatible LocalAccount adapter in lib/kms.ts:kmsAccount. It proxies signTransaction, signMessage and signTypedData through the KMS gateway. Because it's just a viem account, the
   rest of the stack (token transfers in lib/transfers.ts, EIP-5564 stealth sends in lib/payments.ts, SIWE-style auth in app/api/session/route.ts) plugs in unchanged. Tested via pnpm test:kms and pnpm
  test:kms-sepolia.

  We also wired the cTRNG side (lib/cosmic.ts) with attestation passthrough and a labelled mock fallback. Honest disclosure: in the current build cTRNG is not load-bearing for stealth address derivation, that
   uses the ScopeLift SDK's CSPRNG. The wrapper is there for a future stealth-seed re-integration.

  What this means in practice: Maria's Twin can't be drained even if our backend gets compromised, because no key material lives outside Orbitport KMS. Every on-chain tx she triggers settles with the
  KMS-derived address as from.

**Sourcify Bounty**

Sourcify is our anti-blind-signing layer. Maria can't read hex calldata, so we use Sourcify to give the Twin verified-source evidence and turn it into a plain English risk decision before she signs.

  lib/sourcify.ts reads full_match and partial_match metadata, ABI, contract name and source URL from repo.sourcify.dev for Mainnet, Sepolia and Base Sepolia. lib/tx-decoder.ts decodes calldata against the
  verified ABI. lib/contract-risk.ts classifies the call. app/api/decode-transaction/route.ts runs the lookup server side so it doesn't break on CORS.

  components/tx-approval-modal.tsx shows the result as Inspect, Decode, Decide. Sourcify is the Inspect step. The risk classifier is the Decide step. We deliberately keep them separate, because Sourcify
  telling you the source is open is not the same as the action being safe. That was direct mentor feedback, and we built around it.

  The Send tab also has a "Try risky approval demo" button that walks through approve(spender, maxUint256) as a HIGH-risk path without actually broadcasting. It's the most common drain pattern, and it shows
  exactly how Sourcify evidence flows into a safety decision.

  Risk patterns the classifier surfaces include: unverified contract (HIGH), unknown selector (HIGH), unlimited ERC20 approval (HIGH), setApprovalForAll(true) (HIGH), transferFrom (MEDIUM), Sourcify partial
  match (MEDIUM), verified decoded transfer (LOW).

**Best ENS Integration for AI Agents**

Every Twin we mint is a fully ENSIP-25 compliant agent. The text record key format agent-registration[<ERC-7930-interop-address>][<agentId>] is set during onboarding via
  lib/ensip25.ts:encodeInteropAddress(), with the value "1". verifyAgentRegistration() reads it back and checks against the ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry on Base Sepolia
  (0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e). Mainnet entry (0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432) is a one-line config switch.

  The verification runs before an x402 payment fires. If the registry entry is missing, the Twin refuses to pay the peer. That's the agent identity layer doing real work, not a label.

  The full agent manifest lives in ENS text records on the Twin's subname:

  - addr, the smart wallet address
  - twin.persona, the system prompt
  - twin.capabilities, the tool catalog
  - twin.endpoint, the HTTPS endpoint other agents POST to
  - twin.kms-key-id, the Orbitport KMS handle for signing
  - agent-registration[...], the ENSIP-25 entry pointing into ERC-8004
  - stealth-meta-address, the EIP-5564 st:eth:0x... for private payments
  - agents.directory (on the parent ethtwin.eth), the registry of hireable agents

  Demo flow: the Twin reads agents.directory on ethtwin.eth, resolves analyst.ethtwin.eth, fetches its ENSIP-25 record, verifies it against ERC-8004, then pays $1 USDC over x402. Six on-chain ENS reads in one
   user click.

  If we removed ENS, every part of this breaks. Identity, discovery, verification, signing key lookup, privacy meta-key, agent directory. ENS is the product's identity layer, not decoration.

**Most Creative Use of ENS**

We ship two ENS patterns that go beyond name resolution. Both are live and on-chain.

  1. stealth-meta-address text record. There's no official ENSIP for stealth meta-addresses in ENS yet. We propose the pattern: each Twin publishes its EIP-5564 st:eth:0x... meta-address as a text record on
  its own subname. Senders read it, hand it to the ScopeLift SDK, and derive a one-time stealth address. The recipient's main wallet stays unlinked. No registry contract, no extra onboarding for the
  recipient. Privacy infrastructure as an ENS text record.

  2. ENS sub-subnames as a messaging medium. Every twin-to-twin DM is an actual on-chain sub-subname:

  msg-<ts>-<seq>.<recipient>.ethtwin.eth
    text "from"  ->  sender twin
    text "body"  ->  AES-256-GCM ciphertext
    text "at"    ->  timestamp

  The recipient maintains a messages.list text record indexing inbound messages. The interesting part: the message body is encrypted using static-static ECDH on the EIP-5564 spending keys, then AES-256-GCM
  with a domain-tag-bound key. So the same key material that powers private payments also powers private chat. One ENS text record (stealth-meta-address) doing two privacy jobs.

  Tom's auto-reply ("thanks oma! 💜") is a real on-chain ENS sub-subname write back to Maria. The chat is the chain.

Team **TBC Agent Forge** -- Elena Grütter, [Daniel Shamsi](https://github.com/danielshx), Rami Ezzeddine

### TASS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tass-c2c0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/annamarasina/tass-ethprague2026.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> jhwsdhwsjhsw

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![BeeJS](https://img.shields.io/badge/BeeJS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Crawlee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Crawlee-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

To check if smart contracts are safe is often difficult, slow, and spread across many tools. Developers usually need to manually review code, compare trusted contracts, search for exploit history and verify that project claims actually match the code. Our project, SolidScan, simplifies this process by bringing everything into one workflow inside VS Code. It helps developers quickly spot compliance issues and security vulnerabilities before deployment, making smart contract reviews faster, easier and more trustworthy for both builders and users.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was choosing the right idea. We had many creative concepts, but we needed to focus on one that solved a real-world problem and could still be built within 48 hours. Another challenge was working with large datasets and combining many features into one smooth workflow during the fast-paced hackathon environment.

**Ethereum Core**

SolidScan strengthens the Ethereum developer ecosystem by helping developers detect legal compliance risks, security vulnerabilities and unsafe patterns in Solidity smart contracts during development.
Instead of auditing contracts only after deployment, our tool shifts security and compliance checks left into the coding workflow, enabling safer Ethereum applications before they reach mainnet.

**Sourcify Bounty**

**Sourcify** is the core tech stack for our vscode extension **SolidScan**. We used Sourcify dataset as the source of verified on-chain contract dataset for SolidScan. SolidScan takes the Solidity source code being audited then feeds it into embedding-based similarity search to compare against Sourcify dataset in order to find similar smart contracts on-chain (and related hash etc. by **BigQuery**). Then we leverage scraper agents to find known vulnerabilities by sourcing GitHub, Etherscan etc. All the information will be useful as anti-pattern **Few-shot Examples** to improve the security of our source solidity code.

**Verified Fetch — Trust No Gateway**

**Swarm** is the core backend tech for our product vscode extension **SolidScan**. We implement the Swarm verified-fetch idea (the **JS libraries**) and then uses it as the trust layer for our legal knowledge base. SolidScan needs external compliance and exploit intelligence. In the workflow of our product, we create an LLM orchestra for continuous legal text scraping and we need to maintain a backend database to store these data series legal text. However, we did not want to blindly trust a random gateway response, and Swarm is used for it and serves as trustworthy JSON legal knowledge base. We use it during legal-risk analysis without depending on a full Bee node.

**Apify Bounty**

SolidScan qualifies for the Apify bounty by using an on-chain x402 USDC payment flow to dynamically orchestrate a fleet of specialized Apify Actors. When a developer runs our VS Code plugin, our system analyzes the context of the smart contract and programmatically triggers the most relevant Apify Actor for that specific sector. These Actors scrape live, timestamped regulatory sources, including ESMA, EBA, and MiCA frameworks. Apify serves as the core data layer of our architecture, compiling these diverse sources into a structured, time-series legal dataset. This fresh, verifiable intelligence is then ingested by our LLM Agent, allowing it to return a highly accurate, context-aware compliance audit directly to the developer's IDE.

### Panorama
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/panorama-69c4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ohMySol/Panorama) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/CCrazDVZFrk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> DeFi Smart Contract Dependency Visualizer

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Etherscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Etherscan-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. This tool helps both retail and institutional users better understand a DeFi protocol before allocating capital. By simply pasting a vault or pool address, users receive an interactive dependency graph that maps all underlying smart contracts powering the protocol. This provides a better visibility into how funds move across the system, enabling users to make more informed risk management decisions.

2. The solution aggregates all protocol dependencies into a single unified interface and visually demonstrates how contracts are interconnected. Instead of manually searching through explorers and documentation, users get a complete structural overview of the protocol in one place, significantly simplifying due diligence and security analysis.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Dependency Graph Ordering
Getting the correct visual hierarchy in the dependency tree was tricky. Initially, governance contracts (curator, guardian, owner) appeared at the bottom of the tree after all markets and tokens, which didn't reflect their importance. The issue was in the manifest execution order - the system processed dependencies in the order they were defined in the protocol manifest. We solved this by reordering the directCalls array to prioritize governance contracts, ensuring they appear first in the visualization.

- Finding the correct approach how to explore the protocol dependencies. Initially we were using a separate TypeScript files which all logic related to the protocol. But we understood that this approach will become heavy very fast and we come up with an idea to describe protocol in manifest files.

- Collect risk related data from open source for each node. There is a lot of data in the web about smart contracts and a lot of resources. All this data should be somehow structured and after that managed to create a risk scoring engine. For this prototype we decided to move with the risk flags for the beginning. These flags can be quickly identified in the abi (e.g. "upgradeTo", "blacklist") of the smart contract and displayed in the node information.

**Ethereum Core**

Panorama improves Ethereum's security and usability by giving developers, auditors, and DeFi users a practical tool to visualize and understand complex smart contract dependencies. By automatically mapping protocol architectures and revealing hidden connections, we make it significantly easier and safer to audit, integrate with, and build on top of Ethereum protocols.
Our tool addresses a critical infrastructure gap - the ability to quickly understand "what depends on what" in DeFi - which is essential for the security and resilience of interconnected decentralized systems.

**Network Economy**

Panorama automatically visualizes smart contract architectures and protocol dependencies, giving users clear risk insight before deploying capital. By making deep protocol analysis accessible to everyone, it minimizes financial losses caused by knowledge gaps in DeFi workflows - creating a safer, more transparent ecosystem for all participants.

**Future Society**

Panorama promotes transparency and fair governance in DeFi by making protocol architectures visible and understandable to everyone. By revealing governance structures (curators, guardians, owners) and their relationships to protocol components, we empower communities to make informed decisions about which protocols align with their intentions and risk model

**Sourcify Bounty**

We use Sourcify as the primary source for retrieving verified smart contract ABIs. When analyzing a contract, we query Sourcify's API to fetch the ABI, which enables us to identify the contract type and automatically discover dependencies by calling protocol-specific functions. If Sourcify doesn't have the contract, we fall back to Etherscan's API, ensuring maximum coverage.
