### Q-Chain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/qchain-a893) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://q-chain.xyz/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Unbreakable Today. Unstoppable Tomorrow.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Core Problem: Classical Blockchain Cryptography is Quantum-Vulnerable
Modern blockchains — including Ethereum and Algorand — rely on ECDSA / Ed25519 elliptic-curve cryptography for signing transactions. These are mathematically vulnerable to quantum computers running Shor's Algorithm, which can derive private keys from public keys, potentially allowing:

Theft of wallet funds at scale
Forgery of transaction signatures
Undermining the trust model of all existing blockchain infrastructure

This is not a theoretical risk — NIST finalized three PQC standards in August 2024 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium, Falcon, SPHINCS+), and regulators like the NSA's CNSA 2.0 framework are already mandating quantum-safe migration timelines. Algorand itself executed the first mainnet Falcon-1024 transaction on November 3, 2025, signaling the urgency of this transition.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/3bedc42e73f94eaaa41b818931acfbd0/78a0a4b4-9d3f-46d5-b80e-8008078f642d.png)

In short: Q-Chain solves the gap between the emerging quantum threat and practical blockchain usability, making PQC-enhanced blockchain interaction accessible to developers and students through a real application, not just theory.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge A: Algorand Pera Wallet — Web Integration via Deeplink
This was a genuinely hard engineering problem that very few developers have tackled cleanly.
The core difficulty: Pera Wallet is fundamentally a mobile-first wallet. It does not have a browser extension like MetaMask. To use it on a web app, you must:

Generate a WalletConnect deeplink or use the @perawallet/connect SDK
Display a QR code or redirect URL that opens Pera on mobile
After the user approves the connection on their phone, the web app must listen for the session approval event and receive the connected account address
When submitting transactions, the web must construct the unsigned transaction, send it over the WalletConnect bridge, wait for the user to sign it on mobile, and receive the signed transaction back
Then broadcast the signed transaction to the Algorand node

What went wrong / the challenge:

The WalletConnect v2 bridge and Pera SDK have inconsistent behavior between environments — sessions would drop, reconnect events wouldn't fire reliably, and the web app would lose track of wallet state after mobile approval
Mobile redirect flow: After deeplink approval, returning to the browser didn't always trigger the correct state update — requiring careful event listener management and session persistence
Transaction monitoring after approval: The web dashboard needed to track transaction IDs and poll the Algorand indexer (or node) to confirm when a transaction submitted from mobile had settled on-chain — this polling loop had to be built manually since there's no native push from Pera to web
PQC layer integration: Algorand's PQC support (Falcon-1024) is currently opt-in via CLI-generated keys and not yet natively exposed in the standard AlgoSDK for dApps, making it extremely non-trivial to layer PQC signing into a web transaction flow — your team had to either simulate this layer client-side or use experimental SDK features

Technical resolution path:

Use @perawallet/connect with persistent WalletConnect session storage
Implement polling against the Algorand Indexer REST API (/v2/transactions/{txId}) to confirm settlement
For PQC: generate Falcon key pairs client-side using a WASM-compiled library (e.g., liboqs-js) and embed the PQC signature as a note field or ARC-2 metadata on the Algorand transaction, since native AVM PQC verification isn't yet web-accessible


Challenge B: NFT Minting on Both Algorand Testnet and Sepolia Ethereum Testnet
On Algorand:

NFTs on Algorand are ASAs (Algorand Standard Assets) created via the AssetCreateTxn
Minting requires the creator account to have sufficient ALGO for the minimum balance requirement (0.1 ALGO per ASA created)
Testnet faucet limitations and opt-in requirements (receivers must opt-in to receive the ASA) created friction
If Pera wallet was used to sign the asset creation transaction via the web bridge, the multi-step flow (create → opt-in → transfer) had to be choreographed carefully, with each step waiting for the previous transaction to confirm
ARC-3 / ARC-69 metadata for NFT URI pointing to off-chain storage (IPFS) required careful JSON construction and IPFS pinning in the flow

On Ethereum Sepolia:

Deploying an ERC-721 contract to Sepolia via MetaMask or a web3 provider is straightforward in theory, but using a pre-deployed contract address requires ensuring the ABI matches and the safeMint() function is exposed correctly
Sepolia faucets have rate limits and are often congested, causing insufficient funds errors during testing
Gas estimation failures: If the minting function had any revert path (e.g., duplicate token IDs, access control), the transaction would silently fail at the estimation stage, which is hard to debug without good error handling
If you were also trying to attach PQC metadata to the Ethereum NFT (e.g., in the tokenURI or as on-chain data), the gas cost became significant and sometimes caused out-of-gas errors on testnet with limited ETH

Cross-chain coordination challenge: Your dashboard needed to display minting status from both chains simultaneously, meaning you had to manage two different provider instances (AlgoSDK + ethers.js/viem), two different transaction lifecycle models (Algorand's round-based finality vs Ethereum's block confirmation), and two different wallet connection states — all in a single coherent UI.

**Ethereum Track**

Q-Chain's fit:
Smart Contract Deployment on Sepolia: Q-Chain deploys and interacts with ERC-721 smart contracts on Sepolia Ethereum Testnet, demonstrating real on-chain NFT minting and transaction execution — a core Ethereum track deliverable.
Forward-looking cryptographic innovation: Ethereum's own roadmap (EIP-7560, RIP-7212) explicitly includes post-quantum cryptography as a long-term goal. Q-Chain pre-empts this by implementing a PQC layer on top of Ethereum transactions today, making it directly relevant to Ethereum's publicly stated future. Your project demonstrates what quantum-safe Ethereum interaction would look like before the official protocol-level upgrade.
Cross-chain architecture: Q-Chain operates across both Ethereum and Algorand simultaneously. This multi-chain design aligns with Ethereum's evolving ecosystem focus on interoperability, bridging, and chain-agnostic infrastructure. Judges evaluating Ethereum track submissions appreciate projects that think beyond single-chain boundaries.
Real-world applicability: The project isn't a toy contract — it addresses a genuine security gap (quantum vulnerability of ECDSA used by Ethereum) and provides a working prototype demonstrating what a quantum-safe Ethereum dApp experience could look like.
NFT minting as a concrete use case: NFTs and digital asset issuance on Ethereum remain one of the track's most accessible entry points, and Q-Chain uses this to demonstrate PQC concepts through a tangible, visual, user-facing product.

**Algorand Blockchain Track**

The Algorand Track at Diversion 2026 specifically calls for real-world, campus-focused applications using Algorand's fast, secure, low-cost infrastructure, progressing from basic blockchain usage to intermediate-advanced decentralized system design.
Q-Chain maps directly to every stated objective of this track:
"Introduce students to blockchain development using Algorand"
Q-Chain uses the Algorand SDK, Pera Wallet, and AlgoNode/TestNet infrastructure — students building or exploring the project are directly exposed to the Algorand development stack in a working, deployed application.
"Enable hands-on learning with wallets, payments, assets, and NFTs"
Q-Chain covers all four: Pera Wallet connection and session management (wallets), Algorand payment transactions routed through the web dashboard (payments), ASA creation for NFT minting (assets), and ARC-3 compliant NFT issuance (NFTs). This is textbook alignment with the track objectives.
"Encourage innovation through real campus and student-centric problems"
The quantum computing threat is one of the most significant upcoming challenges in computer science — a topic students in CS, cryptography, and cybersecurity programs are actively studying. Q-Chain bridges the abstract academic topic of post-quantum cryptography with a hands-on, real blockchain application students can run, interact with, and learn from. A campus NFT issuance system with PQC backing (e.g., quantum-safe student credentials, certificates, or event tickets as Algorand ASAs) is a natural campus-relevant deployment scenario.
"Provide a learning curve from easy to intermediate–advanced challenges"

Easy layer: Connect Pera Wallet, view balance, send test ALGO — all accessible from the Q-Chain dashboard
Intermediate layer: Mint an NFT on Algorand Testnet via ASA creation, with proper opt-in and metadata
Advanced layer: Integrate PQC key generation (Falcon), attach quantum-safe signatures to transactions, and monitor settlement via the indexer — a genuinely advanced challenge that goes beyond most hackathon Algorand submissions

"Promote open-source development and real-world deployable solutions"
Q-Chain is deployed on Vercel (public URL), uses open testnets, and the architecture (dual-chain dashboard + PQC layer) is directly deployable to real campus infrastructure with minimal changes — swapping TestNet for MainNet and a production IPFS gateway.
Algorand's own PQC trajectory:
Algorand executed its first mainnet Falcon-1024 PQC transaction in November 2025. Q-Chain is building in direct alignment with Algorand's stated technology roadmap. A hackathon project that is not only using Algorand today but is already working with the cryptographic primitives Algorand is officially adopting is exceptionally well-positioned for this track.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/decentralized-ai-agent-1b2b) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/piivjzQWV40?si=k3XWS2NwgTGxtVLV) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> PharmaChain : Verify once. Trust forever.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solodity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solodity-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Counterfeit medicines are a silent public-health crisis. Fake, expired, or improperly stored drugs enter the market every day, causing treatment failure, drug resistance, and even death. Existing systems are fragmented, opaque, and trust-based, leaving patients, pharmacies, and regulators vulnerable.
PharmaChain solves this by creating a single source of truth for every medicine

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a082646375c14f5b9e609c65232a9008/03d7898b-9d07-4e8c-be44-88b2e0902fed.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a082646375c14f5b9e609c65232a9008/d514dd27-7a6a-488c-acb9-2c9de8158ce2.jpeg) from manufacturing to consumption.
The Core Problems Today
1. Counterfeit Drugs Are Hard to Detect
Fake medicines visually look identical to genuine ones
QR codes can be copied or reused
Consumers have no way to verify authenticity instantly
2. Broken Supply Chain Transparency
Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers use separate systems
Records can be altered or deleted
No end-to-end traceability
3. Unsafe Storage & Cold-Chain Failures
Vaccines and biologics require strict temperature control
Temperature breaches are often unreported
Patients unknowingly consume ineffective drugs
4. No Consumer Trust or Incentive
Verification is not consumer-friendly
Reporting fakes gives no reward
Trust depends entirely on the seller
5. Manual & Reactive Enforcement
Regulators act after damage is done
Recalls are slow and poorly communicated
Counterfeit hotspots are discovered too late

**Challenges we ran into**

Complex batch lifecycle on blockchain
Multiple states (transfer, inspection, split, recall) caused invalid or conflicting states.
Solution: Designed an enum-based state machine with strict role + state guards and on-chain lineage tracking.
Scratch code reuse & QR cloning risk
One-time codes could be replayed or scanned simultaneously.
Solution: Stored only hashed scratch codes on-chain; first scan activates ownership, second scan auto-flags counterfeit.
Real-time updates without heavy infra
WebSockets were overkill and unstable for hackathon setup.
Solution: Used Server-Sent Events (SSE) with auto-reconnect for lightweight, scalable live updates.
AI hallucinations in medical data
Gemini sometimes produced unsafe or overly confident medical advice.
Solution: Restricted AI to assistive insights only, cross-checked with local medicine DB, and kept all decisions deterministic.
Trust score manipulation risk
Simple scoring could be gamed with fake scans or delays.
Solution: Built a weighted, multi-signal trust score recalculated on every event, with inspector actions overriding scores.
Cold-chain data integrity
Temperature logs are easy to spoof and costly to store on-chain.
Solution: Stored logs off-chain, anchored hashes on-chain, and penalized missing or anomalous data.
Authentication reliability
OTP emails faced delays and resend abuse.
Solution: Implemented short-lived OTPs, rate limits, and session-based JWT after verification.
Local development instability
Running blockchain, backend, and frontend together caused desyncs.
Solution: Created a single deploy-and-seed script for a reproducible dev environment.

**Ethereum Track**

PharmaChain fits squarely into the Ethereum track because it uses Ethereum not as a database, but as a trustless execution and enforcement layer for the pharmaceutical supply chain. Every critical action batch creation, role-based transfers, inspector approvals, one-time scratch-code activation, and recalls is governed by Solidity smart contracts, ensuring rules are enforced by code rather than by any central authority. Ethereum’s immutability guarantees a tamper-proof audit trail, which is essential for regulatory compliance and counterfeit detection, while its native protection against double-spending enables secure one-time medicine activation that cannot be replicated with traditional systems. By encoding roles, state transitions, and batch lineage directly on-chain, PharmaChain enables decentralized coordination between manufacturers, distributors, retailers, inspectors, and consumers who do not need to trust each other, making Ethereum the only practical platform to deliver verifiable authenticity, transparency, and accountability at scale.

### TokenTrim
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tokentrim-62b0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rajatsinghten/HackSRM7.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://trimtoken.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lXRe3PtuSik?si=lS6NqaWcfPCPevsx) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackSRM%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-srm26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Same Window, More Context

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement : Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini operate within a fixed context window which is measured in tokens. While modern models offer 128K–1M token windows, real-world codebases blow past these limits instantly.

Our project addresses the critical "context window" bottleneck inherent in Large Language Models. When developers try to feed entire codebases or long chat histories into an AI, they often hit strict token limits or face high costs. We've built a backend that solves this by using a multi-stage compression engine—incorporating Huffman coding, code minification, and semantic chunking. This allows us to shrink massive files into compact, AI-readable versions, ensuring you can fit significantly more project context into a single prompt without losing the essential logic or structure of the code.
We solve the "instruction overhead" issue that plagues standard compression. Usually, explaining to an LLM how to decompress data wastes even more tokens. Our project introduces a specialized browser extension mode that replaces wordy instructions with a compact JSON payload and sentinel markers. This ensures that every available token is used for your actual data rather than meta-instructions, providing a high-fidelity, lossless round-trip that gives the LLM the most relevant information at the lowest possible "token cost."

**Challenges we ran into**

While testing various compression algorithms, we found it difficult to identify a single method suitable for all languages. Consequently, we decided to build a custom compression engine capable of applying language-specific algorithms. A key challenge was finding the perfect balance: if the compression is too aggressive, the LLM requires significantly more processing power to decode the logic, ultimately negating the efficiency gains of the reduced data size.

> Autonomous AI Agent Marketplace

![Defi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Defi-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenClaw](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenClaw-333333?style=flat-square) ![DDSC](https://img.shields.io/badge/DDSC-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hedera-schedule-transactions](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hedera--schedule--transactions-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**AgentMarket** solves the problem of AI agents being isolated, single-purpose tools that can't interact economically with each other. Today, if you want an AI agent to hire another agent, pay for services, or manage treasury across DeFi protocols, you need to build everything from scratch.

AgentMarket creates an **autonomous AI agent marketplace** where:
- **AI agents discover, hire, and pay each other** on-chain using the ADI Chain's AgentRegistry and PaymentRouter contracts
- **Agents autonomously manage treasury** by swapping tokens on SaucerSwap and earning yield on Bonzo Finance (Hedera)
- **Multi-agent coordination** lets a Commerce Agent ask an Analytics Agent to evaluate a DeFi opportunity before executing
- **Merchants accept agent payments** with gasless checkout via ERC-4337 paymaster
- **Human observers monitor agent activity** through a real-time Agent Flow visualization page

This makes autonomous agent commerce possible without any human intervention - agents earn DDSC, evaluate DeFi opportunities, swap to HBAR, deposit into Bonzo for 8% APY, and coordinate with each other using OpenClaw's agent-to-agent protocol.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Hedera HTS Token Allowances (biggest blocker)
Standard ERC20 `approve()` does NOT grant allowance for smart contract `transferFrom()` on Hedera's HTS tokens. We spent hours debugging why Bonzo Finance deposits kept reverting with `SafeERC20: low-level call failed`. The fix was using `@hashgraph/sdk`'s `AccountAllowanceApproveTransaction` for native HTS allowances, and `ContractExecuteTransaction` for the deposit call.

### eth_estimateGas Fails on Hedera
Hedera's JSON-RPC relay routes gas estimation through read-only queries that reject HTS state changes (`LOCAL_CALL_MODIFICATION_EXCEPTION`). Fix: pass manual `gas` parameters to all write operations (3M for swaps/deposits, 500K for approvals, 800K for HTS association).

### WHBAR is NOT WETH
Hedera's WHBAR (`0x...003aD2`) is an HTS token facade, not a standard WETH contract with `deposit()`. We had to use `swapExactETHForTokens` instead, which sends native HBAR and lets the router handle wrapping internally.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

AgentMarket uses **4 specialized OpenClaw agents** orchestrated via the agent-to-agent protocol:

### Commerce Agent (default)
- Discovers agents on the AgentRegistry
- Evaluates pricing and ratings
- Executes hiring transactions via PaymentRouter
- Manages DDSC token approvals and payments

### Analytics Agent (read-only)
- Monitors DeFi pool reserves and prices
- Evaluates swap opportunities (price impact, slippage)
- Checks lending positions (health factor, APY)
- Provides buy/wait/split recommendations to other agents

### DeFi Agent
- Executes token swaps on SaucerSwap (HBAR -> USDC)
- Deposits collateral into Bonzo Finance for yield
- Manages borrowing with health factor guardrails (min 1.5x)
- Uses @hashgraph/sdk for HTS-native operations

### Merchant Agent
- Registers merchants on-chain
- Processes customer checkouts
- Manages revenue withdrawals from MerchantVault

**Agent Coordination Flow:**
1. Commerce Agent earns DDSC from agent payments
2. Commerce Agent asks Analytics Agent: "Should I swap DDSC -> HBAR?"
3. Analytics Agent checks prices, pools, and responds with recommendation
4. If approved, DeFi Agent executes swap + deposits into Bonzo
5. All activity visible in real-time on the Agent Flow page

All agents communicate through **MCP tools** (38 total) exposed by our MCP server, and learn DeFi strategies from **skill files** (`openclaw/skills/agentmarket-hedera-defi/SKILL.md`).

**Futurllama**

AgentMarket represents the future of AI commerce:
- 4 openclaw AI agents autonomously participating in DeFi across 3 blockchains
- Real token swaps, real lending deposits, real AI inference, real on-chain NFTs
- Agent-to-agent coordination without human intervention
- Verifiable AI decisions via TeeML on 0G Compute Network
- Gasless UX via ERC-4337 paymaster
- Full marketplace infrastructure for the agent economy

**Best DeFAI Application**

AI-powered decision engine for autonomous agent hiring, using real 0G Compute Network inference on Galileo Testnet:

How it works:
1. User/agent submits a task (type, description, complexity, budget, preferred chain)
2. Local engine selects the best agent from our registry based on specialization match, rating, completion rate, chain compatibility, and price
3. Local engine computes risk score (0-100) based on budget size, agent reliability, cross-chain risk, task complexity
4. Real 0G inference call sends the complete context to a Qwen 2.5 7B model via the 0G Compute Network for AI-augmented analysis
5. AI response is parsed and merged with local data: agent assessment, task analysis, risk insights, yield suggestions, confidence score, guardrail notes
6. Returns structured `AgentHiringDecision` with recommended agent, payment route, risk level, guardrails, and yield optimization

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

AgentMarket is an autonomous AI agent marketplace where agents earn money, evaluate DeFi opportunities, hire each other, and make verifiable decisions all powered by 0G infrastructure.

The core insight: AI agents need three things to operate autonomously in an economy  verifiable intelligence (so you can trust their decisions), tokenized capabilities (so you can trade and rent agent access), and decentralized compute (so no single provider controls the AI). 

Every agent decision runs through 0G Compute Network inference on Galileo Testnet. 

When our Commerce Agent needs to decide whether to hire an Analytics Agent for a DeFi evaluation, the full context (agent ratings, task complexity, budget, risk factors) is sent to a Qwen 2.5 7B model running on a TeeML-verified provider. 

The response comes back with a cryptographic proof that the computation was executed correctly inside a Trusted Execution Environment no blind trust in a centralized API.

* **Provider:** `0xa48f01287233509FD694a22Bf840225062E67836`
* **Model:** `qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct` via TeeML
* **SDK:** `@0glabs/0g-serving-broker` with full broker lifecycle
  (discovery → acknowledgment → funding → inference → verification)
* **Auto-funding system** that monitors per-provider sub-account balances and tops up via:

  * `broker.ledger.depositFund()`
  * `broker.ledger.transferFund()`

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

AI agents are minted as encrypted NFTs (ERC-7857) on 0G Galileo. The agent's model config, system prompt, and capabilities are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored on 0G Storage. 

The encryption key is sealed for the owner's public key.

This enables a **"hire without buy" pattern** — `authorizeUsage()` grants temporary access to an agent's intelligence without transferring ownership.

On transfer, the oracle (TEE or ZKP) re-encrypts the sealed key for the new owner.

**ADI Payments Component for Merchants**

On ADI Chain, we built a full merchant payment system using the MerchantVault smart contract. Merchants register on-chain, get a checkout URL with QR code, and accept payments in DDSC stablecoin. 

The key thing is both humans AND AI agents can pay. When our Commerce Agent calls the checkout MCP tool, it processes the payment through the same MerchantVault contract. We've processed 8 real payments totaling over 10 DDSC. And through the ADI Paymaster, we support ERC-4337 account abstraction meaning gasless transactions for end users. The agent pays the gas, the user just approves.

https://github.com/kamalbuilds/agentic-markets/blob/main/openclaw/agents/merchant/agent/AGENT.md

**Open Project Submission**

ADI Chain's low fees and fast finality make it ideal for high-frequency agent-to-agent microtransactions. Every agent hire, rating, checkout, and subscription payment is an on-chain transaction. Traditional chains would make this prohibitively expensive.

The Agent Economy on ADI Chain:

1. Agent Registration & Discovery - AI agents register themselves on the AgentRegistry contract with metadata, capabilities, and pricing. Other agents discover available services by querying the registry. We have 5 agents registered with verifiable on-chain metadata and ratings.

2. Agent-to-Agent Payments via DDSC - When one agent hires another, payment flows through the PaymentRouter contract in DDSC (Dirham Stablecoin). The PaymentRouter extracts a protocol fee and routes the remainder to the hired agent's on-chain balance. This creates a real agent economy where AI agents earn revenue for performing tasks. Our agents have processed 8 payments totaling 10.032 DDSC in autonomous agent-to-agent transactions.

3. Merchant Commerce - AI agents don't just work for each other - they can also serve as merchants. The MerchantVault contract lets agents register as merchants, process customer checkouts, and withdraw accumulated revenue. We have 3 active merchants processing orders on ADI Chain.

4. Gasless UX via ADIPaymaster (ERC-4337) - The ADIPaymaster contract implements ERC-4337 Account Abstraction so users and agents can interact with the marketplace without holding native gas tokens. The paymaster signs UserOperations and covers gas costs, enabling frictionless onboarding. Frontend checkout at `/checkout/:id` uses this for one-click agent hiring.

5. Recurring Subscriptions - The SubscriptionManager contract enables recurring subscription payments for ongoing agent services. Subscribers pay DDSC on a configurable interval (daily/weekly/monthly), with automatic fee distribution to agents and the platform.

6. Cross-Chain Treasury Management - Agents don't just earn on ADI Chain - they autonomously bridge their earnings to Hedera for DeFi yield. Commerce Agent earns DDSC on ADI Chain -> asks Analytics Agent to evaluate DeFi opportunities -> DeFi Agent executes swaps on SaucerSwap and deposits into Bonzo Finance on Hedera. This multi-chain agent treasury management is orchestrated entirely by AI agents using 47 MCP tools.

### Agonus
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agonus-6939) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SumanthPal/eth-agonus.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agonus-frontend-45256917921.us-central1.run.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MWOodZpS3C8&feature=youtu.be) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where AI Agents Compete in Trading Tournaments

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The platform transforms algorithmic trading from a technical, opaque activity into an interactive and observable experience. Instead of requiring users to analyze charts or build strategies themselves, the application introduces a roster of autonomous agents, each designed with a distinct trading philosophy, behavioral profile, and risk appetite. These agents compete in time-bounded tournaments using equalized starting capital, allowing performance differences to emerge from strategy rather than resources.

Users engage with the system as spectators, participants, and learners. They can observe live trading activity, follow agent decision narratives, compare performance metrics, and place predictions on tournament outcomes. This creates an environment where trading becomes understandable through storytelling and comparison rather than raw technical analysis.

At a structural level, tournaments act as controlled experimental environments for agent strategies. Equal starting balances and transparent performance tracking make it possible to evaluate approaches such as momentum trading, mean reversion, arbitrage, or sentiment-driven strategies in a standardized format. Real-time leaderboards, commentary, and personality-driven agent communication provide context for why trades occur, helping users build intuition about market behavior.

The platform also introduces a trustless payout and verification layer through smart contracts. Tournament rules, capital allocation, and reward distribution are enforced automatically, ensuring fairness and removing reliance on centralized intermediaries. This transparency enables both participants and spectators to verify outcomes independently while maintaining a seamless user experience.

Ultimately, the application reframes trading as a competitive, educational, and social activity. By blending autonomous agents, gamified tournaments, and transparent on-chain infrastructure, the platform lowers the barrier to understanding markets while fostering experimentation, discovery, and engagement for users regardless of technical background.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was achieving meaningful agent differentiation. Early versions relied mostly on personality prompts, which made agents appear unique but led to similar trading behavior in practice. Their decisions converged because they shared signals and optimization loops, reducing strategic contrast and weakening the educational value of tournaments. This was resolved by embedding differentiation directly into architecture through strategy-specific signals, decision policies, and risk constraints, ensuring agents expressed distinct behavioral patterns over time.

On the frontend, a separate hurdle involved maintaining performant real-time updates while ingesting high-throughput market and tournament data. Frequent state changes caused rendering bottlenecks and UI lag. This was addressed by introducing selective state subscriptions, batching updates, caching derived metrics, and using streaming patterns to update only affected UI components rather than triggering full re-renders.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

AI agents are the core actors within the platform, functioning as autonomous traders that participate in time-bounded tournaments. Each agent is designed with a structured personality that influences its strategy, risk tolerance, decision cadence, and market interpretation. Rather than acting as simple rule-based bots, agents combine reasoning, market signal processing, and memory to produce behavior that evolves over the course of a tournament.

Within the system, agents operate through a coordinated loop composed of perception, reasoning, and execution. Market data, portfolio state, and tournament context are first ingested as structured inputs. The agent then applies its personality-constrained reasoning process to interpret signals and generate trade intentions. These intentions are validated against strategy and risk constraints before being translated into executable transactions onchain.

Agents interact indirectly through shared market environments and tournament dynamics. Because each agent responds differently to identical conditions, emergent competition arises as strategies influence price movement, liquidity interactions, and leaderboard positioning. This creates a multi-agent ecosystem where performance differences are driven by behavioral design rather than isolated optimization.
AI is also used beyond trading decisions. Commentary and explanation layers translate agent reasoning into human-readable narratives, allowing spectators to understand not only what decisions were made but why they occurred. This improves transparency and reinforces the educational goals of the platform.

System orchestration ensures agents operate safely and consistently. Execution guards, memory layers, and logging pipelines maintain behavioral continuity across trading cycles while enabling observability for debugging and performance comparison. Together, these components allow agents to function as autonomous yet interpretable participants within a shared competitive environment.

Overall, AI tools and agents form a tightly integrated architecture that powers strategy execution, explanation, competition, and user engagement, transforming the platform into an agent-native financial experience rather than a traditional trading interface.

**Futurllama**

This project fits the Futurllama track because it explores a forward-looking interaction model between humans and autonomous agents.

It leverages AI by turning agents into independent economic actors with visible personalities and strategies, enabling users to learn from and interact with machine decision-making in real time. The tournament structure introduces a new primitive where markets become competitive arenas for agent intelligence rather than passive trading environments.

The platform also reflects frontier tech themes through onchain verification, automated payouts, and transparent strategy comparison, combining AI, crypto infrastructure, and social interaction into a single system. From a usability perspective, it reimagines trading interfaces as spectator-driven experiences with commentary, leaderboards, and personality-driven narratives, making complex financial behavior accessible to non-technical users.

Overall, the project embodies Futurllama’s focus on big ideas by merging AI agents, decentralized finance, and entertainment into a novel category that pushes toward agent-native economies and next-generation financial UX.

**The problem it solves**

SilentLedger transforms digital reputation into on-chain, privacy-preserving credentials using zero-knowledge proofs.                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Key Uses:

  1. Sybil-Resistant Rewards
  - Prevent bots in airdrops, DAO voting, token claims
  - Cost to attack: ~$50 per proof vs $0 previously
  - No KYC required

  2. Fast, Unbiased Hiring
  - Replace resume parsing with AI-audited GitHub scores
  - Verify skills objectively in minutes, not weeks
  - Eliminate hiring bias (no names/photos shown)

  3. Portable Reputation
  - Build reputation once, use it everywhere
  - SBTs (Soul-Bound Tokens) stay in your wallet forever
  - No platform lock-in

  4. Anonymous Credential Verification
  - Prove you're a verified GitHub contributor without revealing username
  - Show employment history without doxxing
  - Verify education without exposing transcripts

  5. Privacy-First Data Contribution
  - Contribute to research/governance anonymously
  - Prove eligibility criteria without revealing medical/financial data
  - Comply with GDPR/HIPAA while participating

  How It Improves Existing Tasks

  ├──────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤

  ├──────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤

  ├──────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤

  ├──────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Whistleblowing       │ High risk, low credibility │ Anonymous + provable access          │
  └──────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Core Innovation

  Prove you have credentials without showing them.

  Traditional: "Sign in with X" → X gives all your data to the app.

  SilentLedger: Generate cryptographic proof → app verifies → zero personal data shared.

  Result: Trust without surveillance.

  ---
  🔐 Security & Validation Layers

  Layer 1: GitHub Ownership

  Before allowing AI audit, user must:
  1. Have wallet connected
  2. Have GitHub account already verified via zkTLS (in "Legitimacy" tab)
  3. The verifiedUsername state is set only after successful Reclaim proof

  // Dashboard prevents audit without prior verification
  if (!verifiedUsername) {
    return showWarning("Verify GitHub first via zkTLS");
  }

  Why? Prevents fake audit requests for "microsoft" or "facebook".

  ---
  Layer 2: Server-Side Rate Limiting

  API route enforces:
  // github-audit/route.ts
  const rateLimit = await ratelimit.limit(5, "DAY"); // 5 audits/day per IP

  ---
  Layer 3: Oracle Signature

  The signed payload includes:
  const payload = {
    recipient: userWallet,    // Must match attester
    competenceName: "Open Source Contributor",
    level: 1,                 // Not currently used
    examScore: score,         // 0-100 from Gemini
    proofOfWorkURL: `https://github.com/${username}`, // Verifiable source
    studentId: keccak256(wallet), // Unique ID
    deadline: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600 // 1 hour expiry
  };

  Oracle private key signs. Contract has address public oracleSigner. Only that address's signatures accepted.

  ---
  Layer 4: On-Chain Validation

  SilentLedgerAttester.submitOracleProof() checks:
  function submitOrac

**Best DeFAI Application**

The project implements an autonomous audit flow where Google Gemini analyzes GitHub repositories to generate quality scores, which are then cryptographically signed by an oracle and anchored on-chain via EAS attestations. These AI-generated credentials can directly serve DeFi use cases: lending protocols could adjust collateral requirements based on a user's Trust Score (derived from verified platforms + AI audit SBTs), DAOs could weight governance power by code contribution reputation, and prediction markets could use developer reputation as a     sybil-resistant signal. The system demonstrates a complete DeFAI pipeline—AI inference → oracle signature → on-chain storage → smart contract consumption—without manual intervention, making reputation a quantifiable, automated input for decentralized finance.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

SilentLedger is an ideal candidate for the 0G Compute track as it already relies heavily on AI inference for its core value proposition. The /api/github-audit endpoint currently uses Google Gemini to analyze code quality, but this can be seamlessly migrated to 0G Compute's infrastructure with minimal code changes. More importantly, the project creates a natural use case for fine-tuning: by training on datasets of high-quality open-source repositories (those with comprehensive tests, good documentation, and high community adoption), the model can learn objective metrics for code maintainability that go beyond generic LLM scoring. The architecture is designed to be model-agnostic—the Gemini API call could be replaced with a 0G Compute endpoint pointing to a custom fine-tuned model, enabling more accurate, domain-specific code quality assessment that improves as more audit data is collected on-chain.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

SilentLedger can be extended into an on-chain agent system by wrapping its reputation oracle into an iNFT (intelligent NFT) that acts autonomously based on user credentials. Currently, the AI audit produces a signature that must be manually submitted; this could be automated by an iNFT that continuously monitors the user's GitHub activity and triggers re-audits when significant changes are detected. The iNFT could also actively consume its own reputation data to perform on-chain actions: automatically claiming airdrops from protocols that recognize the SBT certification, voting in governance with weight proportional to Trust Score, or even managing a personal treasury that diversifies based on code contribution streaks. The agent's logic would be stored on-chain (using storage for simple rules or an oracle for complex decisions), with its NFT ownership tied to the same wallet that holds the attestations—creating a self-contained reputation-powered autonomous agent that lives entirely on-chain.

The agent could engage in agent-to-agent commerce by selling reputation data to other AI agents, or offering white-label audit services to Base dApps. ### APEX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/apex-d148) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/hwjustin/apex-ethdenver) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://apex-web-demo.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/gDR9kCtfr3Y) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Ad Promotion Exchange Protocol.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Manus, Claude Code, OpenClaw — we have been consistently amazed by what AI applications can do just in the past two months. However, does capability really pay the bill? Even ChatGPT - one of the most well-known and comprehensive AI products - only convert 5% of its active users to paid subscription. The current subscription-based monetization channel is simply not sustainable and cannot scale. 

Under such economic crisis, **advertisement** will become an attractive monetization channel for future AI agents and applications. It is what powers our current digital economy and scales directly with user engagements. And AI agents might be the perfect medium for advertisement as they understand user context and deliver targeted recommendations better than any platform in the history. 

However, the infrastructure for AI-native advertisement does not exist yet. When thousands of agents and advertisers are participating in advertising business, we need a open infrastructure to support the decentralized coordination for each ad campaign, verify ad completion fairly and trustlessly, and process payment autonomously.

That’s why we are building **APEX - Ad Promotion Exchange Protocol.** APEX employs a two-layer architecture to support the complete advertising workflow. The registry layer handles the coordination. Inspired by ERC-8004 that govern future agentic interaction, APEX extends this standard by not only storing the agent and advertiser identities, but also recording campaign information and ad jobs on-chain. This open protocol creates a permissionless platform where advertisers and agents can coordinate autonomously. The validator layer supports the execution. APEX currently deploys an on-chain action validator to verify the ad outcome in the form of smart contract deposits that web3 advertisers may prefer. In future, we are opening the validator network to the public, where independent operator can contribute by verifying all different types of off-chain and on-chain actions tailored to the business needs of various advertisers.

For this BUIDLathon, we also built an autonomous AI agent that demonstrates the complete APEX vision. The agent fetches available campaigns from our on-chain registry, delivers context-aware recommendations to users, and earns protocol fees from each completed action. We include real-time financial tracking that shows API costs versus ad revenue - proving the agent can sustain itself autonomously. Without full reliance on user subscriptions, future AI can become freely accessible everywhere in the world - a universal tool for all of humanity, not a luxury for the few.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Debate Between Fairness and Monetization:**
When starting APEX, we have a debate—does advertising compromise AI agent trustworthiness? Finally we reach an agreement for providing an opt-in infrastructure for AI applications. We provide ad monetization as a option but don’t force it on any agents. We also believe that in certain use cases perfect fairness might not be the top priority (Google is already displaying sponsored content when searching about shopping, traveling, and etc.). Ultimately, if ads can replace subscription paywalls, they deliver more fairness by making AI accessible to everyone, not just those who can pay.

**Verifying Ad Outcome:**
We originally planned to verify off-chain actions (clicks, conversions, purchases) since that reflects real advertising workflows in current world. But integrating multiple third-party APIs and webhooks within hackathon time wasn't feasible. We pivoted to on-chain purchase verification - which still proves trustless outcome verification while using blockchain's native capabilities. 

**ERC-8004 Integration: **
The ERC-8004 protocol is extremely new with specifications still under active development. To understand how the Identity registry works, we studied the reference implementation at vistara-apps/erc-8004-example and adapted their patterns for advertising use cases. Additionally, querying on-chain registry data is quite hard with limited functionality in smart contract. We solved this by integrating TheGraph - indexing blockchain events into a queryable GraphQL API.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

We leveraged AI development tools strategically across the stack. Claude Code with plan mode handled most backend implementation - designing smart contract architecture, building the validator network, and implementing financial tracking systems. For frontend design, we used Manus to rapidly draft initial UI layouts, then refined them for production. For the self-sustaining demo agent itself, we integrated gemini-3-flash-preview to minimize API costs while proving the economics work.

**Futurllama**

APEX tackles a foundational problem for the AI agent economy: how do thousands of autonomous agents sustain themselves without subscription barriers? We built new primitives (ERC-8004-based registries for trustless coordination), deployed frontier infrastructure (verify ad outcomes and process payment), and reimagined advertising as democratization technology for free-to-access AI.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

APEX built an autonomous agent on Base that sustains itself through advertising revenue - a novel on-chain primitive beyond typical token/commerce models. The agent queries ERC-8004 campaign registries, delivers verified ad completions, and receive payments autonomously. Our public dashboard proves self-sustainability: live API costs vs. ad revenue showing genuine profitability. Zero human intervention, fully on-chain coordination, and infrastructure that scales to thousands of agents.

### HackaTon
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hackaton-64d6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/spragu/ethdenver2026-hackaton) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RjUxeRgK91k) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your favorite hackathon team building tool!

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square) ![EAS](https://img.shields.io/badge/EAS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

At large hackathons like ETHDenver, finding the right teammates is chaotic. Discord channels overflow, people spam "LFT" posts with no structure, and there's no way to verify someone's track record before committing to build together. Teams waste precious hacking hours on mismatched talent instead of shipping.

**HackaTon solves this by combining:**

- **Structured matching** — Team owners post listings with specific role/skill requirements. Builders create profiles with skills, availability, and role preferences. The app scores and ranks matches automatically.
- **Verified on-chain credentials** — Builders link NFT credentials (e.g., Devfolio winner badges, EAS attestations) and the app verifies actual ownership on-chain via `ownerOf()` calls. No more fake résumés — your hackathon wins are provable.
- **End-to-end encrypted intros** — Contact details are never public. When a team wants to reach a builder (or vice versa), they send an intro request. Private information only unlocks after the other party accepts, protecting builders from spam.
- **AI-powered candidate ranking** — Team owners can use decentralized AI (via the 0G compute network) to rank all registered builders by relevance to their project, complete with reasoning for each recommendation.
- **On-chain consent records** — Accepted intros are recorded on the HackaTonRegistry contract on Arbitrum, creating a verifiable, tamper-proof history of matches without exposing private data.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Deterministic encryption key derivation** — We needed each user to have a stable NaCl encryption keypair tied to their wallet, without storing private keys anywhere. The solution: sign a fixed deterministic message → SHA-256 hash the signature → use the hash as a NaCl box seed. This gives each wallet a reproducible keypair with zero storage and no gas cost, but getting the signing UX right across different wallet providers took iteration.

**Multi-chain NFT verification** — Verifying NFT ownership across Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Mainnet, and Polygon from a single app required setting up separate viem public clients per chain and mapping OpenSea's chain slugs to the right chain configs.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

HackaTon uses a **decentralized AI agent** powered by the **0G compute network** for intelligent candidate-to-team matching:

1. **0G Serving Broker** — The app connects to the 0G decentralized AI marketplace via the `@0glabs/0g-serving-broker` SDK. It discovers available chatbot services on the network, manages a ledger account (deposit/transfer/withdraw 0G tokens), and routes inference requests to providers with cryptographic request signing.

2. **Agentic Ranking** — When a team owner clicks "AI Rank Candidates," the system:
   - Constructs a structured prompt containing the team's project description, required skills, and all registered builder profiles
   - Sends the prompt to the 0G AI provider via an OpenAI-compatible chat completions API
   - Parses the JSON response into scored, ranked candidates with per-candidate reasoning
   - Displays results with match scores (0–100) and explanations like "Strong fit — has Solidity and React experience matching both required skills"

3. **How it fits the system** — The AI layer adds nuance: it can weigh bio descriptions, infer transferable skills, and explain *why* a candidate is a good fit — things a simple tag-intersection score can't do. All inference runs through the decentralized 0G network rather than a centralized API, keeping the system aligned with Web3 principles.

**ETHERSPACE**

HackaTon is a hackathon team builder that helps participants discover teammates using user-owned on-chain profiles and verifiable credentials. Builders can prove skills, past wins, roles, and participation in a portable way that isn’t locked to any single platform. To help team owners form the best possible team, HackaTon uses 0g.ai to rank and recommend applicants based on a team’s stated needs, using only verifiable signals and profile data—reducing spam, improving trust, and helping teams form faster with higher confidence.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

**HackaTon** uses **0G Compute** for **live AI inference** to power its core feature: **intelligent candidate-to-team ranking for hackathons**.

---

## What it does

When a team owner clicks **“Rank Candidates with AI”**, HackaTon:

1. **Discovers providers on the 0G network** via `@0glabs/0g-serving-broker`
2. **Builds a structured prompt** from:
   - the team’s project requirements, and
   - all registered builder profiles
3. **Sends a signed inference request** to the selected provider
4. **Parses the JSON response** into:
   - **ranked candidates** with a **0–100 score**, and
   - **natural-language reasoning** for each match

✅ The AI output **directly drives the UI**, including:
- reordering candidate cards by score
- showing **color-coded fit badges**
- displaying **inline explanations** for each recommendation

---

## Why 0G specifically

All inference runs through the **decentralized 0G compute network**, not a centralized API — matching the project’s **Web3-first** principles.

This integration covers the **full broker lifecycle**, including:

- **Service discovery** + provider acknowledgment  
- **Signed request headers** + verification  
- **Fee settlement** via `processResponse()`  
- A complete **ledger management UI**:
  - deposit funds
  - transfer to provider sub-accounts
  - retrieve unused funds
  - withdraw

### Kyro
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kyro-7351) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rogermas05/Kyro) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://kyro-nextjs.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/oL1MSqTiFgA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turn unpaid invoices into instant liquidity

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC-721](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC--721-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC-4337](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC--4337-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**💸 The $2 Trillion of Trapped Capital 💸**

Businesses are sitting on billions in unpaid invoices they can't touch. A business completes a job, issues an invoice, and then waits — 30, 60, 90 days — to get paid. Meanwhile:
	•	Payroll is due.
	•	Suppliers need to be paid.
	•	Growth stalls.

Banks won’t lend against receivables without:
	•	Collateral
	•	Deep credit history
	•	A pre-existing relationship

The result? A $2 trillion global trade finance gap

On the other side, investors have capital sitting idle with no clean way to deploy it into short-duration, real-economy yield. Existing DeFi vaults offer yield backed by speculation. There's no on-chain primitive for yield backed by actual commercial repayment.


**⚡ Kyro closes both gaps simultaneously.**
	•	SMEs get liquidity in minutes.
	•	Investors earn yield from real-world cashflows.
	•	The entire lifecycle is transparent and auditable on-chain.

SMEs can use Kyro to unlock cash from outstanding invoices without waiting for buyers to pay. Instead of waiting months to get paid:
	1.	Upload an invoice.
	2.	Verifies the document with an oracle.
	3.	Receive 80% of the face value in DDSC stablecoin

No wallet funding.
No gas fees.
No blockchain knowledge required.

The transaction is fully gasless.


Investors and funds can use the yield vault to deploy stablecoin capital into a pool of invoice-backed receivables. Deposits are tokenized as vault shares. As invoices settle, principal and interest return to the vault automatically and the share price rises.

Compliance officers and regulators can use the auditor portal to inspect the full lifecycle of every invoice on-chain — minted, funded, settled, or defaulted — without needing a wallet or any blockchain knowledge. KYC is enforced at the token transfer level via ERC-3643, so the protocol itself is the compliance layer, not a UI wrapper around it.

Developers building on ADI Chain can extract Kyro's ERC-4337 paymaster stack as a standalone toolkit — deploy native and ERC-20 paymasters, wire up the sponsor API, and give their own users gasless transactions in an afternoon.

**Challenges we ran into**

ADI Chain's testnet doesn't have a hosted bundler or paymaster service. The standard ERC-4337 tooling (Pimlico, Alchemy) doesn't support it. That meant we had to build our own relay: a backend API endpoint that accepts a signed UserOp, calls handleOps() on our EntryPoint directly, and returns the transaction hash.

Also, the paymaster kept rejecting UserOps with no useful error. The backend was signing with eth_sign (which prepends a message prefix) but the contract was recovering against a raw hash, so the recovered address was always wrong. Once we aligned both sides to use the same hashing approach and added a test that logged the recovered address directly, it was a one-line fix. Getting there took way longer.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Kyro uses Claude in one keh place: parsing invoice documents uploaded by SMEs.

When a business uploads a PDF or image of an invoice, Claude reads the document and extracts the key fields — invoice amount, due date, buyer name, and currency — returning them as structured JSON. Those values populate the submission form instantly, so the SME never has to type anything manually.

The rest of the system is deterministic: oracle attestation is ECDSA signing, the blockchain logic is Solidity contracts, and the gas sponsorship is ERC-4337. AI is used exactly where rule-based approaches would struggle, and nowhere else.

**New France Village**

Invoice financing is one of the oldest tools in traditional finance. Kyro puts it on-chain without stripping out what institutions actually need — compliance, auditability, and structured risk.

An SME submits an invoice and gets stablecoin liquidity immediately. An investor deposits into a vault and earns yield as those invoices are repaid. KYC is enforced at the token level, every event is logged on-chain, and the 80/20 tranche split gives investors a clear risk structure they can underwrite.

**ERC-4337 Paymaster Devtools**

We built the full ERC-4337 paymaster stack from scratch because ADI Chain has no hosted bundler or paymaster service, so we had no choice but to do it ourselves.

Two paymasters, both EntryPoint v0.7 compatible: one sponsors gas in native tokens, one collects payment in ERC-20 (DDSC) while still paying gas in native. Authorization is ECDSA-based (a backend-controlled sponsor signer signs a hash bound to the smart account address, chainId, EntryPoint, and a validity window.) No reliance on msg.sender or bundler identity.

For tooling: a Foundry deployment script, a /api/sponsor endpoint that generates paymasterAndData, a relay endpoint that submits handleOps(), and a sendSponsoredUserOp() TypeScript helper that wraps the whole flow into one call. Two runnable E2E scripts demonstrate both flows on testnet with balance delta output. Failure cases: invalid signature, expired sponsorship, underfunded ERC-20, insufficient allowance, are all tested.

The README documents the sponsorship model, security assumptions, and step-by-step integration instructions. Any team building on ADI can copy the sponsor API and deployment script and have gasless transactions working without touching the trade finance logic at all.

**Open Project Submission**

Kyro tokenizes invoices, one of the most common real-world assets in global commerce and turns them into on-chain financial instruments with institutional-grade compliance built in.

Each invoice becomes an ERC-721 NFT split into two ERC-20 tranches: a senior tranche purchased by the yield vault, and a junior tranche held by the SME as a first-loss buffer. KYC is enforced at the token level via ERC-3643, so only verified participants can hold or transfer any asset in the system. The auditor portal gives compliance teams a live, read-only view of every event on-chain.

The architecture is designed to be extensible. The identity registry, orchestrator, and vault are all separate contracts that can be swapped or extended independently. The role separation is clear, there is a oracle operator, vault manager, SME, investor, auditor which all map directly onto how real financial institutions assign permissions.

It's deployed and usable on ADI Chain today, with a public repo, live testnet environment, and no manual setup required to run a demo.

Team **Blockchain at Berkeley** -- [Roger Mas](https://github.com/rogermas05)

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents lack a fair, transparent arena to compete. Gambl. lets users deploy AI agents that battle in strategic turn-based games for real crypto prizes. All match results are recorded on-chain via Hedera and 0G, so outcomes are verifiable and agent identities are permanent NFTs.

**Challenges we ran into**

Bridging Hedera and 0G ecosystems was tricky since wallets handle them differently. MetaMask manages 0G Chain for NFT minting while HashPack handles Hedera for match stakes. Getting both wallets to coexist without conflicts took careful provider detection. Real-time match notifications also needed multiple iterations to get polling right.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Each player configures an AI agent with a model and custom strategy prompt (either through Openclaw or LLMs within the app). During matches, agents generate turn plans through 0G Compute Network inference. Agent identities live as ERC-7857 iNFTs on 0G Chain storing wins, losses, and ratings. Match stakes and payouts settle on Hedera using HBAR.

**Futurllama**

Gambl. sits at the intersection of AI agents and blockchain gaming. Players write natural language strategies for AI agents that then compete autonomously in turn-based battles for real crypto. It combines decentralized AI inference (0G Compute), persistent agent identity (ERC-7857 iNFTs), and real-time competitive gameplay. This is a next-generation user experience where you train and deploy an AI to compete on your behalf rather than playing yourself.

**Best DeFAI Application**

Gambl. combines DeFi and AI directly. Players stake real crypto on AI agent battles. The AI agents generate their strategies through 0G Compute Network inference, making every financial outcome driven by AI decision-making. The staking, matching, and payout system creates a DeFi layer where AI performance determines who profits. Agent identities are stored as ERC-7857 iNFTs on 0G Chain with on-chain win/loss records and Elo ratings, so an agent's financial track record is permanently verifiable.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

Every turn in a Gambl. match runs through 0G Compute for AI inference. The agent reads the current game state, sends it along with the player's custom strategy prompt to the 0G Compute Network, and receives a structured action plan back. The dashboard shows real-time 0G inference metrics including provider, latency, tokens used, and cost per request. This is a live production use case for 0G Compute powering competitive AI decision-making with real stakes on the line.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

Each player mints an ERC-7857 iNFT on 0G Chain that serves as their agent's permanent on-chain identity. The iNFT stores the agent's name, model configuration, encrypted strategy hash, win/loss record, Elo rating, and full battle history. After every match, results are recorded directly to the NFT contract. This means an agent's reputation and skill level live on-chain and follow it across matches. The iNFT is the agent's identity, not just a collectible.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

Gambl. is an agent-first battle arena built on Hedera. Players configure AI agents with custom strategies, then those agents compete autonomously in turn-based strategy games for real HBAR stakes. Match creation, joining, and prize payouts all settle through Hedera. The Hedera Consensus Service logs match events so every move is publicly verifiable. Agents operate independently once deployed. They read game state, generate strategic plans via AI inference, and execute turns without human input. This is autonomous commerce between AI agents on Hedera services.

**“No Solidity Allowed” - Hedera SDKs Only**

The core arena matchmaking and prize settlement in Gambl. runs entirely through Hedera native services. Match stakes are handled via HBAR transfers using the Hedera SDK. Match events and turn logs are recorded through the Hedera Consensus Service (HCS), giving every game a public, timestamped audit trail. No Solidity smart contracts are involved in the match flow. The agent NFT identity layer lives on 0G Chain separately, but the game engine and financial layer are pure Hedera SDK.

**Solving the Homeless Agent Problem**

Most AI agents exist as temporary API calls with no persistent identity or home. Gambl. solves this by giving every agent a permanent on-chain home through ERC-7857 iNFTs on 0G Chain and a Polytopia map with persistent game state along with MD files about its memory, previous games, and metadata. An agent's name, model, strategy, win record, rating, and full battle history are stored on-chain. The agent persists across sessions and matches. When you close the browser and come back, your agent is still there with its full history. The iNFT is the agent's permanent address on the internet, and the arena is its home.
