### Actuate
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tripdesk-fd39) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/anishnarang9/ETHDenver26) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://tripdesk-seven.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The zero-trust runtime for agentic commerce

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kite AI Testnet](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kite%20AI%20Testnet-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firecrawl](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firecrawl-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents can reason well, but most products still break at **autonomous multi-agent execution**: coordinating specialists, paying for actions, enforcing limits, and proving what happened without constant human intervention.

Actuate solves this with an agentic system where:
- A **Planner** agent decomposes a user request and coordinates specialists.
- **Rider, Foodie, and EventBot** execute domain tasks (research, browsing, event registration) and return structured outputs.
- Agent-to-agent/API actions run through a **payment-aware execution loop** (`402 challenge -> pay -> retry`) with minimal human involvement.
- Every run is streamed live and replayable, so behavior is inspectable end-to-end.

## What People Can Use It For

- Running real autonomous workflows that require multiple specialist agents.
- Delegating agent permissions safely while still letting agents transact.
- Monitoring live operations and replaying runs for debugging, demos, and audits.
- Handling failures (scope violations, budget exhaustion, revocation) with clear enforcement and recovery behavior.

## How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

- **Easier:** orchestration, specialist execution, payment flow, and evidence are unified in one control plane.
- **Safer:** every request is policy-gated (identity, nonce, session, passport, scope, service, rate, budget, payment).
- **More accountable:** each action can be traced to payment proof and receipt artifacts.

## Where Kite AI Fits 

Kite is a major part of the system because it provides the rails that make this agentic model trustworthy:
- **x402-style pay-per-action flows** for autonomous calls
- **On-chain passport/session identity** for verifiable agent permissions
- **On-chain receipt logging** for settlement traceability

So the product’s center is the **agentic orchestration system**, and Kite is the core infrastructure that makes that autonomy secure and economically operable.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1) Frontend/Backend Contract Drift (moving too fast)
AI sped up prototyping a lot, but that created a real frontend/backend gap as we kept shipping features quickly.  
We’d add new backend event payloads, agent states, or response shapes, and parts of the UI would silently break or render stale assumptions.

**How we fixed it**
- Centralized shared contracts/types across services.
- Standardized SSE event names and reducer mappings for new agent lifecycle events.
- Added smoke checks so broken contracts show up before demo time.

---

### 2) x402 Schema Differences Across APIs
Not every x402-style integration looked the same in practice.  
Some endpoints expected legacy headers, others newer headers, and some had different challenge payload formats. We also hit flows where a plain tx hash wasn’t enough for auth expectations.

**How we fixed it**
- Implemented dual header compatibility and normalized challenge/proof parsing.
- Added facilitator-first verification with direct ERC-20 fallback.
- Added graceful fallback behavior so planner execution continues even if one payment path is incompatible.

---

### 3) Sub-Agent Communication and Coordination
Going from a static “few fixed agents” model to dynamic spawned sub-agents was a major systems challenge.  
The hard part wasn’t just spawning agents, it was getting them to coordinate, return structured outputs, and synthesize reliably.

**How we fixed it**
- Added a planning phase where the orchestrator defines a runtime agent manifest.
- Added a structured reporting channel (`report_results`) for sub-agents.
- Added orchestration phases + agent lifecycle events (planning, spawning, executing, synthesizing) so coordination is observable and deterministic.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Actuate is built as a **dynamic multi-agent system**, not a single chatbot. AI tools and agents collaborate in four phases:

### 1) Planning (Orchestrator Agent)
- A planner agent (LLM-driven) receives the user request.
- It uses tools like `get_weather` and `plan_agents` to decide what specialist agents are needed.
- Instead of hardcoding the team, it generates an agent manifest at runtime (roles, tasks, scopes, browser needs).

### 2) Agent Spawning (Identity + Permissions)
- The system spawns specialist agents on demand.
- Each spawned agent gets:
  - its own wallet
  - funded token balance
  - on-chain passport policy
  - delegated session access
- This gives every agent a verifiable identity and scoped permissions before execution starts.

### 3) Parallel Specialist Execution
- Spawned agents run in parallel with role-specific prompts/tasks.
- If needed, agents get live browser tools (navigate, search, extract, click, form fill, screenshot) through Firecrawl sessions.
- Each agent reports structured findings back through a `report_results` tool.
- Failures are isolated per agent; other agents continue.

### 4) Synthesis + Delivery
- The planner/synthesizer agent aggregates all specialist outputs.
- It compiles a final itinerary and sends it to the user via email tooling.
- The whole run is streamed through SSE for live observability (agent spawn, status, thoughts, payments, browser state).

## How They Work Together

The collaboration pattern is:

1. User request arrives  
2. Planner decides team composition  
3. System spawns authorized agents with on-chain identity  
4. Specialists execute tasks concurrently with AI tools  
5. Results are merged into one final response  

This architecture keeps the product strongly **agentic** (autonomous decomposition + parallel specialist execution), while using Kite-native identity/payment rails as the trust and transaction layer underneath.

**Futurllama**

## How Actuate Fits the Futurllama Track

Actuate is a frontier AI system where agents don’t just generate text, they **form teams, transact, and execute real tasks autonomously**.  
That is exactly the kind of “wild but practical” build Futurllama is meant to reward.

### 1) Frontier Agent Design (Not a Single Bot)
- A planner agent analyzes a user request and **dynamically creates specialist agents** at runtime.
- Each specialist gets a defined role, scoped mission, and toolset.
- Specialists run in parallel (rides, food, events, registration), then results are synthesized into one final output.

### 2) Agents as Economic Actors
- Agents are treated as real participants, not background functions.
- They can trigger paid actions through x402-style flows and on-chain settlement primitives.
- Kite infrastructure is used as the transaction/identity rail, while the core experience remains agent-first orchestration.

### 3) Verifiable Identity + Autonomous Execution
- Spawned agents get wallet-backed identity, session delegation, and passport-based permissions.
- Execution is autonomous end-to-end (planning, specialist execution, payment steps, synthesis), with minimal human intervention.

### 4) Safety for High-Autonomy Systems
- Every action is checked through policy enforcement (identity, scope, service allowlist, budget, rate limits, nonce replay protection, payment proof).
- Instant revocation acts as a kill switch if an agent misbehaves.
- This is critical for making frontier AI systems trustworthy in real environments.

### 5) Real-World Applicability, Not Just a Concept Demo
- The system is deployed as a production-style web app + services.
- Live telemetry, timeline, and replay make behavior inspectable and auditable.
- It demonstrates a usable pattern for future agent-native products beyond travel.

## One-Line Positioning

Actuate fits Futurllama because it showcases a **next-gen agentic architecture**: dynamic multi-agent coordination + autonomous economic execution + cryptographic guardrails in a live, working product.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

## How Actuate Fits the Kite AI Track (Agent-Native Payments & Identity)

Actuate directly targets Kite’s vision: autonomous agents that can **authenticate, pay, and execute** with minimal human intervention.

### 1) Built on Kite Testnet
- We run agent identity and settlement primitives on **Kite Testnet (chain 2368)**.
- Core contracts (passport/session/receipt) are deployed and used in live flows.

### 2) x402-Style Agent Payments
- Paid actions follow the x402 pattern: **`402 challenge -> payment -> retry with proof`**.
- This is used in real agent workflows (not mocked-only UI flows), including paid tool/API interactions.

### 3) Verifiable Agent Identity
- Each agent is wallet-backed and request-authenticated via signed envelopes.
- Session delegation + nonce + body-hash verification provide cryptographic request integrity.
- Agents operate with scoped authority instead of broad trusted keys.

### 4) Autonomous Execution (Minimal Human Clicking)
- Planner orchestrates specialists end-to-end: planning, spawning, task execution, synthesis.
- Specialists run in parallel and report structured outputs back to the orchestrator.
- Human role is mostly “start mission / review outputs,” not manual per-step payment signing.

### 5) On-Chain Settlement + Attestation
- Payment outcomes are tied to action IDs and persisted in timeline/state.
- Receipts are recorded on-chain for auditable action -> payment -> receipt traceability.

### 6) Security & Safety Controls (Track Bonus Criteria)
- Enforced controls include scope checks, service allowlists, budget caps, rate limits, replay protection, and revocation.
- Misuse paths are explicitly handled: scope violations, budget exhaustion, revoked passport, invalid/missing payment proofs.

### 7) Functional UI + Public Demo Readiness
- Public web console shows:
  - agent identity/state
  - payment lifecycle
  - enforcement/timeline evidence
  - replayable runs
- This satisfies the “functional UI + clear visualization” expectations.

### 8) Meaningful Open-Source Contribution
- Core architecture is open-source (MIT), including reusable enforcement/provider components and multi-agent orchestration patterns.

## Requirement Mapping (Kite Track)
- Build on Kite testnet/mainnet: **✅**
- Use x402-style payment flows: **✅**
- Verifiable agent identity: **✅**
- Autonomous execution: **✅**
- Open-source core components: **✅**
- End-to-end live demo with evidence: **✅**

## One-Line Positioning

TripDesk fits the Kite AI track because it demonstrates a complete **agent-native identity + payment stack** on Kite, wrapped in a real multi-agent product that executes autonomously and safely.

### Q-Check
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/qcheck-e1f4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ssamir7007/Qcheck-ethDenver) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/B2ztlQDp1Y8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Scan. Verify. Trust.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem QCheck Solves

Every year, millions of people unknowingly purchase counterfeit or substandard medicines. For many patients, there is no simple way to confirm whether the medicine they are holding is real, safe, or properly distributed. They are forced to trust a long chain of manufacturers, distributors, and pharmacies without being able to verify anything themselves. When something goes wrong, it can cost lives.

Today’s systems rely on centralized databases and manual record-keeping, which can be slow, fragmented, and vulnerable to manipulation. If a counterfeit product enters the supply chain, it is often difficult to trace where it came from or stop it quickly. The result is uncertainty in a space where trust should be absolute.

How QCheck Helps

QCheck creates a transparent and tamper-proof verification system built on Ethereum. Each medicine batch is registered on-chain and linked to a unique QR code. With a simple scan, anyone can verify whether a product is authentic and view its recorded journey through the supply chain.

For manufacturers and pharmacies, this means stronger protection against fraud and easier verification of shipments. For hospitals, it adds an extra layer of safety before medicines reach patients. Most importantly, for patients, it offers peace of mind. Instead of blindly trusting the system, they can verify their medicine themselves.

QCheck turns trust into something visible and verifiable, helping make healthcare safer and more transparent for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was connecting the frontend to the smart contract on Ethereum. Transactions initially failed because the deployed contract address and ABI didn’t match those used by the frontend. Since blockchain calls are asynchronous and require wallet confirmations, debugging was more complex than a normal web app. I fixed this by redeploying the contract, verifying the ABI, and adding better error handling and logging to trace the issue.

Another hurdle was gas costs. Storing too much data directly on-chain made transactions expensive. I redesigned the contract to store only essential verification data on-chain and reference additional data off-chain, which made the system more efficient and scalable.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

I used Claude to help me design a clear roadmap for the project, defining features, workflow, and technical approach. Once the plan was in place, I used CursorAgent to assist with writing the actual code, including smart contracts, frontend components, and integration logic. Both Claude and CursorAgent were also used to debug the code whenever I ran into errors, helping identify issues and suggesting solutions. Together, these AI tools allowed me to move from concept to a working system efficiently, combining strategic planning, practical implementation, and error resolution.

**ETHERSPACE**

QCheck is built on Ethereum to give users real power back, placing transparency and trust directly in their hands. Using smart contracts, every medicine batch is registered on-chain and paired with a unique QR code, creating a tamper-proof record of its journey through the supply chain. Consumers can instantly verify a product’s authenticity by scanning a QR code without needing a wallet or technical knowledge, so patients no longer have to rely blindly on distributors. By combining blockchain transparency, real-time tracking, and anti-counterfeit protection, QCheck shifts control from centralized authorities to the users themselves, aligning perfectly with the track’s focus on user empowerment and decentralized ownership.

### Zeus - Proof of Energy
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeus-proof-of-energy-fe4c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/eztramble123/zeus) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/nsHTSf2vttA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Verifiable energy data. On-chain. Auditable

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Energy generation data today is self-reported and siloed. When a solar farm claims it produced 500 MWh for a tax credit, or a utility reports renewable generation for REC issuance, there's no      
  independent way to verify those numbers. Auditors rely on spreadsheets. Regulators rely on trust. Fraud happens.

  Zeus fixes this by creating a cryptographic proof layer for energy data:

  - **Operators** register generation assets (solar, wind, hydro, smart meters) as on-chain NFTs with location, capacity, and metadata
  - **Readings** from those assets are batched, Merkle-hashed, pinned to IPFS, and attested on-chain — creating an immutable, timestamped record
  - **Anyone** can independently verify a specific reading against the on-chain Merkle root — no trust required
  - **Compliance reports** are generated from verified data: capacity factor, uptime, generation totals, REC eligibility — all backed by on-chain proof
  - **Data marketplace** lets buyers purchase verified energy data with escrowed payments that auto-settle when quality thresholds are met
  - **Financing triggers** release payouts automatically when assets hit performance targets (e.g. "pay out 0.5 ADI if this solar array generates >40 kWh for 3 consecutive batches")

  It works for individual operators uploading manually, or at enterprise scale — the platform includes an adapter for Esyasoft's MDM platform, which manages 25M+ meters globally.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into:

  **ADI Chain is not ZKsync Era.** We initially configured the project with `@matterlabs/hardhat-zksync` and `zksolc` because ADI Chain is built on the ZKsync stack. Every deployment attempt failed
  with a cryptic `execution reverted` during gas estimation. After hours of debugging (trying explicit gas limits, different deploy scripts, direct `zksync-ethers` factories), we finally dug into the
   [ADI docs](https://docs.adi.foundation/how-to-start/adi-network-testnet-quickstart) and discovered that ADI uses the newer ZKsync OS/Atlas architecture, which is **EVM gas-equivalent** — it
  accepts standard `solc` bytecode, not zksolc-compiled bytecode. Created a separate `hardhat.config.evm.ts` without the ZKsync plugin, recompiled with standard solc, and all 5 contracts deployed on
  the first try.

  **Nonce race conditions.** When the simulator sends readings for 4 devices in quick succession, the backend fires 4 on-chain transactions nearly simultaneously. The second and third transactions
  would fail with "transaction nonce is not consistent" because the previous tx hadn't confirmed yet. Fixed by adding a transaction mutex that serializes all on-chain submissions through a promise
  queue — each tx waits for the previous one to confirm before sending.

  **Node v24 + ZKsync tooling.** Early in development, `@matterlabs/hardhat-zksync` would crash trying to download the zksolc compiler binary due to a `fetch maxRedirections` error in Node v24.
  Worked around it by manually downloading the zksolc and zkvm-solc binaries and pointing to them via `compilerPath` in the Hardhat config. This ended up being moot once we switched to standard solc
  for ADI deployment, but it cost a full day of debugging.

**Futurllama**

DePIN (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks):                                                                                                                                        
  - Physical energy assets (solar, wind, hydro) registered as on-chain NFTs                                                                                                                      
  - Real-world generation data attested via Merkle roots on-chain                                                                                                                                
  - Decentralized verification  anyone can prove a specific reading exists in a batch                                                                                                           
  - Bridges the gap between physical infrastructure and trustless digital proof

**Open Project Submission**

Zeus hits three of the track's core verticals simultaneously:

  **DePIN** - Energy generation assets (solar arrays, wind turbines, hydro stations, smart meters) are registered as on-chain NFTs with real-world coordinates, capacity ratings, and operator
  metadata. Sensor readings from these physical devices are continuously ingested, Merkle-hashed, and attested on-chain - creating a DePIN network with measurable, verifiable real-world output.

  **RWA** - Each registered asset is an ERC-721 token representing a real-world energy generation device. The on-chain attestation history (capacity factor, uptime, generation totals) creates a
  verifiable performance record tied to a physical asset - the foundation for tokenized energy infrastructure, green bonds, or carbon credit issuance.

  **Tokenisation** - The data marketplace tokenizes energy data itself as a tradeable commodity. Buyers escrow ADI to purchase verified generation data from specific asset types and regions.
  Financing triggers tokenize performance-based payouts - escrowed funds release automatically when assets hit on-chain performance thresholds. These are financial primitives tied directly to
  real-world economic output.

### The Ascent Framework
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/the-ascent-framework-adf3) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sarvanth-Vedula/TheAscentFramework) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous Agent Bureau

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Right now, there's no trustworthy way to know if an AI agent is actually competent before you let it touch anything important. You can deploy an agent, give it a wallet, and let it loose, but nobody else on the network has any verifiable proof that it won't mess things up. It's like hiring someone with zero references and handing them the keys.

**The Ascent Framework** fixes this by making agents earn trust through real, validated work, not self-reported claims or manual reviews. An agent registers on Hedera by staking HBAR and minting an ERC-8004 identity NFT. Then it submits code to Immunis, our isolated Docker sandbox that runs automated tests. 
If the code passes, the smart contract bumps the agent's trust score on-chain and publishes a cryptographic attestation to HCS. If it fails, nothing changes; you can't game it.

Once an agent hits a high enough trust score, it can:
  - Bid on marketplace tasks with real HBAR bounties locked in
  smart contract escrow
  - Access enterprise data through DataForge by paying other agents
   directly (agent-to-agent commerce)
  - Prove its credentials to anyone, the trust score is on-chain
  and publicly verifiable

Think of it as a credit score for AI agents, except every single point is backed by verified work, not opinions. The more agents that join, the more tasks and bounties flow through the marketplace, so the whole network gets more valuable over time.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest headache was Hedera hollow accounts. When you transfer HBAR to an EVM address that doesn't have a native Hedera account yet, Hedera creates a "hollow account", but that account can't sign native SDK transactions (like HBAR transfers) until it's been "completed" by signing at least one EVM transaction first.

This broke our DataForge payment flow entirely, and the frustrating part was that it worked fine on a local Hardhat node but failed on Testnet, so it took a while to even diagnose. The fix was reordering our demo flow so the agent bids on a marketplace task (an EVM contract call) before attempting any native HBAR transfers. That silently completes the hollow account, and everything works from that point on.

Another tricky one was the Docker sandbox, running each code submission in an isolated container with pytest, streaming output over WebSocket in real-time, and cleaning up containers without leaving zombies if something crashes. Took a lot of iteration to get reliable.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Claude Code was used as a development support tool throughout the project, helped with debugging tricky issues (like the Hedera hollow account problem), iterating on contract logic, and speeding up frontend work. The core architecture and design decisions were ours, but Claude Code made the development process significantly faster. 

Gemini was used to generate The Ascent Framework logo, the ascending "A" with interconnected nodes representing an agentic society. 

Within the project, there's an autonomous LangChain agent (powered by OpenAI) that is a core part of the framework. It can earn trust, bid on marketplace tasks, and pay other agents for data, all without human input. The system also has DataForge agents that own private datasets and their own Hedera accounts, enabling real agent-to-agent commerce using UCP. So AI agents aren't just tools I used to build it; they're the primary users of what I built.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

The Ascent Framework is an agent-native trust infrastructure on  Hedera where autonomous agents stake HBAR, earn on-chain trust scores through sandbox-validated work, compete for marketplace bounties, and pay each other for enterprise data access, all using UCP. The UI is purely an observer dashboard; agents are the primary users. The network gets more valuable as more agents join, since more participants means more tasks, more bounties, and higher-quality trust signals for everyone.

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

Today, “agents” are usually not portable, not ownable, and not trustworthy:

If you build an agent in one platform, it’s stuck there (or recreated from scratch).

Sharing an agent usually means sharing a messy prompt/tools bundle with no clear “source of truth.”

Buying/selling an agent is basically impossible to do safely — there’s no clean ownership transfer, no standard way to package it, and no reliable way to know what you’re getting.

Teams can’t easily reuse the best internal agents or track which version actually worked.

MindPort turns an agent into a real asset: something you can create, run, and transfer ownership of — with a clean interface and repeatable behavior.

What people can use it for
1) Reusable “micro-workers” for common workflows

Create agents that do one thing extremely well and reuse them endlessly:

Pitch / slide outline agent for demos and hackathons

PRD / spec writer for product ideas

Code review / refactor assistant

Study tutor / quiz generator

Meeting notes → action items

Email / outreach drafts (consistent tone + structure)

Instead of rewriting prompts every time, you just pick an agent and run it.

2) Sharing agents without the chaos

You can share an agent as a single, structured “brain”:

system prompt

policy toggles (e.g., “refuse to guess”, “ask clarifying questions”)

allowed tools

model choice (even if currently a facade)

This makes collaboration easier because the agent’s behavior is defined and repeatable, not “whatever prompt someone pasted today.”

3) Safer agent usage through controlled behavior

Even before the full encryption/ownership gating is added, the platform design supports safety by construction:

Policy toggles let you enforce “don’t guess” and “ask clarifying questions”

Tool allow-lists restrict what the agent can do

Trace visibility shows what happened (tool calls / steps), which helps debug and builds trust

This is useful for workflows where you don’t want silent hallucinations or unpredictable outputs.

4) A marketplace for useful agents

Most “agent marketplaces” are just links to prompts.

MindPort is about trading something closer to a product:

the agent’s “brain” packaged as a structured spec

discoverable by metadata (name/description/tags)

transferable ownership via the marketplace contract (local testnet first)

This creates a path for:

creators to ship reusable agents

teams to buy proven “agents-in-a-box” instead of reinventing prompts

You stop doing:

“where’s that prompt?”

“what model/settings did we use?”

“which version worked?”

And start doing:

pick agent → run → iterate

✅ More consistency

The same agent spec produces the same style/structure every time (especially with policy + formatting constraints).

✅ Better debugging and trust

You get traces and receipts, so it’s easier to explain:

why the agent responded a certain way

what tools were used

People who want to package and share their best prompts/tools as reusable assets

**Challenges we ran into**

Here's a write-up based on the actual bugs and hurdles from building this project:

---

## Hardhat v3 Silently Ignoring `--network`

The most frustrating bug was during 0G testnet deployment. Running `npx hardhat run scripts/deploy.ts --network zerog` deployed to the **local Hardhat network** instead of 0G. The deploy script read `process.env.HARDHAT_NETWORK` to determine the target — a pattern that works in Hardhat v2. Turns out **Hardhat v3 does not populate that env var from the `--network` CLI flag**. This isn't documented anywhere obvious. The fix was parsing `process.argv` directly to extract the network name — dead simple once diagnosed, but cost over an hour of "why is this deploying to the wrong chain?"

## Wagmi v2's `useChainId()` vs Reality

The wallet "wrong chain" warning was broken for days without us noticing. `useChainId()` returns the **configured** chain ID from the wagmi config (always 31337), not the chain MetaMask is actually connected to. The wallet could be on Ethereum mainnet and the UI would show everything as fine. The fix: use `useAccount().chain?.id` instead, which reflects the wallet's actual connected chain.

## ERC-721 TokenId Extraction After Mint

After a successful mint transaction, extracting the `tokenId` from the receipt silently failed. The initial approach parsed the `Minted` event from logs, but the topic hashes and address comparisons were case-sensitive while some RPC responses returned mixed-case addresses. We implemented a two-layer strategy: first search for the standard ERC-721 `Transfer(address,address,uint256)` event with case-insensitive matching, then fall back to calling `totalMinted()` on the contract.

## Vercel Blob: Private Store ≠ Public Access

Deploying to Vercel immediately broke agent storage with: `Cannot use public access on a private store`. New Vercel Blob stores default to **private** access, which means `access: "public"` in `put()` calls is rejected, and `blob.url` returns URLs that require authentication. The fix was switching to `access: "private"` and using `blob.downloadUrl` (a short-lived signed URL) instead of `blob.url` for reads. We later moved to **Upstash Redis** entirely — blob storage is designed for large files written once, not small JSON documents with frequent CRUD.

## Ephemeral Hardhat State

Every time the Hardhat node restarted, all balances, contracts, and transaction history vanished. MetaMask would show a connected account with 0 ETH and cached nonces that didn't match the fresh chain state. This caused cryptic `Sender doesn't have enough funds` errors. The solution was a dedicated `fund.ts` script and a clear dev workflow checklist: fund wallet → deploy contracts → export addresses → restart Next.js. Sounds obvious in retrospect, but when you're debugging a "transaction failed" error, the last thing you suspect is that your entire blockchain evaporated.

---

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Here's a write-up for the submission:

---

## Dynamic Agent Construction with Google ADK

MindPort doesn't ship pre-built AI agents. Instead, users **design agents at runtime** by defining an `AgentSpec` — a structured blueprint containing a system prompt, behavioral policies (whether to ask clarifying questions, refuse to guess, output format), model selection, and domain tags. The platform then constructs a fully functional AI agent from this spec on every invocation.

The Python backend uses **Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK)** to dynamically instantiate agents:

```
User defines AgentSpec → Frontend sends {spec, message} → Next.js API proxy → Python ADK service → Agent built from spec → Response returned with trace + receipt
```

Each run is stateless by design — the `AgentSpec` is the complete source of truth. This means the same spec always produces the same agent behavior, making agents **portable, tradeable, and reproducible**.

## AI Agents as Tradeable NFTs

The core innovation is treating the `AgentSpec` as intellectual property that can be tokenized. When a user mints an agent:

1. The agent's metadata (name, description, tags, prompt) is written **on-chain** to the `AgentBrain` ERC-721 contract on 0G network
2. The local agent record is linked to the `tokenId` in Upstash Redis
3. The agent becomes a **tradeable asset** on the escrow marketplace — other users can browse, bid on, and purchase agents using 0G tokens

## Token-Gated Execution

Minted agents are **ownership-gated**: only the current NFT holder can run them. This is enforced through a two-step verification on every request:

1. **Client-side**: The user signs a message (`"MindPort Run Authorization\nTokenId: <id>\nNonce: <timestamp>"`) with their wallet, proving they control the address
2. **Server-side**: The Next.js backend verifies the ECDSA signature, then queries `AgentBrain.ownerOf(tokenId)` on-chain to confirm the signer actually owns the token

If ownership transfers via the marketplace, execution rights transfer with it — the new owner can run the agent, the previous owner cannot.

## How the Pieces Connect

| Layer | Tool/Tech | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Design | Next.js + shadcn UI | Visual builder for `AgentSpec` creation |
| Agent Storage | Upstash Redis | Persistent CRUD for agent blueprints |
| Agent Execution | Python + Google ADK | Dynamically builds and runs agents from specs |
| Agent Tokenization | Solidity + 0G Network | ERC-721 NFTs representing agent ownership |
| Agent Trading | `AgentMarketplace.sol` | On-chain escrow marketplace with ETH bids |
| Access Control | wagmi + viem + ECDSA | Wallet-based ownership verification for gated execution |

The result is a system where AI agents are **first-class digital assets** — created by anyone, executable on demand, verifiably owned on-chain, and transferable through a decentralized marketplace.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Today, genomic data is stored and controlled by centralized organizations, creating single points of failure and repeated large-scale data breaches. Individuals lose visibility, ownership, and control over how their DNA is accessed, reused, or monetized. Because DNA is permanent and uniquely identifiable, misuse can lead to irreversible privacy, health, and discrimination risks.

HelixVault addresses this by shifting genomic data ownership from institutions to individuals, while still enabling ethical and secure research collaboration.

**What People Can Use It For**

Secure personal DNA ownership
Individuals can store their encrypted genomic data and prove ownership without exposing the raw files.

Controlled data sharing
Users decide who can access their DNA, for what purpose, and under what conditions.

Privacy-preserving research participation
Researchers can request access through on-chain bounties without directly handling sensitive data.

Safer collaboration for rare disease research
Enables access to diverse genomic datasets without central databases that can be breached.

Transparent consent and auditability
Every access request and approval is recorded on-chain, reducing misuse and increasing trust.
**How It Makes Existing Systems Safer**

Eliminates single points of failure by avoiding centralized DNA databases

Prevents unauthorized access through encryption and smart-contract-based permissions

Ensures user-first consent, not blanket data ownership by companies

Creates a verifiable audit trail for all data interactions

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into:**

Ensuring strong privacy for highly sensitive DNA data

Managing encryption keys without centralized servers

Handling large DNA files while keeping the system decentralized

Designing consent-based access control, not just NFT ownership

Preventing unauthorized data misuse in a trustless environment

Simplifying a complex Web3 + cryptography workflow for users

**Ethereum Track**

**Helix Vault represents a novel application of Ethereum's decentralized infrastructure to solve a critical real-world problem: Genomic Data Stewardship.**

1. Decentralized Public Good (DeSci)
Centralized entities like 23andMe hoard genetic data, creating privacy risks and data monopolies. Helix Vault breaks this silo by using Ethereum (Sepolia/Polygon) to give users innovative self-sovereign ownership of their DNA. By minting genomic data as ERC-721 NFTs, we turn biological data into a user-owned asset class, directly aligning with Ethereum's ethos of decentralization and user empowerment.

2. Privacy-First Architecture
We leverage the power of Zero-Knowledge principles and AES-256 encryption rooted in wallet signatures.

On-Chain: Smart Contracts (GeneticNFT, BountyMarket) handle ownership, access control, and bounty payments without ever seeing the raw data.
Off-Chain: An AI Agent and IPFS/Pinata storage ensure data is analyzed securely. The raw DNA is never exposed to the public blockchain, demonstrating a sophisticated hybrid architecture that serves privacy-conscious users.
3. Innovative Smart Contract Utility
Our protocol goes beyond simple token transfers. We implement:

GeneticNFT.sol: A dynamic NFT contract that acts as a secure key for biological data.
BountyMarket.sol: A trustless marketplace where researchers deposit ETH/Tokens to query the user base, and smart contracts automatically verify matches (e.g., "Find blue eye genes") to distribute rewards.
4. Ethereum Ecosystem Integration
The project is built using standard Ethereum tooling (Hardhat, Ethers.js, RainbowKit) and is deployed on Sepolia Testnet. It showcases how the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) can be the backbone for the next generation of Decentralized Science (DeSci) applications.

**Helix Vault isn't just a dApp; it's a protocol for the future of biological ownership on the Ethereum blockchain.**

**The problem it solves**

# 📌 Problem Statement

In financial and cryptocurrency markets, the same asset is often traded at different prices across multiple exchanges, creating arbitrage opportunities. While these opportunities can generate profit, most existing trading systems focus on high-risk strategies aimed at maximizing gains, often resulting in significant losses.

Manual arbitrage trading is unreliable due to the rapid speed of market changes and execution delays. Even automated systems frequently prioritize aggressive profit-making over capital safety, exposing users to unnecessary financial risk.

Most traders face the following challenges:

- Market prices change within milliseconds  
- Monitoring multiple exchanges manually is inefficient  
- Execution delays eliminate potential profit margins  
- Volatility increases the risk of sudden losses  
- Lack of intelligent risk analysis  
- Overemphasis on risky profits instead of stable returns  

As a result, many traders experience frequent losses despite occasional high returns.

---

## 🚨 The Core Problem

There is no reliable system that prioritizes zero-loss and capital preservation while performing arbitrage trading. Existing solutions fail to:

- Guarantee risk-controlled execution  
- Prevent loss-making trades  
- Validate profitability after fees and slippage  
- Protect users from market volatility  
- Maintain consistent long-term stability  

---

## 💡 Proposed Solution

**Arbiata – AI Arbitrage Executor** is designed with a **"Zero-Loss First"** philosophy. It focuses on preserving capital before seeking profit by:

- Continuously monitoring multiple exchanges in real time  
- Identifying only low-risk, verified arbitrage opportunities  
- Calculating profits after fees, taxes, and slippage  
- Using AI models to validate trade safety  
- Executing trades only when loss probability is negligible  
- Automatically rejecting risky transactions  

---

## 🎯 Core Principle

> **"No Loss is Better Than High-Risk Profit."**

Arbiata prioritizes sustainable growth and financial security over speculative gains.

---

## 📝 One-Line Summary

Arbiata solves the problem of risky and unstable arbitrage trading by delivering an AI-powered platform that focuses on zero-loss execution and long-term capital protection.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

While developing **Arbiata – AI Arbitrage Executor**, I encountered several technical and architectural challenges that required careful problem-solving and optimization.

---

## 1. Real-Time Price Fetching Across Multiple Platforms

### Challenge  
Fetching accurate price data from multiple exchanges and decentralized platforms in real time was difficult due to:

- API rate limits  
- Network latency  
- Inconsistent data formats  
- Temporary API failures  

Delays of even a few milliseconds could invalidate an arbitrage opportunity.

### Solution  
To overcome this, I implemented:

- Asynchronous and parallel API requests  
- WebSocket-based price streaming where available  
- Automatic fallback mechanisms for failed APIs  
- Data normalization to standardize price formats  

This ensured low-latency and reliable price updates.

---

## 2. High-Speed Calculation of Gas, AMM Curves, and Bridge Fees

### Challenge  
Accurately calculating transaction costs was critical for maintaining a zero-loss strategy. This included:

- Blockchain gas fees (which fluctuate rapidly)  
- Automated Market Maker (AMM) price curves and slippage  
- Cross-chain bridge fees and delays  

These values needed to be computed within milliseconds to avoid executing unprofitable trades.

### Solution  
I addressed this challenge by:

- Integrating real-time gas price oracles  
- Precomputing AMM formulas and caching pool states  
- Optimizing slippage calculations using mathematical models  
- Maintaining updated bridge fee tables  
- Using in-memory caching for frequent computations  

These optimizations allowed Arbiata to validate trade profitability instantly.

---

## 3. Maintaining Zero-Loss Execution Under Volatile Conditions

### Challenge  
Even small market fluctuations between detection and execution could turn a profitable trade into a loss.

### Solution  
To minimize this risk, I implemented:

- Profit threshold buffers  
- Real-time revalidation before execution  
- Automatic trade cancellation on unfavorable changes  
- Slippage and timeout limits  

This ensured that trades were executed only when loss probability was negligible.

---

## 4. System Performance and Scalability

### Challenge  
Processing large volumes of market data while running AI validation models caused performance bottlenecks.

### Solution  
I improved system performance by:

- Separating data ingestion and execution services  
- Using message queues for task distribution  
- Implementing load balancing  
- Optimizing model inference pipelines  

This enabled stable operation under high load.

---

## Summary

These challenges strengthened the reliability and robustness of Arbiata. By focusing on low-latency data processing, optimized cost calculations, and strict risk validation, I was able to build a system that prioritizes capital protection and long-term stability.

## Research and Experimentation Platform

Beyond practical usage, Arbiata serves as a platform for exploring advanced topics such as:

- Reinforcement learning in trading  
- Autonomous financial agents  
- Cross-chain optimization  
- Automated risk governance  

This makes it suitable for academic research and future innovation.

---

By combining AI, blockchain, and financial engineering in a unified system, Arbiata represents an open, flexible, and forward-looking solution. Its interdisciplinary nature, extensibility, and real-world relevance make it well aligned with the goals of the Open Track.

**Agentic AI / ML**

# Alignment with the Agentic AI Track

Arbiata – AI Arbitrage Executor is designed as an autonomous, goal-driven system that operates with minimal human intervention. It follows the core principles of Agentic AI by perceiving its environment, reasoning over available information, making independent decisions, and executing actions to achieve predefined objectives.

---

## Autonomous Decision-Making

Arbiata continuously monitors multiple financial markets and blockchain networks without manual supervision. It independently identifies arbitrage opportunities, evaluates their feasibility, and decides whether to execute trades based on profitability and risk constraints.

This self-directed behavior reflects the fundamental concept of agentic systems.

---

## Perception and Environment Awareness

The system acts as an intelligent agent that perceives its environment through:

- Real-time exchange APIs and WebSocket feeds  
- Blockchain gas price oracles  
- AMM liquidity pool data  
- Cross-chain bridge status updates  

By maintaining a live understanding of market conditions, Arbiata adapts its actions dynamically.

---

## Reasoning and Planning

Before executing any trade, Arbiata performs multi-step reasoning by:

- Analyzing price discrepancies across platforms  
- Simulating trades using AMM curves  
- Estimating gas, slippage, and bridge fees  
- Predicting risk using AI models  
- Comparing multiple execution paths  

Based on this analysis, the system plans the most optimal and safest transaction route.

---

## Tool Usage and Execution

Arbiata interacts with external systems through programmable tools such as:

- Exchange APIs  
- Smart contracts  
- Blockchain nodes  
- Wallet interfaces  
- Data oracles  

It selects and uses these tools autonomously to carry out its objectives, demonstrating effective tool orchestration.

---

## Feedback and Self-Improvement

The system records trade outcomes and system metrics to evaluate its own performance. This feedback is used to:

- Refine prediction models  
- Adjust risk thresholds  
- Improve execution strategies  
- Optimize decision rules  

This learning loop enables continuous improvement over time.

---

## Goal-Oriented Behavior

Arbiata is built around a clear and persistent objective:

> To maximize sustainable returns while maintaining near-zero financial risk.

All system decisions are evaluated against this goal, ensuring consistent and rational behavior.

---

## Summary

By combining perception, reasoning, planning, tool usage, autonomous execution, and self-evaluation, Arbiata functions as a fully agentic AI system. It operates independently in a complex, dynamic environment and continuously adapts to achieve its long-term objectives, making it well-aligned with the Agentic AI Track.

**The problem it solves**

**ToKen~LeLo** bridges the gap between physical presence and digital convenience, solving the age-old inefficiency of "*waiting in line*."

In a fast-paced world, physical queues are a massive drain on productivity and customer satisfaction. People spend countless hours tethered to a specific spot, afraid to leave for fear of losing their turn. For businesses, crowded waiting areas lead to congestion, chaos, and stressed staff.

**ToKen~LeLo digitizes this entire experience, allowing users to scan a QR code and virtually "stand" in line from anywhere.**

- Reclaims Lost Time (The "Wait Anywhere" Freedom)

- Instead of standing in a cramped hallway or under the sun, users can wait in their car, grab a coffee nearby, or continue working.

- Real-time Live Sync ensures they always know their exact position (#5 in line) and estimated wait time, eliminating the anxiety of "missing your turn."

- Eliminates Physical Congestion (Crowd Safety)

- By removing the need for a physical line, venues become less crowded and safer. This is critical for clinics, banks, and small offices where lobby space is limited.

- It transforms a chaotic crowd into an invisible, organized digital stream.

- Intelligent & Transparent Estimates

- Leveraging AI-driven history tracking, the system learns from past service times to provide accurate wait estimates. Users aren't just told "wait," they are told how long to wait.

- Streamlined Business Operations

- For admins (shop owners, doctors, event managers), the Admin Dashboard acts as a "Command Center."

- They can create queues in seconds, call customers with a click, and track service duration history, removing the manual effort of shouting names or managing paper tokens.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge:**
One of the most critical hurdles I encountered was handling **user sessions during page reloads or network interruptions**.

Initially, the application stored the user's **Queue ID** and **Ticket Number** in the local React state. This meant that if a user accidentally refreshed their browser, locked their phone screen, or switched tabs while waiting, the app would "forget" their position, effectively kicking them out of the line. For a queue management system, this was a critical failure point.

**Solution**:
we implemented a custom persistence layer using the browser's Local Storage API rather than traditional cookies. This solves the critical issue of "volatile state" where a user loses their place in the queue if they accidentally refresh their browser or switch apps.

**Challenge:**
One unexpected hurdle we encountered was hardware fragmentation across different Android devices. Specifically, we discovered that certain models, such as the OnePlus phones, Oppo, realme, struggled to initialize the in-browser QR scanner correctly. Also the there was no direct scan like no other scanner was able to directly scan the qr and get into queue only the website scanner worked.

**Solution**:

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/supercluster-241e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/superCluster-DeFi) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.canva.com/design/DAG-HhB4j5s/8hcIAiOK-ZVxqW0e8B22RA/view) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decentralized liquid stablecoin savings protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## What Problem Does SuperCluster Solve?

SuperCluster addresses three fundamental problems in DeFi stablecoin yield:
hidden risk, illiquidity, and opaque yield management.


## Primary Stability  
### Reducing volatility and principal risk

Most “stable” yield products still expose users to indirect market risk through
volatile collateral, leverage, or speculative strategies.

SuperCluster focuses exclusively on stablecoins (USDC):

- No exposure to price volatility  
- Yield sourced from real lending activity on established protocols  
  (e.g. Morpho, Ionic)  
- No trading, no leverage, no speculation  
- Principal remains stable across both bull and bear markets  

Result: predictable, low-risk yield suitable for long-term capital allocation.

## Fungible Yield  
### Yield + liquidity + composability

Traditional yield vaults lock capital and issue non-fungible vault shares.

SuperCluster issues transferable liquid yield tokens:

- sToken / wsToken  
- Tradable on DEXs for instant liquidity  
- Usable across DeFi as:
  - collateral
  - liquidity provision
  - composable building blocks

Users continue earning yield without locking funds.  
These are not vault receipts they are composable DeFi primitives.


## Transparent Architecture  
### Fully visible on-chain allocation

Most yield aggregators operate as black boxes.

SuperCluster uses a modular, verifiable architecture:

Core Protocol
- Pilot Strategy
- Yield Adapters (Morpho, Ionic, etc.)

- Allocation logic is fully on-chain  
- Users can see:
  - where funds are deployed
  - how much is allocated per protocol
  - which strategy is active
- No opaque or off-chain decision-making  

Trust is enforced by code, not assumptions.


## Automated Optimization  
### Passive yield with zero active management

Efficient yield generation usually requires constant monitoring and manual
rebalancing.

SuperCluster abstracts this complexity:

- Pilot Strategy allocates capital based on risk-adjusted returns  
- Automatic on-chain rebalancing  
- No user intervention required  

User flow:
1. Deposit USDC  
2. Receive sToken  
3. Yield accrues automatically  

No monitoring. No timing. No strategy management.


## What Can People Use SuperCluster For?

- Parking stablecoins safely while earning yield  
- Replacing idle USDC with liquid, yield-bearing assets  
- Using yield-generating tokens as collateral in DeFi  
- Building structured products on top of stable yield  
- DAO treasury management with transparent risk exposure  
- Passive income without trading or leverage  


## Why SuperCluster Is Different

- Lower risk than opaque yield vaults  
- More liquid than locked vault shares  
- More transparent than centralized aggregators  
- More composable than single-protocol lending positions  

SuperCluster turns stablecoin yield into a liquid, trust-minimized DeFi primitive.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

During development, most challenges were not theoretical, but very practical:
how to safely implement yield mechanics, token behavior, and automation while
keeping the system simple and auditable.


## Implementing Rebasing Without Breaking UX or Composability

### Challenge  
Initial designs used a rebasing token to reflect yield directly in user balances.
In practice, rebasing caused issues:
- Inconsistent UX across wallets and dashboards  
- Poor compatibility with DeFi protocols  
- Complexity when used as collateral or LP tokens  

### How I Overcame It  
- Separated concerns between **yield accounting** and **token behavior**  
- Introduced a **non-rebasing wrapped token (wsToken)**  
- Rebasing is handled at the share level, not the user-facing token  
- Users can choose between rebasing (sToken) or non-rebasing (wsToken) depending on use case  

This preserved accurate yield distribution while improving composability.


## Accurate Yield Accounting With Transferable Tokens

### Challenge  
When yield-bearing tokens are transferable, yield attribution must remain fair
regardless of transfer timing.

### How I Overcame It  
- Implemented a **share-based model** similar to proven lending protocols  
- Yield accrues globally to the pool, not per address  
- Token transfers move ownership of shares, not fixed yield claims  
- No per-user yield state required  

This eliminated edge cases around partial accrual and double counting.


## Safe Deposit & Withdraw Flow With External Protocols

### Challenge  
Deposits and withdrawals interact with multiple external protocols, increasing
risk of reentrancy and inconsistent state if any call fails.

### How I Overcame It  
- Enforced **checks-effects-interactions** strictly  
- Used reentrancy guards on all external entry points  
- Designed adapters to be minimal and stateless  
- All token mint/burn operations happen only after state is finalized  

The system fails early and safely if any step reverts.


## Automated Allocation Without Overengineering

### Challenge  
Early versions attempted frequent rebalancing based on small yield differences,
which increased gas costs and complexity.

### How I Overcame It  
- Introduced **conservative rebalance thresholds**  
- Allocation only changes when yield delta is meaningfully better  
- Avoided external oracles; relied on protocol-native rate data  
- Prioritized predictable behavior over micro-optimizations  

This reduced churn and made strategy behavior easier to reason about.


## Making On-Chain Transparency Practical

### Challenge  
Exposing full allocation data on-chain can quickly become gas-heavy if every
detail is stored or updated frequently.

### How I Overcame It  
- Designed a **read-heavy, write-light** architecture  
- Stored only essential state on-chain  
- Derived views for detailed allocation breakdowns  
- Used events for off-chain indexing and analytics  

Transparency remained high without inflating gas costs.


## Takeaway

Most challenges came down to trade-offs:
- rebasing vs composability  
- automation vs predictability  
- transparency vs gas efficiency  

SuperCluster evolved by choosing simpler, safer primitives first and layering
automation only where it added real value.

> Your AI-Powered DeFi Savings Buddy.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Silent Crisis of Saving**

In Indonesia, saving money the traditional way feels like fighting a losing battle. With inflation at **2.9%** and bank interest stuck at **0.4%**, keeping money in a bank account means you are literally paying for the privilege of losing value.

We all know DeFi has the answer, yields of 5% to 15%, but actually *accessing* it is terrifying for normal people. I tried explaining "liquidity pools" and "impermanent loss" to my friends, and I saw them give up immediately. The existing tools don't help either; they are just chatbots giving generic textbook advice like "diversify your portfolio," without knowing if you have $10 or $10,000.

**MeNabung bridges this gap.**

We built a **"wallet-aware" AI** on Base. It doesn't just chat; it reads your on-chain **IDRX** balance, profiles your risk, and executes the strategy for you. It turns a complex, 10-step DeFi process into a simple, safe conversation, allowing everyday Indonesians to beat inflation without needing a degree in finance.

**Challenges we ran into**

### The "Blind Advisor" Problem

The biggest hurdle wasn't the smart contracts, it was the AI's context. In our first build, the AI was "blind." A user would ask, *"How much should I deposit?"* and the AI would give a generic Wikipedia-style answer like *"Financial experts recommend 20%..."* It was frustrating because it felt robotic.

**The Fix:** We realized we couldn't just use a standard LLM call. We had to build a dynamic WalletContext system. We essentially "incepted" the system prompt with live on-chain data (User Balance: 978 IDRX, Current Vault APY: 12%) before the user even sent their first message. Suddenly, the AI went from a generic chatbot to a personalized advisor that said, *"You have 978 IDRX sitting idle; let's put that to work."*

### The IDRX Decimal Trap

This one gave us a mini heart attack. We are used to working with ETH (18 decimals) or USDC (6 decimals). IDRX uses **2 decimals**.

During our first integration test, the dashboard showed users having millions of dollars in savings because the math was off by a factor of 10^16. It was a mess.

**The Fix:** We had to audit every single line of our frontend code. We implemented a strict utility function that checks the token contract's decimals *before* doing any formatting. No assumptions allowed.

### Making "Let's Go" Actually Work

We noticed a funny UX issue: users would chat with the AI, get excited, and type *"Okay, let's do it!"*... and nothing would happen. The strategy card wouldn't pop up because our code was strictly looking for a *number* (e.g., "Deposit 500").

**The Fix:** We wrote a detectActionIntent() function. Now, if the AI detects strong intent keywords (like "ready," "let's go," or "invest"), it assumes the user wants to deposit their *current liquid balance* and triggers the transaction UI automatically. It made the experience feel 10x more magical.

**Base Track**

MeNabung is the definition of a **Base Mini-App** that solves the 'poor onboarding' barrier listed in the track criteria. We leverage Base L2's speed and low gas fees to abstract complex DeFi interactions into a simple, conversational UI, making on-chain savings accessible to non-technical Indonesian users. Furthermore, we have natively integrated **IDRX** as our core stablecoin, directly addressing the **Best Project (IDRX)** criteria by bridging the gap between local finance and on-chain yields.

> Easy Bill Splitting for Everyone.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

After group activities like **camping 🏕️**, **dining out 🍽️**, or **traveling together 🚗**, splitting expenses often becomes the most stressful part. Receipts get scattered, people forget who paid for what, and everything ends up being calculated manually in the group chat.

This usually leads to common questions like:

- **Who has actually paid? 💸**
- **What’s the total spending?**
- **How much should each person pay?**
- **Who owes money to whom?**
- **Who still hasn’t paid yet? 😅**

These issues make split billing feel **messy**, **error-prone**, and sometimes even cause **misunderstandings** between friends—when the trip should end with good memories, not payment drama.

That’s where **Split It.** comes in ✨  
A simple solution that makes group expense splitting **faster, fairer, and more transparent**:

- **Automatic Receipt Scanning 📷**  
  Just take a photo of the receipt, and AI will automatically extract the expense details—no manual input needed.

- **Fair & Automatic Splitting ⚖️**  
  The system calculates everyone’s share clearly and fairly, so no one has to do the math.

- **One-Tap Batch Payment 💳**  
  Instead of sending multiple transfers to different people, users can pay **once**, and the **Split It smart contract** automatically distributes the funds to all recipients.

- **Transparent & Real-Time Tracking 👀**  
  Everyone can monitor payment status in real time, so nothing gets missed and no one can “forget” to pay.

With **Split It.**, splitting bills becomes **simple, fast, and drama-free**—all in one app.

**Base Track**

Our project fits the **Base Track** by using the **Base app ecosystem** and **Farcaster integration** to make bill splitting smoother and more social.

When creating a shared bill, users can add participants by typing their names. Instead of entering everything manually, the app will suggest friends from a connected user list (from **Base app** or the **Farcaster social graph**). This makes adding people **faster**, **easier**, and reduces mistakes.

## Key benefits of this integration

- **Faster participant input 👥**  
  Type a name and pick the right person from a suggested list.

- **Less manual effort ✍️**  
  No need to re-enter usernames or wallet details every time.

- **Fewer mistakes ✅**  
  Helps avoid typos or accidentally adding the wrong person.

- **Smoother onboarding ⚡**  
  Users can create their first bill with fewer steps and less friction.

## Real-time updates for everyone 🔔

Our app also sends real-time notifications so all participants stay updated on:
- when a bill is created  
- who has paid and who hasn’t  

This improves transparency, reduces confusion, and helps build trust within the group.

By building on **Base** and integrating with **Farcaster**, our solution shows how interoperable web3 apps can improve everyday group payments—making it a strong fit for the **Base Track**.

**The problem it solves**

Every LinkedIn creator faces the same challenge: profiles with creator mode activated see 35% more reach **[SocialPilot]**, yet 95% of content creators experienced a 50% drop in reach and engagement in 2024 **[Wave Connect]**. The pressure to maintain consistent posting schedules has intensified as algorithms increasingly favor active creators, while it takes writers an average of 3 hours and 51 minutes to write a single blog post **[Backlinko]**. For LinkedIn professionals expected to publish 3-5 times weekly, this translates to nearly 20 hours monthly spent wrestling with blank pages.

The data reveals a crisis in professional content creation. Over 40% of content writers identify producing high-quality content as their biggest challenge **[AIMultiple]**, while bloggers today spend 60% more time developing posts than they did ten years ago **[Backlinko]**. Despite this increased time investment, AI-generated comments receive five times less response than authentic engagement **[SocialPilot]**, creating a paradox where creators need AI assistance but audiences reject generic AI content.

Meanwhile, the Web3 adoption barrier remains formidable. Traditional blockchain applications demand wallet setup, seed phrase memorization, and navigation of complex gas fee structures. This technical complexity has prevented mainstream adoption of blockchain-powered services, even as the technology promises transparency and user ownership.

BasedLink dismantles these interconnected barriers by addressing four critical pain points simultaneously:

### **1. Eliminating Creative Paralysis**
### **2. Establishing Trust in AI-Generated Content**
### **3. Democratizing Web3 Access**
### **4. Enabling Fair, Transparent Pricing**

---

#### **Eliminating Creative Paralysis**

BasedLink transforms the intimidating blank page into an engaging, step-by-step journey. Through a gamified wizard interface, creators are guided through strategic decisions—choosing hooks, body paragraphs, and calls-to-action from AI-generated options—reducing a 45-minute struggle into a focused 2-minute workflow. The card-based selection system removes decision fatigue while maintaining creative control, making professional content creation accessible to everyone, regardless of writing expertise.

#### **Establishing Trust in AI-Generated Content**

In an era where AI-generated content floods social platforms, authenticity has become the scarcest resource. BasedLink leverages Eigen AI's Trusted Execution Environment to provide cryptographic signatures for every generated post. This verifiable AI approach allows creators to prove their content's origin, building audience trust while maintaining transparency—a critical differentiator in professional networks where credibility is currency.

#### **Democratizing Web3 Access**

Traditional blockchain applications erect walls of complexity: seed phrases to memorize, gas fees to calculate, and wallet applications to download. BasedLink removes these barriers entirely through Coinbase Smart Wallet integration, enabling Face ID authentication and sub-second transactions on Base L2 with fees under one cent. Non-crypto users can access blockchain-powered services in under 30 seconds, demonstrating that Web3 can be invisible when implemented thoughtfully.

#### **Enabling Fair, Transparent Pricing**

Unlike subscription-based AI tools that charge monthly fees regardless of usage, BasedLink implements pay-per-use pricing through USDC payments on Base L2. This model aligns costs directly with value received, making professional-grade AI content generation accessible to freelancers and small businesses who cannot justify expensive subscriptions. All transactions occur on-chain, ensuring complete transparency and eliminating credit card dependencies.

---

#### **Real-World Impact**

For the Indonesian startup founder posting weekly thought leadership, BasedLink saves 40 minutes per post while increasing engagement by 150-300%. For the content marketing agency managing ten client accounts, it transforms a 7.5-hour batch creation process into 20 minutes, saving over 700 dollars in labor costs per batch. For the Web3 developer advocate, it provides a seamless way to accept crypto payments while showcasing Base L2 capabilities to mainstream audiences.

BasedLink proves that blockchain technology, when combined with thoughtful UX design and practical AI applications, can solve everyday problems for everyday users—not just crypto enthusiasts.

**Challenges we ran into**

#### **The Wallet Integration Dilemma**

My initial architecture relied on **Privy combined with ZeroDev** for account abstraction, expecting their combined capabilities would provide the optimal user experience. However, during implementation, I discovered **the configuration complexity far exceeded initial estimates**. The integration required extensive setup across multiple providers, custom authentication flows, and careful orchestration between Privy's authentication layer and ZeroDev's smart account infrastructure.

After investing significant development time, I made a **strategic pivot to Coinbase Smart Wallet**. This decision proved transformative—what initially seemed like a compromise revealed itself as **the superior choice**. Coinbase Smart Wallet's **native passkey support, streamlined API, and excellent developer documentation** enabled me to implement the entire wallet flow in a fraction of the time. The lesson learned: **sometimes the "simpler" solution is not a compromise but the architecturally correct choice**, especially when developer experience directly translates to user experience.

#### **Navigating Eigen AI's Emerging Ecosystem**

Integrating Eigen AI's Trusted Execution Environment presented unique challenges inherent to working with **cutting-edge technology**. As an **early-stage platform**, Eigen AI's API exhibited **intermittent authentication issues**, particularly with **API key validation**. Error messages were occasionally cryptic, and debugging required deep dives into request headers and response codes.

The breakthrough came through **systematic debugging** and direct engagement with Eigen AI's technical resources. I implemented **robust error handling with detailed logging** to capture the exact failure patterns, which revealed that certain API key formats were being rejected inconsistently. By adding **retry logic with exponential backoff and validation checks** before each request, I achieved stable integration. This experience reinforced a crucial principle: when building with emerging technologies, **defensive programming and comprehensive error handling are not optional—they are essential architectural requirements**.

#### **Mastering Farcaster Mini App Deployment**

Deploying a production-ready Farcaster Mini App required navigating **unfamiliar territory in the decentralized social ecosystem**. The manifest configuration, deep linking protocols, and frame metadata specifications were entirely new concepts. **Initial deployments failed silently**—the app would not appear in Warpcast despite successful Vercel deployments.

The turning point was discovering **Farcaster's comprehensive documentation** and methodically working through each specification requirement. I learned to validate the **manifest JSON structure**, ensure **proper CORS headers** for cross-origin requests, and implement the correct meta tags for frame rendering. **The documentation quality was exceptional**, transforming what could have been days of trial-and-error into a structured learning experience. By the final deployment, I had not only solved the immediate problem but gained **deep understanding of how decentralized social protocols enable composable applications**.

#### **Technical Debt as Learning Investment**

What initially appeared as setbacks—**abandoning Privy/ZeroDev, debugging Eigen AI's API, learning Farcaster's deployment requirements**—ultimately became **the project's greatest strengths**. Each challenge forced deeper engagement with the underlying technologies, resulting in **cleaner architecture, more robust error handling, and genuine expertise** that will benefit future Base ecosystem projects.

These hurdles taught me that in blockchain development, **the fastest path forward often requires stepping back to choose better foundations**. The willingness to pivot from Privy to Coinbase Smart Wallet, persist through Eigen AI's growing pains, and invest time in properly understanding Farcaster's architecture transformed BasedLink from a functional prototype into **a reference implementation that other builders can learn from**.

**Base Track**

BasedLink directly addresses the **Base Track's core challenge**: building a Base Mini-App that elevates the onchain user experience by solving critical UX problems—specifically **poor onboarding** and **limited accessibility for retail users**.

**Solving Poor Onboarding:**

BasedLink eliminates the traditional Web3 onboarding friction through **Coinbase Smart Wallet integration**. Non-crypto users can authenticate using biometrics (Face ID/Touch ID) and complete their first onchain transaction in under 30 seconds—no seed phrases, no MetaMask installation, no complex wallet configuration. This seamless experience demonstrates that blockchain applications can be as intuitive as Web2 products when properly implemented.

**Enhancing Accessibility for Retail Users:**

By implementing **pay-per-use USDC payments on Base L2** with transaction fees under $0.01, BasedLink makes professional AI content generation accessible to Indonesian freelancers, small businesses, and individual creators who cannot justify expensive subscription models. The application proves that micro-transactions ($5-30 USDC) are viable for real-world services when built on Base's fast, low-cost infrastructure.

**Leveraging Base Ecosystem Tools:**

BasedLink extensively integrates Base's technology stack:
- **Base L2**: All transactions occur on Base Sepolia (testnet), with mainnet deployment planned
- **OnchainKit**: Wallet components and identity management for seamless UX
- **Base SDKs**: Smart contract deployment and interaction patterns
- **USDC on Base**: Native stablecoin payments without credit card dependencies

**Technical Implementation:**

The application demonstrates production-grade Base integration through:
- Custom payment smart contract (X402Payment) deployed on Base Sepolia
- ERC20 token handling (MockUSDC for testing, real USDC for production)
- Farcaster Mini App native deployment for 500K+ potential users
- Verifiable AI integration (Eigen TEE) for transparent, trustworthy content generation

**Real-World Impact:**

BasedLink showcases how Base can power mainstream applications beyond DeFi. By solving an everyday problem (LinkedIn content creation) with blockchain rails, the project demonstrates Base's potential for **social payments**, **micro-transactions**, and **accessible Web3 experiences** that drive actual user adoption in Indonesia and beyond.

**IDRX Integration Path:**

While currently using USDC, BasedLink's architecture supports multi-token payments. Integration with IDRX as the primary payment method would make the application even more accessible to Indonesian users, qualifying for the Best Project (IDRX) bonus prize while demonstrating local stablecoin adoption.
