**The problem it solves**

# GigPay

**A Network Payout & Treasury Coordination Layer**



# 1. Problem

Modern digital businesses operate in a world that legacy payout infrastructure was never designed to handle.



## A. Cross-border settlement is slow and expensive

Traditional bank rails (SWIFT, correspondent banking, ACH) introduce:

* **T+1 to T+5 settlement delays**
* **3-7% total cost** in cross-border corridors (FX spreads + intermediary fees)
* Weekday cutoffs and timezone friction
* Opaque FX spreads layered on top of transfer fees

According to the **World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide database**, global average cross-border remittance costs remain around **6%** ([World Bank, 2023](https://remittanceprices.worldbank.org/)). While B2B flows differ from remittances, correspondent banking layers and FX spreads create comparable multi-percentage costs.

The **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)** and SWIFT documentation show that cross-border payments still rely heavily on multi-hop correspondent networks, where funds can take **1-5 business days** depending on corridor complexity and compliance checks ([BIS CPMI – Cross-border payments](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d193.htm); [SWIFT GPI Overview](https://www.swift.com/our-solutions/swift-gpi)).

By contrast, blockchain settlement can clear within minutes, with transaction costs often measured in cents to low dollars depending on network conditions ([Ethereum Gas Tracker – Etherscan](https://etherscan.io/gastracker); [L2 Fee Analytics](https://l2fees.info/)).

For platforms operating at scale, even a 2-4% efficiency gain across millions in volume translates into substantial margin recovery.



## B. Working capital is trapped in payout operations

Finance teams today must:

* Pre-fund multiple accounts across tools
* Hold excess liquidity “just in case”
* Manually reconcile batches and balances

This creates:

* **Idle float that earns little to no return**
* Fragmented treasury visibility
* Operational overhead in reconciliation

The **BIS Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI)** highlights that cross-border frictions create “liquidity inefficiencies” and capital fragmentation across correspondent chains ([BIS Cross-border Payments – Stage 3 Roadmap](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d205.htm)).

Research from the **Federal Reserve Bank of New York** and BIS further discusses liquidity and capital inefficiencies in correspondent banking networks ([BIS Quarterly Review – Correspondent Banking](https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt1603e.htm)).

Meanwhile, US Treasury yields ranged between **4-5% in 2023–2024**, illustrating the opportunity cost of idle capital ([Federal Reserve Economic Data – 3M Treasury](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS3MO)).

Yet most businesses cannot safely deploy float into yield without breaking accounting boundaries or payout availability guarantees.



## C. Complex payout logic lives off-chain

Real-world payment workflows involve:

* Milestone-based releases
* Multi-sign approvals
* Refunds and disputes
* Revenue splits
* Cross-currency preferences

Today, these conditions exist in:

* Spreadsheets
* Slack threads
* Email approvals

Banks only see the final debit. There is no enforceable state machine representing the payout lifecycle.

The **BIS report on Distributed Ledger Technology in payment systems** notes that programmable settlement and atomic transactions can reduce reconciliation complexity and operational overhead ([BIS DLT in Payment Systems](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d157.htm)).

Traditional ERP reconciliation cycles require manual stitching of:

* Approval logs
* Invoices
* Bank statements
* FX confirmations

The absence of a unified intent ledger increases dispute frequency and audit complexity.



## D. Market scale

The total addressable market is substantial:

* Global payment flows exceed **$190 trillion annually** ([BIS Red Book Statistics](https://www.bis.org/statistics/payment_stats.htm)).
* Global B2B payments exceed **$150 trillion annually** (McKinsey Global Payments Report) ([McKinsey Global Payments Report](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/global-payments-report)).
* Stablecoin transfer volume exceeded **$10 trillion annually** in 2023–2024 ([Chainalysis Crypto Adoption Report](https://www.chainalysis.com/reports/crypto-adoption-report/)).
* Stablecoin circulating supply exceeds **$150B market capitalization** ([CoinGecko Stablecoin Data](https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/stablecoins)).

**Challenges we ran into**

## Postmortem (What happened -> Why -> Fix -> Prevention)

### 1) Vercel deployments crashed (Prisma not initialized / outdated client)
- **What happened**: The API intermittently failed on Vercel with “Database client not initialized” and Prisma errors about Vercel caching causing an outdated Prisma Client.
- **Why**: Serverless builds cached dependencies; Prisma Client generation didn’t reliably run. DB env var naming also differed across providers/prefixes.
- **Fix**: Ran `prisma generate` during build, expanded DB URL resolution across multiple env keys, and returned a clear 503 instead of crashing when Prisma couldn’t initialize.
- **Prevention**: Keep Prisma generation as part of the build pipeline; validate env presence at startup; fail fast with actionable errors.

### 2) Migrations blocked by a failed migration (P3009)
- **What happened**: `prisma migrate deploy` refused to apply new migrations due to a prior failed migration recorded in the database.
- **Why**: Prisma protects production DBs by stopping migration application when a migration is marked failed.
- **Fix**: Made the failing migration idempotent and added a “heal and retry” path using `prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back` followed by re-running deploy.
- **Prevention**: Make production migrations idempotent where possible; monitor migration status; avoid leaving partially applied migrations in shared DBs.

### 3) RPC outages broke indexing and made balances look like zero
- **What happened**: Treasury balances and history went blank; backend event sync threw 503/429 RPC errors.
- **Why**: Public Base Sepolia RPC endpoints were unstable/rate-limited.
- **Fix**: Added multi-RPC fallback on the frontend and defensive RPC handling on the backend (skip/return defaults instead of crashing).
- **Prevention**: Always use fallback RPCs, cache key reads, and treat RPC as a flaky dependency with graceful degradation.

### 4) BigInt JSON serialization errors broke API responses
- **What happened**: Endpoints returned `{"error":"Do not know how to serialize a BigInt"}`.
- **Why**: `JSON.stringify` cannot serialize `BigInt`, and some Prisma/RPC outputs include BigInts.
- **Fix**: Added a JSON-safe response helper that converts BigInts to strings consistently.
- **Prevention**: Normalize numeric types at the boundary (API responses); enforce serialization-safe schemas.

### 5) Payment “Confirm” flow was inconsistent (disabled, stuck, duplicate submits)
- **What happened**: Users couldn’t confirm escrow creation reliably; sometimes Confirm was disabled without clear reason, sometimes it triggered multiple times, and sometimes the UI crashed.
- **Why**:
  - Confirm was gated by strict conditions (wrong chain, swap route missing, token not eligible, yield strategy not allowed).
  - Receipt-handling effects could re-run and re-trigger follow-on actions without idempotency guards.
  - Some UI assumed state fields existed (swap) when older drafts didn’t include them.
- **Fix**:
  - Added network gating with a “Switch to Base Sepolia” CTA.
  - Added idempotency guards (process a txHash once).
  - Added defensive defaults to prevent crashes.
  - Added an eligibility checklist + auto-fallback rules to keep the flow actionable.
- **Prevention**: Treat the confirm path like a state machine with explicit transitions; enforce “exactly-once” handling; always show the user why a CTA is blocked and what the app will do next.

### 6) Explore didn’t show the real “Step 1-4” context
- **What happened**: Jobs appeared in Explore but didn’t reflect the meaningful details users entered.
- **Why**: The UI wasn’t leveraging the backend job/recipient relations and some display fields were hardcoded.
- **Fix**: Updated Explore/ExploreJob mapping to show recipient identity, assets, and flags; removed hardcoded assumptions.
- **Prevention**: Define a stable “public job view model” and render directly from it; avoid duplicating business logic between screens.

**Base Track**

### Base Track Submission (GigPay)

GigPay is a **treasury-first onchain payout and escrow protocol** built on Base that turns real-world payout coordination (approvals, milestones, disputes, refunds, multi-asset preferences) into a **consumer-grade Mini-App timeline**. Our core primitive is an **escrow state machine** (GigPayEscrowCoreV2) backed by a **company treasury vault** (CompanyTreasuryVault) so teams can **fund once, pay many**: capital sits in a single onchain treasury buffer, escrow intents are funded on-demand, and every lifecycle transition (Created, Funded, Submitted, Released/Refunded) is recorded onchain for auditability. This design is specifically viable on Base because payout workflows require frequent small transactions, and Base’s mini-app ecosystem enables fast, mobile-first execution with low friction onboarding. ([Base Indonesia Hackathon 2025][1])

GigPay is implemented as **composable modules** via GigPayRegistry (swap routing, yield routing, protection/RFQ execution) so integrations evolve without redeploying the escrow core. The Mini-App experience uses **MiniKit + OnchainKit** to deliver a clean consumer UX: users connect via Smart Wallet UI, execute intent actions through a single transaction component with lifecycle/status handling, and view escrow events as a timeline feed (milestones, approvals, protection, swap release). Swap releases follow onchain policies (SwapRouteRegistry) and route RFQ-first with optional fallback via CompositeSwapManager, enabling IDRX-native escrow funding and stablecoin payout preferences. This aligns directly with the Base Track objective of shipping **consumer-ready Mini Apps** that showcase low-cost transactions, strong UX, and composable infrastructure. ([Base Documentation][2])

[2]: https://docs.base.org/onchainkit/latest/components/minikit/overview?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Overview - Base Documentation"

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

## Thetanuts Finance Track GigPay

GigPay expands Thetanuts OptionBook beyond trading and embeds it into enterprise-grade treasury and escrow infrastructure.

Repository:
[https://github.com/GigPay-Indonesia/smart-contract-gigpay](https://github.com/GigPay-Indonesia/smart-contract-gigpay)

Instead of treating OptionBook as a standalone RFQ venue, GigPay integrates it as a programmable settlement and protection layer inside a treasury-first payout protocol. We implemented interface-compatible integrations for:

* IOptionBookRFQ
* IThetanutsOptionBook
* OptionBookRFQSwapManager
* ThetanutsVaultStrategyV2 (ERC4626 adapter)

Because Base Sepolia does not currently host live Thetanuts deployments, we built deterministic, interface-accurate mocks that replicate production OptionBook behavior. Our MockOptionBook supports signed maker orders and onchain fillOrder() execution, allowing escrow releases to route RFQ-first with optional fallback via CompositeSwapManager.

GigPay demonstrates three concrete extensions of Thetanuts primitives:

1. **RFQ as Treasury Execution Primitive**
   Escrow releases execute against RFQ quotes instead of AMMs, enabling deterministic payout asset settlement with no slippage exposure.

2. **Structured Protection Attached to Escrow Intents**
   Treasury can purchase RFQ-based protection and bind it to an escrow via protectionPolicyId. Settlement and claim flows are handled inside GigPayEscrowCoreV2, with protection balances isolated from principal.

3. **ERC4626 Vault Compatibility for Yield Routing**
   ThetanutsVaultStrategyV2 enables treasury and escrow funds to route into vault-compatible strategies using share-based accounting consistent with Thetanuts design.

All flows are proven in Foundry tests, including protection settlement, RFQ execution, yield activation, and fallback routing.

GigPay shows how Thetanuts infrastructure can power programmable treasury, escrow risk management, and enterprise payout systems, not just trading venues.

**The problem it solves**

**SentryGate : The Ultimate Gatekeeper for Your Digital Legacy**
SentryGate is an Onchain Mini App built on the Base network that redefines how we store and verify our most critical documents. By combining military-grade encryption with decentralized storage and a seamless onchain payment gateway, SentryGate turns your wallet into a bulletproof digital vault.

**What can people use it for?**
SentryGate is designed for anyone who handles high-stakes documentation that cannot afford to be lost, tampered with, or accessed by unauthorized parties:
- Academic Sovereignty: Students and alumni can store encrypted versions of diplomas, transcripts, and certifications. No more worrying about physical damage or long university verification processes.
- Freelance & Legal Protection: Independent contractors can vault signed SLAs, NDAs, and project milestones. With onchain timestamps, you have immutable proof of your contracts.
- Corporate Credentials (HR): Professionals can maintain a portable, verified record of employment letters (Paklaring) and tax documents that follow them throughout their career.
- Business Continuity for SMEs: Small business owners can secure NIBs, deeds, and rental agreements, ensuring they are always accessible for loan applications or permits, even if local hardware fails.

**How SentryGate Makes Life Easier & Safer**
1. Safer : Zero-Knowledge Privacy
Unlike traditional cloud providers (Google Drive/Dropbox), SentryGate cannot see your files. * Client-Side Encryption: Documents are encrypted on your device using keys derived from your wallet signature before they ever touch the network. Decentralized Resilience: Files are hosted on Pinata (IPFS), removing the "single point of failure" risk. Even if one server goes down, your data remains accessible and untampered.

2. Easier : Seamless Onchain Access
We’ve removed the friction of traditional security systems : x402 Payment Middleware: No more manual subscriptions. The system automatically verifies your access status via the x402 protocol on Base. If you've paid, the gate opens; if not, you can pay and unlock features instantly in one transaction. Mobile-First Scanning: Use the built-in scanner to turn physical papers into encrypted digital assets in seconds.

3. Smarter : Immutable Integrity
By storing the cryptographic hash of your documents on the Base network, SentryGate provides a permanent "fingerprint" of your data. You can prove a document existed at a certain time and hasn't been modified since—without ever revealing the actual content to the public.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building SentryGate was a journey of balancing high-level security with a smooth user experience. Here are the most significant hurdles we faced and how we cleared them :

1. The "Consistent Key" Dilemma (Client-Side Encryption)
**The Hurdle :** The core promise of SentryGate is that even we, the developers, cannot see your files. This required client-side encryption. However, we faced a major UX problem : How do we generate the same encryption key every time a user logs in without asking them to remember a second password or worse storing their private key?
**The Solution :** We implemented a deterministic key derivation flow. When a user connects their wallet (via Privy), we ask them to sign a specific, non-transactional message: "Sign this to unlock your SentryGate Vault".
- This signature is unique to the user but deterministic.
- We then feed this signature into a PBKDF2 (Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2) with a fixed salt to derive a 256-bit AES key.
- This ensures that as long as the user has access to their wallet, they can always derive the same key to decrypt their vault on any device.


2. Development Environment & Toolchain Conflicts
**The Hurdle** : Setting up the development environment for Foundry (to build the Base smart contracts) and the Sui CLI (for related research) within a Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) environment proved to be quite a challenge. We encountered several path conflicts and versioning issues that caused the smart contract deployment scripts to fail unexpectedly during the early stages of the hackathon.
**The Solution** : We had to perform a deep dive into the WSL environment variables and toolchain management. After hard-resetting the local environment and manually configuring the binary paths for Foundry, we established a stable deployment pipeline. This experience taught us the importance of environment isolation and having a robust "clean start" script for the team.


3. Synchronizing x402 Middleware with the Backend
**The Hurdle :** Using x402 as a payment gatekeeper created a "race condition" between the blockchain and our backend. Sometimes, a user would complete their payment on the Base network, but when they immediately tried to upload a document, the backend API (checking the state via a RPC provider) would still see the old "unpaid" status because the block hadn't fully indexed yet.
**The Solution :** We solved this by implementing Optimistic Validation combined with a Retry Mechanism :
- Frontend: Once the transaction hash is received, the UI optimistically unlocks the upload feature.
- Backend: If the initial on-chain check fails, the API doesn't just reject the request. Instead, it enters a short "polling" loop for 5-10 seconds to verify the transaction status directly from the Base sequencer.
- This ensures that by the time the encrypted file is processed, the payment status is confirmed without the user ever seeing a "Payment Required" error after they’ve already paid.


4. Browser-Based Document Scanning
**The Hurdle :** Creating a "Mini App" feel meant the scanner had to work flawlessly on mobile browsers. Initially, the raw image data from the camera was too large to encrypt and upload efficiently, causing the browser to lag or crash on lower-end devices.
**The Solution :** We integrated a client-side compression layer using canvas before the encryption step. By resizing and converting the scan to a high-quality WebP format first, we significantly reduced the payload size, making the subsequent AES encryption much faster and the upload to Pinata nearly instantaneous.

**Base Track**

SentryGate is a purpose-built Base Mini-App designed to solve the critical friction points of document security and Web3 accessibility. Below is how the project directly aligns with the mission and technical requirements of the Base Track.

1. Solving Meaningful UX Challenges
SentryGate focuses on transforming complex onchain processes into a retail-friendly experience:
- Seamless Onboarding : By utilizing a mobile-first scanning interface, we bridge the gap between physical documents and onchain security. Users don't need to be cryptography experts; the app handles the "Heavy Lifting" of encryption and IPFS uploading automatically.
- Integrated Accessibility : We address the "Gatekeeping" challenge by using x402 as a payment middleware. This creates a frictionless "Pay-to-Unlock" flow where the app automatically verifies access status on Base, removing the need for traditional, manual subscription management.

2. Strategic Technical Execution on Base
SentryGate is architected to leverage the core strengths of the Base ecosystem:
- Base L2 Optimization : We utilize Base for its high speed and near-zero gas fees. This allows SentryGate to record document metadata hashes onchain affordably, providing users with immutable "Proof of Existence" without the high costs of Ethereum Mainnet.
- Security & Privacy : Our codebase implements Client-Side AES-256 Encryption. Keys are derived from the user's wallet signature (via Privy/Wagmi), ensuring that the project adheres to the "Not your keys, not your data" principle a core value of the Base and Web3 community.
- Decentralized Resilience: By integrating Pinata (IPFS), we ensure that the storage layer is as decentralized as the execution layer on Base, eliminating single points of failure.

3. IDRX Integration & Localized Experience
- To support the Indonesian Web3 ecosystem and qualify for the Best Project (IDRX) bonus prize, SentryGate has integrated IDRX as a native payment option:
- The SentryGate.sol smart contract is designed to accept IDRX token transfers for vault access.
- By using a stablecoin pegged to the Rupiah, we provide a familiar pricing model for local retail users (SMEs, students, and freelancers), further lowering the barrier to entry for onchain applications.

4. Ecosystem Impact & Market Fit
- SentryGate contributes to the growth of the Base ecosystem by targeting high-utility use cases :
- Target Market: We focus on sectors with high-risk document needs such as Academic Credentials, Freelance Contracts, and Small Business Legal Documents.
- Retention : The vault nature of the app encourages long-term user retention and recurring onchain activity, directly contributing to the "Industry-defining onchain applications" mission of this hackathon.

> Scan, Pay, and Grow with AI

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

DeFi is powerful, but it's still too hard for the average person. New users are often overwhelmed by complex interfaces, the fear of sending money to the wrong 0x... address, and the confusion of choosing where to invest their assets.

DeQRypt bridges the gap between Web2 usability and Web3 power on the Base network. It solves these critical friction points:

1. Eliminates "Address Anxiety": Instead of copy-pasting long, error-prone wallet addresses, users simply scan a QR code to pay—mimicking the familiar experience of Web2 payment apps (like QRIS/Venmo).

2. Democratizes Financial Intelligence: Most users don't know which lending pool (Aave, Moonwell) offers the best safety or APY. Our AI Agent acts as a personal financial copilot, analyzing market rates in real-time and guiding users to the best yield opportunities.

3. Removes Idle Capital: Money sitting in a wallet loses value against inflation. DeQRypt makes it effortless to move funds from a checking account into Yield-Generating Protocols with a single chat command or

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Understanding payment flow vs. asset flow (Treasury confusion)**

     One of the first hurdles was properly separating payment settlement logic from asset custody logic. Initially, it was unclear whether the treasury wallet would need to manually approve transactions when funds passed through it. This caused confusion about who “controls” the funds during a payment.

    **How we solved it**
    We restructured the flow so that:
    1. The router contract is the only executor of transfers.
    2. The treasury wallet is a passive receiver of funds.
    3. All transfers happen atomically inside a single smart contract call.

2. **Swap complexity and testnet liquidity limitations**

    Implementing a real on-chain swap on Base Sepolia turned out to be risky due to low liquidity and high slippage potential during the demo.

    **How we solved it**
    We implemented a simulated swap layer (V2) where the Router accepts USDC, transfers it to treasury, and mints IDRX to the merchant at a fixed oracle rate. This keeps the architecture DeFi-ready while making the demo stable.

3. **Transaction Finality & "Silent Failures" (Backend)**

    We encountered a critical bug where the Backend API returned "Success" immediately after broadcasting a transaction, but the transaction would later revert on-chain. This led to data inconsistency where the database showed a deposit that never actually happened.

    **How we solved it**
    We implemented a strict transaction receipt validation in the Python backend. The system now broadcasts the hash and pauses to wait for the block confirmation (receipt.status == 1). If the chain reverts, the backend catches the error and prevents the database write, ensuring 100% data integrity.

4. **Single-Asset vs. Multi-Asset Pool Architecture**

    While integrating the AI Agent, we found that depositing mUSDC would constantly fail. We realized our initial Mock Lending Pool was hardcoded as a "Single Asset Vault" (only accepting mIDRX), but the backend treated it like a generic pool.

    **How we solved it**
    We refactored the smart contract to a Multi-Asset Pool pattern (similar to Aave). We updated the backend logic to dynamically pass the token_address into the smart contract call, allowing the Agent to manage multiple assets (ETH, mUSDC, mIDRX) through a single contract interface.

5. **Frontend integration clarity**

    Another hurdle was ensuring the frontend team clearly understood which addresses were fixed (router) vs user-provided, and the correct sequence of approve -> pay.

    **How we solved it**
    We created a detailed integration brief covering minimal ABIs, token decimals, and event-based receipt parsing. This allowed frontend development to proceed independently without blockchain-side changes.

**Base Track**

DeQRypt is natively built on the Base Sepolia testnet. We chose Base because our application focuses on everyday payments via QR codes and micro-investments. For this to work in the real world, we need the low gas fees and sub-second transaction speeds that only Base provides.

We have deployed our custom Multi-Asset Lending Pool and Payment Logic smart contracts directly on Base. By leveraging Base's efficient infrastructure, we can offer users a seamless "Web2-like" experience—instant scan-to-pay and automated yield generation—without the friction of high costs or slow confirmations.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Democratizing Legal Protection with Pay-Per-Prompt Access**

- Millions of Indonesian job seekers sign "toxic" employment contracts because professional legal review is prohibitively expensive, and existing AI legal tools often require expensive monthly subscriptions that don't make sense for a one-time user.

- LaborLex AI bridges this gap as a Micro-SaaS Legal Assistant specifically tuned for Indonesian Labor Laws (Omnibus Law).

**Pay-Per-Prompt Accessibility:** Instead of forcing users into expensive subscriptions, we implement a Pay-Per-Prompt model. Users pay a micro-fee (via Visa/Digital Payment) only when they need a contract reviewed. This is powered by an x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) architecture, making high-quality legal analysis accessible to fresh graduates and blue-collar workers.

**RAG-Powered Accuracy:** The system uses Retrieval Augmented Generation to cross-reference uploaded contracts against the latest UU Cipta Kerja and PP Jaminan Sosial, detecting predatory clauses like unlawful penalty fees or hidden "internship" traps.

**Detecting "Toxic" Clauses:** It instantly identifies red flags, such as "salary below minimum wage," "illegal holding of diplomas (ijazah)," or "discriminatory termination clauses," explaining why they are illegal in simple language.

**Cost-Effective Architecture:** By optimizing the token usage and RAG retrieval, we provide "Tier-1 Law Firm" insights at the price of a cup of coffee.

**Empowerment:** It transforms a daunting legal document into actionable insights, giving workers the confidence to negotiate or decline exploitative offers.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. The "Dirty Data" Nightmare**: Scanned PDFs vs. RAG One of the biggest hurdles wasn't the code, but the data itself. The Indonesian Omnibus Law documents available weren't clean digital text files; they were scanned images of printed papers (some seemingly taken with a mobile phone camera) converted into PDF.

- The Hurdle: Standard PDF loaders couldn't extract text for the RAG system, making chunking impossible.

- The Struggle: I spent significant time trying to clean this unstructured data so the AI could actually "read" the laws instead of seeing blank pages.

**2. Prompt Engineering & System Behavior** Getting the AI to act as a strict legal assistant was difficult. Early on, the model would hallucinate or be too conversational. Crafting the perfect System Prompt to ensure the AI strictly adheres to the provided legal context without making up facts required countless iterations of trial and error.

**3. Zero-Budget Development:** From Local PC to Alibaba Cloud As a developer with limited resources, I had to be strategic about costs:

- Local Beginnings: During development, I relied entirely on LM Studio running on my local PC to save money. I utilized text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-8b for vectorization and openai/gpt-oss-20b for inference. This allowed me to iterate fast without burning cash.

- The Switch: Now, for better performance, I've migrated to Alibaba Cloud's Free Tier, utilizing the qwen3-max-2026-01-23 model (which offers a generous 1M token grant). Managing this transition from a local environment to a cloud provider while keeping the system stable was a steep learning curve.

**4. The Two-Week Sprint**: Mastering x402 Perhaps the most personal challenge was the timeline. I was only introduced to the x402 (Payment) protocol less than two weeks ago during the Base Workshop in Jogja.

- We had to learn a completely new monetization standard and deliver a working mini-app in a very short time.

- While this app might look simple to others, for us, shipping a functional RAG system integrated with x402 payment logic in such a tight window is a massive personal

**Base Track**

**LaborLex AI fits the "Base Track" by demonstrating that Onchain Apps can solve real-world, off-chain problems (Legal Access) through seamless micropayments.**

**Specifically, we align with the track's goal of "elevating the onchain user experience" in three ways:**

1. Enabling True Micro-SaaS on Base Legal aid in Indonesia is traditionally expensive. LaborLex AI democratizes this by using a "Pay-Per-Prompt" model. This business model is only viable on Base; the ultra-low gas fees allow us to process micro-transactions (e.g., $0.50 per contract review) without the transaction fee exceeding the service cost—something impossible on L1 chains.

2. Innovative Use of x402 Protocol We go beyond simple token transfers by implementing the x402 (Payment Required) protocol on Base. This turns the API into an autonomous economic agent: the AI service is cryptographically gated and only unlocks upon successful settlement on the Base network. This showcases a sophisticated "Internet-Native Payment" flow that is fast, transparent, and permissionless.

3. Real-World Consumer Adoption Unlike purely speculative DeFi projects, LaborLex AI targets a massive non-crypto native audience: Indonesian workers. By using Base as the invisible settlement layer for checking employment contracts, we bring "Consumer Crypto" to everyday users who simply need legal protection, proving that Base can power essential utility apps, not just financial speculation.

**The problem it solves**

🔴 Problem
In the age of daily content, consistency is the biggest challenge for creators, founders, and social media managers.
Key problems they face:
1.⁠ ⁠Content production is time-consuming
2.⁠ ⁠Inconsistent posting
3.⁠ ⁠Fragmented workflow
4.⁠ ⁠Creator burnout

🟢 Solution
Social Flow is a miniapp that automates the entire content workflow, from idea to publishing.
How Social Flow solves these problems:
1.⁠ ⁠Automated Content Flow
2.⁠ ⁠One Dashboard, All Platforms
3.⁠ ⁠Consistency on Autopilot
4.⁠ ⁠Creator-First Experience

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
Multi-Platform Posting Complexity
One of the biggest challenges was handling content delivery to multiple platforms (Threads, LinkedIn, and Twitter) in a single flow. Each platform has different API requirements, rate limits, and content constraints.
How I solved it:
I designed a unified posting layer that standardizes content before dispatching it to each platform. This abstraction allowed Social Flow to handle platform-specific rules without breaking the user experience.

Scheduling & Reliability
Ensuring scheduled posts were published on time was tricky, especially when handling multiple user requests and edge cases like retries or failed transactions.
How I solved it:
I implemented a queue-based scheduling system with status tracking and automatic retries. This ensures posts are either successfully published or safely retried without user intervention.

Authentication & Permissions
Managing secure authentication for different social platforms while keeping the onboarding simple was a major hurdle.
How I solved it:
I used token-based authentication with scoped permissions and built a permission-check layer to prevent failed posts due to missing access rights.

Balancing Automation & Control
Too much automation can feel “black-boxed,” while too much control can slow users down.
How I solved it:
I designed Social Flow with a clear step-by-step flow — generate → schedule or post → confirm transaction — giving users full visibility without unnecessary friction.

Performance & UX
Generating content, scheduling, and posting had to feel instant, even though multiple processes were happening in the background.
How I solved it:
I optimized background jobs and added clear UI feedback (loading states, status indicators) so users always know what’s happening.

**Base Track**

1. Built for Real Onchain Utility
Social Flow is not just a content tool it introduces onchain interactions into everyday creator workflows. Each content action (posting or scheduling) is abstracted into a transaction, showcasing how blockchain can power real-world automation beyond DeFi.

2. Leveraging Base for Scalability
Base’s low fees and fast confirmation times make it ideal for handling frequent micro-transactions like content publishing and scheduling. Social Flow benefits directly from Base’s infrastructure to deliver a smooth, cost-efficient user experience.

3. Bridging Web2 and Web3
Social Flow connects Web3 wallets with Web2 social platforms (Threads, LinkedIn, Twitter), acting as a bridge between onchain identity and offchain social distribution a key narrative for Base adoption.

4. Base-Native Developer Experience
The project is designed and deployed on Base Sepolia, leveraging Base’s tooling and ecosystem to validate smart contract interactions, transaction flows, and onchain logic in a real application.

5. Expanding Base Use Cases
Most onchain apps focus on finance or governance. Social Flow demonstrates a new category: onchain-powered creator tools, helping expand the Base ecosystem into social, creator, and productivity use cases.

6. Aligned with Base’s Mission
Base aims to bring the next billion users onchain. By embedding blockchain seamlessly into a familiar activity like content posting, Social Flow lowers the barrier for non-crypto users to interact with Base without friction.

### KITAfinance
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kitafinance-ce04) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/13222093/KITAfinance) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://kita.naufarrel.tech/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zLGfeRAyxX8?si=_CIwKNo-XjcTwDtl) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Trading option jadi seru, bareng-bareng.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prism.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prism.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Indonesia has **270 million people** and a rapidly growing crypto community of **12+ million users**. **Options trading offers 8-15% annual returns**, significantly higher than traditional savings, yet these powerful DeFi strategies remain **inaccessible** to most. Why? Traditional options platforms overwhelm users with **intimidating interfaces** - complex order books, unfamiliar jargon like Delta, Gamma, Theta, and Strike Prices, complete with dull UIs and steep learning curve. 

### How KITAfinance Changes the Game

KITAfinance elegantly solves these barriers by transforming Thetanuts V4's powerful options infrastructure into an **intuitive, culturally-relevant, and genuinely fun experience**.


### 1. Gamified Experience 

Let's be honest: finance apps are *boring*. KITAfinance changes that fundamentally.

We turned wealth-building into something people actually *want* to do:

- **XP Progression System**: Level up from "Pemula" (Beginner) to "Master Trader" - every action earns experience points
- **Monthly Campaigns**: Themed events like "Valentine's Special Nabung Bareng" - create a couples saving group for bonus rewards
- **Achievement Badges**: Unlock rewards for hitting milestones like first deposit, first yield, or inviting friends
- **Daily Missions**: "Complete your first trade" → +100 XP. Users return daily to complete challenges
- **Leaderboards**: Compete with friends and the broader community for top positions
- **Streak Badges**: Maintain your "Nabung Bareng Streak" for consistency rewards - shareable badges flex your commitment on social media

**Result**: Finance stops feeling like homework. KITAfinance makes building wealth feel like a game worth playing every day.


### 2. NabungBareng 

In Indonesia, we have a cultural value called *gotong royong* - the belief that we achieve more together than alone. KITAfinance's "Nabung Bareng" feature brings this deeply Indonesian concept to DeFi.

Friends and family can **pool money together for shared life goals**:

| Goal | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Menikah** | Save together for your dream wedding |
| **Beli Rumah** | Pool funds for a house down payment |
| **Liburan Bareng** | Fund that group vacation to Bali or Japan |
| **Pendidikan** | Parents and relatives contribute to a child's education |
| **Beli Kendaraan** | Collective saving for a family car |
| **Dana Darurat** | Build an emergency fund together |

Each group is **personalized to its goal**:
- Visual themes adapt based on the selected goal
- Smart calculators show per-person contribution breakdowns
- AI provides tailored tips ("Biaya nikah rata-rata Rp 50-100 juta")
- Integrated sharing via Telegram and WhatsApp for easy invitations
- **Shareable Group Progress Badges** - show off your group's savings streak and milestones on social media

**Result**: Groups access larger options positions together, democratizing yields that were previously only available to wealthy individuals. KITAfinance makes saving social, not solitary.


### 3. Intuitive Language & UI 

We replaced intimidating financial jargon with simple, everyday Bahasa Indonesia:

| Complex Term | KITAfinance Translation | Meaning |
|--------------|------------------|---------|
| Cash-Secured Put | **Beli Murah Dapat Cashback** | Buy Cheap, Get Cashback |
| Covered Call | **Hold Aset Dapat Bonus** | Hold Assets, Get Bonus |
| Buy Call | **Modal Receh Potensi Jackpot** | Small Capital, Jackpot Potential |

Our **"Ocean Blue" design system** feels like a consumer app, not a trading terminal:

- **Mobile-first**: 95% of Indonesian internet users are mobile-first. Every pixel is optimized for 375px screens
- **44px touch targets**: Thumb-friendly buttons that feel natural to tap
- **Visual metaphors**: Icons and colors communicate risk/reward without requiring text parsing
- **Animated feedback**: Every action provides satisfying micro-interactions

**Result**: Users understand strategies instantly. No finance degree required. A first-time investor in Jakarta can comprehend the app in 30 seconds.


### 4. Personalized AI-Chatbot That Knows You

During onboarding, KITAfinance learns about you through conversational questions. Our AI then provides **personalized guidance** throughout your journey:

- **Risk Profiling**: Simple questions determine your comfort level
  - "Aman" (Safe) → Conservative strategies, steady 8-12% APY
  - "Balance" → Mixed approach for moderate risk
  - "Agresif" → Higher risk, higher potential returns

- **AI Chatbot**: Powered by Google Gemini, available 24/7 in Bahasa Indonesia
  - Ask: "Gimana cara kerja options?"
  - Receive: A friendly, jargon-free explanation tailored to your level

**Result**: Users never feel lost. The AI acts as a personal financial advisor that speaks their language and understands their goals.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Complex Backend Architecture with Prisma

Building a real-time options trading backend required careful data architecture.

**The Hurdle**: We needed to sync on-chain events (deposits, withdrawals, option executions) with off-chain user data while maintaining strict data consistency. Managing relational models for users, positions, groups, and transactions introduced complexity around race conditions and atomic operations.

**The Fix**: We designed a robust Prisma schema with proper indexing, used transactions for critical operations, and implemented an event-driven architecture that listens to on-chain events to update database state. This ensures our user-facing data always reflects the true blockchain state.


### 2. Implementing Cash-Secured Put Logic On-Chain

The smart contract logic for Cash-Secured Put was non-trivial.

**The Hurdle**: We had to handle:
- USDC collateral management and secure locking
- Integration with Thetanuts V4's `IOptionBook.fillOrder()` interface
- Premium distribution and yield calculations
- Edge cases: partial fills, expiration handling, and withdrawal timing

**The Fix**: We built two separate vault contracts (`KITAVault` for solo trading, `GroupVault` for Nabung Bareng) with clearly separated concerns. We used OpenZeppelin's security standards for access control and reentrancy protection. Multiple iterations of yield math ensured accurate premium distribution while keeping user funds secure.


### 3. Designing Mobile-First UI That Doesn't Feel Like a Trading Terminal

Most DeFi apps look like Bloomberg terminals - functional for traders, intimidating for everyone else.

**The Hurdle**: We needed to create an interface that feels like a consumer mobile app while still enabling sophisticated options trading. This required rethinking every UX pattern from scratch.

**The Fix**: We developed our "Ocean Blue" design system with strict mobile-first principles:
- Minimum 44px touch targets for all interactive elements
- Thumb-zone optimization for critical actions
- Animated micro-interactions for every user action
- Progressive disclosure - show complexity only when needed
- Constant testing on actual mobile devices (not just browser simulators)


### 4. Translating DeFi Jargon to Bahasa Indonesia

The hardest challenge wasn't technical - it was **linguistic**.

**The Hurdle**: How do you explain "Cash-Secured Put" to someone who has never traded options? Direct translation fails because the underlying concepts don't map to everyday Indonesian vocabulary. We needed language that conveyed the *benefit*, not the *mechanism*.

**The Fix**: We went through dozens of copywriting iterations with native Indonesian speakers. Key insight: focus on *outcomes*, not *processes*:
- "Cash-Secured Put" → "Beli Murah Dapat Cashback" (Buy Cheap, Get Cashback)
- "Covered Call" → "Hold Aset Dapat Bonus" (Hold Assets, Get Bonus)

We also created contextual AI tips that explain concepts using relatable Indonesian metaphors. This UX copywriting took more time than we expected but was absolutely crucial for true accessibility.


### 5. Thetanuts V4 Integration Complexity

Integrating with Thetanuts V4's RFQ system presented unique challenges.

**The Hurdle**: The RFQ (Request for Quote) flow involves fetching available orders, matching them to user intent, and executing fills - all while presenting a simple UI. Mapping a user's "I want yield" desire to specific option parameters (strike price, expiry, premium) required significant translation logic.

**The Fix**: We built abstraction layers in our backend that handle the complexity:
1. Fetch available orders from Thetanuts V4
2. Filter and rank by liquidity and optimal strike prices
3. Present simplified choices to users ("Safe: 8% APY" vs "Aggressive: 15% APY")
4. Execute the matched order on-chain via our vault contracts

Users never see the complexity. They just pick a strategy and watch their yield grow.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

KITA Finance uses Thetanuts V4 as our core options infrastructure. 

Proof of deployment on Base:
- KITAVault: https://sepolia.basescan.org/address/0x1cF7e8fF49cd61D7AAB9850BaC106E0947c31326
- GroupVault: https://sepolia.basescan.org/address/0x9B2b628b1bad3C9983A2E6C0170185d289489c6e

Technical Integration:
- Our smart contracts (KITAVault and GroupVault) integrate directly with Thetanuts V4's IOptionBook interface
- We use the fillOrder() function to execute options strategies on-chain
- Users deposit USDC → our vaults route capital to Thetanuts V4 → earn yield from options premiums

What we built on top:
- Gamified UI: XP, badges, leaderboards, daily missions
- AI onboarding: Chatbot explains options in Bahasa Indonesia
- Personalized guidance: Risk profiling → strategy recommendations
- Social features: "Nabung Bareng" lets groups pool USDC together to access Thetanuts options
- Result: Complex Thetanuts V4 options become accessible to everyday Indonesian users through simple language ("Beli Murah Dapat Cashback" instead of "Cash-Secured Put") and engaging gamification

**The problem it solves**

# FundLedger – A Transparent Community Funding Platform

## 🧩 Problem Statement

Community-driven funding platforms often lack **transparency, accountability, and clear fund-flow visibility**.

Common challenges include:

* Donors not knowing how funds are allocated
* Pitchers being unclear why proposals succeed or fail
* Silent failures when community funds are insufficient
* No handling of partial or pending funding
* Weak audit trails for administrators

These gaps reduce trust, discourage participation, and make governance difficult.

---

## 💡 Solution: FundLedger

**FundLedger** is a transparent, rule-based community funding platform that ensures every funding decision is **visible, traceable, and accountable**.

Instead of opaque approvals, FundLedger combines **community voting with verifiable fund pools** to decide proposal outcomes.

---

## 🔑 Key Features

### ✅ Transparent Voting System

* Donors vote on proposals during active funding rounds
* Votes remain sealed until the round completes
* Decisions are community-driven, not centrally biased

### 💰 Clear Funding Outcomes

Every winning proposal ends in one of three explicit states:

* **Fully Funded** – Funding goal met from category pool
* **Partially Funded** – Some funds allocated, remainder pending
* **Awaiting Funds** – No funds available at round completion

There are **no silent failures** — every outcome is clearly communicated.

### 🚫 No Fabricated Funds

* Funds are never artificially created
* No negative balances are allowed
* Allocations only occur when real community funds exist

If funds are insufficient, the system records **pending obligations** instead of hiding the issue.

### 📊 Complete Audit Trail

* All fund transfers and pending obligations are logged
* Admins can track unfunded and partially funded proposals
* Pitchers can clearly see received vs pending amounts

### 👥 Role-Based Transparency

**Pitcher**

* Submit funding proposals
* View proposal status
* Track wallet balance and pending payouts

**Donor**

* Vote on proposals
* View funding outcomes after round completion
* Understand how community decisions impact results

**Admin**

* Verify proposals
* Manage funding rounds
* Add community funds
* Monitor pending fund obligations
* Maintain full platform oversight

---

## 🎯 Impact

FundLedger transforms community funding into a **trust-first, governance-driven system** by:

* Eliminating ambiguity in funding decisions
* Making partial and pending funding visible
* Preventing silent failures
* Creating accountability for all stakeholders

---

## 🏁 Summary

FundLedger replaces opaque funding workflows with a **ledger-based, transparent, and accountable platform**, making community funding fairer, safer, and easier to trust.

This project is designed for demonstrations, hackathons, and educational use, with virtual funds used to simulate real-world funding behavior.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🛠️ Key Technical Challenges & Solutions

### 1. 🛡️ Preventing Fake Funding
**Challenge:** Standard demo platforms often credit winners based on projected rather than actual funds, leading to ledger discrepancies.
**Solution:**
* **Strict Validation:** Implemented atomic checks before transaction execution.
* **State Management:** Introduced `partial` and `pending` funding states.
* **Zero-Deficit Logic:** System strictly prevents negative balances and "fabricated" liquidity.

### 2. 🗳️ Sealed Voting without UX Friction
**Challenge:** Hiding vote counts to prevent bandwagoning while ensuring users confirm their vote was registered.
**Solution:**
* **Vote Locking:** Inputs are immutable immediately after submission.
* **Contextual UI:** Displayed specific messaging explaining the "Sealed" state to users.
* **Conditional Revealing:** Results remain encrypted in the frontend until the round strictly concludes.

### 3. 🎨 Frontend Modernization (Zero-Backend Touch)
**Challenge:** Overhauling the UI/UX without risking stability in the core business logic.
**Solution:**
* **Stack:** Upgraded to **Tailwind CSS** and **HTMX**.
* **Constraint:** Achieved a complete visual refresh without modifying a single line of backend `Models`, `Views`, or `URLs`.

### 4. 📉 Handling Insufficient Liquidity
**Challenge:** Ensuring system integrity when a community runs out of funds during a payout round.
**Solution:**
* **Pending Obligations:** Created a ledger system for "Unpaid Commitments."
* **Admin Visibility:** Dedicated dashboard for tracking debt.
* **Future Settlement:** Automated logic allows incoming future funds to transparently settle past obligations.

**The problem it solves**

Air pollution and rising carbon emissions are among the most critical global challenges today. While governments and organizations publish AQI data and carbon statistics daily, this information remains passive — people can see that pollution is increasing, but there is no system that converts this awareness into immediate, organized, community-driven action.

**Challenges we ran into**

Machine Learning Challenges
Data Inconsistency: Historical AQI data had missing values and inconsistent city names. We built a preprocessing pipeline with interpolation and fuzzy matching.

Model Overfitting: Our LSTM memorized training data. Fixed by adding dropout layers and cross-validation across multiple cities.

Real-time Calibration: Model trained on old data gave wrong predictions. Built dynamic calibration using live WAQI API with exponential decay.

API & Routing Challenges
CORS Nightmares: Frontend couldn't talk to 4 different backends on different ports. Spent hours configuring proper CORS headers and cookie credentials.

OAuth Redirect Hell: Google OAuth kept breaking between localhost and production. Created environment-based URL configs.

Protected Routes: Users bypassed frontend guards by typing URLs directly. Added backend middleware + React route guards.
 Blockchain Challenges
Node Sync Issues: Multiple miners created conflicting chains. Implemented longest-chain consensus with automatic resolution.

Double-Spending Bug: Same transaction mined into multiple blocks. Added transaction ID caching to prevent duplicates.

Slow Mining: Pure Python was too slow. Wrote Cython modules for 2-5x speedup.
 Map Challenges
Geospatial Queries: Location-based event search was slow. Added MongoDB 2dsphere indexes with $near operator.

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves:
In many small organizations such as college clubs, societies, committees, and student bodies, elections are usually conducted using manual methods, Google Forms, or centralized online platforms. These methods have several limitations. Votes can be modified or deleted by admins, results are not fully transparent, and participants have to blindly trust the authority conducting the election. There is also no reliable way for a voter to verify whether their vote was actually counted.

ChainVote solves this trust problem:
ChainVote provides a transparent and tamper-proof voting system using blockchain technology. Once a vote is cast, it is permanently recorded on the blockchain and cannot be changed or removed by anyone. This removes the need to trust a central authority and ensures fairness in the election process.

Key features of ChainVote
•	Wallet-based voting:
Each voter uses their crypto wallet (MetaMask) as their identity. This removes the need for usernames and passwords.
•	One person, one vote:
The smart contract ensures that each eligible wallet address can vote only once.
•	Admin-controlled eligibility:
The election admin can allowlist valid voter addresses before the election starts, preventing unauthorized voting.
•	Transparent and verifiable results:
All votes are stored on the blockchain, and results can be publicly verified by anyone.
•	Vote confirmation:
After voting, users receive confirmation that their vote has been successfully recorded on the blockchain.
•	Decentralized backend:
The core election logic runs on a smart contract deployed on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet, making it immutable and trustless.

Working mechanism of the project
1.	Wallet connection
The user connects their MetaMask wallet to the ChainVote website. The wallet address acts as the voter’s identity.
2.	Network verification
The application checks whether the user is connected to the Sepolia testnet. If not, the user is asked to switch networks.
3.	Admin setup
The admin creates a poll and registers eligible voter wallet addresses using the smart contract.
4.	Voting process
An eligible voter selects a candidate and submits their vote. The smart contract verifies eligibility and ensures the voter has not voted before.
5.	Blockchain recording
The vote is recorded on the blockchain as a transaction, making it permanent and tamper-proof.
6.	Result display
Vote counts are fetched directly from the smart contract and displayed on the results page in real time.

Why blockchain is used?
Blockchain is used to ensure immutability, transparency, and trustlessness. Unlike traditional systems, no single authority can manipulate votes or results. Every action is verifiable on the blockchain, making the election process fair and reliable.

Intended use cases:
ChainVote is designed for:
•	College elections
•	Club or society voting
•	Committee decisions
•	Small organizations and DAOs

It is not intended for national-level elections, but as a secure and practical solution for small-scale voting systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

> One of the major challenges I faced while building this project was understanding and setting up the blockchain environment correctly, especially as a beginner in Web3.

>The first issue was network mismatch in MetaMask. Initially, the application was trying to interact with the Sepolia testnet, but MetaMask was connected to the Ethereum Mainnet. This caused errors like “failed to connect to contract” even though the frontend code was working fine. It took time to realize that the problem was not in the code, but in the wallet network configuration.

>Another challenge was adding and configuring the Sepolia network manually. MetaMask did not recognize the network automatically, and incorrect RPC URLs or missing https:// caused connection failures. I had to understand how RPC endpoints work and switch to a more reliable public RPC to make the network stable.

>Getting Sepolia test ETH was also a hurdle. Some faucets required authentication or had rate limits, which slowed down testing. Without test ETH, deploying and interacting with the smart contract was not possible.

>On the frontend side, I faced issues where the UI looked correct, but actions were not working because the smart contract was not deployed yet or the contract address was missing. This helped me understand the importance of connecting all layers properly: frontend, wallet, and smart contract.

I overcame these challenges by carefully debugging each layer step by step, checking MetaMask network settings, reading error messages properly, and testing the workflow incrementally instead of assuming the issue was always in the code.

**The problem it solves**

# Mini Tornado-Cash–Style Private Payments (ZK-Powered)

> **Send money without revealing who paid whom — and without exposing secrets on-chain.**

This project is a **mini privacy payment system** inspired by Tornado Cash, built using **Zero-Knowledge Proofs**.  
It allows a sender to lock funds on-chain and lets the receiver withdraw them **only if they know a secret**, without ever revealing that secret to the blockchain.

---

##  The Core Idea (Visual Flow)


**No secret is ever revealed on-chain.**  
Only a proof that *“I know the correct secret”* is verified.

---

## How it works (Step-by-Step)

### Sender creates a private payment
- Sender chooses a **random secret code**
- A **256-bit hash** of the secret is generated
- The **hash is stored on-chain** as the payment identifier
- Funds are locked in the smart contract

✅ Blockchain only sees a hash  
❌ Blockchain never sees the secret

---

###  Secret is shared off-chain
- Sender sends the secret to the receiver
- Can be done via:
  - Encrypted messaging
  - QR code
  - In-person
  - Any secure channel

 The secret lives **entirely off-chain**

---

### Receiver withdraws using Zero Knowledge
- Receiver enters the secret on a withdrawal page
- A **Zero-Knowledge Proof** is generated:
  > *“I know a secret whose hash matches the one on-chain.”*
- Smart contract verifies the proof
- Funds are released to the receiver

 No one can see:
- the secret
- who sent the payment
- how the receiver got access

---

##  Why Zero-Knowledge here is powerful

Without ZK:
- Receiver would have to reveal the secret
- Anyone watching the mempool could steal funds

With ZK:
- Secret never appears on-chain
- Proof cannot be reused or forged
- Front-running is prevented

**The blockchain verifies math — not trust.**

---

##  Privacy Benefits

| Problem | Traditional Payments | This System |
|------|----------------------|------------|
Sender ↔ Receiver link | Fully visible | Hidden |
Secret exposure | Revealed | Never revealed |
Front-running risk | High | None |
Trust required | Yes | Cryptographic |

---

## Future Extensions (Where this gets exciting)

### Payment Pool
- Multiple payments enter a shared pool
- Withdrawals are unlinkable from deposits
- Increases anonymity set

**Result:** Stronger privacy guarantees.

---

### 🧪 Mixer functionality
- Funds are mixed across many deposits
- Observers cannot trace payment paths
- Inspired by Tornado Cash architecture

**Result:** Transaction graph privacy.

---
- Receiver can **set or rotate their own secret**
- Enables:
  - One-time payments
  - Reusable privacy wallets
  - Password-like control without passwords

**Result:** Flexible, user-controlled privacy.

---

This project shows how **privacy doesn’t require trust**:
- No centralized mixer
- No custodial service
- No leaked secrets

Just math, proofs, and smart contracts.

---


> **A zero-knowledge powered mini Tornado-Cash–style payment system where users can send and receive funds privately using secret-based proofs — without ever revealing secrets or linking identities on-chain.**

---


This isn’t just hiding data.

**It removes sensitive data from the blockchain entirely — while keeping verification trustless.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Faced During the Journey

Building a privacy-preserving payment system using Zero-Knowledge Proofs was **far from straightforward**. The journey involved deep technical challenges, design trade-offs, and tight constraints — each of which shaped the final solution.

---

## Understanding Zero-Knowledge at a Practical Level

Zero-knowledge proofs are often explained conceptually, but **implementing them in practice is a different challenge entirely**.

- Understanding how *circuits*, *witnesses*, *public signals*, and *verifiers* interact took time
- Small misunderstandings (e.g. public vs private signals) caused proofs to silently fail
- Debugging ZK circuits provides very little feedback when something goes wrong

**Lesson learned:** ZK is unforgiving — correctness must be exact.

---

## Circuit Design Trade-offs

Designing the circuit required careful decisions:
- Should the hash be an input or computed inside the circuit?
- How many public signals are safe and necessary?
- How do we keep verification simple while preserving privacy?

Every design choice affected:
- gas cost
- verifier complexity
- usability

 **Lesson learned:** Minimal circuits are safer, cheaper, and easier to reason about.

---

## Tooling & Ecosystem Friction

The ZK ecosystem is powerful but still maturing:
- Tooling errors were often cryptic or undocumented
- Small version mismatches between circom and snarkjs caused failures
- Some expected CLI commands simply did not exist, requiring workarounds

 **Lesson learned:** Always rely on the circuit itself as the source of truth.

---

## On-chain vs Off-chain Coordination

A major challenge was **deciding what belongs on-chain and what must stay off-chain**:
- Secrets must never touch the blockchain
- Hashes must be deterministic and verifiable
- Proof generation happens off-chain but must align perfectly with on-chain logic

Any mismatch broke the entire flow.

 **Lesson learned:** Clear separation of responsibilities is essential in ZK systems.

---

##  Gas & Verifier Constraints

On-chain verification is expensive:
- Pairing-based verification consumes significant gas
- Public inputs directly impact verification cost
- Verifier contracts are rigid — one mismatch means failure

 **Lesson learned:** Optimize public inputs early, not later.

---

##  Testing & Debugging Difficulties

Testing ZK systems is unlike traditional apps:
- A single incorrect constraint invalidates everything
- Failures often appear as a simple `false`
- Debugging requires inspecting witnesses, constraints, and generated proofs

 **Lesson learned:** Build incrementally and test at every stage.

---

## Conceptual vs Real Privacy

Designing for **actual privacy**, not just perceived privacy, was a constant challenge:
- Preventing front-running
- Avoiding on-chain data leaks
- Ensuring secrets cannot be inferred indirectly

 **Lesson learned:** Privacy must be considered holistically, not feature-by-feature.

---

##  Final Reflection

Despite the challenges, this journey highlighted the **power and necessity of zero-knowledge systems**.  
Each obstacle reinforced a core idea:

> **Privacy is hard — but worth building correctly.**

This project represents not just a working prototype, but a deeper understanding of how cryptography can replace trust in modern systems.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem: The Hidden Cost of Flexibility

The gig economy has fundamentally changed how we work, offering unparalleled freedom and flexibility to millions of drivers, delivery couriers, and freelancers. However, this independence comes with a significant structural flaw: the complete absence of a financial safety net.

In the traditional workforce, employment often includes benefits that operate in the background. Things like 401(k) matching, automatic pension contributions, and healthcare plans serve as invisible guardrails for long-term financial health. When you leave a corporate job, you usually have some savings accumulated, often without having actively managed them.

For gig workers, this infrastructure simply does not exist. Every dollar earned is paid out immediately, often to cover immediate expenses like gas, vehicle maintenance, or rent. This creates a difficult psychological barrier to saving. When you live gig-to-gig, the decision to transfer fifty dollars into a savings account feels like a loss of immediate buying power. It requires a conscious, painful choice to prioritize a distant future over a pressing present.

The result is a "liquidity trap" where workers have high cash flow but zero wealth accumulation. They are working harder than ever but finding themselves financially vulnerable the moment they stop. We realized that trying to force traditional banking habits onto this new way of working was not just difficult; it was structurally destined to fail.

## The Solution: Automated Financial Hygiene

GigStream addresses this issue by aligning the saving mechanism with the earning mechanism. If gig workers earn money continuously, their savings should accumulate continuously, without requiring constant manual intervention.

We have built a system that fundamentally changes the psychology of saving for this demographic.

### Seamless Integration
The core of our solution is invisibility. By connecting their wallet and setting a small, manageable percentage (such as one percent), users automate their financial health. There are no monthly transfer decisions to make, and no large lump sums leaving their account.

### The Power of Streaming
We utilize the Superfluid protocol to "stream" this percentage into a savings pool second by second. This matches the flow of their income. A driver dropping off a passenger does not just earn a fare; they incrementally build their future. Over the course of a day, these micro-transactions add up, yet they are small enough to be imperceptible in the moment.

### Immediate Growth
To counter the desire for instant gratification, we visualize the results immediately. Users can watch their pension balance grow in real time. This transforms the boring, passive act of saving into an engaging, active metric of success.

By removing the friction of choice and leveraging the continuous nature of gig work, GigStream helps workers build a substantial safety net without ever feeling the burden of saving. It provides the benefits of a traditional pension, re-engineered for the modern economy.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Technical Challenges and Retrospective

Developing a functional Web3 streaming application within a forty-eight hour timeframe presented several unique engineering hurdles. Below are the key challenges we faced and how we navigated them.

## 1. Environment Conflicts: Server-Side Rendering vs. Browser Storage
One of the first critical issues we encountered was a conflict between the Next.js server-side rendering environment and our Web3 libraries.

Our wallet connection tools, specifically Wagmi and RainbowKit, anticipated a browser environment where localStorage is readily available. However, during the initial server render, this object does not exist. This resulted in immediate application crashes upon launch.

To resolve this, we implemented a custom polyfill mechanism. We wrote a script that detects whether the code is executing on the server or the client. When running on the server, it provides a safe, mock implementation of the storage object. This allowed the application to render the initial interface successfully before hydrating the full interactive capabilities on the client side.

## 2. Protocol Integration on Optimism Sepolia
We selected the Optimism Sepolia testnet for its low transaction costs and high speed, which are essential for a micro-transaction platform. However, integrating the Superfluid protocol on this specific chain proved difficult due to fragmentation in documentation.

Locating the correct contract addresses for the test tokens required was not straightforward. We encountered several "Invalid Address" errors where our application attempted to interact with contracts that did not exist on this specific network.

We solved this by manually auditing the contract addresses through the block explorer. We verified exactly which token contracts were active and compatible with the Superfluid wrapper, ensuring our streams were initializing correctly.

## 3. Managing Asynchronous State
Blockchain transactions are inherently asynchronous and can be slower than standard web interactions. A significant user experience challenge was the delay between a user initiating a stream and the blockchain confirming it.

A five-second delay can feel unresponsive to a modern user. To bridge this gap, we implemented an optimistic UI update strategy. The interface reacts immediately to user actions, displaying a "Starting transaction" state and providing visual feedback before the block is officially confirmed. This keeps the user engaged and confident that the system is working, despite the underlying latency of the network.

## 4. Prioritization Under Time Constraints
The strict forty-eight hour deadline forced us to make difficult product decisions. Our initial vision included complex features such as AI-driven investment advice and social leaderboards for drivers.

However, we recognized that the core value proposition was the streaming mechanic itself. We chose to ruthlessly prioritize the stability of the wallet connection and the stream creation flow. We viewed the other features as distractions that could compromise the reliability of the main demo. This focus allowed us to deliver a polished, working core experience rather than a feature-rich but unstable prototype.

**AI**

GigStream is designed to go beyond simple transaction processing. We have integrated local artificial intelligence to serve as a personalized financial coach for gig workers. This approach helps users understand their financial patterns and plan for the future.

---

## 1. Local Intelligence and Data Privacy

**Concept: On-Device Processing**

To protect sensitive financial information, we prioritize local processing. Rather than sending user data to external cloud providers where it could be stored or sold, we use Ollama to run open-source models directly on the local environment.

* **The Model:** We utilize Qwen 2.5 (3B). This model provides a strong balance between processing speed and logical reasoning while maintaining a small footprint.
* **Security and Strategy:** By running the model locally, we ensure that user data never leaves the system. This also allows us to provide a functional prototype without the high overhead costs associated with cloud-hosted artificial intelligence.

---

## 2. Behavioral Reinforcement and Coaching

**Concept: Motivational Feedback**

Small savings can often feel insignificant to a worker. Our system uses behavioral science to change this perspective by providing immediate, positive feedback.

* **The Process:** When a user logs earnings, the backend sends the data to the model with a specific instructional prompt.
* **The Result:** The system generates personalized messages that connect small daily savings to long-term goals. Instead of viewing a five dollar deposit as a minor entry, the user sees it as a tangible step toward their eventual financial independence.

---

## 3. Integrated Knowledge Systems

**Concept: Context-Aware Support**

Gig workers frequently encounter complex questions regarding platform mechanics or decentralized finance. We address this by providing an intelligent support layer.

* **The Technical Approach:** We provide the model with the full context of the GigStream application, including details on yield rates, payment streams, and pension structures.
* **The Result:** Users can ask specific questions about how the application works and receive accurate, immediate answers. This eliminates the need for manual searches through documentation and helps users make informed decisions.

---

**Blockchain**

# Infrastructure: The Web3 Protocol Layer

GigStream is built on a foundation of decentralized protocols designed to make micro-pensions functional and efficient. By utilizing advanced blockchain technology, the platform facilitates the continuous movement and growth of small financial contributions.

---

## 1. Superfluid Protocol: Continuous Asset Streaming

**Concept: Fluid Value Transfer**

Standard digital transactions typically occur as discrete, one-time events. GigStream utilizes the Superfluid protocol to transition from static payments to continuous streams.

* **Rationale:** Since gig workers often earn income throughout the day, their retirement contributions should follow the same pattern. Continuous streaming allows for the steady accumulation of funds.
* **The Technology:** We implement the Constant Flow Agreement (CFA). This allows the system to open a single stream that transfers value every second. This method eliminates the need for the user to sign a new transaction for every small increment of savings.

---

## 2. Optimism Sepolia: Network Scalability

**Concept: Cost-Effective Layer 2 Solutions**

To ensure the platform remains accessible, we have deployed our architecture on the Optimism network.

* **Rationale:** High transaction fees on the Ethereum main network can often exceed the value of a small pension contribution. Optimism provides a scaling solution that offers near-instant processing with minimal costs.
* **The Technology:** This layer ensures that even very small streams are economically viable for the user, as the overhead costs are reduced to fractions of a cent.

---

## 3. Application Integration and Connectivity

**Concept: Secure User Interface**

We prioritize a secure and professional connection between the user's digital wallet and the GigStream application.

* **Connectivity Tools:** We use Wagmi and Viem to provide a stable and type-safe integration with the blockchain.
* **User Interface:** RainbowKit is used to provide a clear and intuitive process for users to connect their wallets to the platform.
* **Future Integration:** The system architecture is prepared to link these income streams directly into decentralized finance vaults. This will allow the pension balance to automatically generate yield through established protocols.

---
