### VIGIL
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fike-0e31) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/kartikbloc/Vigil) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://vigil-beige-psi.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/0wkrqWniShI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20To%20Devcon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-iitr.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Small transfers flow. Big ones wait

![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Wallets are protected by a single private key. If that key **leaks**, gets **phished**, or is copied by **malware**, the funds behind it can be gone in one transaction. The usual fix, a multi signature wallet, is safe but needs several people online for every payment, which most users will not do for daily spending. **VIGIL** solves the same problem without that cost. Small, normal payments still go through instantly. Anything large or unusual is held for a short delay and can be cancelled by a second key, so a stolen key on its own is not enough to empty the wallet.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part was not the delay itself, that part is well known. It was making sure the delay could not be switched off by whoever stole the key. Our first version let the owner call functions like **disableGuard** directly. The very first test we wrote for that path passed immediately, which was the warning sign, since it meant an attacker who stole the owner key could turn off protection in one transaction and then drain the wallet right after, making the whole system pointless.

The fix was to remove every direct path to those settings. Now **setThreshold**, **setDelay**, **setGuardian**, and **disableGuard** can only be called by the contract calling itself, which only happens after one of these changes has gone through the exact same propose, wait, and cancel process as a normal large transfer. We wrote a dedicated test for this, **test_disablingGuardIsItselfDelayedAndVetoable**, and used it to check every other setting too. Turning the protection off is now protected by the same protection.

**Self-Sovereignty**

**VIGIL** is a self custodied smart account. You hold both keys, the contract holds the funds, and no third party ever has custody or approval power. It fits the track's own call for a smart account wallet with a real policy engine, built around the specific case of a compromised everyday key rather than general session keys or bundlers.

**Censorship Resistance**

Once a queued action has cleared its delay and was not cancelled, **executeAction** can be called by anyone, not just the owner or a fixed relayer. No single party has to stay online or can be pressured into withholding a transfer that was already approved, so finishing a legitimate payment never depends on one gatekeeper.

**Decentralized Coordination Layers**

The owner and guardian are a small two party protocol enforced entirely by the contract, with no backend and no central service coordinating them. Neither key alone can both move funds and silence the other, and the rules that govern that relationship can only change by going through the same rules, which is the kind of trustless coordination logic the track asks for.

### NULLIUS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nullius-1a2f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lookslikeom/Nullius) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://lookslikeom.github.io/Nullius/pitch.html) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1216695573?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20To%20Devcon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-iitr.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Trust Was Never the Protocol !

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. A local chain made valid proofs prove the wrong state**

A stray Anvil process on our RPC port reported a different chain (31337), causing our anchor selection to use an invalidly old block. Proofs were technically valid but against the wrong chain. We fixed this by validating chain IDs and anchoring to the highest block confirmed by at least two independent endpoints. We also correctly distinguish proven zero/absence from missing data.

**2. Our best demo moment was invisible**

Our malicious RPC was correctly detected, but the UI only showed the failure as text because the first valid proof won the race. We now retain and visualize failed proof paths, making the exact point where a forged proof breaks visible to the audience.

**3. Public RPCs and local forks couldn't reliably serve proofs**

Anvil forks inherited upstream **eth_getProof** rate limits, while some public endpoints throttled or refused proofs. We moved to two independent public mainnet endpoints plus our malicious proxy, giving us real mainnet proofs and cross-provider corroboration. Verified results are also cached by address + state root.

**4. Noir's API changed underneath our ZK circuit**

The Poseidon/Keccak hashing APIs we planned to use had changed in Noir 1.0. We switched to Poseidon2 and built a self-consistent, tested circuit, while explicitly marking its JavaScript-side integration as incomplete rather than claiming unsupported ZK functionality.

**5. Making the proof visualization consistent was harder than expected**

Proofs have different depths, making naive scaling distort the visualization. After three iterations, we fixed the row height and scale limits and used browser debug measurements to guarantee consistent rendering across proof states.

**The problem it solves**

When your wallet shows you a balance, that number came from a company.

Your wallet asked a server how much ETH an address holds. The server answered. Your wallet drew the answer on the screen. That is the entire exchange. There is no signature, no proof, and no check anywhere in it. The number you are looking at is a claim, and your wallet believes it the way you believe a stranger who tells you the time. 

This is true of nearly everything you see in crypto: your balance, your token holdings, whether a transaction went through, what a contract currently holds. It all arrives as an unverified assertion from a server you do not control, and every interface presents it as fact.

Three things make that worse than it sounds. A very large share of Ethereum reads flow through a handful of companies. A lying server looks exactly like an honest one, because there is no error and no warning, and the interface renders a lie in the same font as the truth. And if an attacker can make your wallet believe a false balance or a false allowance, they can walk you into signing something you never would have signed.

**Self-Sovereignty**

The smart account is only as sovereign as the endpoint telling it what state it is in, which is the gap we close. Plus Sybil resistance that costs capital instead of privacy.

**Censorship Resistance**

The verifying read path, the relay measurement, and the per transaction flight recorder. This track's brief suggests an RPC aggregator that reaches consensus among providers, and our submission argues that is the weaker primitive and ships the stronger one instead.

**Decentralized Coordination Layers**

Group signalling with no platform in the middle, whose anti Sybil defence is cryptographic and capital based rather than a registry, and which reveals nothing about its members.

### deadHand
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/deadhand-7b13) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gylshaurya/Deadhand) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gylshaurya.github.io/Deadhand/#/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1216695730?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20To%20Devcon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-iitr.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A dead man's switch where nobody holds the key.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

If you are holding a document that someone powerful wants buried, your options today are
to trust a newspaper, a lawyer, or a company. All three can be pressured, and all three
have been.

Deadhand lets you seal a document and set a check-in interval. Keep checking in and
nothing happens. Stop, and the document decrypts itself in public at a deadline fixed in
advance. Nobody can be pressured into releasing it early, because nobody holds the key.

The document's key is encrypted to a **future round of the drand beacon**, a public
randomness network that signs a value every 3 seconds. The signature that decrypts it does
not exist yet, anywhere. It comes into existence on schedule, and then anyone can open the
document. No server, no custodian, and no transaction from anyone.

Existing tools in this space split your key among paid custodians who promise to forget.
it. That is an ongoing cost, a liveness assumption, and a group that can be bribed or.
subpoenaed into opening your file early. We removed that group entirely.

**Who it is for:** journalists protecting a source file, whistleblowers who need insurance.
before they go public, and activists who need something to outlive their arrest.

**Challenges we ran into**

**The hurdle that redefined the project.** We planned for a check-in to push the deadline
back. Our first test proved that is impossible: a published timelock capsule cannot be
extended. If a capsule opens at round R, anyone who saved a copy opens it at round R, and
nothing you do later takes that back. This is precisely why older systems needed paid
custodians, since only a human who agrees to re-share your key can move a deadline.

We redesigned around it. A check-in now **rotates** instead of extending: derive a fresh
key, re-encrypt the document under it, seal that key to a later round, and unpin the
previous copy of the file. The old capsule still opens on schedule and still gives up a
real, working key, but that key now decrypts a file nobody has any more. A check-in
removes availability, not secrecy.

We turned the objection into a feature. The app has a "Try to break it" panel that pulls
old capsules back out of transaction calldata so anyone can replay one and watch a valid
key land on a 404.

**The bug that cost us the most time.** Sealed documents never opened in the UI, even
though the same code worked in Node. The chain poll rebuilt the switch object every 1.5
seconds, which retriggered a React effect whose cleanup cancelled the in-flight beacon
fetch. That fetch takes about 1.4 seconds, so it was cancelled every single time and the
result was never committed. It looked exactly like a broken timelock. The fix was to
depend on the fields that actually change the answer instead of the object identity, and
to read the latest object through a ref. We also stopped swallowing errors in that path,
since a reader that silently stays "sealed" is indistinguishable from a broken product.

**Self-Sovereignty**

The track asks for users to hold their own capability instead of renting it from a
provider. Every existing tool in this space asks you to hand key shares to somebody. We
require you to hand nothing to anybody.

- No custodian, no shard-holder network, no quorum holds any part of your key.
- The encryption key is derived from a signature made with your own wallet, so it is
  recoverable on any device from the key that controls the switch. There is no recovery
  file to lose or have taken.
- All encryption happens in the browser. The key never reaches a server, including ours.
- The owner alone can rotate, stand down, or force an early release.

**Censorship Resistance**

The track asks for tools that remove single points of control from the path a user
depends on. Publishing is exactly that path here, and we removed every controllable point
from it.

- There is no server or company in the release path, so there is nobody to serve an order
  on. Taking our site down does not stop a release.
- The capsule sits on-chain in public. Anyone can open it with about 20 lines of code, so
  the front-end is a convenience and not a dependency.
- Once the beacon reaches the round, release needs no transaction from anyone and cannot
  be recalled. There is no step left for an adversary to block.
- The failure mode is early release, never silent suppression, which is the correct
  direction for a censorship-resistant tool.

**Decentralized Coordination Layers**

The track asks for coordination that does not route through a platform or an operator.
Ours is coordinated entirely by a public randomness beacon and verified in the open.

- Release timing is coordinated by drand, which never sees your ciphertext, does not know
  the switch exists, and signs the same rounds for everyone. It cannot single you out.
- No operator, keeper, or voting quorum decides when anything happens.
- Independent readers can attest on-chain to what they read. Several unrelated addresses
  converging on the same hash is public evidence that no single front-end fabricated the
  contents, which is a decentralized substitute for a trusted publisher.

### Handover

> Tap & verify. Pay with Prava. Ownership transfers.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

1) **Prava** sandbox device binding kept failing with an opaque 409. I drove the checkout with browser automation and network inspection and discovered a specific shared test card was "poisoned" sandbox-wide - switching to another documented test card fixed passkey enrollment instantly.

2) **WebAuthn** does not work inside in-app browsers (Gmail), and Prava's 15-minute session expiry includes the passkey step - learned both the hard way, solved with fresh sessions, a properly enrolled passkey, and moving fast.

3) **The hero item's** token was owned by a wallet lost in an app reinstall. Instead of giving up, I recovered it live using TAGITCore's AIRP recovery protocol (flag -> 2-of-N approveResolve -> resolve) - a blocker turned into a demonstration of the platform's recovery feature, visible in the token's on-chain history.

4) The Prava sandbox has no webhooks, so I built an idempotent polling state machine (created -> awaiting_card -> token_minted -> approved -> transferred) with revoke-on-fail on every unhappy path: DECLINED, timeout, expiry.

**The problem it solves**

P2P resale is a ~$200B/yr market that breaks at the handoff: buyers can't trust the item, sellers can't trust the payment, and escrow middlemen take 10-25% and days to settle. AI agents can't participate at all - there is no machine-readable trust signal for physical goods and no settlement primitive tying "payment cleared" to "ownership transferred".

Handover fixes both sides at once. Every product carries a tamper-proof NFC chip (NXP NTAG 424 DNA TT) bound to an on-chain digital twin NFT. A buyer agent (GPT-4o tool-calling) reads a block-pinned, independently re-derivable verdict - authentic, unflagged, CLAIMED - before a single cent moves. Payment runs through Prava: a single-use card credential, merchant-locked to the seller and amount-locked to the exact price, approved by the buyer's real biometric passkey.

The settlement rule that makes it atomic: Prava's report-status APPROVED is the one and only trigger for the on-chain ownership transfer (TAGITCore.transferAsset on Base Sepolia). Declined or timeout -> session revoked, nothing moves. Remove Prava and the product cannot settle - the payment IS the settlement layer, not a checkout bolt-on.

The refusal path is a first-class feature: a flagged (lost/stolen/recalled) item is rejected before any payment session is even created - the card is never born.

Everything in the demo is real: a real NXP chip tap, a real agent enforcing "genuine and under $120", a real Touch ID passkey, a real single-use network token, and a real confirmed transaction - the item lands in the buyer's actual TAG IT vault app. Settlement tx: https://sepolia.basescan.org/tx/0x5b2f49fb74eb441a5626aabf3467bb5c40f78731a0d837b593ee21a85e379fca

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Handover's payment rail is Visa Intelligent Commerce end to end, via Prava: the agent initiates checkout, the cardholder consents with a real WebAuthn biometric passkey, and Visa's network issues a single-use tokenized credential that is merchant-locked to the seller and amount-locked to the exact price ($89.00) with a 30-minute lifetime. The demo shows the credential minting on camera (masked PAN), and the credential's approval is what releases the physical asset's on-chain ownership transfer - agent-initiated, consumer-consented, token-secured commerce exactly as the Intelligent Commerce model intends. Bonus: for physical goods we pair Visa-side trust with goods-side trust (NFC-chip digital twins), so the agent can prove WHAT it is buying before it pays.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Handover extends a real, operating company - TAG IT Network: tamper-proof NFC chips in stock, TAGITCore contract live on Base Sepolia, verify.tagit.network in production, consumer app on TestFlight. This weekend added the missing revenue layer: agent-driven settlement. The business model is a settlement take-rate on P2P resale, competing with escrow services that charge 10-25% and take days - Handover settles in about sixty seconds. eBay's authentication-guarantee program proves buyers pay for trust in secondary markets; Handover makes that trust programmable and agent-accessible. Everything in the demo runs on infrastructure we own end-to-end: chips, contract, verification rails, settlement.

**OpenAI**

The buyer agent is GPT-4o with function calling (get_listings, verify_item, create_payment) under hard safety guardrails enforced server-side: it may not create a payment for any item that is not verified authentic, unflagged and CLAIMED on-chain, and it must respect the user's plain-language price limit ("genuine and under $120"). The model does the reasoning and the talking; the tools do the truth-telling. The refusal behavior is where it shines: shown a flagged item, the agent explains why and declines - no payment session is ever created. Autonomy with money requires exactly this shape: LLM judgment inside deterministic rails, with a human biometric consent gate before any spend.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

One sentence in, one fingerprint, done. The user types a plain-language instruction; the agent's reasoning streams as live step cards (verify -> price check -> payment -> settlement) with a persistent state tracker (session -> passkey -> token -> approved -> transferred), honest pending states, and a clickable on-chain receipt. Payment approval is a single Touch ID. Refusals are equally clear: a flagged item shows a red card and the words "no payment was created". Trust needs legibility - the UX makes every invisible guarantee visible.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

An agent that finishes the job: it verifies a physical item's authenticity on-chain, enforces the user's price limit, takes payment through Prava (single-use, merchant-locked card credential approved by a real biometric passkey), and atomically transfers ownership on Base Sepolia - report-status APPROVED is the only trigger for the transfer. Real transaction in the demo: https://sepolia.basescan.org/tx/0x5b2f49fb74eb441a5626aabf3467bb5c40f78731a0d837b593ee21a85e379fca. Prava is structurally unremovable: without it the product cannot settle.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. LLM Syntax Hallucinations in Anchor Rust Patches
- **Challenge**: Standard LLMs often fail to generate syntactically correct Anchor Rust code—frequently omitting lifetime parameters (e.g. `Context<Withdraw<'_>>`), breaking Anchor macro expansions, or introducing ownership/borrow checker errors.
- **Solution**: We implemented a RAG pipeline using ChromaDB populated with real-world Solana security audit cases. We engineered specialized prompt templates (`miso_patch_prompt.txt`) that instruct the LLM to output precise line-by-line diffs with strict Anchor syntax rules, and integrated AST-level validations before surfacing patches to developers.

### 2. Cross-Language Bridge (Node.js CLI to Python RAG Pipeline)
- **Challenge**: Node.js is great for fast terminal CLIs and interactive menus, but Python is the standard ecosystem for vector stores (ChromaDB, LangChain). Running a heavy persistent Python daemon for a fast CLI tool was impractical.
- **Solution**: Built an asynchronous, lightweight JSON-over-stdio IPC subprocess bridge (`ragBridge.js` $\leftrightarrow$ `retrieval.py`). The CLI executes python RAG retrieval on demand only during `miso patch`, keeping all other CLI operations ultra-fast and independent.

### 3. Deterministic vs. Non-Deterministic Scoring Alignment
- **Challenge**: Relying solely on static regex/AST parsing leads to high false positives, while relying purely on LLM scoring causes score variance between runs.
- **Solution**: Designed a hybrid scoring formula combining deterministic static AST rule evaluations (25% weight) with deep LLM semantic code analysis (75% weight), bounded by a margin metric. This creates consistent, repeatable confidence scores ranging from 0–100.

### 4. Safe In-Place File Patching & Rollbacks
- **Challenge**: Automatically modifying developer Rust source code in-place carries high risk of accidental code loss or unwanted changes.
- **Solution**: Developed a fail-safe patch applicator (`patchApplicator.js`) that automatically creates timestamped backups (`.bak`) before any mutation, verifies file target ranges, allows instant rollbacks, and provides interactive diff preview screens.

### 5. Multi-Tiered API Provider Management
- **Challenge**: Rate limits and key management across Google Gemini and Groq LLMs.
- **Solution**: Created a centralized provider client (`llmClient.js` & `config.js`) supporting hot-swappable providers, environment variable fallbacks, and CLI key management (`miso provider-gsk_...`).

---

## 🛡️ Solana Security Rules Covered

| Rule ID | Severity | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MISSING_SIGNER_CHECK` | 🔴 Critical | Accounts modified without verifying `is_signer` flag |
| `MISSING_OWNERSHIP_CHECK` | 🔴 Critical | Account owner constraint missing (untrusted account data) |
| `PDA_BUMP_UNVALIDATED` | 🟠 High | Using unverified PDA bump seeds instead of canonical bump |
| `UNCONSTRAINED_CPI` | 🟠 High | Invoking target program via CPI without verifying program ID |
| `UNSAFE_ACCOUNT_CLOSE` | 🟠 High | Closing accounts without zeroing data or clearing lamports |
| `UNCHECKED_ARITHMETIC` | 🟡 Medium | Raw arithmetic operations prone to overflow/underflow |
| `MISSING_RENT_EXEMPTION` | 🟡 Medium | Account initialization missing explicit rent-exemption checks |

**The problem it solves**

**MISO** (Miso Smart Inspector & Optimizer) is an end-to-end security auditing and remediation platform built specifically for **Solana & Anchor Rust smart contracts**. It bridges the gap between static rule-based analysis, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) powered by real Solana audit datasets, and interactive AI-driven code patching—all integrated directly into the developer's terminal workflow and synced with an interactive web dashboard.

---

## 🎯 The Problem It Solves

### 1. High Vulnerability Rates in Solana Smart Contracts
Solana smart contracts written in Rust/Anchor are prone to critical security vulnerabilities such as:
- **Missing Signer / Owner Checks**: Allowing unauthorized account access or fund draining.
- **Unconstrained Cross-Program Invocations (CPIs)**: Allowing arbitrary program execution.
- **PDA Bump Unvalidation**: Enabling spoofed Program Derived Addresses.
- **Unsafe Account Closing & Rent Exemption Flaws**: Exposing accounts to re-initialization attacks.
- **Unchecked Arithmetic**: Causing integer overflows/underflows.

### 2. Manual & Costly Security Audits
Traditional smart contract security audits are manual, expensive (ranging from tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars), and slow down rapid development iterations.

### 3. LLM Hallucinations in Code Remediation
While generic LLMs can suggest code, they frequently generate syntactically invalid Rust/Anchor code, fail to account for Anchor framework constraints (e.g. lifetime parameters, account validation macros), or break existing logic when patching.

### 4. Fragmented Developer Workflows
Existing tools either run only static analysis in CI/CD or operate as separate web interfaces. Developers lack a **terminal-native tool** that scans code locally, presents VS Code-style inline diffs, auto-applies verified patches with rollbacks, and security-gates deployments.

---

## 🔥 Key Features

- 🛡️ **Hybrid Audit Engine**: Combines 7 Solana-specific deterministic static security rules with semantic LLM inspection to calculate a weighted **Confidence Score** (`75% AI Score + 25% Static Score`).
- 🧠 **RAG-Powered AI Auto-Patcher**: Leverages ChromaDB vector embeddings trained on real Solana security audit datasets (`solana_security_audit_dataset.jsonl`) to retrieve relevant vulnerability contexts and generate precise Rust security patches.
- 🖥️ **VS Code-Style Terminal Diffs**: Interactive CLI prompt presenting side-by-side/inline unified diffs, auto-backup creation (`.bak`), interactive patch approval (`[A]pply`, `[S]kip`, `[V]iew`, `[M]anual`), and re-scanning.
- 🚪 **Security-Gated Deployment (`miso deploy`)**: Prevents deploying contracts to Solana devnet/mainnet if the security score drops below a configurable threshold (default: `90/100`).
- 📝 **Automated Audit Logs (`MISO.md`)**: Generates an append-only audit trail markdown file tracking scans, confidence scores, and historical vulnerability trends.
- 🌐 **MISO Hub & Web Platform**: Sleek React/Vite web application featuring 3D visualizers, live audit reporting, documentation, and Neon PostgreSQL database synchronization.

---

**Best Use of Gemini API**

MISO utilizes the Gemini API across two core domains:

Vector Embeddings (RAG Pipeline): Using Gemini's text embedding models (gemini-embedding-001) via Python LangChain to build and query the ChromaDB vector database of Solana security audits.
Generative LLM (Audit & Patch Engine): Using Gemini LLM models (gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-1.5-flash, gemini-1.5-pro) via direct REST API calls in Node.js for code scanning, vulnerability explanation, and precise code patch generation.

**Best Use of Solana**

MISO utilizes Solana across its auditing engine, deployment workflow, and security knowledge base:

1. 🛡️ Solana & Anchor Framework Target Focus
MISO is purpose-built to audit smart contracts written for the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM) in Rust (both native solana_program and the Anchor Framework anchor_lang).

It analyzes core Solana architecture concepts:

Account Validation & Signers: Checking Signer<'info> and is_signer flags on mutable accounts.
Program Derived Addresses (PDAs): Verifying seed derivation and canonical bump seed validation (find_program_address).
Cross-Program Invocations (CPIs): Ensuring target program IDs are verified before executing invoke or invoke_signed.
Account Closure & Rent Exemption: Ensuring lamports are drained and account data is zeroed when closing accounts to prevent re-initialization exploits.

**Open Innovation**

MISO fits the Open Innovation track by addressing a broad challenge faced by Solana developers: making smart contract security and deployment more accessible. Our CLI automates the development workflow by performing static security analysis, identifying common vulnerabilities, generating AI-assisted audit insights, and streamlining deployment to Solana. Instead of requiring multiple tools and deep security expertise, developers can audit and deploy contracts from a single interface. Because MISO is blockchain-agnostic in concept and designed to be extensible, it can be adapted to support additional ecosystems and security checks in the future, making it a practical tool with applications across Web3 development.

**Best Beginner's team**

As beginner Solana developers, we noticed that learning Rust and Anchor framework comes with a steep security learning curve...one missing signer check or unconstrained CPI can lead to millions in exploits. We built MISO as the security tool we wished we had when we started: an interactive terminal mentor and auto-patcher that teaches developers Solana security best practices while keeping their contracts secure.

**The problem it solves**

People with diabetes often do not notice early signs of foot problems, leading to painful ulcers and serious complications. Our smart slipper helps by continuously checking foot pressure and temperature while the user walks or stands. If it detects unusual changes, it immediately alerts the user with a buzzer and sends data for monitoring. 
This allows for early identification of problems, reducing the risk of severe infections and hospital visits. The device makes foot care for diabetics easier, safer, and more convenient for everyday use.

**Challenges we ran into**

Connecting the ESP32 to Firebase was the tricky hurdle.After troubleshooting Wi-Fi and Firebase settings, we achieved a stable link.
This fix made the system more accurate and reliable overall.

**Gemini**

The Google Gemini API adds intelligence to our system by analyzing sensor data and spotting meaningful patterns. Instead of just showing raw values, it provides clear health insights and recommendations, making the solution smarter and easier for users to understand.

**ElevenLabs**

We used ElevenLabs to give the system a natural voice, delivering clear spoken alerts whenever a risk is detected. This makes warnings easier to understand, especially for elderly users, and adds an interactive, accessible touch to the experience.

**Sarvam.ai**

We brought in Sarvam AI to make our system more inclusive and easy to use. It converts sensor data and risk alerts into clear messages in regional languages, so patients who aren’t comfortable with English can still understand them. With voice-based communication, users receive spoken health updates in a natural way. This improves accessibility and ensures the technology can support a wider range of diabetic patients.

**IoT and Embedded System**

Our project sits right at the intersection of embedded systems and IoT. On the embedded side, the ESP32 gathers data from the pressure sensors and potentiometer, processes it, and triggers the buzzer whenever a risk is detected. At the same time, it connects to Firebase over Wi-Fi, sending the data for real-time monitoring. This means caregivers and users can check the information remotely, without being physically present. By linking sensors, a microcontroller, and cloud services, we’ve built a practical IoT-based healthcare solution that blends local processing with remote accessibility.

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement
Urban flooding is often detected only after roads become submerged and drains overflow. Existing systems mainly monitor reservoirs, rivers, and rainfall but lack visibility into local drainage networks where flooding actually begins. Citizens receive limited hyperlocal warnings, authorities struggle to identify vulnerable drainage assets, and sanitation workers face life-threatening risks from toxic sewer gases. There is currently no unified platform that combines flood prediction, drainage intelligence, sewer safety, citizen awareness, and municipal decision support.
Solution
HydroMind Sentinel is an AI-powered Urban Drainage Intelligence and Sewer Safety Platform.
The system uses an ESP32, waterproof ultrasonic sensor, and methane sensor to continuously monitor drainage conditions. Combined with government rainfall data, machine learning models predict flood risk, estimate Time-To-Flood, forecast future water levels, detect drainage anomalies, and evaluate sewer safety conditions.

Real-time Drain Monitoring
Time-To-Flood Prediction
Flood Escalation Forecasting
AI Flood Risk Assessment
Drainage Digital Twin

Urban Risk Score
Sewer Safety Index
Worker Entry Clearance System

Safe Zone Finder

Community Reporting System

Sarvam AI Multilingual Voice Alerts
MongoDB Flood Memory Layer
n8n Automated Emergency Workflows
The platform includes both a Citizen Portal and a Municipal Command Center, enabling proactive disaster management and public safety.
Impact
For Citizens
Receive early flood warnings before overflow occurs
Access live risk maps and AI-generated safety guidance
Find nearby safe zones and safer travel routes
Receive alerts through voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and web notifications
Report flooding and waterlogging directly from the platform
For Municipal Authorities
Monitor drainage assets in real time
Prioritize maintenance using Drain Health Scores
Detect drainage anomalies and possible obstructions
Forecast flood escalation and recovery timelines
Generate AI-powered incident reports and recommendations
Improve emergency response efficiency
For Sanitation Workers
Monitor methane hazards inside drainage systems
Receive worker safety alerts
Reduce risk during inspection and maintenance operations
Social Impact
HydroMind Sentinel helps transform flood management from reactive response to proactive prevention. By combining AI, IoT, multilingual communication, and smart-city analytics, it can reduce flood damage, improve public safety, protect sanitation workers, and support resilient urban infrastructure for flood-prone cities like Chennai.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was obtaining reliable drainage and flood-related datasets. While government sources provide rainfall and flood-event information, detailed drainage-level sensor data and sewer safety datasets were not publicly available. To overcome this, we combined official rainfall records with domain-driven synthetic data generation and built realistic datasets for flood-risk prediction, drainage behavior, recovery estimation, and sewer safety analysis.
Another challenge was integrating multiple technologies including ESP32 hardware, ultrasonic water-level sensing, methane monitoring, AI services, automation workflows, and database systems into a single platform. We solved this by designing a modular architecture where MongoDB Atlas acts as the data layer, n8n manages automation, Gemini generates AI-driven insights, and Sarvam provides multilingual voice alerts.
We also faced challenges in making complex flood analytics understandable for both citizens and municipal authorities. To address this, we developed separate Citizen and Admin portals, ensuring that citizens receive simple AI-generated summaries and safety recommendations, while authorities gain access to advanced analytics, digital twin monitoring, and decision-support tools.
Finally, ensuring real-time communication between sensors, predictive models, AI services, and the dashboard required careful optimization of data flow, API integration, and alert automation to create a seamless end-to-end system.

**Best Hack Built using n8n**

HydroMind Sentinel uses n8n as its central automation and orchestration engine, enabling fully automated flood monitoring and emergency response workflows.
The platform continuously receives sensor data from ESP32-based drainage monitoring nodes. n8n automatically processes incoming data, stores it in MongoDB Atlas, triggers machine learning predictions, invokes Gemini AI for flood analysis and decision support, and uses Sarvam AI to generate multilingual voice alerts.
Automated Workflow
ESP32 Sensor Data → MongoDB Atlas Storage → Flood Risk Prediction → Time-To-Flood Calculation → Gemini AI Situation Analysis → Sarvam AI Voice Alert Generation → SMS / WhatsApp / Voice Notification → Incident Logging → Dashboard Updates
Additional n8n Workflows
Automatic incident report generation
Community report processing
Critical risk escalation workflows
Alert distribution and notification management
Historical event archival
Recovery monitoring and updates
By using n8n as the automation backbone, HydroMind Sentinel reduces manual intervention, enables real-time decision-making, and creates an end-to-end intelligent emergency response system capable of scaling from a single drainage node to a city-wide deployment.
Impact
n8n transforms HydroMind from a monitoring dashboard into an autonomous flood intelligence platform that can sense, analyze, communicate, and respond to flood risks in real time. This significantly improves emergency preparedness, response speed, and public safety.

**IoT and Embedded System**

HydroMind Sentinel is built on an IoT-based sensing architecture that enables continuous real-time monitoring of urban drainage systems and sewer environments.

**The problem it solves**

Our project is an offline first healthcare system designed to solve three major gaps in healthcare: patient access, government preparedness, and hospital efficiency.

report says **41% of India’s population does not access the internet**,

In many rural and low-network areas, patients cannot depend on internet-based apps. So our system works even without Wi-Fi,  or cellular network. A health worker which is an AI agent in our case can collect symptoms and vitals. The system then classifies the patient into Green, Orange, or Red risk and basis on the risk level aid will be provided and multiple agents will work together in finding the aid like best doctors, nearest hospitals and ambulance if needed  routes them to the correct care pathway — our 5 main diseases we worked on are pregnancy, menstrual/PCOS, diabetes, hypertension, or child pneumonia.

The second module is the Government Heatmap Helpline. Every patient call to the agent becomes an early warning signal. If fever, diarrhea, respiratory illness, or maternal risk starts increasing in a particular area, the government dashboard shows it as a heatmap. It also shows medicine availability, doctor availability, ambulance pressure, and AI action recommendations. So instead of reacting after hospitals are full, the government can prepare earlier.

WHO says **1 in every 10 patients is harmed in healthcare**, and more than **3 million deaths occur annually due to unsafe care**.

The third module is hospital automation software. Doctors and nurses spend a lot of time on documentation, patient tracking,  which over burdens them and creates fatigue. Our system gives doctors, nurses, and admins a real-time dashboard. It tracks vitals, medicine schedules, missed tasks, lab reports giving an automated approach to hospital systems.

What makes our solution powerful is that all three systems are connected together. it is a full on end to end system.

Our final vision is simple: healthcare should not stop when the internet stops, and disease response should not begin only after hospitals are overloaded.

**Challenges we ran into**

Technical Challenges
Building a healthcare system that works completely offline, not just in poor network conditions.
Designing safe healthcare recommendations without giving unsafe medical advice.
Creating disease pathways for multiple conditions while keeping the user flow simple.
Synchronizing offline patient records with cloud databases once connectivity returns.
Handling different user types: patients, health workers, doctors, nurses, hospital admins, and government officials.
Converting unstructured symptom descriptions into structured healthcare data.
Designing AI agents that collaborate without generating conflicting recommendations.
Building a scalable architecture that supports patient care, government intelligence, and hospital automation simultaneously.

**Gemini**

### How We Used Gemini

We used **Google Gemini as the intelligence layer** of the system to understand symptoms, assist decision-making, generate recommendations, and automate healthcare workflows.

---

## 1. Patient Intake Understanding

Patients often describe symptoms in natural language such as:

> "I've had fever for three days, dizziness, and difficulty breathing."

Gemini converts this unstructured conversation into structured healthcare data:

```json
{
  "symptoms": ["fever", "dizziness", "breathing difficulty"],
  "severity": "high",
  "recommendedPathway": "Child Pneumonia"
}
```

This removes the need for patients to fill complicated medical forms.

---

## 2. Personalized Care Pathways

After symptoms are collected, Gemini helps generate:

* personalized guidance
* follow-up recommendations
* lifestyle suggestions
* warning signs to monitor
* referral recommendations

Examples:

* Pregnancy danger-sign guidance
* PCOS support recommendations
* Diabetes management advice
* Hypertension lifestyle guidance
* Child pneumonia care instructions

---

## 3. Multi-Agent Decision Making

Gemini powers several AI agents:

* Intake Agent
* Recall Agent
* Triage Agent
* Disease Pathway Agent
* Safety Agent
* Recommendation Agent

These agents work together to understand the patient's condition and provide appropriate next steps.

---

## 4. Government Intelligence Module

Gemini analyzes aggregated healthcare data and generates:

* district-level insights
* outbreak summaries
* resource recommendations
* medicine demand alerts
* ambulance deployment suggestions
* doctor allocation suggestions

Example:

> "Fever and respiratory complaints have increased by 35% in District A during the last week. Additional medicines and one mobile medical unit are recommended."

---

## 5. Hospital Automation Module

Gemini helps automate hospital workflows by generating:

* patient summaries
* nurse handover notes
* discharge summaries
* doctor round summaries
* task prioritization suggestions
* critical patient alerts

This reduces documentation workload for healthcare staff.

---

## 6. Why Gemini Was Important

Without Gemini:

* Staff manually review symptoms.
* Government officers manually analyze reports.
* Doctors and nurses manually write summaries.

With Gemini:

* Symptoms become structured data.
* Recommendations are generated automatically.
* Hospital documentation is streamlined.
* Government dashboards receive actionable insights.

---

## 2. Multi-Agent Architecture

### OICE
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/oice-440c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/avicdr/open-innovation-contribution-escrow) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/18WNSK8xxwrkwzn4XAfzg2np71bnKrnU7/view?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Missing Layer Between Ideas and Execution.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Innovation often fails not because of a lack of ideas, but because of a lack of coordination, trust, and incentives. Today, founders, researchers, students, and communities rely on disconnected tools such as GitHub, Notion, Discord, Jira, and spreadsheets to manage contributors and track progress. These tools help organize work, but they do not solve the fundamental challenge of ensuring contributors are rewarded fairly and transparently for their contributions.

For early-stage projects, it is difficult to:

* Attract and coordinate contributors.
* Define clear milestones and ownership.
* Ensure funds are distributed fairly.
* Track who contributed what.
* Build trust between project owners and contributors.

As a result, many promising ideas never progress beyond the planning stage, while contributors often hesitate to participate because compensation and recognition are uncertain.

How OICE Solves This

OICE (Open Innovation Contribution Escrow) creates a trustless innovation coordination layer where projects, contributors, milestones, and funding are managed in a single platform.

Project owners can:

* Create innovation projects.
* Define milestones and contribution bounties.
* Lock funds into blockchain-backed escrow.
* Review and approve submitted work.
* Automatically distribute rewards upon completion.

Contributors can:

* Discover projects aligned with their skills.
* Claim tasks and submit deliverables.
* Build a verifiable contribution history.
* Receive transparent, guaranteed rewards.

Why This Matters

By combining open collaboration with escrow-backed incentives, OICE makes it significantly easier and safer to coordinate innovation across distributed teams. Instead of relying on trust, manual payments, and fragmented tools, participants operate within a transparent system where expectations, contributions, and rewards are clearly defined.

Potential use cases include:

* Startup product development
* Open-source software funding
* Research and academic collaboration
* Hackathons and innovation challenges
* DAO and community-driven initiatives
* Student project coordination
* Public-good and social impact projects

OICE enables anyone to transform an idea into a coordinated, funded, and executable project while ensuring contributors are fairly rewarded for the value they create.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

1. Designing Fair Contribution Verification

One of the biggest challenges was determining how project owners could verify contributions without making the approval process overly complex. Contributors may submit many different types of work, including research documents, designs, code, and smart contracts. This made it difficult to create a universal validation system.

To address this, we introduced milestone based submissions where deliverables are attached directly to specific project checkpoints. This provides a structured review process while remaining flexible enough to support different contribution types.

2. Escrow and Reward Distribution Logic

Implementing escrow backed rewards introduced several edge cases. We needed to ensure that funds remained secure while still allowing project owners to approve work and distribute rewards efficiently. Managing milestone approvals, partial project completion, and reward allocation required careful smart contract design to prevent funds from becoming locked or distributed incorrectly.

We solved this by separating project management logic from fund custody logic and implementing clear approval workflows before any reward distribution can occur.

3. AI Generated Project Planning

A key feature of OICE is its AI copilot, which helps transform vague ideas into actionable project plans. Early versions frequently generated unrealistic milestones, duplicate tasks, or plans that were too generic to be useful.

We improved results through iterative prompt engineering, structured output schemas, and validation layers that force the AI to produce measurable milestones, realistic timelines, and contributor friendly task breakdowns.

4. Coordinating Complex Project State

Projects can move through multiple stages including creation, funding, milestone approval, contribution submission, review, and reward distribution. Keeping frontend state synchronized with backend data while maintaining a responsive user experience proved challenging.

We addressed this by introducing a clearer state management architecture, strict validation rules, and predictable status transitions throughout the platform.

5. Building a Unified Experience

Many existing collaboration tools solve only part of the problem. Combining project management, contributor coordination, AI planning, and blockchain escrow into a single cohesive experience required significant iteration on both architecture and user experience.

We overcame this by continuously refining the workflow and focusing on a simple principle: every feature should help move an idea one step closer to execution.

**Gemini**

OICE uses Gemini as an intelligent project copilot that transforms vague ideas into structured, executable innovation projects.

When a user submits an idea, Gemini analyzes the concept and generates a complete project framework, including milestones, deliverables, timelines, risks, contributor roles, and success criteria. This helps founders and innovators move from an unstructured idea to an actionable roadmap within minutes.

Gemini is also used to:

* Analyze project proposals and identify potential risks and gaps.
* Generate milestone based execution plans.
* Recommend contributor roles and responsibilities.
* Evaluate contribution submissions against project objectives.
* Provide contextual guidance throughout the project lifecycle.
* Help project owners coordinate complex innovation efforts with less manual planning.

Without Gemini, project owners would need to manually define project structures, milestones, and contribution requirements. By embedding Gemini directly into the workflow, OICE significantly reduces planning overhead and enables users to launch and manage collaborative innovation projects faster and more effectively.

Gemini serves as the intelligence layer of OICE, helping transform ideas into organized, fundable, and executable projects.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB serves as the primary data layer powering OICE's innovation ecosystem. The platform manages highly connected and rapidly evolving data, including projects, milestones, contributors, submissions, reward pools, escrow transactions, AI generated plans, and project activity.

Using MongoDB enables OICE to efficiently store and query complex project structures while maintaining the flexibility needed for projects at different stages of development. As ideas evolve into active collaborations, project requirements, milestones, contributor roles, and submissions can change dynamically without requiring rigid database schemas.

MongoDB is used to:

* Store projects, milestones, and contribution workflows.
* Manage contributor profiles and contribution histories.
* Track submission reviews and approval states.
* Persist AI generated project plans and analyses.
* Maintain project activity feeds and collaboration records.
* Support real time updates across the platform.

The flexibility and scalability of MongoDB make it well suited for an open innovation platform where every project may have unique structures, workflows, and collaboration patterns. MongoDB enables OICE to provide a seamless experience while supporting the complex relationships between ideas, contributors, funding, and execution.

**Open Innovation**

How OICE Fits the Open Innovation Track

OICE is built specifically to enable open innovation by making it easier for people around the world to collaborate on ideas, contribute meaningful work, and be rewarded transparently for their contributions.

Traditional innovation efforts are often limited by organizational boundaries, fragmented tools, unclear ownership, and a lack of trust between project creators and contributors. OICE addresses these challenges by providing a platform where anyone can launch an idea, define milestones, attract contributors, and fund development through escrow backed reward pools.

Contributors can discover projects, submit work, build a verifiable contribution history, and receive rewards when their contributions are approved. Project owners can coordinate distributed teams, manage milestones, and ensure accountability throughout the project lifecycle.

By combining AI powered project planning, collaborative execution, and transparent reward distribution, OICE lowers the barriers to innovation and enables communities, startups, researchers, students, and builders to work together on solving real world problems.

At its core, OICE transforms innovation from a closed organizational process into an open, global, and incentive aligned ecosystem where great ideas can attract talent, funding, and execution regardless of who creates them.

**BlockChain & Web3**

OICE (Open Innovation Contribution Escrow) uses blockchain to solve one of the biggest challenges in collaborative innovation: trust.

Projects can create innovation bounties, define milestones, and lock reward funds in an on-chain escrow. Contributors submit work, project owners review deliverables, and approved contributions automatically trigger transparent reward distribution through smart contracts.

By moving contribution tracking, approvals, and payments onto the blockchain, OICE provides:

Transparent and auditable contribution history
Trustless escrow for bounty and milestone payments
Verifiable ownership and attribution of work
Reduced disputes through immutable records
Global participation without relying on centralized intermediaries

The platform combines AI-assisted project planning with decentralized coordination, enabling innovators, builders, designers, and researchers to collaborate and get rewarded fairly for their contributions.

OICE demonstrates a practical Web3 use case where blockchain is not just a payment layer but the foundation for transparent innovation management and contributor incentive alignment.

> Apna Digital Sahayak

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Applying for government documents in India often involves several common roadblocks for everyday citizens:

- Information Fragmentation: Guidelines, document requirements, and fee structures are scattered across multiple outdated portals.
- Complex Guidelines: Official rulebooks contain legal jargon that is difficult to interpret.
- Unexpected Rejections: Scans are often rejected due to minor mistakes (e.g. upload resolution, expiration states, or wrong document type), resulting in lost appointments and processing delays.
- Vague Timelines: Estimated durations listed on government portals do not reflect real-world waiting times at local centers.

CivicPilot solves this by bringing all instructions into a unified, digital notebook. It uses Google Gemini AI to analyze questions and check documents, and stores user progress and citizen feedback securely on MongoDB. This ensures that you always know what to prepare, where to apply, and what to expect.

CivicPilot is an intelligent, user-friendly digital handbook and checklist planner designed to help citizens understand and complete complex Indian government application processes. Getting documents like passports, driving licenses, or business permits in India can be confusing due to multiple departments, hidden fees, specific document rules, and long wait times. CivicPilot simplifies this by converting complex bureaucratic processes into clear, step-by-step roadmaps, auditing your documents using AI, tracking expiration dates, and hosting a community forum for real-time tips and compliance Q&As.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.Offline Syncing Conflicts
Hurdle: Merging offline progress (localStorage) with cloud database records without overwriting newer data.
Resolution: Developed a client-side union merge algorithm that combines local and remote completed checklist steps, pushed to MongoDB using a debounced 1-second delay.

2. PII (Personal Data) Storage Risk
Hurdle: Uploaded government documents (Aadhaar/PAN) could leak if stored permanently on the server.
Resolution: Configured an Express controller to read uploads into a temporary buffer, send them to Gemini, and trigger an immediate file deletion (fs.unlinkSync) inside a finally block.

3. Analytics Performance Bottleneck
Hurdle: Slow response times when fetching and sorting document expiration dates in JavaScript.
Resolution: Moved calculations to a MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline using $unwind, $cond, and date casting, reducing API payload sizes and response times by 90%.

> Near-Earth objects, near-instant insights

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Nodejs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nodejs-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Faced

1. Making the Dashboard Feel Truly Live

NASA's NeoWs API gives us snapshots of asteroid data—not actual real-time movement. So even if we showed everything correctly, the dashboard still felt kinda frozen. And because we wanted it to feel like a live radar system, static views just weren’t cutting it.

What we did:

Rather than calling the API over and over, we built a custom `useLiveTime` hook that updates every second, but on the client side. We take each asteroid’s velocity plus its miss-distance info, then estimate where it should be “right now.” In practice, this gives a smooth, live-tracking effect while keeping API calls lower and staying inside the free-tier limits. It’s like the page keeps breathing, instead of jumping between old frames.

2. Securing API Keys Without Building a Full Backend

Our project uses both NASA and Gemini APIs, but putting API keys directly in frontend code would’ve been a big security problem. Still, building a full backend felt overkill. Especially because this was a hackathon, and time was… you know, time.

What we did:

We created a lightweight Express proxy that also acts like Vercel serverless endpoints. That way, all API keys stay on the server side where they belong. It also removes the CORS headaches, and we can run the exact same approach for both local development and production, without rewriting everything twice or three times.

3. Dealing with Unpredictable AI Responses

On top of everything else, the AI-generated threat reports added a layer of uncertainty. Things like network delays, rate limits, or weird response structures could easily leave users stuck looking at a loading spinner—especially during a live demo. Nobody wants that moment where everything freezes, and you just smile.

What we did:

We added loading indicators, retry logic, and fallback messaging so the UI stays useful even when Gemini isn’t responding. We also put together a mock-data system with simulated asteroid information that automatically kicks in if the NASA API goes down. So the application remains fully functional even if external services become temporarily unavailable.

4. Simplifying NASA's Complex Data Structure

The raw NeoWs response is deeply nested and organized by date, which makes it difficult to use directly inside the frontend.

What we did:

We created a shared `normalize.js` utility that transforms the API response into a clean, flattened, and sorted list of asteroid objects. By keeping all the parsing and cleanup in one place, the frontend can focus entirely on displaying information and delivering a better user experience.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem

NASA tracks thousands of Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) every week through 
public APIs, but the data is dense, technical, and hard to interpret. 
Distances are given in kilometers or astronomical units, sizes in 
raw diameters, and risk levels in scientific classifications most 
people have never heard of. So when headlines mention an asteroid 
making a "close approach," there's no easy way for the average 
person to answer basic questions:

- How close is it actually — should this be concerning or not?
- How big is it, relative to something I can picture?
- Is there any real risk, explained without jargon?
- Where would this even be in the sky if I looked up?

## How NearMiss Helps

NearMiss takes NASA's raw NEO telemetry and Gemini's reasoning 
capabilities and turns them into a live, visual, easy-to-read 
dashboard:

- Live distance tracking — real-time counters show exactly how 
  far an asteroid is from Earth right now, with countdowns to its 
  closest approach
- Visual size comparisons — diameters are translated into 
  relatable references (e.g., "about the size of a football field" 
  or "taller than a person") instead of raw numbers
- Interactive orbital radar map — a visual representation of 
  multiple tracked objects and their relative distances, instead of 
  a table of coordinates
- Instant AI risk assessments — Gemini generates short, 
  plain-language summaries explaining what an object's size, speed, 
  and distance actually mean
- Local sky lookup — using the user's location, the app estimates 
  where a given object would appear in the sky right now
- Historical grounding — past impact events like Chelyabinsk and 
  Tunguska are shown alongside current data, giving newcomers a 
  reference point for scale and risk
- Resilient by design — if live data is unavailable, the app 
  falls back to simulated data so the experience stays functional

Who It's For

- Students & space enthusiasts who want an engaging, visual way 
  to explore real astronomical data without needing a background in 
  astrophysics
- Educators looking for an interactive tool to demonstrate how 
  NEO tracking and risk assessment work in practice
- Curious general users who've seen "close approach" headlines 
  and want a quick, trustworthy way to understand what's actually 
  happening, without digging through scientific databases
- Developers & hackathon judges interested in seeing how live 
  NASA APIs and an LLM (Gemini) can be combined into a clean, 
  stateless, full-stack application

In short, NearMiss closes the gap between publicly available 
planetary defense data and the people who might want to understand 
it — making space situational awareness something anyone can check 
in seconds, not just specialists with the right tools and training.

### DRIFT
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/drift-0413) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/chandril-saha/drift) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drift-th1w.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/2uTckvmnSsQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Synchronicity%20S2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://synchronicity-s-2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Limit risks, Not Possibilities

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

One of the biggest security risks in Web3 is wallet exposure. Users frequently grant unlimited token approvals to smart contracts without fully understanding the permissions they are giving away. If a contract is malicious or later becomes compromised, attackers can drain funds directly from the user's wallet.

Most users also struggle to understand transaction data because blockchain interactions are often presented as complex hexadecimal payloads and contract calls that are difficult to interpret.

## How Drift Solves It

Drift acts as a transaction firewall between users and decentralized applications.

Instead of connecting a primary wallet directly to an unknown dApp, users create a temporary sandbox wallet with predefined limits. These limits control:

* Maximum spending amount
* Session duration
* Approved contracts
* Token allowances

Before any transaction is executed, Drift simulates and analyzes it to identify suspicious behavior. An integrated AI security layer explains potential risks in plain English, helping users understand exactly what a transaction is attempting to do.

If a session becomes compromised or suspicious activity is detected, users can instantly activate Panic Mode to freeze the session and recover remaining funds.

## Benefits

* Protects primary wallets from malicious contracts
* Prevents unlimited token approval abuse
* Makes transaction risks understandable to everyday users
* Reduces the impact of compromised dApps
* Creates safer experimentation with new Web3 applications
* Provides an emergency recovery mechanism for active sessions

Drift makes interacting with decentralized applications significantly safer while preserving the self-custody principles of Web3.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing a secure session wallet architecture that remained user-friendly while enforcing strict security policies. The session wallets needed to support spending limits, expiration timers, approval controls, and emergency recovery mechanisms without making the user experience overly complex.

Another major hurdle was handling transaction simulation and risk analysis before execution. Blockchain transactions can involve multiple contract calls, token approvals, and complex state changes. Building a reliable transaction firewall required carefully validating transaction parameters and ensuring that spending limits could not be bypassed through unexpected contract behavior.

**Blockchain**

## Blockchain Track

Drift is fundamentally a blockchain security infrastructure project that leverages smart contracts to create a safer way for users to interact with decentralized applications.

The platform is built around a set of on-chain smart contracts that enforce security policies directly on the blockchain. Instead of relying on centralized intermediaries, Drift uses blockchain-native mechanisms such as programmable wallets, token approvals, transaction execution rules, and immutable contract logic to protect user assets.

Key blockchain components include:

- SessionWallet contracts that act as temporary, isolated wallets for interacting with dApps.
- SessionFactory contracts that deploy and manage sandbox wallets using the factory pattern.
- ApprovalManager contracts that control and revoke ERC-20 token allowances to prevent approval abuse.
- EmergencyVault contracts that enable secure recovery of assets when a session is compromised.
- On-chain enforcement of spending limits, expiration periods, and access controls that cannot be bypassed by external applications.

**Open Innovation**

## Open Innovation Track

Drift fits the Open Innovation track because it addresses a fundamental security problem affecting the entire Web3 ecosystem rather than serving a single niche application. Every day, users interact with smart contracts, DeFi protocols, NFT marketplaces, and blockchain games that require wallet permissions and token approvals. A single malicious approval or compromised dApp can result in the loss of user funds.

Drift introduces a new security layer between users and decentralized applications by creating temporary sandboxed wallets that isolate risk from a user's primary wallet. Instead of exposing long-term assets to unknown contracts, users can interact through disposable, policy-controlled sessions with strict spending limits, expiration times, and automatic recovery mechanisms.

The platform combines smart contract security controls, transaction simulation, and AI-powered threat analysis to make blockchain interactions safer and more understandable for both technical and non-technical users. Because this infrastructure can be integrated with virtually any Web3 application, protocol, or wallet ecosystem, Drift represents a broadly applicable innovation that improves security across the decentralized web.

**Best use of Gemini**

We use Gemini API to perform in depth analysis of transactions being routed through our app to provide detailed safety report.

> Turning Green Actions into Assets

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Climate change is one of the world's biggest challenges, yet trust in climate solutions remains fragmented. Billions of dollars flow through carbon markets every year, but buyers often have no simple way to verify whether a carbon credit truly represents real environmental impact. Existing systems suffer from a lack of transparency, fraud, double counting of credits, complex verification processes, and limited accessibility for smaller organizations and individuals.

CarbonX solves this trust gap by creating a blockchain-powered carbon credit marketplace where every credit is transparently verified, tokenized, tracked, traded, and retired on-chain. Instead of relying on claims, users can verify the complete lifecycle of a carbon credit—from project creation to retirement—through immutable blockchain records.

We're not building another crypto platform; we're building trust infrastructure for the sustainability economy. CarbonX democratizes climate action by enabling individuals, startups, organizations, and investors to participate in verified carbon markets while helping environmental projects gain visibility and access to funding.

Our vision is simple: a future where every ton of carbon reduced anywhere in the world can be transparently verified, funded, and tracked. CarbonX bridges the gap between digital ownership and real-world environmental impact, making climate action more transparent, accessible, and trustworthy for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was integrating blockchain functionality with a modern web application while maintaining a seamless user experience. We faced issues with wallet connectivity, smart contract interactions, and dependency conflicts between Web3 libraries such as Wagmi and RainbowKit.

Another challenge was designing a trustworthy carbon credit verification workflow. Since transparency is the core of CarbonX, we had to carefully structure project verification, ownership tracking, and carbon credit retirement mechanisms to prevent fraud and double counting.

We overcame these challenges through extensive testing, dependency management, smart contract optimization, and iterative UI/UX improvements, resulting in a secure, scalable, and user-friendly platform.

**Blockchain**

CarbonX fits the Blockchain track by using smart contracts, tokenized carbon credits, decentralized ownership records, and on-chain verification workflows. By bringing transparency and trust to carbon credit trading, our platform demonstrates a real-world application of blockchain beyond cryptocurrency, helping organizations and individuals contribute to sustainability with confidence.
