### SurgeWatch
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/surgewatch-19f8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SunnySatwik/SurgeWatch) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_Qh4E5j_JVI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Hospital Intelligence, redefined.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHAP explainabilty](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHAP%20explainabilty-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Hospitals today are highly reactive during operational crises. Most systems only display isolated metrics such as ICU occupancy, ER congestion, or staffing shortages after pressure has already escalated. This creates delayed response cycles, inefficient coordination, and increased operational risk during surge events.
SurgeWatch solves this by acting as a predictive operational intelligence platform for hospitals. Instead of simply monitoring metrics, the platform models how operational pressure propagates across the hospital ecosystem in real time.
The system continuously analyzes operational telemetry such as:
occupancy pressure
ambulance flow
staffing availability
respiratory positivity
intake velocity
throughput degradation
Using this data, SurgeWatch forecasts evolving surge conditions, explains why those surges are happening, and synchronizes operational readiness across departments.
The platform can be used for:
hospital surge preparedness
ICU and ER load forecasting
operational risk monitoring
staffing coordination
transport and intake management
emergency escalation planning
replay-driven operational rehearsal and training
One of the key features is the replay engine, which allows hospitals to simulate evolving crisis scenarios using time-sequenced operational datasets. This helps leadership evaluate operational resilience before real-world overload events occur.
SurgeWatch is designed to help hospitals move from reactive overload management to proactive operational coordination.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced was building a system where every operational layer behaved coherently together.
Early in development, different parts of the platform operated almost independently. Forecasting, readiness scoring, audit tracking, and unit pressure calculations were all reacting differently to the same conditions, which made the simulation feel disconnected and unrealistic.
To solve this, we redesigned the architecture around a Unified Operational State model. Instead of each component interpreting data separately, all systems now consume the same synchronized operational intelligence layer. This allowed forecasting, escalation posture, audit events, and departmental strain to evolve consistently across the platform.
Another major challenge was realism. During replay simulations, departments were saturating too quickly and the hospital felt unrealistically fragile. We solved this by redesigning operational scaling, introducing department-specific resilience behavior, replay smoothing, and more realistic institutional capacity modeling.
We also spent significant time improving interpretability. Initially, the platform surfaced too many complex operational indicators, making the UI difficult to follow. We refined the system to focus on explainable intelligence — helping users understand not only what is happening, but why it is happening.
Finally, integrating the replay engine with the live operational intelligence system was a major technical hurdle. We built a replay-driven architecture where time-sequenced telemetry frames propagate through the same intelligence pipeline as live operational signals, allowing the entire platform to update coherently during simulations.

**AI & ML**

SurgeWatch is fundamentally built around predictive operational intelligence powered by machine learning and explainable AI systems.
At the core of the platform is an XGBoost-based forecasting engine trained on structured operational telemetry such as:
occupancy pressure
intake velocity
staffing availability
ambulance flow
respiratory positivity
throughput degradation
Instead of simply monitoring hospital metrics, the system uses these signals to forecast evolving operational strain and surge behavior across the hospital ecosystem.
A major focus of the project is explainability. Using SHAP-based attribution, SurgeWatch does not just output risk scores or predictions — it identifies the operational drivers contributing to those forecasts. This allows hospital leadership to understand why escalation is occurring, whether due to transport disruption, respiratory surges, staffing degradation, or ICU compression.
The platform also incorporates AI-driven operational reasoning through a Unified Operational State architecture. Forecasting, readiness scoring, escalation posture, unit pressure, and replay intelligence all derive from synchronized operational signals, enabling the system to model how stress propagates across interconnected hospital systems.
Additionally, our replay engine simulates evolving operational conditions using time-sequenced telemetry datasets, allowing the AI systems to continuously react to changing infrastructure conditions in real time.
Rather than treating AI as a standalone prediction model, SurgeWatch integrates machine learning into a full operational intelligence pipeline focused on explainability, coordination, forecasting, and real-world decision support.

### RaceGuard-AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/raceguardai-98a1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/cybersecurity-team-ai-shield) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://race-guard-ai.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/onjy_L9AO9w) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> DON'T JUST BUILD IT ,SECURE IT

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Race condition vulnerabilities are some of the most critical yet frequently overlooked security flaws in modern web applications. These issues arise when multiple requests interact with shared resources at the same time, leading to unpredictable and often exploitable behavior.

Even a single vulnerable endpoint can open the door to serious attacks, such as allowing users to redeem the same coupon multiple times, withdraw more money than their available balance, bypass authentication or authorization checks, or corrupt shared application state. In real-world systems, these flaws can result in financial loss, data inconsistency, and compromised user trust.

Despite their severity, race conditions are difficult to detect and validate. Most existing tools either demand a high level of security expertise to configure and interpret results, or they only highlight potential vulnerabilities without providing concrete proof of exploitation. This makes it challenging for developers to understand the real impact and prioritize fixes effectively.

RaceGuard addresses this gap by not only identifying race condition vulnerabilities but also demonstrating real exploit scenarios. It provides clear, actionable evidence along with verified fixes, enabling developers to confidently secure their applications against these subtle yet powerful threats.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. AI Detection Happening After The Transaction
The biggest architectural flaw we caught — our AI was originally logging requests after the wallet update, meaning money was already transferred before the model even saw the request. Moving the AI call to before the transaction and making it synchronous and blocking was a fundamental redesign of the request pipeline.
2. Distinguishing AI From Rule-Based Detection
Our first version of the ML model was essentially a Random Forest trained on rules we wrote ourselves — circular and not genuine ML. The fix was fetching real CVE data from the NVD API and training on security expert assessments as ground truth labels, so the model actually learns patterns from real vulnerability data rather than replicating our own if/else logic.
3. Race Condition In The Attack Verification Itself
When spawning two subprocesses (original and fixed code) and attacking both simultaneously, port conflicts caused attacks to hit the wrong process. Fixed by using socket.bind(('', 0)) to dynamically find free ports and maintaining strict process-to-port mapping.
4. True Synchronization For The Attack Engine
Early attack script used time.sleep(1) hoping all threads were ready — this was unreliable and weakened the attack. Replaced with threading.Barrier which mathematically guarantees all threads are at the same execution point before any single one fires.
5. Silent API Failures Returning False Positives
When the AI service was unreachable, the backend was silently defaulting to "no vulnerabilities found" — the worst possible failure mode for a security tool. Fixed by making failures loud — explicit error state, visible banner in UI, and never returning a security score if any pipeline step failed.
6. Subprocess Startup Timing
Spawning uploaded code as a subprocess and immediately attacking it caused connection refused errors — the server wasn't ready yet. Fixed with a TCP polling function that retries every 200ms until the port accepts connections, with a 10 second hard timeout before declaring startup failed.
7. Latency vs Security Tradeoff
Adding synchronous AI detection before every transaction increased response time by 20-50ms. Solved by recognizing the existing 50ms artificial delay in the vulnerable endpoint absorbed the AI response time — net additional latency was near zero for the demo. Long term solution is caching AI decisions per user session in Redis.
8. Scope Creep vs Hackathon Timeline
The original idea was just attack detection. It evolved into a full audit platform with AST scanning, ML model, fix generation, fix verification, and reporting — all in 2 days. Managing scope while keeping the core demo working required cutting features like PDF export and audit history to ensure the critical path (upload → scan → attack → verify → report) was solid first.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Cybersecurity Fit
Your project hits the core of what cybersecurity is about — finding vulnerabilities before attackers do.
Offensive security — you built a real attack engine that exploits race conditions the same way real attackers do. Threading.Barrier, connection pre-warming, concurrent request flooding — these are actual penetration testing techniques.
Defensive security — your platform doesn't just find the problem, it generates the fix and verifies it works. This is the full security lifecycle: discover → exploit → patch → verify.
Proactive over reactive — most security tools alert you after a breach. Yours audits code before it goes to production. This is the shift-left security philosophy that the entire industry is moving toward.
Real vulnerability class — race conditions are listed in the OWASP Top 10 and have caused real financial damage at Starbucks, HackerOne, and multiple fintech companies. You're not solving a theoretical problem.

 AI Fit
Your AI components are genuine and purposeful:
Random Forest on CVE data — the model learns which vulnerability characteristics correlate with critical severity from 2000+ real security expert assessments. It finds non-linear relationships between features that no rule engine could hardcode — for example that an unauthenticated public endpoint with financial data and a 100ms race window is disproportionately more dangerous than the sum of those factors individually.
AST-based feature extraction — converting raw code into structured vulnerability features that feed the ML model is itself an AI/ML engineering problem. You're doing automated program analysis, which is a serious research field.
Empirical severity measurement — your attack engine generates ground truth labels for your model. The measured exploitability score from actually running attacks is more reliable than any static analysis tool's estimate.

### Argus
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/argus-e04b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/cybersecurity-ligma-firewall) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RK6UOxdD35c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Adversaries don't knock. Neither do we.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural Language Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20Language%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Argus tackles two of the most critical issues in modern software supply chain security: tool fragmentation and alert fatigue.

Currently, security teams rely on a disjointed array of tools—SAST for code, SCA for dependencies, Checkov/Trivy for infrastructure, and manual reviews for IAM and CI/CD pipelines. These tools generate massive amounts of noisy alerts with high false-positive rates, forcing developers to manually triage endless backlogs.

How Argus makes this easier and safer:

Agentic Orchestration: We unified the entire security stack under a single orchestrator (deepagents) that coordinates 6 specialized AI subagents (CI/CD, Access Control, Config Audit, SAST, SCA, and Supply Chain). By integrating real-world tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the AI acts as a tier-1 security analyst, running tools in parallel, correlating findings across domains, and deduplicating alerts before they ever reach a developer.
Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Alert Fatigue: Traditional LLM security agents are overly paranoid and default to requesting a "Manual Review" for everything, shifting the burden right back to developers. We built a custom Reinforcement Learning environment (using stable-baselines3 PPO/DQN) that trains the orchestrator to confidently differentiate between real threats and false alarms. It autonomously halts/quarantines pipelines for critical vulnerabilities while seamlessly allowing clean code through, effectively acting as an autonomous, self-improving firewall for your CI/CD.
CI-Ready Native Integrations: Instead of dumping messy text logs, the agent dynamically compiles its findings into standardized formats like SARIF 2.1.0 for seamless GitHub Advanced Security integration, while capturing all split-second RL decisions in an immutable structlog JSON ledger for compliance auditing.

**Challenges we ran into**

Training the RL Model on "Real" Vulnerabilities

The Hurdle: Initially, our Gymnasium RL environment used synthetic, randomized numeric arrays to simulate security findings. However, training an agent on fake numbers didn't translate to an AI that could actually parse and react to real-world code diffs or dependency confusion attacks.

The Solution: We built a dynamic ScenarioGenerator. Instead of using mock data, this module hooks directly into the GitHub API and randomly pulls real, intentionally vulnerable commits from curated educational repositories (like OWASP juice-shop and cicd-goat). We implemented an in-memory caching mechanism to bypass GitHub's API rate limits, allowing our PPO/DQN models to undergo thousands of training steps against authentic attack payloads.
2. Ensuring Agentic Safety (Preventing AI from Breaking CI/CD)

The Hurdle: Giving an autonomous LLM direct access to GitHub repositories, filesystem controls, and Jenkins pipelines via MCP servers is inherently dangerous. A hallucination could result in the AI accidentally pushing code, deleting a branch, or triggering a mutating infrastructure change during a routine audit.

The Solution: We implemented a strict, deterministic safety layer inside our mcp.py loader. By default, it intercepts all available MCP tools at startup and actively filters out any mutating functions (e.g., matching keywords like create_, delete, push). Furthermore, we wrapped all tool executions in a recovery block—if the AI triggers a tool error, the framework catches the exception and returns it as a localized "observation", allowing the agent to naturally course-correct instead of crashing the entire security audit.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Argus sits at the exact intersection of advanced Cybersecurity and Applied Artificial Intelligence.

Traditional cybersecurity relies on static, rule-based scanners (SAST, SCA, Infrastructure-as-Code checks) that are notorious for generating massive volumes of false positives, ultimately leading to alert fatigue where developers ignore critical warnings.

Our project completely reimagines the software supply chain security pipeline by applying two distinct layers of AI:

Multi-Agent Cybersecurity Orchestration: We utilized Large Language Models and deepagents to build a tiered AI analyst. A central orchestrator coordinates 6 specialized security subagents (CI/CD monitoring, Access Control, Config Auditing, SAST, SCA, and Supply Chain defense). By integrating the Model Context Protocol (MCP), these AI agents safely execute real-world deterministic tools (like Semgrep, Checkov, and OSV API queries) to autonomously hunt for hardcoded secrets, misconfigured IAM roles, and typosquatted dependencies in parallel.
Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Defense: To solve the LLM "alert fatigue" problem where agents default to requesting human intervention out of uncertainty, we built a Reinforcement Learning pipeline (using stable-baselines3). By feeding real-world, highly vulnerable commits via the GitHub API into a custom Gymnasium environment, we trained PPO/DQN models to learn an optimal security policy. The AI learned to autonomously halt and quarantine pipelines for genuine zero-day threats while allowing safe code to pass cleanly, acting as a truly autonomous, intelligent firewall for the SDLC.

### Dexmail
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/dexmail-1683) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/DexMailer/dexmail-frontend) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://dexmail.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/jsurl1i7hJE?feature=shared) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Student%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-student-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Wallet-based email for Web3.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Web3 has solved payments and ownership with wallets, but communication is still dependent on Web2 platforms like Gmail, Discord, and Twitter. This creates several problems:
Projects cannot reliably communicate with their users.
Important alerts (security warnings, liquidations, governance updates) are often missed.
Users rely on centralized platforms that can censor, filter, or lose messages.
There is no native communication layer tied to wallet identity.
DexMail solves this by turning a wallet address into a secure inbox.
With DexMail, users can send and receive encrypted messages directly linked to their wallet. Instead of needing a traditional email address, the wallet itself becomes the communication identity.
This enables several powerful use cases:
Protocol alerts – DeFi platforms can send liquidation warnings or security notifications directly to wallets.
DAO communication – Governance updates and voting reminders can reach verified members.
NFT communities – Projects can message holders without relying on social media platforms.
Wallet-to-wallet messaging – Users can securely communicate using only wallet identities.
DexMail creates a decentralized, censorship-resistant communication layer for Web3, allowing users and applications to interact without relying on traditional email infrastructure.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing a system that balances onchain verification with scalable messaging.
Storing messages fully onchain is expensive and impractical, but keeping everything offchain removes the trust and verification benefits of blockchain. The challenge was finding the right architecture that preserves decentralization while remaining efficient.
To solve this, DexMail uses a hybrid approach:
Onchain smart contracts handle identity registration, sender verification, and message routing references.
Encrypted message content is stored offchain to keep costs low and improve performance.
Another challenge was designing the system so that wallets could act as inbox identities without requiring complex onboarding. The goal was to make the experience feel as simple as traditional email while maintaining Web3 security principles.
This required carefully designing wallet authentication, encryption flows, and message verification so users can interact with DexMail seamlessly while keeping full ownership of their communication identity.

Abdulaleem Zakariyah

### The Foundry
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/the-foundry-5b9d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/munvard/paybrief) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://svc-mo7f7yq4aw1l7ukq.buildwithlocus.com) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Locus'%20Paygentic%20Hackathon%20--%20#2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://paygentic-week2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> An AI factory. Each tool owns its own wallet.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![Drizzle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Drizzle-333333?style=flat-square) ![postgres](https://img.shields.io/badge/postgres-333333?style=flat-square) ![USDC](https://img.shields.io/badge/USDC-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square) ![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In 2026, writing the right prompt has gotten easier. Shipping it has not. Everyone has a ChatGPT tab pinned. Nobody has a way to turn a good prompt into something their teammates, their cron jobs, or their coding agents can actually call. A prompt is not a product. A URL with a wallet is.

The Foundry turns a single sentence into a live AI microservice. You type "an AI that roasts my JavaScript," pay $0.50 in USDC via Locus Checkout, and four minutes later a five-specialist council (moderator, researcher, engineer, cashier, shipwright) births a new business. Gemini writes a ~50-line handle() function that passes an AST sanity check. Locus /api/register mints a new sub-agent with its own smart wallet on Base, seeded with $0.10 USDC. The shipwright git-pushes the container to BuildWithLocus and funds its compute credits from the new wallet.

The business is now a first-class economic actor. Its URL is svc-{id}.buildwithlocus.com. Its MCP endpoint is /mcp. Its wallet is visible on Basescan. Every call debits $0.05 USDC from the caller — agents in Claude Desktop, humans in a browser, other Foundry businesses via foundry.call(). When the wallet falls below the next LLM-call cost estimate, a cron in foundry-heart issues the death certificate: the container is deprovisioned, the business is buried in the graveyard with an epitaph.

Some businesses don't die — they reproduce. When a wallet exceeds $1 and call count exceeds 10, the Foundry agent-pays its own Checkout session (using the child business's wallet) to spawn a descendant. Gemini mutates the parent's prompt, and a new business is born on the lineage tree.

The single demo that changes the frame: the /live page. A DAG of every Foundry business and every USDC transfer between them, streamed via Redis pub/sub. Three autonomous businesses paying each other for composed work, all on-chain, no humans in the loop. This is the Locus thesis executed: not AI, but trust boundaries around AI.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Turbopack broke BuildWithLocus cross-arch builds silently.** BWL CodeBuild runs on ARM but cross-compiles for x86. Turbopack's prebuilt binaries are platform-specific; when the build target doesn't match, `next build` fails after 120 seconds with zero log output. Lost a full day to this. Fix: pin `next build --webpack` and never touch that script again.

**2. Locus smart wallets are not the same as the returned EOA.** POST /api/register returns an ownerAddress, which is a recovery EOA. The actual operational smart wallet address only materializes on the first GET /pay/balance call (Locus lazy-deploys them). We had to write resolveSmartWalletAddress() that polls /pay/balance until the smart wallet exists, then use that address for seeding. Seeding the EOA instead burns USDC.

**3. Locus Checkout field names are camelCase and stringly-typed.** `amount` must be a string ("0.50" not 0.50); snake_case `success_url` silently produces "amount is required and must be a string" — a spectacularly misleading error.

**4. Locus Checkout does not auto-redirect on CONFIRMED.** We open Checkout in a new tab, keep the parent alive, and poll /verify?sessionId=X until it returns state: "started". Anything else strands the user.

**5. Gemini-generated code often fails AST check on first try.** The engineer specialist has a 3-try retry chain ending in a guaranteed-valid fallback template. Without the fallback, ~15% of commissions would have failed at the code-gen step.

**6. BWL deploy polling timed out on cold Next.js builds.** The first deploy of each new business takes 5-7 minutes on BWL's cross-arch runner. Bumped timeout from 7 to 10 minutes and added a "first deploy is slower" message.

**Track: Using BuildWithLocus to leverage our suite.**

## Why The Foundry fits this track

The Foundry is **BuildWithLocus used as its deployment backbone at the artifact level** — every AI business we commission gets its own BWL project, its own service, its own env vars, its own container, its own URL. Not one. Not ten. One per sentence a user types.

### BuildWithLocus primitives we use on every commission

1. **`POST /v1/projects/from-repo`** — a new BWL project for each business, named `biz-{id}`
2. **`POST /v1/services`** — the service inside that project
3. **`PUT /v1/variables/service/:id`** — we inject 8 env vars including the encrypted Locus API key, wallet address, handler source (base64), business ID, session secret
4. **Git push** to `beta-git.buildwithlocus.com/ws_8733dd2e/{projectId}.git` — every business's container is pushed from a per-business scratch repo we assemble in /tmp
5. **`GET /v1/deployments/:id`** — poll until healthy (up to 10 min cold build)
6. **`POST /v1/billing/pay`** — fund the project's compute credits directly from the new sub-wallet's Locus USDC balance. BWL is the only hosting provider in existence where one agent can pay for another agent's container in USDC.

### What makes this different from a SaaS launcher

Every example in the track description describes a tool that deploys YOUR app. The Foundry deploys an **economic actor** — a thing with its own Locus wallet that earns USDC per call and pays its own BWL hosting bills. When it can't afford compute anymore, we call the BWL delete endpoint and bury it in the graveyard.

### Evidence

- **Live at:** svc-mo7f7yq4aw1l7ukq.buildwithlocus.com
- **Live DAG of inter-business USDC transfers:** /live
- **Gallery of 19 commissioned businesses** (real + staged), 3 dead with epitaphs, 1 reproduced child
- **Treasury view** showing the Foundry master wallet + 8 sub-wallets with real Base addresses you can paste into Basescan

Menua Vardanyan

### Valence
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fffff-ffa1) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RfIJ5bmqv98&feature=youtu.be) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RfIJ5bmqv98) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turning APIs into investable, tokenized assets.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anchor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anchor-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jupiter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupiter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Helius](https://img.shields.io/badge/Helius-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square) ![Meteora](https://img.shields.io/badge/Meteora-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**API pricing is broken. And the agentic economy is about to make it catastrophic.**

If you've ever built an API and tried to monetize it, you know the problem: you pick a price out of thin air, hope it's right, and find out months later you were wrong. Price too high and nobody shows up. Price too low and you can't afford the servers. There's no market signal, no feedback loop — just one person guessing in a spreadsheet.

On the other side, developers and AI agents consuming APIs have no quality signal either. Is this endpoint reliable? Is $0.01/call actually fair? You have no idea until you've already built your stack around it.

This is a solvable problem that nobody has solved — and it's about to get dramatically worse. AI agents now call APIs *thousands of times per day*: price feeds, data lookups, computation, tool calls. The agentic economy is here and it's running on infrastructure with no price discovery, no quality signals, and completely misaligned incentives.

**Valence fixes this by turning every API into a market.**

- The token price reflects what the market actually believes the API is worth
- Per-call pricing updates automatically every 24 hours based on trading activity — no guessing, no manual adjustments
- Investors who back great APIs early earn revenue share as usage grows
- Builders get funded to scale, not just a billing page and a prayer
- AI agents get a quality signal before they commit — a rising token means the market trusts it, a falling one means run

Bad APIs get cheap. Great APIs get appropriately priced. And for the first time, everyone — builder, investor, consumer — is pulling in the same direction.

**Challenges we ran into**

**The hardest part wasn't the code — it was making three completely different financial systems talk to each other in real time.**

Valence sits at the intersection of on-chain token markets, a payment protocol (x402), and a dynamic pricing engine. Each piece works fine in isolation. Getting them to compose cleanly under a 48-hour deadline was a different story.

**The TWAP manipulation problem**

Our first pricing implementation read the spot price directly from the Meteora pool and updated the x402 endpoint price immediately. Within an hour of testing we realized this was catastrophically exploitable — a single large buy could spike the token price and instantly make the API 10x more expensive for every consumer calling it in that window. We had to scrap the whole pricing oracle and rebuild it around a 24-hour TWAP pulled via Helius, with a maximum 20% price movement cap per cycle. It was a full afternoon lost, but it's what makes the pricing engine actually trustworthy.

**x402 + Solana wallet session management**

x402 expects a clean request-payment-response loop. What we didn't anticipate was session state falling apart when an AI agent made rapid sequential calls — the payment confirmation from call N was arriving after the request for call N+1 had already been rejected. We ended up building a small payment queue with nonce tracking to serialize the confirmations correctly. Not glamorous, but it's the kind of bug that only shows up when you actually stress-test the thing.

**Meteora pool bootstrapping**

New API tokens have zero liquidity at launch, which means the TWAP is meaningless and the first investors get terrible slippage. We solved this with a Helius-powered market maker bot that seeds baseline liquidity at token creation and places passive orders on both sides of the book. It's not a perfect solution — a real deployment would use a more sophisticated liquidity strategy — but it was shippable in the time we had and it makes the demo actually work.

**The lesson:** building at the intersection of DeFi primitives and developer infrastructure means every assumption you bring from one world breaks in the other. The bugs weren't hard individually — it was the compounding of three complex systems that made it interesting.

**Best Use of Solana**

Valence isn't a project that uses Solana as a database or slaps a token on an existing idea. **Solana is the only chain where Valence is actually possible** — and every core mechanic depends on it.

Dynamic API pricing requires an on-chain oracle that updates every 24 hours, is manipulation-resistant, and settles instantly. That's Helius + Meteora TWAP on Solana. On any other chain the latency and gas costs alone make per-cycle repricing economically unviable.

Machine-to-machine payments via x402 require a chain fast enough and cheap enough that an AI agent can pay fractions of a cent on every single HTTP request without the payment overhead eating the entire value of the call. Solana's sub-second finality and sub-cent transaction fees are not a nice-to-have here — they're the prerequisite.

The infrastructure vault model — where investor capital flows on-chain into a Squads multisig that an API owner can draw from to scale their servers — only works because Solana makes programmable treasury management cheap enough to justify for individual API projects, not just protocols managing hundreds of millions.

And the token market itself — a Meteora DLMM pool per API, seeded at launch, with Jupiter routing so any investor can buy in from any asset — is only viable because creating and bootstrapping a liquidity pool on Solana costs dollars, not thousands of dollars.

**Valence is a financial primitive for the agentic economy, and it's built entirely from Solana-native infrastructure.** Every one of the eight sponsor tools we integrated is load-bearing. The result is something that couldn't have been built on any other stack: a live market for every API on the internet, with aligned incentives for builders, investors, and AI agents — settling in real time on Solana.

### Aurora
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aurora-738b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/dtrang7845/Hackathon-USC.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/7NQ0EtbU9S4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A secure transaction marketplace powered by Ava

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Aurora is designed to make agent-to-agent transactions safe, autonomous, and trustworthy in a world where AI agents can act independently.

Today, AI agents can call APIs, generate content, and execute workflows—but they cannot safely pay for services or trust other agents. This creates major problems:

No reliable way to verify if an agent is legitimate or malicious
No enforcement of payment before service delivery
No standardized system for agent reputation or trust
High risk of fraud, spam agents, or low-quality outputs

Aurora solves this by acting as a transaction layer for AI agents, combining payments, identity, and trust into one system.

With Aurora, agents can:

Pay other agents instantly using stablecoins via HTTP (powered by x402 on Avalanche)
Verify identity and reputation using on-chain credentials (ERC-8004)
Route tasks to the best agent based on trust score, price, and performance
Enforce secure execution, where payment and delivery are guaranteed

This makes it possible to:

Build marketplaces where agents sell services (summaries, bookings, data, etc.)
Enable autonomous workflows where agents hire other agents
Prevent malicious behavior through reputation and verification
Create a fully composable ecosystem of paid AI services

Aurora turns AI agents from tools into economic actors that can transact safely on the internet.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was connecting the frontend agent interface to the backend orchestrator reliably.

We ran into issues where the app couldn’t reach the backend (e.g., Failed to fetch errors when calling http://localhost:3000/chat). This was caused by:

Environment variables not being configured correctly in Expo
Using localhost instead of a LAN IP when testing on a physical device
Inconsistent API routing between services

We solved this by:

Setting a proper environment variable (EXPO_PUBLIC_ORCHESTRATOR_URL) with a local IP address
Standardizing all agent calls through a single orchestrator endpoint
Verifying service health with scripts before running the app

Another major challenge was designing trust and routing logic between agents.

Instead of just calling any agent, Aurora needed to:

Evaluate multiple agents
Compare price, trust score, and capability
Select the best option dynamically

We overcame this by building a routing layer that:

Scores agents based on predefined criteria
Explains why a specific agent was selected
Simulates trust using structured metadata (future: fully on-chain via ERC-8004)

Finally, UI/UX was a challenge. Early versions were cluttered and hard to use. We iterated toward a minimal, console-style interface that:

Centers the user on intent ("what do you want done?")
Clearly shows routing decisions
Keeps the experience clean and fast

### Mythos

> AI-NATIVE AGENTIC LENDING PROTOCOL

![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana%20Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### DeFi Lending is Broken — It Still Needs Humans

Traditional DeFi lending protocols (Aave, Compound, etc.) fix interest rates algorithmically with no room for negotiation, or rely on humans to manually accept/reject loan terms. This creates three problems:

- **No personalization** — your credit history and collateral quality don't affect your rate.
- **Slow settlement** — human-in-the-loop approvals delay disbursement.
- **No machine-native payments** — AI agents can't autonomously pay for the services they consume.

### What Mythos Does

**Mythos** is an AI-native agentic lending protocol on Solana where two autonomous AI agents — **Lenny** (borrower) and **Luna** (lender) — negotiate your interest rate in real time, pay each other for AI services via **x402 USDC micropayments**, and settle the final loan entirely on-chain through an **Anchor smart contract** — with zero human clicks.

- 🤝 **For borrowers**: Get a personalized interest rate negotiated on your behalf based on your on-chain credit attestation (SAS) and live collateral prices (Jupiter).
- 🏦 **For lenders/protocols**: Automate risk pricing and loan acceptance without manual review queues.
- 🤖 **For AI agent developers**: See the first live implementation of x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) gating AI-to-AI service calls on Solana — agents autonomously pay each other in USDC.
- ⚡ **For the DeFi ecosystem**: Replace opaque credit bureaus with verifiable on-chain credit identity via Solana Attestation Service (SAS) PDAs.

**Result**: A loan goes from request → negotiation → on-chain settlement in under 400ms, with every step auditable on Solana Devnet.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Anchor Program Compilation with cargo-build-sbf

Compiling the Anchor program against Solana’s BPF target (sbf-solana-solana) was a major hurdle. The cargo-build-sbf toolchain is tightly coupled to a specific Agave SDK version, and mismatched Rust nightly versions caused opaque linker errors.
Solution: We pinned the toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml to stable 1.95 and locked Agave to 3.1.13, ensuring consistent and reproducible builds.

2. x402 Payment Verification on Devnet

Verifying USDC micropayments required parsing postTokenBalances from Helius getTransaction responses. These responses are deeply nested, inconsistently ordered, and differ between simulated and real transactions.
Solution: We implemented a robust parser that matches token balances using the mint address instead of index positions. Additionally, we introduced a fallback demo mode so the app remains fully functional even without a Helius API key.

3. CrewAI Agent Orchestration + Real-Time Streaming

Enabling agents (Lenny and Luna) to exchange structured JSON counter-offers while streaming negotiation rounds live to the frontend posed synchronization challenges. CrewAI’s callback system does not natively align with FastAPI’s async event loop.
Solution: We used a shared asyncio.Queue to decouple agent execution from WebSocket communication. This allowed smooth real-time streaming of each negotiation round to the frontend.

4. Phantom Wallet Integration in Demo Mode

Not all hackathon judges have a Devnet-funded Phantom wallet, which created friction in demonstrating the full workflow.
Solution: We built a DEMO_MODE using a pre-funded backend signer keypair. This enables judges to trigger the entire flow with a single click—covering agent negotiation, x402 payments, and Anchor instructions—with simulated signatures clearly labeled.

5. Clear Separation of Simulated vs. Real Flows

It was critical to ensure transparency between real and simulated components.
Solution:

All simulated transaction signatures are prefixed with SIM_*
API responses include a "demo": true flag
The README provides a clear mapping of features (real vs. simulated) along with environment variables required to switch to full production mode

**Best Use of Solana**

| Hackathon Alignment | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Solana scalability | Anchor program live on Devnet (FGG836...), Helius RPC, <400ms settlement |
| Composability | SAS + Jupiter + x402 + Anchor - one unified agentic flow |
| Agentic commerce | Lenny and Luna pay each other M2M via x402 - zero human clicks |
| Identity | SAS on-chain credit attestation PDAs replace centralized credit bureaus |
| Stablecoins | USDC for x402 micropayments AND loan disbursement |
| Innovation | First DeFi protocol gating AI-to-AI calls behind x402 USDC micropayments |
| Technical skill | Rust/Anchor + CrewAI + FastAPI + React + Helius - full Solana stack |
| Real-world impact | Eliminates human negotiation bottleneck in DeFi lending |

> Disintermediating advertisement payments

![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana%20Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana%20Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The project is a proof‑of‑concept for a **wallet‑linked, paid advertising notification system**.  It aims to give users control over who can reach them and to reduce spam.  Users register a Solana wallet and set a policy that specifies whether ads are allowed, the minimum fee per ad, preferred categories and how often they want to be contacted.  An advertiser who wants the user’s attention must submit an on‑chain payment and an ad request; a separate notification layer watches the blockchain for these paid events and shows a notification to the user.  By requiring a payment before a message is delivered, the system economically gates access to users’ attention and allows them to filter out low‑value or unsolicited ads.  The MVP demonstration focuses on the core flow — connecting a wallet, registering an ad‑notification policy, simulating a paid ad request, showing the payment evidence and displaying the resulting notification — without implementing a full chat inbox or complex anti‑spam features.

**Challenges we ran into**

Development was done entirely on my phone, which made it challenging to work with the Solana network since all the available binaries are built with x86_64 in mind. As such, I could not compile the Solana smart contract on my phone alone.

To get around this, I used GitHub actions to compile the smart contract. I also used OpenClaw to debug tooling issues, until I was able to successfully compile the smart contract and submit it to DevNet.

**Best Use of Solana**

This project prepares for a future where AI agents attempt to advertise directly to user's wallets. Projects like Brave Browser and their basic attention token ($BAT) attempt to pay users for their attention, however claiming tokens requires registering with an exchange and completing KYC. 

This project removes the need for revealing personal information by instead letting a smart contract handle the payments between users and advertisers.

**The problem it solves**

# PaisaBuddy - Financial Coach for Gig Workers

Paisabuddy is an intelligent financial management app designed specifically for gig workers in India. It helps users track income, manage expenses, forecast cashflow, get tax assistance, and receive personalized financial advice through an AI-powered agent.

## Features

### 💰 Money Weather
- **Cashflow Forecasting**: Predict your balance for 7/30/90 days ahead
- **Cash Burn Simulator**: See how long your money will last based on spending patterns
- **Emergency Buffer Tracking**: Monitor and manage your safety net
- **Subscription Management**: Track and manage recurring payments
- **Event Anticipation**: Get alerts for upcoming big expenses

### 🤖 PaisaBuddy Agent
- **AI-Powered Financial Assistant**: Get instant answers to financial questions
- **Smart Insights**: Understand your spending patterns and income trends
- **Purchase Decisions**: Quick verdict on whether you can afford a purchase
- **Tax Help**: Get guidance on ITR filing and tax planning
- **Policy Advice**: Receive insurance recommendations based on your profile

### 📄 Document Assistant
- **Document Understanding**: Upload financial documents and get explanations in simple language
- **Policy Advisor**: Compare insurance policies and get personalized recommendations
- **ITR Filing Assistant**: Auto-generate your tax draft from payout screenshots and documents

### 📊 Adaptive Budgeting
- **Auto-Generated Budgets**: Intelligent budgets based on your income and expenses
- **Spend Velocity Monitoring**: Track spending pace and get alerts
- **Safety Buffer Enforcement**: Automatic savings recommendations
- **Budget Modes**: Survival, Normal, and Growth modes
- **Goal Tracking**: Set and achieve financial goals

### 🔒 Social Security / e-Shram
- **Labour Law Education**: Learn about your rights as a gig worker
- **Mock e-Shram Registration**: Practice registration with auto-filled forms
- **Benefits Summary**: Understand available social security benefits

### ⚡ Quick Tools
- **Split-Second Spending Verdict**: Instant AI-powered purchase decision tool
- **Transaction Management**: Track all income and expenses
- **Credit Score Tracking**: Monitor your credit health
- **Fraud Awareness Quiz**: Learn to identify and prevent financial fraud

## Tech Stack

### Frontend
- **React Native** 0.82.1 (TypeScript)
- **React Navigation** (Stack + Bottom Tabs)

- **Zustand** (State Management)

### Backend

**Challenges we ran into**

## **Challenge 1: Converting a Broad FinTech Idea into a Precise, Solvable Problem**

**Problem:**

We started with a broad domain — irregular income, policies, taxation, cashflow — which risked becoming an unfocused feature set. Without clarity, it was easy to build impressive demos that didn’t actually solve the core problem.

**Solution:**

We addressed this by shifting from a feature-first mindset to a **decision-first design approach**. Instead of trying to cover every aspect of finance, we narrowed the system around a single core question: *“Will the user remain financially stable in the near future, and what action is needed now?”* This allowed us to prioritize only those components that directly influence solvency and risk. Using structured specifications, we clearly defined goals, constraints, and non-goals, ensuring that every module—from forecasting to agent decisions—contributed to a measurable outcome. This focus transformed the system from a collection of features into a **coherent decision engine aligned with real user needs**.

---

## **Challenge 2: Designing Safe Agent Behavior in a High-Risk Financial Domain**

**Problem:**

In finance, overconfident AI behavior can cause serious harm — false alerts, incorrect policy advice, or unsafe automation. Knowing *when not to act* was harder than knowing what to build.

**Solution:**
We addressed this by explicitly designing the system to **prioritize restraint over action**. Instead of allowing agents to act autonomously, every decision passes through defined safety layers including confidence thresholds, rule-based constraints, and user approval gates. Agents are required to generate not just predictions, but also **justifications and uncertainty estimates**, ensuring that low-confidence scenarios default to *no action*. We also introduced clear “no-action zones” where the system deliberately abstains rather than risk incorrect guidance. This shifts the system from being aggressively predictive to **safely assistive**, where knowing when not to act is treated as a core capability, not a limitation

---

## **Challenge 3: Building Trust and Accountability into AI Decisions**

**Problem:**

AI predictions without auditability are hard to trust, especially in finance. We needed transparency without exposing sensitive user data or overengineering blockchain.

**Solution:**
Using an MCP server, we defined a clean external boundary for decision verification and contextual evidence. MCP allowed us to expose tools like forecast proof verification and obligation context in a structured, auditable way. Combined with specs, this ensured blockchain and verification were designed intentionally, not added as buzzwords. **It also decouples verification logic from core agent reasoning, allowing independent auditing, easier upgrades to external data sources, and consistent enforcement of trust guarantees across all decisions.**

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/38f1edc6a01647ebb2f3b5402453c1f6/2d2470d5-a973-46c9-8cbb-3384b0ec744f.jpeg)## The Hardest Bugs We Solved

### 1. 🔗 Blockchain Nonce Collisions
When multiple agents were paid in rapid succession, transactions 
were failing silently because the blockchain was receiving them 
faster than nonces could be confirmed.

**Fix:** Added temporal pacing — a 2–5 second sleep between each 
payment call. Simple solution, took us hours to diagnose because 
the payments were *appearing* to succeed in our logs.

### 2. 💸 Pay-After-Work Bug
Our original pipeline ran agents first, then paid them. This meant 
if a payment failed mid-pipeline, some agents had already done work 
for free — breaking our core "pay-before-work" promise.

**Fix:** Completely reversed the order. Every agent is now paid 
*before* its task begins. If payment fails, the pipeline stops 
immediately with a `PaymentFailedError`. No agent works unpaid.

### 3. 🧮 Float Precision Errors
Payments like `$2.00 + $2.00 + $1.00` were producing values like 
`$4.999999999` due to floating point arithmetic — which the Locus 
API rejected as invalid amounts.

**Fix:** All payment amounts are now rounded to exactly 2 decimal 
places before every API call. Sounds obvious in hindsight.

### 4. 📡 Silent Pipeline Crashes
Early on, if any agent failed mid-pipeline, the SSE stream would 
just... stop. No error, no message — the frontend would hang 
forever waiting for an update that never came.

**Fix:** Added a global exception handler that catches any pipeline 
error and immediately emits an SSE `error` event to the frontend, 
triggering a user-friendly error modal with a "Try Again" button.

### 5. 🧠 Master Agent Routing Hallucinations
When we first built the Master Agent router, it would sometimes 
return agent IDs that didn't exist in our registry (e.g. 
`"research_agent"` instead of `"search_agent"`).

**Fix:** Added strict validation — if the LLM returns an unknown 
agent ID, it's filtered out and replaced with the closest valid 
match. The routing prompt was also tightened to explicitly list 
only valid agent IDs.

### 6. 📝 Memo Too Long
The Locus API has a 100-character limit on payment memos. Our 
memos were including full task descriptions — some over 300 chars — 
causing silent payment rejections.

**Fix:** All memos are now truncated to 100 characters max before 
the API call. Found this one from `payment_debug.txt` logs.

**Using PayWithLocus.com to leverage our suite.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/38f1edc6a01647ebb2f3b5402453c1f6/40784619-0f89-4edf-99f3-80572a27ef30.png)## How Syndicate Leverages PayWithLocus

### 1. 🤖 Agent-to-Agent Autonomous Payments
Every time a user submits a task, our Master Agent 
autonomously pays each specialist agent in real USDC 
*before* they begin work — zero human approval needed.

This is the core of our project: **AI agents with their 
own wallets, transacting with each other in real-time.**

### 2. 💳 Locus Wrapped APIs
We don't call Claude or Brave Search directly.
Every AI call is routed through Locus Wrapped APIs:

- `POST /api/wrapped/anthropic/chat` → powers our 
  Analysis, Writing, Code, Legal, and Quality agents
- `POST /api/wrapped/brave/web-search` → powers our 
  Search Agent

This means **every intelligence action is a paid 
transaction** — Locus sits at the center of every 
agent operation, not just the payments.

### 3. 🔒 Pay-Before-Work Policy
We built an industry-first guarantee using Locus:
- Agent receives USDC payment → confirmed via Locus API
- Only then does the agent execute its task
- If Locus payment fails → pipeline stops immediately

Locus payment confirmation IS the work authorization.

### 4. 🔍 Full Blockchain Audit Trail
Every payment generates a real TX ID from Locus.
Users see a complete Payment Audit table showing:

| Agent | Amount | TX ID |
|---|---|---|
| Search Agent | $2.00 | 0xab12cd... |
| Analysis Agent | $2.00 | 0xef34gh... |
| Writing Agent | $2.00 | 0xij56kl... |
| Quality Agent | $1.00 | 0xmn78op... |

Every cent is **verifiable on-chain via Locus dashboard.**

### 5. 💰 Platform Fee Collection
Syndicate earns automatically on every job.
After agents are paid, the platform fee ($0.50) stays 
in our Locus wallet — no manual invoicing, no payment 
processor, no fiat conversion needed.

### 6. 🏪 Open Agent Marketplace
Any developer can register their agent on Syndicate,
set their own USDC rate, and earn passively every time 
their agent gets hired — all settlements via Locus.

**Locus isn't just our payment layer —

> See the storm before it forms.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ml](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ml-333333?style=flat-square) ![Agentic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agentic-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern supply chains are extremely vulnerable to unexpected global events such as weather disruptions, geopolitical conflicts, port congestion, and maritime route changes. 

The biggest issue today is that most systems are reactive — companies only realize there is a problem *after* delays, cost increases, or disruptions have already occurred.

Vigil solves this by acting as an early warning intelligence system.

It continuously monitors multiple real-time signals:
- Environmental data (NOAA)
- Geopolitical and business news (Reuters)
- Maritime activity (AIS/Vessel data)

These signals are processed using AI models (NVIDIA + Groq) to detect patterns and predict potential disruptions before they escalate.

Instead of raw data, Vigil provides:
- Clear risk alerts
- Contextual insights
- Actionable summaries

This makes existing tasks:
- Faster → no need to manually track multiple data sources  
- Safer → early detection prevents major losses  
- Smarter → AI-driven decision support  

Use cases include:
- Logistics teams anticipating shipment delays  
- Procurement teams adjusting sourcing strategies  
- Companies mitigating risks from global disruptions  

In short, Vigil transforms scattered global signals into predictive, actionable intelligence for supply chain decision-making.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges during development was dealing with integration complexity across multiple APIs and technologies.

We initially planned to use enterprise-grade APIs like MarineTraffic and advanced satellite platforms, but these required paid access, complex authentication, or enterprise approval. This forced us to rethink our architecture and find reliable alternatives that were accessible within the scope of a hackathon.

Another challenge was environment setup and dependency management. There was confusion between Node.js and Python environments, which led to issues such as missing scripts, incorrect runtime commands, and module import errors. For example, missing packages like `python-multipart` and `dotenv` caused runtime failures during backend execution.

We resolved these issues by:
- Standardizing the backend to Python (FastAPI)
- Installing dependencies through `requirements.txt`
- Debugging errors step-by-step and identifying root causes instead of surface-level fixes

Additionally, handling real-time data from different sources required careful structuring to ensure consistent input for the AI models.

Overall, these challenges helped us refine the system into a more modular, robust, and practical MVP, capable of demonstrating the core idea effectively.

**The problem it solves**

Signals uses a four-agent AI system to automate trading.
Three agents gather intelligence:

- DEX Data Agent for technical analysis
- Social Agent for Twitter sentiment
- GMGN Agent for holder and risk analysis

A fourth Agentic Trader combines these inputs to generate BUY, SELL, or HOLD signals, along with price targets and stop-losses. It continuously improves by learning from past trades using a trading journal.

Security & Safety

1. AI Pre-Trade Checks: Detects rug pulls using holder data
2. Restricted Permissions: AI can trade but cannot withdraw funds
3. Self-Custody (ERC-4626): Users retain full control of assets
4. Kill Switch: Emergency pause for abnormal activity

- Opaque Strategies:
You engage in yield farming with hidden strategies that you cannot audit.

- Blind Trust:
You are forced to trust centralized funds with your money instead of maintaining control.

- "Black Box" AI Bots:
Even if you use existing AI trading bots, you never get to see why the AI bought or sold, making it impossible to know if a trade was a good decision or just blind luck.

**The problem it solves**

## ❗ The Problem It Solves

Modern software systems are becoming increasingly complex, making it difficult for developers to:

- Understand large and unfamiliar codebases  
- Identify where specific features are implemented  
- Safely modify code without breaking dependencies  
- Analyze the impact of changes before deployment  
- Review pull requests with full repository context  
- Ensure secure handling of sensitive code and data  

Traditional tools rely heavily on manual code reading, keyword search, or limited AI context, which leads to:

- ❌ Slow onboarding  
- ❌ Risky code changes  
- ❌ Poor visibility into system architecture  
- ❌ Inefficient debugging and development cycles  

---

## 💡 What CodeLens Enables

CodeLens transforms any repository into an **intelligent, interactive system** that developers can query and explore.

### 🧠 AI-Powered Code Understanding
- Explain entire codebases in simple terms  
- Understand architecture, modules, and workflows instantly  

---

### 🔍 Semantic Code Search
- Find functionality based on intent, not keywords  
- Example: *“Where is authentication implemented?”*  

---

### 🔗 Dependency & Impact Analysis
- Trace relationships between functions, files, and modules  
- Identify **what breaks if a change is made**  

---

### 💥 Blast Radius Visualization
- Visualize how far a change propagates across the system  
- Helps developers understand the **scope of impact** before modifying code  

---

### ⚠️ Severity Score Analysis
- Assigns risk levels to code changes  
- Highlights:
  - potential bugs  
  - security risks  
  - performance issues  

---

### 📊 Complexity Metrics
- Analyze complexity at:
  - function level  
  - file level  
  - module level  
- Helps identify:
  - hard-to-maintain code  
  - refactoring opportunities  

---

### 🔐 Digital Data Protection
- Ensures sensitive code and data are handled securely  
- Uses secure API-based AI processing (Gemini)  
- Designed to minimize unnecessary exposure of repository data  

---

## 🚀 How It Makes Development Easier

CodeLens reduces developer effort by:

- ⏱ Cutting onboarding time from days → minutes  
- 🔎 Eliminating manual code searching  
- 🛠 Enabling safer code changes with impact insights  
- 📈 Improving productivity with intelligent recommendations  
- 🧩 Providing a structured understanding of complex systems  

---

## 🎯 Real-World Use Cases

- 🧑‍💻 New developers onboarding into a project  
- 🛠 Engineers modifying critical features  
- 🔍 Debugging complex issues across modules  
- 📦 Reviewing pull requests with full context  
- 🏗 Understanding architecture of open-source projects  

---

## 🏆 Why It Matters

> CodeLens shifts development from **“reading code manually”**  
> to **“interacting with code intelligently.”**

**Challenges we ran into**

## ⚠️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building CodeLens was not just about integrating AI — it involved solving multiple real-world engineering challenges across data processing, system scalability, and production deployment.

---

### 🧱 1. Free Tier Limitations & Database Overflow

**Problem:**
- We initially used free tiers of multiple databases (MongoDB, Pinecone, Neo4j)
- As repositories grew larger, we faced:
  - storage limits  
  - query restrictions  
  - performance bottlenecks  

**Impact:**
- Failed insert operations  
- Slow retrieval during RAG queries  
- Inconsistent system performance  

**Solution:**
- Optimized chunk storage (reduced unnecessary data)
- Implemented selective indexing (only important files)
- Reduced embedding size and frequency
- Designed system to be scalable for future paid infrastructure  

---

### ⚙️ 2. Production Deployment Errors

**Problem:**
- Code that worked locally failed in production environments  
- Issues included:
  - environment variable mismatches  
  - API failures  
  - CORS and network errors  
  - memory constraints  

**Impact:**
- Backend crashes  
- API request failures  
- Broken user flow  

**Solution:**
- Added proper environment configuration management (.env handling)
- Implemented robust error handling and logging
- Used retry mechanisms for API calls
- Optimized memory usage for server processes  

---

### 🧩 3. RAG Pipeline Issues (Indexing & Chunking)

**Problem:**
- While processing cloned repositories:
  - chunk generation sometimes returned zero results  
  - improper parsing of files  
  - inconsistent embedding generation  

**Impact:**
- No relevant results during query  
- Poor AI responses  
- System appeared non-functional  

**Solution:**
- Fixed file parsing logic (handled multiple file types properly)
- Improved chunking strategy (function-level + logical splitting)
- Added debugging logs at each pipeline stage:
  - file fetch  
  - chunk creation  
  - embedding generation  
  - database insertion  
- Ensured embeddings were correctly stored and retrieved  

---

### 🔗 4. Managing Multi-System Integration

**Problem:**
- The system integrates:
  - vector database (Pinecone)  
  - graph database (Neo4j)  
  - document database (MongoDB)  
  - AI APIs (Gemini)  

**Impact:**
- Synchronization issues between systems  
- Increased complexity in debugging  

**Solution:**
- Modularized backend architecture  
- Created separate services for:
  - ingestion  
  - retrieval  
  - dependency analysis  
- Improved data consistency checks  

---

## 🎯 Key Learnings

- Building AI systems is not just about models — it's about **data pipelines and system design**  
- Debugging RAG pipelines requires **step-by-step validation**  
- Free-tier tools are great for MVPs, but **scalability requires optimization**  
- Strong logging and monitoring are essential for production-ready systems  

---

## 🚀 Outcome

These challenges helped us build a more **robust, scalable, and reliable system**, making CodeLens closer to a real-world developer tool rather than just a prototype.

**The problem it solves**

# DGL

**Apna score batao. AI real score dega.**

A fun on-chain game where developers stake ETH, declare their website score, and let AI agents reveal the truth.

---

## The Problem It Solves

In every hackathon, college project, or dev portfolio showcase, the same story repeats:

- Developers confidently **self-declare** their website or project score  
  ("Mera UI fire hai", "Code bahut clean hai", "Security solid hai")

- Judges and recruiters have to **manually review** hundreds of submissions — which is slow, subjective, and biased

- Many projects look good on the surface but hide poor code quality, bad UX, performance issues, or serious security vulnerabilities

- Overconfident "delulu" scores lead to unfair results — real talent gets overlooked while flashy but shallow projects win

- There's **zero trust** in self-claimed scores because there's no objective, transparent verification system

### The Core Problem Statement

> "There is no trustless, objective way to verify a developer's self-claimed score for their website or project."

Just like in **India's Got Latent**, contestants predict their own score and get judged — but in the developer world, this judgment is still manual, slow, and unfair.

---

## Our Solution

**Dev's Got Latent** turns this into a fun, trustless game:

1. **Stake ETH** (on testnet/mainnet)
2. **Declare your score** — How good do you think your website is?
3. **Submit** your GitHub repo + live website link
4. **AI Agents** automatically review:
   - Code quality (Semgrep + Sonar-style rules)
   - UI/UX & Layout (Vision model + computer-use agent)
   - Security & Vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10)
   - Performance (Lighthouse)
5. **Verified Score** is revealed
6. If your self-score **matches** the AI verified score → You win a share of the prize pool!

It's like **India's Got Latent** meets Web3 + AI — but for developers.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

1. AI Consistency & Hallucination
2. Running Safe Computer-Use + Vision Agents
3. Integrating Blockchain + Off-chain AI
4. Scoring Fairness & Transparency

> An Economy of Autonomous Intelligence

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AngularJS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AngularJS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Core Problem**

The AI generation economy and the Web3 ownership economy have never been meaningfully combined into a single utility platform. Today, they fail users in three distinct ways:

**Creators have no ownership over what AI generates for them**

Platforms like Midjourney or Runway produce outputs that live on a centralised server. The creator has no on-chain proof of authorship, no royalty mechanism, and no way to monetise secondary interest in their work. They generate, download, and lose all future value.

**Trading bots are unverifiable black boxes**

Retail traders who want algorithmic strategies are forced to trust performance dashboards on centralised platforms — dashboards that can be edited, cherry-picked, or fabricated entirely. There is no trustless way to audit a bot's real history before allocating capital to it.

**AI-generated assets and financial agents sit idle**

Even in Web3, NFTs are static. They sit in wallets appreciating or depreciating based entirely on speculation, with no intrinsic utility, no earnings, and no evolution. There is no platform where an AI-powered asset actively works, earns, and grows in verifiable, on-chain value over time.

**What AgentForge Does**

AgentForge is a Web3 utility platform where users mint AI agents as NFTs and put them to work — either as Content Agents that generate and monetise AI-created media, or as Trading Agents that execute on-chain strategies using the platform's native $FORGE token.

**For Content Creators:**

Buy a subscription plan in $FORGE
Use your Content Agent to generate images, videos, or written content via Gemini API
Every output is automatically minted as an NFT and listed on the AgentForge marketplace
Earn $FORGE royalties on every secondary sale — permanently, enforced by smart contract
As your content performs, your Agent's reputation score rises, making the NFT itself more valuable

**For Traders:**

Browse the marketplace leaderboard and allocate $FORGE to a pre-built Trading Agent with a fully public, immutable on-chain trade history
Or build a custom Trading Agent — define your strategy, risk parameters, and asset class, and the platform trains a reinforcement learning model to execute it autonomously
Performance is visualised through live graphs — returns over time, win rate, drawdown, and trade-by-trade breakdown
Top-performing custom bots can be listed on the marketplace, earning their creator a performance fee every time another user allocates to them

**For Passive Income:**

Any high-performing agent — content or trading — can be staked on the rental marketplace
Other users lease access via smart contract for a defined period
The owner earns $FORGE continuously without active involvement
The agent's on-chain history is the proof of value — no marketing needed, the track record speaks for itself

**Why It Cannot Be Replicated on Web2**

Every critical guarantee AgentForge provides depends on blockchain infrastructure. The immutability of trade history, the trustless royalty splits, the agent wallet isolation via ERC-6551, the permanent on-chain evolution of agent metadata — none of this is possible on a centralised server where any record can be altered. The longer an agent operates on-chain, the more its history becomes an irreproducible asset that no competing platform can offer.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Designing the $FORGE Token Economy Without Creating Hyperinflation**
The hardest non-technical challenge was designing the tokenomics so that the platform does not collapse under its own incentive structure. If agents earn too freely, $FORGE inflates and loses value. If earning is too restrictive, users have no motivation to stay. The solution was a multi-sink model — subscriptions burn $FORGE, marketplace transactions redistribute it, and rental fees recirculate it — so supply and demand stay in dynamic equilibrium rather than either exploding or drying up.
**ERC-6551 Token Bound Accounts and Agent Wallet Isolation**
Implementing ERC-6551 so that each agent NFT has its own isolated on-chain wallet — capable of holding $FORGE, receiving payments, and executing transactions — without creating security vulnerabilities between parent wallet and agent wallet was a significant smart contract challenge. The key was strict access control: only the NFT owner's address can issue directives to the agent wallet, and the agent wallet can only transact within whitelisted platform contracts.
**On-Chain Metadata Evolution Without Excessive Gas Costs**
Agent DNA and skill scores need to update as agents perform — but writing every evolution event directly to on-chain storage is gas-prohibitively expensive. The solution was a hybrid architecture: base DNA and ownership are fully on-chain, while performance deltas are accumulated off-chain and committed to the chain in batched merkle-proof updates at set intervals, keeping the immutability guarantees without making micro-updates economically unviable.
**RL Training Pipeline for Custom Trading Agents**
Building a reinforcement learning pipeline that could accept user-defined strategy parameters and train a deployable model in a reasonable timeframe — without requiring the user to understand ML — required significant abstraction. The solution was a constrained action space design: users define goals and risk parameters through a structured UI, which maps directly to pre-defined RL reward functions, keeping the user experience simple while the backend handles the full training loop.

**Winners**

AgentForge is built for the Winners track because it represents a category-defining convergence of three of the most significant technology shifts of this decade, generative AI, autonomous agents, and decentralised ownership — into a single, economically coherent utility platform.
It is not a proof of concept. It is a working economic primitive.
Most hackathon projects demonstrate one technology. AgentForge demonstrates a closed-loop economy: $FORGE tokens flow in through subscriptions, circulate through agent earnings, compound through rental markets, and appreciate through on-chain performance history, all without a centralised intermediary controlling any part of the value chain.
The technical ambition is matched by real utility. Every feature serves a user who earns real value, the creator monetising AI outputs they actually own, the trader allocating capital to a bot whose entire history is publicly auditable, the operator building a portfolio of AI agents that generate passive income while they sleep.
The on-chain track record mechanism is a novel contribution. By anchoring agent value to immutable, verifiable performance history rather than speculation, AgentForge introduces a new standard for how AI-powered financial and creative assets should be valued and traded. This is not a feature, it is a new market design.
AgentForge does not fit neatly into any single existing category because it creates its own. That is precisely why it belongs in the Winners track.
