### OPM
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/opm-c347) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/dhananjaypai08/opm) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://opm-sec.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/9d3ded933558492fa7503d6fe26749b5) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> On-chain security layer for npm

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ink](https://img.shields.io/badge/ink-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**OPM secures your npm workflow by running AI security scans, verifying package integrity on-chain, and analyzing dependency graphs before any code reaches your node_modules**

---

### What it solves

The npm ecosystem runs on trust that often goes unchecked. A single **npm install** can pull in hundreds or thousands of transitive dependencies. Developers usually have no clear way to know whether one of those packages contains malware, a typosquatted name, or a known vulnerability.

Recent supply chain incidents show how dangerous this model is. Wallet drainers, credential stealers, and prototype pollution exploits have all been distributed through packages that looked legitimate at first glance. These attacks have already caused millions in losses and continue to target both Web2 and Web3 developers.

OPM introduces a safety layer in front of the install process. Instead of trusting every dependency blindly, packages are analyzed and verified before they are allowed into a project.

---

### What you can use it for

* **opm install**
A drop-in replacement for npm install. Every package is scanned before installation using AI security agents, vulnerability databases, and blocklists such as ChainPatrol. If a version is unsafe, OPM recommends or installs the safest available alternative.

* **opm check**
Scans your entire dependency tree including transitive dependencies. Multiple AI agents analyze packages in parallel for typosquats, malicious code patterns, and known CVEs. Results are aggregated and anchored to a Merkle root so the analysis can be verified later.

* **opm fix**
Automatically updates vulnerable or suspicious dependencies in package.json. If a package has a safer version or trusted alternative, OPM suggests and applies the fix.

* **opm push**
Publishes your package to npm while also registering its checksum and metadata on-chain. The publish step includes a multi-agent security scan and optional ENS-linked identity so consumers can verify who published the package and what security checks it passed.

* **opm audit**
  Performs a deeper security audit of your project. Dependencies are checked against on-chain risk scores, ChainPatrol blocklists, and the OSV vulnerability database.

---

### How it makes things safer

| Without OPM                                                  | With OPM                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm install` trusts packages by default                     | Packages are checked against vulnerability databases and security scores before install |
| Transitive dependencies are hard to inspect                  | Full dependency graph with risk propagation and verifiable Merkle roots                 |
| Supply chain attacks are often discovered after installation | AI agents and rule-based scanners detect threats before code enters the project         |
| Maintainer identity is only an npm username                  | Optional ENS-linked identities and signed metadata                                      |
| Security audits are static reports                           | Audit results stored on decentralized storage and linked to package records             |
| No verification of how scans were produced                   | Multi-agent analysis with cryptographic integrity for results                           |

---

### Who it's for

* **Developers using npm**
  `opm install` and `opm check` work with existing Node.js projects and require no blockchain knowledge.

* **Package maintainers**
  `opm push` provides verifiable package metadata, identity linking, and security attestations.

* **Security teams**
  Dependency graph scanning and risk propagation highlight vulnerabilities buried deep inside dependency trees.

* **Web3 builders**
  ENS-linked identities, on-chain package records, and verifiable dependency graphs help build more trustworthy software supply chains.

**Challenges we ran into**

Agent onboarding :
How do we onboard agents without verifying? Use labelled datasets without revealing the data itself

Reasoning Model API Constraints
OpenAI's reasoning models (o4-mini) reject temperature and response_format parameters that work fine with standard chat models. The scanner had to detect reasoning models at runtime and strip unsupported parameters from the request body, or every scan with a mixed model pool would fail.

**Privacy**

OPM addresses the #1 threat vector in modern software: npm supply chain attacks. It scans every dependency (direct and transitive) for typosquats, known CVEs, and malicious patterns using multiple AI agents. Packages are verified on-chain with signed checksums. The full dependency tree is cryptographically committed via a Merkle root. New scanning agents must pass **ZK-verified benchmarks** before they can participate. Every audit report is stored immutably on IPFS. The result: no package reaches node_modules without verifiable proof it's safe

**AI**

### 1. Multi-Agent Security Scanning

Every opm push, opm check, and opm fix command runs multiple AI agents in parallel. Each agent analyzes the package source code, version history, dependency list, and CVE data, then returns a structured report with a risk score (0–100), vulnerabilities, supply chain indicators (install scripts, eval usage, network calls, environment access), and a recommendation (SAFE, CAUTION, WARN, BLOCK).

Agents use different LLM models such as GPT-5.4, o4-mini, and community models to avoid single-model blind spots. Results are combined using intelligence-weighted scoring based on benchmark performance in coding and reasoning tasks.

---

### 2. Permissionless Agent Registration with ZK Verification

Anyone can register an AI agent using opm register-agent. Before registration, the agent must pass 10 labeled security test cases covering typosquats, CVEs, obfuscated malware, and safe packages, achieving 100 percent accuracy.

Accuracy is verified with a zero-knowledge proof built using Circom and snarkjs. The circuit computes the accuracy from the agent’s responses and expected labels and generates a proof that accuracy equals 100 percent without revealing the test data. The proof is verified on-chain during registration, and only verified agents can submit scores to the OPM contract.

---

### 3. AI-Powered Dependency Analysis in opm check

When opm check runs, a fast rule-based scan first queries OSV vulnerabilities, checks typosquats, and reads on-chain risk scores across all dependencies. AI agents then analyze the direct dependency list and full dependency tree.

Each agent returns flagged issues, severity levels, recommended replacements, and an overall risk assessment. If two or more agents flag the same package, opm fix can automatically update package.json with a safer version or replacement.

---

### 4. Structured Output and Response Normalization

Each AI agent returns JSON following a strict schema defined in CHECK_SYSTEM_PROMPT. Since LLM providers often return slightly different formats such as different field names or severity labels, OPM includes a normalization layer that validates and converts every response into a consistent AgentScanResult structure before scoring.

---

### 5. Intelligence-Weighted Consensus

Final risk scores are computed using intelligence-weighted consensus rather than simple averaging. Each agent’s contribution is weighted by its model’s benchmark performance from Artificial Analysis rankings. Stronger models therefore have greater influence on the final security score that is stored on-chain.

**Best creative use of ENS**

OPM uses ENS as the identity and metadata backbone for the entire package ecosystem.

**Author identity**: Package authors are identified by their ENS name, not just an npm username. When you run opm push, your ENS name is resolved from your signing key and attached to the on-chain package registration. Consumers can verify the author via opm view djpai.eth to see their on-chain reputation, published packages, and security scores.

**Package metadata as ENS text records**: Each push writes structured records to ENS:

opm.version - current package version
opm.checksum - tarball integrity hash
opm.risk_score - aggregate AI security score
opm.fileverse - link to the Fileverse audit report
opm.deptree - Merkle root of the dependency graph
opm.signature - author's cryptographic signature
**ENS subnames for packages**: Each package gets its own ENS subname (e.g., express.djpai.eth) with package-specific records, so a single author ENS name can host metadata for multiple packages without collision.

**ENS contenthash for IPFS**: The Fileverse audit report's IPFS content hash is read from the Fileverse Portal smart contract and written into the ENS contenthash field, making reports resolvable via ENS-native tooling.

**ENS as version resolver**: In package.json, you can use an ENS name as a version specifier ("express": "djpai.eth"). OPM resolves the ENS name, verifies the author is registered on-chain, and installs the safest available version:

// packages/cli/src/services/version.ts
if (isENSVersion(version)) {
  const authorAddr = await resolveAddress(ensName);
  const profile = await getAuthorByENS(ensName);
  // verify author is registered on-chain
  const safestVersion = await getSafestVersion(packageName);
  return { version: safestVersion, source: 'ens', ensName, authorAddress };
}
**Multicall batching**: All ENS record writes are batched into a single multicall transaction to minimize gas costs, writing 10-14 records in one tx instead of 14 separate transactions.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Hosted on cloud : https://opm-fileverse-4dc48255e118.herokuapp.com

Agent aggregated report sample : https://docs.fileverse.io/0x05EfCD46eC916cA68BF677968cc786E88135d70C/53#key=QQ7Dhuj4gANrs3BW-9nOwHP_qhnyp8jlr9tLUc7tdYx1sK4FScVb5_SVj6sqo7Ww

OPM uses Fileverse as the decentralized storage layer for security audit reports. When a package is scanned through opm push or opm check, the full report including AI agent findings, CVE data, risk scores, and dependency analysis is formatted as markdown and uploaded to Fileverse as a dDoc. The returned link is stored in the OPM registry contract and also written to an ENS text record called opm.fileverse.

OPM then reads the IPFS content hash from the Fileverse Portal contract by extracting the portal address and file ID from the dDoc URL and querying the files() function to obtain the metadataIPFSHash. This CID is written to the ENS contenthash field so the audit report can be resolved directly through ENS.

As a result, every OPM security audit is stored on IPFS through Fileverse, linked via ENS, and referenced on-chain, creating a permanent and verifiable audit trail.

**AI × Onchain**

OPM implements a permissionless multi-agent orchestration protocol anchored entirely on Base Sepolia. The **OPMRegistry** smart contract (deployed at **0x16684391fc9bf48246B08Afe16d1a57BFa181d48**) serves as the canonical source of truth for package integrity, agent authorization, and risk scoring. Every opm push registers a package version on-chain with a signed checksum, **triggers parallel AI agent scans across heterogeneous LLM providers, and writes intelligence-weighted aggregate risk scores** back to the contract via submitScore(). Agent registration itself is on-chain: any wallet can call registerAgent() to join the scanning pool, but only after passing a ZK-verified benchmark gate. The contract enforces authorizedAgents[msg.sender] checks so only verified agents can write scores. This creates a fully on-chain AI agent marketplace where model quality is cryptographically attested and scan results are immutably stored. The dependency graph Merkle root is also committed on-chain during publish, enabling consumers to verify that the entire transitive dependency tree has not degraded since the author's last audit. All of this runs on Base for low-cost, high-throughput settlement while **leveraging EIP-8004 patterns** for structured on-chain data attestation, making OPM a production example of AI inference results being settled and verified on a Layer 2

**Privacy**

OPM uses zero-knowledge proofs (Circom circuits + snarkjs) to verify AI agent quality without exposing the benchmark data or individual test results. When a new agent registers via opm register-agent, it is evaluated against 10 labeled security test cases covering typosquats, CVE exploitation, obfuscated malware, and clean packages. The **ZK circuit takes the agent's responses and the expected labels as private inputs**, computes accuracy internally, and produces a proof that accuracy equals 100% without revealing which test cases exist, what the expected outputs are, or how the agent performed on any individual case. The proof hash and system prompt hash are stored on-chain (proofHash and systemPromptHash in the RegisteredAgent struct), so anyone can verify that a registered agent passed the benchmark without the benchmark dataset ever being exposed. This prevents adversarial agents from gaming the test suite by memorizing answers, since the **labeled data remains a private input to the proof generation circuit**. The verification is fully on-chain: the contract checks the proof before authorizing the agent wallet, ensuring that privacy-preserving attestation is enforced at the protocol level rather than trusted off-chain

**BEST Overall Project**

OPM is a fully functional CLI tool that ships real security infrastructure: multi-agent AI scanning, on-chain package registry, ZK-verified agent onboarding, dependency graph analysis with Merkle proofs, ENS identity integration, and decentralized audit storage on IPFS. It works end-to-end as a drop-in npm replacement that any developer can install and use today on any Node.js project

2) Clipboard API mismatch in React Native flow
What happened:
Copy/paste actions used the old React Native clipboard API, which is no longer the recommended approach in modern Expo setups.

How I fixed it:

Migrated copy/paste logic to Expo Clipboard.
Updated both reusable UI components and screen-level handlers using clipboard actions.
Outcome:
Copy address and paste recipient features worked consistently and passed type checks.

3) Missing icon dependency/type resolution
What happened:
Icon imports failed with type/module resolution errors during diagnostics.

How I fixed it:

Added the vector icons package explicitly to dependencies.
Installed related package updates through Expo-compatible install commands.
Outcome:
Icon-related compile/type issues were resolved across wallet, pay, receive, and settings screens.

4) Data shape mismatch in activity transaction list
What happened:
The activity screen passed props that did not match the transaction row component contract (field names and timestamp type mismatches).

How I fixed it:

Normalized mock data structure to match expected props.
Converted timestamps into compatible date string format.
Added an empty state for filtered results.

Activity screen rendered correctly and no longer threw prop/type errors.

5) APK build and artifact management
What happened:
Release build logs were noisy with Gradle warnings, and the generated APK was nested deep in Android output folders.

How I fixed it:

Completed a full release build using Gradle assembleRelease.
Verified build success and manually copied the APK to the repository root for easy access.
Outcome:
A production release APK was generated successfully and made easy to locate for sharing/testing.

**The problem it solves**

Today's Web3 lending is broken it demands 150–200% collateral, meaning you must already have wealth to borrow. This shuts out billions of people who have demonstrated trustworthiness through their on-chain behavior but lack the capital to over-collateralize. Traditional credit scoring systems don't exist on-chain, and banks are inaccessible to the unbanked and underbanked across the globe. Meanwhile, DeFi protocols have no way to evaluate who a person is or how reliably they repay so they default to brute-force collateral.

Zentra replaces collateral with community trust. It builds a permissionless, privacy-preserving trust score by analyzing wallet age, repayment history, circle participation, and platform activity entirely on-chain. Users form Trust Circles, where community members vouch for each other, creating a decentralized credit network that mirrors how lending works in real-world communities. This enables under-collateralized loans on Polygon without banks, credit bureaus, or identity documents.

The result: faster loans, lower barriers, and financial access for anyone with an honest on-chain history not just those who are already wealthy.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Zentra pushed us into uncharted territory at every layer of the stack. Designing a fair, manipulation-resistant trust score that couldn't be gamed by creating fresh wallets was one of the hardest problems we had to balance multiple on-chain signals without penalizing new users unfairly. Integrating Gemini AI for real-time fraud analysis on loan requests introduced latency and rate-limiting issues that required fallback scoring logic to keep the app functional. Firebase and Wagmi had conflicting async patterns that caused hydration mismatches in Next.js, which took significant debugging to resolve. Deploying the TrustCircles smart contract on Polygon Amoy meant dealing with intermittent RPC failures and gas estimation errors. On Windows, the Next.js dev server threw ESM URL scheme errors with .mjs config files, requiring a full conversion to CommonJS. Making the Trust Circle mechanics fair preventing one bad actor from dragging down an entire circle's score equired careful smart contract design. Connecting live contract state to the fraud profile in real time without over-fetching or causing stale UI was another major engineering challenge. Finally, ensuring the entire system worked without a Gemini API key as a fallback, so the app never fully breaks, required building a complete rule-based scoring engine as a backup.

**Web3**

Why a user would use it?
Need a loan but have no collateral can borrow based on wallet history + circle membership, not locked assets
Capital efficiency  don't need to lock up 2x the amount you want to borrow
Build credit on-chain each successful repayment increases your score and borrowing limit
Community benefit joining a Trust Circle raises everyone's limits; you're incentivized to vouch for trustworthy people
No bank, no delays instant on-chain settlement on Polygon (low fees, fast finality)
Permissionless no ID, no bank account, no credit bureau just a wallet

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

Uniswap v3 introduced concentrated liquidity, which dramatically improved capital efficiency — but it also turned liquidity provision into an active operational task.

Liquidity providers must:

- Continuously monitor price movements  
- Rebalance positions when price drifts  
- Weigh gas costs vs fee opportunity  
- Avoid capital sitting idle out of range  
- Manage volatility regimes  

This creates an operational burden. LPs either:
- Spend significant time manually managing positions, or  
- Run bots with private infrastructure, or  
- Delegate to custodial vaults and lose direct control  

Concentrated liquidity is powerful — but it is not passive.

## What Mercuri Enables

Mercuri Finance provides non-custodial autonomous vaults on Base that:

- Automate liquidity rebalancing
- Enforce deterministic smart contract safety
- Preserve full user custody
- Log and analyze every decision

Users can deposit a token pair into a vault and let protocol-enforced automation manage the position within predefined bounds.

## How It Makes Things Easier

Mercuri reduces:

- Manual monitoring
- Gas-inefficient rebalancing
- Emotional decision-making
- Infrastructure overhead

At the same time, it increases:

- Transparency (every decision is logged)
- Determinism (smart contract-enforced invariants)
- Safety (fail-closed logic)
- Capital efficiency

Instead of “trusting a manager,” users rely on bounded, protocol-first automation.

Liquidity — without the operational overhead.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Major Challenge: Separating AI Reasoning from Asset Control

One of the biggest architectural hurdles was ensuring that AI decision-making never directly controlled assets.

LLMs are probabilistic systems. Smart contracts are deterministic systems. Mixing those two layers incorrectly introduces systemic risk.

The key challenge was:

How do we allow adaptive decision-making without ever giving the model execution authority?

### What We Did

We enforced a strict separation of planes:

- **State Plane:** Smart contracts hold custody and enforce invariants.
- **Execution Plane:** Permissioned agents can call specific contract functions.
- **Decision Plane:** The LLM can only recommend bounded actions.

The LLM:
- Cannot sign transactions
- Cannot withdraw assets
- Cannot invent new actions
- Must return strict JSON
- Defaults to `NO_ACTION` on failure

Even malformed responses or API outages result in safe inaction.

This required:
- Deterministic schema validation
- Fail-closed fallback logic
- Explicit role separation in smart contracts
- Distributed locking to prevent concurrent execution

The result is a system where intelligence operates inside rails — not outside them.

---

## Technical Hurdle: Order-Sensitive Unwind in Uniswap v3

Another non-trivial issue was correctly handling fee collection vs principal withdrawal in Uniswap v3.

Because `collect()` behavior changes depending on whether liquidity is active, incorrect sequencing could cause protocol fees to apply to principal instead of just swap fees.

We solved this by:

1. Explicitly collecting fees while liquidity is active
2. Applying protocol performance fee
3. Removing liquidity
4. Collecting remaining principal
5. Rebalancing inventory
6. Minting a new position

This sequencing guarantees:
- Fees are separated from principal
- No accidental overcharging
- Deterministic accounting

This required careful reading of Uniswap internals and extensive testing.

Mercuri A

**The problem it solves**

# Veridex
### Real-Time AI Hallucination Intelligence — Because Confidence Isn't the Same as Accuracy

---

## AI Lies. Fluently. And You Can't Tell.

AI models don't stutter when they fabricate. They produce wrong answers with the same polished, authoritative prose as correct ones — and in professional settings, that is a crisis waiting to happen.

These aren't hypotheticals. They've already happened.

| Year | Incident | Consequence |
|------|----------|-------------|
| 2023 | Attorney Steven Schwartz submitted six AI-fabricated court cases in a federal brief. None existed. | Sanctions, disciplinary proceedings, reputational collapse |
| 2023 | NEDA's AI counselor gave eating disorder patients advice that violated established clinical guidelines. | Immediate shutdown, global backlash |
| 2024 | Air Canada's chatbot invented a bereavement fare policy. A tribunal ruled the airline liable for its own AI's hallucination. | Forced payout, landmark legal precedent |
| 2023 | CNET published AI-written financial articles riddled with calculation errors — quietly, at scale. | Public correction campaign, lasting credibility damage |

The pattern is identical every time: confident output, professional trust, serious damage.

---

## What Veridex Does

Veridex is a domain-intelligent, claim-level hallucination detection platform — delivered as a Chrome Extension that works silently inside the AI tools you already use. No copy-pasting, no tab-switching, no friction.

Install once. Every response you receive on ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini is analyzed in real time — before it influences a document, a decision, or a patient.

- Fabricated claims are underlined in red, uncertain ones in yellow — directly inside the AI's response
- Hover any underline to see what is wrong, how serious it is, and what the verified fact actually says
- A Trust Score badge appears on every response for an instant reliability read
- The extension panel shows a full claim-by-claim severity breakdown

---

## Three Specialized Engines. Not One Generic Tool.

Most fact-checkers use Wikipedia and broad web search. For casual use, that is acceptable. For professional use, it is dangerously insufficient. Veridex deploys three purpose-built verification modules, each sourced from references that domain experts actually trust.

**Veridex Legal** is verified against official court databases, published case law, and statute archives. It checks whether a cited case exists, whether the ruling is accurately described, and whether the jurisdiction is correct.

**Veridex Medical** is cross-referenced against WHO, FDA, CDC, and NICE guidelines, peer-reviewed literature, and validated drug interaction databases. Primary sources only — not summaries of summaries.

**Veridex Finance** is validated against official regulatory filings, exchange data, central bank publications, and compliance records. When an AI states a market figure, Veridex checks the source of record.

---

## The Intelligence Layer

**It knows the difference between a claim and an opinion.** "The policy was a failure" is a judgment, not a verifiable fact. Veridex's semantic layer classifies every statement before analysis — opinions are excluded entirely, so every alert you receive is meaningful and none are wasted on subjective content.

**It tells you exactly what is wrong — not just that something is.** A score of "68% reliable" is nearly useless without knowing which claim failed and how badly. Veridex identifies the specific claim, its severity, and the verified correction, sourced from authoritative references and displayed inline.

**It catches hallucination drift.** In longer conversations, AI models degrade — performing well early, then fabricating progressively as context pressure builds, precisely when user trust is at its highest. Veridex pinpoints the exact message where fabrication began, so you know precisely how far back to re-examine.

**Fresh Start — when a conversation is too far gone.** Veridex generates a clean, verified re-prompt that preserves your legitimate context and strips out everything fabricated. Continue in a new session without carrying the errors forward.

---

## Who It Is Built For

> Legal professionals — catch fabricated citations before they reach a brief, a contract, or a tribunal.

> Medical practitioners — validate clinical AI outputs against authoritative guidelines before they influence patient care.

> Financial analysts — verify figures and regulatory claims against official records before they appear in reports or filings.

> Any professional where being wrong carries real consequences.

---

## The Founding Premise

Every other AI tool is racing to make AI more capable. Veridex is built on a different conviction: capability without accountability is a liability.

The question is not whether to use AI — it is whether you can trust it. Without a verification layer, the honest answer is: not unconditionally. We built Veridex so that answer can become

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

---

## Chrome's Content Security Policy Blocked Our Options Page

The setup page loaded visually but did nothing — no settings saved, no feedback. Chrome Extensions prohibit inline scripts entirely, blocking any JavaScript written directly inside an HTML file. The page rendered correctly, giving no visual indication anything was wrong. The error only surfaced when we deliberately opened the browser console.

The fix was moving every line of JavaScript into external `.js` files. Simple once diagnosed — expensive in time before it was.

---

## MutationObserver Firing Mid-Stream

The hallucination analysis was triggering while the AI was still generating its response, sending incomplete text to the verification engine and returning incoherent results. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all stream token by token, continuously updating the DOM — and our observer was firing on the first change.

We added platform-specific streaming detection plus an 800ms debounce after the streaming indicator disappears. Each platform signals completion differently, and none of them document it, so this required reading their DOM behavior directly.

---

## Three Platforms, Three Completely Different DOM Structures

A selector that reliably targets AI responses on ChatGPT does nothing on Claude. A streaming detection method that works on Gemini breaks on ChatGPT. No shared standard, no documentation.

We mapped each platform's structure individually and built an auto-detection layer that selects the right configuration based on the active URL. It works — but any frontend update from any of the three platforms can silently break it, making ongoing maintenance a structural part of the product.

---

## The API Response Was Not Always Valid JSON

The verification engine depends on structured JSON from the Groq API. In testing, the model occasionally wrapped responses in markdown code fences, added explanatory text before the JSON object, or produced trailing commas that broke the parser — all silently, with no highlights appearing and no user-facing indication of failure.

We built a layered parsing strategy: direct parse, then strip fences and retry, then regex extraction, then a graceful failure state. Not elegant, but it handles real-world model output variability reliably.

---

## Calibrating Opinion vs. Fact Detection

Early versions were either too aggressive — flagging analytical judgments as verifiable claims — or too permissive, letting factual assertions slip through the opinion filter. Both undermined trust in the product.

Getting the balance right required iterating on the system prompt and testing against a wide range of real AI outputs across legal, medical, and financial domains. The boundary between opinion and fact is genuinely ambiguous in some contexts, but the classifier now sits at a point where alerts are consistently actionable rather than noise.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Veridex utilizes the Google Gemini API not just as a standard conversational chatbot, but as an intelligent orchestration and reasoning engine at the core of our fact-checking pipeline. We leverage Gemini’s advanced natural language understanding to perform Claim Decomposition—taking a monolithic block of AI-generated text and atomizing it into individual, verifiable claims while categorizing their nature (e.g., statistical fact, historical fact, opinion, prediction).

Furthermore, once our backend retrieves external context from knowledge graphs (like Wikipedia, DuckDuckGo, and FactCheck APIs), the raw data is often messy and unstructured. We use Gemini API's powerful reasoning capabilities to triangulate the data, compare the external sources against the original AI claim, analyze discrepancies, and calculate a definitive verdict. This showcases Gemini’s immense power in complex NLP pipelines, multi-step logical reasoning, and structured data extraction rather than simple text generation.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

Building Veridex was a masterclass in human-AI agent collaboration using Google Antigravity. As an advanced agentic coding assistant, Antigravity wasn't just used for autocomplete; it acted as a full-stack co-founder.

From auditing our initial architecture blueprint to writing the complex Python FastAPI backend with parallel asynchronous endpoints, Antigravity handled the heavy lifting of execution. Crucially, Antigravity was able to autonomously debug and rewrite our intricate Chrome Extension injection scripts that intercept Server-Sent Events (SSE) from platforms like ChatGPT—a notoriously difficult task involving stream reading and DOM manipulation. It seamlessly updated our manifest, built the UI popup to toggle API providers, refactored our backend to support dynamic model injection, and pushed the final code to GitHub.

By delegating the complex coding execution, cross-file refactoring, and deep debugging tasks to Antigravity, our human team was able to focus purely on product vision, system architecture, and user experience—dramatically accelerating our development timeline and allowing us to build a sophisticated, multi-platform product within the hackathon's tight constraints.

**The problem it solves**

**Fundify Campus** – A Decentralized Crowdfunding Platform for Students

**Problem Statement**

Many student projects, clubs, and social initiatives require financial support to grow. However, traditional crowdfunding platforms are not specifically designed for campus communities and often involve high platform fees, lack of transparency, and delayed payment processing.

Due to these limitations, students may find it difficult to build trust with contributors and efficiently manage funds for their ideas, events, or social initiatives.

**Proposed Solution**

**Fundify Campus** is a decentralized crowdfunding platform that allows students to create fundraising campaigns and receive contributions securely using blockchain technology.

The platform is built on the **Algorand blockchain**, where every contribution is recorded transparently and cannot be altered. Supporters can contribute ALGO cryptocurrency directly to campaign wallets, eliminating the need for centralized payment intermediaries.

This approach creates a trustless and transparent environment, where donors can verify all transactions on the blockchain, increasing accountability and trust between campaign creators and supporters.

**Key Features**
Campaign Creation

Students can create crowdfunding campaigns by providing details such as title, description, funding goal, deadline, and project images.

**Campaign Discovery**

Users can browse and explore active fundraising campaigns on the platform and support projects that align with their interests.

**Blockchain Contributions**

Supporters can contribute using ALGO cryptocurrency through a secure wallet connection.

Funding Progress Tracking

Each campaign includes a real-time progress tracker showing the funds raised compared to the campaign goal.

Creator Dashboard

Campaign creators can monitor contributions, track progress, and manage their campaigns from a dedicated dashboard.

Technical Implementation
Frontend

React.js is used to build a responsive and interactive user interface.

Blockchain Integration

The platform uses Algorand blockchain for secure and transparent financial transactions.

Wallet Integration

Wallet connectivity allows users to sign and verify transactions securely before sending contributions.

Optional Smart Contract

An escrow mechanism can be implemented where funds are released only if the campaign reaches its funding goal.

Media Storage

Campaign images can be stored using IPFS or traditional cloud storage.

Algorand Partner Tools Used

Our project is built on the Algorand ecosystem, leveraging its fast, secure, and low-cost blockchain infrastructure to enable transparent crowdfunding for campus projects.

We used the **Algorand SDK (algosdk)** to create and manage blockchain transactions directly from the application. This allows contributors to securely send ALGO cryptocurrency to campaign wallets, while ensuring that every transaction is recorded on-chain.

For wallet connectivity, we integrated Pera Wallet Connect, which enables users to securely sign and approve transactions through their crypto wallet.

Additionally, we used the Algonode API to interact with the Algorand network and retrieve blockchain data such as transaction confirmations and account balances.

By combining these tools, Fundify Campus demonstrates how the Algorand ecosystem can be used to build real-world decentralized applications that promote transparency, trust, and community-driven funding.

**Learning Outcomes**

Through this project, developers gain experience in:

Building decentralized applications (dApps)

Integrating blockchain transactions into web applications

Implementing conditional funding mechanisms such as escrow

Designing secure and user-friendly financial interfaces

Real-World Impact

Fundify Campus enables student innovators, clubs, and social initiatives to raise funds transparently from their campus community.

By leveraging blockchain technology, the platform promotes trust, transparency, and accessibility, making it easier for students to bring their ideas, projects, and initiatives to life.

**Challenges we ran into**

*Wallet Integration Issues*
Connecting and maintaining a stable connection with the wallet required careful handling of session states and user authentication.

*Transaction Confirmation Handling*
Blockchain transactions require confirmation on the network, which sometimes caused delays in updating the campaign balance in real time.

*Handling Blockchain Data in JavaScript*
Managing large numbers returned from blockchain transactions led to BigInt conversion issues, which required proper formatting and handling in the frontend.

*Real-Time UI Updates*
Synchronizing the user interface with blockchain data was challenging, especially when displaying updated campaign balances immediately after a contribution.

*User Experience Design*
Designing a simple and intuitive interface for blockchain interactions was important, since many users may not be familiar with crypto wallets or blockchain transactions.

**Algorand Bharat**

Fundify Campus aligns with the Algorand ecosystem by building a decentralized crowdfunding platform that enables transparent and secure fundraising for student projects and campus initiatives.

The platform uses the Algorand blockchain to record every contribution on-chain, ensuring that transactions are tamper-proof, verifiable, and transparent. Contributors can support campaigns by sending ALGO directly to campaign wallets, eliminating the need for intermediaries and reducing transaction costs.

By leveraging Algorand’s fast, low-cost, and scalable blockchain infrastructure, Fundify Campus demonstrates how decentralized technology can be used to create trustworthy financial systems for communities such as colleges and student organizations.

This project supports the vision of Algorand Bharat by promoting blockchain adoption, encouraging innovation among students, and showcasing real-world decentralized applications built on the Algorand network.

> Obsidian: Anti-Cheat Powered by Math, Not Spyware.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Godot](https://img.shields.io/badge/Godot-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![StarkNet](https://img.shields.io/badge/StarkNet-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem: Anti-Cheat has become Spyware
To play modern competitive games, players are forced to install kernel-level rootkits (like Vanguard, Easy Anti-Cheat, or Ricochet). These systems operate at "Ring 0" of your operating system, giving them unrestricted access to monitor your entire PC, your files, and your background processes.

Furthermore, traditional anti-cheats operate entirely behind closed doors. If a player is falsely banned—which happens frequently—they have no way to appeal or prove their innocence. In a Web3 gaming ecosystem where in-game assets and ranks hold real monetary value, a centralized, "black box" ban can mean stealing hundreds of dollars from a legitimate player.

## The Solution: Obsidian
Obsidian replaces invasive PC surveillance with cryptographic mathematics. We protect the integrity of the game without touching the privacy of the player's computer.

## Here is how Obsidian makes gaming safer and fairer:

Kernel Access Denied (Privacy-First): Instead of scanning a player's hard drive for cheat software, Obsidian simply analyzes the physics and outputs of the player. If the game engine's maximum speed is 10, and a player moves at 50, Obsidian's off-chain relayer instantly flags the mathematical anomaly.

Cryptographic Truth (Starknet Integration): When a cheat is detected, the relayer doesn't just quietly ban the player on a centralized server. It submits a payload to our Web3 settlement layer (Katana/Starknet). The ban becomes a transparent, immutable record on the blockchain.

Trustless Dispute Resolution: Because the telemetry validation is settled on-chain, bans are mathematically provable. A Web3 game studio cannot arbitrarily ban players to steal their assets, and players cannot claim they were falsely banned when the on-chain math proves they were teleporting.

Zero Web3 Friction: Web3 mechanics usually ruin gaming speeds (like signing a MetaMask pop-up for every footstep). Obsidian uses Account Abstraction and Relayer Batching to process telemetry off-chain at 60 FPS, subsidize the gas fees, and only push batched state-changes to the blockchain.

## Who is this for?
Web3 Game Studios: Protect their tokenized economies and high-stakes tournaments from exploiters without forcing crypto-native users to install spyware.

Privacy-Conscious Gamers: Play competitive games without sacrificing the security of their personal computers.

Esports Organizers: Maintain a fully transparent, mathematically verifiable ledger of a tournament's integrity.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges
Building a hybrid architecture that bridges a Web2 game engine (Godot) with a Web3 settlement layer (Starknet) introduced several unique bottlenecks. Here are the main challenges we overcame:

1. The 60-FPS Telemetry Flood
The Hurdle: Our initial Godot prototype was capturing player physics (speed, coordinates) and sending it to our Python Relayer. Because Godot's _process function runs 60 times a second, it was firing 60 HTTP POST requests per second. This immediately overloaded Godot's HTTPRequest nodes, causing network jam crashes and dropping critical anti-cheat data.
The Solution: We implemented a custom throttling and batching mechanism. By introducing a cooldown timer and checking the HTTPClient status before firing, we reduced the telemetry output to a manageable 5 times per second. This preserved the fidelity needed to catch speed hackers without crashing the client's network thread.

2. The "Silent" Blockchain Bridge
The Hurdle: We successfully got the Python middleware to detect speed and damage hacks in real-time. However, when we tried to forward this "Guilty" verdict to our local Starknet sequencer (Katana) via JSON-RPC, the blockchain terminal remained completely silent. We spent critical hackathon hours thinking our Web3 bridge was fundamentally broken.
The Solution: We realized we were sending a read-only RPC call (starknet_chainId), which Katana processes silently in the background to prevent terminal spam. We rewrote the JSON-RPC payload to trigger katana_generateBlock. This forced an immediate, hard state change on the sequencer, instantly mining a block and proving our off-chain relayer could successfully dictate on-chain settlement.

3. Engine Dependency Corruption Mid-Hackathon
The Hurdle: Late into the hackathon, we refactored our entire directory structure to prove Obsidian could act as a multi-game SDK (managing two different games at once). Moving the game files completely broke Godot's hidden .godot dependency cache, throwing hundreds of "Invalid UID" and missing resource errors that prevented the games from compiling.
The Solution: Instead of manually relinking hundreds of assets and .tres files, we utilized the command line to force a headless editor rebuild (godot --headless --editor --quit). This wiped the corrupted cache and forced the engine to autonomously rescan and repair the asset library, getting both games back online.

**Web3**

Obsidian fits perfectly into the Web3 track by using decentralized mechanics to solve one of the biggest problems in modern gaming: invasive, centralized anti-cheat spyware.

Instead of forcing players to install dangerous kernel-level rootkits (like Vanguard or Easy Anti-Cheat) and blindly trusting a centralized game developer, Obsidian shifts that trust entirely to mathematics and the blockchain. We integrated Web3 into our architecture in the following ways:

On-Chain Settlement (Starknet): We use Starknet's high-performance Layer 2 environment (via our local Katana sequencer) as the ultimate, immutable source of truth. When a player breaks the laws of game physics, that violation is logged on-chain.

Account Abstraction & Relayer Nodes: To prevent Web3 UX friction (like signing a wallet transaction for every footstep), we built a custom Python relayer. This middleware node acts as a decentralized validator that batches game telemetry in real-time and subsidizes gas fees for the player.

Provable Fairness: In the future, this architecture allows us to use Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proofs to cryptographically verify player inputs. Bans are no longer arbitrary decisions by a black-box server; they are transparent, mathematically proven violations recorded on a public ledger.

**The problem it solves**

# AlgoKYC: Privacy-Preserving Zero-Knowledge Identity for Algorand

AlgoKYC is a comprehensive Zero-Knowledge KYC infrastructure built natively for the Algorand blockchain. It enables users to prove they hold a valid government-issued ID (like Indian Aadhaar) and meet specific criteria (e.g., over 18 years old, citizen of India) **without ever revealing their personal identity, address, or biometrics to the dApp or on-chain.**

It solves the fundamental Web3 dilemma: How do protocols prevent Sybil attacks and comply with regulations while maintaining the absolute privacy and anonymity of their users?


# 🛑 The Problem

Modern Web3 protocols (DeFi, RWAs, DAOs) face a regulatory trilemma:
1. **Compliance vs. Privacy:** Selling real-world assets or launching regulated tokens requires KYC. But forcing users to upload their passports to a smart contract or a centralized third-party risks massive data breaches, doxxing, and censorship.
2. **Sybil Attacks vs. Anonymity:** Airdrops, quadratic voting, and grant distribution are constantly gamed by bot farms. Identifying unique humans without stripping away their pseudonymity has historically been impossible.
3. **The "Data Minimization" Mandate:** New global data protection laws (like DPDP in India and GDPR in Europe) rigidly demand that companies minimize PI collection. Storing raw identity hashes on a public, immutable ledger is increasingly recognized as a permanent violation of these rights.

## 💡 The Solution: AlgoKYC

AlgoKYC uses **Groth16 zk-SNARKs**, **ECIES Encryption**, and **Shamir Secret Sharing** to create a decentralized, privacy-first identity standard for Algorand.

1. **Client-Side ZK Proofs:** The user imports their government-signed XML file directly into their browser. A ZK circuit (written in Circom/gnark) mathematically proves the XML signature is valid, and the user meets the protocol's requirements (e.g., is over 18).
2. **Deterministic Nullifiers:** The circuit outputs a unique `nullifier` hash explicitly tied to the user's ID and the specific dApp they are accessing. This guarantees **1 Human = 1 Wallet per dApp** (Sybil resistance) while keeping them completely anonymous.
3. **Smart Contract Registry:** Algorand smart contracts (written in PuyaPy) verify the ZK proof logic and store the nullifier, issuing a soulbound "KYC Verified" ASA to the user's wallet.
4. **Court-Ordered Revocation:** In the event of a severe legal mandate, the platform employs a decentralized threshold mechanism. The identity data is ECIES-encrypted in the browser (using an ephemeral point) and only decryptable if a 3-of-5 Custodian multisig approves a "Court Order" transaction on Algorand. Without this threshold, the raw PI is mathematically inaccessible even to the protocol deployers.


## ⚡ Deployed Contracts (Algorand Testnet)

All core registry contracts are live on the Algorand Testnet. You can view their transactions and box storage on the Lora Explorer:

- **Nullifier Registry:** [`756272073`](https://lora.algokit.io/testnet/application/756272073)  
  *Prevents sybil attacks by storing unique ZK nullifiers in Box storage.*
- **Sparse Merkle Tree (SMT) Registry:** [`756272075`](https://lora.algokit.io/testnet/application/756272075)  
  *Maintains the state root of all revoked or banned credentials.*
- **KYC Box Storage:** [`756272299`](https://lora.algokit.io/testnet/application/756272299)  
  *Securely stores the ECIES encrypted payloads, gated by issuer logic.*
- **Credential Manager:** [`756281076`](https://lora.algokit.io/testnet/application/756281076)  
  *The core controller logic capable of interacting with the ASA.*
- **KYC Verified ASA:** [`756281102`](https://lora.algokit.io/testnet/asset/756281102)  
  *The soulbound, non-transferable token issued to valid users.*

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the largest engineering hurdles in building cross-platform privacy apps is standardizing Elliptic Curve Integrated Encryption Scheme (ECIES) payloads between the browser (Javascript) and the server (Python). 

AlgoKYC utilizes a custom-built cryptographic bridge to guarantee the `eciesjs` NPM package generates ciphertexts that perfectly decrypt against Python's `cryptography` library.

**The Javascript to Python ECIES Translation:**
1. Javascript uses the explicit **Full Uncompressed Shared Point + Ephemeral Public Key** to derive the HKDF scalar. Python's default implementation derives the key using *only* the Shared Point's X coordinate. We intercept and apply the uncompressed 65-byte point manually using Python's `ecdsa`.
2. `eciesjs` uses an explicit **16-byte nonce** for AES-GCM (standard is 12-byte). We instruct Python to bypass defaults and pad the IV slice explicitly to 16-bytes.
3. The AES GCM MAC Authentication Tag is appended at the very end of the ciphertext (`ct || tag`) in Python, but prepended in Javascript (`tag || ct`). AlgoKYC parses the 109-byte payload mathematically to extract and shift the tag chunks prior to ECDH handshaking.

**Algorand Blockchain Track**

## 2. Algorand-Native Technical Choices

Every layer of the stack uses something Algorand specifically provides.

### 2.1 BN254 Curve — Chosen for the AVM

AlgoKYC uses the BN254 elliptic curve for PLONK proof verification. This is a direct consequence of Algorand's opcode budget:

| Curve | AVM Opcode Cost | Fits LogicSig Budget? |
|---|---|---|
| BN254 | ~145,000 opcodes | ✅ Yes |
| BLS12-381 | ~185,000 opcodes | ❌ No |

BLS12-381 would exceed the AVM's capacity. BN254 was selected because it is the curve that fits. This is an Algorand-first decision.

### 2.2 LogicSig Verifier — Not a Smart Contract

Algorand provides two execution environments with different opcode ceilings:

- **Smart Contracts:** 190,400 opcode budget
- **LogicSig:** 320,000 opcode budget

PLONK verification on BN254 requires ~145,000 opcodes. Routing it through a smart contract would consume the entire contract budget, leaving nothing for application logic. AlgoKYC routes the ZK verifier through LogicSig, preserving the full smart contract budget for the nullifier registry, credential management, and box storage operations. This is a decision that only makes sense on Algorand.

### 2.3 AlgoPlonk — Algorand's ZK Toolchain

AlgoPlonk is an Algorand Foundation-developed toolchain that auto-generates a valid Algorand LogicSig verifier from a gnark (Go) circuit definition. AlgoKYC uses AlgoPlonk to compile the KYC circuit directly into AVM bytecode — no hand-written opcodes, no manual translation. This toolchain exists only for Algorand.

### 2.4 Algorand Standard Assets (ASA) — Native Credential Primitive

The KYC credential issued to a verified user is an Algorand Standard Asset. ASAs on Algorand have two properties AlgoKYC relies on directly:

- **Non-transferable:** ASA freeze + clawback configuration prevents credential resale or transfer between wallets — critical for KYC integrity
- **Clawback:** The issuer can revoke the credential ASA from any wallet on-chain without the user's cooperation — the on-chain revocation mechanism

These are native Algorand features. Replicating them on another chain requires custom contract logic. On Algorand they are configuration parameters.

### 2.5 Box Storage — On-Chain Key-Value for Identity Blobs

Algorand's box storage provides a persistent, per-application key-value store anchored on-chain. AlgoKYC uses box storage to hold the ECIES-encrypted identity blob for every verified user:

```
Key:   nullifier_hash
Value: encrypted_identity_blob
```

This gives the system a cryptographic accountability layer — usable for court-ordered disclosure — without any off-chain database. The blob lives on Algorand, is permanently auditable, and is readable only by the issuer's private key. Box storage is an Algorand-specific primitive that makes this design possible without external infrastructure.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/algomint-288e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SamyaDeb/AlgoMint) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Mint Algorand Contracts from Solidity

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AlgoPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/AlgoPy-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Ethereum has over 500,000 deployed smart contracts, yet migrating to Algorand requires learning an entirely new language and toolchain from scratch a barrier that prevents millions of Solidity developers from adopting a faster, greener, and 99.9% cheaper blockchain. AlgoMint eliminates this barrier by letting developers paste any Solidity contract and instantly receive production-ready Algorand Python code, compiled to real TEAL bytecode with genuine ARC-32/ARC-56 specs generated by the PuyaPy compiler. With a single click, they deploy directly to Algorand Testnet or Mainnet through Pera Wallet, auto-generate ABIs for frontend integration, and receive automatic security audit reports flagging vulnerabilities like reentrancy attacks that cannot exist on Algorand  achieving a 96% compilation success rate across 50 real-world contracts tested.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle was getting the PuyaPy compiler to generate real ARC-32/ARC-56 specs instead of empty files. Puya kept throwing "cannot determine package root" warnings and silently skipping ARC-32 generation because it received a bare .py file in a temp directory with no project context around it. The fix required scaffolding a complete AlgoKit project structure pyproject.toml, .algokit.toml, src/__init__.py around the contract before every compilation, then dynamically discovering output files by listing the out/ directory since Puya names files after the contract class name, not the input filename. The second major challenge was the AI conversion quality early Gemini responses produced algopy code that used deprecated PyTeal patterns, wrong import paths, and incorrect ARC-4 decorators, causing near-zero compilation success. This was solved through aggressive prompt engineering with a 1,600-line expert system prompt covering every algopy pattern, ARC-4 method signatures, box storage, inner transactions, and global state management pushing success rate from under 30% to 96% across 50 real-world contracts.

**The problem it solves**

# 🚀 LifeLine: Your Personal Emergency & Safety Helper

**LifeLine** is a hyper-local emergency response system. It connects people in immediate danger with nearby verified helpers (doctors, nurses, or trained civilians), ensuring help arrives in minutes—not hours.

---

## 🟢 1. Problem (Very Simple)
Let’s think about real life. Sometimes emergencies happen:
*   🏃‍♂️ You feel unsafe at night
*   ❤️ Someone gets a heart attack
*   🚲 Bike accident on road
*   👴 Old person falls
*   📍 You are stuck alone somewhere

**Today’s situation:**
*   ❌ Ambulance takes 30–40 minutes
*   ❌ Police come late
*   ❌ No one nearby knows you need help
*   ❌ You panic & don't know first aid

**But truth is:**
👉 A doctor may be 200 meters away
👉 A nurse may live nearby
👉 A helper may be on the next street

✅ **Main Problem:** In emergencies, people cannot quickly find nearby help, so response is slow and situations become dangerous.

---

## ✅ 2. Solution (Simple Idea)
**LifeLine App** finds nearby helpers instantly.
Just like **Uber finds a driver** or **Zomato finds food**, **LifeLine finds emergency help**.

Instead of waiting 30 minutes… 👉 **help comes in 2–5 minutes.**

---

## 📊 3. How It Works (Very Easy Steps)

### Step 1 — Press SOS 🔴
You press the SOS button, OR your phone automatically detects a **fall, crash, or unconscious state**.

### Step 2 — AI Calls You (within 5 seconds) ⭐
The app calls you like a smart friend and asks: *"What happened? Are you safe? Medical or safety problem?"* You speak or tap.

### Step 3 — AI Understands the Problem 🧠
*   **Small problem?** (lost, minor injury) → Gives tips only.
*   **Big danger?** (heart attack, accident) → Sends emergency alerts.
*   *(This stops false alarms!)*

### Step 4 — Find Nearby Helpers 🤝
The app finds the **nearest doctor, nurse, or volunteer**. Like Uber matching, it picks whoever is closest.

### Step 5 — Alerts Sent 🔔
System sends your **live location** and a **loud alert** to nearby helpers and your family.

### Step 6 — AI Guides You 🗣️
While help is coming, the app talks to you: *"Stay calm. Apply pressure. Help is 2 minutes away."* So you don’t panic.

### Step 7 — Help Arrives Fast ✅
Instead of 30 minutes, help reaches you in **2–5 minutes**. Life saved.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[SOS Triggered] --> B{AI Brain Checks}
    B -- Small Problem --> C[Guidance Tips]
    B -- Big Danger --> D[Notify Nearby Helpers]
    D --> E[Family & Helper Alerts]
    D --> F[Real-time Voice Aid]
    F --> G[Help Arrives in 2-5 min]
```

*   **🚨 Emergency SOS:** One tap to call for help with live tracking.
*   **🧠 AI Assistant:** Talks to you, understands the problem, and decides action.
*   **🤝 Nearby Helpers:** Connects you to doctors, nurses, and volunteers.
*   **🛡️ Safety Mode:** Daily use features like "share trip" and "unsafe area alerts".
*   **🏃‍♂️ Auto Detection:** Fall and crash detection using phone sensors.
*   **📶 Offline Mode:** Works using SMS alerts when internet is down.

### Metamorphosis
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/metamorphosis-dcb0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aloukikjoshi/metamorphosis) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://metamorphosis-cyan.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6YOM2LL54wk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackSRM%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-srm26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where AI meets privacy and performance

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Data haven](https://img.shields.io/badge/Data%20haven-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Metamorphosis acts as an intelligent, privacy-first middleware between users and LLMs, solving the critical trilemma of AI adoption—privacy, cost, and security—through two core pillars:
 Enterprise-Grade Security & Guardrails: It automatically protects your infrastructure by intercepting and masking sensitive PII (like patient/fintech data) before it ever leaves the local environment, while actively filtering and blocking malicious bot attacks and abusive automated traffic at the gateway level.
 Intelligent Routing & Cost Optimization: It drastically reduces API costs and latency through a built-in Prompt Shrinker that compresses redundant tokens, and a dynamic routing engine that seamlessly directs simple queries to local models (zero cost) and complex tasks to cloud LLMs (high performance).

"We request , respected judges to spend some of their valuable time on our prototype as our demo video is a divided into parts to seamlessly integrate backend and blockchain."

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a middleware gateway that intercepts and modifies prompts in real-time came with several technical hurdles. The two biggest challenges were:

Integrating with DataHaven: Hooking up the gateway's semantic memory to DataHaven proved to be much more difficult than anticipated. The initial data structures returning from DataHaven didn't align with the format our Prompt Builder required to construct the LLM context.
How we fixed it: We had to deep-dive into DataHaven's API documentation and build a custom data transformation pipeline in the backend. This ensured the retrieved context snippets were perfectly formatted and token-optimized before being injected into the final prompt.
Building a Unified LLM Wrapper Class: Supporting dynamic routing between completely different ecosystems (local Ollama models and cloud OpenAI models) created massive inconsistencies in how API requests were formatted and how streaming responses were handled.
How we fixed it: We engineered a custom, unified Wrapper Class that acts as an abstraction layer. This class normalizes the input payloads and standardizes the output schemas, allowing our routing engine to seamlessly switch between local and cloud models on the fly without breaking the frontend parsing logic.

**Grand Prize**

AI adoption in industry has outpaced AI governance. Most companies integrate models directly into applications without a structured control layer, leading to opaque routing, reactive guardrails, poor privacy measurement, and limited auditability. This creates operational and regulatory risk.

Metamorphosis AI Gateway addresses this as an infrastructure problem, not a model problem. It introduces a control plane between users and models, enabling mode-based routing (Strict, Balanced, Performance), NLP-driven risk classification using trained BERT/Roberta models, measurable privacy scoring through a privacy meter, and full transparency via token statistics, redaction logs, routing visibility, and agent-level breakdown.

Instead of treating inference as a black-box API call, the system makes every decision traceable and policy-aware. With integration into decentralized storage logistics, data custody remains with the enterprise, allowing guardrails to operate before external transmission and enabling compliance-ready deployment.

This is not about building smarter models. It’s about making AI deployable, auditable, and industry-ready.

> Disaster Recovery

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![DAO](https://img.shields.io/badge/DAO-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The established methods of handling disaster relief and recovery are ripe for disruption. Natural and man-made disasters happen more frequently and are more severe,  Our current systems of relief efforts usually only offer short-term fixes and don't address the long-term economic and individual challenges disaster survivors face. Additionaly, there is also no real way to accurately measure the impact of these unfortunate events on life and property as well as measuring the impact of  large scale regional relief efforts.  When delivering essential aid for civil disaster relief and civil risk reduction, traditional protocols and methods are often slow, bureaucratic, and limited in scope. Technology isn't used effectively in all three key phases of a disaster (preparedness, response, and recovery). Coordination with goverments community groups and philathopic donors is often poor. 

Governments also have strong reasons to buy or hold hypercerts. They fund significant amounts of public-value work — from environmental restoration to digital infrastructure, scientific initiatives, and social programs. Hypercerts give governments a verifiable way to show how public resources were used and what outcomes were achieved. This supports transparency, improves procurement and grant making, strengthens performance-based budgeting, and gives citizens a clearer understanding of government effectiveness. (disastercentral.org)

**Challenges we ran into**

We do not have money to get a public domain.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

These incentive shifts become even more important as AI transforms fundraising and grantmaking. Today, most projects already use AI to write applications. Soon, most projects will have AI agents handling fundraising, and funders will use AI to filter and select proposals. In this world, every project has to present a convincing narrative. In Web3 convincing written narrative disappears as an advantage in grant applications. What remains meaningful is verifiable data: structured contributions, linked to evidence, and transparent evaluation histories. Hypercerts provide exactly that substrate. The Disaster DAO will advance the use of Hypercerts in the natural and manmade disaster recovery space. This is done though its decentalized governance systems.

**Prosperia**

We built Disaster DAO for the Prosperia Track because it embodies the ultimate vision of Ethereum for Social Good. We are replacing the opaque 'black box' of traditional disaster relief NGOs with a fully transparent, decentralized governance protocol. By using ERC-1155 Impact Certificates and Moloch-style DAO voting, we empower global communities to fund frontline real-world verifiable relief instantly—proving that code and cryptography can save lives faster than bureaucracy.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

While most autonomous agents today only generate text, Disaster DAO built a self-sustaining financial agent deployed directly on Base.

In traditional disaster relief, humans act as the intermediaries to handle funds, which creates delays and corruption. We completely eliminated them. Our DAO operates as an unstoppable on-chain agent: once a decentralized network of human reviewers feeds verified impact data (ERC-1155) into the system, the Base smart contract autonomously evaluates the conditions, unlocks the treasury, and routes the ETH directly to frontline responders.

No bank approvals, no human executives cutting checks. By deploying onto Base’s low-cost architecture, our treasury becomes a highly efficient, perpetually self-sustaining relief engine that never sleeps and can never be bribed.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Games are expensive to make. Even testing one mechanic, a single idea you want to try, means building an entire game around it. That kills innovation before it starts. Most good ideas never get prototyped, let alone played by anyone.

ChainCraft makes that friction disappear. Describe your idea to AI, and it builds a playable multiplayer game around it in minutes. Publish it, mint it as an NFT, and it's yours. Your mechanics and game components are broken into ownable, reusable modules. When someone remixes your mechanic into their game, you earn royalties. Build a full game and earn from every match played. Create in-game items like cards, weapons, or characters that players actually own and can carry across games. Imagine earning cards in a campaign adventure, then using those same cards in a competitive duel game someone else built.

Then there's Token Duels, skill-based wagering where players put stakes on matches of creator-built games. Creators earn a cut of every match, players fund the games they enjoy, and the best content attracts more builders and more liquidity. That's the flywheel: good ideas attract players, players bring funding, funding rewards creators, creators build more. Without anyone needing to know they're using a blockchain.

Live at play.chaincraft.games on Arbitrum mainnet with real-time multiplayer, wallet-based identity, and NFT-gated perks building.

**Challenges we ran into**

AI cost sustainability. Our early engine used AI for every player action during gameplay. We ran an experiment called CodeAct that proved we could get deterministic results (three perfect games of rock paper scissors, a first for us) but it cost ~$0.13 per game for just six moves. Card games would hit dollars per session. We pivoted to generating deterministic code once during creation so gameplay runs with zero AI calls. Target: under $0.01 per game. This is what makes Token Duels viable.
Non-determinism vs. bugs. AI generated game logic can be syntactically correct but semantically wrong. A field expecting a number gets a message string instead. A precondition always fails. A transition deadlocks. These aren't bugs in our platform, they're non-deterministic AI behavior. We built validation layers and a simulation system so creators catch issues before publishing. We have clear methods to continually optimize our builder and generation pipeline, it just requires time and iteration.
Cost control vs. accessibility. Every build session costs us real money, so we token-gated the builder behind our Data Drifter NFT. Only holders can build, but published games stay publicly playable and anyone can join a match. We also give Data Drifters to early testers we bring in for feedback. The goal is to make building completely accessible once we can offset and reduce costs through revenue and engine optimization. Controlled rollout that manages burn rate while the platform grows through gameplay.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

# Use of AI Tools and Agents

AI isn't bolted on, it is the engine. But what makes ChainCraft different from other AI builders is that AI doesn't just create the games, it lives inside them. Creators can design games where AI drives narratives, determines outcomes, judges creative submissions, or acts as a dynamic game master. You don't see that in other platforms. Most AI game tools generate a static product and walk away. Ours lets you build games that are fundamentally AI-powered experiences if you choose.

Here's how the AI systems work together:

**Game Builder Agent.** Conversational AI (Claude) guides users through game design via natural language. Rather than one-shot generation, it collaborates with the creator to refine mechanics, rules, and win conditions before outputting structured game specifications.

**Artifact Generation.** Translates those natural language designs into deterministic game code: state schemas, transitions, preconditions, and action handlers. 

**Simulation Agent.** AI driven test players run through gameplay scenarios before publishing to surface broken mechanics or unbalanced designs. Creators iterate here before real players ever touch it.

**Image Generation (Leonardo AI).** Auto-generates artwork for each game's NFT cartridge and visual identity on publish. And in game item NFTs.

AI in Gameplay. This is where it gets interesting. The engine is built with hooks so creators can bring AI into the gameplay itself. Narrative generation, AI judging for creative or subjective mechanics, AI assistants, dynamic game mastering. The base game logic is deterministic for reliability and fairness, but creators can layer AI on top for experiences that wouldn't be possible without it. For wagered matches through Token Duels, the deterministic layer ensures fair outcomes. For everything else, AI can make the experience richer and more dynamic.

Good ideas attract players, players bring funding, funding rewards creators, creators build more. **Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

AI inference is ChainCraft's core product, not a feature bolted on. Every game on our platform is generated through AI inference. Users describe a game concept in conversation and our pipeline handles specification, mechanic design, rule balancing, and narrative creation. Games are expensive to make traditionally. Even testing one mechanic means building an entire game around it. We make that disappear. Our hybrid approach pairs conversational AI with a deterministic SWE engine that compiles output into reliable game logic, making each generation cost-efficient enough to sustain a creator economy around it. This isn't AI tooling. It's a consumer product where inference directly creates economic value on-chain. Every game created, every Token Duel wagered, every item generated runs through inference powering real player experiences. Creators earn from matches played on their AI-generated games. Players fund the content they enjoy through wagering. The better the inference, the better the games, the more revenue flows, the more creators show up to build. That flywheel means inference demand grows with every creator who joins, every game published, every mechanic remixed, and every item generated. Each new creator brings players, each player funds matches, each match proves the model works and attracts more creators. As decentralized compute infrastructure like 0G matures, platforms like ours become the demand side of that equation, consumer applications that need fast, affordable, reliable inference at scale to power real economies.
