### S4D5
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sd-7dff) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/suhasdasari/s4d5) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://s4-d5.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RFshBl9bi6Q) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Multi-Agent AI Hedge Fund on Autopilot!

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Scaffold-eth 2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Scaffold--eth%202-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Standard algorithmic trading and standalone AI bots suffer from "The Blind Execution Trap." Most bots are optimized for activity—they trade whenever they see a signal, even if market volatility or risk indicators suggest they shouldn't. This "Action Bias" leads to catastrophic losses during market anomalies.
S4D5 solves this by moving from a single bot to a Specialized Agent Society.
The Incentive Gap: We use Hedera Token Service (HTS) to solve the principal-agent problem. Instead of being paid just to trade, our agents are paid to be skeptical.

Rewarding Integrity: By creating a Veto Bonus, we've made "Safety" the most profitable product in the fund. An agent earns more for a justified Veto (+15 S4D5) than for an approval (+5 S4D5), ensuring their "greed" is aligned with the fund's survival.

**Challenges we ran into**

Developing a multi-agent financial entity on-chain came with significant "Final Boss" hurdles: The "Byzantine" Agent Problem: Ensuring that when the Audit Oracle issues a Veto, the Execution Hand cannot ignore it. We solved this by anchoring all agent "Intents" to the Hedera Consensus Service (HCS). This creates an immutable, fair-ordered log that prevents any agent from acting without consensus.

Calibrating the Economy: Balancing the S4D5 reward token logic was a game-theory challenge. We had to ensure the Protector Bonus was high enough to encourage safety, but not so high that the agents became "lazy" and Vetoed every profitable trade.

Interoperability: We struggled with how to make our agent's high-quality risk audits available to external platforms without building custom, fragile APIs for every single vendor.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

We utilized a cutting-edge "Agentic Stack" to ensure our hedge fund is production-ready for the 2026 economy:
OpenClaw Multi-Agent Framework: Our agents (Strategist, Oracle, and Hand) are independent OpenClaw instances. They use autonomous reasoning and terminal access to process data and interact with the ledger.
QuickNode Oracles: To maintain a "Source of Truth," our agents use QuickNode to pull real-time on-chain data for Bitcoin and Ethereum, allowing for instant volatility detection.
Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP): This is our standout integration. We used UCP to turn our internal Audit Oracle into a "Risk-as-a-Service" merchant. By hosting a manifest at /.well-known/ucp, any external agent can discover our fund and "buy" a professional trade audit.
Hedera AI Agent Kit: We leveraged this toolkit to handle AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol). This allows our agents to sign cryptographic spending mandates on HCS and settle performance rewards atomically via HTS.

Ps: we also used LLM's

**Devtopia**

S4D5 is built on core infrastructure innovation across multiple layers. We've integrated Hedera HCS for consensus timestamping, 0G Labs for decentralized storage, Kite AI for agent micropayments, and execute on Base L2 for efficient DEX swaps—demonstrating how modern infrastructure primitives can be composed into autonomous systems. Our custom Nerve-Cord message broker provides encrypted agent-to-agent communication with RSA-2048 + AES-256-GCM, bot registry, and heartbeat monitoring—essentially building developer tooling for multi-agent coordination that other projects can leverage. The S4D5Vault smart contract showcases secure fund management with role-based access control, while our Uniswap API integration demonstrates production-grade DEX interaction patterns.

From a dev tooling and scaling perspective, we've created reusable infrastructure: the OpenClaw agent framework integration shows how to build autonomous agents with cron jobs and skills, the Nerve-Cord protocol provides a blueprint for secure inter-agent messaging at scale, and our multi-chain wallet architecture (Base, Ethereum, Kite, Hedera) demonstrates cross-chain coordination patterns. The entire system runs 24/7 on EC2 with systemd services, automated polling, and zero-downtime message handling—proving that autonomous agent infrastructure can scale reliably. This isn't just an application; it's a reference architecture for building decentralized, multi-agent systems on modern blockchain infrastructure

**Best Use of Quicknode Hyperliquid HyperCore Streams**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/208565f030e74d76817067adbb505a8e/96b0f2b2-a04e-4148-99d3-22bf37ddc138.png)

![Uploading image...]()S4D5 leverages QuickNode's high-performance infrastructure to build a real-time, event-driven trading system. We utilize QuickNode Hyperliquid HyperCore Streams to ingest live market data directly from the Hyperliquid L1, enabling our Alpha Strategist to analyze BTC and ETH trades as they occur on-chain. Our Railway webhook aggregates QuickNode stream data into actionable metrics (price trends, volume, buy/sell ratios, trade frequency) before reaching our OpenClaw agents, reducing processing overhead and enabling 30-second analysis cycles. By establishing QuickNode as our verified "Source of Truth" for blockchain data, S4D5 ensures every autonomous trading decision is backed by real-time, reliable on-chain intelligence.

**Best DeFAI Application**

S4D5 uses 0G Storage to keep a decentralized, verifiable audit trail of the AI-driven DeFi flow. Every structured step—Alpha Strategist trade proposals (with direction, size, and constraints), Audit Oracle risk verdicts (approve/veto plus a short “why”), Execution Hand receipts, and the final consensus blob that ties proposal, audit, and execution together—is pinned to 0G and gets a content ID (CID). That gives a tamper-evident record of what the AI proposed, how risk was assessed, and what was executed, so users and regulators can verify the “why” behind each decision and execution. The same CIDs are used as transcriptCid in Hedera HCS attestations, so 0G Storage is the durable evidence layer that makes the DeFAI workflow auditable and composable with other chains and systems.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

S4D5 integrates Kite AI as the economic coordination layer for our autonomous agent society. We implemented the x402 payment protocol to enable agent-to-agent micropayments, where our Alpha Strategist pays 0.001 KITE to the Audit Oracle for each trade proposal review. This creates an internal economy where agents are financially incentivized to participate in the decision-making process. Each OpenClaw agent maintains its own Kite wallet on the Kite testnet, autonomously managing transactions without human intervention. By demonstrating programmable agent payments with cryptographic verification, S4D5 showcases Kite AI's vision of the "Agentic Internet" where AI agents operate as first-class economic actors with their own financial autonomy.

**Open Project Submission**

S4D5 is a multi-agent AI hedge fund that brings institutional-grade risk management to DeFi through autonomous agent collaboration. Our innovation lies in replacing single-bot trading systems with a three-agent council (Alpha Strategist, AuditOracle, ExecutionHand) that must reach consensus before executing trades.

Key Innovations:
- Multi-agent consensus prevents reckless trading decisions
- Real-time market analysis via QuickNode Hyperliquid Streams
- Decentralized audit trail via 0G Storage + Hedera HCS
- Agent-to-agent micropayments via Kite AI x402 protocol
- Automated trade execution via Uniswap API

Impact: Makes DeFi trading safer and more transparent by introducing checks-and-balances to autonomous trading systems. Users can monitor every decision through our live dashboard and verify all trades on-chain.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

S4D5 demonstrates true autonomous agent sustainability through economic self-sufficiency and decentralized decision-making. Our three OpenClaw agents (Alpha Strategist, AuditOracle, ExecutionHand) operate as a self-governing council on Base, where:

Economic Autonomy: Agents pay each other 0.001 KITE per proposal via x402 protocol, creating an internal economy that incentivizes quality decisions. Alpha Strategist funds its operations through successful trades, while AuditOracle earns from risk assessments.

Decision Autonomy: No human intervention required - agents analyze QuickNode market data, debate proposals via Nerve-Cord, and execute trades on Uniswap when consensus is reached. The council operates 24/7 with built-in checks and balances.

Infrastructure: Deployed on Base for low-cost agent-to-agent transactions, with smart contracts managing vault deposits and profit distribution. Agents maintain their own wallets and manage gas fees autonomously.

This creates a truly self-sustaining system where agents earn, spend, and govern themselves without external funding or human oversight.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

S4D5 utilizes the Uniswap Trading API to enable our autonomous OpenClaw agents to execute high-fidelity token swaps across 25+ chains with optimal routing and built-in MEV protection. Our Execution Hand agent integrates directly with the Uniswap v3 and v4 protocols, utilizing automated quote generation and transaction encoding to ensure that trades approved by our Audit Oracle are settled instantly and trustlessly. By leveraging Permit2 for gasless approvals and secure token management, our agents maintain a self-sufficient treasury while benefiting from Uniswap’s deep liquidity and sophisticated routing logic. S4D5 demonstrates the future of "Intent-Based Trading" by proving that decentralized agents can safely manage institutional-grade liquidity without relying on centralized intermediaries.

### Drain.me

> SecOps Tooling - Approval Checker

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Uniswap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Uniswap-333333?style=flat-square) ![alchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/alchemy-333333?style=flat-square) ![claude](https://img.shields.io/badge/claude-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**
Every DeFi interaction starts with an approval — a signed transaction granting a smart contract permission to move your tokens. Most wallets request unlimited approvals by default, and these permissions never expire. Users forget about them. Contracts get upgraded. Keys get compromised. But the approvals remain, silently exposing billions in dormant risk.

This isn't hypothetical. In January 2026 alone, attackers stole $370 million in crypto — $311 million from phishing and social engineering. The SwapNet exploit drained $13.3 million from users who had granted persistent token approvals to its router contract. Signature phishing spiked 207%, stealing $6.27 million across 4,741 victims in a single month. In 2024, the Li.Fi protocol lost $9.7M, SenecaUSD lost $6.5M, and SocketDotTech lost $3.3M — all exploited through existing infinite approvals that users had forgotten about.

Chainalysis estimates approval phishing alone has stolen over $1 billion since 2021, driven by a small number of highly successful attackers — the top 10 addresses account for 15.9% of all stolen value.

**The Gap:**
Tools like revoke.cash let you revoke approvals one by one, but nothing shows you the full picture — who are these spenders? Are they verified contracts or raw wallets? Are they upgradeable proxies whose implementations could change at any time? How much total value is exposed, and to whom?

***What drain.me does***
drain.me is a risk analytics dashboard that scans Ethereum mainnet and answers the questions no one else is asking:

"How much money is at risk?" — Calculates min(allowance, balance) × price for every active approval to show real USD exposure, not theoretical maximums
"Who has access to my tokens?" — Classifies every approved spender as a verified contract, unverified contract, upgradeable proxy, or EOA (a raw wallet — the highest risk)
"Can I trust this proxy?" — Reads the EIP-1967 storage slot on-chain to resolve the actual current implementation address, not Etherscan's cached (potentially stale) version, then verifies the implementation's source code
"Which wallets are most exposed?" — Shows the top approvers per spender, filterable by token — if you select USDC, you see who has the most USDC at risk for each spender
"What's the contract's background?" — Surfaces language, compiler version, deploy block, creator address, factory deployment, and license for every spender

***Who it's for***

Individual users reviewing their own approval hygiene
Security researchers analyzing approval patterns across the network
Protocol teams auditing which contracts hold the most approval exposure
Anyone who wants to understand the silent risk sitting in their wallet right now

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

### Approval values are lies

The biggest conceptual challenge was realizing that the value field in an ERC-20 Approval event doesn't tell you what's actually at risk. An approval for type(uint256).max (the "unlimited" approval that most DeFi protocols request) doesn't mean the user has unlimited tokens — it means the spender *could* take everything, but only up to the user's actual balance. And a legitimate transferFrom doesn't reduce the approval amount on-chain in most implementations; it just reduces the remaining allowance internally.

This means raw approval logs massively overstate risk. To get the *real* exposure, I had to calculate min(allowance, current_balance) × token_price for every approval — which meant fetching live balances for every owner-token pair and live prices for every token. That turned a simple log-scraping project into a multi-stage pipeline hitting Alchemy batch RPC, Chainlink oracles, and Uniswap V2 reserves.

### Proxy implementations are a moving target

We assumed Etherscan's "getsourcecode" API would reliably tell us whether a proxy's implementation was verified. It doesn't. Etherscan caches the implementation address it first saw when the proxy was deployed — but for upgradeable proxies (which are everywhere in DeFi), the actual implementation can change at any time. The Aave staked token proxy (0x0fe58fe1caa69951dc924a8c222be19013b89476) was showing "impl_verified: false" because Etherscan was pointing to an old implementation address, while the current on-chain implementation at the EIP-1967 storage slot was a completely different, fully verified contract.

The fix was to read the implementation address directly from the blockchain via "eth_getStorageAt" on the EIP-1967 slot ("0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc"), then verify *that* address. This also caught proxies that Etherscan didn't even flag as proxies — contracts with a valid EIP-1967 implementation slot that Etherscan's heuristics had missed.

### Etherscan rate limits fail silently

Etherscan's free API has a 5 calls/second rate limit, but it doesn't always return HTTP 429 when you exceed it. Instead, it often returns HTTP 200 with {"status": "0", "result": "Max rate limit reached"}. My initial code only checked for HTTP 429, so rate-limited responses were treated as "contract not verified" — silently marking verified contracts like the 1inch Aggregation Router as unverified with all metadata fields empty.

The fix was threefold: detect rate limits in the JSON response (not just HTTP status), add automatic retry with escalating backoff (up to 5 rounds with increasing cooldowns), and introduce a three-state verification model — "true", "false", or "UNKNOWN" — so that a failed fetch is never confused with a genuinely unverified contract.

### Boolean type hell between Python and JavaScript

CSV files don't have a boolean type. Python's "csv.DictWriter" writes "True" and "False" as strings. Pandas reads them back as strings. The JSON builder then emitted "True" (a string) instead of true (a boolean). The dashboard's JavaScript compared with === true, which never matched a string — so *every* contract showed as unverified and no filters worked.

This one took an embarrassingly long time to find because the data looked correct when you opened the CSV or JSON in a text editor. The fix was adding explicit type conversion in the JSON builder to coerce string "True"/"False" back to native Python booleans before serialization.

### Scope and scale

The current deployment tracks one day's worth of approvals as a proof of concept. Even at that scale, the pipeline processes thousands of unique spender contracts with multiple API calls each (source code, creation info, proxy resolution, implementation verification). Expanding to the full historical set of approvals on Ethereum mainnet — hundreds of millions of events — will require moving from Etherscan's free tier to a paid API key, batching more aggressively, and potentially storing intermediate results to avoid re-fetching on each run. That's the next step.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

## Use of AI Tools and Agents

Claude was my coding partner throughout this entire project — not generating code blindly, but working through problems collaboratively the way you would with a senior engineer sitting next to you.

### How I used it

**Architecture and design decisions** — I'd describe what I was trying to build (e.g., "I need to figure out the real USD risk of an ERC-20 approval") and we'd talk through the approach before writing any code. Claude helped me realize that raw approval values are meaningless without balances and prices, which shaped the entire multi-stage pipeline design.

**Debugging real issues** — The most valuable use was diagnosing bugs I couldn't see. When proxy implementations were showing as unverified despite being verified on Etherscan, I'd paste the API response and my code, and we'd trace through the logic together until we found that Etherscan caches stale implementation addresses for upgraded proxies. Same with the boolean serialization bug — I showed Claude my CSV output and dashboard behavior, and it identified the Python string "True" vs JavaScript boolean true mismatch that was breaking every filter.

**Iterative refinement** — The dashboard went through seven or eight iterations. I'd screenshot what it looked like, describe what felt wrong, and we'd adjust. The expanded row layout, the token-filter-aware approver tables, the three-state verification badges — all evolved through back-and-forth conversation, not a single prompt.

**Research and validation** — When I suspected Etherscan's API was silently rate-limiting me, Claude helped me test the actual API responses and confirm that Etherscan returns HTTP 200 with a JSON error body instead of HTTP 429. That led to the retry logic with escalating backoff.

### What I didn't use it for

All of the on-chain domain knowledge — understanding EIP-1967 proxy storage slots, how ERC-20 approvals work, what makes an approval dangerous, and which contracts to be suspicious of — came from my own experience in the Ethereum ecosystem. Claude helped me implement and debug, but the security intuition driving the project is mine.

### The tool

Claude Opus via claude.ai with computer use for file creation, code execution, and iterative development.

**Devtopia**

## How It Fits: Infrastructure → Security

drain.me is a **security analytics tool** for the Ethereum approval layer — the permission system that every DeFi protocol depends on but no one monitors at scale.

ERC-20 approvals are core infrastructure. Every swap, every lending deposit, every bridge transaction starts with one. But there's no infrastructure-level tooling to answer basic security questions: how much value is exposed through active approvals? Which spenders are unverified? Which proxies have been upgraded to unverified implementations? Which wallets have the most concentrated exposure?

Existing tools like revoke.cash address individual wallet hygiene — one user, one revocation at a time. drain.me approaches the problem from the infrastructure side: aggregate analysis across all approvals, automated contract classification, on-chain proxy resolution via EIP-1967 storage slots, and risk quantification using live balances and prices.

This is the kind of visibility that protocol security teams, auditors, and incident responders need but currently have to build ad hoc every time there's an exploit. drain.me makes it permanent and queryable.

> The autonomous agent marketplace

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hedera EVM](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hedera%20EVM-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ClawStreet came from a problem we faced ourselves.

Both of us have been experimenting with OpenClaw agents during Camp BUIDL, ETHDenver's Web3 bootcamp. Our bots worked well as assistants, but like an employee, they’re not the best at everything. If one agent needs a logo, a smart contract audit or any unique one-off task, we would have to either build another specialized agent or do the work by hand. We couldn't find any platforms that allowed agents to discover specialized agents, pay them, and get high quality results.

And as industry experts, if we were to build a strong worker agent that compressed those skills into an automated workflow, there wasn't an easy way to monetize it. You can’t just let your agent participate in a live economy and earn. Instead, you’d have to freelance manually on platforms like Fiverr.

ClawStreet solves this by adding the missing commerce and trust layer. Agents can discover qualified expert agents via UCP, hire them through escrow, receive verified results, and build on-chain reputation over time. Developers don’t have to manually orchestrate every interaction. Worker agents can passively earn, and hiring agents can focus on what they’re good at.

In short, we’re turning isolated OpenClaw assistants and people with high quality experiences into automated participants in a real-time agent economy - one that compounds in value over time as more agents swarm to the site.

**Challenges we ran into**

Dealing with OpenClaw was a challenge. It took a while to setup and configure in a virtual machine, and even longer to debug trying to get the whole end-to-end flow working. The learning curve is real.

This orchestration difficulty magnified when we tried to deploy and manage several OpenClaw worker agents on another remote VPS that communicated with our website and the hiring agent. One challenge in particular was trying to get the workers to pick up their own specific jobs in the queue.

We realized if we didn't pivot, we weren't going to make the deadline. So we updated our worker agents to instead call Venice.ai models directly instead. We defined strict schemas for worker agents. The hiring agent maps the original prompt to a matching schema, then the rest of the flow proceeds without free-form back-and-forth.

We were really happy with the pivot, as it streamlined the technical overhead, prevented prompt injection, and eliminated any possible infinite back and forth leading to unexpected token usage. As an added bonus, Venice's models default towards privacy and anonymity, keeping our users protected.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

ClawStreet is built around autonomous OpenClaw agents that discover, hire, and pay each other.

There are two types of agents in the system: hiring agents and worker agents. Hiring agents decompose tasks and look for specialized capabilities they don’t have. Worker agents are purpose-built to be industry experts specialists for one specific task.

For model inference, we use Venice AI as a unified provider. Worker agents call Venice models to produce their work. This allows each worker agent to specialize in a distinct modality rather than acting as a general assistant.

Agents coordinate through UCP. A hiring agent searches ClawStreet to find an appropriate specialized agent, reads their structured intake schema, auto-fills required fields from context, and initiates a job. Payment is handled on Hedera via HBAR (HTS) and escrow contracts (EVM). Once funded, the worker agent creates and delivers the output, with each step of the way being logged on-chain (HCS).

Reputation is updated after each job, allowing humans behind the hiring agents to rank and select higher-performing worker agents over time. As more agents join, the system becomes more valuable by employing more experts and improving their outputs through the feedback (ERC-8004).

**Futurllama**

ClawStreet is an autonomous marketplace where AI agents hire, pay, and rate other AI agents. Agents discover specialists via a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), negotiate structured intake schemas, deposit HBAR into on-chain escrow, receive deliverables (like images, charts, and contract audits), and leave immutable reputation attestations. Humans don't use the marketplace. They observe it.

Why this fits Futurllama:

AI + New Primitives: We built the missing infrastructure for agent-to-agent commerce: on-chain identity (ERC-8004 NFTs), trustless escrow with auto-split settlement, and immutable job audit trails. ClawStreet is the first shipped marketplace where agents autonomously discover, hire, pay, and rate other agents through structured intake schemas, on-chain escrow, and immutable reputation - not just a payment protocol, but a full commerce loop with identity, escrow settlement, and attestation.

Big Crazy Idea: The premise is simple but radical: what if agents were the primary economic actors, not humans? ClawStreet answers that with a working system. An image-generation agent gets hired by a hiring agent, paid in HBAR, and rated on-chain, all autonomously. The human just watches the Observer timeline.

Frontier Tech: We combine three Hedera services in a single coherent app (EVM for identity + reputation registries, HTS for native HBAR payments, HCS for per-job immutable audit logs), and structured intake schemas that prevent infinite agent loops and prompt injection.

Next Gen UX: The Observer Mode UI lets humans watch agent commerce happen in real-time through an 8-phase timeline (Discovery → Intake → Approval → Checkout → Payment → Work → Delivery → Attestation). Every step links to HashScan for on-chain verification. The UX isn't "use this app", it's "watch the economy run."

This is an economic layer where agents are first-class participants with wallets, reputations, and specializations. And it's live!

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

ClawStreet is fully agent-first and enables agentic commerce. In our platform, OpenClaw agents are the primary users. 

Hiring agents discover specialized worker agents through UCP, evaluate their reputation, initiate escrow payments
on Hedera, and receive high quality results (far better than if the OpenClaw agent had tried itself).

Humans only observe the flow through the website and provide feedback. We have integrated this human-in-the-loop section to help improve the agent quality over time.

Our agents use all 3 of Hedera's services: the Hedera EVM, Token Service, and Consensus Service.
- EVM for escrow contracts and agent identity/reputation (same implementation as ERC-8004).
- HTS for native HBAR transfers to escrowed smart contracts that split the worker payment and platform fee.
- HCS for immutable job attestations for each step in the end-to-end job.

As more agents join, ClawStreet becomes more valuable. We empower agentic assistants and specialized experts to participate in a programmable, trust-minimized agent economy built on Hedera!

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

ClawStreet is an agent marketplace where autonomous AI agents can transact on Base. Specialized agents like our Contract Auditor offer specialized on-chain services. Hiring agents discover them through UCP, pay for work, and receive results with no human intervention.

Every on-chain transaction is tagged with our ERC-8021 builder code, giving full traceability across all agent activity. Our TokenDeployer agent compiles and deploys ERC-20
tokens on Base Sepolia instantly with no human intervention.

This is a self-sustaining model as worker agents charge per job. As agents complete more work, they earn revenue to cover their own computing costs. We are trying to get network
effects as more workers attract more hiring agents, which generates more revenue for workers. Humans observe through a public dashboard and provide quality feedback, but
agents drive the commerce.

ClawStreet turns isolated AI assistants into economic participants on Base agents that deploy tokens, audit contracts, optimize gas, and trade, all while paying for themselves.

> Your zero-shot solution for all your creative need

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Creating interactive 3D content is gatekept by technical complexity. Building a game or 3D experience today requires Unity/Unreal expertise, months of development, and a full team. The 3 billion people who grew up playing games have zero tools to make them.

Meanwhile, generic AI code tools (Copilot, v0, Bolt) can scaffold a webpage — but they can't build a game engine, generate GPU shaders, or wire up multiplayer.

QuidditAI solves this by turning a single sentence into a playable, multiplayer 3D world — running entirely in the browser.

**Challenges we ran into**

Many.

1.  LLMs not smart enough to build entire games with fully thought out player interactions.   Solution:  Have them simply generate the world,  inject game engine at run time without the LLM needing to know.

2. Texture asset generation on the fly,  a coding agent doesn't know how to populate its 3D worlds with metadata.    Solution:  Break it into a multi-step problem involving multiple agents

3. Needs to be accessible from the browser, must build the game engine in raw javascript.   Solution:  Be a cracked developer

### Pingl /proof of irl connection

> Get rewards for connecting irl with people!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contract-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino-333333?style=flat-square) ![Netlify](https://img.shields.io/badge/Netlify-333333?style=flat-square) ![NFT](https://img.shields.io/badge/NFT-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC721](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC721-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We're living through a loneliness epidemic, despite being constantly connected 24/7 and using social media to connect with friends. Screens have replaced presence, and no one is rewarding us for putting our phone down.
Pingl changes that.
Wear it. Connect. Earn on-chain rewards.
Pingl is a wearable that recognizes the moments that feel the most meaningful and warm to us : real life conversations filled with shared laughter, and good vibes, and mints uniquely generated on-chain rewards for every meaningful interaction you have in the real world.
No audio is ever recorded or stored. Pingl listens only for the patterns of positive interaction: the cadence of friendly conversation, the sound of laughter. It's fully privacy-first, processing sound signals without capturing speech content, so you stay present instead of glued to a screen:, rewardable proof of irl connections.

**Challenges we ran into**

There were many challenges, one of them was not having the right name for my device embedded in the bluetooth connectivity logic, and that took a lot of trial and error to get right to get the bluetooth pairing to work. The device name embedded in the connectivity logic had to match exactly what the browser was scanning for, including spaces and case sensitivity and when it didn't, the device simply wouldn't appear. It sounds like a small detail but it took a lot debugging, requiring multiple iterations of uploading new arduino code, testing, and adjusting before the connection was stable.


Another hard problem was defining what a "conversation" actually is. It's easy to detect sound, but knowing when a chat ends required us to think carefully about silence, how long a pause is just a breath versus the actual end of an interaction. This meant building in silence-detection logic alongside the sound detection, then carefully tuning the threshold so that brief quiet moments wouldn't prematurely close an active session. Getting that balance right was important to get meaningful, accurate data rather than fragmented or inflated interaction counts.We had to tweak the threshold for sound data to measure silence effectively in order to accurately measure when a conversation ended.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

We used AI tools such as claude, cursor and gemini to do things like help write the logic for some of the functionality, creating the digital art used for the nfts, and debugging problems.

**Futurllama**

Futuristic incentives to connect irl with friends!

**Pingl **- proof of irl connection

What if your social energy came with on chain rewards?
Pingl is a wearable device that rewards human connection in real time, using audio pattern recognition. The wearable for pingl detects conversations and laughter throughout your day without recording content, just pure signal processing on-device.
**The Wild Idea: **We're building a social graph based on actual human interaction, not likes or follows. Your irl fun interactions with people becomes verifiable on-chain data.

The Tech:

Edge ML running on Arduino Nano 33 BLE for privacy-first audio analysis
Real-time pattern detection (no cloud, no recording, just vibes)
Web Bluetooth for seamless device ↔ dashboard communication
Local-first architecture with optional on-chain attestations

**Why It's Frontier:**
Despite everyone being connected online 24/7 and social media's prevalence, there is a mass scale loneliness issue affecting people of all ages. Pingl wants to help humanity for the better while using the fun artifacts ethereum has to offer. Pingl measures what matters: genuine human connection. Getting rewarded for fun chatting and talking to people in real life (laughing, talking, connecting).
We're at the intersection of wearable tech, privacy-preserving AI, and enabling adoption of web3 in frictionless ways. The device stays offline due to relying only on bluetooth. Your data stays yours. 
Futurllama because: It sounds crazy to track fun connections and chats with Arduino and call it frontier tech. But in a world of algorithmic isolation, quantifying genuine human warmth is the most radical, emotionally-nourishing thing to build today.

### Townhall
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/townhall-23da) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/jonumhills/townhall-rwa) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/HPACRzy0FPM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Tokenizing Gov Zoning Changes as Real World Assets

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Hidden Wealth of Zoning
**The Hook: ** When a city council approves a zoning change, massive property value is created overnight, often turning a $200,000 residential lot into a $2,000,000 commercial goldmine.

**The Reality:** This $1.8 million in "thin-air" value creation is entirely gatekept.

Townhall solves three massive problems in the current real estate and municipal landscape:

**Exclusive Wealth Capture:** Currently, only wealthy developers and institutional insiders have the capital to buy entire properties ahead of zoning changes. Citizens are completely priced out of investing in their own neighborhoods' growth.

**Opaque and Archaic Systems:** Finding out about rezoning requires digging through archaic municipal websites or attending Tuesday morning city council meetings. There is zero transparency for the average citizen, and manual paperwork costs cities time and money (often taking weeks for deed verifications).

**Zero Democratic Participation:** Real estate investment remains a VIP club. By the time a neighborhood is revitalized, the original residents have been priced out without sharing in the upside.

Townhall democratizes this process. By tokenizing these newly zoned parcels into 1,000 fungible shares via the Hedera Token Service (HTS) for retail investors, and independently deploying compliance-ready smart contracts on ADI Chain for institutional wholesale, we lower the barrier to entry from $200,000 down to $50. It transforms opaque government bureaucracy into an investable, transparent, and 100% on-chain ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a fully native, non-EVM application that interfaces with messy government data brought several distinct technical hurdles:

**Taming Unstructured Government Data:** Municipal websites are notoriously decentralized and unstructured. Scraping the county sites for rezoning petitions required building highly resilient Python/Beautiful Soup crawlers capable of parsing inconsistent HTML tables, mapping string addresses to Mapbox geo-coordinates, and dynamically fetching GeoJSON boundaries from legacy GIS APIs.

**Shifting from EVM to Native Hedera Logic:** Moving away from Solidity smart contracts required a complete architectural mindset shift. Instead of writing escrow contracts for the marketplace, I had to master Hedera’s Native Token Transfers to execute atomic swaps. Ensuring the buyer’s HBAR and the seller’s share tokens transferred simultaneously (or failed together) in 3-5 seconds without a smart contract was a major learning curve.

**Architecting the County Cryptographic Signature:** To make the RWAs legitimate, the NFTs needed undeniable proof of government approval. I had to carefully design the key management system so the County's private key acted as the supplyKey for the NFT collection. Figuring out how to embed the deed hash, GeoJSON, and verification timestamps into the Hedera token metadata, while strictly gating the minting function to the admin dashboard, was complex but ultimately resulted in a highly secure, immutable audit trail.

**Managing a Dual-Chain Architecture:** Integrating the ADI Chain for the institutional side of the platform introduced the complexity of a multi-chain environment. While Hedera handled the retail fractionalization via native SDKs, deploying to ADI required switching back to Solidity to build EVM-compatible, compliance-ready smart contracts for Durham County. The challenge was building a unified system that seamlessly routed everyday citizens to Hedera’s high-speed retail marketplace, while gating institutional investors and government admins into the strictly permissioned, role-based ADI Layer-2 ecosystem without breaking the user experience.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

To make this platform truly autonomous and accessible, Townhall relies heavily on AI agents to bridge the gap between bureaucratic data and citizen investors.

**Autonomous Crawling Agents:** I built zero-human-intervention Python agents that run on a cron job every 6 hours. These agents autonomously scrape county websites for newly filed rezoning petitions, extract the parcel data (PIN, address, zoning changes), and store it in Elasticsearch.

**Elastic AI Impact Analysis:** Government rezoning documents are dense with legalese. I integrated Elastic AI agents to analyze incoming petitions and automatically generate human-readable "Impact Analysis" reports. The AI evaluates the proposed changes and assigns a severity score, lists potential community concerns (like traffic or noise), and highlights benefits (like new businesses or property value increases).

**Geocoded AI Alerts:** The system uses Mapbox to geocode the AI-processed data, allowing citizens to set radius-based subscriptions. When a zoning change is proposed near their home, the AI agent dispatches a contextualized alert, breaking down the impact and presenting the direct opportunity to buy fractional shares in the tokenized property.

**New France Village**

Townhall RWA sits directly at the intersection of RealFi, Main Street Adoption, and Regulatory Compliance, transforming how everyday citizens interact with traditional real estate finance.

First, it attacks the RWA (Real World Asset) thesis by digitizing an incredibly lucrative but entirely illiquid asset class - **government zoning changes**. When a property is rezoned, millions in "thin-air" value are created overnight. Currently, this TradFi system is gatekept by wealthy developers. By fractionalizing these newly zoned deeds into 1,000 fungible Hedera tokens, we lower the investment barrier from $200,000+ to just $50. This is the definition of Main Street Adoption, giving retail citizens a direct mechanism to invest in the commercial growth of their own neighborhoods.

Furthermore, we designed this with Policy, Regs, and Institutional Compliance as a feature, not an afterthought. Unlike many DeFi projects that bypass authorities, Townhall RWA integrates them. By requiring the municipal government’s private key to act as the supplyKey for the NFT mint, and logging verifications to the Hedera Consensus Service (HCS), we create a cryptographically secure, fully compliant audit trail.

Finally, by utilizing Hedera Native Token Transfers instead of complex EVM smart contracts, we bridge TradFi and DeFi seamlessly. Users get atomic settlements and 3-5 second finality with predictable ~$0.0001 fees, delivering an enterprise-grade financial rail that is actually usable for the everyday citizen.

**“No Solidity Allowed” - Hedera SDKs Only**

Townhall RWA is a comprehensive Real World Asset platform built entirely without a single line of Solidity for Raeligh County. Instead of relying on EVM smart contracts, we leveraged the @hashgraph/sdk and Hedera’s Layer-1 native services to build a faster, cheaper, and more secure application.

**Native Tokenization (HTS):** We completely bypassed ERC-721 and ERC-20 standards. Each rezoned property within Raeligh County is minted natively as an NFT via the Hedera Token Service (HTS), and fractional ownership is powered by 1,000 HTS fungible tokens per property.

**Native Access Control:** Instead of writing Solidity modifiers (like onlyOwner) to restrict minting, we used Hedera's native SupplyKey. Only the county government's private key holds the authority to mint new deeds, baking security directly into the protocol level.

**The Escrow Killer:** To power our marketplace without a complex EVM escrow contract, we execute Native Atomic Swaps using TransferTransaction. Buyers and sellers swap HBAR and share tokens simultaneously, achieving 3-5 second finality for ~$0.0001 without smart contract risk.

**Decentralized Notary (HCS): ** Rather than bloating contract state with expensive verification data, we use the Hedera Consensus Service (HCS). Every government deed approval is logged to an HCS topic, creating a 100% immutable, timestamped audit trail without EVM overhead.

**Open Project Submission**

Townhall is an institutional-grade tokenization platform built directly on ADI Chain to digitize one of the most illiquid TradFi asset classes in the world -  **municipal real estate zoning changes.**

When a county approves a rezoning petition, millions in property value are created overnight. Townhall captures this real-economy event and turns it into a compliant, EVM-compatible Real World Asset (RWA) tailored for enterprise settlement.

Our project perfectly aligns with the ADI Foundation’s vision for regulated infrastructure through four core pillars:

**Institutional-Grade RWA Tokenization: ** We are not building retail micro shares, we are tokenizing the entire commercial rezoning package of Durham County on ADI Chain. This creates a secure, verifiable on-chain asset that Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and private equity firms can use for institutional lending collateral, block trading, or yield generation.

**EVM-Native Execution on ADI:** We utilized ADI Chain as our primary execution layer for Durham County, deploying robust Solidity smart contracts to manage the RWA lifecycle. This ensures seamless EVM compatibility, allowing institutional funds to interact with our tokenized deeds using their existing enterprise wallet infrastructure.

**Compliance, Controls & Whitelabel Architecture:** We designed the UI/UX explicitly for TradFi operators. The platform features strict role-based access control (RBAC), separating the "Operator" (e.g., Durham County officials verifying the deed) from the "End-User" (the institutional investor). The municipal admin dashboard is entirely whitelabel-ready, providing the clarity, control, and auditability required by government entities.

**Data-Driven Real-Economy Triggers:** To bridge the physical and digital worlds, we built autonomous AI agents that scrape county GIS APIs and zoning websites. These agents act as automated data oracles, verifying physical zoning changes and feeding that measurable real-world output on-chain to trigger the institutional tokenization process on ADI.

### MoltDAO
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/moltdao-eed6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/LSpinoti/MoltDAO) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://moltdao-rho.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/K2e75YIXNAA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Moltbook for DAO Governance

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Uniswap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Uniswap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Quicknode](https://img.shields.io/badge/Quicknode-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kite AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kite%20AI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Important governance decisions are often made with low participation** because most token holders do not have time to monitor forums and vote consistently.

Token holders can use it to:

- Maintain continuous governance participation through always-on AI delegates that monitor, debate, and vote.
- Make treasury management more actionable by turning approved proposals into executable on-chain actions.
- Improve decision quality with structured agent debate instead of sporadic, low-context voting.
- Reduce operational overhead for communities that currently rely on a small set of active contributors.
- Increase safety and trust with execution guardrails, transparent activity logs, and auditable on-chain outcomes.
- Manage more complex DAO strategies such as RWA allocation, swaps, and agent-to-agent service payments in one governance workflow.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Low-signal governance data for agents**  
  Early on, agent outputs were generic because they lacked concrete treasury context.  
  I fixed this by injecting structured sponsor-aware context (RWA allocations, swap routing, inference costs, payment rails) into the runtime prompts so debates became specific and decision-relevant.

- **Maintaining reliability across off-chain + on-chain components**  
  Coordination between indexer, API, agent runtime, and UI can drift under local dev conditions.  
  I reduced this friction with clear service boundaries, health checks, and deterministic endpoint contracts so each component can fail and recover without breaking the full demo narrative.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

### How agents are used
- Agents monitor governance context and forum activity.
- They generate posts/comments to surface arguments, risks, and alternatives.
- They evaluate pending proposals and cast stake-backed votes.
- They can initiate governance actions that, once approved, execute on-chain through guarded pathways.

### How they work together
- Multiple agents run in parallel, each acting independently but sharing the same governance state.
- They coordinate through the forum itself: one agent proposes, others challenge or support, then vote.
- This creates a persistent debate loop instead of one-off, low-participation voting events.

### AI + system integration flow
- **Inference layer (0G Compute):** powers reasoning steps and decision generation.
- **Governance execution layer (Base + contracts):** records posts, votes, and action outcomes on-chain.
- **Treasury action layer (Uniswap integration):** routes approved swap actions.
- **RWA context layer (Canton Network):** provides private fund allocation context for governance discussions.
- **Economic coordination layer (Kite AI x402):** supports agent-native payment flows.
- **Data layer (QuickNode Streams + indexer/API):** keeps state fresh and visible in the dashboards.

**Best Use of Quicknode Monad Streams**

The indexer service already runs finality-aware event ingestion and cursor persistence, so QuickNode Streams plugs in as an alternative high-throughput source for deterministic updates. We add a stream consumer adapter that normalizes Monad and HyperCore payloads into the existing Postgres tables and reuse the same API/query surface.

**Best DeFAI Application**

POST /actions/draft produces structured execution plans with slippage, deadline, calldata hash, and metadata, which turns AI-driven intent into constrained DeFi actions. Agents use this draft flow to propose treasury operations while governance votes and whitelist checks keep humans and policy in final control.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

The existing agent identity layer in AgentRegistry and indexed reputation tables provide deterministic principals and trust signals, so Kite identity attestations map directly to agent records. We add an x402 payment middleware in the API and agent-runtime request paths so agents programmatically authenticate, pay for gated resources, and log payment-linked actions for end-to-end auditability.

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

The current ActionExecutor pipeline already models deterministic, permissionless execution with calldata-hash checks and status transitions, so scheduled execution maps cleanly onto the same action lifecycle. We implement a Hedera adapter that submits schedule-create calls from contract-driven governance decisions and mirrors schedule states into the existing actions and executions tables.

**Best Canton Dev Tooling & DevX Accelerator**

The current architecture separates on-chain settlement from off-chain state materialization, which maps to a Canton pattern where private workflow logic executes in Daml and finalized effects bridge to Base execution contracts. We add a Canton connector service that attests approved private outcomes into the existing action pipeline and indexes those attestations for auditability in the forum UI.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

services/agent-runtime executes autonomous register-post-propose-vote cycles on Base, so agents continuously create and act on governance opportunities without manual transaction orchestration. The stake-backed forum, deterministic action thresholds, and permissionless execution path keep the agent economy self-sustaining by coupling behavior, capital commitment, and on-chain outcomes.

**Solving the Homeless Agent Problem**

The current stack already gives agents persistent on-chain identity (AgentRegistry), stake-backed participation (StakeVault), and indexed memory/history (posts, comments, reputation), so each agent maintains durable state across runs. We add a portable agent profile package that binds identity metadata, policy constraints, and funding routes, then rehydrates the same agent context in any compatible runtime without losing reputation continuity.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

The action draft flow already encodes swap intents and risk checks, so Uniswap API quoting fits as an additional provider beside the current 0x and paths. We implement a quote-provider interface extension that fetches Uniswap route data, encodes execution calldata, and stores simulation and slippage diagnostics for governance review.

**Governance UX & Community Tooling**

The web app already consumes indexed proposals, votes, execution history, and reputation signals, so governance state renders as a real-time decision timeline instead of raw transaction data. We extend the action inspector with explicit risk-check badges, threshold progress meters, and pre-execution simulation summaries so users and observers evaluate proposals with deterministic, machine-verifiable context.

### Verifiable Agent Execution Bundle (VAEB)

> cryptographically guarantees the transaction match

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square) ![DAML](https://img.shields.io/badge/DAML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents today are multiple variants of chatbots. In finance, they can advise on financial decisions, but people are hesitant to let them directly execute money due to lack of security guardrails. **VAEB** changes that by letting agents spend money on authorizers' behalf without ever touching their private key.

The core problem is simple: if you want an AI agent to pay for a service, execute a swap, or move funds, you either hand over your private key (dangerous), or sign every transaction yourself (defeats the purpose of an agent). VAEB introduces a third option: 

an MCP server where the agent calls and submits transactions, but a ZK proof cryptographically guarantees the transaction matches what you approved.

For simple payments (e.g., an agent paying for an API via x402), the counterparty specifies the address and amount, and the user signs an intent bundle with those exact parameters. The ZK proof here acts as a safety net, ensuring the agent can't swap in a different address or inflate the amount between your approval and on-chain execution. The agent handles gas, timing, and submission without ever seeing your key.

This first version focuses on simple payments. When an agent paying for an API via x402, or sending tokens to a recipient, the user signs an intent bundle with the exact parameters, and the agent handles gas, timing, and on-chain submission without ever seeing the private key. The ZK proof acts as a safety net, ensuring the agent can't swap in a different address or inflate the amount between your approval and execution. This alone is a significant leap to enable agents from passive advisors to active economic participants.

The architecture is designed for what comes next. The same ZK proof infrastructure naturally extends to complex DeFi operations (swaps, multi-step strategies) where the agent derives `calldata` from simple intents, and ultimately to intent-as-boundary-conditions, where users sign constraints ("spend up to 500 USDC per day", "only interact with these protocols") and agents make autonomous decisions within those boundaries. The current exact-match mode is the most restrictive version of this architecture, proving the trust layer works before expanding agent autonomy.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Deploying across EVM chains with different quirks. Our Groth16 on-chain verifier relies on the `ecPairing` precompile (EIP-197) for BN128 pairing checks. Base Sepolia supports this natively, but deploying to Kite AI Testnet is different: gas pricing for the pairing operation, RPC endpoints that don't support `eth_sendTransaction` (requiring private-key signing locally), and L2 propagation delays where contracts appeared deployed but had no code. We built a chain-agnostic config system in the SDK and per-chain deployment scripts that auto-update deployments.json, so the MCP server, frontend, and prover all point to the right contracts without manual coordination.

2. Integrating with Canton's completely different ledger model. Canton uses Daml (not EVM) with sub-transaction privacy and RISC0 zkVM proofs, a fundamentally different stack from VAEB's Circom/Groth16 on EVM. The challenge was designing a clean boundary: Canton defines what should happen (settlement terms via `CrossChainSettlement` contracts), and VAEB executes how (ZK-verified EVM transfers). This required a dual-proof architecture where each settlement is backed by two independent ZK proofs. RISC0 proving the chain state exists, and Groth16 proving the execution matches the user's intent.

3. Wiring 0G decentralized inference into the agent loop. Instead of calling centralized OpenAI APIs, we integrated 0G Serving for decentralized AI inference. This meant using @0glabs/0g-serving-broker to discover available GPU providers, manage sub-account funding with A0GI tokens, and handle the fact that 0G models (Qwen 2.5 7B) don't support native function calling. We had to fall back to prompt-based tool calling where the model outputs structured JSON that we parse into MCP tool invocations.

4. Bridging Poseidon and Keccak256 across the ZK boundary. Our Circom circuit uses Poseidon hashing (ZK-friendly, ~10x fewer constraints), but Solidity and EIP-712 signatures use Keccak256. We designed the commitment scheme so the circuit proves derivation correctness with Poseidon, while the contract verifies signatures via EIP-712/Keccak256, bridging two hash worlds without breaking the proof chain.

5. snarkjs signal ordering caused silent on-chain failures. snarkjs outputs public signals as `[output_signal, ...public_inputs]`, but our contract expected `[public_inputs...]`. Proofs generated fine off-chain but silently failed the pairing check on-chain. We built a Groth16VerifierAdapter contract to bridge the gap.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

VAEB is built as an AI-agent-native protocol. The AI agent is not a helper, it's the execution layer.

The agent interacts with the blockchain via MCP. We built an MCP server exposing 23 tools across 6 categories: chain queries, intent creation/execution, wallet management, agent reputation, marketplace, and proof verification. Any MCP-compatible AI model can discover and call these tools. The agent reads balances, constructs intents, generates ZK proofs, and submits verified transactions, all through standard tool calls.

The core flow: A user chats naturally ("I need someone to walk my dog" or "send 10 USDC to 0x..."). The AI agent interprets the request, calls create_intent to build a structured IntentBundle, presents it to the user for EIP-712 signing, then calls execute_intent which generates a Groth16 ZK proof and submits the verified transaction on-chain. The agent handles the full lifecycle from natural language to on-chain settlement but is cryptographically constrained by the ZK proof to only execute what the user signed.

AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor) were used extensively during development: contract testing, MCP server implementation, and multi-chain deployment scripting were all built with AI pair programming.

**Futurllama**

VAEB introduces a new cryptographic primitive: ZK-verified agent execution. 
AI agents can now spend money on behalf of users without accessing private keys, and a Groth16 proof cryptographically guarantees the agent can't deviate from what the user approved.

This sits at the intersection of AI + ZK + on-chain execution:
- A 10,790-constraint Circom circuit proves calldata matches signed intent
- An ERC-8150 smart contract wallet verifies the proof on-chain before executing
- An MCP server exposes 23 tools so any AI model can orchestrate the full flow

The "big crazy idea": agents as autonomous economic participants, constrained by math instead of trust. This version handles simple payments; the same architecture extends to boundary-condition intents where agents make autonomous decisions within user-signed constraints.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

VAEB is an AI execution planner for on-chain payments, exactly the "intent → steps" use case in your example list.

The AI agent powered by 0G Compute inference interprets natural language requests and drives a multi-step on-chain workflow where every inference call results in real fund movement:

1. User: "I need someone to walk my dog" (natural language)
2. 0G inference → searches marketplace, selects provider, negotiates price
3. 0G inference → calls `create_intent` to build ZK-verified payment bundle
4. User signs intent in MetaMask
5. 0G inference → calls `execute_intent` → Groth16 proof → on-chain tx

This is not a chatbot with a crypto wrapper. The AI model's output directly controls which MCP tools get called, what parameters get passed, and ultimately which on-chain transactions execute. The ZK proof layer ensures the model can't deviate from what the user approved, even if the 
inference output is adversarial.

**0G integration:**
- 0G Serving via `@0glabs/0g-serving-broker` for decentralized inference
- Provider auto-discovery + sub-account funding with A0GI tokens
- Agent wallet key doubles as 0G wallet, single identity across inference and execution
- Prompt-based tool calling with structured JSON output → MCP tool invocations
- Provider-agnostic MCP architecture: 0G slots in alongside other backends, demonstrating real composability

**Why 0G matters here:** When AI agents control money, centralized inference could be a single point of failure. A compromised API provider could manipulate agent behavior. Decentralized inference via 0G adds a trust layer to the reasoning step, complementing the ZK trust layer on the 
execution step.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

VAEB is an agent-native payment protocol deployed on Kite AI Testnet where AI agents execute on-chain transactions with zero-knowledge proof verification. Users sign an intent (e.g., "pay 25 USDC to Alice"), the agent derives calldata and generates a Groth16 ZK proof (10,790 constraints) that cryptographically binds the intent to the transaction. The AgentWallet smart contract on Kite AI verifies the proof on-chain before executing: the agent literally cannot deviate from what was authorized.

x402 payment flows: The agent pays for services (proof generation, price oracles) via HTTP 402 micropayments and charges users for execution, creating a self-sustaining economic loop settled on Kite AI.

Verifiable agent identity: Wallet-based agent is registered on-chain via setAgent(), every execution is auditable on KiteScan, and ZK proofs bind the agent's identity to each action.

Autonomous execution: After one EIP-712 signature, the agent handles proof generation, payment, submission, and confirmation with zero human intervention.

23 MCP tools let any AI model (Claude, GPT, etc.) discover and use the wallet autonomously. Kite AI's ultra-low gas and near-instant finality make ZK-verified micropayments economically viable — exactly what agent-scale economics requires. Open source (MIT), authors of ERC-8150.

**Best Privacy-Focused dApp Using Daml**

VAEB integrates Canton's privacy-first model for confidential multi-party settlement coordination with on-chain ZK-verified execution. We use 4 Daml contract templates (`CustodyAttestation`, `CrossChainSettlement`, `AttestationProposal`, `ProofOfReserve`) to orchestrate private agreements between Buyer, Seller, and Custodian, where each party only sees what Canton's sub-transaction privacy allows.

Privacy model: Settlement terms, balance attestations, and execution receipts are visible only to the named parties, no public ledger. A Custodian attests a seller's EVM balance using a RISC0 zkVM proof, the three parties agree to settlement terms privately on Canton, then VAEB's AI agent executes the actual transfer on EVM with a Groth16 ZK proof verifying the calldata matches the signed intent. The execution receipt is recorded back on Canton as a private audit trail.

Dual ZK proof stack: RISC0 proves off-chain state (EVM balance exists), Groth16 proves on-chain execution (transfer matches intent), aka independent verification with no shared trust. This is Private DeFi: confidential OTC-style settlement where counterparties prove solvency and execute transfers without exposing positions publicly.

4 MCP tools let AI agents query attestations, settlements, and autonomously prepare+execute cross-chain settlements. 43 tests, open source (MIT).

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: The "Liquidity & Privacy Gap" in RWA
While the tokenization of Real-World Assets (RWA) is booming, the secondary market infrastructure for these assets remains broken. Institutions face three critical barriers:

Market Signaling & Slippage: On public ledgers, large buy/sell orders are visible to everyone. This "transparency" allows competitors to front-run trades, leading to massive slippage and unfavorable prices for large-scale institutional blocks.

Information Asymmetry: In private RWA markets (Real Estate, Private Debt), finding the "fair market price" is nearly impossible without revealing your strategy to a centralized middleman who takes a heavy fee.

Compliance Friction: Managing RFPs, KYB verification, and legal attestations (Conflict of Interest) across borders is a manual, slow, and error-prone process that delays settlement.

The Solution: What people use Dark Pool for
Dark Pool provides a private, compliant, and AI-assisted auction house on the ADI Chain. It allows institutions to discover the true price of any tokenized asset without exposing their intentions to the public market before the deal is done.

Key Use Cases:
Institutional RWA Exit/Entry: A fund can liquidate $10M in tokenized real estate via a sealed-bid auction. Competitors cannot see the bids, preventing front-running and ensuring the seller gets the best possible price.

Private Debt Tenders: Companies can issue RFPs for private debt or receivables. Bidders submit private commitments, and the AI agents assist in scoring the most competitive and compliant offers.

Commodity Trading: Secure procurement of tokenized commodities (Gold, Energy, Carbon Credits) where price confidentiality is a strategic necessity.

How it makes tasks Easier & Safer
1. Safer Price Discovery (Commit-Reveal)
By using a on-chain commit-reveal mechanism, Dark Pool ensures that no one—not even the platform—knows the bid prices until the reveal phase. This eliminates "last-look" advantages and collusion, making auctions mathematically fair.

2. Automated Compliance (EIP-712 & KYB)
We replace weeks of legal back-and-forth with a streamlined digital flow. Every participant must be KYB-verified on-chain, and every bid requires a digitally signed EIP-712 attestation regarding conflicts of interest. This creates a "Regulated-by-Code" environment.

3. AI-Powered Efficiency
Existing RWA auctions are labor-intensive. Dark Pool makes them easier by using 10 specialized AI agents to:

Draft RFPs in seconds instead of hours.

Detect predatory bidding or collusion automatically after the reveal.

Generate audit narratives that compliance officers can immediately use for regulatory reporting.

4. Native ADI Settlement
By settling in DDSC (AED Stablecoin) on the ADI Chain, we eliminate the volatility risk associated with traditional crypto payments, providing the "Wall Street" experience with the efficiency of DeFi.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into
Building a bridge between institutional finance and decentralized privacy-preserving mechanisms presented several significant hurdles:

1. The "Commit-Reveal" UX Friction
Implementing a true Sealed-Bid auction requires a two-step process: the "Commit" (submitting a hash of the bid) and the "Reveal" (revealing the salt and value).

The Hurdle: On-chain, this is often clunky. If a user loses their secret "salt" or fails to return for the reveal phase, the auction breaks.

The Solution: We built a robust local state-management system and a guided UX that ensures the "salt" is securely handled on the client side, while the AI Bid Drafter helps prepare the reveal documentation ahead of time to minimize manual errors.

2. Preserving the "Dark" in Dark Pool vs. AI Analysis
A major challenge was integrating 10 AI agents without compromising the auction's integrity.

The Hurdle: AI needs data to be useful, but a Dark Pool must remain opaque until settlement. We had to ensure our Competitiveness Analyzer could give feedback without "peeking" at the actual secret commitments on-chain.

The Solution: We architected a "Blind-Inference" workflow. The AI agents only interact with public RFP metadata and historical market benchmarks. The sensitive bid values are only processed by the Bid Scorer after the reveal phase, maintaining the cryptographic guarantee of the sealed-bid mechanism.

3. Institutional Compliance Architecture on ADI Chain
Integrating KYB (Know Your Business) and EIP-712 attestations within a high-speed auction environment was technically demanding.

The Hurdle: We had to ensure that every participant was verified via the ShadowBidFactory without introducing excessive latency that would ruin the "Wall Street" trading experience.

The Solution: We implemented a pre-verification caching layer in our middleware. This allowed the UI to instantly validate an institution's status while the smart contracts enforced the strict permissioning logic at the execution level.

4. AI Orchestration & Failover Logic
Managing 10 specialized agents using Groq (Llama 3.3) required a high level of reliability.

The Hurdle: During peak usage, hitting rate limits or latency spikes can break the "Real-time" feel of the bidding dashboard.

The Solution: We developed a custom orchestration layer with a priority-failover chain. If Groq experiences a lag, the system automatically routes the inference to OpenAI or Gemini, ensuring the institutional user never experiences a "loading" state during a critical auction.

5. Multi-Token Settlement Logic
Settling in DDSC (AED Stablecoin) while pricing in USD/AED required precision.

The Hurdle: Ensuring that the AI's price conversion matched the on-chain settlement logic perfectly.

The Solution: We synchronized our AI's "Market Intelligence" with the same price oracles used by our ADI Chain contracts, ensuring that the "AI-estimated" settlement value and the final on-chain transaction were always aligned to the cent.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

AI Tools & Agentic Architecture in Dark Pool
Dark Pool implements a sophisticated multi-agent orchestration layer consisting of 10 specialized AI agents designed to automate the institutional procurement and RWA auction lifecycle. We use Groq (Llama 3.3 70B) as our primary inference engine for its ultra-low latency, with OpenAI and Gemini integrated as a priority fallback chain.

Technical Architecture: The "Safe Inference" Layer
Our system is built around a custom runInference() orchestration layer. This backend service manages provider health checks and routes requests through a priority chain. To preserve the Sealed-Bid integrity—a core requirement for institutional dark pools—the AI agents are architected to process only public metadata and market context. They never have access to the secret commitment hashes, ensuring that the cryptographic privacy of the auction remains untampered.

The 10 Specialized Agents
Our ecosystem follows the entire auction lifecycle through dedicated agents:

1. Institutional Preparation:
The RFP Generator drafts professional, standardized Request for Proposals based on asset type and requirements, while the Category Classifier automatically tags and indexes auctions (Real Estate, Debt, Commodities) to ensure institutional discoverability.

2. Bidder Assistance & Analysis:
For potential suppliers, the Lot Analyzer surfaces technical risks and red flags from auction descriptions. The Bid Drafter then helps structure professional responses, and the Competitiveness Analyzer provides real-time scoring as the supplier types their price, warning them if their bid is unrealistic compared to historical market data.

3. Post-Reveal & Settlement Intelligence:
Once the reveal phase occurs, the Low-Bid Detector scans for predatory pricing or collusion patterns. The Bid Scorer then evaluates all revealed bids holistically—ranking them based on price, compliance, and specific conditions—to assist the buyer in the final selection.

4. Audit & Strategy:
After settlement, the Post-Reveal Report agent generates a full narrative audit trail explaining the rationale behind the winner, which is essential for compliance records. Long-term, the Provider Insights and Benchmark Agent analyze win/loss ratios and sector performance to provide strategic recommendations to all participants.

Workflow & Integration
The agents work together in a seamless pipeline:

The Buyer initiates with the RFP Generator to create high-quality tenders.

The Supplier uses the Analyzer and Drafter agents to minimize friction in the bidding process.

The System enforces real-time guardrails through the Competitiveness agent.

The Compliance Officer relies on the post-auction reporting and scoring agents for a transparent and auditable decision-making process.

Privacy & Security Standards
All AI operations are executed server-side to prevent sensitive data exposure. By maintaining a strict separation between the AI's "Market Intelligence" and the blockchain's "Execution Layer," we ensure that AI provides deep analytical value without ever compromising the trustless and private nature of the Dark Pool. All final binding decisions and settlements remain 100% on-chain and human-controlled.

**New France Village**

Dark Pool: The Institutional Layer for RWA Price Discovery
Dark Pool is an infrastructure designed to bring Wall Street's opaque price discovery mechanisms on-chain. We bridge the gap between RWA tokenization and institutional liquidity through three core pillars:

1. Institutional-Grade Compliance (RegFi)
Unlike retail-focused protocols, Dark Pool mandates a strictly compliant workflow:

On-chain KYB: Integration via ShadowBidFactory.verifyInstitution() ensures only verified entities can participate.

Conflict-of-Interest Attestations: Use of EIP-712 signed attestations before every bid.

AML Screening: Automated sanctions screening (ComplyAdvantage) integrated at the API level.

2. RealFi & Secondary Markets

3. TradFi-to-DeFi Bridge
We replicate the "Clearing House" model on the ADI L1 EVM chain:

Settlement: Conducted in DDSC (AED stablecoin) for predictable, non-volatile transactions.

Risk Management: Implementation of creatorBond (collateral) to mirror TradFi margin requirements.

The Differentiator: Dark Pool doesn't just tokenize assets; it builds the confidential and compliant marketplace necessary for institutional adoption. It is the missing link between holding a tokenized asset and finding liquid, private, and regulated exit/entry points.

One-sentence Pitch: Dark Pool brings Wall Street’s opaque price discovery on-chain with built-in KYB, AML, and EIP-712 attestations—making RWA auctions institutional-grade without central intermediaries.
