> BitTorrent Network for Self-Evolving AI Agents

![Cryptography](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cryptography-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cryptocurrency](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cryptocurrency-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Neural Torrent addresses the basic challenge of how AI agents can exchange training data in a fair and autonomous manner in a decentralized system. Currently, high-quality AI training data is costly, centralized, and dominated by a few large players. There is no open infrastructure that enables independent agents or models to find useful datasets, trade them with each other, and get legitimate credit for their contributions. In decentralized systems, agents typically download valuable data without contributing anything in return, causing a free-rider problem that undermines the entire network.
Neural Torrent fills this gap by merging the incentive dynamics of closed BitTorrent trackers with cryptographic reputation on-chain. Each AI participant enters the system with a wallet identity, contributes datasets like video or audio files for AI model fine-tuning, and accumulates a contribution score depending on the ratio of uploaded versus downloaded data. Each unit of data transferred is accompanied by a signed cryptographic receipt, and the upload and download metrics are maintained on-chain. Contributing participants get more access, and those who simply download without seeding get limited access until they pay back by contributing. This establishes a self-reinforcing incentive system where participation is visible, trackable, and incentive-compatible.
By doing so, Neural Torrent creates infrastructure for a decentralized AI data exchange layer, enabling agents to improve themselves through cooperative data sharing rather than relying on centralized brokers. Reputation becomes persistent and portable across tracker instances, ensuring that contribution history survives migrations or downtime. In essence, Neural Torrent solves the trust, incentive, and verification challenges in decentralized AI data sharing, enabling autonomous model self-evolution backed by cryptographic proof.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our team brought together people with very different levels of experience, ranging from researchers and developers to students who were new to distributed systems. This created an initial knowledge gap, particularly around complex concepts such as BitTorrent-style peer-to-peer networks. To overcome this, we leaned heavily on teammate-to-teammate teaching. More experienced members helped others build an intuition for how BitTorrent works—its incentive mechanisms, file sharing model, and network dynamics—so that the entire team could contribute meaningfully.
Another major challenge was direction and scope. We initially focused on improving the BitTorrent network itself, grounding our work in research and attempting to translate those ideas into a real MVP. After building much of the backend infrastructure, we realized that while improving BitTorrent was interesting, it was not the core problem we wanted to solve. This led to a key insight. The true strength of BitTorrent is not the protocol itself, but its ability to efficiently distribute large files in a decentralized way. That realization allowed us to connect our work to a much larger and more relevant problem: AI training data. By reframing training data as a large-scale, shareable asset—similar to files in a BitTorrent network—we aligned our technical foundation with a real-world need. This shift transformed our project from improving a network into applying BitTorrent economics to decentralize and scale access to AI training data.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Over the course of the hackathon, we used GitHub Copilot and Claude to assist in developing Neural Torrent Network. Copilot helped generate key backend components including API routes, the /agent-tools discovery endpoint, CORS configuration, and cryptographic receipt logic.

**Devtopia**

We deliver immutable on-chain reputation contracts (ReputationTracker + RepFactory with single-hop migration), cryptographically signed data receipts (EIP-191). This enables CloudLLM-powered agents to autonomously discover our API, register, trade large video/audio datasets via BitTorrent, and maintain verifiable contribution ratios — all without human intervention.
This provides scalable, persistent, and secure decentralized data infrastructure directly on Ethereum.

**Solving the Homeless Agent Problem**

Our immutable ReputationTracker and RepFactory contracts provide each agent with persistent on-chain identity and portable reputation that survives tracker restarts and migrations. Using CloudLLM, agents autonomously register, seed and trade real video/audio datasets via BitTorrent, submit cryptographically signed receipts, and maintain healthy contribution ratios — all without relying on any central server.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

Neural Torrent Network integrates the Uniswap Trading API to enable seamless cross-token payments in our decentralized AI data marketplace.
Seeders price video and audio datasets in any ERC-20 token (e.g. WETH). Buyers pay with any token they hold (e.g. USDC) via automatic Uniswap swaps. Our backend proxies the Uniswap API for real-time quotes, token approvals, and swap execution. Upon successful payment, access is instantly granted and on-chain reputation is updated.

**The problem it solves**

AI agents are being deployed by the thousands. Every single one is financially illiterate.

Today, when developers run AI agent workflows — research pipelines, document processing, autonomous task completion — their agents default to using the same powerful (and expensive) model for every sub-task, regardless of complexity. Reading a webpage gets the same model as writing a legal memo. Formatting a CSV gets the same model as deep strategic reasoning.

The result: Massive, preventable waste. A task that should cost $0.011 costs $0.034 — not because it needed that compute, but because no one taught the agent to think about money.

What AgentBooks Lets You Do
Cut AI inference costs by 60–70% automatically. AgentBooks decomposes any incoming task into atomic sub-tasks, scores each for cognitive complexity, and routes to the cheapest model capable of doing it well:

Simple retrieval, scraping, formatting → Haiku (~19x cheaper than Opus)
Summarization, writing, analysis → Sonnet
Deep reasoning, legal review, novel judgment → Opus or decentralized compute

At 10,000 tasks/day, that's ~$80,000/year saved — automatically, with no change to your agent's output quality.
See exactly what your agents are spending, in real time. The AgentBooks dashboard gives operators a live P&L for every agent: cost per sub-task, cost per full task, and a running "counterfactual" showing what you would have spent without intelligent routing. Think Bloomberg terminal for AI cognitive spend.
Enable trustless agent-to-agent commerce. When Agent A (Company X) needs to hire Agent B (Company Y) for a specialized sub-task, there's no safe way to do this today without a centralized billing intermediary holding API keys and taking rent. AgentBooks settles these payments on-chain via x402 micropayments — no platform in the middle, no shared credentials.
Create immutable, auditable AI spend records. Every model call is logged on-chain with token counts, model used, and cost. For regulated industries (finance, legal, healthcare), this creates a tamper-proof audit trail that a SaaS database can't match — CFOs and compliance teams can verify AI spend independently, without trusting a vendor's dashboard.

Who It's For

Developers running multi-step agent pipelines who want to stop burning money on over-powered models for simple tasks
Enterprise teams in regulated industries (legal, finance, healthcare) that need compliant, auditable AI cost records without sending sensitive data through third-party servers
AI-native companies building agent marketplaces where agents transact with each other across organizational boundaries

**Challenges we ran into**

1. 0G Labs Has No Traditional API Dashboard
The biggest early blocker was discovering that 0G Labs operates nothing like a standard AI API provider. We assumed we'd sign up, grab an API key, and start routing requests — the same flow as OpenAI or Anthropic. Instead, 0G's decentralized compute network uses wallet-based authentication and an on-chain escrow ledger through their @0glabs/0g-serving-broker npm package.
There's no dashboard. No API key. You fund a ledger account with broker.ledger.addLedger(), and the network authenticates you by your wallet signature. We had to completely rethink our integration approach mid-build, switching from a simple HTTP client pattern to a broker-mediated flow with on-chain settlement. Once we understood the architecture, it actually aligned perfectly with our vision — but the discovery cost us several hours of confused debugging.

2. QuickNode Streams → Webhook → Dashboard Pipeline
Getting real-time cost data flowing from our on-chain AgentCostLedger contract to the dashboard was harder than expected. QuickNode Streams fires webhooks when it detects contract events — but our backend needed to receive those webhooks and immediately broadcast updates to connected frontend clients.
The challenge: standard REST endpoints don't push. We had to implement Server-Sent Events (SSE) on our FastAPI backend so the dashboard could maintain a live connection and receive cost updates as each sub-task completed. Debugging the chain of contract event → QuickNode → webhook → SSE → browser meant failures could happen at any of five points, and each one looked identical from the frontend (just: nothing updated).
We got through it by isolating each segment — confirming the contract was emitting events on-chain first, then verifying QuickNode was picking them up, then testing the webhook locally with ngrok before deploying.

3. Separating Hackathon Demo Scope from Production Architecture
This wasn't a technical bug, but it was the most consequential challenge we hit. Midway through planning, we realized the architecture we were building for the demo — a hosted proxy where agent queries flow through our server — is structurally illegal for our target customers (hospitals, law firms, financial institutions) due to HIPAA, attorney-client privilege, and financial data regulations.
We couldn't build the enterprise product in 48 hours, but we also couldn't pitch a demo that judges in regulated industries would immediately reject as non-viable.
The solution was a deliberate dual-track strategy: build Scenario A (hosted proxy) for the demo to show real working functionality, while pitching Scenario B (SDK/metadata-only) as the production architecture. We scripted explicit responses for judge questions about data handling so the distinction was clear and credible rather than sounding like a pivot or a gap.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Claude (claude.ai + Project Knowledge) Our primary development environment. We created a Claude Project loaded with all technical reference documents, architecture specs, integration guides, and build plans. Every code module — FastAPI endpoints, smart contract logic, x402 payment flows, QuickNode webhook handlers — was written through structured Claude prompts with explicit context. Claude served as our entire engineering team, translating financial and product thinking into working code.

Cursor Used as our AI-native code editor throughout the build. Cursor's inline AI assistance let us iterate on Python and JavaScript files rapidly, catching syntax errors and suggesting completions as we assembled the FastAPI backend and Next.js dashboard. Particularly useful for refactoring — when our webhook handler needed restructuring to support Server-Sent Events, Cursor helped us rewrite the module without breaking upstream dependencies.

Warp Our AI-powered terminal. Warp's natural language command generation meant we could describe what we needed ("start the FastAPI server with hot reload on port 8000" or "check which process is holding this port") without memorizing CLI syntax. During deployment to OpenClaw, Warp's command history and AI-assisted debugging helped us move faster through environment setup and dependency issues.

Oz Agent Cloud Used for agentic task execution — particularly for spinning up research and integration tasks in parallel while the core build was in progress. Oz Agent Cloud let us delegate investigative work (finding the correct 0G broker package methods, verifying Kite AI RPC endpoints, checking QuickNode Streams webhook format) to autonomous agents running in the background, keeping our build momentum without constant context-switching.

OpenClaw (Deployment) Our backend server environment. All FastAPI code was deployed and run on OpenClaw rather than locally, which meant every integration (Claude API calls, x402 payment execution, QuickNode webhook receipt, SSE streaming) was live and publicly accessible throughout the build — giving us a real public URL for judge testing and eliminating "works on my machine" failure modes.

Codex / OpenAI Used for secondary code generation tasks and cross-checking Claude outputs on specific integration patterns. When working through the 0G Labs broker SDK — which had limited documentation — we used Codex to explore the npm package structure and infer correct method signatures from type definitions.

How the Tools Worked Together
The workflow followed a consistent pattern throughout the 48 hours:

Claude (Project Knowledge) produced the architectural spec and initial code for each module
Cursor integrated that code into the live codebase with inline refinements
Warp executed deployments, ran tests, and surfaced environment errors
Oz Agent Cloud (via warp terminal) ran parallel research and integration investigation tasks
OpenClaw kept everything live and accessible on a public URL throughout
No single tool was sufficient alone, the value came from the handoff chain. Claude could generate correct logic but couldn't deploy it. Warp could run commands but needed correct code first. Oz Agent Cloud could find answers to integration questions but couldn't write the implementation. Together, they formed a coherent development pipeline that let a finance team ship a working full-stack AI product in two days.

In a way, building AgentBooks with this AI stack is the proof of concept for the product itself: intelligent task decomposition, routing each piece of work to the right specialized tool, and aggregating the outputs into something that works. We didn't just build a system that teaches agents financial literacy, we ran one to build it.

**Prosperia**

AgentBooks is a bet on a future that doesn't fully exist yet — and we're building the infrastructure for it before anyone else does it wrong.

New Primitive: Financial Identity for AI Agents
Right now, AI agents have no concept of money. They spend, but they don't know they spend. AgentBooks introduces a genuinely new primitive: an agent with a P&L. Not a wallet. Not a payment rail. A full financial identity — earnings, expenditures, cost efficiency ratios, and eventually credit. This has never existed before because agents have never needed it before. They do now, and the infrastructure isn't there yet. We're building it.

Big Crazy Idea: The Agentic Economy Needs a Financial System
Every functional economy in history needed financial infrastructure before it could scale — ledgers, payment rails, credit systems, audit trails. The agentic internet is no different. Thousands of autonomous agents are already transacting. None of them have a financial system designed for them. We're building the Fed for the agentic internet — before someone else does it wrong. That's not a feature. It's a new category.

We're not optimizing something that exists. We're building infrastructure for an economy that's forming right now — and the window to get the primitives right is closing fast.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

AgentBooks is built on Kite AI because x402 micropayments aren't a feature we added — they're the billing model the entire system runs on.
Every task AgentBooks receives gets decomposed into atomic sub-tasks, each routed to a different AI model tier, each charged independently via x402 on the Kite testnet. A single "Research this company and write a one-pager" task generates 5 discrete micropayments — one per sub-task — at a granularity ($0.0001–$0.008 each) that Stripe or traditional rails structurally cannot support. This is exactly what x402 was built for.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem: Influencer Marketing Sucks to Handle

In the creator economy, brands face a persistent, expensive dilemma: **How do you pay for impact without being paralyzed by risk?** Currently, the influencer payment workflow is plagued by three points of friction that "tax" every deal:

1. **The Performance Struggle:** Brands want to pay for results (views/engagement), but creators need security. This leads to endless negotiations over "base pay" vs. "performance bonuses" that often stall partnerships before they begin.
2. **The Content Quality Gap:** A video might hit its view target but fail the "vibe check." Whether it’s bot-inflated engagement or a creator missing the brand's tone, manual quality audits take weeks, delaying payments and frustrating creators.
3. **The Fraud Friction:** Because "inspect element" and fake screenshots are rampant, brands default to slow Net-30 or Net-90 payment terms as a safety net. This cash-flow gap is the #1 reason why talented creators and editors leave the industry.

---

## The Solution: MadeBy - The Autonomous Proof-of-Quality System

**MadeBy** is a decentralized platform that turns content quality into a verifiable, liquid asset. We’ve removed the human middleman and replaced them with **Autonomous Agentic Settlement** powered by **0G Labs**.

### How MadeBy Solves the Friction:

* **Agentic Escrow on 0G:** Brands lock sponsorship funds into a smart contract on the 0G blockchain. These funds aren't controlled by the brand or the creator. They are governed by a **0G Autonomous Agent.** in a conditional escrow.
* **Verifiable Quality Audits (The "Brain"):** MadeBy utilizes **0G Labs’ decentralized inference** to run deep sentiment and quality audits. Our agent analyzes the *nature* of the engagement. It distinguishes between genuine human conversation and bot-driven spam.
* **Instant, Verifiable Payouts:** The moment the 0G Agent verifies the content meets the specific performance and quality thresholds set in the contract, it cryptographically triggers the release of funds.

### Why MadeBy Wins:

* **For Brands:** Total protection from "Vanity Metric" fraud. You only pay when the **0G Agent** confirms real, high-quality engagement.
* **For Creators:** Instant liquidity. The second you deliver value, the 0G blockchain settles your payment. No more chasing invoices or waiting 90 days.

**Challenges we ran into**

* **Which platform to use** We initially explored Base and Kite but pivoted to **0G Labs** mid-hackathon to leverage its AI-native architecture. 0G was the only platform that allowed us to treat AI inference as a first-class citizen for our "Agentic Settlement" logic.
* **Testnet Resource Constraints:** We hit a wall when our initial faucet allocation ran out during contract testing. Huge thanks to **Michael from the 0G team** for manually provisioning the tokens we needed to finalize our on-chain logic.
* **Deployment & Integration Hurdles:** Orchestrating decentralized AI inference with a real-time backend led to configuration issues on Railway. This was resolved with backend fixes and small environment variable tweaks

**Use of AI tools and agents**

The core of our system is an auditor agent powered by 0G Labs’ Decentralized Inference. When content is submitted, the agent uses 0G Serving nodes to run a Qwen model that distinguishes genuine human engagement from bot-driven spam.

Once this audit meets the quality threshold, the agent cryptographically triggers the escrow release on the 0G blockchain. For development, we leveraged Claude Code and Opencode as coding agents to rapidly prototype our system. This allowed us to move from concept to MVP on the Galileo testnet in under 48 hours.

**ETHERSPACE**

MadeBy directly aligns with this track as it targets a critical issue with mainstream social media/content management. Currently, brands which are interested in working with influencers do not have a clear and fast payment system for content performance. MadeBy not only reduces payment friction, but automates brand-to-creator payments by using AI to verify content performance (content engagement metrics) before releasing escrowed funds.

**Best DeFAI Application**

MadeBy is a DeFAI escrow system where AI integrates with DeFi by automating payments based on verifiable content performance. The 0G Labs Llama-3 AI analyzes TikTok comments and outputs a structured decision (quality score + APPROVED/REJECTED verdict) with built-in guardrails (funds only release if the score exceeds an 80+ threshold. 

The autonomous agent holds its own wallet, signs EIP-712 transactions, and executes settlement automatically. Users stay in control by confirming all critical actions. The brand escrows funds upfront, the creator submits content for AI audit, and the smart contract enforces the outcome on-chain.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem VybPass Solves

## Live environments contain unmanaged, high-value scarcity

In live events --- concerts, festivals, conferences, tastings, and
livestreams --- there are scarce, time-bound moments that carry real
economic and emotional value.

Examples include:

-   Visual control during a DJ set
-   Spotlight time at an event
-   Limited-access experiences
-   Autograph priority
-   Livestream overlay control
-   Physical device triggers (lights, robots, effects)

These moments are:

-   Scarce
-   Time-bound
-   High demand
-   Operationally controlled

Yet today they are typically allocated:

-   Informally (staff discretion)
-   Pre-sold (VIP tiers)
-   Centrally controlled and opaque
-   Without transparent enforcement

There is no deterministic, programmable way to allocate **live priority
in real time**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Existing systems monetize entry --- not priority

The live events industry monetizes:

-   Entry (tickets)
-   Food & beverage
-   Merchandise
-   Sponsorship

However, **in-event priority allocation** --- who controls the next
moment --- remains largely unmanaged economically.

This leaves:

-   Revenue opportunity unrealized
-   Allocation opaque or discretionary
-   No programmable fairness controls
-   No trust-minimized enforcement

This is not just a payments gap.
It is a **priority enforcement gap**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Traditional payment infrastructure cannot solve this

Centralized processors can collect money.

They cannot:

-   Enforce transparent, deterministic ordering
-   Atomically escrow access rights
-   Settle execution outcomes trustlessly
-   Encode programmable access rules
-   Allow public verification of allocation logic

What is needed is not a checkout button ---
but a crypto-native enforcement mechanism.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## VybPass: Deterministic, On-Chain Priority Enforcement

VybPass introduces a new primitive: **Monetized Live Priority**.

The system consists of:

-   **VybPassToken (\$VYB)** -- ERC20 utility token representing
    time-based influence
-   **PriorityQueue contract** -- deterministic ordering + escrow logic
-   **TreasurySale contract** -- USDC → VYB minting
-   **Autonomous Relay Agent** -- reads on-chain state and executes
    real-world effects

### How It Works

1.  A user purchases VYB tokens (via USDC).
2.  When claiming priority, tokens are escrowed in the PriorityQueue.
3.  Ordering is enforced deterministically on-chain.
4.  When execution completes, markFinished() settles tokens to the
    Treasury.
5.  The relay agent executes what the chain has already decided.

Key properties:

-   No manual override
-   Transparent queue ordering
-   Escrow-backed spam resistance
-   Autonomous settlement
-   Publicly verifiable logic

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Economic Model & Market Relevance

VybPass creates a new monetization layer within existing
multi-billion-dollar industries.

Live entertainment, conferences, and experiential events already
generate hundreds of billions annually.

VybPass enables:

-   In-event revenue generation without physical transactions
-   Monetization from the dance floor, seat, or conference hall
-   Incremental revenue without replacing ticketing infrastructure
-   A circular Treasury-backed token economy

Because tokens are escrowed and settled programmatically, economic
activity is enforced at the protocol layer --- not administratively.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Where It Can Be Used

VybPass applies anywhere scarce priority exists in real time:

-   DJ visual control
-   Livestream overlays
-   Limited-access tastings
-   Conference speaking priority
-   Interactive art installations
-   Robotic or lighting triggers
-   Token-gated IRL activations

If something is scarce in the moment, it can be monetized ---
deterministically and transparently.

## Architecture Overview

## Summary

VybPass solves the problem of unmanaged live scarcity by introducing:

-   Deterministic on-chain priority ordering
-   Escrow-backed economic enforcement
-   Autonomous real-world execution
-   A programmable, transparent access layer

It monetizes influence in the moment --- and turns live priority into a
crypto-native primitive.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

VybPass integrates AI tools into its development workflow to accelerate architecture design, smart contract implementation, documentation, and UI construction.

While the VybPass protocol and execution logic are deterministic and on-chain, AI tooling was used to increase iteration speed and improve system coherence across components.

## AI Tools Used

### ChatGPT

Used for:
- Refining smart contract interface design
- Clarifying escrow and settlement logic
- Drafting protocol documentation
- Stress-testing architectural assumptions
- Identifying edge cases in queue and settlement flow
- Preparing technical pitch materials

ChatGPT acted as a systems design collaborator — helping validate whether the protocol logic aligned with crypto-native principles such as determinism, escrow enforcement, and autonomous execution.

Cursor accelerated full-stack development across:

It significantly reduced iteration cycles between architectural decisions and implementation.

----

### Warp

Warp improved operational efficiency during rapid iteration.

----

### Gamma

Used for:

### AI Within the System Architecture

VybPass itself does not rely on AI for execution or economic enforcement.

The protocol logic is:
- Deterministic
- On-chain
- Escrow-backed
- Autonomous via smart contracts

However, the Autonomous Relay Agent architecture is compatible with future AI-driven decision layers, such as:
- Dynamic pricing models
- Adaptive priority throttling
- NFT-based weighting
- Predictive demand modeling

In its current form, the agent executes deterministically based on on-chain state.

----

### Summary

AI tools were used as development accelerators, not as core enforcement mechanisms.

They enabled:
- Faster architecture iteration
- Cleaner smart contract interfaces
- Improved documentation clarity
- Rapid debugging across multiple system layers

The result is a crypto-native system whose enforcement remains deterministic and on-chain, while leveraging AI for development velocity and system design rigor.

**Futurllama**

VybPass introduces a new coordination primitive: monetized live priority.

Rather than building another content platform or NFT marketplace, VybPass extends Ethereum into real-time physical and digital environments. It enables deterministic, escrow-backed allocation of scarce moments — enforced on-chain and executed autonomously.

This represents:
- A new economic primitive (time as a programmable asset)
- A novel real-world execution layer tied to smart contracts
- An unexpected intersection of Ethereum and live environments
- A frontier use case beyond traditional DeFi or NFTs

VybPass aligns with FUTURLLAMA because it explores what happens when Ethereum is used not just for financial transactions — but for real-time coordination of scarce influence in the physical world.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

VybPass includes an Autonomous Relay Agent deployed on Base that monitors on-chain state and executes real-world effects (visual triggers, device activations, and timed access windows) based on deterministic smart contract logic.

The agent:
- Monitors the PriorityQueue contract on Base mainnet
- Executes real-world actions when a queued moment becomes active
- Calls markFinished() to settle escrowed tokens
- Directs settled tokens to a Treasury contract

Because tokens are escrowed per second of influence and settled automatically, the system generates protocol-level revenue. A portion of Treasury proceeds can be allocated to fund the agent’s compute and operational costs, enabling a self-sustaining model.

----

## Builder Codes & On-Chain Compliance

All agent-triggered on-chain transactions:
- Integrate ERC-8021 Builder Codes
- Are executed on Base mainnet
- Include structured tagging for analytics and attribution

This enables full transparency into:
- Revenue generation
- Settlement frequency
- Agent activity volume
- Builder-level attribution

----

## Observability & Analytics

VybPass integrates PostHog for:
- Web analytics on user interactions
- Token purchase funnel tracking
- Queue submission behavior
- Agent execution metrics
- Settlement confirmation events
- Treasury inflow monitoring

This allows:
- Real-time visibility into compute cost vs. revenue
- Clear tracking of agent profitability
- Transparent performance metrics via a public dashboard

The public interface includes:
- Agent wallet balance
- Compute expenditure
- Escrow volume
- Settlement totals
- Transaction history
- Usage analytics

No authentication is required to view agent performance.

----

## Autonomy & Self-Sustaining Model

The agent operates with minimal human intervention:
- Reads deterministic queue state
- Executes time-bound logic
- Finalizes settlement autonomously
- Continuously processes new entries

Revenue is generated directly from live priority transactions.

Unlike speculative agent models, VybPass monetizes real-time economic activity in physical and digital environments. This provides a sustainable revenue stream tied to actual user demand.

----

## Novelty on Base

VybPass extends autonomous agents beyond financial trading or yield farming.

It introduces:
- Real-world execution primitives
- Time-based economic enforcement
- Escrow-backed priority markets
- Autonomous settlement tied to physical outcomes

By combining deterministic smart contracts, ERC-8021 builder codes, and full-stack analytics via PostHog, VybPass demonstrates a measurable, self-sustaining autonomous agent operating on Base.

**The problem it solves**

## The Crisis No One Is Watching

Every year, disease outbreaks kill **millions** of people - not because we lack 
medicine, but because we find out too late.

The World Bank estimates **5 million people** in rural communities die annually 
from treatable conditions due to delayed detection. **50% of the world** lacks 
access to essential healthcare. In low-resource clinical settings across the 
Global South, triage is done on paper. Patient data lives in notebooks that 
never leave the clinic. Public health authorities have no real-time signal. 
By the time a regional outbreak is confirmed, it has already spread across 
borders.

The existing tools fail in *three ways*:

**1. No edge-level intelligence.** Patients in remote clinics are assessed 
by overstretched staff with no decision support. Misdiagnosis is common. 
Early warning signals are lost.

**2. No privacy-preserving data sharing.** Sharing patient data across 
institutions requires trusting a central intermediary - which creates 
liability, HIPAA/GDPR risk, and in authoritarian contexts, real danger 
to patients.

**3. No tamper-proof audit trail.** Aid organizations and governments 
can't verify that reported health data hasn't been manipulated - making 
resource allocation decisions unreliable.


## What Beet Does

**Beet** is a decentralized public health triage infrastructure built for 
the edge.

Imagine a patient walks into a clinic in Lagos, Nairobi, or Dhaka. They're handed 
a small device - a **Beet node** (ESP32 microcontroller). They answer a couple of yes/no symptom questions. 

In *under 60 seconds*, Beet:

- Runs a **local weighted inference engine** (no cloud, no ML model, no 
  data leak) to produce a diagnosis and confidence score
- Computes a **SHA-256 hash** of the symptom bitmask - raw symptoms never 
  leave the device
- Posts the session to a **DAML smart contract on Canton Network** - where 
  the clinic, patient, and public health authority each see *only* what they 
  are entitled to see, enforced at the protocol level
- **Anchors the record hash** on the ADI Chain - creating a tamper-proof, 
  publicly verifiable integrity proof without storing any PHI on-chain

The result: a global health surveillance network where **privacy is not a 
policy promise - it's a cryptographic guarantee.**

**Who uses it:**
- **Clinics** - submit and manage triage sessions, track patient load- **Governments/Gov Orgs** - allocate emergency resources based on verified, tamper-proof epidemiological data
- **Public Health Authorities / NGOs -** monitor real-time outbreak signals, 
  trigger escalation protocols
- **Researchers** - audit record integrity via on-chain hashes without ever 
  seeing patient data

**Challenges we ran into**

## We Were New to Blockchain. Here's What Broke (And How We Fixed It.)


### 1. Our LCD Screen Died at ETHDenver

We had everything working on our hardware setup back home - ESP32 with a 
16x2 I2C LCD screen for the patient questionnaire interface. We got to 
Denver and the LCD stopped responding entirely. No backups, no replacement 
hardware on hand.

**Fix:** We improvised with a smaller OLED screen we had spare. Different 
library, different resolution, different I2C address - but it gets the job 
done. The triage flow still works, the display is just more compact. 
Sometimes hackathon hardware just dies and you ship with what you have.

### 2. Learning DAML's Privacy Model From Scratch

Neither of us had written DAML before this hackathon. The Canton privacy 
model - signatories, observers, controllers, two-phase contract workflows - 
is conceptually elegant but has sharp edges. We hit compile errors back to 
back:

- `Archive` is a reserved keyword in DAML Prelude - had to rename our 
  choice to `Discard`
- `DA.Time` doesn't export `Time` as a named type - had to remove the import
- `daml-script` must be explicitly declared as a dependency in `daml.yaml`
- Party IDs reset on every sandbox restart, causing `UNKNOWN_SUBMITTERS` 
  errors until we built proper re-allocation into our workflow

**Fix:** Each error had a clear compiler message once we understood the mental 
model. The DAML compiler errors are actually very good - we just needed to 
learn the system.

### 3. Integrating Two Codebases Built Separately

Our team split up - one person built the ADI anchor service in Node.js/viem, 
the other built the Flask backend in Python. The ADI service expected a 
specific payload shape with keccak256 hashing. We had a placeholder REST 
API sending a completely different format, and the two had never talked to 
each other.

**Fix:** We read through `server.js`, reverse-engineered the exact payload 
schema from the `validate()` function and test JSON files, and rewrote our 
`anchor_to_adi()` function to match exactly. One curl later - a real 
blockchain tx hash came back.


### 4. API Compatibility - Every Python Library Was Wrong

Our first instinct was to use **dazl** (the Python gRPC client for DAML 
ledgers) to talk to Canton. We installed it, wired it up, and got:
```
UNIMPLEMENTED: com.daml.ledger.api.v1.PackageService/ListPackages
```

After digging through the Canton changelog, we found that Canton 3.x only 
supports Ledger API v2, but dazl v8.3.0 still calls v1 internally. We also 
tried the HTTP JSON API on port 7575 - every path returned 404. There was 
no Python client that worked out of the box.

**Fix:** We scrapped both approaches and drove Canton directly via 
`daml script` subprocess calls over gRPC. We wrote DAML Script helpers 
in `Scripts.daml` and had Flask invoke them via `subprocess.run()`, 
passing arguments through temp JSON files. Ugly, but battle-proven - and 
it worked.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

### On-Device Inference Engine (ESP32)

The core AI in Beet runs entirely on the microcontroller - with no cloud, no network call, and no data leaving the device.

We implemented a **weighted rule-based inference engine** that maps six binary symptom inputs (fever, cough, fatigue, stomach pain, shortness of breath, sore throat) to four candidate diagnoses (Flu, Cold, COVID, Strep) using a hand-tuned scoring matrix derived from clinical triage guidelines. The engine runs `argmax` over the scores to select the most likely diagnosis and normalizes the winning score against the theoretical maximum to produce a confidence value between 0 and 1.

This is intentionally lightweight - it runs in microseconds on a $3 chip 
with no GPU, no model weights, and no network dependency. The design 
philosophy is that edge inference must be **deterministic, auditable, and 
offline-capable.** A clinic with intermittent WiFi still gets a diagnosis. 
Only the result - and a hash of the inputs - ever leaves the device.

The symptom bitmask is SHA-256 hashed before transmission, meaning the raw symptom responses never reach the backend, the blockchain, or any external system. Privacy-preserving by design.

**Prosperia**

**Beet** is *infrastructure for communities failed by centralized health systems* - 
built on the cypherpunk principle that privacy is not a feature... it's a right.

**Privacy by design, not by policy.** Raw symptom data never leaves the edge device. On Canton, DAML's signatory/observer model means a public health authority literally cannot read a patient record without cryptographic  authorization - enforced at the protocol level, not by a terms of service. 
On ADI Chain, only the record hash is anchored. No PHI, ever.

**Public goods infrastructure.** Beet runs on $3 hardware with no internet required for triage - just WiFi to submit. Built for clinics that can't afford EHR software, for community health workers in informal settlements, for NGO field teams in disaster zones.

**Decentralized governance.** The Canton multi-party model maps directly to real-world health governance: clinics control their data, patients see their own records, and public health authorities only access aggregate signals unless a clinic explicitly escalates. Governance enforced in code, not in policy.

The cypherpunk vision was always that cryptography would protect individuals from institutional overreach. Beet applies that to one of the most vulnerable contexts imaginable: a sick person in a resource-constrained clinic, trusting that their data is safe.

**Best Privacy-Focused dApp Using Daml**

Beet is a healthcare records system with role-based access - one of the fitting use cases for Canton's privacy-first model. But we went beyond the textbook version and built it for the real world :)

**The DAML contract architecture:**

Beet implements a two-phase contract workflow:

1. `PendingDiagnosis` - created by the clinic alone. Only the clinic can see it. No patient or authority exposure until explicitly confirmed.

2. `DiagnosisRecord` - promoted from Pending via the `Confirm` choice. 
   Now the patient and `publicHealthAuth` become observers - but they can only see what they're supposed to: their own record, no one else's.

3. `EscalateToAuthority` - the clinic can trigger escalation, creating an `AgreementPending` contract that requires co-signing by the public health authority.

4. `JointRecord` - co-signed by both clinic AND publicHealthAuth. Used for outbreak-level events where joint governance is required.

**Privacy model in practice:**
- A patient cannot see another patient's record - Canton enforces this at the protocol level
- A public health authority can see DiagnosisRecords they're observing, but not PendingDiagnoses that haven't been confirmed
- The clinic is signatory on all contracts - they retain ultimate control
- Only the SHA-256 symptom hash is stored in the contract - raw symptoms never reach the ledger

**Why this matters:** This isn't simulated privacy. In Canton, a party that isn't a signatory or observer on a contract *cannot retrieve it* - even with full ledger access. The confidentiality guarantee is cryptographic, not just logical.

**Technical stack:**
- DAML SDK 3.4.11 on Canton sandbox (local, with DevNet path documented)
- `daml script` over gRPC for all ledger interactions (compatible with Canton 3.x Ledger API v2)
- Flask backend orchestrating ESP32 → Canton → ADI pipeline
- Next.js dashboard with live polling of Canton contract data
- 2-5 minute demo video showing full triage flow end-to-end
- Public GitHub repo with README covering setup, privacy model, 
  party roles, and demo instructions

**Open Project Submission**

**Beet** is a **DePIN network for public health data integrity** - and ADI Chain is its trust layer.

**DePIN fit:** Each Beet node (ESP32 device) is a physical sensor node in a decentralized health infrastructure network. Nodes generate structured, cryptographically verified health signals. The network produces measurable real-world output: tamper-proof epidemiological data that governments and NGOs can act on. This is DePIN applied to the most critical infrastructure of all... public health.

**Institutional use case:** WHO, USAID, Médecins Sans Frontières, and national health ministries all face the same problem: they cannot verify the integrity of health data reported from field clinics. Beet solves this 
by anchoring a keccak256 hash of every DiagnosisRecord to ADI Chain at the moment of creation. Any party can verify that a record hasn't been tampered with by recomputing the hash - without ever seeing the underlying patient data.

**ADI Chain as primary execution layer:** Every submission in Beet calls our ADI anchor service, which invokes the `anchor(bytes32 sessionIdHash, bytes32 payloadHash, uint64 submittedAt)` function on our deployed smart contract. The transaction is mined on ADI testnet and the `txHash` + `blockNumber` are returned and stored. This is not a sidechain or wrapper - ADI Chain *is* the integrity layer.

**Compliance and controls:** The DAML layer on Canton enforces role-based access at the contract level. The ADI layer provides public auditability without exposing PHI. This separation of concerns is exactly the architecture required for HIPAA/GDPR-compliant health infrastructure.

**Extensibility:** Beet is designed for institutional deployment at scale. The ESP32 node can be replaced with any HTTP-capable device. The Flask backend is stateless and horizontally scalable. The DAML contracts support 
escalation workflows (`EscalateToAuthority`, `JointRecord`) for multi-institution outbreak response. White-labeling for national health ministries requires only a UI theme change.

**Deployed and usable:** Smart contract deployed on ADI testnet (`0xd5006FC2dC1304d360085E95E7D88D5C15faA7e6`). Every submission produces a verifiable on-chain tx. Public GitHub repo with full setup documentation.

**The problem it solves**

Launching new markets in crypto can be complex, manual, and sometimes gated.

Today, creating a tokenized market can require:

- Smart contract development
- Oracle integration
- Liquidity bootstrapping
- Risk parameter configuration
- Frontend integration
- Ongoing management

At the same time, AI agents are becoming capable of reasoning and planning, but they lack native economic rails to autonomously deploy and operate financial infrastructure.

Atlas solves this through a new primitive, permissionless AI-launched markets. With Atlas:

- A user can describe an asset (including niche or emerging assets) that they want to trade in plain language
- An AI agent can verify data availability
- Deploy infrastructure
- Initialize liquidity
- And enable trading immediately

Once live, users can communicate with a secondary agent to:

- Buy or sell exposure via AMM
- Mint overcollateralized tokens
- Redeem exposure against oracle price
- Provide or remove liquidity

Atlas is built on Kite AI for both execution and settlement. It uses x402 micropayments to make the AI agents completely self-sustaining.

**Challenges we ran into**

Payment token didn’t support EIP-3009 — The testnet token we used had no transferWithAuthorization, so x402 settlement reverted. We added EIP-3009 to MockUSDC and used that for payments. With Kite Agent Passport, a supported token or flow could avoid this.
No facilitator for our network — We got “no facilitator registered” when trying to use an external service. We switched to direct settlement: the backend submits the signed EIP-3009 tx itself. With Agent Passport, we could sign once and let Kite handle submission and gas.
Negative payment amount — A negative agent fee led to a negative uint256 and revert. We clamp payment to ≥ 0 in the backend and set the fee input to min="0" in the UI.
Activity visibility — We wanted mints/redeems visible without scrolling. We added a Recent activity table above the Vault and persist it in localStorage per market.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Atlas operates through two self-sustaining AI agents that coordinate to create and manage tokenized markets on-chain.

1. Market Creation Agent

The Market Creation Agent is responsible for launching new markets. The flow is as follows

- A user describes an asset they want to trade
- The agent researches the asset using external APIs and data sources
- Identifies and validates a stable oracle-compatible pricing source
- Configures market parameters
- Deploys the AMM and vault contracts
- Initializes liquidity using user-provided capital

If no reliable pricing source is found, the agent aborts deployment. This process is executed on-chain and tied to an x402 micropayment.

2. Trading & Execution Agent

The Trading Agent enables users to interact with existing markets through conversation.

It has the ability to:

- Buy from the AMM pool
- Sell to the AMM pool
- Mint overcollateralized exposure
- Redeem exposure
- Add liquidity
- Remove liquidity

These actions are also executed on-chain and tied to an x402 micropayment.

If funds are insufficient or execution conditions fail, the agent returns a structured failure response.

Markets deployed by the Creation Agent are immediately accessible to the Trading Agent. Fees from swaps and minting flow into the vault treasury. Liquidations, mint fees, and swap fees plan to help sustain redemption arbitrage.

**New France Village**

Atlas introduces a new primitive: AI agents that can autonomously create and operate on-chain markets.

Users describe an asset they want to trade. An AI agent researches a data source, deploys an oracle-backed market with liquidity, and enables minting, redemption, and trading. A second AI agent executes buy, sell, mint, redeem, and liquidity actions via conversation.

All actions are powered by on-chain x402 micropayments through Kite AI and executed autonomously.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Atlas is an AI-native market infrastructure protocol built entirely on Kite AI, designed for AI agents to create, operate, and transact in tokenized markets.

It enables users to launch oracle-backed synthetic markets, trade exposure via AMMs, mint and redeem overcollateralized tokens, and manage liquidity through conversation with AI agents. This is all executed and settled on Kite using x402-powered micropayments.

**Alignment with Agent-Native Architecture Payments & Identity**

Atlas operates entirely through two text-prompted AI agents:

A Market Creation Agent
- Researches external APIs
- Validates pricing sources
- Deploys AMM + vault contracts
- Initializes liquidity
- Configures minting and redemption

A Trading & Execution Agent
- Buy from pool
- Sell to pool
- Mint exposure
- Redeem exposure
- Add liquidity
- Remove liquidity

Each agent action is authenticated, paid via x402, and logged and settled on Kite. The micropayments via x402 sustain both agents economically.

**Technical Execution on Kite AI**

Atlas is deployed on Kite as its primary execution and settlement layer.

All core primitives are native to Kite:

- x402 micropayments
- On-chain minting and redemption
- AMM swaps
- Treasury accounting

Atlas shows how Kite can power the agentic economy beyond API consumption through a primitive of permissionless listings

The platform demonstrates:
- Agent-to-protocol payments
- Agent-to-API authentication
- Paid execution per action
- Verifiable on-chain settlement
- Autonomous financial coordination
- Graceful failure handling for insufficient funds

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Last year, Decentralized Finance lost millions due to vulnerabilities and logic errors in smart contracts. Security reviews are slow and hard to act on. Teams wait weeks for audits, get long reports, and still have to turn findings into code changes themselves. There is no single path from “is this safe?” to “here is the fix.” You juggle scanners, auditors, and manual patching instead of one pipeline that finds, explains, and fixes. While developers are increasingly using Web2 AI models such as Anthropic or OpenAI to review their contracts, these models operate as a "black box" with little transparency and verifiability with code changes.

DeFi cannot scale safely without better tooling. Contracts move real value, and teams need fast, clear, reliable audits and fixes so they can ship with confidence. Prophet is built for that: one pipeline with transparency and efficiency so security becomes part of the flow, not a bottleneck.

**Challenges we ran into**

One big hurdle was getting reliable, structured output from the AI. The analyzer and fix generator need JSON and raw Solidity, not markdown or chat. We had to design prompts and response handling so the model returns something we can parse every time (e.g. strict schema, stripping code fences, validating pragma). Another challenge was the fix-review UX. Showing an AI-generated patch in a way that’s clear and stable (diff view, accept/reject, no cursor jumps or accidental overwrites) took several iterations; we simplified to a read-only diff and a single source of truth so the UI doesn’t fight the user. Integrating 0G inference into the agent (calls, error handling, and fitting it into the existing analyze -> report -> fix flow) also required some iteration so the pipeline stays fast and the frontend stays in sync.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Prophet uses AI through a Zero Gravity agent in three places:

When you click Run Analysis, the agent sends your contract to 0G for inference. The model acts as a security auditor and returns a structured report: risk score, findings with locations and explanations. That output is parsed and shown in the UI so you can see what’s wrong and where.

When Generate Test Cases is clicked, the agent goes through all potential transactions that could put the contract in a vulnerable position and creates test cases to test the contract on through reinforcement learning.

When you click Generate Fix, the agent runs a second AI step with your code and the report. The model returns patched Solidity. The agent cleans the response and the UI shows a diff. You review and Accept or Reject. The AI suggests; you decide.
So one flow: analyze with 0G, get the report, create test cases, run them in Dockerized Foundry, generate fixes with AI, then you approve or reject. The AI steps work together and the user always has the final say.

**New France Village**

Prophet fits New France Village because the future of finance on Ethereum needs safe, auditable smart contracts. DeFi, RealFi, RWA, and treasury protocols run on code that holds real value. Prophet gives teams one pipeline to audit contracts, see clear findings, get suggested fixes, and optionally fuzz and deploy. That supports compliance and regulators who want proof of what was reviewed and fixed. For institutions and exchanges, security tooling has to be reliable and explainable. Prophet is built to be accurate, transparent, and reliable so teams can ship with confidence and onchain finance can scale.

**Best DeFAI Application**

Prophet fits Best DeFAI because it uses AI to improve a core DeFi workflow: securing smart contracts. You paste a contract and get a 0G-powered audit with a risk score, clear findings, and a suggested fix. The AI gives structured output you can act on, and you stay in control by reviewing and choosing to accept or reject the patch. Fuzzing works like a simulation step before deploy. That’s AI meaningfully improving a DeFi workflow with explainability and user control.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

Prophet fits this track because it uses 0G for real inference in a full workflow. You paste a contract and 0G runs the analysis. The model returns structured findings, test cases, and a suggested fix, and that drives the app: you see the report, review the patch, and accept or reject it. So 0G powers the AI step, and the output leads to real actions in the product.

### Clean Slate Agent
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/clean-slate-agent-c8e5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/anitasrinivasan/clean-slate-agent) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/WDeBhuHgBMs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Free legal aid to clear your record

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Nearly 1 in 3 American adults has a criminal record. Most are eligible for some form of expungement or record sealing — but the legal system is expensive, confusing, and intimidating. Clean Slate Agent removes those barriers.

**For individuals:** Talk to the agent in plain language about your situation. It assesses your eligibility based on the expungement laws of your state, covering 10 states with different rules, terminology, and waiting periods. You can upload a photo of your RAP sheet and the agent reads it. If you're eligible, you receive a privacy-preserving credential — a proof that you can share with employers without revealing any details about your record.

**For employers:** Verify a candidate's eligibility using only a credential ID. You receive a single answer: eligible or not eligible. You never see the offense type, conviction date, or any underlying record detail. This is what Ban the Box laws intended — and what cryptographic privacy now makes enforceable.

**The privacy guarantee is structural, not policy.** Canton Network's sub-transaction privacy ensures that employers *cannot* see redacted fields — they are cryptographically invisible, not just hidden by the application. The agent operates its own wallet on Base, funded by employer verification micropayments, so individual help is always free.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Canton's Daml type system vs. real-world data.** The Daml `Date` type requires strict YYYY-MM-DD format, but people describe dates loosely — "back in 2019" or "a few years ago." The AI extraction would return `convictionDate: "2019"` and Canton would reject the contract creation with a cryptic `spray.json.DeserializationException`. We had to build a date normalization layer that gracefully converts partial dates into valid Daml values while preserving accuracy.

**Privacy architecture contradictions.** Our first employer flow had employers *typing in* the offense details themselves to get an assessment — which completely defeated the purpose of Canton's privacy layer. We had to rethink the entire flow: the individual now receives a credential ID in the chat, shares it with the employer, and the employer verifies using only that ID. They never input or see any record details. This was the hardest design problem — making sure the privacy guarantee held end-to-end, not just at the ledger layer.

**Consuming vs. nonconsuming Daml choices.** Our initial `VerifyEligibility` choice was consuming, meaning it archived the credential contract after a single employer checked it. A credential that can only be verified once is useless. We had to add the `nonconsuming` keyword, rebuild the DAR, and redeploy — a small code change but a fundamental correctness issue.

**LLM output parsing.** Claude would intermittently wrap JSON responses in markdown code fences (```json ... ```), causing `JSON.parse()` to fail silently and break the case extraction pipeline. We built a `parseLLMJson()` helper to strip formatting, but the deeper lesson was that every LLM output boundary needs defensive parsing.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Claude (Anthropic) is the core intelligence layer. It serves three distinct roles within the system:

**1. Conversational Legal Aid Agent**
The primary interface is a chat powered by Claude claude-sonnet-4-20250514. A dynamic system prompt is built at runtime from a structured JSON knowledge base containing the expungement rules, statutes, waiting periods, and exclusions for 10 U.S. states. When the user mentions a state, the prompt narrows to only that state's rules. The agent guides the user through questions about their offense, timing, and sentence status, then makes an eligibility determination. That determination is the trigger — the backend automatically creates a Canton Network credential when the agent says "eligible."

**2. Document Analysis (Claude Vision)**
Users can upload a photo of their RAP sheet (criminal record summary). The image is sent to Claude as a base64 content block alongside instructions to extract offense types, charge codes, dates, dispositions, and sentence details. The agent confirms what it found before assessing eligibility, since RAP sheets are often hard to read.

**3. Structured Data Extraction**
Every chat exchange runs through a second Claude call with a dedicated extraction prompt. This silently parses the conversation into structured JSON — state, offense type, conviction date, sentence status, eligibility determination — which the backend uses to create Canton credentials and populate the case file. This extraction runs in parallel with the user-facing response.

**How the AI connects to the broader system:**
- Claude determines eligibility → backend creates a Daml credential on Canton Network
- Canton credential gives the individual a credential ID → shareable with employers
- Employer verifies credential via x402 micropayment → receives only "eligible" or "not eligible"
- Agent logs activity to its smart wallet on Base Sepolia

The AI never sees or stores the credential itself. It makes a determination; the cryptographic and economic layers handle the rest.

**Prosperia**

**Privacy as a cypherpunk value.** The entire architecture is built around the principle that people shouldn't have to sacrifice their privacy to prove they deserve a second chance. Canton Network's sub-transaction privacy means employers cryptographically cannot see the underlying record — not through access control, but through the ledger's design itself. This is cypherpunk infrastructure applied to a real civil liberties problem.

**Regenerative finance in practice.** The agent is self-sustaining through x402 micropayments — employers pay $0.10 USDC per verification, which funds free service for individuals. No VC funding, no ads, no data monetization. Revenue flows from those with resources (employers) to subsidize access for those without (people with records). That's regenerative economics, not extractive.

**Public goods for an underserved community.** 70M+ Americans have criminal records. 93% of those eligible for expungement never get it — because attorneys cost $1K-$5K and the process is opaque. Clean Slate Agent makes the first step free and accessible 24/7. It's a public good that uses decentralized technology to remove a barrier that disproportionately affects low-income and minority communities.

**Collective action and reimagining prosperity.** The project directly addresses how old records lock people out of jobs, housing, and economic participation. By combining AI (Claude for legal assessment), privacy infrastructure (Canton), self-sustaining payments (x402 on Base), and cryptographic credentials, it creates a system where technology empowers individuals rather than surveilling them — which is exactly what "reimagining prosperity for all" means.

**TL;DR:** Clean Slate Agent embodies Prosperia's values by using privacy-first blockchain infrastructure (Canton sub-transaction privacy) and regenerative micropayment economics (x402) to make criminal record expungement accessible to the 70M+ Americans locked out of opportunity — free for individuals, self-sustaining through employer fees, with no data extraction or surveillance.

**Best Privacy-Focused dApp Using Daml**

Clean Slate Agent uses a Daml smart contract (CleanSlate.daml) on Canton to create privacy-preserving expungement credentials. The core privacy problem: when someone clears their criminal record, proving eligibility to an employer currently requires disclosing the very details the law intended to protect. Canton's sub-transaction privacy solves this structurally. The ExpungementCredential template has signatories (individual + agent) who see all fields — offense type, conviction date, sentence status — and an observer (employer) who can only exercise the nonconsuming VerifyEligibility choice, which returns a single string: "eligible" or "not_eligible." The employer's Canton node literally cannot see the redacted fields. This is not application-level access control — it's a cryptographic property of the ledger. The individual can also revoke the credential at any time. The app includes a Canton Privacy Inspector that demonstrates the difference side-by-side: what the agent sees vs. what the employer sees.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

Clean Slate Agent operates a smart wallet on Base Sepolia (CleanSlateAgent.sol) that implements an autonomous economic model. Individuals receive free legal aid — the agent assesses expungement eligibility, creates privacy-preserving credentials, and guides people through the process at no cost. Employers pay micropayments (via x402/USDC on Base Sepolia) to verify credentials. Revenue from employer verifications funds the agent's operating costs (Claude API calls, on-chain logging). The smart wallet tracks individuals helped, employer assessments, total revenue, and total expenses on-chain, providing full transparency. This creates a self-sustaining public-interest agent: no donations, no grants, no data monetization — just a B2B revenue stream that subsidizes a free public service.

### meatLayer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meatlayer-9542) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/amanshah0729/meatLayer) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://meat-layer.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1166959889?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Human Orchestration Layer for AI

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Right now the limiting factor behind long and complex AI tasks is trust - AI can do 90 percent of tasks but that 10% failure case is why we can't trust it to autonomously transact money, make purchases, or deal with private information. We don't need models, we just need a reliable fallback layer.

So we built a human orchestration layer for AI agents. AI can call our /human-task API for small micro tasks whenever it has a low confidence score. It's different than other platforms in the space because these are for $0.1, 10-second microtasks that autonomous agents can call on humans for as opposed to the hour/day long tasks that current platforms typically offer. 

Think of it like Uber... the AI is like the consumer that will flash up tasks onto the dashboard and the humans are like uber drivers that can accept tasks in high frequency.

**Challenges we ran into**

Verification that humans accurately do the task. But then we decided to gamify these microtasks by giving out trophies so that humans who accurately do tasks for a longer period of time get paid more per task. It's just like having a 5-star rating as an uber driver.
Also had issues with NFT implementation since it was my first time doing so. I spent an hour on discord with someone who was posing as part of the 0g team but was actually a scammer haha.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Our primary project is an iNFT - an Agent that lives on chain as an NFT. Because these tasks are highly specialized (voting bots, trading bots, messaging bots, etc) there is a lot of parameters in terms of system prompts that they do. Having each bot be an NFT means you can transfer your agent to someone else doing a similar task. Agents can even build preferences as to which humans they work with!

**ETHERSPACE**

Our project is heavily NFT based, specifically inft based. We're giving AI agents their own identity by minting each agent on our platform an iNFT, which they can then use to go and hire humans for microtasks whenever AI is unconfident about a task. 
Our platform is similar to uber where humans can accept these microtasks and get paid on-chain.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

We built a platform for agents to call our /human-task API to get help from humans on tasks whenever it has a low confidence score. But each AI can have it's own personal preferences regarding which humans it works with, which tasks it works on, how often it calls for human help, etc! We save that information in 0g storage and mint an iNFT

**Governance UX & Community Tooling**

The primary use case that we've implemented is having agents vote on dao governance. This has been thought of before but the key component we bring is the human fallback layer that the AI can call our /human-task API if it ever has low confidence. This significantly increases the viability of this kind of solution.
