### ZeroBridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zerobridge-9bbf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/uncletom29/zerobridge) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/xerobridge) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/007a72a94bad4eba8d5617282c5ae3a5) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Privacy Layer for Cross-Chain Liquidity

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Current blockchain bridges expose everything: your transaction amounts, wallet addresses, trading strategies, and holdings across all chains. Front-runners exploit this transparency, competitors copy your DeFi strategies, and your financial privacy is completely compromised. If you bridge 100 NEAR from Near to Solana, everyone can link your addresses, see your capital, and track your every move.

ZeroBridge solves this by routing all cross-chain transfers through Zcash's Orchard shielded pool, creating a privacy layer that breaks transaction graphs. When you bridge assets, they enter Zcash as encrypted notes that hide amounts, senders, and recipients. When you withdraw to the destination chain, zero-knowledge proofs verify ownership without revealing which deposit you're claiming. The result: your NEAR address and Solana address remain completely unlinkable, with no on-chain connection between them.

**What You Can Do With ZeroBridge:**

- Private DeFi Across Chains - Deploy capital from Zcash to fresh addresses on any chain. Provide liquidity on PropellerSwap, AVNU, lend on Rhea Finance, or trade on Jupiter without revealing your total portfolio size or linking positions together. Each interaction appears as an independent user.

- Protected Trading Strategies - Execute high-frequency trading or arbitrage without competitors tracking your moves. Fund bots from Zcash shielded pool to new addresses, run strategies at scale, aggregate profits privately. Front-runners can't target you because they can't see your capital or patterns.

- Anonymous NFT Purchases - Buy NFTs without revealing your wallet's wealth. Bridge from Zcash to a fresh address with just enough funds, make your purchase, then bridge remaining balance back through a different route. The seller never sees your holdings.

- Private Cross-Border Payments - Send value globally without surveillance. Bridge USDC from Solana through Zcash to NEAR in one flow—recipient gets funds from a fresh address with zero connection to your source wallet.

- Institutional Privacy - Institutions can deploy capital across DeFi protocols without revealing their strategies or total AUM. Each position looks like a small independent player.

- Making Privacy Accessible - No need to understand Zcash wallets or manage shielded addresses manually. Bridge in one transaction from any supported chain (Ethereum, StarkNet, Solana, NEAR, Mina, Osmosis), and ZeroBridge handles all Zcash shielded pool interactions automatically.

The system achieves true unlinkability - even if someone knows you deposited 100 OSMO, when you withdraw 50 SOL later, they cannot prove the connection. Your withdrawal could correspond to ANY previous deposit in the entire history of the bridge, creating an anonymity set of thousands of transactions.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1: Two-Step Withdrawal Pattern Discovery**
My first implementation had users call a single withdraw() function with their proof. Relayers would listen, verify nothing, and immediately execute, creating a race condition where multiple relayers would waste gas attempting the same withdrawal. I initially tried complex P2P locking mechanisms, but they added fragility.
**Solution: Split withdrawals into two on-chain steps: requestWithdrawal() and executeWithdrawal(). **
Users submit proofs in step 1, which emits an event. The coordinator verifies the proof off-chain and, if valid, generates an authorization signature stored in its database. Relayers query this database for authorized withdrawals (not blockchain events), claim tasks via P2P gossip, then execute with the coordinator's signature. This eliminated race conditions, gave the coordinator time to verify proofs properly, and created a clean separation: users don't need to wait for verification (step 1 is instant), and relayers only execute pre-approved transactions. The pattern proved so elegant it became the standard across all eight gateway implementations.

**Challenge 2: Cross-Chain Token Canonical Naming Nightmare**
Different chains call the same token different things: USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v on Solana, usdc.token.near on NEAR. Managing mappings manually in each gateway contract would be unmaintainable and error-prone.
**Solution: Built a centralized token registry with canonical token IDs in the coordinator.** 
Each token gets a hash-based ID (e.g., sha256("USDC") -> 0x1f3a...) with a table mapping canonical IDs to chain-specific addresses. When processing deposits, the coordinator looks up the canonical token and ensures sufficient liquidity of the equivalent token exists on the destination chain before creating the Zcash note. This registry lives in a TOML config file (tokens.toml) that can be updated without redeploying contracts. Added benefit: the coordinator can automatically handle token decimals conversions

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZeroBridge gateways inherit from AxelarExecutable, making them Axelar-aware smart contracts. When an Axelar message arrives (via _execute()), the gateway processes it as a ZeroBridge deposit, creating a Zcash note. The coordinator then coordinates with Axelar's validators to ensure the destination chain receives funds from an unlinkable address. This creates a hybrid system: Axelar's cross-chain messaging for reliability and speed, ZeroBridge's Zcash layer for privacy.

ZeroBridge adds the missing privacy layer: instead of sending value directly through Axelar GMP, route it through Zcash first. A user on Polygon deposits to ZeroBridge → Zcash shielded pool → Axelar notifies destination chain → ZeroBridge withdraws to fresh address. The Axelar network handles the cross-chain communication (fast, reliable), while ZeroBridge handles privacy (unlinkable addresses).

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

ZeroBridge's core contribution is cross-chain privacy, our architecture demonstrates best practices for onboarding transparent users to shielded Zcash. When a user bridges from Ethereum (a transparent ecosystem), ZeroBridge's coordinator immediately creates an Orchard shielded output—never touching transparent Zcash addresses. This "shielded by default" design teaches developers the right pattern: treat Zcash as shielded-only, using transparent addresses solely for exchange compatibility when absolutely necessary.

The ZeroBridge coordinator's Rust implementation directly integrates orchard, zcash-primitives, and halo2_proofs crates, the official Zcash libraries. Developers studying ZeroBridge's codebase see production examples of: creating Orchard notes with proper randomness, managing commitment trees using incrementalmerkletree, deriving nullifiers correctly, handling spending keys securely, and constructing shielded transactions that pass Zcash consensus rules.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZeroBridge includes a production-ready Osmosis gateway written in CosmWasm with full support for native OSMO deposits (via Bank module) and CW20 token transfers. The contract uses Osmosis's native features: querying balances through bank queries, transferring tokens via BankMsg::Send, and integrating with Osmosis's gas mechanics. Depositing OSMO to the shielded pool requires just sending native tokens to the gateway contract address, no token approvals or wrapper contracts needed.

ZeroBridge solves a critical problem for Osmosis LPs: position transparency. Concentrated liquidity pools reveal LP ranges, allowing competitors to front-run rebalancing and copy profitable strategies. With ZeroBridge, LPs can deploy capital from Zcash to fresh Osmosis addresses, provide liquidity across multiple pools (each appearing as an independent small LP), and withdraw yields back through Zcash privately. This makes Osmosis competitive with centralized exchanges for institutional LPs who require strategy confidentiality.

Osmosis is the liquidity hub of Cosmos, integrating ZeroBridge means every IBC-connected chain gains privacy capabilities. A user on Cosmos Hub could bridge through Osmosis via ZeroBridge to Zcash, then withdraw to any other Cosmos zone privately. Future IBC integration could wrap ZeroBridge authorizations in IBC packets, enabling native cross-zone privacy. This positions Osmosis as the privacy gateway for the entire Cosmos ecosystem, 40+ chains gaining privacy-preserving cross-chain transfers through a single Osmosis integration.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZeroBridge implements a complete Solana gateway using the Anchor framework, supporting both SOL and SPL token deposits through token-2022 interface compatibility. The program uses PDAs (Program Derived Addresses) for secure vault management, enabling the gateway to custody tokens without centralized control. Deposits emit events via Solana's log system that Helius indexers can efficiently monitor, providing reliable event detection even during network congestion. Withdrawals use cross-program invocations (CPIs) to transfer from the gateway's vault accounts using PDA signatures.

Solana's 50,000 TPS combined with Zcash's privacy creates unprecedented capabilities: high-frequency MEV-protected trading where bots funded from Zcash execute thousands of trades per second without revealing capital size or strategy patterns. Private NFT marketplaces where collectors can make offers without exposing wallet wealth. Anonymous gaming where in-game asset purchases can't be traced to a player's main wallet. The low fees (≈$0.002 per transaction) make privacy practical even for small transactions, unlike Ethereum where gas costs often exceed the privacy benefit for amounts under $1000.

Solana's event system requires robust indexing due to high throughput and potential state replication lag. ZeroBridge relayers use Helius RPC endpoints for reliable event streaming, ensuring deposits and withdrawal requests are detected even during network upgrades or validator transitions. Helius's enhanced APIs provide historical event lookup for relayers joining the network (catch-up sync) and webhook support for real-time deposit notifications.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

ZeroBridge provides the foundational infrastructure that makes private DeFi practical: Instead of building a new private DEX from scratch, existing DEXs become privacy-preserving by routing capital through ZeroBridge. Users deposit from Zcash to fresh addresses with no history, trade on Uniswap/Jupiter/Ref, then withdraw profits through Zcash to new addresses. This "privacy wrapper" approach means every DeFi protocol across multiple chains becomes privacy-enabled without protocol modifications, instant composability with the entire DeFi ecosystem. 

MEV is a $1B+ problem because transparent blockchains let front-runners see pending transactions and extract value. ZeroBridge mitigates this: large traders deploy capital from Zcash across multiple fresh addresses, execute strategies that appear like independent small traders, and aggregate profits privately. Front-runners can't target you because they can't identify your transactions or capital size. This enables "dark pool" style privacy on public blockchains, institutional traders get the liquidity and composability of DEXs with the privacy protections of traditional finance.

ZeroBridge's codebase demonstrates production patterns for Zcash integration: using orchard crate for Orchard pool operations, managing commitment trees with incrementalmerkletree, generating Halo2 proofs with halo2_proofs, and constructing valid Zcash transactions with zcash-primitives. The coordinator implementation shows how to build reliable, secure services on top of Zcash, handling edge cases like merkle tree reorgs, nullifier deduplication, and mempool transaction tracking. Developers building their own Zcash-integrated applications can study ZeroBridge as a reference for production-quality integrations that actually work reliably.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solution**

ZeroBridge enables structured private payment flows: businesses can receive payments from customers globally without revealing their total revenue or customer list. Each customer bridges payment through Zcash to a fresh merchant address, the merchant sees individual payments but customers remain unlinkable to each other. Similarly, payroll or vendor payments can be issued from Zcash to unlinkable recipient addresses, keeping employee compensation and supplier relationships private.

Traditional cross-border payments reveal sender and recipient identities, amounts, and timing to multiple intermediaries (banks, payment processors, compliance systems). ZeroBridge provides censorship-resistant private payments: remittances can flow from any supported source chain through Zcash to recipients on any destination chain. The sender and recipient addresses are cryptographically unlinkable, even if authorities monitor both chains, zero-knowledge proofs prevent linking deposits to withdrawals. This is particularly valuable for humanitarian aid, journalist protection, or privacy-conscious international commerce.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

ZeroBridge's architecture demonstrates patterns for privacy-preserving development frameworks: the coordinator can verify proofs submitted by anonymous contributors without knowing their identities, relayers coordinate via P2P gossip without revealing their stake amounts or earnings, and the token registry enables community-submitted token additions through pull requests without exposing submitter information. These patterns can be adapted for GitHub-style collaboration where contributors remain pseudonymous but their work is verifiably correct.

Developers building privacy applications often struggle with Zcash integration complexity, managing keys, generating proofs, tracking nullifiers, maintaining merkle trees. ZeroBridge's SDK abstracts this: developers call simple functions like bridge.deposit() and bridge.withdraw() without understanding Halo2 circuits or Orchard protocol internals. The testing framework provides mock Zcash nodes and coordinators for local development, eliminating the need to run a full Zcash node during iteration. Documentation includes step-by-step guides for common patterns: private voting systems, anonymous credentials, confidential data marketplaces, each showing how to leverage ZeroBridge's infrastructure for new privacy-preserving applications.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZeroBridge implements a production-ready NEAR gateway contract in Rust that handles both NEAR native token deposits and NEP-141 token standard transfers. The gateway uses NEAR's Promise-based architecture for asynchronous cross-contract calls and stores encrypted bridge metadata in transaction memos. Users can deposit from NEAR to the shielded pool via zerobridge-gateway.testnet::deposit() with just their NEAR account ID and Zcash shielded address—no knowledge of Zcash internals required.

ZeroBridge's architecture enables intent-like patterns: users express desired outcomes ("I want 100 USDC on Ethereum privately") and the coordinator + relayer network orchestrates the multi-chain execution through Zcash. The framework supports intent integration where NEAR users could declare "Lend my ZEC on Aave" and the system would bridge from NEAR through Zcash to Ethereum, deposit to Aave from a fresh address, then return yields through the shielded pool. This privacy-preserving intent execution is exactly what NEAR's DeFi ecosystem needs to compete with transparent chains while maintaining user privacy.

**The problem it solves**

# ZIntents - A Self-hosted, Privacy-First  Automated Trading for ZEC, powered by NEAR Intents

### ⭐ Demo: https://zintents.sctuts.com/

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9fbb13ac9a8745688423310675c23fda/b184aa47-ec8c-4746-b998-1a1e61db0cd3.png)

## The Problem It Solves

### 🔒 True Privacy for Zcash Users

While Zcash offers shielded transactions for privacy, most platforms and automation tools **completely compromise this privacy** by requiring you to:

- Share your IP, location, trading data... with centralized servers

- Trust third parties with your order history and strategies

- Expose wallet addresses and transaction patterns to platform operators

- Accept that your sensitive data may be logged, leaked, or sold

**The Problem**: You can't maintain Zcash's privacy guarantees when using traditional trading bots - they all require cloud services that track everything you do.



### 💼 What ZIntents Solves


**1. Privacy-Preserving Automated Trading**

- Execute limit orders for ZEC/NEAR based on multiple conditions, such as price, market cap, and BTC dominance... without exposing your strategy to anyone.

- All order data stays on YOUR machine, YOUR server - zero 3rd-party dependencies

- No third party can correlate your trades or build a profile of your activity

- Perfect for privacy-conscious traders who want automation without surveillance

**2. Secure Scheduled Withdrawals**

- Automate recurring withdrawals to Zcash shielded addresses

- Ideal for salary payments, DCA strategies, or regular privacy transfers

- Set-and-forget automation that respects transaction privacy

- No manual intervention needed - your bot handles everything 24/7

**3. Cross-Chain Trading Without Bridges**

- Powered by NEAR-Intents for trustless cross-chain swaps

- Trade ZEC ↔ NEAR without wrapped tokens or centralized bridges

- No custody risk - your funds never leave your control during trades

**4. Self-Sovereignty**

- Run on your own infrastructure (laptop, PC, or home server)

- Your private keys never touch external servers

- Password-protect your instance with App Lock

- Open source - audit every line of code yourself

### 🎯 Who Benefits & How It Helps

**Who Benefits**
- Privacy advocates who want automated trading without surveillance
- Zcash users who need tools that respect shielded transactions
- Self-hosters who won’t trust centralized crypto services
- DeFi users seeking cross-chain automation without bridges
- Anyone who believes “not your keys, not your coins” extends to trading data and infrastructure

**Before ZIntents**
- Manual trades → missed opportunities
- Cloud/centralized bots → data tracked and stored
- Bridges → custody risk and hack surface

**After ZIntents**
- 24/7 local automation on your machine
- Data and keys never leave your device
- Trustless swaps via NEAR-Intents (no bridges)
- Telegram alerts without constant dashboard checking

  
I built ZIntents to be a tool you can download right now, run on your laptop or your own server , start using in 5 minutes. Not an impressive-looking tech demo that only PhDs will ever be able to use. Privacy shouldn't require a computer science degree. 

**Privacy isn't a feature - it's the foundation.** ZIntents proves you can have powerful trading automation without sacrificing your privacy or self-sovereignty for ZCash.

**Challenges we ran into**

After researching how to maximize user privacy, I found most solutions forced a trade-off between usability and features.

- Cloud-based tools: easy, but require trusting third parties with sensitive data and assets
- Complex self-hosting: private, but too hard for normal users
- Privacy tools: often lack automation (limit orders, scheduling, alerts)

The practical path was combining **NEAR-Intents** with a **containerized self-hosted setup**:

- NEAR Intents support cross-chain trading without bridges and accommodate all Zcash addresses, including transparent (t), encrypted (z), and unified (u) addresses for deposits and withdrawals!
- Maximum privacy - data and keys never leave the user’s machine
-  Easy setup - single `docker compose up`
-  Features rich - automated trading, privacy enhancement, scheduled withdrawals , Telegram alerts

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

Fully self-custodial and local-first: ZIntents auto-generates a NEAR-Intents wallet and keeps keys on user machine, surfaced in onboarding and setting with password lock, Manage balances and deposit addresses via NEAR Intents balance and schedule privacy-enhanced ZEC withdrawals.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZIntents leverages NEAR-Intents to privately connect Zcash with other ecosystems:
- Place conditional limit orders across ZEC, NEAR, and stablecoins using multiple signals (e.g., price targets, BTC dominance, market cap).
- Seamlessly swap between assets and then withdraw privately to Zcash.
- Enable ZEC holders to access DeFi primitives (e.g., stablecoin routes) while preserving privacy through NEAR Intents

**Private Payments & Transactions**

ZIntents automates private ZEC payouts via NEAR-Intents, with first-class support for Zcash shielded addresses (zs1, z, u):

- Execute conditional limit orders and automatically withdraw proceeds to Zcash shielded addresses.
- Schedule privacy-enhanced withdrawals with timing jitter and amount randomization to reduce linkage.
- Fully self-hosted, non-custodial flow: users control keys and execution end-to-end.

### Privacy is Normal
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/privacy-is-normal-d2f0) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/meichriks/status/1995812258295808471?s=46) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/a0d455fef13f425da21e0b7965e5edd9) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Some moments deserve privacy. Web3 does too

![Elevenlabs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Elevenlabs-333333?style=flat-square) ![SORA](https://img.shields.io/badge/SORA-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people don’t understand privacy technology because it’s usually explained in technical, abstract, or fear-based ways. This creates a major gap: privacy is essential, but it doesn’t feel personal.

The video solves this problem by reframing privacy as an everyday human instinct. Instead of focusing on jargon or threat models, it shows simple, relatable moments, reminding viewers that privacy is something they already practice and value.

By grounding privacy in human stories, the video removes the stigma, confusion, and complexity around privacy tech. It makes people emotionally understand why privacy matters, and therefore why privacy-preserving blockchains exist in the first place.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the primary challenges in producing this video was the limitation of the AI generation tools available. The scenes were created using Sora, which automatically adds visible watermarks to all generated clips.

Because these watermarks were extremely distracting and broke the cinematic immersion of the story, I had to use a third-party watermark removal tool to clean the footage. However, removing the watermarks introduced its own issues- especially blurring, distortion, and softness around edges, which slightly compromised the original video quality.

This forced a trade-off between:
	•	keeping high-quality visuals with watermarks, or
	•	removing watermarks at the expense of sharpness and detail.

Ultimately, I chose to prioritize viewer experience and narrative flow by removing the watermarks, even though it meant accepting some loss of resolution and clarity in certain scenes.

**Privacy-Focused Content & Media**

“Privacy Is Normal” is a cinematic short film that tells the story of privacy through the most powerful medium: everyday human moments. Rather than lecturing or explaining, the video shows how naturally and instinctively people protect their private space. These small, relatable stories build a universal truth: privacy is not secrecy, it’s dignity, control, safety, and freedom.

Lekan Yusuf

**The problem it solves**

# Introduction
The problem is that privacy features are inaccessible. This is the problem that drives our submission. We showcase at least several solutions that stem from the tooling built for this hackathon: (1.) A Starknet & Starknet confidential transfer integration into Zashi (using the Swift SDK we made for confidential transfers and proving) (2.) a privacy maxxing browser extension wallet and confidential transfer network explorer (using the Rust SDK we made for confidential operations and key-management to facilitate a Venmo UX that is privacy maxxing).

# What we built!
## Swift confidential transfer SDK (Starknet & Tongo) - "Ghost SDK"
Making privacy features manifest in existing products requires tooling specific to that product´s distribution. For integrating Starknet and Starknet confidential transfers into Zashi this requires at least a Swift SDK (it would also require a Kotlin SDK too!) to allow users to derive keys from the same Zashi mnemonic and construct zero knowledge proofs that prove their confidential operations meet the constraints of the confidential transfer Cairo verifiers.

This led to the development of the Swift confidential transfer SDK. Users can derive Starknet account contract address, deploy their OpenZeppelin account and also derive confidential asset addresses to send and receive from. The SDK also has a fast-enough prover; the largest proof (the transfer operation proof) is benchmarked at 1.8 seconds.

With this new confidential Starknet transfer wallet SDK we built a new layer in Zashi which allows Zashi users to create Starknet accounts and perform Starknet confidential transfers. Similarly, it also allows Starknet users access to Zcash while maintaining their ability to re-derive their Starknet account contract and associated Starknet confidential transfer accounts. Distribution of privacy features requires tools that facilitate it and easily manifest in products like Zashi, that´s why we built this SDK and integrated it into Zashi. You can see this work manifest in Zashi in the below image: 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a1e508ddfd3748248a73f0331f5cad6f/323ad2f6-8f66-4598-b1de-c93004c6e544.jpeg)2025-12-03 13.47.58.jpg

Current zashi demo video: https://www.loom.com/share/fafa1499a6ce458ba5b9d4507cbb

## Rust SDK for confidential Transfers: Can we do better than 1.8 second proving? Yes!
While working on the Swift SDK for confidential Starknet transfers, it became apparent that even a 1.8 second prover would not facilitate the best user experience. The last thing we need is to increase a user's cognitive load while accessing privacy features & if privacy is a right, we must do better. This is a secondary problem we solved: can we build a Rust SDK that has blazingly fast provers that eliminate any increase in an end-user's cognitive load? The answer is yes we can and this hackathon's Rust SDK achieves that with a >1,000x improvement in the largest prover's speed (from 1.8 seconds in Swift to ~2 milliseconds in Rust). The following benchmarks of the prover operations demonstrate this:

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a1e508ddfd3748248a73f0331f5cad6f/4407d216-d504-4e55-81de-ea2e366d421d.png)

## Venmo Style Browser Extension, Privacy Maxxing Wallet
While the Rust SDK is significantly more performant, it alone does not showcase how we can eliminate cognitive load for end users who require confidentiality. To showcase this for the hackathon, we added a crate to the Rust SDK that created WASM bindings such that the key management, zk-provers, and privacy maxing features can be put to good user in a browser extension.

From there, we built a browser extension wallet to showcase (1.) the speed of the new provers (albeit slightly slower in WASM than Rust but still >100x faster than Swift) and (2.) that a fantastic UX is possible in the style of Venmo peer-to-peer payments. This is shown better in the demo video but there are screenshots below too:

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a1e508ddfd3748248a73f0331f5cad6f/fe8ab04f-48d3-4592-8317-4c288692d4bc.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a1e508ddfd3748248a73f0331f5cad6f/8b591908-d5f9-4fbc-bddf-eb71dabb59fa.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a1e508ddfd3748248a73f0331f5cad6f/86090491-41d9-4e9c-b4d3-b7287ead2daa.png)


## Confidential Transfer Explorer!
Privacy-oriented solutions offer a new paradigm that is under-searched and under-productionised. Part of this is because we label these privacy protocols as "black boxes" when they really are not. Privacy protocols are rich in information, and they are demand as much focus as existing web3 applications. The easiest place to showcase this is with a privacy protocol explorer, which allows anyone to go study, touch, feel, and learn about that protocol. And that is why we built the confidential transfer explorer (which connects to the user's new extension wallet for personal views of the network!)

![Uploading image...]()

**Challenges we ran into**

This hackathon submission was driven by problem-solving. The flow of problem-solving looked something like this:

1. Can we build a Swift SDK that performs confidential transfers on Starknet? Yes.
2. Can we integrate this confidential Swift SDK into Zashi to integrate Zcash and Starknet confidential transfers into a single product? Yes.
3. Does the tooling we built allow for a good enough user experience? Almost. Can we do better? Yes.
4. Let's build a Rust SDK that satisfies the same set of feature requirements as the Swift SDK. Is it faster? Yes, >1,000x faster (from 1.8 seconds to 2 milliseconds).
5. Can we showcase how to build a good wallet that has no technical debt and not constrained by an existing user-flow and interaction design process? Yes, that is the browser extension wallet.
6. Can we let users see under the hood and understand what the protocol "looks" like? Yes, that is the confidential explorer.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

1.) Starknet in Zashi -- using the Confidential Swift SDK for confidential transfers & key management to add a new wallet layer to Zashi, which gives users access to Zcash and Starknet in the same mobile app.
2.) Confidential Swift SDK for Starknet confidential transfers 2.) Confidential Rust SDK for Starknet confidential transfers (>1000x faster than swift)
3.) WASM bindings for using the Rust Starknet confidential transfer provers in TypeScript

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Noir](https://img.shields.io/badge/Noir-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZumpFun: Privacy-Preserving Meme Coin Launchpad

 ZumpFun solves critical privacy and fairness issues in meme coin launches:

  Privacy Problems Solved:
  - Visible Trading Activity: On traditional platforms like Pump.fun, everyone can see who's buying, how much, and when—leading to front-running and whale manipulation. ZumpFun uses Noir ZK proofs with
  Pedersen commitments to hide contribution amounts completely.
  - Identity Exposure: Creators and early contributors are publicly linked to tokens, exposing them to doxxing and targeted attacks. ZumpFun enables anonymous contributions while proving eligibility via
  zero-knowledge Merkle proofs.
  - Whale Tracking: Large holders are easily identified and manipulated. ZumpFun's nullifier system prevents tracking of individual trading patterns.

 Use Cases:
  1. Launch tokens anonymously without revealing creator identity
  2. Contribute to launches privately - amount hidden via ZK commitments
  3. Fair price discovery via sigmoid bonding curve (same mechanics as Pump.fun)
  4. Automatic DEX graduation at 800M tokens → Ekubo AMM
  5. Selective disclosure - reveal only what you choose (e.g., prove you contributed $1000+ without showing exact amount)

Tech Stack: Cairo smart contracts + Noir circuits + Garaga on-chain verification on Ztarknet

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Noir's New map API Breaking 45+ Tests

  The biggest hurdle was Noir's transition from the old HashMap API to the new functional BTreeMap with map() method. Every circuit test failed because map no longer took a closure the same way.

  Solution: Rewrote all 45+ instances to use the new pattern:
  // Old (broken)
  let result = items.map(|x| transform(x));

  // New (working)
  let result = items.iter().map(transform).collect();

  2. Garaga Integration Complexity

  Garaga's on-chain verifier requires Ultra KZG Honk proofs with specific formatting. The Barretenberg prover output didn't match Garaga's expected input format initially.

  Solution: Used garaga gen --system ultra_kzg_honk to generate Cairo verifier code directly from our Noir circuits, ensuring compatibility.

  3. Ztarknet Devnet Connectivity

  The Ztarknet devnet at ztarknet-madara.d.karnot.xyz had intermittent connection issues and required specific Madara-compatible transaction formats.

  Solution: Created deployment scripts with retry logic and proper fee estimation for the Madara stack.

  4. Cairo 2.14 Migration

  Had to migrate from older Cairo syntax to Cairo 2.14's stricter type system, particularly around ByteArray and storage handling.

  Solution: Updated all contracts to use proper felt252 conversions and the new #[storage] macro syntax.

**General Bounty**

Privacy Infrastructure Contribution:

  Reusable ZK Primitives:
  - Pedersen commitments (same as Zcash shielded pool)
  - Nullifier system for double-spend prevention
  - Merkle proofs for anonymous set membership
  - All circuits chain-agnostic, portable to any ZK chain

  Cross-Chain Ready:
  - shield()/unshield() pattern compatible with Zcash bridge design
  - Commitment-based model mirrors Zcash note commitments
  - Shared cryptographic standards enable future interoperability

  Developer Tooling:
  - Open-source circuits others can build on
  - Reference implementation for Starknet privacy patterns
  - Complete documentation for privacy dApp development

  Educational Value:
  - Production examples of commitment schemes, range proofs, nullifiers
  - Cairo-Noir-Garaga integration workflow demonstrated
  - Lowers barrier for future privacy builders

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

1. Meme-Coin Launchpad on Ztarknet 

Full Pump.fun style launchpad with bonding curve, 800M supply, 0.3% fees, and AMM graduation at $66K threshold.

  Live: 0x016ce9383c9f6e75168dd61d0867159bee439038e7bdcd54a154245beac84f0c on Ztarknet Sepolia

  ---
  2. Trading Shielded 

  - buy() takes ZK payment proof + Pedersen commitment (not address)
  - sell() uses nullifiers to prevent double-spend without identity linkage
  - Events emit commitments, never user addresses

  ---
  3. Market-Making Shielded 

  - Sigmoid bonding curve for fair pricing
  - No visible order book - commitments replace balances
  - Hidden amounts prevent MEV/front-running

  ---
  4. Creator Identity Shielded 

  - Creators submit creator_commitment (ZK proof), not wallet address
  - Can prove ownership later via ZK proof for revenue claims

  ---
  5. Noir Contracts

  5 circuits, 26/26 tests passing:
  - contribution.nr - Hidden contribution amounts
  - eligibility.nr - Anonymous whitelist verification
  - allocation.nr - Fair distribution proofs
  - disclosure.nr - Selective attribute reveal
  - lib.nr - Pedersen, Merkle, nullifier utilities

  ---
  6. Garaga Integration

  All 4 contracts have garaga_verifier: ContractAddress storage. Verification hooks ready for Garaga verifier deployment. Proof system: Ultra KZG Honk.

![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![nestjs](https://img.shields.io/badge/nestjs-333333?style=flat-square) ![CDP](https://img.shields.io/badge/CDP-333333?style=flat-square) ![RSA-OAEP-256](https://img.shields.io/badge/RSA--OAEP--256-333333?style=flat-square) ![TLS Certificate Validation](https://img.shields.io/badge/TLS%20Certificate%20Validation-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Majority of stablecoin transactions start or end offchain. Onchain activity is easy to understand because of block explorers, but fiat transfers are a black box. There is no simple way to know if money was actually sent to the correct offchain account.

To solve this we built an SDK that verifies offchain bank transfers. It supports two modes. The first is a manual flow similar to zkP2P. The second is an automated AI flow where users place their login credentials in a secure config file and a headless browser handles the full verification process.

This unlocks real p2p payments from bank accounts across Africa where chargebacks are rare. It also enables OTC level volume for p2p transactions because banks support higher transfer limits.

**Challenges we ran into**

Playwright's securityDetails() doesn't expose the full certificate chain, making complete TLS attestation impossible.Slutions:  Compute fingerprint from available data (issuer, subject, validity, SAN list). Backend validates against known bank certificate database instead of requiring full chain.
The SDK and backend had to perfectly coordinate on the exact byte layout of the encrypted evidence payload. The combined buffer contains: [RSA-encrypted AES key] [IV (12 bytes)] [Auth tag (16 bytes)] [Encrypted data]. A single byte offset error would cause complete decryption failure with cryptic error messages.Solutions:  Made RSA key size configurable from metadata,  Added minimum size validation BEFORE attempting decryption and Explicit component extraction with clear offsets

**General Bounty**

We use cryptography and AI to automatically verify offchain bank transactions in p2p on/off ramps. The user provides credentials in a config file and a headless browser completes the verification flow.

# The Problem It Solves

##  Privacy Crisis in DeFi Lending

Current decentralized lending protocols like Aave, Compound, and Solend suffer from a critical flaw: **complete transparency of user positions**. While blockchain transparency is valuable for verification, it creates serious problems for users:

### 1. **Front-Running & MEV Exploitation**
- Liquidation bots monitor every position 24/7
- Large traders' positions are visible to competitors
- Vulnerable positions get targeted before users can react
- MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) bots extract billions annually from predictable transactions

### 2. **Privacy Violations**
- Anyone can see your exact collateral amounts
- Your debt levels are public knowledge
- Competitors track institutional positions
- Personal financial strategies are exposed
- Whale watchers follow and copy every move

### 3. **Institutional Barriers**
- Hedge funds can't use DeFi without revealing strategies
- Businesses avoid on-chain lending due to competitive intelligence risks
- High-net-worth individuals fear exposure and targeting
- The $50B+ DeFi lending market is inaccessible to privacy-conscious institutions

---

- **Avoid liquidation sniping** - Bots can't target your specific position

####  **For Institutional Users**

**Challenges we ran into**

**Major Technical Hurdle: Arcium MXE Cluster Not Initialized on Devnet**

**The Problem**

The biggest challenge I encountered was getting encrypted computations to run on Arcium's devnet. Our smart contract logic worked flawlessly for both withdraw and deposit instructions on devnet, but for the borrow instruction, We faced a major limitation.

**The Error**

Borrow transactions consistently failed at the queue_computation step with error **0x1772 (MxeKeysNotSet)**.

**What we suspected**

The devnet environment had no valid encryption key for the MPC network because:

- No Distributed Key Generation (DKG) ceremony had been completed
- The MXE public key was all zeros towards the end of the array
- Multiple devnet clusters exhibited the same issue (I tested offsets: **768109697**, **3726127828**, **1078779259**)

**Root Cause**

Arcium's MPC network requires active operator nodes to run a DKG ceremony. Without that ceremony, the MXE (Multi-party Execution) public key is never generated - meaning no encrypted computation can run.

**Debugging Process**

To confirm the source of the failure, We:

- Inspected MXE account data - confirmed empty/zeroed public keys
- Reproduced the failure on devnet
- Tested multiple cluster offsets - all had inactive operator nodes

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/145e9b011ada4df39cf5245f7bba6de3/2d83862c-e20b-4a09-882e-71a886662337.png)

Program logged: "AnchorError thrown in programs/arcium/src/instructions/computation.rs:147. Error Code: MxeKeysNotSet. Error Number: 6002. Error Message: The MXE keys are not set, i.e. not all the nodes of the MXE cluster agreed on the MXE keys."

The screenshot above is a failed borrow transaction on the solana explorer with transaction signature: 4B9AjmUWng9xXsMWuqL5XVggzQqDT9AsNFJjsXBNru2cL2bN1YN7RKGE68nh2MYFLtghsNfsBPW3ctr3j5eewKtP

**General Bounty**

### **Project Name:** Zkredit 
## (Private Lending, Public Trust)

### **What We Built:**
We built **Zkredit**, a fully functional lending protocol that solves DeFi’s biggest UX problem: **"Weaponized Transparency."**

On standard protocols (like Aave or Kamino), every time a user borrows money, they "dox" their financial health to the entire world. This leads to **predatory liquidation hunting, front-running, and copy-trading.**

We built a solution that offers the best of both worlds:
1.  **Privacy:** User balances and debt amounts are encrypted (hidden).
2.  **Trust:** The protocol’s solvency is mathematically verified on-chain.

### **Key Features Delivered**
* **Encrypted Deposits:** Users can deposit SOL/USDC, and the amounts are immediately encrypted into Arcium ciphertexts. The blockchain sees the *transaction*, but not the *value*.
* **Blind Health Factor Logic:** We implemented a Loan-to-Value (LTV) check that runs inside a secure enclave. The protocol asks, *"Is this user safe?"* and receives a verified `YES/NO` answer without ever seeing the raw debt numbers.
* **MEV-Resistant Liquidations:** By hiding the exact liquidation price, we stop bots from "sniping" users. Liquidations only happen when truly necessary, not when a predator manipulates the price to force a crash.
* **Live Devnet Interface:** A complete frontend where users can connect a wallet, deposit funds, and see their "Shielded" status.

### Why This Matters 
We didn't just build a privacy tool; we built the infrastructure for **Institutional DeFi**.
Hedge funds and businesses cannot use public DeFi because they can't reveal their balance sheets to competitors. **Zkredit** unlocks the next trillion dollars of liquidity by allowing big players to participate in DeFi yields without exposing their trade secrets.

### **Tech Stack**
* **Blockchain:** Solana (for speed and settlement).
* **Confidential Compute:** Arcium MPC Network (for encrypted state and logic).
* **Frontend:** Custom dashboard demonstrating "Selective Transparency" (User sees data; Public sees health).

"Zkredit is a confidential lending protocol that uses Arcium's Multi-Party Computation to allow users to borrow against collateral without revealing their net worth or liquidation thresholds to predatory bots."

**Private DeFi & Trading**

We made Zkredit for the Private Lending/Borrowing Track Powered by Arcium

Our project fits the Private Lending & Borrowing track by fundamentally shifting the lending architecture from a transparent ledger to a confidential computing model.

While traditional DeFi protocols force users to expose their entire financial position to prove solvency, we utilize Arcium’s encrypted state to decouple verification from visibility.

Specifically, we achieve this by:

**Encrypting Balances: **Debt amounts are stored as ciphertexts, ensuring that while the network validates the existence of funds, it remains blind to the magnitude of the positions.

**Private Health Checks:** We execute the Loan-to-Value (LTV) logic inside a secure enclave. The protocol blindly queries this encrypted state to receive a simple 'Safe/Unsafe' boolean flag, rather than exposing the raw Health Factor to the public.

**Preventing Predatory Liquidation: **By hiding the exact liquidation threshold, we protect borrowers from 'liquidation hunting' and MEV attacks, ensuring that solvency is enforced mathematically without sacrificing user privacy."

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

**Node Setup & Docker Configuration Hell**

The biggest hurdle was getting a working Zcash node running locally. I initially hit a wall with `zcashd` requiring very specific Docker configurations—the standard setup instructions weren't cutting it, and I spent hours debugging container networking and volume mounting issues.

**The Zebra Migration Confusion**

To make things worse, I came across documentation about Zcash's migration to Zebra and incorrectly assumed `zcashd` was being deprecated or wouldn't work for new projects. This sent me down a rabbit hole trying to integrate Zebra with my backend instead.

**Failed Zebra Integration Attempt**

I spent significant time trying to get Zebra working with my backend RPC calls, but kept running into compatibility issues and incomplete documentation for the specific RPC methods I needed for shielded transactions. Nothing was connecting properly.

**The Pivot That Worked**

Finally, I stepped back and realized `zcashd` was still fully supported. I:
- Created a proper Docker setup with the right configuration flags
- Switched my backend integration back to `zcashd` 
- Connected everything through RPC

**Voilà—it started working.** Sometimes the solution is going back to what you know works rather than chasing the shiny new thing. Lesson learned: validate migration timelines before abandoning working tools.

### Proof of Privacy
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/proof-of-privacy-b014) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/orekbaby/status/1996643995230056734?s=46) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/qMcL3Vsw4B4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Zcash Shields. Mina Verifies.

![Figma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Figma-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Privacy in blockchain is misunderstood — people know the buzzwords but not the cryptography. Many users still believe “private” means “invisible,” without understanding proofs, curves, or how verification works without revealing anything.

My project solves that problem by turning intimidating concepts like Pasta curves, recursion, Zcash shielded pools, and zk-proofs into simple, story-driven visuals.
It makes people understand why privacy is possible, how it works, and what happens when Zcash and Mina work together.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Translating complex cryptography into a human story
One of the biggest challenges was taking highly technical concepts—shielded Zcash transactions, recursive SNARKs, and Pasta curves—and translating them into a story that anyone can understand without losing accuracy. These systems are mathematically dense, so simplifying them while still keeping the explanation verifiable was difficult.
I solved this by building the narrative around Aisha, a relatable small-business owner, and showing how the technology helps her in real life. The human story became the bridge that carried the cryptography.

2. Showing how Zcash and Mina combine without overwhelming the viewer
Another challenge was visually expressing how Zcash’s privacy and Mina’s verifiable proofs fit together. They are two different technologies built by different ecosystems, and it’s easy to confuse viewers with too much terminology.
I overcame this by designing a minimalist visual system: clean shapes, warm colors, and simple diagrams that show what each component does before showing how they merge. This created a clear visual language that builds from privacy → proof → combination.

3. Ensuring technical accuracy while keeping the video engaging
Because both ecosystems care deeply about correctness, I needed the explanation to remain technically precise—especially around zero-knowledge proofs, shielded transactions, and recursive verification.
I solved this through careful iteration, verifying each step of the explanation (privacy → proof creation → proof compression → verification) and cross-checking it with real-world use cases. Then I wrapped that accuracy in story, pacing, and visuals that maintain viewer attention for the full 3.5 minutes.

**Privacy-Focused Content & Media**

My project fits this track by using visual storytelling to explain one of the most important shifts happening in blockchain: how Zcash’s privacy guarantees can combine with Mina’s tiny verifiable proofs to create systems where data stays hidden but trust remains measurable.
Instead of presenting cryptography through academic diagrams, I translate Pasta curves, shielded transactions, and recursive proofs into cinematic visuals and narrative-driven explanations. The content turns dense mathematics into something that feels emotional, intuitive, and accessible — exactly the goal of the Privacy-Focused Content & Media track.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Zblind is a privacy-preserving system for storing Zcash viewing keys in Nillion's Private Storage and enabling secure computations without revealing secrets.

## The Problem It Solves

### The Challenge

When you need to share access to your Zcash transaction data with third parties (tax services, auditors, analytics platforms, etc.), you face a critical dilemma:

- **Option 1**: Share your viewing key directly → **❌ Security Risk** - Once shared, you lose control and the key can be misused
- **Option 2**: Manually export and share transaction data → **❌ Time-consuming** - Requires constant manual work and doesn't scale
- **Option 3**: Don't share at all → **❌ Limited functionality** - Can't use valuable services that require transaction access

### The Solution

This project solves this by enabling **privacy-preserving access control**:

✅ **Store your viewing key securely** in Nillion's encrypted Private Storage  
✅ **Grant selective permissions** to third parties without exposing your key  
✅ **Maintain full control** - revoke access anytime  
✅ **Enable secure computations** - third parties can query/process your data without seeing secrets  
✅ **Meet compliance requirements** - share necessary data for audits/taxes while keeping keys private

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

| **Traditional Approach** | **With This System** | **Benefit** |
|-------------------------|---------------------|-------------|
| 🔴 Share viewing key directly | ✅ Grant execute permissions only | **Security**: Key never leaves secure environment |
| 🔴 Manual transaction exports | ✅ Automated queries via API | **Efficiency**: No manual work, real-time access |
| 🔴 One-time data dumps | ✅ Continuous, controlled access | **Flexibility**: Third parties get live data access |
| 🔴 No way to revoke access | ✅ Instant access revocation | **Control**: Full ownership of your data |
| 🔴 All-or-nothing sharing | ✅ Granular permissions (read/write/execute) | **Precision**: Share only what's needed |
| 🔴 Trust third parties with keys | ✅ Keys never exposed to third parties | **Privacy**: Zero-trust architecture |
| 🔴 Compliance requires key sharing | ✅ Compliance without key exposure | **Regulatory**: Meet requirements safely |

### Real-World Impact

**Before**: 
- ❌ Tax services require you to export and email transaction CSVs (security risk)
- ❌ Auditors need your viewing key to verify transactions (permanent exposure)
- ❌ Analytics services can't access your data without compromising privacy

**After**:
- ✅ Tax services query your transactions securely without seeing your key
- ✅ Auditors verify transactions with temporary, revocable access
- ✅ Analytics services provide insights while your key remains encrypted

Working on getting Zcash shielded transactions.

Built a privacy-preserving data and analytics platform using nilDB (Nillion private storage).

> Seamless transactions, zero footprints.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# 🧩 The Problem It Solves

Today, sending and receiving crypto privately—especially across chains—is still extremely difficult. Users face a fragmented, insecure, and non-private experience that prevents truly seamless payments. **Assura** solves this by collapsing multiple broken parts of the ecosystem into a single, private, user-friendly flow powered by ENS.

## ❌ Problem 1: No Privacy When Receiving Crypto

* If you share a normal EVM address, **your entire on-chain history becomes public**.
* Every future transaction becomes linkable.
* Your net worth, activity, and wallet relationships can be tracked in seconds.

**Assura solves this by giving every incoming payment a fresh stealth address** that is impossible to link back to your ENS name.

---

## ❌ Problem 2: Cross-Chain Receiving Is a Mess

Today, receivers must:

* Create addresses on each chain (Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, etc.)
* Share different addresses with different senders
* Manually bridge funds
* Pay gas on each network
* Keep track of where assets landed

**Assura gives you one ENS subdomain (`you.assuranet.eth`) that works across all supported chains.**
Funds arrive on the chain the sender chooses—*and Assura handles the rest automatically*.

---

## ❌ Problem 3: Bridging to Zcash Is Complicated and Manual

Zcash is private and powerful, but the process of receiving EVM assets and moving them into Zcash is:

* slow
* multi-step
* error-prone
* extremely technical

Users must:

1. Receive tokens on an EVM chain
2. Connect to a bridge
3. Approve tokens
4. Bridge
5. Wait
6. Manually claim
7. Transfer funds again

**Assura automates the entire flow.**
Funds sent to your ENS name → appear as Zcash in your wallet with zero user steps.

---

## ❌ Problem 4: ENS Resolution Is Public & Linkable

Sharing an ENS name usually leaks identity because:

* ENS resolves to a permanent 0x address
* Anyone can observe who pays you and how much
* Anyone can track your activity instantly

**Assura uses a TEE-powered off-chain resolver that returns private smart-account addresses that change over time.**

Your ENS name becomes a *private receiving alias*, not a traceable identity.

---

## ❌ Problem 5: Smart Accounts Are Hard for Users

Account abstraction is powerful but complex:

* Users must deploy a smart account
* Pay deployment gas
* Configure modules
* Manage permissions

**Assura deploys and manages smart accounts automatically**, using stealth addresses as owners and a secured AutoShield module for execution.
Users don’t even know they’re interacting with a smart account—everything feels like normal wallet usage.

---

## ❌ Problem 6: No Simple, Private Payment Request Experience

Today, if you want someone to pay you:

* You share a static address
* You leak privacy
* You can’t control which chain they send on
* You can’t automate fund flows
* You can’t shield funds by default

**Assura turns your ENS name into a universal, private, multi-chain payment endpoint.**

Senders simply type:

```
bob.assuranet.eth
```

…and Assura handles privacy, smart account logic, and bridging invisibly.

---

# ✅ In Summary: What People Can Use Assura For

### ✔ Private multi-chain payments

Receive tokens privately on any EVM chain using just your ENS name.

### ✔ Private donations & public identities

Share an ENS subdomain publicly without leaking your wallet history.

### ✔ Automatic conversion to Zcash

Perfect for Zcash users who want EVM liquidity but Zcash privacy.

### ✔ Burner-proof receiving

Even if someone shares or leaks your ENS name, every deposit is still unlinkable.

### ✔ Universal payment endpoint

Stop sharing multiple chain-specific addresses—use one name for everything.

### ✔ Frictionless onboarding

Senders don’t need to know anything about Zcash or privacy.
They just send tokens to an ENS name, same as always.

**Challenges we ran into**

### **1. Stealth Address Detection Was Tricky**

One of the biggest headaches was getting the wallet to reliably spot incoming payments created from stealth addresses.
Because every payment lands on a brand-new, one-time address, the wallet has to scan the chain and figure out, “Which of these are mine?”

At first, the scan key logic kept missing certain payments.
I solved it by tightening up the key-derivation checks and adding better logging so I could see exactly where it broke. Once I understood the pattern, fixing it was much easier.

---

### **2. Moving Funds Into Zcash Smoothly**

Automatic conversion to shielded Zcash sounded simple… until I actually tried to automate it.
Timing issues, mempool delays, and fee estimation all caused weird edge cases where the funds didn’t convert or got stuck midway.

The fix was to add:

* a retry system
* proper error handling
* a “wait until confirmed” step

After that, everything became way more reliable.

---

### **3. Balancing Privacy With Usability**

Privacy tools can easily get complicated, and I didn’t want users dealing with technical steps or confusing settings.
It took a few attempts to simplify the flow so that privacy just *happens* in the background.

The breakthrough was focusing on one principle: **one action from the user, everything else automated.**

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Assura uses NEAR Intents as the universal routing, bridging, and execution layer for private movement of funds from any EVM chain into Zcash.
It provides cross-chain privacy, private identity resolution, and automatic ZEC settlement with zero friction for users.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Assura uses NEAR Intents as the private settlement engine for a fully automated, private, real-world payment experience built around ENS.
It turns everyday EVM transfers into frictionless private Zcash payments with no user complexity.

### ZKFIED
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zkfied-2074) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/YCE3-C2_boE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The encrypted whistleblower software.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![zkSNARKS](https://img.shields.io/badge/zkSNARKS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This was developed by our team with a single idea/mission: whistleblowing softwares aren't capable of protecting the people who need them. 

SecureDrop rested on centralized servers that governments could subpoena and physically seize so journalists still had to trust their own judgment to verify a source because there was no cryptographic way to prove someon's role inside an organization. 

WikiLeaks was the next big innovation but it had the opposite flaw: extreme centralization of control with a single person had authority over submissions, access, editorial choices. There was still no way to cryptographically prove a source’s legitimacy. You know the story once the platform became politically targeted it was cut off financially by Visa/Mastercard and PayPal.

The failures have names and consequences. When Reality Winner tried to expose Russian interference in U.S. elections in 2017, her identity was revealed because the PDF she printed had microdot tracking. When Edward Snowden went public in 2013, he had only a few journalists and ultimately exile. Chelsea Manning confided in someone she believed she could trust, only to be reported to federal authorities. 

Again and again, whistleblowers were caught because of metadata, IP logs, email headers, printer dots, chain of custody leaks or platforms with a single administrative key that could compromise everything once seized. Lavabit’s shutdown in 2013 is a perfect example because when the U.S. government demanded access, one court order was enough to destroy privacy for every user on the service. 

The architecture itself was the failure mode.

We truly mean it when we say this isn't an issue of courage or even the risk of retaliation. The real problem is that whistleblowing has been resting on centralized, human systems in a world where adversaries operate with subpoenas + full spectrum surveillance. This is what we need to fix! 

We’re solving the problem that none of these systems ever solved by creating a whistleblowing mechanism where identity can be proven without being exposed like where evidence cannot be deleted or tampered with. A tool where no single person can betray the rest and where people can all work together on sensitive topics with evidence intents and real anonimity.

**Challenges we ran into**

We started building ZKFIED with the full vision: all whistleblower boards (healthcare, corporate fraud, environmental crimes, etc.) had its own Zcash Shielded Asset. We've developed the system so that Healthcare Whistleblower Token could prove you submitted evidence to that specific board with your identity completely private. Our team was so hyped because it's the perfect use case.

We spent days architecting around ZSAs, we designed the token issuance flow, viewing keys would work with custom asset types, finished the Rust code to interact with the ZSA protocol. Then we hit a wall because ZSAs aren't live yet on testnet except one that we couldn't get enough info to run the project from it and they're part of the NU6 upgrade that's coming to Zcash.

That was a complex moment for the entire team because you never want to downgrade your project especially when you know this is the perfect ecosystem and tech for it!  We gave up on custom asset types, we're now using standard shielded ZEC  transactions with memo fields to encode the evidence IDs. It works but we just knew we could do so much better and had the infra ready for it. 

it's good news knowing that when ZSAs do launch our architecture is ready to swap them in. So yes it was frustrating to have the perfect solution just out of reach... But when a team hits issue together that's when they work best together towards the solution and it has united us a lot.

**Privacy-Focused Content & Media**

ZKFIED uses Mina's zkSNARKs to solve a critical whistleblower problem proving you belong to a specific community (healthcare workers, corporate employees, etc.) without revealing your identity.

We built zkApps that verify credentials off-chain and post succinct proofs on-chain. A nurse can prove "I work in healthcare" to access the Healthcare Whistleblower board without exposing their hospital, name, or employee ID. The proof is constant-size (~22KB) regardless of the credential complexity thanks to Mina's recursive proof composition.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

"How do you make whistleblowing safe with rewards without doxxing people?", the only answer was Zcash. 

Every time someone submits evidence, they create a shielded transaction. Nobody can see who sent it, how much ZEC it contained, or who received it and the evidence ID lives in the encrypted memo field so even the commitment to the evidence is hidden from public view. 

We're using FROST threshold signatures (3-of-5 setup) because we wanted to avoid the issue we saw in previous famous failures and the viewing key mechanic also sold us on Zcash. 

We really wanted to use Zcash Shielded Assets to create boardtokens like a "Healthcare Whistleblower Token" or "Corporate Fraud Token." We initally developed the entire project based on that and that would have been really clean. But ZSAs aren't live yet (they're coming in NU6), so we had to work with standard shielded ZEC. 

We built everything assuming ZSAs would exist so swapping them in later won't require a rewrite.

We wanted to do this for a long time but was waiting for the right opportunity and this hackathon felt like it and gave us amazing ressources and a lot of support on the Discord!

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZKFIED is a crosschain privacy coordination tool with NEAR integrated everwhere. We use NEAR smart contracts as the public registry and marketplace with the key innovation of NEAR Intents NEP366) so whistleblowers create access requests as intents and solvers compete to fulfill them by routing payments and exchanging encryption keys. 

NEAR can't see the evidence content (encrypted) and without NEAR and Intents protocol, we'd have no way to coordinate the three chain privacy coordination.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

We use NEAR smart contracts as the public registry and marketplace with the key innovation of NEAR Intents NEP366) so whistleblowers create access requests as intents and solvers compete to fulfill them by routing payments and exchanging encryption keys.

NEAR can't see the evidence content (encrypted) and without NEAR and Intents protocol, we'd have no way to coordinate the three chain privacy coordination.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Lighthouse](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lighthouse-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## **The problem it solves**

Today’s 3D/social spaces are fragmented, extractive, and passive - they trap value, hide provenance, and make discovery and ownership clunky. Going on-chain solves part of that, but without thoughtful UX and distribution it still feels like crypto for crypto’s sake. This project fixes both the ownership layer **and** the human layer (how users find, share, and actually *use* assets and spaces).

### Core problems

* **False “ownership” in walled gardens** - purchases are often just platform entries; users can’t truly move, verify, or sell assets outside the host ecosystem.
* **Poor provenance & trust** - you can’t prove who created or legitimately owns an item, which makes trading and lending risky.
* **Limited portability & composability** - assets can’t be used across apps, limiting creativity and reuse.
* **Discovery and retention gaps** - users don’t find reasons to explore spaces; creators struggle to distribute content organically.
* **Collaboration friction** - shared edits, temporary loans, and collaborative items are clunky or impossible.
* **Onboarding & UX for web3 rewards** - token systems exist, but are hard to discover and use for ordinary social experiences.

### How we solve it 

* **Trust-first ownership:** Every object is an on-chain token with verifiable provenance and portable metadata - real ownership, not a locked file.
* **Portable composability:** Standardized metadata + lightweight runtime adapters let assets move between rooms, apps, and marketplaces.
* **Safe exchange & lending:** Minimal on-chain borrow/escrow flows enable temporary loans, rentals, and trustless trades without middlemen.
* **Discovery + distribution layer:** Built-in mechanics for content drops, airdrops, and spatial distribution so creators can seed objects across rooms and users can find them organically.
* **Gamified engagement:** Easter eggs, scavenger hunts, and room-based challenges deliver on-chain rewards (tokens, NFTs, access rights) - turning exploration into a viral distribution loop.
* **Creator-first economy:** Tools for minting, royalty enforcement, and breathable marketplaces that let creators monetize while users trade safely.

### Why gamified, spatial distribution matters

* **Organic onboarding:** Hide easter eggs and token drops in rooms to create viral loops - users invite friends to hunt together, raising retention.
* **Contextual discovery:** Instead of a bland marketplace, rewards and rare items are discovered *in* the world - which is more engaging and less grindy.
* **Meaningful utility:** Finding an easter egg can unlock exclusive assets, governance rights, or access to creator communities - tokens become functional, not speculative.
* **Fairer distribution:** Spatial drops and challenges let creators control scarcity and reward actual engagement, reducing bot/whale capture.

**Challenges we ran into**

## **Challenges I ran into**

* **Asset metadata chaos**
  Different 3D assets followed different formats, so portability kept breaking.
  Fixed it by standardizing metadata + adding a validator before minting.

* **3D performance issues**
  Heavy GLTF files slowed initial loads.
  Compression + lazy loading + caching made scenes actually usable.

* **Security & provenance**
  Verifying creator/origin info for each object was unreliable.
  Fixed with on-chain provenance checks tied directly to minting flow.

> "Track. Understand. Heal."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Mental-health struggles are increasing worldwide, yet most people still do not receive timely support. Traditional systems rely heavily on human availability, clinical visits, and self-reporting—making early detection difficult and causing many individuals to slip through the cracks.

EmotionPulse solves this by providing an AI-powered, always-available emotional companion that helps users understand their mental well-being before issues escalate. It analyzes moods, stress levels, and emotional patterns from text inputs and optional face selfies, giving users a clearer picture of their mental state.

Instead of waiting until a crisis happens, EmotionPulse enables early detection, continuous monitoring, and safe intervention, helping users get support when they need it most. It makes emotional tracking easier, safer, and more accessible for everyone—especially those who hesitate to reach out for help.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Integrating multiple AI models
Different models for sentiment, crisis detection, and face emotion caused accuracy and performance issues. I solved it by optimizing pipelines and reducing heavy computations.

2. Processing messy user text
User text varied a lot, breaking predictions. Added preprocessing and confidence scoring to stabilize outputs.

3. Linking frontend and backend
CORS errors, routing issues, and async problems appeared while connecting React with the Python backend. Fixed by adjusting API endpoints and server configs.

4. Deploying the full stack
Render/Vercel deployments failed due to environment variables, model loading time, and server timeouts. Solved with caching and proper configuration.

5. Ensuring privacy and safety
Handling sensitive mental-health data required careful design. Implemented minimal storage and optional features to protect users.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/insightify-bcf8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20with%20Stack-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-with-stack.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Fake News Detection

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Academic certificates are extremely easy to fake, and traditional verification is slow, manual, and unreliable. Colleges and companies waste time verifying documents, and students face delays when applying for jobs, admissions, or internships.

Insightify solves this by combining AI anomaly detection with Ethereum-based immutable verification.
It automatically checks whether a certificate is forged using AI (layout similarity, seal/logo match, signature analysis) and verifies the certificate’s authenticity by comparing its hash with the secure record stored on the blockchain.

This removes the dependency on manual verification, reduces fraud, speeds up approvals, and provides a transparent trust system for institutions, students, and recruiters.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into:

While building Insightify, our biggest challenge was that both team members were beginners in blockchain and AI development. We had never deployed a smart contract before, and even basic tools like MetaMask, Remix, and Sepolia test ETH were completely new to us.

Some specific hurdles we faced:

MetaMask Setup Issues:
We struggled to switch networks, get Sepolia test ETH, and understand why contract deployment was failing due to insufficient gas.

Remix IDE Confusion:
We had difficulty compiling, deploying, and interacting with our Solidity contract for the first time. Understanding functions like storeReport(), reports(), and how contract state updates work took time.

AI + Blockchain Integration:
Since Insightify uses AI for anomaly detection and Ethereum for immutable report storage, connecting these two parts was initially confusing.

Understanding Gas Fees:
We weren’t sure how gas estimation works or why certain transactions failed even though we thought we had enough balance.

Working With Python Backend:
Creating the folder structure, running Flask, and connecting it to the smart contract was new and required step-by-step learning.

How We Overcame Them:

Followed documentation and troubleshooting guides step-by-step.

Used ChatGPT extensively to debug MetaMask, Remix, and Python errors.

Deployed multiple test contracts to learn how blockchain transactions work.

Simplified the architecture and focused on a minimal working version.

**Ethereum Track**

Our project, Insightify, is built around Ethereum as the core trust layer. We use Solidity smart contracts deployed on the Sepolia Ethereum test network to provide an immutable, transparent, and tamper-proof storage layer for user-submitted reports.

Users submit incident reports through our system, and these reports are stored on-chain using a Solidity contract. Every report is hashed and saved on Ethereum, ensuring:

Immutability: Reports cannot be modified or deleted once stored.

Transparency: Anyone can verify the stored data directly on the blockchain.

Decentralization: No centralized server controls or manipulates the information.

Trustless Operation: The blockchain guarantees the validity of the stored data without intermediaries.

By integrating Ethereum for secure logging and verification, our project aligns directly with the goals of the Ethereum track, demonstrating blockchain-backed data integrity, security, and accountability.
