### ChainWhistle - Decentralised Whistleblower Protect
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/chainwhistle-411e) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://chainwhistle.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-KJSSE%20GajShield%20Hack%20X-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-x.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Stake. Validate. Publish. Get paid. No middlemen.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Whistleblowers carry enormous risk - retaliation, prosecution, and career destruction - with zero financial reward for the public value they create. Existing platforms (SecureDrop, Signal tips) solve the *delivery* problem but leave the economic and trust problems entirely unsolved:

- **No anonymity guarantees**: centralised platforms can be subpoenaed, hacked, or shut down.
- **No financial incentive**: leaking information of massive public value earns the source nothing.
- **No validator accountability**: there's no skin-in-the-game for the people deciding if a claim is real.
- **No outlet accountability**: a news org can win exclusive rights to a story and simply never publish it.

ChainWhistle solves all four by replacing platform trust with economic stakes and on-chain rules:

- **Whistleblowers** submit pseudonymously (wallet = identity). No registration, no email, no IP linkage at the protocol level. Claim content lives on IPFS; only CIDs hit the chain.
- **Validator Orgs** post a 1 ETH stake and vote on claim authenticity via commit-reveal. If their verdict is later contradicted by the oracle cycle, 5% of their stake is slashed.
- **News Outlets** post a 2 ETH stake and bid ETH for the right to break a verified story. If they win the bid but never publish, they are permanently blacklisted and their stake is seized.
- **Oracle Nodes** post a 0.5 ETH stake. Five are randomly selected per claim to verify actual publication. Minority voters are slashed 10% to deter collusion.

On the happy path, the winning bid escrow is split: **60% to the whistleblower**, 30% to validator orgs who voted correctly, 10% to the oracle majority. Bad behaviour is economically irrational, not merely unethical.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Alchemy `eth_getLogs` rate limits**
Our LLM server scans blocks on startup to catch missed events. Alchemy's free tier rejects any `eth_getLogs` call spanning more than a handful of blocks with `block range is too wide`. Fixed by chunking the scan into configurable 10-block batches, accumulating events across all chunks before processing.

**Keeping the Pinata JWT server-side**
Uploading to IPFS directly from the browser would expose the Pinata JWT in the client bundle. Proxied all uploads through the Express server (`POST /upload`, `POST /upload-text`) so the JWT never leaves `server/.env`.

**Commit-reveal salt persistence**
Validator orgs must retain their salt for up to 3 days between commit and reveal. A browser clear makes it unrecoverable. Solved by displaying the salt as a copyable hex string immediately after commit with a persistent warning banner until reveal is confirmed.

**7-state claim lifecycle in React**
Managing 7 on-chain states × 4 time-window deadlines in JSX conditionals became unmaintainable fast. Refactored into a single `getAvailableActions(claim, userRole, now)` utility that returns permitted actions for a given snapshot, making the UI fully declarative.

Third-party verification services become honeypots for attackers

Sybil Attacks & Duplicate Registration

Friction in Privacy-Preserving Access Control

Gender verification systems can't prevent discrimination

Lack of Portable, On-Chain Credentials

No interoperable standard for privacy-preserving proofs
Blockchain dApps have no trustless way to verify humans

✅ Verify location for regional benefits (scholarships, job boards, utilities) without exposing full address
✅ Prove uniqueness to prevent being shadowbanned or rate-limited across platforms
✅ Mint portable identity NFT that works across multiple Web3 services
✅ Prove humanity with biometric liveness to prevent bot attacks
✅ Gender verification for community safety without revealing to third parties
For Platforms & Services:
🔐 Bot Prevention - Verify humans without CAPTCHA or surveillance
🕵️ Airdrop & Incentive Distribution - Prevent Sybil attacks on token distributions

💰 Lending Protocols - Age/uniqueness verification for DeFi without KYC

### MemoryLens
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/memorylens-3038) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sambhandavale/memory_lens) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ip8Ul9QXu-U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-KJSSE%20GajShield%20Hack%20X-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-x.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Assistive Augmented Memory Interface

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deepface](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deepface-333333?style=flat-square) ![vosk](https://img.shields.io/badge/vosk-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Individuals facing cognitive impairment—such as amnesiacs, the elderly, and those with significant cognitive decline—experience profound suffering. The core of the issue is the **loss of personal continuity**:
**Social Anxiety**: Forgetting names and recent conversations leads to a deep-seated anxiety during social interactions.
**Isolation**: This fear often causes people to withdraw from society, leading to worsened social outcomes and loneliness.
**Loss of Identity**: Forgetting everyday events, items, and most importantly, the people they love, strips away the fabric of their daily lives.

### Our Solution
While modern technology often focuses on improving the context memory of AI and LLMs, we believe that intelligence should first serve the humans who need it most. **MemoryLens** shifts the focus back to helping people recognize their loved ones and reclaim their social autonomy.

The system utilizes smart glasses as a camera and microphone, paired with a phone that handles the complex processing.When a user encounters someone, the device identifies the face and displays the person’s name and relationship details directly on the lens.

### Making Life Easier and Safer
MemoryLens transforms how those with memory impairment navigate the world by making existing tasks safer and more intuitive:
**Effortless Identification**: Instead of the stress of trying to remember a face, users can simply ask "Who is this person?" to receive immediate audio or visual confirmation.
**The Memory Vault**: Users can access a "Memory Vault," which serves as a historical ledger of archived conversations.This allows them to recall what was recently discussed, such as a plan to check the garden or an upcoming birthday party.
**Background Learning**: The system "watches, listens, and learns" in the background, autonomously mapping relationships from raw dialogue so the user doesn't have to manage the tool themselves.
**Privacy & Longevity**: Because all face embeddings stay on the device, the user's most personal memories remain private and secure, ensuring the product remains a reliable companion for the long term.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Fast & Private Face Recognition
**The Challenge**: Standard facial recognition is often too slow for real-time social interactions or relies too heavily on the cloud.
**The Solution**: We optimized our pipeline using **DeepFace** and **OpenCV**, storing all facial embeddings locally on the device.This ensures lightning-fast identification while keeping the user's most sensitive data completely private.

### 2. Live Audio & Semantic Understanding
**The Challenge**: It was difficult to stream live audio and "understand" the relationship between the user and the person they were talking to without manual input.
**The Solution**: We built a pipeline using **Vosk** for live listening and **Google Gemini** for **Zero-Shot NLP**. This allows the system to semantically analyze conversations in the background to autonomously identify names and relationships like "Son" or "Friend."

### 3. Optimizing the Memory Vault
**The Challenge**: Storing and retrieving months of conversations in a way that provides instant context was a major storage hurdle.
**The Solution**: We implemented a **Vector Database (MongoDB Atlas)** using **Cosine Similarity**. This allows the "Memory Vault" to instantly recall specific past interactions—like a mention of a birthday party or a garden—the moment a familiar face is detected.

> We're the only one that proves you can't.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Solution Overview

COMPUT3 solves both the cloud trust problem and the agent trust problem in a single platform.

### Three Pillars

**Pillar 1 — Confidential Containers**

Each team gets an isolated Docker container (or set of containers) with filesystem encryption via LUKS, where the encryption key is derived from the team's own keypair. Even with root access on the host, the operator cannot read the team's data. Container isolation is enforced via gVisor or Firecracker sandboxing.

**Pillar 2 — Agentic Deployment**

Instead of requiring teams to write Docker Compose files or configure infrastructure manually, an AI agent handles everything. The user describes their stack in natural language (e.g., "I need React, Express, and MongoDB"). The agent generates a deployment plan, provisions containers, configures networking, installs dependencies, and returns access credentials — all within 60 seconds.

**Pillar 3 — On-Chain Verification**

Every action is logged and attested on-chain. This includes container lifecycle events (created, started, stopped, destroyed), every tool call the agent made during provisioning, a hash of the final container state, and the encryption key derivation proof (proving the operator can't decrypt). Teams can verify their attestation on a block explorer at any time.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

Building COMPUT3 involved solving problems across **systems, security, and Web3**, and one of the biggest challenges was ensuring **true data confidentiality in a hostile environment**.

---

### 🔐 1. Preventing Provider Access to Container Data

A major hurdle was:

> **How do you run a container on someone else’s machine without letting them access your code or data?**

By default, even with Docker isolation, a host-level operator can:
- Inspect volumes  
- Read filesystem data  
- Attach debuggers  

#### ✅ Solution

We implemented **disk-level encryption using LUKS** at the workspace level:

- Each container is backed by an **encrypted volume**
- The encryption key is **not stored**, but **derived dynamically from on-chain attestations**
- Even if someone copies the entire disk, it remains **unreadable ciphertext**

We also ensured:
- Keys are only available during mount time  
- Temporary key files are immediately wiped  
- Access can be revoked by invalidating the attestation  

This shifted the model from:
> “trust the operator” → **“make access cryptographically impossible”**

---

### ⚙️ 2. Verifiable Agent Execution

Another challenge was:

> **How do we prove that the AI agent didn’t modify or inject anything during deployment?**

AI systems are inherently non-deterministic, so we needed a way to make execution **auditable and tamper-evident**.

#### ✅ Solution

We built a structured logging system:

- Every agent action (tool calls, container ops, installs) is:
  - Logged  
  - Hashed  
- All hashes are aggregated into a **Merkle tree**
- The root is **attested on-chain via EAS**

This allows users to:
- Recompute the hash  
- Verify execution independently  

---

### 💰 3. Designing Trustless Payments

We initially implemented simple request-based payments, but ran into a key issue:

> **What if a provider takes payment and then shuts down the service?**

#### ✅ Solution

We redesigned the system into a **hybrid payment model**:

- Partial upfront payment for deployment  
- Remaining payments **streamed based on uptime**
- Providers must continuously submit proofs  
- Payments stop immediately if the service stops  
- Malicious providers can be **slashed via stake**

---

### 🧠 Key Learning

The biggest takeaway was:

> **You can’t rely on trust assumptions — you have to redesign systems so that trust is unnecessary.**

This meant combining:
- Cryptography  
- System isolation  
- On-chain verification  
- Incentive design  

into a single cohesive architecture.

---

## 💣 Final Reflection

> Building COMPUT3 wasn’t just about deploying apps — it was about rethinking how infrastructure works when trust is removed from the system.

> Define Stress Heal

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![API3](https://img.shields.io/badge/API3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🔴 The Problem Statement
In modern microservice architectures, applications rely on hundreds of external and internal APIs. This dependency creates three critical pain points:

Fragile Ecosystems: If one API changes its JSON schema or goes down, the entire frontend or downstream service often crashes, leading to lost revenue and poor user experience.
Monitoring vs. Action: Traditional tools (like Postman or Datadog) are great at alerting you when things break, but they require a human to wake up at 3:00 AM to manually debug and apply a fix.
Slow Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Finding why an API failed (e.g., Is it a header issue? A network timeout? A breaking schema change?) usually takes 30–60 minutes of manual log searching.
🟢 The Solution (Shadow API)
Shadow API Tester is an autonomous, self-healing engine that sits alongside your infrastructure to ensure total API resilience.

1. Autonomous Healing Engine
Instead of just alerting, the system follows a 3-step tactical healing sequence when a failure is detected:

Step 1: Exponential Backoff Retry (Fixes transient network blips).
Step 2: Parameter/Header Mutation (AI tries adjusting Content-Type, Accept, or User-Agent headers to find a working combination).
Step 3: Intelligent Mock Fallback (Intercepts the failure and serves a verified mock response to keep the client application running while the real API is down).
2. High-Fidelity "Shadow" Testing
The system runs on a separate thread/worker and performs Shadow Pings every 10 seconds. It tests the APIs in an isolated environment so it never pollutes your production database or affects real user metrics.

3. AI-Driven Root Cause Analysis
Leveraging Gemini and Ollama, the engine analyzes the raw HTTP response, stack traces, and latency patterns. It generates a human-readable "Thought Stream" that explains exactly what went wrong and how the system is fixing it.

4. Self-Healing Schemas
If an API provider changes their data structure (e.g., changing user_id to id), the Schema Detector identifies the mismatch, analyzes the new structure, and automatically updates the expected model without requiring a code deployment.

5. Tactical Command Dashboard
A premium, cyberpunk-themed React interface provides real-time telemetry, live healing logs, and a "Circuit Breaker" control panel, giving engineers total oversight of their API health.

🏗️ Technical Stack
Backend: FastAPI (Python 3.12+), SQLAlchemy 2.0, SQLite (WAL Mode for high concurrency).
Frontend: React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Framer Motion (for high-fidelity animations).
AI: Google Gemini API / Ollama (for localized RCA).
Communication: WebSockets (Broadcast streaming of live pings and AI thoughts).

> Privacy-first wallet proving humanity, securing AI

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🚨 The Problem It Solves

The internet is facing a growing **trust crisis**.

- Bots and fake users can create unlimited accounts, exploit rewards, and manipulate platforms  
- Wallets only prove **ownership of keys**, not whether the user is a real human  
- AI agents can act autonomously **without strict human control or limits**  
- Existing verification systems either **leak personal identity** or rely on weak, centralized trust  

This leads to:
- Fake engagement and spam  
- Exploited airdrops and marketplaces  
- Uncontrolled AI actions  
- Loss of trust in decentralized systems  


## 💡 How Proofly Solves It

Proofly introduces a **wallet-native trust layer** that makes interactions **verifiable, private, and secure**.

### 🔐 Prove You're Human (Without Revealing Identity)
- Uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify real humans  
- No personal data, no identity leakage  

### ✍️ Secure Every Action
- Every action is **wallet-signed and intentional**  
- Prevents spoofing, fake submissions, and unauthorized activity  

### 🤖 Control AI Agents
- Define strict rules for AI:
  - spending limits  
  - allowed contracts  
  - time restrictions  
- AI cannot act beyond user-defined boundaries  

### 📜 Verifiable Trust Trail
- Actions are backed by:
  - human proof  
  - cryptographic signatures  
  - policy enforcement  
- Anyone can verify trust without needing identity  


## 🚀 What Can People Use It For?

- **Airdrop protection** → only real humans can claim rewards  
- **Marketplaces & gigs** → prevent fake users and spam submissions  
- **AI automation** → safely delegate tasks to AI with strict limits  
- **Content authenticity** → verify human-created, signed content  
- **dApps & platforms** → build trust without KYC or identity leakage  


## ✅ Why It Matters

Proofly makes the internet:
- **Safer** → eliminates bots and fake users  
- **Private** → no personal data exposed  
- **Trustworthy** → every action is verifiable  
- **AI-ready** → humans stay in control of AI systems

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

Building Proofly as a **real, end-to-end trust system** (not just a UI demo) came with several technical challenges:



### 🔌 Wallet + dApp Integration (EIP-1193)

**Problem:**  
Making the Chrome extension behave like a real wallet provider was tricky. Injecting a custom provider and ensuring dApps could properly connect, request accounts, and sign messages caused inconsistencies.

**Solution:**  
We implemented a proper EIP-1193-compatible provider and standardized request/response handling. Careful event management fixed connection issues.



### 🔐 Secure Key Storage in Extension

**Problem:**  
Handling private keys securely inside a Chrome extension without exposing them to content scripts or external access.

**Solution:**  
We encrypted all key material locally using a user-defined password and ensured keys never leave the extension context. Sensitive logic was isolated in the background service worker.



### 🧠 Integrating Human Proof (World ID)

**Problem:**  
Managing the zero-knowledge proof flow and handling proof responses correctly, especially binding proofs to specific actions.

**Solution:**  
We structured proof handling with proper nullifier tracking and stored verification state locally and in the backend, ensuring proofs are reusable only within valid scopes.



### 🤖 AI Policy Enforcement (Core Challenge)

**Problem:**  
Designing a system where an AI agent cannot bypass user permissions and perform unauthorized actions.

**Solution:**  
We built a **policy engine inside the wallet**, where every action request is validated locally before signing. Since the wallet is the signer, AI cannot act outside defined rules.



### 🔗 Sync Between Wallet, Backend, and Chain

**Problem:**  
Keeping state consistent across:
- extension (local state)
- Supabase backend
- smart contracts on Base Sepolia

**Solution:**  
We introduced structured event logging and clear state ownership:
- wallet → source of truth for decisions  
- chain → enforcement & audit  
- backend → indexing and UI sync  



### 🎨 UI vs Real Functionality Trade-off

**Problem:**  
Balancing between building a visually impressive demo and maintaining real, working functionality.

**Solution:**  
We prioritized **real implementations first**, then iteratively improved the UI to match production-grade wallet experiences.


## 🧩 Key Takeaway

The biggest challenge was ensuring **nothing is faked** — every feature (wallet, proof, signing, policy) had to work end-to-end.

This forced us to think like real product engineers, not just prototype builders.

> Killing blind trust in npm , one package at a time

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/bun-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fileverse](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fileverse-333333?style=flat-square) ![NeroChain](https://img.shields.io/badge/NeroChain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional package managers treat centralized registries as "trusted until proven guilty." If a bad actor publishes a compromised package, thousands of developers install it before a CVE is even issued. There is no proactive defense against zero-day supply chain threats, typosquatting, or malicious post-install scripts.

**How APM solves the problem:**
Aegis Package Manager (APM) is a security-first, drop-in replacement for standard npm clients. It shifts the ecosystem to a Zero-Trust model:


- Immutable Publishing (apm push): Every package is cryptographically hashed, audited by an AI swarm, and signed securely on the NeroChain blockchain before it reaches npm.
- Deep-Reasoning Gateway (apm install): Unregistered legacy packages are intercepted. They are run through a localized heuristic engine, followed by Gemini AI Agents to detect malicious code before installation executes.
- Deep Project Audit (apm check): Maps your entire dependency tree and cross-references it with the NeroChain registry. Flags look-alike typosquats, queries CVE databases, and runs local AI assessments on unverified packages.
- ZK-Verified Onboarding (apm register-agent): A decentralized security marketplace. New AI Agents can be registered to the network, but only if they pass a rigid 10-TestCase Gauntlet providing a cryptographic Zero-Knowledge Proof of 100% accuracy.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Latency of AI Security Scans**

Challenge: Running multi-agent LLM analysis on dependencies takes minutes—unacceptable for standard build pipelines.
Solution: On-Chain Security Caching. The first time any user scans an unknown package, its score is cached on NeroChain. Future developers running apm install bypass the heavy AI scan in milliseconds, inheriting the community's blockchain-verified safety.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

APM moves beyond standard chatbot implementations, utilizing a multi-agent "Swarm" of Gemini 2.5 Flash models as autonomous security auditors. Rather than relying on rigid rules, APM feeds package source code, CVE database context, and dependency maps directly into the Gemini API. Gemini leverages its massive context window and deep-reasoning capabilities to semantically analyze the code—detecting obfuscated logic, dangerous local environment exfiltration, and zero-day malicious behavior hidden in postinstall scripts. Gemini powers the Risk Consensus Engine that ultimately decides whether a package is safe for developers to consume.

**Best Build on Nero Chain**

APM leverages NeroChain as a decentralized, immutable "Source of Truth" for global software security. Instead of depending on centralized package authority that could be compromised, APM registers cryptographic checksums, author ECDSA signatures, and Gemini AI Risk Scores natively as smart contract states. Because of NeroChain's extreme performance and low cost, the CLI can query the blockchain in real-time during apm install. This effectively transforms NeroChain into a globally crowdsourced, low-latency security cache—if one user pays the compute to scan a package, NeroChain permanently stores the trust score to protect the rest of the web3 ecosystem instantly.

**The problem it solves**

Current green funding systems suffer from a lack of transparency and trust. Donors are often unable to verify how their contributions are used, leading to uncertainty and reduced participation. Centralized control further limits fairness, as decisions are made by a few entities rather than the community. Additionally, there is no reliable way to track the real-world environmental impact of funded projects, making the entire process opaque and inefficient.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into**

While building our decentralized voting system, we faced significant challenges in integrating blockchain functionality with our frontend.

1.Faced issues while connecting Pera Wallet to the React frontend due to unstable session handling.
2.Wallet connection was not persistent, leading to repeated disconnections.
3.Voting transactions were failing during signing or broadcasting.
4.Encountered network mismatch issues (TestNet vs MainNet).
5.Insufficient test balance also caused transaction failures during testing.


 **How We Solved It**

We approached the problem step-by-step and focused on debugging each layer of the system:

1.Implemented proper session management to maintain stable wallet connections.
2.Used Algorand SDK to correctly construct and validate transaction objects.
3.Fixed the transaction signing flow to ensure smooth interaction with the wallet.
4.Aligned network configuration to avoid TestNet/MainNet conflicts.
5.Funded accounts using TestNet faucet for successful transaction execution.
6.Added detailed logging and error handling to identify and fix issues quickly.
7.Improved user experience by adding loading states and success/error feedback.

**Outcome**

Achieved stable wallet connectivity.
Enabled secure and successful voting transactions.
Improved overall reliability and user experience of the application.

** Key  Learning**

This experience helped us gain hands-on knowledge of Web3 integration, transaction handling, and debugging real-world blockchain issues under time constraints.

**The problem it solves**

**Project Description: FreshSense AI**
FreshSense AI is an innovative solution designed to tackle the problem of food spoilage and authenticity in fruits and vegetables. Our system integrates machine learning, IoT sensors, and blockchain technology to provide accurate freshness prediction and organic/inorganic classification.

**🌱 The Problem It Solves**
Food vendors and consumers often struggle to identify when produce will spoil or whether it is truly organic. This leads to losses, health risks, and mistrust in the supply chain. FreshSense AI solves this by:

- Predicting spoilage 2 days in advance using gas sensors (CO₂, Ethanol, Acetylene, Ammonia, Sulfur compounds).

- Classifying produce as organic or inorganic based on chemical thresholds.

- Logging every reading on Algorand blockchain for tamper‑proof certification. 

**⚙️ How It Works**

- Dataset Engineering: Extended datasets for tomatoes, garlic, onions, and leafy vegetables with freshness and organic markers.
 
- ML Classification: Models trained to classify produce into Fresh, Medium, Spoiled, and Organic/Inorganic categories.
 
- Blockchain Integration: Each prediction is stored on Algorand with a transaction ID, ensuring transparency.
 
- Notification System: Vendors receive alerts 2 days before spoilage, allowing proactive action.

- Examiner-Friendly Demo: Confusion matrices, accuracy scores (~85–90%), and blockchain verification are showcased in a clear, judge‑friendly presentation.

**🌟 Impact**

- For Vendors: Reduced losses, better inventory planning. 
- For Consumers: Trust in freshness and organic authenticity. 
- For Supply Chain: Tamper‑proof records that improve transparency and safety.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building FreshSense AI, we faced several hurdles:

- **Dataset Engineering**

Challenge: Extending vegetable datasets with new parameters (acetylene, ammonia, sulfur compounds) while keeping values realistic.

Solution: We designed synthetic ranges based on scientific literature and balanced distributions across Fresh, Medium, and Spoiled states.

- **Accuracy & Model Reliability**

Challenge: Initial ML models struggled with imbalanced data, leading to biased predictions.

Solution: We applied normalization, balanced sampling, and confusion matrix evaluation to improve accuracy to ~85–90%.

**- Blockchain Integration**

Challenge: Storing sensor readings and freshness predictions on Algorand without bloating transactions.

Solution: We optimized by encoding freshness + organic/inorganic classification in transaction notes, keeping records lightweight but verifiable.

- **Notification System**

Challenge: Triggering alerts exactly 2 days before spoilage prediction.

Solution: We implemented a simple rule‑based scheduler tied to ML outputs, ensuring vendors receive timely alerts.

**Algorand**

Blockchain Logging: Every freshness reading (CO₂, Ethanol, Acetylene, Ammonia, Sulfur compounds) is stored on Algorand as a transaction, ensuring immutable records.

Tamper‑Proof Certification: Vendors and consumers can scan a QR code to verify freshness and organic/inorganic classification directly on Algorand Explorer.

Predictive Alerts: Our ML model predicts spoilage dates, and Algorand smart contracts trigger notifications 2 days before spoilage, helping vendors act proactively.

Trust in Organic Labeling: By combining sensor data with blockchain, FreshSense AI prevents mislabeling and builds consumer confidence in organic produce.

> zkp based college credential system

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The CredChain project solves the fragmentation, privacy risks, and manual overhead associated with traditional academic credentialing.

**The Problem It Solves**
Traditional verification is slow, manual, and privacy-invasive. Currently, students must share entire sensitive documents (like full transcripts) to prove single facts, while institutions waste weeks manually verifying paper or PDF records that are easily forged.

**What People Can Use It For**
Colleges: Issue tamper-proof, W3C-style digital credentials that can be revoked or updated instantly.
Students: Manage an "Identity Wallet" to store degrees and certifications. They can share specific "Presentations" (e.g., just the degree name, not the grades) via QR codes.
Verifiers (Employers/Orgs): Instantly validate credentials without calling the university, ensuring the data hasn't been altered or revoked.

**How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer**
Selective Disclosure: Uses Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) to prove criteria (e.g., "GPA is above 3.5") without revealing the actual GPA, protecting student privacy.
Cryptographic Trust: Every credential is signed with ECDSA and can be anchored to the Polygon blockchain, making forgery mathematically impossible.
Biometric Security: Access to the student wallet is protected by WebAuthn (TouchID/FaceID), ensuring only the owner can share their data.
Automation: Replaces weeks of background checks with a 2-second cryptographic scan.

**Challenges we ran into**

**WebAuthn Cross-Browser Consistency**
The Hurdle: Different browsers (Chrome vs. Safari) and hardware (TouchID vs. Windows Hello) handle biometric "Passkey" prompts differently. Early versions prompted for a fingerprint too frequently, making the app feel slow. 
The Fix: I implemented a Short-Session Grace Window. Once a user successfully authenticates with biometrics, a secure session token is stored in memory. For the next 15 minutes, the user can perform sensitive actions without a re-prompt, balancing security with a premium user experience.

**Ethereum Track**

CredChain fits into the Ethereum/EVM Partner Track by leveraging the core security, decentralization, and privacy-preserving tools of the Ethereum ecosystem:

** EVM Compatibility**
Solidity-Powered Registry: The core logic for anchoring credential hashes is written in Solidity and deployed to Polygon Amoy (an Ethereum Layer 2), making it easily portable to Ethereum Mainnet or any EVM chain.
Standard Tooling: The application uses ethers.js and MetaMask, integrating directly with the standard Ethereum wallet infrastructure for all signed actions.
 Privacy & ZK-Identity (Ethereum Ethos)
ZK-Identity Stack: Following the Ethereum community's push for "ZK-everything," we use Circom and SnarkJS (the same stack used by major Ethereum ZK-protocols) to verify college degrees without exposing raw PII.
Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI): The project aligns with Ethereum’s mission of data ownership, ensuring that students—not institutions—control their identity data via their Ethereum-compatible wallets.

** Scalability & Practicality**
Layer 2 Strategy: By using an EVM-compatible Layer 2, we demonstrate how Ethereum-based identity can be fast and affordable (low gas fees) while maintaining the security guarantees of a global decentralized ledger.
Off-chain/On-chain Balance: We follow the best-practice "Ethereum Pattern" of keeping large data (credentials) off-chain in a privacy-preserving vault, while keeping only the proof of existence (hashes) on the Ethereum/Polygon ledger.

**Blockchain & Decentralized Applications**

CredChain is a decentralized application (dApp) that shifts the "Source of Truth" from centralized databases to the individual and the blockchain.

 How it fits into Blockchain
Immutable Anchoring: Instead of trusting a college's private database, we store a cryptographic SHA-256 hash of every issued credential on the Polygon Amoy network via a smart contract. This creates a permanent, tamper-proof record of "Truth."
Public Verification: Anyone can query the blockchain to see if a specific credential hash exists. This removes the need for a central intermediary (like a background check agency) to confirm authenticity.
Decentralized Trust Registry: The system uses a smart-contract-based "Trust Registry" where reputable colleges can register their public keys, allowing any verifier to confirm an issuer's identity without a middleman.

How it fits into Decentralized Apps (dApps):
Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI): Unlike traditional systems where your data "lives" on a university server, CredChain gives ownership to the student. The credential lives in the Student Wallet, and only the student decides who can see it.
Wallet-Based Authentication: The application uses MetaMask for signing transactions and WebAuthn for biometric security, following the "Not your keys, not your data" principle.
Privacy via ZKP: By using Zero-Knowledge Proofs, the dApp allows "Decentralized Verification" of facts (like a GPA threshold) without actually exposing the underlying private data to the verifier or storing it on-chain.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our biggest challenge was connecting React to the blockchain — unlike a normal API, every write goes through MetaMask, needs user approval, costs gas, and takes seconds to confirm, so we had to carefully manage loading states across every page. The smart contract logic was tricky too — one missing require() check and the entire supply chain enforcement breaks, so we wrote 22 tests to attack our own contract. QR scanning in browsers was unreliable across devices, so we added manual batch ID entry as a fallback. The local Hardhat blockchain loses all data on restart and MetaMask caches old state, which caused nonce errors constantly until we built a one-command seed script to rebuild everything from scratch. And the hardest UX problem was that there's no login system — your wallet IS your identity, so the app has to detect your role from the blockchain on every connection and dynamically show the right dashboard.

**Healthcare**

10% of medicines in developing countries are counterfeit. That kills nearly a million people a year. The core issue is trust — you're trusting paper trails and middlemen to prove a pill is real.
We replaced that trust with math. Every medicine batch gets a blockchain record from the moment it's manufactured. Every handoff is cryptographically signed and permanent. No one can forge it, alter it, or delete it.
The result: any consumer with a phone camera can scan a QR code and know, in under 2 seconds, whether their medicine traveled the correct path from factory to their hands — or whether something is wrong.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

MedChainify addresses the fragmented and disconnected nature of modern healthcare systems, where consultations, laboratories, pharmacies, NGOs, and supply chains operate in isolation. This lack of interoperability leads to inefficiencies such as miscommunication, delays in treatment, and repeated diagnostic procedures. ***By unifying these siloed systems into a single interoperable platform, it significantly streamlines healthcare delivery and coordination.***

### How People Can Use It

Patients can use MedChainify for structured triage, guided care navigation, and seamless sharing of their medical records across providers. This ensures they receive the right care at the right time without losing critical data. Clinicians benefit from standardized records, intelligent case routing, and improved reporting systems, allowing them to make faster and more accurate decisions. ***This reduces unnecessary workload while improving overall care quality.***

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

MedChainify enhances safety and efficiency by introducing verifiable and auditable systems across healthcare operations. Telemedicine interactions become structured and compliant with proper consent and medico-legal traceability. Medicine procurement and logistics are improved with clear tracking of origin, expiry, and delivery. Additionally, NGOs and fundraising processes gain transparency through traceable financial flows and measurable impact tracking. ***This ensures greater trust, accountability, and safety across the entire healthcare ecosystem.***

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### Interoperability Across Disconnected Systems

One of the biggest challenges was designing a system that could unify multiple healthcare actors, patients, clinicians, NGOs, suppliers, and labs, into a single interoperable workflow. Each entity follows different data formats and operational standards, making integration complex. ***The hurdle was ensuring seamless data exchange without forcing existing systems to completely change their infrastructure.***  

To overcome this, we adopted a modular microservices architecture with standardized health data schemas. This allowed each component to function independently while still being interoperable, enabling gradual integration without breaking existing workflows.

### Ensuring Trust, Identity, and Compliance

Another major challenge was handling clinician verification, consent management, and medico-legal auditability. Without proper identity validation and traceability, the system could not be trusted for real-world healthcare usage. ***Building a system that is both secure and compliant while remaining user-friendly was particularly difficult.***  

We addressed this by implementing credential-based onboarding, consent-driven data sharing, and immutable audit trails. This ensured that every interaction is verifiable, traceable, and compliant with emerging digital health standards.

### Making Telemedicine Structured and Auditable

Telemedicine interactions are often unstructured, making them hard to track, audit, or standardize. This created a challenge in converting conversations into meaningful, structured medical data. ***The difficulty was maintaining both usability and clinical accuracy while structuring these interactions.***  

We solved this by integrating AI-driven workflows such as symptom classification and structured reporting, which transform raw consultations into standardized, usable medical records.

### Supply Chain Transparency and Traceability

Tracking medicine provenance, expiry, and last-mile delivery posed another significant hurdle. Traditional systems lack transparency, making it difficult to verify authenticity and delivery status. ***Ensuring end-to-end visibility without adding operational overhead was a key challenge.***  

To tackle this, we introduced a verifiable supply-chain layer with batch-level tracking, expiry monitoring, and delivery attestations, ensuring transparency without disrupting existing logistics processes.

### Coordinating NGO Operations and Fund Flows

Managing NGO campaigns involves synchronizing staffing, inventory, and funding, which is often fragmented and opaque. ***The challenge was creating a system that could track both financial flows and real-world impact in a transparent manner.***  

We overcame this by building an orchestration layer that links resources, funds, and outcomes with auditable tracking, enabling better coordination and trust among stakeholders.

**Healthcare**

MedChainify fits into the healthcare track by directly addressing critical inefficiencies in the healthcare ecosystem, including fragmented care delivery, lack of interoperability, poor data portability, and unstructured telemedicine workflows, by introducing a unified platform that integrates patients, clinicians, NGOs, and supply chains into a single interoperable system; it enhances healthcare delivery through AI-driven triage, structured electronic health records, compliant teleconsultation, and intelligent care routing while also ensuring transparency and trust via verifiable supply chains, credentialed clinician onboarding, and auditable medical and financial processes, ultimately improving care accessibility, operational efficiency, and patient outcomes across the entire healthcare industry

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Building and shipping Web3 frontends is still too manual for most teams.  
Developers often have to stitch together cloning, building, environment setup, IPFS upload, gateway verification, and deployment tracking across multiple tools.

This project simplifies that process into one deployment workflow.

## What You Can Use It For

- Deploy static dApps from a GitHub repository directly to IPFS.
- Handle React and static HTML projects with minimal configuration.
- Stream live deployment logs for faster debugging.
- Track deployment history by project and wallet identity.
- Support webhook-style auto deploys after repo updates.

## Why It Is Easier and Safer

- Removes repetitive deployment steps and manual handoffs.
- Reduces build/output misconfiguration with automatic detection and sensible defaults.
- Protects secrets by rejecting non-public environment variable keys for static IPFS output.
- Improves reliability with deployment concurrency limits and cleanup of temp workspaces.
- Produces immutable, shareable IPFS release artifacts with recorded metadata.

## Typical Users

- Web3 founders shipping landing pages or lightweight dApps.
- Teams that want Vercel-like deployment flow for IPFS-hosted apps.
- Builders who need wallet-linked deployment auditability and reproducible releases.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Monorepo root detection kept picking the wrong folder
At first, deployments failed because the build was running in the repo root instead of the actual frontend directory.  
I fixed this by adding smarter root selection: explicit `rootDirectory` support first, then fallback scoring based on frontend dependencies, React file markers, and folder naming hints.

### 2. `npm install` broke on peer dependency conflicts
Some projects failed with `ERESOLVE` during install, even though the app itself was valid.  
I solved this by retrying `npm install` with `--legacy-peer-deps` only when a peer conflict is detected, so normal installs stay strict while problematic ones still succeed.

### 3. Build output assumptions were too rigid
Early on, the pipeline expected one output folder and would fail if frameworks used a different one.  
I handled this by supporting configurable `outputDirectory` and scanning common build outputs (`dist`, `build`, `out`) before failing.

### 4. Static sites broke on IPFS because of absolute asset URLs
Some HTML sites loaded locally but failed on IPFS because assets used root-absolute paths like `/assets/app.js`.  
I added a rewrite step that converts root-absolute asset paths to relative paths during deployment so the site works from CID-based routes.

### 5. Risk of leaking secrets into static bundles
Users sometimes provided backend-only env vars during deploy. Exposing those in static output is unsafe.  
I introduced a strict allowlist (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, `VITE_*`, `REACT_APP_*`, `PUBLIC_*`) and hard-blocked everything else with a clear error message.

### 6. Gateway URL reliability after upload
A successful IPFS upload did not always mean the first gateway URL was immediately usable.  
I added gateway reachability probing and canonical URL normalization so users get a working, stable link more consistently.

### 7. Debugging long deploys was painful without live feedback
Silent waits during clone/build/upload made failures hard to diagnose.  
I switched to streaming logs over SSE end-to-end, so each stage reports progress and errors in real time.

**Web3**

This project is not just a normal web deploy tool with crypto branding. Its core workflow uses Web3-native principles:

It deploys apps to IPFS, so sites are content-addressed and immutable by CID instead of relying on a centralized server.
It uses wallet identity as part of deployment authorization and ownership, which maps naturally to decentralized user identity.
It enforces safer frontend env handling for decentralized hosting, preventing accidental exposure of backend secrets in public static outputs.
It produces verifiable, shareable artifact links through IPFS gateways, making releases transparent and reproducible.
It is designed for dApp teams shipping static Web3 frontends (wallet connect, contract UI) where decentralized hosting is a real requirement.

**AI/ML**

## Why it is a best fit for the AI/ML track

This project fits the AI/ML category because it uses **Smolify AI** to make deployment decisions automatically.

- It classifies incoming projects as **React** or **HTML** from repo signals.
- It removes manual setup by auto-selecting the correct deployment path.
- It reduces user error in framework detection and build/output handling.
- It makes deployment faster for non-expert users by turning a multi-step technical task into an intelligent one-click flow.

In short, the core value is not only deployment, but **AI-assisted deployment intelligence**: understanding project type and choosing the right execution strategy automatically.

**Open Innovation**

## Why this is a strong fit for Open Innovation

This project is a strong Open Innovation candidate because it is built to be reused, extended, and integrated by many different builders, not locked to one team workflow.

- It is composable: developers can plug in their own repos, frameworks, and deployment settings without changing core architecture.
- It lowers entry barriers: teams can ship to IPFS without deep DevOps knowledge, which helps more people participate.
- It is integration-friendly: API + streaming logs + MCP-style tooling make it easy to connect with IDEs, automations, and external platforms.
- It promotes transparent outputs: IPFS CIDs create verifiable, shareable artifacts that others can inspect and build on.
- It encodes reusable safeguards: env-variable filtering, output detection, and deployment guardrails are patterns other teams can adopt directly.
- It supports community iteration: webhook deploy flow and modular backend logic make contributions and feature experiments straightforward.

In short, it enables collaborative building across teams, tools, and ecosystems, which is exactly the core value of Open Innovation.

**Requestly**

Why It Fits This Project

We have complex API flow and streaming deploy logs, so we need fast request-level control.
We depend on third-party services, so failure simulation is critical.
We need fast iteration in a hackathon, so no-code request mocking and rewriting saves hours.
We need reproducible debugging for team demos, so shared Requestly rules are perfect.
Concrete Project Mapping

Deploy streaming endpoint at deploy.ts:1032: simulate 429, 500, slow responses, and partial stream errors.
SSE success/error behavior at deploy.ts:1192 and deploy.ts:1202: validate frontend handling for both outcomes.
Login/OAuth flow at page.tsx:14: test token missing/invalid/expired paths quickly.
Frontend deploy UX at page.tsx:176: verify retry/cancel/error messaging under network manipulation.

**Algorand**

Algoflow uses Algorand as an on-chain database to store and verify deployment events for frontend applications. Instead of relying on traditional centralized databases, each deployment is recorded as a transaction on Algorand, creating a permanent, tamper-proof history.

Whenever a user deploys a project, metadata such as project ID, deployment timestamp, IPFS CID, and ownership information is encoded and pushed to the blockchain. This ensures that every deployment is publicly verifiable and cannot be altered or deleted.

By leveraging Algorand’s fast finality and low transaction costs, Algoflow provides a reliable and scalable way to maintain deployment records. The system can reconstruct project history directly from on-chain data, making it a trustworthy source of truth.

In this architecture, Algorand acts as a decentralized backend database, enhancing transparency, ownership verification, and auditability for deployed applications.

# The Problem TARK Solves

Cyber scams are growing rapidly in both scale and sophistication.  
Users are constantly targeted through phishing links, fake KYC updates, OTP fraud, and impersonation messages.

The biggest challenge is not just identifying scams, but **understanding them and taking action in time**.



## ❗ Key Problems

###  1. Lack of Awareness
Most users cannot distinguish between:
- Real vs fake bank messages  
- Legitimate vs phishing links  
- Safe vs malicious requests  

Scammers exploit this gap using urgency, fear, and authority.

---

###  2. Generic & Unreliable Tools
Existing solutions:
- Provide **generic warnings**
- Rely heavily on **black-box**
- Do not explain *why* something is a scam  

👉 This reduces trust and usability

---

### 3. No Actionable Output
Even if a scam is detected:
- Users don’t know what to do next  
- Reporting to authorities is complicated  
- No structured evidence is generated  

---

### 4. Privacy Risks
Scam messages often contain:
- Phone numbers  
- Aadhaar details  
- Banking information  

Sending this data to AI systems can lead to **privacy violations**


# 💡 How TARK Solves This

## 🧠 1. Intelligent Scam Analysis
TARK analyzes messages using a **multi-layer AI system** to:
- Detect scam type (KYC, OTP, phishing)
- Identify manipulation techniques (urgency, fear, authority)
- Provide confidence and reasoning

---

## 🔍 2. Explainable Output
Instead of just saying “this is a scam,” TARK explains:
- Why it is a scam, exposes links
- What techniques are being used  
- What risks are involved  

👉 Builds **user trust and awareness**

---

## 🔗 3. Link Safety Detection
- Extracts URLs from messages  
- Flags suspicious domains  
- Identifies phishing patterns  

---

## 📄 4. One-Click Report Generation
- Generates a **professional, structured PDF report**
- Includes analysis, evidence, and blockchain proof  
- Allows users to **directly report to cybercrime authorities via Gmail**

---

## 🔒 5. Privacy-First Processing (🤏 Smolify)
- Masks sensitive data before analysis  
- Ensures no personal information is exposed  
- Enables safe AI usage  

---

## 🔗 6. Tamper-Proof Evidence (Algorand)
- Stores hash of scam data on blockchain  
- Provides verifiable proof for investigations  
- Ensures integrity of reports  

---

# 🚀 Real-World Use Cases

- 🧑‍💻 Users verifying suspicious messages before acting  
- 🏛️ Citizens reporting scams to cybercrime departments  
- 🏦 Banks detecting phishing patterns  
- 📱 Integration into apps for real-time scam detection  
- 🎓 Awareness and training for digital safety  

---

# 🌟 Impact

TARK transforms the process from:

❌ Confusion → ❌ Fear → ❌ Inaction  

to:

✅ Detection → ✅ Understanding → ✅ Action  

---

> TARK doesn’t just detect scams — it empowers users to respond intelligently and safely.

**Challenges we ran into**

# From Challenges We Ran Into to Finding their Solutions

---

## 🔹 1. RAG Not Returning Meaningful Violations
**Problem:** Retrieved chunks lacked source/context, leading to vague outputs like “Violation: NONE”  
**Solution:**  
- Added structured metadata (title, category, violation) to Pinecone  
- Implemented **hybrid fallback (hardcoded policy)** when retrieval fails  

---

## 🔹 2. Gmail Link Breaking (Report Feature)
**Problem:** Email links failed due to extremely long, unencoded body content  
**Solution:**  
- Proper URL encoding using `urllib.parse.quote`  
- Reduced email body to **summary only**, moved full data to PDF  

---

## 🔹 3. API Rate Limits (Embeddings)**
**Problem:** Batch embedding requests caused rate limit errors  
**Solution:**  
- Implemented batching + retry logic  
- Added delays **sleep** between requests  

---

## 🔹 4. Privacy Concerns in User Input
**Problem:** Scam inputs contained sensitive data (phone, Aadhaar, etc.)  
**Solution:**  
- Integrated 🤏 **Smolify** as a local masking layer before processing  

---

## 🔹 5. “LLM Wrapper” Perception
**Problem:** Risk of being seen as just an LLM-based system  
**Solution:**  
- Introduced **dataset-driven vector search (RAG)**  
- Positioned LLM only for explanation, not detection  

---

## 🔹 6. Inconsistent Scam Classification
**Problem:** Pure LLM outputs were sometimes inconsistent  
**Solution:**  
- Added **retrieval-based grounding + heuristic checks**  
- Ensured deterministic fallback logic  

---

## 🔹 7. Lack of Trust in Generated Reports
**Problem:** Reports could be questioned for authenticity  
**Solution:**  
- Integrated **Algorand blockchain** to store hash + TX ID  
- Made reports **tamper-proof and verifiable**

---

# ✅ Key Learning

> Building reliable AI systems requires combining:
> **ML + structured data + fallback logic + trust layers**, not just LLMs.

**Web3**

# Web3 Track ( Algorand )

## TARK Fits 😉

TARK integrates **Algorand blockchain** to bring **trust, transparency, and immutability** into cybercrime reporting.

In real-world investigations, one of the biggest challenges is ensuring that digital evidence is **authentic and untampered**.  
TARK solves this by anchoring scam analysis data onto the blockchain.

---

## ⚙️ Implementation

#### 🔹 1. Data Hashing
- After scam analysis, TARK generates a **cryptographic hash** of:
  - Input message
  - Analysis output
  - Report data

---

#### 🔹 2. Blockchain Storage (Algorand)
- The hash is stored on the **Algorand blockchain**
- A unique **Transaction ID (TX ID)** is generated

---

#### 🔹 3. Report Integration
- The TX ID is embedded into the generated PDF report
- Acts as a **verifiable reference for authorities**

---

### 🧾 Example
```
TX ID: XUUKBG7NUMDKA5ZA...
HASH: b8d5561187a74eae...
```


---

## 🚀 Why Algorand?

- ⚡ Fast finality (instant confirmation)
- 💸 Low transaction cost
- 🔐 High security and decentralization
- 🌍 Scalable infrastructure

---

## 🌐 Impact

- Ensures **tamper-proof evidence**
- Enables **verifiable cybercrime reporting**
- Builds **trust between users and law enforcement**
- Bridges **AI + Blockchain for real-world use**

> With Algorand, TARK transforms scam reports into **immutable digital evidence**.

**AI/ML**

# AI/ML Track

### 🧠 How TARK Fits

Built as a **multi-layered AI/ML system** designed specifically for cyber scam detection, analysis, and response having 3 AI Agents.

Unlike traditional solutions that rely solely on generic LLMs, TARK uses a **hybrid architecture combining machine learning, retrieval systems, and AI reasoning**.

---

## ⚙️ Implementation

####  1. Dataset-Driven Detection (Core ML Layer)
- Scam messages are converted into embeddings using a **local embedding model**
- Stored in a **vector database (Pinecone)**
- Incoming inputs are matched against known scam patterns using **semantic similarity**
- Enables **data-driven classification (e.g., KYC scam, OTP scam, phishing)**

---

#### 2. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Relevant scam patterns and policy contexts are retrieved from the vector database
- Ensures responses are **grounded in real data**, not hallucinated

---

#### 3. AI Reasoning Layer
- LLM is used only for:
  - Explanation of scam
  - Psychological analysis (urgency, fear, authority)
  - Report generation
- Not used for core detection → reduces hallucination risk

---

#### 4. Privacy Layer (🤏 Smolify)
- Sensitive data is masked before processing
- Ensures **privacy-preserving ML pipeline**

---

## 🚀 Impact

- Moves beyond “black-box AI” → **Explainable AI system**
- Combines **ML + RAG + reasoning**
- Reduces false positives and hallucinations
- Provides **actionable intelligence, not just predictions**

> TARK represents a **production-grade AI system**, not just an LLM wrapper.

## 🤏 Smolify 💖 Preserving Privacy in TARK

### **Fits Perfectly**

Processes highly sensitive user inputs such as scam messages, screenshots, and call transcripts, which often contain personal data like phone numbers, Aadhaar numbers, and banking details.

To address this, we integrated **Smolify 🤏 as a pre-processing privacy layer** before any AI or analysis pipeline.

### 🔒 Implementation

- All incoming data is passed through Smolify 🤏 locally
- Sensitive entities are masked:
  - `+91 9907341627 → [PHONE_NO1]`
  - `4200 6974 XXXX → [AADHAAR_1]`
- This ensures that **no personally identifiable information is exposed** to downstream models

### 🚀 Impact

- Enables **privacy-first AI processing**
- Prevents **data leakage to LLMs or external APIs**
- Maintains **semantic structure** for accurate scam detection
- Aligns with **ethical AI and data protection principles**

> Smolify 🤏 allows TARK to be both intelligent and privacy-compliant.

**Algorand**

# Algorand track

## TARK Fits 😉

TARK integrates **Algorand blockchain** to bring **trust, transparency, and immutability** into cybercrime reporting.

In real-world investigations, one of the biggest challenges is ensuring that digital evidence is **authentic and untampered**.  
TARK solves this by anchoring scam analysis data onto the blockchain.

---

## ⚙️ Implementation

#### 🔹 1. Data Hashing
- After scam analysis, TARK generates a **cryptographic hash** of:
  - Input message
  - Analysis output
  - Report data

---

#### 🔹 2. Blockchain Storage (Algorand)
- The hash is stored on the **Algorand blockchain**
- A unique **Transaction ID (TX ID)** is generated

---

#### 🔹 3. Report Integration
- The TX ID is embedded into the generated PDF report
- Acts as a **verifiable reference for authorities**

---

### 🧾 Example
```
TX ID: XUUKBG7NUMDKA5ZA...
HASH: b8d5561187a74eae...
```


---

## 🚀 Why Algorand?

- ⚡ Fast finality (instant confirmation)
- 💸 Low transaction cost
- 🔐 High security and decentralization
- 🌍 Scalable infrastructure

---

## 🌐 Impact

- Ensures **tamper-proof evidence**
- Enables **verifiable cybercrime reporting**
- Builds **trust between users and law enforcement**
- Bridges **AI + Blockchain for real-world use**

> With Algorand, TARK transforms scam reports into **immutable digital evidence**.

> Immutable GL audits from SAP to smart contracts

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![Celery](https://img.shields.io/badge/Celery-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3.py](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3.py-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

A General Ledger lifecycle has 4 stages:-

Preparer → Reviewer → Finance Controller → Department Head

FC and Dept. Head belong to a department under the parent company, however, preparers and reviewers are entities that belong to the parent company. They may be involved with multiple departments, dealing with GL data recorded in multiple sources like SAP ERPs or traditional storages.

This involves entrusting entities from outside your department to preparer GL data for your financial ledgers and review them.

Our system introduces 0% ownership and 100% accountability to the existing system using Web3 technologies.

Instead of relying on a centralized backend as the source of truth, the system uses blockchain to enforce workflow integrity at the protocol level. Every action: submission, review, approval, is a signed transaction tied to a verifiable identity (through wallet token). Roles and permissions are enforced on-chain, making it impossible to bypass approval hierarchies even if the backend is compromised.

Supporting documents are stored on IPFS with content-based hashes which are also appended to the smart contract.

Audit trail can easily be generated as every information is stored in our immutable contracts for each General Ledger Account.

**Challenges we ran into**

Interacting with smart contracts from the frontend (via Ethers.js) and backend (via Web3.py) introduced significant debugging complexity.

Unlike traditional RBAC stored in a database, permissions in this system are enforced via smart contracts. Designing this in Solidity (OrgRegistry) was difficult.

Uploading files to IPFS (via Pinata) and ensuring their integrity using hashes added another layer of complexity.

Working with Hardhat locally was smooth, but deploying and testing on Sepolia introduced issues like RPC inconsistencies and ABIs issues :')

**Web3**

In a General Ledger lifecycle, the initial two stages involve GL preparation and GL review, conducted by entities outside your department/organization. 

These entities are individuals who may operate for multiple departments. Thus, trust plays a major role.

To centralize their contributions across multiple departments, we've created a system that removes the necessity of user & role management.

Auth works cryptographically through a wallet pairing. Roles and permissions are stored on-chain.

Each GL assigned represents a smart contract and all state changes like approvals, rejections, etc. + reconciliation notes, are appended to the blockchain.

This enables trustless auditability.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves :

Modern digital environments expose individuals and communities to multiple threats such as device theft, privacy violations, stalking, emergency situations, and unauthorized access to personal data. In many cases, users are unable to react quickly because existing safety tools require manual interaction or are not integrated into a single platform.

Current safety solutions are often fragmented, one app for emergency alerts, another for phone protection, another for tracking. This lack of integration reduces response time during critical situations.

Trap Eye solves this problem by creating an integrated digital safety ecosystem that combines real-time monitoring, emergency response mechanisms, smart device protection, and community-based threat reporting into one platform.

The goal is to reduce reaction time during emergencies and improve personal digital security through automation and intelligent triggers.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cb56f368e9354f118c8822d5923f1410/07f8be4f-f0d9-4bcc-9038-abc0623b2891.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Real-Time Sensor Detection Reliability
One of the first challenges was implementing the **shake-to-activate safety feature**. Mobile accelerometer data can be noisy, and small phone movements were sometimes falsely triggering the safety mode.

**Solution**

To solve this, we implemented a **threshold-based motion detection algorithm** that filters raw accelerometer data and only triggers the event when the motion intensity crosses a defined limit. This reduced false positives and made the feature more reliable.

---

### 2. Real-Time Location Updates
Another challenge was ensuring that the user's **live location updates continuously during an emergency**. Initial implementations caused delays or stopped updating when the app moved to the background.

**Solution**

We solved this by integrating **background location services** along with real-time database updates. Location coordinates are periodically pushed to the backend, allowing trusted contacts to see live movement without interruption.

---

### 3. Instant Emergency Notifications
Sending alerts instantly to emergency contacts was initially inconsistent due to network delays and message delivery issues.

**Solution**

We implemented **Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)** for push notifications and optimized backend event triggers using **NestJS services**, ensuring that emergency alerts are delivered in real time.

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves:

EquiChain addresses the hidden inequality in AI-driven digital labor, where “ghost workers” responsible for data labeling, content moderation, and model training are underpaid, unrecognized, and exposed to harmful content.

Currently, there is:

No standardized wage system, leading to arbitrary and unfair payments

Lack of transparency, where payments and task records are controlled by platforms

No worker identity or verification, making workers invisible in the ecosystem

Exposure to harmful content without informed consent or safety measures

No accountability for companies, even when exploitative practices occur

How EquiChain solves this

EquiChain introduces a fair, transparent, and accountable system using AI + Blockchain:

A Fair Wage Engine ensures compensation is based on task complexity, time, and risk eliminating underpayment

A Blockchain Ledger records every task and payment immutably, preventing manipulation and ensuring trust

MetaMask-based transactions provide secure and verifiable payment authorization

An AI Risk Detection system analyzes datasets to identify harmful content before assignment

A Monitoring system tracks company behavior and enforces penalties for repeated violations

A Compliance ESG layer ensures companies follow ethical standards and provides audit-ready transparency

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into:

AI and Blockchain integration: ML outputs are probabilistic, while blockchain needs fixed values.
Solved using a controlled pipeline where only validated fair wage is sent on-chain.

Smart contract enforcement: Preventing manipulation of wages.
Added validation logic in settleTask.

MetaMask integration: Handling wallet connection and transaction delays.
Implemented network checks and proper transaction handling.

Lack of dataset: No standard wage dataset available.
Used hybrid data (real-world + synthetic).

**The problem it solves**

****For Video Explanation -****

https://youtu.be/6R-7GleQthg

*To try First hand create a account.*

******For PPT******
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1XDQ6iUjXl_cLz6fg0zuvlGBx4Ltkd2hZ/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=105153641341170148707&rtpof=true&sd=true

**The core problem**
Every time you prove something about yourself online. your age, your citizenship, your employment status, your medical eligibility. you typically hand over far more data than the question actually requires.
ex-To prove you're over 18, you show a passport → the verifier sees your full name, date of birth, nationality, and passport number.

**What a ZKP Credential Verifier does**
A Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) Credential Verifier lets a user cryptographically prove a claim is true — without revealing the underlying data that makes it true.
The math guarantees: the verifier learns the answer to their question (yes/no), and nothing else.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cc6f9b6245d443e489b8915414fa653a/ff6779a4-5de2-4af5-ad55-d96789cfcef9.png)

*Use cases*-
1.Age & identity verification
2.🏥 Healthcare & insurance
3.🎓 Professional credentials & licenses
4.🏛️ Government & civic systems
5.💳 Financial services & credit
6.🔐 Access control & corporate systems
7.🌐 Web3 & decentralised apps

*Who benefits most*

Users — stop over-sharing personal data as a condition of participation
Verifiers — stop storing sensitive data they don't need (and are liable for)
Regulators — compliance checks can happen without creating new surveillance infrastructure
Developers — can build privacy-respecting auth flows without a centralised identity server

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Windows environment (chmod, RUST_LOG, shell scripts)
Unix commands don't work in CMD. Switched to Git Bash for all development — it handles Unix syntax natively without any changes to the scripts.

2. OneDrive file locking (os error 32)
OneDrive and Windows Defender locked Rust's build artifacts mid-compile. Added Defender exclusions for cargo.exe and rustc.exe, and marked the target/ folder with +P to stop OneDrive syncing it.

3. Rust edition2024 not supported (Cargo 1.84.0)
getrandom v0.4.2 required edition2024 which needed Cargo 1.85+. Ran rustup update stable to upgrade the toolchain and added rust-toolchain.toml to pin the version for the whole project.

4. npm audit stuck on underscore vulnerability
snarkjs pulls in underscore <=1.13.7 through bfj → jsonpath — npm audit fix couldn't touch it. Added "overrides": { "underscore": "^1.13.6" } to package.json and re-ran npm install.

5. Missing Rust source files (E0583)
issuer.rs and verifier.rs were declared in mod.rs but never created on disk. Ran touch to create the files and added stub handler functions returning placeholder JSON.

6. Missing Rust imports and crates (E0433, E0599, E0282)
hex crate was used but missing from Cargo.toml, sha2::Digest trait wasn't imported, and verify_groth16 needed a type annotation. Fixed with cargo add hex, added use sha2::Digest, and annotated the return type as bool.

7. Git push rejected (non-fast-forward)
GitHub auto-created a README on repo init, making remote history diverge from local. Ran git pull origin main --rebase to sync, then pushed successfully.

Krishna Khasge

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional event ticketing is plagued by scalping, fraud, and lack of transparency. Centralized platforms like Ticketmaster control ticket supply, enable bots to bulk-purchase tickets, and allow counterfeit tickets to circulate — leaving fans overpaying or getting scammed.

TicketChain solves this by turning every ticket into an ERC-721 NFT on Ethereum:

🎫 No counterfeits — ticket ownership is verified on-chain; fakes are cryptographically impossible
🤖 No bots / scalping — smart contract enforces maxSupply and pricing rules transparently
🔍 Instant verification — anyone can verify a ticket's authenticity by checking the blockchain (no QR scanner needed, no middleman)
💼 True ownership — buyers hold their ticket in their own wallet; it can't be revoked by a platform or payment processor
📦 Decentralized metadata — ticket details (event, date, venue, holder) are stored on IPFS via Pinata, not on a company's server that can go down
It makes existing ticketing trustless, transparent, and tamper-proof — without needing to trust any central authority.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the first challenges we faced was keeping the frontend in sync with the smart contract. Every time we redeployed the contract locally, the contract address changed, which meant we had to manually update the frontend configuration. We solved this by introducing a clean .env-based setup so the address and ABI could be swapped out without touching the source code.

Deploying to the Sepolia testnet was more involved than expected. We ran into issues with incorrect RPC URLs, insufficient test ETH, and MetaMask being connected to the wrong network simultaneously — making it difficult to isolate which layer was failing. Working through each one methodically helped us arrive at a stable deployment.

Integrating IPFS metadata storage through Pinata introduced CORS-related issues when making API calls directly from the browser. We also found that when API keys were missing or incorrect, the minting flow would fail silently with no clear error. We addressed this by adding a local fallback URI for development environments so the app remains functional without a Pinata setup.

Finally, handling MetaMask's network detection required extra attention. When a user is connected to the wrong network, ethers.js surfaces a generic error that isn't user-friendly. We added explicit network validation before any contract interaction to guide users to switch networks properly.
