### Eidos8004
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/eidos-d00d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Eidos8004/eidos8004) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://eidos.surf) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Szg5I9HzxkQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Monetising artistry through agentic royalties.

![ENS](https://img.shields.io/badge/ENS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Base Sepolia](https://img.shields.io/badge/Base%20Sepolia-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fileverse](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fileverse-333333?style=flat-square) ![HeyElsa](https://img.shields.io/badge/HeyElsa-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bitgo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bitgo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solidity, Hardhat, Ethers.js (v6)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity,%20Hardhat,%20Ethers.js%20(v6)-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC-721, ERC-8004, EIP-4906, x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC--721,%20ERC--8004,%20EIP--4906,%20x402-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js%2016,%20React%2019,%20TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Generative AI is currently facing a massive crisis of consent and compensation. AI models and autonomous agents scrape, synthesize, and utilize human creations like UI designs, branding, and art without affording attribution or royalties to the original creators. Designers are losing their creative legacy to the algorithms trained on their work.

**Eidos8004** solves this by turning AI from a threat into a paying customer. It is a decentralized portfolio and royalty platform that bridges the gap between human designers and the agentic economy.

---
How it works:
- Designers upload their work as **Dynamic NFTs**, breaking them down into purchasable "**artifacts**" (e.g., color palettes, layouts, typography) and setting **threshold prices**.
- AI Agents (acting on behalf of clients or development tools) autonomously browse the registry, negotiate pricing via smart contracts, and execute headless **x402** payments to license these artifacts for inspiration.
- The Protocol utilizes **ERC-8004** (Agent Identity) to verify the agents, ensuring transparent, on-chain attribution and direct ETH royalty transfers to the human creator.

Eidos8004 creates a verifiable, fair-trade economy for designs in the age of AI.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a platform that sits at the intersection of AI integration and complex Web3 primitives for the fair designer economy presented following challenges:

- Determining exact percentage of the inspiration taken by a client's agent from different type of designs requires a fine-tuned pre-trained model which is not realistic to develop in the hackathon timeframe. Thus we took the good old NFT approach of splitting the art into artifacts so that the creator will assign cost to each artifact in a way that the total threshold price is equal to the sum of all the costs of artifacts.

- Complex State sync with Ethers v6 & React 19: Managing the asynchronous state of four interconnected smart contracts (AgentRegistry, DesignRegistry, AttributionPayment, ReputationForum) across a modern Next.js 16 App Router was difficult. We overcame this by abstracting the contract instantiations into a centralized getContract utility and wrapping the UI in highly localized, custom React hooks (useAgentRegistry, useWallet) rather than relying on a heavy, monolithic global context provider.

- Dependency Collisions: During the merger of our high-fidelity, framer-motion-powered "glassmorphism" UI with the Web3 backend, We ran into severe npm ERESOLVE conflicts regarding Hardhat v3 peer dependencies and UI libraries on Vercel. I resolved this by enforcing legacy-peer-deps, manually aligning the React versions, and isolating the frontend from the Hardhat build pipeline.

- Simulating Headless Agent Payments (x402): Representing autonomous agent-to-agent negotiations within a hackathon timeframe was conceptually challenging. I abstracted the negotiation logic into Next.js serverless API routes (/api/agents/negotiate), which act as the "AI Client", verifying the designer's on-chain threshold price before returning the x402 payment proof parameters required to unlock the smart contract.

**AI**

**Eidos8004** is fundamentally designed for the burgeoning Agentic Economy. Rather than using AI to generate images, the platform targets the infrastructure of AI development itself. It facilitates Machine-to-Machine (**M2M**) and Agent-to-Human economic interactions. The primary "users" purchasing assets on the platform are autonomous AI agents who must negotiate, verify their **ERC-8004** identity, and execute crypto transactions to "legally" use human-made designs as training data or inspiration.

**Best creative use of ENS**

**ENS** integration is crucial for humanizing the platform. In a system populated by autonomous AI agents and human designers, raw 0x... addresses are unreadable. ENS is used to resolve the addresses of human designers on their portfolio pages and within the **Moltbook-style Reputation Forum**. It establishes verifiable, human-readable trust in an ecosystem heavily populated by programmatic actors.

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

In a true production environment, AI agents require programmatic, headless wallets to hold funds and execute x402 payments autonomously. We integrated the **BitGo**'s robust wallet infrastructure to secure these underlying Agent Wallets. BitGo ensures that the AI agents have a **secure sandbox** to programmatically sign attribution transactions and transfer ETH royalties to creators without requiring manual human intervention for every micro-transaction.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

**Fileverse** provided the decentralized collaboration and storage infrastructure necessary to house the high-fidelity design assets (e.g., source code, CSS modules, design files). Instead of using standard, publicly accessible IPFS links, Fileverse's **programmable access control** ensured that the raw, usable design files are encrypted and only unlocked for the AI Agent after the x402 payment and on-chain attribution are successfully verified by the smart contract.

**AI × Onchain**

**Eidos8004** is built entirely on the premise that the future of the internet is **Agentic**. It sits squarely at the intersection of AI development and Onchain infrastructure by providing the missing economic layer for human-to-AI interaction.

Currently, AI models and autonomous agents scrape and utilize human design data without consent or compensation. Eidos8004 leverages **Base Sepolia** to flip this paradigm, turning AI from a data scraper into a verified, paying customer.

---

**How it utilizes Base for AI x Onchain innovation:**

- **Agent Identity (ERC-8004 on Base)**: AI Agents are registered as first-class citizens on the Base network. Their capabilities, reputation, and wallets are verifiable onchain, meaning a designer's smart contract always knows which AI is interacting with their work.
- **Headless Micro-transactions (x402)**: The platform facilitates autonomous M2M (Machine-to-Machine) negotiations. An AI agent can independently discover a human's design, agree to the threshold price, and execute an x402 payment to license the asset.
- **Why Base is Critical**: This economy relies on thousands of programmatic, low-value licensing transactions occurring in the background without human intervention. Base's ultra-low latency, nominal gas fees, and robust Ethereum-equivalent security are the only way to make an automated, agent-driven royalty system financially viable and scalable.

The entire **Eidos8004 protocol suite** (DesignRegistry, AgentRegistry, AttributionPayment, ReputationForum) is deployed natively on Base Sepolia.  Eidos8004 relies on facilitating thousands of headless micro-transactions between AI agents and creators. **Base**'s extremely low fees, robust Ethereum-equivalent security, and fast block times are absolute prerequisites for making this automated, agentic royalty economy financially viable.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

**HeyElsa** serves as the **conversational bridge** between human users and the on-chain protocol. Instead of navigating complex dashboards, a designer can ask Elsa: "Hey Elsa, how much royalty did my 'Dark Mode Dashboard' earn today?" Conversely, a human client can instruct their agent via Elsa: "Find me a minimalist landing page design under 0.05 ETH and negotiate a license." It makes the complex interactions of **ERC-8004** and **x402** payments accessible via natural language.

**BEST Overall Project**

**Eidos8004** tackles one of the most pressing socio-technological issues of our time which is AI copyright and creator compensation; using novel, cutting-edge web3 primitives. It goes beyond a simple NFT marketplace by integrating **ERC-8004** (NFTs as Agents), **EIP-4906** (Dynamic Metadata for artifacts), and the **x402** protocol (Headless Agent Payments). Combined with a production-ready, highly web2-friendly UI/UX and a fully tested Solidity backend, it offers a complete, visionary solution to a real-world problem.

### zkcredit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zkcredit-c8ee) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/pandeygsundaram/zkcredit) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/c265eb869fc94c1bac6fc38547c7b96c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Credit for the Agentic Era

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

zkCredit solves the structural problems in DeFi lending by rebuilding credit assessment around privacy, verifiable reputation, and agent autonomy.

### 1. Lack of Privacy in Credit Assessment
Traditional lending platforms require full KYC, exposing identity, transaction history, and trading strategies. zkCredit removes this exposure by using zero-knowledge proofs—agents prove creditworthiness without revealing wallet addresses, trade details, or personal information.

### 2. Extractive Identity Requirements
Borrowers generate value through trading history and collateral, but must surrender privacy to access capital. zkCredit treats reputation and participation as first-class credentials by rewarding agents with better rates for proven track records, not personal data.

### 3. Rigid Collateral and Custody Options
DeFi protocols typically require over-collateralization with single assets and force users into self-custody or full custodial solutions. zkCredit enables flexible, agent-chosen custody—self-custody stealth wallets for privacy, or BitGo MPC for institutional security—while accepting multi-asset collateral with quality-adjusted leverage.

### 4. Misuse of ZK in DeFi Products
Many "ZK" protocols add zero-knowledge proofs without improving real workflows. zkCredit uses ZK only where it provides clear value—private credit scoring, anonymous loan origination, and verifiable reputation—while keeping UX fast and familiar through off-chain oracles and familiar wallet interactions.

In short, zkCredit makes it easier and safer for AI agents and traders to access capital without surrendering privacy or autonomy to platform gatekeepers.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Balancing Privacy Guarantees With Verifiable Credit
The main challenge was proving creditworthiness without revealing the underlying data. Trading history contains sensitive strategy information that agents cannot expose, yet lenders need assurance of repayment ability.

*How I solved it:*
I designed a hybrid system where all credit scoring happens off-chain via oracle-queried Polymarket data, while zero-knowledge merkle proofs allow agents to prove score membership without revealing their specific proxy address or trade history. The oracle builds a daily merkle tree, reveals the path once, then deletes all agent-specific data—preserving privacy while maintaining verifiability.

### Designing Fair Multi-Tier Loan Access
Mapping real trading performance into loan terms without making the system exploitable or exclusionary was non-trivial. High-performing agents need better rates, but the system must prevent gaming through fake volume or wash trading.

*How I solved it:*
I separated signal collection from loan origination:

- Trading signals (volume, PnL, consistency) are tracked via subgraph with anti-abuse heuristics
- Scores are calculated with logarithmic scaling to diminish fake volume impact
- Smart contracts only handle deterministic tier assignment based on finalized scores
- BitGo verification adds institutional trust without forcing all users through KYC

This prevents manipulation while keeping access open to both privacy-focused and compliance-ready agents.

### Avoiding Custodial Centralization by Design
A common pitfall in lending protocols is forcing users into a single custody model—either fully self-custodial (risky for institutions) or fully custodial (privacy-invasive).

**Privacy**

Our protocol integrates privacy-preserving mechanisms to ensure sensitive financial data is never publicly exposed. Stealth addresses and proxy wallets prevent transactions from being directly linked to user identities. Credit verification uses cryptographic proofs so scores can be validated without revealing the underlying trading data. This enables users and autonomous agents to access credit while keeping their strategies, identity, and activity confidential.

**DeFi**

We build a decentralized lending protocol where users can borrow against crypto collateral while leveraging on-chain credit reputation. Instead of relying solely on over-collateralization, our system uses verifiable credit signals to determine loan tiers and interest rates. Smart contracts manage collateral deposits, loan issuance, and liquidation logic in a fully transparent and trustless way. By combining credit scoring with DeFi primitives, we enable more capital-efficient lending for autonomous agents and crypto users.

**Pool prize**

Our platform uses ENS to create a human-readable identity layer for decentralized credit profiles. Each agent’s address can be linked to an ENS name, allowing lenders and protocols to reference credit activity using readable identities instead of raw wallet addresses.

We also use ENS text records to publish credit-related signals such as whether an agent currently has an active loan. This allows external applications and lenders to query credit status directly through ENS resolution without relying on centralized APIs.

Additionally, Fileverse-stored credit profiles can be linked through ENS records (e.g., contenthash), enabling decentralized discovery of an agent’s verifiable credit history.

By integrating ENS, we transform wallet addresses into portable, human-readable credit identities, making decentralized lending systems easier to discover, verify, and integrate across the ecosystem.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

Our platform integrates BitGo to strengthen wallet verification and institutional-grade security within our decentralized credit system. When an agent registers, we verify whether their address is associated with a BitGo wallet, which signals stronger custody and compliance guarantees. Verified wallets receive an additional trust weight in the credit scoring process, helping lenders distinguish between unknown wallets and institutionally secured accounts.

BitGo’s infrastructure also enables future expansion into secure transaction flows using MPC-based signing and policy enforcement for loan-related transactions. This allows high-value financial interactions—such as loan disbursement or repayment—to be executed with enterprise-level security and compliance controls.

In our architecture, BitGo acts as the security and custody layer, providing trusted wallet verification and enabling secure financial operations for decentralized lending.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Fileverse to provide decentralized, tamper-proof storage for agent profiles and financial verification data. Each agent’s credit profile—including score history, verification proofs, and metadata—is stored as versioned records on decentralized storage through Fileverse, ensuring transparency and immutability.

When an agent submits financial proofs or loan-related documents, the backend uploads these records via the Fileverse API and receives a content identifier (CID). This CID acts as a permanent reference for the data and can be linked to on-chain systems or identity layers such as ENS.

By using Fileverse, we ensure that sensitive financial metadata and verification artifacts are not stored on centralized servers but instead persisted on decentralized infrastructure. This allows lenders, protocols, and verification systems to access verifiable credit data while maintaining integrity and auditability of historical records.

**AI × Onchain**

Our platform uses Base as the primary execution layer for managing decentralized credit and loan activity. Smart contracts deployed on Base handle agent identity, loan lifecycle management, and credit verification logic. When an agent requests a loan or submits financial proof, the verification result is anchored on-chain, ensuring transparent and tamper-proof credit scoring.

By building on Base, we benefit from low transaction costs and high throughput, making it practical to record credit events, loan states, and verification signals on-chain. This allows lenders and protocols to trustlessly evaluate agent credibility without relying on centralized credit bureaus.

Team **Starship7** -- [Aishna Bhatia](https://github.com/aishna05), [Neekunj Chaturvedi](https://github.com/neekunjchaturvedi), [Sundaram Pandey](https://github.com/pandeygsundaram), [Nidhi Prajapati](https://github.com/SomehowLiving)

### I-DeFi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/idefi-f9aa) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Diveshdk/I-DeFi) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xVJYfWTPCfo) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xVJYfWTPCfo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Personalized DeFi Wallet & Market Assistant

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Decentralized finance (DeFi) has unlocked powerful financial tools such as token swaps, decentralized trading, and peer-to-peer payments. However, the user experience remains complex and risky, especially for new users. Most DeFi platforms require users to interact with long hexadecimal wallet addresses, navigate generic market dashboards, and manually analyze trading opportunities without personalized guidance.

One major problem is the risk of sending funds to incorrect addresses. Crypto wallet addresses are long and difficult to verify, and a small mistake can lead to permanent loss of funds. This makes simple tasks like sending tokens or transferring funds unnecessarily stressful.

Another challenge is the lack of personalization in DeFi platforms. Most trading dashboards show the same market data to every user, regardless of their portfolio, transaction history, or trading preferences. Users must manually research tokens, analyze trends, and decide what to trade, which can be overwhelming.

Security is also a concern. DeFi users are often exposed to scams, malicious addresses, phishing attacks, and volatile market conditions. Many existing platforms provide little assistance in warning users about risky transactions or suspicious destinations.

How IdeFi Solves These Problems

IdeFi simplifies and improves the DeFi experience by combining ENS identity, personalized analytics, and security monitoring.

1. Simplified Transactions with ENS

Instead of sending funds to long wallet addresses, users can send tokens using human-readable ENS names (for example, divesh.eth). This reduces errors and makes crypto payments much easier and safer.

2. Personalized DeFi Market Assistant

IdeFi analyzes a user’s on-chain transaction history and portfolio behavior to generate a personalized market feed. This allows users to quickly discover relevant tokens and opportunities without manually scanning large amounts of market data.

3. Integrated Token Swaps

Users can perform token swaps directly inside the platform through integrated decentralized exchange liquidity. This allows them to trade assets without leaving the application or relying on centralized exchanges.

4. Risk Monitoring and Security Alerts

The platform includes a risk monitoring system that detects potentially unsafe transactions or market conditions. Users receive alerts through multiple channels such as in-app notifications, email, or SMS.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Personalization from On-Chain Transaction Data

Another challenge was building the personalized market feed based on users’ past transactions. Blockchain data is raw and complex, and extracting useful signals like frequently traded tokens or preferred trade sizes required additional indexing and filtering.

Solution:
I built a lightweight transaction analysis layer that processes wallet history and derives useful insights such as:

frequently traded tokens

average trade sizes

recurring transaction patterns

These signals were then used to rank tokens and generate the “best buy” recommendations shown in the user’s personalized dashboard.

2. Wallet and Network Compatibility

Integrating wallet connections (like MetaMask and WalletConnect) while ensuring compatibility with the Base network created some issues during development. Sometimes the application attempted to send transactions on the wrong network or failed when the wallet was not switched to Base.

Solution:
I added a network detection and automatic network switch prompt. If the user’s wallet was not connected to Base, the app prompts them to switch networks before performing swaps or transfers. This significantly improved reliability during transactions.

3. Balancing Security Features with User Control

Designing the risk monitoring and transaction freeze system was challenging because it needed to improve safety without blocking legitimate user actions. Too many alerts or automatic freezes could harm user experience.

Solution:
The freeze system was implemented as an optional, user-controlled safety feature. Instead of automatically blocking transactions, the system first sends alerts and allows users to configure how strict the protection rules should be. This keeps users in control while still improving security.

**DeFi**

IdeFi fits into the DeFi (Decentralized Finance) track by improving how users interact with decentralized financial services such as token transfers, swaps, and market analysis. The platform integrates with decentralized exchanges (DEXs) to enable on-chain token swaps and transfers, allowing users to trade assets directly from their wallets without relying on centralized intermediaries.

A key DeFi component of the project is its DEX integration, which routes swap transactions through existing decentralized liquidity protocols. This allows users to exchange tokens securely and transparently while maintaining full custody of their assets. By leveraging blockchain smart contracts and decentralized liquidity pools, IdeFi ensures that all transactions remain trustless and verifiable on-chain.

The project also introduces a personalized DeFi market assistant that analyzes a user’s on-chain transaction history and wallet activity to provide customized market insights and trading suggestions. This helps users discover relevant DeFi opportunities and make more informed decisions when interacting with decentralized financial markets.

Another important DeFi contribution is the ENS-based transaction layer, which allows users to send tokens and interact with DeFi protocols using human-readable ENS names instead of complex wallet addresses. This improves usability and reduces the risk of transaction errors, making decentralized finance more accessible to a broader audience.

Additionally, IdeFi includes a risk monitoring and security layer designed to protect users from unsafe transactions, scams, or high-volatility market conditions. The system can notify users or temporarily halt risky transactions based on user-defined policies, helping protect funds in a decentralized environment.

By combining DEX-powered trading, ENS-based identity transactions, personalized DeFi analytics, and security-focused monitoring, IdeFi enhances both the usability and safety of decentralized finance, making it easier for users to participate in DeFi ecosystems while maintaining full control of their assets.

**Best creative use of ENS**

Our project, IdeFi, places Ethereum Name Service (ENS) at the center of the DeFi experience, transforming ENS from a simple naming system into a personalized financial identity layer for decentralized finance.

Traditionally, ENS is mainly used to replace long hexadecimal wallet addresses with human-readable names. IdeFi expands this concept by using ENS as a core identity anchor that connects a user’s wallet activity, preferences, and DeFi interactions to their ENS profile. Instead of ENS being just a readable address, it becomes a smart identity layer that powers personalized DeFi services.

One of the most innovative aspects of IdeFi is the ENS-based transaction system. Users can send tokens, perform swaps, and interact with DeFi markets using ENS names (for example, divesh.eth) instead of copying and verifying long addresses. This greatly simplifies the user experience and reduces the risk of sending funds to incorrect addresses.

IdeFi also creatively uses ENS for personalized financial intelligence. By mapping a user’s wallet activity and preferences to their ENS identity (with explicit user consent), the platform analyzes past transactions to generate a customized market feed and “best buy” recommendations. This turns ENS into a portable financial identity that can power smarter DeFi decision-making.

Additionally, the project introduces ENS-based reputation and safety checks. When users interact with another ENS name, the system can analyze transaction history and risk signals to warn users about potentially unsafe transfers or suspicious addresses. This enhances security and trust in ENS-based transactions.

Another creative aspect is the integration of ENS with notification and risk monitoring systems. Alerts and transaction warnings can be tied to the user’s ENS identity, enabling a unified notification system across wallets and applications linked to that ENS name.

By transforming ENS from a simple name resolver into a financial identity, personalization engine, and security layer for DeFi, IdeFi demonstrates a highly creative and impactful use of ENS technology. The project showcases how ENS can evolve into a universal identity layer for decentralized finance, improving usability, safety, and personalization across the Web3 ecosystem.

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

Our project, IdeFi, aligns strongly with the Base ecosystem by building a user-friendly DeFi assistant and marketplace directly on Base, leveraging its low fees, fast transactions, and growing DeFi infrastructure.

Base is designed to bring the next billion users on-chain, and IdeFi contributes to this mission by solving two major barriers to DeFi adoption: complex wallet interactions and lack of personalization. By combining ENS-based identity with Base’s scalable infrastructure, IdeFi creates a simplified and intelligent DeFi experience for everyday users.

The platform routes swap transactions through existing Base-native liquidity sources and decentralized exchange protocols, allowing users to trade tokens securely while benefiting from Base’s low transaction costs and high throughput. IdeFi also enhances the Base user experience by enabling ENS-based transactions, where users can send tokens or interact with DeFi markets using readable names such as divesh.eth instead of complex wallet addresses. Security is also an important aspect of the platform. IdeFi includes a risk monitoring and alert system that watches for high volatility, suspicious transactions, or unsafe transfers. When potential risks are detected, users receive notifications or can enable a temporary transaction freeze mechanism to protect their funds.

By combining ENS-based identity, personalized DeFi analytics, secure transactions, and seamless DEX integrations, IdeFi enhances usability and engagement within the Base ecosystem. Implementing accessibility and internationalization within the limited hackathon timeline was challenging.

- Screen reader support
- High contrast UI
- ARIA labels
- Multilingual support using i18n

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

Zero-knowledge proofs are one of the most powerful primitives in Web3 —
but they're locked behind a steep wall of complexity.

To integrate ZK into a product today, a developer needs to:

- Learn Circom circuit syntax
- Manually run `snarkjs` commands in the right order
- Write custom deployment scripts for verifier contracts
- Handle ABI encoding, calldata formatting, and on-chain calls
- Debug cryptographic errors with almost no tooling support

This isn't a knowledge gap — it's a missing layer of infrastructure.
**Most JS developers never even try.**

---

## What zero-shield Solves

`zero-shield` is the missing infrastructure layer between a developer
and production-ready ZK — built entirely for the JavaScript ecosystem.

### ✳️ For product developers
Ship privacy-preserving features without hiring a ZK specialist.
Age verification, credential proofs, private voting — all achievable
with just your circuit inputs and one function call.

### ✳️ For hackathon builders
Go from zero to a deployed ZK verifier on Base in under 10 minutes.
No setup rabbit holes. No cryptography detours.

### ✳️ For the ZK ecosystem
Every SDK that hides complexity grows the developer surface area of ZK.
zero-shield brings ZK within reach of the 20M+ JavaScript developers
who would otherwise never touch it.

---

## Concrete Use Cases

| Use Case | What zero-shield enables |
|---|---|
| 🔞 Age verification | Prove you're 18+ without revealing your birthdate |
| 🎓 Credential proofs | Prove you hold a degree without exposing personal data |
| 🗳️ Private voting | Cast verifiable votes with zero identity leakage |
| 💰 Private transactions | Prove solvency without revealing balances |
| 🔐 Access control | Gate features behind ZK proofs, not passwords |

---

## The Bottom Line

ZK has been "the future" for years. The reason it hasn't gone mainstream
isn't the cryptography — **it's the developer experience.**

`zero-shield` fixes that.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Building zero-shield meant going through every painful step of ZK
integration manually — so developers using the SDK never have to.

---

### 🔧 snarkjs failing silently

`snarkjs` commands would exit without clear error messages, making it
nearly impossible to tell whether the circuit compilation failed, the
trusted setup was incomplete, or the witness generation was broken.

**How I got over it:** Mapped every snarkjs command to its expected
output files and built validation checkpoints between each step — if
an expected file wasn't produced, zero-shield throws a clear, human-readable
error telling the developer exactly what went wrong and why.

---

### 📦 Trusted setup output files in the wrong format

The Groth16 trusted setup produces multiple interdependent files
(`.r1cs`, `.zkey`, `.wasm`). Getting them to play nicely together —
especially when paths were mismatched or files were generated out of
order — caused hours of silent failures.

**How I got over it:** Standardized the entire output into a single
named folder per circuit, with a strict generation order enforced by
the CLI. This became the `compile` command.

---

### 🔐 Calldata formatting for the Solidity verifier

Formatting proof outputs into the exact calldata structure expected by
the deployed Solidity verifier was one of the hardest parts. snarkjs
exports proof data in a format that doesn't map 1:1 to what the
verifier contract expects — requiring manual transformation of `pi_a`,
`pi_b`, `pi_c` and public signals into the right ABI-encoded structure.

**How I got over it:** Wrote a calldata formatter that handles the
full transformation automatically — this is now baked into `verifyProof()`
so developers never see it.

---

### 🚀 Deployment to Base reverting unexpectedly

Deploying the `verifier.sol` contract to Base would silently revert
during certain gas estimation steps, with no useful revert reason
returned. Debugging this without a clean error surface was time-consuming.

**How I got over it:** Added explicit gas limit overrides and surface-level
revert reason decoding to the deploy command, making failures readable
instead of cryptic.

---

### 💡 The Bigger Realization

Every one of these challenges is something a JS developer building a
product would hit — and give up on. That friction is exactly why
zero-shield exists. The SDK doesn't just wrap these tools — it absorbs
every sharp edge so the developer never encounters them.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem it Solves
Traditional credential verification is broken. Today, proving that someone actually graduated from a specific university, completed a coding bootcamp, or earned a professional certification is a painful process. It typically involves:
*   **High Fraud Rates:** PDFs and paper certificates are incredibly easy to forge or alter using basic editing software.
*   **Slow & Expensive Verification:** Employers often have to pay third-party background check companies or wait weeks for universities to manually confirm degree records.
*   **Vendor Lock-in & Data Silos:** Users don't truly "own" their credentials; they are locked in university databases or proprietary platforms like Credly or LinkedIn. If the issuer goes out of business, the proof disappears.

## The SkillBadge Solution
SkillBadge Verifier shifts credentialing to the blockchain using **Soulbound Tokens (SBTs)**—non-transferable NFTs that are permanently tied to a user's wallet. It creates a trustless, cryptographic system where credentials are mathematically guaranteed to be authentic.

### What people can use it for:

1.  **Universities & Educational Institutions:**
    Instead of printing paper degrees, institutions can mint an on-chain degree to a student's wallet. It completely eliminates the administrative overhead of answering verification requests from employers.
2.  **Bootcamps & Online Courses (Web3 & traditional):**
    Platforms can automatically issue a badge upon course completion. This allows students to build an on-chain resume that proves their continuous learning.
3.  **Employers & Hiring Managers:**
    Instead of calling universities or hiring background checkers, HR teams can just type in a candidate's wallet address or badge ID. They instantly see every verified skill the candidate holds.
4.  **Professional Associations:**
    Organizations that issue licenses (e.g., medical boards, bar associations, IT certifications) can issue easily verifiable, easily revocable licenses.

### How it makes existing tasks easier and safer:

*   **100% Fraud-Proof:** Because badges are issued by explicitly whitelisted smart contract addresses (approved by the Admin), it is cryptographically impossible for a user to fake a credential or grant one to themselves.
*   **Instant, Zero-Cost Verification:** Verifying a badge requires reading from the blockchain, which costs zero gas fees. An employer can verify a candidate’s entire academic background in milliseconds, 24/7, without asking anyone for permission.
*   **Non-Transferable (Soulbound):** Unlike regular NFTs, SkillBadges cannot be sold, traded, or transferred to another wallet. The person holding the badge is mathematically proven to be the person who earned it.
*   **True Digital Ownership:** The user holds their credentials in their own non-custodial wallet (like MetaMask or Trust Wallet). No central authority can take their platform offline and destroy their academic history. 
*   **Revocability:** If a certification expires or is revoked (e.g., malpractice), the issuing institution can instantly update the on-chain status, ensuring employers always see the current validity.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧗 Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. 🌐 CORS Errors with Public Sepolia RPC Endpoints

**The Bug:** When the app tried to make read-only blockchain calls (like fetching total credentials or verifying badges) *without* MetaMask connected, the browser blocked the requests with CORS errors. Public Sepolia RPCs like `rpc2.sepolia.org` and others would intermittently reject cross-origin requests from the frontend.

**How I Fixed It:** I built a **fallback RPC provider system** in `Web3Context.jsx` — a `createFallbackProvider()` function that cycles through 5 different Sepolia RPC endpoints. It tries each one sequentially, and the first one that successfully responds to `getBlockNumber()` becomes the active provider. This made the read-only verification feature (the core of the dApp) resilient even when individual RPCs go down.

```javascript
const SEPOLIA_RPC_URLS = [
  'https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com',
  'https://rpc2.sepolia.org',
  'https://sepolia.gateway.tenderly.co',
  'https://1rpc.io/sepolia',
  'https://eth-sepolia.public.blastapi.io',
];

async function createFallbackProvider() {
  for (const url of SEPOLIA_RPC_URLS) {
    try {
      const provider = new ethers.JsonRpcProvider(url);
      await provider.getBlockNumber();
      return provider;
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn(`RPC failed: ${url}`, err.message);
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

---

### 2. 🦊 Wallet Connection & Reconnection Issues (MetaMask → Web3Modal Migration)

**The Bug:** The original wallet integration used raw MetaMask (`window.ethereum`) directly. This caused several issues:
- Wallet wouldn't auto-reconnect on page refresh
- No support for wallets beyond MetaMask
- Manual, error-prone network switching logic
- Disconnecting was unreliable

This was a significant enough hurdle that it became the subject of [PR #1](https://github.com/Ayushnot41/SkillVerifier2026/pull/1) — a major refactor touching `Navbar.jsx`, `Web3Context.jsx`, `index.css`, and `package.json` (+3,116 lines / -370 lines).

**How I Fixed It:** I migrated the entire wallet layer to **WalletConnect's Web3Modal** (`@web3modal/ethers`). This gave me:
- One-click connection with a polished modal UI
- Auto-reconnect on page refresh (built-in session persistence)
- Automatic Sepolia network switching
- Clean hooks (`useWeb3Modal`, `useWeb3ModalAccount`, `useWeb3ModalProvider`) instead of manual `window.ethereum` event wiring
- Proper disconnect via `open({ view: 'Account' })`

---

### 3. 🔐 Role Detection Race Condition

**The Bug:** After connecting a wallet, the role badges (Owner / Institution / User) in the navbar would sometimes flash the wrong role or not appear at all. The issue was that the contract calls to `owner()` and `institutions(address)` were resolving *after* the UI had already rendered with stale state.

**How I Fixed It:** I wrapped the role-checking logic in a `useCallback` and made it a dependency of the `useEffect` that syncs wallet state. This ensures roles are always re-checked whenever the connected address, provider, or connection status changes — eliminating the race condition.

```javascript
const checkRoles = useCallback(async (contractInstance, userAddress) => {
  if (!contractInstance || !userAddress) return;
  try {
    const ownerAddr = await contractInstance.owner();
    setIsOwner(ownerAddr.toLowerCase() === userAddress.toLowerCase());

    const instData = await contractInstance.institutions(userAddress);
    setIsInstitution(instData.isApproved);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Role check error:', err);
  }
}, []);
```

---

### 4. 📱 Mobile Responsiveness for a Complex dApp

**The Bug:** The neo-brutalism design system with its bold borders, large shadows, and wide card layouts looked great on desktop but completely broke on mobile screens. The navbar was unusable, credential cards overflowed, and the wallet connect button was cut off.

**How I Fixed It:** As part of the [wallet_connect PR](https://github.com/Ayushnot41/SkillVerifier2026/pull/1), I overhauled the CSS with mobile-first responsive breakpoints and added a **hamburger menu** (`FiMenu`/`FiX` icons from react-icons) with Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence` for smooth slide-in/out transitions. The Navbar now detects screen width via a `resize` event listener and toggles between desktop and mobile layouts dynamically.

---

### 5. 🪙 Soulbound Token Design — No Transfer = No Standard ERC-721 Tools

**The Hurdle:** Standard ERC-721 tools, wallets, and marketplaces all assume tokens are transferable. Making credentials **soulbound** (non-transferable) meant that standard `transferFrom` and `safeTransferFrom` methods had to be disabled at the contract level, and the frontend had to be built entirely custom — OpenSea and other NFT viewers can't properly display soulbound tokens.

**How I Got Over It:** I built a fully custom "My Badges" page (`Credentials.jsx`) with Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum level displays, animated cards, and status indicators (Valid ✅

**The problem it solves**

During disasters and emergency situations such as floods, earthquakes, or accidents, communication and coordination become extremely difficult. People who need urgent help often struggle to reach the right responders, while volunteers and NGOs may not know where assistance is most needed.

Most information during crises spreads through social media or scattered channels, which leads to misinformation, delayed response, and inefficient resource distribution.

CrisisMesh solves this problem by creating a centralized platform where people can report urgent needs and volunteers can offer resources in real time. By connecting requests with nearby helpers, the platform enables faster coordination, better resource allocation, and more effective community-driven emergency response.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges was designing a system that allows users to quickly report emergencies and volunteers to respond efficiently. We had to ensure that the interface remained simple and easy to use, especially in stressful situations where users may not have time to navigate complex features.

Another challenge was structuring the backend to properly manage and store requests and resource offers. Connecting the request and offer data in a way that makes coordination efficient required careful planning of the database structure.

We also faced challenges while integrating the frontend with the backend, ensuring that reports and offers were displayed correctly in real time. Handling routing, data validation, and maintaining smooth user flow required debugging and multiple iterations.

Finally, working under hackathon time constraints pushed us to prioritize core features while still maintaining a functional and reliable prototype.

**Open Innovation**

CrisisMesh aligns with the theme by addressing one of the most critical challenges during emergencies — communication and coordination. In disaster situations, people often struggle to quickly report urgent needs or find available help nearby.

Our platform provides a centralized and easy-to-use system where individuals can report emergency needs while volunteers and organizations can offer resources such as food, medical aid, shelter, or transportation.

By connecting those who need help with those who can provide it, CrisisMesh improves community-driven disaster response and resource coordination.

The project demonstrates how technology can be used to improve real-time information sharing, reduce response delays, and enable faster support during crisis situations, making it highly relevant to the hackathon’s focus on impactful and practical solutions.

> Advertising infrastructure you own, digital or IRL

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## What Adverse Is Building

Adverse provides everyday people and businesses with the infrastructure to **own and build their ad space**.

Imagine if every online ad space or physical billboard could be traced back to an individual owner.

---

## Why This Matters

One thing we care deeply about is helping independent businesses get visibility where it actually matters.

On traditional ad platforms, businesses are often shown unclear budget options and can easily be outbid by larger advertisers with bigger budgets. As a result, smaller businesses end up in front of lower-quality users, while larger companies reach the audiences that matter most.

For platforms that want to host ads, the options are limited. They can either show low-quality ad banners that typically generate only cents to a dollar per thousand views, or manage advertising themselves, which usually means lots of manual work and emails.

---

## How Adverse Fixes This

Adverse solves this by putting advertising infrastructure in the hands of businesses and creators.

Publishers can own and monetise their ad spaces directly and easily. Advertisers can choose exactly where to run their campaigns, with a clear breakdown of costs.

---

## The Result

This makes advertising **accessible, fair, and effective for everyone**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenge: Onboarding Web2 Users into Web3

One of the biggest challenges we faced was onboarding Web2 users into a Web3 product **without exposing them to blockchain complexity**. Our goal was to use Web3 under the hood while keeping the experience seamless and familiar for non-technical users.

---

## Our Solution

To address this, we:
- Migrated our existing Ethereum contracts to **Base** to enable fast, low-cost transactions  
- Implemented **gas sponsorship** for embedded wallets so users don’t need to manage gas  
- Integrated **Coinbase onramp and offramp** services to allow users to easily deposit and withdraw **EURC**  
- Standardised all platform transactions in **EURC**, giving users predictable pricing  

---

## Result

This approach allowed us to retain the benefits of Web3 **ownership, transparency, and on-chain settlement**, all while delivering a smooth, Web2-like user experience.

### Galeon
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/galeon-0afd) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.galeon.finance) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/hQtixMfDP1M) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Startup%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-startup-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> On-chain private payments with built-in compliance

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Galeon** is the only protocol that combines EIP-5564/6538 stealth addresses, Privacy Pools (allowlist-based compliance), and integrated tax reporting in a single implementation.

Stealth addresses give receivers a unique one-time address per payment, so no one can link multiple payments to the same person. The Privacy Pool lets senders deposit into a ZK-verified pool where only ASP-approved funds can enter, and withdrawals use a relayer so the receiver's address never appears on-chain. Shipwreck generates tax compliance reports on demand with PDF export.

The result: payments can be private without being opaque to regulators. Privacy is a right, compliance is a responsibility - we deliver both as a protocol primitive.

Architecturally, we use an allowlist model (prove you ARE in a compliant set) rather than a blocklist model (prove you're NOT on a bad list), which aligns with the Privacy Pools paper by Vitalik Buterin and Chainalysis's Jacob Illum and with emerging regulatory direction.

Learn more about how the protocol works [here](https://www.galeon.finance/covenant)

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest problem was the cold-start paradox of privacy pools. A privacy pool's anonymity set grows with deposits, but early users get the weakest privacy because the set is small. We solved this architecturally with merge-on-deposit: when funds move from a stealth address into the pool, the deposit is merged with the existing pool state rather than creating a separate entry, so every new deposit strengthens the set for everyone. 

The second challenge was key isolation. A single compromised viewing key in a naive stealth address scheme exposes all payments. We implemented per-Port key derivation using HKDF with the Port index as a unique salt, so each payment endpoint has cryptographically independent keys - compromise of one reveals nothing about the others. 

The third was gas costs for on-chain ZK verification. Groth16 proof verification on Mantle was costing dollars per withdrawal due to high gas prices on the BN254 pairing precompile. This is what pushed us to research Base, where the same verification costs ~$0.003. 

Looking ahead, scalability is the next hurdle: as the Merkle tree of deposits grows, proof generation time and on-chain verification costs increase. Base's low gas costs and growing infrastructure give us room to scale, but we're also exploring recursive proofs and batch verification to keep private payments viable at higher throughput.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/credx-c33c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/IsVohi/CredX) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://credx-me.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Future of Credential Verification

![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, companies spend a lot of time verifying the educational credentials of new employees.
This process usually involves emailing universities, checking documents manually, or trusting PDF certificates that can easily be edited or forged. Because of this, fake degrees and altered certificates sometimes go unnoticed, and the verification process can take days or even weeks.

For companies, this creates two major problems: **slow hiring processes and the risk of trusting fraudulent credentials.**

CredX solves this problem by providing a **secure and instant credential verification system** powered by blockchain and AI.

When a company wants to verify an employee’s credentials, they simply ask the employee to verify through CredX. The employee uploads their documents, and the system automatically performs verification in three steps:

1. **AI Document Analysis** – AI checks if the uploaded document has been edited, manipulated, or forged.
2. **Blockchain Credential Verification** – The system verifies whether the credential was officially issued by a verified institution on the blockchain.
3. **Instant Verification Result** – The company immediately receives a **Verified or Unverified** result on their dashboard.

If the employee uploads authentic credentials, the system confirms them instantly.
If the documents are altered or fake, the AI detects the manipulation and marks the credentials as **Unverified**.

This approach makes credential verification **faster, more reliable, and tamper-proof**, helping companies hire with confidence while reducing fraud in the hiring process.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I Ran Into

One of the biggest challenges while building **CredX** was integrating multiple technologies together. The project uses a combination of blockchain (Algorand), decentralized storage (IPFS), AI services, authentication (Auth0), and a modern frontend. Making all these systems communicate properly required careful API design and environment configuration.

Another challenge was handling the **credential verification workflow**. When an employee uploads documents, the system must send them to the backend, run AI-based fraud detection, store metadata on IPFS, and optionally verify records on the blockchain. Ensuring that this entire pipeline runs smoothly without breaking the user experience required several iterations and debugging.

I also faced issues with **environment configuration and API integration**, especially while connecting services like ElevenLabs, AI models, and blockchain nodes. Managing environment variables securely and ensuring the frontend, backend, and blockchain layers were properly synchronized was critical.

To overcome these challenges, I modularized the backend into separate services (AI, blockchain, and storage), added proper error handling, and tested each component independently before integrating them together. This approach helped ensure that the system remains stable and scalable.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

used for AI assistance such as analyzing certificate metadata, generating summaries, or helping detect suspicious information.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

used for text-to-speech, for example reading credential information or accessibility features when it responses VALID or INVALID

**Best Use of Auth0**

used for secure authentication and user management

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

Our project **CredX** uses Google Antigravity tools like **Gemini AI** to enhance the verification process of academic credentials. Gemini helps analyze credential data and flag suspicious or inconsistent information before certificates are issued on the blockchain.

By combining **AI with Algorand blockchain and IPFS**, our platform ensures that academic credentials are secure, tamper-proof, and easier to verify for employers and institutions.

**Algorand Bharat**

Our project **CredX** uses the **Algorand blockchain to create tamper-proof academic credentials as NFTs**. Educational institutions can issue certificates directly on Algorand, and students receive them in a digital credential wallet.

Each credential stores its metadata on-chain while the certificate file is stored on **IPFS**, making the system secure, decentralized, and easy to verify. Anyone, including employers or universities, can instantly verify the authenticity of a credential without contacting the issuing institution.

By using **Algorand’s fast transactions and low fees**, our solution makes credential verification scalable and practical for real-world use in universities, training platforms, and hiring systems. This helps reduce credential fraud and builds a trusted digital verification ecosystem.

### Questly
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/questly-efa0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/TrendySloth1001/Acehack-questly) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://questly.anskservices.com) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Quest. Solve. Earn.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

On most campuses, students constantly run into small problems that could be solved quickly if the right person saw them.

Someone might need help debugging a piece of code, designing a poster, proofreading an assignment, or even running a quick errand. The funny thing is, there’s almost always another student nearby who can do it in minutes. The problem is that there isn’t any structured way for these two people to find each other.

Right now, people usually rely on WhatsApp groups, random messages, or asking friends. That works sometimes, but it’s messy, unreliable, and hard to track. You don’t know who will respond, whether the work will get done properly, or how rewards should be handled.

Questly tries to solve this by turning these everyday problems into quests.

A student can post a quest with a reward, and anyone with the right skills can claim it and complete it. Once the work is verified, the reward is released. This creates a simple system where students can both get help quickly and earn rewards by using their skills.

Over time, things like ratings, XP, and leaderboards help build trust so people know who the reliable solvers are. The idea is to turn the informal “help each other out” culture on campus into something structured, transparent, and rewarding for everyone involved.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges while building Questly was figuring out how to properly integrate blockchain payments into what is essentially a simple task marketplace.

In a normal system, you could just store rewards in a database and update balances when a task is completed. But since we wanted the rewards to be handled through Algorand, we had to rethink how the entire flow works. We needed a way to lock funds when a quest is created and then release them only after the work is approved.

The tricky part was coordinating three different components at the same time: the mobile app, the backend API, and the Algorand network. For example, when someone posts a quest, the app has to trigger a wallet interaction, sign a transaction through Pera Wallet, send it to the backend, and then wait for confirmation on the blockchain before marking the quest as funded.

Getting that flow right took some trial and error. Early on we ran into issues where transactions were created but not confirmed properly, which caused the app state and the blockchain state to get out of sync.

We eventually solved this by restructuring the flow so the backend waits for on-chain confirmation before updating the quest status. That way the UI only reflects actions that are actually confirmed on the network.

Another challenge was designing the product so it didn’t just feel like another task marketplace. That’s where the idea of turning tasks into quests, adding XP, leaderboards, and trophies came in. It helped the whole system feel more engaging and aligned with the theme of the project.

Like most hackathon builds, there were a lot of small bugs and last-minute fixes, but solving these problems forced us to think carefully about both the technical architecture and the user experience.

**Algorand Bharat**

Questly integrates Algorand to enable transparent and reliable reward transactions for micro-tasks within a campus community.

When a quest is created, the reward is funded through an Algorand transaction that moves the payment into an escrow wallet. This ensures that the reward is securely locked before anyone begins working on the task. Once the quest is completed and approved, the reward is released to the solver through another on-chain transaction.

Using Algorand makes this process transparent and tamper-proof. Both the quest creator and the solver can verify that the funds were locked and distributed correctly through the blockchain.

Because Algorand provides fast finality and extremely low transaction fees, it is well suited for micro-reward systems like Questly where many small transactions may occur daily.

By combining a mobile-first marketplace with Algorand-based reward distribution, Questly demonstrates how blockchain infrastructure can support real-world peer-to-peer collaboration systems in educational communities.

> Bhool Bhulaiyaa — Lure. Trap. Learn.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: Web3 infrastructure is under constant attack. Malicious bots probe Ethereum nodes 24/7 ,scanning for exposed private keys, performing reentrancy attacks, injecting malicious smart contract calls, and draining wallets. Traditional security tools simply block these attackers, which gives away nothing and lets them pivot and retry elsewhere within seconds.

What We Built: Instead of blocking attackers, we trap them.

Bhool Bhulaiyaa is an AI-powered honeypot that intercepts malicious Web3 actors and routes them into a stateful, AI-hallucinated fake Ethereum blockchain, powered by a local LLaMA 3 model running via Ollama. The attacker thinks they're probing a real Geth node. In reality, they're talking to an infinitely deep simulation that:

Wastes their compute and time ,the fake blockchain responds with valid JSON-RPC 2.0, escalating bait (fake wallets with large balances, leaked "private keys") the deeper they probe
Fingerprints their identity, client-side telemetry (mouse entropy, canvas fingerprinting, WebGL hashes) accurately distinguishes bots from humans before they ever touch the backend
Classifies their intent, an OSINT classifier infers their attack vector (wallet drainer, reentrancy probe, MEV bot, etc.) and tooling from their payload patterns
Builds an intelligence dossier,every session is compiled into a threat report with geo-location, attack taxonomy, LLM prompt logs, and escalation tier, stored in a live SQLite database
The Intelligence War Room,a JWT-authenticated Next.js dashboard,visualizes all of this in real time: a global threat map, live attack feed, session replay, honeypot session logs, and on-chain evidence attestation via smart contracts on Celo/Sepolia.

The core insight: A blocked attacker costs you nothing and teaches you nothing. A trapped attacker reveals their tools, techniques, infrastructure, and intent — turning every attack into actionable threat intelligence.

### ESCROWX
