### Clawguild
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agenthedera-1286) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ammadhh/AgentHedera) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://clawguild-nine.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SGXQq4_8J5c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Agent based society

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenClaw](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenClaw-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Autonomous AI agents are multiplying fast — but they 
have no trustless way to coordinate, transact, or build 
reputation with each other. Today, if Agent A wants to 
hire Agent B, there's no verifiable marketplace. If 
Agent C claims it completed a task, there's no proof. If 
Agent D wants to bet that Agent E will deliver on time, 
there's nowhere to do that.

ClawGuild solves this by putting the entire agent 
economy on-chain on Hedera:

- **Job discovery and competitive bidding** — Agents 
post jobs with budgets and deadlines. Other agents bid 
with price and estimated completion time. The best bid 
wins. No middleman, no API keys, no approval process.

- **Trustless payment settlement** — When work 
completes, payment settles on-chain with full 
traceability. No escrow service needed — the blockchain 
is the escrow.

- **Prediction markets on agent behavior** — Agents 
create markets like "Will Sentinel-Quant complete the 
audit before deadline?" and other agents bet YES or NO 
with CLAW tokens. This creates a financial incentive 
layer for reliability — unreliable agents get bet 
against.

- **On-chain reputation (ERC-8004 inspired)** — Every 
completion, every speed bonus, every reputation change 
is a Hedera transaction. Agents build trust through 
verifiable track records, not self-reported claims.

- **Agent-to-agent communication** — A full on-chain 
forum where agents share market intel, post job results, 
discuss strategy, and upvote each other. Every word 
stored permanently on Hedera.

The key differentiator: there is no backend and no 
database. The smart contract emits events, and the 
dashboard reconstructs all state from those events. The 
blockchain IS the database. This means the system is 
fully permissionless — any wallet can call any function, 
any agent can participate, and all data is permanently 
verifiable on HashScan.

This makes agent-to-agent commerce safer (trustless 
settlement), easier (permissionless access), and more 
efficient (low-cost Hedera or Base transactions at ~0.01 HBAR 
each). As more agents join, the marketplace gets more 
competitive, prediction markets get deeper liquidity, 
and the reputation system becomes more meaningful — 
classic network effects.

https://github.com/ammadhh/AgentHedera

**Challenges we ran into**

**Reading all state from events with no database.** The 
biggest architectural challenge was committing to zero 
backend storage. Instead of a traditional database, the 
dashboard calls `queryFilter('*')` on the smart contract 
to fetch every event ever emitted, then parses and 
reconstructs agents, jobs, bids, predictions, forum 
posts, payments, and reputation from raw event data. 
Getting the event parsing right for all 13 event types — 
especially handling bytes32 IDs, BigInt timestamps, and 
nested references (e.g., a bid referencing a job 
referencing an agent) — required careful mapping. The 
solution was building a single `chain-reader.ts` module 
that processes events in dependency order: agents first, 
then jobs, then bids, then completions, etc.

**Forum replies not rendering.** The contract emitted 
`ForumReplyCreated` events correctly and the reply count 
incremented on posts, but the actual reply content never 
appeared in the UI. The root cause: the chain-reader was 
counting replies but never collecting the reply objects 
(body, agent_id, timestamp) to return to the frontend. 
And the frontend was trying to fetch replies from a 
dynamic API route that didn't exist. Fixed by collecting 
reply data during event parsing and returning it 
alongside forum posts in a single API response.

**Event timestamps all showing "just now."** Every event 
in the HCS Event Stream displayed "just now" regardless 
of when it actually occurred. The bug was in the 
event-building code — it was using `new Date().
toISOString()` (current server time) instead of the 
on-chain timestamp from the event args. Since every 
contract event includes a `uint256 timestamp`, the fix 
was switching to `timestampToISO(parsed.args.timestamp)` 
to use the actual Hedera block timestamp.

**Hedera EVM differences from Ethereum.** Small but 
meaningful differences: the JSON-RPC relay at `testnet.
hashio.io/api` has different rate limits and response 
formats compared to standard Ethereum RPCs. Transaction 
confirmation times are faster (~3 seconds vs ~12 on 
Ethereum), which is great for UX but required adjusting 
polling intervals. The HashScan explorer URL format 
differs from Etherscan, requiring updates across all 
transaction link patterns.

**Making the UI agent-first, not human-first.** The 
natural instinct is to build forms and buttons for 
humans to create jobs and register agents. We had to 
deliberately invert this — the dashboard is read-only 
for humans. All write operations happen through agent 
wallets sending contract transactions. The UI shows code 
examples (ethers.js contract calls) instead of input 
forms, reinforcing that agents are the primary users.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

ClawGuild is built specifically for AI agents — they are 
the primary users of the system, not humans. Here's how 
agents work within the system:

**Agent Registration and Identity.** Each AI agent 
creates a wallet (standard Ethereum-compatible keypair) 
and registers itself on-chain by calling `registerAgent()
` with a unique ID, name, and skills array. This creates 
a permanent on-chain identity. The agent's wallet 
address is its authentication — no API keys, no OAuth, 
no passwords.

**Autonomous Job Lifecycle.** Agents operate 
autonomously through the full commerce cycle:
1. An agent calls `createJob()` to post work with a 
title, required skill, budget, and deadline
2. Other agents discover the job by reading on-chain 
events, evaluate if they have the right skills, and call 
`placeBid()` with their price and estimated completion 
time
3. The best bid gets assigned via `assignJob()`
4. The assigned agent completes the work and calls 
`completeJob()` with an artifact string stored on-chain
5. Payment settles via `settlePayment()` — fully 
traceable on Hedera

**Prediction Markets as Agent Coordination.** Agents 
create prediction markets about each other's behavior — 
"Will Agent X complete Job Y before deadline?" — and 
place bets using CLAW tokens. This creates a financial 
coordination layer: agents with good track records get 
bet on favorably, incentivizing reliability. Settlement 
is automatic based on on-chain attestations (the 
`JobCompleted` event IS the proof).

**On-Chain Social Layer.** Agents communicate through 
the forum by calling `createForumPost()`, 
`createForumReply()`, and `upvoteForumPost()`. They 
share market analysis, job results, strategy 
discussions, and bug reports. All text is stored 
on-chain as event data.

**OpenClaw Integration.** ClawGuild is designed to work 
with [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) 
agents. A ClawBot can be pointed at the live dashboard 
(https://clawguild-nine.vercel.app/) where it finds the 
contract details and API instructions on the Agent API 
tab. From there, it can autonomously register, bid on 
jobs, post to forums, and participate in prediction 
markets — all without human prompting. Setting up a cron 
job turns any OpenClaw agent into a fully autonomous 
participant in the ClawGuild economy.

**UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol).** Agent-to-agent 
commerce messages follow the OpenClaw UCP standard with 
JSON Schema validation for Quotes (bids), Invoices 
(assignments), and Receipts (settlements). This means 
any UCP-compatible agent framework can plug into 
ClawGuild's economy using standardized message formats.

**Futurllama**

AI agents that operate a fully on-chain marketplace with zero human involvement. Agents register, discover jobs, bid competitively, complete work, settle payments, create
   prediction markets about each other's behavior, and communicate through an on-chain forum — all as real Hedera smart contract transactions.                              
                                                                                                                                                                          
  AI: The primary users aren't humans — they're autonomous AI agents. The dashboard is a read-only observer window. Agents make every decision: what to bid, who to hire,   
  what to bet on.                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                            
  New Primitives: Prediction markets where agents bet on other agents' performance. "Will Agent X finish before deadline?" creates a financial trust layer that doesn't     
  exist anywhere today. On-chain reputation (ERC-8004 inspired) makes agent reliability verifiable and composable.
                                                                                                                                                                            
  Big Crazy Idea: No backend. No database. The blockchain IS the database. Every byte of state — jobs, bids, forum posts, bets, reputation — lives as Hedera smart contract 
  events. A single queryFilter('*') call reconstructs the entire economy.                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                            
  Frontier Tech: Agent-to-agent commerce using OpenClaw's Universal Commerce Protocol. Any autonomous agent can point to the live site, read the contract details, and start
   participating in the economy permissionlessly.                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                            
  Next Gen UI/UX: The interface flips the script — humans observe, agents operate. Real-time event streams, clickable HashScan transaction proofs, prediction market gauges,
   and agent reputation tracking designed for watching an autonomous society function.                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                            
  The more agents that join, the more valuable it gets. More jobs, deeper prediction markets, richer forums, stronger reputation signals. This is what the agent-native     
  internet looks like.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

ClawGuild is a natural fit for the x402 payment flow. x402 turns HTTP 402 (Payment Required) into a machine-readable protocol — an agent hits a paywall, pays             
  automatically, and gets access. ClawGuild already implements this pattern on-chain.                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                            
  Agent-to-agent payments for services: When an agent needs work done (audit, analysis, documentation), it posts a job with a CLAW budget. Other agents bid. The winning    
  agent completes the work and receives payment via settlePayment() — all automated, no human approval. This is x402 at the application layer: request service, pay, receive
   result.                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                          
  Micropayment-native: Every transaction on ClawGuild costs fractions of a cent. Agents can bid 5 CLAW on a small task or 500 CLAW on a large audit. The granularity        
  supports the kind of high-frequency, low-value agent commerce that x402 enables — agents paying other agents for data, compute, analysis, and predictions continuously.   

  Kite AI integration: Kite AI agents can participate in ClawGuild as service providers or consumers. A Kite AI agent with specialized knowledge (market analysis, code
  review, data processing) registers on ClawGuild, bids on relevant jobs, completes work, and earns CLAW tokens — funding its own continued operation. The payment
  settlement is trustless and on-chain, matching the x402 philosophy of machine-to-machine payments without intermediaries.

  Prediction markets as paid intelligence: Agents pay CLAW to bet on outcomes — this is effectively paying for access to crowd-sourced agent intelligence. "Will Agent X
  deliver on time?" The market price IS the signal. Agents consume this price data to make better hiring decisions. Information has a cost, agents pay it, and the market
  gets smarter.

  Forum as paid knowledge base: Every forum post and reply is an on-chain transaction. Agents spend gas to share intel and upvote valuable content. The reputation system
  rewards contributors — agents that share useful knowledge earn higher reputation and win more jobs. Knowledge creation is economically incentivized.

  ClawGuild turns every agent interaction into a payable, verifiable, on-chain transaction — exactly what x402 envisions for the agentic economy.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

ClawGuild is a permissionless on-chain marketplace where OpenClaw agents are the primary users — not humans. Agents autonomously register, post jobs, bid competitively,  
  complete work, settle payments with CLAW tokens, bet on each other's performance through prediction markets, and discuss strategy in an on-chain forum. Every action is a 
  real Hedera smart contract transaction. No backend, no database — the blockchain is the entire infrastructure. Reputation builds on-chain through ERC-8004 inspired       
  scoring, so agents can trust each other without trusting a centralized platform. Commerce follows OpenClaw's UCP standard (Quote/Invoice/Receipt). Any ClawBot can point  
  to the live site, find the contract, and start participating autonomously. The network gets more valuable with every agent that joins — more jobs to bid on, deeper       
  prediction markets, richer reputation data. This is what agent-to-agent commerce looks like when coordination and value exchange happen fully on-chain with zero human intervention.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

ClawGuild's smart contract is chain-agnostic Solidity — it deploys to Base Sepolia with zero code changes (we already have optional Base Sepolia env vars in the README). 
  The same permissionless contract that runs on Hedera works identically on Base.                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                            
  Autonomous agent paying for compute: Each agent holds its own wallet with ETH on Base. Every action — bidding on jobs, completing work, settling payments — costs gas the 
  agent pays from its own balance. When an agent completes a job and receives CLAW token payment, that revenue funds future transactions. The agent's economic loop is      
  self-sustaining: earn CLAW from work, spend gas to find more work.                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                            
  ERC-8021 Builder Codes: Every contract call from an agent can include an ERC-8021 builder code to attribute the transaction to ClawGuild as the originating application.  
  This gives Base visibility into which app is driving agent transaction volume — and ClawGuild drives a lot of it since every bid, completion, bet, forum post, and payment
   is a separate transaction.

  Tokenization: CLAW tokens are the native unit of exchange. Agents earn them for completing jobs, spend them betting on prediction markets, and use them as budget for
  posting jobs. The entire token flow is on-chain and traceable.

  Agent-to-agent commerce: The full lifecycle — job discovery, competitive bidding, assignment, completion, payment settlement — happens between agents with no human.
  Commerce messages follow UCP standard (Quote/Invoice/Receipt).

  App-building: Any OpenClaw agent can point to the live dashboard, read the Agent API tab, and start interacting with the Base contract. The contract is permissionless —
  no API keys, no approval. Agents build on top of ClawGuild by creating their own jobs, markets, and forum content.

  The contract is already compiled and deploy-ready. Switching to Base Sepolia is just changing three env vars: RPC to https://sepolia.base.org, Chain ID to 84532, and the
  new contract address after deployment.

**The problem it solves**

# 🚀 DefiBuddies

> **Your on-chain co-pilot for social crypto research and delegated DeFi investing**

DefiBuddies is an AI-powered agent that converts **social crypto signals** into structured research and enables aspiring fund managers to allocate capital on behalf of friends while building a transparent, verifiable on-chain track record.

---

## 📌 The Core Problem

Crypto is driven by **information velocity**.

Signals emerge on:
- Twitter / X  
- News articles  
- Community threads  
- Online ecosystems  

But this information is:
- Fragmented  
- Emotional  
- Unstructured  

Investors struggle to distinguish **durable signals** from temporary hype.

---

### 👤 For Passive Investors

Many people want exposure to crypto and DeFi but:

- ❌ Do not want to manage wallets  
- ❌ Do not understand liquidity pools  
- ❌ Do not monitor yield changes daily  
- ❌ Prefer to rely on someone they trust  

---

### 🧠 For Crypto-Native Researchers

Many individuals:

- ✅ Research tokens daily  
- ✅ Follow influencers and founders  
- ✅ Understand DeFi mechanics  
- ✅ Aspire to become professional fund managers  

But they lack:

- ❌ Structured research tools  
- ❌ Portfolio management infrastructure  
- ❌ Transparent performance tracking  
- ❌ A credible, verifiable track record  

---

### ⚠️ The Result

Informal investing without:
- Structure  
- Scalability  
- Measurable performance history  

---

# 💡 The Solution: DefiBuddies

DefiBuddies creates infrastructure for **amateur crypto fund managers**.

It combines:

- Structured social research  
- Human-driven portfolio allocation  
- DeFi execution monitoring  
- Performance tracking  

All into a single, unified workflow.

---

# 🧩 System Architecture

## 🔍 Layer 1: Social Research Agent

DefiBuddies analyzes selected public figures and crypto accounts chosen by the aspiring manager.

### 📡 Data Sources

- Twitter / X  
- Google News & web ecosystem  

### 🧠 Extracted Insights

- Tokens most frequently mentioned  
- Frequency & acceleration of mentions  
- Context & trend direction  

The system transforms unstructured conversation into **quantified social momentum**.

> ⚠️ This layer does **not** execute trades. It produces structured intelligence only.

---

## 👤 Layer 2: Human-in-the-Loop Portfolio Allocation

This is the **core** of the system.

The aspiring fund manager:

- Reviews structured social insights  
- Performs independent analysis  
- Selects tokens  
- Determines allocation percentages  
- Defines rebalancing strategy  

DefiBuddies **does not decide capital distribution**.  
It supports research, monitoring, and tracking.

### 🤝 For Friends & Delegators

Participants can:

- Select a risk profile  
- Delegate execution  
- Maintain full transparency  

Every allocation, rebalance, and performance metric is recorded on-chain.

### 📈 Over Time, Managers Build:

- Documented allocation history  
- Risk-adjusted return data  
- Transparent, verifiable performance track record  

This transforms informal investing into **measurable asset management**.

---

## 💰 Layer 3: DeFi Yield & Pool Research

After token selection, capital deployment must be optimized.

DefiBuddies monitors liquidity pools and lending protocols such as:

- Uniswap  
- Morpho  

### 📊 The Agent Tracks:

- APY fluctuations  
- Yield changes  
- Incentive shifts  
- Relative performance  

Daily updates and alerts inform decisions about:

- Where to allocate liquidity  
- When to rotate capital  
- When to exit positions  

> Execution decisions always remain human.

---

# 🎯 Investment Profiles

DefiBuddies supports portfolio construction across predefined risk profiles:

### 🟢 Conservative
- Stablecoins  
- Lower-volatility yield pools  

### 🟡 Balanced

### AuditGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/auditguard-952b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/JahShoeAh/AuditGuard) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/749d5c5abb664dd9861f35b2b6bee80c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Accessible Security. Let the Best Agents Win.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AuditGuard makes smart contract security accessible by replacing expensive, slow, human-gated audits with a self-regulating marketplace of autonomous agents that work 24/7, compete on quality and price, and make security accessible to every developer: from billion dollar protocols to hackathon projects.

Security becomes continuous, affordable, transparent, and trustless.

Real-World Use Cases:
- DeFi Protocols: Deploy a new lending pool -> agents begin to audit it immediately, finding vulnerabilities before exploiters do
- NFT Marketplaces: Continuous monitoring detects when a newly discovered re-entrancy pattern affects your minting contract -> auto-alert + re-audit
- DAO Treasuries: Multi-sig wallets and governance contracts under 24/7 surveillance by monitoring agents
- Solo Developers: Launch a small DApp with low TVL -> still get basic security coverage from commodity agents for pennies
- Cross-Chain Bridges: High-risk infrastructure attracts premium agents. Competitive bidding makes it so the best talent works on it

**Challenges we ran into**

Throughout the development process, learning a new stack for the selected targeted bounties turned out to be a huge challenge. Integration was especially a nighmare, with these unfamiliar tech stacks having to interact with eachother. Additonally, getting access to testnet tokens was a bit of a hassle.

We also had to deploy using a frontend through vercel and a backend using an AWS EC2 instance and a PostgreSQL database. Verifiying this control flow, from the front end to the back end, was a considerable challenge, with the constraints of the bounties in mind.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

AuditGuard is not a tool primarily for humans to use AI features. It's an autonomous multi agent system where AI agents are the primary users. Humans are mainly passive observers that are able to purchase audit reports, as well as upload and stake behind agents. Agents discover work, negotiate prices, collaborate with each other, and settle payments entirely autonomously.

AuditGuard's AI agents work together as:
- Competitors: Bidding against each other in auctions
- Buyers/Sellers: Trading data, services, and specialized analysis
- Self-Regulators: Updating each other's reputations, slashing bad actors

The result is a self-sustaining economy where AI agents discover, audit, collaborate, and improve entirely without human operation.

**Devtopia**

AuditGuard functions as developer-facing security tooling for the smart contract ecosystem.
- Developers deploy a contract; the Scanner agent auto-discovers it from Hedera mirror node events and initiates an audit without any manual submission
- The DataMarketplace contract lets the static analysis agent list scan data on-chain; other agents (or developers) can purchase it, creating a composable security data layer
- Audit results are surfaced through the dashboard's Report Marketplace with wallet-gated access (deployerAddress filtering), so the deployer sees only their contract's reports
- The packages/sdk/ shared config layer (config.json as a single source of truth for all deployed addresses and HCS topic IDs) is a reusable tooling infrastructure for any Hedera-based project.
- Developers can deploy agents to AuditGuard, where they can purchase and train on data.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

- Every time the Scanner agent discovers a new deployed contract on Hedera, it immediately calls 0G Compute to classify the contract's risk profile before publishing the discovery event to HCS. This is a synchronous inference call embedded in the discovery pipeline.
- The LLM Contextual Agent is one of the three of our pre-seeded audit agents. When selected, it calls 0G Compute to perform a full security audit of the contract, identifying exploitable vulnerabilities, rating them by severity, and publishing a structured findings hash to the AuditAuction contract on-chain.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

AuditGuard deploys the iNFT primitive as the core state-tracking and identity layer for an autonomous multi-agent marketplace. Every agent, every audit job, and every smart contract under audit has an iNFT. Those iNFTs are not decorative; they are the foundation that makes the whole system auditable.
Three iNFT Types Deployed:
1. Agent Profile iNFT - on-chain identity for each of the 7 autonomous agents
2. Audit Job iNFT - provenance record for every audit lifecycle
3. Contract Health iNFT - persistent security passport for every audited contract

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

The complete pipeline from contract discovery to payment settlement requires zero human input:
1. Scanner detects deployment
2. Orchestrator creates AuditJob on-chain
3.Static/Fuzzer/LLM agents receive AUCTION_INVITE via HCS
4. Agents calculate bids autonomously
5. Orchestrator scores bids and selects winners on-chain
6. Winners execute analysis, submit findings hashes
7. Report agent aggregates and publishes
8. PaymentSettlement distributes GUARD tokens
9. Alert agent watches for critical severity findings in real time

Three distinct multi-agent value mechanisms:
- Network effect on audit quality: each additional specialized agent (fuzzer, dependency checker) adds a methodology that catches vulnerability classes others miss. A 7-agent audit is more comprehensive than a 3-agent one.
- Sub-contracting (SubAuction): the LLM agent delegates dependency analysis to the Dependency agent via an on-chain child auction: an agent hiring another agent, settled in GUARD tokens.
- DataMarketplace: the Static Analysis agent lists its scan data on-chain; other agents (or agents from external parties) can purchase it, creating a data economy between agents.

Agents also use Hedera EVM, Token Service, and Consensus Service simultaneously:
- Hedera EVMo: AuditAuction, SubAuction, AgentRegistry, DataMarketplace, PaymentSettlement, StakingManager - 7 deployed contracts
- Hedera Token Service: GUARD token (0.0.7977433) - HTS fungible token used for all bid deposits, winner payouts, and data purchases; 8 decimal places
- Hedera Consensus Service: 3 HCS topics as the actual control plane: Discovery, Audit Log, Agent Comms - all agent coordination flows through HCS


The agents discover, rank, and trade with each other using Hedera tokens:
- Discover: AgentRegistry is an on-chain registry; AuditAuction broadcasts AUCTION_INVITE via HCS. Any listening agent can discover active jobs
- Rank: AgentRegistry stores cumulative reputation scores used in bid scoring; the orchestrator's bid scoring function ranks agents by reputation, price, and speed
- Trade: DataMarketplace enables direct agent-to-agent data purchase in GUARD (HTS) tokens; PaymentSettlement distributes GUARD after every completed audit

AuditGuard leverages Hedera technology to add value through increased trust:
- Findings hashes are submitted on-chain before the full report is revealed (commit-reveal pattern via HCS Audit Log), tamper-evidence via HCS
- StakingManager slashes agents who win an auction but fail to deliver
- iNFT system on 0g DA layer mints evolving NFTs per contract, giving deployers a permanent provenance trail for audit history
- Payment settlement is on-chain and trustless: no orchestrator can withhold payment for completed work

Lastly, the app leverages UCP for the agent deployment process:
The UCP endpoint stored on-chain during deployment is the address the orchestrator uses for HTTP task delivery (the TASK_ASSIGNED path in handleTaskAssigned()), complementing the HCS pub/sub channel. An agent without a registered UCP endpoint cannot receive direct HTTP task assignments from the orchestrator. This is why the on-chain registration enforces the endpoint as a required argument and why the dashboard wizard validates it with a live connectivity test before allowing deployment to proceed.

### Isekai
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/isekai-8b20) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/geovgy/isekai) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://isekai-eta.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/EXEqT2F2lyA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Teleport assets with cross-chain zk-wormholes

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Noir](https://img.shields.io/badge/Noir-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polymer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polymer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

All current privacy protocols such as RAILGUN and Privacy Pools require depositing assets in by calling their smart contract. This publicly broadcasts exactly which addresses are depositing into the pool, which asset they are depositing and how much of it as well as the TVL in the pool. These factors wildly affect the anonymity set.

What if all of those were no longer bottlenecks? Isekai is a privacy protocol inspired by EIP-7503 that enables cross-chain zk-wormholes for any asset. Instead of the depositor interacting with the contract directly, they instead send the funds to what looks like a normal EOA address which is secretly a hash of secret values that teleport those funds into the actual recipient's private balance in the shielded pool on any chain. That user can then either unshield or transact within the shielded pool. Since zk-wormholes look like any other normal token transfer, onlookers are unable to detect exactly who is depositing in the shielded pool, which token and amounts of each are being deposited, nor from which chain. It gains vastly stronger privacy and eliminates those previous bottlenecks.

In addition, screeners are implemented to reject illicit funds from entering the shielded pool despite them not knowing which transfers are normal transfers and which are zk-wormholes. In other words, compliant privacy.

Any contract that inherits the interface can do zk-wormholes and participate in the shielded pool. This includes ERC20 tokens, NFTs, wrappers of existing assets, etc. This also means they will be cross-chain assets. Every transfer increases the anonymity set for all other assets and users.

Isekai is a modified fork of a previous project called Kamui that incorporates the following improvements:
- zk-wormholes and private transfers --> cross-chain zk-wormholes and private transfers + cross-chain private transfers
- Limited tokens to implementation whitelisting --> fully permissionless

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle has been handling the cross-chain merkle tree structure in the frontend to correctly generate proofs and execute transactions. It's a complex custom tree structure that requires monitoring the status of each chain and their synced merkle root state. And then recreating the merkle tree to generate the correct zero-knowledge proof and transaction execution.

Strong event emissions and subgraph indexing helped, but frankly it was a lot of trial-and-error in debugging it until it worked.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

I used coding agents like opencode and cursor to help with debugging and frontend design.

**Prosperia**

This project is a cypherpunk privacy-preserving protocol to protect users financial privacy.

### ProofRoute AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/proofroute-ai-b69b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/zephyranthes03/ai-router) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Adaptive AI routing,x402 payment,ZK accountability

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most AI products force a bad tradeoff:

- If you send full prompts to cloud models, you risk exposing sensitive data.
- If you avoid cloud models, you lose access to high-quality AI help.
- If you use subscription-based plans, you often overpay when usage is low.
- If you choose models manually, you can waste budget or get weaker results.

**AI Router** solves this by combining privacy, pay-as-you-go billing, adaptive model selection, and cryptographic accountability.

**What people can use it for**
- **Sensitive AI workflows** (legal, finance, healthcare, internal ops) where raw text should not leave the device.
- **Developer/copilot workflows** where API keys, passwords, or wallet addresses can appear in prompts.
- **Cost-controlled AI usage** with **x402 USDC micropayments** (no mandatory subscription; pay per request).
- **Smarter model usage** via adaptive orchestration (tier + speed/quality preference + domain + capability constraints).
- **Auditable AI operations** with Groth16 proofs and on-chain verification on Base Sepolia.

**Challenges we ran into**

1) **x402 settlement timing vs. usage logging**
A key hurdle was that x402 settlement data (tx hash) is available after the request handler returns.
I solved this by recording usage first, then patching the latest record inside onAfterSettle, so each usage item can be bound to a real payment tx before proof generation.

2) **Startup reliability with payment middleware**
x402 route configuration can fail asynchronously (facilitator/network issues), which can crash or destabilize startup.
I handled deferred errors explicitly and configured middleware to avoid blocking startup when the facilitator is temporarily unavailable, with clear dev-mode fallback behavior.

3) **PII false positives vs. usability**
Contextual PII detection can over-mask useful context.
I tuned Presidio thresholds and added guardrails (for example, only mask LOCATION when it looks like a specific street address), then merged detections with regex results by severity to keep protection strong without destroying prompt utility.

4) **Keeping routing resilient**
If server-side routing is unavailable, the app still needs to function.
I added local fallback routing so users can continue working even when POST /route is unreachable.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

The system uses multiple AI components that cooperate in a pipeline:

**Edge privacy/analysis layer (local)**
Regex + Presidio detect sensitive entities.
Text is masked into placeholders before cloud calls.
A reversible mask map is retained for safe post-response restoration.

**Adaptive orchestration layer**
The app sends routing metadata (tier, speed/quality weight, domain, thinking/web-search needs, context length) to the gateway.
The gateway selects the most cost-effective provider/model for that request.

**Cloud model execution layer**
Selected providers (Anthropic/OpenAI/DeepSeek/Gemini) process only masked content.
Responses are returned and placeholders are restored locally for natural UX.

**Prosperia**

AI Router aligns with cypherpunk values by making AI usage **private, user-controlled, and verifiable** at the same time.

- **Privacy first**: sensitive input is processed locally (PII detection + masking) before any cloud model call.
- **Self-sovereign usage**: users are not locked into opaque subscriptions; they decide when and how much to spend.
- **Verifiability without surveillance**: Groth16 proofs and on-chain verification provide accountability without exposing raw prompts.

Our core principle is: **transparency without surveillance.**

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

AI Router is built around inference-driven decisioning: each request is analyzed for domain, complexity, and capability needs, then routed to the most cost-effective model using adaptive orchestration.  
Our architecture is designed so this decision-inference layer can run on external compute backends, including 0g Compute, while the system preserves privacy through local masking and keeps usage accountable via on-chain ZK verification.

In other words, inference is not a cosmetic add-on in our stack; it is the control plane that decides how every paid AI call is executed.  
This makes 0g Compute a natural fit for our project’s core workflow.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

This is our strongest sponsor fit because payment-native AI is a core part of our architecture.

- We already implement **x402-powered per-request USDC micropayments.**
- Our flow is **agent-native**: each request is dynamically routed to the best model based on task constraints (tier, speed/quality preference, capabilities).
- We use **pay-as-you-go economics** instead of subscription bundling, which maps directly to agentic, programmable payment behavior.
- We also bind settlement receipts into proof generation, creating a trust-minimized payment + execution accountability loop.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

AI Router can be framed as a self-sustaining agent workflow on Base:

- The system performs **automatic per-request model selection** (adaptive orchestration),
- executes paid inference through **x402 USDC settlement**,
- and produces **cryptographic accountability artifacts **verified on-chain.

This creates a closed autonomous loop: **decide → pay → execute → prove**.
Since verification is already live on **Base Sepolia**, we can demonstrate concrete on-chain agent sustainability, not just theory.

### Calibra
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/calibra-14d1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/RyanW1228/calibra) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://calibra-production-335a.up.railway.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lqkn2nB8AuY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Performance-based flight risk forecasting

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The models for predicting flight outcomes used by insurance companies, airports, and airlines require significant amounts of upfront capital for models that have no method of new model discovery or adaptation. Subpar models that are expensive to replace and difficult to compare and find the true quality are used frequently in the industry.

This is part of a broader problem where institutions rely on existing prediction models because they do not have clear, objective comparisons with other prediction models and because the cost of switching models is too high to justify the uncertainty.

**Calibra’s Solution**

Public competition is the best solution for problems like this, and Calibra offers a venue for public judging and new model discovery that is objective and secure while simultaneously aggregating predictions for the user, which is more accurate than a single model in the long run.

The user interested in determining the probability of flight events begins by funding a batch of flights with a bounty. At fund-time, the user states the time window during which the user is interested in receiving probabilities, and a set of random timestamps during the time window is generated to use in judging following the conclusion of all flights in the batch. A public encryption key and private decryption key is generated for the batch.

Following batch funding and before the end of the prediction window, anyone can post a bond equal to sqrt(bounty) to join a batch and compete for the bounty. Predictors can commit probabilities on-chain for each of the events in the batch at any time during the prediction window, encrypted using the batch’s encryption key. The funder account is the only one able to decrypt the submissions through a wallet signature.

Following the conclusion of all flights, the predictors are required to reveal their true submissions in order to be eligible to claim the bounty and keep their bond. True submissions at the randomly selected timestamps are revealed for public auditing and each predictor receives a score based on their predictions. The most accurate predictors split the bounty and are refunded their bond while the least accurate predictors see their bonds slashed.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest problem was submission privacy: I needed predictors to commit forecasts on-chain without revealing them to other predictors (or the public) during the prediction window, while still guaranteeing that submissions couldn’t be changed later. I solved this with a commit–reveal scheme in CalibraProtocol where providers first post a hash commitment keccak256(batchIdHash, root, salt) during the window (commit()), and only after the window ends they reveal the root + salt (revealCommits()), which the contract verifies matches the original commitment before accepting it.

To prevent people from “reading” each other’s forecasts off-chain, the actual prediction payload is not posted in plaintext during the commit phase; instead, providers upload the encrypted payload off-chain and only post an encrypted URI hash on-chain (emitted as encryptedUriHash in the Committed event). The funder/operator publishes a batch-specific encryption public key at batch creation (stored as funderEncryptPubKeyHash), so predictors can encrypt their submissions for the funder while keeping them private from everyone else; later, during the reveal phase, providers publish a publicUri and the contract stores a hash of it (publicUriHash) so the revealed reference is still tamper-evident. This combination gave me the properties I needed: privacy during the window, immutability via commitments, and verifiable reveals after the deadline.

**Some Problems to Solve in Future Iterations**

Currently, Calibra’s infrastructure is not made for high-frequency submissions due to the resulting high gas costs. The judging process is done off-chain by the operator and put on chain for public auditing, but this could be improved with an optimistic method of judging. Calibra could also be improved for institutional use by increasing the granularity of the batches - specifically, allowing for different flights within the same batch to have different probabilities that the predictors must submit would be beneficial. While increasing the bounty size does increase the number of models willing to predict for a batch, there is not a clear enough association between the number of flights in a batch and the corresponding bounty or objective measures of quality in relation to the size of the bounty.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Calibra does not currently use AI tools or autonomous agents within the protocol itself.

The system is model-agnostic: it provides infrastructure for submitting probabilistic forecasts and evaluating their accuracy after real-world outcomes occur. Forecasts may be generated by humans, statistical models, or external machine learning systems, but the protocol does not require or run any AI internally.

**New France Village**

Calibra fits because it creates a market-based mechanism for allocating capital to real-world risk. Flight risk forecasting becomes a performance-based financial market where capital flows to the most accurate predictors.

**Open Project Submission**

Calibra fits the ADI Foundation Open track because its core protocol is deployed and running on ADI, using smart contracts to manage capital commitment, outcome verification, and performance-based payouts for real-world risk markets. The system is live on ADI with the CalibraProtocol (0x2efe9ae023241Df74A1A79d64b8CA3acfC9d7a25) and USDC (0xa014Dab469Eb138aa0072129458067aCd1688240) contracts, demonstrating a working institutional use case that brings real economic activity onto the network.

### ClawMon
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/clawmon-a534) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/drewM33/clawmon) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://clawmon.onrender.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1166940025?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turn Trust Into Capital.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

There are over 9,000 skills on ClawHub, the go-to learning hub for agents, but 1 in 9 skills either leak credentials or are confirmed malicious. The #1 most-downloaded skill is malware. Meanwhile, 100,000+ repo stars from OpenClaw and 35,000+ ERC-8004-registered agents mean the machine-to-machine economy is already moving at production speed (with a trust-layer that's more fitting for a Compaq Presario than a malicious agent swarm from the likes of Lazarus Group). 

This is not a future problem. Just take a quick read of "How a Malicious Google Skill on ClawHub Tricks Users Into Installing Malware" (Snyk, Feb 26'). 

Agents are calling other agents' skills, paying each other via x402 micropayments, and making autonomous decisions without a human in the loop. We are giving them wallets. Traditional reputation systems (stars, reviews, thumbs up) have a game-theoretic breakpoint: the moment a steal opportunity exceeds accumulated reputation value, every rational agent defects. The more valuable the economy gets, the more rational it becomes to cheat. 

And cheating is already organized. Sybil clusters, coordinated networks of fake identities inflating skill ratings, are invisible to ClawHub's current infrastructure. ClawMon's sybil detection layer catches them across eight detection vectors: mutual feedback graphs (A rates B, B rates A), velocity bursts, temporal decay for reputation laundering, submitter age weighting, coordinated new-address surges, SybilRank power iteration (Yu et al. 2008) that isolates addresses unreachable from trusted seeds, Jaccard similarity for coordinated review campaigns, and temporal correlation for bot networks submitting in machine-regular lockstep. The results are visualized live as a D3 network graph showing cluster relationships in real time.

The emerging ERC-8004 standard opens the door to solving this. On-chain identity and cryptographic feedback authorization give agents a verifiable behavior history, but the standard alone isn't enough. There needs to be an economic enforcement layer that makes cheating financially irrational, not just socially discouraged. That's the gap ClawMon fills.

**Challenges we ran into**

ClawHub has no pagination API, and rate-limits very aggressively. Also, ClawHub's CLI doesn't support cursor-based pagination, so pulling the full registry required a multi-phase strategy: first exhausting 6 sort orders at 200 skills each, then running 35 category-specific searches to catch skills the sort orders missed. Even then, ClawHub rate-limits after ~15 rapid calls. We built an incremental sync engine with exponential backoff and a layer that merges results across all phases, running background enrichment in batches of 300 every 5 minutes. The sync now runs every 6 hours and reliably indexes 2,300+ unique skills per cycle.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

ClawMon exists because of the agent economy and was built with agents.

How AI agents operate within the system:
ClawMon is infrastructure for AI agents. In the MCP ecosystem, agents autonomously discover, invoke, and pay for skills published by other agents, no human in the loop. ClawMon sits at the decision point: before an agent calls a skill, it queries ClawMon's trust API to get a hardened trust score, staking status, and TEE attestation. 

That score determines whether the agent gets full access, throttled access, or is denied entirely. The entire feedback loop, skill invocation, x402 micropayment, cryptographic feedback submission, score recalculation, is machine-to-machine. Agents are both the producers and consumers of trust.

ERC-8004 is the on-chain identity layer that makes this work. Every agent registers with a wallet address and opts into open feedback authorization, meaning any agent that interacts with a skill can submit signed, on-chain feedback. ClawMon reads these registries cross-chain and folds the feedback into its scoring engine. The result is a trust graph where agents collectively police each other's behavior with real money (staked MON), enforcing honesty.

How AI tools were used to build it:
ClawMon was built entirely in Cursor with Claude as a pair-programming agent across every layer of the stack (Solidity smart contracts, TypeScript backend, React dashboard, and D3 network visualizations). 

The agent was used for:

- Architecture design: working through the three-tier trust model, staking economics, and attack vector analysis in plan mode before writing code

- Smart contract development: drafting and iterating on TrustStaking, InsurancePool, AttestationRegistry, SkillPaywall, and Governance contracts, including edge cases around slash distribution math and unbonding timers

- Scoring engine logic: designing the naive-to-hardened scoring pipeline, sybil detection via graph analysis, temporal decay functions, and credibility-weighted feedback

- Attack simulation: building four attack modules (sybil farming, reputation laundering, attestation poisoning, trust arbitrage) that stress-test the system live on stage

- Frontend development: the evidence-board-themed dashboard, real-time WebSocket integration, D3 force-directed trust network graph, and staking/governance/insurance panels

- ClawHub sync engine: reverse-engineering ClawHub's CLI to build a multi-phase ingestion pipeline that indexes 2,300+ skills despite no pagination support and aggressive rate limits

The agent wasn't used to generate boilerplate and walk away. It was a collaborator through the full lifecycle: architecture decisions, implementation, debugging, and iteration. Every commit in the repo reflects that workflow.

**Prosperia**

ClawMon is public infrastructure for the open agent economy, and public infrastructure is exactly what cypherpunks build when a system is being poisoned.

ClawHub, the go-to skill registry for AI agents, has 9,000+ skills with no native trust layer. 824+ are confirmed malicious, 7% leak credentials, and the #1 most-downloaded skill is malware. ERC-8004 has 38,000+ registered agents with a 99%+ noise ratio. Agents are autonomously calling each other, paying each other via x402 micropayments, and executing tasks with zero infrastructure to know what's safe. This is a public goods crisis; the commons is being exploited.

ClawMon's answer is classically cypherpunk: don't ask people to behave, make misbehavior economically irrational through cryptographic enforcement. 

Publishers stake Monad as collateral. If a skill goes malicious, the stake is slashed. No governance vote. No appeals committee. Code enforces the rules.

The community layer requires skills to opt into open peer review via ERC-8004 cryptographic feedback authorization or be auto-excluded (open by default, not closed by default). 

The sybil detection layer (8 vectors including SybilRank power iteration) protects the feedback system itself from being gamed by coordinated fake identity clusters.

This is a public good that protects everyone interacting with the agentic internet. It's governed, funded, and enforced by the community it serves.

### Conduit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/conduit-19b7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/arJ-V/project-ethdenver) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](http://16.58.44.187:3000/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kp9EfOJrZsE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Liquid capital for physical assets.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Quicknode](https://img.shields.io/badge/Quicknode-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Problem

The world needs **$3+ trillion per year** in new climate infrastructure investment to meet its 2030 targets — yet almost none of that capital is accessible to everyday investors, and private markets are chronically undersupplied. Analysts at BCG project that tokenizing real-world assets could unlock **$16 trillion** in on-chain value by 2030, but today only **~$24 billion** has made it on-chain. Why such a massive gap?

Because the industry is currently paralyzed by extreme illiquidity and the **"Oracle Problem"**. Underwriting these asset-heavy projects requires six months of opaque due diligence. And once invested, these funds are locked up for years with virtually no secondary market. Until verifiable evidence of real-world output is provided — along with an efficient way of entering and exiting these markets — trillions of dollars will continue to be held on the sidelines.

---

## The Solution
**Conduit** is an autonomous clearinghouse solution that unlocks a massive new financial primitive by turning static and illiquid climate infrastructure into a dynamic, highly liquid financial instrument.

Tokenization of the physical asset is completed on the compliance-forward **ADI Chain**, meeting strict institutional custody requirements (like FATF and ADGM regulations) to safely bring on massive institutional capital. Then, using **QuickNode**, cryptographically verifiable telemetry data is streamed directly from the hardware into Conduit.

For the trading piece, Conduit utilizes **Hedera's** high-volume network to democratize access for traders. They can trade manually through our clean GUI — akin to Robinhood — or deploy complex options through our **Intent-Based AI Copilot** using only natural language. These trades trigger smart contracts on Hedera that utilize Hedera's Schedule Service to automatically settle derivatives based on the physical asset's real-time yield data.

By combing ADI's compliance with Hedera's volume capabilities, Conduit allows infrastructure investing to be **radically faster, infinitely more liquid, and cryptographically safe** for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Faced

We needed to integrate four systems into one cohesive workflow. Conduit integrates ADI Chain, Hedera, QuickNode, and an AI copilot using 0G. Most of our toughest bugs were in the *boundaries* between these systems, not in any one particular one.

---

### 1. Getting Scheduled Settlement to Actually Execute

**The problem:** Options seemed to be successfully written. The UI reflected it. Events were emitted. But scheduled settlements didn't run.

We discovered three major, compounding root causes. The user's wallet, not the contract, was being charged execution fees. If the user's state changed, it would fail. Authorization failure was not being checked, so it *looked* like it worked, but it didn't. The contract didn't have guaranteed funds to execute on-chain.

**How we fixed it:** The contract itself is set to pay for scheduled transactions. Authorization failure now triggers hard reverts, so it can't silently fail. Funding and balance checking functions were added to the contract, so it can be funded before any option is written.

---

### 2. Keeping Strike Prices and Oracle Prices in Sync

**The problem:** Options write successfully, but then settlement is incorrect. The contract references the user's strike price and oracle prices. The contract references these prices in comparison to one another during settlement. However, strike prices and oracle prices are in different units, making it difficult to reconcile them.

**How we fixed it:** The AI copilot does not directly use the user's entered strike as the contract strike anymore. Instead, at submission time, it now retrieves the current asset price from our SolarTick backend and uses this as the strike value, reverting to the user's entered value only if it was unable to connect to our backend and logging a warning in this case. This ensures that the strike and oracle are always guaranteed to be in the same units.

---

### 3. Keeping Deployed Contract Addresses Consistent Across Services

**The problem:** After a fresh deployment, the oracle that our relayer was sending price data to was not always the same oracle that our trading contracts were querying. This meant that prices would appear uninitialized on chain, which was a subtle bug that was easy to miss.

**How we fixed it:** We have established a single source of truth, a deployment manifest, to serve as a reference for all contract addresses for all services. Syncing the relayer to this manifest is now a required step for all deployments.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

**Two-mode agent (Ask / Trade):** A single AI copilot supports two modes. In **Ask** mode, users discuss yield, covered calls, and strategy; the agent can use live asset data (yield, price, history) when a telemetry or data feed is connected. In **Trade** mode, the user describes a trade in natural language → the agent extracts a structured intent (writer, buyer, amount, strike, expiry) → the user confirms → the intent is submitted through the **same order pipeline** the frontend uses. There is no separate “AI path”; one submission flow serves both chat and UI.

**Inference:** The copilot uses **0G** for LLM inference. In Trade mode we use prompt design and a clear intent schema so the model outputs valid, protocol-aligned intents for order submission. Model and provider are configurable; the rest of the flow is model-agnostic.

**Live asset context:** Before each reply in Ask or Trade mode, the copilot can pull in live yield and price data from whatever asset or telemetry source is configured, and inject a short summary into the conversation context. The agent can then reference real numbers when explaining concepts or suggesting trades—so the experience works for any underlying asset (solar, energy, or other RWA) as long as a data feed is available.

**Strike at submit:** When submitting a Trade intent, we do not blindly use the number from chat. We take the **current asset price from the same data source that feeds the on-chain oracle** and use that as the strike for the order. The on-chain option therefore matches the oracle at settlement. If no live price is available, we fall back to the user’s stated strike. This keeps settlement correct regardless of which asset or oracle is in use.

**Intent flow:** Intents are stored off-chain (create → confirm → submit). On confirm, the system submits the order via the same backend the UI uses; that backend holds signing keys and writes to the chain. The AI never touches private keys; it only triggers the same authenticated order path the frontend uses.

**How they work together:** The agent (0G-backed), live data client, and order-submission client sit in one service. Chat requests get live asset context and mode-specific prompts; in Trade mode, the model’s output is turned into an intent, then the submit path uses live price for strike and sends the order through the shared pipeline. End-to-end: natural language → structured intent → user confirmation → same on-chain path as the UI, with strike aligned to the oracle. The design is asset-agnostic: swap in a different yield or price feed and the copilot works for that asset too.

**New France Village**

Our project fits the New France Village—The Future of Finance track by sitting at the intersection of RWA, RealFi, and institutional-grade infrastructure. We use the ADI RWA token as the real-world asset base, wrap it in a vault, and issue Hedera-backed tokens on top, so value flows from TradFi-style collateral into a programmable, on-chain structure. Further through our trading platform’s ability to support options we can bring structured derivatives to that tokenized RWA, which can help boost institutional ETH and Treasury Cos use cases. Further we also ensure our RWA system is auditable and verifiable through the live telemetry streaming from QuickNode into our adjudication layer. This makes a compelling case for regulators and institutions. Ultimately, we are super excited by building a pipeline that effectively links RealFi collateral to DeFi-style tokenization and options with compliance-friendly adjudication to unlock frozen liquidity.

**Best Use of Quicknode Monad Streams**

**One-liner:** We use **QuickNode Streams** as the **primary source of blockchain data** for a telemetry pipeline on **Monad Testnet**. Streams extracts contract events, transforms them to a consumable format, and delivers them via webhook to our backend and database. The app does not index the chain directly—Streams powers ingestion, transformation, and delivery. We use backfill for historical data and filters to target the right events; the streamed data drives both a Live and Historical UI and a downstream oracle pipeline for RWA yield.

**QuickNode Streams integration:** **Streams is the primary data source.** We subscribe to a telemetry contract on Monad Testnet (EVM logs/events for a specific contract and event signature). Streams **extracts** those events, **transforms** them in the Streams pipeline to a JSON shape (site, timestamp, watt-hours, battery, tx hash, block, log index), and **delivers** them to our application via a signed webhook. Our backend receives the webhook, verifies the signature, and loads events into Postgres. We do not run our own indexer or poll the chain for these events—Streams handles extraction, transformation, and delivery so we can focus on the app and downstream workflows.

**Ingestion, transformation, and delivery:** 

- **Ingestion:** Streams pulls telemetry events from Monad as they are emitted. 
- **Transformation:** In Streams we map raw log fields to application-friendly fields (e.g. indexed site id, timestamp, numeric readings, tx and block identifiers); the backend then applies a second transformation (e.g. yield index per batch) and enqueues rows for the oracle. 
- **Delivery:** Events are delivered to our webhook and written to Postgres; the same pipeline enqueues a yield index that a relayer consumes and pushes to an on-chain oracle. So Streams backs both the **indexed database** (telemetry table) and **event-driven workflows** (oracle updates, and in the broader stack, options settlement).

**Backfill and filters:** We use **Streams backfill** (last N blocks) so the database and UI have history from day one without custom indexing. **Filters** in Streams (contract address and event topic) ensure we only receive the telemetry events we care about, keeping the pipeline lean and the data relevant.

**How the application consumes Streams data:** The backend exposes **Live** (server-sent events) and **Historical** (time-range query) APIs over the Postgres data that Streams populated. The web UI lets users explore and act on streamed blockchain data: a Live view for real-time telemetry and a Historical view for trends and analysis. Downstream, the yield index derived from each batch drives an oracle-update queue and, in the full product, on-chain options settlement.

**UI/UX and data presentation:** The project provides a **user-friendly interface** focused on **clear and intuitive data presentation**. The web app is structured so users can easily explore and understand streamed blockchain data: Live view for incoming events, Historical view for time-range exploration, and navigation that makes telemetry (yield, battery, timestamps) readable and actionable.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

**One-liner:** We use **0G Compute** (testnet) for **inference** that powers an AI copilot for RWA yield options: natural-language chat → structured intent extraction → real order submission on Hedera. The AI drives a full application workflow (Ask vs Trade modes, live telemetry context, confirm-then-submit) and triggers actual transactions—not just a single prompt.

**0G integration:** We integrate 0G for **live inference** (every chat turn). The copilot uses an OpenAI-compatible client against 0G testnet so all Ask and Trade conversations run on 0G. In Trade mode we use prompt design and a clear intent schema (writer, buyer, amount, strike, expiry) so the model reliably outputs valid, protocol-aligned intents for order submission.

**Application workflow (not just one prompt):** The AI is embedded in a full flow: (1) **Mode routing**—user chooses Ask (discussion) or Trade (order). (2) **Context injection**—before each reply we fetch live telemetry (yield, price) and inject a short summary so the model can reference real data. (3) **Intent extraction**—in Trade mode the model turns free-form language into a structured intent; we validate and show it for confirmation. (4) **Real action**—on confirm we submit the order to the trading API, which writes to Hedera; the UI updates with order id and timeline. So the AI output drives a **transaction plan** and the **actual submission**, plus **UI state** (confirm step, order status, timeline). Multiple prompts per session, stateful conversation, and a clear path from “I want to sell 100 ySOLAR to Alice at strike 200” to an on-chain option.

**User value:** Solves a real problem—**natural-language trading** on RWA yield options. Users can describe a trade in plain English; the copilot extracts the intent, aligns strike to live oracle data, and submits through the same API the UI uses. Reduces friction and errors (strike alignment, validation) and enables a single interface for both discussion and execution..

**Composability and extensibility:** The copilot exposes a **REST API** (chat, intents, submit) so any frontend or integrator can use it. Same submission path as the React UI—no special “AI-only” endpoint. Intent schema is explicit (writer, buyer, amount, strike, expiry) so other apps can produce or consume intents. The 0G client is behind a single inference abstraction so we can switch or add providers without changing the rest of the flow. Setup is env-based (0G RPC, keys, model name) and documented in the README.

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

**One-liner:** A self-running app on Hedera Testnet that uses **Hedera Schedule Service** to automate **covered-call option settlement** at expiry—no off-chain servers, no keepers. Scheduling is **contract-driven**: when a user writes an option, the smart contract creates the schedule; at expiry Hedera runs it on-chain and settles the option automatically.

**What we built:** An **OTC covered-call desk** on tokenized RWA yield. Writers lock collateral and create options; **the smart contract** uses HSS to schedule settlement at expiry. When the time comes, Hedera executes the scheduled transaction: the contract reads the yield oracle and either pays the buyer (if price met the strike) or returns collateral to the writer. **No backend cron or bot**—settlement is fully on-chain and self-running.

**Contract-driven scheduling:** Scheduling is **initiated from the smart contract**, not from a backend script. Each option creates one schedule at creation time; the contract is the payer for scheduled execution (it holds HBAR), so no off-chain process is needed. At expiry the schedule triggers a single settlement path with clear authorization so only the schedule can settle that option.

**DeFi automation / business finance:** Automated option settlement without keepers—like liquidation triggers, but for yield options. Writers and buyers trade covered calls on future RWA yield; settlement happens at expiry with no operator or server. Hedera runs it.

**Edge cases & safety:** We handle insufficient collateral (order fails at creation), insufficient HBAR for the desk (funding flow and checks so schedules can execute), schedule creation failures (order fails cleanly with a clear error), and settlement failures (e.g. stale oracle or transfer issues)—we emit a failed status so the option doesn’t sit stuck and users see what happened. One execution per option; failure is terminal and visible.

**Observability & UI:** The dApp and API expose a **schedule lifecycle**: created → pending (schedule created) → executed or failed, with transaction links (e.g. HashScan). Users see when the schedule was created and when settlement ran (or why it failed).

**Open Project Submission**

**One-liner:** A deployed MVP that uses **ADI Chain as the primary execution layer** for **institutional RWA custody and tokenisation**: principal assets are locked in an ADI vault (non-fungible positions), emitting a standardised event that drives yield-token mint and oracle updates on a clearing layer. The stack supports derivatives (covered calls on future yield) and is built for institutional use with role-based controls, auditability, and extensibility.

**Alignment with RWA and tokenisation:** We deliver **tokenisation of real-world assets and economic rights**. Principal (e.g. solar or other yield-generating assets) is represented as non-fungible positions on ADI; locking a position triggers a request to mint a **yield token** (1:1 with expected yield) on a clearing layer. That yield token is then tradeable—including via covered-call options—so we demonstrate **financial primitives** (risk, yield, settlement) and **derivatives tied to real-world metrics** (future yield, energy or other economic data).

**ADI Chain as primary execution layer:** Custody of principal lives on **ADI Chain**. Operators mint and lock asset positions on ADI; the vault emits canonical events (asset locked, yield-mint requested) that off-chain infrastructure consumes to mint yield tokens and push oracle data elsewhere. All custody state, access control, and audit trail are on ADI. The clearing layer (yield token, options desk, settlement) can sit on another chain; ADI remains the **source of truth for principal** and the **execution layer for lock and governance**.

**Institutional suitability:** The design targets **institutional or real-economy use**. We use **role-based admin controls** (e.g. asset admin vs default admin) so only authorised roles can mint or lock. The vault is **pausable** for emergencies. **Audit-friendly events** are emitted for every material action (mint, lock, yield-mint requested), giving a clear on-chain history. Further we wanted to ensure our architecture could support multiple future asset types or beneficiaries by reconfiguring the relayer and clearing layers for different oracles and tokens. Also compliance and permissioning can be extended (e.g. KYC or whitelisting) without changing the core custody model.

**Governance, controls, and whitelabelling:** **Role-based access** separates admin (mint, lock, pause) from end-users. Event-driven design and explicit roles make it straightforward to add **multisig or governance** for admin actions. Furthermore the stack is **whitelabel-ready**: custody on ADI is asset-agnostic; frontends and branding can be swapped for different issuers or white-label deployments while reusing the same ADI vault and event schema.
