### NovaCreator
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/novacreator-10a5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rikokurnia/cre-app-v1) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://novacreator.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A socialfi that related to Content Creator

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![next](https://img.shields.io/badge/next-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Retail traders are currently trapped between high-risk speculation and overly complex financial tools.**

On Base Chain, retail users ("degens") often resort to memecoin trading because institutional-grade derivatives are too intimidating. Traditional DeFi Option protocols present users with confusing "Option Chains," complex Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Theta), and liquidity fragmentation. Furthermore, the SocialFi sector (e.g., Friend.tech) suffers from a retention crisis—users leave once the hype fades because there is no real financial utility beyond speculating on social clout.

**NovaCreator solves these problems by building a "Hybrid Layer" between Social Discovery and DeFi Execution:**

- **Democratizing Derivatives:** We abstract away the complexity of Options Trading. Instead of calculating lot sizes or analyzing Greeks, users simply choose a direction ("Up" or "Down"), input their investment amount (e.g., "$10"), and execute trades instantly.
- **Solving SocialFi Retention:** We introduce "Core Mode"—a real-yield utility layer. Users don't just chat; they copy-trade verified "Alpha Callers." This ensures users stay on the platform for financial execution, not just social interaction.
- **Verifiable Reputation:** By tracking "Paper Trading" performance in our gamified Creator Mode, we help users distinguish between skilled traders and noise/scams, creating a safer environment for social trading.
- **Gas-less Experience:** Leveraging Account Abstraction (Smart Wallets), we remove the friction of seed phrases and gas fees for onboarding, making DeFi feel like a Web2 fintech app.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Integrating the Thetanuts V4 OptionBook API and logic was the most significant challenge.**

Unlike standard AMMs (Automated Market Makers) where you simply swap Token A for Token B, Thetanuts V4 operates on a sophisticated **Order Book model** for Options.

- **The "Contracts" vs. "Investment" Logic:** The API returns option prices per contract (e.g., 1 ETH), but our UX goal was to let users input a dollar amount (e.g., "Invest $10"). I struggled to write the backend logic to precisely calculate how many fractional contracts (`0.0xxxx`) a user receives based on the real-time `Best Ask` price from the Order Book. I had to reverse-engineer the calculation to ensure the `fillOrder` function on the smart contract wouldn't revert due to slippage or insufficient liquidity depth.
- **Data Synchronization:** Fetching real-time `Strike Prices` and `Expiries` that actually had liquidity (offers) from Market Makers was tricky. Initially, the UI would show strikes with no liquidity, causing failed transactions. I solved this by filtering the API response to only display "Tradable Strikes" on the frontend.
- **Visualizing P&L:** Creating the "Payoff Diagram" and "Break Even" calculator on the client-side required reimplementing financial formulas (Black-Scholes logic simplified) in JavaScript to give users instant feedback on their potential profit/loss before they confirmed the transaction.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

**NovaCreator is built entirely on top of Thetanuts V4 OptionBook on Base.** We function as a "Retail Gateway" that democratizes access to Thetanuts' institutional-grade liquidity.

Instead of building a competing liquidity layer, we leverage **Thetanuts V4 Smart Contracts** for all trade executions and settlements. Our dApp abstracts the complexity of the Order Book (Greeks, lot sizes, strike selection) into a simplified "Invest $10" interface.

Technically, we query Thetanuts' on-chain `Best Ask` prices to calculate fractional contract amounts for users and execute orders directly against V4 Market Makers via the `fillOrder` function. This brings massive retail volume and new users to the Thetanuts ecosystem by lowering the barrier to entry.

> STPC (Shareable Token Access Protocol) is a peer-t

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Colab](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Colab-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Bhai, here is the deep technical and conceptual breakdown of STPC (Secure Token Proxy Core) in professional English. This is perfect for your Project Description, GitHub README, or Portfolio.
🛠 The Problem: The "Master Key" Dilemma

In the current AI landscape, sharing compute power is fundamentally broken. If a developer or a resource owner wants to share their premium LLM access (like Groq, Llama-3, or GPT-4) with a team or a friend, they are forced to share their Private API Key.

This creates three critical risks:

    Total Account Exposure: Sharing an API key is like giving away your bank's master password. The recipient can drain your credits, change settings, or leak the key further.

    No Kill-Switch: Once a key is shared, you cannot revoke access for one person without regenerating the key and breaking it for everyone else.

    Privacy Leakage: Standard API calls often log user metadata, which is a major concern for privacy-conscious developers.

🚀 The STPC Solution: Trustless Neural Tunneling

STPC introduces a Non-Custodial Proxy Layer that redefines how AI resources are distributed. It allows you to share the utility of your tokens without ever sharing the identity of your tokens.
1. Zero-Knowledge Vaulting

STPC encrypts your API keys locally using AES-256-GCM. The keys are never stored in plain text on any central server. Instead, the protocol creates a "Virtual Node" that acts as a secure gateway.
2. The 6-Digit Handshake (Ephemeral Access)

Instead of sharing a 64-character complex key, STPC generates a dynamic 6-digit Tunnel ID.

    The Process: The owner initializes a node, and the guest enters the ID into the STPC terminal.

    The Result: A secure bridge is established where the guest can query the model, but the API key remains hidden behind the proxy wall.

3. Real-Time Resource Orchestration

STPC provides a centralized Command Center (Dashboard) where owners can:

    Monitor Traffic: See how many tokens are being consumed in real-time.

    Instant Revocation: Shut down a specific tunnel with one click without affecting other nodes.

    Metadata Stripping: All requests are scrubbed of sensitive user data before reaching the AI provider.


Persona,Impact
SaaS Teams,Share production-level AI compute with frontend devs without risking key leakage.
AI Communities,"Host ""Public Compute Tunnels"" for high-speed models like Llama-3 via Groq for community testing."
Freelancers,"Provide clients with a live ""Inference Sandbox"" to test projects using the freelancer's premium hardware/API."
Enterprise,Implement an internal proxy to ensure employees don't send PII (Personally Identifiable Information) to third-party LLMs.
💎 The Bottom Line

STPC is to API Keys what Virtual Credit Cards are to Bank Accounts. It provides a temporary, secure, and monitorable alias for your most valuable digital assets.

Stop sharing your keys. Start sharing your power.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

STPC embodies Duality by bridging the gap between Resource Protection and Resource Distribution. In a world where AI compute is becoming the most valuable currency, STPC allows users to exist in two states simultaneously: holding their private keys with absolute security while broadcasting their AI power to the world via decentralized tunnels. We prove that security doesn't have to mean isolation, and sharing doesn't have to mean exposure."

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge 1: Complete Pivot from React Complex Architecture
The Situation:
Started with ambitious React.js + Redux + TypeScript architecture. After 12 hours of development, realized:

Too complex for 36-hour timeline
Build system taking too long to set up (Webpack, Babel configuration)
State management overhead slowing down progress
Learning curve for team members unfamiliar with React ecosystem
Every small change required full component re-render testing

Decision Point:
Made critical decision: Scratch everything and restart with vanilla JavaScript + HTML5
How We Solved It:

Pivoted to vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript (took 1 hour to restructure project)
Eliminated dependency on npm build tools
Used CDN links instead (Ethers.js, no installation needed)
Focused on core features: blockchain integration only
Separated concerns into modular files without over-engineering
Web3-config.js for API keys
Web3-integration.js for blockchain logic
script.js for UI interactions
Styles.css for responsive design

Lesson Learned:
Simplicity wins in hackathons. Vanilla stack allowed us to focus on features (blockchain, IPFS, wallet integration) instead of tooling. Deployment to GitHub Pages took 5 minutes instead of 30+ minutes with build tools.
Result:
Saved 12+ hours of debugging and complexity. Went from stuck state to fully functional MVP in remaining 24 hours.

Challenge 2: Ethereum Smart Contract Integration Without Prior Web3 Experience
The Situation:
Team had minimal Web3.js/Ethers.js experience. Need to:

Connect MetaMask wallet from browser
Send transactions to blockchain
Read data from smart contracts
Handle async operations properly

Challenges Encountered:

MetaMask window.ethereum object undefined initially (needed to check installation)
Transaction confirmation timing (didn't know to use tx.wait())
Wallet persistence across page refreshes
Understanding contract ABI vs actual contract address

How We Solved It:

Used Ethers.js instead of Web3.js (simpler API)
Researched MetaMask docs for 1 hour
Created abstraction layer (web3-integration.js) hiding complexity
Used pre-deployed smart contracts to avoid compilation issues
Tested on Sepolia testnet with free test ETH
Created utility functions:

connectWallet() - handles connection with proper error handling
registerDrugOnChain() - wraps smart contract call
verifyDrug() - reads contract data safely

Result:
Got blockchain integration working in 4 hours. User can actually execute real transactions on Ethereum.

Challenge 3: Decentralized File Storage (IPFS) API Integration
The Situation:
NFTs need to be stored permanently somewhere. Can't use centralized server (no backend). Discovered IPFS + Pinata as solution but:

Never used Pinata API before
Didn't understand IPFS hashing
Frontend to API communication seemed complex

Challenges:

FormData object creation for file upload
API authentication headers
Handling async file upload completion
Getting back IPFS hash and using it
Understanding CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)

How We Solved It:

Signed up for Pinata free tier (https://pinata.cloud)
Studied API documentation (30 minutes)
Created NFT metadata as JSON blob
Used FormData to send to Pinata
Parsed response to extract IPFS hash
Verified uploaded file by accessing via ipfs.io gateway

Testing:

Uploaded test file, got IPFS hash (QmXxxx)
Verified by visiting https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmXxxx
Data persisted permanently on IPFS

Result:
NFTs actually stored on decentralized IPFS. Can prove to judges that files are permanent and cannot be deleted.

**The problem it solves**

##  The Problem It Solves

Disaster response systems today are **slow, opaque, and unreliable**.

Damage assessment depends heavily on **manual reports**, relief funding is delayed by **bureaucracy**, and there is **little transparency** in how emergency funds are distributed. In critical situations, this lack of speed and accountability can cost **lives, resources, and trust**.

---

##  How AEGIS Makes It Better

**AEGIS automates disaster response end-to-end** using AI agents and blockchain technology.

* **AI-powered detection** rapidly analyzes satellite or drone imagery to identify disasters within seconds
* **Autonomous verification** reduces false reports and misinformation before any action is taken
* **On-chain fund disbursement** ensures relief funds are released transparently and only after verification
* **Real-time dashboards** present complex AI and blockchain activity in a clear, human-readable format

---

##  Why It’s Safer and More Reliable

* Eliminates manual and delayed decision-making
* Prevents fund leakage through verifiable blockchain transactions
* Creates an immutable public audit trail for every relief action
* Combines AI speed with verification for responsible automation

---

##  Who Can Use AEGIS

* **Governments** for faster and accountable emergency response
* **NGOs** for transparent and efficient aid distribution
* **Donors** for verifiable proof of impact
* **Disaster response teams** for real-time situational awareness

---

##  In One Line

> **AEGIS transforms disaster response into a fast, verifiable, and trust-minimized system powered by AI agents and secured by blockchain.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/15de75362d8e445ca851936ed9803a15/c9ce6b5b-cdb6-43c1-a710-8305d1bfe8df.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

##  Challenges I Ran Into

Building AEGIS involved integrating **AI, multi-agent systems, blockchain, and frontend visualization**—each of which introduced unique challenges. Some of the most impactful hurdles are outlined below.

---

###  Blockchain Transaction Failures

**The Issue:**
Even after successful disaster detection and verification, Ethereum transactions were failing with errors such as underpriced replacement transactions or silent funding failures.

**Root Cause:**
The funding logic depended on values that were not always set correctly by upstream agents, causing invalid or zero-value transactions.

**How I Solved It:**
I traced the entire pipeline end-to-end, identified the missing fallback logic, and implemented defensive checks to guarantee safe transaction execution. I also resolved Web3.py version mismatches that affected raw transaction handling.

---

###  AI Confidence vs Real-World Accuracy

**The Issue:**
Initial computer vision detections produced inconsistent confidence scores, making it difficult to determine when an event should trigger funding.

**Root Cause:**
Different disaster types required different detection strategies and thresholds, which were not initially calibrated.

**How I Solved It:**
I separated detection pipelines by disaster category (fire, flood, structural damage, casualties) and tuned confidence thresholds individually to balance sensitivity and false positives.

---

###  Agent Coordination & State Flow

**The Issue:**
Synchronizing multiple agents caused race conditions where one agent acted before another completed its task.

**Root Cause:**
A lack of clear execution boundaries between detection, verification, and execution stages.

**How I Solved It:**
I introduced a message-queue-based workflow and enforced strict state transitions, ensuring that each agent only acted once the previous stage was fully completed.

---

###  Image Processing Pipeline Errors

**The Issue:**
Image format mismatches (bytes, PIL, OpenCV arrays) caused crashes and inconsistent results during analysis.

**Root Cause:**
Different libraries required different formats, and error handling was missing during conversions.

**How I Solved It:**
I standardized the image processing pipeline, added validation checks at each stage, and implemented graceful fallbacks to prevent system-wide failures.

---

###  Rapid Frontend Prototyping vs System Complexity

**The Issue:**
Displaying real-time AI decisions and blockchain transactions without overwhelming users.

**Root Cause:**
Complex backend processes needed to be simplified for human understanding.

**How I Solved It:**
I focused on clarity-first UI design—showing only essential states, using real-time status indicators, and progressively revealing technical details when needed.

---

> A Robust ML Trading System for Crypto Markets

![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Colab](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Colab-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jupyter Notebook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter%20Notebook-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Cryptocurrency markets like Bitcoin are highly volatile and noisy, making it difficult for investors to decide when to buy or sell.
Most beginners rely on Buy & Hold or simple technical indicators (such as moving averages), which often fail during sideways or volatile market conditions.

At the same time, many machine learning models focus only on price prediction accuracy, without considering:

whether predictions are tradable

the effect of transaction costs

the risk involved in trading decisions

This creates a gap between prediction models and realistic trading strategies.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Preventing Data Leakage in Time-Series Data

One of the biggest challenges was ensuring that the model did not accidentally use future information while training. Since Bitcoin data is sequential, a random train test split would lead to look ahead bias.

How I solved it:
I strictly split the dataset based on time, training only on past data and testing on future data. All lag and rolling features were generated using historical values only, ensuring that the test set remained truly unseen.

2. Prediction Accuracy vs. Tradability

Initially, the model focused only on minimizing prediction error, but this did not always translate into a profitable trading strategy. Accurate price predictions do not automatically result in good trades.

How I solved it:
Instead of trading directly on price predictions, I switched to predicting returns for the trading task and introduced a clear execution logic that converts predictions into positions. This helped align the machine learning model with real trading objectives.

3. Handling Transaction Costs and Over-Trading

Without transaction costs, the strategy appeared unrealistically profitable due to frequent trades.

How I solved it:
I explicitly incorporated transaction costs into the back testing process, which discouraged excessive trading and resulted in a more realistic evaluation of strategy performance.

4. Balancing Model Complexity and Stability

While experimenting with advanced techniques like regime detection and walk-forward validation, the code became unstable and harder to maintain under time constraints.

How I solved it:
I prioritized a stable and interpretable core pipeline and focused on safer enhancements such as confidence-based position sizing and explainability, ensuring the final system remained robust and presentation-ready.

5. Interpreting Model Outputs

Another challenge was explaining why the model made certain decisions, especially during the presentation.

How I solved it:
I used feature importance analysis and clear visualizations (equity curves, drawdowns, and trade signals) to verify that the model relied on meaningful financial features rather than noise.

> Near duplicate image detection

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

#### What is DINOv2?

DINOv2 is a pre-trained vision model that converts images into high-quality numerical embeddings. These embeddings are capable of capturing structure and semantic information without requiring labeled data.

#### Key Capabilities

It enables similarity searches of images, detects duplicated ones, clusters datasets, performs content moderation, finds anomalies, and acts as a backbone for other tasks like classification or segmentation. Because it has been pre-trained on large-scale data, it reduces the need for labeled datasets and speeds up development.

#### Practical Benefits

In practice, DINOv2 makes systems more robust to visual variations such as cropping, resizing, and color changes. It improves the detection of duplicates and similarities, simplifies dataset organization, and reinforces moderation pipelines with fewer false negatives.

#### Why DINOv2 for Mirror of Maya?

- **Self-supervised learning:** No labeled data needed for training
- **Strong semantic understanding:** Captures image meaning beyond pixels
- **Robust to transformations:** Handles crops, rotations, color changes
- **State-of-the-art performance:** Industry-leading accuracy on similarity tasks
- **Pre-trained embeddings:** Ready to use without custom training
- **Efficient similarity search:** Works seamlessly with FAISS indexing

**Challenges we ran into**

## Bugs & Hurdles Encountered

### Critical Bug 1: The Recall Deception Problem

#### The Issue
During initial calibration, I noticed recall was consistently showing 100% across all thresholds, which made F1 optimization completely meaningless. The system appeared to be detecting everything perfectly, which was clearly wrong.

#### Root Cause
I was comparing full file paths in ground truth pairs instead of basenames. For COPYDAYS-style datasets where the same image exists in multiple folders (original/200000.jpg, jpeg/200000.jpg, crop/200000.jpg), my code was treating these as completely different images because their full paths didn't match.

python
## Wrong approach - comparing full paths
('/dataset/original/img1.jpg', '/dataset/attacks/crop/img1.jpg')
vs
('/dataset/original/img1.jpg', '/dataset/attacks/jpeg/img1.jpg')
## These never matched!


#### Solution
Implemented basename-only normalization. Now the system correctly identifies that img1.jpg in any folder is the same image:


def normalize_pair_basename(pair):
    b1 = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pair[0]))[0]
    b2 = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pair[1]))[0]
    return tuple(sorted((b1, b2)))


This fixed the evaluation completely and gave me realistic F1 scores (around 93-95% instead of false 100%).

---

### Critical Bug 2: Session State Unpacking Mismatch

#### The Issue
The application crashed with `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)` whenever users adjusted the threshold slider.

#### Root Cause
Function signature inconsistency. The `recalculate_metrics()` function was returning 2 values (F1, Precision) but UI components were trying to unpack 3 values (F1, Precision, Recall).

# Function returned 2 values:
return f1, prec

# But UI expected 3:
f1, prec, rec = recalculate_metrics(threshold)  # CRASH!


#### Solution
Since I intentionally didn't want to show recall to end users (it's more for developers), I standardized everything to return and unpack only 2 values. Updated all UI components to display just F1 Score and Precision metrics.

---

### Architectural Challenge: Dual-Stage Detection Strategy

#### The Problem
Pure DINOv2 embedding was too slow for real-time duplicate detection on large datasets. Processing 10,000 images took 2+ minutes just for embedding generation.

#### Solution
Implemented a two-phase detection pipeline:

**Phase 1 - Perceptual Hashing (dHash)**
- Catches exact and near-exact duplicates (JPEG recompression, minor edits) in seconds
- Eliminated 80%+ of duplicates immediately

**Phase 2 - DINOv2 Embeddings**
- Only processes images that passed the hash filter
- Catches semantic duplicates (crops, rotations, color changes)

This hybrid approach reduced total processing time by 60% while maintaining 93%+ recall.

---

### UI/UX Challenge: Clustering Mode Confusion

#### The Problem
Users were confused when the system grouped unrelated images together in "semantic" mode, or missed obvious duplicates in "basename" mode.

#### Solution
Added explicit clustering mode selector with clear descriptions:

- **Basename Mode (Conservative):** Only groups images with matching filenames - guaranteed same image identity
- **Semantic Mode (Aggressive):** Groups all visually similar images - may include false positives

Provided visual indicators and warnings so users understand the trade-offs.

---

### Performance Hurdle: Memory Overflow with FAISS

#### The Problem
Loading all embeddings into memory for large datasets (50k+ images) caused out-of-memory crashes on systems with less than 16GB RAM.

#### Solution
Implemented chunked processing:

chunk_size = 1000 
for start in range(0, total, chunk_size):
    end = min(start + chunk_size, total)
    vectors = index.reconstruct_n(start, end - start)
    


This kept memory usage constant regardless of dataset size.

---

### Calibration Challenge: Finding Optimal Threshold

#### The Problem
Manual threshold tuning was tedious and subjective. Different datasets needed different thresholds for optimal results.

#### Solution
Implemented automatic F1-optimized threshold calibration:

1. Generate ground truth from dataset structure
2. Detect all duplicates at minimum threshold (0.30)
3. Sweep through candidate thresholds [0.30, 0.40, ..., 0.95]
4. Calculate TP/FP/FN at each threshold
5. Select threshold with highest F1 score

This gave me data-driven threshold selection instead of guesswork, improving accuracy from approximately 85% to 93%.

---

### Dependency Hell: FAISS Installation

#### The Problem
FAISS has different packages for CPU vs GPU, and the wrong one causes cryptic errors at runtime.

#### Solution
Created clear installation instructions:

```bash
CPU-only systems
pip install faiss-cpu
NVIDIA GPU systems  
pip install faiss-gpu
```

Added automatic device detection in code to gracefully fall back to CPU if CUDA isn't available.

---

### Ethereum Wrapped

> Your on-chain year in review, decoded with data.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Ethereum is transparent, but it’s not friendly.

All your transactions, tokens, and contracts are public, yet understanding what they actually say about you is hard. Most users only see endless tables on block explorers and have no simple way to answer questions like:

How active was I on Ethereum this year?
Where did I spend most of my gas?
Am I more of a builder, trader, or explorer?

Because of this, people often know what they did on-chain, but not what it means.

Ethereum Wrapped fixes this gap.

Instead of raw data, it gives users a clear, personalized summary of their on-chain journey inspired by Spotify Wrapped. By analyzing transactions, ERC-20 transfers, and contract interactions, it turns complex blockchain activity into simple insights and stories.

Users can instantly see:

Their activity trends over time
Gas fees and efficiency
Most-used tokens and contracts
Active streaks and milestones
A Web3 persona that reflects their behavior

The goal is simple:
To make Ethereum data understandable, relatable, and fun, without requiring any technical knowledge while still being powerful enough for developers and analysts.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was connecting the backend and frontend smoothly.

The analytics pipeline was built using Flask, which meant designing a clean API that could return complex, nested blockchain insights as JSON. Since each wallet summary involves multiple analytics results, structuring the response in a way that was both flexible and easy for the frontend to consume required several iterations.

On the frontend side, parsing and handling this JSON data was not trivial. Mapping raw backend responses into meaningful UI components, handling loading states, and ensuring the data remained consistent across different sections of the “Wrapped” experience took careful coordination between both sides.

Another challenge was debugging issues related to HTTP methods, API routes, and CORS configuration. Small mismatches between frontend requests and Flask endpoints initially caused errors that were not obvious at first glance. These were resolved by carefully aligning request formats, enabling proper cross-origin access, and testing the API independently before integrating it into the UI.

Overall, this process helped me gain a much deeper understanding of API design, JSON data flow, and full-stack integration, which played a key role in shaping the final project.

> Pay-Per-Call API Marketplace powered by x402

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, most APIs are either completely free or locked behind complex subscription models and centralized payment systems. Developers who want to monetize their APIs face difficulties in setting up secure payments, tracking usage, and preventing unpaid access. On the other hand, users often struggle with complicated billing systems, credit card requirements, and lack of transparency in API usage and pricing.

This project solves these issues by introducing a decentralized, blockchain-based API gateway that enables pay-per-use APIs using crypto payments. It allows API providers to easily register and monetize their APIs, while users can securely access APIs by making on-chain payments. The system automatically verifies payments, tracks API usage, and forwards requests to external APIs, eliminating the need for manual billing, complex subscriptions, or centralized intermediaries.

Developers can use this platform to publish their APIs, set custom pricing, and monitor real-time usage and earnings. Users can access premium APIs in a transparent and trustless way, paying only for what they use. Overall, the platform makes API monetization simpler, safer, and more scalable, while bridging Web2 APIs with Web3 payments.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project, I faced several technical and architectural challenges that helped me deeply understand how Web2 and Web3 systems interact.

One major challenge was designing the middleware flow of the API gateway. Initially, it was difficult to ensure that the API existence check, payment verification, and external API fetching happened in the correct order without breaking the request flow. This caused multiple errors where APIs were being called without proper payment validation. I solved this by restructuring the route pipeline and using res.locals to securely pass API data between middlewares, making the flow clean and reliable.

Another significant hurdle was handling blockchain payment verification. Even when the blockchain explorer showed successful transactions, the token balance was not updating as expected in the application. This happened due to misunderstandings around token decimals, and asynchronous transaction confirmations. I overcame this by carefully inspecting smart contract interactions, validating token transfer events, and improving the logic for transaction verification.

I also encountered bugs in the API statistics system, such as undefined variables and incorrect database updates. For example, using an undefined id variable in the stats update logic caused runtime errors. I fixed this by correctly mapping the API identifier from the middleware and adding safeguards like upsert in MongoDB to ensure stats were created and updated reliably.

Additionally, integrating external APIs introduced challenges like handling timeouts, non-200 responses, and inconsistent data formats. I addressed this by adding proper error handling, timeouts, and standardized response structures in the API gateway.

Overall, these challenges pushed me to think beyond basic coding and design a robust, scalable architecture that connects Web2 APIs with Web3 payments in a secure and efficient way.

### SafeSpend

> Safe-Spend: Financial Discipline, Decentralized.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Etherscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Etherscan-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Project Description: Safe-Spend Terminal is a decentralized vault designed to manage student allowances using Ethereum smart contracts. It features a web-based terminal for students to track their balances and a Python-based monitoring agent that sends real-time alerts to Discord.

Key Features
Time-Locked Vault: Funds are mathematically locked on the blockchain until the specific unlock time is reached.

Moderated Flow: The contract enforces a 0.01 ETH allowance limit to prevent the student from draining the vault instantly.

Live Countdown: A real-time pulsing timer displays the status of the vault, showing whether it is "Locked" or "Ready".

USD Price Tracking: Integrated with the CoinGecko API to show live Ethereum balances converted to USD.

Discord Alerts: A Python agent monitors the blockchain for withdrawal events and notifies a Discord webhook immediately.

Reputation System: Tracks student financial discipline through a reputation score stored directly in the contract.

Technical Architecture
1. Smart Contract (Solidity)

The core logic resides on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet.

Contract Address: 0x4a8e6a6aacf44dee097d6f6fddb11a72d4e00b6b.

Withdrawal Logic: Allows the student to claim the 0.01 ETH allowance once the timer hits zero.

Reputation Logic: Increments by 10 for every successful manual withdrawal.

2. Frontend Terminal (Web3.js)

Timer Loop: Updates every second to reflect the vault's lock status.

Transaction History: Pulls the last 5 withdrawal events directly from the blockchain.

3. Monitoring Agent (Python)

Event Listener: Specifically watches for the withdrawal event to extract the amount and remaining balance.

Discord Integration: Forwards event data to a designated Discord channel via webhook.

Setup Instructions
Frontend Setup:

Open the index.html file in any browser with MetaMask installed.

Ensure your MetaMask is set to the Sepolia Test Network.

Click "Connect Wallet" to view your balance and reputation.

Python Agent Setup:

Install dependencies using the command: pip install web3 requests.

Open the agent.py file and replace the Discord URL placeholder with your actual Discord Webhook URL.

Run the agent using the command: python agent.py.

Wisdom Library
The terminal includes a wisdom generator with financial insights such as:

Warren Buffett: "Do not save what is left after spending, but spend what is left after saving."

Benjamin Franklin: "An investment in knowledge pays the best interest."

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a decentralized vault like the Safe-Spend Vault involves several technical and logistical hurdles. Based on common decentralized finance (DeFi) development patterns and the specific logic of your project, here are the core challenges typically faced:

1. The "Open Door" Problem (Time-Lock Synchronization)
A major challenge is ensuring the vault stays "moderated" once the timer hits zero.

The Issue: In basic time-lock contracts, once the unlockTime is reached, the requirement require(block.timestamp >= unlockTime) remains true forever. This allows a student to withdraw 0.01 ETH multiple times in a row until the vault is empty, bypassing the "allowance" concept.

The Fix: You had to implement a cooldown reset inside the payout function, where every withdrawal automatically pushes the unlockTime forward by another week.

2. Transaction Reverts & Gas Management
Handling failed transactions (reverts) is a constant struggle in Solidity development.

Balance Sensitivity: If the user tries to withdraw but the vault has less than the ALLOWANCE (0.01 ETH), the transaction will revert. This costs the user gas (real money/test ETH) even though the transaction failed.

Automation Safety: The Chainlink Automation must be precisely programmed in checkUpkeep to only fire when the balance is sufficient, or the automation nodes will waste gas on failing transactions.

3. Cross-Platform Integration (The "DApp Bridge")
Synchronizing the Smart Contract, Frontend, and Python Agent requires perfect alignment of the Application Binary Interface (ABI).

The ABI Struggle: Every time you change a small detail in the Solidity code (like adding a reputationScore), the ABI changes. If you update the contract on GitHub but forget to update the JSON ABI in the Python script, the agent will "crash" or fail to recognize the new events.

Connectivity Glitches: Relying on public RPC URLs (like PublicNode or Alchemy) can lead to "Network Glitches" in your terminal or Python agent. Your agent.py had to include try/except blocks to handle these disconnects without crashing the monitoring system.

4. Security & Exploits
Protecting the vault from malicious activity is a high priority.

Reentrancy Risks: In DeFi, a common exploit is the "Reentrancy Attack," where an attacker triggers a withdrawal and uses a malicious "fallback" function to call the withdraw again before the contract can update its balance.

Access Control: Ensuring that only the Parent can trigger an emergency unlock and only the Student can claim the allowance requires strict require(msg.sender == ...) checks to prevent unauthorized access.

**The problem it solves**

Today, valuable datasets and trained AI models are difficult to monetize in a transparent and trustworthy way. Data creators often lack a secure platform to sell their assets, while buyers have no reliable method to verify ownership, pricing, or fair revenue sharing. Existing centralized marketplaces create trust issues, single points of failure, and limited control for creators. Our AI Marketplace solves this by providing a decentralized platform where datasets and models can be securely listed, purchased, and transferred using blockchain and IPFS. This ensures transparent ownership, tamper-proof records, fair payments, and verifiable access, making the trading of AI assets safer, more efficient, and truly trustless.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was configuring MetaMask correctly and ensuring all team members were connected to the Sepolia test network. We encountered network mismatches, incorrect RPC settings, and transaction failures when MetaMask could not detect the deployed contract. We resolved this by standardizing the Sepolia configuration and carefully verifying chain IDs and addresses. Another challenge was working with Pinata’s limited 1 GB storage, which required us to enforce file size limits and use small representative datasets. Integrating IPFS also required careful handling of API keys and asynchronous uploads. Through incremental testing and debugging, we achieved stable MetaMask connectivity and reliable decentralized storage.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Swapify is a decentralized application that enables trustless, peer-to-peer atomic swaps of NFTs on the Sepolia testnet. Built with security and simplicity in mind, it leverages Hash Time Locked Contracts (HTLC) to ensure that swaps are all-or-nothing, eliminating the need for trusted intermediaries.

Contract Address: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0xb392a011a5f0547f64ac18f0414adb202e434691

Demo Link: https://swapify-sepolia.vercel.app/

**Key Features:**

- Trustless & Atomic: Swaps are executed directly between users. The entire transaction either completes successfully for both parties or fails, returning the assets to their original owners.
- Secure: Utilizes cryptographic secret hashes and a 24-hour timelock to protect users' assets from getting stuck indefinitely.
- User-Friendly Dashboard: A clean interface to create new swaps, view incoming offers, and manage all your active and completed swaps in one place.
- Real-Time Status: Track the progress of your swaps with clear status indicators (e.g., "Pending Initiator", "Awaiting Response", "Completed").

**How It Works: The Swap Flow**

The atomic swap process is secured by a secret known only to the initiator (User A). The swap can only be completed when the responder (User B) provides this secret.

- Create Swap: User A initiates a swap by specifying their NFT, the desired NFT from User B, and User B's wallet address. A secret is generated, and its hash is stored in the smart contract.
- Share Secret: User A securely shares the secret with User B off-chain (e.g., via a secure messaging app).
- Initiator Locks NFT: User A approves the Swapify contract to access their NFT and then locks it into the contract. The swap is now active and waiting for User B.
- Responder Completes Swap: User B sees the pending swap, approves their NFT for the contract, and provides the secret from User A to lock their NFT and finalize the swap. The smart contract verifies the secret, and instantly transfers both NFTs to their new owners.
- Safety Timelock: If User B does not complete the swap within 24 hours, either user can cancel the swap, safely returning the locked NFT to its original owner.

**Challenges we ran into**

I started with the contract design, I build the complete contract during the hackathon phase. Following which I focused on the frontend development. The project is still in MVP phase and is deployed on the testnet. Further improvements await.

The **main challenge** was to solve for the problem that **"I want to exchange my asset with you, but I do not trust you enough"**

The project is deployed on Mantle Testnet Blockchain.

It solves for a core Blockchain problem, trustless swaps.

The protocol/contract is written in solidity and is deployed on Sepolia Testnet.

**The problem it solves**

EchoMind is a parent-first AI-assisted care platform designed to support families of autistic children by bridging the gap between therapy sessions and real-world daily care. Unlike traditional AAC tools that focus only on child interaction, EchoMind combines a secure child activity interface with an intelligent parent monitoring dashboard.

The platform leverages OnDemand AI agents for text, media, and behavioral analysis, including demo video analysis agents to assess engagement patterns and text-to-speech tools to support speech practice and assisted communication. Children interact through AI-managed routines, cognitive tests, emotional assessment, and speech exercises, while parents receive real-time progress tracking, AI-generated summaries, behavioral insights, and personalized care recommendations.

By creating a continuous AI-powered feedback loop between child engagement and parent supervision, EchoMind improves communication effectiveness, therapy consistency, and daily care efficiency

By integrating external AI agents, speech tools, and media analysis services, the platform enables rapid experimentation and continuous improvement without being limited to a closed ecosystem. EchoMind is designed to be modular and interoperable, allowing future integration with therapists, educational platforms, wearable devices, and public health systems. This open, API-driven architecture encourages community contributions, scalable partnerships, and cross-domain collaboration, accelerating innovation in accessible autism care solutions.

At the API layer, **OnDemand ChatAPI** and **OnDemand MediaAPI** enable **real-time conversational intelligence** and **multimedia processing**. ### ZeroKlue
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeroklue-3d1a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Prajwal-k-tech/Code-kal) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Code%20Kalari-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://code-kalari.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Prove once, use everywhere, reveal nothing

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZeroKlue enables students and professionals to prove their organizational affiliation (university, company) without revealing personal information.

**The Current Problem:**
Traditional verification services like SheerID and UNiDAYS collect sensitive personal data like full name, date of birth, student ID just to confirm you're a student. This creates:
- Privacy risks from data breaches
- GDPR/compliance liability for merchants / issuers of student benefits
- Centralized databases that become honeypots for hackers, in the web3 world associating your mail and name with your wallet makes you a target

**For Web3, the problem is critical:**
DAOs and DeFi protocols desperately need "Proof of Humanity" for fair governance (one person, one vote) and Sybil resistance. But they cannot ask for traditional KYC without breaking their core promise of anonymity. This is an existential problem - bots are draining treasuries, and there's no privacy-preserving solution.

**Our Solution:**
ZeroKlue uses Zero-Knowledge Proofs to verify your Google Workspace email domain without revealing the email itself. The merchant only sees "Verified Student: TRUE" - never your name, email, or institution. Nullifiers make sure you can't use the same email to verify again.
---

**Why Web3 Needs This:**

1. **DAO Governance:** Optimism, Arbitrum, and other L2s give away millions in grants (RPGF). One person with 1,000 wallets can rig votes. ZeroKlue provides Sybil resistance without KYC.

2. **Sybil-Resistant Airdrops:** Projects want to airdrop to future builders (students), not bot farms. ZeroKlue lets them target verified university audiences.

3. **DeFi Student Rates:** Lending protocols want to offer student rates but can't hold PII. We solve this.

4. **Token-Gated Communities:** University alumni groups, company channels, hackathon participants - all verifiable without doxxing.

---

**The Business Model (Per-Verification Revenue):**

We charge protocols/DAOs per verification:
- **Volume Pricing:** $0.01 - $0.10 per verification
- **Comparison:** SheerID charges $0.50 - $2.00 per verification

**Why protocols will pay:**
- 10x cheaper than alternatives
- Zero data liability (no GDPR concerns)
- Works natively with smart contracts (on-chain `isVerified()` check)
- No integration friction (users just "Sign in with Google")

**Revenue Projections:**
- 100K verifications = $10,000 revenue
- 1M verifications = $100,000 revenue (optimisti much lol but not too far fetched)
- Target: Every major DAO, DeFi protocol, and NFT project

---

**Key Benefits:**
- Students verify once, use everywhere (Soulbound NFT as portable credential)
- Merchants get verification without data liability
- DAOs get Sybil resistance without KYC
- All verification happens client-side (no backend, no database)

**Challenges we ran into**

## So yeah, we faced a bunch of challenges and had to pivot a few times + sacrifice a few features
### 1. The Identity Verification Paradox

**Initial Approach - OTP Verification:**
We first explored traditional OTP-based email verification. This would require a backend server to send/receive OTPs, Redis for temporary storage, and an email service like Resend.
**Problem:** This defeats the "trustless" promise. Users would have to trust our server with their email.

**The Breakthrough , JWT Verification:**
We discovered that Google's OAuth tokens (JWTs) are already digitally signed. Instead of verifying emails ourselves, we verify Google's cryptographic signature inside a ZK circuit. This eliminates the need for any backend. and its a quite elegant solution imo, you should read the blogpost 
https://saleel.xyz/blog/stealthnote/

**Credit:** Our ZK circuit is adapted from [StealthNote](https://github.com/saleel/stealthnote), an MIT-licensed project that pioneered JWT verification in Noir.

---

### 2. The Setu API Dead End

**The Dream:** India has API Setu / DigiLocker - official government APIs that could verify student enrollment with 100% accuracy.

**The Reality:** Accessing API Setu requires government partnership agreements and compliance certifications that are impossible for a hackathon team to obtain in 36 hours.

Our Pivot: 
We focused on Google Workspace verification (which covers most universities globally) as the permissionless path. API Setu/DigiLocker integration remains on our roadmap for when we secure the partnerships.
Obviously, now we dont have guarantees these guys are students but probablility is high and since the biggest value it has to web3 is verifiable identity, this is a good start and a sacrifice merchants would be willing to make + already being made in the web2 world. (matters even less here)
Creative solutions can be thought of to mitigate the affect of this, like maybe a reputation system, 
for certain orgs.

---

### 3. The 640 Byte Bug

**The Error:**
```
Error: remainingData after partial hash exceeds maxSignedDataLength
```
**Root Cause:** The StealthNote circuit was hardcoded for JWTs up to 640 bytes. Our university's Google Workspace tokens exceeded this limit (requiring 1024 bytes) due to longer organizational metadata.

**The Fix:**
1. We traced the issue to `maxSignedDataLength` in the Noir circuit configuration
2. Increased the limit from 640 to 1024 bytes
3. Recompiled the circuit and regenerated the Solidity verifier

**Contribution:** I opened [Issue #6](https://github.com/saleel/stealthnote/issues/6) on the StealthNote repository to help out.

---

### 4. Gas Optimization for ZK Verification
**Challenge:** The HonkVerifier contract is 30KB - too large for Ethereum mainnet deployment limits.
**Solution:** We implemented a hybrid verification model:
- Client-side proof verification (in browser using Barretenberg WASM)
- Only a lightweight attestation stored on-chain (~50k gas)
This reduced per-user gas costs from $5-20 to approximately $0.05. honestly, thinking about it now it was stupid to try to verify on chain in the first place, but we were naive and wanted to make it as trustless as possible.

**Ethereum Track**

ZeroKlue is a privacy-preserving identity layer built natively for Ethereum and EVM-compatible chains.

**Why Ethereum:**
- Soulbound NFTs (SBTs) serve as portable, verifiable credentials that cannot be transferred or sold
- On-chain attestations that any dApp can query with a simple `isVerified(address)` call
- L2 deployment ready (Optimism, Base, Arbitrum) for low gas costs

**Technical Integration:**
- Solidity 0.8.21 smart contracts developed with Foundry
- ZK proof verification using UltraHonk prover (Noir/Barretenberg)
- Scaffold-ETH 2 frontend with RainbowKit + wagmi for seamless wallet connection
- Client-side proof generation using WASM (no backend required)

**Use Cases Enabled on Ethereum:**
- DAO governance with Sybil-resistant student voting (one person, one vote)
- DeFi protocols offering verified student/alumni rates
- NFT projects with university-gated access (alumni collections)
- Hackathon applications with verified student status
- Grant programs (like Optimism RPGF) with bot-proof human verification

**Smart Contract Architecture:**
- ZeroKlue.sol: Main registry contract for student attestations
- HonkVerifier.sol: Generated verifier for Noir ZK proofs
- Soulbound implementation prevents credential trading

So yeah, hopefully this is good enough to put us on this track

**The problem it solves**

Most people do meaningful things for their community—tutoring, checking on neighbors, planting trees, donating time—but none of that is visibly tracked or celebrated. Existing tools focus on:

**Formal volunteering only (through NGOs or platforms)**

**Leaderboards and badges that feel like generic “gamification”**

**Organization metrics instead of personal stories and growth**

As a result:

Individuals can’t see how their small actions add up over time.
It’s hard to communicate impact to others (“I help out sometimes” vs a clear record).
People lose motivation because there’s no feedback loop or evolving identity.
Kindred solves this by:
Giving each person a Hero Journal to quickly log real-world actions (what they did, when, and in which area: Environment, Education, Social Work, Healthcare, Animal Welfare, Disaster Relief).
Turning those entries into trackable points per impact area stored safely in a database.
Converting the top 3 impact areas into a human, narrative title (like “Community Wisdom Weaver”) that only changes when the user asks for it.
Providing a community view where users can discover others with similar locations and interests.
In practice, people can use Kindred to:
Build a personal impact portfolio they can show to friends, schools, or organizations.
Reflect on how their energy is distributed across different causes and adjust intentionally.
Stay motivated by watching their contributions evolve into a story, not just a score.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Connecting MongoDB Atlas from a hosted backend**
Problem: After deploying to Render, the server ran but MongoDB kept failing with “could not connect to any servers in your MongoDB Atlas cluster”.
Why it was tricky: Locally everything worked, so the error only appeared in the cloud. The issue turned out to be Atlas IP whitelisting and a slightly incomplete connection string.
How I fixed it:
Allowed 0.0.0.0/0 in Atlas during development so Render’s dynamic IP could connect.
Updated MONGODB_URI to include the database name (e.g. /kindred) and query options.
Added clearer logging in server.js so future connection issues are easier to diagnose.

**Deploying a monorepo-style project (frontend + backend in subfolders)**

Problem: Hosting platforms initially failed builds because they tried to cd into the 
wrong folder (kindred vs Kindred/kindred) or couldn’t find the dist directory.
Why it was tricky: The repo root isn’t the app root, and platform UIs show extra path prefixes that are visually confusing.
How I fixed it:
Carefully mapped my GitHub structure and used Root Directory or cd in build commands to point to the correct subfolder.
On Render, removed the Root Directory for the static site and used
cd Kindred/kindred && npm install && npm run build with Kindred/kindred/dist as the publish directory.
Documented the final setup in QUICK_DEPLOY.md and DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md so I don’t have to relearn it next time.

**Keeping titles in sync with points without confusing the user**
Problem: At first, titles auto‑updated every time points changed, which felt random and made it hard for users to understand why their identity changed.
How I fixed it:
Decoupled title updates from point updates: points are always live from MongoDB, but the title only recalculates when the user clicks “Generate new title”.
This required reorganizing state in MyHeroSpace so it reads tracks from the backend but only calls getCurrentTitle inside the button handler.

**The problem it solves**

Modern software often contains inefficient code patterns that increase CPU usage, execution time, and energy consumption—leading to higher carbon emissions. Existing code optimization tools focus primarily on performance or rely heavily on cloud-based AI, which itself introduces additional environmental costs. There is a need for a carbon-aware code optimization system that minimizes energy usage by prioritizing local analysis and reducing unnecessary cloud computation while still delivering effective and measurable code improvements.

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced the challenge of balancing accurate code optimization with carbon efficiency. Pure cloud-based AI optimization increases energy consumption, while fully local models require high compute resources and longer development time. Designing a system that prioritizes low-energy local analysis, minimizes cloud dependency, and still delivers meaningful optimization results—within hackathon time and hardware constraints—was a key technical challenge.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project addresses the above problems by implementing a modern, responsive, and interactive checkout & payment interface designed to improve user experience and trust.

Key solutions include:

Clean and centered checkout layout that keeps all payment actions focused in one place

Multiple payment method options (UPI, Card, Net Banking, COD, Loyalty Points) with clear visual selection

Real-time form validation to prevent incomplete or incorrect submissions

Processing and success feedback to assure users that their action is being handled

Order placed popup confirmation, providing instant acknowledgment and confidence

Fully responsive design, ensuring usability on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices

**Challenges we ran into**

⚠️ Challenges Faced During the Project

During the development of this checkout and payment interface, several challenges were encountered that required careful debugging and design decisions.

1️⃣ Layout & Alignment Issues

One of the major challenges was maintaining a properly centered and visually balanced layout across different screen sizes. Initially, elements such as the checkout heading, payment methods, and action buttons appeared misaligned or stretched due to incorrect container structure and CSS grid behavior.

Solution:
The issue was resolved by restructuring the HTML layout and using flexbox to centrally align the entire checkout card both vertically and horizontally.

2️⃣ Button Behavior & Page Flow

The “Place Order” button initially behaved like a form submission button, causing the page to reload and interrupt the intended flow. This prevented smooth transitions such as success messages and popups from appearing.

Solution:
JavaScript event handling was implemented to control the button behavior, ensuring that validations and UI feedback occurred before any page navigation.

3️⃣ Real-Time Validation Handling

Ensuring that all user inputs (name, email, and address) were correctly validated without frustrating the user was another challenge. Missing or incorrect inputs could break the flow or cause confusion.

Solution:
Client-side validation logic was added to provide immediate feedback and prevent incomplete form submissions.

4️⃣ User Feedback During Processing

Initially, users received no clear indication that their order was being processed, which could lead to repeated clicks or uncertainty.

Solution:
Processing indicators and success messages were introduced, followed by a confirmation popup to clearly communicate the transaction status.

5️⃣ Managing UI States (Processing → Success → Popup)

Handling multiple UI states in sequence (processing, success, popup confirmation) using JavaScript timers required careful timing to avoid overlap or abrupt transitions.

Solution:
Timed state management using setTimeout() was implemented to ensure smooth and user-friendly transitions.

6️⃣ Responsive Design Challenges

Adapting the checkout interface for smaller screens without breaking the layout or usability was challenging.

Solution:
Media queries and flexible layouts were used to ensure responsiveness across devices.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem Village Gentle Solves
🌾 Bridging the Agricultural Knowledge Gap
Village Gentle addresses the critical disconnect between modern agricultural technology and rural farming communities. Traditional farming relies on generational knowledge and local expertise, but climate change, evolving pest patterns, and market volatility demand data-driven, real-time solutions.

🎯 Core Problems Solved
1. Language Barriers in Agricultural Technology
Problem: Most agricultural apps are English-only, excluding 70% of global farmers
Solution: 20+ language support including all major Indian languages (Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, etc.)
Impact: Farmers can access AI advice in their native language with voice input/output
2. Complex Soil Analysis & Crop Selection
Problem: Soil testing is expensive, time-consuming, and requires lab visits
Solution: AI-powered soil image analysis using computer vision to detect NPK levels, pH, and soil type
Impact: Instant crop recommendations from a simple smartphone photo
3. Pest & Disease Identification Delays
Problem: Crop diseases spread rapidly; farmers lose 20-40% yield waiting for expert diagnosis
Solution: Real-time plant disease detection with treatment recommendations and professional service connections
Impact: Early intervention saves crops and reduces pesticide overuse
4. Weather-Related Crop Losses
Problem: Unpredictable weather causes $5 billion annual losses in agriculture
Solution: Hyper-local weather advisory with AI-generated farming insights and interactive maps
Impact: Proactive farming decisions reduce weather-related losses by 30%
5. Limited Access to Healthcare in Rural Areas
Problem: Rural communities travel 50+ km for basic healthcare, delaying treatment
Solution: AI health assistant with nearby facility finder and nutrition guidance
Impact: Immediate health advice and efficient healthcare facility location
6. Market Information Asymmetry
Problem: Farmers sell at 40-60% below market rates due to information gaps
Solution: Real-time market prices via official Agrimarket 2.0 integration and business opportunities
Impact: Better pricing decisions and access to government schemes
7. Fragmented Government Support
Problem: Farmers unaware of 200+ government schemes worth $50 billion annually
Solution: Centralized government scheme database with eligibility checking and application links
Impact: Increased scheme utilization and farmer income

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
Building Village Gentle was an ambitious journey in merging modern web aesthetics with robust agricultural AI. Here are the key hurdles we overcame:

1. Breaking the "Streamlit Look"
The Hurdle: Streamlit is great for data apps but often looks "boxy" and lacks the premium feel of a modern Next.js application. The Solution: We implemented a custom 
modern_ui.py
 layer using advanced CSS and JavaScript. We bypassed the default sidebar for a sticky, glassmorphic top navigation bar using st.tabs and injected custom DOM manipulation scripts to hide standard Streamlit headers and toolbars, creating a seamless, full-screen experience.

2. AI Model Volatility
The Hurdle: We encountered a critical "404 Model Not Found" error when using high-end vision models (like llama-3.2-90b-vision) for soil analysis, as these models are often in preview or restricted. The Solution: We implemented a fail-safe model strategy. By switching to more stable, production-ready models like llama-3.2-11b-vision-preview and llama-3.3-70b-versatile, we ensured the app remains functional even when specific experimental models are unavailable.

3. Seamless Multilingual State
The Hurdle: Managing translations across 8+ feature pages while keeping the user's context (like chat history or soil analysis results) was complex. The Solution: We built a centralized 
language_manager.py
 that uses session state to track the user's language choice globally. We wrapped our page functions in a @multilingual_page decorator to ensure that every UI element—from buttons to AI responses—translates instantly without losing the user's progress.

4. Blockchain Subscription UX
The Hurdle: Initial client-side MetaMask integration was clunky and often disconnected between page refreshes. The Solution: We moved to a server-side transaction signing approach. By handling the blockchain logic on the backend and using a dedicated subscription manager, we provided a "Web2-like" smooth experience for users while keeping the security and transparency of the Celo blockchain.

**Ethereum Track**

Village Gentle bridges the gap between Web3 and real-world agricultural utility. Our project fits the Ethereum Track by implementing a decentralized subscription layer on the Celo blockchain (EVM-compatible).

We use smart contracts to gate premium AI features—like advanced soil analysis and expert crop recommendations—ensuring transparent, secure, and borderless access for rural farmers. By leveraging Ethereum-based infrastructure, we demonstrate how blockchain can power essential services in emerging markets, providing a scalable model for decentralized service delivery in the agricultural sector.

> Learn regional languages ​​in a trusted way

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Indonesia has hundreds of regional languages that are still used in daily life, but there is **no structured and credible way** for outsiders to learn them.

For people who move between regions like students and workers, language gaps often create:
- Miscommunication in everyday interactions  
- Social friction and exclusion  
- A persistent feeling of being an “outsider” in a new community  

Today, learning usually depends on luck: local friends, long immersion, or unstructured online content. Even when someone makes a real effort, the outcome is **hard to measure** and **impossible to prove** to others.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Choosing the right ERC standards:**  
  Determining how to use Soulbound tokens for non-transferable learning credentials and ERC-1155 for redeemable utilities required careful consideration of responsibilities and scope.

- **Limited provider support on Lisk Sepolia:**  
  Some commonly used third-party providers were not yet fully usable or stable on Lisk Sepolia, which limited certain integrations during development.

- **Heavy reliance on direct RPC calls:**  
  Early implementations used direct RPC calls even for simple on-chain data, which increased complexity on the frontend.

- **Implementing newly learned technologies:**  
  The project involved applying concepts that were recently learned, including Soulbound Tokens, ERC-1155, and email-based login while abstracting blockchain complexity from users.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Transcend** solves critical inefficiencies in **crypto-based payroll and treasury management** for global teams and Web3-native organizations.

Today, paying employees in crypto and managing operational funds is still **expensive, manual, and operationally risky**, especially at scale.

---

## 🚩 Problems

### 1. Expensive & Inefficient Payroll Payments

Sending salaries on-chain requires **one transaction per employee**, resulting in:

* High cumulative gas fees
* Slow execution for large teams
* Poor scalability for growing organizations

---

### 2. Idle Treasury Capital

Payroll funds typically sit idle in wallets while waiting for payout cycles:

* No yield generation
* Capital loses value over time
* Missed opportunity to optimize treasury efficiency

---

### 3. Manual & Error-Prone Treasury Operations

Managing payroll alongside DeFi lending manually increases:

* Human error risk
* Misallocation of funds
* Operational complexity

---

## 💡 How Transcend Makes It Easier & Safer

### ✅ 1. One-Transaction Bulk Payroll

* Pays an entire payroll batch in **a single blockchain transaction**
* Reduces gas costs by up to **90%**
* Enables fast, one-click global payroll execution

---

### ✅ 2. Yield-First Treasury Management

* Automatically deploys idle payroll funds into **Aave**
* Generates yield while funds wait for payout
* Uses earned yield to **offset or subsidize payroll expenses**
* Turns payroll from a pure cost into a capital-efficient process

---

### ✅ 3. Automated & Trust-Minimized Operations

* Smart contracts eliminate manual handling
* Reduces human error and operational risk
* No banks or intermediaries required
* Full user custody of funds

---

### ✅ 4. Transparent & Auditable Payments

* Every transaction is recorded on-chain
* Immutable payroll and treasury history
* Easy auditing for finance and compliance teams

---

## Summary

**Transcend** enables organizations to:

* Pay crypto salaries efficiently at scale
* Optimize treasury capital automatically
* Reduce operational risk through automation
* Maintain full transparency and control

> **Transcend transforms crypto payroll from a costly manual process into an automated, yield-optimized financial system.**

**The problem it solves**

## The Humanitarian Crisis

Disaster relief in Southeast Asia faces a **72-hour latency gap** - funds take 3+ days to reach victims while intermediaries extract hidden fees. Traditional NGOs operate as "black boxes" where donors have no visibility into fund allocation.

**DRCP solves this by:**

🔹 **Instant Parametric Relief** - Funds are automatically allocated when disaster data (BMKG seismic, PetaBencana floods) triggers DAO governance votes

🔹 **Radical Transparency** - Every Rupiah is tracked on-chain via The Graph. Donors can audit the entire fund flow in real-time

🔹 **Trustless Execution** - Smart contracts eliminate intermediary corruption. No admin can secretly divert funds

🔹 **Volunteer Reputation System** - Impact NFTs (Soulbound) create verifiable "Resilience Resumes" for local heroes

**Use Cases:**
- Donors: Transparent giving with full audit trail
- NGOs: Governance tools to coordinate multi-org responses
- Volunteers: Build portable, verified reputation
- Governments: Real-time disaster fund monitoring

**Challenges we ran into**

## Technical Challenges

### 1. RPC Rate Limiting
**Problem:** Free-tier Alchemy endpoints throttled getLogs requests, causing 400 errors on transparency dashboard.
**Solution:** Implemented paginated chunk fetching (2000 blocks per request) with error handling fallback.

### 2. Subgraph Indexing Lag
**Problem:** The Graph took 30-60 seconds to index new transactions, causing stale UI data.
**Solution:** Built optimistic UI pattern - show pending transactions immediately while background sync catches up.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**
Traditional Rotating Savings and Credit Associations (ROSCAs), locally known as "Arisan" in Indonesia, rely entirely on trust. Participants must trust a central organizer ("Bandar") to hold funds and conduct fair drawings. Unfortunately, this manual system is often plagued by fraud (organizers running away with funds), lack of transparency, and administration errors.

ArisanDAO solves these critical issues by migrating the social trust layer onto the blockchain:

Eliminates Counterparty Risk (Safety)
People can start or join savings circles without needing to trust a human organizer.
Smart Contracts act as the verifiable custodian. Funds are locked in the contract and can only be released to the legitimate winner selected by the code. No one can "run away" with the pot.
Guarantees Fairness & Transparency
The winner selection process is executed on-chain. It is mathematically random and verifiable by any participant, ensuring that drawings are never rigged.
Every deposit and payout is recorded permanently on the Lisk blockchain, creating an immutable history.
Simplifies Management
It automates the tedious parts of Arisan: tracking payments, verifying balances, and distributing funds.
Users get a real-time dashboard (powered by Supabase) to instantly see their status, eliminating manual bookkeeping.
Stable & Global Access
By transacting in USDT (Stablecoin), participants avoid the volatility typically associated with crypto, making it a viable tool for actual savings while leveraging the speed and security of the Lisk network.
In short, ArisanDAO makes social savings safer (trustless custody), fairer (verifiable randomness), and easier (automated management).
