**The problem it solves**

Traditional skill certificates are easy to fake and slow to verify. Employers can't trust paper credentials, and verification takes days. SkillChain solves this by using AI to evaluate your knowledge and minting the results as NFTs on Ethereum. Your skills become verifiable in seconds-anyone can check the blockchain to confirm your credentials are real. No fake certificates, no delays, no middlemen.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was making the AI evaluation accurate for open-ended blockchain questions. I solved this by creating detailed rubrics with specific criteria and keyphrases. Another hurdle was deploying to Vercel-Hardhat dependencies kept breaking the build. Fixed it by separating dev dependencies and only deploying frontend code. Finally, I had to balance a premium UI with actual functionality, which I achieved through a minimalist dark theme and subtle animations.

**Ethereum Track**

SkillChain is built entirely on Ethereum infrastructure. Skill credentials are minted as ERC-721 NFTs on Polygon (Ethereum L2), giving users true ownership of their verified achievements. The app uses MetaMask and WalletConnect for authentication, and all credential verification happens on-chain through smart contract queries. Every minted credential is permanently stored on the blockchain, making it tamper-proof and instantly verifiable by anyone without trusting a centralized authority.

### WhistleChain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/whistlechain-47bc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Adityamtl/WhistleChain) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://whistle-chain.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SdIWXswGY98) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20Space%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-space-1.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Expose the crime. Not your name.

![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Imagine you are an employee and you discover fraud inside your company.  
You want to report it, but if your identity is exposed, you could lose your job or face retaliation.

Most existing whistleblowing systems are centralized. This means:
- Evidence can be deleted or altered later
- Submission times can be disputed
- Users must trust the platform owner to protect them

Because of this, many people choose to stay silent, even when they have important information.

---

## The solution

WhistleChain allows people to submit evidence anonymously and make sure it **cannot be erased or changed**.

When a user submits evidence:
- A cryptographic proof is recorded on the blockchain
- The document is stored in decentralized storage
- Anyone can later verify when it was submitted

The platform does not collect names, emails, or accounts.  
It only preserves proof that the evidence existed at a specific time.

---

## How it helps in real situations

- An employee can submit internal documents without revealing their identity  
- A journalist can receive tips with verifiable timestamps  
- An activist can preserve sensitive evidence even if it is later censored  

WhistleChain also includes an optional **Dead Man’s Switch**.  
If the submitter stops checking in, the evidence is automatically released, ensuring it is not silenced.

---

## What WhistleChain focuses on

WhistleChain does not judge whether a claim is true or false.  
It only guarantees that evidence **exists, is timestamped, and has not been modified**.

This makes whistleblowing safer by removing the need to trust a single authority.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I ran into

### 1. Balancing anonymity with blockchain transparency
A major challenge was that blockchains are transparent by default.  
If users submit transactions directly, their wallet address becomes permanently visible, which defeats the purpose of anonymous whistleblowing.

This was especially risky because even a single on-chain link could expose a whistleblower later through transaction history analysis.

**How I solved it:**  
I implemented a **gasless relayer system**. Instead of users sending transactions themselves, the platform submits transactions on their behalf. This removes the need for wallets and prevents any direct on-chain link between the whistleblower and the submission.

This approach preserves blockchain guarantees (immutability and timestamps) while protecting user anonymity.

---

### 2. Preventing spam without collecting identity
Another challenge was stopping spam and abuse without asking users to create accounts, emails, or logins.  
Traditional authentication methods would compromise anonymity.

**How I solved it:**  
I integrated **World ID** to verify that each submission comes from a real human, without revealing who that person is. World ID provides a cryptographic proof of personhood, not identity.

This allowed me to limit spam and automated submissions while keeping the system completely account-less and privacy-preserving.

---

### 3. Avoiding overuse of blockchain and AI
Another challenge was deciding *where not to use* blockchain or AI. Overusing them would add complexity without real benefit.

**How I solved it:**  
Blockchain is used only for immutability and timestamping.  
AI is used only for redaction and summaries, not to judge truth.  

---
These challenges forced careful design decisions to ensure WhistleChain remained both secure and respectful of user privacy.

**Blockchain**

## How WhistleChain Fits the Blockchain Track

WhistleChain uses blockchain to solve a real trust problem: **how to store sensitive evidence in a way that cannot be deleted, altered, or backdated**.

### Why Blockchain is Necessary
In traditional systems, whistleblower evidence is stored in centralized databases that can be:
- Deleted or modified
- Censored under pressure
- Manipulated by administrators

WhistleChain avoids this by anchoring every submission on-chain.

### How Blockchain is Used
- Each submission generates a **cryptographic proof hash**
- The hash and timestamp are recorded on the **Polygon (EVM) blockchain**
- Evidence files are stored on **IPFS**, with their content address linked on-chain
- Anyone can independently verify **when** a submission was made and that it has not changed

### Smart Contract Logic
- A **Dead Man’s Switch** smart contract automatically releases evidence if the submitter stops checking in
- This logic runs autonomously on-chain, without relying on any central server or human approval

### Outcome
Blockchain makes WhistleChain:
- **Tamper-proof** - evidence cannot be edited or erased
- **Censorship-resistant** - no single authority controls submissions
- **Publicly verifiable** - anyone can verify integrity and timestamps

Without blockchain, these guarantees would not be possible.

**Ethereum Track**

## How WhistleChain Fits the Ethereum Track

WhistleChain is built on the **Ethereum ecosystem** using smart contracts to create a trustless and censorship-resistant whistleblowing platform.

The core logic of the system runs on **Solidity smart contracts deployed on Polygon Amoy**, an Ethereum Layer-2 network. Polygon allows WhistleChain to remain fully **EVM-compatible** while keeping transactions fast and gas-efficient. The same contracts can be deployed to Ethereum mainnet without modification.

Ethereum smart contracts are used to:
- Permanently record evidence hashes and submission timestamps
- Enforce immutability and public verifiability
- Power the **Dead Man’s Switch**, which autonomously releases evidence if the user fails to check in

All blockchain interactions are handled using standard **Ethereum tooling** such as Hardhat and ethers.js, following established Ethereum development practices.

WhistleChain reflects core Ethereum values:
- **Decentralization** - no central authority controls evidence
- **Censorship resistance** - submissions cannot be altered or removed
- **Trustlessness** - verification does not rely on a trusted intermediary
- **Permissionless access** - anyone can submit or verify evidence

This makes WhistleChain a practical, real-world Ethereum application focused on transparency, safety, and accountability.

> From factory to patient — every pill verified.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problems that MediChain Solves:**

- Counterfeit medicines are a major threat to patient safety, particularly due to long and opaque supply chains.
- Chemists, hospitals, and patients frequently lack a dependable method to verify a medicine's authenticity.
- The current systems such as paper records, static QR codes, and centralized databases are all very easy to manipulate.
- Counterfeit, expired, or wrongly stored medicines can be given to patients without being noticed.

**How This Project Helps**

- Manufacturers put each batch of medicine on a blockchain that cannot be tampered with, which in turn creates a permanent record of origin.
- Every transfer across the supply chain is logged making it very easy to spot skipped or invalid steps.
- Dynamic QR codes are used to prevent the reuse and copying of the genuine ones.
- Public verification is such that everyone can check authenticity without logging in.
- Hospitals do bulk verification of their inventory which results in less manual audits and safety risks.
- Patients get their trust built through instant and transparent verification.
- Regulators and suppliers gain from better accountability, compliance, and reduced operational risk.

The implementation of this system has transformed the verification of medicines into a process that is secure, automated, and trustworthy.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Wallet State Leakage Across Users**
  When multiple users logged in on the same browser, the app reused the previously connected wallet address without reopening MetaMask. This caused incorrect wallet identities to appear across accounts, which is unacceptable for a blockchain system.

- Fix Applied
  I separated user authentication from wallet connection entirely. Wallet access now happens only on explicit user action, sessions are cleared on logout, and MetaMask listeners detect account or network changes in real time.

- **Dynamic QR Code Mismatch** 
  Regenerating QR codes after each scan initially caused verification failures because off-chain scans and on-chain batch data went out of sync.

- Fix Applied
  I introduced a scan nonce and backend validation layer that invalidates old QR codes while keeping the original batch identity consistent on-chain.

These challenges forced tighter state management, stronger security boundaries, and more reliable verification logic.

**Ethereum Track**

**How Our Project Takes Advantage of Ethereum:**

The core of our project is the Ethereum blockchain, and we are making use of the Sepolia test network to set up a system for medicine supply chain verification that is totally secure against tampering. Rather than being a source of data, Ethereum is a layer of trust and verification, which secures the authenticity, ownership, and openness of the whole process.

Fundamental Ethereum Usage

- Solidity Smart Contracts
We composed and put into action smart contracts to mark medicine batches, control ownership changes, and assure the right supply-chain movement:

- **Manufacturer → Dealer → Pharmacy → Hospital/Customer** 
Any invalid or bypassed transfers are instantly turned down on-chain.

- Unchangeable Batch Identity
There is a specific on-chain identifier for each medicine batch which is not changeable or repeatable, thus stopping the entry of fake products.

- Wallet-Based Identity (MetaMask)
The wallet addresses on Ethereum serve as the cryptograph identities for the manufacturers, distributors, pharmacies, and hospitals—thus, eliminating the risk of a centralized credential.

- On-Chain + Off-Chain Hybrid Model
The most critical and least authentication data and transfer history are kept on Ethereum, while big compliance data (temperature, location) is kept off-chain but cryptographically linked on-chain.

- Public, Trustless Verification
The verification of medicine authenticity by any user is based on the data from Ethereum without the need for logging in. This procedure guarantees transparency and builds patient trust.

**Why Ethereum Matters :**

Ethereum provides the necessary elements of decentralized trust, tamper resistance, and public verifiability, thus it's the perfect platform for healthcare authenticity system with the potential of making an impact in the real world.

**Best Innovation**

• Addresses a real national problem: Tackles the counterfeit medicines, which spread like wildfire, and the very origin of their existence, thus, directly compromising the safety of patients and the trust in healthcare in the whole India.

• Purpose-driven blockchain usage: Employs Ethereum blockchain to forge an unchangeable identity for all medicine batches, thus, guaranteeing the authenticity is non-curable.

• End-to-end traceability: Verifies the entire path of medicines—Manufacturer → Distributor → Pharmacy → Hospital/Customer—by means of blockchain transactions that are validated at every step.

• Dynamic QR Codes (Anti-Reuse): QR codes re-create themselves after each scan, thus, making the previous codes invalid at once, and prohibiting the imitation or re-sale of the drugs made from fake medicines.

• Missing Link Detection Engine: Instantly reports batches with doubtful quality if any step in the supply chain is bypassed or tampered with.

• Hospital Bulk Verification Mode: Hospitals can verify thousands of medicines in a single go by just uploading a CSV file, thus, making the process faster and dominant over the existing process.

• Public verification without login: By scanning a QR code patients can check the authenticity of medicine - there is no need for an app or an account.

• Trust Score System (0–100): Transforms the intricate blockchain and compliance data into an easy, color-coded authenticity score.

• Off-chain compliance via Keplo: With the help of cryptographic proof linked on-chain, temperature, location, and storage data are securely off-chain.

• Wallet-based identity: Decentralized wallet authentication gets rid of password hazards.

• Scalable & production-ready: The system is ready for deployment in the real world, and it is also easy to extend to the entire national healthcare as it was designed that way.

**AWS**

**How We Used Kiro in Our Project**

Our project was planned and executed using Kiro as the primary ideation and planning environment, not just as a coding aid. Before writing production code, we used Kiro to break down the problem of counterfeit medicines, define system boundaries, and structure our blockchain-based solution step by step.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## **The Problem: The "I'll Do It Tomorrow" Trap**

We live in an era of abundant learning resources but scarce attention. Students and self-learners struggle with a massive **Motivation Gap**:

* **Procrastination:** 95% of students admit to procrastinating.
* **Lack of Accountability:** Self-paced courses (like Coursera/Udemy) have completion rates as low as 6% because there are no immediate consequences for quitting.
* **Passive Learning:** Reading a PDF doesn't mean you *understood* it. It's easy to skim without retaining information.

### **The Solution: Skill-Stake**

Skill-Stake turns **Willpower into Smart Contracts**. It is a decentralized commitment platform that forces you to put "skin in the game."

**How it works:**

1. **Stake ETH:** You lock crypto into a Kiro-powered smart contract.
2. **Study:** You read your material.
3. **Prove It:** Our AI (Gemini 3 Flash) acts as a professor, generating a strict quiz to verify your knowledge.
4. **Settle:** Pass the quiz? Get your refund. Fail? Your money goes to charity.

### **Use Cases**

* **Exam Prep:** Students can stake ETH on specific chapters to force themselves to study before finals.
* **Technical Certifications:** Developers preparing for AWS/Azure certs can upload documentation and test their retention.
* **Anti-Procrastination Tool:** Anyone can use it to conquer "doom-scrolling" by making the cost of not studying higher than the comfort of laziness.

### **Why It's Better**

* **Financial Accountability:** Unlike Todoist or Notion, Skill-Stake has real financial consequences. Loss aversion is a powerful psychological motivator.
* **Trustless Verification:** You don't need a human tutor to grade you. **Gemini 3 Flash** provides instant, unbiased grading, while **Kiro** ensures your funds are handled securely without human intervention.

**Challenges we ran into**

### **1. The "Oracle Problem": How do you tell the Blockchain who passed?**

The biggest technical hurdle was figuring out how to connect my Python backend to the Ethereum network. Smart contracts are isolated; they can't just "check" if a user passed a quiz on my server.

* **The Struggle:** I initially struggled with the security architecture. If I exposed an API endpoint like `/release-funds` anyone could curl it and steal the pot.
* **The Fix:** I treated my FastAPI backend as a trusted "Oracle." I implemented a strict verification flow:
1. The user takes the quiz.
2. The backend grades it.
3. **Only if the score is  70%**, the backend uses a stored private key (which the frontend never sees) to call the smart contract’s `release()` function. This turned my backend into the bridge between Web2 logic and Web3 settlement.



### **2. Taming the AI "Professor" (Gemini Hallucinations)**

Gemini 3 Flash is incredibly fast, but initially, it was *too* creative.

* **The Struggle:** I needed the quiz data in a strict JSON format to render it on the frontend. Sometimes Gemini would return the JSON wrapped in markdown ticks, or sometimes it would add a "Here is your quiz!" intro text, which crashed my JSON parser.
* **The Fix:** I learned the power of **Pydantic**. I created a rigid data model in FastAPI. If Gemini’s output didn't perfectly match the schema, my code would automatically catch the validation error and trigger a retry. It was like teaching a messy professor to fill out a scantron sheet correctly.

### **3. The "Solidity Fear" Factor**

Honestly, the scariest part was handling real crypto. In a hackathon, you're tired and rushing. Writing a custom Escrow contract from scratch felt like walking through a minefield—one bug and the ETH gets locked forever.

* **The Fix:** This is where **Kiro** saved me. Instead of writing raw Solidity and worrying about re-entrancy attacks, I used Kiro Track to generate the contract logic. It allowed me to focus on the *application* logic (the studying part) while treating the blockchain as a reliable, pre-secured vault. It took the "fear" out of the equation.

**Ethereum Track**

### **Why Skill-Stake Fits the Ethereum Track**

**1. Smart Contracts as the Core Logic**
Skill-Stake leverages Ethereum's ability to create "programmable money." We use Solidity smart contracts (generated via Kiro) to create a trustless escrow system. The application relies entirely on the blockchain to hold the user's staked ETH (Sepolia) and programmatically enforce the "study or lose" commitment. This demonstrates a practical, non-financial use case for smart contracts—**behavioral enforcement**.

**2. Solving the Oracle Problem**
A key challenge in Ethereum development is getting off-chain data (did the user pass the quiz?) onto the chain securely. Our project demonstrates a working **"Oracle" architecture**:

* 
**Off-Chain:** The Gemini AI analyzes the PDF and grades the user.


* 
**The Bridge:** Our FastAPI backend acts as the trusted oracle, verifying the score.


* 
**On-Chain:** The smart contract only executes the `release_funds` function when cryptographically triggered by the authorized oracle account.



**3. Real-World Utility for ETH**
We are moving beyond simple token transfers. Skill-Stake gives ETH a tangible utility in the EdTech space: using it as a **financial commitment device**. By locking ETH in a contract, we transform it from a speculative asset into a tool for personal productivity and learning validation.

**4. Decentralized Settlement**
Unlike traditional staking apps where a central server creates a database entry saying "User staked $50," our app creates an actual **on-chain transaction**. The settlement—whether refunding the user or slashing the stake to charity—is handled transparently on the Ethereum network, ensuring that the rules of the game cannot be changed by the developer mid-way.

**Best Innovation**

Most apps try to *reward* users (gamification). Our innovation is using **Loss Aversion** (a psychological principle) to force productivity. We are not building "EdTech"; we are building **"Incentive-Tech."**

> **1. Pioneering "Loss-Aversion" EdTech**
> Traditional education platforms rely on willpower, which often fails. We innovated by introducing **financial consequences** to learning. By integrating Ethereum Smart Contracts directly into the study flow, we transformed ETH from a speculative asset into a **productivity tool**. We are creating a new category: **"Proof-of-Learning" protocols**, where knowledge is the only private key that unlocks your funds.
> **2. Solving the "Subjective Oracle" Problem with AI**
> One of the biggest hurdles in blockchain is that smart contracts are blind to the real world (the "Oracle Problem"). Usually, this requires centralized data feeds.
> **Our Innovation:** We built an **"AI Oracle"**. We use **Gemini 3 Flash** not just to summarize text, but to act as a deterministic judge. By combining Gemini's reasoning with **FastAPI's strict Pydantic schemas**, we created a reliable bridge that allows an on-chain contract to trust an off-chain subjective event (passing a quiz).
> **3. "Trustless" Education Architecture**
> We moved the "gradebook" to the blockchain. In standard EdTech, the database administrator can change your grades. In **Skill-Stake**, the logic is immutable. We used **Kiro Track** to generate verifiable escrow logic, ensuring that neither the developer nor the user can cheat the system. This creates the world's first **cryptographically secured exam hall.**

**AWS**

**Skill-Stake is a cloud-native application built entirely on the AWS ecosystem:**

1. **Development**: Built using **AWS Kiro**, leveraging its Agentic capabilities and **MCP** to accelerate full-stack development.
2. **Database**: Powered by **NeonDB**, utilizing **AWS-native serverless storage architecture** for scalable, bottomless Postgres retention.

3. **Compute**: The FastAPI backend is containerized and deployed on **AWS App Runner**, ensuring auto-scaling and high availability.

Funds are locked when donated

No country restrictions

Smart contracts lock funds and release them only when real-world impact is proven.

We fuse live environmental data with funding decisions — action triggered by reality, not emotion.

The platform converts climate data into actionable financial signals.

Global donors can fund projects without banks, borders, or intermediaries.

Accountability is automated — code replaces NGOs’ promises and PDFs.

Impact isn’t marketed; it’s measured, timestamped, and cryptographically provable.

TerraTrack doesn’t ask users to trust climate action — it forces it.

- Aggregate real-time news from multiple trusted sources
- Provide transparent, auditable verification mechanisms

On top of that, switching between frontend logic, backend APIs, and blockchain scripts required constant context switching, which was mentally demanding. **The problem it solves**

PayFlow Protocol solves the problem of slow, opaque, and rigid institutional cross‑border payments by turning stablecoin transfers into programmable, compliance‑aware flows with real‑time fraud intelligence. It compresses multi‑day SWIFT‑style settlement into near‑instant execution, bakes KYC/AML tiers and Travel Rule checks directly into the rails, and attaches escrow, multi‑sig, and oracle‑based conditions so large-value transfers can move with embedded rules, full on‑chain auditability, and AI fraud screening that runs locally on GPU across an ensemble of neural nets, GNNs, and a Qwen3 MoE model.

**Challenges we ran into**

The project still faces challenges around scaling its AI and compliance stack to true institutional volumes, hardening and independently auditing the relatively large smart‑contract surface, and generalizing models trained on datasets like Elliptic++ to new chains, assets, and evolving fraud patterns. Open issues include making the MoE + GNN ensemble more resource‑efficient for diverse hardware, continuously updating regulatory logic across jurisdictions, stress‑testing MEV/oracle defenses in live environments, and shipping production‑grade tooling around monitoring, governance, and incident response beyond the hackathon‑ready prototype.

**Ethereum Track**

PayFlow Protocol uses blockchain smart contracts on Ethereum to create programmable payments with built-in compliance checks and escrow conditions. The system verifies AI fraud detection results cryptographically on-chain, enabling instant cross-border settlements in 12 seconds while maintaining immutable audit trails - unlike traditional payment systems requiring days for settlement.

**Best Innovation**

PayFlow Protocol is a production-ready, programmable payment infrastructure that transforms how institutional stablecoin payments work. We've built the intelligence layer that makes money smart — embedding compliance, AI-powered fraud detection, and programmable conditions directly into payment flows.

> ChainPort: Decentralized Container Ownership

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1.Untrusted Containers in Production
Developers often deploy containers without knowing who created them or whether they were modified.
ChainPort ensures every container has a verified owner and immutable history, reducing security risks.

2.Lack of Proof of Container Behavior
Today, there is no permanent record showing how a container behaved during execution.
ChainPort records behavior attestations, making container execution auditable and traceable.

3.Silent Behavior Changes (Drift)
Containers can change behavior over time without notice, causing failures or breaches.
ChainPort detects and records behavior drift, warning users before deployment.

4.Unsafe Deployment Decisions
Deployment decisions are often manual and subjective.
ChainPort provides a clear trust score and verification status, enabling safer, automated deployment decisions.

5.No Accountability After Incidents
When something goes wrong, it’s hard to identify responsibility.
ChainPort creates tamper-proof records, enabling accountability and forensic analysis.

6.Complex Security for Non-Experts
Security tools are often difficult to understand for non-blockchain users.
ChainPort simplifies trust into visual indicators (Verified / Blocked), making security accessible to everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. ENS Errors on Local Blockchain (Hardhat)

Hardhat does not support ENS name resolution, which caused repeated transaction failures.

Solution:
We removed all ENS-based address resolution and enforced strict address validation using direct Ethereum addresses.

2. Ethers v5 and v6 Compatibility Conflicts

Different parts of the stack depended on different versions of ethers, causing build failures and runtime errors.

Solution:
We standardized the project to a single ethers version and rewrote provider and contract calls accordingly.

3. Smart Contract ABI Mismatch Errors

Frontend calls failed because function names or signatures did not exactly match deployed contracts.

Solution:
We carefully aligned ABI files with deployed contracts and verified function availability before calling them.

4. Trust Data Shape Mismatch (Array vs Object)

Trust score data fetched from InsForge arrived as an array, but the frontend treated it as an object, resulting in missing UI values.

Solution:
We updated the mapping logic to safely extract the first trust record from the array before rendering.

5. Testing Marketplace Without Minting

Since container minting was handled by another module, I initially had no data to test the marketplace UI.

Solution:
We created mock container and trust data using InsForge SQL tables to simulate real blockchain outputs.

6. Controlling Navigation Based on Trust State

Preventing unverified containers from accessing the deployment page required careful routing logic.

Solution:
We added trust-based gating in the frontend to block navigation and show clear “Deployment Blocked” feedback.

**Ethereum Track**

ChainPort aligns strongly with the ETHIndia track because it uses Ethereum as a core trust and verification layer, solving a real developer security problem using decentralized primitives.

 1. Ethereum as the Source of Truth

ChainPort uses Ethereum smart contracts to record container ownership, behavior attestations, and trust decisions.
This ensures immutability, transparency, and tamper-proof verification, which are fundamental goals of Ethereum.

🔹 2. Decentralized Trust Infrastructure

This reflects Ethereum’s mission of enabling trustless coordination.

 3. Real Developer Use Case (Beyond DeFi)

ChainPort applies Ethereum to software supply-chain security, an emerging and highly relevant area.
It demonstrates how Ethereum can secure real-world infrastructure, not just financial applications.

 4. Smart Contracts for Policy Enforcement

Deployment permissions in ChainPort are derived from on-chain trust states, not manual decisions.
This showcases Ethereum’s strength in programmable rules and automated enforcement.

5. ETH Ecosystem Compatibility

ChainPort is designed to work with:

Ethereum wallets (MetaMask)

Local Ethereum networks (Hardhat)

Standard Solidity smart contracts

**The problem it solves**

# 🛡️ The Problem It Solves

In today's digital landscape, **privacy is a myth**.

When we share sensitive information—API keys, passwords, private documents, or confidential notes—via standard messaging apps (WhatsApp, Discord, Slack) or email, we leave a permanent **digital footprint**. These files stay on servers indefinitely, can be forwarded without consent, and often lack audit trails.

**SecureShare** was built to solve the problem of **Data Permanence** and **Unsecured Transmission**. It acts as an ephemeral "Digital Dead Drop" for the modern web.

### 🚀 How It Empowers Users

* **🛡️ The "Self-Destruct" Mechanism**
    Unlike Google Drive or Dropbox, files here aren't meant to stay. Users can set strict **Access Limits** (e.g., "Burn after 1 view") and **Time Limits** (e.g., "Expire in 10 minutes"). Once the criteria are met, the data is wiped from the database instantly.

* **👁️ Zero-Trust Monitoring**
    We provide real-time **Audit Logs**. If you share a link, you can see exactly when it was accessed and from which IP address, giving you total situational awareness.

* **🧑‍💻 For Developers by Developers**
    It is the safest way to share `.env` variables or credentials with teammates without risking them being saved in chat history logs.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

Building a security-focused application came with its own set of unique engineering hurdles. Here are the major ones I faced and how I cracked them:

### 1. The "Offset-Naive" vs. "Offset-Aware" Timezone Hell 🕒

* **The Bug:** During the development of the expiry logic, the backend kept crashing with the error: `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. This happened because Python’s `datetime.now()` defaults to local time (naive), while our Supabase database returns timestamps in UTC (aware).
* **The Fix:** I had to standardize the entire backend to strictly use **UTC**. I refactored the logic to use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` everywhere. This ensured that no matter where the server or user is located, the expiry countdown is always accurate to the second.

### 2. The JPEG Compression Data Loss 🖼️

* **The Bug:** While building the **StegoLab (Steganography)** feature, I initially allowed all image formats. However, I noticed that when users uploaded **JPG/JPEG** images, the hidden secret messages were getting corrupted or disappearing completely.
* **The Reason:** JPEGs use "lossy compression." When the image is saved, it discards "unimportant" pixel data to save space—but that was exactly where my code was hiding the secret bits!
* **The Fix:** I implemented strict validation in the backend to **enforce .PNG format** for the Cloaking module. PNGs are lossless, ensuring the Least Significant Bits (LSB) remain intact for reliable data extraction.

### 3. Balancing "Hacker Aesthetics" with Usability 🎨

* **The Hurdle:** I wanted a "Mr. Robot" style dark terminal look, but often these designs have terrible UX (User Experience) that confuses normal users.
* **The Solution:** I used **React + Tailwind CSS** to create a "Bento Grid" dashboard. It keeps the dark, neon-green cyber aesthetic but organizes features into clean, accessible boxes, ensuring even non-tech users can navigate the "Vault" easily.

> Crypto to fiat(inr) instant payments

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem

In India, if you hold USDC or any stablecoin, it’s essentially illiquid.

Almost all real-world payments run on UPI. To use your crypto, you’re forced to:
	•	Convert a large amount to INR upfront
	•	Wait for bank settlement
	•	Spend from your bank account

This means your stablecoins are locked behind exchanges, not usable for daily payments. You over-convert, wait, and often end up with unused fiat sitting idle in a bank account.


How x402 Fixes This

x402 enables a pay-per-request payment model.

Instead of converting ₹10,000 upfront and hoping you’ll use it all, you pay exactly what you need, exactly when you need it.
	•	Paying ₹100 for chai? → One request, one signature
	•	Sending ₹5,000 to a friend? → Same flow
	•	No pre-conversion, no waiting, no batching

Here’s how it works:
	1.	The backend responds with HTTP 402 Payment Required
	2.	That response specifies exactly how much USDC is needed
	3.	You sign once with MetaMask
	4.	The x402 facilitator settles the payment on-chain
	5.	The receiver instantly gets INR to their UPI ID

Every payment is:
	•	On-chain verified
	•	Non-custodial
	•	Tied to a single API request


Buckets, Pools & Liquidity Providers (INR Side)

To make instant INR payouts possible, x402-Pay uses a bucket-based liquidity system.
	•	Liquidity providers deposit INR into configurable buckets
	•	Each bucket defines:
	•	Exchange rate
	•	Min / max transaction size
	•	Risk and availability parameters
	•	When a payment request comes in, buckets compete in real time
	•	A Dutch-auction style matching engine selects the best combination of buckets

Key Point:

- Anyone can become a liquidity provider.

If your bucket offers:
	•	Better rates
	•	Reliable availability
	•	Healthy liquidity
it gets selected more often, and earns more USDC.

This creates a permissionless, market-driven FX layer where:
	•	No single entity controls pricing
	•	Competition drives better rates
	•	Capital efficiency improves for both users and LPs


Why This Matters for Crypto Adoption in India

This is what finally makes stablecoins usable in India.

Today, holding USDC means very little if you can’t spend it.
x402-Pay turns stablecoins into real money for daily life.
	•	Pay anyone with a UPI ID
	•	No onboarding required for receivers
	•	No pre-conversion
	•	No idle fiat

That’s 300+ million UPI users instantly reachable from a crypto wallet.

x402’s pay-per-request model is perfect for daily payments:
	•	You don’t batch-convert and hope
	•	You pay as you go
	•	Every transaction is verifiable on-chain

Stablecoins finally become liquid, spendable, and useful.

**Challenges we ran into**

First time hearing about x402 didn't even know HTTP 402 was a real status code.

The main challenge was implementing dynamic pricing. Most x402 examples use fixed prices, but our app needs different amounts for each payment. Had to build custom middleware that fetches the quote and returns that exact USDC amount as the x402 price.

Also hit some nasty build issues with WalletConnect + Next.js 16. Packages were bundling test files and breaking the build. Fixed it by switching to webpack and adding aliases to force consistent package versions.

The "sign, don't send" paradigm took a bit to understand, users sign EIP-712 messages and the facilitator does the actual transfer. Once it clicked, I realized how clean this model is for payments.

**The problem it solves**

# TraceSafe: Farm-to-Fork Traceability System

## The Problem It Solves

India loses **40% of its produce** to spoilage and fraud due to zero supply chain transparency. Once food leaves the farm, there's no trusted record of temperature exposure, location, handling, or authenticity. This causes multi-crore losses for farmers, illness outbreaks from contamination, fake organic certificates, QR code cloning, and middlemen fraud. The core issue: **no tamper-proof way to prove what happens to food from farm to shop**.

## How TraceSafe Works

TraceSafe combines **IoT sensors, AI verification, and Hyperledger Fabric blockchain** to create an immutable, real-time traceability system:

- **ESP8266 IoT nodes** continuously monitor crate temperature (DS18B20), ambient conditions (DHT22), GPS location, and automatically control cooling fans to maintain safe environments
- **Machine learning** predicts spoilage, detects temperature abuse.
- **Blockchain** guarantees tamper-proof records—no fake farmers, duplicate QR codes, or manipulated transport logs

## Who Benefits

**Farmers** prove freshness, prevent middlemen fraud, and earn better prices with auto-generated safety certificates. **Transporters** monitor conditions in real-time, get spoilage alerts, and provide verifiable delivery logs. **Retailers** instantly verify temperature history and quality before accepting shipments. **Consumers** scan QR codes to see the complete journey and verify organic claims. **Regulators** trace contamination outbreaks to exact sources and stop certification fraud.

## Making Tasks Safer

Every batch gets a **live digital twin** showing timeline, sensor graphs, location maps, and risk scores. All events (CreateBatch, Pickup, TransitUpdate, Delivery, Certification) are immutably recorded on Hyperledger Fabric across FarmerOrg, DriverOrg, RetailerOrg, and RegulatorOrg. The system blocks fake certificates, duplicate QR stickers, Excel-based fraud, and manual record tampering—creating complete trust with one scan.

**Result**: Provable, tamper-proof food safety from farm to fork.

**Challenges we ran into**

# ⚙️ **Challenges I Ran Into**

Building TraceSafe was exciting, but it came with several tough technical and hardware challenges that pushed us outside our comfort zone.

---

## 🔥 **1. ESP8266 Overheating During Sensor Load**

While running multiple sensors (DS18B20, DHT22, GPS) simultaneously, the ESP8266 frequently **overheated and crashed**. The limited GPIO lanes and high draw from the GPS module made it unstable.

### **How we solved it**

* Switched to proper powering (5V → GPS, 3.3V → sensors)
* Reduced polling frequency
* Added software cooldown intervals
* Optimized Serial logs to prevent blocking

This made the system stable even during long transport simulation tests.

---

## 🧠 **2. ML Model Data Constraints**

Spoilage prediction requires long-term, high-quality datasets. Since real datasets were unavailable, we struggled with **poor accuracy**, missing values, and overfitting.

### **Solution**

* Created synthetic training samples
* Used Random Forest as baseline before testing LSTM
* Incorporated rolling averages and delta-temperature features
* Cleaned sensor noise before inference

This improved prediction reliability significantly.

---

## ⛓️ **3. First-Time Blockchain Development**

Hyperledger Fabric was completely new to us. We struggled with:

* Certificate enrollment
* MSP configuration
* Chaincode packaging
* Endorsement policies

### **Solution**

We followed Fabric docs, used test-network, and built minimal Go chaincode first. After debugging enrollment issues, the network became stable and transactions worked reliably.

---

## 🧬 **4. Exploring LSTM for the First Time**

Using LSTM for time-series spoilage prediction was challenging due to our inexperience. The model initially produced unstable outputs and exploding gradients.

### **Solution**

* Normalized all input sequences
* Switched to smaller hidden layers
* Added early stopping
* Tested GRU as fallback

---

## 🚀 **Outcome**

Each challenge strengthened the project. The failures taught us more than the successes — and every hurdle improved the reliability and innovation of TraceSafe.

### FraudNets

> Decentralized Graph Based Laundering Detection

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gunicorn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gunicorn-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Money laundering costs the global economy $800 billion to $2 trillion annually. Traditional detection systems are slow, rule-based, and easily evaded by sophisticated criminals.

FraudNets is an AI-powered real-time fraud detection system that identifies suspicious transaction patterns as they happen. It uses Graph Neural Networks to detect complex schemes like circular money flows (where money moves in a cycle between accounts), smurfing (breaking large amounts into smaller transactions to avoid detection thresholds), and other anomalies that humans might miss.

The system provides a visual 3D network graph that helps investigators trace money trails instantly, making complex financial networks easy to understand. Fraudulent accounts are recorded on an Ethereum blockchain, creating a shared, tamper-proof blacklist that can be used across institutions.

Banks, fintech companies, and regulators can use FraudNets to reduce compliance costs, build fraud-resistant platforms, and monitor suspicious activities in real-time.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was deploying the backend with PyTorch and GNN dependencies on cloud platforms. Render used Python 3.13 by default which broke pandas compilation due to Cython compatibility issues. I solved this by creating a .python-version file to lock Python to version 3.11.4.

Another issue was PyTorch's large size causing installation timeouts. I fixed this by using CPU-only wheels from PyTorch's dedicated index URL, reducing the package size significantly.

The GNN model training on server startup caused health check failures because the server took too long to respond. I implemented model caching so the model trains once, saves to a file, and loads instantly on subsequent starts.

For the frontend, rendering large transaction networks in 3D caused browser lag. I optimized this using Three.js with custom node geometries and efficient rendering techniques.

**Ethereum Track**

FraudNets uses Ethereum blockchain as the foundation for creating a decentralized, tamper-proof fraud registry that can be shared across financial institutions.

Smart Contract (FraudRegistry.sol)

We built a Solidity smart contract deployed on Ethereum that maintains an immutable blacklist of fraudulent accounts. When our AI system detects fraud, the flagged account address is permanently recorded on-chain. This creates a shared source of truth that cannot be altered or deleted, ensuring that once an account is marked as fraudulent, it stays blacklisted forever.

Key Features:

Blacklisting accounts with fraud type classification
On-chain timestamps for audit trails
Owner-controlled access for adding/removing entries
Public verification function so anyone can check if an account is blacklisted
Web3 Integration

The Python backend uses web3.py to interact with the Ethereum network. When fraud is detected through our GNN model or pattern recognition algorithms, the backend automatically submits a transaction to the smart contract, recording the fraudulent account on-chain.

Why Blockchain Matters for Fraud Detection

Traditional fraud databases are centralized and siloed. Bank A might catch a fraudster, but Bank B has no way to know. With FraudNets, the blockchain acts as a shared, cross-institutional registry. Any participating institution can query the smart contract to check if an account has been flagged, enabling real-time, collaborative fraud prevention across the entire financial ecosystem.

This brings transparency and trust to fraud detection while maintaining the immutability and decentralization that Ethereum provides.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Computer Vision](https://img.shields.io/badge/Computer%20Vision-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3data.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3data.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

****⚠️ Important Note for Judges: ****The backend is deployed on Render's free tier, which may experience cold starts (30-60 seconds initial load time) after periods of inactivity. Please allow a moment for the backend to wake up when first accessing the live demo. This is a limitation of free hosting, not the application architecture.

Every year, drowsy and fatigued driving causes over 100,000 crashes in the United States alone, resulting in thousands of deaths and injuries. The transportation industry faces three major challenges:

**Invisible Threat** - Driver fatigue and stress are difficult to detect until it's too late
**No Standardized Monitoring** - Existing solutions are expensive, intrusive, or unreliable
**Lack of Accountability** - No verifiable way to track and prove driver wellness over time
What Safe Drive AI Does
Safe Drive AI is an intelligent driver wellness monitoring platform that combines:

**🤖 Real-time AI Detection** - Computer vision analyzes facial features to detect drowsiness and stress levels instantly
**💡 Personalized Recommendations** - AI-powered insights using Groq's LLaMA 3.1 provide actionable safety advice
**🔗 Blockchain Verification** - Immutable safety records on Celo (EVM-compatible) create transparent, portable driver credentials
**📊 Data-Driven Insights **- MongoDB-powered analytics track wellness trends and improvement over time

Who Benefits & How
**🚛 Transportation Companies**
Reduce accident rates by 40-60% through proactive fatigue detection
Lower insurance costs with verifiable safety data
Improve driver retention by supporting wellness instead of just monitoring
Real-time fleet monitoring across multiple drivers and vehicles
**🚗 Individual Drivers**
Stay safer with instant alerts when drowsiness or stress is detected
Build safety reputation through blockchain-verified wellness NFTs
Earn rewards with Safe Driving Tokens for maintaining good wellness scores
Get personalized tips to improve alertness and reduce stress
**🏢 Insurance Providers**
Data-driven risk assessment based on actual driving behavior, not demographics
Personalized premiums that reward safe drivers
Fraud prevention through blockchain-verified records
Reduced claim costs from fewer accidents
**🏛️ Fleet Managers**
Compliance monitoring for hours-of-service regulations
Predictive analytics to forecast fatigue before it becomes dangerous
Route optimization with integrated rest stop recommendations
Transparent reporting for stakeholders and regulators
**Key Features That Make It Safer**
✅ Sub-second detection - AI analyzes facial features in real-time with <1s latency
✅ Proactive alerts - Warns drivers BEFORE accidents happen, not after
✅ Smart route planning - Identifies safe rest stops along your journey

✅ Cross-platform - Works on any device with a camera (laptop, phone, tablet)
✅ Offline capable - Core monitoring works without internet connection

Real-World Impact
Before Safe Drive AI:

❌ Drivers rely on subjective feelings of fatigue
❌ Companies have no objective wellness data
❌ Accidents happen without warning
❌ No way to verify safety claims
After Safe Drive AI:

**Technology That Powers Safety**
**Computer Vision** - TensorFlow + MediaPipe for facial analysis
**AI Recommendations** - Groq LLaMA 3.1 for personalized insights
**Blockchain **- Celo (EVM-compatible) for transparent records
**Scalable Backend** - FastAPI + MongoDB Atlas for enterprise-grade performance
**[[Modern Frontend](url)](url)** - Next.js 14 with real-time React **dashboards**

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Safe Drive AI was an incredible learning experience with several technical hurdles. Here are the major challenges and how I overcame them:

**1. Real-Time Facial Analysis Performance 🎥**
**Challenge:**
Initial implementation using TensorFlow.js in the browser caused significant lag (3-5 seconds per frame), making real-time monitoring impossible. The drowsiness detection was too slow to be useful.

**Solution:
**
Migrated facial analysis to Python backend using TensorFlow + MediaPipe
Implemented frame sampling (analyze every 3rd frame instead of every frame)
Used WebSocket connections for low-latency streaming
Optimized model to achieve sub-second detection (<500ms per analysis)

Result: ✅ Real-time monitoring with smooth 30fps video display and instant alerts

**2. MongoDB vs localStorage Data Persistence 💾**
**Challenge:**
Initially used localStorage for storing wellness data, which caused:

Data loss on page refresh
No cross-device synchronization
Couldn't handle large datasets (100+ sessions)
TypeScript errors with async/sync mismatches
**Solution:**

Migrated entire data layer to MongoDB Atlas
Created FastAPI endpoints: /api/wellness/history, /api/wellness/sessions
Implemented automatic session grouping on backend (5-minute gap = new session)
Updated all frontend components to use async/await for data fetching
Fixed TypeScript errors by making getWellnessHistory() return Promise<any[]>

Result: ✅ Persistent, scalable data storage with proper session tracking across devices

**3. Groq AI API Integration Issues 🤖**
**Challenge:**
AI recommendations kept failing with Error 400: Bad Request. The error messages were cryptic, and I couldn't figure out why the API was rejecting requests.

**Solution:**

Discovered Groq deprecated the old model llama3-8b-8192
Updated to new model: llama-3.1-8b-instant
Simplified prompts to reduce token usage
Added detailed error logging to catch API response details
Implemented fallback messages when API is unavailable
Code Fix:

**// Before (Error 400)**
model: "llama3-8b-8192"

**// After (Works!)**
model: "llama-3.1-8b-instant"
Result: ✅ AI recommendations working perfectly with personalized wellness insights

**4. Celo Blockchain Integration Complexity 🔗**
Challenge:
First time working with blockchain. Struggled with:

Understanding EVM-compatible chains vs Ethereum
Smart contract deployment on testnet
Managing private keys securely
Integrating Web3.js with Next.js
**Solution:**

Studied Celo documentation and EVM compatibility
Used Hardhat for smart contract development and testing
Deployed to Alfajores testnet for safe testing
Implemented proper environment variable management for private keys
Created separate service layer (realBlockchainService.ts) for blockchain logic

Result: ✅ Successfully deployed ERC-20 tokens and ERC-721 NFTs on Celo

**5. CORS and API Security Issues 🔒**
**Challenge:**
Frontend couldn't communicate with backend due to CORS errors. Also, accidentally exposed API keys in test files, triggering GitHub security alerts.

Solution:

Configured FastAPI CORS middleware properly:
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://localhost:3000"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
Moved all API keys to .env.local (not committed to Git)
Added .env.local to .gitignore
Removed test files with exposed keys before pushing

Result: ✅ Secure API communication with proper environment variable management

**Ethereum Track**

Safe Drive AI leverages the Ethereum ecosystem through Celo, an EVM-compatible blockchain, to create transparent and immutable driver safety records.

ethers.js compatible architecture
Standard Ethereum development workflow

Can deploy to Ethereum mainnet

**The problem it solves**

WalletX is a production-ready, game-changing DeFi escrow platform that enables trustless P2P transactions using smart contracts.

**Core Innovations:**

**1. Temporary Disposable Wallets:** first in the world, ensuring privacy + easy testing.

**2. Trustless Escrow:** smart contract-powered claim/refund system.

**3. Multi-Chain:** deployed across 8 EVM networks (Base, Lisk, Polygon, Ethereum, BNB, ZetaChain, Somnia, Citrea).
**4. Advanced Analytics & Graphs:**
Real-time stock-market-style charts showing network-wise volume, price, and activity across all 8 EVM networks, filterable by time period (1D, 7D, 30D, All-time).

**5. AI Assistant:** WalletX-powered assistant for user support and smart suggestions.

**6. QR Code Ecosystem:** built-in generation + scanning for instant transactions.
**7. AWS SES Email Automation:** WalletX integrates AWS Simple Email Service (SES) to deliver secure and reliable escrow status notifications.

**Why it matters:**

1. Solves real-world problems like freelance payments, marketplace escrow, property deposits, and B2B contracts.

2. Combines DeFi + AI + multi-chain infra into one unified platform.

3. Fully deployed, mobile responsive, and production-ready.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Multi-Chain Deployment:** Deploying escrow contracts on 8 EVM networks was tough due to different RPC/gas configs. I solved it by creating a unified deployment script with ethers.js.

**2. Temporary Wallets:** Ensuring secure creation & destruction of disposable wallets was challenging. I used bip39 standards and cleanup logic to prevent leaks.

**3. AI Integration:** Running AI inside a decentralized app without backend was hard. I fixed it using a serverless API bridge for real-time assistance.

> A unified private liquidity layer for all chains

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zcash](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zcash-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZBridgeX solves the fundamental issues of privacy, fragmentation, and liquidity in today’s multi-chain ecosystem. As users move assets across networks like NEAR, Solana, Starknet, Mina, and Ethereum L2s, they face a fully public environment where balances, transfer histories, and strategies can be traced by anyone. This not only exposes user activity but also makes cross-chain usage complicated and unsafe. ZBridgeX addresses these challenges by offering a unified, private financial layer where users can interact across chains without revealing sensitive information.

With ZBridgeX, people can move assets privately across chains, use a single private stablecoin (ZUSDx) for payments and DeFi, deposit collateral and mint stablecoins without exposing wallet balances, and participate in fundraising privately through the Launchpad. The platform also enables private routing through ArbRouter, allowing users to execute transactions optimally while hiding intent and protecting against MEV or front-running. Tasks that previously required multiple bridges, tools, and exposed transactions are now simplified into one seamless interface.

By combining privacy-preserving transfers, a private stable currency, shielded collateral vaults, private fundraising, and MEV-safe routing, ZBridgeX makes multi-chain usage significantly safer, easier, and more accessible. Users no longer need to worry about their activity being traced, copied, or exploited, and projects gain a secure way to raise funds without exposing contributors or inflows. Ultimately, ZBridgeX transforms the multi-chain experience into a unified, private, and fully protected financial ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was adapting Zcash’s Sapling system—originally built for a single chain—into a multi-chain environment, which caused issues with nullifier consistency and cross-chain state mapping. We solved this by creating a unified shielded state and moving all ZK proving to a server-side prover to avoid browser performance bottlenecks. Differences in chain finality (Solana vs. Starknet vs. Mina) also caused synchronization problems, which we fixed using a finality-aware scheduler and chain-specific state watchers. Ensuring private vault solvency without revealing collateral required designing new inclusion + solvency circuits. Finally, we had to keep UX simple despite all the cryptography, so we built a 3-step abstracted flow with auto-routing, auto-claiming, and a unified dashboard.

### VectorVault

**The problem it solves**

Modern cybersecurity, facing advanced AI attacks and decentralised networks, finds traditional Security Operation Centres (reliant on signature detection) prone to alert fatigue and slow resolution, hindering proactive threat prediction. Furthermore, the SOC platform itself often uses vulnerable static credentials, weakening overall security.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Software** : A Blockchain Security Operation Centre, engineered using modern libraries of React 18, TypeScript & Javascript, attired with a fully Vectorised Search Engine with cosine similarity & hash-based embeddings.

- It is pliant and aimed to be re-designed for a private network protocol & OS.
- It is completely independent from any third-party microservice providers like AWS, Azure or CloudFlare.

**2. P.E.A.R. Engine** : The P.E.A.R. Engine (Predictive Event Anomaly Recorder) is a LTI, Anti-Causal Dynamic Stable Invertible polyglot persistence model situated between a client's IT infrastructure and our predictive infrastructure. Its Neural engine detects and records anomalies based on the Principle of Deviation due to Over-Saturated Analog Data flowing between these two infrastructures.

**3. A.S.T.R.A Framework** : It is enforced at our to-be-patented cryptographic controls. Daily-rotating credentials using HMAC-SHA256 policy. accessible only via biometrics and geofencing. Our ShuffleRoleBytes Technology binds credentials to roles, preventing privilege pivots. Indigenous MFA Mapping ties the hash to second-factor proof, eliminating MFA bypass risk and limiting hash exposure to >0.05 human hours.

### Zk One
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zk-one-7a7e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/omegateam-ltd/Zk-One) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/zk_One_dapp) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> privacy, zk proofs, verification, data sharing

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZK ONE is a decentralized application (DApp) focused on secure e-identity management, document verification, and privacy-preserving data sharing.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Generating and verifying zk-SNARKs client-side without killing performance Problem:

Initially I tried to generate zk-proofs directly in the browser using circom + snarkjs. For small circuits it was fine, but as soon as the identity document schema grew (multiple fields, timestamps, hashes), proof generation took 15–40 seconds on mid-range laptops and completely drained mobile batteries.Solution:  Split the workflow: heavy proof generation is now done inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) simulation in the backend (Node.js + express + snarkjs worker threads), while the frontend only handles proof verification (which is almost instant).  
Later I replaced full client-side generation with pre-generated “ceremony” parameters and moved to the new halo2 + pse libraries that are 4–6× faster.  
Added a nice animated progress bar + Web Workers so the UI never freezes.

2. Storing large document hashes & metadata on Lisk L2 without exploding gas costsProblem:

Lisk L2 is cheap, but storing raw IPFS CIDs + Merkle paths for every document quickly became expensive when users started uploading multiple documents.Solution:  Implemented a Merkle tree accumulator per user inside the smart contract. Instead of storing each hash individually, only the updated root is written on-chain (~60 bytes per update).  
Off-chain I keep the full Merkle path in localStorage/indexedDB and rebuild it when needed.  
Added batch updates users can upload 5-10 documents at once and commit only one root.

3. Seamless wallet connection + 2FA while keeping the UX actually simpleProblem:
Many users dropped off at the wallet-connect + mandatory 2FA step. The flow felt too “enterprise” for a Web3 product.Solution:  Switched from the usual “Connect → Enable 2FA → Create identity” to a progressive model: users can explore the DApp and even upload documents with a temporary session (encrypted with lit-protocol). Only when they want to commit data on-chain do we ask for wallet + 2FA.  
Used WalletConnect v2 + RainbowKit + custom modal styling with Shadcn - now the connection success rate jumped from ~45 % to 82 %.

4. Making drag-and-drop access control intuitiveProblem:

The first version of the “share with permission” feature was a boring list of addresses + checkboxes. Nobody understood expiration dates and granularity.Solution:  Built a visual canvas (react-dnd + beautiful-dnd) where users literally drag verified contacts onto document cards and set time-limited badges (“24h”, “7 days”, “revoke anytime”).  
Added instant QR-code generation for offline/air-gapped sharing.

5. Deploying a Next.js + static assets + worker backend on a fully decentralized hostProblem:

Vercel and Netlify were easy, but I wanted 100 % decentralized hosting to match the project philosophy. Fleek + IPFS was great for static files, but the proof-generation worker kept timing out.Solution:  Split the app: static frontend → Fleek/IPFS + Filecoin  
Backend proof service → Railway → Cloudflare Workers (for final production I’m migrating to Akash Network containers)  
Added fallback gateways and DNSLink so the DApp stays accessible even if one gateway is down.

These challenges forced me to go deeper into zk, Merkle structures, L2 economics, and UX for privacy-sensitive flows  and honestly made ZK ONE way stronger than my original MVP vision.

Nathan Jessy

### Lunarys
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lunarys-0001) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/tomi204/dex-fhe) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/LunarysLabs) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/LaCXeEJTlnc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Privacy First DEX using FHENIX.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fhenix](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fhenix-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Financial Privacy on Public Blockchains

  Today, every transaction on Ethereum is fully transparent. Anyone can see:
  - Your wallet balance
  - Who you're trading with
  - How much you're swapping
  - Your liquidity positions

  This creates serious problems:
  - Front-running & MEV attacks exploit visible pending transactions
  - Competitive intelligence leaks expose trading strategies
  - Personal security risks from publicly visible wealth
  - Regulatory concerns for institutions handling client data

  ---
  Lunarys DEX: Private DeFi with FHE

  Lunarys is a confidential decentralized exchange powered by Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). It enables:

  | Feature                | What It Does                                                         |
  |------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | Private Swaps          | Trade encrypted tokens without revealing amounts or counterparties   |
  | Confidential Liquidity | Provide liquidity to pools where reserves stay encrypted             |
  | Hidden Balances        | Your token holdings are encrypted on-chain—only you can decrypt them |
  | Encrypted Positions    | LP positions represented as NFTs with confidential data              |

  ---
  How It Makes DeFi Safer

  Traditional DEX:                    Lunarys DEX:
  ┌─────────────────────┐            ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ Swap 10,000 USDC    │            │ Swap ████████ eUSDC │
  │ for 9,200 EURC      │     →      │ for ████████ eEURC  │
  │ Wallet: 0x1234...   │            │ Wallet: 0x1234...   │
  │ Balance: $50,000    │            │ Balance: ██████████ │
  └─────────────────────┘            └─────────────────────┘
     Everyone can see                   Only you can see

  Key Benefits:

  - Zero MEV Exposure — Bots can't front-run trades they can't see
  - Institutional Ready — Trade without exposing client positions
  - Personal Security — No one can target you based on visible wealth
  - Compliance Compatible — Audit trails exist without public exposure

  ---
  Use Cases

  1. Private Token Swaps — Convert between encrypted stablecoins (eUSDC ↔ eEURC) without revealing trade size
  2. Confidential Yield Farming — Earn APY on liquidity pools while keeping position sizes private
  3. Secure Portfolio Management — View and manage encrypted balances, transfer tokens privately
  4. Institutional Trading — Execute large trades without market impact from front-runners

  ---
  Technology Stack

  - FHE (Fhenix CoFHE) — Enables computation on encrypted data without decryption
  - Encrypted Tokens — Encrypted token standard for confidential balances
  - Constant Product AMM — Standard x*y=k formula with encrypted reserves
  - Position NFTs — Liquidity positions as transferable encrypted NFTs

**Challenges we ran into**

The most frustrating issue we encountered was with balance decryption after swaps. After executing a successful swap transaction:

  User swaps eUSDC → eEURC
  Transaction confirmed ✅
  Try to decrypt new eEURC balance... ❌ FAILS
  Wait ~2 minutes...
  Try again... ✅ Works perfectly

  The Problem:
  When a user receives encrypted tokens from a swap, attempting to decrypt the new balance immediately fails. The cofhejs.unseal() call either returns an error or stale data for approximately 2 minutes after
   the transaction confirms.

  What We Tried:
  - Invalidating local FHE permit cache
  - Re-fetching the encrypted balance handle
  - Adding retry logic with exponential backoff

  Current Workaround:
  We implemented a polling mechanism with user feedback:

  // Show "Balance updating..." state
  // Retry decryption every 15 seconds
  // After ~2 min, decryption succeeds

  Uncertainty:
  We're still not 100% sure if this is:
  - A CoFHE SDK limitation — the SDK caches something that needs to invalidate
  - On-chain propagation delay — FHE ciphertext needs a few blocks to be "readable"
  - Fhenix network latency — decryption nodes need time to sync new encrypted state

  This doesn't break functionality, but it impacts UX. Users see their swap succeed but can't immediately verify their new balance.

  ---
  2. Encrypted Arithmetic Precision

  FHE operations on euint64 don't support decimals. Implementing the AMM's constant product formula with proper precision required careful handling:

  // Problem: k = reserveA * reserveB can overflow euint64
  // Solution: Use euint128 for intermediate calculations
  euint128 k = FHE.mul(
      FHE.asEuint128(reserveA), 
      FHE.asEuint128(reserveB)
  );

  Fee calculations with basis points (0.3% = 3000/1000000) needed RAY scaling (10^18) to maintain precision without decimals.

  ---
  3. Async Decryption Pattern

  Unlike regular Solidity where you can read values synchronously, FHE decryption is asynchronous:

  // Step 1: Request decryption (transaction 1)
  FHE.decrypt(encryptedValue);

  // Step 2: Wait for Fhenix network to process...

  // Step 3: Retrieve result (transaction 2 or view call)
  (uint256 result, bool ready) = FHE.getDecryptResultSafe(handle);

  This required restructuring our entire flow for features like "mid-price oracle" — users must wait between requesting and receiving the price.

  ---
  4. Permission Management Complexity

  FHE values require explicit permission grants. When transferring Position NFTs, we had to ensure the new owner gets FHE access:

  function _update(address to, uint256 tokenId, address auth) internal override {
      super._update(to, tokenId, auth);

      // Grant FHE permissions to new owner
      Position storage pos = _positions[tokenId];
      FHE.allow(pos.liquidity, to);
      FHE.allow(pos.token0Amount, to);
      FHE.allow(pos.token1Amount, to);
  }

  Forgetting a single FHE.allow() meant users couldn't access their own encrypted data.

[Tomas Oliver](https://github.com/tomi204)

### ShadowSpend
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/shadowspend-4cd6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/web3devz/ShadowSpend) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/dD7qSwlZNRo) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/dD7qSwlZNRo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous, private, cross-chain ZEC execution.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![near](https://img.shields.io/badge/near-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**ShadowSpend** is a privacy-preserving AI agent that allows users to spend ZEC using natural language while keeping all sensitive data — wallet keys, intentions, and transaction logic — fully confidential inside a **Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)**.

By leveraging **NEAR AI** for secure private inference and **NEAR Intents** for cross-chain settlement, ShadowSpend autonomously interprets user requests, selects optimal routes, and executes shielded or transparent ZEC transactions with guaranteed privacy and correctness.

## 🚀 Features

- **Natural Language Interface**: Simply tell ShadowSpend what you want to do
- **Privacy First**: All sensitive data stays encrypted inside the TEE
- **Autonomous Execution**: Intent parsing, decision-making, and transaction signing all in one
- **Cross-Chain Settlement**: Seamless integration with NEAR Intents protocol
- **Shielded Transactions**: Full Zcash privacy support

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Running AI inside a TEE** — Standard LLM pipelines don’t fit enclave constraints, so I built a lightweight, encrypted inference flow that works entirely inside the TEE.

**2. Zcash shielded transactions** — RPC inconsistencies and slow shielded operations caused errors, so I added retries, normalization, and a stable wallet wrapper.

**3. Accurate intent parsing** — Natural-language commands can be ambiguous, so I enforced strict validation to ensure the LLM’s interpretation was always safe and correct.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

**ShadowSpend connects Zcash to multiple chains using NEAR Intents, enabling fully private cross-chain actions through natural language.**
The agent interprets user commands inside a TEE, constructs optimized intents, and executes actions such as *swapping ZEC cross-chain, lending ZEC-derived assets on other chains, funding DeFi positions, or creating wrapped ZEC flows* — all without exposing keys or transaction logic.
This directly advances the goal of giving Zcash users seamless, private access to multi-chain DeFi powered by NEAR Intents.

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

**ShadowSpend is a privacy-first agent built entirely around NEAR AI’s TEE-based inference.**
All natural-language requests, wallet operations, intent construction, and transaction decisions happen inside an encrypted enclave, ensuring full confidentiality of user intent and ZEC activity.
The project demonstrates precisely what the track calls for: *agentic AI models that privately help users spend, route, and manage ZEC—shielded or cross-chain—through natural language prompts.*

**Private Payments & Transactions**

**ShadowSpend makes real-world ZEC payments as simple as telling an AI agent what to do.**
Using NEAR Intents, the agent can send shielded payments, schedule recurring payments (e.g., VPN subscriptions), donate ZEC, or perform transparent or shielded transfers — all executed automatically and privately.
This delivers exactly what the track seeks: *a practical, privacy-preserving Zcash payment solution powered by NEAR Intents.*
