**The problem it solves**

ZecRep gives Zcash users a way to prove their shielded wallet history without revealing balances, so DeFi protocols can grant loans, rebates, or governance power with a verifiable privacy-preserving credential instead of trusting centralized attestations or forcing users to dox their funds.


Describe what people can use it for / how it helps

Lending desks & OTC venues: require a minimum Zcash tier (Bronze → Platinum) before extending credit, without seeing the borrower’s exact balance.

DAOs & governance: gate proposals, voting weights, or Sybil protection via ZecRepGuards.requireTier, ensuring only reputable shielded accounts participate.

Wallets & dApps: integrate the SDK so users can mint/refresh their tier badge directly in-app, with the Proof Wizard showing every stage of the pipeline.

Partners & compliance teams: subscribe to aggregator webhooks + Prometheus metrics to audit job lifecycles, latency, and failure reasons in real time.

Developers: leverage the soulbound badge + FHE range checks to build private loyalty programs, fee rebates, or KYC-lite access controls.

**Challenges we ran into**

Lightwalletd latency & redundant scans: hitting public endpoints repeatedly was too slow, so I built a disk-backed scan cache (TTL configurable) to memoize Orchard/Sapling totals and unblock rapid prototyping.
Fastify logging + plugin mismatches: Fastify v5 rejects logger objects unless configured properly, and older @fastify/cors versions balked at the new major. I fixed it by exporting typed logger options and upgrading to the v5-compatible plugin.
End-to-end pipeline coordination: the Proof Wizard needed to reflect actual backend job progress—not mock timers—so I rewired the hook to submit/poll aggregator jobs, handle errors, and surface encrypted payloads + total zats live.
README diagrams on GitHub: Mermaid diagrams failed because parentheses break node parsing; quoting node labels made them render correctly for the judges.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Zcash-focused tooling: it exposes a ZIP‑32/lightwalletd scan cache, a Noir proof pipeline, and a Fastify aggregator that other developers can call. That directly supports “build on Zcash and integrate privacy features.”
Developer libraries: the @zecrep/sdk hooks (useProofWizard, useJobs, etc.) and guard contracts (ZecRepGuards.requireTier) are drop-in components other teams can adopt to add shielded-tier checks.
Privacy framework: it combines ZK proofs, FHE encryption, and soulbound badges into a reference architecture, streamlining how others build privacy-preserving DeFi integrations.

**The problem it solves**

## *"Today, I want to talk about identity."* 

Every day, billions of people around the world are asked to prove who they are. To buy a drink, you show your entire ID—revealing your name, address, and exact birthdate—just to prove you're over 21. To join a community, you hand over your passport, exposing everything about yourself to strangers. To be counted in a census, you surrender your privacy to a database that could be hacked, leaked, or misused.

**This is insane.**

We've accepted a world where proving *one thing* about yourself means revealing *everything* about yourself. Where being counted means being tracked. Where identity equals surveillance.

*Today, we're going to change that.*

---

## Introducing **ZK-Citizen**

ZK-Citizen is a privacy-preserving identity and census platform built for the next generation of digital societies—Network States, DAOs, startup communities, and anyone who believes that **privacy is a fundamental human right**.

### 🛂 **zk-Passport: Prove Who You Are, Not What You Are**

Imagine walking into a bar and proving you're over 21 without showing your ID. Imagine applying for a job and proving you're a citizen without revealing your passport number. Imagine joining a community and proving you're a real person without doxxing yourself.

**That's zk-Passport.**

With zero-knowledge proofs, you can:
- ✅ **Prove your age** without revealing your birthdate
- ✅ **Prove your nationality** without exposing your passport
- ✅ **Prove your identity** without surrendering your privacy

Your data never leaves your device. Only mathematical proofs are shared—proofs that are impossible to fake and impossible to trace back to you.

### 📊 **zk-Census: Count Everyone, Identify No One**

How do you measure the population of a digital nation? How do you understand the demographics of a global community? Traditional censuses require everyone to register their personal information in a central database. One breach, and everyone is exposed.

**There's a better way.**

zk-Census lets communities:
- 📈 **Count their population** without collecting personal data
- 📊 **Analyze demographics** without identifying individuals  
- 🛡️ **Prove population thresholds** to governments, investors, or partners—without revealing who their members are

A Network State can prove it has 10,000 citizens without revealing a single name. A DAO can demonstrate its age distribution without knowing anyone's birthday. A startup society can show its growth without building a surveillance database.

---

## Who Is This For?

### 🌐 **Network States & Startup Societies**
Building a new kind of nation? You need citizens, but you don't need surveillance. ZK-Citizen lets you count your population, verify membership, and prove legitimacy—all while respecting the privacy that brought people to you in the first place.

### 🏛️ **DAOs & Digital Communities**
Governance requires knowing who can vote. But voting shouldn't require doxxing. With zk-Passport, members can prove their eligibility without revealing their identity. One person, one vote—verified cryptographically.

### 🔐 **Privacy-Conscious Individuals**
Tired of handing over your personal information to every website, app, and bouncer? ZK-Citizen puts you back in control. Prove what you need to prove, nothing more.

### 🏢 **Businesses & Platforms**
Need to verify age for alcohol sales? Nationality for compliance? Identity for KYC? Do it without becoming a honeypot for hackers. Verify without storing. Comply without compromising.

---

## How It Works

```
Traditional Identity:  You → [All Your Data] → Verifier → Database → 🎯 Hackers

ZK-Citizen:           You → [Mathematical Proof] → Verifier → ✅ Verified, Nothing Stored
```

1. **Create your zk-Passport** — Enter your information once, on your device. It's hashed and committed to the blockchain. Your actual data? Stays with you.

2. **Generate proofs on demand** — Need to prove you're over 18? Generate a proof. Need to prove you're from Singapore? Generate a proof. Each proof reveals only what's necessary.

3. **Join the census anonymously** — Register once with a nullifier that prevents double-counting. You're counted, but never identified.

4. **Communities get insights, not data** — Population counts, age distributions, regional breakdowns—all without a single piece of personal information.

---

## The Technology

Built on **Mina Protocol**, the world's lightest blockchain, ZK-Citizen uses **zkApps** to create succinct, verifiable proofs that anyone can verify in milliseconds.

- **Poseidon hashes** for efficient commitments
- **Merkle trees** for scalable membership proofs  
- **Nullifiers** for sybil-resistant, anonymous participation
- **Zero-knowledge circuits** for selective disclosure

The result? A system that's:
- 🔒 **Private by design** — Your data never touches a server
- ⚡ **Fast** — Proofs verify in milliseconds
- 🌍 **Decentralized** — No central authority, no single

**Challenges we ran into**

Building ZK-Citizen was an incredible learning experience, but it wasn't without its hurdles. Here are the key challenges we faced and how we overcame them:

---

## 🔧 Challenge 1: o1js API Breaking Changes

### The Problem
When implementing the zkApp smart contracts, we encountered TypeScript compilation errors that initially seemed cryptic:

```
error TS2345: Argument of type '() => Promise<Field>' is not assignable to parameter of type '() => Promise<void>'
```

Our `@method` decorated functions like `getTotalPassports()` and `getPopulation()` were returning `Promise<Field>`, but the o1js library's `@method` decorator strictly requires `Promise<void>` return types.

### The Solution
We realized that in o1js, `@method` decorated functions are **provable methods** meant for state transitions, not getters. The fix was simple but required understanding the framework's design philosophy:

```typescript
// ❌ Before (broken)
@method async getTotalPassports(): Promise<Field> {
  const total = this.totalPassports.get();
  this.totalPassports.requireEquals(total);
  return total;
}

// ✅ After (working)
getTotalPassportsCount(): Field {
  return this.totalPassports.get();
}
```

**Lesson learned:** Read the framework documentation carefully. Provable methods in zkApps are for proving state transitions, not for reading state.

---

## 🔧 Challenge 2: CircuitString Deprecation

### The Problem
We initially used `CircuitString` from o1js to handle string-to-Field conversions for nationality verification:

```typescript
import { CircuitString } from 'o1js';

// This threw: Property 'toFields' does not exist on type 'typeof CircuitString'
const nationalityFields = CircuitString.toFields(CircuitString.fromString(nationality));
```

The `CircuitString.toFields()` method we expected simply didn't exist in the version of o1js we were using.

### The Solution
We implemented our own string-to-Field conversion using `TextEncoder`:

```typescript
private createStringCommitment(str: string, salt: Field): Field {
  // Convert string to bytes using TextEncoder
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const bytes = encoder.encode(str.toLowerCase().trim());
  
  // Convert bytes to Field elements (8 bytes per Field for safety)
  const fields: Field[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 8) {
    let value = BigInt(0);
    for (let j = 0; j < 8 && i + j < bytes.length; j++) {
      value = value | (BigInt(bytes[i + j]) << BigInt(j * 8));
    }
    fields.push(Field(value));
  }
  
  // Hash with salt for commitment
  return Poseidon.hash([...fields, salt]);
}
```

**Lesson learned:** When library APIs change, don't fight it—implement your own solution using primitives. It often results in cleaner, more maintainable code.

---

## 🔧 Challenge 3: Vercel Deployment 404 Errors

### The Problem
After fixing all TypeScript errors and successfully building the project, we deployed to Vercel only to be greeted with:

```
404: NOT_FOUND
Code: NOT_FOUND
```

The deployment succeeded, but Vercel couldn't find our frontend files.

### The Solution
The issue was that our frontend files were in a `frontend/` subdirectory, but Vercel was looking for files in the root. We created a `vercel.json` configuration:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "buildCommand": "echo 'No build needed'",
  "outputDirectory": "frontend"
}
```

This told Vercel:
1. Skip the build step (we have static HTML/CSS/JS)
2. Serve files from the `frontend` directory

**Lesson learned:** Always configure your deployment platform explicitly. Don't assume it will "figure out" your project structure.

---

## 🔧 Challenge 4: Merkle Tree Height Optimization

### The Problem
We initially set our Merkle tree height to 32, which would support 2³² (~4 billion) entries. However, this made proof generation extremely slow during testing—taking several minutes per proof.

### The Solution
We analyzed our actual requirements:
- Network States typically have thousands to millions of citizens, not billions
- A height of 20 supports 2²⁰ (~1 million) entries
- This reduced proof generation time from minutes to seconds

```typescript
// Optimized for realistic Network State sizes
export class PassportMerkleWitness extends MerkleWitness(20) {}
export class CensusMerkleWitness extends MerkleWitness(20) {}
```

**Lesson learned:** Optimize for your actual use case, not theoretical maximums. Premature optimization for scale you'll never reach hurts performance today.

---

Preventing users from registering multiple times (sybil attacks) while maintaining privacy is tricky. We couldn't just store user IDs—that would defeat the purpose of privacy.

**The problem it solves**

Whisperrkeep tackles the privacy gaps that plague modern Web3 tooling: forgotten wallet phrases, scattered credentials, secret keys, and 2FA tokens across chains and devices, all while requiring constant trust in third parties. We solve this by encrypting every secret locally, keeping the cloud zero-knowledge, and pairing the experience with AI intelligence that helps users organize and automate their recovery options without exposing data. This lets builders stay compliant in privacy-focused hackathons and keep sensitive keys safe while still interacting with AI-powered tooling.

**Challenges we ran into**

Balancing easy user experience with battle tested end-to-end encryption was a major problem. We did a lot of prototyping on how to maintain military grade security throughout the application, without making it any clunkier for users to use. Also security hardening, vulnerability testing and enforcement was a real deal.

**General Bounty**

Whisperrkeep delivers bank-grade security by combining AES-256 local encryption with a strict Zero-Knowledge architecture, ensuring that neither the platform nor any third party can ever access user data. This approach guarantees total privacy and sovereignty over sensitive credentials, making it a critical tool for protecting digital identities against centralized breaches and surveillance.

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

Whisperrkeep demonstrates privacy-preserving computation by running sensitive AI workflows—like organizing keys or generating recovery paths—entirely within the user's secure context, ensuring raw secrets never leave local storage. By decoupling intelligence from data exposure, it proves that AI-driven utility can coexist with strict Zero-Knowledge guarantees, setting a new standard for confidential personal standard for confidential computing standard for secure, private interactions.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Whisperrkeep provides privacy infrastructure by encrypting sensitive credentials and keys locally (Zero Knowledge) before they ever touch the network, ensuring users retain full custody of their secrets. As a developer tool, it offers secure, AI-assisted recovery workflows and granular export capabilities that help builders manage and migrate complex key materials without compromising security without relying on centralized trust.

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

Whisperrkeep redefines self-custody by unifying fragmented keys, seeds, and credentials into a single, locally encrypted vault that users alone control, eliminating reliance on vulnerable cloud backups. This innovation empowers individuals to securely manage their entire digital asset portfolio across chains and devices, fostering true financial sovereignty and safer wallet adoption.

**Zcash Data & Analytics**

Whisperrkeep aligns with Zcash’s mission by providing a privacy-first layer for managing ZEC wallet keys and shielded transaction notes, ensuring that the metadata of financial privacy tools remains as secure as the transactions themselves. By enabling users to analyze and organize their own encrypted data locally without leakage, it supports the broader ecosystem of private, sovereignty-respecting analytics.

**The problem it solves**

# Private Prediction Markets Using Fhenix FHE

## **Problem**
Traditional prediction markets expose all user activity publicly:
- who placed a bet  
- which side they chose (YES/NO)  
- how much money they staked  

This leads to:
- **zero privacy**,  
- **easy manipulation**,  
- **unsuitable markets for sensitive questions**.

A private prediction market must hide individual bets **without breaking fair settlement or payouts**.

---

## **Solution**
We designed a **privacy-preserving prediction market** using **Fhenix's Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE)** through `cofhejs`.

Our system keeps the market itself public, but all user bets remain encrypted.

### **What stays public**
- Market question & close time  
- Fees and creator info  
- User deposit balances  
- Total escrow available  

### **What stays private**
- Individual stake amounts  
- Whether a user bet YES or NO  
- Each user’s payout amount  

### **How it works**
1. Users **deposit funds publicly** into the contract.  
2. When placing a bet, users submit:
   - **encrypted stake**  
   - **encrypted outcome (YES/NO)**  
   - a **binding signature** to link encrypted data to escrowed funds  
3. The contract updates encrypted totals using **on-chain FHE operations**.  
4. After the market closes, an authorized FHE worker:
   - processes all encrypted bets,  
   - computes payouts homomorphically,  
   - submits **encrypted payout results** to the contract.  
5. Users **decrypt their own payout privately** and withdraw from escrow.

This ensures fair settlement *without revealing* who bet what.

---

## **How We Use Fhenix**
We leverage Fhenix FHE in three key stages:

### **1. Encrypting User Inputs**
- the amount they are betting  
- their YES/NO choice  

The contract receives only ciphertexts.

### **2. Homomorphic On-Chain Computation**
The contract uses:
- `euint64` encrypted types  
- FHE operations to update encrypted totals like:
- total pool  
- total YES stake  

All without ever seeing the underlying numbers.

### **3. Encrypted Outputs + Private User Decryption**
The FHE worker submits encrypted payouts.  
Users retrieve their own encrypted payout and call:

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🔧 Challenges We Faced

### **1. Keeping real-money bets private**
Blockchain transactions are public, so hiding how much a user actually bet is difficult.  
**Solution:** Users deposit funds publicly, but the *actual bet amounts* they place are encrypted using Fhenix FHE.  
This keeps economic value real while preserving stake privacy.

---

### **2. Ensuring encrypted stakes correspond to actual escrow**
A malicious user could encrypt a fake value while only escrowing a small amount.  
**Solution:** Each bettor signs a **binding signature** that links:
- the encrypted stake ciphertext  
- the public escrowed amount  

This prevents mismatches without revealing the encrypted value.

---

### **3. Computing payouts under encryption**
Payout formulas involve division and selecting winners, which are expensive or impractical to run purely under FHE.  
**Solution:** A **hybrid settlement model**:  
- encrypted totals are computed homomorphically,  
- only the aggregate totals are selectively decrypted by the FHE worker,  
- per-user payouts are then computed homomorphically using these values.  

This approach keeps individual bets private while making settlement practical.

---

### **4. Identifying winning bets without revealing bet choices**
We must decide who won, but decrypting outcome bits would reveal each user’s side.  
**Solution:** Use an **encrypted winning bit**, and compute  
`encryptedOutcome * encryptedWinningBit` homomorphically  
so the FHE can determine winners *without ever seeing choices*.

---

### **5. Enforcing secure and private withdrawals**
Users must claim rewards without revealing their identity or bet details.  
**Solution:** Each bet has a hidden **payoutCommit** and the user generates an **ephemeral payout key**.  
Withdrawals are authorized by signatures from this private key, ensuring unlinkability.

### ZyberLink v0.0.2-zyb: Shadow Markets for Solana's Hidden Computations

In the underbelly of blockchain, where data demands invisibility, ZyberLink emerges as the decentralized forge for privacy-preserving compute. Built on Solana's relentless speed, this marketplace wields Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and multi-prover consensus to execute operations on encrypted payloads—verifiable, trustless, and utterly concealed from prying eyes.

This release marks our gauntlet thrown into the Zypherpunk Hackathon 2025: a live prototype that turns encrypted witnesses into actionable intelligence, from sanction-proof wallets to aggregated financial shadows.

**Core Arsenal:**
- **Custom FHE Jobs:** Chain operations like sums, averages, conditional counts, and multiplications across datasets up to 100 values strong. Pre-upload server keys for seamless handling of 117MB payloads, with real-time consensus tracking and direct UI downloads of sealed results.
- **Proof of Innocence:** Zero-knowledge attestation that a wallet evades blacklists—predicate-matched counts without exposing a single transaction echo.
- **Private Analytics:** Aggregate encrypted ledgers for totals and means, validated against expected volumes, shielding corporate metrics from the grid's gaze.

Under the hood: Rust-forged backend with Actix, TFHE-rs for FHE muscle, Halo2 for ZK proofs, and Svelte frontend—all anchored in Solana for settlement. Race conditions purged, error flows armored, and endpoints sharpened for prover feeds and chain vitals.

Witness it in action at [demo.zyberlink.fun](https://demo.zyberlink.fun). Fork the repo at [github.com/8ctag0n/13](https://github.com/8ctag0n/13), decrypt a sample with our CLI, and join the build: privacy isn't a luxury—it's the next chain's edge. What shadows will you illuminate?

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

Pushing ZyberLink through the Zypherpunk gauntlet was a grind—FHE on Solana doesn't play nice with real-world constraints. Bandwidth choked on those 117MB server keys during uploads, stalling jobs mid-stream; we hacked it with chunked async transfers in Actix, turning frustration into a progress-tracked feature.
Memory was the silent killer: prover nodes ballooned to OOM on multi-value tests, crashing consensus. Squeezed it down by compressing TFHE intermediates and lazy-loading in Rust—now holds steady under 8GB, proven on devnet stress runs.
And yeah, the real beast was scope creep: from simple sums to full "Proof of Innocence" ZK flows, it nearly derailed us with races in witness handling. Daily prototypes and a ruthless refactor kept it alive—ambition wins when you iterate without mercy.

**General Bounty**

ZyberLink is a primitive for privacy-preserving computation on Solana. Today we have a
  working FHE marketplace with two operations: Sum (aggregate encrypted values) and
  CountIf (count items matching a threshold). Multiple independent provers execute on
  ciphertext and reach consensus before results hit the chain. It's basic, but it
  works—55/56 tests passing, E2E verified. The vision: eventually prove things about
  people without revealing their data. Credit scores without exposing finances. Age
  verification without showing IDs. Compliance without surveillance. We're not there yet,
  but the foundation is live and functional. Primitive today, infrastructure tomorrow.

**General Bounty**

ZyberLink is a decentralized FHE compute marketplace built on Solana. We enable
  privacy-preserving computation where encrypted data never gets exposed—not to provers,
  not to the network, not to anyone except the data owner. Our multi-prover consensus
  (2-of-3, 3-of-5) ensures trustless verification without single points of failure. The
  platform supports Sum and CountIf operations for private analytics and compliance checks
   (Proof of Innocence). Built with TFHE-rs, our system includes a Rust SDK, REST API, and
   fhe-cli for local encryption. All 55/56 tests passing, E2E verified. Privacy
  infrastructure ready for production.

> Use ZEC privately across chains and stay protected

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square) ![FHE](https://img.shields.io/badge/FHE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Zcash has one of the strongest privacy models in crypto, but its privacy is locked inside its own chain.

This creates two major issues:

## Usability

- ZEC can’t be used as collateral, can’t earn yield, and can’t interact with protocols while staying private.

## Accessibility

- Users and developers outside the Zcash ecosystem have no practical way to access ZEC’s privacy features.
- Even if they want shielding, it’s not available on the chains where most activity happens.

---

## Our Vision

We want to make Zcash’s privacy accessible across the multichain world without compromising confidentiality.

ZEC should be usable on Ethereum, Solana, and other ecosystems **while remaining fully shielded**.

We achieve this by combining zero-knowledge proofs with fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) to create a trustless, privacy-preserving transfer tool.

---

## How It Works

### Zcash side

Users burn shielded ZEC to a designated address.  
Our watcher detects the burn but cannot see the sender or amount.  
The destination address is optionally placed in the encrypted memo field.

### Zero-knowledge proof

We generate a ZK proof that confirms:

- A valid burn happened
- It went to the correct burn address
- Amount and recipient match the commitments

All proven without revealing any values.

### Destination chain

We mint **FHZEC**, a confidential wrapped token.  
Balances remain encrypted through FHE, allowing transfers and DeFi usage while amounts stay hidden.

---

## The Result

- Zcash privacy extends beyond Zcash
- Balances remain confidential on transparent chains
- DeFi becomes possible without sacrificing privacy
- Smart contracts can operate on encrypted values

This isn’t just a tool, it’s privacy infrastructure bringing Zcash’s shielding model to the multichain ecosystem.

---

## How We Can Use mumtaZ’s Solution in the Future

mumtaZ opens the door to using shielded ZEC across multiple ecosystems without revealing any data.

Here are some of the ways mumtaZ’s solution can be used going forward:

- Use shielded ZEC as collateral, earn yield, borrow, or lend. All privately and across chains.
- Interact with protocols on Ethereum or Solana while keeping inputs, outputs, and states encrypted.
- Send encrypted value between networks without exposing amounts or addresses.
- Run automated strategies (e.g., rebalancing, yield optimization) without exposing portfolios.

here is the claim contract: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x9815aD7b9E6076ddA6D84A34864fF0c0F8E06744

here is the FHZEC contract: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0xe97BcaFd6b75c1EF765912451d65a5c5f23A5Eb2

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a privacy-preserving cross-chain bridge presented several unique technical challenges. The biggest hurdle was designing a ZK circuit that could parse and verify Zcash transaction data, Zcash's shielded transaction format is complex and we needed to prove burn validity without revealing any private information. I was expecting integrating CoFHE (Fully Homomorphic Encryption) on the Ethereum side was going to be a significant challenge; however it was fairly easy and well-documented even though FHE is still an emerging technology, but we still had to carefully structure our smart contracts to work with encrypted values while maintaining compatibility and keeping the privacy from start to finish.

We also faced difficulties with the Zcash light client integration – decrypting shielded transactions and extracting memo data required deep diving into zcash_client_backend crate internals, and unfortunately documentation on Zcash was not sufficient to build so I had to experiment some code to get a better grasp. 

On the frontend, bundling snarkjs and cofhejs together with Next.js proved tricky due to WASM loading conflicts and SSR compatibility issues. Finally, coordinating state across three different systems – the Zcash watcher, the backend API, and the Ethereum contracts – required careful orchestration to ensure transactions couldn't be double-spent while still providing a smooth user experience.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Users can send their ZEC to Ethereum privately using ZK and FHE. They can prove they burned x amount of ZEC using circuits and claim the equivalent amount on Ethereum in FHERC20, which is a confidential token standart for keeping balances hidden with FHE.

Arion enables Zcash holders to earn DeFi yields (**Aave**) on **Base L2 network** while maintaining privacy through shielded transactions. Users deposit from shielded addresses, the system handles cross-chain swaps via **NEAR Intents**, and withdrawals return to shielded addresses — keeping on-chain activity unlinkable.

**Problem**

4. Private Withdrawals: Reverse swap ETH → ZEC to user’s transparent address
5. Shield Again: Users shield ZEC back to their shielded address

**The problem it solves**

Blockchain analytics tools are either **easy to use but not private**, or **privacy-preserving but too complex** for normal users. Public dashboards can’t analyze Zcash’s shielded activity safely, and existing privacy tools require deep cryptographic expertise, complex setups, and provide no readable insights.

**Nexa** solves this by combining public analytics with **fully encrypted privacy analytics** powered by FHE (CoFHE), nilDB, and nilAI. It lets users:

* Understand Zcash activity **without exposing sensitive data**
* View private network trends computed entirely on **encrypted data**
* Get clear AI summaries using **safe embeddings**, never raw values
* Monitor privacy health, anomalies, and shielded metrics with strong guarantees

Nexa makes advanced, privacy-preserving blockchain analytics **accessible, safe, and easy to understand** for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One challenge was learning how to work with encrypted analytics for the first time. FHE computations don’t behave like normal arithmetic, and early results were incorrect due to scaling issues.I solved this by adopting a consistent fixed-point encoding strategy and batching all values into a stable vector format.

Another hurdle was CoFHE’s asynchronous job model.
Results don’t come back immediately, and some were initially lost or returned out of order. Adding a simple job queue, retry logic, and storing metadata alongside ciphertexts in nilDB stabilized the workflow.

Finally, the 3xpl sandbox API had rate limits and occasional gaps in data.
Implementing caching, backoff, and graceful fallback windows made the ingestion pipeline reliable.

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

Nexa uses **nilAI Model** so it can generate AI summaries without ever accessing raw data or ciphertext.
Only anonymized, high-level feature vectors are sent to nilAI, proving a **real, practical privacy-preserving AI workflow**.
This directly matches the objective of building AI that respects user and network privacy.

**Zcash Data & Analytics**

Nexa uses **nilDB** to store encrypted analytics generated from CoFHE and applies **nilAI** for producing privacy-preserving insights.
It demonstrates a full encrypted analytics pipeline for Zcash:

* encrypted metrics → stored in nilDB → converted to embeddings → interpreted by nilAI.
  This fits the bounty perfectly by showing how Zcash data can be computed, stored, and analyzed privately.

**Zcash Data & Analytics**

Nexa’s Normal Mode provides clean, intuitive charts and trends powered by 3xpl Zcash data.
It makes Zcash activity easier for the community to explore and understand.
nilAI generates human-readable summaries for each window, lowering the barrier to analytics.
This aligns perfectly with RayBot’s goal of **accessible, meaningful Zcash insights**.

### zinnocence
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zinnocence-e2b7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/cinaxriver/zinnocence) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> proof of innocence

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Privacy usually comes with a heavy price: suspicion.**

In ecosystems like Zcash, the moment you shield your assets, you become a black box. To prove to an exchange or a regulator that your funds aren't derived from a hack or a sanctioned list, you typically have to dox yourself. You have to hand over your viewing keys, effectively destroying the privacy you sought in the first place.

We built Zinnocence to fix this trade-off.

It is a developer tool and privacy infrastructure that allows zcash users to generate a **Proof of Innocence** without revealing which transaction belongs to them.

The core idea is simple, even if the math under the hood is heavy. We utilize Fhenix's FHE to create an onchain "dark-room"

Instead of the user checking their own innocence locally (which can be manipulated) or revealing their data to a server (which kills privacy), we shift the burden of judgment entirely to the smart contract.

**Here is how it works:**

The Rust client fetches real zcash data using your **viewing key**. It packages your transaction into an encrypted payload.

The Fhenix contract receives this payload. It holds an encrypted blacklist of known bad actors.

Inside the encrypted domain, the contract compares your transaction against the blacklist.

The magic is that the contract performs this check blind. It does not know your tx ID, and it does not know the contents of the blacklist. It simply computes the math and issues a verdict: Innocent or Guilty.

we didn't want to rely on trusted oracles or complex ZK circuits for this specific task. we wanted to see if FHE could handle the logic of a negative proof - proving who you are not, rather than who you are.

It turns out, it can. Zinnocence creates a path for compliance that doesn't require compromise. It is a tool for developers who want to integrate trustless auditing into private applications.

**Challenges we ran into**

halfway through, we realized client-side filtering was insecure and rebuilt the architecture to force the Fhenix contract as the absolute judge. we also battled incompatible byte orders between zcash and solidity, requiring manual reversal logic. finally, to fit within FHE gas limits, we implemented a 64-bit truncation strategy for hash comparisons.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Zinnocence unlocks a critical path for Zcash adoption by allowing users to prove their funds are legitimate without ever revealing their private transaction history. We built this as a foundational tool for the community, giving developers a plug-and-play way to integrate privacy-preserving compliance into their own applications, ensuring that financial freedom and regulatory safety can finally coexist.

**The problem it solves**

💡 Problem It Solves

In today's gig and freelance economy, trust and transparency in milestone-based payments remain a major challenge. Clients hesitate to pay upfront, while developers and creators risk working without guaranteed compensation. At the same time, AI-powered assistance often lacks accountability, making it hard to build intelligent systems tied to real financial actions.

We wanted to solve this by combining blockchain payments with intelligent automation — enabling a system where users can securely pay, verify, and complete milestones while interacting with a smart, AI-powered assistant that automates progress tracking and insights.

The CDP Wallet Agent bridges this gap by merging AI, blockchain, and token gating to create a programmable, milestone-driven ecosystem — where every interaction, payment, and assistant action is secure, transparent, and verifiable.

**Challenges we ran into**

CDP Wallet Integration: Ensuring smooth wallet connections and real-time payment status updates was tricky, especially when syncing blockchain transactions with the frontend state.

Token Gating Logic: Managing token validation through x402pay while maintaining a seamless user flow required careful backend coordination.

Claude 3 Sonnet Activation: Making sure the AI assistant only responded after token verification introduced complex async handling and edge case management.

Voice + Text Handling: Balancing real-time voice recognition, text prompts, and dynamic AI responses without lag or crashes was a key technical challenge.

UI State Management: Keeping the milestone cards, token payments, and assistant responses synchronized in real time tested our frontend architecture.

AWS Bedrock Integration: Setting up secure, efficient access to Claude 3 Sonnet APIs while maintaining fast response times required extensive optimization.

**The problem it solves**

## **Making Privacy Accessible in Multi-Chain Finance**

GhostBridge AI solves critical privacy gaps in blockchain operations through 9 AI-powered workflows, making complex privacy operations as simple as chatting with an assistant.

***

### **Key Problems Solved**

#### **1. Complex Cross-Chain Privacy**
Traditional bridges expose all transaction details publicly. **GhostBridge AI** enables shielded transfers across 8 blockchains through natural language—just say *"Bridge 5 ZEC to NEAR privately"* instead of navigating complex protocols.

#### **2. MEV Attacks & Front-Running**
Transparent transactions leak trading strategies to MEV bots. **ShadowTrader AI** provides encrypted order books and private execution, protecting traders from front-running and millions in annual losses.

#### **3. No Private Computation**
Sensitive calculations require exposing raw data. **EnigmaAI** uses homomorphic encryption to compute on encrypted data—calculate portfolio returns or salaries without ever decrypting the information.

#### **4. Multi-Chain Chaos**
Managing 8+ wallets is overwhelming. **VaultAI** unifies multi-chain balance tracking—connect once, view all assets (ZEC, ETH, MATIC, NEAR) in real-time across all chains.

#### **5. Steep Privacy Dev Learning Curve**
Learning ZK proofs takes months. **ShieldCoder AI** generates production-ready ZK circuits and Noir contracts conversationally—ask for a "private voting contract" and get audited code instantly.

#### **6. Lack of Privacy Awareness**
Complex cryptography creates barriers. **PrivaMuse** and **EchoPrivacy** create engaging memes, stories, and educational content that normalize privacy and demystify ZK technology.

#### **7. No Private Recurring Payments**
Subscriptions reveal transaction patterns. **AnonPay AI** enables shielded scheduled payments through Zcash—automate monthly subscriptions, payroll, or donations while maintaining complete privacy.

#### **8. Limited Zcash Analytics**
Understanding privacy adoption is difficult. **ZInsight AI** provides real-time analytics on shielded pool growth, transaction volumes, and trends through interactive dashboards.

***

### **Who Benefits?**

**Privacy Advocates:** Execute cross-chain operations without surveillance  
**DeFi Traders:** Protect strategies from MEV bots, eliminate front-running  
**Developers:** Build privacy dApps 10x faster with AI-generated ZK circuits  
**Businesses:** Process confidential payroll with private recurring payments  
**Educators:** Produce privacy content at scale to drive mainstream adoption

***

### **Why It's Easier & Safer**

✅ **Natural Language Interface** - No complex UIs, just chat  
✅ **MEV Protection** - Encrypted orders prevent front-running  
✅ **Homomorphic Encryption** - Compute without decrypting data  
✅ **Unified Dashboard** - Manage 8 chains from one interface  
✅ **AI Code Generation** - No cryptography expertise needed  
✅ **Shielded Transactions** - Privacy-preserving by default  
✅ **Real-Time Analytics** - Instant Zcash insights  

**GhostBridge AI makes privacy technology intuitive, powerful, and accessible to everyone—from traders to developers to everyday users seeking financial privacy.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## **1. Multi-Wallet Integration Complexity**
**Challenge:** Integrating NEAR Wallet Selector with 10+ different wallet providers (MyNearWallet, Meteor, Ledger, HOT, etc.) led to inconsistent connection behaviors and state management issues across wallets.

**Solution:** Implemented a unified `WalletContext` provider using React Context API that normalizes wallet interactions. Created a centralized state management system that handles wallet disconnections gracefully and maintains session persistence across page refreshes.

***

## **2. Gemini AI Function Calling Reliability**
**Challenge:** Gemini AI's function calling sometimes returned malformed JSON or failed to trigger the correct workflow-specific functions, especially when switching between 9 different AI personas (GhostBridge, ShadowTrader, EnigmaAI, etc.).

**Solution:** Built a robust error handling layer with Zod schema validation that catches malformed responses before execution. Implemented workflow-specific system prompts that guide the AI more precisely, and added fallback mechanisms that retry failed function calls with clarified parameters.

***

## **3. Cross-Chain Balance Fetching Performance**
**Challenge:** Querying balances across 8 blockchains (Zcash, NEAR, Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, Avalanche, Starknet, Mina) sequentially caused 15+ second load times, creating poor UX.

**Solution:** Implemented parallel RPC calls using `Promise.all()` to fetch all chain balances simultaneously. Added intelligent caching with TanStack Query that refreshes balances every 30 seconds instead of on every user interaction, reducing API calls by 80%.

***

## **4. Homomorphic Encryption Library Limitations**
**Challenge:** The `paillier-bigint` library had poor documentation and threw cryptic errors when handling large numbers during encrypted computations. BigInt serialization for JSON responses also caused issues.

**Solution:** Created wrapper functions that handle BigInt serialization/deserialization automatically. Built a comprehensive test suite to validate encryption/decryption accuracy and documented edge cases. Implemented input validation that prevents overflow errors before they reach the encryption layer.

***

## **5. Bridge Quote Generation Logic**
**Challenge:** Calculating accurate bridge quotes with fees, gas estimates, and slippage across 8 chains with different fee structures was mathematically complex and error-prone.

**Solution:** Built a `BridgeService` class that encapsulates chain-specific fee logic and uses a standardized quote interface. Implemented extensive unit tests for each chain's calculation logic and added visual comparison tools that let users verify quotes before execution.

***

## **7. TypeScript Type Safety with Dynamic AI Responses**
**Challenge:** AI responses are inherently unpredictable, making it difficult to maintain type safety while parsing Gemini's function call outputs.

**Solution:** Leveraged Zod schemas for runtime validation that auto-generates TypeScript types. Every AI function output is validated against a strict schema before reaching the frontend, catching type errors at runtime and providing helpful error messages.

***

## **9. NEAR Testnet RPC Rate Limiting**
**Challenge:** Frequent balance checks and transaction status polling hit NEAR testnet RPC rate limits during development, causing request failures.

**Solution:** Implemented exponential backoff retry logic and reduced polling frequency from 1s to 5s. Added request deduplication that prevents identical RPC calls within a 10-second window. Cached transaction results to minimize redundant queries.

SILENCE


's Key Features:

1. Intent-Based Cross-Chain DEX

Instead of manually bridging assets and exposing yourself to bridge risks, Silence uses Near Intents. Users simply sign an intent ("Swap 100 USDC on Near for SOL on Solana"), and a solver network executes it.

Slippage Protection: Solvers compete to fill the order, guaranteeing the best price.

Gas Abstraction: Users pay in the source token; solvers handle gas on destination chains.

2. Multi-Workflow Shielded Privacy (via Zcash)

We integrate Zcash's Shielded Pools into the DeFi workflow.

The "Silence" Layer: Assets can be routed through Zcash shielded addresses (z-addrs) during the swap process, breaking the on-chain link between the sender and the receiver.

zk-SNARKs Verification: Proofs are generated to verify funds exist without revealing the amount or the history.

3. Private AI Agents (TEE-Based)

DeFi trading bots usually suffer from the "dark forest" problem—their strategies are visible on-chain.

Near AI + TEE: Silence hosts AI agents inside Intel SGX Trusted Execution Environments.

Secret Strategies: Users can deploy AI agents to execute trades based on private data or complex algorithms. The code runs off-chain in a secure enclave, and only the final intent is published.

**General Bounty**

Silence Bridge
Intent-based cross-chain bridge for seamless transfers between Solana, NEAR, and Zcash.

Key Features:

Intent-based cross-chain execution (no manual bridging)
Solver network with reputation and staking
Shielded privacy support via encrypted amounts
Automatic settlement and reward distribution
Protocol fee mechanism
Intent Lifecycle:

Created - User creates intent with deposit
Matched - Solver matches and commits to execute
Executing - Cross-chain transfer in progress
Executed - Transfer completed on destination chain
Settled - Fully settled, rewards distributed
Failed - Execution failed, refund issued

Arcium's confidential computing enables private on-chain computation:

Encrypted data processing in TEE enclaves
Verifiable computation without data exposure
Privacy proofs enable auditability without disclosure
Compliance-friendly architecture for regulated industries

### Zephyr Wallet
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zephyr-wallet-d529) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/NextGenSoftwareUK/zypherpunk) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://share.descript.com/view/vCoWYIMajqn) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Zypherpunk privacy, MetaMask simplicity

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![.NET](https://img.shields.io/badge/.NET-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Privacy is a huge upcoming meta, but it’s still hard to access - complex UX, steep learning curves, and siloed ecosystems currently pose a barrier to entry.  

The Zephyr wallet by OASIS Web4 solves this. In addition to Solana and Ethereum, it integrates 4 Zypherpunk providers (Zcash, Starknet, Miden, Aztec) in a single wallet that works like Phantom or Metamask - retaining the core privacy features of each chain, while keeping the UX exactly as regular people have come to expect. 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0f561eae72064b4689d93873c61eebaa/f63c20e1-fb91-4186-b2ed-4347bc46d13b.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0f561eae72064b4689d93873c61eebaa/1da84bd1-413e-4cae-87ed-dbeeb318b28e.png)

Zephyr leverages several powerful cross-chain APIs that we’ve been working on with OASIS WEB4, to handle complexity and present a unified, secure user experience. Users authenticate with a single secure cross-chain avatar (which can also be anonymous) - which then generates unique wallet addresses for each of the providers. Users manage this account with a single seed phrase. Important to note - our provider architecture can extend to include any chain.

We’ve included all the wallet features that users expect - send, receive, swap (atomic), view token history. In addition to this, we’ve added useful new privacy tools, such as one-click shielded transfers, and send / receive drops. And, a stablecoin function between ZCash and Aztec. 

Users shouldn’t have to understand the underlying technology to get their benefits - as we move into a world with increasing surveillance, making sure as many people have access to privacy tools as possible, and allowing privacy ecosystems to share liquidity and overcome silos, without compromising on their core principles, is worth fighting for.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges we faced was tackling wallet address derivation for each provider, using our own API (which is .NET based). Each provider works differently - so generating working wallet addresses for all our chains at the same time required a lot of research. We got around it by finding existing .NET based SDKs, and switching from a generic key generation to a custom approach per chain. 

Massive thanks to Starknet, and Andrew Arnott of Zcash's Nerdbank for their SDKs, without which we wouldn't have been able to integrate Starknet / Zcash. 

Building the underlying back-end technology we are using has been a huge undertaking - in fact it's a 10 year project, and we are extremely excited to be using it for this use case.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

OASIS Architecture Integration

Zephyr integrates **Aztec Network as a native provider** within the OASIS platform architecture, enabling seamless interoperability with other blockchain ecosystems. Through the OASIS provider abstraction layer, AztecOASIS connects to the unified wallet system, allowing Aztec to participate in cross-chain operations alongside Zcash, Starknet, Miden, Solana, and Ethereum. This architectural approach means Aztec benefits from OASIS's holonic data structures and universal asset bridge framework, while maintaining its unique private note system and zero-knowledge privacy guarantees.

## Native Aztec Support

Our implementation uses the **Aztec SDK** for proper address generation and private note management, ensuring that all generated Aztec addresses are valid and compatible with native Aztec wallets. This native integration means users can manage their Aztec assets with the same ease as any other supported chain, with addresses automatically generated from a single keypair through our unified address derivation system. Users can create private notes, manage viewing keys for selective disclosure, and interact with Aztec's privacy-preserving smart contracts directly from Zephyr.

## Cross-Chain Privacy Operations

Zephyr enables **bi-directional private bridges between Aztec and Zcash**, demonstrating how zero-knowledge privacy can interoperate with shielded pool technology. These cross-chain operations preserve privacy throughout the transaction—users can bridge assets between Aztec and Zcash while maintaining transaction privacy through private notes and shielded transactions. The bridge supports partial notes for flexible privacy levels and viewing keys for compliance, allowing users to choose their privacy/auditability balance. The atomic swap mechanism ensures security with automatic rollback on failure, protecting users from partial transaction states.

## Zcash-Backed Stablecoin (zUSD)

Zephyr implements the first **truly private stablecoin (zUSD) backed by ZEC** on Aztec Network. Users can mint zUSD by locking ZEC in Zcash's shielded pool, then use the zUSD on Aztec for private DeFi operations. The stablecoin maintains privacy at every layer—the collateral is in Zcash's shielded pool, and the zUSD tokens exist as private notes on Aztec. Users can redeem zUSD to unlock their ZEC collateral, with automatic position health monitoring and liquidation protection. This creates a privacy-first stablecoin that enables DeFi operations while maintaining complete transaction privacy.

## Unified Privacy Ecosystem

By integrating Aztec into a unified wallet alongside Zcash, Starknet, Miden, and other privacy chains, Zephyr eliminates the fragmentation that currently isolates Aztec from the broader privacy ecosystem. Users manage all their privacy-focused assets from a single interface with one seed phrase, while each chain maintains its unique privacy features—Aztec's private notes, Zcash's shielded pools, Starknet's STARK proofs, and Miden's STARK-based privacy all work together seamlessly. This unified approach enables new use cases like cross-chain private DeFi, where users can leverage liquidity from multiple privacy chains while maintaining privacy guarantees.

## Proof of Concept

Zephyr proves that **Aztec's zero-knowledge privacy can seamlessly interoperate with other privacy technologies**. By demonstrating that Aztec's private notes can bridge to Zcash's shielded pools and interact with other privacy chains, we set the foundation for a future where Aztec serves as a privacy hub connecting multiple blockchain ecosystems. This interoperability opens new use cases for Aztec users, enabling them to access liquidity and DeFi opportunities across the entire privacy-first blockchain landscape while maintaining their zero-knowledge privacy guarantees.

**The problem it solves**

Crypto payments today are **public and traceable**.  
Every transaction reveals:

- Wallet identity  
- Income & spending patterns  
- Social and business connections  
- Trading behavior  

This leads to:

- Wallet surveillance  
- Personal safety risks  
- MEV exploitation & copy-trading  
- Business intelligence leaks  

> People deserve financial freedom **without being watched**.

---

What People Can Use It For?

**PrivatePay** enables users to:

- Make **private payments & donations**
- Perform **shielded cross-chain transfers**
- Trade in **private DeFi** without exposure
- Protect wealth with **secure self-custody**
- Use **one interface** for privacy across chains

> Privacy becomes the **default**, not a premium feature.

**Challenges we ran into**

1️⃣ **Connecting Privacy Systems Across Different Chains**
Each partner ecosystem (Starknet, Arcium, Aztec, Zcash, Osmosis, Axelar, FHENIX) uses its own cryptography, account model, and transaction format.  
I built **bridge adapters** to translate shielded commitments and intents between them.

2️⃣ **Maintaining Privacy During Cross-Chain Execution**
Even when values are hidden, **metadata leaks** (timing, routing, bridge hops) can reveal identity.  
I fixed this using **encrypted intents**, **randomized relayers**, and **delayed reveal logic**.

3️⃣ **Secure Self-Custody With Multichain Support**
Wallets like Zashi, Unstoppable, and Noah all manage keys differently.  
I implemented a **unified key abstraction layer** so users keep full control without breaking privacy.

4️⃣ **Private AI Computation Without Trusting a Backend**
Running AI on private data typically requires exposing it somewhere.  
I solved this using **distributed private compute** Arcium to keep user data encrypted end-to-end.

5️⃣ **Private DeFi Liquidity Without Breaking UX**
Shielded swaps and trading often feel slow or complex.  
I optimized ZK circuits and added **intent batching** to make private transactions feel as fast as normal swaps.

> It was making privacy **usable, fast, and interoperable across chains**.

> Private Capital for Public Impact

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloud-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![NEAR Protocol](https://img.shields.io/badge/NEAR%20Protocol-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fhenix](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fhenix-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**1. The "Transparency Trap" in Philanthropy**
We face a dangerous paradox: builders and activists in high-risk jurisdictions need funding the most, but they cannot afford to be seen. Current tools force a deadly choice: Doxx yourself (GoFundMe/KYC) or leak your financial graph (Public Blockchains).

**Privora's Solution:** We decoupled Verification from Identity. We use Reclaim Protocol to generate Zero-Knowledge proofs of real-world attributes (like GitHub commits or Location) without revealing the user's identity. Combined with NEAR AI (TEEs) to sanitize bio data and Zcash for shielded payments, we allow capital to flow to verified builders without exposing the humans behind the code.

**2. The "Public Reputation" Dilemma (FHE)**
In Web3, reputation is usually public. If you receive a "Scholarship SBT" or a "Patron Badge," the whole world sees it. For privacy-centric communities like the Network School, a public list of residents is a security vulnerability.

**Privora's Solution:** We built Encrypted On-Chain Reputation using Fhenix.
Our ImpactSBT contract mints Soulbound Tokens where the donation amount is encrypted (euint128). Patrons can prove they supported the cause without revealing how much, preserving the privacy of their wealth.
Our NetworkSchoolVerifier stores residency status as an encrypted boolean (ebool). The contract knows who is a member, but the public blockchain explorer shows only encrypted bytes. This allows for a "Dark Census"—we can verify and count the population without doxxing the list of members.

**3. "Vetting Fatigue" for Donors**
Donors want to help but lack the time to manually verify hundreds of anonymous profiles to distinguish real builders from scammers.

**Privora's Solution:** We introduced Agentic Philanthropy. Instead of manual browsing, Donors use natural language to command an AI Agent ("Fund verified anti-censorship devs"). The Agent uses TEE-based inference to semantically match the Donor's intent with the Reclaim-verified anonymous personas, ensuring funds only go to candidates who have mathematically proven their skills and location.


![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f986ac51f28944b6b307a3dc953723f4/7b80f6d9-c60e-42e2-a9af-544a17a8bdc4.png)
Architecture Diagram

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. The "Reputation Leaks Privacy" Paradox**

We wanted to gamify philanthropy with Soulbound Tokens (SBTs), but realizing that a standard ERC-721 token would doxx the shielded Zcash transaction was a major hurdle. If an address holds a "1000 ZEC Donor" badge, the privacy of the Zcash layer is broken by the Ethereum layer.

How we solved it: We moved the logic to Fhenix. We wrote the ImpactSBT.sol contract using Fully Homomorphic Encryption. Instead of storing uint256 amount, we store euint128 amountEnc. This allows the contract to track total impact mathematically without ever revealing the plain-text values to the public network. Debugging the type conversions between Solidity uint and FHE euint was a significant learning curve.

**2. Bridging Stateless Inference with Stateful Money**
The NEAR AI TEE is a stateless inference engine—it processes text and outputs JSON, but it cannot "hold" a wallet or sign transactions. We needed a way to turn the AI's matching advice into a secure financial action.

How we solved it: We implemented a QR-Based Handshake. The TEE performs the matching logic and outputs a JSON decision. Our frontend immediately converts this decision into a Payment QR Code (complete with the recipient's shielded address and an encrypted memo). This allows the AI to drive the logic while keeping the cryptographic signing keys air-gapped on the user's mobile Zashi wallet.

**3. Verifying "Invisible" Residents**

We needed to verify Network School members on-chain without creating a public "hit list" of addresses. A standard whitelist contract (mapping(address => bool)) is publicly readable, which defeats the purpose of a privacy society.

How we solved it: We implemented NetworkSchoolVerifier.sol on Fhenix using mapping(address => ebool). By storing the verification status as an encrypted boolean, we created a registry that is programmable but opaque. The contract logic can check membership, but an external observer cannot scrape the list of members. Combining this FHE logic with the off-chain Reclaim Protocol proofs required careful orchestration to ensure the "Verified" status was updated securely.

**General Bounty**

Privora solves the "zk-Census" challenge by deploying NetworkSchoolVerifier.sol, an FHE-enabled smart contract on Fhenix that acts as a privacy-preserving registry for Network School residents.

https://github.com/abhiraj-mengade/privora/blob/main/contracts/NetworkSchoolVerifier.sol

FHE-Based Residency Verification: Unlike standard allowlists that expose every member's address publicly, our contract uses Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE).
The Mechanism: The contract verifies an ECDSA signature off-chain, but crucially, it stores the result as an encrypted boolean (ebool verifiedEnc).
The Privacy: We use FHE.asEbool(true) to store the status. This means the public state of the blockchain does not reveal who is verified to external observers. Only the resident (Claimant) can decrypt their own status via the CoFHE coprocessor to prove membership to the app.
Sybil-Resistant Census: The contract tracks consumedNonces to ensure one signature equals one entry, effectively counting the population (Census) without doxxing the individual members via public boolean flags.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

While often associated with trading, "DeFi" (Decentralized Finance) fundamentally includes Capital Allocation and Grants. Privora builds a decentralized financial primitive for private funding.

Prioritizing User Privacy: We strictly utilize Z-Addresses (Shielded). By generating Zcash QR codes that keep both the sender and receiver anonymous on-chain, we protect the "financial graph" of high-risk activists.
Unstoppable Architecture: By using a Local-First approach (Client-side WASM/QR generation) + IPFS for data, Privora has no central server that can be censored. It allows financial support to flow to anyone, anywhere, regardless of sanctions or borders.
Agentic DeFi: We are introducing a new primitive where AI Agents act as Hedge Fund Managers for philanthropy, automating the flow of ZEC based on semantic criteria rather than manual transfers.

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

Privora is built entirely around the requirements of this bounty. We don't just use AI as a chatbot; we use it as a secure, privacy-preserving reasoning engine for financial transactions.

**Verifiable & Private TEE Inference**: We use NEAR AI Cloud as a "Data Incinerator." By processing sensitive user bios inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), we ensure that raw data (names, locations) is sanitized into anonymous personas without ever being logged or exposed.
**Agentic Spending of ZEC**: The core functionality is an AI Agent that holds a semantic understanding of the donor's intent (e.g., "Fund anti-censorship tools"). The Agent autonomously matches this intent to verified profiles and constructs the payment logic.

**The problem it solves**

1. **Complexity barrier:** Crypto wallets are too technical.
**Solution**: Natural language interface: chat with your wallet in plain English.
2. **Privacy is hard:** Users struggle to use privacy features effectively.
**Solution**: Automatic zero-link routing that optimizes for privacy by default.
3. **Manual transaction management:** Too many steps to send funds.
**Solution**: Single conversation flow: "Send 0.5 ZEC to..." → AI handles the rest.
4. **Transaction traceability**: Blockchain analysis can link transactions.
**Solution**: Intelligent UTXO selection and shielded routing to prevent traceability.
5. **Cross-chain fragmentation**: Swaps require multiple platforms.
**Solution**: Unified cross-chain execution: "Swap 0.5 BTC to ZEC" in one conversation.
6. **No intelligent automation** : Wallets are reactive tools.
**Solution**: Autonomous agent that evaluates, optimizes, and executes transactions intelligently.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Zcash Node Setup Complexity**
**Problem**: Running a full Zcash node locally required large downloads, slow sync, and complex configuration.
**Solution**: We deployed a local TAZ node via docker which is why we have not been able to fully deploy our working application as we need a premium server to have the resources needed to sync the blockchain history
2. **AI Hallucination in Transaction Parsing**
**Problem**: The AI generated incorrect amounts, addresses, and misinterpreted user intents.
**Solution**: Added strict validation layers, balance checks, and transaction previews so users can verify before execution.

We're implementing Gemini Exchange's SDK to enable users to trade and exchange assets through natural language commands. Users say "Swap 0.5 BTC to ZEC" and we execute it through Gemini's exchange infrastructure, while routing the ZEC through shielded pools for privacy.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

**The Problem: **When you trade or use DeFi, everyone can see your transactions, amounts, and strategies on the blockchain.
**The Solution**: ZecFinder lets you trade and swap assets privately. Say "Swap 0.5 BTC to ZEC" and it executes through shielded pools where amounts and addresses are hidden. Zero-link routing prevents anyone from linking your transactions together.
**Why It Matters**: Your trading strategies, portfolio moves, and profits stay private. You can participate in DeFi and execute trades without exposing your activity to competitors or surveillance. It's like having a private trading desk that hides your moves from the public blockchain.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

**Cross-chain swaps expose transaction patterns across chains.**

**The Solution:** ZecFinder uses NEAR Intents for cross-chain execution and Zcash privacy for private receipt.

Imagine, user says "Swap 0.5 BTC to ZEC"
NEAR Intents API executes the cross-chain swap
Received ZEC automatically enters Zcash shielded pools
Zero-link routing prevents transaction correlation

Hence, users can swap assets from any chain (BTC, SOL, USDC) to ZEC while maintaining privacy. The swap is visible on the source chain, but received funds are private and untraceable on Zcash.

**The problem it solves**

In India’s fast-moving fashion SME ecosystem, where trends shift overnight, demand is unpredictable, inventory cycles are short, and GST regulations evolve constantly, businesses struggle with fragmented tools, unreliable forecasting, manual compliance, mismatched inventory, and deadstock leakage, creating financial risk and audit exposure.

The problem intensifies due to disconnected systems for trend insights, procurement, stock valuation, GST filing, and profitability tracking, pushing SMEs into error-prone spreadsheets and outdated ERPs
.
Our solution introduces a unified AI-driven Financial and GST Compliance Platform tailored for fashion SMEs—converting real-time trend signals into structured revenue forecasts, automated inventory valuation, precise COGS allocation, HSN-wise GST projections, and audit-ready documentation.

By integrating forecasting to procurement to inventory to COGS to GST to profitability into one workflow, the platform eliminates manual reconciliation and ensures traceable calculations, seamless integration, and multi-year compliance storage.

It becomes the financial operating system for fashion businesses, bringing accuracy, intelligence, and scalability to a volatile sector.

**Ethereum Track**

Our project uses a hybrid AI + Blockchain architecture where the calculations happen off-chain (in Python) for speed and efficiency, and the final inventory state is securely stored on the Ethereum blockchain for transparency, trust, and auditability.

Although the blockchain module is intentionally minimal, it performs the core purpose of Ethereum in supply chain and inventory systems:
✔ Store critical data in a tamper-proof way
✔ Provide transparent updates via smart-contract events
✔ Ensure no employee or system can manipulate stock values
✔ Maintain immutable records of restocking and discount actions

We deployed a Solidity smart contract using Remix (JavaScript VM).
The contract stores a lightweight inventory structure:

product ID

current quantity

last updated timestamp

discount-applied flag

Every time the AI module recommends stock changes or discounts, the backend updates these values on the blockchain using web3.py.
The smart contract emits events like ProductUpdated and DiscountApplied, creating a verifiable audit trail.

This design fits the Blockchain Track because it uses Ethereum exactly as intended:

off-chain computation for efficiency

on-chain verification for trust

immutable logs to prevent stock manipulation

transparent inventory state that managers or auditors can check anytime

In a real-world fashion SME environment where inventory fraud, inconsistent reporting, or manual errors are common, blockchain ensures every critical update is public, permanent, and tamper-proof, making the system significantly more trustworthy.

> Your Personal AI Outfit Planner

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project simplifies outfit selection using AI to recommend weather-appropriate, stylish outfits. It enhances user experience, saves time, integrates e-commerce, and provides a VR try-on feature to visualize clothes on a user model(provided image).

**Challenges we ran into**

1. How can real-time weather data be converted into meaningful outfit logic that reflects 
human decision-making? 
Weather APIs provide raw numbers (temperature, humidity, etc.), but humans think in terms of 
“too hot,” “mildly cold,” “raining,” “windy,” etc. This raises a research-level question in data 
translation and semantic mapping. 
2. How accurate and reliable can AI-generated clothing suggestions be when the input is 
dynamic and contextual instead of static? 
Unlike normal LLM use, fashion suggestions must be functionally wearable, not just linguistically 
correct. 
3. Can a chatbot interface replace a traditional UI for outfit selection, and does it improve user 
comfort or add complexity? 
This involves studying user perception, clarity of interaction, and conversational efficiency. 
4. How can the system be designed today so that it supports advanced features like AR try-on 
and e-commerce integration later, without rewriting the entire system? 
This question is based on architectural scalability. 
5. What limitations arise from dependency on external APIs, and how can the system remain 
usable even when APIs fail or slow down? 
This leads to research in fault tolerance and fallback logic. 
6. Which AI model (Gemini, GPT, LLaMA etc.) is most suitable for real-time fashion 
recommendation, and why? 
This relates to model suitability, cost, latency, generative tone, and safety.

**Challenges we ran into**

Problem: Counterfeit drugs closely mimic originals

Problem: On-chain storage was expensive on Ethereum
Solution: Used Keccak-256 hashing for proof storage, reduced gas costs by 70%

 3. Real-time Risk Scoring
Problem: Process massive supply chain data instantly
Solution: Built FastAPI backend with async processing, achieved 200ms response time

 4. Web3 Integration
Problem: Seamless blockchain interaction
Solution: Integrated wagmi + rainbowkit with retry logic, 99% transaction success

> Scrape Ethically, Pay Transparently

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

As AI chatbots become primary information sources, website owners lose ad traffic and block scraping. There is no system for AI systems to ethically pay for the content they consume.
We solve this by building a decentralized pay-per-scrape gateway, enabling AI chatbots to compensate websites automatically whenever they fetch data.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. ## Wallet Integration Issues (ethers.js)

- Connecting MetaMask to the frontend caused multiple issues:
- Detecting if the user even had MetaMask installed
- Handling account switching & network switching (e.g., to Sepolia)
- Getting the provider, signer, and contract instance without breaking the UI
- Handling “user rejected transaction” errors
- Handling asynchronous blockchain calls inside React components

2. ## Smart Contract Modification Challenges (Solidity)

- Every change required re-deployment
- Deployment generates a new contract address → frontend breaks
- Storage layout issues when modifying structs & mappings
- Gas limitations for storing large website metadata
- Ensuring payable functions were secure (avoiding re-entrancy and failed transfers)

3. ## On-Chain Database Limitations

- We wanted to store website data directly on-chain, but:
- Storing long website metadata (titles, descriptions, tags) is expensive
- Strings on-chain cost a lot of gas

4. ## UI/UX Flow Challenges (React)

- Showing loading states for transactions
- Showing confirmations after MetaMask prompts
- Preventing users from paying twice
- Displaying transaction hashes and success notifications
- Real-time updates of registered websites (using events or manual refresh)

5. ## Choosing the Right AI API (Groq )

We needed an AI model to fetch/interpret website content. But each API had limitations.
Chosen -> Grok:
- Extremely fast inference
- Cheap

**Ethereum Track**

Chain_Talk is deeply designed around Ethereum’s principles—decentralization, transparency, trustless execution, and fair economic incentives.
Our entire system—website registry, payment flows, scraping permissions, proof-of-access, and history tracking—lives on-chain, demonstrating practical Web3 engineering.

> Certificates that don't lie...

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Certificate authenticity is a rising concern among all fields. Our project is a certificate authenticity verifier that checks whether the uploaded certificate is forged or authentic. We have built a full-stack application for issuing, managing, and verifying educational certificates using Ethereum blockchain hash check, and multiple layers of AI-powered forgery detection. Institutes can issue certificates that are permanently recorded on the Ethereum blockchain, making them immutable and globally verifiable, students can view their issued certificates, and verifiers can ensure authenticity using Blockchain or AI Forge Detection where we analyze PDFs for manipulation, layout inconsistencies, and authenticity markers.

-AI-Powered Forgery Detection:
  - OCR text extraction
  - Layout similarity analysis
  - Logo/seal detection and matching
  - Signature authenticity analysis
  - Image tamper detection (ELA, clone detection)
  - NLP content validation

**Challenges we ran into**

- Blockchain implementation in local that has access to original wallets through logins with wallet addresses.
- Building a full stack app with security and blockchain implementations in a day.
- Integrating so many different frameworks like react and tailwind for frontend to a python backend which has access to solidity for blockchain uploads.

**Ethereum Track**

- Store certificate hashes on Ethereum blockchain when issuer uploads.
- Ethereum Blockchain Verification: Check if certificate hash exists on-chain.
