### MySteadyAid
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mysteadyaid-95a5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dabking228/MUBA-BLOCKCHAIN) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/wL9G7HtVQSo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Transparent disaster-relief distribution

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OAuth](https://img.shields.io/badge/OAuth-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![move](https://img.shields.io/badge/move-333333?style=flat-square) ![sui](https://img.shields.io/badge/sui-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### zkLogin: "Groth16 proof verify failed" at the final on-chain step

Our zkLogin flow completes every off-chain step correctly — Google OAuth, nonce binding, server-side JWT verification, deterministic salt derivation, and the Mysten prover call all succeed — but the assembled zkLogin signature is rejected on-chain with `Groth16 proof verify failed` when it reaches a validator. We ruled out ephemeral-key staleness (it reproduced on a completely fresh login), re-checked the address-seed and `maxEpoch`assembly against the Sui docs line by line, and confirmed the prover response shape was correct — but couldn't isolate the root cause within the hackathon window.

Rather than fake it, we kept the full zkLogin implementation in the codebase and demo the **identical downstream flow** (sponsored transaction → `claim_and_link` → payout) using a standard `Ed25519Keypair` signer, which shares the exact same `Signer` abstraction. The zkLogin design and its entire off-chain half are real and working; only the final proof verification is unresolved, and we document that openly rather than leaving it hidden.

### Sui SDK v2 and the sponsored-transaction dual-signature flow

The `@mysten/sui` v2 SDK replaced `SuiClient` with `SuiGrpcClient` and changed many method shapes, so our early integration code matched no tutorial. The sharpest single bug: role resolution ("which capability objects does this address own?") silently returned nothing because the gRPC `listOwnedObjects` type filter needs a **fully-qualified datatype** (`0xPKG::relief_v3::RegistrarCap`), not the `0xPKG::relief_v3` prefix the older API accepted.

Sponsored (gasless) transactions also took real iteration: the sponsor and the user must sign the **exact same transaction bytes**, the sponsor's coin must be pinned as gas payment before the transaction is built, and both signatures are submitted together. We settled on a clean three-step split — server builds + pre-signs as sponsor → browser signs the same bytes with the user's key → server executes with both signatures — which is now the single path every end-user action flows through.

### Making multi-model AI consensus survive real model failures

Two things broke the first working version of our 3-model zone-credibility check:

- **`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7` is a reasoning model** that emits a `<think>…</think>` preamble before its JSON answer. Our 400-token budget was consumed entirely by that preamble, so the route failed with `No JSON found in model output`. Raising the budget to 1200 tokens fixed it.
- **`moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6` is listed by GonkaRouter's `/models` endpoint but rejected by `/chat/completions`** with `unsupported model`. Because we'd built the consensus call on `Promise.allSettled` with a persisted row per model (including failures), this upstream inconsistency degraded gracefully to a clean "2 of 3 models responded" instead of taking down the whole check. The partial-failure handling we designed for turned out to be load-bearing in practice, not just theory.

### Supabase mirror drifting out of sync after a rejected registration

Our database is a rebuildable read-mirror of chain state, kept current by an event indexer. A verifier rejecting a registration and the household re-registering is a valid flow (the contract releases the household-ID lock on rejection), but it creates a second on-chain object with the same `household_id`. Our mirror had a naive `UNIQUE(household_id)` index, so the indexer's upsert of the new row failed silently (logged, not surfaced), the new reference code was never mirrored, and lookups 404'd. We replaced it with a **partial** unique index (`WHERE status <> 2`, i.e. not-Rejected) that mirrors the contract's own semantics exactly.

### Server-side evidence extraction drowning in page chrome

For the credibility checker, a URL's page text is fetched and stripped to plain text
server-side (no headless browser). Testing against a real Wikipedia article showed the first ~2,600 characters of "extracted text" were navigation, sidebar, and table-of-contents markup — which would have consumed our 6,000-char cap before reaching any real content. We added block-level stripping of `<nav>` / `<header>` / `<footer>` / `<aside>` / `<table>` before the generic tag strip. We also tried a regex to remove specific `<div id="toc">` wrappers and deliberately removed it — regex can't balance nested tags, so it was a correctness risk pretending to be a fix.

**The problem it solves**

Malaysia experiences severe, recurring monsoon flooding nearly every year. When it happens, financial aid needs to move from donors and government budgets to affected households — and today, that process is slow and opaque in ways that are well understood but not well solved:

- **Bureaucratic delay across multiple layers.** Aid moves through several administrative layers before it reaches a household, and each layer adds processing time — real households can wait weeks for funds they need immediately.
- **A gap between PPS and non-PPS victims.** People sheltering in official evacuation centres (Pusat Pemindahan Sementara) are generally easier to register and track. People who don't evacuate to a PPS — staying with relatives, in a partially damaged home, or elsewhere — often fall into a slower, less-defined process.
- **Opacity in fund flow.** Donors and the public generally cannot see, in any verifiable way, that a specific donation actually reached a specific affected household. Trust is asked for, not demonstrated.
- **Duplicate and "ghost" claims.** Without a hard, systemic guarantee that one household can only be paid once, duplicate or fraudulent claims are a structural risk, not just a hypothetical one.
- **Connectivity loss.** The disasters this system is meant to help with often damage the same telecom infrastructure people would need to access a digital wallet or app — a real design constraint, not an edge case.
- **Digital literacy and accessibility.** Elderly and digitally illiterate residents — a real and significant share of affected populations — struggle with typical crypto wallet UX (seed phrases, gas fees, unfamiliar apps).
- **No independent check that a declared disaster zone is real.** Publishing the fund flow on-chain proves money moved correctly *once a zone exists* — but a donor still has to take the relief authority's word for it that a given "disaster zone" corresponds to a real, ongoing event. A convincingly-named fake zone, or a real zone whose severity is inflated, is a scam vector transparency of *fund flow* alone doesn't close.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

- **Real workflow:** donor → transparent on-chain treasury → verified household payout — a genuine treasury + escrow + disbursement pattern (the track names "treasury", "escrow", "payroll" as target ideas).
- **Fast, intuitive UX:** zkLogin login, no wallet install, no gas — a flood-affected household claims aid with a Google account and a printed reference code.
- **Effective Sui use:** sponsored transactions and zkLogin are load-bearing — they directly remove the wallet/gas/literacy barrier that is the core problem — and Programmable Transaction Blocks bundle multi-step actions atomically.
- **Working live demo:** yes (household claim path demoed with the dev-key signer).

**Caveat:** the demo treasury holds **testnet SUI as a documented stand-in for a stablecoin**, not USDC/USDsui. The contract is written generically over `Coin<T>` /
`ReliefTreasury<T>`, so switching to a real stablecoin type is a configuration change, not a rewrite — but at demo time it is SUI. If the track requires an actual stablecoin token in
the demo, treat this as a partial fit.

**AI × SUI**

Sui is the spine of the product, not an add-on:

Identity: zkLogin turns a Google login into the household's own Sui address — the login is the wallet.
Payments: a shared on-chain treasury funds fixed-tier payouts; sponsored transactions mean no user ever holds SUI.
On-chain execution: the Move contract enforces one-household-one-payout, per-zone budget caps, and "only the household's own login can set its payout address" — as code, not policy.
AI's role: GonkaRouter assists the humans who operate the system — triaging ambiguous registrations, drafting bulk registrations, and running the multi-model zone credibility check. It advises; a human always makes the funds-moving decision.

**AI For Society**

We meet every mandatory requirement and most of the preferred "fact checker" criteria.

| Requirement | How MySteadyAid meets it |
|---|---|
| **Mandatory — all AI reasoning via gonkarouter.io** | Every AI call (verifier triage, bulk-registration drafting, and the zone credibility checker) runs server-side through GonkaRouter exclusively. No other inference provider anywhere. |
| Input a URL or text | The zone credibility checker takes either a source URL (fetched + extracted to plain text server-side) or pasted text. |
| Multi-model cross-verification (≥2 models encouraged) | **3 models run in parallel** on every credibility check. |
| Truth Score (0–100%) + reasoning trace | A 0–100 Evidence Credibility Score plus a per-model reasoning summary that is *required* to cite the specific evidence phrase it relied on. |
| Consensus logic for disagreement ("a major plus") | Deterministic, non-AI resolution: when models disagree, the **most cautious label wins** (any `inconsistent` outranks any `well-supported`), and the UI states plainly that the models differed. |
| Display Gonka Request IDs ("on-chain proof") | Every per-model result — successes **and** failures — is persisted and displayed with its own Gonka Request ID, on both the admin console and the public dashboard. |
| Neutrality prompt | Each model is instructed to judge only from the provided text, to treat missing evidence as `insufficient-evidence` (explicitly *not* an accusation of fraud), and to cite concrete facts. |

**On "on-chain Truth Score":** our score lives in Supabase, not on Sui. The track's concrete stated requirement — *display the Gonka Request ID to prove the result wasn't generated by a centralized server* — is met. Writing the score as a Move event is a documented, deferred enhancement (it moves no funds, and the Request-ID trail already makes every verdict auditable).

**On scope:** GonkaRouter's models have no internet access, so we don't claim autonomous fact-checking. We built an honest **evidence credibility review** — the app supplies the evidence text, the models judge whether it specifically and consistently supports the zone's claims. That is a narrower, defensible claim that plays directly to the track's "fully traceable reasoning trail" ask: a judge can read the exact text every model saw.

### RemitGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/remitguard-0861) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AIHunter109/MUBA_2026.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://muba2026.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Send money home, without the middleman.

![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![sui sdk](https://img.shields.io/badge/sui%20sdk-333333?style=flat-square) ![GonkaRouter](https://img.shields.io/badge/GonkaRouter-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

- Mobile Compatibility: Initially we targeted full web-hosted development but hit compatibility issues with mobile devices such as Android and iOS environments. Attempting to run as web-app on Android or iOS causes it to crash. To solve this, we pivoted to building and bundling actual APK binaries using Expo Application Services (EAS Build), ensuring native execution directly on target devices rather than relying on a wrapper.

- Google OAuth Redirect: Initializing Google Sign-In to implement SUI zklogin caused URI mismatch errors the moment we moved away from localhost. we resolved this by explicitly configuring authorized origins and callbacks URIs in the Google Cloud Console for both our production web domain and backend endpoints

**The problem it solves**

Foreign workers and international students in Malaysia routinely send part of their earnings home, or receive support money from family abroad: "every month I need to send Mum 150 USDC", "this month send an extra 30 for school fees". This recurring task is harder than it should be:

- It is expensive and slow. The global average remittance cost is around 6.4% of the amount sent; banks specifically average closer to 15%. Cross-border rails are also slow to settle.

- It is easy to lose track of. Repeated transfers to several recipients, changing amounts, and one-off payments (fees, emergencies) pile up with no single view.

- It is a prime target for scams. "Urgent family emergency, send money now" social engineering preys specifically on people who send money to relatives. A person mid-transfer is exactly the wrong moment to be unprotected.

Existing apps solve the sending but not the judgement - nothing sits between "I got a worrying message" and "the money is gone".

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

RemitGuard AI is a cross-border family-remittance app: foreign workers and students in Malaysia use it to send and receive support money as USDC on Sui. It covers the full money-movement workflow the track asks for sending (a plain-language instruction or a manual entry becomes a reviewed transaction), receiving (incoming transfers are detected directly on-chain and shown in history, even when sent from an outside wallet), managing (recipient book, sent/received history, spending breakdown, budget planner), and automating (recurring rules with a duplicate-payment reconciliation check). It leans on the exact Sui features listed: zkLogin gives every user a self-custodial wallet from a Google sign-in with no seed phrase, every transfer is a Programmable Transaction Block built by the backend, and sponsored transactions mean the user never pays gas. The UX is a chat: you say "send Mum 150 USDC for school fees" and confirm. The whole thing runs live on web and a native Android build from one codebase. The AI scam-check layer is what makes it real-world-ready rather than just another payments demo: remittance is one of the most scammed transaction types, and RemitGuard is the only step that sits between "I got a worrying message" and "the money is gone."

**AI × SUI**

RemitGuard is a transaction-execution assistant. You describe a payment in natural language; two AI models parse and cross-check it; deterministic code resolves the recipient, runs the risk checks, and builds the plan; and only after you confirm does Sui execute it. Sui is integral, not an add-on, for three concrete reasons. First, no bank API lets third-party software let alone an AI agent construct and submit a payment on a user's behalf without a licensed fintech partnership; on Sui that is a PTB the backend builds directly, so the agent can genuinely act. Second, the architecture is enforced on-chain: the AI never signs anything, and the server-side confirmation token is cryptographically bound to a hash of the exact transaction bytes, so a model response alone can never move money. Third, every transfer and every fact-check verdict is independently verifiable on a public Sui explorer, so a parent or auditor doesn't have to trust our backend's word. It uses zkLogin for identity, USDC PTBs for payments, sponsored transactions for gas, and a Move package for the on-chain verification record. The AI solves a real problem, remittance friction and scam exposure. The demo is live on two platforms.

**AI For Society**

RemitGuard contains a full AI Fact Checker that meets the preferred spec point for point, and it is the mandatory kind of integration: every piece of AI reasoning in the product runs through Gonka Router and nothing else, via a single client. You can paste any claim, headline, tweet, or URL text into the standalone checker and get multi-model cross-verification. Two different Gonka models (DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiniMax M2.7) each read the same evidence and give an independent stance A Truth Score from 0 to 100, a full reasoning trace showing each model's rationale and the article it cited, and the Gonka Request ID for every inference call displayed in the UI as proof the reasoning ran on the network and was not fabricated by our server. Crucially, the models never answer from memory: the checker first retrieves real news through NewsAPI, and if there is no coverage the verdict is "unverifiable". It never guesses. A deterministic combiner, not another model, turns the two stances into the verdict, and disagreement is surfaced rather than averaged. Each verdict is also recorded as a hash-only event on Sui for an auditable public trail. The genuine public value is the deployment context: this checker fires at the exact moment a false "family emergency" claim would otherwise cost someone their savings.

### MandateAgent
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mandateagent-59fd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Jens0343/MandateAgent) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/g0N4CjYk9Hs) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/g0N4CjYk9Hs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI proposes. Policy constrains. Base settles.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Keeping live options quotes valid
Thetanuts orders can change or disappear between market analysis and wallet confirmation. We addressed this by refreshing the selected order immediately before execution. The transaction is rejected if its premium, strikes, expiry, quantity, venue, or contract differs from the approved proposal.
Making AI safe enough for wallet actions
AI recommendations are probabilistic, while financial limits must be deterministic. We separated the AI committee from the policy engine. Agents can recommend a strategy, but they cannot increase the budget, approve an unverified contract, bypass the verifier, ignore an expired mandate, or disable the emergency stop.
Preventing duplicate spending
Manual MetaMask execution and autonomous execution could attempt to use the same mandate budget concurrently. We introduced atomic budget reservations and idempotency keys. Pending, submitted, and confirmed transactions all count toward the cumulative spending ceiling.
Explaining what the agents are doing
An early interface only showed that the committee was “waiting,” which made it difficult to understand its progress. We added named agent stages, current tasks, completion percentages, evidence summaries, sources, timestamps, reliability labels, and verifier conclusions.
Handling incomplete data and unavailable liquidity
News services, model providers, market APIs, and OptionBook liquidity can fail independently. Each source is time-bounded and scored for freshness and reliability. Missing evidence, model disagreement, or a lack of qualifying liquidity produces HOLD instead of a fabricated trade opportunity.
Building reliable transaction tracking
A transaction request can time out even when it was submitted successfully, so blindly retrying could create a duplicate trade. MandateAgent stores transaction hashes and reconciles receipts before deciding whether another submission is safe. Every lifecycle change is written to an append-only execution ledger.
Integrating changing on-chain SDKs
Thetanuts orders use signed structures, contract-specific units, and live allowlists. We used the official client for discovery, previews, and calldata encoding, normalized token decimals explicitly, and kept OptionFactory settlement fail-closed until its production parameters can be independently verified.

**The problem it solves**

Trading on-chain options requires users to complete several complex tasks at the same time: understand market conditions, compare strategies, find live liquidity, calculate potential loss, verify contract details, manage token approvals, and submit a transaction before the quote expires.
MandateAgent makes this workflow easier and safer by:
- Turning a natural-language trading objective into clear, reviewable rules, including strategy type, expiry range, spending limit, maximum fills, and prohibited actions.
- Combining live ETH prices, volatility indicators, market news, public on-chain activity, and Thetanuts liquidity in one command center.
- Using a committee of specialist AI agents to research the market, recommend a strategy, and independently verify the recommendation.
- Showing evidence sources, confidence scores, payoff outcomes, policy checks, and agent progress so users understand exactly what they are approving.
- Enforcing deterministic safety controls that AI cannot override, including a maximum 25 USDC cumulative budget, quote freshness, contract allowlists, strike ordering, wallet balances, and an emergency stop.
- Preparing live Thetanuts OptionBook transactions on Base mainnet through MetaMask, with a bounded Coinbase CDP wallet path for autonomous execution.
- Recording every prepared, submitted, confirmed, failed, or cancelled execution in an auditable trade ledger.
If the evidence is unreliable, the quote is stale, liquidity is unavailable, or any rule fails, MandateAgent returns HOLD and refuses to prepare the transaction.

**AI × OPTIONS**

MandateAgent combines AI decision-making with decentralized options on Base. Users describe their ETH exposure, risk tolerance, budget, and mandate duration in natural language. A committee of specialist agents then:

Collects cited market evidence.

Measures ETH momentum and realized volatility.

Searches Thetanuts OptionBook for live options liquidity.

Selects a suitable strategy, such as an ETH put debit spread.

Sends the recommendation to an independent AI verifier.

Applies deterministic risk checks before preparing the transaction.

Supports signing through MetaMask or bounded automation with a Coinbase CDP wallet.

The AI can propose a trade, but it cannot override the user’s budget, approved strategy, expiry range, contract allowlist, fill limit, or emergency stop. The execution flow uses live Thetanuts pricing and prepares OptionBook transactions for settlement on Base mainnet.

**AI For Society**

MandateAgent uses GonkaRouter as the inference layer for a multi-agent ETH options risk committee. Specialist agents analyze cited evidence, live market conditions, historical momentum, and realized volatility. A Strategy Head combines these findings into a BUY PUT, SELL PUT, or HOLD recommendation, while an independent Verifier recalculates the decision and challenges unsupported assumptions.

GonkaRouter enables MandateAgent to separate research, strategy selection, and verification into distinct inference stages. Every model response is validated against a strict schema, and unavailable or invalid inference causes the system to fail closed. AI produces the recommendation, while deterministic policy code controls whether a transaction may proceed.

> Dual AI Public Fact-Checking & Phishing Guard

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### The Hurdle: Dual-Engine Latency Bottlenecks & Node Timeouts

Because CivicPulse relies on a parallel cross-audit pipeline querying two distinct models on the Gonka network (DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M2.7), our total response time was fundamentally bottlenecked by the slowest responding node. During peak network loads or decentralized cold starts, one engine would occasionally hang or take 6+ seconds, causing frontend request timeouts and broken consensus calculations.

### How We Overcame It

1. **Parallel Execution via Promise Orchestration:** We refactored the verification pipeline to dispatch both inference requests concurrently rather than sequentially, cutting nominal response latency in half.
2. **Hedged Timeout & Fallback Architecture:** We implemented a strict 3.5-second timeout window per node. If a model fails to return within this threshold, the system automatically triggers a retry against an alternate node or falls back safely rather than hanging indefinitely.
3. **Graceful Degradation:** Instead of failing silently or crashing the client session, the frontend transparently flags the verdict as a partial audit when a node fails to respond, maintaining transparency without giving users false certainties.

📖 **Want to know more?**  
 Check out our comprehensive [`README.md`](./README.md) for full technical specifications, architecture diagrams, and local setup instructions.

**The problem it solves**

### What People Can Use CivicPulse For

CivicPulse acts as a real-time, decentralized digital safety filter against viral misinformation and cyber fraud. Key use cases include:

* **Verifying Private Scams & Phishing Alerts:** Citizens can paste suspicious bank warnings, parcel delivery alerts, or tax notices directly into the app to detect malicious links and phishing attempts before clicking.
* **Debunking Viral Family Chat Rumors:** Users can inspect forwarded WhatsApp/Telegram claims or breaking news headlines to verify their factual accuracy before sharing them further.
* **Instant Peer Education:** Users can generate a clean, visual Share Card with clear safety advice to counter fake news directly in community or group chats.
* **Auditing Digital Claims:** Journalists, researchers, and skeptical users can independently trace every verification back to an auditable decentralized execution ID.

---

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

* **Sub-3-Second Turnaround (vs. Hours or Days):** Traditional fact-checking agencies take hours or days to research and publish editorial debunks. CivicPulse provides instant verification in under 3 seconds, stopping fraud before panic sets in.
* **Reaches Dark Social & Private Channels:** Most existing verification tools only monitor public platforms (like Twitter/X or news feeds). CivicPulse allows users to paste raw private messages directly, bypassing website scrapers and anti-bot firewalls.
* **Removes "Blind Trust" with Multi-AI Consensus:** Instead of relying on a single black-box AI that can hallucinate or exhibit bias, CivicPulse cross-audits claims across two independent models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M2.7). If the models disagree by more than 25 points, the system explicitly flags the uncertainty rather than forcing a misleading answer.
* **Actionable Evidence Over Vague Labels:** Rather than merely labeling a message as "Fake," CivicPulse breaks down specific forensic markers—such as fake lookalike domains, manufactured urgency, and credential-harvesting tactics—making it easy for non-technical users and seniors to understand *why* it is dangerous.
* **Auditable Verification Trail:** Every verification is linked to a Gonka Request ID and stored with an integrity hash, giving users a tamper-evident receipt that proves the verdict was generated transparently and honestly.
* **Zero-Friction Accessibility:** Delivered as a lightweight web app supporting English, Bahasa Melayu, Chinese, and Tamil, with high-contrast options for seniors, ensuring protection is accessible across generations without requiring complex installations.

📖 **Want to know more?**  
 Check out our comprehensive [`README.md`](./README.md) for full technical specifications, architecture diagrams, and local setup instructions.

**AI For Society**

CivicPulse is an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) designed for zero-friction citizen media literacy and fraud protection.

Instead of relying on a single AI model or asking users to trust a centralized authority, CivicPulse routes claims to two independent AI models from different model families running on the decentralized Gonka inference network.

Model 1 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) extracts structural context, impact, and safety advice.
Model 2 (MiniMax-M2.7) independently audits the claim for financial traps, phishing URLs, and manipulative urgency.
If the two models disagree by >25 points, CivicPulse surfaces the score gap explicitly to warn the user. Every verification generates a public Gonka Request ID and node receipt, ensuring that truth verification is auditable, transparent, and decentralized.

### Cekgu
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cekgu-acad) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MUBA-M1KU/Cekgu) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://cekgu-op7lf5dspq-as.a.run.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zFASN69yQr8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Two blind AI readers. One fairer assessment.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Drizzle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Drizzle-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cloud Run](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloud%20Run-333333?style=flat-square) ![TailWindCSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/TailWindCSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hono](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hono-333333?style=flat-square) ![neon](https://img.shields.io/badge/neon-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

A wrong answer key does not cost the person who wrote it. It costs every learner who sat the paper — the ones who understood the material and were marked wrong, and the ones who guessed the setter's intent and were rewarded for it. A question with two defensible options does the same thing more quietly. Both are usually found **after** publication, from a complaint rather than from the paper.

### Who this is for

Educators who write multiple-choice questions again and again: lecturers running weekly practice sets, independent tutors publishing question banks, anyone maintaining items that get reused. They are simultaneously the most exposed to their own defects and the least resourced to catch them.

### Why the existing options do not work

- **Self-review is anchored.** You read the question already knowing the answer you meant to write, which is exactly what makes the second defensible option invisible to you.
- **Asking a colleague to re-solve every item works** — and spends the scarcest resource in any department, another subject expert's time.
- **A single AI chat gives one opaque opinion.** One model agreeing with you is not evidence, and there is nothing behind the answer to check.

### What Cekgu does

Each question goes to **two distinct model families through GonkaRouter with the answer key withheld**, so neither reader can be anchored by it. A fixed rule compares the two readings *with each other* before either is compared with the key, and returns one of five verdicts:

- **Clear** — both verified readings agree with the key
- **Possible Key Error** — both agree with each other, and neither matches the key
- **Possible Ambiguity** — both readings list more than one defensible option
- **Split Opinion** — the two readings differ
- **Unverified** — fewer than two receipt-verified readings, so no verdict is claimed

Every admitted reading carries a Gonka Request ID and a public gateway receipt naming the model that actually served it, so a reviewer can check any claim against the gateway instead of taking ours.

### What it does not claim

Cekgu does not grade, does not certify a paper, and does not change a key. It directs human attention to the few items that warrant a second look, and leaves the decision — and the record of that decision — with the educator.

It is a risk signal for practice assessments, not proof of correctness. Two confident readers who agree are indistinguishable from an unambiguous question, and the public sample record carries a real instance of exactly that: a question written to be ambiguous came back **Clear**. We left it in the demo rather than hiding it.

### Where it goes

The commercial wedge is high-volume, lower-sensitivity work — tutors and lecturers repeatedly publishing practice MCQs, where a defect has real cost but the material is not confidential. That shape is self-serve prosumer SaaS, not an enterprise assessment contract.

**Challenges we ran into**

### The receipt arrived after the answer

GonkaRouter is not an ordinary low-latency API, and our first client assumed it was. In measurement, a completion could arrive **before its public receipt existed** — the receipt followed **664–808 ms** later. A one-shot receipt lookup was therefore rejecting genuine readings as unverifiable.

The client now polls inside a bounded **five-second receipt budget** and **fails closed**: a reading whose receipt never appears never enters a verdict. Bounded rather than unbounded matters, because the case being defended against is a gateway that simply never answers.

### A hedge that amplified the problem it existed to solve

Our first hedge fired below the observed completion floor. Instead of rescuing slow calls it duplicated them, and helped trigger the rate limiting it was meant to survive.

The hedge moved to **45 seconds**, behind a hard **90-second evidence cutoff**. Both the winner and the loser are recorded, so a duplicate is visible in the trail rather than quietly dropped.

### Health filtering that could strand a round

The subtlest one. Removing every recently-failing model family sounds obviously correct, and is wrong: it can leave a single candidate, and one family cannot produce two *distinct* readings. Every item would return Unverified without a second call ever being attempted.

The scheduler now **demotes an unhealthy family rather than dropping it**, so a round always retains enough candidates to pair two distinct readers. A round that still cannot obtain two receipt-verified readings ends as Unverified rather than guessing.

That design earned itself on submission day: the network took one of the three families we had built against offline, and calls to it began returning HTTP 400. Because the rule is two distinct verified readings rather than three, and because the scheduler pairs whatever remains, the product absorbed a change to the model catalogue we did not control.

### Everything that failed is still on the record

The habit underneath all three: **every attempt — failed, duplicated, refused, or admitted — stays visible** in the evidence trail. Showing only the winning call would have been easier, and would have made the receipts worth less. A trail you can only inspect when it flatters us is not a trail.

**AI For Society**

**Every reasoning and verification decision runs through GonkaRouter.** `src/server/gateway/only-gonkarouter.test.ts` fails the build if a provider host appears anywhere else in the codebase. Two narrow exemptions are documented and neither can reach a verdict: OCR of an uploaded image, and phrasing the record assistant's replies from facts the Gonka readers already produced. Neither may import the verdict rule, and the test enforces that too.

**The models answer independently.** Each question is sent to two distinct model families with the educator's answer key withheld. Neither reader sees the key, and neither sees the other's reading. Anchoring is prevented by construction, not by instruction.

**Distinctness is proven, not asserted.** Two readings count as independent only if the public receipts name two different *served* models. We compare the served-model identity recorded in the receipt, not the model we requested — a substituted model is a different reader wearing the requested one's name.

**Gonka Request IDs are displayed beside every reading**, together with the public receipt and the model that actually served the call, including the attempts that failed or timed out. Anyone can open the gateway's public receipts endpoint and check a request ID without an account or an API key.

**No fallback response enters consensus.** A reading without a receipt-verified request ID is not admitted. The system fails closed to Unverified rather than manufacturing agreement out of whatever came back.

**Explicit consensus logic.** Five outcomes, evaluated in a fixed order: Unverified (fewer than two receipt-verified readings), Split Opinion (the readings differ), Possible Ambiguity (both list more than one option), Possible Key Error (both agree, neither matches the key), Clear. Disagreement is surfaced to a human, never averaged away.

**The public web is consulted, and quoted.** Before the readers run, one search fetches pages relevant to the question and shows the same snippets to both of them as background rather than authority. The supplied key is never in the query — searching for the key returns pages that agree with the key. Where a record was checked with retrieval, every page is listed under the readings with a live link and the quoted text; a record checked before retrieval shipped says so on itself rather than leaving the feature looking absent. This is a search API, not a model: `include_answer` is hard-coded false, because a generated answer would be reasoning on a provider that is not the gateway, and a test asserts both that flag and that no generated answer is ever read off the response. Retrieval never blocks a verdict — no key, a timeout or an unreadable reply all return nothing and the round proceeds on the readers alone.

**A score puts a number on it.** The same two readings produce a Truth Score from 0 to 100, computed by a pure function over them: no extra inference call, and no model asked how confident it feels. Where retrieval ran, each reader also reports what the pages did to its own answer, and that folds in as a confidence adjustment rather than a vote — corroboration makes a reading count for more, contradiction for half, and neither can flip a reading into meaning its opposite. A web page must not be able to outrank two receipt-verified readings. **Unverified carries no score at all, never zero**: zero is what two readers agreeing against the key earns, and an item nobody could read has not earned it.

**Three ways in.** A paper can be typed, pasted as a link to a page that already holds the questions, or uploaded as a scan. The link path is reduced to its words by a parser that runs no model; the scan path is the one documented exemption where an image becomes text before any reasoning begins.

**The educator makes and records the final decision.** Cekgu produces a risk signal for practice assessments. It does not grade, certify a question as correct, or prove a question unambiguous — two confident readers who agree are indistinguishable from an unambiguous question, and the public sample record carries a real instance of that. The final call, and the record of who made it, stays with the educator.

The public value is direct: a wrong answer key takes marks from every learner who sits the paper, and the people writing practice papers are the least resourced to catch it.

### Shield
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/shield-47a2) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Zero-cost collars for everyday ETH holders

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Everyday ETH holders keep crypto as savings not as a trade. Today ETH holders face a choice: sell all ETH to avoid a crash (and lose all future upside) or hold ETH and hope risking a large part of ETH holders’ savings overnight with no safety net. Buying insurance‑style protection like a put option can help,. It costs a recurring premium that is wasted most of the time it is not needed just like paying for insurance you never use.

What Shield Does

Shield lets ordinary ETH holders protect ETH holders’ savings from a crash at zero cost. Shield uses an idea from traditional finance called a collar now turned into an easy tool through Thetanuts’ on‑chain options protocol on Base.

Of paying an ongoing premium the user gives up a small amount of extreme upside that the user probably would not have captured anyway. That trade‑off pays for downside protection so the net cost of the whole Shield deal is close to zero.

How People Use It

Describe the goal in English, for example "I have 2 ETH I cannot afford to lose more than 10% and I am fine with capping my gains at 15% this month." No need to understand strike prices, expiries or options terminology.

Shield finds the deal automatically. Shield pulls pricing from Thetanuts’ market makers and calculates the exact floor (protection level) and cap (gains limit) where the cost cancels out to near zero.

See the deal explained in language before committing. "Your range is locked: floor $2,700 cap $3,350. Net cost: $2.”

Confirm and execute. Shield runs a safety check—verifying the contract, approval amount and transaction details—and only executes after confirmation directly on Base mainnet.

Why It Makes This Safer and Easier

No manual options knowledge required. The AI layer translates a plain‑language goal into the trade parameters and a deterministic solver and safety validator double‑check every number before any transaction is signed.

No recurring cost that goes to waste. Unlike insurance protection is funded by the trade itself not by an out‑of‑pocket premium paid every cycle.

No surprise. Forced sales. This is not a loan; there is no bot monitoring ratios. The only outcomes are: stay protected stay unaffected or sell at a price the user explicitly agreed to.

Transparent, on‑chain and verifiable. Every position is backed by collateralized options on Thetanuts not by a promise from a company. Anyone can verify it on Base.

Who It's For

Anyone holding ETH as savings who wants a safety net without becoming an options trader. People who have never touched DeFi derivatives but understand "I do not want to lose more, than X.”

**Challenges we ran into**

The most critical bug: clicking "Process Request" on the Protect page always returned "Failed to interpret goal".

The root cause was subtle. The Gemini API key in .env.local started with AQ. — a malformed key. Valid Gemini API keys start with AIza. Because the route called generateObject() unconditionally, it always threw a 500 with no fallback, leaving users stuck at the very first step.

The fix: We rewrote the API route with a two-tier strategy:

AI parsing is only attempted if a valid AIza... key is present.
A deterministic regex parser runs as the guaranteed fallback — no API key needed.
But even the regex parser had a bug: "protect 2 ETH below $3,900" returned desiredFloorPct: 2 instead of 3900. The generic number regex was greedily matching the ETH size (2) before reaching the floor price. We fixed it by anchoring the size regex to N ETH / N BTC patterns only.

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

Shield is built entirely on the Thetanuts SDK as its core execution layer. The product’s main feature. A zero-cost collar. Is made by combining two Thetanuts primitives: a PUT purchase for protection and a CALL sale for upside. These are executed using client.optionBook.fillOrder with RFQ fallback handled through client.optionFactory. Real-time pricing, from client.mmPricing feeds into a solver. This solver finds the strike pair where the premiums of both legs exactly cancel each other out. So the SDK’s pricing data doesn’t just show value. It actually powers the product’s value.

We also use client.api to discover orders and client.events to track positions all the way through settlement. Since Thetanuts hasn’t yet released a multi-leg collar (client.collar writes are blocked until v12) we currently sequence the two legs safely.. We’re designing for smooth, direct adoption of the atomic module once it ships. This shows we’re not just using the SDK. We’re actively engaged with its roadmap.

On top of this foundation an AI layer. Powered by Gemini. Turns plain-language protection goals into SDK parameters. That means someone who’s never heard of a "strike price" can still set up protection. Shield doesn’t just call the SDK. It builds a self-funding protection product on top of Thetanuts’ composable options primitives.

**The problem it solves**

##

People often struggle to understand medical information because symptoms, medical reports, medicines, and health terminology can be complex and difficult to interpret. Searching online can also lead to confusing, unreliable, or misleading information.

**MediMatrix AI** helps make healthcare information easier to understand and access by providing AI-powered explanations in simple language. Users can use it to:

* Understand symptoms and possible health concerns
*  Get easy-to-understand explanations of medical reports
* Learn about medicines, their common uses, and precautions
* Ask health-related questions through an AI assistant
*  Find relevant and understandable medical information
*  Identify situations where professional medical attention may be important
*  Organize and review personal health information

By simplifying complex medical information and providing structured guidance, MediMatrix AI can help people make more informed decisions, reduce confusion, and prepare better questions for healthcare professionals.

MediMatrix AI is designed for health information and guidance, not for replacing doctors or providing definitive medical diagnoses.

**Challenges we ran into**

##

While developing **MediMatrix AI**, we faced several challenges:

* Ensuring medical information is accurate, reliable, and easy to understand.
* Designing AI responses that are helpful without giving unsafe or misleading medical advice.
* Handling different ways users describe the same symptoms or health concerns.
* Making complex medical reports and terminology understandable to non-medical users.
* Maintaining user privacy and protecting sensitive health-related information.
* Balancing AI functionality with a simple, fast, and user-friendly interface.
* Clearly communicating that the platform provides guidance and does not replace professional medical diagnosis.

**AI For Society**

MediMatrix AI is an AI-powered healthcare assistant that simplifies medical information, helping users understand symptoms, reports, medicines, and health questions through clear and accessible guidance.

### RELIEFCHAIN
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/reliefchain-2722) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Riju79/relief-chain) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://relief-chain-cyan.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zmKse7QxKLk?si=Nv8RRjgtxEU4_33P) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> REBUILDING HUMINITY THROUGH RELIEFCHAIN

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![move](https://img.shields.io/badge/move-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building ReliefChain as a genuinely Web3-native disaster-relief protocol came with several challenges — especially around making **on-chain funds, verification logic, and decentralized evidence work together reliably.**

### 1. Designing Non-Custodial Fund Management

One of our biggest challenges was ensuring that donated funds were **not simply transferred to a campaign creator's wallet**.

We redesigned the flow around a Move smart-contract treasury where donations remain controlled by the protocol. Instead of relying on the frontend to enforce rules, the Move contract becomes the source of truth for:

**Donation → Campaign Treasury → Milestone Verification → Fund Release**

This forced us to think carefully about authorization, object ownership, treasury accounting, and preventing unauthorized withdrawals.

### 2. Connecting On-Chain State With the Frontend

Another hurdle was keeping the frontend synchronized with blockchain state.

Initially, some UI state could become stale after transactions or page refreshes. We moved toward treating **Sui as the source of truth**, fetching campaign and transaction state from the blockchain rather than relying on temporary frontend state.

This was especially important for ensuring that campaigns and donation history remain verifiable after a refresh.

### 3. Wallet & Transaction Handling

Wallet integration introduced another layer of complexity.

Transaction signing, gas management, network configuration, wallet connection state, and transaction confirmation all had to work together. A transaction could be successfully submitted while the frontend was still waiting for confirmation or displaying stale information.

We addressed this by improving transaction lifecycle handling:

`Connect → Build Transaction → Sign → Execute → Confirm → Refresh On-Chain State`

This made the application much more resilient to delayed confirmations and RPC responses.

### 4. Making Relief Evidence Verifiable

Disaster-relief evidence can include large files such as photographs, invoices, delivery manifests, and reports. Storing everything directly on-chain would be inefficient and expensive.

We therefore separated the architecture into two layers:

**Sui = Financial & Verification Layer**
**Decentralized Storage = Evidence Layer**

Instead of putting large files on-chain, the system stores the evidence off-chain in decentralized storage and anchors its identifier/hash to the corresponding on-chain milestone.

This gives us the scalability of decentralized storage while preserving a verifiable connection between **evidence and fund releases.**

### 5. Designing for Real-World Failure

A disaster-relief application cannot assume that every transaction, upload, RPC request, or verification step will succeed.

We added explicit handling for failed transactions, rejected wallet signatures, missing evidence, invalid campaign states, and incomplete milestone flows.

The result is a system where failures are treated as expected protocol states rather than silent frontend errors.

### 💡 Biggest Lesson

The hardest part wasn't simply putting a donation button on a blockchain.

It was designing the system so that **money, evidence, permissions, and verification all share the same source of truth.**

That led us to our core design principle:

> **The frontend can display the truth — but the smart contract must enforce it.**

**The problem it solves**

**## 🌍 The Problem It Solves

When disaster strikes, **people donate fast — but accountability moves slowly.**

Traditional disaster-relief funding relies on banks, crowdfunding platforms, organizations, spreadsheets, and centralized databases. Donors often have no way to independently verify:

* **Where their money went**
* **Who received it**
* **What it was spent on**
* **Whether the reported relief actually happened**

This creates a fundamental problem:

> **You can trust the intention of a donation without being able to verify its journey.**

ReliefChain changes that by turning disaster relief into a **transparent, programmable, and auditable on-chain process.**

### 🚨 What ReliefChain Enables

**For Donors**

Donate directly through Sui and follow the movement of funds on-chain — from the campaign treasury to verified relief milestones.

**For Relief Organizations**

Create structured campaigns with defined funding milestones such as:

`Emergency Supplies → Medical Aid → Food Distribution → Reconstruction`

Funds are managed by Move smart contracts rather than being immediately handed to a campaign creator.

**For Verifiers**

Authorized verifiers can review submitted relief evidence and approve milestone-based fund releases, creating an additional accountability layer between donations and spending.

**For Auditors & the Public**

Every important financial action can be independently inspected on-chain, creating a permanent and transparent audit trail.

### 🔐 Making Disaster Relief Safer

| Traditional Relief                        | ReliefChain                                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Trust the organization to report spending | **Verify transactions on-chain**                      |
| Funds controlled by intermediaries        | **Funds governed by Move smart contracts**            |
| Manual milestone tracking                 | **Programmable milestone-based releases**             |
| Centralized records                       | **Public blockchain audit trail**                     |
| Difficult to trace donations              | **Trackable fund flow from donation to disbursement** |
| Evidence disconnected from payments       | **Relief evidence linked to on-chain milestones**     |

### ⚡ The Core Idea

**ReliefChain separates *trust* from *transparency*.**

Instead of asking donors to simply believe that their donation reached the right place, the protocol makes the financial journey **cryptographically verifiable**.

**Donate → Verify → Release → Audit**

The result is a disaster-relief system designed to make humanitarian funding **more transparent, accountable, and programmable.**

> **Don't just donate. Know where your relief goes.****

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

## 💸 How ReliefChain Fits the Payments & Stablecoin Track

ReliefChain applies blockchain payments to one of the most important real-world payment problems: **getting humanitarian money to the right people quickly, transparently, and with less dependence on intermediaries.**

Today, international disaster relief can involve multiple payment processors, banks, organizations, and manual reconciliation steps. ReliefChain turns this process into a **programmable payment flow secured by smart contracts.**

### 🌍 Stablecoins as the Humanitarian Payment Rail

While SUI can be used for native on-chain payments, the protocol is designed to support **stablecoin-based humanitarian funding** as the ecosystem evolves.

A stablecoin such as a USD-pegged asset can provide a predictable unit of account for:

* International donations
* NGO and relief-organization funding
* Contractor payments
* Medical and emergency-supply procurement
* Cross-border humanitarian disbursements

This is particularly useful when donors and relief providers operate across different currencies and financial systems.

### 🔄 From Donation to Real-World Payment

ReliefChain transforms a donation into a programmable payment lifecycle:

**Donor → Campaign Treasury → Verified Milestone → Relief Provider → On-Chain Settlement**

Instead of releasing an entire campaign balance upfront, funds can be tied to predefined milestones.

For example:

> **$10,000 stablecoin campaign**
>
> → $3,000 for emergency food & water
> → $2,500 for medical supplies
> → $2,000 for temporary shelter
> → $2,500 for reconstruction

Each payment can be governed by the campaign's smart-contract rules and released when the corresponding milestone is approved.

### 🔐 Why Blockchain Payments Matter Here

ReliefChain combines **payments + programmable money + verification**.

Traditional payment systems answer:

> **“Did the payment happen?”**

ReliefChain aims to additionally answer:

> **“Why was the payment released, who authorized it, where did it go, and which relief milestone did it fund?”**

Because the financial activity is recorded on-chain, donors, verifiers, and auditors can independently inspect the payment trail.

### 🚀 Why This Belongs in the Stablecoin Track

Stablecoins make the model particularly powerful for **cross-border disaster response**.

A donor in one country can fund a relief campaign while a verified organization or contractor in another country receives a blockchain-native payment — without requiring the entire payment flow to depend on traditional correspondent banking infrastructure.

The long-term vision is:

**Global donations → Stablecoin settlement → Programmable escrow → Verified milestone → Direct humanitarian payment**

ReliefChain therefore isn't simply using crypto as a donation method.

**It is exploring how stablecoins can become programmable infrastructure for faster, more transparent humanitarian payments.**

### TrustFlow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trustflow-6a46) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AyushPaul26/TRUSTFLOW) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RBy8Vhepc68) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Milestone escrow powered by AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prisma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prisma-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fastify](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fastify-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

AI Hallucinations in Contract Terms: The language model initially assumed missing details, such as fabricating wallet addresses or guessing review deadlines. We resolved this by constraining the AI strictly to data structuring, adding a deterministic Zod validation layer, and introducing an explicit "Help us fill in the gaps" step for mandatory human input.  Upstream AI Outages & Timeouts: Live API calls to the LLM backend occasionally timed out or returned unexpected formats. We fixed this by saving raw terms as local drafts first and adding a fallback manual entry path that enforces the same strict validation rules.  Balancing Privacy with On-Chain Integrity: Writing plain-text contracts and evidence to the blockchain would expose private business data and increase costs. We implemented a hybrid architecture where sensitive records remain off-chain in PostgreSQL, while only an immutable SHA-256 agreement hash and coordination anchors interact with Sui.  Escrow Math & State Safety in Move: Ensuring locked funds could never be double-spent across multi-milestone lifecycles or disputes required rigid accounting. We built and verified 18 Move unit tests to strictly enforce single-release invariant checks and freeze disputed milestones until resolved.  Mobile Key Management: Exposing private keys or burdening users with seed phrases undermines mobile security and UX. We decoupled custody by leveraging native Google sign-in with Enoki nonces, generating unsigned transaction builders locally, and never storing keys on the backend.

**The problem it solves**

In freelance and service-based work, trust frequently breaks down before any payment actually occurs because informal communication over chat, email, or calls leaves payment conditions, deliverables, and revision rules open to conflicting interpretations. This creates a stalemate where clients risk losing their money by paying upfront for incomplete or substandard work, while contractors risk working without compensation if payment is withheld. Without a shared, objective source of truth, vague agreements inevitably result in payment friction, stalled projects, and contentious disputes. TrustFlow resolves this dilemma by bridging casual conversational terms into deterministic, milestone-structured agreements backed by non-custodial smart contracts, protecting both parties with clear review windows, objective evidence requirements, and controlled fund releases.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

TrustFlow integrates Sui’s payment infrastructure through a dedicated PaymentFlow Move smart contract that operates as an autonomous, non-custodial escrow using native SUI tokens scaled to nine decimal places. When an agreement is finalized, the client locks the full project deposit into the contract via create_flow, ensuring funds cannot be withdrawn arbitrarily once the contractor accepts. The contract coordinates sequential milestone progression: funds are released either through explicit client approval or automatically claimed by the contractor via claim_after_review if the client fails to review the work before the deadline expires. If a dispute arises, the milestone freezes until an authorized resolver determines a precise fund split, backed by strict invariant math ensuring no locked balance can ever be released twice. On the client side, the Android application binds user identities using Enoki and constructs unsigned Sui transaction builders locally, keeping private key custody and execution authority entirely in the user's hands rather than on the backend.

Team **Ironclad** -- [Chandan Koley](https://github.com/ELITECROWN), [Ayush Paul](https://github.com/AyushPaul26)

**Challenges we ran into**

Resume Data Extraction: PDF aur DOCX resumes ka content different formats mein hota hai, isliye resume se accurate text aur relevant skills extract karna challenging tha.
Accurate Skill Identification: Resume mein explicitly mention na ki gayi skills ko identify karna aur technical skills ko properly categorize karna difficult tha.
AI-Based Evaluation: Gemini AI se meaningful strengths, weaknesses aur career recommendations generate karwana challenging tha, especially because AI output ko relevant aur consistent rakhna zaroori tha.
Career Matching: User ke skills ko suitable job roles ke saath accurately match karna aur meaningful match percentages provide karna ek major challenge tha.
Personalized Roadmap Generation: Har user ke skill gaps ke according customized learning roadmap generate karna challenging tha, instead of providing the same roadmap to everyone.
Frontend–Backend Integration: HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend ko Flask backend, AI services aur database ke saath properly integrate karna debugging aur API handling ke perspective se challenging tha.
Database Management: Users, resumes, analysis reports, jobs, required skills, roadmaps aur progress ko relational database mein properly connect aur manage karna challenging tha.
Progress Tracking: User ke completed roadmap steps ko accurately store karna aur dashboard par real-time progress reflect karna additional implementation challenge tha.
AI Response Reliability: AI-generated responses kabhi-kabhi inconsistent ya unexpected format mein aa sakte hain, isliye responses ko handle aur validate karna important tha.
Security & File Handling: Resume uploads ko securely handle karna, supported file types validate karna aur sensitive user/resume data ko safely manage karna bhi challenging tha.

> Blockchain based land verification

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![POSTGIS](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSTGIS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prism.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prism.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges we Ran Into

One of the main challenges we faced was making sure a land record could not be added or updated without proper verification. We had to connect the user’s land details, map location, admin approval, OTP authentication, and blockchain transaction into one flow.
We also faced issues while checking whether a newly submitted land record already existed. A survey number alone was not always enough, so we added checks against previous records and land boundaries shown on the map.
To solve these problems, we divided the process into separate steps: **user submission → admin validation → OTP confirmation → blockchain update**. We also kept detailed land information in the database while storing its hash and transaction details on the blockchain. This made the system easier to manage while still maintaining a tamper-evident record.

**The problem it solves**

Land records are still difficult to verify in many situations. A person may have the correct documents, but it can be hard to know whether the land has already been registered under someone else, whether the records have been changed, or whether the actual land boundary matches the submitted details.
This can lead to duplicate registrations, ownership disputes, fraudulent transactions, and lengthy manual verification processes.
Our project aims to make land verification faster, more transparent, and easier to trust by combining digital land records, map-based verification, OTP authentication, and blockchain-based history.

> "Turn Any Dream Career into an Unstoppable Daily E

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an autonomous multi-agent career transformation platform with real-time 3D graphics, psychological gamification, and instant dynamic roadmaps came with significant full-stack engineering hurdles:

1. Server-Client Boundary Leaks & Vercel Hydration Crashes
The Hurdle: Our execution protocol engine worked seamlessly on localhost but threw client-side runtime error boundaries on Vercel production.
The Investigation: A "use client" component imported curriculum helpers from our agent pipeline (deployer.ts), which pulled server-only Node.js dependencies (OpenRouter, OpenAI SDK, crypto, and private environment variables) into the client bundle.
The Solution: We cleanly decoupled the architecture by building a pure TypeScript, zero-dependency engine (curriculumGenerator.ts) using strict import type definitions. We also added an autonomous client-side synthesis guard that dynamically reconstructs missing curricula on direct tab refreshes without network bottlenecks.
2. Three.js Matrix Projections & 3D Orbit Physics Tuning
The Hurdle: In the 3D Holographic Growth Timeline, DOM cards warped into awkward aspect ratios on viewport resizing, and the 3D cylinder orbit suffered from aggressive damping and jittery physics.
The Investigation: Three.js <Html transform> non-linearly scaled DOM projection matrices across dynamic screen dimensions, while vertical bobbing frequency (1.5x) was too fast for readable typography.
The Solution: We normalized camera optics (fov: 46, cameraZ: 9.6, distance factor 5.0) to lock fixed card dimensions (320px × 460px). We re-engineered the damping physics to a silky-smooth inertia factor (3.2) with a calm floating frequency (0.35), and added on-canvas step navigation for 1-click milestone centering.
3. Eliminating AI Latency in Visual Roadmap Generation
The Hurdle: Relying on real-time remote image diffusion models caused 3–7 second latency spikes, leaving empty placeholder boxes and blocking fast PDF exports.
The Solution: We engineered a dual-layer rendering pipeline. We built an instant (<1ms) high-resolution Vector SVG Blueprint Engine that renders structured 3-step milestones with glowing obsidian-neon themes directly from client memory. Remote AI visuals preload in the background and smoothly cross-fade into view without ever blocking user interaction or PDF generation.
4. Deep State Null-Safety Across Multi-Year Timelines
The Hurdle: Uninitialized local storage states or varied user inputs (6_weeks to 10_years) caused runtime NaN calculations and unhandled null property exceptions.
The Solution: We implemented an effectiveState proxy pattern that guarantees complete fallback to validated demo schemas, paired with a comprehensive mapping table covering all duration horizons. We also wrapped all 3D canvas subsystems in React <Suspense> boundaries to ensure WebGL context loss never crashes the application.

**The problem it solves**

1. The Core Problem: The Execution Void
Most people have ambitious dream careers (e.g., Trader, AI Engineer, Creator, Founder), but fail because of two fatal bottlenecks:

Analysis Paralysis: They don't know the exact, day-by-day sequence of tasks and tools needed to transition from their current baseline.
Procrastination & Zero Accountability: Motivation fades after a few days without an active pressure system to keep them consistent.
2. How VibeForge Solves It (The 3 Pillars):
🎯 100% Tailored Execution Protocol Takes your exact starting point (e.g., Student in Kolkata) and goal (Full-time Trader), delivering a week-by-week curriculum with practical deliverables and verified top-rated video guides.

⚔️ Psychological Rival & Ego-Hurt Engine Pits you against a relentless AI adversary who is outpacing you. It triggers competitive urgency through live taunts, 25-minute focus sprints, and pace-lead counters that eliminate laziness.

📊 Visual Multi-Dimensional Blueprints Transforms abstract career growth into tangible 2D/3D visual roadmap holograms and instant printable protocols so you always know your exact progress and upcoming milestones.

### METER
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meter-d2b8) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://meter402.netlify.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Tq3qvdxQ_S0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Dora%20Hack%202.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dora-hack.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> An API that charges per call, not per month.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part wasn't the payment logic: it was that x402 is new enough that two incompatible versions were in circulation at the same time, and the docs hadn't caught up.

My endpoint was correctly returning 402 with payment requirements, but the client couldn't generate a signature. The only error I got was Cannot convert undefined to a BigInt:  which doesn't tell you which field is missing or why.

**The problem it solves**

Every API is sold by the month, and that's not a product choice it's a payments. Card networks charge ~$0.30 in fixed fees per transaction. A single LLM call costs $0.000037. You cannot sell that on card rails, so it gets bundled into a subscription instead.

**The result:** a developer who needs five API calls has to create an account, hand over a card, and commit to a month. An AI agent, which can do none of those things, is locked out entirely.

**METER** makes the API pay for itself, mid-request. The client sends a request with no credentials. The server responds **402 Payment Required** with a price. The wallet signs a USDC authorization, the request retries, and settlement happens onchain about one second, end to end.

What this enables:
**Pay for what you use :** five calls costs five calls, not a month
**No signup, no API key :** nothing to issue, rotate, or leak
**No card required :** works for developers who can't easily get international cards, which is a real barrier in India
**Agents can buy things : **an autonomous client can't fill in a signup form, but it can sign a payment inside an HTTP request

Why it's safer: there's no stored credential to steal. Each payment is a single-use signature, scoped to one amount, one recipient, with an expiry.

Built on the x402 protocol, running on Base Sepolia.
