![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves
Today's voice assistants — Alexa, Google Home, Siri — only work when the internet works. The moment your Wi-Fi drops (still common across much of India), they can't even switch off a light. They're also expensive (₹4,000+) and send everything you say to the cloud, raising real privacy concerns. And the people who could benefit most — elders, non-English speakers, and homes with weak connectivity — are often the ones left out.
TecnoVoice fixes this. It's a hybrid assistant that stays useful with or without the internet: when connected, it answers questions intelligently in your own language; when offline, it still controls your home appliances instantly and locally.
What people can use it for

🏠 Smart home control — turn lights, fans and appliances on/off by voice, even during an internet outage.
🗣️ Speak in your own language — Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati and more, including mixed speech, so non-English speakers and elders aren't excluded.
🏥 Hands-free help — useful in hospitals and for people with limited mobility who can't reach switches.
🏫 Learning & everyday Q&A — ask general-knowledge questions; great for students and curious minds.
🌾 Rural & low-connectivity homes — works where cloud-only assistants simply fail.

How it makes things easier and safer

✅ Reliable — core controls never depend on the internet, so there's no single point of failure.
🔐 Private — offline commands never leave your home; the cloud is used only when you choose to ask something.
💸 Affordable — roughly half the cost of commercial assistants (₹1,800–2,200).
♿ Accessible — voice-first design helps elders, the visually impaired, and anyone who finds apps or switches hard to use.

**Challenges we ran into**

Yeh field hackathon submission ka common part hai — isme bataana hota hai ki banate waqt kya-kya mushkilein aayi. Maine tumhare actual project ke hisaab se honest aur real-sounding likha hai (markdown ke saath). Copy karke paste kar do 👇

Challenges I ran into
Making offline and online work as one system. The hardest part wasn't either mode on its own — it was getting them to hand off cleanly. Building the "decision layer" that senses connectivity and routes each request to the right brain (cloud AI vs. local control) without the user noticing took a lot of trial and error.
Connecting the AI APIs as first-time builders. Most of us hadn't wired up real APIs before, so getting Sarvam and Gemini keys, building a backend to call them, and parsing the responses was a steep learning curve. We also hit CORS restrictions trying to call Sarvam straight from the browser, which pushed us to route those calls through our own server instead.
Multi-language voice recognition. Real people don't speak in clean, single-language sentences — they mix Hindi and English, like "light band karo please." Getting commands recognised reliably across several Indian languages, without misfiring on similar-sounding words, needed a lot of tuning.
Wi-Fi reliability on the ESP32. Since the whole point is to survive bad connectivity, we had to handle drops and reconnections gracefully so the device falls back to offline mode instead of freezing.
Switching 220V appliances safely. Controlling real mains appliances meant being very careful with the relay wiring and isolation. Getting hardware to switch high voltage reliably — and safely — was nerve-wracking the first few times.
Keeping it affordable. Every component was a balance between capability and cost, because the goal was a device far cheaper than commercial assistants without dropping the features that actually matter.

**Sarvam.ai**

TecnoVoice is, at its core, an embedded systems and IoT project. The entire system runs on an ESP32 microcontroller that handles real-time audio capture, on-device processing, and network communication. Voice is captured through an I2S MEMS microphone (INMP441) and played back through an I2S amplifier (MAX98357A) and speaker, while a 0.96" OLED shows live device status — all driven by custom firmware written in embedded C/C++.
What makes it a true IoT device is its control over the physical world: the ESP32 drives GPIO pins connected to a relay module that safely switches real 220V appliances like lights and fans on and off. A dedicated offline voice module (Sasi) performs local command recognition, so this physical control works instantly even with no internet — a key reliability feature for embedded deployment in areas with unstable connectivity.
The system is hybrid by design. When connected, the ESP32 streams voice over Wi-Fi to the cloud for AI-powered responses; when offline, it falls back entirely to embedded, on-device control. This blend of microcontroller firmware, sensor and actuator interfacing, relay-based automation, and networked intelligence places TecnoVoice squarely in the IoT and Embedded Systems domain — a low-cost, battery-powered, privacy-friendly smart-home node built from the silicon up.

**The problem it solves**

Modern learners often face challenges while learning new skills, building projects, preparing for interviews, or solving technical problems. Although search engines, tutorials, forums, and AI assistants provide large amounts of information, users frequently struggle to find solutions that fit their specific context.
Many learners spend hours searching across multiple platforms, repeating the same questions, and trying different approaches without success. AI tools can provide guidance, but they may lack the practical experience, domain expertise, and personalized mentorship needed to fully resolve complex or unique situations.
As a result, learners experience frustration, wasted time, slower learning progress, and difficulty finding the right person who can help them move forward.
SkillNow solves this problem by understanding the learner's goals, challenges, context, and previous attempts, then connecting them with the most relevant human expert for personalized assistance and mentorship.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge 1: Extracting meaningful context from webpages
Most webpages contain large amounts of irrelevant information such as navigation menus, advertisements, and repeated content.
Solution:
We built a browser extension that extracts relevant page content and uses AI to identify the user's actual goal, challenge, technologies involved, and required expertise.

Challenge 2: Converting unstructured content into structured tickets
Raw webpage content is difficult to use for expert matching.
Solution:
We integrated Sarvam AI to automatically generate structured support tickets containing problem summaries, root causes, priority levels, and expert requirements.

Challenge 3: Matching Learners with Relevant Experts
Finding the right expert is often more important than finding any expert.
Solution:
We designed a categorization and matching mechanism that uses the extracted context to identify the most suitable experts based on skills and expertise.

**Sarvam.ai**

SkillNow uses Sarvam AI as its intelligence layer for understanding user problems, extracting context, identifying challenges, generating structured tickets, and categorizing expertise requirements.
Sarvam AI enables the platform to process real-world learning problems and convert them into expert-ready support requests, making expert matching significantly more effective.

**Gen AI&ML**

SkillNow uses AI to understand a learner's context, goals, challenges, and previous attempts. Instead of simply answering questions, the AI analyzes the problem, generates a structured support ticket, identifies required expertise, and facilitates expert matching.
The platform leverages Large Language Models to transform unstructured information from webpages, conversations, and learning resources into actionable insights that help learners receive personalized human assistance.

**The problem it solves**

InternX addresses the inefficiencies in traditional internship management by providing a centralized and automated platform for students, mentors, and organizations.

**Challenges we ran into**

Current Challenges
Students miss task deadlines and struggle to track internship progress.
Mentors spend significant time manually assigning tasks and reviewing submissions.
Organizations rely on spreadsheets, emails, and multiple tools to manage internships.
Communication is fragmented, leading to missed updates and confusion.
Certificate generation and distribution are often manual, time-consuming, and error-prone.
There is limited visibility into intern performance and program progress.

**Open Innovation**

InternX fits the Open Innovation track because it addresses a real-world challenge faced by educational institutions, training organizations, companies, mentors, and students. Internship management is often fragmented, relying on spreadsheets, emails, and manual processes, leading to inefficiencies and poor communication. InternX provides an innovative, scalable, and technology-driven solution by centralizing internship management, automating task tracking, email notifications, progress monitoring, and certificate generation on a single platform. The solution can be adopted across multiple industries and educational ecosystems, making internship programs more efficient, transparent, and impactful for all stakeholders.

**The problem it solves**

# Echo

## Decision Blind Spot Detector

**Every decision has blind spots. Echo finds them before they become consequences.**

Built for **ZenysLab HackPrix 2026**, Echo helps organizations identify overlooked stakeholders, hidden consequences, and competing interests before implementing policies or major decisions.

---

## The Problem

Many decisions fail because key stakeholders are unintentionally excluded from the process.

Whether it's a government policy, university rule, workplace change, or community initiative, the people most affected are often the least represented.

---

## The Solution

Echo analyzes proposed policies and answers a simple question:

> **Who did we forget?**

It identifies affected stakeholders, detects blind spots, measures fairness, facilitates stakeholder debates, and generates improved policy recommendations.

---

## Features

* **Stakeholder Discovery**
  Identifies affected and overlooked groups.

* **Blind Spot Detection**
  Highlights hidden risks and unintended consequences.

* **Equity Index**
  Scores policy fairness on a scale of 0–100.

* **AI Stakeholder Debate**
  Simulates realistic debates between conflicting stakeholders.

* **Voice-Based Consultation**
  Converts stakeholder perspectives into natural speech.

* **Policy Improvement Draft**
  Generates a more inclusive version of the original policy.

* **Multilingual Input**
  Supports English, Hindi, and Telugu voice submissions.

* **Blockchain Accountability**
  Records analysis results on Solana for transparency.

---

## Tech Stack

### Frontend

* React Native
* Expo
* TypeScript

### Backend

* Node.js
* Express
* MongoDB

### AI & Automation

* Gemini 2.5 Flash
* Sarvam AI
* ElevenLabs
* n8n

### Infrastructure

* Vultr
* Solana Web3.js

---

## How It Works

1. User submits a policy through text or voice.
2. Echo identifies affected stakeholders.
3. Hidden impacts and blind spots are detected.
4. An Equity Index is calculated.
5. Stakeholders debate competing viewpoints.
6. Debate is converted into realistic voice conversations.
7. Echo generates an improved policy draft.
8. Results can be logged on Solana.

---

## Example

**Policy:** All university classes move fully online.

**Echo identifies:**

* Rural students
* Low-income households
* Disabled students
* Faculty members

**Echo generates:**

* Stakeholder Impact Report
* Equity Index
* AI Stakeholder Debate
* Voice Consultation
* Improved Policy Draft

---

### Gov Nexus AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gov-nexus-ai-add2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sadiya-125/GovNexus-AI) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gov-nexus-ai.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lc0m_VtRGtk?si=DOLMRo5Qg-If0l1q) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Ensuring Every Resource Reaches Where It Matters

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every year, governments, NGOs, and disaster relief agencies manage millions of units of essential resources such as food, medicines, vaccines, sanitation kits, educational materials, and emergency supplies. Despite significant investments, resource distribution remains largely reactive and fragmented.

Many organizations lack real-time visibility into inventory levels across regions, making it difficult to identify shortages before they become critical. Resources are often overstocked in one location while communities in another face urgent shortages. During floods, disease outbreaks, heatwaves, and other emergencies, delayed decision-making and poor coordination can further slow relief efforts and increase human impact.

SmartResource AI addresses these challenges through an AI-powered public resource intelligence platform that predicts future demand, identifies high-risk regions, and recommends optimal resource allocation strategies before shortages occur.

The platform enables governments, NGOs, suppliers, and disaster management authorities to collaborate through a unified system where they can monitor resources, forecast needs, coordinate distribution, and receive real-time alerts.

### What can it be used for?

* Predicting demand for food, medicines, vaccines, drinking water, and relief kits.
* Planning disaster preparedness and emergency resource deployment.
* Detecting shortages, wastage, and inefficient resource utilization.
* Coordinating resource allocation between government departments and NGOs.
* Tracking resource distribution, delivery timelines, and beneficiary coverage.
* Improving transparency and accountability in welfare and relief programs.


By shifting public resource management from reactive decision-making to predictive intelligence, Gov Nexus AI helps ensure that critical supplies reach the right communities at the right time while reducing waste, improving efficiency, and supporting sustainable development goals.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

One of the biggest challenges was building a system capable of generating reliable demand forecasts from highly diverse and inconsistent data sources. Unlike traditional inventory systems, our platform combines historical resource consumption, demographic information, weather indicators, disaster-related data, and stakeholder requests to predict future demand. Integrating these datasets required significant preprocessing, normalization, and feature engineering to ensure meaningful predictions.

Another major challenge was designing an AI pipeline that could produce actionable recommendations rather than just predictions. Forecasting demand is only one part of the problem; the system also needed to identify shortages, detect overstock situations, assess regional risks, and recommend resource transfers. Balancing prediction accuracy with practical decision-making required multiple iterations of our machine learning workflow.

We also faced challenges while integrating real-time communication services. Using Twilio for automated notifications and alerts required handling message delivery reliability, event triggers, and stakeholder-specific notification logic. Ensuring that critical shortage and emergency alerts reached the right users without overwhelming them with unnecessary notifications was a key design challenge.

Integrating Sarvam AI introduced another layer of complexity. We wanted alerts and recommendations to be understandable by a diverse audience, including government officers, NGO workers, and local coordinators. Generating context-aware summaries and multilingual communications required careful prompt engineering and workflow orchestration to maintain both accuracy and clarity.

Scalability was another hurdle. During disaster scenarios, thousands of simultaneous resource requests and updates may occur. To address this, we designed the architecture around centralized data processing, optimized database queries, and modular services that can scale independently as demand grows.

Finally, one of the most challenging aspects was ensuring that recommendations remained explainable. Public-sector decision-making requires transparency, so we focused on generating AI-driven insights that clearly show why a particular allocation, transfer, or alert was recommended instead of treating the AI model as a black box.

**Gemini**

Gov Nexus AI utilizes the Gemini API as the intelligence layer powering its conversational assistant for public resource management. The chatbot enables government officials, NGO workers, suppliers, healthcare agencies, and disaster response teams to interact with complex resource data using natural language instead of navigating multiple dashboards and reports.

Through the Gemini-powered assistant, users can ask questions such as:

* "Which districts are expected to face food shortages next month?"
* "Show regions with the highest medicine demand forecast."
* "What resources should be pre-positioned before an approaching cyclone?"
* "Which warehouses currently have excess inventory available for transfer?"
* "Summarize resource distribution performance for the last quarter."

Gemini processes these queries, analyzes the available data, and generates clear, context-aware responses that help stakeholders make informed decisions quickly. The chatbot can also summarize large datasets, explain AI-generated recommendations, and provide actionable insights in a user-friendly format.

In disaster management and public welfare scenarios, decision-makers often need immediate access to information. Instead of manually searching through reports, users can simply converse with the Gemini-powered assistant to obtain forecasts, risk assessments, resource availability information, and operational recommendations.

By integrating Gemini API, Gov Nexus AI transforms complex public resource data into accessible, conversational intelligence, enabling faster decision-making, improved coordination, and more effective resource allocation for sustainable development initiatives.

**ElevenLabs**

Gov Nexus AI leverages ElevenLabs to power an AI voice agent that enables natural, voice-based interaction with the platform. In public resource management, many stakeholders—including government officers, NGO field workers, healthcare personnel, and disaster response teams—often operate in fast-paced environments where typing reports or navigating dashboards is not practical.

Using ElevenLabs' advanced voice technology, users can communicate with the platform through natural conversations. Field personnel can report shortages, request resources, check inventory status, receive emergency updates, and access AI-generated insights simply by speaking. The voice agent converts complex system interactions into intuitive conversations, reducing response time and improving accessibility.

The ElevenLabs-powered voice agent also delivers critical alerts and recommendations through realistic, human-like speech. During emergencies, users can receive spoken notifications about resource shortages, disaster preparedness actions, delivery updates, and allocation recommendations without needing to constantly monitor a dashboard.

This voice-first approach is especially valuable in disaster response scenarios where rapid communication and hands-free access to information can significantly improve operational efficiency. By integrating ElevenLabs, Gov Nexus AI makes public resource intelligence more accessible, responsive, and user-friendly, ensuring that critical information reaches decision-makers and field workers when they need it most.

**MongoDB**

Gov Nexus AI relies on MongoDB as the central data platform for managing large volumes of dynamic, real-time, and heterogeneous resource management data. The platform collects and processes information from multiple sources, including resource inventories, NGO requests, government records, disaster indicators, weather data, demographic information, distribution logs, and AI-generated forecasts.

MongoDB's flexible document-based architecture enables us to efficiently store and manage diverse data structures without requiring rigid schemas. This is particularly important because different stakeholders—government agencies, NGOs, suppliers, and relief organizations—generate varying types of data that need to be integrated into a single system.

The platform uses MongoDB to:

* Store resource inventory and warehouse information across multiple regions.
* Manage stakeholder profiles, requests, approvals, and allocation workflows.
* Track resource distribution history and delivery records.
* Store AI-generated demand forecasts, risk assessments, and optimization recommendations.
* Maintain real-time status updates for shortages, emergencies, and resource transfers.
* Support analytics dashboards that provide operational and strategic insights.

MongoDB's scalability and high-performance querying capabilities allow Gov Nexus AI to handle increasing volumes of data during large-scale operations and disaster response scenarios. As resource requests, alerts, and monitoring events grow, MongoDB provides the flexibility and reliability needed to maintain real-time visibility across the entire platform.

By using MongoDB as the backbone of our public resource intelligence system, Gov Nexus AI can efficiently manage complex datasets, support AI-driven decision-making, and deliver a scalable solution for sustainable and transparent resource management.

**Sarvam.ai**

Gov Nexus AI leverages Sarvam AI's Speech-to-Text (STT) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities to make public resource management more accessible, inclusive, and efficient for diverse stakeholders.

In real-world scenarios, government officers, NGO workers, field coordinators, healthcare staff, and disaster response teams often operate in environments where typing detailed reports or navigating complex dashboards is inconvenient or impractical. Using Sarvam AI's Speech-to-Text technology, users can submit resource requests, shortage reports, inventory updates, and emergency information through natural voice conversations, reducing friction and improving data collection speed.

The platform also utilizes Sarvam AI's Text-to-Speech capabilities to convert AI-generated insights, shortage alerts, allocation recommendations, and emergency notifications into spoken messages. This enables faster communication, especially for field personnel who may be on the move or operating in high-pressure situations.

Additionally, Sarvam AI's multilingual capabilities help bridge language barriers by allowing stakeholders to interact with the system in their preferred language. This is particularly valuable for large-scale public resource management where multiple regions, communities, and organizations are involved.

By integrating Sarvam AI into the workflow, Gov Nexus AI transforms traditional dashboards into a voice-enabled, multilingual public resource intelligence platform, making critical information more accessible and ensuring that resource management decisions can be communicated quickly and effectively during both routine operations and emergency situations.

**Sustainable Development**

Gov Nexus AI directly addresses one of the core challenges of sustainable development: ensuring that limited public resources are distributed efficiently, equitably, and transparently.

Today, governments, NGOs, healthcare agencies, and disaster management authorities often struggle with resource shortages, overstocking, delayed distribution, and poor coordination. These inefficiencies can lead to food insecurity, reduced access to healthcare supplies, ineffective disaster response, and wastage of valuable public resources.

Our platform uses AI-driven demand forecasting, resource optimization, and stakeholder coordination to ensure that critical resources such as food supplies, medicines, vaccines, educational materials, sanitation kits, and emergency relief equipment reach the communities that need them most.

By reducing waste, improving resource utilization, strengthening disaster preparedness, and increasing transparency in public resource management, Gov Nexus AI contributes directly to multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including:

* **SDG 1 – No Poverty** by improving the delivery of welfare resources and public assistance programs.
* **SDG 2 – Zero Hunger** through better forecasting and distribution of food supplies.
* **SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being** by ensuring timely availability of medicines, vaccines, and healthcare resources.
* **SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities** through proactive disaster preparedness and resilient resource planning.
* **SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production** by minimizing resource wastage and preventing unnecessary stock accumulation.
* **SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions** by improving transparency and accountability in public resource allocation.
* **SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals** by enabling collaboration between governments, NGOs, suppliers, and communities.

Rather than reacting to shortages after they occur, Gov Nexus AI helps organizations make proactive, data-driven decisions that maximize social impact, improve resource accessibility, and support long-term sustainable development.

**The problem it solves**

✦  1. model scanner SC solves the critical "Pickle" vulnerability by preventing arbitrary code execution during neural weight loading.
   2. It provides a deep structural audit of model files to detect hidden RCE vectors, malicious globals, and obfuscated shellcode.
   3. Teams use it to automate hazardous model sanitization, migrating risky artifacts into the secure SafeTensors format.
   4. It acts as an automated CI/CD security gate, ensuring that only verified and safe neural assets reach production environments.
   5. The tool facilitates DPDP Act compliance in India by identifying exposed Aadhaar/PAN identifiers within model weights.
   6. Its cinematic Neural Topology visualizes complex n8n orchestration, making AI security flows intuitive for all stakeholders.
   7. It replaces manual analysis with interactive Neural Info Pods, delivering instant technical definitions for every audit stage.
   8. Integrated with Sarvam AI, it generates expert forensic reports that deconstruct Indic-language safety filter bypasses.
   9. The Autonomous Action Center enables rapid response through one-click quarantine and "Auto-Patch" remediation workflows.
   10. By uncovering hidden C2 callbacks, it prevents malicious models from exfiltrating proprietary data or weights after deployment.

**Challenges we ran into**

model scanner SC acts as a critical security gatekeeper, auditing neural weights for RCE vectors and supply-chain injections before deployment.
  It automates the hazardous task of "pickle" vulnerability remediation by sanitizing risky models into the secure SafeTensors format.
  For the Indian market, it provides specialized DPDP Act compliance by detecting Aadhaar/PAN leaks and Indic-language safety filter bypasses.
  The cinematic Neural Topology visualizes complex orchestration flows, making it easier for stakeholders to understand the AI security lifecycle.
  It replaces manual weight inspection with an Autonomous Decision Layer, utilizing Sarvam AI to provide high-fidelity technical advisories.
  The Live Security Event Log delivers real-time forensic streams, allowing DevOps teams to pinpoint architectural anomalies with millisecond precision.
  Ultimately, it transforms model auditing into a transparent, high-performance command center, ensuring total integrity for enterprise AI assets.

> Advanced threat detection system for satellite tel

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keras](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keras-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![NLP](https://img.shields.io/badge/NLP-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Space missions conducted by organizations like ISRO and NASA involve extremely high financial and strategic stakes, with satellites costing millions of dollars to design, launch, and maintain. These systems remain vulnerable to two critical risks: undetected system failures and sophisticated cyberattacks. Both can lead to mission degradation or complete failure, resulting in irreversible losses.

Existing infrastructures lack a unified, proactive framework for real-time anomaly detection and response. Additionally, telemetry data and system logs which are crucial for monitoring and post-incident analysis are often mutable, making them susceptible to tampering. This compromises forensic integrity, leaving investigators without a reliable trail to trace the root cause of failures or breaches.

ARGUS addresses these gaps through a 3+1 layered architecture that combines AI-driven detection with blockchain-based auditing. It enables:

Real-time anomaly detection across satellite subsystems using multi-layered AI models
Automated threat response mechanisms to mitigate failures before escalation
Tamper-proof logging using blockchain, ensuring immutable and verifiable telemetry records
Reliable forensic traceability, allowing precise post-incident analysis
By integrating intelligent monitoring with secure, decentralized auditing, ARGUS transforms satellite operations into a more resilient, transparent, and failure-resistant ecosystem saving space agencies millions of dollars.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was handling the overall system complexity. ARGUS combines multiple technologies, and getting everything to work smoothly together wasn’t straightforward. Blockchain was completely new to us, so figuring out how to use it for secure, tamper-proof logging took a lot of trial and error.

But the worst issue was RESOLVING MERGE CONFLICTS ON GITHUB.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

EternalMind is built for one major human problem: people leave behind photos and files, but their stories, values, explanations, and advice often disappear.

Our solution is a blockchain-backed memory capsule.

It lets a person seal private memories today, define when they can be unlocked, and allow a chosen heir to claim access later through a verified wallet

**Challenges we ran into**

Integration of back end and frontend, 
Onboarding on chain
Encryption algorithm slection

**Blockchain**

Blockchain is used for shared state that benefits from transparent verification: vault ownership, minting,
authorized heir addresses, unlock conditions, and immutable content references. It is not used to store
plaintext memories because public blockchains are unsuitable for private personal content and on-chain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-image](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--image-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

TruthLens was built to tackle one of the biggest problems growing with modern AI  figuring out what’s real and what’s not online.

Today, AI tools can generate highly realistic images, voices, videos, and even news articles within seconds. While this technology is powerful, it also makes misinformation, fake media, scams, and manipulated content much harder to identify for everyday users.

TruthLens makes this process simple.

It allows users to upload images, videos, audio clips, or text and instantly analyze whether the content is likely real or AI-generated. Instead of using multiple tools for different media types, TruthLens brings everything together into one clean and easy-to-use platform.

The project is designed for students, creators, journalists, researchers, and normal internet users who want a quick way to verify suspicious content before trusting or sharing it.

Some practical ways people can use TruthLens:

- Checking whether an image was generated using AI
- Detecting manipulated or deepfake videos
- Identifying AI-generated voices or cloned audio
- Verifying fake news or AI-written text
- Avoiding misinformation on social media

TruthLens focuses on speed, accessibility, and simplicity through both a modern website and Android application, making AI detection easier for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges while building TruthLens was handling large AI models efficiently without crashing the backend server.

Initially, all detection models were loading at startup, including image, video, audio, and news detection models. This caused serious memory issues during deployment, especially on cloud platforms with limited RAM. The backend would either crash during startup or take a very long time to respond.

Another major challenge was reducing the response time for users. Some detections, especially video and audio analysis, were taking too long because the models had to download and initialize repeatedly.

To solve this, the backend architecture was redesigned using a smarter model-loading strategy. Lightweight and frequently used models were preloaded during startup, while heavier models such as video and audio detectors were switched to lazy loading so they only load when actually needed.

I also optimized the deployment pipeline, cleaned unnecessary dependencies, fixed package conflicts, improved API handling, and connected the frontend, backend, and Flutter application into a single working production setup.

Apart from backend optimization, integrating the live Railway backend with the frontend and Android app while maintaining stable API communication was another challenge during deployment.

Working through these issues helped improve both the performance and scalability of the project, and it gave me a much deeper understanding of real-world AI deployment and optimization.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles we faced while building this project was during deployment on Render. Even though the application worked perfectly in the local environment, the deployment kept failing with an `ENOENT package.json not found` error.

At first, we thought the issue was related to dependencies or build commands, but after carefully checking the deployment logs, we discovered that Render was trying to build the project from the wrong directory. The actual project files were inside a nested folder, so the platform could not locate the `package.json` file required for installation and build processes.

To solve this issue, we configured the correct Root Directory in Render and redeployed the application. After updating the deployment settings, the build completed successfully and the website went live.

This challenge helped us better understand project structures, deployment workflows, and the importance of debugging build logs carefully. It was a great learning experience in handling real-world deployment issues.

### VigilBot.eth
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/audit-agent-5916) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Riki0923/Vigil) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://vigil-production-0ca5.up.railway.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/U4il4BOrepc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Real-time AI monitor for proxy upgrades.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Swarm](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swarm-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**🚨 The Problem: The Window of Vulnerability**

Proxy patterns (UUPS, Transparent Proxies) are essential to DeFi. They let protocols upgrade their smart contracts. But they're also one of the most heavily exploited attack vectors in the ecosystem.

When a compromised admin or malicious governance proposal upgrades a proxy to a new implementation, the damage is instant. The gap between *"an upgrade lands on-chain"* and *"a qualified human understands what the new code does"* is currently measured in hours or days. In crypto, that means the funds are already gone.

Current tools fall short:

* **Passive monitors** (like Tenderly) only tell you *that* an upgrade happened. Analysis is still on humans
* **Generic bots** (like Forta) lack semantic understanding of never-before-seen code pushed during an upgrade
* **Human auditors** are precise but unscalable and asleep at 3 AM

**🛡️ How Vigil Solves This**

Vigil closes the window of vulnerability by combining the speed of a bot with the semantic understanding of a human auditor.

It is a fully autonomous AI agent that watches Ethereum proxy upgrades in real time. The moment an upgrade fires on Base mainnet, Vigil's pipeline runs automatically with no human in the loop:

1. **Detects** the EIP-1967 `Upgraded` event and reads both old and new implementation addresses
2. **Verifies** the new contract on Sourcify. If unverified, runs bytecode similarity search across 27M+ contracts to flag possible clones of known exploits
3. **Diffs** storage layouts and ABIs, detects moved storage slots (the #1 cause of proxy exploits), removed functions, and sensitive additions like `withdraw()` or `selfdestruct()`
4. **Scores** severity: `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` / `CRITICAL` based on the diff
5. **Analyses** with GPT-4o, reads the full diff plus NatSpec documentation to produce a plain-English summary, technical explanation, and recommendation
6. **Pays autonomously** for off-chain intelligence via Apify X402 micropayments on Base, scraping news context about the protocol without any human approval or API key management
7. **Publishes** the complete alert (diff, AI analysis, block data) to a permanent Swarm feed indexed by block number, retrievable by anyone, forever, no centralized server
8. **Delivers** an instant Telegram alert with AI summary, Swarm permalink, and Basescan link
9. **Writes reputation back to ENS**: `vigil.last-severity`, `vigil.last-upgrade-at`, `vigil.last-tx`, and `vigil.upgrade-count` (auto-incremented) on the protocol's subname under `vigilbot.eth`

**🎯 Who Can Use It**

* **DAOs & Protocol Teams**: subscribe to Vigil's Swarm feed to build automated circuit breakers. If a critical dependency upgrades to a suspicious implementation, pause your own contracts before funds are drained
* **Security Researchers & Whitehats**: get instantaneous AI-filtered leads on potential exploits instead of manually parsing Etherscan diffs
* **Other AI Agents**: Vigil publishes its feed URL on ENS (`agent.vigilbot.eth`) so agents can discover and subscribe programmatically, zero human configuration needed
* **Everyday DeFi Users**: benefit from a safer ecosystem where protocols react to malicious upgrades in seconds, not hours. The "revoke approval" banner in Vigil's dashboard lets users instantly revoke token approvals the moment a proxy they've interacted with upgrades to a suspicious implementation

**🔧 Technical Stack**

* **Agent:** TypeScript / Node.js, ethers v6, GPT-4o
* **Sourcify:** v2 API, verification, storage layout diff, ABI diff, NatSpec, bytecode similarity search across 27M+ contracts
* **Apify:** autonomous X402 micropayments on Base for news enrichment, agent pays per scrape, no human approval
* **Swarm:** `@ethersphere/bee-js` Mantaray manifest via `bzz.limo`, `NULL_STAMP` gateway, permanent feed indexed by block number
* **ENS:** agent identity on `vigilbot.eth` (mainnet) and `vigil.eth` (Sepolia), ENSIP-11 multichain records, per-protocol reputation text records
* **Frontend:** Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind v4, wagmi v2, viem, Recharts, Vercel AI SDK
* **Telegram:** real-time alert delivery with AI summary and Swarm permalink

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a real-time, cross-stack agent (RPC + AI + decentralized storage + payments) during a hackathon brought several unique hurdles:

## 1. LLM Context vs. Massive Smart Contracts

Modern DeFi protocols are huge. When a proxy upgrades, naively feeding the entire source code diff into GPT-4o blew up the context window or caused the model to miss critical changes buried in noise. We solved this by preprocessing the diff to extract only what matters: changed storage variables, modified external/public function selectors, ownership changes, and NatSpec documentation. By stripping unmodified library code and focusing strictly on deltas, we made the AI assessment both faster and significantly more accurate.

## 2. The Unverified Contract Race Condition

Vigil triggers the moment an `Upgraded` event lands on-chain. Sometimes the deployer hasn't verified the new implementation on Sourcify yet. Instead of dropping the alert, we implemented a retry mechanism. If verification returns 404, Vigil retries up to 2 times, 15 seconds apart (~30s total ceiling, demo-tuned to keep the booth pitch responsive), before falling back to bytecode similarity search across Sourcify's 27M+ contract database. This means even unverified contracts get meaningful analysis rather than a silent failure.

## 3. Swarm Manifest Path Resolution

Getting MantarayNode paths to resolve correctly via `bzz.limo` was the hardest integration of the hackathon. The `addFork` API required exact path formatting without leading slashes, and the difference between `uploadData` (which routes to the `/bytes/` endpoint) and `uploadFile` (which routes to `/bzz/`) caused hours of 404 debugging. We also had to switch from a three-manifest nested architecture to a single flat manifest after the nested approach consistently failed path resolution. Áron from the Swarm team helped us identify the root cause in person at the venue. Without that, we would have lost the entire Swarm integration.

## 4. Apify X402 Payment Signing

The `x402` npm package doesn't natively support Apify's exact payment scheme. It only handles ERC-20. After trying viem's `signPayment`, we discovered the only reliable path was using Apify's own `mcpc` CLI tool via Node.js `execSync`, then parsing the base64 signature from the CLI output line by line. The signature extraction itself was a debugging challenge. The CLI output includes metadata, MCP config snippets, and the actual signature, and we had to find the correct line by scanning for `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header:` and taking the next line. Not obvious from any documentation.

**Ethereum Core**

Vigil is core Ethereum infrastructure, an autonomous agent that makes proxy upgrades, the most exploited attack vector in DeFi, transparent and auditable in real time.

It watches every EIP-1967 `Upgraded` event on Base mainnet, verifies new implementations against Sourcify's 27M+ contract database, diffs storage layouts and ABIs to detect dangerous changes, runs AI-powered risk assessment, and publishes permanent verifiable alerts to Swarm, all within seconds of an upgrade landing on-chain.

Automated semantic understanding of contract upgrades at machine speed, with results stored permanently on decentralised infrastructure and discoverable via ENS.

**Sourcify Bounty**

Vigil uses Sourcify as its primary intelligence layer for smart contract analysis, going far deeper than simple verification checks.

When an upgrade is detected, Vigil queries the Sourcify v2 API for the new implementation to:

* Check verification status (with retries, 2 attempts, 15 seconds apart)
* Extract the full storage layout to diff slot-by-slot against the old implementation
* Compare ABIs to detect added/removed/modified functions
* Pull NatSpec documentation to give the AI analyser developer context
* Run bytecode similarity search across verified contracts when the new impl is unverified, identifying possible clones of known exploits

The storage layout diff is the key differentiator. Sourcify is the only source that exposes this data, and moved storage slots are the #1 cause of proxy upgrade exploits.

**Best Agentic Venture**

Vigil is a fully autonomous security agent with a clear path to becoming a venture.

**Agentic execution:** Every step runs without human involvement: detect upgrade, verify contract, diff code, run AI analysis, pay for intelligence via X402, publish to Swarm, alert via Telegram. The agent operates 24/7 with no human in the loop.

**Revenue path:** Protocol teams pay a subscription fee to have their contracts monitored. Premium tiers include faster alerts, more chains, and API access for other agents to query Vigil's threat feed. The $500M+ smart contract security market is proven and growing.

**Token consideration:** A `VIGIL` token makes sense as governance over which chains and contracts are monitored, staking to receive priority alerts, and payment for API access. Protocol teams stake `VIGIL` to whitelist their contracts, creating real demand tied to real usage.

**Why Umia:** Vigil's on-chain reputation system (writing threat data back to ENS after every alert) is a natural fit for Umia's credible public capital formation model. The token's value is directly tied to verifiable, on-chain security data that anyone can audit, exactly the kind of public good Umia is designed to reward.

**Ethereum Chain State on Swarm**

Vigil stores every proxy upgrade alert and its corresponding Ethereum block data permanently on Swarm, creating a decentralised, trustless archive of smart contract upgrade history.

When an alert fires, Vigil uploads a combined JSON envelope `{alert, block}` to Swarm via `bzz.limo` using `NULL_STAMP` (no postage batch required), then adds it to a Mantaray manifest at path `blocks/{blockNumber}`. The manifest is saved and its reference pushed to a signed Swarm Feed (topic `vigil-manifest`). The feed URL never changes. It always resolves to the latest manifest containing the full upgrade history.

Anyone can retrieve any upgrade by block number: `bzz.limo/bzz/{manifestHash}/blocks/45782287`. No Infura, no Alchemy, no centralized provider, just Swarm.

The permanent feed URL is published on ENS (`vigil.feed` on `agent.vigilbot.eth`) so subscribers discover it without any out-of-band URL sharing.

**Best ENS Integration for AI Agents**

Vigil uses ENS as the backbone of its agent identity and protocol reputation system, not just for naming, but as a live, on-chain data layer that other agents can query programmatically.

**Agent Identity:** Vigil reads its own capabilities, severity threshold, and Swarm feed URL from `agent.vigilbot.eth` text records at boot (production mainnet) or `agent.vigil.eth` (Sepolia dev). This means any other agent can discover Vigil's feed URL and capabilities entirely through ENS, no out-of-band configuration.

**Per-Protocol Reputation:** After every alert, Vigil writes 4 text records back to the matching protocol subname under `vigilbot.eth`: `vigil.last-severity`, `vigil.last-upgrade-at`, `vigil.last-tx`, and `vigil.upgrade-count` (auto-incremented). ENS becomes a live, verifiable reputation log. Any agent can call `tsx scripts/ens/resolve.ts --network=mainnet usdc.vigilbot.eth` and see Vigil's full threat history for that protocol.

**ENSIP-11 Multichain Records:** Demo proxy addresses on Base mainnet are anchored to Ethereum mainnet ENS names via ENSIP-11 coin type records, so `demo.vigilbot.eth` resolves to a Base address without any centralized registry.

**ENSIP-19 L2 Reverse Naming:** The demo proxy on Base mainnet has `demo.vigilbot.eth` set as its primary name via the L2ReverseRegistrar, so block explorers display the human name instead of hex.

**Frontend Resolution:** The dashboard resolves `agent.vigilbot.eth` live on every page load, displaying capabilities chips, severity floor, the live `vigil.feed` URL, and a `vigil.payment` X402 endpoint, all served from ENS, no centralized backend.

**Most Creative Use of ENS**

We turned ENS into a live threat intelligence layer for AI agents.

Most projects use ENS for human-readable names. Vigil uses it as a machine-readable reputation database. After every proxy upgrade alert, Vigil autonomously writes `vigil.last-severity`, `vigil.last-upgrade-at`, `vigil.last-tx`, and `vigil.upgrade-count` back to the protocol's ENS subname under `vigilbot.eth`. Any agent in the ecosystem can query `demo.vigilbot.eth` and instantly know Vigil's full threat history for that contract, no API, no centralized server, just ENS.

The agent's own identity, capabilities, severity threshold, and Swarm feed URL all live on `agent.vigilbot.eth` text records, so other agents can discover and subscribe to Vigil's feed entirely through ENS resolution. We also used ENSIP-11 for multichain address records and ENSIP-19 for L2 reverse naming on Base. Three ENS standards working together to make a fully sovereign, agent-native identity system.

**Apify Bounty**

Vigil uses Apify via the X402 protocol to autonomously enrich upgrade alerts with real-world context, no human approval, no API key management, just an agent paying for data it needs.

When a proxy upgrade is detected, Vigil autonomously signs a $1 USDC payment on Base mainnet using a funded wallet, calls the Apify `google-search-scraper` Actor via the X402 payment flow, and enriches the alert with news context about the upgraded protocol. The payment fires mid-pipeline with zero human involvement. The agent decides it needs data, pays for it, and uses it.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents are increasingly acting on behalf of users. executing trades, auditing contracts, scraping data, but 87% have no safety documentation (MIT CSAIL AI Agent Index) and there's no trustworthy way to discover, evaluate, or pay them. Existing tools rely on centralized ratings, opaque reputation systems, and no financial accountability.

Stovera solves this with three guarantees:

**Verifiable reputation** — Every agent goes through a community-driven Verify Pool before listing. Ratings are on-chain and tamper-proof.

**Accountable payments** — Users deposit ETH via StoveraEscrow on Base Mainnet. The actual cost is deducted after task completion; the remainder is automatically refunded. No trust required.

**Fair discovery** — Featured agents are selected daily using SpaceComputer's cTRNG — true randomness sourced from cosmic ray interactions with satellites. No pay-to-play, no algorithmic bias.

**On-chain identity** — Every verified agent receives an ERC-8004 identity: a global ID tied to its chain, registry, reputation score, and operator wallet. Human-readable via ENS subdomains (agent.stovera.eth).

**Challenges we ran into**

**Reputation Manipulation** — The hardest problem to solve. In an open marketplace, anyone can flood ratings with fake reviews. inflating bad agents or burying good ones. We couldn't just let anyone review; that breaks the whole trust model.

Our solution: a permissioned verifier network. Not everyone can submit reviews or verify agents. you have to earn that right. Verifiers gain access through an invite-only system: existing trusted verifiers can issue access codes, but only after they've crossed a trust threshold themselves. That threshold is calculated from wallet quality, on-chain activity, social influence, and a track record of high-quality, consistent reviews.

This creates a web of accountable trust. every verifier is vouched for by someone who had skin in the game. Sybil attacks become expensive. Reputation scores become harder to game. The mechanism mirrors how real-world credibility works: you don't get to be a critic just by showing up. You earn it.

**Anti-sybil for reviews** — We added a second layer: deposit-gating. Only wallets that have paid for an agent task can leave a review. This ties reputation to real economic activity on-chain — not just identity.

**ERC-8004 compatibility** — The standard is still in draft. We designed Stovera's architecture to be compatible: every agent has a global ID in the format eip155:{chainId}:{registry}:{agentId}, a reputation registry (on-chain reviews), and a validation registry (the Verify Pool). Rather than waiting for a finalized spec, we implemented the three-registry pattern the EIP describes and can migrate to the canonical contracts when they deploy.

**ENS resolution across chains** — Agent operators have ENS names but Stovera runs on Base. We configured wagmi with dual-chain support: Base Mainnet for transactions, Ethereum Mainnet (read-only via LlamaRPC) for ENS resolution.

**First-time hackers** — We are first-year computer programming students who entered the builder ecosystem 7 months ago. ETHPrague 2026 is our first global hackathon. There are rough edges in the code and ideas we didn't have time to fully execute — but we pushed as hard as we could to express a vision we genuinely believe in: that trust should be a protocol, not a privilege.

**Network Economy**

Stovera is a marketplace where AI agents earn income through verifiable work. Agents are paid in ETH via an escrow contract — deposit upfront, actual cost deducted, remainder refunded. This creates a direct economic loop: agents that perform well earn more, get better reviews, rank higher, and attract more tasks.

The permissioned verifier network adds a second economic layer — trust itself becomes a scarce, earned resource. Verifiers with high trust scores can issue invites, creating accountability chains that make reputation manipulation costly.

**Future Society**

As AI agents take on more real-world tasks — trading, auditing, researching — society needs infrastructure to hold them accountable. Stovera is that infrastructure.

Every agent has a verifiable on-chain identity (ERC-8004), a public reputation score built from real economic interactions, and an ENS subdomain as a human-readable identity. Anyone can audit an agent's history. No black boxes.

The permissioned verifier network models how trust should work in an agentic future: not granted by a platform, but earned through proof-of-contribution and vouched for by peers. This is what accountable AI looks like — not regulation, but cryptographic accountability.

**SpaceComputer Bounty**

Stovera uses SpaceComputer's @spacecomputer-io/orbitport-sdk-ts to power daily featured agent selection with verifiable cosmic randomness.

Every time the marketplace loads, a server-side Next.js API route (/api/random) fetches a fresh cTRNG value from SpaceComputer's public IPFS beacon, entropy sourced from cosmic ray interactions detected by satellites. The hex value is used to deterministically pick 3 agents for the "Cosmic Picks" spotlight, rotating daily.

The integration is live at stovera.xyz/market. The source, entropy value, and provider are displayed transparently on the page. No pay-to-play, no algorithmic bias. just physics.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/2b8e814c50a04425bc6c259a6b6904b0/13a18522-a8fd-4a6e-8431-ac775719b768.png)

**Best ENS Integration for AI Agents**

Stovera uses ENS as the identity layer for AI agents. Every agent operator's 0x address is resolved to their ENS name and avatar in real-time using useEnsName and useEnsAvatar from wagmi. visible on the agent detail page, the verify pool, and the wallet connect button in the nav.

Beyond reverse resolution, Stovera introduces the concept of agent.stovera.eth subdomains. a human-readable, on-chain identity for every verified agent, linking their ENS name to their ERC-8004 record, reputation score, and operator wallet.

ENS turns anonymous 0x addresses into accountable identities. In a marketplace where trust is the core primitive, that's not a nice-to-have, it's the foundation.

**Most Creative Use of ENS**

Most ENS integrations stop at name lookup. Stovera uses ENS as the trust layer for an entire AI agent economy.

Every verified agent gets an agent.stovera.eth subdomain. a human-readable, on-chain identity that links directly to their ERC-8004 record, reputation score, operator wallet, and task history. Instead of interacting with 0x88E6...38C6, you hire contract-auditor.stovera.eth. The name carries accountability.

On the operator side, ENS avatars and names are resolved live across the marketplace. in agent cards, the verify pool, and wallet connections. turning anonymous addresses into recognizable identities with social proof.

ENS becomes the namespace for a new class of economic actor: the AI agent.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Prediction markets like Polymarket are powerful because they turn public belief into a live price. But they still have one major weakness: **someone has to decide what actually happened.**

That works for simple outcomes. But many of the most interesting markets are messy, subjective, probabilistic, or hard to verify:

- Did this DAO proposal achieve its stated goal?
- Was this AI agent’s decision correct?
- Did this creator actually hit the promised milestone?
- Was this prediction resolved fairly?
- Did the event happen according to the rules?

Today, these outcomes often depend on a centralized resolver, moderator, oracle, admin, or social consensus. That creates disputes, bias, pressure, and unclear resolutions.

**TruthMarket is a prediction market where the truth is resolved by the market itself.**

Every market starts with a locked claim and rules document, so everyone knows exactly what **YES** and **NO** mean before they stake. Voters commit their votes privately, so nobody can copy, influence, or pressure the outcome during the voting period. When voting closes, a randomly selected jury of staked participants reveals their votes and resolves the market.

This creates a fairer way to settle non-obvious outcomes. Instead of relying on one platform, one oracle, or one powerful moderator, TruthMarket lets communities resolve claims through staked, private, randomly selected judgment.

TruthMarket can be used for **DAO decisions, public predictions, creator promises, AI agent actions, community bets, impact claims, and any outcome that is too subjective, probabilistic, or non-verifiable for a normal oracle.**

**Polymarket shows what people believe. TruthMarket helps decide what is true.**

**Challenges we ran into**

### The Core Design Challenge

Polymarket is great when the answer is obvious later.

But what about questions like:

- Was this AI demo real progress or just hype?
- Did a DAO actually deliver what it promised?
- Is this prediction still credible?
- Was a claim misleading, even if not technically false?

These are valuable markets, but they are hard to resolve.

Our biggest hurdle was making those markets feel fair without handing the final decision to one admin.

We solved it with a random staked jury:

> **Stake shows conviction. Random jurors decide the outcome.**

Votes stay private with commit-reveal, rules are locked before anyone stakes, and the final result comes from selected jurors instead of a centralized moderator.

That turned TruthMarket into something simple:

**Polymarket for questions too messy for a normal oracle.**

**Future Society**

### Why TruthMarket Matters for the Future Society

AI is the clearest example of why we need this.

Models and agents are starting to make predictions, recommendations, summaries, evaluations, and decisions at massive scale. Many of those claims will not be clearly true or false. They will be uncertain, probabilistic, or only obvious much later.

TruthMarket turns markets into a way to make sense of that uncertainty.

People and agents can stake on hard claims, commit privately, and resolve through a randomly selected jury of staked participants. Instead of one platform, moderator, or model deciding what is “true,” the market produces a public signal from people willing to take real risk.

That matters beyond AI too:

- DAOs can resolve whether proposals delivered;
- communities can judge disputed public claims;
- researchers can test early forecasts;
- builders can price trust in roadmaps and promises;
- agents can build reputation through resolved predictions.

Markets are powerful because they turn scattered beliefs into one signal. TruthMarket brings that to questions where the answer is messy, early, or probabilistic.

> **A market layer for uncertain truth.**

**SpaceComputer Bounty**

## Space-Powered Security: Fair, verifiable Jury selection

TruthMarket is applying under the **Space-Powered Security APIs** direction.

We use SpaceComputer cTRNG for the protocol’s most important security function:

> **selecting the jurors who decide the market outcome.**

TruthMarket is built for claims where truth is uncertain: AI forecasts, agent reputation, DAO accountability, public claims, model evaluations, and questions too messy for a normal prediction market.

For these markets, the game theory only works if jury selection cannot be predicted, manipulated, or front-run.

### Why randomness is core

TruthMarket uses private commit-reveal voting. Voters stake on a claim without revealing their vote during the voting phase. Only after voting closes does the protocol use SpaceComputer randomness to select a jury from the committed voters.

That timing matters.

If jurors were known early, voters could bribe them, copy them, intimidate them, or coordinate around them. If the operator could choose the jury, the market would collapse into a trusted moderation system. If large stakers could influence the draw, the outcome could be bought.

SpaceComputer randomness prevents that.

The jury is selected only after commits are locked, using external unpredictable entropy.

> **SpaceComputer is the fairness engine of TruthMarket: it makes the market game playable by preventing predictable, operator-controlled, or front-runnable jury selection.**

### Working prototype

Our prototype demonstrates the full core flow:

1. Voters privately commit their belief.
2. Stake is locked.
3. Voting closes.
4. SpaceComputer cTRNG provides randomness.
5. The protocol selects a random jury from committed voters.
6. Selected jurors reveal.
7. The market resolves.
8. Payouts are calculated from the outcome.

The randomness is directly tied to market settlement. It decides the selected jurors, the selected jurors decide the outcome, and the outcome decides payouts.

### Technical integration depth

This is not a cosmetic API call.

The cTRNG is in the critical path of the protocol:

- it protects juror selection from prediction;
- it prevents pre-selection coordination;
- it makes front-running the jury draw impractical;
- it keeps the operator from hand-picking resolvers;
- it gives every committed voter a fair chance to be selected;
- it supports the one-juror, one-vote resolution design.

We also store randomness evidence so the draw can be inspected and replayed:

- cTRNG value;
- randomness hash;
- beacon metadata;
- selected jurors;
- deterministic selection process.

### Why this matters

TruthMarket creates markets for uncertain truth:

- AI predictions;
- agent reputation;
- DAO accountability;
- disputed public claims;
- model evaluations;
- research forecasts;
- probabilistic questions.

These markets are only credible if participants believe the resolution process cannot be gamed.

SpaceComputer randomness gives the protocol the neutral entropy it needs for fair selection. Without it, the mechanism becomes vulnerable to manipulation. With it, humans and agents can stake, reveal, and resolve under a process no single party controls.

### Creativity

Most randomness integrations are lotteries, games, or NFT traits.

TruthMarket uses randomness for something more structural:

> **randomly assigning temporary judgment power in markets for disputed claims.**

That creates a new primitive: a random-jury market where the crowd provides the voter pool, SpaceComputer provides the entropy, and selected participants resolve uncertainty.

### Future direction

As SpaceComputer moves toward fully verifiable, space-signed randomness, TruthMarket can upgrade the jury draw into an even stronger system.

Future markets could prove not only that jurors were selected deterministically, but that the entropy itself came from a verifiable space-grade source.

That is the long-term vision:

> **space-signed randomness for public market resolution.**

### In one line

**TruthMarket uses SpaceComputer randomness as its fairness engine: the unpredictable draw that makes random-jury markets possible by enabling the game theory behind fair market resolution.**

**Sourcify Bounty**

## Sourcify: verified contract infrastructure for efficient market factories

TruthMarket uses a split contract architecture:

- one **MarketRegistry** as the public creation and discovery entry point;
- many lightweight **TruthMarket** instances, one per market, all referencing a core script

This is important for performance and scalability, future updates plus context isolation in case something goes wrong.

Instead of one giant contract trying to store and manage every market forever, each market gets its own isolated contract with its own immutable parameters, lifecycle, jury selection, reveal phase, slashing, and payouts. The registry stays thin: it creates markets, records them, and routes shared operational settings like treasury, admin, stake token, and jury committer.

That gives us a cleaner and more efficient architecture:

- markets are isolated from each other;
- per-market storage stays small and local;
- each market can resolve without touching unrelated market state;
- agents and humans use one simple `createMarket()` path;
- the registry gives the app one canonical place to discover markets;
- protocol fees from registry-created markets route consistently to the same treasury.

### Why Sourcify matters

The tradeoff with many contracts is trust.

If TruthMarket can create many market contracts, users need to know which ones are real, which ones follow the canonical logic, and which ones are modified forks.

Sourcify gives us the verified-contract infrastructure to check that.

We can use Sourcify data to verify:

- whether the registry is verified;
- whether a market contract is verified;
- whether a market’s bytecode matches the expected TruthMarket implementation;
- whether ABI and compiler metadata match the canonical contract family;
- whether a deployment is a trusted market, a verified fork, or an unknown contract.

### Why this improves UX

Before users stake, the frontend can show a simple trust status:

- **Canonical market from verified registry**
- **Verified market fork**
- **Unverified market**
- **Unknown deployment**

That means users do not need to trust our frontend, a market creator, or a random link. They can verify both the entry point and the individual market contract.

### Why this fits the bounty

TruthMarket uses Sourcify data as a real safety layer for a multi-contract protocol.

The registry gives us performance and clean scaling. Sourcify gives users confidence that the many contracts created through that registry are actually running the expected code.

This uses the most important parts of Sourcify’s dataset:

- verified source code;
- deployed bytecode;
- ABI;
- compiler metadata;
- contract identity across deployments.

### The full trust flow

For a user, trust comes from two checks:

1. **Swarm verifies the claim rules**  
   The app proves the rules document shown to the user is the one stored for the market.

2. **Sourcify verifies the contract code**  
   The app proves the registry and market contract are running the expected verified logic.

Together, this removes middleman trust.

The user can see the rules, verify the code, and stake into a market without trusting a centralized operator.

### In one line

**TruthMarket uses one verified registry for scalable market creation, and Sourcify proves every market it creates is running the code users expect.**
