### LifeBridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lifebridge-f3ef) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/maitri25jain/LifeBride-Hackmol-.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackMol%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackmol-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Empowering Donors. Saving Lives.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Fatal Gap in India's Donation System

Every year, over 25,000 transplantable organs are wasted in India — not because donors don't exist, but because the system to match them is broken.

NOTTO's current process is manual.- A coordinator picks up the phone, calls hospitals one by one, mentally weighs compatibility, and hopes the organ arrives before the viability window closes. This takes 6–8 hours. A heart only survives 4.

Consent is fragile.- Paper pledges get lost. Families dispute them at the ICU door. Hospital staff have been documented altering records under pressure. There is no tamper-proof record of a donor's last wish.

Blood emergencies are chaotic. - When a trauma patient needs O- blood at 2 AM, coordinators broadcast on WhatsApp groups and pray someone responds. There is no structured system to find compatible donors nearby.

What LifeBridge Does

Matches organs in minutes, not hours.- Our AI engine scores every donor-recipient pair across all hospitals simultaneously — weighing HLA tissue compatibility, ABO blood group rules, cold ischemia viability with real-time transport distance, clinical urgency, and waitlist equity. The coordinator sees ranked results with feasibility scores instead of making phone calls.

Makes consent un-tamperable.- When a citizen pledges, we mint a Soulbound NFT (ERC-5192) on Polygon — a blockchain token that cannot be transferred, sold, deleted, or forged. In the ICU, the hospital verifies consent with one API call. The donor's Aadhaar identity is SHA-256 hashed before it touches the blockchain — no personal data exposed.

Turns blood emergencies into structured responses.- Coordinators broadcast alerts specifying blood type, urgency, and radius. Citizens within range see the alert on their dashboard and respond with one tap. The coordinator sees confirmed responders with contact details instantly.

Who Uses It

- Citizens register, pledge organs/blood/plasma, receive nearby blood alerts, and respond to emergencies
- Hospital Coordinators register donors and recipients, run AI matching, broadcast blood alerts, and coordinate logistics
- Hospital Admins manage coordinator accounts and oversee operations
- Ethics Boards can audit allocation fairness through the audit log and blockchain records

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
1. The Cultural Consent Barrier

Hurdle: In India, families ultimately have the final say on organ donation, making it hard to enforce a registered donor's wishes.

Solution: We combatted this by minting pledges as Soulbound NFTs. This creates an immutable, tamper-proof record on the blockchain, providing doctors and families with indisputable cryptographic proof of the donor's exact wishes.

2. Web3 Deployment Complexity

Hurdle: Integrating our FastAPI backend with live blockchain smart contracts resulted in transaction timeouts and 500 errors mid-hackathon.

Solution: We isolated our blockchain logic, tested the smart contracts locally using Hardhat to ensure stability, and then successfully bridged the connection to our backend using web3.py.

3. DigiLocker / Aadhaar Verification

Hurdle: Navigating the strict government API sandboxes for official DigiLocker identity verification proved to be a massive bottleneck.

Solution: Instead of halting development, we built an "API-ready" architecture. We implemented a simulated SHA-256 Aadhaar hashing mechanism that mimics the exact cryptographic security we will use once official API access is granted, proving our privacy-first concept works today.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLOv3 Algorithm](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLOv3%20Algorithm-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# ZENVOY

Safety-first urban navigation that helps users compare the safest and fastest routes before they move.


## Problem

Most navigation tools optimize for time, not personal safety. For late-night travel or unfamiliar areas, users often need more than ETA:

- Is the route well lit?
- Are there recent crime reports nearby?
- Does the street actually look safe on the ground?
- Can I verify the route before I commit to it?

ZENVOY was built to make route decisions more evidence-based instead of instinct-based.

## Solution

ZENVOY compares a safest route and fastest route on the same map, then explains the tradeoff using:

- route-level safety scoring
- lighting coverage
- nearby crime reports
- street-view verification with Mapillary
- map overlays for traffic signs and street objects
- an SOS action inside the live navigation experience

The goal is simple: give users enough context to choose a route that feels defensible, not just shorter.

## Key Features

- Compare safest vs fastest routes in one interface
- Inspect route breakdown with safety score, lighting score, and crime signals
- Show nearby crime reports inside the breakdown panel
- Open the nearest Mapillary street image by clicking on the map
- Filter Mapillary traffic signs and street objects with an in-app data panel
- Access SOS directly from the live map flow
- Explore a landing page and a `How It Works` page for user and developer views

## How It Works

1. The user selects an origin and destination.
2. The frontend requests both the safe route and the fast route.
3. The backend returns route geometry plus score breakdown data.
4. ZENVOY renders both routes and opens a safety analysis panel.
5. The user can inspect street-level imagery and additional map overlays before deciding.

## Tech Stack

### Frontend

- React
- Vite
- Mapbox GL JS
- Mapillary JS
- Axios

### Backend

- FastAPI
- Routing and safety scoring services
- Crime data pipeline
- YOLOv8-assisted street-view preprocessing for visual safety metadata


## What Makes It Different

- It does not treat safety as a vague label. It exposes the reasoning signals behind the recommendation.
- It combines route-level scoring with street-level verification.
- It keeps the decision loop in one place instead of forcing users across multiple tools.
- It is designed around real-world hesitation: "Should I take the shorter road, or the safer one?"


## Accomplishments That We're Proud Of

- A working live route comparison interface
- Integrated safety breakdown panel with route metrics and crime reports
- Mapillary street-view lookup directly from map clicks
- Filterable map data overlays for better street context
- A polished landing experience and supporting documentation page

## What We Learned

- Safety UX needs explanation, not just scores
- Street-level evidence makes route recommendations more trustworthy
- Even small schema mismatches between frontend and backend can break critical trust signals
- Navigation products can be designed around confidence, not only speed

## Future Scope

- Real-time crime and crowd-density updates
- Better route explanation with segment-level highlights
- User alerts based on time of day and neighborhood risk patterns
- Share-live-trip and trusted contact workflows
- More robust backend/API standardization and deployment

## Run Locally

```bash
cd zenvoy-web
npm install
npm run dev
```

Create `zenvoy-web/.env` with:

```bash
VITE_MAPBOX_TOKEN=your_mapbox_token
VITE_MAPILLARY_TOKEN=your_mapillary_token
VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
VITE_USE_MOCK=false
```

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

- Turning safety into something measurable was the hardest product challenge. It is easy to say a route is "safe," but much harder to justify that claim with signals users can actually trust.
- We had to merge very different inputs like route geometry, lighting coverage, crime reports, and street-level imagery into one decision flow without making the interface feel overloaded.
- Frontend and backend integration was not always clean. Small response-shape mismatches, especially around score breakdowns and crime-report fields, created UI failures that had to be debugged carefully.
- Street-view verification added another layer of complexity because map interaction, external imagery lookup, and loading states all needed to feel fast and understandable.
- Designing for trust was a constant challenge. The UI had to look polished, but more importantly it had to explain why one route was better than another instead of behaving like a black box.

**AI/ML**

# Why This Project Fits The AI/ML Track

ZENVOY fits the AI/ML track because it does more than display maps and routes. The core value of the product comes from using intelligent analysis to help users make safer navigation decisions.

## AI/ML Relevance

- The project uses machine-learning-assisted street analysis to extract visual safety signals from street imagery instead of relying only on raw map data.
- YOLOv8-based preprocessing is used to detect objects from street-view images and convert those detections into route-level visual safety metadata.
- The route comparison is not just shortest-path logic. It combines multiple signals such as lighting, crime reports, and visual evidence into a safety-oriented scoring system.
- The platform turns unstructured real-world inputs like street imagery into structured decision signals that users can actually act on.
- The product is designed to support explainable decision-making: users are not only shown a route recommendation, but also the signals and evidence behind it.

## Why That Matters

This makes ZENVOY an AI/ML project rather than just a mapping interface. AI is used to interpret street-level context, enrich route intelligence, and improve safety recommendations in a way that traditional navigation systems usually do not.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Metabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Metabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Remix (IDE)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Remix%20(IDE)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional donation systems often lack transparency, making it difficult for donors to know how their contributions are used. This lack of visibility can reduce trust and discourage people from donating to important causes.

OpenDonate solves this problem by using blockchain technology to create a transparent and verifiable donation platform. Every donation is recorded on the Ethereum blockchain, allowing anyone to view the total funds raised and the history of contributions in real time.

By removing intermediaries and storing transactions on a decentralized ledger, OpenDonate ensures that donations cannot be altered or hidden. This increases trust between donors and organizations, encourages accountability, and makes charitable giving more transparent and secure.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of OpenDonate, one of the main challenges was integrating the smart contract with the frontend application. Ensuring that the React application could correctly interact with the Ethereum smart contract using ethers.js required careful handling of asynchronous blockchain transactions and wallet connections.

Another challenge was handling MetaMask wallet connectivity and maintaining the user's session across page refreshes. Initially, the application would lose the connected wallet state when the page reloaded. This was resolved by checking the wallet connection on application load and restoring the session if the user had already granted permission.

I also encountered issues related to transaction handling and user experience, such as properly managing loading states during donations and handling errors when users rejected transactions. These were solved by implementing proper error handling, transaction status indicators, and UI feedback to improve the overall user experience.

Finally, deploying and connecting the smart contract to the frontend required careful management of contract addresses and ABI configurations. By modularizing the contract interaction logic and testing transactions on a test network, I was able to ensure that the donation functionality worked reliably.

> Donate with proof. Give with trust.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Charitable giving is built on trust—but trust alone is not enough. Every year, billions of dollars are donated to social causes, yet donors rarely have visibility into how their contributions are actually used.

Traditional charity systems suffer from several critical problems:
1. Lack of transparency – Once a donation is made, donors have little to no visibility into how funds are spent or whether they reach the intended beneficiaries. 
2. Misappropriation of funds – Without transparent tracking, funds may be misused or diverted without donors being aware.
3. Limited public accountability – Most charities rely on centralized systems or delayed reports that can be difficult to verify.
4. Donor skepticism – Because impact cannot be easily verified, many potential donors hesitate to contribute.

As a result, trust in charitable ecosystems declines and important causes struggle to receive the support they need.

**How Our Solution Helps**

ProofOfGiving introduces transparency through blockchain technology.

1. Every donation is recorded on-chain, making it permanently visible and verifiable.
2. Charities can upload proof of fund usage to IPFS, ensuring evidence cannot be altered or removed.
3. Donors can track transactions and verify impact in real time.
4. The system creates a trustless, transparent donation ecosystem where accountability is built into the infrastructure.

By combining Ethereum smart contracts and IPFS, ProofOfGiving enables donors to give with confidence and ensures that charitable organizations remain accountable.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1: Hardhat Version Hell**
**Problem:** Incompatible versions between Hardhat v3 and required plugins, plus ESM vs CommonJS conflicts.
**Fix:** Removed node_modules, set module commonjs in tsconfig.json, and installed hardhat-toolboxhh2. Learned to always check version compatibility first.

**Challenge 2: RPC Connection Failures**
**Problem:** Public RPC endpoints kept failing with ENOTFOUND or invalid project id during deployment.
**Fix:** Switched between multiple providers (Infura, public endpoints) and tested with curl before deploying. Kept backup RPCs ready.

**Challenge 3: ethers.js v5 to v6 Migration**
**Problem:** Deployment script crashed with contract.deployed is not a function after upgrading ethers.
**Fix:** Updated to v6 syntax replaced deployed with waitForDeployment and contract.address with await contract.getAddress.

**Challenge 4: IPFS CORS Errors**
**Problem:** Browser blocked Pinata API requests due to cross-origin restrictions.
**Fix:** Properly configured JWT in .env, added correct headers to axios requests, and tested with small files first.

**Challenge 5: UI Not Updating After Transactions**
**Problem:** Donation ledger and progress bar showed stale data after blockchain transactions.
**Fix:** Created refreshCampaigns callback that re-fetches all on-chain data and passed it to buttons for automatic updates.

**Challenge 6: MetaMask Network Confusion**
**Problem:** Users forgot to switch to Sepolia, causing transaction errors.
**Fix:** Added network validation in connectWallet checks chain ID 11155111 and alerts if wrong network.

**Challenge 7: Edge Case Bugs**
**Problem:** Donations after withdrawal, exceeding target, or non-owners withdrawing weren't handled.
**Fix:** Wrote comprehensive Hardhat tests covering all edge cases before frontend integration.

**The problem it solves**

What People Can Use AI DeFi Guardian For

AI DeFi Guardian is a Web3 security platform that helps users quickly evaluate the safety of wallets, tokens, and DeFi positions before making financial decisions. It combines multiple blockchain checks into a single dashboard so users can detect risks such as honeypots, hidden taxes, unsafe smart contracts, or liquidation threats.

1. Checking Token Safety Before Investing

Users can paste a token contract address and instantly analyze it for common scams such as honeypots, hidden sell taxes, unlocked liquidity, or suspicious owner privileges. This helps investors avoid buying tokens that they may not be able to sell later.

2. Monitoring Wallet and Portfolio Risk

By connecting a wallet, users can see a risk overview of their entire portfolio. The platform highlights potentially unsafe tokens, unaudited contracts, and other vulnerabilities so users can identify risky assets quickly.

3. Protecting DeFi Lending Positions

For users who borrow funds on lending platforms, the tool calculates and monitors their health factor. It also includes a liquidation simulator that shows how price changes can affect their position, allowing users to act before liquidation happens.

4. Performing Smart Contract Due Diligence

Researchers and advanced users can analyze contracts using automated vulnerability scans. The platform checks for multiple security risks and presents a structured report that helps evaluate whether a protocol is trustworthy.

5. Replacing Multiple Manual Security Checks

Normally, users must check several different tools to verify contract safety, liquidity locks, wallet activity, and portfolio exposure. AI DeFi Guardian automates these checks and provides results in seconds, significantly reducing the time and effort required to research DeFi investments.

6. Improving Safety and Accessibility in DeFi

The platform simplifies complex blockchain data into clear risk indicators and warnings, making it easier for beginners to understand potential threats while still providing detailed analysis for experienced traders.

In summary, AI DeFi Guardian makes DeFi safer by turning a complex research process into a fast automated scan that helps users detect risks, protect their assets, and make more informed decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Bug #1 — MetaMask Stuck on "CONNECTING..."

Fix

Replaced the single boolean connection state with a multi-phase connection state system so MetaMask connection and wallet scanning no longer interfere with each other.

Added a 60-second timeout that automatically cancels the connection if the MetaMask popup is ignored.

Implemented specific handling for MetaMask error code -32002 so users are instructed to open the existing popup instead of retrying blindly.

Bug #2 — Wallet Showing $0 Net Worth

Fix

Removed the Etherscan integration that required an API key and replaced it with Ethplorer, which provides wallet balances and token data without requiring authentication.

Corrected the JSON-RPC result filtering logic so valid zero-balance responses are accepted instead of being discarded.

Replaced number parsing with BigInt conversion to correctly handle large 256-bit Ethereum balance values without precision loss.

Fixed the Cloudflare Ethereum RPC endpoint URL, which was previously incorrect and returning errors.

Bug #3 — Blockchain APIs Blocked (CORS / Network Error)

Fix

Replaced APIs that block browser requests with CORS-enabled blockchain APIs suitable for frontend applications.

Updated the error message to accurately explain network, extension, or API downtime causes instead of incorrectly blaming iframe restrictions.

Implemented a multi-provider fallback system so if one API fails the application automatically retries with another provider.

Bug #4 — File Not Opening / Browser Hanging

Fix

Removed the React + Babel setup that compiled JSX in the browser at runtime.

Rewrote the entire frontend using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with no external runtime dependencies.

This eliminated heavy downloads and runtime compilation, allowing the application to load instantly and render in under 200ms.

Bug #5 — Wrong Wallet Data Displayed

Fix

Removed hardcoded mock wallet data that was bypassing the user-entered address.

Moved the wallet address state from the child component to the top-level application state so it persists during re-renders.

Updated the connection flow so the correct entered wallet address is always used during scanning.

Bug #6 — Multiple Minor Bugs

Fix

Corrected incorrect formatting of the liquidation price display.

Prevented division by zero errors when wallets have no assets.

Added safeguards to prevent NaN values when token balances are undefined.

Added unique keys to mapped UI elements to eliminate React console warnings.

Ensured alert IDs are unique for every scan to prevent collisions.

Added clamping to prevent negative health factor values during simulations.

Improved wallet address validation using a strict hexadecimal regex pattern.

Implemented price caching for CoinGecko API requests to avoid rate limits.

Fixed alert badge counting so dismissed alerts are no longer included.

Added a skeleton loading UI during scans instead of displaying a blank screen.

Replaced number parsing with BigInt conversion for accurate Ethereum balance calculations.

> Movies meet Web3

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most Web3 apps force you to have a wallet - 99% users just leave. IMDb owns your reviews and can delete them anytime. Writing a review takes too many steps.

CINEVERSE fixes this with Guest Mode - write reviews instantly, no wallet needed. Later connect wallet to own them forever on blockchain. Your reviews follow you everywhere, and you can prove you were first with timestamp. Simple for everyone, powerful for those who want it

**Challenges we ran into**

CHALLENGE 1: Overview Blocking Review Button
Problem: Movie overview would pop up on hover and cover the "Write Review" button. Users couldn't click it!

Fix: Made overview hidden by default. Added small icon to click and show overview. Review button always visible now.

CHALLENGE 2: WalletConnect Version Error
Problem: MetaMask showed Unsupported version error when connecting. Users got confused and left.

Fix: Removed version conflicts, simplified the code. Added proper error messages and fallbacks. Now works smoothly.

**The problem it solves**

🚨 **The Problem It Solves**

Crypto fundraising is broken. Founders raise millions, then vanish — leaving investors with nothing. There's no accountability, no recourse, and no protection.

**$2 billion+** lost to rug pulls in 2024 alone. 90% of new token launches fail or scam within 3 months.

TrustLaunch fixes this by making rug pulls **mathematically impossible** — not through promises, but through code.

- 💰 **Investors** get automatic refunds if founders disappear — no lawyers, no waiting
- 🚀 **Founders** gain instant credibility by putting real skin in the game
- 🔒 **Everyone** benefits from funds locked in auditable smart contracts, released only when real milestones are met

**Challenges we ran into**

⚙️ **Challenges We Ran Into**

**1. Four Smart Contracts, One Atomic Flow**
Coordinating all contracts without reentrancy bugs was the hardest hurdle. Fixed using OpenZeppelin's `ReentrancyGuard` and strict checks-effects-interactions pattern.

**2. AI Scanner Without a Backend**
Built a deterministic scoring engine using real project inputs — milestone count, collateral %, tokenomics — to generate genuine risk scores. No fake data.

**3. Unstable Testnet RPC**
BSC Testnet endpoints kept dropping mid-demo. Fixed by configuring multiple fallback RPC URLs across Hardhat and MetaMask config.

### MED-TRACK
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/medtrack-f364) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Shreyshrx/med-track-blockchain.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Track Every Pill. Trust Every Dose.”

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

MED-TRACK can be used to improve transparency and trust in the pharmaceutical supply chain by allowing different stakeholders to track and verify medicine authenticity.
Manufacturers can use the system to register new medicine batches and generate unique QR codes that are printed on medicine packaging. This ensures that every batch entering the supply chain has a digital identity.
Distributors and pharmacies can use MED-TRACK to update the movement of medicines as they pass through different stages of the supply chain. This creates a verifiable history of how the medicine traveled from the manufacturer to the pharmacy.
Consumers can scan the QR code on the medicine packaging using the web application to instantly verify whether the medicine is authentic. The system displays the batch information, manufacturer details, and supply chain timeline, helping users confirm that the product came from legitimate sources.
Healthcare regulators and pharmaceutical companies can also use the platform to monitor distribution channels and detect irregularities in the movement of medicines, helping reduce the spread of counterfeit drugs.
Overall, MED-TRACK helps ensure safer medicines by providing a transparent and traceable system for tracking pharmaceutical products from production to consumption.

**Challenges we ran into**

Setting up the blockchain development environment was challenging at the beginning. Hardhat and Node.js compatibility issues caused compilation problems, and the smart contract was not detected until the project structure and configuration were corrected.

Smart contract compilation errors occurred when the Solidity file was not placed in the correct folder or when the Hardhat configuration did not match the Solidity version. Fixing the project structure solved this issue.

Managing the local blockchain network was another challenge. The Hardhat local blockchain resets every time it restarts, which caused all stored medicine data to disappear. This required redeploying the smart contract and re-uploading the dataset each time.

Integrating the backend with the blockchain required careful handling of asynchronous transactions. The backend had to correctly interact with the smart contract using libraries like ethers.js and wait for transactions to be confirmed before returning results.

Contract address synchronization was a problem during development. Whenever the contract was redeployed, the backend needed to be updated with the new contract address to fetch the correct data from the blockchain.

Uploading and managing the medicine dataset also created difficulties. Some entries failed during upload because of duplicate batch IDs or transaction timing issues, which required adding checks to prevent duplicates.

Frontend and backend communication issues occurred when the API responses did not match the frontend expectations. This initially caused valid medicines to appear as “Fake or Unknown” until the verification API was corrected.

Version control and repository management was another challenge. Large folders like node_modules caused Git push issues, so .gitignore had to be configured properly to exclude unnecessary files before uploading the project to GitHub.

Team **YOLO** -- Shreysh Shekhar, [Arpan Kumar Sahoo](https://github.com/ArpanKrSahoo), [Shayan Ghosh](https://github.com/Shayan006OG)

### OnStream
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/onstream-d21a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/anuragcode-16/INNOVAT3_web3) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://onsteam.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Build Credit, Unlock Freedom

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem It Solves

Web3 lending is broken. If a user wants to borrow on platforms like Aave, they must lock up more collateral than they intend to borrow. This severely limits capital efficiency and prevents true credit building.

**OnStream** solves this by building Web3's first trust-based, zero-collateral **Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL)** payment layer.

1. **Credit from Scratch:** Users earn a dynamic "Trust Score" starting with a $10 USDC base limit, built on wallet history and repayment behavior—allowing genuine on-chain credit growth.
2. **Privacy-Preserving Proofs:** Users can boost their credit limit using Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proofs to verify their financial capacity (>100 USDC holdings) without ever exposing their exact balances to the public or the merchant.
3. **Unlocking Liquidity:** Crypto natives can buy NFTs, event tickets, or services instantly via Installment Payments without triggering taxable events or selling their staked crypto assets.
4. **Zero Merchant Risk:** Merchants get paid the full USDC amount upfront instantly by the protocol, letting OnStream handle the repayment risk.

OnStream creates the missing FICO score for Web3, allowing consumers to start with trust and grow with reputation.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I Ran Into

**1. The Cold Start Credit Problem**
Giving anonymous wallets an instant credit limit without collateral or KYC was our biggest hurdle. 
**The Fix:** 
We built the **WalletAnalyzer** contract to act as an on-chain underwriter. It instantly scans a wallet's age, transaction nonce, and native token balances using Solidity assembly to dynamically generate a safe baseline "Trust Score" and starting credit limit.

**2. Balancing Proof of Funds with Privacy**
To increase credit limits, we needed users to prove they held significant assets elsewhere, but users won't dox their main wallets for a BNPL loan. 
**The Fix:**
Integrating Zero-Knowledge proofs. Writing the Circom circuits to mathematically prove a user held over 100 USDC *without revealing the actual number* was a major learning curve, as was optimizing the on-chain verification on Polygon Amoy.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/proofos-0dbf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Prajusha2004/proof-of-skill) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://asset-manager--prajusha794.replit.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your Code Is Your Reputation

![npm](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Core Problem:

The modern developer’s actual work lives on the internet:

GitHub commits

Pull requests

Hackathon participation

Open-source contributions

Smart contracts deployed

Bug bounties

Technical articles

But when it comes to proving those achievements, the system falls apart.

Three big issues appear.

1. Resumes Are Easily Inflated
A resume is basically self-reported data.

Someone can write:

“Contributed to large open-source systems”

Maybe they fixed one typo.

Recruiters have no easy way to verify the depth or authenticity.

Truth becomes fuzzy.

2. Contributions Are Fragmented
A developer’s achievements are scattered across:

GitHub

Devpost

Kaggle

Hackathon platforms

Blogs

Discord communities

Web3 wallets

There’s no unified proof of skill identity.

It’s like a scientist publishing papers but every paper lives on a different planet.

3. Reputation Isn’t Portable
If you move platforms, you lose your history.

Your GitHub reputation does not automatically translate into:

hiring systems

hackathon credibility

web3 ecosystems

freelancing platforms

Your reputation is locked inside platforms instead of belonging to you.

The Idea Behind Proof_OS
Proof_OS turns work into cryptographic proof.

Instead of saying:

“I contributed to a project”

You have a verifiable on-chain credential proving it.

Think of it like:

GitHub achievements + blockchain verification + portable developer identity

How It Solves the Problem
1. Verifiable Proof of Work
When you do something meaningful:

merge a PR

win a hackathon

ship a project

complete a bounty

Proof_OS mints a credential NFT or verifiable token.

Now your contribution becomes:

Tamper-proof
Publicly verifiable
Owned by your wallet
No résumé exaggeration required.

Your work speaks mathematically.

2. Unified Skill Identity
Proof_OS acts like a developer operating system for reputation.

It aggregates:

GitHub activity

hackathon results

certifications

contributions

All under one identity wallet.

Your career becomes a timeline of proof objects.

3. Recruiters Query Proof Instead of Trust
Instead of reading resumes, companies can search:

“Find developers who shipped 5+ production smart contracts”

or

“Developers with merged PRs in top OSS projects”

Because those proofs exist on chain, verification becomes instant.

No LinkedIn theater required.

In One Sentence
Proof_OS solves the problem of fakeable resumes and fragmented developer reputation by turning real work into verifiable on-chain proof of skill.

Your code literally becomes your reputation ledger.

The Philosophical Twist (This Is Where It Gets Interesting)
Human societies always struggled with proving competence.

Medieval guilds used masterpieces.
Academia uses published papers.
Developers use… PDF resumes. Which is frankly hilarious.

Proof_OS is basically trying to build:

A scientific citation system for developers.

Except instead of citations, you collect cryptographic proofs of contribution.

Your reputation becomes a public graph of verified work.

And that’s a fascinating direction for the internet.

[Prajusha Dhar](https://github.com/Prajusha2004)

**The problem it solves**

Lack of Trust in Cross-Border Freelance Collaboration

Global freelance collaboration is growing rapidly, but current platforms suffer from several major challenges:

* Payment Uncertainty – Freelancers fear not getting paid, while clients worry about paying for incomplete or poor-quality work.

* Subjective Work Evaluation – Project completion is often judged manually, leading to disputes and unclear deliverables.

* Expensive Platform Fees – Traditional marketplaces charge 10–20% commissions, increasing costs for both clients and freelancers.

* Cross-Border Payment Friction – International payments face delays, currency conversion issues, and banking limitations.

* Biased Dispute Resolution – Current arbitration systems rely on centralized moderators, which can be slow, opaque, and sometimes biased.

### Paycrow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/paycrow-52dc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Prg-Yash/devally-fintechps1) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/QcEcIyh_dfs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Bytecamp'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://bytecamp-26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart Escrow. Automated Trust.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**PayCrow** solves the **biggest** problem in freelance and contract work: trust in payments.

In most remote projects, clients worry about paying before delivery, and freelancers worry about delivering without a guaranteed payout. Traditional workflows are fragmented across chats, **invoices**, **contracts**, and **manual payment** **follow-ups**, which leads to **delays**, **disputes**, and **non-payment risk**.

**PayCrow** makes this safer and simpler by combining agreements, escrow, milestone tracking, and dispute handling in **one** flow:

- Funds are locked in escrow before work starts, so freelancers know budget is secured.
- Payments are released milestone-by-milestone, so clients pay only when progress is verified.
- Every action is traceable through a transparent audit trail, reducing ambiguity in disputes.
- If conflict happens, support/admin can resolve tickets and release escrow to the rightful party quickly.
- Both sides get a clearer, fairer process without chasing messages, screenshots, or manual proofs.

**Who benefits most:**
- Freelancers and independent contractors
- Startups and agencies hiring remote talent
- Any team managing milestone-based project payments across borders





![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e6319ab1df24442580a9812d19b6a514/c5f67d16-5133-4f7e-884a-5bf6c025af50.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Hybrid State Syncing:** Maintaining consistency between the Prisma/PostgreSQL database (off-chain) and the Blockchain (on-chain) was difficult. I had to architect a robust "Draft-to-Active" state machine to ensure agreements only went on-chain after both parties negotiated and approved the terms off-chain.
- **Bridging IDs:** Linking non-numeric Prisma CUIDs to the smart contract’s uint256 reference IDs required a deterministic hashing strategy. This was necessary to allow the frontend to reliably map on-chain events back to the specific agreement records in the database.
- **UX for Web3:** Designing a smooth "one-click" funding experience involved abstracting complex cryptographic signatures behind a simple UI. Balancing the security of Smart Accounts (ERC-4337) with the familiarity of a traditional web interface required deep integration with the Thirdweb SDK.

**FinTech**

**PayCrow** fits the **FinTech** track because it transforms **risky** contract payments into a **secure**, **programmable** flow.

Instead of relying on **trust**, **funds** are locked in **escrow** before work starts, released milestone by milestone, and recorded with a transparent audit trail. This reduces **non-payment** risk for **freelancers**, protects clients from **premature** payouts, and makes dispute resolution faster with evidence-backed decisions and controlled escrow release.

In short, PayCrow is a financial **infrastructure** for modern work: **safer settlement**, l**ower counterparty risk**, and **better cash-flow** confidence for both sides of a transaction.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SolanaSDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/SolanaSDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini-API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini--API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Vega enables users to easily access and execute specialized AI agents through a single chat interface while paying securely with blockchain micropayments. Instead of subscribing to multiple AI tools or services, users can simply connect their wallet, ask questions in plain English, or choose an agent from the marketplace to perform tasks such as market analysis, content generation, or smart contract auditing. Payments are processed through the Solana network and verified on-chain, ensuring transparency and trust.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of Vega, we faced several technical challenges while integrating AI services with blockchain infrastructure. One major challenge was implementing reliable on-chain payment verification on the Solana network to ensure that every AI agent execution only occurs after a valid transaction is confirmed. Handling wallet integration through Phantom and managing transaction signatures from the frontend to the backend also required careful implementation to maintain security and prevent fraudulent requests. Additionally, coordinating real-time AI responses with blockchain transaction confirmation introduced latency challenges, which we addressed by designing a robust verification workflow. Integrating external services such as Google Gemini for AI execution and crypto market data APIs while maintaining a smooth user experience across the marketplace and chat interface was another complexity we successfully overcame.

**Ethereum Track**

Vega aligns strongly with the goals of ETHIndia by demonstrating how blockchain infrastructure can power real-world decentralized applications. The project introduces a Web3-native marketplace where AI agents can be registered, discovered, and executed with transparent on-chain micropayments. By leveraging blockchain technology to verify every payment and execution, the platform removes reliance on centralized payment systems and enables trustless interactions between users and AI services. This approach showcases how decentralized technologies can be combined with AI to create new economic models for developers, where AI agents can operate as independent services and receive payments directly through blockchain transactions.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Vega deserves to win Electrothon because it demonstrates a practical and innovative fusion of AI and Web3 technologies to solve real problems in the AI service ecosystem. Our platform goes beyond a simple prototype by implementing a fully functional marketplace where AI agents can be registered, discovered, and executed with verified on-chain micropayments. By leveraging the intelligence of Gemini and the decentralized infrastructure of Solana, Vega introduces a new economic model where developers can monetize AI agents transparently while users pay only for what they use. This combination of real blockchain transactions, autonomous AI agents, and a seamless user experience demonstrates both technical depth and real-world applicability, making Vega a strong and impactful solution worthy of recognition at Electrothon.

**Electrothon 8.0 Honors Track**

(Best all girls team)
Our team strongly represents the spirit of the Women in Tech honor at Electrothon because Vega was entirely designed and built by an all-girls team tackling complex technologies such as AI, blockchain, and decentralized payments. In a field where female representation is still limited, our team demonstrated strong technical capability by integrating advanced AI from Gemini with decentralized infrastructure on the Solana network to build a fully functional AI agent marketplace. Beyond just building a working product, our team proved that women can lead innovation in emerging technologies like Web3 and AI. By successfully designing the architecture, implementing on-chain verification, and delivering a practical solution, we hope to inspire more women to participate and build in the blockchain and AI ecosystem, which aligns perfectly with the purpose of this honor.

**Nullshot Track**

Vega fits well within the NullShot track by combining AI-powered agents with decentralized blockchain infrastructure to create autonomous, pay-per-use services. The platform allows users to interact with specialized AI agents through a unified chat interface while executing secure micropayments on-chain using the Solana network. By verifying every payment and agent execution directly on the blockchain, the system ensures transparency, trustless transactions, and fair monetization for developers. This demonstrates how AI agents can function as independent digital services in a decentralized ecosystem, which strongly aligns with NullShot’s focus on building intelligent systems that operate natively within Web3 environments.

**IQ AI**

Vega aligns strongly with the goals of the Web3 IQAI track by integrating AI-powered agents with decentralized blockchain payments to build a Web3-native AI service ecosystem. The platform allows developers to publish specialized AI agents that users can discover and execute through a unified chat interface while paying with on-chain micropayments on the Solana network. By combining AI capabilities with transparent blockchain verification, Vega enables trustless execution, fair monetization for developers, and secure pay-per-use AI services. This demonstrates how AI can operate within decentralized systems to create scalable, transparent, and economically sustainable AI marketplaces.

**Solana**

Vega demonstrates an effective use of the Solana ecosystem by leveraging its high throughput and low transaction costs to enable real-time micropayments for AI agent execution. Each interaction with an AI agent requires a verified on-chain SOL transaction, ensuring transparent and trustless payments between users and developers. The platform also records agent registrations and executions through blockchain transactions, creating a verifiable marketplace for AI services. By combining Solana’s fast transaction speeds with wallet integrations such as Phantom, Vega showcases how decentralized infrastructure can support scalable, pay-per-use AI services and enable new economic models for autonomous AI agents.

**Best Use of Gemini 3 [Google Deepmind]**

Vega demonstrates a strong use case for Gemini by leveraging it as the core intelligence behind autonomous AI agents in the platform. Gemini powers the system’s natural language understanding, allowing users to interact with the platform in plain English through a unified chat interface. The model interprets user intent, routes requests to the appropriate specialized AI agent, and generates intelligent responses based on real-time data and agent capabilities. By integrating Gemini with a decentralized payment and verification system on the Solana network, Vega showcases how powerful AI models can be combined with Web3 infrastructure to create scalable, pay-per-use AI services and intelligent agent marketplaces.

Convert PDFs or question papers → CBT tests
Generate flashcards automatically from notes in bulk as well

Provide Kindle-style focused reading mode

Voice commanded for challenged people (mute)
Pomodoro timer to increase efficency
Detailed Test Analysis 
Clean UI
Future -
Community Section , Wake Me Up , Multi Platform App , Kernel based DRM for monitoring of cheating , ML model to check eye contact with camera

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
1️⃣ Accurate PDF & Question Extraction

Converting PDFs or scanned question papers into structured CBT tests was challenging.
Many papers contain mixed layouts, diagrams, and irregular formatting, making extraction difficult.

Ensuring near-zero errors in question parsing while preserving options, numbering, and formatting required careful preprocessing and prompt engineering.

2️⃣ Diagram & Visual Content Handling

Many study materials contain diagrams, graphs, and figures that are important for understanding concepts.

Extracting these elements correctly and maintaining their context with the related questions or notes was difficult, especially when converting documents into structured digital content.

3️⃣ Contextual Doubt Solving

Implementing portion-based doubt solving required the AI to understand only the selected section of notes rather than the entire document.

Maintaining accurate context while keeping responses relevant and concise required tuning prompts and context limits.

4️⃣ Deep Student Learning Analysis

Designing features that could analyze student interaction with study material (notes, tests, flashcards) was complex.

The challenge was structuring data in a way that could eventually support AI-driven insights like weak topic detection, revision suggestions, and performance patterns.

5️⃣ Automation Without Losing Simplicity

The goal was to automate tasks like flashcard creation, test generation, and note explanations while keeping the platform simple and intuitive for students.

Balancing powerful AI automation with a clean user experience was an important design challenge.

**Ethereum Track**

Trustless Academic Integrity: The backend utilizes Web3 infrastructure to interact with the blockchain. When an administrator creates a new live test, the system generates a cryptographic hash of the test content and stores this transaction hash on-chain. This ensures that once an exam is scheduled and published, its questions and parameters cannot be secretly altered.

Immutable Student Submissions: When a test attempt is finalized, a hash of the student's answers and their calculated score is immediately submitted to the blockchain. In an ethHACK context, this is a strong use case for decentralized technology, as it creates an immutable ledger of student performance that prevents post-exam grade manipulation.

Verifiable Auditing: The platform includes dedicated administrative routes specifically designed to verify test integrity against the blockchain record. This demonstrates a practical application of using a public ledger as a source of truth for Web2 applications

**Google Cloud**

Google Cloud Usage in Shingaku

Shingaku leverages multiple Google Cloud technologies to build an AI-driven, automated learning platform.

1️⃣ Google Gemini API

The Gemini API serves as the core intelligence layer of the platform. It is used for multiple AI-driven learning workflows such as:

PDF → CBT Conversion by analyzing question papers and structuring them into digital tests

AI Flashcard Generation from notes for active recall learning

Portion-based Doubt Solving where students select a specific part of their notes and receive contextual explanations

Student Schedule & Academic Calendar Assistance to fetch and organize academic schedules

Test Analysis to interpret student performance and highlight improvement areas

Skill Roadmap Generation where students can request step-by-step learning paths for any skill

Dynamic Quiz Generation allowing quizzes to be created for any topic, even very small subtopics

Gemini’s reasoning and language understanding enable Shingaku to automate study workflows and provide personalized learning assistance.

2️⃣ Google Cloud Text-to-Speech (TTS)

Shingaku integrates Google Cloud TTS to support audio-based learning.

This allows the platform to:

Convert notes or explanations into spoken audio

Enable listening-based revision

Improve accessibility and support different learning styles

3️⃣ Google Cloud VM Instances (Hosting Infrastructure)

The application backend and services are hosted on Google Cloud Virtual Machine instances, which provide:

Reliable cloud hosting for the platform

Scalable infrastructure to handle multiple users

A stable environment for running the backend services and AI integrations

4️⃣ Google Classroom Integration

Shingaku integrates with Google Classroom to streamline academic workflows. Students can automatically fetch assignments, class materials, and academic schedules from their classroom.

Using AI processing, Shingaku can:

Convert classroom materials into flashcards or quizzes

Analyze assignment and test performance

Help students track deadlines and academic schedules

Provide AI-powered explanations for classroom content

This integration ensures that students can directly transform their classroom resources into structured study tools within Shingaku, reducing manual effort and improving learning efficiency.

**ElevenLabs**

How Shingaku Uses ElevenLabs

Shingaku integrates ElevenLabs voice AI to make the learning experience more interactive and accessible through natural speech.

1️⃣ Pronunciation & Audio Explanations

When a student selects a portion of notes or asks a doubt, Shingaku generates an explanation using AI and ElevenLabs converts the response into natural-sounding speech.
This allows students to listen to explanations instead of only reading them.

2️⃣ Flashcard Voice Revision

Flashcards generated from notes can also be read aloud using ElevenLabs, enabling students to revise while listening, which improves retention and supports auditory learning.

3️⃣ Voice-based Doubt Solving

Students can ask doubts using voice input, and the system responds with AI-generated spoken answers, creating a conversational learning experience.

4️⃣ Voice Commands

ElevenLabs enables voice interaction with the platform, allowing students to:

Navigate notes

Ask questions

Request explanations

Trigger flashcard revision

using simple voice commands.

By integrating ElevenLabs, Shingaku transforms traditional studying into a voice-assisted AI learning experience, making studying more interactive, accessible, and hands-free.

### Gas-Aware Yield Optimizer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gasaware-yield-optimizer-1aed) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Ankur17nith/gas-aware-yield-optimizer) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gas-aware-yield-optimizer.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/O88m4e9bEEM?si=Fhy3qKJU56kKLxpa) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Electrothon%208.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://electrothon-8.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Maximise yield of defi investors on stablecoins

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most DeFi dashboards show only APY, which is the interest rate.
But when users move their funds between protocols, they must pay gas fees, and those fees can significantly reduce the real profit.
For example, a pool might show 8% APY, but if you spend a lot on gas while moving funds, the actual return becomes much lower.
Another problem is that users must manually check many protocols and pools to find the best opportunity, and yield rates change frequently.
So users spend time comparing platforms and often miss better opportunities or lose profit due to gas costs.
If a user has to migrate between pools, there are 3-4 steps which consist of withdrawing from on epool, then swapping the tokens if needed and then deposit into another pool. So firstly there are gas costs for each step of the transaction and many times funds get stuck if the transaction fails. Our website allows atomic transaction (all in one step) which minimises the gas cost as well as solves the second issue regarding migration.

Our solution is a gas-aware yield optimizer.
It brings all the pools of all chains such as Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon and Base on one page which makes it easy to compare and invest.
Instead of showing only APY, our platform calculates the net yield after considering gas costs.
We collect yield data from multiple DeFi protocols and rank pools based on actual profitability.
We also include a AI prediction system that analyses yield trends and suggests whether users should move funds now or wait.
Finally, we simplify the process by allowing users to interact with a router smart contract, which can execute optimised strategies more efficiently.
For the beginners, there is also an AI chatbot which would explain the reasoning behind decision making of investing into different pools.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Integrating Real-Time DeFi Data

One of the main challenges was collecting accurate and up-to-date DeFi pool data such as APY, liquidity (TVL), and token information from multiple sources. Different protocols expose data differently, so we had to normalize the data structure before comparing pools across platforms.

2. Calculating Net Yield After Gas Costs

Most DeFi dashboards only show raw APY, but our system calculates gas-adjusted net yield. This required building a model that estimates the gas cost of migrating funds between pools and subtracting it from the potential yield gain. Designing this logic so that recommendations remained realistic was a significant challenge.

3. Multi-Chain Gas Tracking

Gas behaves differently across chains such as Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, and Base. Fetching gas prices from different APIs and displaying them correctly for each chain required building a chain-aware backend system and handling multiple RPC endpoints.

4. Building the AI DeFi Assistant

Integrating the Gemini API into the platform required designing prompts and context pipelines so the assistant could answer questions using live platform data instead of generic responses. Ensuring the assistant gave useful explanations about pools, APY, and migration strategies was challenging.

5. Synchronizing Backend Data With the UI

Another challenge was ensuring the frontend dashboard updated correctly when data such as pool rankings, gas prices, or predictions changed. We had to carefully design APIs and state management so that the user interface reflected real-time analytics.

6. Designing an Intuitive User Experience

DeFi tools are often difficult for beginners to understand. We focused on presenting complex metrics like APY, gas impact, and migration decisions in a way that is simple and actionable for users.

**Ethereum Track**

Our project, Gas-Aware Yield Optimizer, fits the Ethereum track by building an AI-powered DeFi analytics platform that operates on Ethereum and Ethereum-compatible networks.

The platform analyzes yield opportunities across Ethereum-based DeFi protocols such as Curve, Compound, and Yearn. These protocols operate through Ethereum smart contracts, and our system evaluates their pools by collecting on-chain and protocol data including APY, liquidity (TVL), and token information.

A key feature of the platform is gas-aware yield optimization. Since Ethereum transaction fees significantly affect DeFi profitability, our system integrates real-time Ethereum gas data using gas tracking APIs and calculates gas-adjusted net yield instead of relying only on raw APY. This allows the platform to determine whether migrating funds between pools will actually increase a user’s net returns after accounting for Ethereum transaction costs.

The application also integrates Ethereum wallet connectivity through MetaMask, allowing users to interact with the platform using their Ethereum address. Migration strategies and pool comparisons are designed around Ethereum-based DeFi smart contracts and transaction mechanics.

In addition, the system includes a Gas Timing Optimizer that analyzes Ethereum gas trends over time to determine the most efficient time to execute DeFi transactions.

By combining on-chain DeFi analytics, Ethereum gas awareness, and wallet-based interaction, the platform demonstrates how intelligent tools can help users optimize yield strategies within the Ethereum ecosystem.

**Electrothon 8.0 Honors Track**

the team consists of all first year members

**IQ AI**

Our project, Gas-Aware Yield Optimizer, fits the IQ AI track by implementing an autonomous DeFi strategy agent that analyzes yield opportunities across multiple protocols and chains.

The platform continuously monitors DeFi pools across protocols such as Curve, Compound, and Yearn and evaluates them based on multiple factors including gross APY, gas costs, liquidity (TVL), and estimated net yield. Instead of simply ranking pools by APY, the system calculates a gas-adjusted yield score and determines whether migrating funds will actually increase the user’s profit.

The AI strategy agent performs continuous scoring of available pools and generates a migration decision such as “Migrate” or “Hold.” This decision is based on predicted net yield improvement, gas costs, and liquidity stability. The system also estimates migration probability and provides a reasoning layer explaining the decision.

In addition to strategy optimization, the platform includes a DeFi AI assistant powered by Gemini that acts as a conversational interface for users. The assistant can answer questions about pools, APY, gas fees, and migration strategies while referencing live platform data.

By combining real-time DeFi analytics, gas-aware yield optimization, and an autonomous strategy agent, our platform demonstrates how AI agents can assist users in making smarter decentralized finance decisions.

**Google Cloud**

Our platform uses the Gemini API to power an intelligent DeFi assistant inside the Gas-Aware Yield Optimizer.  Gemini acts as a real-time DeFi copilot that helps users understand blockchain concepts and make better yield decisions. More importantly, Gemini analyzes live platform data such as pool APY, TVL, risk level, and gas costs to provide strategy recommendations. When users ask questions like “Which pool should I use?” or “Should I migrate now?”, the assistant evaluates real pool data from the backend APIs and explains the optimal strategy in simple language.  Gemini also integrates with the Gas Timing Optimizer, which uses live Ethereum gas data to determine the best time to migrate funds between pools. The assistant can explain migration decisions, gas impact, and estimated savings.  By combining real-time DeFi analytics with Gemini’s reasoning and explanation capabilities, the platform becomes an AI-powered DeFi copilot that helps users make smarter yield optimization decisions.

> Privacy-first P2P dec. collaborative platform

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

- Privacy-first collaborative docs lets people co-edit documents without storing plaintext content on a central server.
- User can login using social logins and optional wallet connection. For every user GhostID will be created so that there identity remains completely non-exposed. User can create public and private documents, only public documents are searchable. User will remain completely non-exposed using peerIDs, they can edit docs, chat during live sessions while non-exposed.
- Safer identity model, combines login + optional wallet binding, but uses GhostID in collaboration so raw wallet identity is not exposed in normal flows.
- Decentralized real-time editing, uses peer-to-peer session sync for presence, chat, cursor/events, reducing dependence on a single relay/server path.
- supports private, link-based, and public access modes for docs sharing
- Better trust boundary by keeping backend minimal (metadata, permissions, access checks) while pushing sensitive content handling to client-side encryption.
- Useful for teams handling sensitive notes/specs especially where auditability, ownership control, and resilience matter more than convenience-only cloud docs

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/edf94b25080648e68db0bafbc7e17384/0be444ff-4cb2-435f-a1f3-d420db7c36e3.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

- Browser P2P connectivity was unstable (frequent dial failures): fixed by adding better relay target selection, peer hints, retry backoff/muting, and diagnostics to see failure reasons.
- Early collaboration encryption design caused cross-peer decrypt issues: solved by switching from per-peer token secret usage to a shared per-document session key.
- Pubsub behavior in sparse sessions caused noisy failures: treated zero-subscriber publish errors as transient and enabled safer publish behavior to avoid false fatal states.
- Concurrent editing merge quality had edge cases: improved local edit handling to smaller text deltas and added periodic full-state sync for late joiners.
- Auth versus anonymous link-join flow conflicted: updated join flow to support access-token joins with GhostID fallback while still enforcing role checks.
- Async collaboration tests were flaky: replaced short fixed waits with polling/wait-for style checks so integration tests stay stable under load.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

- Built on Fileverse as the decentralized document backend, so users can create, update, search, and share documents through API/CLI while keeping data portable and censorship-resistant
- Makes document workflows safer by storing encrypted content and publishing asynchronously, reducing dependence on a single centralized storage provider.
- Implemented fileverse API for encryption and decryption of docs, which is also supported in P2P docs editing.
