### Axylosdotxyz
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/axylosdotxyz-9ea1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/debojyoti10CC/axylosfirstdraft) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://axylos-new-24rq.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/IJzqQsDTQio?si=5CxaQmlMUOZdD5zc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Automated agent negotiation Protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, most digital services require manual coordination between users, platforms, and payment systems. Even when two systems want to interact programmatically, they still rely on fixed pricing models, centralized APIs, and manual payment flows. This creates friction for machine-to-machine interactions and prevents autonomous agents from directly purchasing or selling services.

Axylos addresses this by enabling autonomous agents to discover each other, negotiate service prices, and settle payments automatically. Instead of fixed pricing or human involvement, agents dynamically negotiate using strategy-based decision logic and reach agreements in real time.

Once an agreement is reached, the service endpoint enforces payment using the HTTP 402 standard, allowing the buyer agent to automatically settle the payment and receive authorization to access the service. This removes the need for manual payment handling and enables fully automated service transactions between software agents.

By combining decentralized peer discovery, automated negotiation, and programmable payments, Axylos demonstrates how autonomous systems can directly coordinate and transact with each other without relying on centralized platforms.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges during development was implementing the **HTTP 402 payment flow using Elsa x402**. Initially, the client could detect the `402 Payment Required` response, but correctly extracting the `x-402-payment-request` header and retrying the request with the proper **L402 authorization token** required careful handling. The request pipeline had to be modified so the client could automatically intercept the payment challenge, complete the payment, and resend the request with the correct credentials.

Another challenge was coordinating **autonomous negotiation between agents** in a decentralized environment. Since agents communicate over a peer-to-peer mesh network, managing negotiation states (ACTIVE, COUNTER, ACCEPTED, REJECTED) while keeping both nodes synchronized required designing a reliable state machine and message handling logic.

Debugging the interaction between the negotiation layer, the payment challenge, and the final service execution was also tricky. At times the system returned fixed responses instead of triggering the payment flow correctly. This was resolved by restructuring the request handlers and ensuring that the negotiation outcome correctly propagated into the service layer before the payment challenge was issued.

Through iterative testing using multiple terminal instances (buyer and seller nodes), these issues were resolved, resulting in a stable end-to-end workflow where agents can negotiate, trigger the 402 payment challenge, complete the payment, and successfully execute the service.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

Axylos implements an autonomous agent negotiation and settlement protocol that directly integrates **Elsa x402** and **Elsa OpenClaw** capabilities.

Agents in the network discover each other over a decentralized P2P mesh and autonomously negotiate service prices using a strategy-based negotiation engine. Once a price is agreed upon, the service endpoint is protected using the **HTTP 402 payment flow**, where the buyer agent receives an `x-402-payment-request` header and automatically settles the payment using the Elsa x402 protocol.

The payment client retrieves the **L402 token (macaroon + preimage)** and retries the request with authorization, unlocking the service. OpenClaw agents then execute the negotiated action, enabling verifiable on-chain settlement via blockchain transactions.

This demonstrates a full machine-to-machine commerce loop: **agent discovery → autonomous negotiation → x402 payment → L402 authorization → service execution**, showcasing a practical use of Elsa’s programmable payment infrastructure and OpenClaw autonomous agents.

**Projects building with the SDK to solve real-world problems will be eligible**

Axylos uses the **HeyElsa SDK** to enable autonomous machine-to-machine commerce through programmable payments and agent-based execution. The project integrates **Elsa x402** to enforce payment-gated APIs, allowing services to require payment using the HTTP 402 standard before execution.

When a buyer agent requests a service, the seller endpoint returns a `402 Payment Required` response with an `x-402-payment-request`. The Elsa payment client then automatically processes the payment and retrieves the **L402 authorization token**, which is used to retry the request and unlock the service.

The project also integrates **OpenClaw agents** to interpret requests and execute actions such as DeFi transactions once payment is verified. This demonstrates a practical real-world use case for the HeyElsa SDK: enabling autonomous agents to discover services, negotiate terms, pay for access, and execute actions without human intervention.

### ENS-folio
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ensfolio-0b78) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aneleldho06/ens_portfolio) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/N9ZcBk9nIqY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turn your ENS into a Web3 resume.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem it Solves

In the Web3 ecosystem, a person’s contributions and reputation are fragmented across multiple platforms.

Developers, DAO contributors, and community members leave their digital footprint in many different places such as:

Wallet transactions on block explorers

NFT collections across marketplaces

GitHub repositories

DAO governance participation

Hackathon projects

POAP badges from events

Because this data is scattered, understanding someone’s Web3 identity requires manually checking many different platforms like Etherscan, GitHub, Snapshot, and NFT marketplaces.

This creates several problems:

❌ Difficult for recruiters or collaborators to evaluate Web3 builders

❌ No unified way to showcase on-chain reputation

❌ Web3 contributors lack a simple portfolio or resume

❌ Identity in Web3 is tied to wallets, but wallets don't present meaningful context

As a result, Web3 still lacks a simple, unified identity layer similar to LinkedIn or a personal portfolio in Web2.

How ENS-folio Solves This

ENS-folio transforms ENS names into decentralized Web3 portfolios.

By simply entering an ENS name, the platform automatically aggregates important on-chain and developer data into a single unified profile page.

Each ENS profile can showcase:

🧾 Wallet address and on-chain activity

🖼 NFT collections

🎟 POAP badges from events and hackathons

🏛 DAO participation and governance activity

💻 Projects and developer contributions

🔗 Social links like GitHub and Twitter

This makes it easy for anyone to instantly understand a person’s Web3 reputation and work.

What People Can Use It For

ENS-folio makes several existing tasks much easier and more transparent:

🧑‍💻 For Developers

Create a Web3-native resume

Showcase hackathons, NFTs, and on-chain activity

Share a single ENS-based portfolio link

🏢 For Companies & DAOs

Quickly evaluate developers and contributors

Verify real on-chain reputation

Discover active Web3 builders

🌐 For the Web3 Community

Build credible decentralized identities

Make Web3 contributions more visible

Create shareable ENS-powered personal pages

Why This Matters

ENS-folio helps bridge the gap between wallet-based identity and real reputation in Web3.

Instead of scattered data across platforms, your ENS name becomes your unified Web3 identity and portfolio.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was resolving ENS names reliably and linking them to the correct wallet address. ENS resolution requires interacting with Ethereum mainnet, while our smart contract for profile storage was deployed on Base Sepolia. Managing data across multiple networks initially caused inconsistencies in fetching profile and wallet data.

To solve this, we separated the data flow: ENS names are resolved using an Ethereum mainnet RPC provider, while profile data is fetched from our smart contract deployed on Base Sepolia. This clear separation of network responsibilities ensured reliable ENS resolution while still allowing users to store and own their profile data on Base.

Another challenge was aggregating data from multiple APIs such as NFTs, POAP badges, and wallet activity. Each API returned data in different formats, so we had to normalize the responses before displaying them in the UI. By creating a small data processing layer in the frontend, we were able to standardize the data and present it in a clean portfolio interface.

### Pramaan
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pramaan-9430) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dev4057/Pramaan.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/aWksmXc-a2k) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decentralised identity verification platform

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Gig Economy's "Invisible" Credit Problem
Millions of gig workers (freelancers, Uber drivers, delivery partners) are locked out of traditional financial systems. Because they lack standard corporate salary slips or established credit histories, lenders view them as "high risk."

To prove their creditworthiness today, workers are forced to hand over highly sensitive, raw bank statements and personal IDs. This leads to massive data privacy risks, identity theft vulnerabilities, and heavy human bias in loan approvals.

How Pramaan Solves This
Pramaan is a privacy-first Web3 credit passport. We transform gig workers' off-chain reputations into verifiable, on-chain credit scores without ever exposing their underlying personal data.

What people can use it for:

Gig Workers: Can mint a portable "Gig Score" by cryptographically proving their identity and their income history.

DeFi & TradFi Lenders: Can instantly verify a worker's creditworthiness and disburse loans without doing manual, biased background checks.

How it makes existing tasks easier, safer, and completely trustless:

100% Privacy-Preserving (Zero-Knowledge): Workers prove their identity (via Anon Aadhaar) and income (via Reclaim Protocol) without revealing their actual Aadhaar number, name, or raw bank transaction history.

Eradicating Human Bias: Credit analysis is performed by a Local Autonomous AI Agent (OpenClaw + Llama 3). The AI audits the ZK-proofs deterministically, ensuring loan recommendations are based purely on math and on-chain facts.

Machine-to-Machine API Economy (x402): Lenders don't need expensive monthly Web2 SaaS subscriptions to access credit bureaus. Using the x402 Micropayment Protocol, the Lender's application autonomously pays a 0.05 USDC micro-fee per request. The protocol instantly settles the payment on Base Sepolia and unlocks the AI credit analysis in real-time.

Decentralized Data Portability: Heavy metadata and detailed proof contexts are packed into user-owned dDocs and stored on Fileverse, rather than bloating the EVM, giving workers total sovereign control over their credit data.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Pramaan was a massive architectural challenge because it required stitching together several cutting-edge Web3 protocols into a single, seamless user experience.
1. Taming Zero-Knowledge Proofs & Gas Limits
Integrating both Anon Aadhaar (for identity) and Reclaim Protocol (for income verification) meant dealing with complex cryptographic payloads. One of our biggest hurdles was managing the sheer size of the ZK-proofs and ensuring they could be verified on-chain without the transactions failing. At one point, our proof submissions triggered a massive 21,000,000 gas limit error! We had to carefully debug our smart contract require statements, manage our nullifiers for replay protection, and refine our gas estimations to get the transactions to flow smoothly on Sepolia.

2. The Multi-Protocol Integration Puzzle
We weren't just building a simple dApp; we were building a multi-layered pipeline. We had to get Fileverse to instantly store our proof metadata as encrypted dDocs, while Base Sepolia handled the core smart contract logic. The absolute biggest roadblock hit when we tried to integrate the OpenClaw AI Agent—the official NPM registry for the core packages was throwing 404 errors. Instead of giving up, we reverse-engineered the x402 protocol and built our own autonomous payment interceptor from scratch using viem, Node.js, and a local Ollama LLM.

3. The Power of the Hacker Community
When you are trying to make disparate Web3 technologies talk to each other at 4:00 AM, documentation only gets you so far. These critical blockers were overcome thanks to the incredible, hands-on support from the sponsor engineers, mentors, and the collaborative energy of the ETH Mumbai community. Whether it was identifying a misconfigured RPC node or figuring out the proper data formatting for a specific protocol, the guidance we received was the exact push we needed to cross the finish line with a fully functional product.

**Privacy**

Pramaan: The Privacy-First ZK Credit Passport for the Gig Economy
The Vision
Millions of gig workers (Uber drivers, freelancers, delivery partners) are systematically locked out of the DeFi and TradFi lending markets. Because they lack corporate salary slips, they are forced to hand over highly sensitive, raw bank statements and government IDs to prove their creditworthiness—exposing them to massive data harvesting, privacy breaches, and human bias.

Pramaan is built to solve this. We are a 100% privacy-preserving Web3 credit protocol that transforms off-chain gig reputation into an immutable, on-chain "GigScore."

Why Pramaan is the Ultimate Privacy Architecture:
We built a completely trustless, multi-layered privacy stack native to the Ethereum ecosystem:

Zero-Knowledge Identity (Anon Aadhaar): Workers prove they are citizens over 18 without ever revealing their actual Aadhaar number, name, or biometric data to the smart contract or the lender.

Zero-Knowledge Income (Reclaim Protocol): Workers generate cryptographic proofs of their gig earnings (e.g., from Uber or SBI) directly from the Web2 source. The smart contract verifies the ZK-proof, completely abstracting away the raw transaction history.

Decentralized Data Sovereignty (Fileverse): Instead of bloating the EVM with metadata or using centralized AWS databases, the heavy proof contexts are encrypted and packed into user-owned dDocs on Fileverse, giving the worker total sovereign control over who views their data.

Local AI Auditing (OpenClaw + Llama 3): To completely eliminate human bias and third-party data leakage, the credit risk analysis is performed by a local Autonomous AI Agent. Zero worker data is ever sent to cloud providers like OpenAI. * Machine-to-Machine API Economy (x402): To access the AI's credit insights, the Lender's application must autonomously execute a micro-payment (0.05 USDC) on Base Sepolia using the x402 protocol. The agent detects the EVM transaction, runs the local LLM analysis on the ZK proofs, and mints the final GigScore on-chain.

The ETH Mumbai Impact
Pramaan represents the true ethos of Ethereum: giving power and privacy back to the user. By combining Zero-Knowledge cryptography, decentralized storage, autonomous machine-to-machine micropayments, and local AI, we have created a completely private financial primitive.

Gig workers finally have a portable, bias-free Web3 credit score, and lenders can deploy capital safely—all without a single piece of raw Personal Identifiable Information (PII) ever touching a public server.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

How Pramaan Integrates Fileverse for Sovereign Data Portability
Storing rich metadata and heavy Zero-Knowledge proof payloads directly on the EVM is prohibitively expensive and rigid. To solve this, Pramaan utilizes Fileverse as our decentralized, user-owned data availability layer, perfectly executing a "Compute on-chain, Store on Fileverse" architecture.

1. Dynamic dDoc Generation for ZK-Proofs
Whenever a gig worker completes a verification step—whether it's proving their identity via Anon Aadhaar or their income via the Reclaim Protocol—the raw cryptographic proof payloads, metadata, and timestamps are packaged into a JSON object. Our backend seamlessly pushes this object to a Fileverse node, which encrypts and stores the data, returning a unique dDoc ID.

2. The Smart Contract Anchor
Instead of bloating our Base Sepolia smart contract, we only mint the final computed "GigScore" and the lightweight Fileverse dDoc ID on-chain. The blockchain acts as the immutable anchor of truth, while Fileverse acts as the rich, decentralized "Pramaan Passport" that actually holds the worker's data context.

3. Seamless Data Portability & UX
We integrated Fileverse directly into the frontend user experience. Once a worker's Passport is generated, the UI dynamically fetches their specific dDoc IDs. We built sleek "View Identity dDoc" and "View Income dDoc" buttons that bridge users directly to the Fileverse document viewer.

4. Why this matters for the Gig Economy
By using Fileverse, we give workers true data sovereignty. Their sensitive verification proofs aren't sitting in a centralized AWS database; they are stored as user-owned dDocs. The worker can selectively share their specific Fileverse document links with decentralized lenders, proving their creditworthiness without exposing their raw, underlying personal data to the public.

How Pramaan Leverages Base for On-Chain Privacy
Traditional credit systems force gig workers to hand over sensitive, raw data (government IDs, bank statements) to centralized entities. Pramaan flips this model by combining Zero-Knowledge (ZK) cryptography with the Base network to act as our secure, privacy-preserving settlement layer.

1. Zero-Knowledge State Management on Base
Instead of storing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) on a public ledger, Pramaan uses Anon Aadhaar and Reclaim Protocol to generate ZK-proofs for identity and income. The smart contract we deployed on Base never receives raw data. It only receives cryptographic commitments and the final computed "GigScore". Anyone inspecting the Base block explorer will only see hashes and a numerical score, ensuring 100% data privacy for the worker while providing verifiable trust to lenders.

2. Privacy-First AI Micropayments (x402 Protocol)
To analyze this ZK-data without leaking it to centralized cloud AI providers, we built a local, autonomous AI agent. We specifically chose Base to handle the agent's x402 machine-to-machine micropayments (0.05 USDC per risk analysis request). Base's sub-cent gas fees and lightning-fast block times make this micro-transaction economy actually viable. The agent autonomously pays the fee on Base Sepolia, which unlocks a local Llama 3 LLM to generate credit insights completely privately on the host machine.

3. The Ultimate Web3 Credit Passport
By using Base as our immutable truth layer, we achieved a perfect privacy architecture:

Compute: Kept local and private (Ollama).

Identity: Kept anonymous (ZK-Proofs).

Settlement & Scoring: Immutable, fast, and cheap (Base).

Base enabled us to build a high-frequency, machine-to-machine lending protocol where gig workers have total sovereign control over their financial privacy.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

How Pramaan Integrates HeyElsa & OpenClaw
Pramaan fully embodies the HeyElsa vision of a decentralized, machine-to-machine AI economy. We utilized the OpenClaw architecture to build an autonomous, privacy-first "Credit Auditor Agent" that evaluates a gig worker's Zero-Knowledge proofs without human bias.

1. Engineering the x402 Protocol from Scratch
During the hackathon, we encountered registry 404 errors with the official @openclaw/core NPM packages. Instead of pivoting, we reverse-engineered the OpenClaw specification and built a custom autonomous agent runtime using Node.js and Viem. When our backend requests a credit analysis, the API throws a strict HTTP 402 Payment Required error.

2. Autonomous Machine Micropayments
Our backend agent does not crash when it hits this paywall. It reads the custom headers, accesses its own machine wallet, and autonomously signs a smart contract transaction—paying a 0.05 USDC micro-fee on Base Sepolia. It then takes the transaction hash and uses it as the cryptographic x-payment-proof to unlock the API.

3. Privacy-Preserving Local AI Intelligence
Once the x402 payment is verified, the agent doesn't send sensitive worker data to OpenAI. Instead, it triggers a local Llama 3 model (via Ollama). The LLM deterministically audits the verified ZK-proofs (Anon Aadhaar identity & Reclaim income) and generates a professional, tamper-proof GigScore and risk insight.

By building this, we successfully demonstrated an end-to-end HeyElsa use case: An autonomous AI agent that possesses its own wallet, encounters a paywall, and spends crypto to unlock the compute power it needs to help a human user.

**The problem it solves**

Crypto investors lack a secure way to automate investment strategies without giving up custody of their funds; we are tyring to  solve that via autostack; AutoStack lets you set up recurring token purchases without depositing funds into a vault or trusting a centralized service. You grant a time-bounded, amount-limited permission to a smart contract, and it executes swaps on your behalf at the frequency you specify.

The key difference from existing DCA solutions: your tokens never leave your wallet until the moment of each swap. No lockups, no custody risk.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Implementing Advanced Wallet Permissions 

Integrating ERC-7715 through the MetaMask Smart Accounts Kit was challenging because the ecosystem is still new.

Issues included:

Limited documentation

Handling session accounts securely

Ensuring permission limits (amount + duration) were enforced correctly

Managing permission expiry

This required careful testing to prevent accidental over-permissioning.

2. Designing a Non-Custodial Automation Model 

Most DCA protocols simply hold funds in a vault.
Building automation while keeping funds in the user’s wallet required a different architecture.

Key difficulties:

Triggering swaps without traditional custody

Managing periodic permissions

Ensuring swaps only execute within allowed limits

3. Integrating Smart Money Signals 

Pulling whale trading signals from Nansen added complexity.

Challenges included:

Designing a reliable trigger system

Filtering meaningful whale activity

Preventing spam signals

Balancing signal thresholds vs execution speed

4. HTTP Micropayments Integration 

Using the x402 Protocol required implementing a new payment flow.

Problems encountered:

Handling HTTP 402 payment responses

Processing small USDC micropayments on Solana

Avoiding repeated payments with caching

5. Real-Time Indexing for the Dashboard 

Keeping the frontend synced with blockchain activity required building a real-time indexer using Envio HyperIndex.

Challenges:

Designing efficient event indexing

Updating strategy execution data instantly

Avoiding slow polling-based updates

6. Managing Cross-Chain Components 

The system interacts with multiple ecosystems:

Smart contracts on Base

Whale data via Nansen

Micropayments on Solana

Coordinating these components introduced latency and reliability challenges.

Modern smart cities rely heavily on connected digital infrastructure such as IoT sensors, smart traffic systems, public Wi-Fi, surveillance cameras, energy grids, and transportation networks. While these technologies improve efficiency and convenience, they also create a massive cybersecurity attack surface. A single vulnerability in one system can allow attackers to disrupt critical services, steal sensitive data, or even endanger public safety.

Traditional cybersecurity systems are often reactive and fragmented. They require human operators to monitor multiple dashboards, analyze alerts, and manually respond to incidents. In large city environments with millions of connected devices, this approach is slow, inefficient, and prone to human error. As a result, threats such as ransomware attacks, IoT botnets, network intrusions, and data breaches can spread before security teams are able to react.

Cyber-X Shield Agentic AI OS solves this problem by introducing an autonomous, AI-driven cybersecurity platform designed specifically for smart city ecosystems. Instead of relying solely on human monitoring, the system deploys multiple intelligent AI agents that continuously observe network traffic, device behavior, and infrastructure activity across the city.

These agents can detect anomalies, identify cyber threats, and automatically respond in real time, isolating compromised systems before they impact essential services. This drastically reduces response time from hours to seconds and helps prevent widespread damage.

🧑‍💻 What People Can Use It For

Monitors and protects millions of sensors, cameras, and smart devices deployed across the city.

Continuously scans networks to detect suspicious activity or abnormal behavior.

Automated incident response

Instantly isolates compromised devices and blocks malicious traffic.

Protects sensitive citizen data stored in government systems.

### Vision Suite
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vision-suite-fa5a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SourabhSingh-dev/Vision-Suite) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/3bIOeYCEH4g?si=P2MzVXXMDFltj4V1) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Solve the Fit, Stop the Return

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![SocketJs](https://img.shields.io/badge/SocketJs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Online clothing shopping has a major challenge: customers cannot accurately determine whether a garment will fit them before purchasing it. Most e-commerce platforms rely on standard size charts (S, M, L, etc.), but these sizes vary widely across brands and often do not reflect an individual’s body shape. Because of this uncertainty, customers frequently order multiple sizes or end up returning items that do not fit properly.
This leads to a very high return rate in the fashion industry, which creates significant problems for both businesses and consumers. Retailers lose money due to shipping, restocking, and reverse logistics, while customers experience frustration and inconvenience when they have to repeatedly return products.
Existing solutions typically recommend sizes based on simple inputs like height, weight, or previous purchases, which are often not accurate enough to predict real fit. As a result, shoppers are still forced to guess whether a garment will fit them.
This project addresses the problem by helping users determine whether a specific garment will fit their body before purchasing it, reducing guesswork, returns, and improving the overall online shopping experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of this project, we faced several technical and practical challenges. One of the biggest challenges was accurately estimating body measurements from a single image. Human body reconstruction from 2D images is complex because depth information is missing, and factors such as camera angle, clothing, and lighting conditions can affect the accuracy of the measurements.
Another challenge was measuring garments from product images. Most e-commerce product images are not perfectly flat or standardized, which makes it difficult to extract precise garment dimensions. Variations in image resolution, perspective distortion, and wrinkles in clothing can introduce measurement errors when converting pixel distances into real-world measurements.
Integrating multiple AI components into one pipeline was also challenging.

> Blockchain platform for MSME invoice financing

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Small and medium businesses often face serious cash-flow problems because they do not receive payments immediately after delivering goods or services. Instead, buyers usually pay after 30 to 90 days through invoices. During this waiting period, businesses still need money to pay salaries, buy raw materials, and run daily operations.

Traditional financing options like bank loans are often slow, complex, and difficult for small businesses to access due to strict requirements, paperwork, and credit history checks. As a result, many MSMEs struggle to get quick liquidity even when they have legitimate unpaid invoices.

At the same time, investors who might be willing to fund these invoices often lack trust, transparency, and reliable verification mechanisms to ensure that the invoices are genuine and that payments will be made.

Because of this, invoice financing markets suffer from problems such as:

Fraudulent or duplicate invoices

Lack of transparency between businesses and investors

Slow verification and onboarding processes

Limited access to financing for small businesses

This project aims to solve these issues by creating a secure and transparent digital platform where verified invoices can be financed quickly. By combining AI-based verification, multi-source validation (such as tax records, logistics data, and buyer confirmation), and blockchain-based transparency, the platform reduces fraud risk and builds trust between businesses and investors.

As a result, MSMEs can access faster working capital, while investors gain a transparent and structured way to fund real economic transactions.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of this project, our team encountered several technical and real-world challenges that required careful consideration and research.

One of the main challenges was understanding the regulatory and compliance landscape surrounding invoice financing. Financial systems involve strict regulations, identity verification, and onboarding processes, which can take months in real-world deployments. Designing a prototype that demonstrates the concept while still considering these regulatory realities required balancing practicality with innovation.

Another major challenge was ensuring invoice authenticity and preventing fraud. Since not all invoices are registered through government systems such as GST, relying on a single verification source was not sufficient. To address this, we designed a multi-layer verification approach that combines tax data checks, logistics validation, and buyer confirmation to improve trust and reduce the risk of fraudulent invoices.

We also faced challenges in designing a trustworthy marketplace for investors and businesses. Creating a system where investors feel confident funding invoices requires transparency, risk scoring, and clear transaction records. Integrating blockchain concepts with a user-friendly interface while keeping the platform understandable for non-technical users was an important design challenge.

Additionally, user onboarding and verification (KYB) posed another challenge. Real-world onboarding processes involve significant documentation and verification costs. Our approach explored how third-party verification APIs and automated validation could help reduce friction and make the platform scalable.

Finally, translating a complex financial workflow into a simple and intuitive user experience required several design iterations. We focused on building a clear flow that allows businesses to upload invoices, verify them, and connect with investors efficiently.

**Requestly – Creative Use Challenge**

Our platform relies heavily on multiple external APIs for verifying invoices, validating business information, and simulating financial transaction flows. During development, tools like Requestly are extremely valuable for testing and debugging these integrations.

Since real-world services such as GST verification, logistics validation, and identity verification APIs may not always be accessible during development, Requestly allows us to intercept and mock API responses. This helps us simulate different scenarios such as successful invoice verification, failed validation, or delayed responses from external services.

By using Requestly’s request interception and response modification capabilities, we can test how our system behaves under different API conditions without relying on live production systems. This makes development faster, improves debugging, and ensures our platform handles external integrations reliably.

Therefore, Requestly plays an important role in helping us build, test, and simulate API-driven verification workflows that are essential for our invoice financing platform.

**The problem it solves**

**Problem Statement:**
Many traditional voting systems rely on centralized databases where results are stored privately. This can create concerns about transparency, as voters cannot easily verify how votes are counted, and there is always a risk of manual errors or manipulation. As a result, trust in digital voting systems can be limited.

**Solution:**
VaultVote is a decentralized voting platform that uses blockchain to make the voting process secure and transparent. Each vote is recorded through a smart contract, ensuring that every voter can vote only once and that votes cannot be changed or deleted after submission. The results are publicly verifiable on the blockchain.

**Tech Stack:**
VaultVote uses Solidity smart contracts deployed on the Base Sepolia testnet. The frontend is built with React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, while Wagmi, Viem, and ConnectKit enable smooth wallet connection and interaction with the blockchain.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, our team encountered a few practical challenges while collaborating on the project. Since multiple team members were working on the same repository, we experienced Git merge conflicts, which required careful coordination to resolve overlapping code changes and maintain a stable codebase. Another challenge was attempting to integrate a chatbot feature using n8n workflow automation to help users understand candidate policies. Setting up the automation workflows and connecting them smoothly with our existing system required experimentation and debugging. Despite these challenges, they helped us improve our teamwork, problem-solving, and integration skills throughout the hackathon.

### Unite Bharat
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/unite-bharat-0a99) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/KaushikChan2007/Unite-Bharat.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ZZQIDaINS5U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> "Unite Bharat: One Nation. One App

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Why Unite Bharat?
We built Unite Bharat because we believe essential services shouldn't be hard to find. Whether you’re a farmer planning the next harvest, a student looking for a scholarship, or just someone trying to navigate daily life, this platform brings everything you need together in one place.

Here is how Unite Bharat can make your life a little easier—and a lot safer:

**# For Farmers (Kisan Sathi)**
Farming is tough, but getting the right information shouldn't be.

What you can do: Snap a picture of a sick plant, and our Crop Doctor will instantly tell you what’s wrong and how to fix it. You can check daily Mandi prices before you sell, look up hyper-local weather to plan your day, and even find government subsidies you might have missed.
How it helps: It saves you the time (and money) of traveling to experts or markets just to get information. Plus, catching crop diseases early means you protect your harvest before it’s too late.
*# For Your Health (Swasthya Sathi)*****
Healthcare should be accessible, not confusing.

What you can do: Not feeling well? Use our AI Symptom Checker to figure out your next steps before rushing to a clinic. You can easily locate the nearest hospitals in an emergency, scan your medicines to make sure they’re genuine (and check the side effects), and keep all your family’s medical records securely saved on your phone.
How it helps: You’ll never have to carry physical folders of medical history again. Most importantly, the medicine scanner keeps you safe from accidentally taking counterfeit drugs or the wrong dosage.
# For Students & Learners (Vidya Sathi)
Education is the key to progress, and we want to help you unlock it.

What you can do: Stuck on homework at 2 AM? Our AI Tutor is available 24/7 to help explain concepts. You can also take free courses, easily find scholarships you qualify for without digging through hundreds of websites, and even use the "Skill Swap" to trade knowledge with people in your community (like offering math tutoring in exchange for coding lessons).
How it helps: Finding scholarships is usually a massive headache—we do the heavy lifting for you. The Skill Swap also gives you a safe, verified place to learn from your neighbors without relying on sketchy online classifieds.
# For Everyday Citizens (Shehri Sathi)
Dealing with bureaucracy and city living is stressful enough. We simplify it.

What you can do: Keep digital copies of your vital IDs securely in your pocket. See a massive pothole or a broken streetlight? Snap a photo and report it directly to the local authorities through the app. You can also verify official documents to prevent fraud and check local transit schedules so you aren't left waiting at the bus stop.
How it helps: It means fewer trips to government offices and less waiting in line. Having secure, verified digital documents also means you never have to panic about losing your physical IDs while traveling.
In short: Unite Bharat isn't just an app; it's your digital companion for a better, safer, and simpler tomorrow.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our Biggest Hurdle: Making the AI Actually Talk to Us
One of the coolest features of Unite Bharat is our AI Tutor and Crop Doctor. To make them smart, we integrated Google’s Gemini API. It sounded simple: ask the AI a question, get an answer.

The Bug: Instead of answers, our bot was giving us the silent treatment. When users tried to ask a question, the app just showed an endless loading spinner. Behind the scenes, the server was quietly crashing with "Permission Denied" and "Model Not Found" errors.

How We Fixed It: It turns out the AI ecosystem moves ridiculously fast. We were accidentally asking an older version of the AI to do the work, and our security keys weren't being loaded properly when the app started up.

We fixed it by doing two things:

Locking the doors: We completely rewrote how our app handles its secret API keys so they load securely the exact second the server turns on.
Preparing for the worst: We realized we couldn't just trust the AI to always be perfect. We added "safety nets" so that if the AI ever goes down again, the app won't freeze. Instead, it politely tells the user, "Our experts are busy right now, please try again in a moment."
It taught us a valuable lesson: when you plug into someone else's tools, always build a backup plan for when they break

**The problem it solves**

- Most DeFi platforms require high collateral to borrow funds.

- ChaiFund introduces a trust-based lending system instead of relying only on collateral.
- Borrowers can get loans based on their trust score and reputation.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Frontend not updating after blockchain transactions
  The loan status and trust score were not updating immediately after repayment.

- Cause
  Blockchain transactions are asynchronous, so the frontend was showing outdated data.

- Solution
  We implemented smart contract events (e.g., "LoanRepaid", "TrustScoreUpdated") and used Ethers.js in the frontend to listen for these events.

- Result
  The application now automatically refreshes loan status and trust scores, making the platform more accurate and user-friendly.

**Open Innovation**

- Solves a real-world problem: ChaiFund addresses the challenge of accessing loans without high collateral in traditional DeFi platforms.

- Open and decentralized system: The platform uses blockchain smart contracts, allowing transparent and trustless lending without intermediaries.

- Encourages community participation: Trust scores and community endorsements allow users to participate in building a decentralized credit system.

- Extensible platform: Other developers and DeFi applications can integrate the trust scoring or lending mechanism into their own platforms.

- Promotes financial inclusion: By enabling trust-based lending, the platform allows more people to access decentralized financial services.

### ZeroTrace (RoboGenesis)
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zerotrace-robogenesis-e60b) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/DbLdX7J9OKU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Peer-to-peer messaging, redefined for security

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![AES](https://img.shields.io/badge/AES-333333?style=flat-square) ![Encryption](https://img.shields.io/badge/Encryption-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![EF: Privacy and Scaling](https://img.shields.io/badge/EF:%20Privacy%20and%20Scaling-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most chat apps today rely on centralized servers that log conversations, store metadata, and expose users to surveillance or breaches. Even “secure” messengers often keep backups or sync data to the cloud, leaving traces that compromise privacy.

ZeroTrace eliminates these risks by enabling direct peer‑to‑peer communication with end‑to‑end encryption and ephemeral messaging.

🔐 What People Can Use It For
Private Conversations  
Exchange sensitive information without fear of logs, leaks, or server compromise.

Ephemeral Messaging  
Messages self‑destruct after a chosen timer (TTL), ensuring no permanent history remains.

Anonymous Communication  
No metadata logging — even the signaling server avoids storing identifiers, IPs, or timestamps.

Cross‑Device Secure Chat  
Works seamlessly across devices using WebRTC DataChannels for direct encrypted transfer.

⚡ How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer
No Central Servers → Removes single points of failure and surveillance risks.

Zero Trust Design → Only sender and receiver can decrypt; signaling servers see nothing.

Dual‑Side Auto‑Deletion → Ensures both devices erase expired messages simultaneously.

Lightweight & Modular → Easy to deploy, test, and scale without complex infrastructure.

User‑Friendly UI → Minimal, modern Jetpack Compose interface with real‑time updates.

**Challenges we ran into**

Data Channel Negotiation:
◦
Bug: P2P connection established, but the Data Channel failed to open.
◦
Fix: Created the DataChannel before generating the SDP Offer in PeerConnectionManager to ensure data headers were included in the negotiation.
•
ICE Candidate Race Conditions:
◦
Bug: addIceCandidate failed because it arrived before the remote description was set.
◦
Fix: Implemented a candidate queue that stores incoming candidates and "drains" them only after setRemoteDescription succeeds.
•
Secure TTL Implementation:
◦
Hurdle: Message expiration (TTL) metadata was vulnerable if sent in plaintext.
◦
Fix: Prefixed the raw message with the TTL Long value using a ByteBuffer and encrypted the entire block as a single Libsodium Sealed Box in CryptoManag
Thread Safety & UI:
◦
Hurdle: WebRTC callbacks run on background threads, causing crashes when updating Compose state.
◦
Fix: Used Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()) to route all incoming messages and connection state changes back to the Main Thread.
•
P2P Signaling Sync:
◦
Hurdle: Managing OFFER, ANSWER, and CANDIDATE exchange via Socket.io without collision.
◦
Fix: Created a robust SignalingClient that maps specific socket events to PeerConnectionManager methods, ensuring strict order of operations.

**The problem it solves**

Most people first encounter crypto through trading, gambling applications, or scams. This creates fear, loss of money, and misunderstanding of what blockchain technology is actually useful for.

In many regions, especially emerging markets, users have smartphones and internet access but no safe path to participate in the digital economy. Wallets, private keys, gas fees, and DeFi interfaces are too complex for normal users.

As a result, blockchain adoption is dominated by traders instead of everyday users.
HustleCoin introduces blockchain through a mobile game economy instead of financial speculation.

Users perform activities, complete jobs, build reputation, and unlock roles such as professions and land ownership. NFTs represent identity and participation inside the economy rather than collectibles or speculation.

The system teaches wallets, ownership, and digital assets naturally through use, not investment. Users learn before they ever need to trade.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was making NFTs function as real in-app assets instead of simple collectibles.
Initially, NFTs were minting correctly but not displaying properly on marketplaces or inside the application. The issue was caused by metadata formatting and decentralized storage requirements. I had to learn how tokenURI works, how OpenSea reads metadata, and how IPFS CIDs must be structured for each individual asset rather than a shared folder reference.
Another challenge was connecting a mobile-first user experience to blockchain wallets. Many users we target have never used private keys or gas fees. We needed a system where users could interact with blockchain ownership without needing deep technical knowledge. This required restructuring how NFTs represent roles (jobs and land) instead of speculative assets.
We also worked through smart contract verification and network deployment on Base. Ensuring contracts were verified and readable by explorers and marketplaces was necessary for trust and transparency.
These challenges shaped the project’s design philosophy: blockchain should be invisible to the user while ownership remains real and verifiable.

### Mistwick
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mistwick-4904) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.mistwick.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/UA_JlI4urHI?si=JJJKIoVQbFLMhJFm) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Startup%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-startup-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Skill Over Luck: The Anti-Casino of Web3.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: Web3 is a Rigged Casino

Most Web3 gaming today isn't about gaming—it's about gambling. Players are trapped in a cycle of inflationary tokens, opaque "luck" mechanics, and a "house edge" that ensures the house always wins.

The Trust Deficit: P2P wagering usually requires a risky middleman or manual escrow.

Opaque Odds: Traditional betting platforms rely on hidden algorithms that favor the platform, not the player.

High Friction: On other chains, slow settlement and high gas fees make competitive play feel like a chore.

The Solution: Mistwick – The On-Chain Arena
Mistwick shifts the paradigm from Speculation to Skill. We’ve built a meritocratic arena on Base where "Your Brain is Your Capital."

Zero House Edge: We’ve removed the "House." In Mistwick, you aren't playing against a rigged system; you are wagering against an opponent in a fair, 1v1 environment.

Pure Skill, No Luck: Whether it’s Chess, Rock-Paper-Scissors, or Connect4, the outcome is determined by your intelligence, not a random number generator.

Trustless & Instant: Leveraging Base’s L2 speed, our smart contracts handle everything. The second a game ends, the winner is paid instantly and automatically on-chain.

Creator-Centric Economy: We provide tools for community leads and influencers to host tournaments with automated revenue sharing, making competitive engagement seamless and profitable for everyone involved.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Hurdles of Building a Trustless Arena
Building a peer-to-peer wagering system on-chain isn't just about moving funds; it’s about ensuring absolute fairness without a centralized referee. Here are the specific hurdles I faced:

1. The "Withdrawal-on-Loss" Exploit
The Hurdle: During the early Beta, I discovered a race condition where a player could potentially trigger a withdrawal transaction right before the smart contract finalized the game result.
The Fix: I implemented a State-Locking Mechanism in the Solidity contract. Once a duel begins, the funds are moved into a secure escrow state that cannot be interacted with until a valid 'Game-End' signal is received or a specific timeout period (for inactivity) expires. This ensured that no one could "rage-quit" with their funds intact.

2. Balancing On-Chain Finality with UX
The Hurdle: Even though Base is incredibly fast, waiting for block confirmation to show the "Next Move" in a Chess game felt laggy for users.
The Fix: I moved to an Optimistic UI Update strategy. I used an off-chain event listener (subgraph/indexer) to provide instant feedback to the player's UI while the transaction was being processed in the background. If the on-chain transaction failed, the UI gracefully rolls back. This made the "Arena" feel like a real-time app, not a slow blockchain tool.

3. Gas Optimization for Micro-Wagers
The Hurdle: Initial contract iterations had high gas costs for "Connect4" logic due to complex board state checks on-chain.
The Fix: I optimized the contract by moving the heavy board-checking logic to Bitwise operations. Instead of storing arrays, I represented the board as bitstrings, significantly reducing the gas cost per move and keeping the arena accessible for low-stake players.

Nedim Can

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nightz-8295) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://Nightz.co) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Startup%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-startup-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Access is the asset.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![USDC](https://img.shields.io/badge/USDC-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Hotel nights are the largest perishable asset class in the world — and they have zero financial infrastructure.

Every unsold night is revenue destroyed forever. Property owners lose $100B+ annually to perishable inventory, while OTAs like Booking.com and Airbnb extract 15-25% commissions as middlemen. Guests have no way to trade, resell, or speculate on access — once you book, you're locked in.

What Nightz Does

Nightz tokenizes property nights as ERC-20 tokens on Base. Each token = 1 night of stay. This unlocks three things that don't exist today:

• Buy early, stay later — Tokens are purchased at a fixed price during primary sale. Holders redeem (burn) them to book specific dates whenever they want.
• Trade access like an asset — Nights become liquid. Can't travel anymore? Sell your token on a DEX instead of fighting cancellation policies. Think a property is getting popular? Buy tokens before prices rise on secondary.
• AI agents can book autonomously — Because tokens are standard ERC-20s on-chain, AI agents can discover availability, compare prices, buy tokens, and burn-to-book — all without APIs, logins, or credit cards. ~30 seconds, near-zero fees vs ~15 minutes and 15-25% commission through traditional OTAs.
How It Works

1. Property owner mints a fixed supply of night-tokens (e.g., 5,000 tokens for Casa Akaw)
2. Users buy tokens via the Nightz launchpad (USDC on Base)
3. To book: select dates → burn tokens → reservation confirmed on-chain
4. Unused tokens can be traded on secondary markets (DEX liquidity)
Who It's For

• Property owners — Monetize future inventory upfront, bypass OTA fees, build direct guest relationships
• Travelers — Lock in prices early, trade nights freely, no cancellation headaches
• Investors — Speculate on property demand as a new asset class
• AI agents — Permissionless booking infrastructure with no API keys or rate limits
Live Today

Two properties on Base mainnet: Casa Akaw (La Saladita, Mexico — $80/night, 5,000 supply) and Tulum Penthouse (Selva Norte — $130/night, 2,000 supply). Smart contracts verified on BaseScan, affiliate system live with 8% commission.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Burn-to-Book Date Collision

The core mechanic — burn tokens to reserve dates — needed to prevent double-bookings without a centralized server. We solved it with an on-chain calendar registry: each property has a mapping of date → booked, checked at burn time. If the date is taken, the transaction reverts. No backend needed.

2. Per-Property Token Isolation

Early designs used a single global token across all properties. This created risk contagion — one property's issues could affect all token holders. We pivoted to one ERC-20 per property, each with independent supply, pricing, and sale contracts. More contracts to deploy, but each property is a self-contained financial unit with zero cross-contamination.

3. Affiliate Commission Accounting

The 8% referral system needed to track commissions per affiliate across multiple properties without letting the owner withdraw funds owed to affiliates. We built a pendingCommissions ledger inside the sale contract — the owner can only withdraw balance - totalPendingCommissions, and affiliates claim independently.

4. USDC Decimal Handling on Base

USDC on Base uses 6 decimals, not 18. Early tests passed with mock tokens (18 decimals) but broke on mainnet. Every price calculation, approval, and display had to be audited for the 6-decimal standard. Lesson: always test with the real token contract on a fork.

5. AI Agent Discoverability

We wanted AI agents to book without custom API integrations. The key insight: by using standard ERC-20 tokens and verified contracts on BaseScan, any agent with a wallet can read supply, check prices, approve USDC, and buy — all through standard contract calls. No API keys, no rate limits, no documentation needed. The blockchain is the API.

**The problem it solves**

I framed this section around The Middleman Tax and The Scalping Monopoly. I specifically wrote it to highlight your "Magic Trick": abstracting the blockchain away from the user. I explained how an organizer just types into the AI (Groq/Llama), and the viem backend does the heavy Smart Contract lifting, giving the attendee a simple Web2 QR code. It makes the project sound incredibly polished.

**Challenges we ran into**

I listed three highly technical problems we actually solved together today:

1) The 'Invalid Address' Wagmi Crash: How we handled the async delay of generating a contract vs. rendering the React UI using strict checksum validation.
2) Bridging Blockchain Finality with Real-World Check-ins: How we fixed the problem of 12-second block times at the door using a webhook that instantly injects a proxy "Registration ID" into PostgreSQL.
3) Next.js 15 Asynchronous Route Handlers: How we fixed the production build by refactoring the dynamic Web3 API routes to securely await parameters.

**BlockChain**

This project uses blockchain strictly to solve real-world industry problems: the middleman monopoly and ticket scalping.

By natively integrating Ethereum (Sepolia) Smart Contracts into a seamless Web2 Next.js application, we leverage the blockchain as an immutable ledger and settlement layer.

We use ERC-721 NFTs to represent event tickets.
We enforce a hardcoded "1 ticket per wallet" rule at the protocol level, mathematically eliminating scalping.
We use Node.js (viem) to automatically compile and deploy contracts for non-technical event organizers in the background.
It proves that blockchain can easily replace $70B corporate ticketing middlemen if the UX is abstracted efficiently.

**Ethereum Track**

This project was built from the ground up to demonstrate the utility of Ethereum as a decentralized backend for mass-market consumer applications. We wanted to solve a real-world problem ticket scalping and platform monopolies without forcing users to understand crypto.

Ethereum as the Settlement Layer: Every event generated on our platform instantly spins up a dedicated ERC-721 Smart Contract on the Ethereum Sepolia Testnet. We chose Ethereum for its unparalleled security and robust smart contract tooling (Solidity, Viem, Hardhat), which allowed us to programmatically enforce a strictly immutable "1 ticket per wallet" rule. This makes ticket scalping mathematically impossible.

Abstracting the Blockchain: Instead of expecting the event organizer to know how to use Remix or fund a deployment wallet, we utilize a Node.js backend to securely compile, sign, and fund the Ethereum contract deployment on their behalf. For the attendee, Ethereum acts as the invisible trust layer. They purchase their NFT ticket via MetaMask (integrated using wagmi), and our backend webhooks instantly synchronize the Ethereum ethers transaction data with a centralized PostgreSQL database to render a scannable Web2 QR code.

By bridging a modern Next.js 15 stack directly with Ethereum smart contracts, we have created a scalable blueprint for how Web3 technology can natively disrupt Web2 monopolies while maintaining a frictionless user experience.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

This entire Web3 ticketing platform was co-developed using Google Antigravity. Antigravity acted as our technical co-founder, enabling us to seamlessly bridge a complex centralized Next.js 15 / PostgreSQL architecture with decentralized Ethereum smart contracts within a hackathon timeline.

Antigravity was instrumental in executing multi-layered tasks:

Blockchain Automation: It wrote and debugged the automated Node.js deployment pipeline that compiles and pushes Solidity smart contracts to the Sepolia testnet entirely behind the scenes.
Component Engineering: We used Antigravity to rapidly prototype and integrate complex React/Wagmi UI components, navigating strict Next.js 15 server/client boundary constraints.
Intelligent Debugging: It autonomously read the terminal output to diagnose and fix critical state mismatch bugs and TypeScript compiler errors on the fly, saving hours of manual debugging.
By leveraging Antigravity's deep context window and agentic execution tools, we were able to build a cohesive, production-ready Web3 application that would otherwise require an entire engineering team.

**Red Hat**

This project demonstrates enterprise-grade scalability by utilizing Red Hat technologies to underpin our cloud-native infrastructure.

While the core application logic handles centralized Web2 data structures and decentralized EVM smart contracts, the robust deployment environment is where Red Hat shines. Our automated Node.js contract-deployment pipeline—which requires extremely high uptime and secure execution environments to handle private keys and RPC node requests—was packaged to run seamlessly on Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) instances. Additionally, the containerized architecture of the Next.js frontend and PostgreSQL database is designed to be fully compatible with Red Hat OpenShift, ensuring that as the ticketing platform scales during massive demand spikes, the orchestration layer remains incredibly stable, secure, and performant.

### ZeroPass
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeropass-735e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/chandril-saha/ZeroPass) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://zeropass-seven.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/BEu7opoX-mQ?si=fHHCJ2EksmMssWzG) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DoubleSlash%204.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://doubleslash4.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Fair Tickets. Verified Fans. Zero Knowledge.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The modern event ticketing industry is broken. It suffers from three catastrophic failures:
1. **Aggressive Data Harvesting:** Platforms force users to surrender their name, email, phone number, and wallet addresses just to buy a ticket. This data is routinely sold or breached.
2. **High Platform Fees:** Most widely used platforms charge significant amount of extra platform fees for purchasing tickets 
3. **Counterfeit and Easily Shareable Tickets:** Traditional QR codes are easily screenshot and duplicated, leading to chaos at the door when multiple people claim the same seat.

**ZeroPass** entirely eradicates these issues. By tying a single cryptographic hash derived from biometric data to a non-transferrable NFT, we make the event hosting and attending process smooth. Because verification happens via Zero-Knowledge proofs locally on the user's device, the organizer never receives a single piece of personally identifiable information. Being built on Flow EVM Testnet (a layer-2 EVM Blockchain), platform fees (gas fees) are negligible.

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced a couple challenges :
* Web Worker Concurrency: Generating a Groth16 proof directly inside the browser using snarkjs is extremely resource-intensive. If executed linearly, it severely freezes the DOM. We had to carefully asynchronous-wrap the fullProve mathematics to ensure the React UI remained highly responsive and didn't crash on mobile devices.
* Deriving Non-Forgeable Anonymous Identities: We had to invent a mechanism where a user could prove they were the same human across multiple ticket purchases without ever revealing *who* they were to the smart contract. Resolving this required combining off-chain Web3 ECDSA wallet signatures with static biometric data (like Aadhar) to seed a multi-layered Poseidon Hash. This successfully created a localized, deterministic secretId that was both mathematically impossible to reverse-engineer and totally invisible to the blockchain.
* Defeating the Replay Attack Vector: Because ZK-proofs are inherently public signals once submitted on-chain, a malicious actor could intercept a valid proof from the mempool and resubmit it to steal a check-in. We successfully neutered this vulnerability by injecting a highly specific nullifier map (isTicketUsed[hash1][eventId] = true) directly into the solidity Verifier logic, guaranteeing that even mathematically pristine proofs are permanently burned the millisecond they are used.

### AgentMesh
