**The problem it solves**

Altair makes it easy for normies to get into defi as a user-friendly chat interface for defi. Users can swap cryptocurrencies, open limit orders, and even create simple trading automations (e.g. DCA) by describing them in English to an AI agent. This spares users from needing to struggle with web wallets and complex trading UIs. More advanced users can make helpful, time-saving automations with zero coding or crypto knowledge all while Altair learns and personalizes to users over time from stored user context data on 0G.ai

**Challenges we ran into**

Privy user / wallet authentication to execute swap thru uniswapActionProvider, got through it by enforcing strict-signing and swaps working.

Got stuck on our 0G integration, specifically with KVs and flow.submit with primary blocker being on-chain writes to 0G Galileo fail at flow.submit with execution reverted (require(false)), even with correct chain (16602) and funded wallet.
Read-side instability: KV endpoint access has been slow/unreachable (timeout / All KV endpoints failed), so direct KV reads were unreliable.
Root cause scope: behavior appears network/contract-side or endpoint-side, not just app logic (reproduced through diagnostics outside normal chat flow).
Current mitigation in app: storage provider was refactored to prefer 0G file-storage flow and use local fallback when 0G write/read fails, so UX continues even during 0G outages.
Net effect right now: user memory may be saved locally when 0G is unhealthy; on-chain 0G persistence is not consistently guaranteed until flow.submit path is resolved.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Custom fine-tuned openai model, agentkit, 0G inferenceActionProvider training and user chat and past swap data for user-specific context memory.

**Futurllama**

We developed a DeFi AI wingman for those who want easy engagement

**Best DeFAI Application**

The Altair UI makes it incredibly easy for users new to crypto to have a safe, warm, and helpful introduction to web3. Using 0G's AI storage, Altair stores information about past conversations, as well as important preferences, such as token pairs, chains, and even price levels. It is also aware of a user's experience level, and can adjust its responses accordingly. As a user swaps with Altair, it continues to give better and more curated guidance, leaving the user feeling cared for, and not afraid that web3 will exploit them.

Meanwhile, for more experienced traders, the AI storage allows for building and expanding on trading algorithms that represent the user's preferences and run automatically, saving them the time of checking prices and making swaps themselves.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

When a user creates their account on Altair with their email, Google account, or phone, an EVM wallet is created for them using Privy. When a user confirms a swap in Altair's chat UI, usePrivy() and useWallets() obtain an EVM provider, which is wrapped by ethers.providers.Web3Provider for signing and sending transactions. Uniswap routing is generated in POST() using AlphaRouter and CurrencyAmount.fromRawAmount(). Then, the client uses the returned calldata to execute swaps via sendTransaction.

### DealForge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/dealforge-084d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/andrevandeven/ETHDenver-2026) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/watch?v=3UHnHeZCwqY&feature=youtu.be) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Ownable AI negotiators and verifiable deals on 0G

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![NFT](https://img.shields.io/badge/NFT-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Procurement is broken for small and mid-sized businesses. Getting competitive supplier quotes means hours of phone tag, inconsistent negotiation, and institutional knowledge that lives only in someone's head or gets lost entirely when that person leaves.                                             
                                                                                                                                                        The status quo looks like this: a buyer manually calls three to five suppliers for every order. Each negotiation is only as good as the person making the call their mood, their memory of past deals, whether they remember to mention a competing quote. Supplier pricing history, negotiation tactics, and leverage points are stored in spreadsheets or nowhere at all. There's no verifiable record of what was agreed and why. The whole process can take days and still produce a mediocre deal.                                                                                                                

Procurement Negotiator iNFT replaces that process with an AI agent that makes real phone calls and negotiates for you.
You describe what you need and the agent dials the supplier, introduces itself, anchors on a low opening price, drops competitor quotes as leverage, and pushes for a final commitment. All via a live voice call, powered by 0G Compute LLM inference.

More importantly, the agent gets smarter with every call it makes. After each negotiation it writes what it learned (the supplier's best price, their willingness to negotiate) into its brain, a document stored on 0G Storage with the hash committed on-chain. The next time it calls that supplier, it already knows their floor price and uses competing quotes from other suppliers it has previously called as leverage. The agent compounds its knowledge the same way a seasoned procurement professional does, except it never forgets and never leaves the company.

Because the agent is an iNFT on 0G Chain, that accumulated intelligence is a verifiable on-chain asset. The agent is owned by whoever holds the NFT. You can mint one, train it across hundreds of negotiations until it has deep supplier relationships and hard-won pricing intel baked into its brain, and then sell access to other businesses — or sell the NFT itself, transferring all of that accumulated knowledge to the new owner. Usage is sold through an on-chain credit system: buyers purchase credits to run RFQs through your agent, and the fee flows directly to the NFT holder's wallet. The smarter your agent gets, the more valuable it becomes, and the more you can charge for access to it.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest technical hurdle was making the voice negotiation actually work with the model available on the 0G Compute testnet. We were constrained to Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct a small model that doesn't have the reasoning depth you'd want for a multi-turn negotiation that needs to track what step it's on, remember what the supplier just said, and respond naturally in one or two sentences without going off-script.                                      
                                                                                                                                                         The first version of the agent was a mess. It would skip steps, repeat itself, ignore what the supplier said entirely, or produce responses so long that the conversation felt robotic. Getting a 7B model to reliably follow a multi-step negotiation script, anchoring on price, dropping a competitor quote at the right moment, pushing for a final offer and then closing, required a lot of prompt engineering iteration.                                

We eventually landed on a very rigid step-by-step system prompt that told the model exactly what to say at each stage, almost word for word. Less creative, but far more reliable with a small model. The challenge was finding the right level of specificity, too loose and the model wandered off script, too rigid and it stopped responding naturally to what the supplier actually said.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

The core of the project is a voice AI agent that negotiates procurement deals over real phone calls. When a buyer submits an RFQ, the agent initiates an outbound call via Twilio to the supplier's phone number. Twilio's ConversationRelay connects that live call to a WebSocket server where the agent processes each turn of the conversation in real time.
                                                                                                                                                         
 Every time the supplier speaks, the transcribed text is sent to 0G Compute,  0G's decentralized inference network, where a Qwen 2.5 7B model generate the agent's next response. That response is streamed back token by token to Twilio's text-to-speech engine, which reads it aloud on the call. The result is a fully autonomous back-and-forth voice negotiation with no human in the loop.                                                             

After the call ends, the agent uses 0G Compute again to extract the structured quote details, unit price, minimum order quantity, and lead time, from the negotiation transcript. That transcript and quote are then uploaded to 0G Storage and committed on-chain, making every negotiated price fully verifiable.

We use 0G compute for all of our AI inference in our procurement agent.

**Best Use of On-Chain Agent (iNFT)**

iNFTs are central to our application. Our entire application is an agent marketplace with agent permissions and information governed by iNFTs.

### StreamPay
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/streampay-0e2c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/emilyjiji/eth-denver-2.0) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/GaL6a2OO1mo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Payment Streaming Protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Electricity payments today are slow, opaque, and locked into legacy billing cycles - you pay weeks after you've already consumed the power. For energy providers, this means cash flow risk and reconciliation headaches. For consumers, there's no transparency into what they're paying or when.

StreamPay brings electricity payments on-chain with real-time, automated settlement using cross-chain infrastructure:
  - Consumers fund a payment stream with ETH (via Uniswap on Base), which is automatically converted to HBAR and deposited into a self-executing Hedera payment stream
  - Payments settle automatically on a recurring schedule using the Hedera Schedule Service - no manual intervention, no missed payments
  - Energy providers receive tokenized receivables on the ADI chain the moment a consumer stops streaming funds, enabling on-chain factoring

This makes electricity payments faster, more transparent, and programmable, turning a monthly bill into a continuous, auditable, cross-chain money stream.

**Challenges we ran into**

Cross-chain token bridging                                                    
There's no direct path to swap EVM tokens (like USDC on Base) into native HBAR on Hedera. To work around this, we demonstrated the full Uniswap Trading API swap flow with ERC-20 tokens on Sepolia, then built a relay service that listens for successful swaps and bridges the equivalent value to Hedera, converting the USDC amount to HBAR and calling topUpDeposit() on our Hedera payment stream contract. This let us showcase both the Uniswap API integration and the Hedera payment stream end-to-end, connected by a lightweight off-chain relay.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

AI was used throughout the development process as a pair programmer and ops assistant:

  - Code generation & debugging: Claude helped write and iterate on the Solidity smart contracts, the TypeScript relay services, and the React/Vite frontends
  - Cross-chain architecture design: We used Claude to reason through the relay design - how to safely bridge a Base swap event to a Hedera contract call, and then propagate settlement events to ADI

**New France Village**

StreamPay sits at the intersection of DeFi infrastructure and real-world financial obligations.
                                                                                
  RWA & RealFi: Electricity bills are one of the most universal real-world financial obligations. We tokenize them: every settlement on our Hedera payment stream mints a receivable NFT on the ADI chain representing a paid (or outstanding) electricity obligation. This turns a utility bill into a programmable, on-chain asset that energy providers can track, factor, or eventually use as collateral.

  TradFi meets DeFi: The consumer-facing flow uses Uniswap (DeFi-native) to fund what is essentially a recurring utility payment (TradFi-native). A user doesn't need to think about HBAR or Hedera — they just swap ETH and their electricity stream is funded. This is the kind of UX abstraction that enables Main Street adoption.

  Institutional & Treasury use case: Energy providers typically manage accounts receivable on spreadsheets or legacy ERP systems with 30–90 day payment cycles. Our tokenized receivables give them an on-chain, auditable record of every settlement - a foundation for DeFi-native treasury management, invoice factoring, or integration with institutional lending protocols.

  Stablecoins as the bridge: USDC is the unit of account throughout the swap leg, demonstrating how stablecoins act as the practical connective tissue between DeFi activity and real-world payment obligations.

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

StreamPay is built around a self-perpetuating payment stream powered entirely by the Hedera Schedule Service - no off chain cron jobs, no backend schedulers, no human intervention required after stream creation.

  How it works: When a consumer funds their electricity stream, our ElectricityPaymentStream contract calls the HSS precompile directly to schedule the first settle() execution. When that scheduled transaction fires and settle() runs, the contract immediately schedules the next settlement before returning creating an infinite, self-renewing payment cycle driven entirely by on-chain contract logic.

Contract-driven scheduling: All schedule creation happens inside the smart contract using the HSS system contract precompile. The backend relay is only involved in topping up the deposit balance - the scheduling logic itself lives entirely on-chain, deterministically, with clear authorization rules tied to the stream's payer and payee.

  Edge case handling: The contract handles insufficient balance gracefully - if settle() runs and there isn't enough deposit to cover the accrued amount, it emits a SettlementFailed event with the shortfall, still re-schedules the next attempt, and waits for the payer to top up. Partial execution, expired schedules, and retry logic are all handled in Solidity.

  Observability: The merchant dashboard shows a full settlement history with on-chain timestamps and HashScan links. Every SettlementExecuted and SettlementFailed event is indexed and surfaced in the UI, giving both payer and payee a clear view of the schedule lifecycle - created → pending → executed or failed.

This is exactly the DeFi automation and business finance flow the bounty targets: a real-world billing primitive that runs itself on Hedera with no off-chain orchestration.

**Open Project Submission**

StreamPay delivers a working MVP of tokenized electricity receivables on ADI Chain - turning real-world utility payment obligations into on-chain assets suitable for institutional use.

  The real-world asset: Every electricity settlement on our Hedera stream contract emits an on-chain event, either SettlementExecuted (paid) or SettlementFailed (outstanding). Our Hedera→ADI relay picks up these events and mints a UtilityReceivable NFT on ADI Chain for each one. Each token encodes the utility provider, customer, USD amount, due date, and payment status (PAID, OUTSTANDING, PARTIAL) - a fully auditable, on-chain record of a real electricity obligation.

  Institutional relevance: Energy providers today manage accounts receivable in spreadsheets or legacy ERP systems, with payment cycles of 30–90 days and no on-chain auditability. StreamPay gives them a live, tokenized ledger of every receivable the moment settlement occurs. These tokens are the foundation for invoice factoring, DeFi-native collateralization, or integration with institutional lending protocols - turning illiquid utility receivables into  programmable financial instruments.

  ADI Chain as primary execution layer: The UtilityReceivable contract is deployed on ADI Testnet. All receivable minting, status tracking, and ownership happens on ADI Chain. The merchant dashboard connects directly to ADI to read and display the receivables portfolio in real time.

  Architecture: The system enforces a permissioned relayer model - only an authorized address can mint receivables, preventing spoofed settlement events. The contract tracks processed Hedera transaction hashes to ensure idempotency. Role-based access (owner vs. relayer) and whitelabel-ready UI design make it extensible for institutional deployment.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

StreamPay integrates the Uniswap Trading API as the entry point for the entire cross-chain payment flow; it's the first step of every deposit a consumer makes.

  How the integration works: When a user wants to fund their electricity stream, they enter an ETH amount in the consumer app. The frontend calls the Uniswap Trading API to fetch a live quote for ETH→USDC on Sepolia, displaying the expected USDC output and route in real time. On confirmation, the app executes the full swap flow: auto-wrapping ETH to WETH, signing a Permit2 approval (gasless token authorization), and submitting the swap transaction - all via Uniswap API infrastructure.

  Rather than swapping for the sake of swapping, the Uniswap API here serves as a cross-chain payment rail. The USDC output from the swap is the signal that triggers the relay, which converts the amount to HBAR and calls topUpDeposit() on a Hedera smart contract. Uniswap becomes the on-ramp for a Hedera payment stream. The user never has to touch HBAR or think about Hedera, they just deposit ETH and their electricity bill is funded.

  Shipped MVP on testnet: The full flow is live and demoed on Sepolia - quote fetching, Permit2 signing, swap execution, and relay trigger all work end to end. The consumer UI is publicly accessible, open source, and intuitive: connect MetaMask, enter an amount, see a live quote, click swap.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AAVE](https://img.shields.io/badge/AAVE-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Finding affordable housing in San Francisco is brutal. Data is scattered across dozens of sources — crime stats on one site, school ratings on another, transit info somewhere else, and affordable housing listings on yet another portal. People spend hours manually researching neighborhoods, and the data goes stale fast.RealBase solves this by aggregating 7 data sources into a single composite neighborhood score (0-10) across 43 SF neighborhoods, updated autonomously every 15 minutes. Anyone can:
Renters & homebuyers — Compare neighborhoods instantly based on schools, safety, transit, walkability, and affordability instead of juggling multiple websites
Housing nonprofits & policy orgs — Access structured, up-to-date neighborhood data via API to power their own tools and reports
Other Base developers — Query our onchain oracle directly from their smart contracts to build housing, lending, or insurance products on top of real neighborhood data
Researchers — Mint NFT report snapshots to preserve point-in-time neighborhood analysis onchain
The x402 micropayment model also makes neighborhood data accessible without subscriptions or accounts — just pay per request in USDC. No middlemen, no sign-ups.

**Challenges we ran into**

The 15-minute tick cycle and gas management were the hardest part. The agent needs to update oracle scores onchain, but gas costs on Base fluctuate and the agent has a limited USDC balance. I had to build a conservation mode that detects when the wallet drops below $5 and starts skipping non-critical updates, plus an auto-swap mechanism that converts USDC to ETH via Uniswap V3 only when gas reserves are actually low — not every tick. Getting the thresholds right took a lot of trial and error.Batch oracle updates were another challenge. Updating 43 neighborhoods individually would be prohibitively expensive, so I had to design RealBaseOracle.sol to accept batch updates in a single transaction. Packing the data efficiently while keeping the contract readable and queryable by other contracts required several iterations.Data source reliability was a constant issue. Some APIs rate-limit aggressively, others return inconsistent formats, and Census ACS data only updates monthly. I built a freshness tracking system so the dashboard shows exactly how stale each data source is, and the agent gracefully falls back to cached data when a source is unavailable rather than serving incomplete scores.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

RealBase's core is an autonomous onchain agent — not a chatbot, but a self-operating economic entity on Base that makes decisions without human intervention.
The Agent Loop:
Every 15 minutes the agent executes an autonomous tick cycle:

Health check — verify wallet balance, gas reserves, contract connectivity
Fetch — pull fresh data from all 7 sources
Score — compute composite neighborhood scores using weighted formula
Update — batch-write scores to the onchain oracle
Decide — autonomous economic decisions: deposit idle USDC into Aave for yield, swap USDC→ETH when gas is low, activate conservation mode if funds are critically low

The agent is self-sustaining — it earns revenue through x402 data API payments, NFT mints, and oracle query fees, then reinvests that revenue to cover gas costs and generate yield. No human tops up the wallet or triggers updates.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

Here's a write-up you can submit:

RealBase is built entirely on Base Mainnet with two deployed smart contracts (RealBaseOracle and RealBaseReport) and a dedicated agent wallet. Every transaction includes ERC-8021 builder codes for Base attribution.
The project is a self-sustaining autonomous agent that aggregates affordable housing data from 7 sources, scores 43 SF neighborhoods, and operates a closed-loop onchain economy — all on Base. The agent runs a 15-minute tick cycle autonomously: fetching data, computing scores, updating its onchain oracle, and making economic decisions like swapping USDC to ETH for gas via Uniswap V3 when reserves are low.
Revenue is generated through four onchain streams: x402 micropayments for detailed neighborhood data, ERC-721 NFT report mints, paid oracle queries from other smart contracts, and Aave V3 yield on idle USDC. All of this happens on Base — the agent earns, spends, and reinvests without human intervention, with a conservation mode that activates when funds drop below $5.
Beyond the economic loop, RealBase is deeply composable within the Base ecosystem. The oracle contract is queryable by any other Base contract, meaning other developers can build on top of our neighborhood scoring data. We see this as infrastructure for Base — affordable housing data as a public good with a sustainable economic model powering it.

**New France Village**

It is a DEFI protocol that is a flight insurance

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

**The problem:** Smart contracts on Hedera cannot wake themselves up. There is no native `cron` equivalent in EVM. The Controller needs to check flight statuses every 10 minutes and trigger settlements — but something has to call it.

**The solution: Hedera Schedule Service (HSS)**

HSS lets you pre-schedule a transaction to execute at a future time, or on a recurring basis. We use it to create an automated loop that calls the Controller on a fixed interval without any centralized keeper bot.

```
HSS Scheduled Transaction
        │
        │  fires every 10 minutes
        ▼
Controller.checkAndSettle(flightId, flightDate)
        │
        ├── calls FlightDataAggregator.getFlightStatus()
        │
        ├── if status == Delayed  → FlightPool.settleDelayed()
        ├── if status == Cancelled → FlightPool.settleCancelled()
        └── if status == OnTime + flight date passed → FlightPool.settleOnTime()
```

**Why this matters:**

Without HSS, the system would need a trusted off-chain keeper to call the Controller — introducing a centralisation point and a failure mode (what if the keeper goes down?). With HSS, the settlement loop is scheduled at the protocol level and executes regardless of whether any operator is watching.

**What the HSS loop does on each tick:**
1. Reads the current flight status from the Aggregator
2. Checks whether settlement conditions are met
3. If yes — triggers the FlightPool to pay out or close
4. If no — does nothing, waits for the next tick
5. **HSS reschedules itself** for the next interval — no keeper required

**HTS usage in Controller:** [Controller.sol](https://github.com/enderNakamoto/flight_hedera/blob/main/contracts/src/Controller.sol)

> SocialFi risk management dashboard for creators.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Creators live in a weird in-between space financially.

Their income depends heavily on engagement, views, likes, comments, but their savings or treasury often sits in volatile assets like crypto. When engagement drops, income becomes uncertain. But nothing signals them to reduce financial risk at that moment. And when engagement is strong and stable, they might be sitting entirely in stablecoins doing nothing.

Right now, there’s no connection between a creator’s social performance and their capital allocation.

Analytics dashboards tell you what happened.
Wallet apps let you swap tokens.
But there’s no bridge between the two.

FlowFi connects those dots.

**Challenges we ran into**

Instagram OAuth was more annoying than expected. If the redirect URI was even slightly off, the whole flow would fail and not give a helpful error. We had to carefully match the callback URL in the Meta dashboard and our local environment.

On the Uniswap side, the swap flow isn’t just “press button → swap.” We had to:
- fetch a quote
- handle permit data
- pass the correct calldata
- make sure amounts were in base units
- then send everything through wagmi/viem correctly

If one value was wrong, the transaction would fail. Most of our time went into making sure the quote → swap → wallet signature pipeline actually worked end-to-end.

Another challenge was figuring out how to turn engagement into something that feels actionable but not over-engineered. We kept it simple: measure volatility and trend, then map that to a risk level. Getting that balance right took iteration.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

FlowFi does not rely on AI agents or machine learning models in its core decision-making.

We intentionally kept the risk logic deterministic and transparent. Engagement volatility and trend direction are calculated directly from Instagram media data using straightforward statistical methods. The hedge recommendation is rule-based (e.g., higher volatility + downward trend → suggest ETH → USDC).

We made this choice on purpose. For financial decisions, especially during a hackathon, we felt it was more responsible to keep the logic explainable rather than hide it behind a black-box model.

**Futurllama**

FlowFi introduces a new primitive performance-linked capital allocation.

Right now, social performance and financial positioning live in completely separate worlds. Creators check engagement on Instagram. They manage capital in a wallet. There’s no system that connects the two.

We built that bridge.

FlowFi treats engagement volatility as a financial signal. When engagement becomes unstable, the system suggests reducing exposure. When performance stabilizes, it suggests re-entering growth assets. The swap executes on Ethereum through Uniswap.

It’s an experiment in making off-chain social data influence on-chain capital in a programmable way.

That’s the frontier.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

FlowFi doesn’t just “integrate swaps.” Uniswap is the execution engine of the product.

Our core idea is simple: when a creator’s engagement becomes unstable, their financial exposure should adjust. But that adjustment has to happen on-chain, in real time, through a liquid, trustless market.

That’s where Uniswap comes in.

When our system detects higher engagement volatility, we don’t simulate a hedge, we execute it. We call Uniswap’s Trading API to fetch a real quote, surface price impact and routing data to the user, and generate transaction calldata. The user signs and broadcasts the swap directly from their wallet.

Uniswap isn’t just a backend dependency. It’s the bridge that turns a social signal into a capital move.

No custody. No fake balances. No mock swaps.

We’re using Uniswap exactly how it’s meant to be used: as neutral, permissionless liquidity infrastructure that powers new applications.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/intelligence-cubed-i-12e3) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://intelligence3.io/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/2kCCtwM-CzU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> World’s First AI Model Nasdaq

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Core Problem: AI Has Scaled — Its Economic Infrastructure Has Not

AI models are becoming cheaper, faster, and increasingly specialized. Efficient open foundation models have triggered a small-model renaissance, enabling thousands of researchers and independent teams to build high-performance niche systems.

However, the economic infrastructure around AI has not evolved.

Today, AI models exist in two structurally incomplete states. In centralized API silos, pricing is opaque, subscription-based, and detached from real usage. Creators cannot meaningfully capture long-term value, and users are locked into bundled services without ownership or transparent benchmarking. In open-source repositories, models are freely distributed but lack embedded mechanisms for ownership, capital formation, attribution, or recurring monetization. As models are reused and fine-tuned, upstream contributors lose economic participation.

In both cases, AI models are treated as software artifacts rather than economic units. They are composable and reusable, yet economically invisible. This misalignment discourages sustainable innovation, prevents efficient capital allocation, and pushes the ecosystem toward re-centralization.

The urgency of this problem is increasing. The supply of specialized models is exploding as training costs decline, but without programmable ownership and usage-linked incentives, high-quality models are buried under noise, and capital cannot efficiently flow to strong systems. The AI model market is scaling rapidly, yet no neutral economic infrastructure exists to support discovery, ownership, and value distribution.

Our Solution: A Decentralized Economic Layer for AI Models

Intelligence Cubed builds the Modelverse, a decentralized marketplace where AI models function as programmable, on-chain economic assets.

When a creator launches a model, it is minted as an on-chain AI asset with a persistent cryptographic watermark establishing identity and lineage. Ownership and royalty rules are encoded directly in smart contracts. Creators may optionally initiate an Initial Model Offering (IMO), allowing public participation and capital formation. Once 51% of ownership is decentralized, the model automatically transitions into an open-source state under predefined protocol rules, ensuring decentralization without platform discretion.

Models are accessed through stateless pay-per-request APIs rather than subscription contracts. Each inference generates a verifiable on-chain usage record, and revenue is automatically distributed to creators and contributors according to predefined royalty logic.

When a model is fine-tuned, forked, or embedded into downstream workflows, its watermark preserves attribution across the derivative graph. Royalty logic propagates automatically through this lineage, allowing upstream contributors to continue participating economically as intelligence compounds.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the most difficult technical challenges was designing a watermarking and lineage system that is both cryptographically persistent and economically enforceable.

We did not want a superficial metadata tag that could be stripped or bypassed. The watermark needed to function as a permanent identity layer for AI models — surviving fine-tuning, forking, sharding, quantization, and even partial parameter reuse. At the same time, it had to remain lightweight enough not to degrade inference performance.

The core problem was this: once a model is open-sourced or fine-tuned, how do you guarantee attribution without reintroducing centralized enforcement?

We solved this by separating watermark identity from model weights while anchoring both through deterministic hashing and on-chain commitments. Each model is issued with a cryptographic root identity recorded on-chain. Derivative models must reference upstream hashes during registration, and revenue routing logic is computed based on an immutable lineage tree. Instead of trusting off-chain claims, we made economic attribution dependent on provable lineage linkage.

The second major challenge was implementing recursive royalty propagation without creating gas inefficiency or economic fragility.

In theory, N-degree royalty distribution is simple. In practice, recursive value routing across potentially deep derivative trees becomes computationally expensive and vulnerable to manipulation. We had to design a royalty compression mechanism that aggregates upstream claims deterministically while keeping settlement O(1) at execution time. This required building a lineage indexing layer that pre-computes distribution weights and avoids iterative on-chain traversal.

Another critical hurdle was building the Proof-of-Intelligence (PoI) system in a way that is credibly neutral yet resistant to gaming.

Static benchmarks are trivial to manipulate. Pure voting systems are political. Pure usage metrics can be sybil-attacked. We needed a dynamic scoring engine that blends usage, reliability, cost-efficiency, and economic participation into a continuously updating signal. The difficulty was balancing neutrality with robustness — making it expensive to game without introducing centralized discretion.

We addressed this by anchoring evaluation to verifiable usage receipts, cryptographic model identities, and deterministic scoring functions. Rather than allowing subjective curation, PoI updates are derived from measurable production signals recorded on-chain.

Finally, we faced the broader architectural challenge of reconciling decentralization with performance.

AI inference is latency-sensitive. On-chain systems are not. The solution required a hybrid architecture: inference runs off-chain on optimized compute infrastructure, while identity, ownership, royalty logic, and settlement are enforced on-chain. Designing this boundary — deciding exactly what must be trustless and what must be performant — required multiple iterations and threat modeling cycles.

Each of these challenges forced us to think beyond simple marketplace design. We were not building a model hub. We were building economic infrastructure for intelligence.

And infrastructure has to be correct before it can be elegant.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

AI agents are deeply embedded in both our development workflow and our production validation pipeline. We do not use AI tools merely for code completion; we use them as automated systems testers, workflow simulators, and performance profilers.

One of the most critical areas where AI agents contribute is workflow and pipeline testing. The Modelverse supports multi-step model orchestration, where a single user request may trigger routing, retrieval, reasoning, validation, and royalty settlement layers. Testing these pipelines manually would be slow and incomplete. Instead, we deploy AI agents to simulate high-volume, heterogeneous user behavior across different routing configurations.

These agents automatically generate diverse task distributions, invoke multi-model chains, and measure end-to-end latency, token consumption, routing decisions, and settlement correctness. By running thousands of synthetic execution traces, they allow us to stress-test throughput limits, identify bottlenecks, and detect pathological latency spikes under adversarial patterns.

We also use AI agents for dynamic routing optimization. Agents simulate cost–latency tradeoffs by invoking models across different compute backends, then feed performance telemetry into optimization loops. This enables us to evaluate how routing heuristics behave under real-world variance, including burst traffic, partial node failure, and fluctuating GPU availability.

For benchmarking and Proof-of-Intelligence calibration, AI agents continuously execute evaluation tasks to detect performance regression and reliability drift. Rather than relying on static benchmark datasets, agents run rolling validation workloads and compare real production outputs across model versions. This ensures that scoring signals remain responsive to actual behavior rather than offline claims.

On the smart contract side, AI-driven fuzzing agents generate deep derivative trees to test royalty propagation logic. They create synthetic model lineages with randomized branching structures, simulate recursive revenue flows, and verify settlement integrity under extreme scenarios. This has been critical in validating that royalty compression and distribution logic remains deterministic and gas-efficient even under high-complexity lineage graphs.

In short, AI agents function as autonomous stress-testers and optimization engines within our system. They help us validate latency ceilings, pipeline stability, routing robustness, and economic correctness at scale.

**Futurllama**

Futurlama is for frontier builders experimenting with what comes next — AI, DePIN, and new primitives at the edge of Ethereum. Intelligence Cubed belongs in this track because we are not building an AI application. We are introducing a new primitive for decentralized intelligence markets.

AI is rapidly becoming a foundational production unit of the digital economy. Training costs are collapsing. Specialized models are proliferating. Multi-model orchestration is replacing monolithic systems. The next phase of AI is not about building a bigger model — it is about coordinating millions of smaller ones.

Yet the economic layer for intelligence does not exist.

Models today have no native ownership, no programmable royalties, no dynamic valuation tied to real usage, and no credibly neutral benchmarking mechanism. Intelligence compounds technically, but not economically.

We are building that missing layer.

At the protocol level, we introduce AI models as on-chain economic entities. Ownership can be issued, transferred, and capitalized. Every model invocation generates usage-linked revenue flows. Royalty logic propagates across derivative graphs through watermark-anchored lineage. Fine-tunes and workflow compositions become economically structured rather than socially attributed.

This is not an interface innovation. It is a mechanism design innovation.

The watermark functions as a persistent identity primitive for models. Proof-of-Intelligence functions as a dynamic market-evaluation primitive. Ownership and royalties function as programmable incentive primitives. Together, they create an AI-native economic substrate enforced by Ethereum-native logic.

If decentralized finance introduced programmable capital, and DePIN introduced programmable compute, then Intelligence Cubed introduces programmable intelligence as a new primitive.

This is deeply AI, deeply technical, and deeply emerging.

We are integrating multi-model routing, cryptographic identity anchoring, recursive royalty settlement, and dynamic market benchmarking into a coherent protocol. It is an experiment in how intelligence itself can be owned, priced, and coordinated under decentralized rules.

That is why this project belongs in Futurlama.

Because it is not simply applying AI to crypto.

It is redefining how intelligence participates in decentralized systems.

### Horus
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/horus-a42b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/REB007/horus) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://horus-xyz.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Fully on Chain Prediction Markets (no order book)

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Uniswap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Uniswap-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Prediction markets today are either centralized (the operator picks the outcome) or limited to assets on a single chain. Horus solves both problems:

**Multi-chain price markets for any token.** Users can bet on whether *any* token with Uniswap liquidity — on Ethereum, Base, or any supported chain — will go up in 10 minutes. The market contract lives on Ethereum Sepolia, but the price oracle reads from tokens on other chains via the Uniswap API. This means you can create a prediction market for a Base memecoin while settling in USDC on Sepolia.

**Auditable oracle with a path to trustlessness.** The admin submits the price, but *cannot fabricate it*. Every market stores its oracle metadata on-chain — the API endpoint, source chain, pool address, and token address. Anyone can independently query the same Uniswap API endpoint and verify the submitted price matches. This metadata is also the exact input specification for a future zkTLS verifier, which would make resolution fully permissionless and provably correct without any admin involvement.

**What users can do:**
- **Create markets** — anyone with ≥10 USDC can create a 10-minute prediction market for any token (permissionless on the contract level)
- **Trade** — buy YES/NO tokens with USDC. Prices reflect crowd probability via a constant-product AMM (CPMM)
- **Provide liquidity** — earn 2% swap fees by adding USDC to the pool
- **Claim winnings** — after resolution, winning token holders redeem 1:1 for USDC
- **Mint/Redeem** — always mint 1 YES + 1 NO for 1 USDC, or redeem the pair back. Fully collateralized at all times.

**Why it matters:** Short-duration prediction markets on memecoins are a natural fit — high volatility, high engagement, fast feedback loops. Horus makes this possible across chains with an auditable oracle, moving the trust model from "trust the operator" to "verify the data source yourself."

**Challenges we ran into**

**Decoupling the oracle from the market chain.** V1 and V2 of the contract read the price directly from a Uniswap V3 pool on the same chain (`slot0().tick`). This meant markets could only exist for tokens with pools on the deployment chain. Moving to a submitted-price model (V3) required rethinking the entire resolution flow — the contract no longer reads the price itself, so we needed to store oracle metadata on-chain to keep the system auditable. Getting the right balance between "fast to build" and "architecturally sound for future zkTLS" took several iterations.

**Uniswap API response format inconsistencies.** The Uniswap Trade API returns price data in different formats depending on the routing path — sometimes `quote.output.amount` (raw bigint), sometimes `quote.outputAmount`, sometimes `quote.quoteDecimals` (human-readable float). We had to handle all three variants and normalize to a consistent 18-decimal int256 format for the contract. The API also returns 504 gateway timeouts under load, so we added retry logic with exponential backoff.

**Multi-hop price routing.** Many tokens (especially memecoins) don't have a direct USDC pool. The initial implementation failed silently for these tokens. We had to build a two-hop fallback (token → WETH → USDC) using two sequential quote calls, which introduced complexity around decimal handling — WETH uses 18 decimals while USDC uses 6.

**USDC approval flow for permissionless creation.** V2's factory pulled USDC from the admin wallet. V3 allows anyone to create a market, so the factory now pulls USDC from `msg.sender`. This required adding an explicit `approve` transaction before `createMarket` — a two-step flow that needed careful handling in both the API (for admin-created markets) and the frontend (for user-created markets).

**Frontend crashes from undefined on-chain data.** When the API failed to read on-chain data (e.g. during RPC timeouts), it returned market objects without `yesReserve`, `noReserve`, or price fields. The frontend called `BigInt(undefined)` and crashed. We had to add defensive fallbacks at both the API layer (return zero defaults on failure) and the frontend (guard every BigInt conversion).

**Contract version migration.** Upgrading from V2 to V3 ABIs across the entire stack (API routes, chain service, test scripts, frontend config) was error-prone. A single missed ABI reference would cause silent failures where the contract call returned unexpected data. We caught several of these only through the integration test suite.

**New France Village**

Horus is a **fully on-chain DeFi primitive**: binary prediction markets with USDC collateral, a constant-product AMM, and permissionless market creation. It sits at the intersection of several Future of Finance themes:

**DeFi infrastructure.** Every component is on-chain and composable — ERC-20 outcome tokens, a CPMM pool, fully collateralized minting (`1 YES + 1 NO = 1 USDC`), and permissionless liquidity provision with fee accrual. The contracts are standard Solidity with OpenZeppelin, deployable on any EVM chain.

**Main Street adoption.** Prediction markets are one of the most intuitive DeFi products — "Will this token go up?" is a question anyone understands. Horus reduces the barrier further: 10-minute markets, USDC-denominated, one-click trading via RainbowKit, and a clean UI that abstracts away the on-chain complexity. Users don't need to understand AMM math or oracle mechanics to participate.

**Cross-chain price discovery.** Markets settle on Ethereum Sepolia but price tokens on *any* Uniswap-supported chain (Ethereum mainnet, Base, etc.) via the Uniswap Developer API. This is a practical demonstration of cross-chain DeFi — using off-chain price feeds with on-chain auditability, bridging liquidity information across chains without bridges.

**Path to trustlessness.** The architecture is designed for progressive decentralization. Today: admin submits prices, but oracle metadata on-chain makes every submission auditable. Tomorrow: zkTLS proofs verify the Uniswap API response cryptographically, removing the admin entirely. The contract already stores everything a verifier needs — no migration required, just add a `resolveWithProof()` function.

**Stablecoins as settlement.** All collateral is USDC — prediction markets become a stablecoin-native financial product where users speculate on volatile assets while their principal and winnings are always denominated in dollars.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

Horus uses the **Uniswap Developer API** as its **sole price oracle** for prediction market creation and resolution. This is not a peripheral integration — the Uniswap API is the core infrastructure that makes the entire protocol work.

### How it's integrated

The backend service (`api/src/services/uniswap.ts`) calls the Uniswap Trade API at `https://trade-api.gateway.uniswap.org/v1/quote` with an API key generated from the [Uniswap Developer Platform](https://developers.uniswap.org/dashboard).

**Two critical price fetches per market:**

1. **At market creation** — fetches the current USD price of the token via `POST /v1/quote` (EXACT_INPUT, 1e18 token → USDC). This becomes the `snapshotPrice` stored on-chain.
2. **At resolution (10 min later)** — fetches the price again via the same endpoint. This `resolutionPrice` is submitted to the contract, which compares: `resolutionPrice > snapshotPrice` → YES wins.

**Multi-chain support:** The API is called with the token's native `chainId` (e.g. 8453 for Base), so Horus can create prediction markets for tokens on *any* Uniswap-supported chain while the market contract itself lives on Sepolia.

**Multi-hop routing:** If no direct token/USDC pool exists, the service automatically routes through WETH (token → WETH → USDC) using two sequential quote calls.

**Reliability:** Built-in retry logic with exponential backoff for 504 gateway timeouts and AbortController-based request timeouts (15s).

**Price check endpoint:** `GET /api/admin/price-check/:chainId/:tokenAddress` lets the frontend verify a token is priceable on Uniswap *before* creating a market, preventing failed transactions.

### Why this is a creative use of the API

Most Uniswap API integrations use it for swap execution. Horus uses it as a **cross-chain price oracle for a prediction market protocol** — a novel use case where the quote endpoint provides the price data that determines binary market outcomes. The oracle metadata (including the API endpoint URL) is stored on-chain per market, making every price submission auditable and laying the groundwork for zkTLS-verified trustless resolution.

### Meta Senate
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meta-senate-3e8e) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A governing body for the metaverse

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

NFT communities have cultural influence but no political power. DAO governance is fragmented across dozens of protocols, each with low voter turnout and whale-dominated outcomes. There's no way for communities to speak with one voice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
MetaSenate fixes this by creating an onchain congress for NFT communities:                                                                                                                                                  
  - NFT holders elect senators who represent their community in a shared governance body, turning passive collectibles into active political infrastructure
  - Senators control a Gnosis Safe multisig that aggregates delegated voting power across SporkDAO, ENS, Uniswap, Arbitrum, and Optimism
  - Anonymous voting via zero-knowledge proofs ensures ballot secrecy on a public blockchain
  - Continuous vote allocation means communities can recall and replace their senators at any time 
  - Communities nominate and onboard new collections through an onchain process, letting the Senate grow democratically.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Anonymous voting on a public blockchain:** Enabling ballot secrecy when every transaction is visible required integrating Semaphore v4 zero-knowledge proofs. The challenge was managing the full lifecycle — voter registration, identity commitment collection, and proof verification — across multiple contract versions (V2 and V3) as we iterated on the right UX for commitment phases vs. direct voting.

**Cross-chain delegation:** Supporting token delegation across mainnet, Arbitrum, and Optimism meant managing multiple chain contexts in a single UI. Wagmi's chain switching and ensuring the right RPC endpoints are hit for each delegation token
  added real complexity to what seems like a simple "delegate" button.

**ENS resolution at scale:** Resolving ENS names for every candidate and senator created a flood of RPC calls. We had to batch requests and add caching through React Query to keep the UI responsive without hammering public endpoints.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Claude code to write it, no agents run as part of it

**ETHERSPACE**

MetaSenate turns the NFT community into an onchain representative democracy.                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
**NFTs as Political Infrastructure:** Your CryptoPunk or BAYC isn't just a PFP — it's your voter registration card. NFT holders declare candidacy, vote for senators, and nominate new communities to join.                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
**Onchain Ownership Structure:** Elected senators automatically become owners of a shared Gnosis Safe multisig.

**Anonymous Voting via ZK Proofs:** Semaphore zero-knowledge proofs give NFT holders ballot secrecy on a public blockchain. Prove you're eligible without revealing which wallet voted for whom.

**Cross-DAO Power Aggregation:** Token holders delegate governance rights (not custody) across ENS, Uniswap, Arbitrum, and Optimism to the Senate Safe. One representative body, multiple ecosystems.

**Built for Mainstream:** Elections, senators, nominations, proposals — familiar democratic concepts that make crypto governance accessible to anyone, not just DeFi natives.

### ShipYield

> Earn with fractionalized cargo ship ownership

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Maritime assets like cargo ships are large, capital‑intensive, and extremely illiquid, which means only big institutions can typically participate in ship finance and secondary trading is slow and opaque. Ship owners looking for capital often rely on complex debt structures, bank syndicates, or private equity, all of which come with high friction, long negotiations, and limited transparency for investors. At the same time, there is growing demand in DeFi and RWA for yield-bearing products that are backed by real cash flows, not just on-chain leverage or purely speculative tokens.

ShipYield addresses these gaps by turning a cargo ship into a yield‑bearing NFT collection, where each NFT represents roughly 200 USD of fractional economic exposure to the vessel and its revenue stream. This makes ship finance accessible to smaller investors, improves liquidity via on‑chain secondary markets, and automates monthly yield distribution to NFT holders through smart contracts, creating a transparent, programmable “maritime income” asset class.

**Challenges we ran into**

I implemented most of the project using an AI‑assisted IDE for the coding and an AI design assistant for generating visual assets and refining the UX copy. The workflow was surprisingly smooth, but it still required me to carefully validate contract logic, front‑end state flows, and asset usage rather than just accepting AI output as‑is. The main challenge was learning how to “orchestrate” these tools effectively: breaking down tasks into small prompts, keeping the architecture consistent across multiple files, and iterating quickly without losing track of the overall product vision for ShipYield.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

I integrated AI tools directly into the development and design workflow to move faster and explore the problem space more deeply:

Cursor with Composer 1.5

Used as an AI‑assisted IDE to scaffold the smart contract architecture (collection factory, NFT contracts, yield distributor) and the basic front‑end structure (pages for collection creation, marketplace, collection detail, user dashboard, and yield claim).

Leveraged it to iterate on TypeScript/React and Solidity patterns quickly, refactor components, and enforce consistent patterns for state management and contract interaction, which is especially helpful when dealing with multiple contracts (collection, treasury, yield) and user flows.

Nanobanana for image and logos generation

**New France Village**

ShipYield directly targets the “Future of Finance” by bringing a traditionally off‑chain, illiquid asset class cargo ships on‑chain as programmable, yield‑bearing NFTs. Maritime assets represent a multi‑trillion‑dollar industry, but access is usually restricted to banks and large institutions; tokenization enables fractional ownership and turns ships into accessible, tradable real‑world assets for a global investor base.

Within this track, ShipYield demonstrates how DeFi and RWA infrastructure can be combined to:

Democratize access to ship finance through fractional NFTs priced at around 200 USD per share, significantly lowering the minimum ticket size compared to traditional ship investment products.

Automate cash‑flow distribution from real economic activity (cargo shipping revenue) via on‑chain yield claims, moving beyond speculative tokens to asset‑backed, income‑generating positions.

Improve transparency and liquidity by putting issuance, secondary trading, and yield accounting on a public ledger, addressing key pain points of traditional maritime finance where valuations, fees, and ownership structures can be opaque and hard to exit.

From a track perspective, ShipYield showcases how next‑generation financial rails can turn complex, illiquid infrastructure into simple digital products that anyone with a wallet can understand and invest in. It aligns with ongoing trends around on‑chain finance and real‑world asset tokenization, and illustrates a concrete pathway for institutional‑grade RWAs to plug into DeFi while keeping UX approachable and institutional‑looking for both issuers and investors.

**Open Project Submission**

ShipYield is closely aligned with the ADI Foundation blockchain track because it showcases how sovereign‑grade, compliance‑first infrastructure can power real‑world asset tokenization at institutional scale. The protocol takes a traditionally off‑chain, illiquid maritime asset a cargo ship and issues it as a yield‑bearing NFT collection, enabling regulated fractional exposure, secondary liquidity, and transparent yield distribution on-chain. This mirrors ADI’s focus on bringing tokenized products and stablecoin use cases from “concept into execution” on infrastructure designed for governments, banks, and large enterprises.

By design, ShipYield fits the ADI vision of onboarding the next billion users into blockchain through trusted, asset‑backed financial products rather than speculative tokens. Fractional 200 USD shares lower the entry barrier for investors in emerging markets, while the institutional, compliance‑ready UX is compatible with the kind of regulated environments ADI Chain targets (e.g., RWAs, payments, and national‑scale financial rails). The architecture of separate contracts for issuance, marketplace trading, and treasury‑backed yield distribution is well‑suited to a jurisdiction‑aware L2 like ADI Chain, where governance can enforce KYC/AML policies and asset onboarding rules at the infrastructure level.

ShipYield illustrates the type of real‑economy application ADI wants to support: tokenized infrastructure assets (ships) that generate programmable, auditable cash flows, can plug into compliant stablecoin rails (like AED‑backed or other fiat stablecoins), and can eventually serve as collateral or investment products for institutions and citizens across the Middle East, Asia, and Africa. In this way, the project is not just another DeFi experiment; it is a concrete blueprint for how ADI’s sovereign‑grade blockchain stack can be used to modernize traditional asset financing and expand financial inclusion through secure, regulated tokenization.

### Communiqué
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/communique-f6c8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/communisaas/voter-protocol) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://communi.email/demo/fresh) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/1ecf8502d35041bc865839e082df059f) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The coordination layer democracy never built.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every power structure that governs your life — your congressional representative, your HOA board, your school district, your hospital district, your landlord, your employer, your utility company — has the same accountability gap: there is no infrastructure for organized, verified, privacy-preserving constituent pressure.

> One complaint gets filed. 5,000 coordinated messages get meetings.

**But today, coordination fails in three ways:**

1. **Participation means surveillance.** To contact your representative, you surrender your home address. To organize tenants, you expose yourself to retaliation. To pressure your employer, you risk your job. Every advocacy platform is a data broker's dream. The cost of civic participation is your privacy.
2. **Institutions can't tell real people from bots.** [Staff report that most digital constituent contact has minimal policy value.](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/19331681.2020.1740907) School boards, HOA boards, and hospital districts face the same problem — when anyone can submit a form, no submission carries weight. There is no cryptographic difference between 10,000 real constituents and a script.
3. **There's no economic counterweight to lobbying.** Corporations spend $4.4B/year on professional lobbying infrastructure. Citizens get a webform. Effective civic coordination — the kind that produces the [Kansas City 247-day rent strike](https://shelterforce.org/2025/07/29/striking-tenants-withhold-rent-for-247-days-and-win/), [the Boeing 38% raise](https://www.psca.org/news/psca-news/2024/11/boeing-workers-union-gets-38-pay-raise-and-up-to-12-401k-contribution/), or [Missouri Prop A](https://mochamber.com/news-archive/proposition-a-what-employers-need-to-know/) — happens despite the tools, not because of them.

---

### Communique + VOTER Protocol

**Communique + VOTER Protocol is cryptographic coordination infrastructure for holding any power structure accountable.**

A user verifies their identity once — free, in-browser. From that point forward, a single zero-knowledge proof generated on their device proves membership across all layers of democratic governance simultaneously — congressional district, state senate, county, city council, school board, water district, hospital district, transit authority, and more — without revealing their name, address, or any personal information. The address never leaves the browser.

**What people use it for:**

* **Legislative advocacy** — Send ZK-verified messages to Congress, state legislatures, and city councils. Offices see "847 cryptographically verified constituents sent this" instead of "847 emails from unknown senders." Adapters support US (CWC API), UK (WriteToThem), and any legislature reachable by email.
* **School board and special district accountability** — The same proof that establishes your congressional district also proves your school district, library district, fire district, and community college district. Coordinate verified parent/resident pressure on boards that govern your kids' schools and your local services.
* **Tenant and workplace organizing** — Coordinate rent strikes, union card campaigns, and employer accountability with cryptographic privacy. Threshold signatures ensure anonymity sets of 10+ before revealing participation counts. Landlords and employers see coordinated, verified pressure — not individual targets for retaliation.
* **Corporate, university, and nonprofit governance** — Verified stakeholder pressure on any institution. A certified arborist challenging an HOA's tree removal policy, a nurse pressuring a hospital board on staffing ratios, a CPACC-certified consultant pushing a university on accessibility — each carries a cryptographically verified credibility multiplier from state licensing APIs.
* **Astroturf-proof coordination** — Every campaign carries a Coordination Authenticity Index: the ratio of ZK-verified senders to anonymous supporters. Example: Genuine grassroots shows 5-15% conversion. Astroturf shows 45,000 clicks and 23 proofs. On-chain engagement tiers (earned over months of diverse civic participation, not purchasable) make fake campaigns detectable.
* **Portable civic reputation** — Engagement history accrues as a soulbound on-chain credential. Action count, diversity of participation, and tenure combine into an engagement tier (0-4) that travels across campaigns and institutions. It cannot be bought, sold, or delegated — only earned.
