### ProtectedPay
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/protectedpay-18fc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Spydiecy/ProtectedPay_Base) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://protected-pay.netlify.app/dashboard) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/fQPVwutKkoI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Crypto transfers that don't suck

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Making Crypto Transfers Actually Safe**
Ever sent crypto to the wrong address? With traditional transfers, your funds are gone forever. ProtectedPay adds an escrow layer - funds stay secure until the recipient claims them, and you can refund if you made a mistake. No more "oops, there goes my life savings."

**Killing the Complexity Barrier**
Most people don't want to learn about gas fees, hex addresses, and transaction hashes, they just want to send money. Our AI lets you literally say "send 10 ETH to alice" and handles everything. Voice commands, natural language, zero crypto jargon required.

**Bringing Real Financial Tools to Base**
You shouldn't need a finance degree to trade options. We integrated Thetanuts V4 with AI explanations so anyone can understand spreads, butterflies, and condors in plain English. Plus group payments and savings pots make Base useful for everyday people, not just traders.

**Regional Access with IDRX**
Indonesia has 280M people who deserve stablecoin access. We deployed IDRX (Indonesian Rupiah) on Base Sepolia to show how the network can serve underbanked regions with low fees and fast settlement -making DeFi actually inclusive.

**Security Without the Stress**
QR code payments, username transfers instead of addresses, refundable transactions, and transparent tracking. We turned crypto from "scary and permanent" into "safe and reversible" while keeping everything non-custodial.

---

## All Platform Features

**🔐 Protected Transfers**
- Escrow protection with refunds • Username transfers (@alice) • Multi-token (ETH, USDT, USDC, IDRX) • Custom remarks • QR payments • Full transaction history

**🤖 AI Assistant**
- Natural language commands • Voice input • Balance queries • Transaction management via chat • Context-aware conversations • Multi-language support

**📊 Options Trading** (Base Mainnet)
- BTC & ETH options • Advanced strategies (Spreads, Butterflies, Condors) • AI explanations • Smart filters • Real-time data • Position tracking • Referral rewards

**👥 Group Payments**
- Create payment pools • Multi-contributor • Auto-distribution • Real-time tracking • Transparent history

**💰 Savings Pots**
- Goal-based saving •Flexible contributions • Visual progress • Yield earning • Multiple pots • Emergency withdrawals

**📱 QR System**
- Generate payment QRs • Camera/image scanning • Auto-fill forms • Secure validation • Share anywhere

**🛡️ Security**
- Non-custodial • Escrow protection • Local voice processing • Transaction transparency • Refund safety net

**🌐 Network**
- Dual network (Base Sepolia + Mainnet) • Fast finality • Low fees • Seamless switching • Network warnings

**👤 User Management**
- Username registration • Profile management • Activity feed • Balance overview • Transaction filtering

**🔧 Developer Tools**
- MCP Agent API • Smart contract integration • CLI operations • Batch transactions

**Challenges we ran into**

- Biggest pain was Thetanuts V4 only working on Base Mainnet while my other features needed Sepolia - users kept hitting confusing errors. Fixed it with network detection and clear warnings that tell people to switch chains.

- AI explanations kept failing silently because I mixed up the API key variable names
 
- Had to deploy a mock IDRX token on Base Sepolia since no real Indonesian Rupiah stablecoin exists yet, made sure it behaved exactly like USDT/USDC with proper 18 decimals.

**Base Track**

We built ProtectedPay specifically for the Base ecosystem, utilizing both Base Sepolia Testnet and Base Mainnet to showcase the network's full potential. The entire platform is designed around Base's infrastructure, our core contracts (protected transfers, group payments, savings pots) are deployed on Base Sepolia, taking advantage of its low fees and fast finality. We're not just using Base as another chain option; it's the foundation of everything we do.

What makes this a true Base project is that we're leveraging the network's unique strengths at every level. We deployed IDRX (Indonesian Rupiah stablecoin) as a mock token on Base Sepolia to demonstrate multi-token support and regional accessibility. We integrated Thetanuts V4 options trading on Base Mainnet to bring sophisticated DeFi tools to Base users. Our AI assistant makes Base accessible to everyone—you can literally say "send 10 ETH on Base" and it handles the blockchain interaction. We're showing how Base can be both user-friendly for everyday payments AND powerful enough for advanced trading, all while growing the Base ecosystem with features like yield-earning savings pots that increase TVL.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

ProtectedPay started as a secure transfer platform, but we wanted to give users more than just sending money - they needed real financial tools. We integrated Thetanuts V4 options trading so users can trade professional BTC/ETH options (spreads, butterflies, condors) right alongside their everyday transfers. It's about creating a complete DeFi experience where you can both protect funds AND actively trade.

The integration works perfectly because our AI assistant can explain complex option strategies in plain English—making advanced trading actually accessible. Users seamlessly switch between Base Sepolia for daily transfers and Base Mainnet for options trading, all in one interface. We're basically evolving from a payment app into a full-stack DeFi platform powered by Thetanuts' proven infrastructure.

> Post Jobs. Take Jobs. Get Paid.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ponder](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ponder-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The gig economy should help creators, but it often does the opposite.

Freelancers lose a big cut to platform fees, wait a long time to get paid, and don’t truly own their reputation. One account problem can erase their work history. Clients also struggle — hiring globally feels risky, disputes are slow, and cross-border payments are complicated.

Crypto offers fast, borderless payments, but it brings new confusion. Wallets, gas fees, and smart contracts feel intimidating, and new users without onchain history are hard to trust.

So we’re stuck between expensive Web2 platforms and complicated Web3 tools.

What’s missing is simple, portable trust that belongs to the user.

🎮 How Side-QUEST Changes the Game
Side-QUEST turns freelancing into an RPG-style quest system where trust, payments, and reputation live onchain — but the experience feels like a game, not a financial tool.

Instead of dealing with contracts, escrows, and invoices, users interact with a quest-based world. Jobs are presented as Quests. Clients act as Quest Givers. Freelancers become Adventurers. Payments are treated as Loot that is safely stored in a vault until the work is approved. Reputation is represented through XP and badges that show skill and reliability.

All the complex blockchain processes happen behind the scenes. Users simply play through clear, game-like actions while the technology quietly handles security, escrow, and verification in the background.
🧙 1. Invisible Web3 for Everyday Users

Most people don’t understand things like smart contracts, gas fees, or token approvals — and they shouldn’t have to.

Side-QUEST hides these technical steps. Users only see simple actions like posting a quest, completing work, and claiming rewards. Behind the scenes, smart wallets and onchain tools handle transactions, security, and escrow automatically.

This gives users the smooth experience of a normal app, while still giving them the ownership and transparency of Web3.

💰 2. Stable, Real-World Rewards

All quests are paid in IDRX, a Rupiah-backed stablecoin. This protects users from crypto price volatility.

Freelancers can earn money that holds stable value and can be used for real-life expenses. This connects onchain work with practical, everyday financial needs.

🏆 3. Reputation Becomes Onchain XP

Instead of traditional resumes or platform ratings, Side-QUEST uses a progression system.

Each completed quest gives XP. More XP unlocks higher tiers and access to better opportunities. Users also earn Soulbound badges that act as permanent, non-transferable proof of their skills and achievements.

This makes reputation verifiable, portable, and independent from any single platform.

🤝 4. Trust Without History

New users often struggle because they don’t have past reviews. Side-QUEST solves this with two systems.

Experienced users can vouch for newcomers, sharing their credibility. New users can also stake a bond, locking funds as proof of commitment and reducing risk for clients.

Trust is built through social backing and economic responsibility, not just past ratings.

🔁 The Core Work Loop

The experience follows a clear and rewarding cycle.

A client posts a quest and locks the payment in a vault.
An adventurer completes the task and submits proof.
The client approves the work.
Funds are released automatically and XP is awarded.

This loop turns freelancing into a progression journey where users grow their level and unlock new opportunities over time.

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges We Faced Building Side-QUEST

Behind the game-like design, this system is complex to build.

⚖️ 1. Designing Trust Without a Central Authority

Traditional platforms rely on support teams to resolve disputes and judge trust. Side-QUEST replaces this with smart contracts, XP systems, bond staking, and vouching logic.

We had to design rules that reduce fraud while still giving new users a fair chance. This required careful economic and game-theory balance.

🎭 2. Hiding Web3 Complexity Without Losing Security

We wanted the app to feel simple, but financial transactions are happening in the background.

Wallet signatures, contract interactions, and fund releases must remain secure and reliable. At the same time, users need clarity without being overwhelmed. Designing something both simple and safe is a major UX challenge.

💸 3. Building a Smooth Onchain Escrow System

Using IDRX required handling token approvals, vault contracts, payment release conditions, and refunds. We also had to consider edge cases like canceled work or disagreements.

All of this had to work seamlessly on mobile with minimal steps.

📈 4. Designing a Fair XP Economy

XP controls access to better quests, so balance is critical.

If XP is too easy to earn, reputation loses meaning. If it’s too hard, new users cannot grow. We had to carefully design reward rates, level thresholds, and mentorship incentives to keep the system fair and motivating.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 5. Turning Social Trust into System Rules

Vouching introduces responsibility. If an expert vouches for a bad actor, there must be consequences. We had to think about risk sharing, abuse prevention, and how to stop groups from gaming the system.

Combining social trust with economic incentives is one of the hardest design problems in Web3.

📱 6. Making Finance Feel Like a Game

We weren’t just building contracts. We were designing animations, feedback systems, progression mechanics, and emotional rewards.

Balancing fun, clarity, and financial accuracy at the same time was one of the toughest parts of the project.'

🌍 The Vision

Side-QUEST isn’t just a freelance tool.

It’s a trust layer for the onchain creator economy —
where reputation is owned, payments are stable, and work feels like leveling up in a game.

Instead of “finding clients,” creators go on Quests.
Instead of “platform ratings,” they earn XP.
Instead of “escrow services,” there are Loot Vaults.

We’re not gamifying work.

We’re making digital labor feel rewarding, fair, and truly owned

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem:**
The NFT market suffers from a lack of clear, reliable information. AI-generated art creators lack data-driven pricing tools, leading to systematic undervaluation or failed listings due to guesswork. Collectors face discovery paralysis in oversaturated marketplaces with millions of uncurated listings. Existing platforms function as passive storefronts, offering no intelligent guidance on asset valuation or market opportunities.

**The Solution:**
ArtVal is a cross-platform AI analytics tool that transforms NFT decision-making from guesswork into data-driven strategy. By analyzing visual features, historical sales data, and market dynamics across major NFT marketplaces, ArtVal provides creators with explainable pricing recommendations and offers collectors algorithmic discovery of undervalued assets before they appreciate.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. API Volatility & Integration Hurdles
Our initial backend architecture relied on the **Reservoir API** for NFT data, but we discovered it had been archived mid-development, forcing an immediate migration. We pivoted to the **OpenSea API**, but encountered persistent friction with API key authentication and email verification delays.

**The Fix:** We successfully migrated to the **Moralis API**, which provided a robust, stable alternative for fetching real-time NFT metadata without the access bottlenecks.

### 2. Adapting to Next.js & Server-Side Rendering
While our team is proficient in **React**, adopting **Next.js** presented a steep learning curve. Shifting our mindset from client-side rendering to handling Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and the Next.js App Router required rapid upskilling.

**The Fix:** We dedicated time to deep-diving into Next.js documentation, ultimately leveraging its powerful routing and optimization features to enhance ArtVal's performance.

### 3. Dependency Conflict Resolution
We faced significant dependency hell when integrating **RainbowKit** for wallet connection. The library had outdated peer dependencies that conflicted with our newer build tools.

**The Fix:** We manually resolved version mismatches and locked specific package versions to ensure compatibility across our tech stack.

### 4. Data Curation for AI Models
A major challenge was gathering high-quality, diverse datasets to fine-tune our **CLIP Embedding** and **Gemini API** models. Sourcing test NFTs that accurately represented the variance needed for effective valuation and analysis was time-consuming.

**The Fix:** We curated a custom dataset of NFTs across multiple collections to rigorously test and validate the inference capabilities of our AI models.

> National Cryptographic Firmware Portal

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest hurdles was bridging a **Linux-first reverse-engineering toolchain with a Windows development environment**. Our main development workflow runs in Windows, while tools such as Binwalk and Ghidra were installed inside Ubuntu WSL. This created path, environment-variable, process and filesystem compatibility issues when trying to automate everything from Python.

The toughest incident was the **Ghidra bridge**. Our Windows Python runner successfully launched Ghidra through WSL, but the analysis initially produced no JSON. We traced this through multiple layers: incorrect Windows-to-WSL paths, the Ghidra script receiving a directory instead of the expected JSON file path, and finally a temporary Ghidra project directory that Ghidra expected to already exist. We fixed the bridge by explicitly creating the WSL project directory, converting paths between Windows and Linux formats, passing the exact JSON output path to the Java script, and exporting Ghidra's instructions into a structured JSON format.

We also had to handle differences between Linux commands/environment variables and Windows PowerShell, while keeping the pipeline reproducible. After resolving these issues, the bridge successfully allowed us to run:

**Windows Python → WSL → Binwalk/Ghidra → JSON → Capstone → Python analysis**

That debugging process became part of the architecture itself: instead of treating each tool as an isolated utility, we built a reusable orchestration layer that can connect the Linux security tooling with our Windows-based application stack.

**The problem it solves**

Modern firmware is often a black box: security teams may receive only a compiled firmware image, with no source code or reliable documentation of what cryptography, libraries, protocols, or security-sensitive components are actually inside it. NIST’s IR 8517 (2024) documents 98 hardware security failure scenarios, explicitly covering weaknesses involving code, hardware, and firmware, highlighting how broadly security failures can occur below the application layer.

Today, investigating an unknown firmware image can require manually unpacking it, identifying binaries, reverse-engineering them, disassembling instructions, and then correlating the findings. CINDER turns this into one repeatable analysis workflow:

What changes with CINDER

**From one opaque firmware file → to an explainable security map.**

In our validated OpenWrt prototype, a 126 MB firmware image contained 171 ELF binaries; a test run automatically analyzed 5 binaries, 9,631 functions and 790,422 instructions.

For example, CINDER's analysis of libmbedcrypto.so.3.6.6 surfaced concrete implementations including AES, ChaCha20, DES, RSA, ECC, SHA, MD5, HMAC and Poly1305, with the corresponding Ghidra-recognized functions as evidence.

This matters because real firmware vulnerabilities can originate from exactly these kinds of hidden components and configurations. For example, the NIST NVD records 2024 firmware issues involving hard-coded credentials and firmware-level memory-safety flaws, illustrating why visibility into the firmware layer matters.

**Who can use it**

CINDER is designed for:

1) IoT/device manufacturers - audit released firmware before deployment.

2) Product security teams - quickly understand third-party or legacy firmware without source code.

3) Critical infrastructure/industrial environments - inspect firmware in sensitive or isolated environments.

4) Security auditors and researchers - automate the repetitive extraction and reverse-engineering stages and retain evidence for reporting.

**The core uniqueness**

CINDER is not just a vulnerability scanner. It is a binary-first firmware intelligence layer that turns an opaque firmware image into an explainable map of its contents, cryptographic implementations, binary behavior and security-relevant findings.

The immediate value is visibility and triage: instead of manually asking “What is hidden inside this firmware?”, CINDER systematically answers “What binaries are present, what code was found, where is cryptography implemented, what evidence supports it, and what deserves investigation?”

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![The Graph](https://img.shields.io/badge/The%20Graph-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Problem Statement

### **“This isn’t just a bug in supply chains — it’s a billion-dollar blind spot.”**

Global supply chains move **trillions of dollars worth of goods**, yet the systems tracking them are still **centralized, opaque, and fragmented**.

Today, supply chain data lives in disconnected databases owned by manufacturers, logistics firms, warehouses, and retailers. Each party maintains its own version of the truth — making **end-to-end verification nearly impossible**.

As a result, trust is assumed instead of proven.

### What’s broken in existing systems?

* **No real transparency**
  Participants, auditors, and regulators cannot independently verify supply chain events.

* **High data manipulation risk**
  Centralized records can be altered, backdated, or selectively hidden.

* **Slow, reactive audits**
  Auditing happens after failures — not in real time.

* **Poor real-world scalability**
  Item-level tracking doesn’t scale for bulk, high-volume logistics.

* **Dispute chaos**
  When something goes wrong, there’s no single source of truth for ownership or responsibility.

---

### Why existing blockchain solutions still fail

While researching this problem space, we uncovered **critical research and design gaps** — especially around **optimization, scalability, and efficiency**.

Even blockchain-based supply chain platforms struggle because they:

* **Tokenize individual items instead of batches**
  → Explodes transaction counts and gas costs.

* **Use inefficient on-chain storage models**
  → Overwrites state instead of appending history.

* **Ignore batch minting & aggregation**
  → Miss massive cost and performance gains.

* **Store updates as flat records**
  → Lose historical structure and traceability.

* **Can’t handle real-world throughput**
  → Break down under frequent updates and large logistics volumes.

---

##  Solution: **ChainTrack**

**ChainTrack** is a **decentralized, batch-based supply chain traceability system built on public Ethereum**.

It transforms supply chains into a **real-time, tamper-proof, auditable network** — where every participant contributes verified history instead of maintaining private records.

**Trust is no longer assumed. It’s enforced by design.**

---

##  How ChainTrack Solves the Problem

### Manufacturers / Producers

* Mint **batch-level ERC-1155 tokens** representing real production lots
* Attach certificates, origin, and specs via **IPFS**
* Establish **cryptographic proof of origin** from day one

###  Logistics & Warehousing

* Append **on-chain commits** for dispatch, transit, and storage
* Transfer ownership transparently between entities
* Replace paperwork with verifiable blockchain history

###  Retailers

* Verify full batch provenance before accepting goods
* Prove authenticity, compliance, and sourcing to customers
* Reduce counterfeit and gray-market exposure

###  Auditors & Regulators

* Perform **live, on-chain audits**
* Detect missing steps, anomalies, or unauthorized transfers instantly
* Eliminate reliance on internal company databases

###  Consumers

* View a product’s **complete provenance**
* Verify sustainability, origin, and handling claims
* Trust the product — not the intermediary

---

##  Why ChainTrack Wins (USP)

* **Batch-first architecture**
  → Built for how supply chains actually operate

* **Git-style commit model**
  → Append-only, immutable history — no overwrites

* **ERC-1155 efficiency**
  → Scalable, gas-optimized tracking at volume

* **Public Ethereum security**
  → No private ledgers, no hidden data

* **IPFS-backed metadata**
  → Rich documentation without on-chain bloat

---

##  In Simple Terms

> **ChainTrack turns the supply chain into a shared, tamper-proof timeline — where every movement is verifiable, every transfer is accountable, and trust is built into the system itself.**

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/41b82d3570804af3be05bf8d2a683062/3939e430-f14b-4f90-8407-e36922b24447.png)One major hurdle was **integrating multiple layers of the system**—smart contracts, role-based access control, IPFS metadata, The Graph indexing, and the frontend—without breaking consistency across the supply chain flow.

We faced issues with **role misconfiguration and contract–frontend mismatches**, especially when validating who could mint batch roots versus who could append commits. This caused runtime errors and failed transactions initially.

We resolved this by:

* Clearly **separating responsibilities** (producer-only batch minting, participant commit appending).
* Aligning **contract roles, ABI, and frontend checks**.
* Using **event-driven indexing** (The Graph) instead of direct state polling.

This approach stabilized the system and made the full pipeline reliable and scalable.

**The problem it solves**

💰 Expense Tracker Web Application – Project Description

This project is a simple Expense Tracker Web Application developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The main purpose of this project is to help users track their income and expenses and manage their daily finances effectively.

The application allows users to add transactions by entering a description (text) and an amount. If the amount is positive, it is treated as income, and if it is negative, it is considered an expense. Each transaction is displayed in a list with a plus (income) or minus (expense) indicator for better visual understanding.

The project dynamically calculates and displays:

Total Balance

Total Income

Total Expense

One of the key features of this project is the use of Local Storage. All transactions are stored in the browser’s local storage, which means the data does not disappear after refreshing the page. Users can also delete any transaction, and the balance, income, and expense values update automatically.

This project demonstrates important JavaScript concepts such as:

DOM manipulation

Event handling

Array methods (map, filter, reduce)

Local Storage usage

Overall, this Expense Tracker is a beginner-friendly yet practical project that shows how JavaScript can be used to build real-time, interactive web applications for personal finance management.

### GigChain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gigchain-0482) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gigchain-kappa.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/utV5NiCGaLc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous AI-Agent Payroll & Credit Protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India’s gig economy is exploding, but the workers powering it are financially the most fragile part of the system.

Platforms pay them late, earnings are opaque, and almost all social protection or formal credit is missing.

GigChain is a Web3 + AI payroll and credit protocol that gives gig workers three things they don’t have today:

    Real‑time, on‑demand payouts
    Instead of waiting for weekly or biweekly settlements, workers can get instant micro‑payouts (even per ride/order) via smart contracts triggered as soon as a task is verified as completed.​
    This reduces cash‑flow stress in a context where 90% of gig workers have little to no savings and are highly vulnerable to emergencies.​

    Transparent, verifiable earnings history
    Every payment is recorded on-chain as a tamper‑proof transaction tied to a worker’s decentralized identity.
    Workers can generate an AI‑readable, human‑friendly earnings report (in local languages) that lenders, landlords, or family can trust without screenshots or Excel hacks.​

    Fair credit access based on actual work, not CIBIL score
    Traditional banks exclude gig workers because their income is irregular and not documented in standard formats.

    GigChain uses on‑chain earnings and platform performance data to underwrite micro‑loans and salary advances via a smart‑contract credit pool, similar in spirit to the RBI Innovation Hub’s unsecured loans pilot but fully programmable and transparent.

For platforms, GigChain makes operations safer and more efficient:

    Reduces support overhead around “missing payments” by providing a single verifiable ledger for payouts.

    Allows them to offer UPI Autopay–style recurring disbursements without building their own complex payments stack, piggybacking on the massive adoption of UPI recurring payments in India.

For fintechs and lenders:

    Provides a standardized, consented data layer for assessing gig worker creditworthiness using alternative data, aligning with experiments regulators and lenders are already running in India.

In short, people use GigChain to get instant, transparent, and credit‑aware payouts, and institutions use it to safely extend financial services to a segment that has historically been invisible to formal finance.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Designing a fair on‑chain credit scoring model

Problem:
It was non‑trivial to translate messy gig platform data (irregular hours, surge pricing, multi‑app usage) into a simple, on‑chain score that is both fair to workers and usable by lenders.​

How I solved it:

    Started with NITI Aayog’s framing of key vulnerabilities (lack of savings, income volatility, no social security) and identified the minimum signals that actually correlate with reliability: streak of active days, cancellation rate, and net monthly earnings.

    Built an off‑chain scoring microservice (Python) that computes a normalized score from these signals, then writes only the final score and proof hash to the smart contract to avoid storing raw sensitive data.

    Left room for lenders to plug in their own risk multipliers while keeping the base score transparent and consistent.

2. Reconciling UPI flows with on‑chain events

Problem:
UPI Autopay lives in the traditional banking world, while GigChain’s core logic is on-chain. Ensuring that “salary released on UPI” and “payout recorded on-chain” stayed perfectly in sync was tricky, especially because UPI mandates can fail or be delayed.

How I solved it:

    Implemented a webhook listener that receives UPI status updates and only finalizes the on‑chain payout event when UPI returns a confirmed success code.

    Added a reconciliation cron job that periodically checks for mismatches between UPI transaction IDs and on‑chain records and flags them for manual review instead of silently assuming success.

    This made the system robust against partial failures and aligned with how large banks in India are handling high‑volume UPI Autopay traffic.

3. Handling identity and privacy for workers

Problem:
Gig workers often authenticate via Aadhaar or phone‑based KYC, but putting any of that directly on-chain would be a privacy and compliance nightmare.

How I solved it:

    Created a DID (decentralized identity) layer where Aadhaar/phone verification happens off‑chain with a trusted provider, which then issues a signed credential.

    The chain stores only a hash of this credential plus a revocation status, inspired by decentralized identity and verifiable credentials patterns already discussed for the gig economy.

    This way, lenders and platforms can trust that “this wallet belongs to a verified worker” without seeing or storing raw Aadhaar details.

> Blockchain + RFID to tackle fake products

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem Statement**

1. Counterfeit products are a growing threat to both online and offline retail markets, causing severe brand reputation damage and loss of consumer trust. Once a customer buys a fake product, the brand is blamed, not the counterfeit seller.
2. Global economic loss due to counterfeiting exceeds hundreds of billions of dollars annually, impacting manufacturers, retailers, governments, and end consumers through lost revenue, taxes, and jobs.
3. Existing product authentication solutions rely heavily on QR codes, barcodes, or serial numbers, all of which are easy to copy, photograph, and reuse across fake products.
4. Consumers currently have no reliable way to verify product authenticity at the point of purchase, especially in offline retail or resale markets.
5. Manufacturers lack real-time visibility into where counterfeits are appearing, making enforcement slow, reactive, and ineffective.
6. Ownership transfer and resale markets operate without trust or transparency, enabling gray markets and repeated circulation of fake goods.
7. Current systems treat physical products and digital records as separate entities, creating gaps where fraud easily occurs.


**Flow of the Solution**

1. Each physical product is linked to a unique cryptographic NFC tag that cannot be cloned or duplicated, creating a secure bridge between the physical item and its digital identity.
2. A blockchain-backed product identity is created at manufacturing time, storing a tamper-proof hash of the product metadata and manufacturer credentials.
3. When a user scans the product, the system verifies authenticity by matching the NFC-provided identifier with both the blockchain record and the backend product data.
4. Authentication works instantly at the point of sale, resale, or inspection, making verification as simple as tapping a phone. (no other software or blockchain knowledge required)
5. Every scan generates analytics data, giving manufacturers insights into scan frequency, locations, and suspicious activity patterns.
6. Failed or suspicious scans can be reported by users, along with images and location data, feeding into an AI-powered anomaly detection system.
7. The system identifies counterfeit hotspots and alerts manufacturers through a dedicated dashboard, enabling proactive action instead of delayed enforcement.
8. Ownership transfers are securely recorded, creating a transparent lifecycle history for each product and enabling safer resale markets.
9. The platform acts as a “Stripe/RazorPay for product authentication,” abstracting complex security, blockchain, and verification workflows into a simple, scalable service for brands.
10. By tightly linking physical products, digital verification, analytics, and intelligence, the solution restores trust, protects brand value, and modernizes retail authentication infrastructure.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was handling blockchain interactions reliably across different user flows, especially when MetaMask behaved differently for read-only calls versus signed transactions. I faced issues like circuit breaker errors, gas limit miscalculations, and user-denied signatures during ownership transfers. Debugging these required separating read-only verification calls from write operations and carefully tuning gas estimation instead of relying on defaults. Another hurdle was integrating multiple backends running on different ports without breaking existing functionality, which I solved by clearly isolating responsibilities and routing between services. Data consistency between blockchain state and MongoDB records was also tricky, so I enforced a strict flow where on-chain transactions complete first before updating the backend. Finally, integrating AI models like CLIP without impacting system performance required moving heavy inference to a dedicated backend and optimizing request payloads.

### AgriFinance
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agrifinance-88b5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Ritinpaul/AgriFinanceProduction) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://crop-cash-3.emergent.host/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1155706487?fl=ip&fe=ec) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Rebuilding Agricultural Finance with Trust

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We started working on AgriFinance after noticing that most problems in agriculture aren’t about production they’re about trust and access.
Many small farmers still can’t get loans without collateral or heavy paperwork. Credit decisions are often unclear, slow, and biased, which pushes farmers toward informal lenders with high interest rates. On the other side, lenders and buyers don’t have reliable ways to verify farm data, certifications, or where produce actually comes from. Supply chain records are fragmented and easy to manipulate.

AgriFinance tries to fix this gap.
It allows farmers to apply for collateral-free loans where every step from approval to repayment is visible on-chain. Instead of relying on a single opaque score, we use multiple data points to evaluate creditworthiness more fairly. Land records, produce batches, and certifications are represented digitally so they can be verified without manual paperwork.
For buyers, the platform makes it easy to scan a QR code and see where the product came from, who produced it, and how it moved through the supply chain. For lenders, it reduces risk by making loan data transparent and auditable.
Our goal is simple: make agricultural finance clearer, safer, and more accessible, without forcing users to understand blockchain or manage complex tools.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was making Web3 usable for non-technical users. Farmers shouldn’t have to worry about wallets, gas fees, or failed transactions.

To solve this, we used account abstraction so users can interact with the platform without managing gas or private keys directly. This made the experience feel much closer to a regular app.

Another major challenge was handling the loan lifecycle on-chain. Managing approvals, repayments, and real token transfers while keeping the frontend and backend in sync took several iterations. We solved this by designing a dedicated Loan Vault contract with clear state transitions and syncing it with an indexer for accurate analytics.
Privacy was also tricky. Land documents and certifications need to be verified, but storing them openly on-chain isn’t practical. We addressed this using zero-knowledge proofs so users can prove validity without exposing sensitive information.
Finally, ensuring QR codes couldn’t be reused or tampered with required careful design. Each QR is linked directly to immutable on-chain records, which prevents duplication or manipulation.
These challenges pushed us to focus on building something practical and production-ready, not just a demo.

### AmnesiaChain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/amnesiachain-52e9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/monish-instinct/AmnesiaChain.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://amnesia-chain.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decentralized memory. Intentional forgetting.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🚨 The Problem AmnesiaChain Solves

Today’s digital systems are built to **remember everything forever**.

That’s not how humans work — and it’s not how safe systems should work.

### What’s broken in existing systems?

- **Data hoarding by default**  
  Once data is stored, it’s rarely deleted — even when it’s no longer useful or relevant.

- **Permanent risk exposure**  
  Old data becomes a liability: breaches, leaks, compliance failures, and misuse.

- **No concept of relevance decay**  
  A file accessed once years ago is treated the same as critical, frequently used data.

- **“Delete” isn’t real**  
  In most platforms, deletion is reversible, cached, backed up, or still accessible by admins.

- **User has no real control**  
  Centralized platforms decide retention, not the data owner.

---

## 🧠 How AmnesiaChain Fixes This

AmnesiaChain introduces **human-like memory behavior** into digital data systems.

It allows data to be **remembered, archived, or permanently forgotten** — by design.

### What people can use it for

- **Secure personal data storage**  
  Store sensitive data with the ability to truly erase it later.

- **Time-bound data sharing**  
  Share data that automatically expires or fades based on relevance or access patterns.

- **Compliance-safe data retention**  
  Automatically forget data to meet privacy requirements and reduce legal exposure.

- **Decentralized knowledge management**  
  Keep important data active, archive rarely used data, and discard irrelevant data.

- **Risk-reduced backups**  
  Old data does not remain as a long-term security liability.

---

## 🔐 Why This Is Safer Than Existing Systems

- Permanent forgetting is enforced cryptographically  
- No central authority controls data lifecycle  
- Cognitive relevance scoring adapts over time  
- Attack surface decreases as data is forgotten

---

## ⚡ In One Line

**AmnesiaChain solves the problem of permanent data by giving digital systems the ability to forget — safely, intelligently, and irreversibly.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧱 Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Making “Forgetting” Truly Irreversible

**The challenge:**  
In most systems, deleting data is superficial — the data may still exist in backups, replicas, or node histories. For AmnesiaChain, this directly undermined its core promise.

**Why this was difficult:**  
- Blockchains are append-only by design  
- Nodes replicate historical data  
- Encrypted data can still be recovered if keys persist

**How I solved it:**  
- Ensured data is never stored directly on-chain  
- Stored only cryptographic references and metadata on the blockchain  
- Controlled access using ephemeral encryption keys  
- Implemented irreversible key destruction to enforce forgetting  

Once keys are destroyed, the data becomes mathematically unrecoverable.

---

### 2. Balancing Decentralization With Cognitive Intelligence

**The challenge:**  
Cognitive relevance scoring requires contextual awareness, but decentralization avoids centralized decision-making. This caused inconsistent memory behavior across nodes.

**Why this was difficult:**  
- Nodes observe different access patterns  
- Global scoring risks reintroducing centralization  
- Conflicting relevance scores could trigger unintended forgetting

**How I solved it:**  
- Used deterministic, rule-based relevance signals  
- Anchored memory state transitions to on-chain consensus  
- Allowed local optimization while enforcing global state agreement

This preserved decentralization without sacrificing predictability.

---

### 3. Preventing Accidental or Malicious Data Loss

**The challenge:**  
Irreversible forgetting introduces the risk of permanent loss due to mistakes or malicious actions.

**How I addressed it:**  
- Added a configurable grace period before permanent deletion  
- Required explicit confirmation for destructive actions  
- Logged all memory state transitions immutably for auditing

---

## 🧠 Key Learning

Designing a system that can safely forget required rethinking traditional blockchain assumptions. True data ownership means not just storing data securely, but also knowing when and how to let it go.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

AmnesiaChain aligns with the Duality AI track by applying **semantic intelligence to decentralized data management**, similar to how Duality AI performs semantic understanding of complex environments.

While Duality AI focuses on semantic scene segmentation in physical offroad environments, AmnesiaChain brings the same core idea to **digital environments** — identifying what data is relevant, what can be archived, and what should be forgotten.

The project uses cognitive intelligence to:
- Classify stored data based on relevance, access patterns, and age
- Semantically segment data into memory states (active, archived, forgotten)
- Optimize decentralized storage by removing low-value or obsolete data

Just as Duality AI reduces noise and improves decision-making by understanding scene context, AmnesiaChain reduces digital risk and storage overhead by understanding **data context** and enforcing intelligent, irreversible forgetting on a decentralized system.

This makes AmnesiaChain a semantic, AI-driven system operating in a non-visual but equally complex environment: decentralized data memory.

> A private, fair, bot-resistant ticket system

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contract-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Current live event ticketing platforms suffer from two major problems: large-scale ticket scalping by automated bots, and privacy risks caused by centralized storage of user data. These issues result in unfair access to tickets, inflated resale prices, and loss of user trust.

My solution, ZeroPass, is a semi-centralized live event booking system that combines blockchain and zero-knowledge proofs to address both challenges. Tickets are issued as blockchain-based tokens to prevent unauthorized duplication and resale. To protect user privacy, I use zero-knowledge proofs to verify ticket ownership and eligibility without exposing personal user information to the blockchain or event organizers.

By combining decentralized verification with selective off-chain components for scalability, ZeroPass enables fair ticket distribution, strong anti-scalping protections, and privacy-preserving identity verification, creating a more transparent and user-centric ticketing experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Balancing decentralization with real-world performance**
Fully on-chain ticketing and identity management introduced high gas costs and slow user experience. I had to design a semi-centralized architecture where critical verification happens on-chain, while user data and metadata are handled off-chain for scalability.

**Integrating zero-knowledge identity with real users**
Mapping real users (phone/email login via Privy) to zero-knowledge identities (Semaphore commitments) without leaking personal data required careful design. Ensuring that identities remain private while still being verifiable at entry gates was a major technical challenge.

**User experience for a complex cryptographic system**
Zero-knowledge proofs, wallets, and blockchain concepts are complex for normal users. A major challenge was abstracting this complexity through UI and services like Privy so users can sign up and buy tickets without understanding cryptography.

**The problem it solves**

SecureDocChain allows universities, government bodies, companies, and individuals to issue, store, and verify documents in a fast, secure, and tamper-proof way. Universities and authorities can generate blockchain-backed degrees, licenses, and official documents with one click, while professionals receive permanent, portable certificates they can share anywhere. Employers and verifiers can instantly validate any credential using just a certificate hash—no registration, no emails, no waiting. Since every document is stored on decentralized IPFS and protected by SHA-256 hashing, any attempt at forgery or tampering becomes immediately detectable. Real-time revocation checks, expiry validation, and issuer authentication ensure that only legitimate, up-to-date documents pass verification. In simple terms, SecureDocChain replaces slow, manual, trust-based verification processes with an instant, automated, and fraud-proof system that works globally, 24/7, making document handling easier, safer, and completely reliable for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, we planned to embed a QR code inside every certificate.
The QR would contain the certificate hash and link to our verification page.

However, we discovered a major loophole:

❌ Real‑world certificates (govt docs, degrees, licenses) already come with their own QR codes
Those QRs lead to their official verification portals

They do not contain our certificate hash

They cannot be replaced or overwritten

Scanning our custom QR on top of an original certificate would create confusion and conflict

Many documents don’t have any QR at all — meaning no standard way to embed our hash

This made our QR idea unreliable and disconnected from real-world workflows.

✔️ How We Solved It
Instead of forcing a QR system that doesn’t align with actual documents, we switched to a simpler, more robust, universal verification method:

🔥 We introduced a hash-based verification link, not depend on QR.
Every issued certificate gets a unique cryptographic hash. The recipient receives a mail of the document.

> Enforcing B2B payments without trust or follow-ups

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In B2B trade, sellers often provide credit to buyers, but delayed or missed payments are extremely common. This blocks working capital, disrupts cash flow, and forces sellers to rely on trust, manual follow-ups, or weak enforcement mechanisms.

SettleFlow solves this by introducing automated payment discipline using a rolling security deposit enforced through smart contracts. Instead of chasing payments, sellers get predictable enforcement, while buyers operate under clear and transparent rules—without changing existing trade workflows or pricing structures.

**Challenges we ran into**

- One major challenge was deciding what logic should stay off-chain versus on-chain. Putting everything on blockchain would be expensive and inflexible, while keeping everything off-chain would reintroduce trust issues.

This was solved by clearly separating responsibilities:

- The backend handles business logic like exposure calculation, deadlines, and risk evaluation.

- The smart contract only handles fund custody and penalty enforcement.

- Another challenge was integrating the backend with the smart contract securely. This was addressed using ethers.js, strict role-based access control, and wallet-level enforcement in the smart contract to prevent unauthorized actions.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem it solves
Investing in **government bonds** is often ***confusing, inaccessible, and limited to large minimum amounts***. For most people, understanding how bonds work or even seeing where their money goes is difficult. ***Bondbuy*** makes this simpler and safer by enabling fractional ownership of government bonds, allowing users to invest small amounts, see every transaction on-chain, and receive clear NFT-based proof of ownership. It removes opacity, lowers entry barriers, and helps users learn how real-world bond investing works in a transparent, **Web3-**native way.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I ran into

One of the biggest challenges was ****handling wallet interactions reliably****. Phantom wallet behavior on *Devnet* was sometimes inconsistent, especially during transaction signing and NFT minting. At times, transactions appeared successful on the frontend but failed silently on-chain. I overcame this by adding ***explicit transaction confirmation checks***, improving error handling, and closely monitoring logs on Solana Explorer to trace failures.

Another hurdle was ****implementing fractional bond logic**** in a way that felt realistic but still fit a hackathon demo. Mapping small ₹ investments to SOL values and ensuring accurate fractional ownership required careful validation. I solved this by *normalizing inputs*, locking exchange assumptions, and clearly communicating that this is an educational prototype.

Finally, ****on-chain data syncing with the dashboard**** was tricky. Keeping portfolio metrics in sync with live blockchain state required better state management and re-fetching strategies, which I refined through testing and iteration.

**Ethereum Track**

### ETHIndia — Track Justification

Bondby aligns with the ETHIndia track by incorporating **Ethereum-compatible smart contract concepts** in its system design. While the demo implementation uses Solana Devnet for faster transactions and lower friction during a hackathon, the **core bond registry, fractional ownership logic, and NFT-based proof of ownership are designed to be EVM-compatible** and can be deployed on Ethereum or Layer-2 networks without architectural changes.

The project demonstrates how **Ethereum smart contracts** can act as a canonical source of truth for bond definitions, ownership records, and verification, enabling transparent and tamper-resistant financial infrastructure. Bondby showcases how traditional financial instruments like government bonds can be modeled and owned fractionally using Ethereum’s programmable trust layer.

**AOPS**

### AOPS $100 (Open) — Track Justification

Bondby aligns with the AOPS (Art of Problem Solving) track by emphasizing **learning through structured problem-solving and conceptual understanding**, rather than just outcomes. The project breaks down complex financial concepts like government bonds, yields, maturity, and fractional ownership into clear, logical steps that users can explore hands-on. By interacting with on-chain transactions and NFT-based ownership, users actively reason about value distribution, proportions, and long-term returns—skills closely tied to mathematical thinking.

Bondby encourages users to understand *why* a system works, not just *what* it does, mirroring AOPS’ philosophy of deep comprehension and analytical reasoning. As an educational Web3 demo, it helps learners build intuition around real-world financial and mathematical systems in an interactive, problem-driven way.

**The problem it solves**

## The problem WOC Proposal solves

**Proposal 1 (Programmers Paradise):**  
Programmers Paradise addresses the difficulty learners face in transitioning from theoretical programming knowledge to real-world development and meaningful open-source contribution. Many beginners struggle with scattered learning resources, lack of structured guidance, and limited exposure to production-grade workflows. This proposal provides a **centralized, guided learning and collaboration platform** that enables users to practice through real projects, collaborate with peers, and progressively build confidence in contributing to professional open-source ecosystems.

**Proposal 2 (Kornia):**  
Modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as BLIP-2 and LLaVA are powerful but difficult to fine-tune and deploy due to fragmented training pipelines, model-specific scripts, and the absence of standardized multimodal data handling. This proposal introduces a **Kornia-native fine-tuning and training API** that unifies dataset ingestion, model integration, and scalable training workflows, reducing technical barriers while improving reproducibility and accessibility for researchers, students, and open-source contributors.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I ran into

**Proposal 1 (Programmers Paradise):**  
One significant challenge is designing a learning platform that remains beginner-friendly while still supporting advanced users and collaborative development workflows. This can be addressed by implementing a **modular feature and learning system**, where users progressively unlock advanced tools and project capabilities based on experience level, ensuring both accessibility and long-term scalability.

**Proposal 2 (Kornia):**  
A key challenge is creating APIs that are flexible enough to support diverse Vision-Language Model architectures while remaining consistent with Kornia’s modular design philosophy. This can be tackled by designing a **plugin-based model registry and standardized configuration schema**, enabling new models to be integrated cleanly without modifying the core training framework.

**Ethereum Track**

This project integrates with the Ethereum track by addressing the critical need for **Data Integrity and Provenance** in decentralized machine learning. Trust in ML models depends heavily on the quality and history of the training data; our system provides a pathway to verify that data has not been tampered with or poorly prepared.

The integration points include:
* **On-Chain Transformation Manifests:** The JSON-based "Transformation Manifests" generated by our system can be hashed and stored on the Ethereum blockchain. This creates a permanent, immutable record of exactly how a dataset was cleaned and transformed.
* **Verifiable Preprocessing:** In a decentralized AI ecosystem, this framework can act as a "Proof of Preparation." Users can verify on-chain that a specific "ML-Readiness Score" was achieved before a model was trained, enhancing transparency in collaborative Web3 data environments.
* **Decentralized Data Quality Audits:** Our Validation Layer can be extended to verify data quality for decentralized data marketplaces, ensuring that "garbage" data is never sold or used for model training in a permissionless network.

**AOPS**

This project directly addresses the core mission of AI Operations by automating the "Data-to-Model" lifecycle, which currently consumes 80% of an engineer's time. It introduces a production-ready **Strategy-Execution-Validation** pipeline that transforms Ak-dskit from a simple wrapper library into a reasoning-driven ML engineering framework.



**Key AOPS Contributions:**
* **Operational Automation:** Uses the RGPTT framework to autonomously profile, plan, and execute data transformations without manual intervention.
* **Quality Assurance:** Implements a rigorous **Validation Layer** with a weighted ML-Readiness Score (missingness, variance, multicollinearity) to ensure only high-quality data enters the training pipeline.
* **Governance & Auditability:** Every pipeline decision is captured in a machine-readable **Transformation Manifest (JSON)**, allowing for full audit trails and environment-independent reproducibility.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nexus-governance-24fd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rbanik1204/NEXUS-GOVERNANCE) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://nexus-org.web.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decentralized Autonomous Organization

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🚨 The Problem It Solves

Modern governance — in governments, universities, cooperatives, and public institutions — still relies on opaque, manual, and trust-based processes.

Decisions that affect thousands of people are often:

Recorded in centralized databases

Approved via emails, meetings, or paperwork

Executed manually

Audited after the fact

This creates several critical problems:

❌ Lack of transparency – citizens must trust reports rather than verify decisions

❌ Delayed execution – approved decisions take weeks or months to implement

❌ Centralized control – a small group can override or modify outcomes

❌ Weak auditability – audits depend on internal records, not proof

❌ Low participation – complex processes discourage engagement

In short, governance today depends more on trust than on verification.

🧠 What This Project Enables (DGOS)

This project introduces a Decentralized Governance Operating System (DGOS) — a blockchain-based platform that turns governance rules into enforceable code.

Instead of relying on people to follow procedures, the system enforces them automatically.

🔁 How It Makes Governance Easier, Safer, and Verifiable
🔹 1. Transparent Decision-Making

Every proposal, vote, and result is:

Publicly visible

Cryptographically verifiable

Permanently recorded

Anyone can independently verify outcomes — no special access required.

🔹 2. Trustless Voting

Votes are:

Counted automatically

Protected from tampering

Enforced by smart contracts

No manual counting.
No hidden changes.
No post-hoc corrections.

🔹 3. Automatic Execution

Once a decision is approved:

Funds are released automatically

Actions execute without human discretion

Delays and bottlenecks are eliminated

Approved decisions are not just recorded — they are executed.

🔹 4. Built-In Accountability

Every action creates:

An immutable audit trail

Verifiable transaction records

Public proof of compliance

Audits no longer depend on internal documents — they depend on facts.

🔹 5. Reduced Risk of Misuse

The system ensures:

No single person can override results

No funds can move without approval

No data can be quietly altered

Power is distributed, rules are enforced, and abuse becomes detectable.

👥 What People Can Use It For

This platform can be used by:

🏛️ Governments & Public Bodies

Budget approvals

Policy voting

Grant distribution

Community fund management

🎓 Universities & Institutions

Senate decisions

Student governance

Research funding allocation

🤝 Cooperatives & NGOs

Member voting

Transparent fund usage

Proposal-based decision-making

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Large Communities

Delegated governance

Shared treasury control

Community-driven initiatives

📘 Example: Community Development Fund

A local authority wants to allocate funds for public projects.

A proposal is created for funding a project

Eligible members vote digitally

The system enforces quorum and voting rules

Once approved, funds are released automatically

Every step is publicly auditable

No paperwork. No manual approvals. No ambiguity.

✨ Why This Matters

This project does not aim to replace existing democratic systems overnight.

Instead, it provides:

A verifiable governance layer

A pilot-ready digital infrastructure

A transparent alternative to trust-based workflows

It replaces “Trust us” with “Verify it yourself.”

🧭 In One Sentence

This project transforms governance from a trust-based process into a transparent, verifiable, and automatically enforced system.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a decentralized governance system is very different from building a typical web application. The biggest challenges were not visual or UI-related, but architectural, correctness-related, and ethical.

Below are the most important hurdles I faced and how I resolved them.

1. Mistaking a Polished UI for a Working System

The Challenge

Initially, the platform looked complete:

Proposals were visible

Voting buttons existed

Treasury numbers were displayed

However, after running an external audit, I realized that many core features were only simulated in the frontend and not enforced on-chain.

This was a critical wake-up call.

How I Addressed It

Paused all demonstrations immediately

Audited every feature end-to-end

Classified components as real, partial, or UI-only

Stopped relying on mock data

This shifted my mindset from “feature completeness” to system correctness.

2. Voting That Looked Functional but Was Not Real

The Challenge

The voting flow appeared to work visually, but:

No blockchain transaction was created

Vote counts were updated using local state

Demo logic masked failures

This is extremely dangerous in governance systems.

How I Addressed It

Removed all frontend vote simulations

Disabled voting unless a valid on-chain transaction is confirmed

Forced failures when contracts are missing or misconfigured

If a vote does not create a transaction hash, it is not considered a vote.

3. Contract Addresses Without Deployed Bytecode

The Challenge

Frontend code pointed to smart contract addresses that:

Existed as addresses

But had zero bytecode deployed

This caused silent failures that were easy to miss.

How I Addressed It

Verified every contract address on Etherscan

Added bytecode checks before contract interaction

Blocked UI actions if contracts are not deployed

An address existing is not the same as a contract existing.

4. Demo Data Contaminating Real Data

The Challenge

For early visualization, demo data was used:

Fake proposal counts

Fake treasury values

Hardcoded analytics

Over time, this became misleading and unsafe for demos.

How I Addressed It

Removed all hardcoded metrics

Clearly separated demo and live modes

Defaulted the system to show empty but honest data

Empty truth is better than polished falsehood.

5. Designing an “Admin Panel” Without Centralized Power

The Challenge

Governance systems need administration, but:

Traditional admin panels imply override power

This contradicts decentralization and public trust

How I Addressed It

Redesigned the admin section as an Operations Panel

Limited actions to configuration and safety controls

Ensured no admin could change votes or move funds

Admins manage the system, not the decisions.

6. Balancing Transparency With Usability

The Challenge

Blockchain systems are inherently complex, but:

Government staff and citizens are non-technical

Raw blockchain data is intimidating

How I Addressed It

Used plain-language explanations

Added clear warnings and confirmations

Displayed transaction hashes and proofs without jargon

Transparency should reduce confusion, not create it.

7. Knowing When Not to Demo

The Challenge

The hardest decision was choosing not to demo certain features until they were real.

It is tempting to show polished flows, but governance systems require integrity.

How I Addressed It

Disabled incomplete features

Clearly communicated system limitations

Focused on correctness over presentation

Trust, once lost, cannot be regained with better UI.

Key Takeaway

This project taught me that governance software is not about appearance, but about truth.

Every feature must answer one question:

Can this be independently verified?

If the answer is no, the feature is not finished.

### Signal2Trade
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/signaltrade-45a4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AyUsHPaNcHoLIIIITA/Ayush_67/blob/main/Final.ipynb) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Out%20Of%20Context'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://out-of-context-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Predicting the future, trading with discipline.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Cryptocurrency markets are highly volatile, making reliable price prediction and decision‑making difficult.
Our project addresses this by using leakage‑free time‑series forecasting to predict Bitcoin prices and converting those predictions into a realistic, rule‑based trading strategy evaluated with proper backtesting and risk metrics.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the key challenges we faced was reducing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) while maintaining a leakage‑free time‑series setup.
More complex models such as XGBoost did not perform well due to limited daily data and sensitivity to hyperparameters, often leading to unstable results.
We addressed this by shifting to a regularized linear approach and successfully reduced error using Ridge Regression with appropriate alpha tuning, achieving more stable and reliable predictions.

**Ethereum Track**

The Ethereum ecosystem powers a wide range of decentralized financial applications, including trading, lending, and asset management.
A key challenge in this ecosystem is making informed decisions in highly volatile markets using reliable, data‑driven methods.

Our project addresses this challenge by building a leakage‑free time‑series forecasting and strategy evaluation framework for crypto assets. While demonstrated using Bitcoin price data, the same pipeline is directly applicable to Ethereum and ERC‑20 tokens, as they share similar market dynamics and are actively traded within DeFi protocols.

The project’s ability to convert predictions into transparent, rule‑based trading signals and evaluate them with realistic backtesting and risk metrics makes it highly relevant for Ethereum‑based use cases such as:

DeFi trading bots

Portfolio management for Ethereum assets

Risk analysis for on‑chain financial applications

This makes the solution a strong analytical foundation for building smarter, data‑driven tools in the Ethereum ecosystem.

**The problem it solves**

The main problem with today's DNS is that it is highly centralised, hence the maintenance and security of the records of DNS depends on the small number of servers and authorities it is trusted with.
DeDNS solves this problem by decentralising and treating DNS as a public good: resolution remains free and accessible to everyone, while write operations pay a small protocol fee that sustainably funds the shared infrastructure.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges I faced was syncing the state of transactions between the frontend, wallet and blockchain. At one point, when transactions were successfully executed from the frontend and ETH was deducted from my wallet, but the on-chain public goods pool appeared to remain at zero. 
The root cause turned out to be a provider mismatch in Remix. It was not connected to the same MetaMask environment and network that the frontend was using. As a result, I was inspecting the state of a different contract instance than the one actually receiving the transactions.

> “Freedom to spend. Safety to trust.”

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Smart Allowance Wallet is a rule-based digital wallet that lets guardians safely control how money is spent instead of just sending it blindly. Parents, companies, or DAOs can set limits like spending amount, allowed categories, time windows, and approval requirements, while users can spend freely within those rules or request permission when needed. By enforcing these rules automatically, it prevents misuse before it happens, improves transparency, and makes everyday spending safer, smarter, and more responsible.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building the Smart Allowance Wallet, I faced a few hurdles:

Pending Requests Not Updating in Real-Time

Problem: When a receiver sent a spend request, the guardian dashboard didn’t show it immediately.

Solution: I implemented a state-based system in React with useEffect and context updates, so any new request triggers a real-time dashboard refresh.

TypeScript Type Errors

Problem: The Transaction type didn’t include certain fields like id or time, which caused red underlines in the IDE.

Solution: I updated the type definitions to include all necessary fields and ensured consistency across components.

Enforcing Category & Time-Based Rules

Problem: Preventing spending outside allowed categories or time windows required extra logic.

Solution: I built a rule-checking function that runs before every transaction and blocks invalid attempts with a clear error message.

Emergency Unlock Logic

Problem: Allowing guardians to unlock funds in emergencies without bypassing other rules was tricky.

Solution: I added a separate “emergency mode” in the smart contract/context that temporarily overrides limits but logs every action for transparency.

**Freshers**

The Smart Allowance Wallet is perfect for the Freshers Track because it demonstrates practical problem-solving with real-world impact while using fundamental web3, React, and TypeScript skills—all achievable for beginners:

Hands-On Learning: Freshers get to work with frontend (React), state management, TypeScript types, and smart contract logic in one project.

Real-World Problem: It solves a common, relatable problem—safe and controlled money management for children, students, or employees—without needing advanced domain expertise.

Scalable & Extendable: Even as a beginner project, it shows good architecture (wallet context, rule enforcement, approval flows), which can be scaled later.

Judges-Friendly: The problem is easy to understand, the solution is visible through the UI, and the impact is measurable—perfect for a beginner track.

Essentially, it’s a full-stack beginner-friendly project with visible results, demonstrating both coding skills and thoughtful design.
