**Challenges we ran into**

First, integrating x402 with Solana Pay was a total nightmare: Phantom QR scans wouldn't auto-unlock, localhost links immediately broke upon deploying to Vercel, and USDC decimal math confused atomic units. We solved this by reference tracking for instant payment detection, dynamic URLs that adapt to production, and correcting token formatting. Meanwhile, we had to escape Next.js "hydration hell": wallet providers would cause upwards of 50 mismatch errors; dynamic imports are breaking server components. Moving the Navbar client-side, suppressing hydration warnings, and strictly using CSS variables over Tailwind defaults finally stabilized our brutalist UI and eliminated the layout shifts.

**Open Track**

Meed is a perfect fit for the Open Category because it solves the "subscription fatigue" of the music industry by enabling a high-frequency, low-cost business model that is technically impossible in traditional finance. By leveraging Solana’s high speed and minimal gas fees, the platform facilitates true micro-commerce, allowing users to buy individual tracks for fractions of a cent ($0.002) without the heavy transaction fees of a credit card. This project moves blockchain beyond speculation and into everyday mass adoption, replacing the "rental" model of streaming with digital ownership and a fair 95% revenue split for artists. As a fully-functional, full-stack application integrated with Solana Pay and deployed on Vercel, Meed demonstrates a practical, consumer-ready use case that justifies the existence of Web3 technology in the real world.

### Sentinel-Vault
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sentinelvault-b131) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sarnav07/Sentinel-Vault-) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-oV-GApxmI4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-StackTooDeep%20v3.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stacktoodeep-v-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Investing the smart way ...

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solodity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solodity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: DeFi is too complex, risky, and fragmented for the average user. Currently, users who want to earn yield have to navigate a fragmented landscape. They must manually monitor lending rates on Aave, manage complex liquidity ranges on Uniswap V3 to avoid impermanent loss, and constantly watch the market for crashes. This requires:

Constant Monitoring: 24/7 attention to prevent liquidations or heavy losses.

High Gas Costs: Manually moving funds between protocols to chase the best yield is expensive.

Technical Complexity: Understanding "ticks" and "health factors" is a barrier to entry.

The Solution: A "Set-and-Forget" Smart Vault Our DeFi Vault simplifies this entire process into a single ERC4626 deposit. It acts as an autonomous hedge fund manager that:

Automates Yield: Smart contracts automatically route capital between Aave V3 (Lending) and Uniswap V3 (Liquidity) based on real-time performance, ensuring capital is always working efficiently.

Mitigates Risk: The "Risk Guardian" module (powered by Chainlink Automation) monitors market health off-chain. If a market crash or de-peg event is detected, it automatically triggers an on-chain "Stop-Loss," exiting risky positions to protect user principal.

Standardizes Access: By using the ERC4626 standard, our vault is fully composable, meaning other protocols can build on top of our strategy easily.

In short, we turn complex, active portfolio management into a simple, passive savings account.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a vault that interacts with two major protocols (Aave & Uniswap) while keeping the user experience simple was significantly harder than expected. Here are the main hurdles:

1. The "Uniswap Tick Math" Nightmare

The Problem: Integrating Uniswap V3 is not like V2. You can't just provide token amounts; you have to calculate "Ticks" and "Square Root Prices" (SqrtPriceX96). Doing this math inside Solidity is gas-heavy and prone to overflow errors.

The Fix: Instead of forcing the smart contract to calculate the range, I moved the complex math to the frontend. I used the Uniswap SDK to calculate the optimal tickLower and tickUpper client-side and passed those raw integers to the smart contract. This saved massive amounts of gas and prevented transaction reverts.

2. Handling "Zero State" in the Dashboard

The Problem: My charts and data visualizations worked perfectly when the vault had money in it. But when I tested with a fresh wallet, the entire dashboard crashed with NaN (Not a Number) errors and "Division by Zero" exceptions because the Total Value Locked (TVL) was 0.

The Fix: I had to rewrite the frontend data hooks to strictly handle "null" states. As you can see in my screenshots, I implemented dedicated "No Active Strategy" UI states and placeholders that appear only when the user has no deposits, ensuring the app looks professional even for a first-time user.

3. Chainlink Automation Gas Limits

The Problem: The "Risk Guardian" needs to check the health of the portfolio off-chain. Initially, my checkUpkeep function was too heavy, trying to simulate the entire withdrawal process to see if a stop-loss was needed. This caused the Chainlink nodes to timeout.

The Fix: I optimized the off-chain check to rely strictly on the latestRoundData() from the Price Feeds. I created a lightweight "Health Factor" view function that returns a simple boolean, allowing the Automation nodes to check the system status instantly without running complex logic.

### ChainAid
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/chainaid-2473) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AvniMittal07/ChainAid) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/y8mJLBniBYc?si=efu-bEyOVBuurZIO) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-StackTooDeep%20v3.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stacktoodeep-v-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> ChainAid: The Immutable Memory of Giving.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ChainAid bridges the gap between the momentary spark of empathy and the technical execution of a donation. In the fast-paced Web3 world, many users experience "compassion fade"—the phenomenon where a genuine intent to help a cause is lost because the user isn't near their wallet, is on the wrong network, or simply gets distracted by daily life. By providing a decentralized Memory Vault, ChainAid allows users to anchor their philanthropic intentions onto the blockchain the moment they feel them, transforming a fleeting thought into a permanent commitment.

Beyond solving the problem of forgetfulness, the platform tackles the high "cognitive load" associated with crypto transactions. Manually managing wallet addresses, checking gas fees, and remembering specific amounts for different charities can be overwhelming, often leading to "donation procrastination." ChainAid streamlines this process by linking smart reminders directly to non-custodial wallets, allowing for a "planned giving" workflow. It replaces the anxiety of manual execution with a secure, transparent, and tech-driven system that ensures every act of kindness finds its destination, turning the cold technology of the blockchain into a warm tool for consistent global impact.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building ChainAid involved navigating several technical and design hurdles unique to the Web3 ecosystem. One of the primary challenges was asynchronous state management, where the app had to constantly synchronize with MetaMask to handle account changes and transaction statuses without freezing the user interface. This was compounded by asset-routing complexities in React, specifically learning how the src and public folders interact when referencing high-resolution background images within CSS modules.

From a design perspective, transitioning from a standard light-themed layout to a dark, image-heavy Glassmorphic UI required a deep dive into CSS layering and transparency. Ensuring high readability meant balancing background blur effects with rgba color values so that critical donation reminders remained the focal point. Finally, managing transaction lifecycle logic—from triggering the initial provider request to handling user rejections and waiting for block confirmations—required robust error-handling to prevent the "silent failures" that often frustrate decentralized application (dApp) users.

**Freshers**

For a fresher's track, ChainAid is a standout project because it demonstrates a holistic understanding of the decentralized ecosystem, moving beyond simple "smart contract" tutorials to solve a genuine human-centric problem. It proves that the developer can navigate the full-stack Web3 lifecycle, from building an intuitive, high-end React interface with modern design patterns like Glassmorphism to managing complex asynchronous logic with ethers.js. By tackling challenges like persistent state synchronization, non-custodial wallet integration, and the "compassion fade" problem, the project showcases product-level thinking—the ability to identify a social friction and engineer a secure, technical solution.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### RaiseX — Trust, Raised on Chain

Crowdfunding has become a powerful tool for raising money for education, medical emergencies, social causes, and early-stage startups. However, most existing crowdfunding platforms are built on **centralized systems**, which introduces serious issues related to trust, transparency, and control.

In traditional platforms:
- Donors must blindly trust that funds will be used for the intended purpose
- Fundraisers can withdraw or misuse funds without providing verifiable proof
- Platforms act as centralized intermediaries, controlling access and charging high fees
- Campaign data, images, and proof documents are stored on centralized servers and can be modified or removed
- There is no transparent, tamper-proof record of donations and fund flow

These limitations reduce donor confidence and make crowdfunding vulnerable to misuse and fraud.

---

### The core problem

At its core, crowdfunding today suffers from a **trust gap**.

Donors want transparency and accountability.  
Fundraisers want fair access and timely fund release.  
Platforms, however, sit in the middle as trusted authorities — creating a single point of failure.

RaiseX addresses this fundamental problem by **removing the need for blind trust altogether**.

---

### How RaiseX solves this problem

RaiseX is a **blockchain-based decentralized crowdfunding platform** where trust is enforced by **code**, not by intermediaries.

Instead of relying on a centralized platform:
- Campaigns are created and stored on-chain
- Donations are recorded permanently on the blockchain
- Fund withdrawals are governed by smart contract rules
- Proof documents are stored using decentralized storage (IPFS)

This ensures that no single party can manipulate funds or data.

---

### What people can use RaiseX for

RaiseX can be used to create transparent and secure fundraising campaigns for:
- Education and student funding
- Medical emergencies and healthcare support
- Social and community-driven causes
- Startup and project-based fundraising

Anyone can:
- Create a campaign with a defined goal and deadline
- Donate using crypto with full on-chain traceability
- Verify how much money a campaign has raised
- Track fund movement without relying on a third party

---

### How RaiseX makes crowdfunding safer and more trustworthy

- 💡 **Smart contracts control fund flow**  
  Funds are locked inside smart contracts and can only be withdrawn when predefined conditions (goal and deadline) are satisfied.

- 🔐 **On-chain transparency**  
  Every donation is recorded on the blockchain, making it publicly verifiable and immutable.

- 📦 **Decentralized storage with IPFS**  
  Campaign images and proof-of-usage documents are stored on IPFS, preventing tampering or censorship.

- ⏳ **Condition-based withdrawals**  
  Fundraisers cannot arbitrarily withdraw funds — the contract enforces rules automatically.

- 🧾 **Accountability through proof submission**  
  Fundraisers are required to upload proof of fund usage before withdrawal, increasing donor confidence.

---

### Why RaiseX matters

RaiseX replaces centralized trust with **verifiable, programmable trust**.

By combining blockchain, smart contracts, and decentralized storage, RaiseX demonstrates how Web3 can solve real-world problems beyond speculation — making crowdfunding **fair, transparent, and trust-minimized**.

This makes RaiseX not just a technical project, but a practical application of blockchain for social and financial impact.

### Feature highlights shown above

- **Campaign discovery** – Browse active, funded, and expired campaigns with on-chain progress.
- **Refunds** – Donors can claim refunds via smart contracts if goals are not met.
- **Refund history** – View refund amounts, timestamps, and explorer links.
- **Withdrawals** – Creators withdraw funds only when contract conditions are met.
- **Donations** – Track total donations and transaction details.
- **Campaigns** – Manage created campaigns and their status.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building RaiseX was not just about writing smart contracts or a frontend, it required carefully combining **blockchain logic, decentralized storage, and modern web technologies** into a single reliable system. Throughout development, I faced multiple technical and architectural challenges that pushed me to think beyond tutorials and handle real-world constraints.

---

### 1. Designing secure and scalable smart contracts

One of the biggest challenges was designing Solidity smart contracts that could securely manage multiple crowdfunding campaigns while handling real ETH value.

Key challenges included:
- Supporting multiple campaigns in a single contract
- Tracking donors and donation amounts accurately
- Preventing unauthorized or premature fund withdrawals
- Avoiding logic flaws that could lock or misuse funds

**How I solved it:**  
I carefully designed the contract architecture with:
- Clear data structures for campaigns and donors
- Strict access control to ensure only campaign creators can withdraw funds
- Condition-based withdrawal logic enforced by the contract itself

Funds can only be withdrawn after **both the funding goal is met and the campaign deadline has passed**, eliminating manual intervention and preventing misuse. This ensured that trust is enforced by code, not by assumptions.

---

### 2. Bridging blockchain logic with the frontend

Integrating smart contracts with a React-based frontend introduced several challenges, especially due to the asynchronous and stateful nature of blockchain interactions.

Some issues I faced:
- Handling asynchronous blockchain reads and writes
- Managing wallet connection and user session state
- Dealing with network mismatches and rejected transactions
- Keeping the UI in sync with on-chain data

**How I solved it:**  
I used **ethers.js** to create a clean abstraction layer between the frontend and the smart contracts. By carefully managing provider, signer, and contract instances, I ensured reliable interaction with the blockchain.

I also implemented proper state management and transaction feedback, resulting in a responsive UI that accurately reflects on-chain state and improves overall user experience.

---

### 3. Implementing decentralized file storage with IPFS

Another major challenge was storing campaign images and proof-of-fund-usage documents in a decentralized and tamper-proof way.

Problems encountered:
- Uploading and retrieving files from IPFS
- Mapping off-chain files to on-chain campaign data
- Minimizing gas costs while maintaining decentralization

**How I solved it:**  
I integrated **IPFS** for decentralized storage and stored only the **content hash** on-chain instead of raw data. This approach ensured:
- Permanent and censorship-resistant file storage
- Reduced gas consumption
- Verifiable linkage between blockchain records and campaign media

This design preserved decentralization while keeping the system efficient.

---

### 4. Testnet deployment and real-world UX challenges

Deploying RaiseX on the **Base Sepolia testnet** exposed real-world usability issues that are often overlooked in simple demos.

Challenges included:
- Dependency on testnet faucet ETH
- Handling incorrect network selection in wallets
- Managing transaction failures and reverts
- Educating users unfamiliar with Web3 flows

**How I solved it:**  
I added network validation, clear wallet prompts, and user-friendly error handling to guide users through the process. These improvements made the dApp usable even for first-time Web3 users and closer to a production-ready experience.

---

### What these challenges taught me

Overcoming these challenges helped me build RaiseX as a **production-style decentralized application** rather than a simple proof-of-concept. It strengthened my understanding of:
- Smart contract security
- Blockchain–frontend architecture
- Decentralized storage systems
- Real-world UX considerations in Web3

These learnings were critical in turning RaiseX into a reliable, transparent, and functional decentralized crowdfunding platform.

**Blockchain**

RaiseX is fundamentally a blockchain-driven application that uses decentralized technology to solve real-world trust and transparency issues in crowdfunding.

The platform leverages **blockchain immutability** to ensure that all campaign data, donations, and fund movements are permanently recorded and publicly verifiable. By executing core logic through smart contracts, RaiseX removes centralized control and replaces it with deterministic, trustless execution.

Blockchain enables RaiseX to:
- Prevent fund misuse through condition-based withdrawals
- Provide transparent donation tracking for contributors
- Eliminate intermediaries and centralized points of failure
- Ensure tamper-proof campaign records

By combining on-chain logic with decentralized storage (IPFS), RaiseX demonstrates how blockchain technology can be applied beyond speculation to build secure, transparent, and socially impactful applications.

**Ethereum Track**

RaiseX is a native Ethereum-based decentralized application that directly leverages core Ethereum principles such as smart contracts, transparency, and trustless execution.

The entire crowdfunding logic of RaiseX is implemented using **Solidity smart contracts**, where campaign creation, donations, fund tracking, and withdrawals are executed fully on-chain. This removes the need for centralized intermediaries and ensures that all transactions are transparent, verifiable, and immutable.

RaiseX is deployed on an **Ethereum-compatible network (Base Sepolia)** and interacts with user wallets through **ethers.js**, making it fully aligned with the Ethereum ecosystem. Donations and fund releases are governed by deterministic smart contract conditions, showcasing real-world use of Ethereum for decentralized finance and social impact.

By combining Ethereum smart contracts with decentralized storage (IPFS), RaiseX demonstrates how Ethereum can be used to build secure, trust-minimized crowdfunding platforms with real utility beyond speculation.

> Decentralized Subscription Payment System

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Infura](https://img.shields.io/badge/Infura-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

##  **What Problem It Solves**

## **The Problem**

Traditional subscription systems force users to trust companies with sensitive payment data, creating security risks through centralized data storage. Companies can arbitrarily change prices, ban users without recourse, and manipulate subscriber metrics with no independent verification possible. Payment processors extract high fees (2.9% + $0.30 per transaction) while excluding billions globally through geographic restrictions. Users have zero control over their subscriptions and no transparency into how systems operate.

---

### **Our Solution**

We built a fully decentralized subscription platform on Ethereum blockchain where users pay directly from their crypto wallets. 

**Smart Contract Architecture**: Deployed on Ethereum Sepolia testnet, our Solidity contract enforces immutable subscription logic—0.001 ETH for 30 days with automatic expiry tracking. Every payment is a blockchain transaction creating permanent, tamper-proof records. The contract emits events (Subscribed, Cancelled) for real-time monitoring and handles all business logic autonomously.

**Web3 Integration**: Frontend connects directly to Ethereum via ethers.js and MetaMask. Users approve transactions in their wallet—payments go straight to the contract address, bypassing traditional payment infrastructure entirely. No intermediaries, no stored credentials, no payment processors.

**Read-Only Backend API**: Built a Python Flask REST API using web3.py that queries smart contract view functions (isActive, getExpiry, totalSubscribers) and returns JSON responses. Critically, the backend holds no private keys and cannot send transactions—purely read-only for security.

**Transparency**: All data lives on-chain and is publicly verifiable through Etherscan. Anyone can audit subscriber counts, total revenue, and transaction history. No databases to manipulate, no admin panels—mathematical proof replaces corporate trust.

**Global Infrastructure**: Runs on Ethereum's decentralized network of thousands of nodes worldwide. No single point of failure. Deployed frontend on Vercel's global CDN for fast access anywhere.

---

### **Technical Implementation**

**Smart Contract (Solidity)**
- Gas-optimized storage using mappings for O(1) lookups
- Custom error handling reducing gas costs
- Event emission for off-chain indexing
- View functions for zero-cost data queries
- Immutable constants preventing price manipulation

**Backend (Python + Flask + Web3.py)**
- Blockchain service layer abstracting Web3 complexity
- RESTful API with comprehensive error handling
- Environment-based configuration (Infura RPC URLs never exposed)
- Checksum address validation preventing transaction errors
- Stateless design enabling horizontal scalability

**Frontend (HTML/JavaScript + ethers.js)**
- MetaMask wallet integration with automatic network detection
- Multiple RPC fallback logic for reliability
- Real-time subscription status updates
- Transaction lifecycle management (pending, confirmed, failed)
- Responsive UI with loading states

**Security & DevOps**
- Zero private key storage anywhere in stack
- All transactions require explicit MetaMask approval
- Git-based version control with `.gitignore` for sensitive data
- Vercel deployment with automatic GitHub CI/CD
- Read-only backend (cannot initiate transactions)

---

### **Who Benefits**

**Content Creators**: Receive 100% of payments directly to wallets. No platform fees, no payment holds, complete subscriber relationship ownership.

**Global Users**: Access from anywhere with just a crypto wallet. No banking requirements, no geographic restrictions, no KYC friction.

**SaaS Businesses**: Eliminate payment processing fees, chargeback fraud, and billing database maintenance. Smart contracts handle subscription logic automatically.

**Privacy-Focused Users**: Transact pseudonymously using wallet addresses. No personal data collection, no advertising profiles, no surveillance.

**Decentralized Communities**: Token-gated membership with on-chain verification. Composable with other smart contracts and services.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

First big problem was transactions getting stuck , we'd click subscribe in Remix and it would just sit there saying "pending" forever. Took us a while to figure out 

MetaMask was holding things up .
The Web3 kept getting "ethers is not defined" errors because the script wasn't loading properly. We tried different CDN links until one finally worked.

Then connecting to Sepolia was unreliable. The public RPC nodes would randomly fail or timeout, so our stats wouldn't load. We ended up trying multiple fallback options and eventually just signed up for Infura to get a stable connection.

Managing multiple test accounts was harder than expected. We wanted to show multiple subscribers but kept running into "insufficient funds" errors when trying to send ETH between accounts. Gas fees were eating up more than we thought.

**Blockchain**

Smart Contract Implementation
Written in Solidity (blockchain programming language)
Deployed contract at verified address
Automated payment logic runs on blockchain


Cryptocurrency Payments
Users pay with ETH (cryptocurrency)
No credit cards or traditional payment systems
Direct wallet-to-contract transactions


Decentralized Architecture
No central server controls subscriptions
Contract enforces rules automatically
Can't be shut down by any authority


Web3 Integration
MetaMask wallet connection
Uses ethers.js (Web3 library)
Follows Web3 development standards


Transparent & Verifiable
All transactions visible on Etherscan
Anyone can verify subscriber count
Public blockchain explorer access

### PayFlow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/payflow-68a1) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://payflowhackathon.netlify.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bWZcCEhi9wY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decentralized subscriptions, done right.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**main website** - https://payflowhackathon.netlify.app/
**merchant verifier website** - https://merchantaccesscheck.netlify.app/

**PayFlow** is a solution for the recurring payment issue, utilizing a completely trustless and transparent method. Users nowadays have to utilize third party services that store user electronic card information, maintain the control over the subscription billing process, and charge users without having visibility as to what they are charging for. Unlike this, PayFlow provides subscriptions via a Smart Contract, where by the user authorizes the subscription only once, after which every future subscription payment is executed automatically via the Ethereum Blockchain.

- Transactions visible publicly of each merchant, which offers transparent and prevents fraud.

- No one controls anything, everything is decentralized. 

- Easy to use, it's a one click solution.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge faced when creating the ability for users to set up automatic payments was to create a true autopay where users do not have to go through the process of signing transactions through metamask each month. The original design required manual interaction by users to make payments and therefore, did not allow for the true subscriptions. I solved it by allowing users to set up one time ERC20 approvals, which then enabled the contract to automatically withdraw funds when due, using Chainlink service.

Another challenge faced was how to properly integrate Chainlink Automation into the subscriptions. There was a learning curve around how checkUpkeep and performUpkeep work together and how Chainlink determines when to call both functions.

There was a delay between the execution of transactions and the updates of the UI state, which resulted in buttons showing old statuses. To solve this, I made it like that the contract state was rechecked after each transaction and any buttons enabled or disabled when in a happening state.

**Blockchain**

**PayFlow** is a blockchain based subscription and autopay system built using smart contracts. It uses on chain approvals and **Chainlink** Automation to enable secure recurring payments without requiring repeated user interaction. Payments are transparent trustless and fully controlled by the user through their wallet.

Team **suitcase** -- Hardik Jain, Ritwik Wadhawan, Mohak Singh

**The problem it solves**

### **The Problem Altis Solves**

*Let’s be honest* — investing in government bonds in India has always been a game for the wealthy. Traditional platforms demand **₹10,000 minimum investments**, locking out millions of young professionals, students, and first-time investors who want to build wealth safely.

Even if you have the money, you’re stuck waiting *T+2 days for settlement*, drowning in paperwork, and dealing with opaque processes that feel more like a maze than an investment platform.

***Altis changes everything.***

---

### **Making Safe Investing Accessible**

We’ve taken *India’s safest investment — government bonds backed by sovereign guarantee* — and made them available for just **₹100**. That’s less than a dinner out.

Now anyone can start building a stable, fixed-income portfolio without breaking the bank.

---

### **Here’s what Altis does for you:**

- **Fractional Ownership**  
  Buy *0.1 units of a bond* instead of being forced to purchase whole units worth thousands.

- **Instant Settlement**  
  Solana blockchain processes your investment in *seconds, not days*.

- **Complete Transparency**  
  Every transaction is recorded *on-chain with tamper-proof receipts via Weil Chain*.

- **AI-Powered Guidance**  
  Get *personalized bond recommendations* based on your risk tolerance and goals — **no financial advisor fees required**.

---

### **Real Problems, Real Solutions**

**For Students & Young Professionals**  
Start investing with *pocket money*. Build a habit of saving without waiting until you have lakhs in the bank.

**For Risk-Averse Investors**  
Government bonds offer *zero default risk with predictable returns*.  
No stock market volatility. No crypto crashes. Just **steady, sovereign-backed growth**.

**For Tech-Savvy Users**  
Skip the bank branches and demat accounts. *Connect your Phantom wallet and invest in 30 seconds*.

**For Everyone**  
Watch your money grow *in real-time*. Our dashboard shows yield accruing every second — not quarterly statements you need to decode.

---

### **The Bigger Picture**

Traditional finance makes you feel *small*.  
Minimum investments. Complex jargon. Hidden fees. Systems designed for institutions — **not individuals**.

Altis flips this model.

We’ve combined:
- *The safety of government bonds*
- *The speed of blockchain*
- *The intelligence of AI*

to create something genuinely new:

***Accessible, transparent, and smart fixed-income investing for the next generation.***

---

**No middlemen.**  
**No minimums that matter.**  
**No waiting.**

***Just you, your goals, and government-backed securities that actually work for your life.***

**Challenges we ran into**

### **Challenges I Ran Into**

Building Altis wasn’t just about writing code — it was about **making very different systems behave like one coherent product**. A few challenges stood out during development:

---

#### **Coordinating Multiple Blockchains**

One of the biggest hurdles was **orchestrating interactions across three different blockchain layers** — Solana for payments, Ethereum for bond metadata, and Weil Chain for compliance verification. Each system has its own assumptions, latency, and failure modes.

**How I solved it:**  
I designed a strict, step-by-step execution flow where **Weil Chain verification always happens first**, before any on-chain payment. This ensured that invalid transactions never reached Solana, eliminating wasted fees and inconsistent states. Clear boundaries between layers made debugging much easier.

---

#### **Preventing Partial Failures During Minting**

A tricky bug appeared when a Solana transaction succeeded, but the corresponding database update or receipt linkage failed. This caused temporary inconsistencies between on-chain state and off-chain records.

**How I solved it:**  
I restructured the minting flow to behave like a **pseudo-atomic transaction**:
1. Verify on Weil Chain  
2. Execute Solana transaction  
3. Confirm transaction  
4. Persist data to Supabase  

Each step only proceeds if the previous one succeeds, with explicit error handling and rollback-friendly logic.

---

#### **Wallet Integration Edge Cases**

Phantom wallet integration introduced several edge cases — users rejecting connection requests, switching accounts mid-session, or having insufficient SOL during confirmation.

**How I solved it:**  
I added **defensive checks at every wallet interaction point**, graceful error messages, and state resets when a wallet disconnects or changes. This significantly improved reliability and user experience.

---

#### **Real-Time Yield Calculation Accuracy**

Displaying yield “accruing every second” sounds simple, but it required careful handling of time calculations to avoid rounding errors or unrealistic projections.

**How I solved it:**  
Instead of polling a backend or blockchain, I implemented a **pure client-side time-based calculation** using purchase timestamps and APY snapshots. This keeps the UI responsive, accurate, and backend-free.

---

#### **Balancing Innovation with Trust**

From a design perspective, the biggest non-technical challenge was **making a Web3 product feel trustworthy enough for government bond investing**. Too much “crypto” styling reduced credibility.

**How I solved it:**  
I intentionally adopted a **clean, institutional UI**, restrained animations, and classical visual metaphors (like the Thinker sculpture) to communicate long-term thinking and stability rather than speculation.

---

Overall, these challenges shaped Altis into a more robust and thoughtful system. Each hurdle forced better architectural decisions, ultimately resulting in a platform that is **simpler for users but stronger under the hood**.

**Software Development**

### **Why This Fits the Software Development Track**

Altis is a full-stack software system that focuses on **architecture, integration, and execution**, not just ideas.

It combines frontend engineering, backend services, blockchain integration, database design, AI-based logic, and system reliability into one working product. The core challenge solved is **building scalable, real-world software that coordinates multiple technologies into a single user experience**.

At its heart, Altis is a software engineering problem — and its solution is a carefully designed, production-ready system.

**AI**

### **How AI Is Used in Altis**

Altis uses AI as a **bond analyzer and recommendation engine** to simplify decision-making for users.

The AI analyzes bond parameters such as **APY, maturity period, risk profile, and investment amount**, then matches them with the user’s **goals and risk tolerance**. Based on this, it suggests the most suitable government bonds instead of forcing users to compare complex data manually.

In short, AI in Altis acts like a **personal bond advisor** — helping users choose safer, better-aligned investments without needing financial expertise.

**Blockchain**

### **How Blockchain Is Used in Altis**

In Altis, blockchain is used for quick and easy transactions. It is used because **traditional systems make safe investing slow, expensive, and inaccessible**. Blockchain allows us to fix those problems at the infrastructure level.

---

#### **Instant Settlement Instead of Waiting Days**

Normally, buying government bonds means waiting **T+2 days** for settlement. With blockchain, this delay disappears.

Altis uses **Solana** to process investments in **seconds**. When a user invests, the transaction is settled almost instantly and permanently recorded. There are no clearing houses, no manual reconciliation, and no waiting.

---

#### **Trust Without Blind Faith**

In traditional platforms, users are asked to trust dashboards, PDFs, and intermediaries. In Altis, users can **verify everything themselves**.

- Payments are visible on-chain on Solana
- Bond details are stored immutably on Ethereum
- Every investment is verified and logged via Weil Chain before it happens

Blockchain turns trust into something **provable**, not promised.

---

#### **Built-In Compliance, Not Afterthoughts**

One major problem with financial systems is that validation often happens *after* money moves.

Altis flips this.

Before any transaction is executed, **Weil Chain verifies all rules** — whether the bond is active, whether supply is available, and whether the investment meets platform constraints. Only verified transactions are allowed to proceed.

This prevents errors, failed transactions, and hidden risks.

---

#### **Fractional Investing Made Possible**

Government bonds usually require large minimum investments. Blockchain lets us represent bonds in **small, precise units**, which makes fractional ownership practical.

That’s how Altis enables investing from **₹100**, without breaking or approximating ownership records.

---

#### **No Middlemen, No Black Boxes**

Users don’t need banks, brokers, or demat accounts to participate.

They connect a wallet, approve a transaction, and their investment is recorded transparently. Ownership, verification, and settlement all happen through blockchain-backed systems.

---

#### **Why Blockchain Matters Here**

Blockchain helps Altis:
- Remove settlement delays
- Lower entry barriers
- Increase transparency
- Prove compliance
- Give users direct control

It doesn’t replace traditional finance — it **fixes its weakest parts**.

---

**Simply put:**  
Blockchain allows Altis to offer **safe, government-backed investing** in a way that is faster, clearer, and more accessible than traditional systems ever allowed.

**Ethereum Track**

### **Why This Fits the Ethereum Track**

Altis uses Ethereum as an **immutable bond registry**, where all government bond definitions are stored on-chain. This ensures that critical parameters like **APY, maturity, and supply** cannot be altered silently.

Ethereum provides a **transparent, verifiable source of truth** for financial instruments, making the system trustworthy, auditable, and suitable for regulated use cases.

**The problem it solves**

## 🎯 The Problem It Solves

AgroFlow solves two major gaps in agriculture today:

✅ **Farm inefficiency due to manual monitoring**  
✅ **Lack of transparency and trust in the food supply chain**

### 👨‍🌾 For Farmers

**1. Manual Monitoring is Exhausting**  
Farmers spend hours checking soil moisture, temperature, and weather conditions. AgroFlow automates this using **ESP32 IoT sensors** that stream real-time data to a clean dashboard, making decisions faster and easier.

**2. No Proof of Quality / Authenticity**  
Organic certifications are expensive, paper-based, and easy to fake. AgroFlow lets farmers mint harvest batches as **blockchain NFTs**, creating tamper-proof proof of authenticity, farming practices, and harvest history.

**3. Language Barriers**  
Most farming apps are English-only. AgroFlow includes an AI chatbot that supports **8+ Indian languages** (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati) so farmers can get help in their native language.

---

### 🛒 For Consumers

**1. Food Fraud is Rampant**  
A large percentage of organic produce is falsely labeled. AgroFlow allows consumers to scan a **QR code** on produce packaging and instantly view an immutable **blockchain record** proving origin, farmer info, and batch details.

**2. No Transparency in the Supply Chain**  
Consumers usually have no visibility into where food came from or how it was grown. AgroFlow’s verification page shows farm details, sensor-linked records, and on-chain proof in one place.

---

### 🏢 For the Industry

**1. Smart Irrigation Saves Water**  
AgroFlow can trigger irrigation automatically when soil moisture drops below a threshold, helping reduce water wastage and improving sustainability.

**2. Data-Driven Decisions**  
Historical sensor data enables smarter planning like optimizing irrigation cycles, improving planting schedules, and supporting yield prediction.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Blockchain Gas Estimation Failures (MetaMask)
**Problem:** MetaMask kept throwing `"Internal JSON-RPC error"` when minting NFTs on Polygon Amoy testnet due to unreliable gas estimation.

✅ **Solution:**  
- Added an explicit `gasLimit: 300000`  
- Implemented dynamic `gasPrice` (2× network rate)  
- Added wallet balance checks before minting for clear user feedback

---

### 2. Browser vs Server Hash Functions
**Problem:** Used Node.js `crypto` module for SHA-256 hashing, but it crashed in the browser during NFT minting.

✅ **Solution:** Implemented browser hashing using the Web Crypto API:

```js
const hashBuffer = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", msgBuffer);
````

---

### 3. Supabase Row-Level Security (RLS) Blocking Demo

**Problem:** Supabase RLS policies rejected anonymous inserts with
`"new row violates row-level security policy"` errors.

✅ **Solution:** Created `fix_rls.sql` with permissive demo-mode policies and documented that production would require strict user-scoped rules.

---

### 4. Keeping UI State in Sync After Minting

**Problem:** After minting, the “Mint NFT” button still appeared because `nft_token_id` wasn’t persisting to the database correctly.

✅ **Solution:**

* Fixed API mapping for `blockchain_tx_hash`, `nft_token_id`, and mint status updates
* Added fallback UI checks like `status !== "minted"` to prevent incorrect states

---

### 5. OpenSea Dropped Testnet Support

**Problem:** Planned to display NFTs on OpenSea, but OpenSea discontinued testnet support in 2024.

✅ **Solution:** Replaced OpenSea links with PolygonScan NFT viewer URLs

---

### 6. Real-Time Sensor Sync + Stable Logging

**Problem:** ESP32 sensor values were noisy and inconsistent, causing sudden spikes in dashboard graphs.

✅ **Solution:** Added filtering + validation before storing values, and ensured logging happens at a stable fixed interval for smooth and accurate dashboards.

```

**Software Development**

AgroFlow fits the Software Development track as a complete end-to-end platform built for real-world agriculture use cases.

We built a full-stack web app using Next.js with a responsive dashboard that visualizes live IoT sensor data (temperature, humidity, soil moisture) stored in Supabase. The system includes APIs for harvest batch creation, verification pages, irrigation control, and real-time farm monitoring.

This project focuses heavily on product-level engineering: clean UI/UX, reliable data logging, stable backend integration, and a working demo that connects IoT + database + blockchain + AI into one unified workflow.

**AI**

AgroFlow fits the AI track through AgriBot, an AI-powered farming assistant built using Google Gemini.

AgriBot provides actionable recommendations using real farm context such as sensor readings and current environmental conditions. It also supports 8+ Indian languages (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati), making the platform accessible to farmers who are not comfortable with English.

The AI layer improves decision-making by guiding farmers on irrigation timing, crop actions, and best practices, while also handling fallback responses when the API is rate-limited or unavailable.

**Blockchain**

AgroFlow fits the Blockchain track by implementing tamper-proof agricultural traceability using Polygon (EVM-compatible).

Each harvest batch can be minted as an ERC-721 NFT, acting as an immutable certificate that stores key details like crop info, planting date, farm location, and organic status. AgroFlow also generates a QR code for every batch so consumers can scan and verify authenticity via our public verification page.

To ensure integrity, we store a hash of the batch data on-chain and verify it later, preventing fraud and making supply chain records verifiable and transparent.

**Ethereum Track**

AgroFlow fits the Ethereum Track by using an EVM-based blockchain (Polygon Amoy testnet) to create **verifiable, tamper-proof traceability** for agricultural harvest batches.

Each harvest is minted as an **ERC-721 NFT**, which acts as a digital certificate containing key batch details like crop type, planting date, farm location, and organic status. The NFT ensures that once the record is written on-chain, it cannot be edited or forged.

We also generate a unique QR code for every harvest batch. Consumers can scan the QR code to instantly verify authenticity through our public verification page, which fetches on-chain data and confirms integrity using a stored `dataHash`.

By combining IoT sensor monitoring + immutable NFT certificates, AgroFlow uses Ethereum-compatible infrastructure to improve trust, transparency, and accountability in the food supply chain.

### ChainSeat

> End of Fake Tickets using Invisible Web3

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves-
The Ticketing Industry is Broken. Traditional QR code tickets are just static images. They are easily screenshotted, photocopied, and sold to multiple unsuspecting victims on Instagram or WhatsApp. Scalpers buy bulk tickets using bots and resell them at 10x prices, while the actual event organizers see zero revenue from this secondary market.

ChainSeat fixes this by replacing static images with "Invisible" Smart Tickets.

We solve three critical problems using a blend of Blockchain, Fintech, and Cryptography:

1. Eliminating Fake Tickets & Screenshots (Offline TOTP)
The Problem: A standard QR code can be screenshotted and sent to 10 people. The first one to arrive gets in; the rest get scammed.

Our Solution: We implemented an Offline TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) system inside the ticket.

The QR code regenerates locally on the user's phone every 30 seconds (like Google Authenticator).

It requires Zero Server Requests to refresh, so the app works even in crowded networks.

Result: A screenshot taken 5 minutes ago is mathematically invalid at the gate.

2. Killing the Scalper Market & Automating Royalties
The Problem: Organizers lose millions because they have no control over resale prices or who owns the ticket after the primary sale.

Our Solution: We use Razorpay Route combined with an internal Ledger to automate the money flow.

When a user resells a ticket, the system automatically splits the payment.

90% goes to the Seller.

10% is instantly routed to the Organizer as a Royalty.

Price caps are enforced by the platform, making predatory scalping impossible.

3. Removing the "Web3 Barrier" (Invisible Blockchain)
The Problem: NFT ticketing exists, but it sucks. Users hate installing MetaMask, buying ETH, and paying gas fees just to see a concert.

Our Solution: Invisible Web3.

Users login with Google.

Users pay with UPI, Credit Card, or Netbanking (Rupees).

We manage Custodial Wallets (via Supabase Vault) in the background. The user owns the asset on Polygon, but they never see a private key or a gas fee.

4. Data-Driven Event Planning (AI Insights)
The Problem: Organizers often guess where to host events.

Our Solution: We integrated Google Gemini AI to act as a marketing strategist. It analyzes the event type and predicts demand hotspots across Indian cities, helping organizers target the right audience.

In short: ChainSeat gives buyers the Simplicity of Web2 (UPI/Email) with the Security of Web3 (Immutable Ownership/Anti-Fraud).

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a bridge between Web2 Fintech (UPI/Fiat) and Web3 (NFTs) introduced several unique architectural hurdles. Here are the biggest ones we faced and how we solved them:

1. The "Anti-Screenshot" Dilemma (Security vs. Server Costs)
The Hurdle: To prevent users from entering with a screenshot, we initially designed a system where the app polled the server every 30 seconds to fetch a new QR signature. However, we realized that at a stadium entrance with 20,000 people, 20,000 concurrent API requests every 30 seconds would crush our Supabase Edge Functions and skyrocket costs.

The Solution: We pivoted to an "Offline TOTP" (Time-based One-Time Password) model, similar to Google Authenticator.

We generate a qr_secret during ticket creation.

The React app uses the otpauth library to generate the changing QR code locally on the user's device using the CPU.

Result: The QR changes every 30 seconds to prevent screenshots, but requires Zero Server Requests, making it infinitely scalable.

2. Managing Custodial Private Keys Securely
The Hurdle: Since we promised "Invisible Web3," we couldn't ask users to install MetaMask. We had to manage wallets for them. Storing private keys in the database as plain text is a massive security risk, but storing them in LocalStorage is even worse.

The Solution: We utilized Supabase Vault, a Postgres extension for managing secrets.

We wrote custom Postgres RPC functions so that the private keys are encrypted at rest.

The keys are never sent to the frontend. They are only accessible by specific, authorized Edge Functions running in a secure server-side environment to sign transactions.

3. Syncing Fiat Payments with Blockchain State
The Hurdle: Razorpay (Fiat) is instant, but Blockchain (Polygon) is asynchronous. If a user pays via UPI, and the blockchain transaction fails or lags, the user loses money without getting the ticket.

The Solution: We decoupled the payment from the transfer.

We use Razorpay Route to handle the financial split (Seller/Organizer) immediately.

On a successful webhook trigger, we update the internal SQL database to reflect the new owner instantly (optimistic UI).

The actual blockchain transfer happens in a background job. If it fails (e.g., gas spike), the database is the "source of truth" for the gate scanner, and a retry mechanism handles the blockchain sync later.

4. Getting Consistent JSON from Gemini AI
The Hurdle: We used Google Gemini to generate audience insights. However, the AI would often return conversational text ("Here is your data...") or Markdown backticks along with the JSON, which broke our frontend parser.

The Solution: We implemented robust Prompt Engineering to demand "JSON ONLY" and added a Regex cleaning layer in our Edge Function to strip out markdown formatting before passing the data to the React frontend.

**AI**

We integrated Google Trends to provide organizers with a live, visual Heatmap of event demand across India, democratizing access to tour planning data.
integrated Google Gemini AI to act as a marketing strategist, analyzing event types to generate data-driven audience and location insights for organizers.

**Blockchain**

The core engine uses Ethereum NFTs for ownership verification and Custodial Wallets (Supabase Vault) to abstract away complexity, making Web3 invisible to the end user.

**Ethereum Track**

The core engine uses Ethereum NFTs for ownership verification and Custodial Wallets (Supabase Vault) to abstract away complexity.

### AgriFinance
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agrifinance-6d08) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gaaarrrgiiiiiiiiiii/agriWallet1) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1155706487?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Finance Farmers Can Actually Trust

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We started working on AgriFinance after noticing that most problems in agriculture aren’t about production  they’re about trust and access.
Many small farmers still can’t get loans without collateral or heavy paperwork. Credit decisions are often unclear, slow, and biased, which pushes farmers toward informal lenders with high interest rates. On the other side, lenders and buyers don’t have reliable ways to verify farm data, certifications, or where produce actually comes from. Supply chain records are fragmented and easy to manipulate.

AgriFinance tries to fix this gap.
It allows farmers to apply for collateral-free loans where every step  from approval to repayment  is visible on-chain. Instead of relying on a single opaque score, we use multiple data points to evaluate creditworthiness more fairly. Land records, produce batches, and certifications are represented digitally so they can be verified without manual paperwork.
For buyers, the platform makes it easy to scan a QR code and see where the product came from, who produced it, and how it moved through the supply chain. For lenders, it reduces risk by making loan data transparent and auditable.
Our goal is simple: make agricultural finance clearer, safer, and more accessible, without forcing users to understand blockchain or manage complex tools.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was making Web3 usable for non-technical users. Farmers shouldn’t have to worry about wallets, gas fees, or failed transactions.

To solve this, we used account abstraction so users can interact with the platform without managing gas or private keys directly. This made the experience feel much closer to a regular app.

Another major challenge was handling the loan lifecycle on-chain. Managing approvals, repayments, and real token transfers while keeping the frontend and backend in sync took several iterations. We solved this by designing a dedicated Loan Vault contract with clear state transitions and syncing it with an indexer for accurate analytics.
Privacy was also tricky. Land documents and certifications need to be verified, but storing them openly on-chain isn’t practical. We addressed this using zero-knowledge proofs so users can prove validity without exposing sensitive information.
Finally, ensuring QR codes couldn’t be reused or tampered with required careful design. Each QR is linked directly to immutable on-chain records, which prevents duplication or manipulation.
These challenges pushed us to focus on building something practical and production-ready, not just a demo.

**Blockchain**

AgriFinance is built around problems where trust, transparency, and tamper-proof records are essential, which is exactly where blockchain makes sense.
We use blockchain to manage the full lifecycle of agricultural loans  from approval to repayment  in a way that can’t be altered after the fact. Smart contracts ensure loan terms are enforced automatically, reducing dependence on intermediaries and manual oversight.
Land records, produce batches, and certifications are represented on-chain so they can be verified instead of trusted. Buyers can scan a QR code and independently confirm origin and authenticity, while lenders get a clear, auditable view of risk and repayments.
Blockchain also allows us to support gasless transactions and account abstraction, making the system usable for non-technical users without exposing them to wallet or fee complexity.
In short, AgriFinance uses blockchain not as a buzzword, but as a practical tool to bring accountability, fairness, and transparency to agricultural finance.

**The problem it solves**

## 🧩 The Problem GitSplit Solves

Hackathon success often creates an **unexpected problem**:  
**“Who owns how much?”**

After winning, many teams fall apart due to **prize distribution conflicts**, unclear ownership, and subjective judgments about contributions. These disputes:

- Destroy team trust  
- Delay or completely stop project continuation  
- Lead to legal and IP ownership conflicts  
- Waste time, money, and future opportunities  

Despite hackathons being innovation-driven, **prize and ownership distribution is still handled manually**, emotionally, and unfairly.

---

## 🚀 What GitSplit Is Used For

GitSplit is a **fair, automated, and transparent system** that calculates and proves contribution-based ownership using GitHub data and blockchain verification.

### People use GitSplit to:
- Split hackathon prize money fairly  
- Determine ownership percentages objectively  
- Avoid arguments and post-win disputes  
- Create legal-grade proof of contribution  
- Safely continue projects after hackathons  

---

## 🔍 How GitSplit Makes Things Easier & Safer

### ✅ Objective Contribution Analysis
Instead of subjective opinions, GitSplit:
- Analyzes **actual GitHub commits**
- Weighs different contribution types (features, bug fixes, docs, chores)
- Filters spam, bots, and trivial commits
- Produces **clear ownership percentages**

➡️ No favoritism. No guesswork.

---

### ⚡ Automated Prize Distribution
What used to take **hours of negotiation** now takes **seconds**.

- Upload repo → Analyze → Get split  
- Automatically calculates fair prize allocation  
- Exports results (CSV, links, records)  

➡️ Faster, cleaner, and dispute-free.

---

### 🔐 Blockchain-Backed Proof
GitSplit records the final distribution on-chain:

- **Immutable & tamper-proof**
- Acts as legal-grade proof of ownership
- Verifiable by judges, sponsors, or investors  

➡️ No rewrites. No manipulation. No disputes.

---

### 🛡️ Conflict & Legal Risk Prevention
GitSplit removes the biggest post-hackathon risks:

- ❌ “I did more work”
- ❌ “You joined late”
- ❌ “We don’t agree on the split”
- ❌ Legal ownership ambiguity  

➡️ One transparent system everyone can trust.

---

## 👥 Who Benefits from GitSplit

### 👨‍💻 Hackathon Participants
- Fair prize sharing  
- Clear ownership percentages  
- Preserved team relationships  
- Confidence to continue building together  

### 🏆 Hackathon Organizers
- Fewer post-event disputes  
- Professional prize handling  
- Stronger platform credibility  
- Scalable solution for many teams  

### 🧑‍⚖️ Judges & Sponsors
- Verifiable proof of contribution  
- Assurance prizes go to real contributors  
- Transparent and accountable outcomes  

---

## 🌍 In Simple Terms

> **GitSplit turns “Who deserves what?” into a math problem — not a fight.**

It replaces:
- Emotion → **Data**
- Arguments → **Algorithms**
- Trust issues → **Transparency**
- Legal risk → **Blockchain proof**

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges Faced During Development

### 1. Port Conflicts
**Issue:** Port `5000` was already in use  
**Fix:** Killed the process or used a different port via environment variables  

---

### 2. GitHub API Rate Limits
**Issue:** API limits blocked real-time analysis  
**Fix:** Automatic fallback to mock data and offline demo mode  

---

### 3. Dependency Installation Errors
**Issue:** npm cache and version conflicts  
**Fix:** Cleared cache and reinstalled dependencies  

---

### 4. Frontend Not Rendering
**Issue:** Blank pages or missing charts  
**Fix:** Hard refresh, backend health check, browser console debugging  

---

### 5. Demo Reliability
**Issue:** Live demos failing due to network/API issues  
**Fix:** Mock data by default, offline-ready demo, backups available  

---

### 6. Error Handling
**Issue:** Unhandled errors caused crashes  
**Fix:** Centralized custom error system with clear messages  

---

### 7. Edge Cases
**Issue:** Special repo cases broke analysis  
**Fix:** Handled single contributor, bot commits, empty repos, invalid URLs  

---

## ✅ Key Takeaway
Building fallback systems, strong error handling, and offline demos made GitSplit reliable, demo-ready, and production-safe.

### FanFirst
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fanfirst-98d4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/x3mitul/FanFirst) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/3BACerP2XmQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-brAInwave%202.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://brainwave2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where AI Meets Superfan Energy

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSOC](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSOC-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: Bots and scalpers buy tickets in seconds, then resell them at 5-10x the price-real fans are priced out or left empty-handed. Artists have no control over their secondary market, and traditional platforms profit from the chaos. FanFirst solves this by verifying genuine fans through an AI-powered quiz before purchase, issuing unforgeable NFT tickets on blockchain, and enforcing smart contract resale caps-ensuring tickets go to real fans at fair prices, while artists earn royalties on every resale.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Multi-Agent AI System
Building the Support Swarm with 4 specialized agents (Router, Ticket, Event, FAQ, Account) required careful prompt engineering to ensure accurate routing. The initial keyword matching was too simplistic-"Ticketmaster" was incorrectly routing to the Ticket agent because it contained "ticket". We solved this with priority-ordered keyword matching and exclusion patterns.

2. Gemini API Integration Issues
LangChain's Gemini integration repeatedly failed with "NOT_FOUND" and retry errors. We had to switch from LangChain wrappers to direct google-generativeai SDK calls, and implement robust fallback responses when API calls failed.

3. RAG Implementation
Implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with ChromaDB required balancing between cached responses (free, instant) and LLM calls (cost, latency). We created a hybrid 3-layer system: keyword cache → RAG semantic search → LLM generation.

4. Environment Variable Loading
The Python backend wasn't finding the Gemini API key because 
.env.local
 wasn't being loaded correctly. We had to explicitly load multiple env files in the correct order with override flags.

5. Next.js Hydration Errors
Browser extensions (like Jetski) injecting attributes into the HTML caused React hydration mismatches, requiring us to understand these weren't code bugs.

**Ethereum Track**

FanFirst is highly relevant for ETHIndia because it solves a real, billion-dollar problem—ticket scalping—using blockchain and AI, not just theoretical Web3 concepts. Built on Polygon for low gas fees, our platform uses NFT tickets with smart contract-enforced resale caps to prevent price gouging, while ensuring artists earn royalties on every secondary sale. What makes us unique is the AI-powered FanIQ Quiz that uses Gemini to verify genuine fans before purchase, effectively eliminating bots and scalpers at the source. With India's massive live events market (IPL, concerts, festivals), this isn't just a hackathon project—it's a production-ready solution to a pain point every fan has experienced. We combine full-stack Web3 (wallet integration, on-chain ticketing, transparent audit trails) with cutting-edge AI (multi-agent support swarm, knowledge base RAG), demonstrating how these technologies can work together to democratize access and put real fans first.

**Open Innovation**

FanFirst fits the Open Innovation track by combining AI and blockchain to democratize access to live events. Traditional ticketing is broken—bots and scalpers exploit fans, and artists lose control over their tickets. FanFirst solves this through open, transparent technology: our AI-powered FanIQ Quiz verifies genuine fans before purchase, NFT tickets on Polygon provide an immutable, publicly auditable ownership trail, and smart contract-enforced resale caps prevent price gouging while ensuring artists earn royalties on every secondary sale. Our multi-agent AI Support Swarm uses RAG and Gemini to provide instant, intelligent customer service. By making fan verification open (AI-driven, not gatekept), ticketing transparent (blockchain, not black boxes), and access fair (fans first, not highest bidder), FanFirst demonstrates how open innovation can disrupt exploitative industries and create value for communities, not just corporations.

> AI-Powered Smart Loan Investment Platform

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FinVest addresses one of the most overlooked gaps in modern finance — the lack of access to formal funding for small entrepreneurs, local business owners, and individuals with little education or no banking history. Many of these borrowers have strong business ideas but struggle to present their needs professionally or meet traditional bank requirements. Their informal language and absence of financial records often make investors hesitant to trust them. FinVest solves this by using AI-driven Natural Language Processing to translate informal requests into professional pitches, bridging the communication gap between grassroots borrowers and formal investors. Through smart contracts, blockchain-backed transparency, and AI-based fund tracking, FinVest builds trust, ensures responsible fund usage, and creates an inclusive lending ecosystem where even those without credit histories or banking access can secure investments confidently and fairly.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced During Development

1) Natural Language Understanding:
One of the major challenges was accurately interpreting informal or regional borrower inputs and converting them into clear, investor-ready pitches using NLP, while ensuring the borrower’s original intent and tone remained intact.

2) Backend Development & Deployment:
Building a reliable backend to handle user authentication, data exchange, and AI integration was complex. Deploying it on a real, responsive web platform while maintaining performance, uptime, and data integrity added to the challenge.

3) System Integration & Scalability:
Integrating multiple technologies — Gemini AI, MongoDB Atlas into a unified, scalable architecture required careful synchronisation to ensure smooth communication and a consistent user experience across all modules.

**Ethereum Track**

# Why FinVest Fits the Ethereum Track

FinVest uses Ethereum as a **trust and verification layer** for micro-finance.  
While INR funds move through an off-chain escrow, all critical actions are **anchored on-chain** to create tamper-proof accountability between borrowers, investors, and the platform.

---

## What We Put On-Chain

Our smart contract records:

- Hash of finalized deal terms (amount, tenure, tranches)  
- Lifecycle events:  
  - InvestorFunded  
  - TrancheRequested  
  - TrancheApproved  
  - TranchePaid  
  - TrancheFrozen  
  - RepaymentPaid  
  - DefaultDeclared  
- Hashes of invoices and payout proofs

This creates an **immutable timeline** that no party can edit.

---

## Why Ethereum Matters Here

Ethereum provides:

- **Non-repudiation** – investors can prove what was agreed  
- **Transparency** – verifiable use of funds  
- **Dispute evidence** – invoices and actions cryptographically anchored  
- **Trust without central control** – platform cannot rewrite history

We combine DeFi transparency with compliant INR escrow, making a realistic bridge between blockchain and everyday micro-lending.

---

## Example Flow

1. Deal finalized → `DealCreated` on-chain  
2. Investor funds → `InvestorFunded`  
3. Tranche released → `TrancheApproved` + `TranchePaid`  
4. Repayment/default → `RepaymentPaid` / `DefaultDeclared`

Anyone can verify the full lifecycle independently.

---

## Outcome

Ethereum turns FinVest from “another lending app” into a **trust protocol** where:

> Agreements are immutable, actions are verifiable, and small-ticket investing becomes safe.

This is a real-world use of Ethereum for **financial inclusion and accountable capital deployment.**

**Google Gemini API**

# Why FinVest Fits the Gemini API Track

FinVest uses the Gemini API as the intelligence layer that converts informal stories into investable opportunities.  
Most micro-entrepreneurs cannot write business plans—Gemini transforms **voice notes, messy text, and images** into structured pitches that investors can compare.

### Where Gemini Is Used
- **Pitch Normalization:** Converts raw borrower input → structured fields (funding need, use of funds, milestones, risks).  
- **Invoice Understanding:** Extracts key data from uploaded bills to validate tranche requests.  
- **Risk Insights:** Generates human-readable reasons behind trust health (e.g., inactivity, delayed payments).  
- **Borrower Assistance:** Suggests repayment plans and simple explanations in local language.

### Impact
Gemini removes literacy barriers, reduces manual review, and enables fairer decision making.  
Without Gemini, FinVest would require formal documentation; with it, everyday entrepreneurs can access capital through natural conversation.

**Gemini = the bridge between informal users and structured finance.**

**MongoDB**

# Why FinVest Fits the MongoDB Track

FinVest is a data-intensive platform where every deal evolves through events—pitches, bids, tranches, payouts, and repayments.  
MongoDB’s flexible document model perfectly fits this lifecycle and enables real-time trust scoring.

### How MongoDB Powers FinVest
- **Event Store:** ActivityEvent collection tracks proofs, delays, uploads, and reminders for risk computation.  
- **Escrow Ledger:** Deal documents maintain lockedBalance, usedBalance, and tranche states atomically.  
- **Vendor Graph:** Verified sellers linked per borrower with dynamic KYC fields.  
- **Fast Queries:** Investor dashboards aggregate payouts, invoices, and repayment history instantly.  
- **Schema Flexibility:** Pitches and invoices vary widely—MongoDB handles unstructured data without migrations.

### Why It Matters
Financial inclusion requires adapting to messy real-world data.  
MongoDB enables FinVest to model evolving relationships and power the risk engine without rigid tables.

**MongoDB = the operational backbone of transparent, behavior-driven micro-finance.**

> Anti-Corruption Decentralized Block-Chain App

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves :
Modern whistleblowing systems force an impossible trade-off between trust and anonymity.
Fully anonymous reports are often dismissed as unreliable, fake, or malicious.
Verified reports expose whistleblowers to retaliation, job loss, legal action, or worse.
Even so-called “anonymous” platforms usually require trust in administrators, servers, or governments not to reveal identities.
As a result, many cases of corruption, abuse, and wrongdoing go unreported — not because people don’t care, but because the personal risk is simply too high.

How WhisperVault fixes this
WhisperVault eliminates the identity vs. anonymity trade-off.
It enables insiders to submit reports and evidence while providing cryptographic proof that they are authorized members of an organization — without revealing who they are, even to system administrators.

Using zero-knowledge proofs
With zero-knowledge cryptography, reporters can:
Prove “I am a legitimate insider”
Without revealing which insider they are
And without trusting any central authority to protect their identity
The result is whistleblowing that is both verifiable and truly anonymous.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into
1. Zero-knowledge proofs in the browser

Generating ZK proofs client-side was one of the biggest challenges. Proof generation is computationally heavy, slow on low-end devices, and difficult to debug when something fails silently.

How I solved it:
Instead of writing custom circuits from scratch, I used Semaphore, a battle-tested ZK library that abstracts away most of the cryptographic complexity. I optimized the UX by clearly showing loading states during proof generation and keeping proofs small enough to be practical for a demo (~5–10 seconds).

2. Proving authorization without leaking identity

A core challenge was ensuring that users could prove they were legitimate insiders without exposing wallet addresses, metadata, or allowing admins to deanonymize submissions.

How I solved it:
I designed the smart contract so it never stores user addresses or personal data. It only stores a Merkle root of identity commitments and verifies zero-knowledge proofs against it. This guarantees that verification happens purely through math, not trust.

3. Secure file storage without central servers

Storing evidence directly on-chain was impossible due to cost and size limits, but using a traditional server would undermine anonymity and trust.

How I solved it:
I used IPFS for decentralized storage and only stored the content hash on-chain. This ensures evidence is tamper-resistant, verifiable, and not controlled by any single party.

4. Balancing privacy with usability

Privacy-preserving systems are often confusing for non-technical users. Wallet connections, proof generation, and decentralized storage can easily overwhelm users.

How I solved it:
I focused on UX simplicity: a familiar upload flow, clear explanations, and minimal crypto jargon. All cryptographic steps happen behind a single “Generate Proof & Submit” action.

5. Designing a system with zero trust in admins

It was challenging to ensure that even platform administrators could not identify or track whistleblowers.

How I solved it:
The system architecture assumes admins are not trusted. No logs, emails, IPs, or addresses are stored. Identity verification is enforced entirely by cryptographic proofs and smart contracts, not permissions or databases.

**Ethereum Track**

We use Polygon Amoy Blockchain which is a layer 2 block chain built on Ethereum Blockchain.

**Solution:** Focused on a clear MVP and core workflow.

### 🔁 Time-Credit Logic
- Designing a fair **“1 hour = 1 credit”** system was tricky.  
**Solution:** Used a simple mutual-confirmation approach to avoid misuse.

### 🔐 Authentication & Flow
- Connecting login, profiles, and skill requests smoothly was challenging.  
**Solution:** Kept authentication basic and prioritized a clear user flow.

### 🎨 UI vs Features
- Balancing design quality with functionality was difficult.  
**Solution:** Chose a simple, clean UI that was easy to demo.

---

Hackathons are about **proving the idea**, not building a full implementation.
