Portfolio management today is fragmented, opaque, and trust-dependent.
Investors lack transparent decision-making, verifiable portfolio states, and AI-driven risk intelligence in one unified system.

QuantAI solves this by:

Automating portfolio construction with AI & quantitative finance

Providing real-time risk and market intelligence

Anchoring portfolio states on blockchain for auditability and trust

Enabling institutional-grade insights without institutional complexity

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was integrating AI models, real-time financial data, and blockchain verification into a single production system while maintaining performance and reliability.

How I solved it:

Modular architecture to isolate AI, data, and blockchain layers

Robust error handling and fallback mechanisms for APIs

Secure environment-based secret management for cloud deployment

Progressive enhancement: ensuring the platform remains functional even if advanced services are temporarily unavailable

This resulted in a resilient, scalable, and hackathon-ready system.

**Ethereum Track**

QuantAI Portfolio Manager leverages Ethereum as a trust and verification layer for institutional finance.
Every portfolio state and investment decision is cryptographically hashed (SHA-256) and anchored on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet via smart contracts, creating an immutable, publicly verifiable audit trail.

By combining AI-driven portfolio optimization and risk analytics with Ethereum’s decentralization and immutability, QuantAI transforms traditionally opaque financial decision-making into a transparent, tamper-proof, and auditable system.

This enables:

On-chain verification of portfolio decisions

Regulatory-ready audit trails for compliance

Trustless validation for clients and institutions

QuantAI demonstrates how Ethereum can power real-world financial accountability, bridging advanced AI finance with decentralized trust infrastructure.

**Best Innovation**

QuantAI Portfolio Manager redefines portfolio management by unifying AI-driven optimization, real-time market intelligence, and blockchain-based verification into a single institutional-grade platform.
Unlike traditional tools that operate in silos, QuantAI delivers transparent, explainable, and tamper-proof portfolio decisions, making advanced investment intelligence accessible, verifiable, and future-ready.
This convergence of AI + blockchain + quantitative finance represents a novel, production-ready innovation rather than a prototype concept.

**AWS**

QuantAI Portfolio Manager is architected and deployed using AWS to deliver scalable, production-grade AI finance infrastructure.
The platform leverages AWS compute, networking, and security primitives to run AI/ML models, real-time market data pipelines, and blockchain verification workflows reliably at scale.

AWS enables:

Scalable model execution for portfolio optimization, risk analytics, and AI inference

Secure environment management using IAM-style separation and encrypted secrets

Cloud-native deployment of the Streamlit frontend and Python backend services

High availability and low latency for real-time financial analytics

By using AWS as the backbone, QuantAI demonstrates how cloud-native infrastructure can power institutional-grade AI and blockchain applications, making advanced financial intelligence accessible, secure, and globally scalable.

### Arbiata
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/arbiata-2f1d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/santu8597/Arbiata) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Calcutta%20<Hacks/>-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://calcutta-lesshacksgreater.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Arbitrage Executor

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Uniswap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Uniswap-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Arbitrage trading in DeFi is fundamentally broken. Most arbitrage bots and tools make a critical mistake: they chase theoretical price differences without accounting for the brutal reality of execution costs. A bot might detect that ETH costs $2,100 on one DEX and $2,103 on another, calculate a $3 profit, and execute the trade—only to lose $5 after accounting for gas fees, slippage, and MEV attacks.

The root problem is that these systems conflate **detection** with **execution**. They assume that because an opportunity exists in theory, it will be profitable in practice. This leads to:

- Lost capital from unprofitable trades that looked good on paper
- Wasted gas fees on reverted transactions
- MEV bot sandwich attacks eating into profits
- Slippage in low-liquidity pools destroying margins
- No accountability when trades fail

Arbfarm solves this by inverting the entire model. Instead of predicting profits, we **enforce** them on-chain. The smart contract includes a simple but powerful invariant:

```solidity
uint256 profit = ethAfter - ethBefore;
require(profit >= minProfit, "Trade not profitable");
```

If this check fails, the entire transaction reverts. Your principal is preserved, and you only pay the cost of a failed transaction (typically under $0.10 on Layer 2 networks).

But enforcement alone isn't enough. We need to avoid attempting unprofitable trades in the first place. This is where our AI layer comes in—not to predict prices, but to act as a **risk filter**. The AI receives deterministic simulation data (gas costs, slippage estimates, fee breakdowns) and makes a binary decision: EXECUTE or SKIP.

**Ethereum Track**

This is a pure Ethereum application—no centralized APIs for execution, no off-chain orderbooks, no trusted third parties. Everything that matters happens on-chain:

User deposits: logged in contract state
Trade execution: atomic Uniswap V3 swaps
Profit enforcement: on-chain require statement
Transaction history: emitted events, queryable via RPC
The contract integrates with Uniswap V3 SwapRouter02, demonstrating proper WETH wrapping, deadline protection, and slippage tolerance. The code handles the full complexity of Uniswap's interface (pool fees, sqrtPriceX96, tick math) while keeping the user-facing API simple.

Deployed on Base (Coinbase's L2) and Arbitrum (Offchain Labs' L2), showing multi-chain compatibility and awareness of the Ethereum L2 ecosystem. The frontend uses modern Ethereum libraries (wagmi, viem, RainbowKit) instead of legacy ethers.js patterns.

The transaction history feature queries contract events directly via ethers.js providers, demonstrating that blockchain data is the source of truth—no databases, no backend state synchronization.

> CrossChain Private DeFi Eligibility Layer

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon RPC Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20RPC%20Node-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Plight addresses a core inefficiency in DeFi risk management: protocols are forced to treat every wallet as equally risky, regardless of on-chain behavior. Lacking a privacy-preserving way to distinguish reckless activity from consistently responsible use, protocols default to extreme overcollateralization, locking excess capital even from reliable participants.

Plight enables users to prove recent responsible on-chain behavior such as maintaining healthy positions or avoiding liquidations without revealing identity, wallet history, or transaction details. Rather than introducing identity systems or reputation scores, Plight provides a narrow, time-bounded eligibility proof. If a user can cryptographically demonstrate responsible behavior within a recent window, a protocol may safely offer better terms; otherwise, it falls back to existing conservative defaults.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Enabling selective trust without creating a new trust surface

The hardest challenge was allowing protocols to treat users differently based on behavior without introducing a new authority that protocols must trust more than the user. Any behavioral layer risks becoming a centralized arbiter of “good” and “bad” wallets. Plight had to be designed so that it refines existing collateral-based security rather than replacing it, ensuring protocols never depend solely on Plight for safety and can safely ignore it at any time.

### Making behavior verifiable without making it portable or permanent

Another fundamental challenge was preventing responsible behavior from becoming a transferable or long-lived asset. If eligibility could be reused indefinitely or across contexts, it would quickly turn into a de facto credit score. Plight had to enforce strict time bounds and immediate revocation so that behavior remains contextual, non-accumulative, and non-transferable, even while remaining useful to protocols

> WHERE DIGITAL HISTORY BECOMES THE PROOF OF TRUST

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon (Matic)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20(Matic)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Synthetic identity fraud allows criminals to create “fake people” using a mix of real stolen data and AI-generated documents. These identities often pass traditional KYC checks and are later used to commit large-scale financial fraud.

---

## What It Can Be Used For

- **Banks & Fintechs:** Detect fake identities during onboarding and reduce loan/credit fraud  
- **Lending & Insurance Platforms:** Stop long-term synthetic borrowers and false claims  
- **Digital Platforms:** Prevent fake or bot-driven account creation  

---

How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer

- Goes beyond “document looks real” checks by verifying real digital history  
- Uses multiple signals (documents, online presence, relationships, behavior) instead of one fragile check  
- Automates identity risk scoring, reducing manual reviews and false approvals  
- Flags high-risk identities early, before financial damage occurs  

In short: It helps organizations verify real people, block AI-generated fake identities, and reduce fraud with faster, more reliable decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge I ran into was handling third-party API keys and external service dependencies, especially in Layer 2 (OSINT). Some APIs had strict rate limits, slow responses, or intermittent failures, which caused verification requests to time out. I addressed this by adding request timeouts, fallback logic, and allowing the system to continue with partial scores instead of failing completely when an external API was unavailable.
Another hurdle was collecting and analyzing behavioral data in real time (Layer 4). Initially, behavior was only captured after form submission, which produced unreliable results. I fixed this by starting data collection as soon as the page loads using JavaScript hooks and aggregating the data throughout the session, then analyzing it only when the user clicks “Verify.”
I also faced challenges with identity graph analysis (Layer 3). In early testing, real users were sometimes flagged due to sparse or incomplete data. I overcame this by refining the scoring logic to prioritize relationship age, consistency, and cross-link validation rather than just the number of connections.
Overall, the key challenge was building a system that remained resilient despite unreliable external APIs and imperfect data, ensuring that no single layer or service could break the entire verification process.

> A Milestone-Based Crowdfunding Platform

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem DeFund Solves**

The Trust Problem in Crowdfunding

Traditional crowdfunding platforms operate on blind trust

. Backers send all funds upfront
. Project creators self-report progress
. Platforms rely on manual, centralized review
. Once funds are released, there is no technical enforcement

As a result:

. Backers have no guarantee that milestones will be completed
. Fraud, abandonment, and misuse of funds are common
. Legitimate creators suffer from low investor confidence
. Crowdfunding today asks people to trust promises instead of progress.

**Key Risks in Existing Systems**

. Upfront Fund Release → High risk if the project fails
. Manual Verification → Slow, subjective, and non-scalable
. Centralized Control → Single point of failure and bias
. No On-Chain Accountability → Funds can’t be programmatically recovered

**How DeFund Solves This**

. DeFund replaces trust with verification and enforcement.
. It enables people to use crowdfunding in a safer, automated, and transparent way by combining AI, workflow orchestration, and blockchain escrow.

**What People Can Use DeFund For**

🧑‍💻 Creators can raise funds in stages by committing to verifiable milestones

💰 Backers fund projects knowing money is released only after progress is proven

🧪 Validators & reviewers can audit milestones with AI-assisted evidence

🌍 Teams & DAOs can fund R&D, open-source, and innovation projects globally

**How DeFund Makes Crowdfunding Safer**

Milestone-Based Escrow
Funds are locked in smart contracts and released only after milestone approval

AI-Driven Verification
AI audits code, documents, and proofs to objectively verify progress

Workflow-Enforced Logic
Orchestrated workflows ensure no step is skipped or manually bypassed

Immutable Settlement
Blockchain enforces rules transparently—no platform or creator can override them

**How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier**

| Task                     | Traditional Platforms | DeFund                      |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Fund Release          | Manual & upfront      | Automatic & milestone-based |
| Progress Verification | Self-reported         | AI + workflow enforced      |
| Trust                 | Social trust          | Cryptographic trust         |
| Risk Management       | Platform-dependent    | Code-enforced               |
| Transparency          | Limited               | Fully auditable             |


**Outcome**

DeFund enables crowdfunding where:

. Builders are rewarded for real progress
. Backers are protected by code, not promises
. Trust is programmatically enforced
. Funding becomes fair, transparent, and accountable

DeFund turns “trust me” into “verify and release.”

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into:

**1. Synchronizing AI Decisions with Blockchain Execution**

Challenge:
AI verification, backend logic, and blockchain transactions operate asynchronously, which initially caused inconsistent milestone states.

Resolution:
I introduced workflow-driven orchestration using Orkes Conductor, modeling milestone approval as a deterministic state machine. Blockchain actions are triggered only after AI verification steps complete successfully.

Impact:

Eliminated race conditions

Ensured milestone approval is atomic and auditable

**2. Preventing AI from Becoming a Single Point of Trust**

Challenge:
Using AI directly to release funds posed explainability and safety risks.

Resolution:
AI was restricted to an auditing role. It generates structured verification reports that are stored and reviewed by the workflow before any on-chain action.

Impact:

AI decisions are traceable and reviewable

Funds are never released based on opaque AI output

**3. Enforcing Secure Role-Based Authorization**

Challenge:
Only authorized roles should be able to trigger sensitive actions like milestone approval.

Resolution:
Implemented Auth0 with JWT claims, enforcing strict role-based access at the backend before workflows can proceed.

Impact:

Clear trust boundaries

No unauthorized on-chain actions

**4. Abstracting Blockchain Complexity for Non-Technical Users**

Challenge:
Direct blockchain interactions degrade UX and confuse non-technical users.

Resolution:
All blockchain logic was abstracted behind backend APIs, and the frontend displays workflow status instead of raw transaction data.

Impact:

Web2-like UX

Web3-level security guarantees

**5. Designing for Failure Scenarios**

Challenge:
Partial failures (AI timeouts, transaction failures) could previously leave the system in undefined states.

Resolution:
Explicit failure states and retry logic were added to workflows, ensuring funds remain locked unless all checks pass.

Impact:

System fails closed, not open

Stronger investor protection

**Key Takeaway**

The primary challenge was not implementing AI or blockchain individually, but orchestrating trust across multiple systems.

By using workflow orchestration as the backbone, AI as an auditor, and blockchain as the final authority, the platform achieves deterministic, secure, and user-friendly milestone-based funding.

**Aptos**

DeFund leverages Aptos as a core settlement and execution layer for its milestone-based crowdfunding model, taking advantage of Aptos’s Move-based safety guarantees, parallel execution, and strong resource semantics.

**Secure Milestone-Based Escrow with Move**

In DeFund, project funds are locked in on-chain vaults implemented using Aptos Move smart contracts.
Each vault represents a resource, ensuring:

Funds cannot be duplicated or accidentally leaked

Unauthorized access is impossible by design

Milestones act as explicit state gates enforced at the contract level

This makes Aptos ideal for modeling financial escrow logic, where correctness and safety are critical.

**Deterministic State Transitions via Move**

Milestone approvals in DeFund are implemented as explicit state transitions within Move modules:

A milestone can only transition from Pending → Approved

Fund release can only occur after a valid state transition

Invalid or repeated transitions are rejected by the VM

By encoding these rules in Move, DeFund ensures that fund release is mathematically and programmatically enforced, not reliant on off-chain trust.

**High-Throughput & Parallel Execution**

DeFund is designed to support multiple projects, milestones, and contributors concurrently.

Aptos’s parallel execution engine allows:

Independent milestones to be processed simultaneously

High transaction throughput during funding events

Low latency for approvals and fund releases

This makes Aptos well-suited for scalable crowdfunding systems.

**Clean Separation Between Off-Chain Logic and On-Chain Authority**

In DeFund’s architecture:

AI verification and workflow orchestration happen off-chain

Final authority always resides on-chain in Aptos contracts

Aptos serves as the trust anchor, ensuring that:

No off-chain service can bypass escrow rules

Funds remain locked unless all on-chain conditions are satisfied

**Why Aptos (and Not Just Any Chain)**

DeFund uses Aptos specifically because:

Move resources naturally model escrow vaults and milestones

Strong typing and safety guarantees reduce financial bugs

High performance supports real-world crowdfunding scale

Upgradeable modules allow protocol evolution without compromising safety

**Aptos Track Summary**

DeFund uses Aptos not as an add-on, but as a core execution engine where milestone gates, escrow vaults, and fund release logic are immutably enforced through Move smart contracts.

This makes DeFund a natural fit for the Aptos track, showcasing how Aptos can be used to build secure, scalable, real-world financial infrastructure.

**Solana**

DeFund uses Solana as a core settlement and enforcement layer for its milestone-based crowdfunding model, leveraging Solana’s high throughput, low fees, and programmatic account model to enable fast, trustless fund release tied to verified progress.

Rather than treating Solana as a payment rail, DeFund uses it as a financial state machine that enforces escrow logic, milestone gates, and irreversible fund release conditions.

**On-Chain Escrow & Vault Architecture (Solana Programs)**

In DeFund, all contributed funds are locked into on-chain escrow vaults implemented using Anchor programs.

Each project on DeFund maps to:

A Program Derived Address (PDA) vault that securely holds funds

On-chain milestone accounts that track approval state

Strict program constraints that prevent unauthorized withdrawals

This ensures:

Funds cannot be accessed prematurely

Neither creators nor the platform can bypass escrow rules

All fund movements are fully transparent and auditable

Solana’s account-based design makes this escrow model clean, explicit, and secure.

**Milestone Gates as On-Chain State Transitions**

Milestones in DeFund are not off-chain flags—they are explicit on-chain states.

Each milestone:

Starts in a Pending state

Can only transition to Approved after backend-triggered verification

Unlocks a predefined fund tranche only once

The Solana program enforces:

One-way state transitions

No duplicate approvals

No partial or manual overrides

This makes Solana the final authority in the system, not the backend or AI.

**Why Solana Is Critical for Performance & UX**

Crowdfunding platforms must handle:

Many contributors funding simultaneously

Frequent milestone approvals

Real-time feedback to users

Solana’s:

High throughput

Low transaction fees

Fast confirmation times

allow DeFund to:

Release funds immediately after milestone approval

Avoid gas-fee friction for users

Maintain a smooth, Web2-like UX

This performance profile is essential for consumer-facing financial applications, which many chains struggle to support.

**Clean Separation of Responsibilities**

DeFund follows a clear trust hierarchy:

Off-chain (Web2 + AI):

Milestone submission

AI auditing and workflow orchestration

On-chain (Solana):

Escrow custody

Milestone gate enforcement

Final fund release

Even if AI or backend services fail or are compromised, Solana programs prevent invalid fund movement. This design makes Solana the trust anchor of the platform.

**Anchor Framework for Safety & Developer Velocity**

Using Anchor enables:

Strong account validation

Clear instruction constraints

Reduced risk of common Solana bugs

Faster iteration during hackathon development

This allowed DeFund to focus on correct financial logic instead of low-level boilerplate, while still maintaining safety guarantees.

**Real-World Use Case for Solana**

DeFund demonstrates how Solana can power:

Consumer-friendly fintech products

Trustless crowdfunding and capital allocation

Escrow systems with real accountability

It moves beyond NFTs or simple transfers and showcases Solana as a serious settlement layer for real economic workflows.

**Solana Track Summary**

DeFund uses Solana as a high-performance, low-cost, trustless settlement engine where milestone-based escrow, fund custody, and release logic are enforced on-chain. By combining Solana programs with off-chain AI verification and workflow orchestration, DeFund demonstrates a practical, scalable financial application that Solana is uniquely well-suited to support.

**Orkes Conductor**

DeFund uses Orkes Conductor as the central orchestration backbone of the entire platform. Rather than handling business logic through ad-hoc backend code, DeFund models milestone-based crowdfunding as deterministic, state-driven workflows, which is exactly the class of problems Orkes Conductor is designed to solve.

In DeFund, every sensitive operation that can affect funds is coordinated through Orkes workflows, making Conductor the single source of truth for system state and execution order.

**Orkes as the Backbone of Milestone-Based Funding**

Crowdfunding with milestones is inherently a long-running, multi-step process, involving:

User submissions

AI-based verification

Data persistence

Blockchain transactions

Failure handling and retries

These steps:

Cannot be executed synchronously

Cannot be safely handled with simple API calls

Must never be skipped or reordered

DeFund uses Orkes Conductor to model this as a workflow state machine, where each milestone progresses through clearly defined stages such as:

SUBMITTED → AI_AUDIT → REVIEWED → CHAIN_EXECUTED → COMPLETED


This ensures deterministic execution, even across retries, crashes, or partial failures.

**JSON-Defined Workflows for Deterministic Logic**

All milestone approval logic in DeFund is defined using Conductor’s JSON workflow definitions, not hardcoded business logic.

Each workflow explicitly defines:

Task dependencies

Conditional branching based on AI audit results

Retry and timeout policies

Failure states that halt fund release

This approach provides:

Transparency – workflows are readable and auditable

Safety – no hidden logic paths

Flexibility – workflows can evolve without redeploying the entire backend

**Coordinating AI Audits Without Trusting AI Blindly**

AI verification is asynchronous, probabilistic, and non-deterministic—making it unsafe to directly trigger financial actions.

In DeFund:

AI (Gemini + OpenRouter) is invoked as a workflow task

AI output is treated as data, not authority

Orkes evaluates the AI result before proceeding

Only if the workflow conditions are satisfied does Orkes allow execution to continue toward blockchain interaction.

This ensures:

AI assists decisions but never bypasses rules

All AI actions are traceable within workflow history

**Safe Coordination with Blockchain Transactions**

Blockchain calls are expensive, slow, and irreversible.

DeFund uses Orkes to:

Gate blockchain execution behind verified workflow states

Ensure smart contract calls happen exactly once

Prevent duplicate or premature fund release

Handle transaction failures cleanly

If a blockchain transaction fails:

The workflow transitions to a defined failure state

Funds remain locked on-chain

The system can safely retry or escalate

This makes Orkes critical to financial correctness.

**Designing for Failure, Not Just the Happy Path**

Real systems fail. DeFund explicitly models failure in Orkes workflows:

AI timeouts

Database write failures

Blockchain rejections

Network issues

Orkes allows DeFund to:

Retry only safe steps

Stop execution when invariants are violated

Avoid partial or corrupted states

This is essential for a platform that handles real money.

**Clear Separation of Responsibilities**

DeFund’s trust model is cleanly separated:

Frontend → User interaction

Backend services → Task execution

Orkes Conductor → Control plane & orchestration

Blockchain → Final authority

By moving orchestration into Orkes, DeFund avoids:

Fragile custom state management

Complex, hard-to-audit backend logic

Implicit execution order bugs

**Orkes Track Summary**

DeFund uses Orkes Conductor as a deterministic workflow engine to orchestrate AI audits, database updates, and blockchain execution in a milestone-based crowdfunding system. By modeling financial logic as explicit workflows, DeFund ensures correctness, traceability, and failure safety—demonstrating a real-world, production-grade use of Orkes for trust-critical systems.

**Requestly**

DeFund integrates Requestly as a critical development, testing, and debugging tool while building a complex Web2.5 system that spans frontend UI, backend orchestration, AI services, and blockchain interactions.

Because DeFund relies on multiple asynchronous external services, Requestly plays a key role in simulating, inspecting, and validating real-world behavior without risking funds or breaking live systems.

**Testing Complex API Interactions Safely**

DeFund’s frontend communicates with backend APIs that eventually trigger:

AI audits (Gemini + OpenRouter)

Orkes Conductor workflows

Blockchain transactions on Solana and Aptos

During development, directly calling these services is:

Slow

Expensive

Risky (especially for blockchain actions)

Requestly was used to:

Intercept API requests from the frontend

Mock backend responses for milestone submission and approval

Simulate success and failure scenarios without executing real workflows

This enabled rapid frontend iteration without waiting on backend or blockchain execution.

**Simulating Failure & Edge Cases (Critical for Financial Systems)**

One of the hardest parts of DeFund is handling non-happy paths, such as:

AI verification failure

Workflow rejection

Blockchain transaction errors

Network timeouts

Requestly allowed us to:

Override API responses to simulate AI audit failures

Inject error payloads into workflow responses

Test frontend and backend error-handling logic safely

This ensured the system:

Fails closed (funds remain locked)

Communicates clear status updates to users

Handles real-world instability gracefully

**Debugging Auth & Authorization Flows**

DeFund uses Auth0 with JWT claims for role-based access control (Investor, Creator, Validator).

Requestly was used to:

Inspect outgoing authorization headers

Validate JWT payloads reaching backend services

Debug permission-related failures without changing code

Simulate different role claims during testing

This was especially useful when verifying that:

Only authorized roles can trigger milestone workflows

Unauthorized actions never reach Orkes or blockchain layers

**Frontend–Backend Contract Validation**

With multiple moving parts, keeping frontend and backend API contracts aligned is non-trivial.

Requestly helped by:

Logging and inspecting request/response payloads

Catching schema mismatches early

Verifying that frontend expectations matched backend outputs

Allowing rapid fixes before issues reached workflow or chain layers

This reduced integration friction significantly.

**Accelerating Iteration Speed in a Hackathon Environment**

In a hackathon setting, speed matters.

Requestly enabled:

Instant mocking instead of redeploying services

Parallel frontend and backend development

Faster debugging without redeploying smart contracts

Safe testing without real funds or chain calls

This allowed DeFund to move faster without compromising correctness or security.

**Why Requestly Was the Right Tool**

DeFund is a system where:

Bugs can be expensive

Failures can impact trust

External services are asynchronous and unpredictable

Requestly provided:

Controlled simulation

Observability into live requests

Safe experimentation

Faster feedback loops

This made it an essential part of the development and testing workflow, even though it doesn’t run in production.

**Requestly Track Summary**

DeFund uses Requestly as a development and testing accelerator to safely intercept, mock, and validate API interactions across frontend, backend, AI, and workflow layers. This enables rapid iteration, secure testing of failure scenarios, and reliable integration—critical for building a trust-sensitive, multi-service Web2.5 platform.

Our drone and IoT-based system enables safe, automated, and real-time water sampling, providing accurate, geo-tagged data from hard-to-reach locations. It allows faster pollution detection, wider monitoring coverage, and publicly accessible water health data, supporting better governance, research, and environmental protection.

### AquaSafe
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aquapredict-0498) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Mridula341/AquaSafe) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CloudCraft%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://cloudcraft-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart cloud intelligence for safer water

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Access to safe drinking water remains a major challenge due to increasing water contamination caused by industrial waste, salinity, and improper monitoring. Traditional water quality testing methods are often manual, time-consuming, expensive, and not available in real time, especially in rural or resource-limited areas.

As a result, contamination is frequently detected after people are exposed, leading to serious health risks such as waterborne diseases. There is also a lack of easy-to-use digital tools that allow non-experts to quickly assess water safety using available data.

AquaSafe addresses this problem by providing a cloud-based, machine-learning powered solution that enables users to instantly predict whether water is safe or contaminated based on key quality parameters. By offering fast predictions, clear risk levels, and an intuitive interface, AquaSafe makes water quality assessment simpler, faster, and safer, supporting better decision-making for individuals, communities, and authorities.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was setting up smooth communication between the frontend and backend. Since the frontend and Flask backend were running on different local ports, I initially faced CORS-related errors that prevented the UI from receiving predictions. This was resolved by correctly configuring CORS in the Flask backend and ensuring the API endpoint remained consistent.

Another challenge involved model file management. The trained ML model was not being detected due to incorrect file paths and execution directories, which caused runtime errors. I fixed this by standardizing the project structure and explicitly loading the model from a relative path inside the backend.

Additionally, environment setup on Windows posed difficulties, particularly with Python installation, PATH configuration, and dependency mismatches. These issues were resolved by validating the Python installation, using pip for dependency management, and verifying versions through testing.

Finally, improving the frontend user experience without breaking the working backend required careful coordination. This was addressed by isolating UI changes strictly to frontend files while keeping API calls unchanged.

Overcoming these challenges helped ensure the application is stable, fully functional, and production-ready for demonstration.

**Ethereum Track**

AquaSafe focuses on predicting water quality using machine learning to support safer and more transparent decision-making. While the current prototype operates as a cloud-based ML system, it aligns with the Ethereum track through its future scope and architectural compatibility with decentralized systems.

In a blockchain-enabled extension, Ethereum smart contracts can be used to store immutable water quality reports, ensuring transparency and tamper-proof records for government bodies, NGOs, and communities. Decentralized storage solutions can further enable secure sharing of water safety data across regions.

By combining off-chain ML inference with on-chain verification and auditability, AquaSafe demonstrates how real-world environmental data can be integrated into the Ethereum ecosystem to promote trust, accountability, and decentralized public infrastructure.

### Kredifi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kredifi-f9ab) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/stonecoldjgm/kredify) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Credit Without Borders, Privacy Without Compromise

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

280+ million migrants and international workers face "credit invisibility" when they move to a new country. Their financial history doesn't travel with them, forcing them to:

>Pay higher interest rates (up to 10% more)
>Get rejected for apartments, loans, and credit cards
>Rebuild credit from zero despite years of responsible borrowing
>Traditional credit systems are:

🔒 Siloed - Credit scores don't cross borders
🔓 Privacy-invasive - Require exposing raw financial data
⚖️ Biased - AI models often discriminate against certain demographics


💡 How Kredify Solves This
Kredify creates a portable, encrypted credit identity that works globally:

1.Encrypted Behavioral Identity (EBI) - Your financial patterns are transformed into encrypted vectors that banks can verify but never see
2.Real Zero-Knowledge Proofs - Prove you're creditworthy without revealing your actual data
3.ML-Powered Embeddings - Neural network-based behavioral analysis
4.Blockchain Anchoring - Proofs are stored on-chain for immutable verification
>>Result: Fair credit access anywhere in the world, with complete privacy.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Implementing Real Zero-Knowledge Proofs
Building actual cryptographic proofs (not just simulated ones) was challenging. We implemented SHA-256 commitment schemes with Fiat-Shamir heuristics for range proofs that can verify trust scores without revealing the actual value.

 2. ML Embeddings Without Heavy Dependencies
Creating meaningful behavioral embeddings without TensorFlow.js (to keep bundle size small). We built a custom neural network-inspired transformation with pre-trained weight matrices that generates 32-dimensional vectors from behavioral metrics.

 3. Cross-Border Compatibility
Designing a schema that works across different financial systems and regulations (GDPR, CCPA, FCRA) while maintaining privacy guarantees.

 4. Blockchain Integration Trade-offs
Balancing between real on-chain storage (expensive, slow) vs. simulated blockchain (demo-friendly). We chose simulated Polygon with realistic transaction flows for the hackathon demo.

**Ethereum Track**

Kredify leverages blockchain technology for **immutable proof anchoring**:

🔗 **On-Chain Verification**
- ZK proof hashes are stored on Polygon (EVM-compatible)
- Anyone can verify a credit proof exists without seeing the underlying data
- Smart contract tracks verification records

- Zero-Knowledge Proofs ensure data never leaves the user's control

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/solidity-scanner-48fa) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/abdel-az/SmartScan-Advanced-FV) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/qH9lgmUcogM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous Smart Contract Security Scanner.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![LLM](https://img.shields.io/badge/LLM-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Smart contract vulnerabilities cause millions in losses each year. Audits are slow, expensive, and inaccessible to small developers. Existing automated scanners are limited and generate weak or generic reports. There is a major gap between fast AI-driven feedback and full human audits.

Solution
SmartScan AI provides:

LLM reasoning engine trained on 5,000+ exploit samples
Hybrid static + semantic AI analysis
Instant high-quality vulnerability detection
Deep audit-style report with explanations and fixes
MetaMask pay-per-scan system
Integration API for Web3 builders and launchpads
This makes professional-level security accessible to everyone

Unique Angle (“Vibe”)

Unlike traditional scanners, SmartScan AI uses contextual understanding, not just pattern matching. It explains why an issue exists and shows how to fix it — turning security into an interactive learning experience. This creates an educational + audit hybrid product with strong retention.

AI Technology Used
Custom-fine-tuned LLM (code + cybersecurity)
Embedding vector search for exploit similarity
Threat classification model (Python)
Django backend for inference
React frontend with real-time analysis viewer
Revenue Model
SmartScan AI is revenue-first:

Pay-per-scan via MetaMask
$1 basic scan
$12 deep scan
API subscription for companies
$99 → $499 monthly tiers
SmartScan Token (Vibe Coin) utilities:
50% discount on scans
Staking for extra analysis credits
Access to premium AI models
Governance of roadmap
Revenue share pool funded by platform fees
This makes SmartScan a sustainable and profitable project — exactly what Seedify wants.

**Challenges we ran into**

Taming the AI "Hallucinations": Early on, the AI would sometimes flag a piece of code as a "re-entrancy" bug when it was actually perfectly safe. To fix this, we stopped relying on generic AI and fed it a specialized dataset of 5,000+ real-world exploits. This helped the model learn the difference between "bad-looking code" and an "actual exploit."

Processing Speed vs. Accuracy: Running a "Deep Scan" on a long smart contract was taking too long for a web app. Users don't want to wait 2 minutes for a report. We optimized this by using Vector Search—essentially letting the AI "skim" the code for suspicious patterns first before doing a deep dive into the logic, making the results nearly instant.

MetaMask & Web3 UX: Integrating the "Pay-per-Scan" feature was tricky. We had to make sure the backend didn't start the scan until the transaction was confirmed on-chain, but we didn't want the user staring at a loading screen. We built a custom listener that triggers the AI engine the moment the payment is detected, smoothing out the transition from "Pay" to "Result."

Handling Code Imports: Most developers use external libraries like OpenZeppelin. Initially, our scanner would crash because it couldn't "see" those imported files. We had to build a pre-processor to "flatten" the code so the AI could analyze everything in one single view without missing any dependencies.

### SkillChain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/skillchain-5496) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/qrUoJZhB3K4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Future of Digital Trust

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SkillChain is a decentralized identity platform that replaces the broken system of digital credentials. Currently, we face a "Privacy Paradox": standard NFTs expose too much personal data (grades, home address) on the public blockchain, while PDF certificates are easily forged and hard to verify.

SkillChain solves this by creating a privacy-first "Verifiable Credentials" layer.

1. For Students (The Holders):

True Ownership: Students hold their degrees in a "Skills Wallet" rather than leaving them trapped in university databases.

Privacy Control: Users can prove they are qualified (e.g., "I have a B.Tech degree") without revealing their grades or birthdate, using our Selective Disclosure logic.

Secure Sharing: Instead of sharing a permanent wallet address, students can generate a "One-Time Burner Link"—a QR code that allows an employer to view a credential once before self-destructing.

2. For Employers (The Verifiers):

Instant Verification: No more waiting weeks for background checks. Employers can cryptographically verify the authenticity of a degree in seconds.

Trustless Validity: The system checks the on-chain registry to ensure the issuer is a valid, accredited institution, eliminating fake degrees.

Live Status Checks: Our Dynamic Credential engine ensures skills are current. If a certification (like First Aid) has expired, the badge visually "rusts" and the verification fails, preventing the use of outdated credentials.

3. For Universities (The Issuers):

Fraud Protection: Their reputation is protected by the blockchain immutable registry.

Revocability: If a degree needs to be revoked (e.g., due to plagiarism), they can toggle the status on-chain, instantly invalidating the student's proof without needing access to the student's device.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Privacy vs. Transparency" Conflict: The biggest hurdle was architecting a system that uses the Blockchain for trust but keeps the data off-chain for privacy. Initially, I thought about storing the certificate metadata directly on-chain. I quickly realized this would violate GDPR and expose student data.

Solution: I pivoted to a "Hash-on-Chain, Data-off-Chain" architecture. We store the heavy, private data on IPFS (encrypted) and only store the cryptographic hash on the Smart Contract. This allows verification without exposure.

2. The "One-Time Link" Logic: Implementing the "Burner Link" feature was tricky. I needed a way to share a credential that works exactly once without a centralized database tracking every user move.

Solution: I used a cryptographic signature approach. The wallet signs a message with a unique nonce and an expiration timestamp. The backend verifies this signature and checks an in-memory "used nonce" list. Once scanned, that specific signature is blacklisted, effectively "burning" the link.

3. Onboarding Non-Crypto Users: I realized that asking a student to "Install MetaMask" and "Buy ETH for gas" would kill adoption immediately.

Solution: I integrated Privy for the authentication flow. This allows students to log in with just an email (Gmail), and the app spins up a secure embedded wallet for them in the background. It abstracts away the complexity of seed phrases.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/datacrypt-0754) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/cxgx4/DataCryptic) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ysq4soSvgGg) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ysq4soSvgGg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Research That Transcends Failure

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, only positive results are published. When an experiment fails, it’s buried in a lab notebook. This creates a massive global inefficiency:

**Redundant Spending:** Billions in funding are wasted as labs unknowingly repeat the same failed experiments.

**Knowledge Gaps:** Scientists lack a "map" of what doesn’t work, slowing down the pace of discovery.

**Lost IP:** Months of rigorous work provide zero value or credit to the researcher if the hypothesis is proven wrong.

**The Solution: DataCrypt**

DataCrypt is a Decentralized Science (DeSci) archive that transforms "failed" research into valuable, liquid assets.

**Key Features & Benefits**

- Monetized Failure: Researchers mint findings as IP-NFTs. While abstracts are public, raw data is encrypted and accessible only via MATIC/ETH payments, creating a new economy for scientific dead-ends.

- Immutable Proof of Work: Using the Polygon blockchain, we provide an unalterable timestamp of authorship. Researchers get permanent credit for their work, regardless of the outcome.

- Verified Quality: A decentralized Admin Command Center ensures submissions are peer-reviewed and verified before being committed to the chain.

- Accelerated Discovery: A robust, domain-specific search engine allows scientists to perform "due diligence" in seconds, preventing months of redundant trial and error.

**DataCrypt** makes scientific inquiry safer by protecting intellectual property and more efficient by ensuring no data is ever wasted. We are turning the world’s "file drawer" of failures into a transparent, revenue-generating engine for global innovation.

**Challenges we ran into**

We hit a massive wall with **Hydration Errors** that threatened to break the entire UI. Our dynamic starfield caused a critical server/client mismatch because **Math.random()** generated different positions on each side. We were forced to restructure our rendering lifecycle, moving generation to a **useEffect** hook to ensure the UI remained stable and consistent.
We also spent hours battling constant **Internal JSON-RPC errors (code -32603)** that made minting impossible. We discovered this stemmed from severe Cross-Chain UX friction with MetaMask defaulting to Ethereum. We engineered a programmatic "network guard" that intercepts transactions and forces the correct Polygon Amoy context automatically.
We nearly scrapped our "**Deep Glassmorphism**" aesthetic because scientific data became unreadable against the cosmic nebulas. After multiple failed iterations, we solved this by layering backdrop-blur-xl surfaces with glowing drop-shadow text to maintain high visibility without losing the sci-fi vibe.

> A fully decentralized and automated lottery DApp u

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mocha](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mocha-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chainlink](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chainlink-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project solves the problem of trust and automation in lotteries by creating a fully decentralized, transparent, and autonomous system. Traditional lotteries often require a central authority to manage ticket sales, pick winners, and distribute prizes, which introduces risks like manipulation, fraud, or human error. This DApp removes that dependency by using smart contracts on Ethereum-compatible networks to handle all aspects of the lottery.

Participants can buy tickets by sending ETH, and the winner is randomly selected using Chainlink VRF, which provides verifiable and tamper-proof randomness. The process is fully automated using Chainlink Automation (Keepers), which triggers winner selection once certain conditions are met, without requiring any manual intervention. The winner automatically receives the prize, and the lottery resets for the next round.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building the decentralized lottery DApp, I faced several hurdles, particularly around Chainlink VRF integration and Automation:

Getting Verifiable Randomness (VRF) to Work Properly

Issue: Initially, the contract wasn’t receiving the random number from Chainlink VRF. The fulfillRandomWords() function wasn’t being called, which broke winner selection.

Cause: I had misconfigured the subscription ID, Key Hash, and VRF Coordinator address in the deployment scripts.

Solution: I carefully reviewed the Chainlink documentation, created a proper subscription in the VRF Subscription Manager, added the contract as a consumer, and updated all values in the scripts. After redeploying, the VRF started returning valid random numbers reliably.

Automating the Lottery Draw with Chainlink Keepers

Issue: The automated draw wasn’t triggering because checkUpkeep() always returned false.

Cause: My conditions for upkeep weren’t aligning correctly with the contract state (time interval, player count, and balance checks).

Solution: I logged the contract state and carefully adjusted the logic in checkUpkeep() to accurately reflect when the lottery should run. After that, Keepers successfully triggered performUpkeep().

Frontend–Smart Contract Integration

Issue: Connecting the Next.js frontend to the deployed contract was tricky, especially for reading live contract state and sending transactions.

Solution: I leveraged ethers.js with proper provider, signer, and contract instances, and tested each function incrementally. This approach made the frontend responsive and reliable.

> Intent-based Web3 wallet for X402

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Railway (Deployment)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Railway%20(Deployment)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite (development frontend)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite%20(development%20frontend)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Middleware pattern](https://img.shields.io/badge/Middleware%20pattern-333333?style=flat-square) ![Raw body capture](https://img.shields.io/badge/Raw%20body%20capture-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most Web3 applications today still rely on low-level transaction signing, confusing wallet popups, and complex flows that overwhelm users. Developers who want to build intent-based or abstracted experiences struggle with:

1. Setting up a clean backend structure

2. Handling signatures, verification, or webhook-style flows

3. Managing API routes, logging, raw request capture

4. Quickly iterating on a frontend + backend together

5. Deploying a production-ready server without friction

IntentWallet solves this by providing a minimal, modular, and scalable boilerplate for intent-driven applications.
It offers an Express + TypeScript backend with automatic logging, raw body capture, JSON introspection, Vite-powered frontend development, and seamless Railway deployment.

This allows developers to focus on building intent logic instead of fighting framework setup.
With IntentWallet, building modern intent-based dApps or payment flows becomes much faster, cleaner, and more reliable.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Raw Body Parsing for Verification**
Handling raw request bodies (for signature verification or webhook flows) conflicted with Express’ JSON middleware.
I solved this by creating a custom middleware that captures raw data before parsing.

**Shared Server Instance for WebSocket Upgrades**
I needed both Express routes and potential WebSocket upgrades from a single server instance.
The fix was exporting the server reference and restructuring the initialization logic.

**Vite + Express Integration**
Running a full-stack dev environment with hot reload on both backend and frontend was tricky.
I solved it by conditionally enabling Vite in development and static serving in production.

**Railway Deployment Port Issues**
Railway assigns dynamic ports, which initially caused binding failures.
This was fixed by using process.env.PORT and binding to 0.0.0.0.

**Maintaining Clean Route Structure**
Express projects often get messy as they grow.
I designed a registerRoutes loader that automatically registers modular routes.

These challenges helped me build a cleaner, scalable foundation for future intent-based applications.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Inferno enables DeFi developers and API creators to confidently launch payment-gated services on Base by stress-testing x402 micropayment infrastructure before production. Developers can simulate realistic payment volume by spawning thousands of concurrent agents making authentic x402 requests, identify bottlenecks early by discovering performance degradation and transaction failures, test on Base testnet risk-free by executing full payment flows without production risk, measure actual gas economics to understand transaction costs at scale and optimize pricing, and reduce go-to-market friction by deploying with confidence knowing payment infrastructure is battle-tested. Instead of manually testing with a handful of users or hoping payment systems work at scale, developers get production-ready validation through automated, comprehensive stress testing tailored to x402 micropayment flows on Base.

**Challenges we ran into**

The primary challenge was understanding the x402 payment flow specification and translating it into a robust simulation engine that accurately reproduces real-world micropayment scenarios on Base. The x402 protocol involves multiple steps—initial API requests, 402 responses, transaction construction, signing, and authenticated retries—and getting the transaction signing and gas estimation correct for Base's EVM environment required deep familiarity with ethers.js and Base's RPC interactions.
Another hurdle was managing concurrent agent execution at scale without overwhelming the RPC endpoint or creating bottlenecks. Implementing proper rate limiting, wallet rotation, and error handling for failed transactions took careful consideration.
We overcame these by studying the x402 specification thoroughly, testing the engine locally against a mock x402 server to validate payment flows, and implementing incremental improvements to concurrency management. Moving forward, we're focused on building the CLI and dashboard components to make the engine accessible to developers, which will require translating engine metrics into meaningful performance insights and creating an intuitive configuration interface.

### RPSX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/rpgx-f824) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1joDQ2Wp3Ty4BZTfayD0d_tNdkwLFN6rI/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=113271088447576639051&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20Onchain%20with%20FBI-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://build-onchain-fbi.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Rock Paper Scissors Onchain x402

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square) ![Farcaster SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Farcaster%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Onchain games are technically decentralized but practically unplayable.

Even simple games require multiple onchain transactions for setup, moves, and settlement. This results in:

$3–$5 in gas fees to play a $1 game

Slow gameplay due to block confirmations

Repeated wallet popups that break UX

Because of this, real-time and casual onchain gaming has failed to gain adoption.

How RPSX Solves It

RPSX removes blockchain friction from gameplay.

Players deposit once using x402 and then play multiple games instantly.
Games are played offchain in real time and settled onchain in batches, reducing per-game cost to a few cents.

This enables:

Real-time gameplay with no signing during play

Micro-stake games that are economically viable

A web-like UX with onchain security

Why This Matters

RPSX demonstrates a practical pattern for consumer crypto:

Offchain interaction

Onchain custody

Batch settlement

x402-powered payments

This approach makes onchain gaming usable for real users and can be extended to many simple games beyond Rock Paper Scissors.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-Time Gameplay vs Onchain Finality

Onchain execution is too slow for interactive games, but fully offchain games break trust.

Fix:
I split the system into offchain execution + onchain settlement.
Moves are exchanged over WebSockets and each round is finalized via mutual signed messages. The contract only verifies signatures and applies payouts during batch settlement.

Gas Costs at Micro-Stakes

Per-game settlement made small-stake games economically impossible.

Fix:
I implemented batched settlement where multiple signed game results are committed in a single transaction. Gas is amortized across players, pushing per-game costs down to cents while keeping funds non-custodial.

Wallet UX Friction

Signing transactions per move kills retention.

Fix:
I used x402 for balance-based payments. Players deposit once, play many games without signing, and withdraw later. x402 removes wallet prompts from the critical path while keeping payment logic verifiable.

> Usage and payment, perfectly synced.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

x402-streamsocket solves the gap between real-time usage and real-time payment.

Most live systems today serve users continuously but charge them discretely. Once a WebSocket connection is open, there’s no native, trust-minimized way to guarantee the user is still paying while consuming resources. Payment usually happens before or after usage, not during it.

This creates real problems:

Overpayment: Users pay upfront even if they disconnect early.

Underpayment risk: Services keep connections open without knowing if payment still reflects usage.

Complex billing logic: Developers need off-chain tracking, reconciliation jobs, refunds, and abuse protection.

Poor fit for AI and agents: Autonomous systems need payment and access to stay perfectly in sync.


x402-streamsocket fixes this by making payment itself the access signal.

A Superfluid stream becomes a live proof of intent. As long as value is flowing, access continues. The moment it stops, access ends. No trust, no guessing, no cleanup

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Absence of Economic Primitives in Stateless Agent Communications**

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) successfully standardizes the transport layer for Large Language Model (LLM) agents to access external context. However, the current HTTP/JSON-RPC transport layer lacks a native Economic Settlement Primitive.

This results in three architectural deficiencies:

**Sybil Vulnerability & Resource Exhaustion: **Open endpoints are susceptible to spam and Denial of Service (DoS) by autonomous agents, as there is no economic cost to execution (cost > 0).

**Lack of Atomic Value Exchange:** Current architectures decouple service delivery from payment (e.g., monthly SaaS subscriptions), which is incompatible with the ephemeral, high-frequency, and transactional nature of AI agent operations.

**Protocol-Level Friction:** Agents encounter "soft" paywalls (HTML login pages) rather than "hard" protocol-level signals (HTTP 402), preventing autonomous negotiation and payment settlement.

> Rule the chain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Product in One Sentence

Base Cartel is an onchain, social-strategy game on Base where users earn, steal, and redistribute value through provable onchain actions like raids, referrals, and alliances, turning attention and activity into a competitive economic game.



2. What’s the Problem Statement

Most onchain applications today struggle with sustained user engagement. Incentives are often passive (airdrops, yield farming) or purely financial, which leads to short-term participation and rapid drop-off once rewards dry up. Social layers exist, but they are usually offchain, opaque, and disconnected from actual value flow.

At the same time, new primitives like x402 enable programmable, HTTP-native payments, but they are mostly used in isolated, utilitarian contexts. There is very little exploration of how payments, incentives, and social behavior can combine into a persistent, competitive system that rewards real activity rather than speculation.

Users lack:

Meaningful reasons to stay active daily
Transparent, onchain reward distribution
Social competition that actually affects outcomes
Systems where reputation, behavior, and economic impact are directly linked



3. How is this solved today?

Today, most projects solve engagement through:

Points systems that are offchain and easily exploitable
Centralized leaderboards with no economic consequence
One-time incentives like NFTs or tokens
Social tasks that can be farmed without verification

Games that do exist often rely on closed logic, custodial assets, or complex tokenomics that are hard to reason about and difficult to extend.

There is no standard way to build a trust-minimized, event-driven social economy where actions between users directly move value onchain.



4. How does Base Cartel improve this flow?

Base Cartel introduces a fully onchain, event-driven social economy where every meaningful action has economic consequences.

Key improvements:

Onchain-first logic: Raids, referrals, rewards, and penalties are enforced by smart contracts, not assumptions.
Conflict-based incentives: Value flows based on interaction (raiding, defending, betraying), not passive holding.
Transparent revenue flow: Fees generated by activity are visible, measurable, and claimable.
Reputation with purpose: REP is earned through verifiable actions and used to unlock gameplay advantages.
Composable with x402: Payments, agents, and automation can interact with the system using standard HTTP-native payment flows.

Instead of farming points, users are competing in a live, onchain power structure.



5. How does the final product flow work?

a. User joins the Cartel
A user connects their wallet and joins the game, receiving initial shares that represent their stake.

b. Activity generates value
Users perform actions like raids or high-stakes raids. These actions:

Transfer or burn shares
Generate protocol revenue
Emit onchain events

c. Revenue is distributed transparently
Fees collected from activity flow into a shared pot. Distribution logic determines how much each user can claim based on their shares and participation.

d. Social dynamics emerge

Referrals bring new users and rewards
Aggressive players rise on the "Most Wanted” list
Clans coordinate actions
Betrayal and defense change outcomes

e. Automation & agents
Using x402, agents can:

Pay to fetch intelligence
Trigger actions
Automate strategies
  All without custodial trust or centralized control.



Summary

Base Cartel turns onchain activity into a living social economy—where behavior, conflict, and coordination directly shape who earns, who loses, and who controls value. It’s not just a game or a payment system, but a framework for experimenting with incentive-driven social coordination onchain.

**Challenges we ran into**

I come from a non-technical background and I’m not a coder by training, so the biggest challenge was simply understanding how things actually work under the hood. In Web3, a lot of concepts sound simple on the surface, but once you start building, you realize how many moving parts there really are — smart contracts, indexers, APIs, frontend state, and how all of them interact.

To build this, I relied heavily on LLMs and AI agents as my primary way of learning and implementing features. That helped me move much faster, but it also introduced a different kind of challenge:
most of the time, the agent would try to solve problems based on assumptions instead of deeply understanding the existing codebase. This led to situations where things “worked” temporarily, broke something else, or had to be rewritten entirely.

Because of that, a lot of the development process became iterative and experimental — designing systems, testing them, breaking them, auditing them, and rebuilding them properly once the flaws were clear. Many core systems (joins, revenue, quests, reputation) went through multiple versions before they were stable.

The hardest part wasn’t writing code — it was learning how to think like a system designer without a traditional technical foundation, and validating every assumption manually. I got through it by slowing down, doing read-only audits first, breaking big problems into smaller ones, and being willing to throw away work when the architecture wasn’t right.

It was challenging, sometimes frustrating, but also the most valuable learning experience of the project.

[Kushagra Mohan](https://github.com/HeloworldPuni)

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aarika-24d4) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zMrDBjbWEwc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20Onchain%20with%20FBI-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://build-onchain-fbi.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Fiverr for ai agents

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Aarika removes the biggest friction in AI creation today: **manual, single-model workflows**.

Right now, creating with AI means repeating the same prompt across multiple platforms, switching tabs, comparing outputs by eye, and wasting time, tokens, and creative momentum. Discovery is broken. Users only see what ranks on search, not what actually produces the best results.

Aarika replaces this with a **single-prompt, multi-model workflow**.

---

## What People Use It For

- **Rapid creative exploration**  
  Generate images, videos, thumbnails, ads, or concept art from multiple AI platforms at once.

- **Side-by-side comparison**  
  Instantly see how different models interpret the same prompt, without re-prompting or tab hopping.

- **Merit-based discovery**  
  Find the best AI outputs based on quality and relevance, not SEO or platform popularity.

- **Fair marketplace for AI platforms**  
  New and niche AI models can compete on output quality by paying a small x402 fee, instead of fighting search algorithms.

---

## How It Makes Existing Workflows Better

- **Faster**: One prompt replaces dozens of manual retries.
- **Cheaper**: Users only pay to download the output they actually want.
- **Safer & Trustless**: Payments, participation, and rewards are handled via x402 on Avalanche.
- **More Open**: Breaks the monopoly of top AI tools and unlocks the long-tail of innovation.

Aarika turns AI creation from a slow, fragmented process into a **real-time competitive marketplace** where the best output wins.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

The biggest challenge was **integrating x402 end-to-end across agents, backend services, and the user flow**.

x402 is powerful, but it’s still very new. There isn’t a clear, battle-tested reference for how to wire payments between:
- AI agents submitting outputs  
- a backend coordinating rounds  
- and users triggering final purchases  

Getting all three to speak the same economic language took iteration.

---

## The Core Hurdles

- **Payment orchestration**  
  Ensuring that AI platforms could pay to participate, submit outputs, and later receive rewards — all without blocking the creative flow.

- **Agent coordination**  
  Agents needed to respond asynchronously, submit multiple outputs, and still be correctly mapped to a single prompt round.

- **Trust boundaries**  
  Making sure payments, downloads, and rewards happened atomically so no party could game the system.

---

## How I Solved It

- Broke the problem into **clear x402 checkpoints**:  
  *pay-to-compete → output submission → pay-to-download*.

- Centralized coordination in the backend, treating each prompt as a **deterministic round** with strict state transitions.

- Used x402 links as the single source of truth for value transfer, keeping agents stateless and simple.

This approach turned a messy, multi-actor flow into a **clean, auditable payment-driven pipeline**, and unlocked the core economic loop that makes Aarika work.
