### CrowdFund
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/crowdfund-e750) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/amitsudhir/crowdfund) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeMatrix:%20Genesis-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codematrix-genesis.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Blockchain Based Crowdfund Platform

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Crowdfunding today is largely based on trusting intermediaries and individuals, which creates several real-world problems:

Donors cannot be sure whether their money is securely held.

Campaign owners may withdraw funds even if goals are not fully achieved.

Refunds are often manual, delayed, or not guaranteed.

Fund handling happens off-chain, making misuse difficult to verify.

Users must trust platforms and organizers instead of enforceable rules.


This lack of transparency and automation discourages participation and reduces trust in crowdfunding systems.

How our project helps

Our project provides a blockchain-based crowdfunding platform that makes fundraising safer, more transparent, and automated.

People can use it to:

Create fundraising campaigns for medical aid, education, emergencies, or community causes.

Donate to campaigns with confidence, knowing funds are protected by smart contracts.

Track all donations, withdrawals, and refunds publicly on the blockchain.

Ensure funds are released only when predefined conditions are met.

What makes it easier and safer

Smart contract escrow
Funds are locked inside a smart contract, not held by the platform or campaign owner.

Automatic rule enforcement

If the funding goal is reached before the deadline → withdrawal is allowed.

If the goal is not reached → donors can claim refunds automatically.

On-chain transparency
All financial actions are publicly verifiable and immutable.

Proof of utilization (prototype)
Campaign owners upload utilization proofs stored on IPFS, allowing donors to see how funds were used.

In short, the platform replaces trust in people with trust in code, making crowdfunding more reliable and secure.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Understanding smart contract fund locking

One of the initial challenges was understanding how funds can be securely locked without relying on a central wallet.
I solved this by designing the smart contract to act as an automated escrow, where ETH is stored directly in the contract balance and can only be moved through predefined functions.


2. Ensuring safe withdrawals and refunds

Handling withdrawals and refunds safely was critical.
I had to ensure:

Only campaign owners could withdraw.

Withdrawals were allowed only after successful funding.

Refunds were available only when campaigns failed.


This was solved by carefully structuring require conditions and using a reentrancy guard to prevent common attack patterns.


3. Integrating IPFS for proof of utilization

Adding proof uploads introduced challenges around:

File handling in the frontend

IPFS uploads

Environment variables in deployment


Locally everything worked, but deployment failed because the IPFS API key was missing in the hosting environment.
I resolved this by correctly configuring environment variables in Vercel and improving error handling to catch such issues early.


4. Deployment and environment mismatches

Another hurdle was inconsistent behavior between localhost and the deployed version due to caching and environment configuration differences.
This was resolved by forcing clean redeployments and ensuring all environment variables were correctly set in production.


What I learned

Smart contracts require minimal and precise logic to remain secure.

Blockchain applications demand careful handling of deployment environments.

Building trustless systems means thinking defensively and anticipating edge cases.

These challenges helped me better understand real-world blockchain development beyond just writing code.

Team **Fund3** -- [Sudhir Pratap Singh](https://github.com/amitsudhir)

**The problem it solves**

This project focuses on real-time crypto price forecasting and automated decision support. It helps traders analyze fast-moving markets by combining live MT5 data, technical indicators, and an LSTM prediction model. The system provides instant insights that reduce human error and speed up decision-making.

Crypto markets are highly volatile and difficult to predict manually. This project solves the problem of delayed or inaccurate analysis by offering automated forecasting and instant signal generation. It enables traders to react quickly, avoid losses, and capture profitable opportunities.
-Eliminates manual chart analysis delays
-Reduces errors in technical indicator interpretation

**Challenges we ran into**

I faced major problems starting with the API integration and MT5 initialization errors, where getting stable 1-minute BTCUSD data required multiple retries, reinitializations, and handling empty or corrupted feeds. While building the LSTM model pipeline, I encountered issues like undesired analysis outputs, highly fluctuating predictions, scaling mismatches, and overall model instability. These errors, ranging from preprocessing mistakes to training-time exceptions, challenged both my debugging skills and my understanding of time-series modeling.

To resolve them, I systematically debugged the entire workflow by adding data validation checks, ensuring no missing values or NULL entered the model, and fixing the inverse-scaling logic. I refined the LSTM architecture, cleaned and normalized the features, and corrected the sequence-generation and prediction loop. Through steps like hyperparameter tuning, indicator recalculation, and noise reduction, I was able to eliminate erratic behavior and turn unstable results into a consistent and reliable forecasting.

Team **Triton** -- [Hiten Gupta](https://github.com/hitengupta44-oss)

### Zk-census
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zkcensus-9cca) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/suchit1010/Zk-Census) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://zcensus.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zteUdhL1UcE?si=y5lYsqqS4pbxflP-) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> solving network state census concept

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![SolanaSDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/SolanaSDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🌍 The Census Paradox
Every nation, community, and organization faces the same fundamental challenge: How do you count your population without compromising individual privacy?

Traditional census methods require collecting personal information — names, addresses, demographics. This creates a tension between two legitimate needs:

Organizations need accurate headcounts for resource allocation, legitimacy, and governance
Individuals deserve privacy and protection from surveillance or data breaches
ZK Census solves this paradox using Zero-Knowledge Proofs.

🎯 Real-World Use Cases
1. Network States & Digital Nations
Emerging digital communities need to prove their population to the world — for diplomatic recognition, resource allocation, or demonstrating growth — without doxxing their citizens.


2. DAO Governance & Quadratic Voting
DAOs struggle with Sybil attacks where one person creates multiple wallets to gain outsized voting power. ZK Census enables:

One-person-one-vote guarantees
Quorum verification without exposing voter identities
Anonymous participation in sensitive governance decisions

3. Privacy-Preserving Event Attendance
Conferences, rallies, or community gatherings can verify attendance numbers without tracking individuals:

Prove 10,000 people attended without a sign-in sheet
No surveillance, no data to breach, no tracking

4. Fair Airdrops & Token Distribution
Crypto projects lose millions to Sybil farmers. ZK Census enables:

Distribution to unique humans only
Passport-verified identity (via Zassport) without storing passport data
No personal information on-chain — just cryptographic proofs

5. Anonymous Surveys & Polls
Organizations can run surveys where:

Each member can respond exactly once
Responses are unlinkable to identities
Results are verifiable and tamper-proof

⚡ How It Makes Things Easier & Safer
Traditional Approach	ZK Census Approach
Collect names, addresses, IDs	Only 32-byte cryptographic commitments
Centralized database (breach risk)	Decentralized, nothing to breach
Trust the census taker	Trustless — math proves correctness
Expensive infrastructure	~$0.00015 per proof on Solana
Months to compile results	Real-time population counter
Identity tied to participation	Participation is anonymous

🔐 The Privacy Guarantee
When a citizen participates in ZK Census, they prove:

✅ "I am a registered member of this community"
✅ "I haven't been counted yet in this period"
✅ "Count me as present"
They never reveal:

❌ Who they are
❌ Where they're from
❌ Any personal information
The math guarantees privacy. Not policy. Not promises. Math.

🛂 Sybil Resistance with Zassport
For communities requiring real-world identity verification, ZK Census integrates with Zassport — a passport verification system using NFC scanning:

Scan passport → Verify identity off-chain
Only a derived attestation reaches the blockchain
One passport = One identity (no fake accounts)
Zero personal data stored anywhere

💡 Bottom Line
ZK Census lets any community answer the question "How many of us are there?" without ever asking "Who are you?"

It's infrastructure for the sovereign internet — where privacy and accountability coexist.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

🔴 Challenge 1: Solana's alt_bn128 Syscalls Not Production-Ready
The Problem:
Our original plan was to verify Groth16 ZK proofs directly on-chain using Solana's alt_bn128 precompiles (pairing, addition, multiplication). However, we discovered these syscalls are still experimental and not fully stable for production use.

How We Solved It:
We pivoted to an off-chain verification + on-chain attestation architecture:

Real Groth16 verification happens in our Verifier API using snarkjs
The verifier signs an Ed25519 attestation confirming proof validity
On-chain, we only verify the Ed25519 signature (which Solana handles natively)
This actually improved UX — verification dropped from ~200ms (on-chain) to ~15ms (off-chain), and we avoided compute unit limits.

🔴 Challenge 2: Merkle Root Synchronization
The Problem:
The on-chain Merkle root kept getting out of sync with our off-chain incremental Merkle tree. When users tried to prove membership, the root mismatch caused proof verification to fail.

The Root Cause:

Registration transactions were being indexed with delays
The indexer was building the tree, but the on-chain root wasn't being updated
Race conditions when multiple registrations happened quickly
How We Solved It:

Built an event-driven indexer that listens to CitizenRegistered events
Added an admin set_merkle_root instruction to sync the on-chain root
Implemented a /tree-info endpoint to check current state before proving
Added root validation in the frontend before generating proofs

🔴 Challenge 3: Browser-Side ZK Proof Generation
The Problem:
Initial proof generation in the browser was taking 8-12 seconds — way too slow for good UX. Users thought the app was frozen.

What We Tried:

Loading WASM synchronously → blocked the UI thread
Using Web Workers → helped but still slow
Reducing circuit constraints → broke the security model
The Fix:

Optimized the circuit to 5,341 constraints (minimum for Semaphore-style proofs)
Preloaded the .wasm and .zkey files on page load
Added clear loading states with progress indicators
Final result: ~800ms proof generation — fast enough for real-time use

🔴 Challenge 4: Nullifier Scope Management
The Problem:
Users who had already participated in a census period could still generate valid ZK proofs — the nullifier wasn't being checked correctly, allowing potential double-counting.

The Bug:
The nullifier hash was being computed without the externalNullifier (census scope), so all proofs had the same nullifier regardless of which census period they were for.

The Fix:
Updated the circuit to properly include externalNullifier in the nullifier hash:

Now each census scope generates unique nullifiers, and advancing the scope resets everyone's ability to participate.

🔴 Challenge 5: Zassport Integration Complexity
The Problem:
Integrating real passport verification (Zassport) without storing any personal data on-chain required careful architecture. The naive approach would leak identity information.

The Challenge:

Zassport creates a PDA with passport attestation data
We needed to link this to a ZK Census identity
But we couldn't store the link on-chain (privacy leak!)
The Solution:
We designed a privacy-preserving derivation:

The commitment goes on-chain (anonymous 32-byte hash)
The link to Zassport only exists in the derivation (off-chain)
Even if someone knows your wallet, they can't reverse the commitment


::
"The best architecture isn't the one you planned — it's the one that survives contact with reality."

We started with a pure on-chain ZK verification design. Reality (Solana's experimental syscalls) forced us to a hybrid approach — which actually turned out to be faster, cheaper, and more flexible.

**General Bounty**

How ZK Census Fits the Network School Track
ZK Census is core infrastructure for Network States — it solves the foundational problem every digital nation faces: proving population without compromising citizen privacy.

🏛️ Direct Alignment with Network State Vision
Balaji's Network State concept requires communities to demonstrate:

Collective action — people working together
Measurable population — provable citizen count
Real-world legitimacy — credibility with external observers
ZK Census enables all three:

Network State Need	ZK Census Solution
Prove population exists	On-chain verifiable headcount
Protect citizen identity	Zero-Knowledge proofs — count without doxxing
Prevent fake members	Zassport integration — one passport = one citizen
Scale globally	Solana-native, supports 1M+ citizens
Real-time census	Live population counter, not annual surveys
🎯 Why Network School Specifically?
Network School is building a real community of builders and citizens. ZK Census provides:

Membership verification — prove you're part of Network School without revealing who you are
Anonymous attendance — count participants at events/sessions privately
Governance infrastructure — one-person-one-vote for community decisions
Growth metrics — demonstrate community size to the world
🔐 The Technical Fit
Built specifically for the Network State ecosystem:

Solana-native — fast, cheap, scalable
Semaphore-style ZK — battle-tested privacy protocol adapted for census
Zassport integration — passport-based Sybil resistance using NFC verification
Open source — infrastructure the whole ecosystem can build on
💡 One-Line Summary
ZK Census lets Network States answer "How many citizens do we have?" to the world — without ever revealing who those citizens are.

### ZstarkWarp
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zstarkwarp-ab30) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/merkle-groot/ZstarkWarp) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://zstarkwarp.com) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> ZK bridge between Starknet and Ztarknet

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square) ![Garaga](https://img.shields.io/badge/Garaga-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZstarkSwap is a private bridge between Starknet and Ztarknet, built on a mix of game-theory and zero-knowledge security.

The underlying framework allows private token transfers between any chains without exposing users to typical bridge-hack risks. It works through a Tornado-Cash-style pool where users lock funds on one chain and then prove, using a ZK proof that they deposited, without linking their withdrawal to their deposit. Because withdrawals aren’t instant, a user could try to cheat by submitting an invalid Merkle root and a proof computed over that fake root.

This is where the solvers step in. They lock funds in the withdrawal contract and are responsible for checking that the Merkle roots being proven are correct. The protocol then optimistically sends funds that come from the solvers who approve the withdrawal. Solvers earn a small fee for every withdrawal they validate.

They also take on real risk: if a solver approves an invalid withdrawal, their stake can be slashed. The protocol stays safe as long as enough observers watch approvals and flag bad ones. There’s a cooldown period, during which a multisig or later a DAO can slash the solver if they misbehave.

**Challenges we ran into**

Writing tests for the circuits was brutal. One tiny mistake and the Merkle root from the test wouldn’t match the one in the contract. I just had to grind through it and make sure the circuit and the contract actually behaved the way they were supposed to.

And working with Garaga lib was not fun.

### Aidra

> A Programmable Wallet for Cross-Chain Transfers

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**What Aidra Is**

Aidra is a **bridge-only smart wallet** designed to make cross-chain transfers safe.  
Instead of allowing raw, unrestricted sending like a normal wallet, Aidra routes every outbound action through a **programmable security engine** made of modular, plug-and-play policies.

Users can enable or disable any of the 13+ policy modules, giving them full control over how their wallet is allowed to behave.  
This is the core value of the project: Aidra is a wallet that enforces the user’s intent before a bridge transfer can ever happen.

 Once a transfer passes all policy checks, Aidra uses NEAR Intents to actually execute the cross-chain swap, giving users a secure, reliable, programmable path from Zcash to all supported chains and assets.

---

## 🔧 **Programmable, Plug-and-Play Security Policies**

Aidra introduces **policy-restricted bridging**.  
Each policy is modular and can be toggled or configured independently. These include:

- Daily and per-transaction spending limits  
- Velocity and burst protection  
- Cooldown periods and allowed hours  
- Blackout days  
- Asset and recipient whitelists  
- High-value guardian approvals  
- New-recipient confirmation  
- Suspicious-pattern detection  

Every transfer must pass all active policies.  
If any rule fails, the wallet stops the bridge request — even if the signature is valid.  
This is something normal wallets and bridges simply cannot do.



---

 **1. Safer Cross-Chain Transfers by Default**

People use Aidra to bridge ZEC without exposing themselves to:

- malware  
- phishing prompts  
- malicious scripts  
- unapproved smart contract calls  
- accidental taps or clicks  

Because the wallet layer blocks anything that violates user policies, a unauthorized operation cannot move funds.

---

**2. Protection From Human Mistakes (Fat-Finger & Copy/Paste Errors)**

Aidra removes common failure modes:

- sending to the wrong chain  
- pasting the wrong recipient  
- extra zeros or decimal-place mistakes  
- sending more than intended  
- rapid misclicking  

The policy engine prevents these errors from becoming irreversible losses.

---

**3. Secure Bridging From Zcash Shielded Addresses**

When ZEC leaves the shielded pool, all traces are gone.  
Aidra enforces policies **before** funds exit, ensuring:

- no unwanted operations  
- no accidental loss  
- no unreviewed outbound transfers  

Shielded funds stay protected until the user’s exact conditions are met.

---

**4. Team, DAO, and Small-Organization Spending Controls**

Teams can use Aidra as a lightweight treasury wallet with:

- multi-sig approvals  
- time-restricted spending  
- limits specific to or scenarios  
- tamper-resistant policies  


---

**5. A Wallet Where Users Define the Rules**

Aidra makes bridging easier because users don’t have to think about safety each time.

They:

- Set their policies once  
- Deposit ZEC  
- Bridge safely, every time  

The wallet enforces the rules automatically.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Major Hurdle #1 — Running Shielded Wallets in the Browser**

I originally tried to build a fully self-custodial Zcash wallet directly in the web environment using zcash-devtools.  
But:

- The tools rely heavily on Rust and native bindings  
- I didn’t know Rust before the hackathon  
- Compiling and using them inside a browser environment was extremely difficult  
- This consumed a huge portion of my hackathon time

  **How I solved it**

I pivoted to using **Zingo CLI**, which has a much simpler interface and allowed me to spin up shielded wallets quickly.

The tradeoff was significant:

- I had to switch from **self-custodial (user holds keys)**  
  to  
  **custodial (backend manages keys)**
---

  **Major Hurdle #2 — Building a Modular Security Policy Engine**

Aidra’s core innovation is its 13-module programmable security system, but:

- policies had different data structures  
- some policies needed historical context  
- some required real-time locks and atomic reservations  
- concurrency issues led to race conditions  
- I had to prevent double-spending even under rapid requests

  **How I solved it**

I redesigned the system as a **plug-and-play policy pipeline** with:

- atomic DB transactions  
- “pending” state reservations  
- modular JSON schemas  
- consistent execution order  
- a unified evaluation framework

Some policies are still slightly buggy at the edges, but the core enforcement logic works reliably and is extendable.


---

**Major Hurdle #3 — Learning the Zcash Ecosystem on the Fly**

Zcash’s tooling, terminology, and shielded workflows were initially unfamiliar:

- lightwalletd  
- unified addresses  
- shielded vs transparent flows

  **How I solved it**

I spent a chunk of time reading docs, testing commands, and experimenting with real wallets.  
This slowed early progress but ultimately helped me build a correct and safe integration.

**Major Hurdle #4 — Couldn't Implement WebAuthn-Protected Policy Updates**

Another feature I planned but couldn’t implement in time was **WebAuthn-secured policy updates**.

Originally, my vision was:

- Users authenticate with WebAuthn to log in and  
- The same WebAuthn credential would be required to change any security policy  
  (limits, whitelists, guardian config, etc.)

This matters because without that second layer:

- Anyone with access to the device (friend, sibling, coworker)  
- Could modify a user’s policy settings  
- Which could weaken their security posture  
- Even if they cannot directly sign outbound transfers

 **Why it didn’t make the final build**

The limitation wasn’t technical difficulty, it was purely **time**.

Implementing:

- WebAuthn ceremony prompts for policy changes  
- backend verification flows  
- signed mutation logs  
- re-authentication middleware  

…would have required more time than I had left in the hackathon.

I chose to ship a stable core system rather than rush a critical security feature.


---

 **How I plan to fix it post-hackathon**

The post-hackathon version will include:

- **WebAuthn-signed policy updates**  
- **Separate “admin” passkey for policy management**  
- **Tamper-proof policy mutation logs**  
- **Optional guardian approval for policy changes**

This will harden the system so that policy changes are as secure as outbound transfers.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Secure cross-chain communication requires a secure origin. While protocols like Axelar secure the transport of assets, Aidra secures the intent to transport them.

Aidra is a Programmable Smart Wallet that creates a 'pre-flight check' for every bridge transaction. Our Modular Security Engine enforces strict policies, verifying destination chains, amounts, and recipient whitelists, before the bridge logic is triggered. We are the perfect complement to secure cross-chain infrastructure: you ensure the message arrives safely; we ensure the message should have been sent in the first place. We bring programmable, policy-based access control to the cross-chain world.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Osmosis is the gateway to the Interchain, and Aidra is the Smart Gate that makes entering that ecosystem safe for Zcash users. We built a wallet that enforces Programmable Security on every bridge transfer.

By integrating a Modular Policy Engine, we allow users to define exactly how their ZEC interacts with the Interchain. Whether it's enforcing a cooldown period on transfers to Osmosis or requiring Multi-Sig approval for large liquidity moves, Aidra validates the user's intent before funds leave the shielded pool. We are bringing Zcash liquidity to the Interchain with an embedded compliance and safety layer that raw wallets simply cannot provide.

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

Self-custody usually means 'you are on your own.' Aidra changes that by introducing Programmable Self-Custody. We are a wallet that doesn't just hold keys; it holds Policies.

Our innovation is a Plug-and-Play Security Engine that allows users to 'program' their safety. Instead of relying on a seed phrase alone, users can configure Aidra to block transfers to new addresses or cap daily spending. We enforce these intents before a transaction is signed, effectively protecting the user from malware, phishing, and their own mistakes. Aidra makes self-custody intelligent, granular, and forgiving.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Private payments fail when they lack controls. A corporate treasury cannot use a wallet that allows unlimited, anonymous spending. Aidra solves this by merging Zcash privacy with Programmable Access Control.

We built a wallet where every payment is subject to a Modular Security Policy. Users can define rules like 'Only allow payments to Whitelisted Addresses' or 'Alert on transactions over 50 ZEC.' Aidra strictly enforces this intent before the bridge transfer occurs, ensuring that private payments are also compliant and authorized. We are the infrastructure that makes Zcash viable for organized, high-volume commerce.

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

Unstoppable Wallet champions decentralized access; Aidra champions Decentralized Safety. We are applying the concept of 'Smart Contract Wallets' to the Zcash ecosystem.

Our project features a Programmable Security Engine that sits between the user and the network. By using Plug-and-Play Policies, like 'Burst Protection' or 'Guardian Recovery', we enforce the user's safety intent before a transfer can ever be executed.

**Privacy-Focused Content & Media**

Bitlux enables private cross-border payments; Aidra ensures those payments are authorized. We built a Programmable Smart Wallet that turns cross-border bridging into a managed workflow.

Our Modular Security Engine allows users to set strict parameters for their transfers—limiting amounts per day or restricting destination chains. Aidra enforces these constraints before the bridge transfer happens, ensuring that a remittance payment doesn't turn into a wallet drain. We make cross-border ZEC flows predictable, secure, and policy-compliant.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

You asked for a solution that connects Zcash to multiple chains using the NEAR Intents SDK. Aidra delivers this, but we go further: we built a Programmable Smart Wallet that treats every cross-chain intent as a policy-restricted action.

Existing bridges are vulnerable because they lack context,  they simply execute raw transactions. Aidra introduces a Programmable Security Engine that sits upstream of the NEAR 1Click aggregator. Before a Zcash user’s intent to bridge to Ethereum or Solana is ever broadcast, it must pass through our modular, plug-and-play security policies (like Velocity Limits or Whitelists). We use NEAR’s chain abstraction to make ZEC interoperable, and our Policy Engine to make that interoperability safe. We are the 'Smart Gate' for the NEAR-Zcash liquidity corridor.

We allow users to construct the baseline for 'Conditional Payment Intents' using our Modular Security Engine. Aidra enforces this intent before the transfer happens, by utilizing the "daily transaction limit security policy". Project Tachyon fuels Zcash innovation, and Aidra represents the evolution of the wallet from a passive storage tool into an Active Security Protocol. We recognized that the biggest barrier to Zcash adoption isn't just usability, it's safety.

Aidra is a Programmable Smart Wallet designed specifically for secure cross-chain transfers. We built a Plug-and-Play Security Engine where users can snap together rules—Multi-Sig Guardians, Blackout Dates, or Spending Limits—to create a bespoke security environment. Aidra ensures that Zcash remains the gold standard for privacy while becoming the gold standard for programmable safety.

This is the 'Shark Tank' pitch: Zcash is the best money, but it has the worst safety rails. If you get hacked, it's gone. Aidra fixes this by building the first Programmable Security Engine for Zcash.

**The problem it solves**

Traditional crypto trading is fragmented, manual, and emotionally driven. PawPad solves this by deploying autonomous AI trading agents that executes strategies such as Zcash buy-and-hold accumulation using predictions on a time series transformer and Solana DCA via dark-pool liquidity with zero user complexity.

The platform abstracts away wallet security risks by supporting both seed-based and seedless MPC wallets, giving users institution-grade protection while agents trade on their behalf. PawPad makes advanced, automated crypto accumulation accessible, safer, and fully hands-off.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into
1. Solana Rent-Exemption Errors
When implementing SOL → ZEC swaps, we hit transaction simulation failures. Solana requires accounts to maintain a minimum balance (~0.00089 SOL) for rent exemption. Our initial swap logic didn't account for this, causing transactions to fail when users tried to swap near their full balance. We solved this by reserving rent + fees before calculating the max swappable amount.
2. NEAR Intents — Slow Swaps & Lost Funds
NEAR Intents became our biggest time sink. Swaps that should take seconds sometimes took 2-4 hours to complete, killing productivity during development. Worse , we were testing on mainnet with real funds, and the refund routes weren't configured properly initially. When swaps failed or timed out, funds got stuck or lost entirely. Expensive lessons learned the hard way. Had to rebuild the fallback and refund logic from scratch.
3. NEAR Intents & Shielded ZEC Incompatibility
On top of timing issues, NEAR Intents only supports unshielded (transparent) ZEC addresses but our wallet is privacy-first. We needed shielded transactions. This meant integrating zingolib and other Zcash libraries to handle the transparent-to-shielded conversion post-swap. Lots of trial and error getting the shielding flow to work reliably after receiving funds from NEAR.
4. Solana Key Derivation & MPC Wallet Complexity
Setting up the seedless wallet was significantly harder than expected. Integrating Oasis TEE for secure key share storage, implementing FROST 2-of-2 threshold signing, and coordinating the distributed key generation all required deep cryptographic work. Getting both shares to cooperate for signing while ensuring neither could independently access funds took multiple iterations to get right.
5. Arcium MXE Threshold Signing — Dropped After Week-Long Effort
We spent over a week trying to build Arcium MXE-based threshold signing for wallet keys. The vision was powerful: private keys never reconstructed in one place, signature generation distributed across Arcium's MPC nodes, and AI agents that could execute trades without ever holding your key. You'd set policies — maybe agent + user + Arcium quorum all required for a valid signature. Safe autonomous execution with distributed trust. But the integration complexity was significant, documentation was sparse for our specific use case, and with hackathon time constraints, we had to make a hard call. We dropped Arcium for key management and fell back to our FROST + Oasis TEE approach. The Arcium dark pool integration for private order matching remained,  that worked. But the threshold signing service for wallet keys will have to wait for v2.
6. Philanthropy Foundation Registry Issues
We used paywithz.cash to source verified organizations accepting ZEC. But several listed foundations had quietly dropped ZEC support  their addresses were outdated or disabled. We had to manually verify each organization, remove defunct ones, and curate a working subset. The AI matching only works if the underlying registry is accurate.
7. Autonomous Trading Engine — Storage & Signing
Building the trading agent backend required solving persistent state management, secure signing without exposing keys, and reliable order execution. Storing agent configurations, position state, and trade history while keeping signing keys isolated was a recurring challenge. Every component touching keys needed careful security review.
8. Lit Protocol Dropped
We initially planned to use Lit Protocol for PKPs (Programmable Key Pairs) and threshold signing. But Lit requires LIT token for operations, adding token dependency and extra onboarding friction. The setup complexity wasn't justified for our use case. We dropped Lit in favor of our own FROST + Oasis TEE approach — simpler, no token requirement, fully self-contained.
9. Expo Compatibility with Native Crypto Modules
We initially planned to use Expo SDK for faster development, but it caused compatibility issues with native crypto modules specifically react-native-keychain for secure key storage and @solana/web3.js polyfills. We had to migrate to bare React Native to get full native module support.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

- Helius serves as the RPC infrastructure for all Solana operations in PawPad.
- Wallet Home uses the Helius DAS API to fetch SOL balance, SPL tokens, and NFTs in a single optimized call  no need to poll multiple endpoints.
- Send SOL uses Helius RPC with priority fee estimation to send transactions with optimal fees and confirm landing reliably.
- SOL → ZEC Swap uses Helius RPC and webhooks to send SOL to the NEAR Intents deposit address and track confirmation status in real-time.
- Agent Trades use Helius RPC and transaction parsing to execute orders, parse results, and update the dashboard with trade outcomes.
- Transaction History uses the Helius Enhanced TX API to return parsed, human-readable transaction data instead of raw blockchain output.
- In short, Helius is the Solana engine under the hood. Every time PawPad touches Solana  checking balances, sending transactions, executing trades , Helius makes it fast and reliable.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

- PawPad uses NEAR Intents to bridge Zcash into the multi-chain DeFi ecosystem while preserving privacy at every step.What We BuiltPrivate Cross-Chain Swaps
- ZEC holders can swap to SOL and back without leaving PawPad. NEAR Intents handles the cross-chain routing  user sends ZEC, receives SOL on Solana. The reverse works too. This unlocks Solana's entire DeFi ecosystem for Zcash users.Shielded On-Ramp & Off-Ramp
- NEAR Intents only supports transparent ZEC addresses. We solved this by integrating zingolib for automatic shielding. When ZEC arrives from a swap, PawPad immediately moves it to a shielded z-address. When sending ZEC out for a swap, funds are unshielded just-in-time. Users stay private by default , transparency is only momentary and internal.AI-Powered Private Donations
- The Philanthropy Agent lets ZEC holders donate to causes using natural language. If the user's funds are in SOL, the agent auto-converts via NEAR Intents to ZEC before sending a shielded donation. Foundations receive ZEC at their z-address  donor identity and amount stay private.Autonomous Trading with ZEC Liquidity
- Users can allocate ZEC to the trading agent. The agent swaps ZEC → SOL via NEAR Intents to trade on Solana DeFi (via Arcium dark pools for MEV protection), then converts profits back to shielded ZEC. ZEC becomes productive capital without sacrificing privacy.

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

- NEAR Intents powers all cross-chain swaps between Solana and Zcash. When a user wants to swap SOL for ZEC, the transaction routes through NEAR Intents as a bridge. The user's SOL is sent to a deposit address, NEAR Intents handles the cross-chain routing, and ZEC is delivered to the user's Zcash wallet.
- However, NEAR Intents only supports unshielded (transparent) ZEC addresses. Since PawPad is privacy-first, we can't stop there. After receiving ZEC at a transparent t-address, we use zingolib to shield the funds, moving them to a private z-address or unified u-address. This gives users the privacy they expect.
- The Philanthropy Agent also relies on NEAR Intents. When a user wants to donate but their funds are in SOL, the agent automatically converts SOL to ZEC via NEAR Intents before sending the shielded donation to the foundation's z-address. The user doesn't have to manually swap, the agent handles conversion seamlessly.
- During development, NEAR Intents caused significant pain. Swaps sometimes took 2-4 hours instead of seconds. Refund routes weren't configured properly at first, so when swaps failed, funds got stuck or lost on mainnet. We had to rebuild the fallback and refund logic from scratch after losing real funds to failed swaps.

**The problem it solves**

### **Zypherpunk Hackathon Progress**

We built a crucial upgrade for Openbands:  
**mobile verification for nationality and age**, which was previously not possible.  
You can read more about this in **Challenge 2** above.

### **Short Project Context**
We started building Openbands during Aztec’s NoirHack hackathon, where we won 1st place.  
We later joined the Self Protocol ZK Residency, where we implemented nationality and age verification.  
Most recently, we were selected as a finalist in Base Batches 002 and presented Openbands at Devconnect Buenos Aires.

---

### **What is Openbands?**

Openbands is a social space where you can speak freely **without exposing who you are**.  
A place where identity stays private, but authenticity is verified.

It enables:
- Citizens to voice honest opinions
- Employees to share real workplace insights
- Creators to build private communities
- All without fear of judgment or surveillance

Openbands brings **credibility back to anonymity** and **privacy back to online discussion**.

Think of it as **Reddit with authentic communities**:  
you can only join a group if you truly belong there.

For example:
- Only verified U.S. citizens can access the U.S. community
- Only verified employees can join their company’s community

This approach enables genuine, human interaction while minimizing **bots, fakes, and sybils**
  
We see this as an urgent need in a world increasingly dominated by AI-generated content.

---

### **Live Product**

Our MVP is live: **https://app.openbands.xyz**

Users can verify multiple real-world attributes:

- **Company affiliation** via work email (**zkJWT**)  
  → post anonymously inside your company community
- **Nationality & age** via passport (**Self Protocol**)  
  → join nationality or age-based communities

After verification, users can:
- Create and join communities with custom badge requirements
- Post anonymously
- Engage with verified members while staying private

We are early adopters of **zkEmail** and **Aztec’s zkJWT repo**, and our code is **open-source**.

---

## **Technical Context**

### **zkJWT (Company Verification)**

- ZK proof of a **JWT from Google** after signing in with a company email
- JWT fields: ``$headers`` ``$payload`` ``$signature`` Verified using Google’s public key
- Noir circuit verifies **RSA signature** and extracts **email domain**
- Only **domain** and **JWT public key** are public outputs
- Proof is generated **client-side**. Nothing leaves the user’s device

---

### **Self Protocol (Nationality & Age Verification)**

- Users scan passport in the Self mobile app
- On-chain verifications stored on **Celo**
- Mobile-first UX via **deeplinks** for smooth flow
- Desktop users scan QR with their phone

---

### **Communities**

- Permissionless creation with customizable **badge requirements**
- Supports **AND/OR** logic for multi-attribute membership
- Posts are always **anonymous**

---

## **Onchain Contracts**

**Base (Company Verification)**  
- Honk Verifier  
  → 0x8Cda51EBA880183C5F4174b553b1C7ea175c7a90

  → 0x0bC7F66F9b76eA37Ae37e3965E866bDeD8b2824C

- Age Registry  
  → 0x72f1619824bcD499F4a27E28Bf9F1aa913c2EF2a

## **Why This Matters**

When users remain private → trust collapses due to bots and misinformation.  
When platforms demand trust → privacy disappears through surveillance and data leaks.

AI makes this worse...

- Meta deletes **millions** of fake profiles every year  
- **16B+** credentials exposed in breaches in 2024  
- Malicious bots make up **37%** of the internet, and rising  

Authenticity online is breaking.  
**Openbands restores integrity without sacrificing privacy.**

---

## **Vision**

A world where:

> **Verifiability and privacy coexist** Not one at the cost of the other.

One trusted place with:
- Verifiable human presence
- No blind faith
- No surveillance
- No data exposure

**Challenges we ran into**

### **Challenge 1 (Open): Client-Side Proof Generation**

The current verification for nationality and age works via **Self Protocol**, which does not provide client-side proving yet. The proofs are currently generated in **trusted execution environments (TEEs)**, which still pose certain security risks and potential backdoors that could be exploited to retrieve users’ passport credentials.

This challenge is still unsolved. However, we are exploring possible solutions such as **zkPassport** (https://zkpassport.id/). Client-side proving is not yet very efficient—it takes a long time to generate proofs, which creates a poor user experience.

We are working closely with Self Protocol to develop a UX-friendly solution for client-side proving. This is essential to **Openbands**, as we want to ensure users remain anonymous and that their passport credentials are never exposed.

---

### **Challenge 2 (Solved): Mobile Verification Flow**

Verifying nationality and age via Self Protocol works seamlessly on desktop using a QR code scan. However, Openbands is a **consumer mobile-first app**. Mobile devices cannot scan a QR code from their own screen, so the verification process could not rely solely on this method.

To solve this, we implemented a verification button that allows users to verify their passport credentials directly on mobile without QR scanning. This challenge has been successfully resolved and was the main focus of this hackathon update.

---

### **How It Works (Simple Flow)**

1. **Start Verification**
   - User clicks **“Add New Badge”** → Selects **“Nationality”** or **“Age”** → Chooses **Self Protocol**

2. **Desktop Flow**
   - A QR code is displayed
   - User scans it with their phone
   - Verification happens in the Self app

3. **Mobile Flow (Challenge solved)**
   - A button appears: **“Open Self App to Verify”**
   - User taps the button
   - Device automatically opens the Self app

4. **In the Self App**
   - Already scanned passport: tap **“Approve”**
   - First-time verification: scan passport → tap **“Approve”**

5. **Blockchain Verification**
   - Self app sends verification to the blockchain (**Celo network**)
   - User is redirected back to the website
   - A “Checking verification...” screen polls the blockchain every 3 seconds
   - Once confirmed: **Success!** 🎉 Redirect to the badges page

6. **Result**
   - The newly verified badge appears in **“My Badges”**

**The problem it solves**

# Fheny – Confidential Web3 Wallet

Fheny is a Next.js 16-based web3 wallet application that supports confidential tokens (FHERC20) powered by Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE).

---

## Key Features

- **Wallet Management**
  - Create new wallets
  - Import existing wallets via private key

- **Confidential Token Support**
  - Native FHERC20 token support
  - Balances are stored encrypted on-chain

- **FHE Integration**
  - Uses cofhejs SDK for encryption/decryption of balances
  - Supports confidential (encrypted) transfers

- **Dual Token Support**
  - Manages both ERC20 and FHERC20 tokens

- **Privacy-Preserving Transfers**
  - Execute encrypted transfers where amounts remain hidden on-chain

---

## Architecture Highlights

### CofheProvider
- Initializes the FHE client per wallet  
- Manages permit creation and caching

### Permit System
- Generates and caches cryptographic permits required to decrypt balances

### Indicated Balance
- FHERC20 tokens expose a public “indicator” (0.0000–0.9999)
- Actual balances remain encrypted

### Balance Decryption
- Asynchronous decryption flow  
- Includes loading states and error handling

Team **Fheny** -- Arda Sari, Seyfi Susmaz

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem:
Crypto projects still struggle to pick the right KOLs. Finding them takes time, costs a lot, and most choices are based on hype. Current tools don’t track video platforms, even though most people in Web3 watch YouTube, TikTok, and Shorts.

Solution:
We analyze KOLs through their videos — what they talk about, who watches them, and how their content performs. This helps projects quickly find the influencers who actually match their audience and spend their budget the right way.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major issue was handling different user machines. Everyone had a slightly different setup, so running ZKKIT locally never worked the same way. Some users needed extra dependencies, some had missing libraries, and others had version conflicts. Because of that, onboarding new contributors and testers became slow.

Another challenge was the number of commands required to get the system running. There were too many steps, and people often got stuck midway because they missed one command or ran it in the wrong order.

To fix both problems, we built a documentation site. It detects the user’s OS and shows only the commands needed for their device. We also simplified setup flows and grouped commands into single scripts where possible. Now anyone can start the project with minimal friction.

**General Bounty**

This project fits the Network School track because it helps crypto teams connect with the right people. Today, KOL marketing in Web3 runs mostly on guesswork and private contacts. With ZKKIT, projects can discover the right influencers through real video-based data instead of relying on who they already know. It makes collaboration easier, faster, and more accessible for everyone in the ecosystem.

This is a privacy-first content series that educates and entertains through humor, relatable analogies, and real talk about why crypto privacy matters. The content spans tweets, short videos, and a long-form article all aimed at normalizing privacy as a fundamental right, not a suspicious choice.

**The problem it solves**

Most people never reach the useful side of crypto, not because they don’t need it.

"the everything-wallet"

Your money sits in a shielded Zcash wallet by default, you hold the keys. When you need proof of funds for rental deposit or a loan, you get a zk proof-of-funds without revealing any other details.

If you wish, you can link that proof to your identity with zkPassport, or maybe you want to prove you're over 18 and nothing else, we got you. Other times not being on the sanction-list is enough, np.

ZEC privacy is great and all, but people want to spend it, people want to find stuff to buy, people want to sell! Zbay facilitates a p2p marketplace for goods and services, with p2p chat between parties for fast negotiation. Other times you are on vacationing in 3rd world, Zbay will facilitate exchange from ZEC to local currency.

But how can you trust anon? What If I sell my homemade wine to a minor??
Again, the wallet will foster trust and verification leveraging the zkpassport integration. Prove you even have the money before I bother negotiating with you. Prove you are over 18 before I sell you this beer. Prove you are not on the sanctions list before I sell you this uranium! Prove you are a human before...

You do not upload documents. You do not send bank statements. The wallet speaks for you, in a very limited, controlled way, sharing only what you choose.

Trading between coins and moving value to other chains are handled the same way. There is a DEX for trading, and a cross-chain w/ NEAR-intents for swap swappin'.

ZKPF extends what ordinary people can do in crypto.

Our **mission** is to make useful crypto accessible to everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

Proofs to work reliably inside the browser across different devices and browsers.

Solved it by routing each device to their correct path at runtime.

**General Bounty**

Our wallet-bound zkPassport identity can be used as a building block for zk-census: any community could ask wallets to submit zk membership proofs and get a headcount without revealing identities. And many other possibilities.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

ZKPF wallet facilitate privacy centric capitalism for normal people.
By giving them the tools to buy and sell goods and services to each other.

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

ZKPF Wallet extends what a self-custody wallet can do within the privacy realm, giving users tools they need, without adding complexity! :)

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Proof-of-funds is a staple of our tradfi system: “show me you can really pay”. We allow this without exposing your whole wallet. That unlocks a lot in trading and DeFi.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Our wallet is a privacy multi-tool: it generates proof of funds, proof of ID (zkPassport), routes cross-chain actions (with the help of NEAR), and exposes only minimal, necessary information to the outside world.

**General Bounty**

ZKPF begun as a Tachyon-inspired web wallet.

Proof-of-funds, wallet-bound identity, and a prototype for proof-carrying wallet state and oblivious synchronization, so the wallet does more of the heavy lifting while keeping Zcash’s ledger indistinguishability and user privacy intact.

### TrendZap
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trendzap-aeb9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Ayomisco/trendzap-zypherpunk) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.trendzap.xyz/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Predict the viral future of any social content in

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Social virality is fast, opaque, and fleeting. Creators, traders, and culture watchers lack a structured way to express conviction about short-term performance ("Will this TikTok break 1M views in 24h?").

**TrendZap solves this by:**

### 1. **Converting Social Uncertainty into Tradable Markets**

- Transforms real-time social metrics (views, likes, retweets) into time-bound, on-chain prediction markets
- Allows anyone to express conviction on content performance: "Will this tweet reach 10K likes in 6 hours?"
- Creates financial upside for early trend discovery and accurate predictions

### 2. **Cross-Chain Accessibility with Privacy Guarantees**

- Users can bet from **any blockchain** (Solana, Arbitrum, or other EVM chains) using a unified interface
- **NEAR Intents SDK** orchestrates cross-chain transactions seamlessly
- **Zcash privacy pools** protect whale positions and prevent frontrunning
- **Helius enhanced RPC** provides sub-second Solana transaction confirmation

### 3. **Transparent, On-Chain Liquidity & Fair Odds**

- Pooled liquidity mechanism (Over vs Under) with transparent odds calculation
- No centralized bookmaker - odds determined purely by market participation
- Instant settlement via automated oracle monitoring social APIs
- All positions, payouts, and outcomes verifiable on-chain

### 4. **Rewarding Predictive Accuracy**

Early adopters get better odds before markets saturate

* Successful predictors earn yield proportional to their conviction and timing

Gamifies content discovery - spot viral trends before they peak

### 5. **Making Social Trading Safer & More Efficient**

- **Automated resolution** via decentralized oracle (no human disputes)
- **Cross-chain settlement** reduces gas fees (bet on Solana, settle on Arbitrum)
- **Privacy-first design** prevents position frontrunning and manipulation
- **Time-bound markets** eliminate indefinite capital lockup

**Challenges we ran into**

. **Cross-Chain Message Orchestration**

**Challenge:** Coordinating bets from Solana (fast, cheap) with EVM settlement on Arbitrum while maintaining atomicity.

**Solution:**

- Implemented **NEAR Intents SDK** as the orchestration layer
- Created stateless relayer service that listens to Solana program events via Helius WebSockets
- Used **Axelar GMP** for trustless EVM cross-chain messaging
- Added fallback mechanisms: if Axelar bridge fails, bets remain locked in source chain until manual recovery

**Technical Details:**

```typescript
// Relayer bridges Solana bet → Arbitrum orchestrator
const intent = await nearIntents.createIntent({
  source: 'solana',
  target: 'arbitrum',
  action: 'place_bet',
  payload: { marketId, amount, outcome }
});
```

### 2. **Oracle Reliability vs Decentralization Tradeoff**

**Challenge:** Twitter API rate limits (300 requests/15min) + need for real-time monitoring of viral content metrics.

**Solution:**

- Built cron-based oracle with exponential backoff and request pooling
- Implemented **multi-source verification**: cross-checks Twitter API with Helius on-chain events
- Added community dispute mechanism (fallback): if oracle fails, users can submit proof via IPFS
- For MVP: Allow mock data toggle (`TWITTER_API_MOCK=true`) to test system without hitting rate limits

**Key Insight:** Prioritized "good enough" decentralization over perfect decentralization for hackathon MVP

### 3. **Zcash Privacy Integration Complexity**

**Challenge:** Full Zcash testnet node sync takes 2-3 hours, blocking development velocity.

**Solution:**

- Implemented **privacy layer simulation** for MVP demo
- Created mock Zcash shielded pool that demonstrates privacy guarantees conceptually

**The problem it solves**

The project, **AetherPay**, solves the critical and highly sensitive problem of **privacy breaches and stigma associated with payments for mental health services.**

It addresses the fundamental dilemma: how to conduct a financial transaction that proves a patient is eligible (e.g., of age) and has paid, while ensuring no one (not the chain, not the public, not third parties) can link the payment back to the patient's identity or their use of therapy services.

---

## 🫂 What People Can Use It For

The system is primarily used by **patients** and **mental health therapists** to complete payment for services with unprecedented privacy guarantees.

### 1. For Patients (Enhanced Security & Trust)

| Feature | The Problem It Solves | How It Makes the Task Safer/Easier |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Anonymous Payments** | Current payment methods (credit cards, P2P apps like Venmo/Cash App, or bank transfers) leave a **permanent, traceable financial record** that links a person to a therapy provider. This record can be exposed in breaches or sold to data brokers, leading to potential stigma, discrimination (e.g., from employers, insurance), or targeted advertising. | The patient's identity is **never revealed on-chain**. They deposit funds using a one-time cryptographic **commitment**, which is an opaque hash, ensuring their mental health journey remains completely private. |
| **Age Verification (18+)** | Providers need to verify a patient meets the legal age requirement for certain services, but traditional ID checks require collecting and storing sensitive documents (driver's license, passport). | The system uses **ZkPassport** to prove the patient is $\text{18+}$ *without* revealing their name, exact birthdate, or ID document. It's a "yes/no" answer, not a data transfer. 


### 2. For Therapists (Compliance & Simple Claims)

| Feature | The Problem It Solves | How It Makes the Task Safer/Easier |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Secure Withdrawal** | Traditional payment systems can suffer from chargebacks or complicated reconciliation processes. | The therapist receives a **private secret code** (off-chain) from the patient. Using this code, they generate a zero-knowledge proof to claim the funds. This process is secure and guarantees the funds are available. |
| **Double-Spend Protection** | A payment commitment could potentially be claimed multiple times if not tracked carefully. | The use of a cryptographic **nullifier** ensures that once a claim is made and verified, the associated payment can **never be claimed again** by anyone, preventing fraud and protecting the therapist's earnings. |
| **Regulatory Risk Reduction** | Therapists must comply with stringent data protection laws (like HIPAA or GDPR) regarding patient data. Using a system that **avoids collecting or storing PII** (Personally Identifiable Information) on-chain significantly reduces their regulatory risk and liability in case of a data breach. |

---

## 💡 How It Makes Tasks Easier/Safer

The project utilizes **Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)** to separate the act of *proving* a fact from the act of *revealing* the underlying data.

* **Safer:** It removes the **traceability** of sensitive healthcare payments, protecting patients from the negative consequences of having their mental health status exposed. By not collecting PII, it becomes *impossible* to leak or sell that information.
* **Easier:** It streamlines age and payment verification. A single ZK process (**Noir + Garaga**) confirms both eligibility (age) and payment validity (commitment + nullifier) in one go, replacing the need for document storage, manual age checks, and traceable financial data.

This creates a **Sanctuary Protocol** for finance, allowing patients to seek necessary mental healthcare with confidence that their decision will not be weaponized against them in the future.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges and How They Were Solved

### 1. ZKPassport Only Works with NFC Enabled IDs

This is a **limitation of the dependency** that impacts the user experience and testing accessibility.

* **The Hurdle:** The core identity verification step relies on **ZkPassport**, which requires users to have an NFC-enabled ID (like a modern passport or driver's license) to generate the initial zero-knowledge proof. This excludes users with older IDs and makes development/demo testing difficult for anyone without the required ID or hardware.
* **How I Mitigated It:** I explicitly addressed this in the project documentation:
    > Use the **"Skip (dev/demo)"** button to bypass verification for testing.

    * **Solution:** I implemented a **development/demo bypass feature** in the frontend (e.g., in `app/src/hooks/useZkPassport.ts`). This allows testers to test the entire complex payment flow (commitment generation, nullifier hashing, proof creation, and contract withdrawal) without needing a physical, NFC-enabled ID, making the project viable for demonstration and local development.

### 2. Sepolia was Upgraded Earlier Today, Forcing a Class Hash Mismatch

This is a common **deployment-related hurdle** when working with rapidly evolving Layer 2 solutions like Starknet.

* **The Hurdle:** Starknet (running on the Sepolia testnet) was upgraded. This change means the underlying **Cairo compiler or runtime environment changed**, which invalidates the previously calculated `class_hash` for your deployed contracts (`verifier` and `payment`). When you try to interact with the old deployed contracts, the network throws a mismatch error.
* **How I Solved It:** I documented the standard operational fix for this issue:
    > If I modified contracts, update the class hashes in `Makefile` after `declare-*` commands.

    * **Solution:** When a breaking change or upgrade occurs, I have to **re-declare and re-deploy** the contracts. Specifically, after running `make declare-verifier` and `make declare-payment`, you had to manually **update the new class hashes** generated in the project's configuration (in the `Makefile` and tools file `.tool-versions` to use rc dev tools) to point to the freshly declared code. This ensures the subsequent deployment or interaction calls use the correct, current class hash.

### 3. Using the Nullifiers to Protect State

This is a **cryptographic and contract logic challenge** inherent in building ZK-based anonymous systems.

* **The Hurdle:** In a zero-knowledge payment system, the patient's identity is hidden. To prevent a patient from claiming the same deposited funds twice (a "double spend"), a **nullifier** must be used. The challenge is ensuring the **`nullifier` is calculated correctly** within the ZK circuit (in **Noir**), and then **efficiently tracked and secured** within the payment contract (**Cairo/Starknet state**) to guarantee it's unique.
* **How I Solved It:** I relied on the **integrity of the ZK system and contract logic**:
    * **Noir Circuit Logic:** I ensured the `nullifier` is generated by hashing the **secret** and a unique **salt** (`nullifier = hash(secret, salt)`). Since the `secret` and `salt` are unique to the transaction, the `nullifier` derived from them is also unique.
    * **Contract Logic:** The `therapy_payment.cairo` contract has logic to **store and check all used nullifiers** before releasing funds. This ensures that the first time a valid proof (which contains the `nullifier`) is submitted, the funds are released and the `nullifier` is marked as spent, making subsequent attempts fail. This protects the contract state from double-spending.

**General Bounty**

The Private Therapy Payments project fits perfectly under the **Network School** focus area—specifically **"zk-Passport"** and **"Privacy-preserving cryptoidentity solutions"**—*because* it uses **ZkPassport** to solve a highly sensitive, real-world privacy problem.

Here is a breakdown of how the app directly addresses the Network School's objectives:

---

## 🔑 How the Project Utilizes ZkPassport for Cryptoidentity

The project is an innovative, working demonstration of how **ZkPassport** moves identity from a centralized, data-leaking liability to a decentralized, privacy-preserving asset.

### 1. **Focus Area: zk-Passport**

The project makes **ZkPassport** a core, non-optional component of the payment flow, demonstrating a high-value application beyond simple login.

* **Problem Solved by ZkPassport:** In a sensitive context like mental health, the simple act of proving eligibility (age 18+) should not expose a patient's full identity data.
* **Application:** The patient uses **ZkPassport** to prove only one necessary attribute: **Age 18+**. This proof is generated entirely on the patient's device using their government-issued ID, and the full PII (name, exact birth date, ID number) is never revealed to the payment contract, the therapist, or the public blockchain.
* **Why it Fits:** It shows how to use the **ZkPassport SDK** to issue a zero-knowledge credential for a specific, regulatory-driven requirement (**age verification**) in a way that respects user privacy completely. 

---

### 2. **Focus Area: Privacy-Preserving Cryptoidentity Solutions**

The entire system is a robust **privacy-preserving solution** because the identity proofs and the financial transaction proofs are decoupled and hidden by ZKPs.

| Component | Privacy Function | Cryptoidentity Element |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ZkPassport Proof** | Proves the **patient is eligible (18+)** without revealing *who* the patient is. | Establishes a **privacy-first, age-verified digital identity** for a session. |
| **Commitment** | Hides the patient's identity and specific payment details in an opaque hash (`commitment = hash(secret, therapist_id, amount, salt)`). | The patient's **cryptographic secret** acts as the temporary, anonymous identity for the transaction. |
| **Nullifier** | Ensures the anonymous patient can only claim the commitment once. | Provides **proof of uniqueness** (anti-double-spend) without linking the transaction to a public wallet address. |

**Conclusion for Network School:**

By combining **ZkPassport** for attribute-based identity verification with **Noir/Garaga/Starknet** for anonymous payment settlement, the project delivers a comprehensive, end-to-end **privacy-preserving cryptoidentity solution** that is immediately applicable to the high-stakes sector of healthcare finance. It moves beyond theoretical exploration into a deployable product that protects sensitive user data.

The video below explains how ZKPs can be used for secure and private identity verification. [ZKpassport: Private Unforgeable Identity | Devcon SEA - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W6C-duDEiOU)

The core function of the project is creating a private payment system for a specific service (therapy). It builds a confidential transaction layer (using commitments and nullifiers) to send and receive value privately between two parties. This is a direct match for this track's goal of building private payment solutions.

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement — Digital Service Billing

Modern digital service platforms face several critical challenges:

Rigid Payment Models

Most platforms require upfront payments or fixed subscriptions, regardless of how much a user actually consumes.

This creates wasted funds for users and friction for service adoption.

Lack of Granular Usage Control

Users cannot pay for the exact services or features they use, leading to inflexible billing.

Vendors cannot offer micro-usage options without building complex systems themselves.

Limited Privacy

Traditional payment systems expose user spending patterns, which can be sensitive.

Users have little control over their transaction data.

Complex Backend Integration

Service providers struggle to integrate live streaming, session tracking, and payments in a unified system.

Real-time billing, crypto wallets, and analytics are usually fragmented across multiple systems.

High Entry Barrier for Small Vendors

Smaller service providers cannot afford to implement secure, scalable billing systems.

They lose potential revenue or are forced to rely on large platforms with limited control.

Lack of Real-Time Transparency

Users cannot see live session costs as they accrue.

Vendors cannot track earnings in real-time, making revenue monitoring difficult.

How PayGo Solves These Problems

Implements real-time micro-billing, charging users per minute or action.

Provides automatic Zcash wallet creation for privacy-first transactions.

Integrates live streaming and session management seamlessly with payments.

Offers transparent analytics for users, vendors, and the platform.

Simplifies the architecture so small vendors can onboard without heavy infrastructure.

Bridges Web2 convenience with Web3 security, providing a unified, privacy-conscious ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1. Integrating Real-Time Micro-Billing

Problem: Calculating per-minute/second charges in live sessions while ensuring consistency between the frontend, backend, and blockchain was tricky.
Solution: I implemented a centralized billing engine in the backend with live socket updates to the frontend, and verified transactions using the Zcash blockchain via NOWNodes API.

2. Wallet Creation & Blockchain Integration

Problem: Automatically generating and managing Zcash wallets for users at signup required secure key handling and real-time verification.
Solution: I used server-side wallet creation with encrypted storage of private keys, and connected to NOWNodes API for balance and transaction verification, ensuring security and privacy.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

PayGo enables private, real-time payments and micro-billing for digital services. By integrating shielded Zcash transactions, multi-chain wallet support, and encrypted key management, it provides a privacy-first transaction system that protects user financial data while enabling seamless service payments.”

**The problem it solves**

### The Zcash Developer Experience Gap

Zcash has a critical developer experience problem: **setting up shielded transaction support is exponentially more difficult than it should be**. While Ethereum developers enjoy mature toolkits like Hardhat, Foundry, and Remix that enable rapid development and debugging, Zcash developers face:

1. **Complex Setup Barriers**
   - Manual node configuration requiring deep protocol knowledge
   - Hours spent wrestling with zcashd/Zebra configuration files
   - No standardized local development environment
   - Fragmented tooling across multiple repositories

2. **Opaque Debugging Experience**
   - Zero-knowledge proofs are black boxes - when transactions fail, developers get cryptic error messages with no visibility into *why*
   - No visual tools to understand shielded transaction structure
   - Difficult to validate if nullifiers, note commitments, or viewing keys are correctly generated
   - Impossible to quickly inspect what's happening inside encrypted notes

3. **Slow Iteration Cycles**
   - Testing requires full node synchronization
   - No deterministic testing environment for edge cases
   - Chain reorganizations and specific scenarios are hard to reproduce
   - Each test cycle takes minutes to hours instead of seconds

4. **Steep Learning Curve**
   - Developers must understand advanced cryptography (nullifiers, Merkle trees, commitment schemes) before building anything
   - No interactive tools to learn by experimentation
   - Documentation assumes expert-level knowledge
   - Newcomers struggle to identify "what building blocks to grab to achieve their goals"

### How Zev Toolkit Solves This

Zev Toolkit is a **comprehensive, visual developer toolkit** that makes Zcash development as accessible as Ethereum development by providing:

#### 🚀 One-Command Local Development Environment
```bash
zev init  # Complete Zcash testnet running in <5 minutes
```
- Automated Docker orchestration of Zebra/zcashd + lightwalletd
- Pre-funded test accounts (transparent and shielded)
- Fast block generation for rapid testing
- Zero manual configuration required

#### 🔍 Visual Transaction Inspector (Web UI)
- **Paste any transaction hex or hash** → See complete breakdown with human-readable labels
- **Visual diagrams** showing flow between transparent and shielded pools
- **Expandable sections** for:
  - Transparent inputs/outputs with address decoding
  - Sapling spends (nullifiers, anchors, proofs)
  - Sapling outputs (note commitments, encrypted ciphertexts)
  - Orchard actions (for v5 transactions)
  - Zero-knowledge proof metadata
  - Memo fields (automatically decoded)
- **Viewing key tester** - Test if a viewing key can decrypt transaction notes
- **Transaction diff mode** - Compare working vs. failing transactions side-by-side

#### 🛠️ Interactive CLI Transaction Builder
```bash
zev tx create  # Guided prompts for building shielded transactions
zev tx simulate  # Test without broadcasting
zev tx decode <txid>  # Inspect any transaction
```
- Step-by-step transaction construction with validation at each step
- Support for transparent → shielded, shielded → shielded, and shielded → transparent flows
- Memo field helpers with encoding validation
- Fee estimation before broadcast
- Save/load transaction templates for common patterns

#### 🧪 Deterministic Testing Harness
```bash

zev test mine 10  # Mine exactly 10 blocks
zev test snapshot  # Save blockchain state
```
- Integration with darksidewalletd for reproducible testing
