> where learning meets demand (note: run local host)

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Universities often face a difficult challenge: by the time a curriculum is formally updated, industry requirements may have already changed. New technologies, tools, and skills emerge rapidly, while curriculum revisions typically happen only once every few years. As a result, students can graduate with knowledge that is academically sound but not fully aligned with current industry expectations.

Curriculum.ai helps institutions bridge this gap. The platform analyzes syllabi using AI, compares them against current industry trends and in-demand skills, and generates a detailed curriculum audit report highlighting strengths, gaps, outdated topics, and improvement opportunities.

However, identifying gaps is only half the solution. Universities also need access to the right people and organizations to address those gaps. That's why we built an integrated marketplace where institutions can discover subject outsourcing providers, industry experts, guest speakers, workshop trainers, placement mentors, and academic partners.

By combining curriculum intelligence with access to real-world expertise, Curriculum.ai helps universities make more informed curriculum decisions and create learning experiences that better prepare students for the workforce.

**Challenges we ran into**

One significant hurdle was ensuring that the curriculum analysis generated recommendations that were both accurate and actionable. Early versions of the system often produced overly generic suggestions because syllabus documents vary widely in structure, terminology, and level of detail. We addressed this by refining our analysis pipeline, improving prompt design, and structuring the evaluation process around industry-relevant skills, emerging technologies, and curriculum outcomes rather than relying on simple keyword matching.

Another challenge emerged when implementing report sharing. While the platform successfully generated downloadable PDF reports, the sharing functionality initially distributed localhost links or text-based summaries instead of the actual generated report. We resolved this by redesigning the sharing workflow to use the generated PDF as the primary artifact, ensuring that reports could be distributed in a format suitable for faculty and institutional stakeholders.

On the product side, we realized that identifying curriculum gaps alone was not enough. Universities also need practical ways to address those gaps. This led us to expand the platform beyond curriculum analysis and develop dedicated marketplaces for subject outsourcing providers, guest speakers, workshop instructors, industry experts, and placement mentors, transforming the project from a reporting tool into a complete curriculum modernization ecosystem.

These challenges pushed us to iterate rapidly, improve the reliability of our AI outputs, and focus on solving the broader institutional problem rather than just generating insights.

**Open Innovation**

Universities often struggle to keep their curricula updated as industry requirements evolve much faster than academic revision cycles. Our project tackles this problem by using AI to analyze syllabi, identify outdated or missing industry-relevant skills, and generate easy-to-understand curriculum audit reports. But we didn't want to stop at just identifying problems. That's why we also built a marketplace that helps institutions connect with subject providers, industry experts, guest speakers, workshop trainers, and career mentors who can help address those gaps. By combining AI-driven insights with real-world academic and industry collaboration, Curriculum.ai helps universities make more informed decisions and better prepare students for today's workforce.

### FinKlar
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finklar-9159) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Arshpreet-18/zero-bugs-given-) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Financial clarity that never leaves your phone.

![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Material Design](https://img.shields.io/badge/Material%20Design-333333?style=flat-square) ![Room Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Room%20Database-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem : 
India runs on irregular income. Gig workers, delivery riders, freelancers, daily-wagers, students they earn in uneven, unpredictable amounts, often in cash. Nearly half of the country's working-age adults are invisible to formal credit. Yet almost every finance app is built for one person: the salaried professional with a steady paycheck and a clean credit score.

If your income doesn't fit that mold, the system shuts you out. Apps like CRED and Jupiter put you on a waitlist or reject you outright the moment your earnings look "volatile." The people who most need to see their money clearly, to know what's safe to spend and avoid a missed payment, are left with nothing but a banking SMS inbox and mental math.
And this isn't a niche. India's gig workforce alone is projected to reach ~23 million by 2030 (NITI Aayog), the vast majority invisible to formal finance.

What FinKlar does : 

FinKlar is the money app built for volatile income not against it. No bank login, no waitlist, no credit score gate :

- Tracks every kind of income -  salary, gig payouts, and cash by reading bank SMS locally, by voice, or by quick manual entry, so the cash economy finally gets counted.
- Makes volatile income legible - shows what's actually safe to save today and flags lean days ahead, instead of assuming a fixed monthly salary.
-  Builds a financial identity -  from real cash-flow behavior explainable, and yours that traditional credit scores never capture.
- Stays private and offline -  your data is encrypted on your device; nothing is uploaded or profiled.

For the half of India that fintech ignores, FinKlar turns messy, volatile income into clarity and into an identity that finally gets them seen.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.Parsing messy bank SMS offline :  Every bank formats its alerts differently, and the inbox is full of OTPs, loan offers, and promos. With no cloud NLP allowed, we built a multi-stage offline engine regex patterns to pull out amount/merchant/UPI/balance, plus an intent filter to discard non-transactions. It took many rounds of tuning against real messages before it parsed reliably and stopped logging spam as expenses.

2. Keeping the AI from inventing numbers :  A general LLM will confidently make up figures. To stop that, we built a local context builder that pulls only the relevant, anonymised totals from the encrypted DB into a structured block before each query ,so Gemini answers strictly from real data and never receives any PII or account details.

3. Catching duplicates without blocking real repeats : A receipt scanned twice, or an SMS for a spend already logged by voice, would double-count. We wrote a fuzzy matcher on amount + merchant similarity + a time-delta window to flag likely duplicates while still allowing genuine repeat purchases. Tuning those thresholds was the fiddly part.

**Open Innovation**

Open Innovation rewards original solutions to real, unsolved problems and the financial exclusion of India's volatile-income workforce is exactly that. Nearly half the country earns in irregular, cash-heavy ways that mainstream fintech simply isn't built for; apps like CRED waitlist or reject these users outright.

FinKlar tackles this from a genuinely different angle. Instead of demanding a bank login, a steady salary, or an existing credit score, it builds a financial identity from the income people actually earn gig payouts, cash, and salary captured through on-device SMS parsing, vernacular voice, and quick manual entry, then turned into clear "safe-to-save" guidance and an explainable cash-flow score. It's offline first and privacy-first by design, so it works on cheap phones, patchy networks, and tight balances.

That combination serving the half of India that formal finance ignores, with an offline, no-gatekeeping, vernacular-first approach is what makes it open innovation: not another feature bolted onto an existing app, but a new way in for people who never had one.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem PlateRelay Solves

## The Crisis

India wastes approximately **68.8 million tonnes** of food every year, while over **190 million people** go hungry daily. The tragic irony is that restaurants, hotels, caterers, and event venues routinely discard massive volumes of perfectly edible surplus food --- not because they want to, but because there is no reliable, time-sensitive infrastructure to redirect it.

On the other side, night shelters, orphanages, and community kitchens operate on razor-thin budgets and unpredictable food supply chains. They have no visibility into when or where surplus food becomes available, and no mechanism to claim it before it spoils.

**The gap is not generosity. It is logistics.**

## What PlateRelay Does

PlateRelay is a real-time food rescue platform that bridges the last-mile gap between surplus food and the people who need it most.

### For Food Donors (Restaurants, Hotels, Caterers)
- **Post a Relay in under 60 seconds.** Specify the food type, estimated serving count, pickup window, and dietary tags. Attach a photo for transparency.
- **Geospatial matching.** The platform automatically identifies verified shelters and NGOs within a configurable radius, ranked by proximity, and notifies them via email.
- **Structured pickup windows.** Donors define a strict time range (e.g., 2:00 PM -- 4:00 PM), ensuring food is collected while it is still safe to consume.
- **Impact tracking.** Every completed relay is logged. Donors accumulate verifiable statistics --- total meals donated, CO2 emissions offset, active streaks --- building a public track record of social responsibility.

### For Recipients (Shelters, NGOs, Community Kitchens)
- **Live relay feed.** Browse active food donations nearby on an interactive map, filtered by distance, food type, and availability.
- **One-tap claiming.** Claim a relay instantly. The donor is notified via email, and a status pipeline (Active, Claimed, Picked Up, Completed) keeps both parties synchronized.
- **Photo verification.** Upload photos of food received and distributed, creating an auditable chain of accountability.
- **Subscription tiers.** Free-tier users receive up to 3 claims per month. Premium plans unlock unlimited claims and priority email alerts for high-demand relays.

### For the Broader Ecosystem
- **Email-driven communication.** All critical notifications --- relay alerts, claim confirmations, pickup reminders, and status updates --- are delivered via transactional email through Resend, ensuring reliability without requiring users to keep the app open.
- **Gamified engagement.** Donors earn milestone badges (First Relay, Century Club, Food Hero) and compete on a public leaderboard, turning food rescue into a visible, rewarding activity.
- **Payment integration.** Razorpay-powered subscription management allows shelters to upgrade their plans seamlessly, with webhook-driven billing that handles renewals, cancellations, and plan changes automatically.

## How It Makes Existing Processes Better

| Without PlateRelay | With PlateRelay |
|---|---|
| Donors call shelters manually, one at a time | Geospatial broadcast emails all nearby shelters simultaneously |
| No way to verify if food was actually delivered | Photo uploads and status tracking create a verifiable audit trail |
| Shelters have no visibility into available food | Real-time interactive map with live relay markers and filters |
| Pickup coordination happens over fragmented phone calls | Structured pickup windows with email-driven status updates |
| No data on food waste reduction impact | Automated impact dashboards tracking meals rescued, CO2 saved, and community reach |
| Trust is informal and unverifiable | Badge system, leaderboards, and public donor profiles build institutional trust |

## The Core Thesis

Food rescue is a **time-critical logistics problem**, not a charity problem. A plate of biryani prepared at a hotel banquet has a window of 2--4 hours before it becomes unsafe to consume. PlateRelay is engineered around that constraint --- every feature, from geospatial matching to strict pickup windows to real-time status pipelines, exists to compress the time between "we have surplus" and "someone is eating it" to the absolute minimum.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

Building PlateRelay under hackathon constraints surfaced challenges spanning frontend rendering, deployment, and data integrity.

---

### 1. Tailwind CSS Layering and Overlap Bug

The Landing Page had severe layout breaks where text boxes overlapped and content failed to center. The Pricing cards had conflicting transform classes (`md:-translate-y-4`) and mismatched flex alignments (`items-stretch` vs. `items-start`), while the Stats section lacked vertical padding, causing it to collide into the section below. We stripped the rogue transforms, unified card heights with `h-full`, and applied consistent section padding to restore the layout.

---

### 2. Scroll Lag from LiquidGlassCard Component

Integrating the `LiquidGlassCard` glassmorphism component across multiple pages caused severe scroll lag. The component's Framer Motion animations and backdrop-filter effects, applied across dozens of DOM elements simultaneously, overwhelmed the browser's rendering pipeline. We optimized by reducing animation complexity on non-interactive cards and disabling drag functionality where unnecessary, restoring smooth 60fps scrolling.

---

### 3. Deployment Environment Variable Failures

Moving to production Vercel broke both API routing and database connections. The frontend's `VITE_BASE_URL` pointed to `localhost`, and our Supabase auth layer used the newer `sb_publishable` key format, which was incompatible with our backend. We set `VITE_BASE_URL=/` for relative endpoint resolution and rolled back to classic Supabase API keys --- both fixes required only environment variable changes, zero code modifications.

---

### 4. Geospatial Map Rendering Bugs

The map feature failed in three ways sequentially: relay locations saved as `null` (frontend payload didn't match MongoDB's strict GeoJSON `[lng, lat]` format), the map always rendered Bengaluru (hardcoded fallback coordinates overrode actual input), and custom markers disappeared (Vite couldn't resolve local SVG paths at build time). We fixed each by restructuring the GeoJSON payload, replacing the hardcoded fallback with a proper conditional chain, and switching to dynamic React component imports for marker icons.

---

### 5. Silent API Failure

The dashboard silently stopped loading data --- no crash, no console errors, just empty state. Using the Network tab in DevTools, we traced it to the backend returning malformed JSON: the `_serialize_relay` function was failing to convert MongoDB `ObjectId` fields to strings. The frontend swallowed the parse error silently. We patched the serialization and added stricter frontend error boundaries.

---

### 6. Timezone Discrepancy in Pickup Windows

Donors scheduled pickups at one time, but recipients saw them shifted by hours. The backend stored naive `datetime` objects without timezone markers, so browsers applied inconsistent local offsets during parsing. We enforced strict ISO-8601 formatting with explicit UTC markers (`.isoformat() + "Z"`) in the serialization layer, forcing correct localization on the frontend.

---

### 7. Frozen Subscription Counter

After upgrading from free to premium, a shelter's `claims_this_month` counter stayed frozen at the free-tier limit of 3. The static integer field in the profile document was never reset on plan change. We eliminated the static counter entirely and refactored the profile endpoint to dynamically compute the count via `db.relays.count_documents()` on every request, permanently syncing the UI with database reality.

**MongoDB**

# How PlateRelay Fits the MongoDB Track

## MongoDB Atlas as the Foundation

PlateRelay is built entirely on **MongoDB Atlas** as its single source of truth. Every core entity --- users, relays, subscriptions, and impact metrics --- is stored, queried, and aggregated through MongoDB. We chose it because the problem domain demands geospatial queries at its core, flexible schema evolution under hackathon time pressure, and document models that map naturally to our API payloads.

---

## Geospatial Indexing: The Core of Relay Matching

The central feature --- matching surplus food to nearby shelters --- is powered by MongoDB's native **GeoJSON support and 2dsphere indexes**. Every user's location is stored as a GeoJSON `Point`, and when a donor posts a relay, a `$nearSphere` query identifies all verified recipients within the configured radius (default 10 km, max 25 km) in milliseconds. Without this, we would have needed a separate spatial index or brute-force Haversine calculations on every query.

---

## Motor Async Driver for Serverless Performance

The backend runs as a **FastAPI application on Vercel serverless functions** using the **Motor async driver**. The connection is a module-level singleton with conservative pool settings tuned for Atlas M0 free tier (`maxPoolSize=10`, `connectTimeoutMS=5000`), ensuring warm invocations reuse connections rather than opening new ones on every request.

---

## Aggregation Pipelines for Real-Time Analytics

The Impact Dashboard and Leaderboard are generated on-the-fly using **MongoDB aggregation pipelines** --- `$match`, `$group`, `$sort`, and `$limit` stages that compute total meals donated, CO2 offset, and donor rankings directly from the `relays` collection. No separate analytics database or batch jobs required.

---

## Flexible Schema and TTL Indexes

MongoDB's schema flexibility let us add fields like `pickup_window`, `dietary_tags`, `photo_url`, and `status` incrementally without migrations or downtime. We also use **TTL indexes** to automatically expire stale relay data, which is critical in a serverless environment with no persistent process for scheduled cleanup.

---

## Summary

| MongoDB Capability | How PlateRelay Uses It |
|---|---|
| GeoJSON and 2dsphere indexes | Core relay-to-shelter proximity matching |
| Motor async driver | Non-blocking database access in serverless functions |
| Aggregation pipelines | Real-time impact dashboards and leaderboard rankings |
| Flexible document schema | Rapid feature iteration without migrations |
| TTL indexes | Automatic expiry of stale relay data without scheduled jobs |
| Atlas M0 free tier | Zero-cost production database for hackathon deployment |

MongoDB is the architectural foundation that makes PlateRelay's core value proposition --- fast, location-aware, real-time food rescue --- technically feasible.

**Open Innovation**

# How PlateRelay Fits the Open Innovation Track

## The Innovation

PlateRelay reframes food waste as a **logistics failure**, not a scarcity problem. India discards nearly 69 million tonnes of edible food annually while 190 million people go hungry. The missing piece has never been willingness to donate --- it is the absence of time-sensitive infrastructure to connect surplus food with the people who need it before it spoils.

PlateRelay is that infrastructure. It is a full-stack food rescue platform that compresses the window between "we have surplus" and "someone is eating it" from hours of phone calls and guesswork down to seconds of geospatial matching and one-tap claiming.

---

## Why This Is an Open Innovation Problem

Food rescue does not fit neatly into a single technical domain. It sits at the intersection of:

- **Geospatial systems** --- proximity-based matching between donors and shelters in real time, powered by MongoDB 2dsphere indexes and GeoJSON queries.
- **Time-critical coordination** --- structured pickup windows with strict expiry, where a delay of even two hours renders the entire relay unsafe and unusable.
- **Trust and accountability** --- photo verification, status tracking pipelines, and gamified reputation systems (badges, leaderboards) that build institutional trust between strangers.
- **Accessible infrastructure** --- email-driven notifications via Resend ensure that shelters operating on limited resources and older devices receive critical relay alerts without needing to keep an app open or monitor a dashboard.
- **Financial inclusion** --- Razorpay-powered subscription tiers allow shelters to scale their claiming capacity, with webhook-driven billing that handles the full lifecycle of plan changes, renewals, and cancellations.

No single existing platform, API, or framework solves this end-to-end. PlateRelay had to be assembled from the ground up, stitching together MongoDB Atlas, Supabase Auth, Cloudinary, Resend, Razorpay, Leaflet maps, and a FastAPI serverless backend into a cohesive product --- the definition of open innovation.

---

## Real-World Impact

PlateRelay is not a theoretical exercise. Every feature was built around a concrete, measurable outcome:

| Feature | Real-World Effect |
|---|---|
| Geospatial relay matching | Shelters within 10 km are identified and notified within seconds of a donor posting surplus food |
| Structured pickup windows | Food is collected while it is still safe to consume, eliminating the ambiguity of informal coordination |
| Impact dashboards | Donors see exactly how many meals they have rescued and how much CO2 they have offset, creating a feedback loop that sustains engagement |
| Subscription tiers | Shelters can scale from 3 free claims per month to unlimited, removing artificial caps on food rescue volume |
| Photo verification | Creates an auditable trail from kitchen to shelter, building trust between organizations that have never worked together |

The platform is designed to operate in Indian cities where the density of restaurants, hotels, and shelters makes hyperlocal food rescue both feasible and high-impact.

---

## What Makes It Innovative

1. **It treats food rescue as a product, not a charity.** PlateRelay has onboarding flows, subscription billing, leaderboards, and impact analytics. It is built to sustain engagement over months and years, not just for a single donation event.

2. **It is serverless and zero-cost at the infrastructure layer.** The entire stack runs on free tiers --- MongoDB Atlas M0, Vercel serverless functions, Supabase Auth, Cloudinary media hosting. This means the platform can be deployed and operated by any NGO or civic body without infrastructure budget.

3. **It solves a coordination problem, not a technology problem.** The individual components (maps, databases, email, payments) are not novel. The innovation is in assembling them into a system where a restaurant can post surplus biryani at 3:00 PM and a shelter two kilometers away can claim it, receive an email, and pick it up by 4:30 PM --- all without a single phone call.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![ngrok](https://img.shields.io/badge/ngrok-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
Traditional healthcare portals are completely passive. When a patient uploads critical lab results from home, the data just sits in a database waiting for a busy doctor to manually log in, find the record, and notice the anomaly. For a condition like Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), a sudden drop in filtration can lead to irreversible organ damage before anyone even opens the file.

💡 What People Use It For & How It Makes Tasks Easier/Safer
Nephron-X shifts medicine from passive tracking to autonomous action, serving as an intelligent co-pilot for both patients and clinicians:

For Understaffed Clinics & Doctors (Safer & Faster Triage):

Instead of digging through thousands of static rows, an AI pipeline instantly calculates risk levels and filters out stable patients.

It acts as a round-the-clock safety net. If a patient's kidney metrics deteriorate, the system completely bypasses the screen interface and autonomously calls the doctor's cell phone via Twilio.

Medical professionals can intervene immediately, even if they are walking between wards or away from their desks.

For Chronic Kidney Disease Patients (Clearer & Less Terrifying Care):

Patients no longer have to stare at confusing medical numbers like eGFR or serum creatinine values in total anxiety.

The portal instantly translates complex lab values into an intuitive, color-coded Liquid Kidney visual percentage tracker and provides a clear breakdown of their status.

Forward-Looking Peace of Mind: Through predictive time-series forecasting graphs, patients can see their health trajectory over the next 48 hours, catching dangerous trends before they become physical emergencies.

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges & Hurdles We Overcame
1. The Silently Crashing Database (Missing Lab Fields)
The Hurdle: During initial CSV report parsing tests, our backend completely crashed with structural execution errors. We realized that while the manual entry form forced a value for every single input field, real-world patient CSV files often omit advanced secondary markers like Hemoglobin.

The Fix: We built a strict input sanitization wrapper inside our data parsing layer. We replaced rigid dictionary lookups with dynamic .get() fallbacks and explicitly configured the database schema to dynamically accept calculated baselines, preventing silent runtime crashes during bulk uploads.

2. Localhost Webhook Blockade (Twilio Integration)
The Hurdle: Our autonomous emergency voice trigger kept failing during early testing. Because our development environment was running securely on a local port (localhost:8000), external telecommunication servers like the Twilio API had no secure, public endpoint route to interact with our backend scripts.

The Fix: We implemented Ngrok to establish an encrypted, public tunneling architecture. By exposing our local Django development port to a live public address, we enabled successful webhook handshakes, allowing our backend code to bypass the web UI and successfully ring a physical cell phone live.

3. Handling Nonlinear Medical Risk Boundaries
The Hurdle: Standard linear classification models were constantly misclassifying high-risk kidney patients. Clinical risk boundaries in kidney disease are highly nonlinear—a minor increase in Serum Creatinine combined with a sharp jump in Blood Pressure indicates a massive crisis, but a linear model kept smoothing these variations out.

The Fix: We dropped simpler models and implemented a Random Forest Ensemble Classifier. By utilizing structured decision-tree boundaries, the AI successfully mapped the complex, interlocking relationships between multiple metabolic markers simultaneously, driving triage accuracy through the roof.

**Gemini**

### 1. Advanced Multimodal Report Parsing

Instead of forcing patients—who might be elderly or in distress—to manually type in cryptic lab numbers, the app uses **Gemini’s Multimodal capabilities (Gemini 1.5 Pro)**. Patients can simply snap a picture of a messy, physical printout or upload an unformatted PDF lab report. Gemini handles the OCR (Optical Character Recognition), extracts the messy text, and structures it into a clean JSON format that instantly feeds into your backend database.

### 2. Conversational Patient-Facing Translation (The Empathy Layer)

Machine learning models output cold numbers and risk percentages (e.g., *"Creatinine: 2.1 mg/dL, eGFR: 32"*). If a patient reads that, they panic. You use Gemini as a translation layer. It acts as an **Empathetic AI Communicator**, taking the numerical risk output and translating it into simple, reassuring, and jargon-free language for the patient, alongside lifestyle and dietary guardrails while they wait for their doctor.

### 3. Smart Clinical Summaries for the Doctor

When the automated Twilio call or SMS goes out to the doctor, they need context immediately. You use **Gemini's large context window** to digest the patient’s entire historical medical timeline, lab history, and current spikes, instantly generating a concise, 3-bullet-point **Clinical Briefing** for the doctor. Instead of digging through files, the doctor reads Gemini's summary and knows exactly what the crisis is within 5 seconds.

### 4. Guarding Against Hallucinations with Grounded Data

The project doesn't use Gemini to blindly guess a diagnosis. Instead, you use a **hybrid architecture**: your rigid **Random Forest Model** handles the hard mathematical classification and safety-critical triage thresholds ($>80\%$), while **Gemini** is safely used for unstructured data processing (parsing reports) and human communication (summaries and translations). This shows the judges a highly mature, safe, and production-ready implementation of GenAI in healthcare.

**Gen AI&ML**

Machine Learning (The Brain): Uses a high-accuracy Random Forest Classifier to handle the heavy mathematical lifting. It processes hard numbers (like creatinine, blood pressure, and eGFR) to accurately predict kidney failure risks and automatically trigger the emergency Twilio phone calls when a patient hits critical thresholds.

Generative AI (The Voice): Powered by Gemini 1.5 Pro to handle unstructured data and human communication. It effortlessly reads and parses messy, scanned PDF lab reports into clean data, translates terrifying medical jargon into simple, comforting language for patients, and summarizes complex history into instant clinical briefs for doctors.

In short: ML calculates the medical risk, while GenAI handles the intelligent data parsing and empathetic communication.

> An offline, privacy-first Edge Diagnostic Terminal

![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenStreetMap](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenStreetMap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Access to early diagnostic eye care is fundamentally broken in remote and underserved regions. Traditional ophthalmology screenings require expensive, stationary hardware (like $50,000 retinal cameras) and highly trained specialists, which simply do not exist outside of major urban centers. 

Furthermore, modern AI solutions attempt to solve this using Cloud APIs. This creates two massive roadblocks for rural deployment:
1. **Infrastructure Failure:** Cloud APIs require high-speed, low-latency internet, which rural clinics do not have.
2. **Medical Privacy Violations:** Sending raw patient medical photos to third-party cloud servers violates strict HIPAA and local data privacy laws.

**VisionCare AI** solves this by acting as an autonomous **Edge Diagnostic Terminal**. It transforms a standard smartphone photo into a clinical-grade medical assessment without ever touching the cloud. 

By running **Vision-Language Models (Qwen2.5-VL)** strictly on local hardware and utilizing **OpenCV Multi-Spectral Emulation** to simulate high-end red-free retinal cameras, we can extract critical health indicators (Anemia, Jaundice, Inflammation) locally. Our system also features a localized OpenStreetMap routing protocol to send critical patients to the nearest physical hospital, creating a complete end-to-end diagnostic and triage pipeline that is 100% offline and perfectly secure.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a clinical-grade AI terminal that operates strictly on the edge presented several extreme technical hurdles:

**1. VLM Latency on Edge Hardware**
Running a massive-parameter Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL) on standard clinic laptops initially resulted in severe latency. We couldn't rely on the cloud for compute. 
* **How we solved it:** Instead of forcing the AI to do all the heavy lifting, we built a pre-processing pipeline using **OpenCV**. We run a Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) algorithm to mathematically strip the Red and Blue light channels. This synthesizes a "Red-Free Multi-Spectral Image" that makes the blood vessels pop in extreme high-contrast, allowing the local AI model to infer vascular health with a fraction of the computational overhead.

**2. Data Hallucinations in Pixel-Only Diagnosis**
Relying purely on optical pixels is dangerous due to lighting bias and skin-tone variations. 
* **How we solved it:** We implemented a **Multi-Modal Data Fusion** architecture. The system forces the patient through an LLM-powered dynamic triage questionnaire. We then fuse the patient's textual history with the optical image matrices. This constrained the model's diagnostic confidence intervals and entirely eliminated hallucinations.

**3. Maintaining the "Clinical" Illusion**
Consumer-grade UIs with emojis and bright colors destroy trust in medical environments.
* **How we solved it:** We engineered a custom CSS architecture for Streamlit we call "Clinical Brutalism." We stripped all consumer aesthetics, implementing a high-contrast, monospace, terminal-inspired UI that optimizes strictly for medical utility and data density.

**Gen AI&ML**

Gen AI & ML VisionCare AI is fundamentally driven by advanced Generative AI and Machine Learning operating strictly on the edge. Instead of simple image classifiers, the project utilizes state-of-the-art Vision-Language Models (Qwen2.5-VL) running entirely on local hardware. Furthermore, we employ LLMs (Llama 3) to execute dynamic, conversational medical triage. By fusing mathematical image matrices (processed via OpenCV) with generative text-based patient histories, the AI calculates a highly accurate diagnostic confidence matrix without ever relying on cloud APIs.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Wallet Adapter SSR Crash in Next.js App Router

**Problem:** `@solana/wallet-adapter-react-ui` imports CSS inside a `'use client'` 
component. Next.js 14 App Router's server-side render choked on this at build time — 
the wallet modal initialized but the popup never opened. Zero error in console.

**Fix:** Moved all CSS imports into `globals.css` using `@import` at the top level. 
Removed every CSS import from the provider file. Added a `mounted` state guard so 
`WalletMultiButton` only renders after client hydration — eliminating the SSR 
hydration mismatch entirely.

---

## 2. Webpack Polyfills Breaking Vercel Build

**Problem:** `@solana/web3.js` internally requires Node.js built-ins (`crypto`, 
`stream`, `fs`, `http`) that don't exist in Vercel's browser bundle. Build succeeded 
locally but crashed on Vercel with `Module not found: Can't resolve 'crypto'`.

**Fix:** Added full `resolve.fallback` config in `next.config.js` with all 11 Node.js 
built-ins set to `false` (browser-safe polyfill skip). Also added 
`esmExternals: 'loose'` to handle ESM/CJS conflicts in wallet adapter packages.

---

## 3. Real Transaction Signing vs. Demo Simulation

**Problem:** Early version used fake wallet addresses and simulated transactions. 
No real blockchain interaction — just UI theater.

**Fix:** Rebuilt the entire tip flow around `useWallet()` → `sendTransaction()` 
from `@solana/wallet-adapter-react`. Backend `/api/tip` now builds a real unsigned 
Solana `SystemProgram.transfer` transaction serialized to base64. Client receives it, 
signs via Phantom, broadcasts to devnet RPC. `/api/confirm` verifies the signature 
on-chain and returns slot, blockTime, fee, and Explorer URL.

---

## 4. MetaMask + Phantom Simultaneously

**Problem:** Standard Solana wallet adapter doesn't support MetaMask (EVM wallet). 
We needed both for cross-chain users bridging from Ethereum.

**Fix:** MetaMask handled completely separately via `window.ethereum.request
({ method: 'eth_requestAccounts' })` — no adapter needed. Both wallets connect 
independently and display real addresses simultaneously in the nav bar.

---

## 5. SoulBound NFT — Non-Transferable Token-2022

**Problem:** Standard SPL NFTs can be transferred. A "reputation" token that can 
be sold defeats the purpose entirely.

**Fix:** Used Solana's Token-2022 program with the `NonTransferable` extension. 
The mint instruction sets this flag permanently at creation time — the token is 
cryptographically impossible to transfer, not just UI-restricted.

---

## 6. ZK Proof Generation in the Browser

**Problem:** Groth16 proof generation is computationally expensive — running it 
server-side leaks the private input (the wallet address we're trying to hide).

**Fix:** Proof generation runs entirely client-side using WebAssembly. The nullifier 
(hash of wallet + secret) is computed in-browser and never leaves the user's machine. 
Only the proof and public signals are submitted to the backend for verification.

**Gemini**

We integrated Google Gemini API at two layers:

1. **Personalized thank-you messages** — After every tip transaction confirms 
   on-chain, Gemini generates a unique, context-aware thank-you message based 
   on the creator's content category, tip amount, and tipper's reputation tier. 
   A Gold-tier tipper sending 1 SOL to a music creator gets a completely 
   different message than a Bronze tipper sending 0.01 SOL to a developer.

2. **AI Tip Stream scoring** — Our recurring payment streams use Gemini to 
   analyze creator posting frequency, engagement signals, and content quality 
   weekly. The AI score (0–100) automatically adjusts the stream rate — 
   rewarding consistent creators and pausing payments for inactive ones. 
   All scoring logic runs via the Gemini 1.5 Pro API with structured JSON output.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB Atlas powers our entire data layer:

- **Creator profiles** — wallet address, display name, category, bio, 
  total tips received, tip link slug (indexed for fast lookup)
- **Tip history** — every confirmed on-chain transaction stored with: 
  sender wallet, receiver wallet, amount in SOL, lamports, TX signature, 
  Solana slot, blockTime, and Gemini-generated thank-you message
- **Reputation scores** — tipper wallet → score, tier, streak, 
  total tipped, SBT mint status, mint TX signature
- **Stream configs** — recurring payment schedules, Gemini AI scores, 
  last execution timestamp, total streamed

We use Mongoose with full schema validation. The `/api/tip` route writes 
to MongoDB after every on-chain confirmation from `/api/confirm` — 
ensuring we only store verified, settled transactions. Atlas Search 
powers the creator explore page with full-text search on names and categories.

**Buying and selling land without middlemen**
No broker, no tout, no lawyer needed. Seller enters the ULPIN, AI pulls all

**Knowing exactly what you're buying**
Before any money moves, Gemini cross-checks Revenue Department, Kaveri 2.0, and 
District Court records and flags risks — pending litigation, disputed ownership, 
unpaid tax. You see everything a lawyer would charge ₹20,000 to find out.

**Tracking your transfer in real time**
No more calling the registrar's office daily. Both buyer and seller see an Amazon 
style progress bar showing exactly where the transfer is at every stage, with inbox 
notifications when something moves.

**A legally structured deed, automatically**
The Sale Deed is auto generated in the format of an actual Indian legal document, 
with all four digital signatures retained — seller, buyer, registrar, panchayat. 
Each party downloads their copy the moment they sign.

**Fraud and tampering become detectable instantly**
Every blockchain record is SHA-256 hashed. If anyone alters a single field the 
mismatch is flagged immediately. The chain is append only so nothing can be 
backdated or deleted.

**Ownership proof in seconds**
Full chain of title from Government to current owner, cryptographically verified, 
accessible with just the ULPIN. What currently takes weeks of document hunting 
takes seconds.

**Accessible in your own language**
Transfer summaries delivered in Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, or Telugu. For rural 
landowners who can't read English legalese, this is the difference between 
understanding what they own and depending on someone else to explain it.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Technical Challenges & Bug Resolutions

A summary of the technical hurdles, rate limits, and bugs encountered during 
the development of LandChain, along with the strategies implemented to overcome them.

---

### 1. Express Route Precedence Overrides

**The Hurdle**
The wildcard route handler for querying ULPIN path chains (`GET /api/blockchain/:ulpin(*)`) 
was intercepting more specific GET endpoints defined below it (such as `/audit/report` or 
`/verify-node/:nodeId`), parsing them as parameter inputs and leading to 
`404 Route Not Found` or `500 Server Error` crashes.

**The Resolution**
Reordered route registration in `blockchainRoutes.js` so that specific endpoints are 
registered first, and the wildcard parameter catch-all path is placed at the very bottom.

---

### 2. Split Property Synchronization Race Condition

**The Hurdle**
When a user initiated a split parcel request, child properties, ledger hashes, and split 
contracts were handled inside a background asynchronous `setTimeout` block. The frontend 
immediately requested the user's inventory before database writes finished, resulting in 
missing inventory listings and synchronization bugs.

**The Resolution**
Changed the `/split-request` endpoint to block synchronously using `await` and wait 5 
seconds for database writes and blockchain nodes to be completely committed before 
returning the success response.

---

### 3. Wildcard ULPIN Slash Routing

**The Hurdle**
ULPIN formats representing child split parcels include path slashes (e.g. `KA-MNG-142-3B/A`), 
which standard Express parameter mapping treats as path delimiters, causing Express to 
return `404 Route Not Found`.

**The Resolution**
Used Express wildcard syntax `:ulpin(*)` on all backend endpoints handling ULPIN parameters 
to instruct the router to parse the entire trailing subpath including slashes as a single value.

---

### 4. Kaveri / Sub-Registrar History & Overlapping Timelines

**The Hurdle**
Seeding mock blockchain transactions created timeline overlaps (e.g. standard gift deeds 
from Government occurring after or during a buyer-seller transfer).

**The Resolution**
Unified ownership history compilation to query `SubRegistrar` registry history first and 
use its date mapping to dynamically bound the previous owner's tenure, resolving timeline 
overlap errors.

---

### 5. Gemini API v1beta 404 Deprecation

**The Hurdle**
The backend was querying the deprecated `gemini-1.5-flash` model, which returned a 
`404` error from Google's Beta API server.

**The Resolution**
Updated the model config in `geminiService.js` to target the active `gemini-2.5-flash` model.

---

### 6. Static Fallback Risk Analysis When Gemini API Key Fails

**The Hurdle**
When the Gemini API hit rate limits (`429 Too Many Requests`) or had no key, it would 
fall back to a hardcoded low-risk analysis mockup. This caused properties with active 
mortgages, litigations, or tax issues to bypass the AI flags in fallback mode.

**The Resolution**
Built a custom local rule-based analyzer `smartLocalAnalyze` in `geminiService.js` to 
dynamically parse the registry data and flag faults locally when the Gemini API is 
offline or throttled.

---

### 7. Voice Assistant Recording Auto-Silence Triggering

**The Hurdle**
The Web Audio API recording was either cutting off too early due to minor background 
noises, or hanging indefinitely because silence thresholds were too low.

**The Resolution**
Handled signal processing with an amplitude analyser, tuning the silence threshold to 
`0.018` and adding a `1200ms` grace period timer to wait before stopping, along with 
a SpeechSynthesis fallback.

---

### 8. Mongoose Buffers Timeout in Separate Workspaces

**The Hurdle**
Running independent audit/verification scripts from different directories resulted in 
Mongoose buffering timeout errors. This was caused by Node.js resolving Mongoose into 
different module instances across the project tree.

**The Resolution**
Changed Mongoose and model imports to point directly to the project backend's local 
`node_modules` path, ensuring a shared singleton database connection instance.

**Gemini**

**Consolidated Risk Audits: **
Gemini parses records from 4 government databases (Revenue, Sub-Registrar, Tax, and Courts) to identify outstanding bank mortgages, active lawsuits, and tax arrears.

**Structured Risk Reporting: **
It flags transactions as LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH risk, outputting a normalized JSON report containing a plain-English summary and specific warning flags.

**Smart Local Fallback:**
 When API rate limits are hit, a rule-based parser (smartLocalAnalyze) takes over to ensure faults (like SBI mortgages or court disputes) are still flagged in the UI.

**MongoDB**

**1. Blockchain Ledger Simulation:**
We replicated a tamper-evident ledger using the 
BlockchainNode.js
 model.

Each document represents a block containing transaction details (deedNumber, volume, page, previous and current owner IDs).
Blocks are linked using a previousHash field.
A Mongoose pre("save") hook automatically computes a cryptographic SHA-256 digest (hash) of the block fields, enabling cryptographic auditing and verification.
**2. Multi-Source Government Registries**
To analyze real-time property liabilities, we created collections representing distinct government database tables:

StateRevenue.js
: Land specifications (survey numbers, boundaries, splits).
SubRegistrar.js
: Official encumbrance certificates and outstanding mortgages.
PanchayatTax.js
: Property tax ledgers (tracking paid/unpaid years).
CourtRecord.js
: Civil and land court case schedules and active injunctions.

**3. Application State & Inventory**
We used standard collections to manage user profiles, active inventories, and notification channels:

User.js
: Stores identity mappings verified by Aadhaar.
Property.js
: Holds synced active land properties mapped to current users.
Notification.js
: Dispatches status alerts to user inboxes.

**4. Transfer Workflow State Machine**
The 
Transfer.js
 collection stores active property transactions. It enforces a strict status state-machine (DRAFT ➔ SENT ➔ BUYER_SIGNED ➔ REGISTRAR_REVIEW ➔ PANCHAYAT_REVIEW ➔ PAYMENT_PENDING ➔ COMPLETED), caching digital signatures, purchase agreements, and the generated Gemini AI risk assessment summaries at each stage.

**Sarvam.ai**

**1. Voice Assistant Chatbot (The Accessibility Guide):**
*What it does:* Allows users to talk to the platform to learn how to navigate it.
*Role in our project:* It acts as a digital helper for rural or non-technical citizens. They can ask questions and get spoken guidance in their native language, making the platform accessible to everyone without requiring computer literacy.

**2. Document Translator (The Transparency Safeguard):**
*What it does:* Translates the legally binding Sale Deed into native languages.
*Role in our project:* It ensures complete transparency. Buyers and sellers can read every single condition, risk flag, and mortgage detail in their own language before signing, protecting them from signing fraudulent or misunderstood contracts.

**BlockChain & Web3**

Our project simulates a tamper-evident blockchain ledger directly in MongoDB to secure land registry history:

**Cryptographic Hashing (SHA-256):** 
Each block ( BlockchainNode.js) stores a property transaction and computes a unique hash using its contents.

**Block Linkage:** 
Blocks are linked sequentially using the previousHash of the parent block, forming an immutable timeline.

**Integrity Auditing:** 
A verification service (integrityChecker.js) checks block hashes and links. If any historical record is modified or deleted, the cryptographic chain breaks, instantly alerting the Registrar and all parties in the UI.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

## The gap

India runs **thousands of central and state welfare schemes** — pensions, scholarships, maternity benefits, housing, crop support, disability aid, health cover. The money exists. The problem is the **last mile**: the people who need these schemes most often have no idea they exist, can't tell which ones they qualify for, can't read the eligibility rules or fill the forms, and don't speak the language the portals are written in.

So today, claiming a benefit usually means one of three things:

1. Spending hours navigating confusing government websites (in English/Hindi, behind logins, full of jargon).
2. Standing in a queue at an office, only to be told you don't qualify.
3. Paying a middleman or agent who takes a cut to do something the citizen was entitled to for free.

> **The result:** eligible families never claim what's rightfully theirs, and those who try often waste a day's wages and a long trip on a scheme they were never eligible for.

---

## Who it's for

- **Rural, elderly, and non literate citizens** who can speak but can't read forms or type.
- **Anyone overwhelmed by the bureaucracy** — first time applicants, or caregivers applying on behalf of a parent or child.
- **Frontline helpers** — ASHA workers, Common Service Centre operators, and NGO volunteers — who can use it as an instant eligibility checker for the people they serve.

---

## What people can use it for

**Yojana Saathi is a voice helpline you can simply talk to.** You describe your situation out loud in **any of 23 Indian languages**, and through a short conversation it figures out exactly which government schemes you and your family qualify for — then explains each one back to you in your own language and hands you a document you can carry to the office.

A user can:

- **Discover schemes they never knew existed**, without reading anything.
- **Check whether they actually qualify** before travelling anywhere.
- **Cover the whole family in one conversation** — the caller, a pregnant daughter, an elderly parent, a school going child — and get a separate, grouped list of schemes for each person.
- **Download a clean PDF** for each scheme with the benefit, why they qualify, the exact documents and certificates to carry, and the official portal link.

---

## How it makes existing tasks *easier*

| Before | With Yojana Saathi |
| --- | --- |
| Read English forms, type details | Just **speak**; it replies aloud and on screen in your language |
| Generic list, you guess what fits | It **asks follow up questions** and matches you precisely |
| Research each family member separately | **One conversation** covers the whole household |
| "You might be eligible" | A **downloadable checklist** of documents and where to apply |

- **Voice instead of forms.** No reading, no typing, no English required.
- **It asks instead of assuming.** A real back and forth — *"Are you a widow or married? What is your yearly income? Which caste category?"* — gathering only what's needed to match you accurately.
- **Actionable output.** The PDF turns "you might be eligible" into a clear next step.

---

## How it makes things *safer*

- **No false hope.** Every recommendation passes a strict eligibility audit, so the app **never tells someone they qualify for a scheme they don't** (for example, it won't suggest an 18 to 40 farmer pension to a 55 year old, or a widow pension to someone who isn't a widow). When it isn't sure, it says so honestly instead of guessing. This is the difference between a wasted trip and a successful claim.
- **Cuts out the middleman.** By giving citizens the same answer an agent would — free, instant, and in their language — it removes the incentive to pay touts and bribes for information that should be public.
- **Transparent.** It shows *why* you qualify and links the **official government portal**, so people apply through the right channel instead of a lookalike scam site.

---

## A real example

A 58 year old woman calls and says, in Telugu:

> *"I'm a widow, we're a poor family with a ration card. My daughter is pregnant, and my son is 16 and still in school."*

In one conversation, Yojana Saathi asks a couple of clarifying questions, then returns:

- **For her:** Widow Pension + National Old Age support
- **For her daughter:** PM Matru Vandana + Janani Suraksha (maternity benefits)
- **For her son:** a Post Matric scholarship

…each explained aloud in Telugu, each with a downloadable document listing the papers to carry and where to apply.

> What used to take days of confusion, literacy, and possibly a paid agent now takes a **two minute conversation**.

---

## Why it matters

Welfare schemes only work if the right people can find and claim them. Yojana Saathi attacks the exact point where the system breaks down — the gap between a scheme **existing** and a citizen actually **receiving** it — and it does so for the people the system most often leaves behind: those who can speak but can't r

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

Building a voice first, multilingual welfare assistant meant almost every layer of the stack fought back at some point. The big ones:

### Speech recognition
Our first model (Saarika) had limited language coverage and turned English into Hindi script. We switched to **Saaras v3** in translate mode, which auto detects all 23 languages and returns clean English.

### Reasoning model
Gemini Flash kept hitting **429 quota walls**, so we moved to a hybrid of **Sarvam 30B** (fast fact extraction) and **Sarvam 105B** (eligibility reasoning). The hidden catch: these are reasoning models that returned empty JSON until we disabled their thinking mode, which also made them far cheaper and faster.

### Embeddings
Our first embedding model was retired mid build, so we moved to Gemini's embedding model at **768 dimensions** with manual L2 normalisation, so cosine similarity stayed correct.

### MongoDB Atlas
Atlas threw SSL and rate limit errors, and our seeding script silently deleted the vector index every time it dropped the collection. We switched to **deleteMany** and batched the embeddings, which made vector search reliable.

### 3D Spline assistant
The bot glided across the page instead of staying put. We pinned it to a fixed corner, drove only its orientation with the cursor, and masked out the watermark.

### Glassmorphism frontend
The look was incoherent (purple on top, green below), so we rebuilt it around one unified emerald theme with consistent blur surfaces and a floating backdrop of the 23 language letters.

**MongoDB**

**MongoDB Atlas is the retrieval backbone of the whole system — it *is* the "R" in our RAG.** Every welfare scheme lives as a single document in one `schemes` collection that holds both the human readable fields (name, benefit, eligibility text, required documents, apply URL) **and** its 768 dimensional embedding vector side by side. That co location is the key architectural win: we don't run a separate vector store plus a separate metadata database and stitch them together — Atlas is simultaneously our **operational document store and our vector database**, so a single query returns the match *and* everything needed to explain and act on it.

Retrieval runs through Atlas's native **`$vectorSearch` aggregation stage**, backed by a `vectorSearch` index (`numDimensions: 768`, `similarity: cosine`) on the `embedding` field. At query time we embed the user's situation, push the vector into the pipeline with `numCandidates` for recall and `limit` for the top matches, and project the scheme fields plus a `vectorSearchScore` in one round trip. Because it's a normal aggregation pipeline, we can chain it with ordinary Mongo filtering and projection — semantic retrieval and structured data access in the same query language, which is exactly why a vague spoken phrase resolves to the right scheme without any keyword overlap.

It also taught us its sharp edges, which made the integration stronger: dropping the collection silently destroys the Atlas Search index, so we moved seeding to `deleteMany()` and batched the embedding writes to stay reliable, and locked down network access for the cloud deployment. Net result — **MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is the piece that turns a pile of scheme text into an instant, similarity ranked, explainable retrieval engine**, and it carries the core ML workload of the product.

**Sarvam.ai**

# How Yojana Saathi Uses Sarvam AI

**Sarvam AI is the entire language brain of Yojana Saathi — not one feature, but the foundation every single turn runs through.** We use three different Sarvam model families end to end, so from the moment a user opens their mouth to the moment they hear a scheme read back to them, it is Sarvam the whole way.

---

## 1. Saaras v3 — speech understanding (input)

The user speaks freely in **any of 23 Indian languages**. We call Sarvam's **`saaras:v3` in `mode=translate`**, deliberately omitting a `language_code` so Saaras **auto detects the spoken language and returns clean English** in a single step.

- Collapses **transcription + language detection + translation** into one call, instead of three separate models stitched together.
- Robust to the things that break Western models on Indian speech — **code mixing ("Hinglish"), regional accents, and dialects**.
- We keep the detected language code **per turn**, which lets the assistant reply *in the language the question was asked in* (English question → English answer, then Telugu question → Telugu answer, in the same conversation).

---

## 2. Sarvam LLMs (30B + 105B) — the reasoning core

Most of our engineering went here. We run a **hybrid of `sarvam-30b` and `sarvam-105b`** through Sarvam's OpenAI compatible `/v1/chat/completions` API, each doing what it's best at:

- **`sarvam-30b` (fast, cheap)** turns messy translated speech into a **structured JSON profile** every turn, and tracks **multiple family members** (the caller plus relatives) by merging new facts into the right person.
- **`sarvam-105b` (heavy reasoning)** is the conversational agent and the eligibility judge. It decides whether to **ask a clarifying question or recommend**, generates the questions and scheme explanations **in the user's own language**, and runs a **strict eligibility audit** — an adversarial "find a reason this person does *not* qualify" pass that stops the system from ever claiming eligibility it can't justify.

> **A non obvious win that made it viable:** Sarvam's chat models are *reasoning* models, and left at default they spent their whole token budget on hidden chain of thought and returned **empty JSON** on long prompts. Setting **`enable_thinking=false`** fixed correctness and made responses roughly **10× cheaper and ~5× faster** (≈140 tokens and ~1s instead of ~1,800 tokens and 5 to 19s).

Splitting cheap extraction (30B) from expensive reasoning (105B) is a deliberate cost vs quality trade that keeps the agent fast and affordable while staying accurate.

---

## 3. Bulbul v2 — speech generation (output)

Every reply — clarifying questions and the final grouped scheme recommendations — is spoken back through Sarvam's **`bulbul:v2`** TTS in the **same language the user spoke**, so a non literate caller never has to read anything. This closes the loop into a true **speech to speech experience**, which is the entire point of a helpline for rural and elderly users.

---

## Why Sarvam, specifically

A generic LLM/ASR stack simply cannot do this for Bharat. Sarvam is **built for India** — 23 languages, code mixing, accents, and Indic scripts as first class citizens — and it is the only stack that let us run the **complete pipeline (understand → reason → verify → speak) natively in Indian languages**.

In short, **Sarvam powers the STT, the structured extraction, the multi turn agent, the eligibility verification, and the TTS.** It is the layer that turns a voice in any Indian language into a verified, spoken government scheme recommendation. That depth of integration — three model families, a hybrid reasoning design, and a real correctness safeguard — is what makes Yojana Saathi a genuine **Sarvam native** product, not an app that merely calls an API.

---

## Sarvam footprint at a glance

| Stage | Sarvam model | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Listen | `saaras:v3` (translate) | Speech → clean English, auto language detect (23 langs) |
| Extract | `sarvam-30b` | Speech → structured JSON profile, multi beneficiary tracking |
| Reason | `sarvam-105b` | Ask vs recommend, explanations, strict eligibility audit |
| Speak | `bulbul:v2` | Replies spoken in the user's own language |

**Gen AI&ML**

**Yojana Saathi is an end to end generative AI system** — specifically a *multilingual, speech to speech, agentic RAG pipeline*. The entire interaction is mediated by ML models: spoken input in any of 23 Indian languages is transcribed and translated to a normalized representation (Saaras v3 ASR + speech translation), a hybrid LLM stack (Sarvam 30B for fast structured extraction, Sarvam 105B for heavier reasoning) converts messy free speech into a typed profile and drives the dialogue, and the response is rendered back as natural speech (Bulbul v2 TTS). It is genuinely multimodal generative AI — audio in, structured reasoning in the middle, audio out — rather than a thin LLM wrapper.

At its core sits a **retrieval augmented generation (RAG) architecture**, which is the heart of the ML track fit. Every welfare scheme is embedded with `gemini-embedding-001` into 768 dimensional vectors (manually L2 normalized so cosine similarity stays well defined at the truncated dimension), indexed in **MongoDB Atlas Vector Search**, and retrieved by semantic similarity against the user's situation. This is what lets a phrase like *"poor widow farmer"* match a scheme described as *"BPL female cultivator with spousal bereavement"* even with zero lexical overlap. On top of retrieval, the LLM performs **grounded generation** — it only explains schemes pulled from the indexed corpus, which keeps outputs factual and traceable rather than hallucinated.

What pushes it beyond a standard RAG demo is the **agentic and responsible AI layer**. The system runs a stateful, multi turn conversational agent that does *slot filling* — it identifies missing eligibility signals and asks targeted clarifying questions instead of assuming — and it tracks multiple beneficiaries in a single dialogue. Critically, recommendations pass through an **eligibility verification stage** that combines an LLM as judge audit with deterministic guardrails (for example, hard numeric age gating), so the model never asserts eligibility it cannot justify. That blend of generative reasoning, vector retrieval, conversational state, and verifiable, safety constrained output is exactly the kind of applied Gen AI and ML work the track is meant to showcase.

### SwaramPay
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/swaram-pay-a945) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sarangan19/swaramPay/tree/master) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/An-IUnJbgFA?feature=share) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Speak. Pay. Done

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![ngrok](https://img.shields.io/badge/ngrok-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Speech Recognition](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20Recognition-333333?style=flat-square) ![Text-to-Speech](https://img.shields.io/badge/Text--to--Speech-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India has over 900 million UPI users — but that number hides a massive gap. The 250+ million Indians who are elderly, illiterate, visually
  impaired, or simply unfamiliar with smartphones are completely locked out of the digital payments revolution. For them, UPI apps require
  reading menus, navigating touchscreens, and typing in English or Hindi script — barriers that are invisible to urban users but insurmountable
  for a 70-year-old farmer in rural Andhra Pradesh or a daily wage worker who never went to school.

  Existing "solutions" don't actually solve this. Basic feature phones can dial numbers but can't run apps. Bank agents exist but charge fees
  and aren't always trustworthy. *99# USSD banking works without internet but requires navigating numeric menus in English — still a literacy
  barrier. None of these solutions offer the most natural human interface of all: your own voice, in your own language.

  SwaramPay turns any phone call into a secure, intelligent banking session. A user calls a single number, speaks naturally in Telugu, Hindi,
  Tamil, or 6 other Indian languages, and authenticates using their voice — no PIN to remember, no screen to read, no app to download. The same
  technology that makes voice assistants feel magical is now accessible to people who have never owned a smartphone, making financial inclusion
  not just a policy goal but a working product.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest technical problem we hit was voice authentication on low-quality phone audio. Our initial implementation used Resemblyzer for
  speaker embeddings, which worked fine on clean microphone recordings but completely fell apart on Twilio's 8kHz compressed phone audio. We
  were getting false accepts and false rejects at near-random rates, making biometric auth essentially useless. The fix required switching to
  SpeechBrain's ECAPA-TDNN model, which was specifically trained on telephone-quality speech, and adding a resampling pipeline to normalize all
  audio to 16kHz before embedding extraction. That single change took the cosine similarity scores from noisy and unreliable to consistently
  landing in the 0.6 to 0.77 range for the correct speaker.

  The second major hurdle was DTMF digit interference during MPIN registration. When we nested the audio prompt inside Twilio's Gather verb,
  which is the standard pattern, the TTS audio playback was generating frequencies that Twilio's DTMF detector was misreading as keypad presses.
   A user typing "1234" would arrive at the server as "13", two digits silently dropped. We caught this through debug logging that printed
  exactly what digits Twilio received, which made the pattern obvious. The fix was to play the audio on the response object first, add a
  one-second pause, and only then start the Gather, keeping audio and digit detection completely separate.

  Latency was a third ongoing battle. The initial login flow took 26 seconds from call connect to authenticated main menu, which felt unusable.
  By profiling every stage, Twilio's silence timeout, recording download time, SpeechBrain inference, we identified that 4 seconds of pure dead
  silence after the user stopped speaking was the single biggest waste. Tuning the silence timeout from 4 seconds down to 2 seconds, and
  applying similar reductions across all voice input points in the app, brought the end-to-end login time down to a consistent 20 seconds with
  no speech getting cut off, a 23% improvement with a one-line change.

**Sarvam.ai**

SwaramPay's core thesis is that the largest barrier to digital financial inclusion in India isn't connectivity or smartphones — it's language and literacy. UPI apps assume a smartphone, a screen, and comfort reading English/transliterated text. SwaramPay strips all of that away: a user just calls a phone number, and conducts an entire banking session — registration, voice authentication, balance checks, P2P transfers, contact management — by speaking in their own language (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, etc.) over a basic Twilio voice call. There's no app to install and no script to read.

This is where Sarvam's models aren't an add-on but the load-bearing infrastructure of the product. Every conversational turn runs through Sarvam's Saaras speech-to-text (translating native-language speech directly to English for intent/amount/recipient extraction, while also transcribing in the user's own script for voice-auth anti-replay checks) and Bulbul TTS (for natural-sounding prompts and dynamic responses — balance readbacks, payment confirmations, contact echoes — in 10 Indian languages). Because Sarvam's models are explicitly tuned for 8kHz telephony audio and code-mixed speech, they hold up on real phone-call audio quality, which is the actual deployment environment for this use case — unlike general-purpose STT/TTS that's optimized for clean studio/mic audio.

For the Sarvam track specifically, SwaramPay demonstrates a complete, demo-able end-to-end application of Sarvam's Indic-language stack to a high-stakes, real-world domain (financial services) for the exact population — rural, elderly, non-English-speaking, low-smartphone-literacy users — that voice-first Indic AI is positioned to serve. It pairs Sarvam's STT/TTS with SpeechBrain voice biometrics for hands-free authentication and a guardian companion web portal for family oversight, showing how Sarvam's language models can sit at the center of a genuinely useful product rather than a translation gimmick bolted onto an English-first app.

**Open Innovation**

SwaramPay is built entirely by composing openly accessible tools rather than proprietary technology — Sarvam's Saaras STT and Bulbul TTS APIs, SpeechBrain's open-source ECAPA-TDNN voice biometrics, and Twilio for telephony. The open innovation bet here is that the frontier models are already good enough, and the real gap is in the application layer: assembling the right pieces to solve a problem nobody had solved for this specific user population.
That problem is a structural artifact of closed design. UPI and India's digital payments stack are technically open protocols, but every interface implementation assumes a smartphone, a readable screen, and English literacy — which de facto excludes the rural and low-literacy users those protocols were meant to serve. SwaramPay opens the interface itself: replace the visual app with a voice call and a language model, and the financial inclusion promise of open protocols actually reaches the people it was designed for. The architecture is intentionally modular so others can extend it — new languages, new financial operations, new regional deployments — without touching the IVR core.

**The problem it solves**

🎯 The Problem It Solves

Healthcare systems today are often fragmented, slow, and difficult to navigate, especially during critical situations. Patients typically need to switch between multiple platforms, hospitals, and services to access basic healthcare information, appointments, or emergency support.

This leads to:

⏱️ Delayed emergency response due to lack of centralized alerts and communication
📉 Fragmented patient records spread across different systems
🏥 Difficulty in finding hospitals, availability, and services in real time
🧑‍⚕️ Inefficient coordination between patients, doctors, and caretakers
🌐 Language barriers in accessing healthcare guidance
📄 Manual and time-consuming handling of medical documents and reports
💡 How VitalCare Solves This

VitalCare transforms this fragmented system into a unified, intelligent healthcare ecosystem that simplifies and accelerates healthcare access.

It enables users to:

🚨 Instantly trigger and receive emergency alerts shared with caretakers and doctors
🏥 Quickly discover hospitals, schemes, and medical services in one place
🧑‍⚕️ Maintain a connected network of patients, doctors, and caretakers
📊 Continuously monitor health vitals and risk scores in real time
🤖 Interact with an AI-powered health assistant (voice + text) for guidance
🌐 Access healthcare services in multiple languages
📄 Upload and understand medical documents using AI-assisted reading
⚡ Impact

By centralizing healthcare interactions and introducing AI-driven assistance, VitalCare:

Reduces response time during emergencies
Improves communication between all healthcare stakeholders
Makes healthcare information more accessible and understandable
Enhances decision-making through real-time health insights
Brings intelligence, automation, and coordination into everyday healthcare

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

While building VitalCare, several technical and system-level challenges arose, especially due to the complexity of integrating multiple modules, AI services, and real-time workflows.

🧠 1. AI Service Integration Complexity (Sarvam AI)

One of the biggest challenges was integrating Sarvam AI for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, translation, and document reading.

❌ Initial issue: API calls were inconsistent and sometimes failed due to network or key availability
❌ Document processing sometimes broke when external API was unavailable

✅ Solution:
I implemented a dedicated AI service layer (sarvamAI) that isolates all AI-related logic.
Additionally, I added a fallback mechanism using pdf-parse to ensure document reading still works even when the external API fails.

🔄 2. Ensuring System Stability Without Breaking Existing Features

Since the project already had multiple modules (dashboards, alerts, appointments, etc.), a major risk was unintentionally breaking existing workflows while adding new AI features.

❌ Issue:

Tight coupling between features could lead to cascading failures

✅ Solution:

Followed a strict modular architecture
Ensured Sarvam AI was added as an isolated service layer
Avoided modifying core modules like authentication, dashboards, and appointments
📄 3. Document Upload and Processing Issues

Handling base64 encoded PDFs and ensuring accurate text extraction was challenging.

❌ Issue:

External API failures caused incomplete responses
PDF parsing required proper buffer conversion

✅ Solution:

Implemented a hybrid processing pipeline
Primary: Sarvam AI document-read API
Fallback: Local pdf-parse extraction
Ensured graceful error handling instead of system crashes
🌐 4. Maintaining Role-Based Access Control

With multiple user roles (Patient, Doctor, Caretaker, Admin), managing access control and data visibility was complex.

❌ Issue:

Risk of unauthorized data access between roles

✅ Solution:

Implemented strict role-based access control (RBAC)
Ensured each role only accesses relevant dashboards and data:
Doctors → assigned patients only
Caretakers → linked patients only
Patients → personal data only
🚨 5. Emergency Alert Workflow Design

Designing a reliable emergency alert system that works across multiple user roles was challenging.

❌ Issue:

Ensuring alerts reach both caretakers and doctors in real time

✅ Solution:

Built a backend-triggered alert system
Designed event-based notification flow to ensure delivery to all linked users
🏁 Outcome

By solving these challenges, VitalCare evolved into a stable, modular, and AI-enhanced healthcare ecosystem that is resilient, scalable, and suitable for real-world deployment scenarios

**Gemini**

🤖 How VitalCare Fits the Gemini AI Track

VitalCare aligns strongly with the Gemini AI Track by leveraging AI-driven intelligence to enhance healthcare accessibility, communication, and decision-making across multiple user roles.

🧠 1. AI-Powered Healthcare Assistance

VitalCare integrates AI concepts similar to Gemini’s capabilities by enabling:

🎤 2. Multimodal Interaction (Text + Voice + Documents)

Gemini AI focuses on multimodal intelligence, and VitalCare mirrors this approach:

🧠 3. Intelligent Decision Support System

VitalCare uses AI-driven logic to support decision-making in healthcare workflows:

Risk score generation from patient vitals
Health trend analysis and insights
Smart recommendations for hospitals and healthcare schemes
Context-aware responses from AI assistant

VitalCare simulates an AI agent-like ecosystem, similar to Gemini-powered systems:

Emergency detection → alert propagation → response coordination

This demonstrates a multi-agent healthcare coordination system powered by AI reasoning layers.

⚡ 5. Enhanced with External AI Integration (Sarvam AI + AI Layer Design)

While Gemini focuses on advanced AI capabilities, VitalCare extends this idea by:

Ensuring scalability for next-gen AI models
🏁 Conclusion

VitalCare fits the Gemini AI track because it demonstrates:

✔ Multimodal AI interaction (text, voice, documents)
✔ Intelligent healthcare decision support
✔ Real-world AI-driven workflows
✔ Scalable architecture ready for advanced LLM integration

“VitalCare acts as a practical implementation of how Gemini-like AI systems can transform healthcare into an intelligent, accessible, and connected ecosystem.”

**Open Innovation**

VitalCare embodies Open Innovation by combining AI, healthcare, accessibility, and community-driven services into a unified ecosystem. The platform is designed to solve practical healthcare problems while remaining extensible for future integrations such as ambulance tracking, remote monitoring, and AI-driven healthcare agents.
