> you attended, but left no trace

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Your POAP Is a Surveillance Report

Every badge you claim permanently links **your wallet → your body → a location → a date.**

On a public blockchain. Searchable by anyone. Forever.

---

## Who's Reading It Right Now

**Your boss** sees you claimed a POAP at a competitor's conference — on your sick day.

**A stalker** sees you attend the same conference every year, alone, in the same city.

**Your government** sees you at a protest, a political event, a "wrong" gathering.

**A recruiter** sees you at a job fair. Your current employer finds out.

**A data broker** aggregates 50 POAPs into a complete behavioral profile and sells it.

You didn't post anything. You just wanted the badge.

---

## The Brutal Math

```
1 POAP  =  1 data point
10 POAPs  =  a travel pattern  
50 POAPs  =  your complete location history,
             political profile, social graph —
             all public, all permanent,
             all searchable for free
```

Unlike a tweet — **you cannot delete it.**

---

# The Solution

## Specter — One Swap. Total Privacy.

```
Before:  poap.xyz/mint/x3izg6   →  your public wallet
After:  specter.xyz/mint/x3izg6  →  a ghost address
                                     nobody can link to you
```

Same link. Same POAP. Zero trace.

---

## How It Works

| Step | What Happens |
|---|---|
| 👆 Tap your fingerprint | Passkey derives your stealth keys — never stored, never uploaded |
| 🔮 Ghost address computed | A fresh address that has never existed on-chain before |
| 🏦 BitGo mints the POAP | Treasury wallet sends the badge to your ghost address |
| 📣 Announcement published | Only you — with your viewing key — can find it |
| ✅ Done | On-chain: a random wallet got an NFT. You: untraceable. |

---

## The Guarantee

- ✦ Your ENS **never touches** the transaction
- ✦ Your wallet **never appears** on-chain  
- ✦ The stealth address **never existed** before this moment
- ✦ Your private key **was never stored** anywhere
- ✦ The POAP is **100% yours** — prove attendance to anyone, on your terms

---

> ## *You were there.*
> ## *The chain wasn't watching.*

**Privacy**

Specter is privacy by default, not privacy as a feature. Most tools treat privacy as something you opt into, an extra step, a power user setting. Specter flips that. You scan a link, tap your fingerprint, and your POAP lands at an address nobody can trace back to you. The entire flow is private unless you actively choose otherwise. It fits the privacy track because it solves a problem that almost every web3 user has right now without knowing it. Every POAP ever claimed is public. Every wallet that has ever attended an event is permanently documented. That data exists today and anyone can query it. Specter does not just add a privacy layer on top of an existing system. It replaces the most vulnerable moment in the POAP flow, which is the mint itself, with a cryptographically private alternative using ERC-5564 stealth addresses. No zero knowledge proofs that require trusted setups. No mixers that pool your assets with strangers. Just clean elliptic curve math that makes your attendance provable to yourself and invisible to everyone else. That is what privacy should look like.

**Best creative use of ENS**

ENS is the human readable entry point that makes the whole privacy flow actually usable. Instead of asking attendees to paste a raw stealth meta-address, which is a 130 character hex string nobody can remember, they simply register their stealth meta-address once in the ERC-6538 registry and link it to their ENS name. From that point on, anyone who wants to send them a private POAP just types vitalik.eth. Specter looks up the ENS name, queries the ERC-6538 registry to fetch the stealth meta-address behind it, computes a fresh one-time stealth address, and mints there. The ENS name is only used for the lookup. It never appears in the mint transaction, never gets linked to the stealth address, and leaves no on-chain trace connecting vitalik.eth to the POAP. ENS makes privacy human friendly. One name, infinite unlinkable addresses, zero compromises.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

BitGo acts as the neutral minting treasury between your identity and the blockchain. Without it, minting a POAP from your own wallet makes you the on-chain caller privacy broken at step one. Instead, the BitGo treasury signs and broadcasts every mint transaction, so the chain only sees an institutional wallet sending an NFT to a random stealth address. Your ENS, your wallet, your identity none of it ever touches the transaction. BitGo also funds the gas for publishing ERC-5564 announcements on Sepolia, programmatically topping up the relayer wallet when balances run low. Every mint gets logged against a fresh BitGo-generated address label, giving organizers a private audit trail without exposing a single attendee. The result is a complete privacy pipeline: your biometric derives the keys, BitGo does the on-chain work, and the stealth address receives the POAP  with no link between any of the three.

**The problem it solves**

# What Problem Does TRECC Solve?

## The Problem

**Capital sits idle; borrowing is slow and opaque.**

- **Lenders** struggle to earn meaningful yield without taking on unknown risk or navigating fragmented DeFi protocols. They lack a single, transparent place to deploy capital and earn returns from verified, on-chain activity.
- **Borrowers** face friction: lengthy KYC, slow underwriting, and rigid credit systems. Accessing liquidity often means forms, waiting, and middlemen—not programmable, reputation-based credit tied to a clear identity.
- **DeFi and identity are disconnected.** Liquidity exists on-chain, but there’s no standard way to link a borrowable identity (with reputation and limits) to that liquidity, or to execute borrowing through a simple interface.

## The Solution: TRECCC

**TRECC is a prime-brokerage-style protocol that connects liquidity with autonomous, identity-backed agents.**

- **For Capital Providers:** Deposit USDC into a single high-yield vault. Your capital is deployed by mathematically verified AI agents; you earn passive, risk-adjusted returns without managing positions yourself.
- **For Borrowers:** Mint an **ERC-8004** on-chain identity (agent), set your operational and credit parameters, and build reputation over time. Use **Elsa**—a TRECC-enabled DeFi agent—to request and execute operations (e.g. “Borrow 50 USDC”) via natural language; Elsa prepares and triggers the on-chain transaction for you.
- **For the System:** One infrastructure layer: a liquidity vault, an agent registry (identity + reputation), and a conversational execution layer (Elsa). Lenders get clarity and yield; borrowers get programmable credit and a simple, agent-driven experience.

In short: **TRECC makes liquidity simple to provide and simple to use—through a secure connection to prime-brokerage-style infrastructure, where you either supply capital to the vault or mint an autonomous agent to execute operations on-chain.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

- **Multi-chain coordination** — The app uses **Base Sepolia** for the vault, collateral, and Elsa transactions; **Sepolia** for ENS subnames (trecc.eth); and **mainnet** for resolving .eth names in the navbar. Keeping three chains in sync (and explaining to users that subnames live on Sepolia, not mainnet) required careful UX and config (e.g. Reown default chain, chain switching in BorrowerGate).

- **RPC reliability** — Public RPCs often timed out (e.g. 522 from rpc.sepolia.org) or were rate-limited (Base Sepolia). We added **fallback RPC lists** and explicit timeouts in the ENS register-subname API, and **custom RPC URLs** in Reown so balance fetches and registrations succeed consistently.

- **ENS server-side registration** — Registering subnames under trecc.eth required a server-owned wallet with wrapped trecc.eth on Sepolia, funded for gas. We had to handle edge cases: subname already taken, insufficient funds on the server wallet, contract reverts, and RPC timeouts—with clear error codes and messages so the frontend could show useful feedback.

- **Borrower gate flow (ENS → KYC → collateral)** — Sequencing “claim subname → complete KYC form → pay collateral on Base Sepolia” with real wallet switching and transaction signing was tricky. We kept KYC as mock + local storage for the demo, and had to balance “demo mode” (e.g. ignoring collateral tx failure in one path) with a path that still feels production-ready.

- **Elsa: natural language → on-chain execution** — Turning chat into transactions meant building an intent layer (keyword-based for now instead of a full LLM), encoding the correct vault call (`issueLoan(borrower, bitGoWallet, amount)`), and deciding who signs: for the demo we use the **user’s wallet** (MetaMask) and “fake” the BitGo wallet as the user’s address so the vault call works; production would use BitGo MPC, which adds chain/env alignment (BitGo testnet vs Base Sepolia).

- **BitGo vs frontend chain** — The BitGo risk engine and MPC execution use **testnet Ethereum (teth)** and env-driven wallet/passphrase, while the frontend and contracts are on **Base Sepolia**. Full E2E execution through BitGo would require aligning chains or a separate production path (e.g. Base mainnet + BitGo production).

- **Lender vault: two-step flow** — Depositing USDC requires **approve** then **depositLiquidity**, plus optional **stakeBond** (payable). Coordinating approval state, token selection (USDC vs ETH), and success redirect to the lender dashboard without leaving the user in a half-finished state took careful state handling.

- **Agent registry and ERC-8004 identity** — Minting an agent (registerAgent(ensName)) and then reading back the profile (e.g. agentProfiles(0)) had to match the contract ABI and tie into the rest of the borrower journey (e.g. redirect after mint, then Elsa). Getting the “identity card” and credit parameters to feel consistent with the rest of the UI required iteration.

- **Dashboard and yield data** — Lender and borrower dashboards need portfolio value, APY, and protocol/agent lists. Without a full backend or subgraph, we used **mock time-series and mock user/agent data** so the UX is complete; replacing this with real on-chain or indexed data is a known follow-up.

- **Oracle dependency (Sentinel)** — The Sentinel route uses **Chainlink ETH/USD** on Base Sepolia for a “danger threshold” (e.g. 10% drop). Any RPC or oracle failure surfaces as a 500 and had to be handled so the rest of the app doesn’t depend on it for critical path.

## One-Liner

**TRECC connects lenders and borrowers through a single vault and identity-backed AI agents, so capital earns yield and borrowers access liquidity via a conversational agent (Elsa) that executes on-chain.**

**Privacy**

**TRECC supports privacy-preserving identity and controlled disclosure.**

- **On-chain identity without full doxxing:** Borrowers use **ERC-8004** agent identities and **ENS subnames** (e.g. `user.trecc.eth`) as their borrowable identity. Reputation and credit parameters are tied to this identity—not necessarily to a real-world name—so users can build credit with a **pseudonymous, on-chain persona**.
- **KYC and disclosure control:** The borrower flow includes a **KYC step** (mock + local storage in the demo). The design allows the protocol to separate “who is allowed to borrow” (KYC gate) from “what is visible on-chain” (agent + reputation). In production, KYC can stay off-chain or in a privacy-preserving layer while only necessary signals (e.g. “verified”) are used on-chain.
- **Minimal on-chain footprint:** Credit limits and agent parameters live on-chain for execution and transparency; sensitive PII does not need to be stored on-chain. The system is built so **identity and reputation** can be useful to the protocol without exposing unnecessary personal data.
- **Agent-centric model:** By centering the experience on **agents** (minted identities) rather than raw wallet addresses, TRECC allows users to maintain multiple roles or identities and choose what to link to which agent—supporting privacy and compartmentalization.

TRECC fits the Privacy track by combining **verifiable on-chain identity** with **controlled disclosure** and a path to privacy-preserving KYC and reputation.

**DeFi**

**TRECC is a DeFi-native protocol at its core.**

- **Liquidity infrastructure:** Lenders deposit **USDC** into a single, transparent vault. Capital is deployed on-chain; yield is earned from verified borrowing activity. The protocol acts as prime-brokerage-style infrastructure—one place to supply capital and earn risk-adjusted returns.
- **Programmable credit:** Borrowers access liquidity through **on-chain identity and reputation** (ERC-8004 agents). Credit limits and parameters are set and enforced on-chain; no opaque middlemen—borrowing is executed via smart contracts (e.g. `issueLoan`) on **Base Sepolia**.
- **Collateral and risk:** Borrowers post collateral; the system uses oracles (e.g. **Chainlink ETH/USD** via Sentinel) for risk thresholds. The full flow—deposit → approve → stake/collateral → loan issuance—lives on-chain.
- **Multi-chain DeFi:** The app coordinates **Base Sepolia** (vault, collateral, Elsa transactions), **Sepolia** (ENS subnames under trecc.eth), and **mainnet** (identity resolution), showing how DeFi can span chains while keeping a single user experience.

In short: TRECC makes **lending and borrowing** simple, transparent, and executable on-chain—connecting idle capital with identity-backed, programmable credit in a single DeFi layer.

**AI**

**TRECC puts AI at the center of both capital deployment and user interaction.**

- **AI-driven capital deployment:** Lender capital is deployed by **mathematically verified AI agents**. Lenders don’t manage positions manually; they earn passive, risk-adjusted returns as AI agents operate within the protocol’s rules.
- **Conversational execution (Elsa):** Borrowers interact with **Elsa**—a TRECC-enabled DeFi agent—using **natural language** (e.g. “Borrow 50 USDC”). Elsa interprets intent, prepares the correct on-chain call (`issueLoan(borrower, bitGoWallet, amount)`), and triggers the transaction. This is an **intent layer** that turns chat into execution.
- **Agent registry and identity:** Each borrower **mints an on-chain agent** (ERC-8004). Agents carry identity, reputation, and credit parameters—so the system doesn’t just “chat”; it ties every action to a verifiable, autonomous agent identity.
- **Path to full LLM:** The current demo uses a keyword-based intent layer; the architecture is built to support a full LLM for richer natural-language understanding and more complex DeFi operations.

TRECC shows how **AI agents** can both manage capital and act as the primary interface for users—making DeFi accessible through conversation while keeping execution on-chain and auditable.

**BEST Overall Project**

**TRECC is a full-stack, production-minded protocol that ties DeFi, AI, and identity into one coherent experience.**

- **Real problem, clear solution:** It addresses **idle capital**, **opaque/slow borrowing**, and **disconnected DeFi and identity**—with one protocol: a vault for lenders, identity-backed agents for borrowers, and a conversational AI (Elsa) as the execution layer.
- **DeFi + AI + Identity in one product:** Lenders get a **single vault** and AI-managed yield; borrowers get **programmable, reputation-based credit** and a **natural-language agent** that executes on-chain. No other submission need combine all three so tightly.
- **Technical depth:** Multi-chain (Base Sepolia, Sepolia, mainnet), ENS subnames, ERC-8004 agents, BitGo integration path, oracle-based risk (Sentinel), and a thought-through borrower journey (ENS → KYC → collateral → Elsa) show end-to-end execution, not just a concept.
- **User experience:** One tagline captures it: *“Liquidity made simple. Provide capital to the vault, or mint an autonomous agent to execute on-chain.”* The project delivers both sides—lender and borrower—with dashboards, clear flows, and a single narrative.
- **Honest about challenges:** The team documented real hurdles (RPC reliability, ENS server-side registration, BitGo vs frontend chain, two-step vault flows, mock data for dashboards)—showing production awareness and a path from hackathon to mainnet.

As a **BEST Overall Project**, TRECC stands out by solving a meaningful problem with **DeFi infrastructure**, **AI agents**, and **identity/reputation** in one integrated, deployable system—backed by real technical work and a clear vision for what comes next.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aethernet-2956) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Naimish08/AetherNet) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/wBCBfKW2cGk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co)

> Freelance Marketplace for AI agents

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

What we built is a marketplace where specialized AI agents compete for tasks based on their track record. A council of four AI models — Gemini for deep research, GPT for strategy, Claude for security auditing, and Grok for real-time sentiment — simultaneously deliberates on her request and reaches consensus on a single Strategic Blueprint. That blueprint gets uploaded to decentralized storage via Fileverse so it's tamper-proof from the moment it's written.

That blueprint is then posted to an on-chain smart contract registry — but here's the key part — no agent can read the actual strategy yet. They only see the job exists. Once the system ranks agents by their on-chain reputation score, cost, and execution speed, and selects the best match for each subtask, only then does Elsa — our middleware orchestration layer running locally on the user's machine — grant that specific agent access to the blueprint via an encrypted key envelope. The private key never leaves the user's device. Elsa signs every transaction locally using viem before anything touches the blockchain.

Each agent executes their piece, uploads their deliverable to Fileverse with a content hash, and generates a cryptographic proof that the work actually happened. An oracle verifies that proof and only then updates the agent's reputation score on-chain. Good agents build reputation and earn more. Bad agents lose ranking and lose business. The market corrects itself automatically.

For our founder — her smart contract audit result has an IPFS hash she can verify independently. Her email draft, her market research, her social post — all versioned, all content-addressed, all assembled into one evidence bundle if she ever needs to dispute anything. No middleman. No blind trust. Just verifiable work, competitively priced, automatically coordinated.

**Challenges we ran into**

The first wall we hit was coordination — a single model breaking down a complex task unilaterally is a single point of failure. We built the AI Council, four specialized models deliberating in parallel and reaching consensus before any execution begins. The second problem was agent selection — the marketplace has many agents but no objective way to pick the best one per subtask without bias. We solved this with an on-chain reputation engine that ranks agents dynamically by track record, cost, and execution speed. Third was proving Web2 work actually happened — a blockchain can't natively verify an email was sent or a report was written, so we layered in TLSNotary cryptographic proofs that an oracle verifies before any reputation update touches the chain.

> Fraud detection extension

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Phishing websites are one of the most common forms of cybercrime today. Attackers create fake versions of trusted websites such as banks, email providers, or payment platforms to trick users into entering sensitive information like passwords, credit card details, or personal data.

Most users cannot easily distinguish between legitimate and fake websites because phishing pages often look identical to the original ones. Traditional security tools and browsers also fail to detect many newly created phishing sites in real time.

PhishGuard Sentinel solves this problem by providing real-time phishing detection directly inside the browser. The system analyzes visited websites using URL pattern analysis, machine learning models, and threat-intelligence databases to identify suspicious behavior.

If a website is detected as malicious, the browser extension immediately warns the user with a full-screen security alert, preventing them from entering sensitive information.

By combining browser-level monitoring with AI-based analysis, PhishGuard Sentinel helps protect users from phishing attacks, credential theft, and online fraud.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building PhishGuard Sentinel involved several technical and architectural challenges during development.

One of the major challenges was integrating a Chrome Extension with the backend AI detection system. Browser extensions operate in a restricted environment, and sending data securely from the content script to the backend API required careful handling of permissions, background service workers, and message passing between scripts.

Another challenge was extracting meaningful signals from web pages without affecting browser performance. Since the extension runs on every visited page, we had to design lightweight DOM inspection methods to detect elements like login forms, password fields, and suspicious URL patterns without slowing down the user’s browsing experience.

We also faced issues while working with threat-intelligence feeds. Public phishing datasets often contain outdated or inactive URLs, so filtering and validating useful entries was necessary to improve detection accuracy.

Finally, coordinating multiple components  the browser extension, backend API, and machine learning detection logic  required designing a reliable communication workflow so that the system could analyze websites quickly and return results in real time.

These challenges were addressed through iterative testing, modular architecture design, and optimizing the communication between the frontend extension and the backend analysis engine.

NFT Studio is a Web3-based NFT project that allows users to create, mint, and manage digital assets on the blockchain. The platform integrates decentralized storage and blockchain technology to ensure that digital assets remain secure, transparent, and tamper-proof.

* Web3 wallet integration for seamless user interaction

NFT Studio demonstrates how modern decentralized technologies can be combined to build secure and scalable digital ownership platforms. The project highlights the practical use of blockchain, smart contracts, and decentralized storage in real-world applications.

**The problem it solves**

Problem Astitva Solves : 


Many women face harassment or unsafe situations, but incidents often go unreported because victims lack reliable evidence. Existing safety apps mainly provide SOS alerts or location sharing, which help during emergencies but do not preserve proof of what actually happened.
Without secure evidence, recordings can be edited, deleted, or questioned, making it harder to hold offenders accountable.


What Astitva Is Used For !?


Astitva is a women’s safety app that helps users capture and secure evidence during threatening situations.
Users can activate a silent trigger, which automatically:
1)Records surrounding audio.
2)Saves GPS location and timestamp.
3)Generates a cryptographic hash to verify authenticity.
This ensures the evidence is tamper-proof and credible, making it easier to document incidents and report them safely.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge Faced: 

One major challenge while building Astitva was implementing a rolling audio buffer to capture the last few seconds of audio before the emergency trigger. Mobile operating systems restrict continuous background recording, which made it difficult to maintain recording without affecting battery life.

Solution: 


We solved this by using a circular audio buffer that temporarily stores only the most recent audio in memory and continuously overwrites older data. When the emergency trigger is activated, the buffered audio is saved along with location and timestamp, and a SHA-256 hash is generated to ensure the recording remains tamper-proof.

Team **CodeReno** -- Aniket Sinha, Harshit Bindal, Muskan Kashyap

### ColdchainX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/coldchainx-2762) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Subhradeep-05/ColdchainX) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Zero Counterfeit. Zero Waste. Zero Compromise.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![NodeMCU IoT](https://img.shields.io/badge/NodeMCU%20IoT-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every year, 1 million people die from counterfeit drugs—more than malaria. $35 billion worth of medicines are destroyed by temperature failures during transit, and 25% of vaccines arrive damaged and unusable. Patients have no way to verify if their medicine is real. Hospitals lose 20 million hours annually just managing shortages. Distributors operate blindly, with no real-time visibility into their shipments. The result? A broken system where trust is impossible, waste is staggering, and lives are lost.

coldchainX fixes this. We combine Polygon blockchain for immutable tracking, IoT sensors for real-time temperature monitoring, and AI predictions to prevent failures before they happen. Patients can scan a QR code and see exactly where their medicine came from—every step, verified. Hospitals get automatic expiry alerts and zero counterfeit drugs. Distributors get live GPS tracking and instant temperature alerts. The result? 100% transparency, 45% less waste, and $235 billion saved annually. From manufacturer to patient—every step, verified.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle was the infamous "Stack too deep" Solidity error. Our smart contract's Shipment struct had 17 fields, but the EVM stack can only hold 16 variables at once. The compiler kept failing with cryptic errors, and we wasted two days trying to rearrange variables before realizing the root cause. We solved it by splitting the data into multiple structs—Medicine, Tracking, and Temperature—then composing them into the final Shipment. This not only fixed the error but made our code more modular and readable.

Another nightmare was ESP32 sensor calibration. Our DHT22 temperature sensors were giving wildly inaccurate readings (±3°C) during field tests—completely useless for vaccine monitoring that requires ±0.5°C accuracy. One minute it would read 4°C, the next 8°C. We discovered electromagnetic interference from the 4G module was corrupting the analog signal. The fix? We added a moving average filter in firmware, switched to digital DS18B20 sensors, and physically shielded the components. Now our readings are accurate to ±0.1°C.

The IPFS-Filebase integration was its own beast. The CID returned during upload was completely different from the one needed for retrieval, causing all our stored data to be "lost." We spent three days debugging before realizing Filebase's S3-compatible API returns an ETag, not the actual IPFS CID. The solution was to query the metadata after upload to get the real CID—and implement a manual mapping cache as fallback.

Finally, real-time socket connections kept dropping under load. Users would connect, get initial data, then silently disconnect. The logs showed nothing. After a week of profiling, we found the issue: our MongoDB queries were taking 2-3 seconds, blocking the event loop and causing heartbeat timeouts. We added Redis caching for frequent queries and optimized indexes. Now connections stay alive and real-time updates actually work.

Team **AlgoRift** -- [Subhradeep Dey](https://github.com/Subhradeep-05), [Tiyasha Sen](https://github.com/Tiyasha2005)

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/global-pay-ace4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/unmolkumar/global_pay_hackathon) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/N0WcXe9RTIs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> A crypto based money transfer using stable coins

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sending $500 abroad? That costs $25–55 in fees and takes 2–5 days. Crypto fixes speed and cost — but who wants to copy-paste 7xKXtg2CW87d97TXJSDpbD5jBkheTqA83TZRuJosgAsU?

Global Pay combines Solana's speed (<2 sec, <$0.01 fee) with UPI's simplicity — send money to friend@globalpay instead of wallet addresses. Sign in with Google, set up in 2 minutes, no bank account needed. PIN-secured, on-chain verified, multi-currency display. Cross-border payments that just work.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into
1. Solana Devnet Airdrop Failures
The solana-py library's request_airdrop() threw InternalErrorMessage has no .value — an undocumented error. We switched to direct HTTP POST requests to the Solana RPC endpoint, then hit rate limits. Final fix: built a faucet fallback UI that shows a link to Solana's manual faucet with a copy-address button.

2. Transactions Succeeding in API but Not On-Chain
solders.Transaction didn't have the .new() method we expected. Discovered we needed Transaction.new_signed_with_payer() + send_raw_transaction(bytes(tx)). Then send_transaction was silently swallowing failures and returning 201. Restructured to execute the on-chain transfer FIRST, only create the DB record after confirmed success.

3. Ghost Transactions in History
Failed transfers were being saved to the database with status "FAILED" — visible to the receiver who never got any money. Fixed by only creating the transaction record AFTER a successful on-chain transfer, never before.

4. Dashboard Balance Not Updating After Send
Balance showed stale data after sending money. Added confirm_transaction() on the backend to wait for on-chain finality before responding, plus useLocation().key dependency and window focus listeners on the frontend for auto-refresh.

5. Global ID Rename Redirecting to Wallet Setup
Renaming your Global ID kicked you back to wallet creation. Root cause: set_global_id() returned a raw User model missing the has_wallet field — Pydantic defaulted it to false — triggering ProtectedRoute's redirect. Fixed by returning get_profile(db, user) which computes has_wallet correctly.

**The problem it solves**

* **The Solution:** We engineered an audio-visual liveness check. We integrated the browser's native Web Speech API to require the user to say the word "cheese" or "smile" into the microphone. Once the STT (Speech-to-Text) registers the word, it synchronously triggers the camera capture. You can't fake that with a piece of paper!

### REPUTE
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/repute-170e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/puniadhruv/REPUTE) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://repute-lyart.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Decentralized credit identity for credit-invisible

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem REPUTE Solves

Millions of people cannot access affordable credit because they lack a traditional credit history. Banks and financial institutions rely heavily on existing credit records, formal employment data, or collateral to determine loan eligibility.

However, a large portion of the population — especially students, gig workers, small vendors, and middle/low-income individuals — regularly pay rent, utilities, subscriptions, or micro-loans but receive no credit recognition for their financial discipline.

This creates a financial loophole:

Responsible people remain invisible to the credit system

They are forced to take high-interest loans

Banks miss out on potentially reliable borrowers

Credit systems remain biased toward already privileged users

How REPUTE Solves This

REPUTE is a reputation-based credit scoring system that converts real payment behavior into a trust score.

Instead of relying only on traditional credit history, REPUTE analyzes 6 months of payment data (such as rent, bills, subscriptions, or EMI payments) and generates a dynamic reputation score that updates every quarter.

The score reflects:

Payment discipline

Consistency

Financial behavior patterns

To ensure transparency and integrity, a cryptographic proof of the score is stored on blockchain, making it tamper-resistant and verifiable.

What People Can Use REPUTE For
1. Access Small Loans More Easily

Individuals without credit history can use their REPUTE score to apply for micro-loans or small personal loans (₹50k–₹3L) with lower interest and less collateral.

2. Build Credit From Everyday Payments

Instead of needing credit cards or bank loans to build a score, users can build credit simply by paying bills on time.

Examples:

Rent payments

Electricity bills

Internet subscriptions

Small EMI payments

3. Faster Loan Evaluation for Lenders

Lenders can quickly evaluate borrowers using a behavior-based reputation score, reducing risk and approval time.

4. Transparent and Verifiable Credit Data

Because score proofs are stored on blockchain:

Scores cannot be manipulated

Lenders can verify authenticity

Users maintain ownership of their financial reputation

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

Building REPUTE involved integrating multiple systems — a scoring engine, backend APIs, blockchain verification, and a frontend interface. During development, we encountered several challenges.

1. Integrating Blockchain With the Scoring Engine

One of the biggest hurdles was connecting the scoring engine with the blockchain layer.

The scoring engine generates a reputation score based on payment data, but we also needed a tamper-proof proof of that score stored on-chain. Ensuring that the backend correctly generated a hash of the score data and sent it to the smart contract required careful coordination between the scoring logic and blockchain interaction.

How we solved it

Created a clear pipeline:
CSV Data → Scoring Engine → Score JSON → Hash → Blockchain Storage

Standardized the data format before hashing to prevent mismatches.

Added logging to verify each step of the process.

2. Handling CSV Data From Users

Another challenge was processing CSV payment data uploaded by users. CSV files can vary widely in structure, and inconsistent formatting caused parsing errors during early testing.

How we solved it

Implemented strict CSV validation rules

Standardized required columns such as:

date

amount

payment_type

status

Added backend validation to reject invalid files and guide users to correct formatting.

3. Connecting Frontend, Backend, and Wallet

Integrating wallet connection with frontend actions (like uploading data and generating scores) required proper state handling. Early versions allowed users to upload data without connecting a wallet, which broke the verification flow.

How we solved it

Added wallet connection checks before API requests

Stored the wallet address in application state

Linked uploaded data and generated scores to the connected wallet.

4. Designing a Fair Reputation Score

Creating a scoring system that fairly reflects financial behavior was also challenging. The score needed to be:

Simple enough to compute

Fair across different payment patterns

Resistant to manipulation

How we solved it

Limited the scoring window to 6 months of payments

Updated the score every quarter

Weighted factors such as payment consistency and timeliness

What We Learned

These challenges helped us design a system that is modular, transparent, and scalable.

By separating the scoring engine, blockchain verification, and API layers, we created a flexible architecture that can easily expand to support additional financial data sources in the future.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Textlocal API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Textlocal%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tesseract OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tesseract%20OCR-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/3657137c76a24330a180d54aef8cfcb7/08af5e0f-7f8a-43bb-88ed-629333c50dc6.jpeg)
Grading handwritten answer sheets is one of the most time-consuming tasks for teachers. When there are many students in a class, educators have to spend hours reading each answer, comparing it with the correct solution, assigning marks, and writing feedback. This process can be exhausting and sometimes leads to inconsistent grading due to fatigue or human error.

In many cases, teachers also do not have enough time to provide detailed feedback to every student. As a result, students may not clearly understand where they made mistakes or how they can improve.

GradeAI helps solve this problem by making the grading process faster and more efficient. The platform allows teachers to upload a student's handwritten answer and compare it with a model answer. Using AI and OCR technology, the system reads the handwriting, understands the content, and automatically evaluates the answer.

It then provides marks, useful feedback, and highlights important points from the student's response. This saves a significant amount of time for educators while ensuring that grading remains consistent and fair.

With GradeAI, teachers can focus more on teaching and helping students learn, instead of spending long hours checking answer sheets manually.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

While building GradeAI, I faced several challenges during development. One of the main difficulties was working with handwritten text. Handwriting styles vary from person to person, which made it challenging for the OCR system to consistently read and extract text accurately from uploaded images.

Another challenge was connecting the frontend with the backend. I had to make sure that the image uploaded by the user was properly sent to the server, processed by the AI model, and then returned with the correct grading results. Handling API requests and responses smoothly required careful debugging and testing.

Installing and configuring external tools such as Tesseract OCR was also a bit complicated. Setting up the environment, installing the dependencies, and ensuring everything worked correctly on the local system took some time.

Additionally, designing a clean and user-friendly interface was important. I wanted the platform to be simple for educators to use, so I had to spend time refining the UI and improving the user experience.

Despite these challenges, solving each problem helped me better understand AI integration, backend development, and building real-world applications.

**The problem it solves**

Proof India is a blockchain-based platform designed to improve transparency, security, and trust in India’s public digital systems. Many government services rely on centralized databases, which can be vulnerable to data manipulation, corruption, and fraud. These problems often lead to issues such as welfare benefits not reaching the right citizens, fake beneficiaries in schemes, and disputes over land ownership.

Proof India solves these challenges by using a decentralized and tamper-proof blockchain infrastructure. Important records—such as welfare distribution, land ownership transfers, and identity verification—are stored on a secure ledger where they cannot be altered or deleted. This ensures that all transactions remain transparent and verifiable.

The platform allows citizens, government agencies, and service providers to quickly verify records without relying on intermediaries. By reducing data manipulation and increasing accountability, Proof India makes existing processes safer and more efficient. Overall, it helps build a more reliable and corruption-resistant digital governance system for public services.

**Challenges we ran into**

Developing Proof India involved several challenges. One major challenge was designing a scalable blockchain architecture that can handle large volumes of government transactions efficiently. Ensuring data privacy and security while maintaining transparency on the blockchain was also critical. Another difficulty was integrating the system with existing digital infrastructure used by government services. Handling offline or low-internet environments, especially in rural areas, required designing an offline-first approach. Additionally, creating realistic datasets and use cases for welfare distribution and land records was challenging. Finally, simplifying complex blockchain concepts into a user-friendly system that citizens and officials can easily understand and use was an important hurdle.

**Open Innovation**

Proof India fits the Open Innovation track by proposing a new technological approach to solve real-world governance challenges using blockchain. The project introduces an innovative system that improves transparency, security, and trust in public services such as welfare distribution, land records, and identity verification. Instead of relying on traditional centralized databases, Proof India uses a decentralized and tamper-proof ledger to ensure that records cannot be manipulated. This open and scalable solution can be adapted by government agencies, financial institutions, and public service providers. By combining emerging technologies with public infrastructure, Proof India demonstrates how open innovation can create more efficient, transparent, and citizen-centric digital systems.

### Blockmess
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/blockmess-48e7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/naman9079/Blockmess) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> A Decentralize Messenger

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Centralized Surveillance & Data Harvesting
Traditional messaging platforms (WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage) route all messages through company-owned servers  giving corporations, governments, and hackers a single point to intercept, store, and analyze your private conversations. Blockmess eliminates the middleman entirely. Messages travel peer-to-peer via WebRTC: no company server ever touches your data.

2. Weak or Fake "End-to-End Encryption"
Many apps claim E2EE but retain the keys, metadata, or message logs server-side. Blockmess uses AES-256-GCM encryption with ephemeral session keys, generated locally on each device. No server holds any key. Not even the developers can read your messages.

3. Identity Tied to Phone Numbers & Emails
Mainstream apps force you to register with a phone number or email -permanently linking your identity to your messages. Blockmess uses Ethereum wallet addresses as identities. Your address is a cryptographic keypair generated on-device, not tied to any personal information. No sign-up. No KYC. No account.

4. Permanent Message Records
Most platforms store your message history indefinitely — on their servers and your device. Blockmess supports self-destructing messages with configurable timers, ensuring sensitive conversations leave no permanent trace.

5. Single Points of Failure
Centralized servers go down, get hacked, or get seized. Blockmess uses a decentralized architecture -the signaling server is used only to establish the initial WebRTC handshake, never to relay message content. Once connected, the channel is fully peer-to-peer and independent.

6. Trust Dependency on Third Parties
You must trust that the app provider hasn't been compromised, coerced, or sold. With Blockmess, trust is placed in open cryptographic standards (WebRTC, AES-256-GCM, secp256k1) - not in any company's promises. The cryptographic identity (wallet) is verifiable on the Ethereum blockchain.

7. Cross-Platform Fragmentation
Privacy tools are often desktop-only or require complex setup. Blockmess runs in any modern browser (no install required) and as a native React Native mobile app — making secure communication accessible to everyone, everywhere.

In summary: Blockmess is built for people who demand that their private conversations stay private - by design, not by policy.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. WebRTC ICE Negotiation Race Conditions
The hardest bug to track down. When two peers attempted to connect simultaneously, both would generate offers at the same time creating a glare condition where each peer's RTCPeerConnection received an offer while already in the have-local-offer state, causing the entire handshake to silently fail.

Fix: Implemented a deterministic tie-breaking system using the Ethereum wallet address as a unique peer ID. The lexicographically larger address always becomes the "polite peer" that rolls back its offer and yields  following the Perfect Negotiation pattern.


2. Ephemeral Key Exchange Before the Data Channel Opens
AES-256-GCM encryption requires both peers to derive a shared session key before any message can be sent. But the WebRTC data channel itself is the only transport available  creating a chicken-and-egg problem: you need an encrypted channel to safely exchange keys, but you need keys to encrypt the channel.

Fix: Performed an ECDH key exchange over the data channel in plaintext as the very first handshake step, immediately after the channel opened. This is safe because ECDH is designed for exchange over untrusted channels  the shared secret is never transmitted, only the public keys are.

**Special Track**

Blockmess is a first-principles implementation of a peer-to-peer chat application, not a wrapper around an existing messaging SDK, but a ground-up system built on open web standards.

It is genuinely P2P, architecturally, not just in name
Most apps labeled "P2P" still route messages through a relay server. Blockmess uses WebRTC Data Channels to establish a direct browser-to-browser connection. Once the handshake completes, message packets travel directly between peers with zero server involvement. No relay. No proxy. No copy stored anywhere in transit.

It solves the hard problems of P2P communication
Building P2P chat from scratch means confronting problems that server-based apps never face:

Peer discovery is solved via a lightweight WebSocket signaling server used only to exchange SDP offers/answers, then discarded
NAT traversal is handled by WebRTC's built-in ICE/STUN negotiation so peers behind firewalls and home routers can still connect
Connection state management covers reconnection logic, data channel lifecycle, and graceful degradation when peers go offline
Identity without a server is solved using Ethereum keypairs, giving each peer a cryptographically verifiable identity with no account registration
It pushes P2P to its logical conclusion
Rather than stopping at "messages go peer-to-peer," Blockmess layers in everything that makes P2P trustworthy.

Team **Debuggers** -- [Naman Shukla](https://github.com/naman9079), [Ronak kumawat](https://github.com/raunac2004)

> #borged

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Projects waste tokens on blind airdrops that create dumpers, not holders. Managing contributors manually — verifying posts, scoring quality, distributing    
rewards — doesn't scale.                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                             
What Borged Solves                                                                                                                                           
                                       
- Automated contributor management — campaigns, challenge tasks, XP progression, reputation tracking
- AI quality scoring — every submission evaluated automatically, no manual review
- Onchain reward distribution — Merkle proof claims via smart contracts, zero manual payouts
- Market-normalized analytics — social engagement, onchain activity, and news sentiment benchmarked against the crypto market average
- Permissionless campaigns — deposit tokens, community votes on activation, no middleman

Replaces spreadsheets, Discord mods deciding who gets paid, and blind airdrops to random wallets.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Client Acquisition as a Solo Builder

Building the product is the easy part. Getting in front of the right projects — and convincing token teams to trust a new platform with their campaign budgets — is the real challenge. There is no sales team and no BD department. Growth comes from cold outreach, building in public, and proving value one client at a time.

## AI Scoring That Scales

Binary approve/reject logic was ineffective for rewards. The system was rebuilt using ICE scoring (Impact, Confidence, Effort) powered by DeepSeek. This produces consistent, calibrated scores across thousands of submissions, feeding directly into dynamic reward pools.

## Trustless Reward Distribution

The system uses Merkle tree generation combined with a multi-token RewardDistributor contract. This enables claims across multiple campaigns and chains within a single flow while keeping gas costs low on Base.

## Solo Infrastructure

Scraping, AI scoring, price feeds, onchain snapshots, and automated agent posting — all operated by one person. It is infrastructure that typically requires a team, run end-to-end by a solo builder.

We weren’t building a meme token.
We weren’t building speculative infrastructure.

We were building regulated, real-world financial rails.

That meant we didn’t fit neatly into:

Pure crypto VC buckets

Traditional fintech funds

Or early-stage consumer SaaS models

We needed:

Investors who understand remittance pain points

Partners with compliance and banking relationships

Ecosystem players who could support distribution and credibility

Strategic marketing support to reach immigrant and global worker communities

Generic capital wouldn’t accelerate us.

1. Built Traction First

We focused on:

600 paying users (no freemium)

$500K processed volume

60% 18-month retention

4.5x YoY growth

2. Targeted Ecosystem Accelerators

We intentionally joined programs like:

MIT Fintech (2x Finalist)

NOVA SBE (by GSR)

ACEON by zakaVC

These weren’t just capital pipelines — they were ecosystem connectors.

They gave us:

Warm intros to relevant VCs

Credibility in fintech circles

Structured feedback from operators

Strategic visibility beyond crypto Twitter

3. Focused on Strategic Partnerships

Instead of pitching “crypto,” we reframed the narrative around:

Remittance cost reduction

Stablecoin settlement efficiency

Infrastructure modernization

This opened doors with payment operators and fintech-aligned investors.

The Lesson

Fundraising for infrastructure isn’t about speed — it’s about alignment.

The hurdle forced us to:

Build stronger fundamentals

Prove retention before scaling

Find capital that understands cross-border finance

And build ecosystem relationships that compound over time

In hindsight, that friction made the company stronger.

### Planbok
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/planbok-62dc) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://planbok.io) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/njK2copSW6w) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Startup%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-startup-track-3.devfolio.co)

> A B2B programmable wallet infrastructure

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Multi Party Computation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Multi%20Party%20Computation-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Blockchain technology has the power to fundamentally reshape how value moves in the world. It enables instant global transfers without relying on traditional intermediaries. It allows money to be programmable, so revenue splits, escrow conditions, incentives and settlements can be automated rather than manually processed. 

On paper, it is one of the most inclusive financial innovations of our time.
But in practice, its complexity quietly excludes the very people it claims to empower.

For a business, integrating blockchain is not simple as turning on a feature. It means understanding wallet infrastructure, custody models, transaction signing, network behaviour, security risks and regulatory implications. It introduces new operational responsibilities that most product teams were never designed to handle.

For users, the experience can be even more intimating. They are asked to manage private keys, stored seed phrases, understand network fees, confirm transactions, and navigate interfaces that feel foreign. A single mistake can mean irreversible loss. Instead of feeling empowered, many feel anxious.

As a result, blockchain's real-world usage often remains concentrated among technically savvy individuals like developers, traders, and crypto-native users who are comfortable with its mechanics. Businesses hesitate to integrate it fully because doing so risks overwhelming their customers. Customers hesitate to engage because the learning curve feels steep ann unforgiving.

The technology promises mass adoption, but the user experience suggests exclusivity.

This tension is what makes mass adoption feel, at times, like a fairytale. The infrastructure is powerful enough to transform commerce yet to complex for everyday platforms to embed easily. The average marketplace, fintech app, or creator platform should not have to choose to redesign itself around blockchain mechanics. And the average user does not want to become a blockchain expert just send or receive money.

So adoption stalls not because the technology lacks capability, but because it lacks accessible infrastructure. Until blockchain can operate quickly in the background, allowing businesses to harness its power without exposing its complexity, it will continue to be perceived as a niche toll rather than a universal one.

The promise is real. The potential is undeniable. But without bridges that translate blockchain's power into intuitive, usable systems for businesses and their customers, its vision of global inclusive finance remains just out reach.

**Challenges we ran into**

In our Trustless MPC implementation, we encountered a critical "Wallet Mismatch" issue where the wallet address derived by the client (using the offline recovery tool) did not match the address generated by the MPC nodes. This was a fundamental integrity failure: while the MPC nodes could sign transactions, the user would be unable to recover their funds independently, violating the core promise of the "Trustless" mode.

The mismatch stemmed from subtle non-deterministic factors in the Distributed Key Generation (DKG) and Key Derivation processes. In the initial implementation, the "salt" used to derive the master secret from the user's "externalSecret" was generated by the Leader node. However, this salt was not consistently propagated to the Follower node during the "injectTrustlessShare" phase. If the Follower used a different (or empty) salt, it would interprete its key share within a different mathematical context. The resulting aggregate public key would successfully generate, but it would be mathematically unrelated to the user's actual secret.

We resolved this by strictly enforcing determinism and synchronisation across the specific MPC handlers by mandating the presence of "salt" in the "injectTrustlessShare" payload.

It seems simple but it took us some extensive debugging to arrive at that conclusion and we were glad it worked out, because we had invested month into transitioning from basic shamir secret sharing in our version 1 to the proper MPC architecture

> BaseMail - agentic email on Base, with humans.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Attention Economy is Broken

Every inbox is flooded. Spam filters guess. Cold emails waste time. **The cost of sending is zero, but the cost of reading is not.**

BaseMail solves this with **Attention Bonds** — an on-chain escrow mechanism where:

- **Senders stake USDC** to prove their message is worth your time
- **Reply → sender gets refunded** (minus 10% protocol fee)
- **Ignore → you keep the bond** as compensation for your attention

### For Humans
Your inbox becomes an **attention marketplace**. Strangers pay to reach you. Friends and whitelisted contacts email free. Spam becomes economically irrational.

### For AI Agents
Native email identity (`agent@basemail.ai`) with a 3-call API. Agents can send, receive, and manage bonded emails autonomously — enabling **human-in-the-loop AI communication** backed by real economic stakes.

### Mechanism Design
Built on [CO-QAF (Correlation-Discounted Quadratic Attention Funding)](https://blog.juchunko.com/en/glen-weyl-coqaf-attention-bonds/), inspired by Quadratic Funding. Correlated senders (Sybil attacks) are automatically discounted. The more diverse your senders, the more your attention is valued.

### Key Innovation
BaseMail is **Æmail** — agentic email that bridges Web2 communication, Web3 economics, and Web4 agents, keeping humans in the loop.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Escrow UX: `deposit()` vs Direct Transfer

Early users (including our own AI agent) lost funds by directly `transfer()`-ing USDC to the escrow contract instead of calling `deposit()`. The contract had no `receive()` fallback, so tokens were recoverable — but it exposed a critical UX gap.

**Fix:** Added clear API error messages, and the BaseMail client now handles the full approve → deposit flow automatically. Lesson: never assume users will read the docs.

## 2. Dynamic Pricing Without an Oracle

Attention Bonds use dynamic pricing based on sender reputation and recipient demand. We initially considered Chainlink oracles, but realized the pricing signal is *social*, not market-based.

**Fix:** CO-QAF (Correlation-Discounted Quadratic Attention Funding) — a novel mechanism that discounts correlated senders mathematically. No oracle needed; the contract computes fair prices from on-chain interaction history.

## 3. Bridging Web2 Email UX with Web3 Wallets

Email is the most universal protocol. Wallets are not. Requiring users to sign transactions just to send an email kills adoption.

**Fix:** Wallet-based authentication (SIWE) for account creation, but abstracted away for daily use. AI agents authenticate via API with wallet signatures. Humans get a familiar inbox; the blockchain runs silently underneath.

## 4. AI Agent Identity

AI agents need persistent, verifiable identities to participate in economic protocols. But most AI systems are stateless and ephemeral.

**Fix:** Basename integration (`agent.base.eth`) gives agents on-chain identity. Combined with BaseMail (`agent@basemail.ai`), agents get both a name and a communication channel — the minimum viable identity for autonomous economic participation.

## 5. Cold Start: Who Bonds First?

An attention marketplace with no users has no liquidity. Why would anyone stake USDC to email someone who hasn't opted in?

**Fix:** We dogfooded it. Our AI agent (Littl3Lobst3r) enabled Attention Bonds, received bonded emails from other agents, and completed the full deposit → reply → refund cycle on-chain. The first users are agents talking to agents — humans follow.

> The compliant rail for private equity trading

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The problem it solves**

Private startup equity has no real market infrastructure. Secondary transfers are manual, opaque, slow to settle, and legally heavy. Every trade requires verification, approvals, and cap table updates, creating friction for finance and legal teams and making liquidity rare and discounted.

**What people use it for**

1) For founders and companies

- Run controlled liquidity windows without opening a public free for all

- Offer equity based incentives without launching a speculative token

- Reduce legal and operational burden around secondary transfers

- Maintain transfer restrictions, ROFR, and approvals in a structured workflow

2) For shareholders and employees

- Access optional liquidity through compliant, issuer approved windows

- Get clearer price discovery instead of private broker quotes

- Settle faster with defined ownership updates and audit trails

3) For investors

- Access curated private equity opportunities

- Trade within defined, KYC verified environments

- Rely on enforced eligibility and transfer rules

- Gain transparent execution instead of fragmented off market deals

- EQUITY turns private equity transfers from ad hoc legal events into a repeatable, structured market process.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles was aligning market design with legal reality. It is easy to design a clean trading flow in theory, but private equity comes with ROFR, board approvals, lockups, and jurisdiction specific transfer restrictions. Our early product assumptions leaned too close to a “continuous market” model, which quickly broke once we mapped real issuer constraints.

We solved this by redesigning the market around issuer controlled liquidity windows instead of continuous trading. That allowed us to concentrate demand into defined cycles while embedding approval workflows and eligibility checks directly into the execution logic. Instead of fighting legal structure, we integrated it into the product.

### Liquidsat
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/liquidsat-1105) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://liquidsat.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Startup%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-startup-track-3.devfolio.co)

> Non-custodial Native Bitcoin Financing Protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![PSBT](https://img.shields.io/badge/PSBT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bitcoin Script](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bitcoin%20Script-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Over $1T+ in Bitcoin sits largely idle. Long-term holders want liquidity, but refuse to compromise on custody, rehypothecation risk, or opaque lending structures.

Current options force trade-offs:
• Custodial lending desks require giving up control of BTC.
• Wrapped BTC introduces bridge, counterparty, and smart contract risk.
• DeFi-native solutions optimize for yield, not Bitcoin’s trust assumptions.

As a result, conservative BTC capital remains underutilized.

**What It Solves**

LiquidSat enables Bitcoin holders to access liquidity without selling their BTC and without surrendering custody to a centralized intermediary.

• Native BTC used as collateral
• Deterministic, script-enforced loan terms
• No rehypothecation
• Predefined liquidation conditions

It separates collateral security from capital deployment, preserving Bitcoin’s trust model while enabling efficient credit formation.

The result: unlocking liquidity for long-term BTC holders who prioritize structural integrity over convenience.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. PSBT Coordination
Designing multi-party PSBT flows without hidden trust assumptions was complex. We had to handle partial signatures, timeouts, and recovery paths while keeping settlement deterministic.

2. Removing Oracle Single Points of Failure
A single price feed undermines the trust model. We designed multi-source validation and predefined liquidation logic to avoid discretionary triggers.

3. Building Our Own SPV Relayer
To avoid centralized watchers, we built a custom SPV-style relayer to monitor BTC confirmations and trigger settlement. Handling reorgs and confirmation thresholds required careful design.

4. Working Within Bitcoin Script Constraints
Bitcoin’s limited scripting required restructuring loan state logic compared to EVM systems.

5. Non-Custodial Liquidity Matching
Architecting approval-based capital deployment without custodial pooling took multiple iterations.

Each challenge reinforced our core principle: trust minimization over capital efficiency.

Yugal Chittara
