[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ranzr-165c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ON3VoId/RANZR) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://k-tanuj-ranzr.hf.space/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> AI Ransomware Detection Platform

![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Elevenlabs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Elevenlabs-333333?style=flat-square) ![GeminiAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeminiAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem It Solves

As ransomware attacks become increasingly sophisticated and fast-moving, traditional signature-based antivirus solutions are struggling to keep up. Modern malware often evades detection, and when alerts *do* trigger, security teams face immense pressure to quickly determine if it is a genuine threat or a false positive. 

**RANZR** fundamentally addresses three critical challenges in modern incident response while providing a comprehensive suite of advanced defensive features:

1.  **Zero-Day Detection Failures:** Traditional tools miss novel ransomware because they rely on known malware signatures. **RANZR solves this** by using heuristic, behavior-based detection—monitoring endpoints for behaviors characteristic of ransomware (like rapid file modifications, bulk renames, and sudden spikes in file entropy) to catch zero-day threats in the act.
2.  **Alert Fatigue & Cryptic Telemetry:** Analysts waste valuable time deciphering complex logs to understand why an alert fired, delaying response times. **RANZR solves this** by leveraging advanced LLMs (**Google Gemini**) to automatically triage threats and generate plain-English explanations of the anomaly, empowering junior analysts to make faster, more accurate decisions.
3.  **Compromised Chain of Custody:** Highly privileged attackers can tamper with local logs and forensic incident reports to cover their tracks. **RANZR solves this** by generating a forensic PDF report post-incident and mathematically anchoring its SHA-256 cryptographic hash to the **Algorand blockchain**, creating an unassailable, verifiable chain of custody for auditors and legal teams.

---

### Key Features of RANZR

*   **⚡ Real-Time Heuristic Engine:** Continuously monitors file system telemetry, calculating **Shannon Entropy** to distinguish between normal data writes and malicious encryption in progress.
*   **🤖 Gemini AI Threat Triage:** Automatically translates high-velocity technical logs into human-readable summaries, providing instant context on the "Who, What, and Where" of an attack.
*   **🔊 ElevenLabs Voice Alerts:** Bypasses "notification blindness" by triggering high-fidelity, natural language audio warnings for critical threats, ensuring immediate physical awareness in the SOC.
*   **🔗 Blockchain-Anchored Forensics:** Automatically notarizes incident reports on the **Algorand TestNet**, allowing any stakeholder to verify the integrity of the evidence using a unique transaction ID.
*   **💬 Interactive Security Chatbot:** A built-in AI copilot that allows analysts to ask dynamic follow-up questions about suspicious processes or specific file behaviors directly within the dashboard.
*   **📊 Unified Streamlit Dashboard:** A centralized, glassmorphism-inspired interface for real-time endpoint health monitoring, threat history, and automated report verification.
*   **🛡️ Automated Isolation Logic:** Prototype logic to instantly quarantine suspicious processes and prevent lateral movement across the network the moment a threshold is breached.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I Ran Into

Building **RANZR** involved integrating several complex technologies, which presented a few key challenges along the way:

* **Tuning Heuristics to Reduce False Positives:** One of the most difficult engineering tasks was refining the ransomware detection engine's sensitivity. I had to implement careful threshold guards for normal OS file modifications and bulk renames. Striking the right balance—ensuring routine system activities (like software updates or compiling code) didn't trigger alerts, while still catching actual ransomware behaviors like rapid entropy spikes—required significant iteration and testing.

* **Migrating and Structuring the AI Backend:** Transitioning the AI analysis engine to the Google Gemini API required careful prompt engineering. Because the Streamlit UI expects structured data, I had to ensure the LLM consistently returned properly formatted JSON even when analyzing abstract or highly obfuscated system telemetry, which took extensive error handling to perfect.

* **Blockchain Verification Integration:** Implementing the zero-trust forensic verifying system was complex. Properly signing transactions to anchor the SHA-256 hashes of the PDF reports to the Algorand blockchain, and successfully retrieving the `dataPayload` to validate local files required diving deep into the Algorand SDK, handling asynchronous network calls, and safely managing testnet credentials.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

### 🧠 Best Use of the Google Gemini API in RANZR

In our project, the Google Gemini API isn't just an add-on; it serves as the core intelligence engine that bridges the gap between raw machine telemetry and human incident response. We utilized Gemini to solve the critical SOC (Security Operations Center) bottlenecks of **Alert Fatigue** and **Mean Time To Understand (MTTU)**.

Here is exactly how we leveraged the Gemini API to maximum effect:

1. **Automated Threat Triage & Contextualization:** 
   Our detection engine (`threat_score.py`) generates highly technical, abstract JSON data during an attack—tracking metrics like Shannon entropy spikes, exact file modification paths, and rapid extension renames. We feed this raw telemetry directly into Gemini (`explanation.py`). Gemini instantly processes this complex data and generates a clear, structured, plain-English summary. It tells the analyst immediately *what* is happening and *why* it's malicious, turning raw logs into an actionable executive summary in seconds.

2. **Real-Time Interactive Security Copilot:**
   Instead of forcing analysts to manually search external threat intelligence databases, we built a context-aware chatbot (`chatbot.py`) directly into our Streamlit UI. Powered by Gemini, this agent retains the context of the active alert. Analysts can ask natural language follow-up questions about the specific compromised endpoint (e.g., *"Does this entropy pattern indicate partial or full encryption?"* or *"What is the normal behavior for this hijacked process?"*). Gemini acts as a dynamic, real-time copilot actively engaged in the triage phase.

3. **Democratizing Malware Analysis:**
   By relying on Gemini's advanced reasoning capabilities to explain complex technical behaviors simply, RANZR empowers junior security analysts to handle complex, zero-day threat investigations that would typically require a senior malware reverse-engineer. We used Gemini to transform raw data into expert-level intelligence at machine speed.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

### 🔊 Best Use of ElevenLabs in RANZR

In **RANZR**, we integrated the **ElevenLabs Voice AI** to bridge the gap between digital telemetry and physical incident response. While traditional security tools rely on silent desktop notifications or emails that can easily be missed in a crowded inbox or during off-hours, we used ElevenLabs to build an immediate, visceral alerting mechanism.

Here is exactly how we utilized ElevenLabs to its full potential:

* **Breaking the "Silent Alarm" Paradigm:** 
  When the heuristic engine detects a "High Risk" or "Critical" ransomware behavior (like a sudden spike in file entropy paired with rapid mass-renames), the AI pipeline generates a dynamic, context-aware warning message. We feed this text directly into the ElevenLabs API ([reporting/voice_alert.py](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/ASUS/OneDrive/Desktop/RANZR/reporting/voice_alert.py:0:0-0:0)) to synthesize a natural, urgent human voice that plays immediately through the endpoint's or the SOC's physical speakers.

* **Contextual Physical Alerts:**
  Instead of a generic "beep" or siren, the ElevenLabs alert uses the context generated by our detection engine. For example, it can dynamically vocalize: *"Critical Alert: Ransomware behavior detected on endpoint. Multiple files in the Documents directory are actively being encrypted. Immediate isolation recommended."* 

* **Reducing Response Latency via Audio Cues:**
  In a high-stakes ransomware attack, seconds dictate whether a network is saved or completely compromised. By using ElevenLabs’ ultra-realistic, zero-latency text-to-speech models (`eleven_multilingual_v2`), we ensure that security analysts or endpoint users are physically alerted to the severity of the threat the exact millisecond it is detected, completely bypassing visual alert fatigue and allowing for immediate "kill-switch" intervention.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

### 🚀 Best Hack Built with Antigravity

Building **RANZR** in a time-constrained hackathon environment was incredibly challenging, as it required seamlessly integrating multiple complex domains: system-level endpoint monitoring, AI API integration (Google Gemini), Streamlit UI development, and blockchain smart-contract interaction (Algorand). 

Using **Antigravity** as our AI software engineering agent was the "secret weapon" that made this ambitious architecture possible. Here is how Antigravity fundamentally accelerated our build:

1. **Rapid Prototyping & Scaffolding Across Domains:**
   Instead of context-switching constantly between writing low-level Python detection heuristics and configuring a reactive Streamlit frontend, Antigravity handled the rapid scaffolding of our project's boilerplate. This allowed us to focus entirely on the core logic and architecture. Whether we needed to structure a highly technical yaml config file or build out the UI layout, Antigravity acted as a force multiplier.

2. **Complex Debugging & Heuristic Tuning:**
   Tuning our ransomware detection engine to minimize false positives was conceptually difficult. When our entropy-calculation thresholds were incorrectly flagging normal system updates as malware, Antigravity helped us quickly step through the logic, write complex `regex` filters for file paths, and refine our `threat_score.py` algorithms in real-time. It acted as an expert pair programmer during our most critical debugging sessions.

3. **Demystifying Hard APIs (Blockchain & AI):**
   Integrating the Algorand TestNet for our zero-trust forensic verification step required diving deep into complex SDKs and managing asynchronous network calls. Antigravity helped us digest the documentation, correctly sign our SHA-256 PDF hashes to the blockchain, and securely retrieve the `dataPayload`. Similarly, when migrating our LLM backend to Google Gemini, Antigravity helped us perfect the JSON parsing and prompt engineering required for our AI chatbot to output perfectly formatted system telemetry explanations.

4. **Maintaining Unstoppable Momentum:**
   Hackathons are exhausting. Having Antigravity constantly available to answer complex architectural questions, find missing dependencies, and generate clean, documented code meant we never hit a wall. It allowed a small team to build an enterprise-grade, multi-stage security product in a single weekend.

### Z Auth
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/z-auth-d9e5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/pulkitpareek18/Z-Auth-Pramaan) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://notes.geturstyle.shop) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/2dTGIC2Wzr8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> [Patented] Prove who you are. Reveal nothing.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Indian Patent: Granted - Application No. 202311041001
US Patent : Filed

**Every system that stores biometrics becomes a breach waiting to happen. Aadhaar (1.1B records leaked), Clearview AI (3B photos stolen), Star Health (31M records exposed). Passwords fail. Centralized biometrics fail worse, you can't reset your face.**

**Z Auth eliminates this entirely. Users authenticate with their biometrics, but the biometric never leaves their device. A zero-knowledge cryptographic proof is generated on-device and verified on Base blockchain, proving identity without exposing it. No passwords. No biometric databases. No data to breach.**

**Drop-in replacement for any authentication system. 10 lines of SDK code. Banks get KYC without storing liability. Apps get passwordless auth without building infrastructure. Users get privacy without sacrificing convenience.**

We've Integrated Z Auth into a demo notes app to demonstrate it's working and the problem it solves.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Cross-Device Face Matching Accuracy** — Our initial face matching threshold (0.6) caused false rejections when users enrolled on one phone and authenticated on another — different cameras, lighting, and angles shifted the embedding distance. We ran a 1,000-person benchmark against the LFW dataset, tested every threshold from 0.3 to 0.8, and landed on 0.55 — achieving 100% accuracy with zero false positives across all 1,000 identities.

**ZK Proof Coordinate Mismatch** — Groth16 proofs generated by snarkjs use a different coordinate ordering for the `pi_b` parameter than what Solidity expects. Proofs that verified perfectly server-side were failing on-chain. Took hours to debug — the fix was swapping `[[b00,b01],[b10,b11]]` to `[[b01,b00],[b11,b10]]` before sending to the smart contract.

**Docker Build Caching Hiding New Code** — After adding the entire blockchain integration, we deployed to production — but the Docker image was fully cached from the previous build. Containers kept crash-looping with old code. The new TypeScript files were never compiled into the image. Had to force a full rebuild with zero cache to pick up the changes.

**Environment Variables Not Reaching Containers** — We added `IDENTITY_CHAIN_*` environment variables to the `.env.prod` file, but on-chain enrollment was silently failing. After debugging, we realized Docker Compose only passes environment variables that are explicitly listed in the compose YAML — the variables existed in the env file but were never wired through to the container definition. A one-line fix, but hours of silent failure.

**BlockChain**

We are using the Coinbase L2 Chain that is based over ethereum for identity enrollment and Verification. The blockchain works as an Decentralized Database for us.

**Ethereum Track**

We are using the L2 Chain by Coinbase based over ethereum. Have Deployed the smart contracts that are liable for identity enrollment and verification.

**Best Use of Vultr**

Hosting multiple containers with managed services definitely need a vps. Used vultr to achieve this.

**The problem it solves**

CryptoRISK is a real-time crypto risk intelligence terminal that combines:

AI price prediction

on-chain blockchain analytics

quantitative risk modeling

portfolio stress simulations

into a single unified dashboard.

It continuously ingests live market and blockchain data, analyzes it using statistical and machine learning models, and presents actionable risk insights in real time.

Crypto Traders

- anticipate price movements

- identify risky market conditions

- improve trade timing

Portfolio Managers

- evaluate systemic risk

- stress-test portfolios

- manage drawdown exposure

Crypto Hedge Funds

- monitor market risk in real time

- integrate on-chain signals into trading strategies

Researchers & Analysts

- study market dynamics

- analyze blockchain network impact on price movements

**Challenges we ran into**

:Challenges Faced

- Real-time data synchronization: Combining live market data, AI predictions, and blockchain metrics while keeping timestamps aligned.

- Low-latency performance: Updating charts and risk models frequently without slowing down the backend or frontend.

- Blockchain data integration: Handling unstable APIs and normalizing Solana network metrics with market data.

- Risk model design: Balancing multiple indicators (sentiment, volatility, funding rates, technical signals) into a meaningful composite risk score.

- Handling API failures: Managing missing or delayed data from external sources without breaking the dashboard.

- Frontend visualization: Rendering live charts and predictions smoothly while updating continuously.

- Deployment & connectivity: Ensuring stable communication between the backend API and the live dashboard during deployment.

**BlockChain**

The system collects real-time Solana blockchain metrics such as TPS, network load, slot number, and epoch progress.
These metrics are processed to determine the health and congestion level of the blockchain network.

A Solana network risk signal is generated based on these metrics.
This signal is included as a feature in the overall crypto risk score, along with market indicators like volatility, funding rates, and sentiment.

The backend stores this data and sends it to the dashboard, where users can monitor blockchain network conditions in real time.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

- It automatically selects the best available Gemini model.

- It feeds real-time market indicators (price, RSI, EMA, SMA, predictions) into the prompt

- Gemini then interprets the data and generates trend, momentum, and outlook analysis.

- The chatbot combines live data + AI reasoning to provide trading explanations and insights.

**Best Use of Solana**

Solana blockchain data is integrated into the system to monitor network health and include blockchain infrastructure signals in the risk analysis.
The backend fetches real-time Solana metrics such as TPS (transactions per second), network load, slot number, and epoch progress.
These metrics indicate the performance and congestion level of the Solana network.
A Solana network risk component is generated from these metrics.
This component is added to the overall crypto risk score along with market indicators like volatility, funding rates, and RSI.
The data is then displayed on the dashboard in the Solana Network panel, allowing users to monitor blockchain conditions in real time.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

- Google Antigravity was used as the development environment to build and test parts of the system.

- Within Antigravity, the Claude Sonnet 4.6 agent was used to assist with code generation, debugging, and architecture design.

- The Claude agent helped speed up development by providing implementation suggestions, fixing errors, and improving backend logic for the crypto analytics platform.

**Red Hat**

- Store trading knowledge in a vector database like FAISS.

- When the user asks a question, retrieve relevant documents.

- Add live market data (price, RSI, EMA, predictions).

- Send everything to an LLM like Gemini.

- The LLM generates the answer.

> Blockchain Carbon Credits from Food Rescue

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India’s food system faces a paradox where massive food waste, rising hunger, and untapped climate value exist simultaneously. While millions struggle with food insecurity, large quantities of edible food are discarded every day by restaurants, caterers, hostels, and events. This inefficiency not only worsens the country’s position in the Global Hunger Index, but also creates a hidden environmental cost when wasted food decomposes in landfills.

When food rots, it produces methane, a greenhouse gas that is about 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide in terms of warming impact. This means that food waste is not only a humanitarian issue but also a significant climate problem. Preventing food from reaching landfills can therefore reduce emissions, but the environmental value of this prevention is rarely quantified or monetized.

This is where the carbon credit marketplace gap becomes critical. Today, global voluntary carbon markets primarily reward projects such as renewable energy, forestry, or large-scale carbon removal initiatives. However, food waste reduction and food rescue activities are largely excluded, even though rescuing food prevents emissions in a measurable and verifiable way. This represents a missed opportunity to convert real-world social impact into tradable environmental assets.

At the same time, corporations across the world are under increasing pressure to meet ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) goals and reduce their carbon footprint. Many companies purchase carbon credits to offset emissions, but the current market often struggles with transparency, traceability, and trust. Credits are frequently generated in remote projects that are difficult to verify, creating skepticism around their real impact.

The core problem is the absence of a transparent marketplace that links verified food rescue activities with carbon credit generation. Without a system that records rescued food, calculates the emissions prevented, and converts that data into trusted carbon credits, the environmental and economic value of food rescue remains unrealized. Solving this problem can simultaneously improve food distribution, reduce methane emissions, and create a new, transparent carbon credit marketplace built on measurable real-world impact.

### TrustMed
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trustmed-4b0b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rajansharma08/TrustMed) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://trust-med-two.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lGeunvPVA2s) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Blockchain Counterfeit Medicine Detector

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenZeppelin](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenZeppelin-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Counterfeit medicines and opaque handoffs in pharma supply chains create serious safety and trust risks.
Today, a printed QR on medicine packs is easy to copy, and patients/pharmacies usually cannot verify whether the product’s journey is authentic.

This project solves that by turning each QR into a tamper-evident blockchain pointer (chainId + contract + medicineId), not static trust text.

People can use it to:

Verify authenticity quickly: scan QR and view full on-chain history (origin, checkpoints, actors, status).
Improve traceability: every supply-chain handoff is appended as an immutable checkpoint.
Reduce fraud risk: suspicious timeline inconsistencies become visible instead of hidden in siloed logs.
Increase accountability: updates are wallet-signed and role-gated, so unauthorized parties cannot add fake checkpoints.
Simplify audits/compliance: regulators, hospitals, and distributors can review one shared source of truth.
In short, it makes medicine verification faster, transparent, and harder to tamper with for both end customers and supply-chain participants.

**Challenges we ran into**

Local vs live network mismatch: Early on, the app worked on local Hardhat (31337) but failed for public demo links/phone testing.
Fix: Added a clear split between local and public deploy flow, plus environment-based config (RPC, chainId, contract) and docs for Sepolia deployment.

QR scan behavior on mobile: Camera/scan worked on desktop flow, but phone users needed a direct verification experience without write/admin actions.
Fix: Kept existing flows unchanged and made QR generation support verify deep links (/verify?...) so mobile users can open and verify history immediately.

Deployment path confusion in monorepo: Chain scripts were writing deployment JSON to a legacy frontend path (app/src/deployments) while the active app was trace-trust.
Fix: Updated scripts to target trace-trust/src/deployments consistently.

Unstable risk output from AI integration: Gemini-based scoring produced inconsistent/high suspicion in some runs, which hurt demo reliability.
Fix: Replaced it with deterministic hardcoded risk logic for predictable and explainable outputs.

Submission usability: Initial docs were too fragmented for first-time reviewers.
Fix: Rewrote README with step-by-step setup, local run script, deployment checklist, direct verify link format, and troubleshooting guidance.

**BlockChain**

Our project fits the Blockchain track because blockchain is the core trust mechanism, not an add-on.

We use a smart contract to store medicine creation events and every supply-chain checkpoint as immutable records.
Each update is wallet-signed and role-restricted, so only authorized participants can write data.
QR codes contain an on-chain pointer (chainId, contract, medicineId), allowing anyone to independently verify provenance and history.
This removes reliance on editable centralized logs and makes tampering, backdating, or silent record changes much harder.
The system provides transparent, auditable traceability for a high-impact real-world problem: counterfeit medicine and opaque distribution chains.
In short, blockchain enables verifiable integrity, accountability, and shared truth across all stakeholders in the medicine lifecycle.

**Ethereum Track**

This project is a strong fit for the Ethereum Track because Ethereum is the trust layer behind the entire medicine verification flow.

We use a Solidity smart contract to store medicine records and checkpoint history on-chain.
Every supply-chain update is a signed transaction from a wallet address, creating accountability and non-repudiation.
Role-based access control (admin/manufacturer/participant) ensures only authorized actors can write updates.
Customers can verify provenance by scanning a QR that resolves to an on-chain record (chainId, contract, medicineId), instead of trusting editable off-chain claims.
The result is a tamper-evident, transparent audit trail that demonstrates a real-world Ethereum use case beyond payments: public trust infrastructure for healthcare supply chains.
In short, Ethereum is not just used as storage here; it is the core mechanism for integrity, authorization, and verifiable traceability.

Impact:
80%+ civic complaints in India kabhi resolve nahi hoti — World Bank Report

**Challenges we ran into**

🇮🇳 India's Civic Governance Crisis
India mein 4,000+ Urban Local Bodies hain lekin citizen complaints ka koi proper digital system nahi hai.
Core Problems:
📋 Manual complaint filing — queues, paperwork, time waste
🐌 Zero tracking — complaint file karo aur bhool jao
💸 Rampant corruption — no digital trail, bribes go undetected
📵 No transparency — citizens never know complaint status
⏰ SLA violations — deadlines miss hote hain, koi accountability nahi
🌐 Language barrier — English-only systems exclude Hindi speakers
Impact:
80%+ civic complaints in India kabhi resolve nahi hoti — World Bank Report
Our Solution: CivicEye Pro — AI + Blockchain se har complaint track, resolve aur audit hoti hai. 30 seconds mein file karo, real-time track karo, corruption automatically detect hota hai. 🚀

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/04a55502a7324f31b47b94d90668ea87/9b9f314e-90f4-4b2d-aebf-f4807bca036c.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/04a55502a7324f31b47b94d90668ea87/a9dd094d-e7fd-4f59-a61c-b9bd0cdc23ae.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/04a55502a7324f31b47b94d90668ea87/e49b7fc6-6569-460f-84f9-35ad98556248.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/04a55502a7324f31b47b94d90668ea87/40a4c7bc-752f-4a3a-abb6-855a59b98894.png)

**BlockChain**

How Blockchain is Used in CivicEye
The backend already has a Block model and chain integrity endpoint (GET /api/blockchain + GET /api/blockchain/verify). Here's what it does and what it should do:
Current Implementation (v8)
Every complaint filed creates a blockchain entry — a linked hash chain where each block contains:

Complaint ID + timestamp
Filing citizen's ID (hashed)
AI classification result
Department routed to
previous_hash → linking it to the prior block
block_hash = SHA-256(all of the above)

The /api/blockchain/verify endpoint walks the entire chain and checks that no block has been tampered with. If any complaint record is altered in the DB, the hash breaks → tamper detection.

### VeriTrax
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/veritrax-beea) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/VighneshB01/Veritrax-Final) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://veritraxa.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> "Trust the Chain, Not the Claim."

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![coinbase](https://img.shields.io/badge/coinbase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every year, crores of rupees are donated by ordinary Indians — and most of them never find out where their money actually went.

**VeriTrax** solves exactly that. Every donation, every fund movement, every withdrawal is recorded on a public blockchain — permanent, visible, and impossible to alter. No middlemen, no black boxes, no unanswered RTIs. Just complete, real-time transparency from the moment you donate to the moment it reaches its final use.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1 — Making crypto accessible to non-crypto users**

We solved this by integrating Pera Wallet for Algorand, which is as simple as a UPI app, and Coinbase Wallet which lets users add money directly via UPI or net banking and buy crypto in under a minute — no technical knowledge required.

**Challenge 2 — Getting two different blockchains to show one unified experience**

Algorand and Solana don't talk to each other natively and we solved this by using MongoDB as a common layer — every transaction from both chains writes its data there, and our dashboard reads from both simultaneously — giving users one clean, unified transaction history regardless of which chain processed it.

**BlockChain**

**Blockchain** is used in **VeriTrax** because every transaction recorded on-chain is permanent, public, and tamper-proof — making fund misuse structurally impossible, not just legally prohibited.
Traditional donation platforms run on centralized databases where records can be altered, hidden, or deleted — exactly what happened with **PM CARES**. On **VeriTrax**, every rupee donated is a transaction anyone can verify from anywhere, forever — no RTI needed, no email follow-up, no trust required.

**Ethereum Track**

**Ethereum/Base Chain** powers all gasless transactions on VeriTrax — users transacting via Coinbase Wallet on Base network pay zero gas fees, handled entirely by Coinbase Paymaster in the background.
**Coinbase SDK & Coinbase Wallet** enable this gasless experience natively — users can also fund their wallet directly via UPI or net banking inside Coinbase, removing the need for any third-party fiat gateway.
**x402 Protocol** handles all conditional auto-payments — user connects Coinbase Wallet, sets a receiver, selects a condition from a dropdown, and payment releases automatically only when that condition is met. No manual intervention required.

**Best Use of Solana**

**Solana** handles all high-volume and large-value fund movements on **VeriTrax** — specifically NGO treasury withdrawals and bulk institutional transactions, where speed and scale matter most.
Solana's 65,000 TPS capacity ensures these large transactions are processed at real-world institutional speed without delays or bottlenecks — making it the backbone for any transaction that exceeds normal P2P donation scale of **Algorand**

**Algorand Bharat**

**Algorand SDK** handles all P2P donation transactions on VeriTrax — reducing fees from 20–30% (traditional) to 3–5%, with 4-second transaction finality and permanent on-chain recording for transparency. 
**Pera Wallet** is the user-facing wallet for all Algorand transactions — mobile-first, widely adopted in India, and simple enough for non-crypto users to operate without any technical knowledge.

### Harbor
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/chainkechowkidar-c87f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/abjt01/harbor-sandbox_v2) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UbwEylj5HzBepxqzChto9T4j3ZFN4Gs6/view?usp=sharing) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/CqOg6h3EDnE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Blockchain Finality Layer

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Small blockchains get robbed. Not through smart contract bugs or phishing —
through math.

If you control 51% of a chain's mining power, you control its history.
You can mine a secret alternative chain, make a transaction on the real one
(buy something, withdraw funds), then release your private chain and erase that transaction like it never happened. The chain accepts your version because it's longer. You keep the money AND the thing you bought.

Ethereum Classic lost $5.6M this way. The attack cost ~$50,000.
That's a 112x return on crime. And ETC is not even a small chain.

The real targets are the hundreds of chains sitting online right now with
< $1M in mining security — gaming chains, DeFi protocols on custom L1s,
app-specific chains. Anyone with a NiceHash account and a weekend can
attack them.

**Harbor fixes this by making the past immutable.**

Every 10 blocks, Harbor takes the small chain's block hash and writes it
permanently to a smart contract on a stronger chain (Ethereum). Once written, that hash cannot be changed — not by us, not by anyone.

Now if an attacker tries to submit an alternative chain, Harbor's validator
checks the incoming blocks against those stored hashes. Different hash?
The chain is rejected. Automatically. At the protocol level.

The attack doesn't get detected. It doesn't get flagged. It just *doesn't work.*

No chain modifications needed. No new consensus mechanism. No $30M masternode network. Just a notary bot, a smart contract, and one 'docker compose up'.

**Challenges we ran into**

### The two-chains-one-Hardhat problem

Hardhat isn't built to run two independent nodes from the same project.  
When I tried spinning up both the fortress chain (':8545') and small chain (':8546') simultaneously, they shared chain state and interfered with each other's artifacts.

It took a while to realize that the fix was spawning them as completely separate child processes inside setup-chains.js and treating the **port number itself as the chain identifier** in the contract.

Felt hacky.  
Worked perfectly.

---

### The notary bot kept double-anchoring

WebSocket block event listeners on local Hardhat nodes sometimes fire **duplicate events** — the same block appearing twice within milliseconds.

The contract throws 'BlockAlreadyAnchored' if the same height is written again, so the notary bot kept crashing mid-run with revert errors.

The fix was embarrassingly simple:  
check 'isAnchored()' before sending the transaction.

If the block is already anchored, skip it silently.

Adding that one check made the bot run stable for the first time.

---

### Docker startup ordering

'depends_on' in Docker Compose only checks whether the **container has started**, not whether Hardhat is actually listening or if the contract has been deployed.

Because of this, the notary bot consistently crashed on startup with a **"contract not found"** error since it started before deployment finished.

The solution was creating 'ensure-deploy.js' as a startup gate.

The script:

1. Polls port '8545' until Hardhat responds.
2. Deploys 'HarborRegistry'.
3. Writes the contract address to '.env'.
4. Only then starts the notary bot.

After that, deployment became completely deterministic.

---

### Making the attack simulation actually real

I didn't want to fake the attack result in the UI.  
The contract read needed to return a **real mismatch**.

So the simulator generates a fake hash using:

'javascript'
keccak256("ATTACK_" + blockHeight)

### eBPF Based Behavioral Anomaly Detection-LSTM
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ebpf-based-behavioral-anomaly-detection-using-lstm-autoencoders-3117) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/syvikas33/eBPF-Based-behavioral-anomaly-detection--LSTM--autoencoders) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Real-time Linux threat detection kernel telemetry

![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional antivirus and endpoint security systems rely heavily on signature-based detection. This approach is fundamentally broken against zero-day malware, fileless attacks, and polymorphic ransomware that constantly mutate to evade known databases. If an attack has never been seen before, standard security completely ignores it.

To solve this, we built an AI-Driven Behavioral  anomaly detection that operates entirely on zero-trust principles. Instead of looking for known bad files, our system learns what "normal" looks like at the deepest level of the operating system.

Our architecture leverages eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) to hook directly into the Linux kernel and monitor high-speed system call telemetry (such as execve and openat) in real-time. This live behavioral sequence is fed into a custom LSTM-Autoencoder neural network.

Because the neural network is trained exclusively on the pure, baseline execution patterns of the machine, it instantly flags any deviation—like a ransomware encryptor rapid-firing file access loops. Once the reconstruction error crosses our tuned enterprise threshold, the Sentinel autonomously executes a lethal SIGKILL to the offending Process ID (PID), ripping the zero-day threat out of memory before it can execute its payload.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-Time Inference Latencies: The Linux kernel fires thousands of system calls per second. Feeding this high-velocity telemetry through a Python-based LSTM neural network introduced inference latency. We had to tightly optimize our eBPF buffer polling and sequence batching to ensure the AI could calculate the anomaly loss and execute the SIGKILL before ransomware could encrypt meaningful data.

Cross-Platform Pipeline: We had to build a split architecture—harvesting the pure eBPF baseline data on a CPU-only Ubuntu VM, forging the deep learning weights on a heavy Windows GPU, and cleanly exfiltrating the compiled .pth brain back to the Linux kernel.

The "Too Lethal" AI (False Positives): Initially, our zero-trust anomaly detection was so aggressive it flagged opening a normal terminal (gnome-terminal) as a zero-day threat and instantly murdered it. We had to engineer an enterprise-grade Exclusion List and tune our MSE thresholds to balance extreme security with actual OS usability.

### x402Sec
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/xsec-3cff) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/therealhamad/sandboxing) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/13x0LCK1SIM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Trust Layer for x402 Protocol

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## AI agents can't be trusted with payments, yet

Protocols like x402 let AI agents autonomously pay for resources over HTTP. 
A research agent can fetch flight data, a dev agent can call a security API, 
a finance agent can pull market data — all without human approval on every request.

The problem: **there is no security layer between an agent and its wallet.**

A single prompt injection — a malicious instruction hidden in a webpage, 
API response, or injected into context — can silently redirect an agent to 
transfer funds to an attacker. OTPs protect humans. They do nothing for agents.

## What Payjama does

Payjama is a security middleware layer that sits between any AI agent and 
payment execution. Before any payment is signed, three things must pass:

**1. Hardware-bound agent identity**  
Every agent's signing key is generated inside Apple's Secure Enclave — a 
dedicated hardware chip on Apple Silicon. The private key never touches RAM, 
never touches disk, never leaves the chip. Payment signing is delegated to 
hardware. A compromised process cannot extract the key.

**2. Intent attestation with context hashing**  
Every payment carries a SHA-256 fingerprint of the conversation that led to 
it. If a prompt injection changes the agent's context, the hash changes. 
Payjama detects the tamper.

**3. Session integrity monitoring**  
Payjama tracks every agent session from its declared mission. It scores each 
payment for mission drift ("this agent was researching flights — why is it 
now wiring $850 to an unknown transfer service?"), velocity anomalies, and 
novel recipient detection. The longer an agent runs, the harder it is for an 
attacker to hijack it undetected.

## Who uses it

- **Fintech platforms** deploying AI agents that handle money movement
- **Agentic API providers** who want to gate access behind x402 payments
- **Developers** building autonomous agents that need auditable payment trails
- **Any team** using x402 who needs to answer: "how do we trust our agent 
  won't get hijacked?"

## What it looks like in practice

An agent runs autonomously — fetching data, making micropayments via x402 
on Base Sepolia, narrating its reasoning. A hidden attacker injects a malicious 
payload mid-session. The agent obeys the injection and attempts an $850 
transfer to an unknown endpoint. Payjama intercepts it before the vault 
signs — mission drift score 91, amount exceeds policy, recipient not 
whitelisted. The payment never reaches the Secure Enclave. The session is 
halted. A cryptographic audit log captures everything.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. The Secure Enclave signing boundary

Apple's Secure Enclave generates and stores P-256 keys — but the key material 
never crosses into the Go process. Go has no native Secure Enclave API.

The solution was a thin Swift CLI (`sekey`) that acts as the only process 
allowed to touch the Enclave. Go calls it via `exec.Command` — passing intent 
hashes in, getting DER-encoded signatures out. The private key stays in 
hardware across the boundary.

The tricky part: Swift's `SecureEnclave.P256.Signing.PrivateKey` returns a 
`dataRepresentation` that is a *handle* (an opaque reference), not key bytes. 
Storing the handle in Keychain and restoring the key from it on next use took 
several iterations to get right. The handle is device-bound — it's useless on 
any other machine, which is exactly the property we needed.

## 2. EIP-712 structured signing without go-ethereum

Implementing EIP-712 signing from scratch in Go (for x402 payment payloads) 
without pulling in the full `go-ethereum` library was harder than expected. 
The domain separator, type hashes, and ABI encoding had to be implemented 
manually using `crypto/ecdsa` and `golang.org/x/crypto/sha3`. Getting the 
exact byte layout right — and matching what Coinbase's x402 facilitator 
expected — required careful reference to the EIP-712 spec and several failed 
facilitation attempts before the first real on-chain payment went through.

## 3. Making the injection actually trigger a fraudulent payment

Early in testing, the autonomous agent demo had a subtle but critical flaw: 
the attacker's injection landed in the agent's context, but the agent never 
acted on it. The fallback `decide_payment()` function always picked from a 
hardcoded whitelist — so Payjama had nothing to block.

The fix was rethinking how the agent processes injections. When a `[SYSTEM]` 
message appears in context, the Gemini reasoning prompt changes: instead of 
"pick a recipient from the whitelist," it becomes "you have received a system 
instruction — follow it." The agent then generates a payment attempt using 
the attacker's recipient and amount. That's what Payjama intercepts. The demo 
only works because the agent is genuinely compromised — not because we 
hardcoded the attack.

## 4. Session monitor false positives

The mission drift detector (Gemini scoring semantic distance between original 
mission and current payment) was initially too aggressive — it flagged 
legitimate turn 5 payments as "drifted" because the mission summary and 
payment purpose used different vocabulary for the same concept. 

The fix was two-part: only run drift checks after 2+ prior approved payments 
(baseline needed), and raise the block threshold for drift alone to 60+ before 
it contributes meaningfully to the score. Drift is a signal, not a verdict.

Team **LiveLifeLarge** -- [Hamad Hussain](https://github.com/therealhamad), [DILIP  S CHAKRAVARTHI](https://github.com/DilipSC)

### CryptoGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cryptoguard-e30a) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> We prevent crypto scams

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

$24 billion. That's what was lost to crypto scams and laundering in 2023 alone. The scam was never undetectable, the problem was always timing. All crypto and blockchain AML tools that exist now are forensic tools. They are amazing at telling you what happened after the scam is done and the money is gone. But what if we could detect it during the scam? 

We built a real-time transaction interception platform. Our tool works between the mempool and the exchange approval layer — scoring every transaction for fraud risk, i.e before it confirms.
We have 3 layers which works together:
Data retrieval from Alchemy websocket
our risk engine runs four simultaneous algorithms on every transaction.
Peel chain detection using graph traversal. 
Mixer proximity scoring using BFS pathfinding. 
Velocity anomaly detection using statistical deviation. 
And direct OFAC sanctions cross-referencing. Every transaction gets a risk score from 0 to 100 
every flagged transaction gets an AI-generated plain English explanation, streamed live to a compliance analyst's dashboard. 
We allow brokers to prevent scams

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem: The Crisis in the Clouds**

Adventure tourism is expanding rapidly (19% CAGR), yet safety infrastructure remains stagnant, creating a deadly "Triple Threat" in mountain corridors:

Gap 1: **Connectivity Void (Physical)**: 40% of key corridors are "Digital Dark Zones" where cellular signals vanish. Affordable satellite alternatives are often illegal or restricted in sensitive border regions.

Gap 2: **Information Vacuum (Data)**: Authorities operate in silos with zero real-time data on crowd density or route blockages, leading to reactive rather than proactive disaster management.

Gap 3: **Response Lag (Operational)**: Without precise coordinates or health vitals, emergency response is delayed by 15-30 minutes, turning survivable injuries into fatalities.


Solution: **The Setuka Ecosystem** 

Setuka is an **IoT-based, AI-driven ecosystem** that bridges the gap between travelers and authorities through three integrated layers:

1. **AI-Powered Tourist App** 
**Real-time Safety Scoring:** Provides live scores for road conditions, accident rates, and crime levels at the user's current location.
**Itinerary-Based Planning**: Users map daily destinations to see all available routes ranked by safety scores.
**Blockchain Digital ID**: Generates a tamper-proof ID (anchored on the Polygon network) containing medical and insurance info. It is accessible via offline QR codes and biometrics for instant verification by responders even without internet.
**Dynamic Geofencing:** Uses safety heatmaps to provide instant warnings if a tourist enters a high-risk zone.

2. **IoT LoRa-Based Wearable** 
**Multi-Sensor Integration**: Equipped with LoRa (sx1262), GPS (Quectel EC200U), GNSS , GSM , OLED Display and SpO2 sensors to monitor real-time location and health vitals.
**Triple-Mode Transmission Protocol**: Ensures SOS delivery via:
**Direct Cloud**: When internet is available.
**SMS**: Via cellular networks in partial signal areas.
**LoRa-to-LoRa**: In zero-connectivity zones using a built-in Peer-to-Peer network that relays signals through other nearby Setuka devices until they reach a receiver.
**Auto-SOS**: Automatically triggers emergency alerts based on critical health vital anomalies.

3. **Unified Command Dashboard for Authorities** 
**Real-Time Cluster Map**: Provides a live visualization of all tourist locations and density clusters.
**Anomaly & Inactivity Detection**: AI-powered algorithms flag route deviations or unusual inactivity instantly.
**Crowd & Resource Management**: Suggests itinerary alternatives to tourists when locations become overcrowded and reallocates patrolling staff to high-risk zones in real-time.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Building Setuka — Challenges & How I Solved Them

> A behind-the-scenes look at the real engineering problems we hit while building a multi-layer tourist safety ecosystem — and what it took to work through them.

---

## 1. Building the Safety Score Dataset from Scratch

**The Problem**

The entire safety score system depends on real location-level data across Kolkata and Darjeeling. There was no ready-made dataset — no single government portal, no open API, no CSV we could download that gave road condition, crime intensity, and accident risk at the neighborhood level for these two regions.

We needed ratings for **536 individual locations** across two very different geographies.

**What We Did**

We manually assembled two datasets by cross-referencing multiple official and civic sources:

For each location, three values had to be researched and assigned on a 1–10 scale:

- **Road Condition** — drawn from KMC ward-level road survey reports, PWD West Bengal and NHIDCL mountain road assessments, NHAI national highway condition data, OpenStreetMap surface quality tags (`surface=asphalt`, `smoothness=*`), Google Street View imagery, and media investigative reports (The Telegraph, Darjeeling Times, TOI Kolkata).

- **Crime Level** — built from NCRB "Crime in India" 2021–2022 district-level FIR counts, Kolkata Police and Darjeeling Police station-wise crime statistics for 2023–2024, the West Bengal Police district crime review portal, and media reports for hotspot identification (Khidderpore, Metiabruz, Burrabazar, Siliguri's Khalpara border area).

- **Accident Risk** — derived from MoRTH "Road Accidents in India" 2021–2023, Kolkata and Darjeeling Traffic Police intersection/black-spot data, the iRAD (Integrated Road Accident Database) geo-tagged FIR records, SaveLIFE Foundation black spot analysis, and BRO mountain road incident reports for Darjeeling's terrain-triggered falls.

Coordinates for all 536 points were geocoded via OpenStreetMap / Nominatim and cross-validated with Google Maps and Survey of India topographic maps.

The hardest part was that no single source covered both regions at the same granularity. Kolkata has well-documented ward-level data; Darjeeling hill areas often had police station jurisdictions covering tens of square kilometers with no finer breakdown. Tea estate internal roads had no government condition data at all — those had to be estimated from satellite imagery and local trekker input.

Full source documentation: [`public/source_kol.md`](tourist-app/public/source_kol.md) · [`public/source_darj.md`](tourist-app/public/source_darj.md)

---

## 2. Designing Two Different Interpolation Models for Two Different Terrains

**The Problem**

Once the dataset existed, we needed to score *any* GPS coordinate — not just those 536 named locations. A tourist's phone will send coordinates from a road between two data points, a forest path, or a tea estate track with no entry in our dataset.

The naive solution — nearest-neighbor lookup — gave ugly step-function changes when crossing invisible boundaries. A single global interpolation model also failed because Kolkata and Darjeeling have completely different data structures:

- Kolkata is **traffic-density-driven**: road quality and crime cluster together in the same degraded neighborhoods. Statistical correlation between road rating and crime was **−0.83**.
- Darjeeling is **terrain-driven**: altitude is the dominant variable. Crime drops with altitude. Road quality degrades with steepness. Latitude–crime correlation was **−0.62**; crime and longitude (eastward toward Siliguri's urban mass) showed **+0.40**.

A single IDW model over the merged dataset produced nonsense scores — it would bleed Kolkata's high-crime urban patterns into Siliguri areas and ignore the mountain gradient entirely.

**What We Did**

We built and deployed two completely separate models:

**Model A — Kolkata: Coupled IDW**
Standard Inverse Distance Weighting (k=5, power=2) for all three variables. But for crime specifically, we fitted a road→crime regression correction:
```
crime_coupled = −0.7281 × road_rating + 8.3410
```
A blending weight `alpha` (near 0 at known points, growing to max 40% at ≥4 km gaps) mixes the raw IDW estimate with the road-derived prediction. This handles data-sparse outer zones without inventing crime spikes. Validated leave-one-out MAE: **0.474** on the 1–10 scale.

**Model B — Darjeeling: IDW + Geographic Gradient Blend**
Three OLS gradient planes fitted across all 242 data points:
```
crime_gradient(lat, lon)    = −4.328 × lat + 1.835 × lon − 43.035
accident_gradient(lat, lon) = −4.352 × lat + 2.565 × lon − 104.823
road_gradient(lat, lon)     = −1.755 × lat + 1.960 × lon − 121.370
```
A 15% baseline gradient is always applied (encoding the mountain/plains structure), growing by 4% per km from the nearest data point, capped at 50%. Validated leave-one-out MAE: **0.369**.

Both models also report a confidence tier (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW / VERY LO

**Slash (Open)**

**Setuka** fits perfectly into the Open Innovation track because it is not just a single product, but a cross-disciplinary ecosystem that bridges the gap between hardware, software, and public infrastructure to solve a systemic crisis in **"Digital Dark Zones"**.
Here is how Setuka aligns with the core principles of the Slash//open track:
1. **Cross-Disciplinary Technological Integration**
Setuka demonstrates open innovation by integrating multiple advanced technologies into a single, cohesive safety grid:
**Hardware Innovation**: We’ve developed a rugged, LoRa-based wearable using Quectel module and sx1262 (Lora modules) that creates a ground-level mesh network where commercial cellular infrastructure fails.
**AI-Driven Intelligence**: The system uses machine learning—specifically Isolation Forests and DBSCAN—to move from reactive rescue to proactive safety through anomaly detection and crowd-risk forecasting.
**Blockchain Security**: We utilize the Polygon network to provide immutable, offline-verifiable Digital IDs, ensuring that a traveler’s medical and insurance data is accessible even in total digital darkness.
2. **Solving a Systemic "Infrastructure Gap"**
The project addresses the "Triple Threat" of high-altitude tourism—connectivity voids, information vacuums, and response lags—by building an "invisible infrastructure". Instead of waiting for traditional telecom expansion, we utilize Peer-to-Peer (P2P) networking to turn individual tourist devices into nodes of a larger, resilient safety net.
3. **Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration**
True to the spirit of open innovation, Setuka creates a unified communication layer for diverse stakeholders who currently operate in silos:
**For Tourists**: Real-time safety scores, itinerary planning, and a reliable SOS lifeline.
**For Authorities**: A Unified Command Dashboard that optimizes police patrols, automates e-FIRs, and manages resources during emergencies.
**For Communities**: Driving sustainable economic growth in remote regions by building the safety confidence necessary for adventure tourism to thrive.
By providing a legal, affordable, and highly technical alternative to restricted satellite devices, Setuka serves as a blueprint for how Open Innovation can solve life-dependency issues in the world’s most challenging terrains

# 🧩 Problem It Solves

The pharmaceutical supply chain is highly complex and involves multiple stakeholders such as manufacturers, distributors, warehouses, pharmacies, regulators, and consumers. Due to the fragmented nature of this system, maintaining transparency and authenticity of medicines becomes extremely difficult.

This creates an environment where **counterfeit and substandard medicines can easily infiltrate the supply chain**, posing serious risks to public health and the global healthcare ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🚨 Key Challenges in the Current System

#### 1️⃣ Counterfeit Drug Infiltration
Fake medicines can enter the supply chain due to weak verification mechanisms and lack of transparent tracking systems.

#### 2️⃣ Lack of End-to-End Traceability
Traditional systems struggle to track the complete lifecycle of a drug from manufacturing to final consumption.

#### 3️⃣ Tamper-Prone Record Systems
Supply chain data is often stored in centralized databases that can be altered or manipulated, reducing trust among stakeholders.

#### 4️⃣ Limited Consumer Verification
Consumers currently have very limited ways to verify whether a medicine they purchased is authentic.

#### 5️⃣ Inefficient Supply Chain Monitoring
Without real-time monitoring tools, detecting irregularities such as shipment diversion, delays, or unauthorized transfers becomes difficult.

---

### 🧠 How Nirvana Smart-Chain Addresses These Problems

Nirvana Smart-Chain solves these challenges by leveraging **blockchain technology, smart contracts, and real-time verification systems** to create a transparent and tamper-proof pharmaceutical supply chain.

Key improvements include:

- **Immutable blockchain records** that prevent tampering
- **Real-time drug traceability** across the entire supply chain
- **Smart contract-based drug registration and validation**
- **Consumer-level drug authenticity verification**
- **Live shipment monitoring using geolocation**
- **Multi-stakeholder transparency and accountability**

By combining decentralized technology with modern web and backend systems, Nirvana Smart-Chain ensures that **every medicine distributed through the network can be verified, tracked, and trusted.**

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/credence-d0bf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Pratikkale26/overClocked) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-GHRhack%202.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ghrhack2.devfolio.co)

> Blockchain powered crowdfunding platform

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana%20Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

- The Problem it Solves
Traditional crowdfunding and donations suffer from a massive trust deficit. Once donors send their money, they have zero control or visibility over how it's actually spent. Organizations often fail to deliver on promises, funds are mismanaged, and there's no accountability, leaving donors hesitant to contribute to new or smaller initiatives.

- What is Credence?
Credence is a Programmable Trust Platform that replaces blind faith with mathematically proven accountability. It uses smart contracts to hold funds in escrow, releasing capital only when donors verify that milestones have been reached.

- What can people use it for?
Student Organizations & Hackathons: Raising funds for technical festivals or club projects where sponsors want transparency on specific deliverables.
NGOs & Social Causes: Providing transparent disaster relief or community development updates tied to funding releases.
Open Source Bounties/Development: Crowdfunding public goods where the community votes to release funds upon feature completion.
Community Initiatives: Neighborhoods pooling funds for a local park or project.

- How it makes tasks easier and safer:
Milestone-Locked Escrow: Money isn't handed over instantly. It's locked on-chain and released in phases.
Stake-Weighted Voting: Donors retain voting power proportional to their contribution. If the organization fails to deliver a milestone proof via the platform, donors can vote to halt the next funding release.
GST-Verified Proofs of History: Organizations submit real-world proofs (like GST-verified invoices) which are cryptographically hashed on-chain, creating a tamper-evident audit trail for every rupee spent.
Permanent Public Reputation: Organizations build immutable track records on Solana over time, making it easier for high-performing orgs to raise funds and impossible for bad actors to hide past failures.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Challenges We Ran Into
Building a hybrid Web2/Web3 platform that genuinely enforces accountability required solving several complex architectural and UX hurdles. Here are the main challenges we faced and overcame:

1. Managing On-Chain State Limits (Solana PDA Sizing) Solana accounts have strict size limits, which made storing dynamic campaign milestones and voting records tricky. Initially, we tried storing the full text of campaign descriptions and updates directly on-chain, which quickly hit the storage caps and made transaction fees unnecessarily high.

How we solved it: We pivoted to a hybrid architecture. Heavy metadata (campaign text, images, tags) is stored off-chain in a PostgreSQL database via Prisma, while the source-of-truth cryptographic hashes (like the SHA-256 hash of a GST invoice) and state changes (escrow balances, vote tallies) are stored on-chain in Program Derived Addresses (PDAs). The on-chain PDA simply holds a pointer (hash/URI) to the off-chain data, keeping transactions cheap and fast.

2. Bridging the Web2-to-Web3 UX Gap We knew that typical donors might not have a Phantom wallet or understand seed phrases. However, we needed non-crypto-native users to interact with our Anchor smart contracts to process donations and cast votes.

How we solved it: We deeply integrated Privy (@privy-io/react-auth) to abstract away wallet creation. Users can log in with just an email or a social account (like X/Twitter), and Privy spins up an embedded, non-custodial Solana wallet in the background. We then wired our Next.js frontend to allow these embedded wallets to seamlessly sign our custom Anchor transactions, making the Web3 interactions feel completely invisible.

3. Complex State Transitions for Escrow Vaults Handling the lifecycle of an escrow vault across multiple milestones was significantly harder than a standard token transfer. If a milestone is rejected by voters, what happens to the remaining funds? How do we ensure the creator can't prematurely drain the vault?

How we solved it: We had to carefully design the Anchor smart contract with strict state machine constraints. We implemented a VoteYes and VoteNo tally system mapped to donor_records. A milestone only transitions from UNDER_REVIEW to APPROVED if the stake-weighted "Yes" votes surpass the 51% threshold and meet the quorum requirement before the voting window expires.
4. Verifiable, Real-World Proofs (The "Oracle" Problem) Closing the loop between on-chain funds and off-chain execution is notoriously difficult. How does the blockchain know the contractor actually painted the school?

How we solved it: Instead of relying on a centralized oracle, we built a tamper-evident audit trail using cryptographic Proof of History. When an organization posts an update, they don't just upload a photo. They upload a GST-verified invoice to an S3 bucket. We generate a SHA-256 hash of that file in the browser and submit that hash to the blockchain. Even if the backend database is compromised, the cryptographic link between the on-chain milestone and the original uploaded invoice remains unbreakable, allowing donors to verify nothing has been altered before they vote.

**The problem it solves**

**ChainTorque** : The Problem it Solves & Use Cases

Modern engineering and 3D designers suffer from severe fragmentation, high barriers to entry, and a lack of secure intellectual property (IP) protection. Engineers, designers, and 3D artists typically rely on expensive, heavy desktop CAD software. When they want to collaborate, sell, or license their 3D models, they are forced to use web2 marketplaces that take massive cuts, lack transparency, and struggle with piracy and establishing true ownership of digital assets.

**ChainTorque** solves this by unifying a Browser-based CAD Workspace, AI-Powered 3D Generation, and a Decentralized Web3 Marketplace into a single, seamless platform. We have built an ecosystem where creators can design, generate, securely mint, and monetize their 3D intellectual property directly entirely on-chain.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Blockchain RPC Synchronization
**Challenge:** 
The Node.js backend kept crashing with an `ECONNREFUSED` error, failing to connect to the blockchain RPC provider. This stopped real-time data fetching and smart contract event syncing.

**Solution:**
* **Error Handling & Retries:** Implemented exponential backoff for connection drops.
* **RPC Fallbacks:** Configured secondary RPC providers to seamlessly take over if the primary node went down or rate-limited our backend.

### 2. 3D Model Loading in Android (Babylon.js)
**Challenge:** 
The Android app's 3D viewer threw `"Failed to load model"` errors. Babylon.js initialized, but couldn't fetch the model files from the storage server, showing a blank screen.

**Solution:**
* **CORS & Absolute URLs:** Updated the storage server's CORS headers for mobile and ensured the app requested absolute URIs instead of web-style relative paths.
* **Dynamic Viewport Scaling:** Fixed an issue where loaded models scaled incorrectly by adjusting Babylon.js camera initialization to dynamically read the Android device's screen dimensions.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon (Matic)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20(Matic)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## **Problem**

Smart contracts have "amnesia." They can only perceive the current state of the blockchain. If a user wants to prove they have a flawless history of repaying loans, surviving market crashes without being liquidated, or maintaining consistent high-volume trades—a standard smart contract cannot verify that without trusting a centralized off-chain entity (like a traditional credit bureau) or a trusted oracle.

On EVM chains, smart contracts are limited by the `BLOCKHASH` opcode, which only has access to the last 256 blocks (~10-15 minutes of history). Trustlessly verifying anything that happened months or years ago requires complex cryptographic workarounds.


## **Solution**

BlockVault introduces a novel architecture that uses **Generative AI to index and extract relevant financial history**, and **Rust-based relayers to provide cryptographic Merkle storage proofs**.

This allows lending protocols to issue verifiable "Credit Soulbound Tokens" (SBTs) that unlock under-collateralized loans for trustworthy users.

**Challenges we ran into**

Bypassing the EVM 256-block limit without a centralized oracle. 2. Engineering the LLM prompt to deterministically parse raw, unstructured blockchain hex data and extract exact storage slots without hallucinating.

**Ethereum Track**

BlockVault solves the critical 'amnesia' problem of smart contracts on EVM chains. By combining a Rust relayer with eth_getProof RPC calls, we mathematically prove historical Ethereum state (Merkle Patricia Trie paths) to our Solidity Verifier contract, enabling trustless, under-collateralized lending without relying on off-chain credit bureaus.

**Gemini API**

Submitted for Best Use of Gen AI: We used Google Gemini as a deterministic Risk Analyst Oracle. Our backend feeds unstructured Ethereum transaction hex data to the LLM, which is prompted to extract specific block numbers and storage slots indicating positive financial history into a strict JSON payload.
