### Zerotrace
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zerotrace-7987) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ambar-chakravartty/zerotrace) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RIcfmPyetro) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/RIcfmPyetro) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACK%20THE%20THRONE-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-the-throne.devfolio.co)

> Secure Data Wiping for IT Asset Recycling

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

When devices are sold, recycled, or discarded, normal deletion or formatting does not fully erase data, making it recoverable. This leads to data privacy risks, lack of trust in recyclers, and growing e-waste, as users hesitate to reuse or dispose of devices safely.

There is also no reliable, tamper-proof proof that data was securely destroyed.

💡** How ZeroTrace Helps**

ZeroTrace securely wipes storage devices at a low (firmware) level and generates a blockchain-verified Certificate of Destruction, ensuring data is permanently unrecoverable and publicly verifiable.

👥 **What People Can Use It For**

- Safely sell, donate, or recycle old devices

- Prevent data leaks and identity theft

- Prove secure data destruction for audits and compliance

- Build trust between users, enterprises, and recycling vendors

🔐**Why It’s Safer & Easier**

- Works below the operating system

- Uses NIST-compliant wipe methods

- Provides tamper-proof blockchain verification

- Simple, one-click interface for all users

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Limited Access to Real Hardware**

One major challenge was the unavailability of diverse physical storage devices (HDDs, SSDs, NVMe) for testing low-level wipe operations.

**Solution:** I relied on controlled environments, virtual testing, and manufacturer documentation to validate logic, while designing the system to remain hardware-agnostic and extensible for real-world deployment.

**2. Blockchain Integration with C++**

Directly integrating Ethereum blockchain logic with a low-level C++ core proved difficult due to limited native libraries and tooling.

**Solution:**I designed a Node.js helper service using ethers.js that acts as a bridge between the C++ wiping engine and the blockchain, cleanly separating system-level operations from blockchain interactions.

**3. GitHub Merge & Version Conflicts**

Frequent updates across multiple modules caused merge conflicts and branch inconsistencies.

**Solution: **I adopted structured branching, smaller commits, and regular rebasing to keep development stable and collaborative.

**4. GUI Modeling Failures with Raylib & Clay**

Building a professional-grade GUI using Raylib and Clay was challenging due to limited ecosystem support and rendering constraints.

**Solution:** I iterated through multiple UI prototypes, simplified rendering logic, and focused on usability and clarity over visual complexity.

**5. Blockchain Certification Design Dilemma**

Choosing between IPFS-based storage (Pinata) and on-chain JSON certification raised concerns around cost, immutability, and scalability.

**Solution:** I implemented a hybrid approach storing certificates on IPFS and anchoring only cryptographic hashes on Ethereum for verification.

**6. Delayed Thread Execution During Disk Wiping**

Long-running wipe operations caused thread blocking and delayed UI updates, affecting responsiveness.

**Solution:** I optimized thread handling by decoupling wipe execution from UI rendering and managing progress updates asynchronously.

**Ethereum Track**

**Certificate of Data Destruction Validation System**

A blockchain-based solution for generating, issuing, verifying, and downloading tamper-proof Certificates of Data Destruction. This system ensures device destruction records are immutable, transparent, and verifiable which is ideal for audits and compliance.

### PharmaTrace
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pharmatrace-f47d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Aman-Maurya-coder/PharmaTrace) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACK%20THE%20THRONE-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-the-throne.devfolio.co)

> Securing the chain of care.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The core problem this project solves is the lack of trust and transparency in the pharmaceutical supply chain, where counterfeit or tampered medicines can easily enter circulation due to fragmented, centralized record-keeping. In the current system, consumers and even distributors have no reliable way to independently verify whether a medicine is genuine. By anchoring verification data on the Ethereum blockchain, this project creates a tamper-proof source of truth for medicine authenticity. Each QR code links a physical product to immutable on-chain records, enabling instant, trustless verification by anyone without relying on manufacturers, vendors, or regulators as intermediaries. This directly addresses counterfeiting, data manipulation, and opacity—replacing blind trust with cryptographic proof and transparent smart contract logic.

**Challenges we ran into**

Here are the key challenges we ran into during the project, framed clearly for an Ethereum-track evaluation:

Scalability and Gas Costs
Writing data for thousands of medicine bottles directly on Ethereum quickly raised concerns around gas fees and transaction limits. We had to carefully decide what truly belongs on-chain versus what should stay off-chain (analytics, dashboards, metadata), while still preserving verifiability.

On-chain vs Off-chain Data Design
Designing the smart contract to store only cryptographic hashes instead of full product details was a major challenge. This required rethinking the data model so Ethereum is used as a source of truth, not a data warehouse, while still enabling meaningful verification.

QR Code Granularity
We debated between batch-level and bottle-level QR codes. Batch-level codes are cheaper and simpler, but reduce consumer-level trust. Bottle-level codes improve verification but significantly increase on-chain interactions and backend complexity.

Smart Contract Upgradability vs Immutability
Ethereum smart contracts are immutable by design, but real-world supply chains evolve. Balancing future-proofing (via upgrade patterns or versioning) without compromising trust and simplicity was a non-trivial design decision.

Wallet & Transaction UX
Expecting manufacturers or distributors to sign large numbers of transactions with wallets introduces friction. Designing a workflow that keeps Ethereum’s security guarantees while remaining usable for non-crypto-native users was a practical challenge.

Blockchain–Backend Synchronization
Keeping the backend database perfectly in sync with on-chain events (for analytics and dashboards) required reliable event indexing and error handling, especially when transactions are pending, reverted, or delayed.

Security & Trust Assumptions
Ensuring that only authorized manufacturers can mint or register medicine batches on-chain—and preventing misuse of the contract—required careful access control and threat modeling.

**Ethereum Track**

This project fits squarely into the Ethereum track by leveraging Ethereum’s core strengths—decentralization, immutability, and trustless verification—to solve a real-world problem in the pharmaceutical supply chain. By recording batch and bottle-level medicine data on smart contracts, the system ensures that once manufacturing details are written on-chain, they cannot be altered or forged. QR codes act as a bridge between the physical and digital worlds, allowing anyone—patients, pharmacists, or regulators—to instantly verify authenticity directly against the Ethereum blockchain without relying on a central authority. This aligns perfectly with the Ethereum track’s focus on building transparent, censorship-resistant, and verifiable applications that replace fragile, centralized trust with cryptographic guarantees and smart contract logic.

> FraudLense – AI-Powered Payment Fraud Detection

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Seaborn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Seaborn-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FraudLense is an intelligent machine learning–based system built to identify fraudulent online payment transactions in real-time. Using the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection dataset, the system applies advanced feature engineering, PCA-based dimensionality reduction, and XGBoost classification to deliver highly accurate, low-latency predictions.
The project is designed for scalable fintech environments and aligns strongly with the Fintech for Bharat mission to make digital payments safe and accessible for all.
As India rapidly transitions into a digital-first economy, online payment fraud has become a critical challenge. Fraudsters exploit device spoofing, behavioral manipulation, and high-velocity attacks to bypass traditional rule-based systems.

FraudLense solves these challenges by combining:

⚡ Real-time ML inference
📉 Dimensionality reduction (394 → 53 optimized features)
🤖 XGBoost with tuned hyperparameters
🧩 KMeans clustering for behavioral pattern detection
🖥️ A smooth, interactive Streamlit UI
📂 Clean ML pipeline with preprocessing, training, and evaluation
📊 Achieved 0.9456 Mean AUC ROC
🛡️ Helps identify fraud before it causes financial loss
The result is a fast, reliable, scalable solution ready for real-world fintech deployment.

**Challenges we ran into**

🟠 Memory Overload During Preprocessing
Large feature sets caused RAM issues → optimized using chunk processing and dtype reduction.

🟠 Label Encoding Failures
Unexpected categories triggered errors → added validation and fallback mappings.

🟠 Streamlit Secrets Configuration Errors
Missing keys caused UI breaks → implemented safe loaders and key checks.

🟠 Google Drive Pickle File Failures
Corrupted downloads due to invalid IDs → restructured downloader with verified file IDs.

🟠 UI Stability Issues
Broken components when users skipped fields → implemented validation wrappers and default values.

These challenges improved the robustness, reliability, and production-readiness of the entire pipeline.

**Open Innovation**

FraudLens is an advanced machine learning–based fraud detection system designed to analyze UPI and card transactions in real time. It identifies suspicious patterns, unusual behaviors, and high-risk activities using feature engineering, anomaly detection, and XGBoost classification

**The problem it solves**

Freelancers lose money to high platform fees.
Payments can be delayed, frozen, or disputed.
Current systems are opaque and rely on trust in companies.

How EscrowX Helps : 

1. Secure Payments: Funds locked in smart contracts, released only on completion.

2. No Middlemen: Freelancers get full payment; clients pay only for delivered work.

3. Transparent: All transactions are on-chain and verifiable.

4. Fair Negotiation: Handled fairly by supporting milestones and automated contract terms.

In short: EscrowX makes freelance work safe, fair, and transparent using blockchain.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was enabling negotiation between clients and service providers and then locking the agreed terms into the smart contract securely:

The Challenge:
Freelancers and clients needed a way to discuss and finalize terms such as scope of work, price, milestones, and deadlines. The system had to ensure that once an agreement was finalized, the rules could be fixed and automatically enforced by the smart contract. Any mismatch could lead to incorrect payments or disputes.

How We Solved It:
Implemented a negotiation chat system where both parties could agree on the terms interactively. Once confirmed, the terms are locked into the smart contract, making them immutable and automatically enforceable. This ensures payment security, transparency, and fairness without any human intervention.

The solution ensures that negotiated agreements become enforceable rules, giving both freelancers and clients confidence that payments and work conditions are secure and transparent.

**Emerging Technologies**

Blockchain Based Escrow: Uses smart contracts to automate payments, removing intermediaries and reducing commission, a practical application of blockchain technology.

Decentralized Trust: Eliminates reliance on centralized platforms, demonstrating trustless systems and decentralized workflows.

Interactive Negotiation & Rule Enforcement: Negotiation chat finalizes terms which are then locked into immutable contracts, showing innovation in automated agreement enforcement.

Transparency and Security: All transactions are recorded on-chain, highlighting emerging practices in secure, verifiable digital transactions.

EscrowX leverages cutting edge technologies (blockchain, smart contracts, decentralized systems) to solve real world problems in freelance marketplaces, making it a strong fit for the Emerging Technologies track.

> Decarbonizing the World, One Footprint at a Time

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Path2Zero helps individuals, companies, and farming communities take meaningful climate action without dealing with the complexity that usually comes with sustainability work. People can use it to understand their carbon impact through an easy-to-use calculator that adjusts for real-life factors like industry type, travel habits, energy use, and lifestyle. This gives users a clear picture of where their emissions come from and what they can do to reduce them.

The platform also makes it safer and simpler for companies to buy genuine carbon credits. Every credit on Path2Zero is backed by transparent monitoring and verification, so organisations don’t have to worry about greenwashing or unreliable offsets. It also creates a direct link between large organisations and farmers, allowing companies to support on-ground climate-friendly farming practices while farmers earn extra income for the environmental benefits they create.

Path2Zero also helps businesses save time by automating sustainability reporting and providing clean dashboards that track emissions, reductions, and offsets in one place. Individuals and companies can follow guided steps toward carbon neutrality, making the process more practical and achievable.

Overall, Path2Zero makes climate action easier, safer, and more accessible by turning complex environmental tasks into simple tools that anyone can use while ensuring the impact genuinely supports communities and contributes to SDG 13.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles we ran into while building Path2Zero was integrating all the different features into one smooth, functional platform. Each tool, the certificate authentication system, the carbon footprint calculator, and the chatbot worked perfectly on its own.
- The calculator’s output wasn’t syncing properly with the certificate generator.
- Authentication checks sometimes failed when users jumped between tools.
- The chatbot couldn’t always access user-specific data to answer questions.
We reorganized the backend using a centralized routing and shared data model. Instead of each feature storing information separately, we created a single structure where all components could pull and push data consistently. We also added asynchronous handling for API calls to prevent conflicts and made sure each tool authenticated through the same verification method.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges I ran into was setting up and correctly configuring the Gemini API. [![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finvest-3b09) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gargi-m21/finvest) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.canva.com/design/DAG4KbntFA4/aEOpIv53FDqC_swc5MAYAQ/edit) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackTU%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacktu7.devfolio.co)

> digital pitches, real deals

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Access to small-ticket capital is still broken for many micro-entrepreneurs. The two-sided problem is clear:

- Borrowers need quick, practical funding for inventory, equipment, and short-term working capital.
- Investors avoid these deals because risk is hard to observe and cash usage is hard to control.

Traditional options fail in opposite ways:

1. Formal lending is slow and document-heavy for small, urgent capital needs.
2. Informal lending is fast, but investors have weak visibility once cash leaves their account.
3. Even when intent is good, there is often no structured flow to enforce disciplined fund usage.

### What people can use FinVest for

- Funding small retail inventory cycles (kirana restock, seasonal goods)
- Small manufacturing or food business working capital
- Service business equipment purchases
- Vendor-tied micro expansion (raw materials, tools, service contracts)

### How FinVest makes this safer and easier

- Funds are not handed as unrestricted cash; they are controlled by escrow logic.
- Borrower progress is tied to tranches and proof submissions.
- Payouts go to verified vendors, reducing end-use ambiguity.
- Investor and borrower both get transparent status for deal funding, release, repayment, and risk.
- Recovery actions are progressive (reminders -> pause -> freeze -> default), balancing empathy with enforceability.

In short, FinVest enables capital flow where trust is low by replacing manual trust checks with product rules.

---

## What FinVest Does

FinVest supports the full borrower-investor lifecycle:

1. Borrower creates a pitch.
2. Investors place bids with deal terms.
3. Borrower accepts one offer and a deal is created.
4. Investor funds the deal (locked balance).
5. Borrower requests tranche releases with evidence.
6. Admin/investor approves release.
7. Payout executes to verified vendor.
8. Repayments are tracked with trust/risk signals.

### Key capabilities

- Multi-role platform: Borrower, Investor, Admin
- Escrow-backed state tracking (locked vs used balance)
- Tranche workflow with verification and approvals
- Vendor verification workflow
- Repayment schedule and overdue handling
- Risk engine for trust health (GREEN/YELLOW/RED)
- Optional blockchain audit trail (hash/event logging)

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest challenge was consistency across a multi-step, interdependent transaction system.

### Challenge 1: Maintaining consistent state across dependent operations

A single user action could trigger multiple updates:
- bid acceptance -> deal creation
- deal funding -> balance update
- tranche approval -> payout request
- payout execution -> tranche status + event logs

Risk: partial completion could leave records mismatched.

How we handled it:
- enforced explicit state transitions
- added guard checks to avoid invalid repeats
- centralized business rules in controllers/services

### Challenge 2: Optional integrations should not break core flow

AI services and blockchain logging are useful but should not become single points of failure.

How we handled it:
- optional model endpoints with fallback behavior
- blockchain queue/retry pattern
- core escrow/deal operations continue even if optional systems are unavailable

### Challenge 3: Balancing strict enforcement with borrower realism

Overly rigid systems can punish temporary delays.

How we handled it:
- progressive recovery ladder
- pause/freeze/default in stages
- risk score + reason codes to support transparent decisions

**Google Gemini**

# Why FinVest Fits the Gemini API Track

FinVest uses the Gemini API as the intelligence layer that converts informal stories into investable opportunities.  
Most micro-entrepreneurs cannot write business plans—Gemini transforms **voice notes, messy text, and images** into structured pitches that investors can compare.

### Where Gemini Is Used
- **Pitch Normalization:** Converts raw borrower input → structured fields (funding need, use of funds, milestones, risks).  
- **Invoice Understanding:** Extracts key data from uploaded bills to validate tranche requests.  
- **Risk Insights:** Generates human-readable reasons behind trust health (e.g., inactivity, delayed payments).  
- **Borrower Assistance:** Suggests repayment plans and simple explanations in local language.

### Impact
Gemini removes literacy barriers, reduces manual review, and enables fairer decision making.  
Without Gemini, FinVest would require formal documentation; with it, everyday entrepreneurs can access capital through natural conversation.

**Gemini = the bridge between informal users and structured finance.**

**MongoDB Atlas**

# Why FinVest Fits the MongoDB Track

FinVest is a data-intensive platform where every deal evolves through events—pitches, bids, tranches, payouts, and repayments.  
MongoDB’s flexible document model perfectly fits this lifecycle and enables real-time trust scoring.

### How MongoDB Powers FinVest
- **Event Store:** ActivityEvent collection tracks proofs, delays, uploads, and reminders for risk computation.  
- **Escrow Ledger:** Deal documents maintain lockedBalance, usedBalance, and tranche states atomically.  
- **Vendor Graph:** Verified sellers linked per borrower with dynamic KYC fields.  
- **Fast Queries:** Investor dashboards aggregate payouts, invoices, and repayment history instantly.  
- **Schema Flexibility:** Pitches and invoices vary widely—MongoDB handles unstructured data without migrations.

### Why It Matters
Financial inclusion requires adapting to messy real-world data.  
MongoDB enables FinVest to model evolving relationships and power the risk engine without rigid tables.

**MongoDB = the operational backbone of transparent, behavior-driven micro-finance.**

> Redifining property trust with passive profit

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Charts.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Charts.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional real estate investment is inaccessible, inflexible, and risky for a large section of people. Investing in property usually requires high upfront capital, extensive paperwork, long lock-in periods, and strong market knowledge. As a result, students, young professionals, and small investors are often excluded from one of the most stable asset classes.

Additionally, even for those who can invest:

Tracking investments is manual and confusing

There is low transparency in returns

Managing multiple properties requires spreadsheets or third-party tools

Entry and exit from investments are slow and illiquid

There is no simple, beginner-friendly digital platform that allows users to start small, track everything in one place, and understand returns clearly.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

Building a tokenized real-estate investment platform involved multiple technical and design challenges. Below are the key hurdles I faced and how I overcame them.

🔹 1. State Synchronization Across Pages

Problem:
The wallet balance and investments needed to stay in sync across multiple pages (Dashboard, Add Money, Marketplace, Property Details). Initially, updates made on one page were not reflected on others unless the page was refreshed.

Solution:
I centralized all wallet and investment logic using a shared utility (wallet.js) backed by localStorage. Additionally, I implemented a storage event listener to auto-refresh data when changes occur, ensuring real-time consistency across the application.

🔹 2. Preventing Invalid Transactions

Problem:
Users could attempt to invest more money than they had in their wallet, which would break the logical flow of the application.

Solution:
I added validation checks in the wallet utility functions (deductMoneyFromWallet). The system now blocks insufficient balance transactions and throws clear errors, ensuring financial logic remains consistent and safe.

🔹 3. Designing Flexible Token-Based Investments

Problem:
Early versions used fixed token prices, which limited user flexibility and reduced realism.

Solution:
I redesigned the investment flow to allow customizable token purchases, enabling users to choose how many tokens they want to buy based on available wallet balance. This made the platform more realistic and user-centric.

🔹 4. White Screen Errors During Navigation

Problem:
Clicking on certain routes (e.g., Marketplace or Property Details) resulted in a blank white screen due to missing or misconfigured routes.

Solution:
I carefully audited the routing setup in App.jsx, ensured all components were properly imported, and verified that dynamic routes were correctly defined. This resolved rendering issues and stabilized navigation.

🔹 5. Tailwind CSS Class Errors

Problem:
Certain Tailwind gradient classes caused build or rendering issues due to incorrect syntax or missing configuration.

Solution:
I validated all Tailwind classes and ensured they matched Tailwind’s supported utility format. I also avoided dynamically generated class names that Tailwind could not detect during build time.

🔹 6. Keeping the UI Beginner-Friendly Without Losing Depth

Problem:
Balancing advanced investment features while keeping the UI simple was challenging, especially for first-time users.

Solution:
I structured the UI with clear sections, minimal actions per screen, and meaningful labels. Advanced details are progressively revealed, ensuring usability without overwhelming the user.

🔹 7. No Backend / Payment Gateway in Hackathon Time

Problem:
Integrating real payment systems like Stripe within the hackathon timeframe would have required backend infrastructure and secure API handling.

Solution:
I implemented a simulated wallet system that mirrors real-world payment flows. This approach allowed me to demonstrate the full product logic while keeping the architecture ready for future Stripe integration.

**Open Innovation**

🔹 1. Democratizing Access to Real Estate Investment

Traditionally, real estate investment is:

Capital-intensive

Limited to high-net-worth individuals

Opaque and difficult to access

This project introduces fractional, token-based property ownership, enabling any user to participate with small amounts of money. By lowering the entry barrier, the platform opens real estate investment to a much broader and more diverse community, which is a core goal of open innovation.

🔹 2. Built Using Open-Source Technologies

The entire platform is developed using open-source tools and frameworks, such as:

React for the frontend

Tailwind CSS for UI design

Open browser APIs like localStorage

Charting libraries for data visualization

Because the tech stack is open, any developer can study, extend, or improve the system, encouraging shared innovation rather than closed, proprietary development.

🔹 3. Modular and Extensible Architecture

The project is designed with clearly separated modules:

Wallet utilities

Investment logic

UI components

Marketplace and analytics

This modularity makes it easy for external contributors to:

Add new investment models

Integrate blockchain or Stripe payments

Replace mock data with real APIs

Such extensibility is essential for open innovation ecosystems, where ideas evolve collaboratively.

🔹 4. Encouraging Community-Driven Enhancements

The platform is intentionally designed to be:

Backend-agnostic

Payment-gateway ready

Blockchain-ready

This allows innovators, startups, or researchers to:

Plug in real payment providers (Stripe, UPI, crypto wallets)

Add smart contracts for ownership verification

Integrate AI-based risk analysis or ROI predictions

The project acts as a foundation, inviting experimentation and co-creation.

🔹 5. Transparency Through Open Logic

Unlike traditional financial platforms that hide investment calculations, this project makes:

Token pricing

Return calculations

Wallet deductions

fully transparent in code and UI. Transparency builds trust and enables others to audit, validate, and improve the system—key principles of open innovation.

🔹 6. Real-World Problem, Shared Solution

The project tackles real problems:

Lack of investment accessibility

Poor financial inclusion

Limited exposure to passive income models

By presenting a replicable, open, and adaptable solution, the project encourages others to:

Apply it to different regions

Customize it for different asset classes

Use it for education, research, or startups

### The FalconSeg
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/the-falconseg-f5e2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Saanvi-gug/Payload-SaanviGuglani) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/136hKQVEz2lEnkSmtZmz4x9eh6VUjvi2f/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=109596582300470907190&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PayLoad'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pay-load.devfolio.co)

> Redefining Off-Road Navigation

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ResNet](https://img.shields.io/badge/ResNet-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In my opinion, the main issue is that "*modern autonomous navigation is spoiled by the presence of structured environments such as roads with lane markings, signs, and smooth asphalt.*" When an AI is tested in an off-road desert setting, these cues are absent, and conventional navigation systems are unable to differentiate between a safe sandy path and a dangerous rock or a misleading bush.

FalconSeg addresses this issue in the following ways:

**Bridging the Visual Gap:**FalconSeg offers the pixel-level "eyes" necessary to decode the raw, unstructured terrain where there are no roads.

**Handling High Complexity:** My AI system does not simply "see the ground"; it identifies 10 different types of environmental features, enabling a rover to make life-or-death decisions such as avoiding a log while safely crossing dry grass.

**Overcoming Data Reality:** A significant part of the challenge was the "noise" in the simulated data. By designing a custom remapping of mask labels, I overcame the technical challenge of data misalignment, which is a prevalent real-world issue when training an AI on a simulated environment.

In conclusion, this project addresses the issue of off-road blindness, transforming a messy desert landscape into a legible map for autonomous exploration.

**Challenges we ran into**

The process of reaching a 0.7580 mIoU was not linear. I encountered three main challenges that needed innovative problem-solving skills:
**The "Mask Value" Mismatch:** The most significant technical challenge was finding out that the synthetic masks involved pixel values such as 100, 200, and 255, as opposed to the expected class label values of 0-9. At first, this resulted in my model not working at all, but I overcame this by designing a custom DesertDataset class to adjust for these values, which eventually allowed my model to learn.
**The Model Depth and Speed Trade-Off:** At first, I thought of using more complex models, but since off-road navigation involves real-time processing, I had to make a deliberate choice about the ResNet34 backbone architecture—it was deep enough to capture complex textures such as "Dry Bushes" versus "Lush Bushes," but not so complex that it hindered real-time processing.
**Resource Constraints:** Since I was constrained by the memory capacity of a single T4 GPU in Google Colab, I had to be extremely careful about my batch size and training epochs. I invested considerable time in adjusting the learning rate to 1*10^-4. which helped my model learn without "forgetting" features during extended training sessions.
**Data Scarcity for Rare Classes: **Certain classes, such as "Flowers" or "Logs," appeared much less frequently in the synthetic desert scenes. While I achieved a strong overall mIoU, it was a challenge to ensure the model didn't just ignore these rare objects in favor of the dominant "Sand" and "Sky" classes.

**Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation Challenge - LLMs and AI**

FalconSeg addresses the core challenge of the* Off-Road Semantic Scene Segmentation* track: enabling autonomous systems to perceive unstructured, non-road environments. While standard AI relies on paved roads and lane markings, our model provides the "eyes" for complex desert navigation.

***Technical Highlights***

**Architecture:** Utilizes a U-Net with a ResNet34 backbone to balance high-resolution feature extraction with real-time inference speed.

**Data Engineering:** Resolved a critical "Reality Gap" by remapping synthetic mask values (100-255) into discrete class IDs (0-9), unlocking the model's ability to learn.

**Performance:** Achieved a 0.7580 mIoU, demonstrating reliable identification of 10 complex classes, including hazardous obstacles like Rocks and Logs.

> “Turning Trees into Climate Assets”

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Figma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Figma-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Package JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/Package%20JSON-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem Carbonly Solves

Climate action today suffers from lack of trust, transparency, and incentives.

: Fake or unverifiable carbon credits are widely traded.
: Tree planting efforts go unrewarded and untracked.
: Companies struggle to find reliable carbon offset sources.
: Common people and farmers have no motivation to participate in carbon markets.
: No unified system exists to track real environmental impact from the ground level.
[-->As a result, many “green” initiatives exist only on paper, with little real-world impact.]

What People Can Use Carbonly For
Individuals & Communities

:Earn rewards for planting and maintaining trees
:Track the real impact of their green actions
:Participate in climate action without technical knowledge

Farmers & Rural Workers

:Generate additional income from agroforestry
:Monetize unused land sustainably
:Get fair value for long-term environmental contribution

Companies & Industries

:Purchase authentic, traceable carbon credits
:Meet ESG and sustainability goals
:Avoid reputational risks from fake offsets

Governments & NGOs

:Monitor real-time green initiatives
:Ensure funds go to actual environmental work
:Improve policy enforcement and transparency

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a16829b0c7d644289811cc9941deed64/6551ea29-5e1d-4bea-9e72-3dbeffe1780b.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Technical Challenges Faced...

While building Carbonly, I encountered several technical issues, mainly around blockchain integration and backend stability.

Blockchain immutability vs dynamic tree data...
Tree data changes over time, but blockchain data cannot. I solved this by storing only hashes and proofs on-chain and keeping dynamic data off-chain in the backend.

Smart contract deployment & Hardhat issues...
Faced network mismatch errors, gas limit failures, and inconsistent test results in Hardhat. Fixed this by optimizing contracts, configuring environments correctly, and writing unit tests before deployment.

Backend–blockchain sync bug...
Some transactions succeeded on-chain but failed to update the backend, causing credit mismatch. I resolved this by updating the backend only after transaction confirmation.

API performance problems..

Carbon calculation logic initially slowed the backend under load. This was fixed using async processing and separating verification and minting services.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a16829b0c7d644289811cc9941deed64/5e6d616e-f331-4ce2-a8aa-021929c9a45c.png)

**Open Innovation**

Carbonly fits into the Open Track as it addresses a real-world problem trust and transparency in carbon credits using a flexible and innovative approach. The project combines environmental sustainability, blockchain, and backend systems to convert real tree-based carbon absorption into verifiable digital credits.

Since the Open Track encourages solutions without domain restrictions, Carbonly leverages technology creatively to solve a global climate challenge, while remaining scalable and adaptable for individuals, companies, NGOs, and governments. The idea is not limited to a single industry and can evolve with future integrations like IoT and satellite verification.

> Decoding Market Stress. Defining Market Regimes.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Analytics](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Analytics-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

StrataQuant helps users understand market behavior beyond price movements.

Financial markets generate massive amounts of data, but traditional tools often analyze returns, volatility, risk, drawdowns, and market regimes in isolation. This fragmented approach makes it difficult for users to understand when markets are stable, stressed, or transitioning into crisis.

StrataQuant solves this by:

Combining returns, volatility, drawdowns, stress indicators, and regime detection into one unified framework.

Translating complex quantitative metrics into clear, explainable insights.

Helping users identify market stress periods, downside risk, and structural regime shifts.

Enabling cross-market comparisons (e.g., emerging vs developed markets) with proper context.

Acting as an educational tool through an integrated analytics assistant that explains charts, indicators, and financial concepts.

**Challenges we ran into**

Designing a meaningful Market Stress Index
Combining multiple indicators into a single composite stress score without overfitting or bias was challenging. We solved this by carefully normalizing metrics and testing behavior across different market conditions.

Regime detection without prediction bias
The goal was to understand market states, not predict prices. Ensuring regime classification remained explainable and data-driven required multiple iterations of rolling statistics and threshold tuning.

Data consistency and preprocessing
Historical market data often contains missing values and inconsistent time ranges. We implemented robust preprocessing pipelines to ensure accurate rolling calculations and comparisons.

Balancing depth with usability
Advanced analytics can overwhelm users. Designing dashboards that were both enterprise-grade and easy to interpret required continuous UI refinement and user-centric thinking.

**Quantifying the Markets - Machine Learning**

StrataQuant fits naturally into the “Quantifying the Markets – Machine Learning” track by applying data-driven and machine learning techniques to interpret market behavior in a structured and explainable way.

The project processes historical market index data and uses statistical learning, rolling analytics, and regime classification techniques to quantify market stress, volatility, drawdowns, and structural shifts. Instead of predicting prices, StrataQuant focuses on understanding market dynamics, identifying stable, volatile, and crisis regimes through data-backed models.

Machine learning and quantitative methods are used to:

Detect market regimes and transitions

Aggregate multiple risk indicators into a composite Market Stress Index

Analyze volatility patterns and downside risk across time

Enable cross-market behavioral comparisons

By combining machine learning with financial analytics and explainable insights, StrataQuant transforms raw market data into actionable intelligence—perfectly aligning with the goal of quantifying markets using ML-driven approaches.

### Blockchain Based Health Record Wallet
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/blockchain-based-health-record-wallet-733d) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/DwRqx4H04fE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> Patient-Owned Medical Records on Blockchain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Healthcare records today are stored across different hospitals, labs, and clinics in disconnected systems. Patients do not truly own their medical data and must rely on centralized servers that are vulnerable to breaches, loss, and unauthorized access. Sharing records between doctors is slow, manual, and often insecure, leading to delays in treatment and repeated tests.

There is also no transparent way for patients to track who accessed their medical data and when, creating privacy and accountability concerns.

The Decentralized Health Records Wallet (DHRW) provides a secure, patient-controlled solution using blockchain and encryption. Medical records are encrypted and stored on decentralized storage (IPFS), while smart contracts manage access permissions and maintain an immutable audit trail.

Users can safely upload records, grant or revoke doctor access, and view transparent access logs. This makes healthcare data sharing faster, safer, and more reliable while ensuring full patient ownership and privacy.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was integrating the frontend with blockchain wallets such as MetaMask and Trust Wallet. Initially, transaction popups were not appearing due to incorrect provider initialization and event handling. We solved this by properly configuring ethers.js and separating wallet connection logic from contract interaction logic.

Another hurdle was smart contract compilation and deployment errors caused by mismatched Solidity versions and Hardhat configuration issues. This was resolved by aligning compiler versions and setting up the Hardhat project cleanly.

Integrating encrypted IPFS uploads with blockchain storage was also challenging, as both backend and smart contract processes needed to work sequentially. We fixed this by ensuring files were encrypted and uploaded to IPFS first, and only the returned CID was written to the blockchain.

Finally, updating audit logs in real time required implementing blockchain event listeners, which helped synchronize UI updates with smart contract events.

These challenges improved our understanding of decentralized application architecture and debugging across frontend, backend, and blockchain layers.

	•	Information overload: To find the best yield, a user has to keep 10+ tabs open (Aave, Uniswap, Curve, etc.) and manually compare rates.
	•	Stale data: Many dashboards update slowly, meaning the APY you see might not be the APY you get.
	•	Complexity: Understanding "impermanent loss" or "health factors" requires technical knowledge allowing for costly mistakes.
2. What People Can Use Plutus For
Plutus acts as a unified operating system for DeFi activities:
		**Yield Hunting (The Market Page)**
	•	Use case: A user has 10,000 USDC and wants the best return. instead of checking every protocol individually, they visit the Market page.
	•	Action: They filter by "Stablecoins" and "Low Risk" to instantly see that Aave V3 on Arbitrum offers the best risk-adjusted rate.
		**Intelligent Portfolio Tracking**
	•	Use case: A user wants to know their net worth and asset breakdown across chains.
	•	Action: They connect their wallet via RainbowKit to see a live visualization of their holdings, analyzing their exposure to different assets.
		**AI-Powered Financial Analysis (Agent X402)**
	•	Use case: A user is unsure if a specific pool is safe or how it works.
	•	Action: They ask Agent X402: "Explain the risks of the ETH-USDC pool on Uniswap," and receive a data-backed explanation rather than generic advice.
		**Developer Integration**
	•	Use case: A developer wants to build a trading bot but doesn't want to index the blockchain themselves.
	•	Action: They use the Developer API (/api/yields) to fetch aggregated, clean yield data to power their own application.

2. Normalizing Fragmented DeFi Data

**Plutus** is an intelligent, real-time DeFi dashboard designed to simplify yield farming and portfolio management on Ethereum. By aggregating live data from major protocols and integrating an AI-driven analyst, Plutus empowers users to discover high-yield opportunities and make data-backed investment decisions with confidence.

### TrendVault AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trendvault-ai-37b7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Midnight-Maverick/TrendVault-AI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> Advanced Cryptocurrency Forecasting Engine

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Project Utility: Why TrendVault AI?
TrendVault AI is designed to demystify cryptocurrency volatility for retail traders and developers. It makes existing financial analysis tasks significantly easier and safer through:

Automated Technical Analysis: Instead of manually calculating indicators across different platforms, TrendVault provides a unified "Health Score" by aggregating RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands in real-time.

Safety via Data-Driven Insights: By using an iterative regression model, the platform identifies potential "trend exhaustion" points, helping users avoid emotional trading decisions during market spikes.

Developer-First Architecture: With a structured FastAPI backend, other developers can easily integrate TrendVault’s prediction engine into their own trading bots or notification systems via our standardized REST endpoints.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Recursive Lag" Prediction Bug
The Hurdle: During the initial build of the iterative forecast loop, the model’s predictions would quickly "flatline" after 3 or 4 steps. This happened because the feature-engineering pipeline wasn't correctly shifting the "predicted" price back into the close_lag_1 and close_lag_2 columns for the next step.

The Fix: I re-engineered the Predictor class to use a dynamic sliding window. Every time the engine predicts a price, it appends a synthetic row to a temporary DataFrame and re-calculates the rolling indicators (SMA/RSI) before the next iteration. This ensured the 24-hour forecast remained reactive to the simulated trend.

2. Asynchronous Data Inconsistentency
The Hurdle: Fetching live data from the Binance API while maintaining a high-speed frontend resulted in "flickering" UI components when the API rate-limited the backend.

The Fix: I implemented a Caching & Middleware Strategy. I added a custom FastAPI middleware to track X-Process-Time and implemented an in-memory NEWS_CACHE with a 10-minute TTL (Time-To-Live). This reduced redundant API calls and ensured the dashboard remained snappy even under heavy load.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ruon-1df9) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://merchant.ruon.click/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> RUON

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express%20js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next%20JS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

RUON solves critical pain points in Indonesia's retail payment ecosystem:

🔴 HIGH MDR FEES: Indonesian merchants are burdened with 0.7%+ admin fees for QRIS transactions, eating into their thin profit margins.

⏰ DELAYED SETTLEMENT: Traditional payment systems require H+1 (next-day) settlement, creating cash flow problems for small businesses.

🔒 COMPLEX WEB3 ONBOARDING: Seed phrases and gas fees scare away everyday users from adopting crypto payments.

💡 OUR SOLUTION:
- Instant settlement using IDRX stablecoin on Base L2
- Zero gas fees for users via Paymaster integration  
- No seed phrase needed - login with Biometric/Passkey via Coinbase Smart Wallet
- Real-time "Cair!" notification for merchants in <3 seconds

RUON empowers Indonesian UMKM (micro-businesses) with crypto-level efficiency while maintaining Web2-level simplicity. Merchants get instant access to funds, users pay seamlessly with QR scan, and everyone benefits from transparent onchain transactions.

**Challenges we ran into**

🔧 REAL-TIME PAYMENT NOTIFICATIONS:
Implementing instant payment confirmations was challenging. We explored Alchemy webhooks but switched to a polling-based solution for reliability. Getting the Socket.io integration to work seamlessly between backend and merchant dashboard required multiple iterations.

⛽ GASLESS TRANSACTIONS:
Integrating the Paymaster for gasless transactions while maintaining security was tricky. We needed to carefully configure OnchainKit to sponsor gas fees without exposing vulnerabilities.

🔐 WALLET ABSTRACTION:
Making Smart Wallet creation invisible to users while maintaining proper onchain identity was complex. Balancing Web2 UX expectations with Web3 security requirements took significant effort.

🔗 CONTRACT-FRONTEND SYNC:
Keeping frontend state in sync with blockchain state, especially for payment status updates, required careful architecture of the hybrid onchain/offchain system.

📱 QR CODE PARSING:
Implementing EIP-681 compliant QR code generation and parsing for dynamic payment amounts and order IDs across different mobile camera implementations was challenging.

**Base Track**

1. Our application runs on Ethereum Layer 2 (Base), ensuring fast transactions with low fees while leveraging Ethereum's security.

2. We integrate with IDRX (Indonesian Rupiah Stablecoin), making our application fully compliant with the hackathon requirements.

3. RUON's core focus is simplification — aligned with Base Track's mission to simplify complex DeFi processes and deliver an intuitive UX for everyday users who are new to Web3.

> Readable proof for onchain transactions

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

Blockchain transactions are transparent and verifiable, but they are not easy to understand for non-technical users.
Most transactions are represented only by hashes, addresses, and raw data, which makes it difficult to explain what the transaction was for, why it happened, or how it should be interpreted.

As a result:

Non-technical users struggle to understand onchain activity.

Transaction hashes are hard to use as proof of payment or action.

Block explorers are built for developers, not for everyday communication.

Explaining onchain transactions still requires technical knowledge.

Proofly solves this UX gap by adding a human-readable layer on top of blockchain transactions.

Instead of relying on raw transaction hashes, users can create transactions through Proofly and attach meaningful context such as a title and note. The transaction is then presented as a clear, readable receipt that anyone can understand and share, without needing blockchain expertise.

By translating onchain data into human-friendly receipts, Proofly makes blockchain interactions more approachable, explainable, and practical for everyday use.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into

Making the onchain transaction flow feel as simple and familiar as a Web2 experience for non-technical users.

Designing a product that users would actually want to use, despite not changing how transactions technically work.

Defining a realistic monetization path without hurting early adoption, leading to a freemium-first approach.

**Base Track**

How Proofly fits into the Base Track

Proofly fits naturally into the Base Track as a mini-app focused on improving onchain user experience.

Base enables fast and low-cost transactions, making it suitable for everyday usage. However, everyday usage also requires everyday clarity. While transactions on Base are transparent and verifiable, they are still represented in a technical format that is difficult for non-technical users to understand.

Proofly addresses this UX gap by adding a human-readable layer on top of Base transactions. Instead of relying on raw transaction hashes or developer-focused block explorers, Proofly presents transactions as clear, contextual receipts that can be easily read and shared by anyone.

By turning Base transactions into understandable receipts without changing the underlying protocol, Proofly demonstrates how better UX can make onchain interactions more approachable and practical for real-world use cases.

### EscrowKita
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/escrowkita-2df7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/nayrbryanGaming/EscrowKita/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://escrowkita.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> IDRX Onchain Escrow for Events & Freelancers

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In many real-world work arrangements such as events and freelance projects, payment trust remains a major issue. Clients worry about non-delivery, while freelancers and vendors often face delayed or unpaid work. Existing solutions rely on manual transfers, screenshots, and informal agreements, which lack transparency and enforcement.

EscrowKita addresses this by providing a trustless onchain escrow system using IDRX (IDR-pegged stablecoin) on Base. Funds are locked in a smart contract and only released after proof of work is submitted and approved. Timeout rules protect both parties, and all transactions are transparent and verifiable onchain.

EscrowKita makes payments for events and freelance work safer, clearer, and more reliable, without requiring users to understand complex crypto concepts.

**Challenges we ran into**

One key challenge was designing a secure escrow state machine that prevents double payouts, early claims, and unauthorized actions. This was solved by defining strict escrow states, enforcing role-based permissions, and validating every state transition onchain.

Another challenge was handling the ERC20 approval flow on the frontend, as users must approve tokens before depositing. This was addressed by guiding users through a clear two-step process: Approve Token → Deposit Funds, with UI feedback at each step.

Since IDRX is not available on testnet, a MockIDRX ERC20 token was deployed on Base Sepolia to demonstrate the full escrow flow, with a clearly documented path to migrate to the official IDRX token on mainnet.

**Base Track**

EscrowKita fits naturally into the Base Track by focusing on real-world, retail-friendly onchain payments and trust mechanisms built directly on Base.

The project addresses key Base Track goals such as improving onchain user experience, simplifying onboarding, and enabling practical adoption beyond crypto-native users. By using an IDR-pegged stablecoin (IDRX) and a transparent smart contract escrow model, EscrowKita allows users to interact with onchain infrastructure without dealing with volatility or complex DeFi flows.

EscrowKita is fully deployed on Base, leverages Base’s low-cost and fast transaction environment, and demonstrates how Base can be used to power practical, real-world applications such as event payments and freelance work—making it a strong and relevant submission for the Base Track.

> IDRX Paylink Mini‑App on Base

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

BayarR solves the friction of payment coordination over chat. Today, a creator has to send bank details or a wallet address, wait for proof, manually confirm, and reconcile later. That process is slow and error‑prone for small payments.  
BayarR compresses the flow into a single onchain link: create once, share anywhere, and the buyer pays directly from their wallet. The receipt is onchain, so there is no manual confirmation step.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Onchain vs. offchain data**: We wanted the paylink note to sync across devices without a backend. The initial approach stored a hash, which made the note unreadable. We updated the contract to store the note string onchain so the UX stays consistent everywhere.  
- **RPC limitations**: Free RPC tiers restrict log queries. We removed heavy log polling and moved receipt hashes into the post‑payment URL, while keeping paid status onchain.  
- **Wallet UX consistency**: OnchainKit wallet widgets behave differently across wallets. We added a custom wallet summary panel (balances + explorer link) to provide a consistent experience for all wallets.

**Base Track**

BayarR is a Base mini‑app focused on improving onchain UX for everyday payments. It leverages Base’s fast, low‑cost confirmations to make a paylink feel as simple as sending a message. The app uses OnchainKit for wallet and transaction flows and is built to be mobile‑first, minimal, and immediately usable.  
This directly aligns with the Base Track goal of improving onboarding and simplifying onchain interactions for retail users.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![EBay API](https://img.shields.io/badge/EBay%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FLIPT bridges the gap between Web2 e-commerce giants and Web3 liquidity by allowing users to instantly tokenize and crowdfund high-value items directly from eBay listings.

**The Core Problem:**
High-value real-world assets (RWAs) like vintage watches, graded trading cards, or luxury sneakers are often illiquid and inaccessible to the average retail investor due to high price points. Furthermore, bringing these assets on-chain usually requires complex oracle setups or manual verification processes.

**Our Solution:**
FLIPT creates an automated, trust-minimized "Click-to-Deploy" infrastructure on Base.

Instant RWA Deployment: Users simply paste an eBay URL. The system scrapes the metadata, validates the listing (ensuring it is "Buy It Now" and in stock), and automatically deploys a specific Smart Contract (RWAPool) on Base Sepolia representing that specific item.

Democratized Ownership: Instead of one person paying $10,000 for a collectible, 100 people can contribute $100 USDC via the smart contract.
Wallet Abstraction: We solve the onboarding friction by generating server-side wallets (using Viem and Supabase) for users who sign up with email. This allows web2-native users to interact with the blockchain seamlessly while retaining the security of on-chain settlement.

It makes the task of pooling capital for real-world acquisitions transparent, auditable via the blockchain, and accessible via a familiar e-commerce interface.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Secure Server-Side Wallet Management**
One of the biggest hurdles was creating a seamless "Web2-like" experience where the application handles transactions on behalf of the user without custodying plain-text private keys.

The Hurdle: We needed to generate wallets for users (via api/wallet/create) and sign transactions (like contributing to a pool) without exposing keys or requiring a browser extension popup for every action.

The Fix: I implemented an encryption system using crypto (AES-256-GCM) to store encrypted private keys and IVs in Supabase. When a user initiates a contribution, the server retrieves the encrypted key, decrypts it in memory for milliseconds to sign the transaction using Viem, and then discards it.

**2. Handling ERC-20 Approvals in a "Headless" Flow**
The smart contract logic requires an ERC-20 approve transaction before a deposit can occur.

The Hurdle: In a standard dApp, the user approves via MetaMask. Since our server controls the user's interaction wallet, managing the asynchronous nature of waiting for the Approval block confirmation before triggering the Deposit transaction caused race conditions.

The Fix: I wrote a robust handler in api/listing/contribute that checks the allowance first. If insufficient, it broadcasts an Infinite Approval transaction, awaits the transaction receipt explicitly using client.waitForTransactionReceipt, and only then executes the deposit function.

**3. Validating eBay Data for Smart Contracts**
Not all eBay items are suitable for crowdfunding (e.g., Auctions with dynamic ending times).

The Fix: I built a validation layer (api/validate-item) that interacts with the eBay Browse API. It parses the URL for the Legacy ID and strictly enforces that items must be FIXED_PRICE (Buy It Now) before allowing the UI to proceed to the smart contract deployment stage.

**Base Track**

FLIPT fits the "Elevated Onchain User Experience" track by radically abstracting the complexity of DeFi interaction into a familiar Web2 e-commerce flow. We address three specific UX challenges:

**Eliminating Poor Onboarding:**
We removed the "empty wallet problem." Instead of forcing users to install a browser extension and manage seed phrases immediately, FLIPT uses a managed server-side wallet architecture (via Viem and Supabase). Users sign up with an email ("Connect ID"), and the system generates an encrypted wallet on Base Sepolia for them in the background. This allows users to start interacting with the protocol immediately.

**Simplifying Complex DeFi Processes:**
Deploying a smart contract usually requires developer tooling (Remix/Hardhat). FLIPT turns this into a consumer action. By pasting an eBay URL, the app validates the metadata and executes a raw bytecode deployment of our RWAPool contract. Furthermore, the contribution flow automates the tedious ERC20 Approve -> Wait -> Deposit cycle into a single "Confirm Deposit" button press, handling the gas and sequence management on the backend.

**Enhancing Social Coordination:**
We turn the solitary act of buying an item on eBay into a multiplayer coordination game. By leveraging Base's low gas fees, we can afford to deploy a unique contract for every single item, allowing communities to pool capital for specific assets (like a rare trading card) in real-time without the friction of high transaction costs eating into their contribution.
