# BrainBase

## Decentralized Q&A Platform Powered by BRAIN Token on Base

### Executive Summary

BrainBase is a decentralized Q&A platform built on Base L2 that transforms knowledge sharing from unpaid labor into a sustainable economic model. By leveraging BRAIN tokens (ERC-20 on Base Network) and smart contract escrow, we enable experts to earn fair compensation for quality answers while providing askers with fast, reliable solutions. Unlike traditional platforms that extract 20-40% fees and operate on opaque algorithms, BrainBase ensures 98-100% of bounties reach experts through trustless, transparent blockchain transactions with ultra-low fees (~$0.01 per transaction).

Our key innovation lies in monetizing the $50B expert knowledge market with near-zero-fee, trustless payments via Base L2 blockchain using BRAIN token and mIDRX stablecoin support for Indonesian users.

---

### The Problem

The current landscape of knowledge sharing and expert consultation is fundamentally broken. On platforms like Stack Overflow, 58 million answers were provided in 2023, representing approximately $2.1 billion in value, yet contributors earned nothing. Approximately 40% of complex questions receive zero answers because there is no economic incentive for experts to invest their time. Collectively, experts donate an estimated $12 billion annually in knowledge while platforms profit $3.8 billion.

Platform exploitation compounds this problem. Services like Upwork and Fiverr extract 20-40% in fees, meaning a $100 job results in only $60-77 reaching the expert. Additionally, 2.3 billion unbanked adults worldwide are excluded from these platforms entirely due to traditional payment infrastructure requirements. Payment delays of 14-30 days further discourage participation.

Response times on existing platforms create real economic damage. Stack Overflow averages 48-72 hours for answers, while Upwork projects take 3-5 days just to begin. With production bugs costing businesses $5,600 per minute, these delays are unacceptable. The trust issues on centralized platforms, with 8.2% dispute rates and freelancers winning only 43% of disputes, result in $1.3 billion in annual fraud losses.

---

### Our Solution

BrainBase solves these problems through a token-powered bounty system built on Base L2. Users lock 1-10,000+ BRAIN tokens in a smart contract when posting questions. These funds are guaranteed until the question asker selects a winning answer, with 100% transparency on the blockchain. The competitive marketplace allows multiple experts to answer the same question, supporting rich content including code snippets, images, and detailed explanations with real-time WebSocket updates.

Our smart contract escrow system ensures trustless automatic payouts in BRAIN tokens with zero platform custody and zero payment disputes. The system is designed for speed, targeting response times under 1 hour compared to 48-72 hours on traditional platforms.

For accessibility, BrainBase includes a free BRAIN faucet that provides new users with 10 BRAIN tokens for free through a one-time claim per account, significantly lowering the entry barrier for new participants.

---

### Token Economics

BrainBase operates on a dual-token model designed for the Base ecosystem. BRAIN Token serves as the native utility token for the platform, used for all bounty payments and redeemable through our integrated swap system. mIDRX (Mock IDRX) provides stablecoin functionality, particularly valuable for Indonesian users, and is fully swappable with BRAIN at a rate of 5,000 mIDRX to 1 BRAIN.

The BRAIN token enables micro-transaction economics that traditional payment systems cannot support. Where credit card fees of $0.45 on a $5 transaction represent 9%, BRAIN transactions on Base cost approximately $0.01, representing only 0.2%. This unlocks millions of small-value questions that would be economically unviable on traditional platforms. The global inclusion aspect means the platform works in all 195 countries without requiring bank accounts, with instant settlement available to the 2.3 billion unbanked adults worldwide.

---

### Tech Stack

The frontend is built with Next.js 15 using the App Router, TailwindCSS for styling, and OnchainKit for seamless wallet integration supporting both Coinbase Smart Wallet and MetaMask. The application uses Wagmi and Viem for blockchain interactions with full Base Sepolia testnet support.

The backend runs on NestJS with PostgreSQL database managed through Prisma ORM. Real-time updates are handled via WebSocket connections, and the authentication flow uses Google OAuth for seamless onboarding.

Smart contracts are developed in Solidity and deployed on Base Sepolia. The contract architecture includes BrainToken.sol (ERC-20 BRAIN token with 1 billion supply), MockIDRX.sol (stablecoin with faucet functionality), BrainSwap.sol (AMM-style swap between mIDRX and BRAIN with configurable rates), and QnAWithBounty.sol (Q&A bounty escrow

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

## Smart Contract Deployment and Configuration on Base Sepolia

Deploying multiple interconnected smart contracts (BrainToken, MockIDRX, BrainSwap, and QnAWithBounty) on Base Sepolia required careful sequencing. The BrainSwap contract needed the addresses of both BrainToken and MockIDRX during construction, meaning we had to deploy them in the correct order. After deployment, we needed to transfer initial liquidity (100M BRAIN and 100M mIDRX) to the swap contract and verify that all contract addresses were correctly configured in both the backend and frontend environment files.

## Backend ABI Synchronization with Smart Contracts

During development, we updated the BrainSwap contract to add new features like mutable IDRX token addresses and different swap rate naming conventions. This caused a 500 error on the `/faucet-swap/info` endpoint because the backend ABI did not match the deployed contract. The service was calling functions like `swapRate()` that had been renamed to `ethToBrainRate()`. We resolved this by carefully regenerating the ABI from the compiled contract and updating all service method calls to use the correct function signatures.

## OnchainKit Wallet Aggregator Configuration

When implementing wallet connectivity with OnchainKit, the initial setup only connected directly to Coinbase Smart Wallet without showing a wallet selection modal. Users could not choose between Coinbase Wallet and MetaMask. We solved this by configuring the `OnchainKitProvider` with `wallet: { display: 'modal' }` to enable the wallet aggregator. Additionally, we had to add the MetaMask connector to the wagmi configuration alongside the Coinbase Wallet connector.

## Token Swap Rate Precision Across the Stack

Implementing the mIDRX ↔ BRAIN swap feature required synchronizing rate calculations between the smart contract (using 1e18 precision for all values) and the frontend UI (displaying human-readable decimals). The `idrxToBrainRate` of `0.0002` (meaning 5,000 mIDRX = 1 BRAIN) needed to be consistently represented across the Solidity contract, the NestJS backend API responses, and the React frontend calculations to ensure users saw accurate conversion estimates before executing swaps.

**Base Track**

# Why BrainBase Fits the Base Track

## Overview

BrainBase is a decentralized Q&A platform built as a Base Mini-App that directly addresses the problems outlined in the Base Track. It combines **social coordination**, **DeFi mechanics**, and **consumer-friendly UX** to create a knowledge-sharing economy powered by low-cost Base L2 transactions.

---

## 1. Social Coordination Tool

BrainBase enables meaningful social coordination through:

- **Bounty-Driven Q&A**: Users post questions with BRAIN token bounties, creating economic incentives for community knowledge sharing
- **Collaborative Verification**: Question askers verify answers, creating a trust layer where quality knowledge is rewarded
- **Author-Answerer Economy**: Direct value transfer between knowledge seekers and providers without intermediaries

This transforms isolated interactions into **coordinated, incentivized collaboration**.

---

## 2. Low-Cost Base L2 Transactions

Every core interaction leverages Base's **~$0.01 transaction fees**:

| Action                      | On-Chain          |
| --------------------------- | ----------------- |
| Post Question with Bounty   | ✅ Smart Contract |
| Submit Answer               | ✅ Smart Contract |
| Claim Bounty Reward         | ✅ Smart Contract |
| Token Swaps (mIDRX ↔ BRAIN) | ✅ Smart Contract |

These low fees make **micro-bounties economically viable**—users can post 1 BRAIN bounties without fee overhead eating the reward.

---

## 3. Consumer-Grade UX with OnchainKit

BrainBase implements mobile-first, intuitive workflows:

- **Smart Wallet Support**: Coinbase Smart Wallet + MetaMask via OnchainKit
- **One-Click Swaps**: mIDRX ↔ BRAIN token swaps with automatic approval flow
- **Seamless Onboarding**: Google OAuth sign-in, wallet connection in 2 clicks
- **No Expert Knowledge Required**: Clean UI abstracts blockchain complexity

---

## 4. DeFi & Payments Integration

Built-in token economy for the Indonesian market:

- **mIDRX Support**: Mock IDRX stablecoin integration (ready for real IDRX when available)
- **BrainSwap Contract**: On-chain liquidity pool for token swaps
- **Faucet System**: Easy onboarding with free BRAIN tokens for new users

---

## 5. Composable Smart Contracts

Modular contract architecture on Base Sepolia:

| Contract            | Purpose                                |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `BrainToken.sol`    | ERC20 governance/utility token         |
| `BrainSwap.sol`     | AMM-style swap with configurable rates |
| `QnAWithBounty.sol` | Bounty escrow and reward distribution  |
| `MockIDRX.sol`      | Stablecoin integration layer           |

All contracts are upgradeable and composable with future Base ecosystem primitives.

---

## Summary

| Base Track Requirement | BrainBase Implementation                 |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Social coordination    | Bounty Q&A, community knowledge sharing  |
| Low-cost transactions  | Base L2 ~$0.01 fees for all interactions |
| Consumer-friendly UX   | OnchainKit, Smart Wallet, one-tap flows  |
| DeFi/Payments          | mIDRX swaps, BRAIN token economy         |
| Mobile-first           | Responsive Mini-App design               |

**BrainBase demonstrates that Base can power real-world knowledge economies with mainstream-ready UX, making onchain social coordination accessible to everyday users.**

**The problem it solves**

Peer-to-peer NFT transactions require a high level of trust between buyers and sellers.
Buyers risk losing funds if the seller fails to deliver the NFT, while sellers risk transferring NFTs without guaranteed payment. Most existing NFT marketplaces rely on centralized escrow systems, introducing custody risks, additional fees, and single points of failure.
There is currently no simple, decentralized solution that allows users to trade NFTs directly with each other while ensuring secure payment, guaranteed delivery, and automatic refunds — all enforced by smart contracts.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing the escrow logic to handle multiple transaction states securely, including successful transfers, timeouts, and refunds, without introducing vulnerabilities such as re-entrancy or double execution.
Another challenge was ensuring that NFT ownership verification and fund release logic were synchronized correctly to prevent edge cases where either party could exploit the transaction flow.
We overcame these challenges by carefully structuring state transitions in the smart contract, using well-tested Solidity patterns, and thoroughly testing different transaction scenarios such as successful completion, cancellation, and timeout-based refunds.

**Base Track**

This project directly addresses challenges in the NFT ecosystem by enabling secure peer-to-peer NFT trading. The escrow mechanism ensures that NFTs and payments are exchanged fairly and transparently, reducing fraud and increasing trust between users. It enhances the usability and safety of NFTs as digital assets in real-world transactions.

> Turning social signals into prediction markets

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem Warex Protocol Solves

Modern financial markets struggle to efficiently capture, price, and act on real-time public information—especially information that emerges first on social platforms like Twitter. While social media has become the primary source of breaking news, public statements, and market-moving narratives, this information remains fragmented, noisy, and difficult to translate into actionable, verifiable market signals.

At the same time, existing prediction markets face two major limitations:

### 1. Idle Capital Inefficiency
Most prediction markets lock user funds in passive vaults until market resolution. This results in capital sitting idle for days or weeks, creating a significant opportunity cost for participants and limiting overall capital efficiency.

**Warex Protocol solves this by:**
- Deploying market liquidity into yield-generating DeFi strategies while predictions are active
- Allowing participants to earn yield regardless of prediction outcome
- Improving risk-adjusted returns without increasing prediction exposure

---

### 2. Slow and Curated Market Creation
Traditional prediction markets rely on centralized or manually curated market creation. This causes delays, limits coverage of fast-moving narratives, and introduces censorship or bias.

**Warex Protocol solves this by:**
- Enabling permissionless market creation directly from public Twitter URLs
- Using AI to extract event context, define outcomes, and deploy markets automatically
- Allowing markets to form instantly around breaking news and emerging trends

---

### 3. Poor Signal-to-Noise Ratio in Social Media
Social platforms surface opinions, speculation, and misinformation without a reliable mechanism to measure credibility or consensus.

**Warex Protocol solves this by:**
- Converting social narratives into markets where participants put capital at risk
- Using price discovery as a credibility filter for social signals
- Surfacing high-confidence outcomes through collective intelligence

---

### 4. Misaligned Incentives in Information Markets
In many systems, content creators, participants, and platforms are misaligned—leading to spam, low-quality markets, or extractive platform behavior.

**Warex Protocol solves this by:**
- Incentivizing high-quality market creation and curation
- Rewarding participants for early, accurate forecasts
- Aligning protocol growth with community contribution

---

## What People Use Warex Protocol For

- **Forecasting outcomes** of public statements, geopolitical events, crypto developments, and market narratives
- **Hedging uncertainty** around events discussed on social media
- **Earning yield** while participating in prediction markets
- **Measuring market consensus** around breaking news in real time
- **Building applications** on top of social-signal-driven on-chain markets

---

## Why This Matters

Warex Protocol turns fragmented social information into a capital-efficient coordination layer. Instead of speculation based on noise, it enables users to express conviction, aggregate intelligence, and allocate capital productively—bridging the gap between social discourse and on-chain truth.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Translating Unstructured Tweets Into Valid On-Chain Markets
Tweets are noisy, ambiguous, and often lack explicit outcome definitions. Turning a short, informal post into a well-defined prediction market (with clear resolution criteria and outcomes) was a major challenge.

**How I addressed it:**  
I introduced an AI preprocessing layer that classifies tweet intent, extracts the core event, and enforces a strict market schema (binary or bounded outcomes, resolution timestamp, and verifiable source). Ambiguous tweets are either normalized into conservative outcome sets or rejected before deployment.

---

### 2. Balancing Yield Strategies With Market Safety
Deploying locked capital into yield-generating DeFi strategies introduces smart contract, liquidity, and timing risk—especially when funds must be available immediately at market settlement.

**How I addressed it:**  
I constrained yield deployment to low-volatility, highly liquid strategies and implemented exit buffers to guarantee capital availability at settlement. Yield strategies are abstracted behind a risk-controlled module, allowing them to be upgraded or disabled without affecting active markets.

---

### 3. Preventing Market Spam and Low-Quality Submissions
Because market creation is permissionless, there is a risk of spam markets, poorly defined events, or intentionally misleading narratives.

**How I addressed it:**  
I designed an incentive and friction model: creators stake a small amount when creating a market, earn rewards only if their markets attract meaningful participation, and lose credibility if markets resolve poorly. This economically discourages low-quality submissions without centralized moderation.

---

### 4. Ensuring Deterministic Market Resolution
Prediction markets require objective and verifiable settlement conditions, but many social-signal-driven events are subjective or evolve over time.

**How I addressed it:**  
I restricted supported markets to events with clear public resolution sources (e.g., official announcements, on-chain data, or verifiable outcomes) and encoded resolution rules at market creation. This minimizes oracle ambiguity and post-hoc disputes.

---

### 5. Coordinating AI, Off-Chain Data, and On-Chain Execution
Synchronizing AI analysis, off-chain Twitter data, and on-chain market deployment introduced latency, failure modes, and consistency issues.

**How I addressed it:**  
I separated concerns into distinct pipelines: AI analysis and validation off-chain, followed by deterministic on-chain execution with minimal assumptions. Each step is idempotent and failure-tolerant, allowing safe retries without duplicating markets or misallocating funds.

---

### 6. Designing UX Around a Complex Mental Model
Combining prediction risk, yield generation, and AI-generated markets can be confusing for new users.

**How I addressed it:**  
I simplified the user flow into a single action—*predict*—while abstracting yield mechanics in the background. Advanced users can inspect yield sources and risk parameters, but defaults are optimized for clarity and safety.

---

These challenges shaped Warex Protocol into a system that prioritizes **capital efficiency, signal quality, and operational safety**, while remaining fully permissionless and composable.

**Base Track**

## Why Choose the Base Track

Warex Protocol is built as a **social-first, consumer-facing onchain app**, making Base the ideal deployment environment.

- **Low fees & fast transactions** enable real-time, narrative-driven prediction markets sourced from Twitter.
- **Smart wallets & mini-app UX** reduce onboarding friction and make predicting feel simple and mobile-native.
- **Strong DeFi infrastructure** supports safe, liquid yield strategies for capital-efficient markets.
- **AI-friendly tooling (AgentKit)** allows automated market creation and onchain execution.

Base allows Warex to deliver prediction markets that are **fast, affordable, and usable by non-technical users**, aligning perfectly with the Base Track’s goals.

> High-Intent Scheduling Prevent No-Shows

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Free** is a magnet for flakes. You offer a free mentorship slot out of the goodness of your heart, and the mentee treats it like a "maybe" on a Facebook event.

**0xCAL** help to reduce **No-show** on every booking session you made, **Commitment Fee** is refundable but the respect is mandatory.

**The Problem**
The "I’ll Be There" is a Lie. You as mentor staring at your own reflection in a Zoom window for 15 minutes. People booking "just in case" and then ghosting because there are zero consequences. Mentors get cynical, serious mentees get blocked by spammers, and the world loses a little bit of magic.

**The Solution: Skin In The Game**

We’ve added a simple accountability layer to the booking process:
1. Mentees secure their spot with a "Commitment Fee" (e.g., 15K IDRX).
2. The mentoring session happens. Value is shared. High fives all around.
3. Once the mentor confirms attendance, the deposit can be claim back by mentee.
4. If the mentee misses the window without canceling, the deposit is forfeited and goes to mentor. Simple. Fair. Effective.

**Challenges we ran into**

Timezone issues make it challenging to create future schedules, especially when either the mentor or the mentee lives in a region that observes Daylight Saving Time (DST).

Designing a system that is fair to everyone is difficult. Our platform places a significant amount of trust in mentors. When a mentor acts unfairly—such as not acknowledging that a mentee attended a session—the only option we currently have is manual intervention.

As mentioned earlier, mentees are in a weaker position, and it remains challenging to design a system that is truly fair for all parties.

**Base Track**

Everyone, including mentors and consultants, can use this platform through a web app to create booking sessions. The app makes it easy to manage availability and time efficiently. We use IDRX stablecoin as the primary currency, ensuring no price volatility and making it suitable for non-native crypto users.

> Elevate Your Lifestyle with the Vault of Games

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The main problem in the local gaming industry is the high initial barrier. For small developers, the USD 100 listing fee on global platforms is often the first obstacle, even though they may not be commercially ready. Many developers just want to try publishing, testing, or asking for feedback, but are forced to spend money up front. In addition, the game testing process often involves real money, which is risky and not conducive to experimentation. As a result, many local games remain at the prototype stage and never reach the public. Peridot addresses this need: lowering the entry barrier (from USD 100 to USD 10) and providing a safe space for developers to experiment, including testing without real money, so that more Indonesian game IPs can be born and thrive within their own ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Designing a Multi-Chain System Without Fragmenting UX**

One major challenge was building PeridotVault as a multi-chain platform while keeping the user experience consistent. Different chains expose different RPC behaviors, confirmation times, event formats, and wallet capabilities—which easily leads to fragmented logic and UX inconsistency.

How we solved it:
We introduced a chain-agnostic abstraction layer:
- Each supported chain exposes a unified interface for ownership checks and transactions
- Chain-specific logic is isolated behind adapters
- The Mini-App consumes a single normalized data model

This allowed us to deploy and optimize specifically for Base during the hackathon, while keeping the architecture future-proof for additional chains.

**2. Implementing a Hybrid Onchain–Offchain Architecture**

Purely onchain solutions quickly became impractical for a consumer app:
- Scanning ownership events on every load was slow
- RPC limits affected reliability
- UI responsiveness suffered under real usage

At the same time, moving too much logic offchain would weaken ownership guarantees.

How we solved it:
We adopted a hybrid architecture:
- Onchain: license ownership, verification, and critical state
- Offchain: indexing, aggregation, caching, and UX state
- Onchain data remains the single source of truth Offchain services only reflect and accelerate what is provably onchain.

This balance allowed PeridotVault to scale without sacrificing trustlessness.

**Base Track**

PeridotVault fits the Base Track by transforming a complex onchain concept—digital game ownership and distribution—into a practical, user-friendly Base Mini-App.

One of the biggest challenges in Web3 today is that real asset ownership (licenses, NFTs, access rights) is often disconnected from actual user experience. Game distribution is a clear example: ownership is abstract, onboarding is complex, and users rarely feel the benefit of being onchain.

PeridotVault solves this by delivering an onchain game library and licensing system deployed on Base, where users can:

Purchase and own game licenses as onchain assets

Manage their library through a simple Mini-App interface

Interact with smart contracts without deep Web3 knowledge

By leveraging Base L2, PeridotVault ensures fast, low-cost transactions suitable for retail users and gamers. We focus heavily on UX-first onboarding, abstracting wallet complexity while still preserving true onchain ownership.

Using Base-compatible SDKs and tooling, our Mini-App bridges Web2-like usability with Web3 guarantees:

Ownership is verifiable onchain

Transactions are fast and affordable

The app remains accessible to non-crypto-native users

Ultimately, PeridotVault turns an idea—onchain digital ownership—into a functional, deployed product that demonstrates how Base can support consumer-facing applications at scale, especially for Indonesia’s growing gaming and creative economy.

This is not a scripted chat; it is a dynamic interaction that shapes the game’s environment and soundscape in real-time. Each session culminates in the minting of a "Memory Fragment" (NFT on Base/Avalanche)—a unique on-chain record of the player's psychological profile and progress within the 808347 universe.

Transmedia Foundation & Business Model: The project is rooted in a massive Sci-Fi universe previously developed across 6+ seasons of original content (handpicked for the Amazon Prime-curated GO GLOBAL program). We are converting this deep lore into a sustainable Web3 ecosystem:

Retention: By integrating with Farcaster Frames, we enable viral, social-graph distribution, allowing players to start their interrogation directly in their feed and bridge their progress to the full on-chain experience.

Why Base: To achieve mass adoption, we require the high-speed, low-fee infrastructure of Base to power our "Audio-as-Progress" and "Video Achives as progress" mechanics. By making the blockchain layer invisible but essential for ownership, we turn every player’s memory into a tradable, collectible asset.

The Vision: We are not just building a game; we are building a transmedia franchise where AI agents, cinematic audio, and blockchain provenance create a new standard for digital entertainment.

### Hearz
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hearz-2bd2) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://legacy-vault-ashy.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> Your Digital Legacy on the Blockchain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The "Lost Crypto" Crisis & The Inefficiency of Traditional Inheritance

The Problem: In the world of Web3, "Self-Custody" is a double-edged sword. While it gives us total control, it also creates a single point of failure: Death.

Asset Loss: When a crypto holder passes away without sharing their private keys, their assets are lost forever on the blockchain. Billions of dollars in crypto are currently inaccessible due to this issue.

Security Dilemma: Sharing private keys with family members while alive poses a major security risk (theft, accidental exposure, or trust issues).

Traditional Friction: Traditional inheritance (wills, lawyers, notaries) is slow, expensive, paper-based, and often fails to account for digital assets held on-chain.

How LegacyVault Solves It: LegacyVault provides a trustless, decentralized dead man's switch for your digital assets.

Automation: Users set a "Check-In" interval (e.g., every 6 months). If they fail to check in (confirming they are active), the smart contract assumes they are incapacitated.

Security: No private keys are ever shared. The protocol uses smart contracts to automatically transfer the rights/assets to pre-assigned beneficiary wallets.

No Middleman: It eliminates the need for lawyers or expensive legal fees. The code is the executor.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Designing the "Dead Man's Switch" Logic: The biggest technical challenge was creating a reliable logic for the inactivity timer. We had to ensure that the "Check-In" mechanism was secure and couldn't be triggered by unauthorized wallets, while also ensuring the asset transfer happens seamlessly when the time expires.

2. Frontend & Blockchain Integration: Connecting our Next.js frontend with the smart contract provided some hurdles, specifically in handling real-time state updates (e.g., showing the correct "Time Remaining" for the user). We had to debug several hydration errors to ensure the UI perfectly matches the on-chain data.

3. Balancing Security with UX: We wanted LegacyVault to be accessible even to non-technical users (the heirs). Simplifying the claim process without compromising the strict security of a decentralized protocol was a tough design challenge we had to iterate on multiple times.

**Base Track**

LegacyVault is natively built and deployed on the Base blockchain.

We chose Base specifically for two reasons that are critical to our "Dead Man's Switch" mechanism:

Low Gas Fees: Our protocol requires users to perform periodic "Check-Ins" (on-chain transactions) to prove they are alive. Base's low transaction costs make this frequent interaction affordable for everyday users, which would be too expensive on L1 Ethereum.

Speed & Scalability: We aim to bring mass adoption to crypto inheritance. Base's high throughput ensures that when the time comes to transfer assets to heirs, the process is fast, reliable, and seamless.

By building on Base, LegacyVault adds a critical layer of long-term security to the ecosystem, encouraging users to store their wealth on Base confidently.

> Every School Deserves a Champion’s Jersey

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Our Pitch Deck:** https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1E6atRCR1NoKEcvWPupbr90AfByx1HegVHyteBfI0inI/edit?usp=sharing

KAL addresses a missed opportunity in the school sportswear ecosystem. While schools, parents, and students already purchase uniforms every year, those purchases deliver no added value beyond clothing. KAL turns an existing, recurring activity into a connected, rewarding, and transparent experience, without changing how schools operate.

**What people use KAL for:**

Students use KAL to track school activities, complete missions, and earn rewards from things they already do (PE classes, sports, quizzes, events).

Schools use KAL to modernize their sports programs, engage students, and distribute incentives or scholarships in a transparent, measurable way.

Parents benefit from clear visibility into participation and rewards, with stable, predictable value through IDRX-based rewards.

**How it makes existing tasks easier and safer:**

Converts offline school activities into verifiable onchain records, reducing manual tracking.

Automates reward and incentive distribution, removing bias and paperwork.

Uses stablecoins to ensure safe, predictable value instead of speculative tokens.

Onboards users seamlessly, without requiring crypto knowledge.

KAL doesn’t ask schools to change their behavior, it simply adds a digital and onchain layer that makes everyday school activities more meaningful, measurable, and rewarding.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the first challenges was figuring out how to connect and register a real-world asset (RWA)—the school jersey—into the app in a way that is feasible, scalable, and easy for schools and students. Jerseys are physical, used daily, and must work in real environments without adding friction. After exploring several options, we found that combining NFC tags embedded in the jersey with a QR code fallback was the most practical solution. NFC enables fast, seamless onboarding and authentication for supported devices, while QR codes ensure inclusivity for students whose phones do not support NFC.

Another challenge was planning the stablecoin integration, specifically with IDRX, to support payments, monetization, and reward distribution. While we haven’t fully implemented IDRX yet, we’ve already designed the system architecture so that sales revenue and sponsorship funds can flow into an IDRX-based reward pool in future iterations. This allows us to move fast with an MVP while keeping the path clear for compliant, stable, and user-friendly financial integration in the next development phase.

Finally, due to limited time before submission, some features in the current build may not be fully stable or working as intended. We prioritized demonstrating the core concept and end-to-end flow rather than polishing every edge case. We are fully committed to continuing development and, if selected, will ensure the product is stable, complete, and ready for a full presentation on February 7th.

**Base Track**

KAL fits naturally into the Base track by onboarding users at massive scale through schools, where uniforms are purchased every year and hundreds of students are onboarded at once. KAL is a consumer-ready app where everyday school activities become onchain interactions without crypto complexity, connecting real-world uniforms and revenue to onchain rewards as a practical RWA use case. By integrating $IDRXstablecoins, KAL enables simple payments, transparent monetization, and fair reward distribution, making Base the ideal infrastructure for recurring, real-world adoption.

### NoaSight
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/noasight-bdc8) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://c1kchqwg-5173.asse.devtunnels.ms/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> The Future of Prediction Markets

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

NoaSight is a decentralized prediction market platform built on the BASE blockchain, inspired by platforms like Polymarket but leveraging BASE's superior transaction speed and cost efficiency.
- Lightning-fast transactions on BASE testnet
- Unique NFT profile system with benefits
- Community-driven oracle resolution
- DAO governance for platform decisions

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of NoaSight, the biggest challenge was bridging the gap between Web2 usability and Web3 complexity, specifically regarding Wallet Abstraction and Cross-Chain Synchronization.
1. The "Gas Fee Barrier" & Seamless Onboarding
The Hurdle:
We wanted users to trade prediction shares instantly using just their email, without worrying about seed phrases or gas fees (ETH/SUI). However, on-chain transactions inherently require gas, which is a major friction point for non-crypto natives. Integrating standard wallets meant users had to buy ETH first, killing the conversion rate.
The Solution:
We implemented a robust Gas Sponsorship System combined with Circle Programmable Wallets.
- I built a backend service (treasurySweeper.js and gas monitors) that monitors user wallets created via Circle.
- When a user initiates a trade (buy/sell), our backend verifies the transaction intent and automatically sponsors the gas fees using a centralized Treasury Wallet on Base Sepolia.
- This creates a truly "gasless" experience where users just see their balance update, while complex blockchain interactions happen invisibly in the background.

2. Synchronizing Off-Chain & On-Chain State
The Hurdle:
A prediction market requires real-time speed. Relying solely on blockchain confirmations made the UI feel sluggish. However, relying on a database introduced the risk of "state drift" where the user's displayed balance didn't match their actual on-chain assets, especially after failed transactions or reorgs.
The Solution:
I architected a Dual-State System with Self-Healing Monitors:
- Optimistic UI: The frontend updates instantly based on API responses.
- Background Monitors: I created specialized background services (suiDepositMonitor.js, circleDepositMonitor.js) running on the backend. These services constantly poll the blockchain RPCs to detect deposits and confirm transaction finality.
- Auto-Retry & Sweep: If a minting or transfer transaction fails (e.g., due to RPC timeout), the system automatically retries with exponential backoff. A "Treasury Sweeper" service ensures that funds deposited by users are securely aggregated to the main liquidity pool periodically, keeping the ecosystem solvent and liquid.

3. Multi-Chain Compatibility (EVM + Sui + Solana)
The Hurdle:
Designing a backend that could handle prediction markets across different architectures (EVM-based Base Chain vs. Move-based Sui vs. Solana) was architecturally demanding due to different address formats, signing mechanisms, and RPC behaviors.
The Solution:
I adopted a Modular Service Architecture. Instead of a monolithic codebase, I separated blockchain logic into distinct service modules (suiWalletService.js, solanaIntegration.js, standard EVM providers).
- This allowed me to abstract the logic: The core market engine doesn't care which chain a user is on; it just calls a standardized createWallet() or getBalance() interface.
- I used ethers.js for EVM chains and dedicated libraries/APIs for Sui/Solana, unifying them under a single PostgreSQL schema that maps generic wallet_id and derivation_index to specific chain implementations.

### Yilnes
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/yilnes-c10d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/hmiftachul11/yilnes-contract) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://yilnes.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n296SkOns6I) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> Customize Your Safety. Maximize Your Yield.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: Bringing "Based" Safety to Consumer DeFi. Base is onboarding the next billion users to onchain finance. However, for a retail user depositing their first $100 or $1,000, the barrier isn't just UX—it’s fear.

- The "Rug" Anxiety: New onchain users often hesitate to explore high-yield RWA strategies (like Maple or Goldfinch) because they fear smart contract exploits or defaults.
- Insurance is for Whales: Traditional DeFi insurance (like Nexus Mutual) is often too expensive or complex for the average Base user. High gas fees on L1 make insuring small amounts economically unviable.
- The "Cold Start" Liquidity Risk: Most yield aggregators build insurance funds by taxing profits after they are earned. If a hack happens on Day 1, the reserve is empty, and early adopters are left with zero protection.

The Solution: Yilnes – The Safety Layer for Base. Yilnes is a specialized RWA Yield Aggregator built natively on Base that enables "Micro-Insurance" for every user, no matter how small their deposit.

- Upfront Safety Reserve: We use a "Nexus Mutual-style" logic where users pay a small premium immediately upon deposit. Because Base's gas fees are so low, this transaction is negligible for the user but ensures the Safety Reserve has immediate liquidity to cover losses from Block 1.
- Native USDC Integration: Built specifically for the Base DeFi ecosystem, Yilnes leverages the ubiquity of USDC on Base. Users can seamlessly move from Coinbase to Yilnes and start earning protected yields without complex swaps or wrappers.
- Customizable "Consumer-Grade" Coverage: Users utilize a simple, dynamic slider to choose their protection period (28 days to 365 days). The smart contract calculates the risk premium in real-time, making institutional-grade hedging accessible to anyone with a wallet.

Revenue Model:

- Spread on Premiums: A portion of the insurance premium flows to the Protocol Treasury.
- Unclaimed Yields: Yields generated by the Safety Reserve itself (which is deployed into low-risk Base strategies like Aave/Moonwell) compound the protocol's value.

**Challenges we ran into**

Multi-Chain Token Standards (The Base USDC Trap) Deploying on Base exposed us to critical differences in token standards compared to local testnets.

- The Hurdle: While developing locally, we used standard 18-decimal ERC20 mocks. However, native USDC on Base uses 6 decimals. When we first deployed our Vault to Base Sepolia, our math for calculating premiums broke completely—users were being charged 1 trillion times less than intended because of the decimal mismatch.
- The Solution: We rewrote our MockUSDC contracts and re-engineered our frontend hooks (useToken.ts, InvestModal.tsx) to dynamically handle 6-decimal precision. We now use parseUnits(amount, 6) specifically for Base deployments, ensuring our math aligns perfectly with Circle's native USDC standard.

The Pivot: Yield Tax vs. Upfront Premium Initially, we built the protocol using a standard "Performance Fee" model, where 10% of a user's profit was deducted to fund the insurance pool.

- The Hurdle: We realized this failed the "Day 1 Hack" scenario. If the protocol was exploited early, the reserve would be empty because no one had claimed yields yet.
- The Solution: We completely refactored the Smart Contract logic to an Upfront Premium model. We implemented time-weighted math (Principal * Rate * Duration / 365) directly in Solidity. This makes the protocol robust from the very first deposit, solving the "Cold Start" problem.

Handling "Expired" Coverage on Low-Latency Chains Building the logic for what happens when a user's chosen coverage period ends was tricky, especially with Base's fast block times.

- The Hurdle: We didn't want to lock user funds or force-withdraw them when coverage expired.
- The Solution: We implemented a "Grace Period" state in the UI. If a user stays past their covered date, their dashboard badges change from "Premium Coverage" (Green) to "Uninsured" (Yellow). They stop paying premiums but immediately lose protection. This required precise timestamp synchronization between the client (Wagmi/Viem) and the Base blockchain state.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

Yilnes makes Thetanuts options invisible.

- For the User: They see a simple "Insurance Slider" to protect their deposit. They don't know (or care) about complex options trading.
- For the Protocol: When a user pays the insurance fee, Yilnes automatically deposits that money into a Thetanuts Option Vault to earn high yields.
- The Win: You use Thetanuts to grow the insurance fund faster, while giving retail users a super simple UI.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/auroom-7147) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AuRoom-xyz) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://auroom-finance.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> Unlock Cash Keep Your Gold

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem AuRoom Solves

In emerging markets like Indonesia, **gold is widely used as a store of value**, not as a liquid asset. People save in gold to protect against inflation and currency depreciation, but when urgent cash needs arise—such as medical expenses, education fees, or small business capital—the only practical option today is **to sell the gold**.

This creates three fundamental problems:

1. **Forced Loss of Long-Term Value**  
   Selling gold breaks long-term savings discipline and removes exposure to an asset meant to hedge inflation. Users often regret selling when gold prices rise afterward.

2. **Inefficient and Costly Liquidity Access**  
   Traditional solutions like pawnshops or gold-backed loans are custodial, opaque, and expensive, with high interest rates and limited transparency.

3. **Lack of Onchain Utility for Real-World Assets**  
   Existing DeFi protocols focus heavily on crypto-native assets. Real-world assets like gold are underutilized onchain, despite strong real demand and cultural relevance.

AuRoom addresses this gap by enabling users to **unlock fiat liquidity without selling their gold**, transforming gold from a passive store of value into a productive, non-custodial financial asset.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges We Ran Into

Building AuRoom required navigating both onchain constraints and real-world financial integration. The main challenges we encountered were:

- **Integration with IDRX (Fiat-Denominated Stablecoin)**  
  Unlike crypto-native assets, IDRX represents off-chain fiat value. This required careful handling of minting, burning, decimals, and accounting to ensure that onchain debt accurately maps to real-world fiat exposure without breaking DeFi assumptions.

- **Off-Chain Withdrawal & Redemption of IDRX**  
  Enabling users to ultimately redeem IDRX into real fiat introduces an off-chain dependency layer. This creates challenges around user experience, trust boundaries, and compliance, since the onchain protocol must remain non-custodial while relying on external fiat on/off-ramp infrastructure.

- **Maintaining DeFi Simplicity While Being RWA-Compatible**  
  Most DeFi lending designs assume purely onchain assets. Designing a system that works with real-world assets like gold and fiat—without over-engineering or adding excessive custodial risk—required strict separation between onchain logic and off-chain processes.

- **Balancing Safety and Accessibility for Early Users**  
  For an MVP, parameters like LTV, liquidation thresholds, and minimum borrow sizes had to be conservative enough to be safe, yet simple and intuitive for non-crypto-native users.

These challenges shaped AuRoom’s architecture: keeping the core protocol fully onchain and deterministic, while treating fiat redemption and compliance as modular, off-chain extensions.

**Base Track**

### How AuRoom Fits Into the Base Track

AuRoom is designed as a **practical, user-facing DeFi protocol built for scale on Base**, aligning directly with Base’s goal of bringing real-world users and real-world assets onchain.

- **Built for Low-Cost, High-Frequency Usage**  
  Gold-backed borrowing targets everyday liquidity needs, not speculative trading. Base’s low fees and fast confirmations make it feasible for retail users to deposit collateral, repay loans, and manage positions without prohibitive costs.

- **Expanding the Base RWA Ecosystem**  
  AuRoom extends Base beyond crypto-native assets by integrating **real-world assets (gold) and fiat-denominated stablecoins (IDRX)**. This supports Base’s vision of becoming a settlement layer for real economic activity, not just onchain speculation.

- **Simple, Secure Smart Contract Design**  
  The protocol prioritizes minimalism, clear invariants, and auditability—well-suited for Base’s emphasis on safe, production-ready applications that can onboard non-crypto-native users.

- **Composable with the Base Ecosystem**  
  AuRoom’s contracts are modular and can integrate with Base-native stablecoins, wallets, on/off-ramps, and future RWA primitives, making it a building block rather than a siloed application.

- **Onchain Transparency for Offchain Finance**  
  While fiat redemption happens offchain, all collateralization, debt, and liquidation logic remains fully onchain on Base, preserving transparency and trust while bridging real-world finance.

In short, AuRoom uses Base as a foundation to transform a familiar real-world asset into an onchain financial primitive, helping Base move closer to mass adoption through real utility.

### AEGIS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegis-0393) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://aegis-web-39hu.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> The credit score for AI agents.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3.py](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3.py-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents are starting to hire and pay each other, but none of them have a credit history. So **every job is paid in full before work starts**, and that money sits locked — an agent can only run one job at a time.

**Aegis gives each agent a credit score** based on what it has actually done. Good score, put down **20%**. Unknown or bad score, pay the full amount.

You can check any agent before hiring it — one API call returns its score and the reasons behind it. If the work is bad, **the dispute settles by rule**: money comes back, the score drops, and that agent pays 100% from then on.

The score lives **on-chain**, so it follows the agent to every platform instead of resetting each time it moves.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Everyone scored top marks.** 79% of agents landed in the best band, so every agent got the same deposit and our tiers meant nothing. Changed how we map risk to a score.

- **A bug quietly stole money.** If the hirer only approved its deposit, the job still "succeeded" — the worker was paid a fifth and the hirer was marked a defaulter. No error. Added a check that now fails loudly.

- **Doing a good job lowered your score.** Two causes stacked up. Fixed both, then found scores alternating between +11 and +1 from a rounding bug.

- **The demo only ran on our laptop.** Account age came from the chain's clock, which our seeder faked. Stored it as data instead — contracts now live on Base Sepolia.

- **We found we could cheat our own system.** A fresh wallet farmed a 904 score in an afternoon on one-cent jobs. Blocked it at the contract level and shipped risk flags.

**VIP Membership of CodeCrafters**

- **Built from first principles.** Our own data generator, logistic regression and FICO-style score mapping. No scoring library.

- **Two Solidity contracts from scratch.** State machine enforced at every entry point, 100+ tests across Foundry and pytest.

- **Our own oracle.** Replays chain events, rescores, writes back with a plain-English reason. No indexer, no third-party service.

- **Explainable scores.** The API returns the top three factors, so "−230 from one lost dispute" traces to real coefficients, not a black box.

- **We audited ourselves.** Found a self-dealing exploit, a silent settlement bug and a sign error — all documented, fixed or named as limitations.

### Compliance-Aware-Block-Builder
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/complianceawareblockbuilder-5fbb) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/takenrohit/Compliance-Aware-Block-Builder) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> Compliance wins the block — the highest clean bid

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement — Compliance-Aware Block Builder & PBS Relay

Ethereum's block production pipeline (builders + PBS relays) optimizes purely for profit: the highest-paying block wins, with no regard for what's inside it. This creates an unresolved compliance crisis for anyone operating builder or relay infrastructure:

Inclusion risk — Builders unknowingly package transactions from OFAC-sanctioned wallets, exposing operators to criminal liability under sanctions law.
Relay auction blindness — Relays select winners by bid value alone, so a tainted 2.5 ETH block beats a clean 2.0 ETH block.
Layering evasion — Illicit actors route funds through intermediary hops and mixers (e.g., Tornado Cash), defeating naive direct-address sanctions checks.
Travel Rule gaps — High-value transfers move without identifying counterparty VASPs, violating FATF Recommendation 16.
No audit trail — Operators cannot produce cryptographically verifiable proof of compliance for regulators, and existing systems fail open (include on error) instead of fail-closed.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Unit-testing Chainlink Functions code The production DON script uses top-level await and the Functions sandbox global, so plain node can't execute it. Solved by splitting into verifyIdentity.js (production, parse-checked via vm.Script wrapped as async) and verifyIdentity.demo.js (Node-runnable simulation covered by test_compliance_flow.js).

2. Foundry dependency maze The smartcontractkit/chainlink monorepo contains no Solidity contracts — the correct source is chainlink-brownie-contracts plus a remappings.txt for @chainlink/contracts/. A stale monorepo submodule, a missing forge-std (needed by the deploy script), and a stale foundry.lock each broke builds until cleaned up.

3. Chainlink v1_0_0 API mismatches addDONHostedSecrets takes (slot, version), not bytes; the helper is setArgs, not addArgs; address.bytes[i] doesn't exist in Solidity; and our onlyOwner modifier initially missed its body. Each surfaced only at forge build.

4. Constructor encoding bug The Sepolia DON ID hex literal was 66 chars instead of 64 (wrong zero-padding), rejected by the compiler — fixed by recomputing the padded bytes32.

5. Painful three-way merge The fable and relay-mvp branches both rewrote the identity gate (ComplianceRegistry.sol, verifyIdentity.js, server.ts). Resolved by keeping the FunctionsClient architecture and porting the other branch's hardening (strict router, provider whitelist, chain-gated mocks, revoke()).

6. CI went red post-merge Unformatted Rust, 3 Clippy collapsible_if errors, and a test referencing the removed identity_verified field. Fixed with cargo fmt, Clippy autofix, and test cleanup — verified with the exact CI sequence before pushing.

7. Demo regressions The merge added admin-auth to a public demo endpoint (dashboard sends no key → 401), moved storage to Postgres without applying migration 004 (→ 500s), and a hash-bucket change flipped a demo wallet's outcome. Fixed by reopening the endpoint (rate-limited), applying the migration, and pinning pill wallets to verified buckets.

8. Tainted demo addresses A supposedly "clean" address (0x8888…) turned out to be 1 hop from a blocked transaction and would have been flagged live — caught by querying Redis + decision history before the demo, and replaced.

9. Wallet/tooling friction Brave Wallet wouldn't connect via Chainlist, and faucets rate-limit. Worked around with cast wallet new, public RPCs, and alternate faucets — no browser needed for deploy.

### T-REX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trex-8260) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sn-2006/T-REX) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://t-rex-kappa.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-BkUOhpTjP4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> Decode. Reconcile. Comply.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building T-REX came with a few challenges across blockchain integration, exchange reconciliation, AI, and deployment.

Decentralized/on-chain integration: Getting live Ethereum data involved handling RPC configuration, wallet history, token transfers, internal transactions, and event logs. We created a separate on-chain analysis layer to organize this data before reconciliation.
Different transaction types: A single blockchain transaction can contain multiple events, swaps, token movements, and gas fees. We had to make sure these were classified correctly and not counted multiple times.
Transaction failures: RPC and API requests sometimes failed, timed out, or returned incomplete data. We added validation and error handling to prevent these from affecting the reconciliation results.
Gas fluctuations: Gas fees change with network conditions, so we had to make sure the system used actual transaction data rather than fixed values.
MetaMask connectivity: We faced issues with wallet connections, network selection, invalid addresses, and provider availability. We added validation and clearer error handling.
Exchange data: Different exchanges provide transaction histories in different formats. We solved this by normalizing the data into a common structure before reconciliation.
Transaction matching: Differences in transaction IDs, timestamps, asset names, and amounts made matching challenging. We use multiple attributes to improve matching and send unclear cases for manual review.
TDS and valuation: Some transactions don't have enough information to confidently determine their INR value or expected TDS. Instead of guessing, we flag them for verification.
AI reliability: We had to ensure the AI didn't make up transaction or tax information. The reconciliation engine handles the actual calculations, while AI is mainly used to explain the results.
Deployment: Moving the backend to Vercel introduced issues with routing, CORS, environment variables, and server configuration. We had to account for differences between local and deployed environments.
Testing: We tested different wallet activity patterns, including transfers, DEX transactions, token movements, and ambiguous cases, to make sure the system wasn't dependent on a single test scenario.

**The problem it solves**

Crypto investors often use multiple centralized exchanges while also holding and moving assets through personal blockchain wallets and decentralized platforms. This creates fragmented records across exchange statements, transaction histories, and on-chain data, making it difficult to determine which transactions correspond to each other and whether TDS has been correctly accounted for.

T-REX solves this problem by bringing centralized exchange data and decentralized wallet activity into a single reconciliation workflow. It normalizes different exchange formats into a common transaction structure, matches related transactions, identifies unmatched or duplicate activity, and compares expected and recorded TDS to highlight discrepancies.

For decentralized activity, T-REX analyzes on-chain transfers and DEX transactions while distinguishing between confirmed facts and transactions that require additional context. Instead of automatically treating every wallet movement as taxable, ambiguous transactions are flagged for manual review.

The platform then uses AI to explain the deterministic reconciliation results in a clear and actionable way, highlighting discrepancies, unresolved transactions, and the evidence behind each finding. Finally, T-REX can generate an auditable reconciliation report with a cryptographic hash for integrity.

This makes a traditionally fragmented and manual crypto-tax reconciliation process more structured, traceable, and easier to investigate.

### GigVault
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gigvault-bf3e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/divyanshuacharya0990-lab/GigVault) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gigvault-1.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> A work passport for gig workers

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**A bank account is not a payslip.** Our first income calculation counted every credit on the statement — friends' UPI transfers, refunds, self-transfers included. Judges caught it at Checkpoint 1. We rebuilt income as four ordered layers, each catching what the previous one can't: (1) transaction-ID dedupe and channel filter, so nothing counts twice and cash or cheque deposits are never payouts; (2) only known gig platforms, by the remitter name on the statement, count; (3) unlisted payers who pay in most weeks are surfaced, counted only if the rider confirms, and then named on the passport as "rider-confirmed" so a lender can judge it; (4) a transaction graph across every account the consent returned, which catches money the rider moves to himself and labels as a payout — a same-day, same-amount debit from his own account is a cycle, not income, and such a payer can never be confirmed. On the demo statement: 300 credits, 156 counted, 144 ignored, one manufactured payer blocked.

**Zero-knowledge artifacts must move together.** The circuit, proving key, verification key and Solidity verifier are one set. Regenerating one and not the others fails with an error that looks exactly like a logic bug. One script now rebuilds all four, every time, and fingerprints the set.

**The Aadhaar library doesn't reveal what we assumed.** Anon Aadhaar exposes age-over-18, gender, state and pincode — not name. We moved the name match off-circuit: the Secure QR is decoded on the device, the name is matched to the bank account holder, and we say so plainly rather than claim in-circuit matching.

**Cameras only work on localhost or trusted HTTPS.** A phone opening the laptop over the LAN gets no camera. We made the passport QR a URL, so a judge's own camera app opens the verifier page and submits the token — no in-page camera on the phone at all.

**Two ports, three processes, one nonce.** A redeployed local chain with a still-running backend produced "nonce already used" mid-demo. The chain client now resets its nonce view and retries once, and a 35-check smoke test runs before every demo so a dead process is found in ten seconds, not on stage.

**What we chose not to fake.** The bank feed is a signed simulator emitting the exact Account Aggregator schema, because sandbox approval takes days; Aadhaar is decoded but not yet signature-verified. Both are stated on the README with where they plug in. We'd rather judges know than find out.

**The problem it solves**

**Aadhaar made identity portable. UPI made money portable. Nobody has made work portable.**

77 lakh gig workers in India (2.35 crore by 2029-30, NITI Aayog) are paid every week into a bank account — and that history is invisible to everyone who decides their lives. A rider with three years of steady payouts cannot show a lender, a landlord, or a new platform a single verified rupee. 1.5 lakh riders leave one platform every month and start from zero. Karnataka's Gig Workers Act 2025 promises a portable ID; none has been issued.

**GigVault is a work passport, proved by the bank, held by the worker, readable by anyone — disclosing nothing underneath.**

**What people use it for**
- **Riders** get a passport on their phone after one consent on the RBI Account Aggregator rail. It proves *"≥ 24 months, ≥ 100 weeks paid, ≥ ₹18,000/month, paid by Swiggy"* — never the actual figures. It travels with them to the next platform, so tenure is never reset.
- **Platforms** onboard an experienced rider in one QR scan — true or false in under 100 ms — instead of restarting a fresher.
- **Lenders and landlords** underwrite without payslips, from a bank-signed record they can verify themselves.
- **Welfare boards** get the portable ID the law promised, on infrastructure that already exists.

**Why it can't be faked**
- The rider never types or uploads anything. Only the bank's signed statement is accepted; edit a number and the proof fails — live, in the demo.
- Only known gig-platform payouts count as income. Friends' transfers, refunds, self-transfers, and money cycled through the rider's own accounts are detected and excluded.
- One Aadhaar, one passport. Only the phone holding the wallet can present it. Each QR works once, for two minutes. Soulbound — cannot be sold. Revocable — one switch, every scan says no.

**Who is worse off?** Nobody. The passport only ever says *at least*. A fresher's counter starts at week one and keeps counting across platforms — today it resets every time he switches.

The rider pays nothing. The verifier pays per check, like a credit report.

### Hivion
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hivion-5e9d) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://hivion.sivaganesh.in/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co)

> Trust, Written on the Blockchain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Hivion solves the fundamental problems with how legal agreements are created, signed, and stored today:
---
1. Trust & Verification Issues
Traditional contracts rely on centralized authorities (lawyers, notaries, DocuSign) that can be:
- Expensive and slow
- Subject to tampering or disputes
- Lost or destroyed over time
Hivion's Solution: Every agreement is hashed and stored on the Ethereum blockchain, creating an immutable, tamper-proof record. Anyone can verify the authenticity of a document by comparing its hash no middleman required.
---
2. Complex Legal Language Barriers
Most people can't afford lawyers to draft agreements, leading to:
- Poorly written contracts with loopholes
- Misunderstandings between parties
- Unenforceable terms
Hivion's Solution: Our AI-powered agreement generator (Gemini 2.5) creates professional, legally-structured documents from simple inputs. Just describe your community name, purpose, and rules get a complete agreement in seconds.
---
3. Multi-Party Coordination Nightmare
Getting multiple parties to review, edit, and sign a document traditionally involves:
- Endless email chains with version conflicts
- "Which version is the latest?" confusion
- Waiting days for signatures
Hivion's Solution: Real-time collaboration rooms (like Google Docs) where all parties can:
- Edit documents simultaneously with live sync
- See who's online and their cursor positions
- Lock the document when ready for signing
- Complete a multi-party signing ceremony, all in one session
---
4. Document Storage & Accessibility
Paper contracts get lost. Cloud storage can be deleted. Companies shut down.
Hivion's Solution: Documents are permanently stored on IPFS (InterPlanetary File System) a decentralized storage network. Your agreement exists forever, accessible by anyone with the hash, even if Hivion disappears.
---
5. Signature Authenticity
How do you prove a digital signature is real? Email confirmations can be faked.
Hivion's Solution: Signatures are cryptographic wallet signatures on the Ethereum blockchain. Each signature includes:
- Wallet address (your unique identity)
- Timestamp (when you signed)
- Transaction hash (permanent proof on-chain)
---
Use Cases
| Who | What They Can Do |
|-----|------------------|
| DAOs & Web3 Communities | Create governance rules, membership agreements, and contributor contracts with on-chain verification |
| Freelancers & Clients | Draft and sign project agreements without expensive legal fees |
| Roommates & Landlords | Create rental agreements with immutable proof of terms |
| Business Partners | Formalize partnerships with multi-signature verification |
| Content Creators | License agreements for collaborations with permanent proof |
| Open Source Projects | Contributor license agreements (CLAs) with transparent signing |
---
Key Features
- AI Agreement Generation — Natural language to legal document in seconds
- Real-Time Collaboration — Google Docs-style editing with live sync
- Multi-Party Signing — Invite unlimited signers via wallet address or link
- Blockchain Verification — Immutable proof on Ethereum Sepolia
- IPFS Storage — Permanent, decentralized document storage
- PDF Export — Download professional documents anytime
- 2-Step Signing Ceremony — Verify content → Sign with wallet
---
How It Makes Things Easier
| Traditional Way | With Hivion |
|----------------|-------------|
| Hire a lawyer  | AI generates for free |
| Email back and forth for days | Real-time collaboration in minutes |
| Print, sign, scan, email | One-click wallet signature |
| Store in filing cabinet | Permanent on IPFS + blockchain |
| "Did they really sign this?" | Verify on Etherscan instantly |
| Lost the contract? Too bad | Retrieve anytime with IPFS hash |
---
The Web3 Advantage
Hivion brings the trustless, permissionless nature of blockchain to everyday agreements:
> **"Don't trust, verify."**
Every signature, every document, every timestamp is publicly verifiable on the blockchain. No company, government, or individual can alter or delete your agreements. This is the future of digital trust.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1.  Multi-Party Signature Tracking:**
Designing the contract to handle multiple signers was tricky. I needed to track which addresses had signed, prevent double-signing, and emit events only when all required parties had signed. Managing dynamic arrays of signers and mapping their signature status required careful state management to avoid gas inefficiencies.

**2. Socket.io Real-Time Sync:**

Building the Live Room collaboration feature required careful handling of Socket.io connections. Race conditions occurred when multiple users edited the same agreement simultaneously. I had to implement proper event debouncing and conflict resolution to prevent users from overwriting each other's changes.

**3. Event Emission on frontend:**

The frontend needed to react to on-chain events in real-time. Getting the contract to emit the right events with indexed parameters for efficient filtering took several iterations. I had to balance between emitting too much data (expensive) and too little (hard to query).
