> Tamper-proof academic certificates on blockchain

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Academic certificate fraud is a widespread issue, where fake or tampered certificates are used during job applications and higher education admissions. Traditional certificate verification processes are manual, time-consuming, and require dependency on issuing institutions, making them inefficient and unreliable.

CertiChain solves this problem by providing a tamper-proof, blockchain-based certificate issuance and verification system. Educational institutions can issue certificates that are securely stored on the blockchain, ensuring immutability and long-term trust.

With CertiChain, certificates can be verified in multiple secure ways:

- By entering the Certificate ID

- By entering the Certificate Hash

- By scanning a QR code embedded in the certificate

The QR code verification enables instant validation using any device, making the process fast, user-friendly, and accessible even for non-technical users. Once verified, the system securely retrieves and displays the student’s authentic details directly from the blockchain.

This approach completely eliminates certificate forgery, reduces verification time from days to seconds, and removes the need for manual confirmation from institutions. CertiChain ensures transparency, trust, and scalability for students, educational institutions, employers, and recruiters.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges was understanding how to securely store certificate data on the blockchain while avoiding storage of large or sensitive information. Since storing complete certificate details on-chain is costly and inefficient, we had to carefully design a structure using a Certificate Hash and Certificate ID instead of raw data.

Another challenge was integrating blockchain data with the web application. Fetching certificate details in real time using the Certificate ID and hash, and ensuring the frontend correctly reflected the blockchain response, required multiple iterations and debugging.

Generating and managing QR code–based verification links was also challenging. We had to ensure that scanning the QR code consistently redirected to the correct verification page and reliably fetched the corresponding student details without errors.

Handling blockchain transaction delays and ensuring a smooth user experience during certificate issuance was another hurdle. We addressed this by providing clear status feedback to the user while the transaction was being confirmed.

Finally, coordinating development within a limited hackathon timeframe required careful task division and rapid testing to ensure all components—smart contracts, backend logic, and frontend UI—worked seamlessly together.

**Blockchain**

CertiChain fits strongly into the Blockchain track as it addresses a real-world and widely faced problem—academic certificate forgery—using a practical and scalable blockchain-based solution.

Educational institutions currently rely on paper-based or editable digital certificates, which are easy to forge or manipulate. Verification by employers or organizations is time-consuming and often unreliable. CertiChain eliminates this issue by issuing tamper-proof academic certificates secured on the blockchain.

Each certificate is minted with a unique certificate ID and cryptographic hash, ensuring authenticity and immutability. A QR code embedded in the certificate links directly to a verification page, where employers or institutions can instantly verify student details without intermediaries.

The project demonstrates strong technical implementation, real-world applicability, and clear user impact. It simplifies certificate issuance, prevents fraud, and enables instant trust-based verification, making CertiChain a strong contender for recognition under the Winner Classification track.

**The problem it solves**

Micro-lenders and small financial institutions play a critical role in providing credit to underserved individuals and small businesses. However, most of these lenders rely on manual evaluation, limited data, or rigid rule-based systems to assess borrower risk. Traditional credit scoring models often fail in such contexts because many borrowers have thin or no formal credit history, informal income sources, and dynamic financial behavior.

As a result, lenders face two major challenges:

High default risk due to inaccurate or delayed risk assessment

Credit exclusion, where eligible borrowers are rejected because existing systems cannot fairly evaluate them

Additionally, current loan assessment processes are:

Time-consuming and costly

Difficult to scale

Lacking transparency and real-time insights

Poorly suited for micro-loans and small-ticket lending

This creates a system where lenders lose capital, and borrowers lose access to timely credit, slowing financial inclusion and economic growth.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🚨 The Problem It Solves

Web3 security today is **hard to act on**.  
While many tools can detect risks, they often present **technical alerts** that only security experts understand.  
As a result, users, developers, and DAOs are forced to make **high‑stakes decisions** without clear guidance, leading to losses, poor governance decisions, and security failures.

ChainSentinel.ai bridges this gap by turning **complex blockchain risks into clear, actionable decisions**.

---

## 🧠 What People Can Use ChainSentinel.ai For

### 👤 For Web3 Users
- Understand whether a wallet action (approve, transfer, swap) is **safe or risky**
- Get **plain‑English explanations** instead of confusing alerts
- Know **exactly what to do next** (proceed, revoke, or stop)

**Result:** Safer transactions without needing security expertise.

---

### 👨‍💻 For Developers & Protocol Teams
- Quickly evaluate smart contract actions and configurations
- Detect risky patterns like unlimited approvals or admin abuse
- Get consistent **risk scoring** before deploying or interacting

**Result:** Faster, safer development decisions.

---

### 🏛️ For DAOs & Governance Members
- Analyze DAO proposals beyond surface‑level descriptions
- Understand **financial, technical, and governance risks**
- See what could go wrong *before* voting

**Result:** More informed voting and reduced governance failures.

---

## 🔐 How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

| Existing Task | Before ChainSentinel | With ChainSentinel |
|---------------|----------------------|--------------------|
| Reading security alerts | Highly technical, confusing | Simple, human‑readable explanations |
| DAO voting | Blind trust or expert‑only | Clear risk & impact summary |
| Transaction approval | Guesswork | Clear risk level + recommendation |
| Security decisions | Reactive | Proactive and guided |

---

## ✅ Key Benefits

- **No deep security knowledge required**
- **Faster decision‑making**
- **Reduced risk of scams, exploits, and governance mistakes**
- **Scalable across wallets, dApps, and DAOs**

---

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into (and How We Solved Them)

Building ChainSentinel.ai was a strong learning experience, especially because we were working with a **new agent‑based platform (On‑Demand)** and integrating multiple agents, tools, and workflows. Below are the key challenges we faced and how we overcame them.

---

## 1. Understanding the On‑Demand Agent & Tool Architecture

**Challenge:**  
At the beginning, it was not very clear how **agents**, **tools**, **RAG knowledge bases**, and **workflows** are supposed to work together on the On‑Demand platform. Unlike traditional backend systems, logic is split between:
- Agent prompts (defined in the UI)
- Tool logic (REST / Knowledge / Policy tools)
- Workflow orchestration (how agents are chained)

This caused initial confusion about *where logic should live*.

**How we solved it:**  
We clearly separated responsibilities:
- **Agents** → reasoning and explanation (prompts only)
- **Tools** → deterministic logic (policy checks, risk scoring)
- **Workflow** → orchestration (agent → tool → agent)

Once this mental model was clear, the system became much easier to build and debug.

---

## 2. On‑Demand Platform Configuration Issues

**Challenge:**  
We ran into multiple **platform‑specific hurdles**, such as:
- Agent IDs not being available immediately after creation  
- Confusion between **agent adapters** (REST API vs Knowledge Base)
- Configuration fields (OpenAPI schema, config values) being mandatory but poorly documented
- Sessions failing silently when agent IDs or adapters were misconfigured

This slowed down development and caused unexpected failures during early testing.

**How we solved it:**  
- We standardized **agent IDs** in one place and reused them consistently  
- Chose **REST API adapters** for logic‑based tools and **Knowledge Base adapters** only for RAG  
- Incrementally tested each agent and tool in isolation before chaining them  
- Used debug mode and simple test queries to validate configuration step‑by‑step

This helped stabilize the platform behavior.

---

## 3. Chaining Multiple Agents Reliably

**Challenge:**  
Chaining multiple agents (transaction → policy → RAG → risk → explanation) introduced issues such as:
- Passing noisy or unstructured outputs between agents
- LLM responses becoming verbose or inconsistent
- Difficulty ensuring explainability across steps

**How we solved it:**  
- Enforced **structured outputs** at each stage (policy result, risk level, explanation)
- Kept agent prompts **focused and minimal**
- Used a final “Explanation Agent” to translate everything into clean, human‑readable language

This ensured consistent, understandable outputs for demos and judges.

---

## 4. RAG Knowledge Integration Limitations

**Challenge:**  
While adding knowledge bases (documents, spreadsheets), we noticed:
- Strict permission and format requirements
- Service account / access configuration complexity
- Limited feedback when knowledge retrieval failed

**How we solved it:**  
- Started with **small, clean datasets** (Ethereum security cases)
- Tested retrieval independently before using it in workflows
- Added fallback logic so the agent clearly states when no relevant knowledge is found

This made the system more reliable and honest.

---

## 5. Balancing Technical Depth with Judge Clarity

**Challenge:**  
It was easy to over‑engineer the system and lose clarity for judges who are not deeply technical.

**How we solved it:**  
- Focused the demo on **clear outcomes**, not internal complexity
- Reduced jargon in UI and explanations
- Ensured every output answers:
  *Is it risky? Why? What should I do next?*

This balance helped make the project both **technically strong and easy to understand**.

---

## ✅ Key Takeaway

The biggest challenge was not writing code, but **learning how to think in an agent‑first, platform‑driven architecture** on On‑Demand. By iterating, simplifying, and clearly separating responsibilities, we turned these hurdles into a strong, scalable solution.

These challenges ultimately helped us build a **more robust, explainable, and judge‑friendly product**.

**Open Innovation**

The Open Innovation track focuses on solutions that are **broadly applicable**, **cross‑domain**, and capable of creating **ecosystem‑level impact** rather than solving a narrow, isolated problem.  
ChainSentinel.ai strongly aligns with this vision.

---

## 🔗 1. Cross‑Industry Applicability

Although ChainSentinel.ai is built for **Web3 and blockchain**, the core idea is **domain‑agnostic**:

- Turning complex technical signals into clear decisions
- Using AI agents + policies + knowledge to guide human actions
- Making expert‑level insights accessible to non‑experts

This approach can extend beyond crypto into:
- FinTech risk assessment
- Compliance and governance systems
- Cybersecurity decision support
- Enterprise approval workflows

➡️ This makes ChainSentinel.ai an **open innovation platform**, not just a niche Web3 tool.

---

## 🤖 2. Agent‑Based Innovation Using AI

Open Innovation encourages experimentation with **new computing paradigms**.  
ChainSentinel.ai uses:

- Multiple specialized AI agents
- Clear separation of reasoning, policy, and explanation
- Retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) for grounded insights

Instead of a single monolithic AI, we designed a **modular, extensible agent system** that others can build on, extend, or adapt.

➡️ This aligns directly with open, composable innovation.

---

## 🧩 3. Platform & Ecosystem Thinking

ChainSentinel.ai is not a closed application. It is designed to be:

- Integrated into wallets, DAOs, dashboards, and dApps
- Used as an API or middleware
- Extended with new agents, policies, and knowledge bases

This enables:
- Developers to build on top of it
- Communities to adapt it to their own governance rules
- Ecosystems to improve safety without reinventing security logic

➡️ This ecosystem‑first mindset is central to the Open Innovation track.

---

## 🛡️ 4. Solving a Shared, Global Problem

Security, trust, and decision‑making are **universal challenges** in decentralized systems.

ChainSentinel.ai addresses:
- Information asymmetry
- Lack of security expertise
- Poor decision clarity in high‑risk environments

By making security understandable, the project contributes to a **safer and more inclusive digital ecosystem**, which is a key goal of open innovation initiatives.

---

## 🚀 5. Scalable Future Scope

ChainSentinel.ai has a clear path beyond the hackathon:
- Multi‑chain support
- DAO governance automation
- Real‑time transaction protection
- Agent marketplaces and plugins

This demonstrates that the project is not a one‑off prototype, but a **scalable innovation framework**.

---

**OnDemand Track**

**The problem it solves**

Today’s crypto wallets assume users are blockchain engineers. Everyday actions like sending money require understanding gas fees, monitoring network congestion, handling long hexadecimal addresses, and fixing nonce errors. This makes simple tasks stressful, time-consuming, and risky, where a single mistake can lead to permanent financial loss.

Lumina solves this by shifting Web3 from “manual control” to “intent-driven intelligence.”
Instead of forcing users to think in protocol-level details, Lumina allows them to think like humans.

What People Can Use It For

* Sending money without worrying about gas prices or timing
* Scheduling crypto transfers automatically when fees are low
* Avoiding costly mistakes caused by wrong addresses or poor fee selection
* Making crypto remittances safer and stress-free
* Interacting with blockchain using natural language instead of complex UIs

By combining Gemini’s semantic reasoning, machine learning–based prediction, and automated execution, Lumina transforms crypto wallets into proactive assistants that optimize cost, reduce risk, and dramatically improve user experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Lumina came with both technical and architectural challenges.

One major hurdle was *bridging prediction with real execution. While scheduling transactions in MongoDB was straightforward, nothing happened when the scheduled time arrived. The system lacked an active execution layer. This was solved by designing a **background worker (Executioner)* that continuously monitors scheduled transactions and triggers execution automatically, creating a closed-loop system.

Another challenge was *handling volatile gas prices. Gas values change rapidly, making static logic unreliable. I overcame this by introducing a **machine learning–based time-series prediction approach*, allowing the system to make data-driven decisions instead of fixed assumptions.

Finally, converting *natural language user intent into structured blockchain logic* was non-trivial. Integrating Gemini as a reasoning layer helped extract intent, constraints, and conditions accurately, enabling seamless automation without user confusion.

Each challenge pushed the project closer to a real-world, production-grade system rather than a simple prototype.

**Ethereum Track**

Our app strongly aligns with ETHIndia because it is built to solve a real-world problem within the Ethereum ecosystem using Ethereum-compatible blockchains and Web3 principles. It focuses on improving everyday Ethereum usage by making ETH transactions safer, cheaper, and more accessible to non-technical users.

The application directly addresses common Ethereum challenges such as high and volatile gas fees, poor user experience in wallets, and transaction failures. By using AI and machine learning to predict gas trends, and automating transaction execution, the app enhances how users interact with Ethereum without changing the underlying protocol.

Additionally, the project promotes Ethereum’s core values of openness, decentralization, and user empowerment by lowering the barrier to entry for new users. Instead of requiring deep technical knowledge, it enables natural and intuitive interaction with Ethereum, supporting ETHIndia’s mission of building practical, user-centric applications that drive real adoption of the Ethereum ecosystem.

**Open Innovation**

Our app represents Open Innovation because it combines existing technologies—AI, machine learning, and blockchain—in a new and creative way to solve a real-world problem. Instead of building isolated solutions, it integrates external AI intelligence (Gemini), open blockchain networks, and open-source tools to create an intelligent, intent-based wallet. By reimagining how users interact with Web3 and making complex systems accessible to everyone, our app demonstrates innovation through integration, openness, and real-world impact, rather than reinventing technology from scratch.

**Google Gemini API**

Google Gemini API powers the core intelligence of the application. It understands user intent expressed in natural language, interprets context and conditions, and converts human instructions into structured actions. This allows users to interact with the wallet intuitively instead of dealing with technical blockchain parameters.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB acts as the system’s memory and scheduling layer. It stores user actions, transaction details, predictions, and execution schedules in a flexible, time-based structure. This allows the app to track transaction states, automate execution, and scale efficiently.

**ElevenLabs**

ElevenLabs enhances the user experience by enabling voice-based interaction and feedback. Users can give commands or receive confirmations through natural-sounding voice responses, making the wallet more accessible and human-centric.

**The problem it solves**

## Problem Statement

Modern AI systems are powerful but unreliable: they can act misaligned under pressure, **exhibit hidden bias**, and **produce hallucinated or non-compliant outputs**. There is no unified, practical way to audit these risks before AI systems are trusted in real-world, high-stakes use.

## How This Project Solves It

This project builds a **unified AI guardrails layer** that sits between users and models:

- **Agentic Misalignment Auditing**  stress-tests agentic prompts to measure insider-threat-like behaviors and enforces operational controls (tool gating, human approval, refusal rules).
- **FairCheck** – audits black-box models for demographic bias using counterfactual and statistical fairness analysis, producing an actionable fairness report card.
- **AlignCheck** – verifies outputs against policy rules, detects hallucinations, and blocks or rewrites unsafe responses.

Together, these guardrails turn AI from a blind trust system into a **measurable, auditable, and controllable component** suitable for real-world deployment.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

## 1) Time constraint
One major challenge was keeping the system reliable under hackathon time pressure while integrating multiple guardrails (misalignment detection, fairness auditing, and policy checks).

## Solution 
Our team worked relentless hours, broke down the project in different components and divided work according to individual expertise. By doing this we worked seamless and completed the project in a streamline flow.


### 2) Tool & Dependency Fragility
- **Issue:** Fairness libraries (e.g., AIF360) and policy engines (OPA) can be brittle to install, version-sensitive, or fail silently in containerized environments.
- **Risk:** A single dependency failure could break the entire demo.

**How I Solved It**
- Designed graceful fallbacks:
  - If AIF360 fails -  fall back to deterministic fairness metrics.
  - If OPA is unreachable -  switch to an internal policy fallback.
- This ensured the system never crashes and always returns an audit result.

**OnDemand Track**

# OnDemand Track Compliance – AI Guardrails Suite

AI Guardrails Suite is built directly on top of the OnDemand platform and fully satisfies the minimum criteria for the OnDemand Track by using OnDemand’s tools, APIs, and platform capabilities to address a real-world problem: the safe, accountable, and compliant deployment of autonomous AI systems.

## Use of OnDemand Tools and APIs

The system uses the **OnDemand Chat API** as the core reasoning and evaluation layer across all guardrail checks, including agentic risk detection, fairness auditing, policy compliance, hallucination detection, and final decision making. The **OnDemand Media API** is used to ingest documents and contextual data for fact verification and policy evaluation, enabling compliance checks against external and internal sources.

## OnDemand Agents Integration

AI Guardrails Suite integrates **seven OnDemand agents**, each with a fixed and specialized role, orchestrated through the **OnDemand Agents Flow Builder**. These agents work together as a structured workflow rather than isolated prompts, enabling explainable, auditable, and robust safety decisions. This exceeds the minimum requirement of six OnDemand agents for the track.

## Custom Tool Integrations

The project incorporates more than three types of custom tool integrations within the OnDemand workflow:
- **Policy Enforcement** using structured allow/deny rules instead of prompt-based safety
- **Tool Permission Gating** to dynamically allow or revoke access to sensitive actions based on risk
- **Human-in-the-Loop Approval** for high-risk actions and decisions
- **Counterfactual Generation for Fairness Auditing** to detect hidden bias in black-box models
- **Audit Logging** to create immutable records for compliance and accountability

## Real-World Applicability

AI Guardrails Suite is designed for real-world deployment in enterprise and regulated environments such as hiring, finance, healthcare, and infrastructure. It works with black-box models and produces actionable outcomes, including enforceable controls, safe rewrites, and audit trails, rather than simple warnings.

## Summary

By combining the OnDemand Chat and Media APIs, orchestrating seven OnDemand agents through the Flow Builder, and integrating multiple custom enforcement and auditing tools, AI Guardrails Suite demonstrates deep and meaningful use of the OnDemand platform while delivering a practical, enterprise-ready AI governance solution.

> Crypto Trading bot using OnDemand

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🧩 The problem it solves

Trading newly launched tokens on Solana is fast but risky. People often rely on Telegram calls, Twitter hype, or manual checks, which can lead to rug pulls, locked liquidity issues, or highly concentrated ownership. Doing all checks manually also takes time, and by the time a user reacts, the opportunity is often gone.

This project solves that by automating the entire decision flow in a safe way. It continuously discovers trending new tokens, runs basic security checks automatically, and only allows trades when minimum safety conditions are met.

People can use it to:

Quickly spot high-momentum Solana tokens

Avoid obvious scams like unrenounced contracts or unlocked liquidity

Reduce emotional and impulsive trading

Save time by removing repetitive manual checks

Overall, it makes early-stage token trading faster, safer, and more structured, especially for users who are not security experts.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was designing the workflow without making it strictly step-by-step. OnDemand runs agents independently, but our logic depended on outputs from previous tools (like passing the mint address safely between agents).

Another challenge was handling security checks correctly. Different data sources sometimes returned incomplete or delayed information, which could lead to false positives. I solved this by adding clear decision rules and stopping execution immediately if any critical safety condition failed.

Managing private key access was also tricky. I had to ensure that only the execution agent could access it and that no other agent could accidentally expose sensitive data. This was solved by scoping permissions strictly at the agent level.

Overall, these challenges helped me better understand agent orchestration, conditional execution, and secure tool access in an agentic system like OnDemand

**OnDemand Track**

---

## How This Workflow Fits into the OnDemand Agent Track

In OnDemand, workflows are **not rigid pipelines**. They are **agent-orchestrated tracks**, where each tool is invoked dynamically based on context, validation signals, and previous outputs.

Our Solana trading system is implemented as a **single autonomous OnDemand track** composed of specialized agents and custom tools that coordinate through shared state — not hardcoded steps.

---

## OnDemand Execution Model (Conceptual)

### 1️⃣ Trigger-Driven Discovery Agent

Instead of a “Step 1”, an **OnDemand Trigger Agent** initiates the track when invoked (manual, scheduled, or event-based).

* Uses **Dex Screener** as a **custom discovery tool**
* Fetches all Solana tokens created in the last 24 hours
* Filters by:

  * Volume > $100k
  * Momentum / volume delta
* Automatically selects the token with the **highest volume acceleration**
* Persists the `mintAddress` into shared track memory

📌 No user intervention — the agent decides *what matters now*.

---

### 2️⃣ Autonomous Safety & Risk Agent

Once a mint address appears in shared memory, a **Security Audit Agent** is automatically invoked.

* Calls **Solscan** via a transaction-analysis tool
* Evaluates risk heuristics:

  * Ownership renounced ❌ → hard stop
  * Liquidity unlocked ❌ → hard stop
  * Top 10 holders > 50% → soft warning

🔁 **Conditional branching is native in OnDemand**

* If flagged **Risky** → track terminates with a structured report
* If **Safe** → execution permission is granted downstream

This keeps trading logic **non-reckless and explainable**.

---

### 3️⃣ Execution Agent (On-Demand, Not Always-On)

Only when safety conditions pass, the **Execution Agent** activates.

* Uses **Jupiter** as a swap execution tool
* Parameters are injected dynamically:

  * Amount: `0.001 SOL`
  * Slippage: `1%`
  * Token: derived `mintAddress`

🔐 Private key access is **scoped only to this agent**

* No other agent can read or leak it
* Execution is single-shot and auditable

This aligns perfectly with OnDemand’s **principle of least privilege**.

---

### 4️⃣ Post-Execution Verification Agent

Rather than polling endlessly, a **Verification Agent** runs with a delayed execution policy.

* Waits ~20 seconds
* Queries wallet state via a Portfolio Tracker tool
* Confirms:

  * Token balance exists
  * Transaction finalized
* Emits a final success/failure signal

📊 This creates a **closed-loop autonomous trade cycle**.

---

## Why This Is Native to OnDemand (Key Value)

✔ **Not stepwise — state-driven**
✔ **Each agent is independently callable and replaceable**
✔ **Tools are invoked contextually, not sequentially**
✔ **Failure paths are first-class citizens**
✔ **Secure key handling via agent-scoped permissions**

In short:

> This workflow is not “automation.”
> It is **agentic execution under a single OnDemand track**.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Scraping Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/Scraping%20Tools-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

problem statement: In emerging economies, millions of people are financially active but remain credit-invisible. They use UPI, SMS payments, and gig platforms daily, yet lack formal credit scores. Existing systems force users to share raw financial data, creating a privacy vs access dilemma.

solution: ZK-Sentinel is a privacy-first financial identity protocol that verifies creditworthiness without exposing sensitive data. We analyze user financial behavior using secure local AI and generate zero-knowledge proofs that certify eligibility—such as “risk score above a threshold”—without revealing transactions or identity.

**Challenges we ran into**

Fragmented & Noisy Financial Data
User data from UPI, SMS, and gig platforms is unstructured and inconsistent, making accurate financial profiling difficult.
Privacy-Preserving AI Computation
Running meaningful credit analysis while ensuring raw data never leaves the user’s device or secure environment is technically complex.
Zero-Knowledge Proof Generation Cost
zk-SNARKs require significant computation and optimization to remain fast, affordable, and scalable for mass adoption.
On-Chain Verification Efficiency
Verifying proofs on-chain must be gas-efficient and fast to be viable for real-world lending systems.
Institutional Trust & Adoption
Convincing lenders to accept cryptographic proofs instead of traditional credit scores requires education and gradual integration

**Ethereum Track**

ZK-Sentinel is designed to be blockchain-agnostic, with Ethereum supported as an alternative verification layer alongside Solana. Ethereum can be used to anchor cryptographic hashes of zero-knowledge financial proofs, enabling public, tamper-proof, and trustless verification of user claims.

Similar to Solana, all heavy computation—AI analysis and zero-knowledge proof generation—remains off-chain. Ethereum is used only for proof anchoring and verification, ensuring that no sensitive financial data or documents are ever stored on-chain.

While Solana is preferred for its low fees and fast finality, Ethereum provides strong decentralization and a mature ecosystem, making ZK-Sentinel compatible with EVM-based DeFi protocols, lenders, and identity systems. This flexibility allows ZK-Sentinel to integrate seamlessly across both high-throughput and EVM-native environments.

**Open Innovation**

problem: In emerging economies, millions of people are financially active but remain credit-invisible. They use UPI, SMS payments, and gig platforms daily, yet lack formal credit scores. Existing systems force users to share raw financial data, creating a privacy vs access dilemma.

solution: ZK-Sentinel is a privacy-first financial identity protocol that verifies creditworthiness without exposing sensitive data. We analyze user financial behavior using secure local AI and generate zero-knowledge proofs that certify eligibility—such as “risk score above a threshold”—without revealing transactions or identity.
Innovation:
Instead of data sharing, we use cryptographic proof. Lenders trust the proof, not the data. This removes surveillance while maintaining underwriting confidence.
Technology:
Local AI + Zero-Knowledge Proofs (zk-SNARKs) with on-chain verification. No raw data ever leaves the user’s control.
Impact:
This enables financial access for the unbanked and underbanked while preserving dignity, privacy, and security.
Vision:
ZK-Sentinel is not just a credit score—it’s a trust layer for the decentralized economy

**SCAILE Track**

Why we align: "SCAILE looks for comprehensive, production-ready solutions with real-world impact, and ZK-Sentinel delivers exactly that for the 'Next Billion Users.'

High-Impact AI: We aren't just summarizing text; we are deploying AI to solve a critical economic problem—financial exclusion—by analyzing alternative data (SMS, Gig-work) that traditional banks ignore.

Modular & Adaptable: Our architecture is designed to be flexible. Whether the specific SCAILE problem statement (revealed at the venue) targets fraud detection, data privacy, or ethical AI, ZK-Sentinel’s core engine can be instantly adapted to meet the criteria while maintaining our focus on verifiable trust.

End-to-End Polish: From the ElevenLabs voice interface to the Ethereum settlement layer, we offer a fully functional product, not just a prototype, aligning with SCAILE’s standard for high-quality engineering.

**OnDemand Track**

ZK-Sentinel uses Solana in an on-demand manner, meaning the blockchain is accessed only when trustless public verification is required. All intensive and sensitive operations—such as AI-based document analysis and zero-knowledge proof generation—are performed off-chain by default.

Solana is invoked on demand to anchor cryptographic hashes of zero-knowledge proofs once a user chooses to make a financial claim verifiable. These hashes allow third parties, such as lenders or decentralized applications, to independently confirm the authenticity and integrity of a proof directly from the blockchain without accessing raw financial data or relying on a centralized backend.

By limiting blockchain interaction to verification and audit checkpoints, ZK-Sentinel achieves scalability, low transaction costs, and strong privacy guarantees while still benefiting from Solana’s immutability and fast finality.

**Best UI/UX**

ZK-Sentinel’s UI/UX is designed with a strong focus on privacy, trust, and simplicity, ensuring that users can interact with complex technologies like AI, zero-knowledge proofs, and blockchain without feeling overwhelmed. The interface follows a clean, card-based layout with a clear step-by-step flow—from authentication and document upload to proof generation and verification—so users always understand where they are in the process.

The color theme is built around calm, professional tones such as deep blues and neutral greys to convey security and reliability, with subtle green accents used to indicate successful verification and eligibility. Warning or in-progress states use muted amber tones, avoiding harsh colors that could create anxiety. High contrast and readable typography are maintained throughout to ensure accessibility and clarity across devices and lighting conditions.

Animations and micro-interactions are used purposefully to communicate system states rather than for decoration. Smooth transitions, progress indicators, and loading animations reassure users during longer operations like AI analysis or zero-knowledge proof generation, clearly signaling that the system is working in the background. Results appear with gentle fade-ins or slide-up effects, reinforcing completion and confidence.

From a privacy perspective, the UI never displays raw financial data. Instead, it uses ranges, indicators, and visual health metrics to communicate outcomes without exposing sensitive information—even at the interface level. Combined with simple language, minimal jargon, and optional voice-based feedback, the UI/UX makes ZK-Sentinel accessible to a wide range of users, including those in emerging markets, while visually reinforcing the project’s privacy-first and trust-driven philosophy.

**Auth0**

ZK-Sentinel uses Auth0 as its authentication and access-control layer to securely identify users before they interact with the system. Auth0 handles user login and identity verification using industry-standard OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flows, issuing JWT access tokens after successful authentication.

These tokens are required to access protected backend APIs such as document upload, financial analysis, zero-knowledge proof generation, and verification. The backend validates each request by verifying the Auth0-issued token, ensuring that only authenticated users can generate or verify proofs.

Importantly, Auth0 is used only for identity and session management. It never has access to users’ financial data, documents, AI-derived insights, zero-knowledge proofs, or blockchain transactions. This clean separation ensures strong security while preserving ZK-Sentinel’s privacy-first design.

In short, Auth0 answers “who is the user,” while ZK-Sentinel proves “what the user is eligible for” without revealing sensitive data.

**Google Gemini API**

ZK-Sentinel integrates the Google Gemini API to intelligently analyze user-provided financial documents and unstructured data in a privacy-conscious manner. Gemini is used as an AI reasoning layer that converts raw inputs—such as bank statements, transaction summaries, or gig-work records—into structured financial signals required for zero-knowledge proof generation.

Instead of making eligibility decisions directly, Gemini extracts high-level attributes like income ranges, consistency indicators, and risk categories. These attributes are treated as private inputs and are never exposed to verifiers or stored on-chain. They are passed only to the zero-knowledge prover, which cryptographically proves claims about the user without revealing the underlying data.

The Gemini API is invoked off-chain and on-demand, ensuring that sensitive data remains outside the blockchain and is processed only when a user explicitly requests proof generation. This design combines the strengths of AI-based understanding with cryptographic privacy guarantees.

In essence, Google Gemini provides intelligence without authority—it interprets data, while ZK-Sentinel enforces trust through zero-knowledge proofs and blockchain verification.

**ElevenLabs**

ZK-Sentinel integrates ElevenLabs to provide a natural, human-like voice interaction layer for accessibility and user guidance. ElevenLabs is used to convert system-generated text—such as onboarding instructions, verification status, and proof results—into high-quality speech in real time.

This feature is especially valuable for users in emerging markets or low-literacy environments, where voice-based interaction significantly improves usability and trust. By offering spoken explanations of verification outcomes and next steps, ZK-Sentinel makes privacy-preserving financial identity more inclusive.

ElevenLabs operates strictly as an output-only layer. No financial data, documents, zero-knowledge proofs, or blockchain information are sent for processing. Only minimal, non-sensitive text messages are converted to audio, ensuring user privacy is fully preserved.

In short, ElevenLabs enhances accessibility and user experience without touching or learning any sensitive financial data, aligning seamlessly with ZK-Sentinel’s privacy-first architecture.

**Solana**

ZK-Sentinel uses Solana as an on-demand blockchain verification layer to provide public, tamper-proof validation of zero-knowledge financial proofs. Instead of storing sensitive data on-chain, only cryptographic proof hashes are anchored, allowing anyone to verify the authenticity of user claims without accessing private information.

All heavy computation—AI analysis and zero-knowledge proof generation—happens off-chain. Solana is used only when public verification is required, ensuring scalability, low cost, and strong privacy guarantees.

By anchoring proofs on Solana, lenders and decentralized applications can independently verify financial eligibility without trusting a centralized backend. In this design, Solana acts as a decentralized verification and notarization layer, while ZK-Sentinel preserves privacy through zero-knowledge cryptography.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### **The Problem It Solves**  

People and companies today lose **significant money** to:  
- Forgotten subscriptions  
- Unused tools  
- Silent price hikes  
- Auto-renewing free trials  

Most existing solutions only **list subscriptions**.  
They do **not** highlight what is actually wasting money or needs urgent action.  
As a result, users remain unaware of **hidden financial leaks**.




### **How Sub-Zero Solves It**  

Sub-Zero transforms raw subscription data into **Waste Intelligence**.  
Instead of just showing what users are subscribed to, it clearly reveals:

- **How much money is being wasted annually**  
- **Which subscriptions have increased prices without notice**  
- **Which free trials are about to charge**  
- **Which tools overlap in functionality**  
- **Which subscriptions are likely no longer being used**  

This makes financial waste **visible, emotional, and actionable**.



### **Real-World Impact**  

For individuals, Sub-Zero helps:  
- Avoid surprise charges  
- Cancel unused services  
- Regain control over spending  

For businesses, Sub-Zero enables:  
- Detection of redundant SaaS tools  
- Identification of unused licenses  
- Control over rising subscription costs  

It turns **subscription chaos** into **clear spend control**.


### **Why It Matters**  

Sub-Zero doesn’t just track spending.  
It **exposes waste** and drives **better financial decisions**.

**Challenges we ran into**

### **Challenges I Ran Into**

### **1. Slow Gmail Email Sync**

Fetching hundreds of emails using the Gmail API was initially very slow because requests were processed sequentially. Syncing around 500 emails took over 75 seconds, which was not practical for real users or live demos.

**How I solved it:**  
I implemented parallel processing using a controlled thread pool with safe batch sizes. This reduced sync time by 5 to 10 times while avoiding Gmail API rate limits.

---

### **2. Detecting Real Subscriptions vs Noise**

Many emails contained promotions, newsletters, or unrelated receipts. Accurately identifying actual recurring subscriptions without false positives was a challenge.

**How I solved it:**  
I used:
- Keyword-based filtering  
- Metadata scoring  
- Vendor normalization  
- Amount and frequency checks  

This ensured only true subscription-related emails were processed.



### **3. Handling Silent Price Increases**

Subscriptions often change prices without clear notifications. Tracking these changes across historical receipts required consistent amount parsing and proper storage.

**How I solved it:**  
I created a price history table to store past charges and compared them over time to detect percentage increases automatically.



### **4. Free Trial Detection**

Free trials appear in many formats and are not always labeled clearly. Some emails do not mention the trial duration.

**How I solved it:**  
I combined:
- Amount-based detection (0 dollar charges)  
- Keyword matching (free, trial)  
- Fallback duration logic  

This ensured reliable trial ending alerts.



### **5. Performance vs Accuracy Balance**

Aggressive API calls caused timeouts and rate-limit errors, while conservative calls slowed the system.

**How I solved it:**  
I tuned:
- Batch sizes  
- Worker limits  
- Retry logic with exponential backoff  

This achieved a stable balance between speed and reliability.



### **What I Learned**

Building Sub-Zero required solving real-world problems related to API limits, data accuracy, performance optimization, and user trust. These challenges helped shape a more robust, scalable, and reliable system.

**Open Innovation**

Sub-Zero fits the Open Innovation track by solving a real-world financial problem using existing platforms in a new, smarter way. Instead of just listing subscriptions, it turns Gmail receipt data into actionable “waste intelligence” by detecting hidden price hikes, forgotten free trials, overlapping services, and unused subscriptions.

It innovates on top of widely used tools like Gmail and modern web APIs to create a privacy-first system that helps users and businesses actively reduce financial waste, not just track it. The focus is on practical impact, usability, and smarter decision-making rather than just building another dashboard.

**The problem it solves**

The project enables users to invest in crypto safely and consistently without timing the market. It replaces risky, centralized crypto SIPs with a non-custodial, on-chain alternative, ensuring users always control their funds.

By automating recurring investments through smart contracts, it removes manual effort, reduces emotional trading, and provides transparent, verifiable execution—making long-term crypto investing simpler, safer, and more reliable.

**Challenges we ran into**

A key challenge was automating recurring SIP executions on-chain, since smart contracts cannot self-trigger. We solved this by using time-based execution checks with an external trigger, while keeping all validation and fund transfers fully on-chain and preventing double execution.

Another hurdle was multi-asset allocation within a single SIP while controlling gas costs. We optimized the contract by batching operations and reducing state writes, improving efficiency without sacrificing functionality.

**Ethereum Track**

Our project is a non-custodial, on-chain SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) protocol built using Ethereum-compatible smart contracts. It automates recurring crypto investments through trustless smart contract execution, removing dependence on centralized exchanges.

Users retain full control of their funds via Web3 wallets, while all SIP parameters amount, frequency, asset allocation, and maturity are enforced onchain. The protocol follows EVM standards, allowing seamless deployment across Ethereum and EVM networks.

By enabling transparent, automated, and decentralized investing, the project strongly aligns with the Ethereum Track’s focus on DeFi innovation and trustless financial infrastructure.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

In today’s digital ecosystem, users continuously generate sensitive personal data such as health records, financial information, behavioral patterns, and location data. However, most platforms lack transparency and accountability in how this data is accessed and used.

Key problems addressed:
- Users are unaware of **when**, **why**, or **by whom** their data is accessed  
- Consent is treated as a **one-time checkbox**, not an ongoing agreement  
- No real-time visibility or alerts when data is used  
- Organizations struggle to clearly demonstrate **regulatory compliance**  

This leads to:
- Privacy violations  
- Silent misuse of data  
- Compliance and legal risks  
- Loss of user trust  

---

## What People Can Use It For / How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer

This project functions as a **Consent & Data Access Firewall**, ensuring that every data request is validated against active user consent.

### For Users
- Real-time visibility into data access events  
- Instant email notifications when their data is accessed  
- A transparent consent and access history  
- Stronger control and confidence over personal data  

### For Organizations
- Automated consent enforcement before data access  
- Tamper-proof audit logs for compliance  
- Reduced legal and regulatory risk  
- Increased user trust through transparency  

### For Developers & Platforms
- Middleware-based consent validation  
- Detection of abnormal or unauthorized data access  
- Consent drift monitoring  
- Safer data pipelines by design

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Monitoring Data Access Without Performance Overhead
Intercepting all data access requests risked increasing latency.
- **Solution:** Implemented lightweight metadata logging instead of raw data capture.

### 2. Handling Consent Drift
Outdated consent permissions can be misused by systems.
- **Solution:** Introduced consent versioning to validate every request against the latest consent state.

### 3. Real-Time Notifications Without Spamming Users
Frequent alerts could overwhelm users.
- **Solution:** Applied rule-based and throttled notification logic.

### 4. Making Compliance Logs Human-Readable
Technical logs are difficult for non-technical stakeholders.
- **Solution:** Built a simplified dashboard translating logs into clear timelines and actions.

**Ethereum Track**

## Tracks Applied

- Privacy & Data Protection  
- Cybersecurity  
- Ethical AI & Responsible Technology  
- Trust & Transparency Systems

### Blockchain-Based Learning Effort Proof System

> PoLE

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Remix IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Remix%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In traditional academic and professional learning environments, verifying a student's learning effort, submitted work, and achievements is often centralized, manual, and vulnerable to manipulation. Institutions store records in internal databases, making them susceptible to data loss, unauthorized modification, or lack of transparency. Additionally, recruiters or external evaluators must rely on institutional verification, which is time-consuming and sometimes unreliable.

There is no secure, tamper-proof, and decentralized mechanism to ensure that student learning records and effort proofs remain authentic, verifiable, and accessible across organizations.

What People Can Use It For

The Proof of Learning Effort (PoLE) system provides a secure and transparent platform where:

Students can upload learning artifacts such as reports, assignments, certificates, project files, and multimedia evidence of work.

Mentors or instructors review and validate submitted records.

Once approved, records are permanently stored on the blockchain, ensuring immutability.

HR professionals and recruiters can view only verified blockchain-stored records, ensuring trust in candidate credentials.

How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

Tamper-Proof Academic Records: Once approved and stored on the blockchain, records cannot be altered or deleted.

Decentralized Verification: Eliminates dependence on centralized institutional databases for credential verification.

Transparent Approval Process: Mentor validation ensures only legitimate records reach the blockchain.

Efficient Recruitment Screening: HR teams can instantly verify authentic student achievements without contacting institutions.

Data Integrity and Trust: Ensures lifelong, trustworthy ownership of learning evidence by students.

Real-World Applications

Academic credential verification

Internship and project proof validation

Skill certification tracking

Recruitment background verification

Lifelong learning portfolios

**Challenges we ran into**

Smart Contract Deployment Failures: Transactions initially failed due to incorrect gas estimation and contract constructor parameters. This was resolved by optimizing contract functions and validating deployment parameters before execution.

Blockchain–Database Synchronization: Maintaining consistency between MongoDB student records and blockchain-approved data was challenging. I implemented a mentor-approval workflow to ensure only validated records were written to the blockchain.

IPFS File Retrieval Issues: Uploaded files occasionally returned invalid gateway responses. I fixed this by switching to a stable Pinata gateway and adding fallback retry logic for file fetching.

MetaMask Transaction Handling: Users faced transaction rejection errors due to improper network configuration. I added automatic network detection and prompts to switch to the correct testnet.

Role-Based Access Control: Preventing unauthorized access to mentor and HR dashboards required careful backend route protection. This was addressed by implementing role validation middleware.

These challenges strengthened system reliability, security, and user experience.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

##  The Problem It Solves — **EthosHealth**

EthosHealth addresses the complexity, inefficiency, and lack of transparency in today’s healthcare benefit systems by simplifying how patients access care and how hospitals get paid.

People can use EthosHealth to **verify their identity, discover eligible healthcare schemes, and use those benefits at hospitals without paperwork or payment stress**.

### Problems in the Current System
- Patients don’t clearly know which healthcare schemes they are eligible for.
- Scheme applications and claims are mostly handled by hospitals, giving patients little visibility.
- Claims are paper-heavy, slow, and often approved only after treatment.
- Hospital payments are delayed and opaque, reducing trust on all sides.
- Multiple disconnected portals make the process confusing and error-prone.

### How EthosHealth Makes It Easier & Safer
- **Instant ABHA-based identity verification** removes manual checks and repeated form filling.
- **AI-powered eligibility detection** automatically matches patients with the right government schemes.
- **Digital healthcare vouchers** pre-approve treatment costs and prevent over-claiming or misuse.
- **Proof-based payments** ensure hospitals are paid only after verified treatment.
- **Blockchain-backed receipts** provide tamper-proof records and full transparency.
- **Gasless transactions** eliminate fees and complexity for non-technical users.

### Real-World Impact
- Patients get faster access to treatment without upfront payments.
- Hospitals receive trusted, faster settlements with less paperwork.
- Governments and insurers gain real-time auditability and reduced fraud.

**In short, EthosHealth transforms a fragmented, manual healthcare workflow into a single, transparent, and patient-controlled digital experience.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we Ran Into

Building EthosHealth involved several technical and design challenges, especially while balancing real-world healthcare workflows with emerging Eherium Ecosystem.

### ABHA ID Verification Without Public APIs
**Challenge:**  
There is no publicly available real-time API for ABHA ID verification, which made direct integration impossible during development.

**How we Solved It:**  
we designed a secure mock verification layer that simulates real ABHA workflows, including input validation and profile generation. This allowed the system to function realistically while keeping the architecture ready for official API integration.

---

### Wallet Connection & Network Issues
**Challenge:**  
Wallet connections failed frequently due to incorrect chain IDs, unstable RPC endpoints, and delayed provider injection from MetaMask.

**How we Solved It:**  
we added strict network checks, fallback RPC providers, and improved asynchronous handling of wallet initialization to ensure reliable wallet connections.

---

###  Implementing Gasless Transactions
**Challenge:**  
Enabling gasless transactions was complex because users should not pay gas fees, yet transactions still needed blockchain verification.

**How we Solved It:**  
we implemented a relayer-based (X402-style) workflow that separates user signing from transaction submission, allowing the backend to handle gas costs while maintaining security and transparency.

---

###  Preventing Double Voucher Redemption
**Challenge:**  
Vouchers were occasionally redeemed more than once due to duplicate API calls or page refreshes.

**How we Solved It:**  
we introduced idempotent APIs, redemption status flags, and record-level locking to guarantee single-use voucher redemption.

---

###  Syncing Frontend State with Blockchain State
**Challenge:**  
Keeping wallet balances, voucher status, and transaction history consistent across UI and blockchain caused race conditions and stale data.

**How we Solved It:**  
we separated UI state from blockchain state, used a centralized store, and added refresh triggers after every blockchain-related action.

---

###  Generating Accurate Digital Receipts
**Challenge:**  
Combining blockchain transaction data, voucher details, and medical metadata into a single receipt required precise coordination.

**How I Solved It:**  
we centralized receipt generation in the backend, ensuring consistent formatting, verified data sources, and reliable PDF output.

---

###  Key Takeaway
These challenges pushed me to design EthosHealth with a production-ready mindset—focusing on reliability, security, and user experience while working within real-world constraints.

**Ethereum Track**

##  How EthosHealth Fits into the Ethereum Track

EthosHealth is built around Ethereum as a **trust and verification layer**, demonstrating how blockchain can solve real-world problems beyond finance—specifically in public healthcare systems.

###  Ethereum as the Trust Layer
Healthcare benefits involve multiple parties (patients, hospitals, governments, insurers) who must trust the same data. Ethereum provides:
- **Immutable records** for voucher issuance, redemption, and payments  
- **Tamper-proof audit trails** that cannot be altered by any single party  
- **Public verifiability** without exposing sensitive health data  

This makes Ethereum ideal for high-trust, multi-stakeholder workflows.

---

### Native Ethereum Wallet Integration
EthosHealth integrates Ethereum wallets (MetaMask/WalletConnect) to:
- establish cryptographic user identity  
- securely authorize voucher usage  
- sign transactions without exposing private keys  

Wallets act as the patient’s **digital healthcare authorization tool**, not just a payment method.

---

### On-Chain Voucher Lifecycle
Healthcare benefits are modeled as **digital vouchers**, following an Ethereum-compatible lifecycle:
- voucher creation (pre-authorization)  
- voucher locking (hospital assignment)  
- voucher redemption (after proof of treatment)  

This shows a practical application of Ethereum smart contract patterns for real-world benefits.

---

### Gasless Transactions (Relayer Model)
To remove friction for non-technical users, EthosHealth uses a **gasless transaction flow**:
- users sign messages  
- a relayer submits transactions on-chain  
- users pay zero gas fees  

This aligns with modern Ethereum standards like meta-transactions and paymaster-style workflows.

---

###  Transparency Without Privacy Loss
EthosHealth stores:
- sensitive health data **off-chain**  
- cryptographic proofs and transaction hashes **on-chain**  

This balances Ethereum’s transparency with healthcare privacy requirements.

---

### Ethereum-Ready & Scalable Architecture
The project follows Ethereum best practices:
- EVM-compatible design  
- seamless migration to Layer 2 networks (Polygon, Base, Arbitrum)  
- hybrid on-chain/off-chain execution for scalability  

---

###  Why This Matters for the Ethereum Track
EthosHealth demonstrates:
- Ethereum as infrastructure for public good  
- blockchain-backed transparency in government workflows  
- real-world, non-DeFi use cases  
- user-friendly Web3 experiences through gas abstraction  

**EthosHealth shows how Ethereum can power secure, auditable, and citizen-centric healthcare systems at scale.**

> "Collateral-Free Loans for the Underbanked"

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India has over 450 million workers in the informal economy — domestic workers, street vendors, auto-rickshaw drivers, daily wage laborers, and gig workers. Despite contributing significantly to the economy, they face a critical barrier: they are financially invisible.

Why Traditional Credit Fails Them:
1.No Collateral — Banks require property, gold, or fixed deposits as security. Informal workers rarely own such assets.
2.No Formal Income Proof — Without salary slips, ITR filings, or bank statements, lenders cannot assess their repayment capacity.
3.No Credit History — CIBIL and traditional credit bureaus have no data on people who've never had a bank loan or credit card.
4.Digital Literacy Barriers — Complex banking apps and English-only interfaces exclude millions who are more comfortable with voice and regional languages.

The Result:
1.Forced to borrow from predatory moneylenders at 50-100% annual interest
2.Trapped in debt cycles with no path to financial stability
3.Unable to access opportunities that require credit — education, healthcare, small business capital

**Challenges we ran into**

🔴 Challenge 1: Building Trust Without Traditional Data
Problem: Traditional credit scoring relies on financial history — we had none of that for our target users.

Solution: We designed a novel Social Trust Graph algorithm that weights endorsements based on relationship type, duration, and endorser credibility. An employer's endorsement carries more weight than a stranger's, and the algorithm accounts for gaming attempts.

🔴 Challenge 2: Blockchain Gas Fees on Every Endorsement
Problem: Writing every endorsement directly to Polygon blockchain was expensive and slow, making the app impractical for users making multiple transactions.

Solution: Implemented a batch processing system — endorsements are collected off-chain and periodically committed to the blockchain in batches, reducing gas costs by 90% while maintaining verifiability.

🔴 Challenge 3: Voice AI for Low-Literacy Users
Problem: Our target users (domestic workers, daily laborers) often have limited reading ability. Text-based interfaces were a barrier.

Solution: Integrated Groq's ultra-fast LLM for natural language understanding and ElevenLabs for voice synthesis. Users can navigate the entire app using voice commands in Hindi, Malayalam, or English — no reading required.

🔴 Challenge 4: Real-time Multilingual Translation
Problem: Translating AI responses on-the-fly while maintaining natural conversation flow was technically complex.

Solution: Built a streaming translation pipeline using Groq's low-latency inference, achieving <500ms response times even for voice interactions.

🔴 Challenge 5: Designing for Trust in a Low-Trust Environment
Problem: Users skeptical of apps needed to feel safe sharing information and trusting the platform.

Solution: Made everything transparent and verifiable — users can see exactly who endorsed them, their trust score calculation, and blockchain proof of their credentials. We used simple, warm UI language that builds confidence.

**Ethereum Track**

Kredefy leverages Polygon (Ethereum L2) as the backbone of our trust verification system:

🔹 On-Chain Trust Endorsements
Every endorsement (employer vouching for a domestic worker, neighbor confirming reliability) is cryptographically hashed and stored on Polygon Amoy/Mainnet. This creates an immutable, tamper-proof trust record that users truly own.

🔹 Verifiable Portable Credentials
Unlike traditional references that live in siloed databases, our blockchain-stored endorsements are:

🔹Portable — Users carry their reputation across jobs and cities
Verifiable — Any lender can independently verify endorsement authenticity via smart contract
Sovereign — Users own their data, not platforms

🔹 Smart Contract Architecture
TrustEndorsement.sol — Stores endorsement hashes with endorser signatures
TrustScore.sol — On-chain computation of aggregate trust scores
Gas-optimized batch processing for cost-effective writes

🔹 Why Ethereum/Polygon?
We chose Polygon for its low gas fees and fast finality — critical for a high-volume consumer app serving India's underbanked. The Ethereum ecosystem's maturity and tooling made development reliable.

Kredefy brings 450M informal workers onto Web3 — using blockchain not for speculation, but for real-world financial inclusion.

**The problem it solves**

🧭 Tenjiku – Smart Travel Companion
Tenjiku is a web‑based travel companion platform built to solve real‑world problems faced by travelers, especially group, student, and budget travelers. Unlike conventional travel applications that mainly focus on bookings and destinations, Tenjiku focuses on planning before booking, transparent trip money management, and traveler safety.

The platform enables users to plan trips realistically by organizing destinations, schedules, and budgets in advance, helping them avoid last‑minute confusion and overspending. Its integrated Group Expense (Splitmoney) module allows users to add participants, track shared expenses, record payments, and automatically calculate settlements, ensuring fairness and reducing money‑related conflicts during group travel.

Tenjiku also includes an SOS & Safety feature that provides quick access to emergency information, nearby essentials, and safety awareness, making it especially useful when traveling in unfamiliar or low‑network areas. By combining trip planning, expense transparency, and safety preparedness into a single platform, Tenjiku promotes responsible tourism, mindful spending, and stress‑free travel.

Overall, Tenjiku aims to transform travel from a chaotic and stressful experience into a smart, organized, and reliable journey companion.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building Tenjiku, one of the main challenges was defining the right scope of the project, as travel is a very broad domain and it was initially tempting to include features like bookings and live maps. This was solved by clearly focusing on real‑world problems such as trip planning, group expense management, and safety instead of feature overload. Another major hurdle was managing routing across multiple modules like Planning, Split, and SOS, where some buttons initially did not work due to missing or mismatched routes; this was resolved by centralizing navigation using React Router and adopting a clean, feature‑based routing structure. Designing the group expense (Splitwise‑like) feature was also challenging, as the logic needed to be fair and easy to understand—this was addressed by keeping the calculations simple, transparent, and clearly visible to users. Since the project did not use a backend, handling data persistence was another concern, which was managed by storing trip and expense data locally in the browser to prevent data loss during refreshes. Finally, implementing the SOS feature required careful consideration to avoid over‑promising emergency support, so the focus was placed on safety awareness and quick access to essential information rather than real‑time intervention. Overall, these challenges helped us learn the importance of solving the right problems with honest limitations and user‑centric design.

![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jupyter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jupyter Notebook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter%20Notebook-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

It is an advanced cybersecurity tool designed to bridge the gap between human error and web safety. While most security tools rely on static "blacklists" that expire quickly, PhishShield uses a Hybrid Detection Engine. It combines Logistic Regression (Machine Learning) to identify malicious patterns with Heuristic Analysis to catch Typosquatting, Homograph attacks, and high-entropy (randomized) domains.

1. The Web Analyzer (Central Intelligence)
This web platform serves as the research hub. Users can manually input any suspicious URL to receive a comprehensive "Safety Score Card."

Deep Scan: Beyond a simple "Safe/Unsafe" result, it provides a breakdown of why a site was flagged (e.g., "95% similarity to Amazon.com" or "High-entropy domain detected").

History & Analytics: Users can track previously scanned links to monitor local threat trends.

2. The Chrome Extension (Proactive Shield)
The real power of our project 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cbde6f0e17594fa6b9f8c02bc2419451/6af12b9e-9f22-448f-a87e-54479c5c0882.png)lies in its browser integration. We developed a lightweight Chrome extension that acts as a Real-Time Firewall.

API Integration: The extension calls our Flask-based API every time a user attempts to navigate to a new site.

Instant Interception: If the API returns a "DANGER" status based on ML prediction or Typosquatting heuristics, the extension injects an overlay that instantly blocks access, preventing the user from entering credentials or downloading malware before the page even loads.

**Challenges we ran into**

I went through an error of typosquatting where the phishing websites are ofgten hosted under the domain as an instance "rnicrosoft: that looks similar  to microsoft so i solved it using 
1. Vector Space Alignment (The "Mismatch" Fix)You resolved the critical error where the model expected 460,927 features but only received a handful.Logical Implementation: Instead of creating a new feature set for every request, you integrated a pre-trained TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) Vectorizer.Technical Result: This maps the raw string of the URL into a high-dimensional sparse matrix. Every character sequence (n-gram) in the user's input is projected onto the exact same 460,927-dimensional coordinate system used during the model's training phase, ensuring mathematical compatibility.2. Hybrid Inference ArchitectureYou moved away from a "single-point-of-failure" model. Your system now uses a Weighted Logic Gate:The ML Path: Uses a Logistic Regression classifier to perform probabilistic analysis. It looks for "malicious DNA"—specific patterns in the path, queries, and character distribution that suggest a site is used for phishing.The Heuristic Path: Runs parallel algorithms for Deterministic Threats. If a URL is mathematically similar to a known brand (via Levenshtein Distance) or contains non-ASCII characters (Homographs), the system overrides or augments the ML result.3. Algorithmic Typosquatting DetectionInstead of a simple database lookup, you implemented Fuzzy String Logic:Levenshtein Distance ($L$): You implemented a function where $L$ is the minimum number of edits (insertions, deletions, substitutions) to transform the input $S_1$ to a brand $S_2$.Thresholding: You set an $L \leq 2$ limit. This mathematically identifies "Visual Spoofing" without requiring the specific fake domain to be previously known or blacklisted.

**The problem it solves**

An intelligent multi-agent AI system that acts as your virtual DevOps engineer. Monitor GitHub Pull Requests, perform deep security audits, execute code in sandboxes, and auto-generate documentation — all while maintaining full observability through Weights & Biases Weave. Sit back, relax ☕, and let AI handle your DevOps workflows!

🌟 Features
🔍 Automated PR Audits – AI-powered analysis of every pull request with detailed insights
🛡️ Security Scanning – Detect hardcoded secrets, SQL injections, and vulnerable dependencies
⚡ Runtime Validation – Execute code in secure sandboxes to verify logic and catch bugs
📝 Auto Documentation – Generate comprehensive docs from code changes automatically
📊 Real-Time Observability – Full tracing and monitoring via W&B Weave integration
🏥 Repository Health Scores – Track code quality and security trends over time

**Challenges we ran into**

Inter-Service Communication (Deployment)
The Challenge: The system is a distributed microservice architecture (Python Agent Engine + Node.js Backend + Next.js Frontend). We faced a critical issue where the Node.js backend deployed on Render failed to communicate with the Python service, returning connection errors.

The Solution: We diagnosed that the services were healthy but the routing configuration was incorrect. The backend was posting to the root URL (/) instead of the specific API endpoint.

Fix: We corrected the environment configuration to explicitly point to the specific /analyze endpoint.
Result: Seamless 2-way communication between the GitHub webhook listener and the AI engine.
2. "Hallucinated" Validation vs. Real Execution
The Challenge: The initial Runtime Validator agent could only simulate testing—effectively "guessing" if code would pass based on the diff. This is insufficient for a professional DevOps tool that needs to guarantee code correctness.

The Solution: We designed a Sandboxed Execution Architecture.

Strategy: Instead of relying solely on the LLM's prediction, we architected a plan to use secure sandboxed environments (like E2B).
Workflow: The agent now (conceptually) generates a test script $\to$ spins up an isolated sandbox $\to$ installs dependencies $\to$ and actually runs the code to capture real execution logs.
3. Consistent "Cyber-Professional" Aesthetics
The Challenge: The project uses a highly specific, premium design language (Dark Mode, neon green #69E300 accents, glassmorphism). Adding new pages (like the Ghostwriter component) without breaking this consistency is difficult.

The Solution: We implemented a strict Design System reuse strategy.

Implementation: We analyzed 
globals.css
 and existing components to extract the exact color tokens and Tailwind utility classes.
Result: The new pages feel like a native part of the original premium template, not a tacked-on addition.
4. Orchestrating Multi-Agent Workflows
The Challenge: A single LLM call is too overwhelming for complex PR audits (Security check + Runtime check + Final Report).

The Solution: We utilized a Chained Agent Pattern (Orchestrator Pattern).

Architecture: We separated concerns into specialized agents:
Security Auditor: Dedicated solely to vulnerability scanning (SQLi, Secrets).
Runtime Validator: Dedicated to logic and testing.
Orchestrator: A master agent that decomposes the PR, assigns tasks to the sub-agents, and synthesizes their outputs into a single, coherent verification report.
Result: This improved accuracy significantly compared to a "one-shot" approach, as each agent can focus on a specific domain (Security vs. Logic).

### RESCUE-AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/rescueai-28c5) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ai-help-now.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20Technique%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-technique2026.devfolio.co)

> ResQ AI: Rescue Smarter. Save Faster

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ResQ AI (Rescue-Nexus) transforms chaotic disaster data into structured action through an automated Report-Analyze-Dispatch cycle. The platform eliminates information overload by using Natural Language Processing (NLP) to filter noise, categorize threats, and prioritize life-critical incidents with Urgency Levels. To slash response delays, it features Zero-Friction Reporting for victims and an Intelligent Matching algorithm that dispatches volunteers based on their verified skills and proximity. Furthermore, it simplifies complex navigation by merging fragmented data into a high-contrast dashboard with Dynamic Routing and a Live Map View, ensuring responders can move safely and coordinate without duplication of effort.

**Challenges we ran into**

There were bugs, breakdowns, stress, and moments where giving up felt tempting. But every time I thought of someone waiting for help, I kept going.

Because innovation isn’t about perfection.
It’s about purpose.

ResQ is my attempt to turn empathy into action, and code into impact.

Team **Segmentation Fault Squad** -- [Nandini Mahto](https://github.com/nandinimahto65), [Subhajit Roy](https://github.com/bitwise-shadowfx), Sohamjit RoyChowdhury
