![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem WebWarden Solves

In many hostels, the outpass approval process is still handled **manually**. Students are required to physically visit the hostel warden, fill out paper forms, and wait for approval. This traditional method leads to several issues such as time consumption, miscommunication, lack of transparency, and poor record management.

WebWarden addresses these challenges by **digitizing the entire hostel outpass system**, making it more efficient, secure, and reliable for both students and wardens.

---

## How WebWarden Makes Things Easier and Safer

### 👩‍🎓 For Students
- Submit outpass requests **online anytime, anywhere**
- No need to stand in queues or repeatedly visit the warden
- Receive **email notifications** when requests are approved or rejected
- Reduced stress and faster approvals

### 🧑‍✈️ For Hostel Wardens
- View all student requests in **one centralized dashboard**
- Approve or reject outpasses with a single click
- Maintain **clear digital records** for future reference
- Avoid paperwork, errors, and misplaced forms

### 🏢 For Hostel Administration
- Ensures **better security and monitoring** of student movement
- Provides a **transparent and traceable approval system**
- Enables easy audits and reporting
- Reduces manual effort and administrative overhead

---

## Key Benefits

- ✅ Eliminates paper-based processes  
- 🔒 Improves security and accountability  
- ⏱️ Saves time for students and staff  
- 📧 Reliable communication through email alerts  
- 📊 Centralized and organized data management  

---

## Use Cases

- Students requesting permission to leave the hostel
- Wardens managing and tracking outpass approvals
- Administrators monitoring hostel activity and compliance

---

**WebWarden transforms a slow, manual process into a fast, secure, and user-friendly digital experience.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Bug / Hurdle Faced During Development

One major hurdle we faced while building **WebWarden** was handling the **outpass approval visibility and notification flow** correctly.

Initially, when a warden approved or rejected an outpass request, the status was visible to both the **warden and the student in real time**. This created confusion and also went against the requirement that **only the warden should see the approval status**, while students should be informed only through email.

### How We Solved It

- We modified the backend logic to **restrict status visibility** on the student dashboard.
- Implemented **role-based access control**, ensuring only wardens can view and change request statuses.
- Integrated an **email notification system** that sends approval or rejection messages to students without exposing the internal status directly.
- Thoroughly tested different user roles to confirm proper access and data flow.

This fix improved **security, clarity, and user experience**, making the system behave exactly as intended.

> EduSathi — Offline AI Learning App

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Navigation](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Navigation-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem EduSathi Solves**

**Millions of students in rural and remote areas face serious barriers to learning because of poor or unreliable internet connectivity. Most modern AI-powered education platforms depend heavily on cloud servers and constant network access. When the internet is slow, unavailable, or expensive, these tools become unusable.**

As a result:

Students cannot access AI explanations or personalized learning support

Teachers and NGOs cannot rely on online platforms in low-connectivity regions

Learning completely stops whenever the internet goes down

Existing solutions are not optimized for low-end devices or offline usage

EduSathi solves this by providing an offline-first AI learning system that works without continuous internet access. By running AI models directly on the device and using offline learning packs, EduSathi ensures that learning can continue anytime, anywhere — even with zero connectivity.

**What People Can Use EduSathi For**

EduSathi is a hybrid mobile app (Android & iOS) designed for students, teachers, and community educators in low-connectivity environments. It makes learning more accessible, reliable, and inclusive.

**1. Learn and Study Completely Offline**

- Students can learn subjects like Math, Science, and Languages without internet

- AI teaches specific topics step by step, like a personal tutor

- Works even if the user stays offline for weeks

**2. Ask AI Questions Without Internet**

- Users can ask questions such as:

1. “Explain photosynthesis”

2. “Teach me fractions”

3. “How do I solve this equation?”

- The AI searches offline content packs and provides clear explanations

- No cloud APIs or network dependency

**3. Topic-Based AI Teaching**

- Users can select a topic and the AI will:

1. Explain concepts
2. Show examples
3. Provide practice questions
4. Give summaries

- This turns AI from a chatbot into an offline teacher

**4. Practice and Self-Assess**

Adaptive quizzes work fully offline

Difficulty adjusts based on performance

Progress is saved locally on the device

**5. Voice-Based Learning**

- Supports offline speech-to-text and text-to-speech

- Helpful for learners with low literacy

- Students can speak questions and hear explanations

**6. Low Data Usage & Safe Learning**

- Content packs are small and reusable

- No constant data consumption

- Student data stays on the device, improving privacy and safety

**7. Built for Real-World Constraints**

- Runs smoothly on low-end smartphones

- Designed for rural schools, NGOs, and community learning centers

- Hybrid app ensures a single codebase works on both Android and iOS

**Why EduSathi Matters**

EduSathi does not just make learning easier — it makes it possible in places where digital education usually fails. By combining offline AI, hybrid mobile technology, and structured educational content, EduSathi bridges the learning gap created by poor connectivity and brings AI education to underserved communities.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**
**1. Designing an Offline-First UX Without Backend Support**

One of the biggest challenges was designing the user experience for an offline-first app while having no backend or AI services implemented yet. Most learning apps assume constant connectivity, but EduSathi had to clearly communicate to users that learning content and AI responses would work offline in the future.

How I handled it:
I focused on building a clear and intuitive frontend flow:

- Created dedicated screens for offline learning packs
- Designed UI states for offline availability
- Structured the app so AI and backend logic can be plugged in later without breaking the UI

**2. Structuring the App for Future AI Integration**

Since this project was built in a short time frame, implementing full AI pipelines (LangChain, RAG, embeddings, vector databases) was not possible during the hackathon. However, the frontend still needed to be future-ready.

How I handled it:

- Designed modular components for AI chat, topic teaching, and quizzes
- Used placeholder services and mock data
- Ensured screens and state management are compatible with future AI responses (streaming, multi-step explanations)

This makes it easy to integrate LangChain, RAG, and offline/online AI systems in future development.

**3. Cross-Platform Consistency (Hybrid App)**

Building a hybrid app for both Android and iOS introduced challenges in maintaining consistent UI behavior, layouts, and navigation across platforms within limited time.

How I handled it:

- Used platform-agnostic UI components
- Followed responsive design principles
- Tested layouts to ensure smooth experience on different screen sizes

**4. Time Constraints During the Hackathon**

Due to limited hackathon time, it was not possible to complete:

- Backend infrastructure
- AI model integration
- Offline AI inference pipeline

How I handled it:
I prioritized:

- Completing a functional, polished frontend
- Clearly demonstrating the vision and architecture
- Building a scalable foundation for future development

**5. Planning Offline AI Without Over-Promising**

A key challenge was ensuring the project vision was ambitious but realistic. Offline AI systems require careful optimization, and over-promising could reduce credibility.

How I handled it:

- Clearly scoped the current submission as frontend-focused
- Documented future plans separately
- Explained how AI (LangChain, RAG, vector search) will be integrated in later phases

**Future Improvements**

In future iterations, EduSathi will be expanded with:

- Backend services for sync and content updates
- AI integration using LangChain, RAG, embeddings, and vector databases
- Offline-first AI inference pipelines
- Teacher dashboards and analytics

**Summary**

**Despite limited time, the main challenge was balancing scope, realism, and vision. By focusing on a strong frontend and designing with future AI integration in mind, EduSathi now has a solid foundation that can be expanded into a full offline AI learning platform.**

> Predictive care that helps you stay healthy

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem **Heallense** Solves

It is often difficult for individuals to obtain trustworthy health-related information. Many may resort to searching on the internet or social media platforms, and even general **AI** solutions that may give **incomplete**, **misleading**, and **dangerous** health suggestions.

Current solutions commonly have complex architectures, subscription-based pricing models, or solutions targeting only one aspect of users' health while disregarding concerns about users' **privacy** and **security**.

**Heallense** remedies these issues by developing a browser-supporting AI wellness buddy to educate patients on health conditions, symptoms, and common medicines through credible health resources. **Heallense** explains information given in a simplified manner without providing diagnosis or prescriptions.

Moreover, the **Heallense** feature assists customers in taking care of healthy habits such as intelligent reminders to drink water and breathe, as well as wellness checks using the breathing feature even when the customers forget to set reminders.

Through integrating responsible AI, **privacy**-first design, and user experience, **Heallense** ensures that health knowledge and information are made easier, safer, and more accessible without diminishing or replacing medical professionals.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing a health-focused AI system that is useful without being unsafe. Unlike general chatbots, Heallense needed strict boundaries to avoid diagnosis, prescriptions, or misleading medical advice. Defining what the AI should not do was as important as defining what it can do.

Another challenge was structuring reliable medical knowledge. Instead of relying on live AI responses, I had to curate and organize disease and medicine data from trusted sources and design logic to retrieve relevant information accurately.

Integrating authentication, Firestore rules, and user-specific data while maintaining privacy and security was also challenging, especially under time constraints.

Performance and stability were additional concerns, as the project had to run smoothly in the browser without backend-heavy infrastructure.

Finally, managing time and feature scope during the hackathon was difficult. I had to consciously stop adding features and focus on polishing core functionality to ensure a stable and demo-ready product

### AI Career Path Recommender
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-career-path-recommender-5d66) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Joshigasankar/AI-Career-Path-Recommender) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackFiesta-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackfiesta.devfolio.co)

> Turning Potential into Career Paths

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural Language Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20Language%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The career path recommender system using artificial intelligence resolves the widespread and very important issue most students and young professionals face—career confusion due to the lack of personalized directions and industry needs awareness. Most people tend to seek common directions or follow the path suggested by friends or unavailable information sources. Consequently, most end up choosing the wrong career paths or possessing inappropriate skills for the tasks assigned to them. The project will offer a vital direction to students or young professionals by analyzing the individual’s skills, interests, academic records, and objectives to offer necessary directions for the most suitable career paths according to industry needs. This will allow individuals to assess their current status, identify the most suitable career path for them, or identify the areas requiring additional skills. The project will ensure simplified decision-making through the application of artificial intelligence to avoid the possibility of selecting the wrong career paths or wasting money on unnecessary courses.

**Challenges we ran into**

A challenge in the developmental stage was forming the basis for the career suggestions given the constraints of little data. The fact that the input for the career guidance exercise has components such as skills, interests, and educational background meant that linking the inputs to the careers requires extensive data that was not the case in the developmental stage. This problem was addressed in the model by developing the skill-to-role mapping as per the job roles in normalized input data.
Another challenge involved managing model complexity within the context of the hackathon timeline. These sophisticated models entail rigorous training and optimization. To incorporate these into the hackathon timeline of just 24 hours was a challenge. Here, the approach involved the use of a simplified machine learning method cued with logic.
In my own work, I also experienced issues while presenting the results of AI in an understandable manner. The original prediction results were difficult for the user to comprehend. I added an interface that could present recommendations and also details such as skill and confidence levels.

> Smart PCOS Care, Locally Adapted

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

OvaWell Clinical Suite

AI-Powered PCOS Diagnosis & Nutrition Management for Healthcare Professionals

Bridging the gap between PCOS diagnosis and treatment through geographic nutrition intelligence

Built with Streamlit | Powered by Gemini AI | Python 3.9+

---

Problem Statement

The PCOS Care Gap Crisis

Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) affects:
- 200+ million women globally
- 116 million women in India (1 in 5 women of reproductive age)
- 10 million women in the USA (1 in 10 women)

Yet 90% of diagnosed patients receive NO actionable nutrition plan.

Current Healthcare Reality:
- Diagnosis takes 2+ years on average
- Patients get vague advice: "eat healthy, lose weight"
- No tools bridge diagnosis to personalized management
- Generic Western meal plans ignore local food cultures
- Expensive imported "superfoods" financially unviable
- Patients abandon treatment due to lack of guidance

OvaWell's Solution:

Healthcare providers get a complete care platform:
1. AI-powered PCOS assessment using Rotterdam Criteria + ultrasound analysis
2. Geographically-adapted meal plans using local ingredients (Pune is not equal to London)
3. Smart shopping lists with local stores and cost estimates
4. Leftover recipe generator to improve compliance and reduce waste
5. Patient tracking dashboard for outcome monitoring

---

Key Features

1. Clinical PCOS Assessment
- Rotterdam Criteria (international gold standard since 2003)
- Symptom analysis: menstrual irregularity, hyperandrogenism, clinical signs
- Ultrasound analysis: OpenCV-based follicle detection (upgradeable to CNN)
- Gemini AI intelligent risk scoring and recommendation generation
- Phenotype classification: A (severe), B (classic), C (ovulatory), D (mild)
- Evidence-based recommendations for each patient profile

2. Geographic Nutrition Intelligence - Our Innovation

The Problem: A PCOS patient in Pune can't buy quinoa. A patient in London doesn't know what jowar is.

Our Solution: Same medical science, locally adapted execution.

- 7 cities configured (Pune, Chennai, Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, London, New York)
- Spoonacular API fetches 5000+ PCOS-safe recipes (low-GI, high-protein, high-fiber)
- Gemini AI adapts recipes to local ingredients:
  - Pune patient: Jowar, bajra, leafy greens from Mandai Market
  - London patient: Oats, quinoa, kale from Tesco
- Budget-aware planning (Low/Medium/High) with cost estimates
- Professional PDF exports for patient handouts
- Smart shopping lists categorized by local store sections

Why this matters: 60% compliance with culturally adapted plans vs. 10% with generic advice.

3. Smart Leftover Recipe Generator
- Input available ingredients from patient's kitchen
- PCOS-friendly recipe suggestions filtered by nutrition criteria
- PCOS score (0-100) for each recipe
- Reduces food waste, improves compliance, better outcomes

4. Patient Tracking Dashboard
- Multi-patient management in one interface
- Quick statistics: Total patients, PCOS diagnosed, high-risk cases
- Export capabilities: Save patient data for EHR integration
- Professional PDF reports with clinic branding

---

Tech Stack

Component | Technology | Purpose
Frontend | Streamlit | Rapid healthcare UI development
LLM | Google Gemini API | Symptom analysis, recipe adaptation
Recipe Data | Spoonacular API | PCOS-filtered recipe database
Image Analysis | OpenCV / TensorFlow | Ultrasound cyst detection
Visualization | Plotly | Patient progress charts
PDF Export | ReportLab | Professional meal plan reports
Config | YAML/JSON | Minimal city metadata only

### Decentralised Registry System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/decentralised-registry-system-6062) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ashaygupta-cc/TitleVault) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackFiesta-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackfiesta.devfolio.co)

> Immutable ownership. Verifiable truth.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Land records, affidavits, and legal documents today rely heavily on fragmented databases, manual verification, and institutional trust. This makes them vulnerable to data tampering, record duplication, ownership disputes, and delayed verification — especially in high-stake legal and court environments.

The Decentralised Registry System solves this by creating a tamper-proof, verifiable registry where every record is cryptographically hashed, canonically structured, and anchored on blockchain. Any attempt to modify a document or ownership history is immediately detectable.

People can use this system to:

Verify ownership and authenticity of land records

Validate affidavits and legal documents without relying on intermediaries

Detect tampering or post-registration modification

Establish court-grade proof of integrity using blockchain anchoring

By combining canonical data models, IPFS storage, and on-chain verification, the system makes registry operations transparent, auditable, and trustless.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was enforcing strict, court-grade verification rules instead of allowing approximate or forgiving validation. Even extremely small coordinate mismatches, reordered JSON fields, or re-uploaded IPFS content would break blockchain verification — which initially appeared as false negatives.

Another major challenge was handling post-anchor data mutations. Traditional systems allow silent edits, but blockchain does not. This required redesigning the flow to treat every change as a new immutable record rather than an update.

On the frontend side, ensuring that verification remained centralized in a single Docs / Verify panel — without duplicating logic across features like Court Bundles — required careful architectural discipline.

These challenges were overcome by:

Enforcing canonical JSON generation before hashing

Making blockchain anchoring the single source of truth

Using strict geometric validation for land subdivision

Designing a unified verification pipeline for all file types (JSON, TXT, PDF)

The result is a system that behaves correctly even under adversarial or real-world legal conditions.

**Ethereum Track**

The Decentralised Registry System is fundamentally aligned with the ETHIndia track because it leverages Ethereum-compatible blockchain infrastructure to solve real-world problems around trust, ownership, and verification.

At its core, the project uses:

EVM-compatible smart contracts to anchor registry records immutably on-chain

Keccak-256 hashing to ensure cryptographic integrity

Decentralized verification instead of centralized authority-based trust

Ethereum’s properties of immutability, transparency, and verifiability make it uniquely suited for high-stakes domains such as land records, affidavits, and legal documents. This project demonstrates how Ethereum can move beyond DeFi and NFTs to power court-grade, governance, and public infrastructure systems.

By combining Ethereum anchoring with IPFS-based document storage and off-chain canonical data models, the system ensures that:

Any document tampering is immediately detectable

Ownership and history can be independently verified by anyone

Trust is derived from cryptography and consensus, not institutions

This aligns strongly with ETHIndia’s vision of using Ethereum to build impactful, decentralized applications that address real societal and governance challenges at scale.

**AI TRACK**

The Decentralised Registry System strongly aligns with the CodeCrafters track through its emphasis on correctness, precision, and robust system design in a high-stakes domain.

The project goes beyond building a functional prototype and instead focuses on engineering-grade guarantees, where small implementation details directly affect legal validity. This required careful attention to canonical data modeling, deterministic hashing, and strict validation logic across the entire system.

Key aspects that reflect CodeCrafters principles:

Canonical JSON generation to ensure deterministic hashing and prevent subtle data drift

Strict geometric validation for land parcels, rejecting approximate or overlapping subdivisions

Immutable record lifecycle design, where post-anchor changes create new records instead of mutating existing ones

**Open Innovation**

The Decentralised Registry System fits the Lovable track by prioritizing clarity, usability, and trust in a domain that is traditionally complex, opaque, and intimidating to users.

Legal registries, land records, and affidavit verification systems are usually difficult to understand and inaccessible to non-technical users. This project focuses on making court-grade verification understandable at a glance, without requiring users to understand blockchain or cryptography.

Key aspects that align with the Lovable track:

A single Docs / Verify panel that acts as the user’s central point for verifying all documents

Clear, step-by-step verification feedback instead of technical error messages

Visual previews of affidavits and records alongside their verification status

Consistent verification flow for JSON, TXT, and PDF documents

Immediate, human-readable indicators for authenticity, tampering, and trust

Rather than exposing raw blockchain complexity, the system abstracts it into a simple, confidence-driven experience where users can intuitively understand whether a document is authentic, modified, or unverifiable.

By focusing on user trust, transparency, and ease of verification, the project makes decentralized infrastructure approachable and genuinely useful — which is at the core of what the Lovable track represents.

**The problem it solves**

### Problem:
---

Despite growing environmental awareness, **most consumers still struggle to make sustainable choices** during everyday shopping.
&nbsp; 
Why?

* Sustainability labels are **confusing, inconsistent, or misleading (greenwashing)**
* Environmental impact data is **too complex and time-consuming** to evaluate
* Shoppers typically spend **less than 5 seconds** deciding on a product
* Even motivated users don’t know:

  * *Is this product recyclable where I live?*
  * *Is there a better alternative available nearby?*
  * *What real difference does my choice make?*

As a result, **good intentions rarely turn into real climate action**.

&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; 

### Solution:
---

**EcoSage is an AI-powered sustainability companion** that transforms everyday purchases into **informed, climate-positive decisions** instantly.

People can use EcoSage to:

* **Scan any product** and instantly get a clear sustainability score
* Understand *why* a product is eco-friendly or harmful (packaging, production, ethics, lifecycle)
* Discover **better, greener alternatives** available in real stores
* See **real-time carbon savings** translated into tangible comparisons (trees planted, cars removed)
* Find **nearby recycling centers** based on location and waste type
* Track their **personal sustainability journey** over time

**EcoSage removes friction from sustainable living** by making the *right choice the easy choice* in seconds, not hours.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1️⃣ AI Accuracy & Context Awareness
---

**Challenge:**
Early AI scans focused too much on surface-level features (like recycling symbols) and missed deeper sustainability factors such as company ethics, lifecycle impact, and supply-chain transparency.

**How we solved it:**
We implemented a **multi-layered AI analysis pipeline** that combines:

* Image-based material recognition
* Brand sustainability research
* Packaging & lifecycle heuristics
* Context-aware scoring logic

This resulted in **more reliable and explainable sustainability scores** instead of black-box ratings.

&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; 

### 2️⃣ Real-Time Map Performance
---

**Challenge:**
Rendering hundreds of recycling centers caused noticeable lag, especially on lower-end devices.

**How we solved it:**
We optimized performance using:

* Radius-based filtering
* Distance calculations
* Memoized rendering of visible markers only

This reduced unnecessary renders and ensured **smooth map interactions** even with large datasets.

&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; 

### 3️⃣ Cross-Platform Camera Integration
---

**Challenge:**
Ensuring consistent image capture quality across **web, Android, and iOS** was difficult due to different camera APIs and formats.

**How we solved it:**
We created a **unified media processing pipeline** that:

* Normalizes image formats
* Optimizes resolution for AI analysis
* Preserves detail while reducing latency

This ensured reliable scans across platforms.

&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; 

### 4️⃣ Sustainability Data Standardization
---

**Challenge:**
Different product categories use **different sustainability metrics**, making fair comparison difficult.

**How we solved it:**
We designed a **normalized scoring framework** that converts diverse environmental factors into a **clear 10-point sustainability score**, enabling:

* Cross-category comparison
* Easy understanding for non-experts
* Transparent breakdowns for advanced users

- Designed as an open-source, extensible platform, allowing developers and communities to build upon and adapt it for local needs

### MADR (Mobile Accessible Document Reader)
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/madr-mobile-accessible-document-reader-75ba) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Nishanth1812/MADR) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackFiesta-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackfiesta.devfolio.co)

> Instant document access through AI vision

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem MADR Solves
Approximately 2.2 billion people worldwide experience vision impairment, facing daily barriers when encountering physical documents—from medication labels that could prevent life-threatening errors to restaurant menus, bills, contracts, and emergency notices. Current solutions fall critically short: dedicated OCR devices cost $2,000+, mobile apps require constant connectivity, and human assistance introduces delays while compromising privacy for sensitive medical, financial, and personal documents. MADR addresses this accessibility gap through a privacy-first, offline-capable progressive web app that delivers sub-second document processing (<1000ms capture-to-audio), achieving 85%+ first-attempt success rates with real-time guidance and confidence scoring. By combining state-of-the-art computer vision (PaddleOCR with 40ms inference), on-device processing that ensures sensitive documents never leave the user's control, and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance that makes every interaction keyboard-navigable and screen-reader optimized, MADR eliminates the "dependence tax" that forces blind and low-vision users to wait for assistance, pay premium prices, or compromise privacy. The result is a free, open-source solution that works instantly via browser on any device, enabling spontaneous access to healthcare information, financial independence, workplace productivity, and social participation—transforming what was once a planned activity requiring assistance into an immediate, private, and reliable capability that restores agency and dignity in everyday life.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-Time Document Detection Killed Performance
Initial implementation was running edge detection on every camera frame at 30 FPS, which tanked performance to 8-12 FPS on mid-range phones. Fixed by throttling contour detection to every 3rd frame using requestAnimationFrame and adding a motion detection pre-filter that skips processing when the camera is stationary. Cut CPU usage by 60% while keeping the guidance responsive.
ONNX Memory Leaks Crashed the App
The 50MB PaddleOCR model was leaking memory on every inference call—app would crash after 20-30 captures on iOS Safari. ONNX Runtime Web wasn't releasing tensors properly. Fixed by implementing explicit tensor disposal, creating a singleton session manager instead of recreating sessions, and adding a memory pressure monitor. Memory footprint dropped 75%, crashes eliminated.

**AI TRACK**

How MADR Fits the AI Track
Core AI Components
PaddleOCR (ONNX): 50MB convolutional neural network running client-side with 40-100ms inference. Required optimizing tensor operations, WebGL acceleration, and memory management for in-browser deep learning.

### Kiro-CI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kiroci-165a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mannshah24/Kiro-CI.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/rCiApHhYeLk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackxios%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackxios2k25.devfolio.co)

> Trustless CI: AI fixes, Chain verifies.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves
The Problem: "Blind Trust" in DevOps Modern CI/CD pipelines (like GitHub Actions or CircleCI) are centralized "black boxes." Developers blindly trust that the code they wrote is the code being deployed.

Supply Chain Attacks: If a CI server is compromised, hackers can inject malicious backdoors into trusted apps (similar to the infamous SolarWinds or xz-utils attacks).

Slow Feedback Loops: Developers waste hours waiting for cloud pipelines to queue and run, only to fail on a simple error.

The "Web3 Verification Gap": In crypto, "Code is Law," but we currently have no on-chain proof that a deployed smart contract actually passed its security tests.

The Solution: Kiro-CI (The Trustless Pipeline) Kiro-CI moves the entire DevOps pipeline "Left"—running it locally and securely inside the Kiro IDE before the code ever leaves your machine.

Eliminates Centralized Risk (Local-First): By using Kiro Native Hooks, we run tests and security audits locally. No external CI server has access to your private keys or uncompiled code.

Agentic "Self-Healing" Workflows: Most tools just report errors. Kiro-CI fixes them. Our AI Agent detects vulnerabilities (like Reentrancy), autonomously rewrites the code to patch them, and re-runs the tests to ensure safety without human intervention.

Cryptographic Enforcement (EAS on Base): We replace "trust me, I tested it" with on-chain proof. Kiro-CI mints an Ethereum Attestation (EAS) linked to the specific Git Commit Hash. Our custom "Gatekeeper" smart contract prevents deployment unless this validity proof exists on-chain.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Fragile Regex" Problem (Agentic Repair) Building the "Self-Healing" agent was the hardest part. Initially, our regex patterns for detecting and fixing Solidity vulnerabilities (like Reentrancy) were too brittle. If a developer formatted their code with different spacing or comments, the Agent would break the file while trying to inject the nonReentrant modifier.

How we solved it: We moved from simple string replacement to a more robust AST-like parsing strategy. We created a rigorous test suite of "badly formatted" contracts to ensure the Agent could identify the correct injection point 100% of the time without corrupting the syntax.

2. Verifying Attestations On-Chain (Foundry + EAS) Integrating the Ethereum Attestation Service (EAS) into a Foundry deployment script was tricky. We needed the deployment transaction to revert if an attestation didn't exist, but checking dynamic bytes and schema UIDs inside a Solidity constructor is complex and prone to gas errors.

How we solved it: We built a custom "Gatekeeper" contract that acts as a proxy. It uses a specialized Resolver to pre-validate the schema structure before allowing the final CREATE2 deployment call. This ensured that our "Code is Law" promise was mathematically enforced on Base Sepolia.

3. Async Race Conditions (Local vs. Cloud) We faced a race condition where the CLI would try to upload the build artifact to AWS S3 before the file zipping process had fully closed the stream, resulting in corrupted 0-byte uploads.

How we solved it: We refactored the CLI's control flow to use strict await promises. We implemented a "lockfile" system that prevents the S3 upload from initializing until the local archiver library emits a distinct finalize event, ensuring data integrity.

**Ethereum Track**

On-Chain Supply Chain Security with EAS & Base We are building critical infrastructure for the Ethereum ecosystem. Kiro-CI ensures that "Code is Law" starts before deployment.

EAS Integration: We use the Ethereum Attestation Service on Base Sepolia to mint immutable proofs of code integrity linked to Git Commit Hashes.

The Gatekeeper Protocol: We built a custom smart contract that acts as a deployment proxy. It queries the EAS Registry on-chain and reverts any deployment transaction that lacks a valid audit attestation from our Kiro Agent.

Public Good: By enforcing verification at the contract level, we prevent developers from accidentally deploying vulnerable code, raising the security standard for all dApps on Ethereum.

**Best Innovation**

Redefining CI/CD as an Agentic Security Protocol Most DevOps tools are passive notification systems—they just tell you "Something broke." Kiro-CI is innovative because it is active and autonomous.

It Heals Code: We built an AI Agent that doesn't just lint code; it rewrites it to fix security flaws automatically.

It Enforces Trust: We innovated on the "Checkmark" concept. Instead of a green UI badge on GitHub (which can be faked), we created a Cryptographic Attestation on-chain.

Local-First Architecture: We completely removed the need for a centralized CI server, proving that complex pipelines can run entirely within the Kiro IDE environment, drastically reducing the attack surface for supply chain hacks.

**AWS**

Most Creative Use of Kiro Platform

Turning the IDE into an Autonomous DevOps Agent We didn't just build a "dApp" using Kiro; we used Kiro's internal architecture to build a platform extension that fundamentally changes how developers work.

Native Hooks Implementation: We creatively used Kiro Hooks (.kiro/hooks/) to intercept the native Git Commit workflow. Instead of a standard commit, Kiro now wakes up, runs tests, and even fixes code itself before allowing the action. This turns the IDE from a passive text editor into an active partner.

The HERO Planning Framework: We fully embraced the "Ideation" focus of Kiro by maintaining our entire architectural PRD, vision, and logic flows inside the .kiro/HERO/ directory. This allowed us to keep our planning context switch-free and native to the environment.

Local-First Infrastructure: We proved that you don't need expensive cloud CI servers. By leveraging Kiro's local runtime for the heavy lifting (testing & compiling), we created a "Serverless" pipeline that is faster, cheaper, and more private than GitHub Actions.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem ETH Cash Back Solves

### 1. The Problem It Solves

Web3 adoption faces a critical barrier: **gas fees**. Every blockchain interaction costs money, creating friction that prevents mainstream users from engaging with decentralized applications. Current challenges include:

1. **User Onboarding Friction**: New users must purchase cryptocurrency before they can even try a dApp, creating a significant barrier to entry.

2. **Transaction Cost Anxiety**: Users hesitate to interact with dApps due to unpredictable and often high gas fees, especially during network congestion.

3. **Poor User Experience**: Unlike Web2 applications where usage is "free" to end users, Web3 forces users to pay for every action, making the experience feel expensive and cumbersome.

4. **dApp Growth Limitations**: Projects struggle to attract and retain users when every interaction requires users to spend their own ETH on gas fees.

5. **Lack of Incentive Mechanisms**: Traditional dApps have no built-in way to reward users for their engagement or offset the costs of participation.

### 2. What People Can Use It For

ETH Cash Back provides a **plug-and-play infrastructure layer** that enables:

1. **Cashback Rewards**: Return **2-5% of transaction value** as ETH cashback, transforming transaction costs into a reward experience.

2. **User Acquisition**: Attract new users by offering cashback-enabled transactions, significantly lowering the perceived cost of trying new dApps.

3. **User Retention**: Keep users engaged by rewarding their activity with tangible ETH returns, creating a positive feedback loop.

4. **Configurable Rules**: Set up flexible cashback rules with customizable percentages (1-10%), caps, cumulative user limits, and validity periods without writing custom smart contract logic.

5. **Usage Analytics**: Track user engagement through built-in usage statistics (total cashback received, transaction count, last activity).

### 3. How It Makes Things Easier

**For dApp Developers:**
1. **No Custom Logic Required**: Simply integrate the CashbackManager contract—no need to build complex cashback systems from scratch.
2. **Flexible Configuration**: Adjust cashback rules on-the-fly without redeploying contracts.
3. **Security Built-In**: Leverages OpenZeppelin's battle-tested security patterns (ReentrancyGuard, Pausable).
4. **Gas Optimized**: Highly efficient implementation (~90k gas for transactions) keeps operational costs low.
5. **Emergency Controls**: Pause/unpause functionality for quick response to security issues.

**For End Users:**
1. **Lower Effective Costs**: Receive ETH cashback on transactions, reducing the net cost of using dApps.
2. **Predictable Rewards**: Know exactly how much cashback to expect before making a transaction via *calculateCashback* view function.
3. **Seamless Experience**: Cashback is automatically distributed during transaction processing—no claiming required.
4. **Fair Limits**: Per-user cumulative limits prevent abuse while ensuring fair distribution.

**For the Ecosystem:**
1. **Accelerated Adoption**: Reduces financial barriers that prevent mainstream users from trying Web3.
2. **Sustainable Growth**: Creates a win-win model where users are rewarded for engagement.
3. **Standardized Solution**: Provides a common infrastructure that multiple dApps can leverage.

### 4. TL;DR

**Problem**: Gas fees create massive friction for Web3 adoption—users must pay for every interaction, making dApps expensive and intimidating.

**Solution**: ETH Cash Back is a plug-and-play smart contract infrastructure that lets dApps reward users with **2-5% ETH cashback** per transaction (configurable up to 10%).

**Impact**: Transforms transaction costs from a barrier into a reward, making Web3 more accessible and attractive to mainstream users while giving dApps a powerful tool for user acquisition and retention.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

### 1. For Smart Contract

**Challenge 1: Gas Optimization with Security**
- **Issue**: Balancing comprehensive security measures with gas efficiency. Initial implementations with extensive checks exceeded 150k gas per transaction.
- **Solution**: Implemented custom errors instead of string-based reverts, optimized storage patterns, and enabled Solidity's IR-based optimizer (*viaIR: true*). Achieved ~90k gas average for *processTransaction*.
- **Learning**: Security and efficiency aren't mutually exclusive—careful design and modern Solidity features enable both.

**Challenge 2: Reentrancy Protection in Cashback Distribution**
- **Issue**: The cashback distribution involves external ETH transfers, creating potential reentrancy attack vectors.
- **Solution**: Implemented strict Checks-Effects-Interactions (CEI) pattern combined with OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard. All state updates occur before external calls.
- **Learning**: Defense-in-depth is crucial—multiple security layers provide robust protection even if one fails.

**Challenge 3: Flexible Rule System Design**
- **Issue**: Creating a rule system flexible enough for various use cases (freemium, loyalty, campaigns) while maintaining simplicity and preventing admin errors.
- **Solution**: Designed a comprehensive Rule struct with percentage (basis points), per-transaction cap, cumulative user limit, and validity window. Added extensive validation to prevent misconfiguration.
- **Learning**: Good API design requires anticipating edge cases and providing guardrails without sacrificing flexibility.

**Challenge 4: Testing Edge Cases**
- **Issue**: Ensuring comprehensive test coverage for all possible scenarios including expired rules, exhausted limits, and concurrent transactions.
- **Solution**: Developed **59 test cases** covering normal operations, edge cases, security scenarios, and integration flows. Achieved **98%+ coverage** across all metrics.
- **Learning**: Systematic testing reveals issues that code review alone cannot catch. Time invested in tests pays dividends in confidence and reliability.

**Challenge 5: Deployment and Verification on Sepolia**
- **Issue**: Initial deployment attempts failed due to RPC rate limiting and network congestion. Contract verification required specific compiler settings.
- **Solution**: Configured multiple RPC endpoints with fallback logic, increased timeout settings to 180 seconds, and documented exact compiler configuration for verification.
- **Learning**: Testnet deployment requires patience and robust error handling—production-like infrastructure even in testing environments.

### 2. For Frontend

**Challenge 1: Development Environment Constraints**
- **Issue**: Slow internet connection made it challenging to use Lovable.dev effectively for frontend development.
- **Solution**: Focused on completing and perfecting the smart contract layer first, ensuring a solid foundation for frontend integration.
- **Learning**: Prioritizing core infrastructure before UI development ensures a stable base to build upon.

**Challenge 2: Time Management**
- **Issue**: Balancing comprehensive smart contract development with frontend implementation within hackathon timeline.
- **Solution**: Adopted an MVP-first approach—deliver a fully functional, tested, and deployed smart contract that can be integrated with any frontend.
- **Learning**: A working backend is more valuable than a beautiful frontend with no functionality. Infrastructure-first approach enables multiple frontend options.

### 3. TL;DR

**Smart Contract**: Overcame gas optimization challenges, reentrancy protection complexity, and testnet deployment issues through careful design, comprehensive testing (**59 tests, 98.08% statement coverage, 100% function coverage**), and modern Solidity optimization techniques. Achieved production-ready contract with **~90k gas efficiency**.

**Frontend**: Slow internet limited Lovable.dev usage, so we prioritized delivering a fully functional, tested, and deployed smart contract infrastructure that any frontend can integrate with.

**Key Learning**: Focus on core infrastructure first. A solid, well-tested backend is the foundation for any successful dApp.

**Ethereum Track**

## C. How Does This Project Fit Within the Ethereum Track?

### I. Main Content

ETH Cash Back is fundamentally an **Ethereum-native infrastructure project** that addresses one of the ecosystem's most critical challenges: gas fee friction. Here's how it aligns with the Ethereum track:

**1. Built on Ethereum Standards**
- Developed using **Solidity 0.8.20**, the latest stable version of Ethereum's smart contract language.
- Leverages **OpenZeppelin 5.x** contracts, the gold standard for Ethereum security patterns.
- Follows **Ethereum best practices** including custom errors for gas efficiency.
- Deployed and verified on **Ethereum Sepolia testnet** (Chain ID: 11155111).
- Contract Address: [`0x63b4889Ddf3e7889f39dAe1Cbd467D824b340cea`](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x63b4889Ddf3e7889f39dAe1Cbd467D824b340cea#code)

**2. Solves Ethereum-Specific Problems**
- **Gas Fee Barrier**: Directly addresses Ethereum's transaction cost challenge through cashback incentives.
- **User Onboarding**: Tackles the Ethereum-specific problem of requiring users to hold ETH before interacting with any dApp.
- **Network Effect**: Designed to work across any Ethereum dApp, creating network effects that benefit the entire ecosystem.

**3. Ethereum Security Best Practices**
- **ReentrancyGuard**: Protects against the infamous DAO-style reentrancy attacks that are unique to Ethereum's execution model.
- **Checks-Effects-Interactions Pattern**: Follows Ethereum's recommended security pattern for state changes and external calls.
- **Custom Errors**: Uses Solidity 0.8.4+ custom errors for gas-efficient error handling.
- **Pausable Pattern**: Implements emergency stop mechanism common in Ethereum DeFi protocols.

**4. Gas Optimization for Ethereum**
- **IR-based Optimizer**: Enables Solidity's *viaIR* compilation for maximum gas efficiency on EVM.
- **Storage Optimization**: Carefully designed storage layout to minimize SLOAD/SSTORE costs.
- **Custom Errors**: Saves ~50 gas per error compared to string reverts.
- **Measured Results**: Achieved **~90k gas** for main user interaction, **~160k** for admin operations—highly competitive for Ethereum.

**5. Ethereum Ecosystem Integration**
- **Hardhat Development**: Uses Hardhat 2.x, the leading Ethereum development framework.
- **Etherscan Verification**: Contract verified on Etherscan for transparency and trust.
- **Standard Interfaces**: Designed for easy integration with existing Ethereum tools (wagmi, viem, ethers.js).
- **Testnet First**: Follows Ethereum best practice of thorough testnet deployment before mainnet.

**6. Contributes to Ethereum's Vision**
- **Accessibility**: Aligns with Ethereum's goal of being accessible to everyone by reducing financial barriers.
- **Decentralization**: Maintains decentralization while improving UX—no centralized intermediaries required.
- **Composability**: Designed as infrastructure that other Ethereum dApps can build upon.
- **Sustainability**: Creates sustainable incentive mechanisms for user engagement without compromising security.

**7. Technical Excellence on Ethereum**
- **98.08% Statement Coverage**: Comprehensive testing using Hardhat's Ethereum testing framework.
- **59 Test Cases**: Covers all scenarios including edge cases specific to Ethereum's execution model.
- **Gas Reporting**: Detailed gas analysis to ensure efficiency on Ethereum's fee market.
- **Production Ready**: Deployed, verified, and ready for mainnet with proper security auditing.

### II. TL;DR

ETH Cash Back is a **pure Ethereum infrastructure project** that:
1. **Solves Ethereum's gas fee problem** using Ethereum-native smart contracts
2. **Follows Ethereum best practices** (OpenZeppelin, CEI pattern, ReentrancyGuard)
3. **Optimized for Ethereum** (~90k gas, IR-based compilation, storage optimization)
4. **Deployed on Ethereum** (Sepolia testnet, verified on Etherscan)
5. **Contributes to Ethereum's vision** of accessible, decentralized applications

It's not just built *on* Ethereum—it's built *for* Ethereum, addressing ecosystem-specific challenges with Ethereum-native solutions.

**Best Innovation**

## How Does This Project Fit Within the Best Innovation Track?

### I. Main Content

ETH Cash Back represents a **paradigm shift** in how we think about blockchain transaction costs. Here's why it qualifies as best innovation:

**1. Novel Approach to Transaction Costs**

Traditional thinking: *"Gas fees are a necessary cost of using blockchain."*

Our innovation: *"Transaction costs can be transformed into user rewards."*

- **First-of-its-kind**: A plug-and-play infrastructure that turns transaction costs into an incentive mechanism.
- **Psychological Shift**: Changes user perception from "I'm paying to use this" to "I'm earning while using this."
- **Market Creation**: Opens up new possibilities for dApp business models and user acquisition strategies.

**2. Technical Innovation**

**Smart Contract Architecture:**
- **Flexible Rule Engine**: Dynamic cashback rules without redeployment—unprecedented flexibility for a gas-efficient contract.
- **Deterministic Rule IDs**: Uses *keccak256* hash of rule parameters for unique, collision-resistant identifiers.
- **Usage Tracking**: Built-in analytics that most cashback systems require off-chain infrastructure for.

**Gas Optimization Breakthroughs:**
- Achieved **~90,273 gas** for complex operations involving:

Sonar Kolkata: Bridging Heritage and Technology
Sonar Kolkata is a sophisticated heritage discovery platform designed to transform the way residents and tourists interact with the rich cultural landscape of Kolkata. Developed during an intensive hackathon using the Kiro IDE, the project serves as a digital bridge between the city’s historic past and modern technological innovation. The application moves beyond static information by providing an immersive, community-driven experience that preserves the "soul" of the city.
Core Functionality and User Experience
The user journey begins with an Interactive Map Interface, meticulously planned and prototyped within the Kiro framework. Unlike standard maps, Sonar Kolkata allows users to browse iconic landmarks such as the Victoria Memorial, Marble Palace, and Jorasanko Thakur Bari. Through a "Personalized Tour" feature, users can add specific sites to their preferences and launch a curated exploration of the city.
To bring these locations to life, the platform utilizes an AI-powered Audio Engine. By integrating the Eleven Labs API, the app generates high-quality, immersive narratives that turn historical facts into engaging oral traditions. Complementing this is the AI Historian Agent, a specialized tool trained on Kolkata’s history that provides real-time answers to user queries about architecture, culture, and local legends.
Community-Driven Preservation
A standout feature of the project is the "Explore & Upload" portal. Recognizing that heritage is a living thing, the platform empowers the community to map "unmapped" locations. Users can upload images of hidden heritage spots, share local stories, and input precise Latitude and Longitude coordinates to ensure these sites are pinned accurately for future explorers. This crowdsourced data ensures that local history is documented and preserved digitally before it is lost to time.
Innovative Technical Architecture
The technical execution of Sonar Kolkata is rooted in structured planning and resilience. For gamification and verifiable exploration, the project utilizes the Avalanche Fuji Testnet to mint Proof-of-Visit NFTs. These tokens serve as permanent, digital souvenirs for users who visit specific sites or contribute to the community map.
Understanding the challenges of mobile usage in Kolkata’s narrow lanes, the development team used Requestly within the Kiro environment to simulate and optimize for slow 3G/4G network conditions. This ensures that the app remains responsive with offline fallbacks and cached content, regardless of signal strength.
The Kiro Advantage
The entire project lifecycle was managed within the Kiro IDE, which acted as a unified source of truth for the team. From blueprinting user flows to generating an Architecture and Design README for AWS deployment, the Kiro framework ensured the project was built for scalability. This structured approach allowed the team to resolve architectural bottlenecks early and produce a robust, cloud-ready application that is currently optimized for the AWS Free Tier.
Sonar Kolkata is more than a mobile application; it is a movement to save the heart of the city through technology.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Current navigation methods mainly optimize time or distance, without considering **fuel economy, CO₂ emissions, driving behavior, or route reliability**. As a result, transportation companies and road users often follow routes that appear optimal but, in reality, lead to:

- Increased fuel consumption  
- Higher CO₂ emissions  
- Unpredictable delays  
- Operational inefficiencies  

Additionally, many existing eco-routing systems operate as black boxes. Users cannot understand why a particular route was chosen or which factors influenced the decision. This lack of transparency limits their applicability in logistics planning, policy formulation, and sustainability analysis.

 What This Project Solves:-

This project implements an ML-Enhanced Eco-Routing System that selects routes from an environmental, reliability, and explainability perspective.

Instead of only answering:

>“Which route is the fastest?

The system answers:

> “Which route is the most fuel-efficient, low-emission, and reliable for this driver under current conditions?

The system combines predictive machine learning with deterministic and explainable routing algorithms to ensure transparency and reliability.

 Smarter Route Decisions

- Considers fuel consumption, CO₂ emissions, traffic congestion, driving behavior**, and **route risk
- Avoids routes that appear optimal but have historically shown **high delays or unreliability**

 Explainable & Trustworthy Routing

- Each routing decision is based on an **explicit and interpretable cost function**
- Human-readable explanations describe **why one route is chosen over another**
- Enables trust and accountability in logistics and planning use cases

 Safer and More Reliable Navigation

- Penalizes routes with frequent congestion, rerouting, or delays
- Prioritizes **predictable and stable routes**, improving delivery planning accuracy

Where Machine Learning Matters (Not Black-Box Routing):-

- Machine learning is used **only to predict real-world conditions** (e.g., congestion likelihood, emission trends)
- Final routing decisions are made using **deterministic algorithms**
- Includes **fallback mechanisms** so the system remains functional even when ML predictions fail



Who Can Use This System:-

 Logistics & Fleet Operators

- Reduce fuel costs and emissions
- Plan stable and reliable delivery routes
- Track sustainability metrics and meet environmental goals

 Urban Mobility & Smart Cities

- Support environment-friendly navigation policies
- Analyze emission-aware routing at city scale
- Enable data-driven traffic and sustainability planning

Environmentally Conscious Road Users

- Choose routes that minimize environmental impact
- Understand trade-offs between time, fuel usage, and emissions

Researchers & Developers

- Experiment with explainable eco-routing algorithms
- Extend the system with new prediction models or policies
- Study sustainable transportation systems

**Challenges we ran into**

#  Challenges We Ran Into (and How We Solved Them)

## OSMnx Version Compatibility

### Problem  
While creating the road network graph using **OSMnx**, the backend system failed during initialization due to **API inconsistencies across OSMnx versions**.  
Functions such as `graph_from_bbox()` changed their parameter structure and behavior, causing the application to crash even before the API server could start.

### Solution  
- Refactored the graph construction logic to be **fully compatible with OSMnx 2.x**
- Passed the **bounding box as a single tuple** as required by the updated API
- Enriched graph edges with required attributes such as:
  - `length`
  - `speed`
  - `travel_time`
- Added **defensive validation checks** to ensure the graph contains valid nodes and edges before routing begins


## Ensuring ML Didn’t Break Deterministic Routing

### Challenge  
Using multiple ML models (traffic, fuel consumption, driver behavior, route risk) risked making the routing logic **unstable or unpredictable**, especially if models failed or produced noisy outputs.

### Solution  
- Machine Learning models were designed to be **strictly advisory**
- Final routing decisions are made using **deterministic algorithms**
- Every ML output has a **rules-based fallback**
- The system remains fully functional even when:
  - ML predictions fail
  - Data is missing or incomplete



##  Integrating ML Outputs Across Multiple Components

### Problem  
ML predictions needed to influence routing decisions **without tightly coupling components** or breaking system modularity.

### Solution  
Each ML model was integrated at the **correct abstraction layer**:

- **Traffic Prediction** → Environmental Model  
- **Driver Behavior** → Driver Model  
- **Fuel Prediction** → Fuel & Emission Agent  
- **Route Risk Estimation** → Route Ranking Phase  

This ensured:
- Clear separation of concerns  
- Clean modular design  
- Controlled and explainable influence of ML on routing decisions  



##  API Startup & Lifecycle Errors

### Problem  
The FastAPI application experienced startup failures when heavy initialization tasks (such as road graph construction) encountered errors, making failures hard to debug.

### Solution  
- Moved critical initialization logic into controlled startup phases
- Added robust **error handling and logging**
- Introduced **graph construction validation**
- Ensured startup failures are **explicit and visible**, rather than silent runtime errors



## Balancing Realism vs Demo Stability

### Problem  
Using live map data and real-time ML predictions increased the risk of demo-time failures due to:
- Network issues  
- Missing data  
- Unstable predictions  

### Solution  
Focused on **graceful degradation**:
- Deterministic fallbacks
- Explainable and human-readable outputs
- Clear separation between:
  - Decision logic
  - Visualization layer  

This ensured the system is **demo-ready**, while remaining realistic and extensible.



## Key Learning

Building a **production-grade eco-routing system** requires more focus on:

- Real-world uncertainty
- Library and dependency incompatibilities
- System robustness and reliability  

…rather than simply adding more AI.

> **Engineering reliability and explainability mattered more than model complexity.**

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/smart-solid-waste-management-and-payment-transparency-5c2a) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://my-wastedbin.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/hS1Tz-dQQxM?si=-zALhI45XSKR6Eoz) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co)

> Waste Managed, Trust Delivered

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI False Positives & Lighting Conditions
The Hurdle: Our initial Image Classification model (likely CNN or ResNet) worked perfectly in bright daylight but failed miserably during early morning or evening pickups. Shadows were often misclassified as "overflowing waste," and shiny metallic bins were sometimes not detected at all due to glare.

How we got over it: We used Data Augmentation during the training phase.

We didn't just feed the model standard images; we programmatically altered our training dataset by adjusting brightness, contrast, and adding artificial noise.

We also implemented a confidence threshold logic: The AI only triggers an automatic ticket if the confidence score is >85%. If it is between 50-85%, it flags it for manual human review on the dashboard rather than rejecting it outright.

**Challenges we ran into**

AI Reliability: Struggling with false positives where shadows, lighting, or large flat objects (like cardboard) tricked the AI into seeing a "full" bin when it was actually empty.

The "Truth" Gap: Ensuring the blockchain record matched reality—preventing staff from logging a "completed" pickup without actually being at the bin (requiring GPS geofencing).

Blockchain Friction: High Gas fees and slow transaction speeds on Ethereum, which forced a move toward Layer 2 solutions (like Polygon) to keep the system affordable.

Logistics Complexity: The mathematical difficulty of dynamic rerouting—constantly updating truck paths in real-time as new citizen requests poured in.

User Participation: Finding ways to motivate citizens to actually take and upload photos regularly without a built-in incentive/reward system.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/foodlink-ai-53e9) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://fooddonateweb.netlify.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/q60gPEoOdm4?si=R-8ICF7YVdfbfP7W) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co)

> “AI that matches every meal with a need.”

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every day, a large amount of fresh and edible food is wasted by restaurants, canteens, events, and food vendors. At the same time, many people still suffer from hunger and lack of access to basic meals.
The main issue is not food availability, but poor coordination and slow communication between food donors and people who need food. Most food donation processes depend on manual calls, WhatsApp messages, or volunteers’ availability, which often leads to delays and food spoilage.
FoodLink AI solves this by creating a smart and fast way to connect food donors with NGOs, shelters, and volunteers in real time. Using an AI agent, the platform automatically matches surplus food with nearby receivers based on location, quantity, and urgency, reducing waste and improving fair distribution.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing the AI-based matching logic in a short time. Deciding how to prioritize food requests based on distance, time, and availability was tricky.
Another challenge was handling real-time updates and notifications, especially when multiple donors and receivers are active at the same time.
To overcome this, I started with a simple rule-based system and then improved it step by step. I also focused on building a clean and minimal user flow first, instead of adding too many features early. This helped in making the system more stable and easier to test.

**Ethereum Track**

HTML, CSS, JavaScript
React (Frontend)
Node.js & Express (Backend)
MongoDB (Database)
AI Agent logic (rule-based + ML-ready design)
Google Maps / Location APIs

### TinySubs- Onchain Micro Subscriptions for Creators
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tinysubs-frictionless-onchain-microsubscriptions-0db1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lesliefdo08/TinySubs) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/mwPR5jGu9oA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20Onchain%20with%20FBI-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://build-onchain-fbi.devfolio.co)

> Instant on-chain tips for every creator.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

TinySubs solves one of the biggest missing pieces in the blockchain ecosystem — frictionless, low-cost recurring payments.

Traditionally, setting up small, periodic payments (₹10/₹20/₹50 equivalents) is either expensive due to gas fees, requires complex smart contract setups, or forces creators and developers to rely on centralized platforms that take high cuts.

TinySubs makes micro-subscriptions possible onchain by providing:

- Instant, low-fee payments using smart contracts
- Recurring billing that doesn’t require manual user approval each time
- A simple UI where creators can create subscription tiers in seconds
- Developer-friendly APIs for integrating subscription logic into any app
- Security-by-default, since funds flow directly from user → creator
- No middlemen, meaning creators keep almost everything

Users can subscribe to newsletters, premium content, tools, communities, or even pay small periodic donations — fully onchain, fully automated, and completely transparent.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building TinySubs came with several technical hurdles.
One of the first challenges was figuring out how to model on-chain recurring micro-payments. Traditional subscriptions rely on automated off-chain billing, so translating that into a decentralized, pull-based flow required experimenting with token approvals, transfer permissions, and finding a safe pattern that doesn’t compromise user control.

Another challenge was gas optimization. My earlier contract designs were functional but unnecessarily heavy. After profiling the gas usage, I had to refactor the architecture into a more modular and minimal structure, which reduced cost and made the code easier to maintain.

Integrating the frontend with smart contracts also brought difficulties. Simple actions like approving tokens or checking subscription state required careful handling of asynchronous blockchain calls, transaction confirmations, and error states. Ensuring that the UI always reflected the latest on-chain data took multiple iterations.

I also ran into issues with testnet liquidity. Some networks didn’t have stablecoin faucets available, which made it hard to simulate real micro-transactions. To work around this, I switched networks, used fallback tokens, and created mock flows to keep development moving without blocking the user experience.

Finally, working solo meant managing both the contract layer and the full UI/UX within limited time. Balancing speed with correctness was challenging, especially while ensuring the system behaved reliably across multiple wallet combinations and test networks.
